notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Research Summary

### Scope
Web UI for viewing/editing kspec state with:
1. Local daemon mode for real-time interactive editing
2. Static GitHub Pages export for read-only display/linking

### Tech Stack (per user preference)
- **Frontend**: Svelte 5 + SvelteKit + shadcn-svelte
- **Backend**: Hono (lightweight HTTP server) with SSE for real-time
- **File watching**: Chokidar with debouncing
- **IPC**: Unix socket for CLI-daemon, HTTP for web UI

---

## Codebase Findings

The kspec codebase is **excellently architected** for web API:
- **Library-first**: All logic in src/parser/ and src/schema/, independent of CLI
- **Pre-built indexes**: ItemIndex, ReferenceIndex, TraitIndex ready for query APIs
- **Zod schemas**: Validation for all types, input/patch schemas exist
- **Pagination**: ItemIndex.queryPaginated() already built
- **Shadow branch**: Auto-commit infrastructure handles persistence

Key files for API layer:
- src/parser/yaml.ts - Core YAML I/O, context init
- src/parser/items.ts - ItemIndex for queries
- src/parser/refs.ts - ReferenceIndex for @refs
- src/schema/*.ts - All Zod schemas

---

## Architecture Recommendation

```
CLI ←→ Unix Socket ←→ Daemon ←→ HTTP/SSE ←→ Web UI
                         ↓
                    Chokidar (file watching)
                         ↓
                    .kspec/*.yaml
```

### Daemon Mode
- `kspec serve` - foreground server
- `kspec serve --daemon` - background with PID file
- `kspec serve stop` - graceful shutdown
- Health endpoints: /livez, /readyz

### API Endpoints (based on existing operations)
- GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/tasks/:ref
- GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/items/:ref
- GET/POST/DELETE /api/inbox/:ref
- GET /api/meta/{agents,workflows,conventions,observations}
- POST /api/query (advanced filtering)
- GET /api/events (SSE stream)

### Web UI Structure
```
/                    - Dashboard overview
/tasks/              - Task list with filters
/tasks/@slug/        - Task detail (notes, todos, actions)
/specs/              - Spec tree view
/specs/@ref/         - Spec item detail with ACs
/inbox/              - Inbox management
/session/            - Current session context
```

### Dual Deployment
- **Dynamic**: adapter-node for local daemon
- **Static**: adapter-static for GitHub Pages
- Conditional adapter via env var at build time
- Static mode loads from pre-built JSON snapshots

---

## Svelte 5 Notes

- Uses runes: $state, $derived, $effect
- .svelte.ts files for shared reactive state
- shadcn-svelte has 50+ components (data-table, sidebar, etc.)
- SSE integration works well with runes for real-time

---

## GitHub Pages Patterns

- Trigger GitHub Action on kspec-meta branch push
- Checkout both branches (data + site code)
- Prerender routes for deep linking: /tasks/@slug/
- Show last-updated timestamps from git history
- Add .nojekyll to static/ dir

---

## Phased Implementation Suggestion

**Phase 1: Foundation**
- Daemon server with Hono
- Core API endpoints (tasks, items, inbox)
- SSE for real-time updates
- File watching with Chokidar

**Phase 2: Web Dashboard**
- SvelteKit project setup
- Dashboard overview page
- Task list and detail views
- Real-time update integration

**Phase 3: Full CRUD**
- Task actions (start, complete, add notes)
- Spec item viewing
- Inbox management

**Phase 4: GitHub Pages**
- Static export configuration
- GitHub Actions workflow
- Deep linking support

---

## Open Questions
- Should daemon auto-start when CLI is used, or always explicit?
- Port configuration: fixed vs dynamic with service discovery?
- Auth for multi-user scenarios (future)?

tasks.title: Meta resolve and promote commands missing commitIfShadow calls
tasks.description:
The `kspec meta resolve` command updates observations in kynetic.meta.yaml but does not auto-commit changes to the shadow branch.

## Root Cause

In src/cli/commands/meta.ts:
- Line 1076: `await saveObservation(ctx, observation)` saves the update
- BUT no `commitIfShadow()` call follows, unlike other meta commands

## Secondary Issue

The `meta promote` command has a similar gap:
- Line 969: Calls `commitIfShadow()` for task creation
- Line 979: Saves updated observation with promoted_to field
- Missing second `commitIfShadow()` after the observation update

- Shadow branch state diverges from observation state
- Resolution changes not tracked in git history
- `kspec log @obs-ref` misses resolution events
- Remote shadow sync issues

Add `commitIfShadow()` calls:
1. After `saveObservation()` in resolve command (~line 1076)
2. After `saveObservation()` in promote command (~line 979)

Pattern to follow (from meta observe command):
```typescript
await commitIfShadow(
  ctx.shadow,
  "meta-resolve",
  observation._ulid.substring(0, 8),
  "Resolved observation",
);
```

tasks.title: Implement: Semantic YAML Merge Driver
tasks.closed_reason: Breaking into smaller tasks for manageable session scope

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

A custom git merge driver that parses both versions of kspec YAML files and merges them semantically, understanding the structure of tasks, items, and other kspec entities. This prevents git from creating conflict markers that would corrupt YAML files.

Note on exit codes: This command intentionally does NOT use @trait-semantic-exit-codes because git merge drivers have special requirements - they must exit 0 to prevent git from falling back to its text merge, which would corrupt YAML.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given git attempts to merge two versions of a kspec YAML file, when the merge driver is configured, then kspec parses all three versions (base, ours, theirs) as structured data instead of text
- ac-2: Given both versions add different items to an array (tasks, inbox, specs), when merge runs, then both additions are included in result (union merge by ULID)
- ac-3: Given both versions modify different fields of the same item, when merge runs, then fields are merged (non-conflicting field changes combined)
- ac-4: Given both versions modify the same scalar field (title, description, priority) of the same item, when merge runs, then user is prompted interactively to choose which value to keep
- ac-5: Given both versions modify append-only arrays (notes, todos), when merge runs, then arrays are union merged by ULID (notes never conflict)
- ac-6: Given both versions modify set-like arrays (tags, depends_on), when merge runs, then arrays are set-unioned (duplicates removed)
- ac-7: Given both versions modify nested objects (status, traceability), when merge runs, then nested fields are merged recursively at field level
- ac-8: Given one version deletes an item while other modifies it, when merge runs, then user is prompted interactively to choose delete vs keep modified
- ac-9: Given merge completes with no true conflicts, when driver exits, then exit code 0, merged YAML written to output path
- ac-10: Given merge has unresolvable conflicts and --non-interactive flag set, when driver exits, then conflict markers written as YAML comments, exit code 0 (prevents git fallback)
- ac-11: Given YAML parsing fails on any input file, when driver runs, then falls back gracefully: copies ours verbatim, creates .kspec-merge-failed marker, exits 0
- ac-12: Given kspec init runs in a new repo, when initialization completes, then merge driver is configured in .git/config and .gitattributes updated in shadow branch

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation approach from plan:

**Files to create:**
- src/merge/index.ts - Public API exports
- src/merge/driver.ts - Git driver entry point
- src/merge/semantic.ts - Merge algorithms by entity type
- src/merge/conflicts.ts - Conflict detection, prompting, comment format
- src/merge/types.ts - MergeResult, ConflictInfo types

**Files to modify:**
- src/cli/index.ts - Register merge-driver command
- src/parser/shadow.ts - Add configureMergeDriver() to init

**Key merge strategies by field type:**
- ULID-keyed arrays: Union by ULID, merge matching items (tasks, items, agents, workflows)
- Append-only arrays: Union by ULID, never conflict (notes, todos)
- Set-like arrays: Set union (tags, depends_on, implements)
- Scalar fields: Prompt on conflict (title, description, priority)
- Nested objects: Recursive field merge (status, traceability, project)

**Critical git behavior:**
- Always exit 0 to prevent git from falling back to text merge
- On conflict in non-interactive mode: write conflicts as YAML comments
- On parse failure: copy ours verbatim, create .kspec-merge-failed marker

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

Long-running Elysia.js server on Bun runtime that exposes kspec state via HTTP API and WebSocket
for real-time updates. Binds to localhost only for security. Supports foreground and background
modes with PID file management. Includes heartbeat ping/pong for connection health monitoring.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given kspec is installed, when user runs 'kspec serve', then Elysia HTTP server starts on configurable port (default 3456) binding to localhost only
- ac-2: Given daemon is starting, when server binds to network interface, then only accepts connections from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (IPv6 localhost)
- ac-3: Given connection attempt from non-localhost IP, when request received, then connection rejected with 403 Forbidden
- ac-4: Given daemon is running, when any .kspec/*.yaml file changes, then connected WebSocket clients receive update event via topic subscription
- ac-5: Given file watching is active, when rapid changes occur (< 500ms apart), then events are debounced and aggregated into single notification
- ac-6: Given watched file has YAML parse error, when change detected, then error logged and WebSocket broadcasts error event (daemon does not crash)
- ac-7: Given .kspec directory becomes inaccessible, when watcher encounters error, then daemon logs error and attempts recovery with exponential backoff
- ac-8: Given Bun fs.watch fails or misses events, when reliability issue detected, then automatically fall back to Chokidar file watcher
- ac-9: Given daemon is running, when user runs 'kspec serve --daemon', then process detaches to background, writes PID to .kspec/.daemon.pid, CLI returns immediately
- ac-10: Given daemon is running in background, when user runs 'kspec serve stop', then daemon shuts down gracefully, removes PID file, closes all WebSocket connections
- ac-11: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/health is called, then returns {status, uptime, connections, version} JSON
- ac-12: Given daemon receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, when shutdown signal received, then graceful shutdown (flush pending messages, close connections, save state)
- ac-13: Given WebSocket connection established, when 30 seconds pass without activity, then server sends ping frame
- ac-14: Given ping was sent, when no pong received within 90 seconds, then connection closed with code 1001
- ac-15: Given Elysia server is configured, when routes are registered, then use plugin pattern for middleware (CORS, logging, validation)
- ac-16: Given daemon code is ready, when bun build --compile runs, then produces standalone executable without requiring Bun installation

- ac-11: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/items/:ref/tasks is called, then returns tasks linked to this spec via AlignmentIndex
- ac-12: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/inbox is called, then returns all inbox items ordered by created_at desc
- ac-13: Given daemon is running, when POST /api/inbox with {text} body, then creates inbox item, returns with generated ULID
- ac-14: Given daemon is running, when DELETE /api/inbox/:ref is called, then removes inbox item, returns success confirmation
- ac-15: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/meta/session is called, then returns current session context (focus, threads, questions)
- ac-16: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/meta/agents is called, then returns all defined agents
- ac-17: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/meta/workflows is called, then returns all defined workflows
- ac-18: Given daemon is running, when GET /api/meta/observations with filter (?resolved=false), then returns observations matching filter

- ac-23: Given API request has validation error, when POST/PUT with invalid body, then returns {error, details:[{field, message}]} with 400 status
- ac-24: Given API request causes state transition error, when POST action violates state machine, then returns {error, current, valid_transitions} with 409 status
- ac-25: Given client connects to /ws, when WebSocket connection established, then receives connected event with {session_id}
- ac-26: Given WebSocket connection active, when client sends command, then command format is {action, request_id?, payload}
- ac-27: Given command received, when processed, then server sends {ack: true, request_id, success, error?}
- ac-28: Given WebSocket connection, when client sends {action: 'subscribe', topics: ['files:updates']}, then server tracks subscription and sends events for that topic
- ac-29: Given file changes in .kspec/, when WebSocket client subscribed to files:updates, then receives event with format {msg_id, seq, timestamp, topic, event, data: {ref, action}}
- ac-30: Given malformed command received, when parsed, then return {ack: false, error: 'validation_error', details: ...}

backoff reconnection and sequence deduplication.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given daemon is running and browser opens localhost:3456, when page loads, then dashboard shows task overview with ready, in_progress, pending_review, blocked, completed counts
- ac-2: Given dashboard is displayed, when task counts update on server, then counts animate to new values without page refresh (WebSocket-driven)
- ac-3: Given dashboard is displayed, when user clicks a task count badge, then navigates to task list filtered by that status
- ac-4: Given user is viewing task list, when list loads, then shows task title, status badge, priority indicator, spec_ref link, notes count
- ac-5: Given user is viewing task list, when clicking a task row, then task detail panel opens showing description, notes (chronological), todos, dependencies
- ac-6: Given user is viewing task detail, when task has spec_ref, then spec reference is clickable link to spec item detail
- ac-7: Given user is viewing task detail, when user clicks Start Task button, then POST to /api/tasks/:ref/start, task status updates, UI reflects change
- ac-8: Given user is viewing task detail, when user types in note textarea and clicks Add Note, then POST to /api/tasks/:ref/note, note appears in list
- ac-9: Given user is viewing task list, when filter controls are visible, then can filter by status, type, tag, assignee, automation status
- ac-10: Given user applies filter, when filter selection changes, then URL updates with query params, list updates without full reload
- ac-11: Given user navigates to /items, when spec tree displays, then shows hierarchical tree with modules > features > requirements, expand/collapse
- ac-12: Given user clicks spec item in tree, when item detail panel opens, then shows title, description, acceptance criteria (GWT format), traits, implementation status
- ac-13: Given spec item has linked tasks, when viewing item detail, then Implementation section shows linked tasks with their status
- ac-14: Given spec item has traits, when viewing item detail, then Traits section shows trait titles as chips, clickable to trait detail
- ac-15: Given user clicks acceptance criterion, when AC row expands, then shows full Given/When/Then text with test coverage indicator if available
- ac-16: Given user navigates to /inbox, when inbox list displays, then shows items ordered by created_at desc with text preview, tags, added_by
- ac-17: Given user clicks Add button, when input field appears, then user can type text, press Enter to submit
- ac-18: Given new inbox item submitted, when POST succeeds, then item appears at top of list with animation
- ac-19: Given user clicks delete button on item, when confirmation appears, then on confirm, item removed from list
- ac-20: Given dashboard header area, when session has focus set, then displays current focus text prominently
- ac-21: Given dashboard sidebar, when observations exist, then shows unresolved observations count badge
- ac-22: Given user clicks observations badge, when observations panel opens, then lists unresolved observations with type icons (friction/success/question/idea)
- ac-23: Given user presses Cmd+K (or Ctrl+K), when command palette opens, then shows search input with placeholder
- ac-24: Given user types in search box, when debounced search fires (300ms), then results show tasks, items, inbox matching query grouped by type
- ac-25: Given search results display, when user clicks a result, then navigates to detail view for that item
- ac-26: Given browser width < 768px, when viewing any page, then layout adapts to single column, sidebar becomes bottom nav
- ac-27: Given browser width >= 1024px, when viewing detail panels, then detail panel opens as slide-over without navigating away from list
- ac-28: Given WebSocket connection drops, when reconnect logic triggers, then automatic reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s... max 30s)
- ac-29: Given WebSocket disconnected for >10s, when viewing dashboard, then Connection lost indicator shown
- ac-30: Given events received via WebSocket, when seq <= lastSeqProcessed, then skip duplicate events (sequence deduplication)
- ac-31: Given WebSocket reconnects, when connection established, then client resets lastSeqProcessed = -1 (server generates new sequence)
- ac-32: Given WebSocket reconnects, when connection established, then client re-subscribes to all previous topics
- ac-33: Given another client modifies task, when WebSocket update received, then task list/detail updates without refresh, subtle highlight animation on changed item

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

Static site generation from kspec state for hosting read-only views on GitHub Pages.
CI workflow builds JSON snapshot from shadow branch on push, SPA reads this JSON for rendering.
Enables deep linking to tasks/specs from PRs and issues with data freshness indicator.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given kspec is installed, when user runs 'kspec export --format json', then writes kspec-snapshot.json containing all tasks, items, inbox, meta to stdout or --output path
- ac-2: Given export runs, when output is generated, then JSON includes exported_at timestamp, version (kspec version), project metadata
- ac-3: Given export runs, when tasks are included, then each task includes resolved spec_ref title (not just ref string) for display without resolution
- ac-4: Given export runs, when items are included, then hierarchical structure preserved, acceptance_criteria expanded, traits resolved to include inherited ACs
- ac-5: Given export runs with --include-validation, when validation is run, then JSON includes validation block with error/warning counts and details
- ac-6: Given kspec is installed, when user runs 'kspec export --format html', then generates self-contained HTML file with embedded JSON and SPA code
- ac-7: Given kspec is installed, when user runs 'kspec export --dry-run', then shows what would be exported without writing files
- ac-8: Given push to kspec-meta branch, when CI workflow triggers, then runs kspec export, commits to gh-pages branch
- ac-9: Given CI workflow runs, when SPA assets don't exist, then copies SPA static assets (HTML, JS, CSS) to docs/ alongside JSON
- ac-10: Given rapid commits to kspec-meta, when multiple pushes within 30 seconds, then CI debounces and runs once with latest state
- ac-11: Given user opens gh-pages URL, when SPA loads, then fetches kspec-snapshot.json from same origin, renders dashboard
- ac-12: Given user navigates to /tasks/@task-slug, when deep link resolves, then SPA parses path (history API), shows task detail for that ref
- ac-13: Given user navigates to /items/@spec-slug, when deep link resolves, then SPA shows spec item detail for that ref
- ac-14: Given SPA renders, when validation data present in snapshot, then shows validation summary badge (green check or red X with count)
- ac-15: Given static export page, when displayed to user, then shows 'Data as of: [timestamp]' indicator prominently
- ac-16: Given viewing task in SPA mode, when user sees Start Task button area, then button is disabled with tooltip explaining read-only mode
- ac-17: Given viewing inbox in SPA mode, when Add button area visible, then button is disabled/hidden
- ac-18: Given SPA mode, when any write action attempted, then graceful no-op with informative message

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

CLI commands for managing the daemon server lifecycle. Provides human and script-friendly
interfaces to start, stop, and monitor the daemon.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given daemon not running, when kspec serve executed, then starts server in foreground, logs to stdout, Ctrl+C stops
- ac-2: Given daemon not running, when kspec serve --daemon executed, then starts in background, writes PID file, returns immediately with status message
- ac-3: Given daemon not running, when kspec serve --port 8080 executed, then starts on specified port
- ac-4: Given daemon running, when kspec serve stop executed, then sends SIGTERM to daemon PID, waits for clean shutdown, removes PID file
- ac-5: Given daemon not running, when kspec serve stop executed, then outputs 'Daemon not running' with exit code 0 (idempotent)
- ac-6: Given any state, when kspec serve status executed, then outputs JSON with {running, pid, port, uptime, connections}
- ac-7: Given daemon running, when kspec serve restart executed, then stops existing daemon, starts new one, preserves port setting
- ac-8: Given any state, when kspec serve logs executed, then tails daemon log file (.kspec/.daemon.log)
- ac-9: Given daemon running, when kspec serve logs --follow executed, then streams log output continuously until Ctrl+C
- ac-10: Given port already in use, when kspec serve attempts to start, then fails with clear error message suggesting --port flag

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Notes

### Objective
Implement file watcher for .kspec/ directory with debouncing and WebSocket broadcast.

### Steps
1. Create file watcher using Bun fs.watch (primary) with Chokidar fallback:
   ```typescript
   import { watch } from 'fs';
   function watchKspec(callback: (files: string[]) => void) {
     const watcher = watch('.kspec', { recursive: true }, (event, filename) => {
       // Debounce and aggregate
       debouncedNotify(filename);
     });
   }
   ```

2. Implement 500ms debounce for rapid changes

3. Handle YAML parse errors gracefully (log, broadcast error event, don't crash)

4. Handle directory inaccessible errors with exponential backoff recovery

5. Broadcast changes to subscribed WebSocket clients via topic 'files:updates'

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Notes

### Objective
Implement WebSocket protocol with Elysia ws(), topic-based pub/sub, heartbeat, and request_id correlation.

### Steps
1. Create WebSocket route with Elysia:
   ```typescript
   app.ws('/ws', {
     open(ws) {
       ws.data.sessionId = ulid();
       ws.send({ event: 'connected', data: { session_id: ws.data.sessionId } });
     },
     message(ws, message) {
       handleCommand(ws, JSON.parse(message));
     },
     close(ws) {
       // Cleanup subscriptions
     }
   })
   ```

2. Implement command handling:
   - subscribe: Track topics, send ack
   - unsubscribe: Remove topics, send ack
   - Other commands: Process and ack

3. Implement heartbeat ping/pong (30s interval, 90s timeout)

4. Implement backpressure handling (pause broadcasts on slow clients)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Notes

### Objective
Implement WebSocketManager with connection state machine, reconnection, and sequence deduplication.

### Steps
1. WebSocketManager class (based on kynetic pattern):
   - States: disconnected -> connecting -> connected -> reconnecting

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Notes

### Objective
Create GitHub Actions workflow to build and deploy to GitHub Pages.

### Steps
1. Create .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:
   - Trigger on push to kspec-meta branch
   - Debounce rapid commits (30s)
   - Run kspec export
   - Build SPA
   - Deploy to gh-pages branch

2. Workflow steps:
   ```yaml
   on:
     push:
       branches: [kspec-meta]
   jobs:
     deploy:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
           with:
             ref: kspec-meta
         - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
         - run: bun install
         - run: bun run kspec export --format json -o docs/kspec-snapshot.json
         - run: bun run build:web-ui
         - uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
   ```

3. Copy SPA assets alongside JSON

### ACs Covered
- ac-8: Trigger on kspec-meta push
- ac-9: Copy SPA assets
- ac-10: Debounce rapid commits

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Investigation Findings

### Root Cause
The path resolution in serve.ts uses fragile relative path math:
```typescript
const packageRoot = join(__dirname, '../../..');
```

This works in development (goes from dist/cli/commands to project root) but fails for npm installs where the package structure is different.

### Current Test Failures
The 7 failing serve tests are actually caused by a **separate bug** in test setup:
- Tests call `setupTempFixtures(tempDir)` but function takes no args
- Function ignores tempDir and creates a NEW directory
- Result: test's .kspec/ directory never created, daemon can't write PID file

### Decision: Bundle Daemon
User confirmed daemon is a core feature, should be bundled into main package rather than separate install.

**Size impact:** ~3-4% increase (daemon is 2K lines, 116KB source vs 2.7MB dist)
**Build impact:** Minimal - add to tsconfig include
**New deps:** elysia, @elysiajs/cors, chokidar

## Implementation Plan

1. Add daemon deps to main package.json
2. Update tsconfig to include packages/daemon/src
3. Update serve.ts path resolution to use dist/daemon/index.js
4. Fix test setup (create .kspec/ dir explicitly)
5. Ensure daemon auto-creates PID directory for robustness

2. **serve.ts** - Updated daemon path resolution:
   - Now resolves to dist/daemon/index.ts (bundled with package)

3. **pid-utils.ts** (both CLI and daemon):

### Architecture Decision
Daemon source is bundled as TypeScript (not compiled) because:
- Daemon requires Bun runtime for best performance (Elysia optimized for Bun)
- Bun runs TypeScript directly
- Avoids TypeScript strict mode issues in daemon code

notes.content:
## Session Progress - Architecture Research

### Issue Identified
The immediate E2E test failures stemmed from:
1. **BUN_ENV not set to production** - Bun's dev mode was transforming HTML at runtime, causing asset hash mismatches
2. **Asset path resolution** - daemon wasn't finding web UI relative to package install location

### Root Cause: Architectural Limitation
Current daemon architecture has fundamental issues for the desired use case:
- One daemon per project directory (not scalable)
- Web UI assets resolved from cwd, not package install location
- No support for npm global/local install scenarios

### Research Findings (via subagent)
Recommended multi-directory daemon pattern (like eslint_d):
1. **Single daemon process** with LRU cache of project contexts
2. **Asset resolution chain**: Bun.embeddedFiles → import.meta.dirname/../web-ui/build → cwd dev fallback
3. **API design**: X-Kspec-Dir header to specify project context per request
4. **Memory management**: Max ~10 project contexts, auto-evict LRU

### Immediate Fixes Applied
- Discovered BUN_ENV=production fixes HTML hash mismatch
- Daemon API returning '{} is not iterable' error needs debugging (separate issue from assets)

### Blocking Decision Needed
This E2E task is blocked on architectural decision:
- **Option A**: Minimal fix for current architecture (just fix asset paths, single project)
- **Option B**: Implement multi-directory daemon architecture first

Task remains in_progress pending user decision on approach.

## Debugging the Blocking Issue

### Symptom
E2E test shows '1 items total' with only 'Test Requirement' visible.
Expected: 4 items (module, trait, feature, requirement) with proper hierarchy.

### What We Know
1. Shadow worktree simulation IS working - fixtures are being found (observations show as '4')
2. Items API returns data but only 1 item
3. ItemTree.svelte builds hierarchy using `item.parent` field
4. `extractItemsFromRaw()` in src/parser/yaml.ts does NOT set `parent` field

### Likely Root Causes (investigate in order)

1. **Schema validation failing silently** - SpecItemSchema.safeParse() may be rejecting items
   - Check: Add console.log in extractItemsFromRaw to see what items pass/fail validation
   - File: src/parser/yaml.ts:942-948

2. **Parent field not computed** - Items load flat, no parent ULIDs
   - ItemTree expects `item.parent` to be the parent's ULID
   - extractItemsFromRaw knows the parent (it's processing nested items) but doesn't set it
   - Fix: Pass parent ULID when recursing into nested items

3. **ULID validation** - Some fixture ULIDs may still be invalid
   - Already fixed AC ULIDs (were 25 chars, now 26)
   - Validate all ULIDs match: /^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/i

```bash

console.log('Loaded items:', items.length, items.map(i => i.title));

```

- src/parser/yaml.ts - extractItemsFromRaw() and loadAllItems()
- packages/daemon/src/routes/items.ts - API endpoint
- tests/fixtures/modules/core.yaml - Fixture structure

tasks.title: Spec multi-directory daemon architecture
tasks.description:
## Objective
Design and spec the multi-directory daemon architecture. This task produces specs and derived implementation tasks, not code.

## Background
Current daemon architecture has limitations:
- One daemon instance per project directory
- Web UI assets resolved from cwd, not package install location
- No support for npm global/local install scenarios
- E2E tests blocked by these architectural issues

## Research Findings (from @01KFP84J session)

### 1. Asset Resolution Pattern
Use `import.meta.dirname` to find assets relative to npm package installation:
```typescript
const packageRoot = import.meta.dirname;
const webUiPath = join(packageRoot, '../web-ui/build');
```

Resolution chain (in priority order):
1. `Bun.embeddedFiles` - for single-file executables via `bun build --compile`
2. `import.meta.dirname/../web-ui/build` - for npm installed package
3. `cwd/packages/web-ui/build` - for monorepo development

### 2. Multi-Directory Pattern (eslint_d style)
Single daemon process with LRU cache of project contexts:
- Max ~10 project contexts in memory
- Each context has: kspecDir, watcher, lastAccess timestamp
- Auto-evict least recently used when at capacity

### 3. API Design
- Add `X-Kspec-Dir` header to all API requests to specify project context
- New endpoints:
  - `POST /api/projects/register` - add project directory
  - `GET /api/projects` - list registered projects
  - `DELETE /api/projects/:id` - unregister project
- WebSocket subscriptions scoped to project context

### 4. Bun Single-File Executable
Can embed web UI into daemon binary:
```bash
bun build --compile ./server.ts ./web-ui/build/**/* --outfile kspec-daemon
```

## Deliverables
1. [ ] Create/update spec item for daemon server with new ACs
2. [ ] Create spec item for multi-project support
3. [ ] Create spec item for asset resolution
4. [ ] Derive implementation tasks from specs
5. [ ] Update E2E test infrastructure task dependencies

## References
- eslint_d architecture: https://github.com/mantoni/eslint_d.js
- Bun embeddedFiles: https://bun.com/docs/bundler/executables
- LSP workspaceFolders pattern

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Complete

Implemented loop mode error handling with per-task failure tracking.

### What was implemented:
1. **Error tracking utilities** (src/ralph/loop-errors.ts):
   - parseFailureCount() - Parse [LOOP-FAIL:N] prefix from notes (AC-4)
   - getTaskFailureCount() - Get highest failure count from task notes (AC-4)
   - createFailureNote() - Create failure note with incremented count (AC-1, AC-3)
   - shouldEscalate() - Check if threshold reached (AC-5)
   - isIterationFailure() - Determine if iteration result is a failure (AC-7)
   - hasTaskProgress() - Check for progress via new notes (AC-8)
   - processFailedIteration() - Main orchestration function (AC-2, AC-6, AC-8)

2. **Ralph integration** (src/cli/commands/ralph.ts):
   - handleIterationFailure() - Called after iteration fails
   - Tracks tasks in_progress at iteration start
   - Re-loads tasks after failure to check progress
   - Adds [LOOP-FAIL:N] notes to tasks without progress
   - Escalates to automation:needs_review at 3 failures (AC-5)

3. **Test coverage** (tests/ralph-loop-errors.test.ts):
   - 23 tests covering all 9 acceptance criteria
   - All tests passing

### How it works:
- At iteration start: capture active_tasks and timestamp
- After iteration fails: handleIterationFailure() is called
- For each task that was in_progress:
  - Check if it made progress (new non-LOOP-FAIL notes)
  - If no progress: add [LOOP-FAIL:N] note
  - If N reaches 3: set automation:needs_review

- src/ralph/loop-errors.ts (new)
- src/ralph/index.ts (exports)

tasks.description:
## Problem

The ralph loop does not exit when all in_progress tasks are marked automation:needs_review. This caused an overnight session to run 30 iterations with no progress because:

1. Tasks were picked up and marked in_progress
2. Agent correctly marked them automation:needs_review (needing daemon/E2E testing)
3. But the exit condition checks `\!hasActiveTasks && \!hasReadyTasks`
4. active_tasks includes ALL in_progress tasks regardless of automation status
5. Loop kept running, adding redundant notes each iteration

## Root Cause

In `src/cli/commands/session.ts`, `gatherSessionContext()`:
- `ready_tasks` correctly filters by `automation === 'eligible'` when `options.eligible` is true (line 394)
- `active_tasks` has NO automation filter - includes all in_progress tasks (lines 365-369)

In `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` (lines 736-742):
```typescript
const hasActiveTasks = sessionCtx.active_tasks.length > 0;
const hasReadyTasks = sessionCtx.ready_tasks.length > 0;
if (\!hasActiveTasks && \!hasReadyTasks) {
  info('No active or eligible ready tasks. Exiting loop.');
  break;
}
```

## Fix Required

When `options.eligible` is true, filter `activeTasks` the same way as `readyTasks`:
```typescript
const activeTasks = allTasks
  .filter((t) => t.status === 'in_progress')
  .filter((t) => \!options.eligible || t.automation === 'eligible')  // Add this
  ...
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-16: Both ready and in_progress tasks filtered by automation eligibility
- AC-19: Loop exits when no eligible tasks remain (ready OR in_progress)

## Testing

- Verify loop exits when all in_progress tasks are needs_review
- Verify loop continues when eligible in_progress tasks exist
- Existing tests should still pass

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
**Background - Why this matters:**

When two branches modify `depends_on` arrays using different reference formats for the same item, the merge driver treats them as different values, creating false conflicts or duplicate entries.

**How to reproduce:**
1. Branch A adds: `depends_on: ["@task-watcher-impl"]` (slug format)
2. Branch B adds: `depends_on: ["@01KFPRX9"]` (ULID format)
3. Both reference the SAME task
4. Merge results in: `depends_on: ["@task-watcher-impl", "@01KFPRX9"]` (duplicate!)

**Example conflict seen in real merge:**
```
Ours:   ["@task-watcher-impl"]
Theirs: ["@01KFPRX9"]
```

These are the same ref - merge driver should recognize equivalence and deduplicate.

**Expected behavior:**
After merge, `depends_on` should have ONE entry (either format is acceptable, preferring ours).

**Key insight:**
The merge driver runs during git operations. It may not have full kspec context loaded. Implementation needs to either:
1. Load a minimal ref index during merge, or
2. Document that ref normalization is best-effort (works in project context)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
**Open design question (resolve before implementation):**

The merge driver is invoked by git with just file paths - it doesn't have the full kspec context loaded. To normalize refs, we need to resolve @slug → @ULID.

**Options:**
1. **Lazy load index**: During merge, call `loadKspecContext()` to get ref resolution. Adds latency but works everywhere.

2. **Best-effort**: Only normalize if running in a kspec project context. Document that normalization may not work in bare repos or outside project.

3. **ULID-only comparison**: Skip slug resolution entirely. Only deduplicate exact string matches. Simpler but doesn't solve the original problem.

**Recommendation:** Option 1 (lazy load) - the merge driver already reads YAML files, loading the index is similar overhead and provides correct behavior.

This question should be answered before starting implementation.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
**Design decision resolved:** Use Option 1 (lazy load index).

During merge, load the kspec context to resolve refs to canonical ULIDs before comparison. The merge driver already does file I/O, so loading the index is acceptable overhead for correct behavior.

Implementation:
1. In `mergeSetArray` (or a wrapper), detect if array contains @ refs
2. If refs detected, call `loadKspecContext()` or similar to get ref resolver
3. Normalize all refs to ULIDs before Set comparison
4. Output uses 'ours' format preference

This removes the open question - task is now fully actionable.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
**Background - Why this matters:**

When merging kspec-meta branches (e.g., during git merge/rebase of shadow branches), the merge driver corrupts *.tasks.yaml files.

**How to reproduce:**
1. Have two branches with different task changes
2. Attempt merge: `git merge other-branch`
3. Observe: Output YAML has object keys instead of array items

**Example of corruption:**

Input (correct):
```yaml
- _ulid: 01KEZFXCM3...
  title: Task A
- _ulid: 01KEZG58FJ...
  title: Task B
```

Output (corrupted):
```yaml
"0":
  _ulid: 01KEZFXCM3...
  title: Task A
"1":
  _ulid: 01KEZG58FJ...
  title: Task B
```

The file is no longer valid kspec YAML - arrays become objects with numeric string keys.

**Root cause:**
`src/cli/commands/merge-driver.ts:183-187` casts `versions.base/ours/theirs` as `Record<string, unknown>`. When JavaScript iterates an array as an object, you get numeric keys ("0", "1", etc).

tasks.title: Split GitHub Pages workflow: separate web UI deploy from JSON snapshot generation

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem
Current gh-pages.yml triggers only on kspec-meta push. Web UI code changes on main don't trigger deployment.

## Desired Behavior
1. Web UI deploy: trigger when packages/web-ui/** changes on main
2. JSON snapshot: trigger when kspec-meta branch changes

## Constraints (GitHub Actions)
- Workflow files MUST live on default branch (main), not kspec-meta
- kspec-meta is an orphan branch, can't contain workflow files that execute
- Use workflow_run event to chain workflows if needed

## Proposed Architecture

### Workflow 1: gh-pages-ui.yml (on main)
- Trigger: push to main, paths: packages/web-ui/**
- Build web UI with VITE_STATIC_MODE=true
- Download latest kspec-snapshot.json artifact (or fetch from gh-pages branch)
- Deploy combined output to gh-pages

### Workflow 2: gh-pages-snapshot.yml (on main)
- Trigger: push to kspec-meta branch
- Checkout kspec-meta + main (for CLI build)
- Generate kspec-snapshot.json
- Either: upload artifact OR commit directly to gh-pages branch
- Optionally trigger Workflow 1 via workflow_dispatch or repository_dispatch

### Alternative: Single workflow with multiple triggers
- on: push to main (web-ui paths) OR push to kspec-meta
- Conditional steps based on which trigger fired
- Always combines latest of both

## References
- GitHub docs: workflow_run event for chaining
- Artifacts v4 allows cross-workflow download with run-id
- Current workflow: .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Root Cause Found

The gh-pages workflow NEVER triggered on kspec-meta push because:

**GitHub Actions runs workflows from the branch being pushed to, not from main.**

Since kspec-meta is an orphan branch with no .github/workflows/ directory, push events to it have nothing to run.

## Options

1. **Add workflow file to kspec-meta branch** - Works but pollutes the clean spec-only branch
2. **repository_dispatch from kspec CLI** - CLI calls GitHub API after shadow sync to trigger workflow
3. **Scheduled workflow** - Runs periodically, checks if kspec-meta changed, deploys if so
4. **workflow_run watching main** - Doesn't help since main isn't changing

## Recommended: repository_dispatch

Add to kspec shadow sync:
1. After git push to kspec-meta
2. Call GitHub API: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches with event_type
3. Workflow on main has 'on: repository_dispatch' trigger

This keeps kspec-meta clean and gives explicit control over when deployments happen.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Revised Approach: Add workflow to kspec-meta

User pointed out kspec-meta already has .gitattributes, .gitignore, CLAUDE.md - supporting files are not pollution.

**Simple fix:**
1. Copy gh-pages.yml to kspec-meta branch's .github/workflows/
2. Modify trigger: on push to kspec-meta (self-trigger)
3. Keep the dual-checkout pattern (main for code, kspec-meta for data)

This is simpler than repository_dispatch and requires no CLI changes.

- let items = $state<InboxItem[]>([])

- let error = $state('')

The data loads correctly but the UI never updates from 'loading' state because the variable assignment has no reactive effect.

tasks.title: Implement: Ralph max-tasks-per-iteration limiting
tasks.closed_reason: Implemented --max-tasks flag for ralph. PR #278 merged. Adds soft enforcement (wrap-up message) and hard enforcement (PreToolUse hook). Default is 1 task per iteration, 0 for unlimited.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

Limits how many tasks can be completed per iteration via --max-tasks flag. Default is 1 (conservative), 0 means unlimited. Enforcement is soft (message injection) then hard (PreToolUse hook blocking task start). Counts only kspec task complete commands (not submit, which is status change to pending_review).


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-flag: Given User runs kspec ralph, when --max-tasks flag is provided or defaults, then Parses N as positive integer (1-999) or 0 for unlimited; default is 1; invalid values exit with code 2
- ac-detection: Given Agent completes a task (kspec task complete), when ACP update handler receives Bash tool call containing kspec task complete, then Ralph queries kspec for actual completion count since iteration start, not relying on pattern alone
- ac-wrapup: Given N tasks completed this iteration (N equals max-tasks), when Detection triggers and count verified via kspec query, then Ralph writes marker file and injects wrap-up message telling agent to stop starting new tasks
- ac-unlimited: Given --max-tasks 0 is specified, when Ralph runs iteration, then No task limit enforced (legacy behavior); no marker file written
- ac-hook-block: Given Marker file exists at .claude/ralph-task-limit.json with active:true, when PreToolUse hook intercepts kspec task start command, then Hook blocks with message explaining task limit reached; allows other commands
- ac-reset: Given New iteration begins, when Ralph starts iteration loop, then Counter resets to 0; stale marker files older than 1 hour are cleared
- ac-marker-format: Given Task limit reached, when Marker file written, then File is JSON with active, since (ISO8601), max, completed, sessionId fields
- ac-dryrun: Given --dry-run flag provided with --max-tasks N, when Ralph shows config, then Displays max-tasks configuration in dry-run output

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Context

### Purpose
Add --max-tasks N flag to ralph that limits how many tasks can be completed per iteration. This prevents runaway automation and gives humans control over batch sizes.

### Files to Modify

1. **src/cli/commands/ralph.ts** - Core logic
   - Add CLI option after line 598: .option('--max-tasks <n>', 'Max tasks per iteration (0 = unlimited)', '1')
   - Track tasksCompletedThisIteration counter (reset at iteration start)
   - Add detection in ACP update handler (around line 817-834) - pattern match 'kspec task complete' in Bash tool calls
   - On detection: query kspec for actual completion count since iteration start
   - If count >= maxTasks: write marker file, inject wrap-up message
   - Clear marker file at iteration end

2. **src/cli/commands/session.ts** - Stats query
   - Add getIterationStats(ctx, since) function
   - Returns { tasks_completed, tasks_started, completed_refs }
   - Uses loadAllTasks() and filters by completed_at >= since

3. **.claude/hooks/ralph-task-limit-guard.sh** - New hook
   - Pattern follows existing kspec-worktree-guard.sh
   - Intercepts 'kspec task start' commands
   - Checks for marker file at .claude/ralph-task-limit.json
   - If marker exists and active:true, block with explanatory message
   - Otherwise allow

4. **.claude/settings.json** - Register hook
   - Add to existing PreToolUse[0].hooks array:
   { 'type': 'command', 'command': '.claude/hooks/ralph-task-limit-guard.sh' }

### Marker File Format (.claude/ralph-task-limit.json)
{
  'active': true,
  'since': 'ISO8601 timestamp',
  'max': 2,
  'completed': 2,
  'sessionId': 'ralph session ULID'
}

### Key Implementation Details

**Detection Flow:**
1. ACP update handler sees Bash tool call
2. Pattern match 'kspec task complete' (not submit - submit just changes status to pending_review)
3. Query kspec for completions since iteration start
4. If threshold reached: write marker, inject message

**Soft Enforcement (message injection):**
- Use agent.client.prompt() to send a follow-up message
- Message: 'Task limit reached (N tasks completed). Wrap up current work and exit cleanly. Do not start new tasks.'

**Hard Enforcement (hook):**
- PreToolUse hook blocks 'kspec task start'
- Provides clear error message explaining limit
- Agent can still run other commands

**Stale Marker Protection:**
- At iteration start, if marker exists and is > 1 hour old, delete it
- Prevents stale markers from blocking future runs

### Edge Cases
- --max-tasks 0: Unlimited (legacy behavior)
- kspec query failure: Log warning, don't crash iteration
- Multiple ralph instances: Marker in project root means conflict possible - document this

### Test Files to Create

1. tests/ralph/task-limit.test.ts - Unit tests
   - detectTaskCommand() pattern matching
   - checkTaskCompletionCount() with time filtering
   - Marker file operations (write/read/clear)
   - getIterationStats() function

2. tests/cli/ralph-task-limit.test.ts - CLI tests
   - Flag parsing (valid, invalid, default)
   - Dry-run shows max-tasks config

3. tests/hooks/ralph-task-limit-guard.test.ts - Hook tests
   - Allows when no marker
   - Blocks when marker exists
   - Ignores stale markers

tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #282. Fixed PR review subagent to complete task after merge by updating prompt exit conditions and adding defensive verification in ralph.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Issue Analysis

The PR review subagent merges PRs but doesn't complete the associated task, leaving it in pending_review for the next iteration where the task limit gets triggered.

### Root Cause

1. **Subagent prompt exit conditions** (src/ralph/subagent.ts:133-136):
   - Says 'Exit when: PR is merged successfully'
   - But task completion is step 8 in @pr-review-loop workflow (after merge at step 7)
   - So subagent exits BEFORE completing the task

2. **Conflicting documentation**:
   - SKILL.md says task completion is caller's responsibility
   - @pr-review-loop workflow includes task completion as ac-7
   - Subagent follows the 'exit when merged' instruction

### Fix Approach

1. **Update subagent prompt** - Change exit conditions to require task completion:
   - 'PR merged and task completed successfully' (not just 'PR merged')

2. **Check @pr-review-loop workflow** - Ensure consistent messaging

3. **Add defensive check in ralph** - After subagent success:
   - Verify task transitioned from pending_review to completed
   - If still pending_review, instruct subagent to complete properly (not auto-complete)

### Files to Modify

- src/ralph/subagent.ts (buildSubagentPrompt)
- src/cli/commands/ralph.ts (processPendingReviewTasks success path)
- .kspec/kynetic.meta.yaml (@pr-review-loop if needed)
- .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md (remove conflicting guidance)

notes.author: @claude

Scope: Add process signal handlers (SIGINT, SIGTERM) to ralph run command that clean up both marker files before exit.

Cross-platform considerations:
- Node.js process.on('SIGINT') works on Unix

tasks.title: Fix stale context after processPendingReviewTasks in ralph loop
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #297. Fixed ralph loop to refresh context after processPendingReviewTasks completes, preventing premature exit when tasks become unblocked. Added comprehensive integration tests for AC-20 with mock ACP that actually completes tasks. All tests pass in CI.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Bug analysis:

The ralph loop gathers session context at iteration start, then processes pending_review tasks (which may complete blocking tasks), but then checks for ready tasks using the STALE context.

Flow:
1. gatherSessionContext() - blocking tasks are in pending_review, dependent tasks show as blocked
2. processPendingReviewTasks() - subagents complete the blocking tasks  
3. Check sessionCtx.ready_tasks - STALE! Still shows empty because context was gathered before completions

Result: Loop exits with 'No automation-eligible tasks' even though tasks just became unblocked.

Fix: Re-gather context (or re-check ready tasks) AFTER processPendingReviewTasks completes, before the early exit check at lines 1108-1116.

Relevant code: src/cli/commands/ralph.ts lines 1080-1116

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Spec gap confirmed:

AC-19 specifies WHAT to check (automation:eligible ready/in_progress tasks) but not WHEN relative to pending_review processing.

AC-8 in @ralph-subagent-spawning specifies subagent spawning BEFORE main agent, but no AC specifies context refresh AFTER pending_review completes.

Proposed AC for @cli-ralph:
  id: ac-context-refresh-after-pending-review
  given: processPendingReviewTasks completes during iteration
  when: checking for loop continuation
  then: uses freshly gathered task context (not stale from iteration start) to detect tasks that became ready due to dependency unblocking

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix implemented:

Added context refresh after processPendingReviewTasks (AC-20). When pending_review tasks exist and are processed, context is re-gathered to detect tasks that became ready due to dependency unblocking.

Changes:
- src/cli/commands/ralph.ts: After processPendingReviewTasks, check if pending_review_tasks existed. If so, re-gather context before the ready task check. Use refreshed context for prompt building.

All existing tests pass. Build succeeds.

tasks.title: Create zero-dependency bootstrap script for agent sessions
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #300 - 36565a76

notes.author: Claude
notes.content:
## Problem

When an agent starts a session on a fresh clone or machine, kspec may not be built/linked/initialized. The agent then has to:
1. Run npm install
2. Run npm run build  
3. Run npm link
4. Run kspec init (which prompts interactively)
5. Run kspec session start

This creates friction and the agent may not know the correct sequence.

## Solution

Create a zero-dependency Node.js bootstrap script at `scripts/bootstrap.js` that:

1. **Runs without npm install** - Uses only Node.js built-ins (child_process, fs, path)
2. **Detects current state** - Checks if kspec is already working
3. **Does minimal work** - Only runs steps that are needed
4. **Is transparent** - Reports exactly what it did to the agent
5. **Outputs session context** - Ends with session start info

## Detection Logic

1. Check if `kspec --version` works (command exists and runs)
2. Check if `.kspec/` directory exists and is healthy
3. If both pass, just run session start
4. Otherwise, run the setup steps needed

## Setup Steps (when needed)

1. `npm install` - if node_modules missing or stale
2. `npm run build` - if dist/ missing or stale  
3. `npm link` - if kspec command not found
4. `kspec init --no-prompt` - if .kspec/ not initialized
5. `kspec session start` - always at the end

## Output Format

Script should output structured info for the agent:
```
=== Kspec Bootstrap ===
Status: [fresh_setup | already_configured | repaired]

Actions taken:
- Installed dependencies (npm install)
- Built project (npm run build)
- Linked CLI (npm link)
- Initialized shadow branch (kspec init)

[session start output here]
```

## Location & Invocation

- File: `scripts/bootstrap.js`
- Run: `node scripts/bootstrap.js`
- Add npm script: `"bootstrap": "node scripts/bootstrap.js"`

## Documentation Updates

1. Add to AGENTS.md - new section on session bootstrap
2. Update INSTALL.md - mention bootstrap as alternative to manual steps
3. Update CLAUDE.md - instruct agents to run bootstrap first

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

In Ralph session 01KGHBQ9WYVVK3PWNS55B8N108, the agent prematurely ended the loop after 2 iterations (of 10) by calling:

```
kspec ralph end-iteration --reason "Task 01KGGTR7 requires architectural decisions beyond automation scope. Investigation complete, documented findings."
```

The CORRECT behavior should have been:
1. Mark task @01KGGTR7 as blocked with reason
2. Mark automation status as needs_review
3. Check `kspec tasks ready --eligible` for other work
4. Continue the loop with remaining tasks

## Root Cause

The documentation teaches what NOT to do but doesn't explain what TO do instead. The agent saw:
- "Task seems complex is NOT an exit condition" (task-work SKILL.md:335)
- "You can signal: kspec ralph end-iteration" (task-work SKILL.md:327)

But there was no guidance saying: "Block the task and continue to other work"

## Files Requiring Updates

### 1. .claude/skills/task-work/SKILL.md

**Section: Exit Conditions (lines 316-320)**
Current text only mentions "no eligible tasks" - needs to clarify:
- Check `kspec tasks ready --eligible` for OTHER tasks
- Only end-iteration when ALL eligible tasks are blocked/done
- One blocked task is not "no eligible tasks"

**Section: What Is NOT an Exit Condition (lines 332-348)**
Tells agents what NOT to do but missing what TO do:
- Add escalation pattern: try → block → continue → end-iteration
- Explicitly state: "Never use end-iteration just because ONE task is complex"

**Section: Explicit Loop End Signal (lines 322-330)**
Vague wording "completed your focused work" - needs tightening:
- Valid: all eligible tasks blocked/completed
- Invalid: one task is hard so I'm done

**NEW SECTION NEEDED: Blocking vs End-Iteration**
Add table comparing three mechanisms:
| Situation | Action | When to Use |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Task requires other task first | `kspec task block` | True dependency |
| Task needs external input | `kspec task block` | Human decision needed |
| Task is complex/hard | DO THE WORK | Always - complexity is not a blocker |
| No more work possible | `kspec ralph end-iteration` | ALL tasks blocked/done |

### 2. AGENTS.md

**NEW SECTION: Using Task Blocking in Loop Mode (after line 234)**
Add guidance with examples:

```bash
# Pattern: When you discover a genuine blocker
kspec task block @complex-task --reason "Requires architectural decision on X"
kspec task set @complex-task --automation needs_review
kspec tasks ready --eligible  # Check for other work
# Continue with unblocked tasks
```

Valid blocking reasons:
- External dependency (API spec needed)
- Human architectural decision required
- Spec gap blocking understanding

Invalid blocking reasons (DO THE WORK):
- Task seems complex
- Multiple test failures
- Service needs to be running

Cross-reference the new loop mode blocking guidance from task-work skill.

The loop should ONLY end when:
1. All automation-eligible tasks are completed, OR
2. All remaining eligible tasks are blocked AND no unblocked work exists

One hard task should result in:
1. Block that task with reason
2. Mark as needs_review
3. Move to next eligible task
4. Loop continues

tasks.title: Implement Batch Command Execution
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #324. Implemented kspec batch with atomic (default) and immediate (--no-atomic) execution modes. 40 tests, 22 spec ACs. notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes from plan:

Architecture builds on existing infrastructure:

1. **Command registry** — Extend `src/cli/introspection.ts` to produce a map of command paths to their handler functions and metadata, including a `mutating: boolean` annotation. This enables dynamic dispatch without Commander.js parsing overhead and drives the allow/deny classification.

2. **Batch executor** (`src/cli/batch-exec.ts`) — New module:
   - `parseBatchInput(source)` — Reads from stdin/file/inline, parses JSON array
   - `validateBatch(commands, registry, context)` — Pre-validates all commands: known command, required args, ref resolution (including forward refs from earlier commands in batch)
   - `executeBatch(commands, registry, context, options)` — Executes validated commands sequentially, collects results, handles stop-on-error vs continue

3. **Shadow commit batching** — Use a `context.batchMode` flag. When set, `commitIfShadow()` skips the commit. The batch executor issues a single commit after all operations complete (or after partial completion with `--continue`). The flag is set before execution and cleared after.

4. **Forward reference resolution** — During pre-validation, track slugs that will be created by earlier commands. Build a "planned refs" set that the validator checks against when a ref doesn't exist yet. Only tracks creates, not deletes (documented limitation).

5. **Confirmation suppression** — When `context.batchMode` is set, commands that check for `@trait-confirmation-prompt` behavior skip the prompt and proceed as if `--force` were passed.

6. **Handler extraction** — Each command's `.action()` handler needs to be callable programmatically (not just via Commander.js parsing). Extract the core logic into importable functions that batch can call directly. Many commands already follow this pattern (e.g., `resolveTaskRefForBatch()`).

7. **Test approach** — Unit tests for parse/validate/execute phases. Integration test with a temp kspec project running a real batch payload end-to-end. Test the full matrix: stdin/file/inline × stop-on-error/continue × success/failure/partial.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Scope: This is the main feature task. Responsible for the batch command itself (src/cli/commands/batch.ts), the batch executor module (src/cli/batch-exec.ts), shadow commit batching (context.batchMode flag), forward reference resolution, confirmation suppression, and the kspec batch CLI registration. Covers ACs: ac-stdin, ac-file, ac-inline, ac-stop-on-error, ac-continue, ac-prevalidate, ac-dry-run, ac-forward-ref, ac-single-commit, ac-partial-commit, ac-confirmation-suppressed, ac-invalid-json, ac-empty-batch. Depends on the other two tasks being done first or simultaneously — the command schema defines the input format and the allowed commands list drives validation.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation complete: batch command execution with two modes.

**Atomic mode** (default): copies .kspec/ to temp dir, executes against copy, rolls back on failure, copies back + single shadow commit on success. Uses KSPEC_SPEC_DIR env var override in initContext() and setBatchMode() to suppress per-command shadow commits.

**Immediate mode** (--no-atomic): executes against real .kspec/ state, per-command auto-commits via existing shadow machinery. No rollback on failure. --continue flag implies immediate mode.

Key implementation details:
- KSPEC_SPEC_DIR env var in initContext() for temp dir redirection
- BatchExitError + exit interceptor to catch process.exit() calls
- OutputCapture to intercept console.log/error/warn per command
- resetCommandTree() to clear Commander state between dispatches
- Auto-append --force for confirmation suppression
- Strip ANSI via chalk.level=0 during dispatch
- .git removed from temp copy to prevent worktree pointer leaks
- Copy-back handles deletions by clearing real specDir first

Files created: batch-context.ts, commands/batch.ts
Files modified: batch-exec.ts, schema/batch.ts, parser/yaml.ts, parser/shadow.ts, cli/index.ts, commands/index.ts

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes from plan:

Architecture builds on existing infrastructure:

1. **Command registry** — Extend `src/cli/introspection.ts` to produce a map of command paths to their handler functions and metadata, including a `mutating: boolean` annotation. This enables dynamic dispatch without Commander.js parsing overhead and drives the allow/deny classification.

2. **Batch executor** (`src/cli/batch-exec.ts`) — New module:
   - `parseBatchInput(source)` — Reads from stdin/file/inline, parses JSON array
   - `validateBatch(commands, registry, context)` — Pre-validates all commands: known command, required args, ref resolution (including forward refs from earlier commands in batch)
   - `executeBatch(commands, registry, context, options)` — Executes validated commands sequentially, collects results, handles stop-on-error vs continue

3. **Shadow commit batching** — Use a `context.batchMode` flag. When set, `commitIfShadow()` skips the commit. The batch executor issues a single commit after all operations complete (or after partial completion with `--continue`). The flag is set before execution and cleared after.

4. **Forward reference resolution** — During pre-validation, track slugs that will be created by earlier commands. Build a "planned refs" set that the validator checks against when a ref doesn't exist yet. Only tracks creates, not deletes (documented limitation).

5. **Confirmation suppression** — When `context.batchMode` is set, commands that check for `@trait-confirmation-prompt` behavior skip the prompt and proceed as if `--force` were passed.

6. **Handler extraction** — Each command's `.action()` handler needs to be callable programmatically (not just via Commander.js parsing). Extract the core logic into importable functions that batch can call directly. Many commands already follow this pattern (e.g., `resolveTaskRefForBatch()`).

7. **Test approach** — Unit tests for parse/validate/execute phases. Integration test with a temp kspec project running a real batch payload end-to-end. Test the full matrix: stdin/file/inline × stop-on-error/continue × success/failure/partial.

tasks.title: Fix ralph log: String() on array of objects produces [object Object]
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #329. Added stringify() helper to handle array-of-content-blocks and plain objects in ralph event output extraction.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Bug Report

When a subagent completes in the ralph loop, tool results are sometimes rendered as `[object Object],[object Object]` instead of actual content.

### Root Cause

`src/ralph/events.ts` — `extractToolOutput()` and `extractOriginalOutput()` use `String()` to convert values:

- Line 212: `String(update.rawOutput)`
- Line 229: `String(toolResponse)` (fallback when no stdout)
- Line 235: `String(update.output)`
- Lines 248, 266: same pattern in `extractOriginalOutput()`

When ACP delivers tool results as an array of content blocks (e.g. `[{type: 'text', text: '...'}, ...]`), `String()` on an array of objects produces `[object Object],[object Object]`.

The output then flows through `cli-renderer.ts:231-238` which prints it verbatim.

### Fix

Add a helper function that checks if the value is a string, array, or object, and handles each:
- String → use as-is
- Array of content blocks → extract `.text` fields and join
- Object → `JSON.stringify()`

Apply to all 5 `String()` call sites in `extractToolOutput()` and `extractOriginalOutput()`.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Added stringify() helper in events.ts that handles string/array/object values. Replaced all 5 String() call sites in extractToolOutput() and extractOriginalOutput(). Arrays of content blocks (e.g. [{type:'text',text:'...'}]) now extract .text fields and join with newlines. Plain objects get JSON.stringify(). Added 3 test cases covering array-of-blocks, single-block, and plain-object scenarios.

tasks.title: Fix: 'No onPostToolUseHook found' leaks past noise suppression
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #345. Fixed noise suppression for hook warnings by changing from skip-entire-chunk to strip-patterns strategy. The stripNoise function now removes noise patterns from content while preserving surrounding text, handling both standalone noise and embedded noise concatenated with agent messages. Added comprehensive tests covering whitespace preservation, greedy matching prevention, and cross-chunk accumulation.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Bug Report

`No onPostToolUseHook found for tool use ID: toolu_...` appears in ralph output despite existing suppression pattern.

### What exists

`src/ralph/events.ts:304-307` has SUPPRESSED_PATTERNS including `/No onPostToolUseHook found/i`.
`shouldSuppress()` is called at lines 355 and 405 — but ONLY for `agent_message_chunk` and `agent_thought_chunk` update types.

### Likely cause

The hook message is arriving through a code path that bypasses the suppression check. Possible scenarios:
1. It arrives as a different ACP update type (not message/thought chunk)
2. It arrives concatenated with normal agent text in the same chunk — suppressing the whole chunk would lose good content, so the check needs to strip the noise substring rather than suppress the entire chunk
3. It comes through stderr or a side channel that doesn't go through the translator

### Observed output
```
Excellent creative brief. Now launching Phase 2...No onPostToolUseHook found for tool use ID: toolu_01LCkxN6GwoWUfvy7wqwp3sW
```

Note the concatenation with no newline — suggests it's in the same streaming content.

### Suggested fix

Change suppression from 'skip entire chunk' to 'strip matching patterns from chunk content'. This handles both standalone noise chunks and noise embedded in real content.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fixed by changing suppression strategy from skip-entire-chunk to strip-patterns. The stripNoise function now removes noise patterns from content while preserving surrounding text. This handles the observed bug where hook warnings were concatenated directly with agent messages (no newline). Added tests for: standalone noise suppression, embedded noise stripping, multiple patterns in same chunk, and accumulation across chunks.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Known limitation: Split-chunk noise during streaming cannot be fully suppressed because text is emitted before the complete pattern is known. The fix ensures final accumulated content is clean at finalization. Streaming output is ephemeral and scrolls away, so this is acceptable.

tasks.title: Increase ralph loop prompt timeout from 5min to 30min
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #328. Added RALPH_PROMPT_TIMEOUT (30min) override for both ralph agent and subagent spawn sites.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Context

The ACP framing layer at `src/acp/framing.ts:64-67` sets a 5-minute (300,000ms) timeout for `session/prompt` and `session/resume` methods. The timer resets on any agent activity (tool calls, notifications) via `resetPendingTimers()` at line 245.

However, the 5-minute default is too aggressive for ralph loop usage. The agent can go silent for extended periods due to:
- Anthropic API slowness/throttling
- Extended thinking on complex tasks
- Large context processing before first output

### Proposed fix

The ralph loop should override the default timeout when spawning agents. Options:
1. Pass a higher `methodTimeouts` override in `JsonRpcFramingOptions` when creating the framing layer for ralph agents (preferred — keeps default reasonable for non-ralph usage)
2. Increase the default globally (less ideal — 30min is too long for general use)

The framing constructor already supports overrides via `options.methodTimeouts` (line 94-97), so ralph just needs to pass `{ 'session/prompt': 30 * 60 * 1000 }` through the spawner.

### Files
- `src/acp/framing.ts` — timeout defaults and override mechanism
- `src/ralph/index.ts` or `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` — where agents are spawned
- `src/agents/spawner.ts` — may need to thread timeout options through

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation

Added `RALPH_PROMPT_TIMEOUT` constant (30 minutes) in `src/ralph/subagent.ts` and applied it to both ACP agent spawn sites:

1. **Main ralph agent** (`src/cli/commands/ralph.ts:1235`) — `clientOptions.methodTimeouts` override for `session/prompt` and `session/resume`
2. **Review subagent** (`src/ralph/subagent.ts:173`) — same override

The framing layer's constructor already merges user-provided `methodTimeouts` over defaults (line 94-97), so this cleanly overrides the 5-minute default without touching the default for non-ralph usage.

Exported through `src/ralph/index.ts`.

All 104 ralph tests + 43 ACP tests pass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Context

PR kynetic-ai/kynetic-bot#90 restructured kynetic-bot's AGENTS.md from 287 → 496 lines, 
modeled on kynetic-spec's tightened AGENTS.md (PR #350). Codex reviewed the PR and found 
5 issues — all fixed. Several patterns discovered during that work should be back-ported 
to kynetic-spec's AGENTS.md.

## Findings That Translate

### 1. MUST-FIX: Verify doc claims against source code
Codex caught that AGENTS.md claimed supervisor "Notifies ESCALATION_CHANNEL" but code only 
emits/logs. **Audit kynetic-spec AGENTS.md for similar claim-vs-reality gaps**, especially 
in Running Services, Shadow Branch Architecture, and Test Fixture Patterns sections.

### 2. SHOULD-FIX: Distinguish auto-commit mechanisms
kynetic-spec rule 1 says "CLI auto-commits to shadow branch" which is accurate since it only 
has .kspec/. But if/when kynetic-spec adds runtime data (e.g., web-ui sessions), the same 
ambiguity would appear. Low priority — just awareness.

### 3. SHOULD-FIX: PR agent limitations note
kynetic-bot AGENTS.md added: "PR agent limitations: Review subagent can't run kspec/npm — 
must delegate those to main agent." This is equally true for kynetic-spec but not documented. 
Add to PR Workflow section.

### 4. SHOULD-FIX: Dual defaults documentation pattern
kynetic-bot had SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT defaulting to 10s in bot config but 30s in supervisor CLI. 
Check kynetic-spec for similar split-default env vars (daemon port, health check intervals) 
and document explicitly if found.

### 5. SUGGESTION: Consolidate duplicate guidance
kynetic-bot had "Creating Work" duplicated in two sections. Check kynetic-spec for similar 
redundancy — the "Creating Work" subsection under Spec-First Development exists, verify 
nothing overlaps elsewhere.

### 6. SUGGESTION: Add bot-style "Running" gotchas section
kynetic-spec's Running Services section could benefit from explicit gotchas like:
- E2E port hardcoded (already in CI Limitations table but not in Running)
- daemon health endpoint path
- web-ui BASE_PATH requirement for local static builds

## What Was Done in kynetic-bot#90

- Rewrote AGENTS.md: 20 sections, ~496 lines
- Slimmed CLAUDE.md to single `@AGENTS.md` directive
- New sections: project identity, dual shadow branches, bot architecture (ACP/supervisor/memory), ralph loop mode, PR workflow, running the bot, expanded troubleshooting

CLAUDE.md is just `@AGENTS.md`.

## Reference: kynetic-bot#90

PR kynetic-ai/kynetic-bot#90 completed this same work for kynetic-bot. Key patterns:

### Section structure (20 sections, adapt as needed for imgen)
1. What This Project Is — package overview with responsibilities
2. Finding Information — skill routing table
3. Quick Start — prerequisites, install, env vars
4. Essential Rules — 6 numbered rules (CLI not YAML, spec before code, etc.)
5. Project Structure — file tree
6. Shadow Branch Architecture — .kspec/ worktree explanation
7. Project-Specific Architecture — the core of what makes imgen unique
8. Key Concepts — IDs, spec vs tasks, task states, notes
9. Task Workflow — session start, working, creating work
10. Session Context & Observations — focus/observe/thread + types table
11. Spec-First Development — decision table, plan mode workflow, creating work
12. Staying Aligned — scope expansion guardrails
13. PR Workflow — 3-step lifecycle, quality gates, PR agent limitations note
14. Commit Convention — trailers
15. Code Annotations — AC test links
16. Ralph Loop Mode — loop, task inheritance, blocking rules
17. Running/Development — how to run the project, env vars, gotchas
18. Workflows — table of all defined workflows
19. Troubleshooting — expanded table
20. Environment — KSPEC_AUTHOR

### Codex review findings that apply universally
- **Verify doc claims against source code** — don't document behavior that isn't implemented
- **Distinguish auto-commit mechanisms** if project has multiple shadow branches
- **Document dual defaults** when same env var has different defaults in different contexts
- **PR agent limitations** — "Review subagent can't run kspec/npm" applies to all projects
- **Consolidate duplicate guidance** — check for redundant "Creating Work" or similar sections

tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #369. Implemented ralph wrap-up agent that spawns on loop exit (all exit reasons: no_tasks, end_loop_signal, max_iterations, error, max_failures, explicit_tasks_done). notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

When the ralph loop exits for any reason (no eligible tasks, agent signaled end-loop, max iterations reached, error), spawn a final wrap-up subagent before terminating. The wrap-up agent ensures the workspace is in a clean state: uncommitted changes are identified and handled (committed, stashed, or flagged), stale markers are cleaned up, and a brief exit summary is produced. Runs as a subagent like PR review, with a focused prompt and short timeout.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given Ralph loop exits for any reason (no tasks, end-loop signal, max iterations, error), when exit sequence begins, then a wrap-up subagent is spawned before the process terminates
- ac-2: Given Wrap-up agent starts, when it inspects the working tree, then identifies uncommitted changes (staged, unstaged, untracked) and reports what they appear to relate to (task refs, file patterns)
- ac-3: Given Wrap-up agent finds uncommitted changes, when changes are present, then commits with appropriate message, stashes, or flags for human review depending on context; does not silently discard work
- ac-4: Given Wrap-up agent completes, when cleanup is done, then produces a brief exit summary: what was cleaned up, final task states, any items flagged for human attention
- ac-5: Given Wrap-up agent is running, when timeout is reached (default 2 minutes), then agent is terminated and ralph exits without wrap-up; wrap-up must not block shutdown indefinitely

tasks.title: Revisit ralph wrap-up agent design and test coverage
tasks.description: PR #369 added a wrap-up agent that runs on ralph loop exit. Retrospective flagged it as over-engineered but the intent is broader than simple cleanup: it ensures all work is completed, finds in-progress work where task state doesn't match reality, root-causes whether work is still needed, and does best-effort to get the project into a clean state (either continue the loop or put work on a branch with a task for the user). Too many possible states to rely on code alone — the agent approach is intentional. However: runWrapUpAgent() has zero integration tests (all 37 tests only check prompt strings and boolean helpers). Revisit AC coverage, add integration tests for the actual agent spawn/timeout/cleanup paths, and verify the prompt adequately covers the intended scenarios.
tasks.closed_reason: Ralph deprecated. Wrap-up agent concept doesn't apply to dispatch model — invocations are independent.

tasks.title: Add code-level reflect gating in ralph based on iteration delta
tasks.description: PR #357 added skill-file instructions to gate reflection on meaningful work, but this has no enforcement. Instead: ralph should snapshot session state (task statuses, working tree, commit count) before each iteration, compare at the end, and only issue the reflect prompt if something measurably changed (task transitions, commits, file changes). The reflect prompt itself was already efficient at avoiding noisy observations — the issue is invoking it at all when nothing happened.
tasks.closed_reason: Ralph loop gone. Dispatch invocations are discrete — no iteration delta. Reflection gating is a skill concern now.

notes.content:

Unify the setup command to use the same code paths as the rest of the CLI instead of reimplementing agent instruction generation and skill rendering. Highest impact for portable install - new projects currently get output from divergent code paths.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given setup.ts needs to generate agent instructions, when the setup pipeline runs, then it calls the exported generateAgentsContent() from agents.ts (not a local reimplementation)
