tasks.title: Generalize agent template sections for consumer projects
tasks.description:
The 6 template files in templates/agents-sections/ are used by 'kspec agents generate' to produce kspec-agents.md for any project. Currently they contain kspec-repo-specific references that break on consumer projects.

## Evidence from consumer projects (kynetic-bot, imgen, comfy-ecaj-nodes)

All three consumers copy-paste these sections verbatim into their AGENTS.md because the generated output isn't right. They all independently converged on the same Quick Start pattern:
```bash
kspec init          # first time
kspec setup         # configure agent environment  
kspec session start # get context
```

None use bootstrap.cjs or npm run dev. All three have the same hooks pattern (prompt-check, checkpoint, worktree-guard). All suffer from stale copies when upstream templates change.

## Specific fixes needed per file

**01-quick-start.md** (CRITICAL):
- Replace 'node scripts/bootstrap.cjs' with generic 'kspec init && kspec setup' 
- Remove 'npm run dev --' reference (kspec-repo-only)
- Add 'kspec session start' as the returning-session command
- Consider mentioning 'kspec shadow status' for health verification

**02-shadow-branch.md**: Already generic. No changes needed.

**03-task-lifecycle.md**: Already generic. No changes needed.

**04-pr-workflow.md**: Already generic. No changes needed.

**05-commit-convention.md**:
- Code annotation example is TypeScript-only (`// AC: @spec-item ac-N`)
- Should be language-agnostic or show both styles (// for TS/JS, # for Python/Ruby/Shell)
- comfy-ecaj-nodes uses '# AC:' pattern already

**06-ralph-loop.md**: Already generic. No changes needed.

## Additional considerations

- Consumer AGENTS.md files range from 358 (kspec) to 710 lines (imgen) — the generated output should be lean since projects add their own domain content on top
- The 'Finding Information' skill table in kspec's AGENTS.md is duplicated by all consumers with project-specific skills added — consider generating this table dynamically from installed skills
- All consumers have project-specific sections (architecture, tech stack, testing patterns) that live OUTSIDE the generated sections — the template output should compose well with custom content

tasks.title: Write getting-started tutorial and README for external users
tasks.description:
kspec has no end-to-end tutorial for new users. INSTALL.md covers setup mechanics but doesn't show the workflow. README.md is either missing or developer-focused on the kspec project itself, not on using kspec as a tool.

## What's needed

**README.md** — Public-facing, explains:
- What kspec is (spec-first task management for AI-assisted development)
- Why (shadow branch, spec-driven workflow, agent integration)
- Quick install and init
- Link to getting-started tutorial

**Getting-started tutorial** (docs/getting-started.md or similar):
- Walk through from 'npm install -g' to first completed task
- Create a spec item with acceptance criteria
- Derive a task from the spec
- Work the task (start, implement, note, submit)
- Create a PR with kspec trailers
- Complete the task
- Show the spec-first loop in action

**Reference points:**
- kynetic-bot, imgen, comfy-ecaj-nodes are real consumer projects showing actual usage patterns
- All three independently converged on the same Quick Start: kspec init → kspec setup → kspec session start
- The workflow skills (task-work, pr, spec) contain detailed command references that the tutorial can link to rather than duplicate
- INSTALL.md already covers setup mechanics — tutorial should reference it, not repeat it

## Scope boundaries
- README is for the npm package / GitHub repo landing page
- Tutorial is for humans AND agents onboarding to a new kspec project
- Don't duplicate skill content — link to skills for detailed command syntax
- Keep it practical with real examples, not abstract descriptions

Implementation notes:

Thread config through shadow.ts functions via optional parameters that default to
SHADOW_BRANCH_NAME / SHADOW_WORKTREE_DIR constants. ShadowConfig already carries
branchName — extend it.

Key functions needing config threading: detectShadow(), initializeShadow(),
hasRemoteTracking(), ensureRemoteTracking(), pushShadowBranch(), shadowPull(),
shadowSync(), ensureGitignore(), getShadowStatus(), repairShadow(),
resolveShadowPath().

Remote type detection algorithm for shadow.remote:
- Starts with /, ./, or ~ -> local filesystem path
- Contains :// or starts with git@ -> git URL
- Otherwise -> git remote name
For path/URL types, git remote add with configured value. For remote name,
verify it exists before push/pull. Authentication for URLs delegated to git
credential helpers — do not store tokens in config. Add guidance in error
messages recommending remote names over inline URLs with credentials.

Two options: (1) read config first with a lightweight non-throwing load, or
(2) make detection generic by checking if cwd is ANY git worktree via the .git
file being a worktree pointer, regardless of directory name. Option 2 preferred.

config and warn on mismatch rather than silently using stale settings.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes from plan @plan-unified-health-check-command-kspec-doctor:

**Severity model:** Each check gets ok | warning | error. Shadow broken = error. Setup missing = error. Daemon not running = warning. Staleness unknown = warning. Exit 0 when no errors (warnings are fine). Exit 1 when any error exists.

**Library layer: src/parser/doctor.ts (new)**
Place alongside existing parser modules (src/parser/shadow.ts, src/parser/yaml.ts). Returns DoctorReport with CheckResult per subsystem.

Flow:
1. getShadowStatus(projectRoot) — if !exists, return early with not-initialized report
2. If shadow exists, run setup + daemon in parallel via Promise.allSettled
3. For setup: call getSetupStatus(projectRoot) — fix staleness bug (unknown, not false-current)
4. For daemon: call new getDaemonStatus() extracted from serve.ts
5. Compute overall: healthy = (errors === 0)

**Extract getDaemonStatus() from serve.ts**
Currently statusServer() in serve.ts mixes data-gathering with output. Extract into shared function in pid-utils.ts or new daemon-status.ts. Include projects array to avoid regressing serve status output. readPort() throws on missing/invalid port file — wrap in try/catch returning null.

**Fix getSetupStatus staleness false-positive**
In setup.ts lines 1106 and 1109, status falls back to "current" when hash can't be checked. Change to "unknown". Update SetupStatus.agentsMd.status type to include "unknown" (line 965). Update text renderer in setup.ts.

**Extract setup status logic to avoid CLI coupling**
Extract pure status-gathering logic into src/parser/setup-status.ts. CLI command keeps formatter, calls extracted function. Avoids doctor.ts depending on CLI command module.

**CLI layer: src/cli/commands/doctor.ts (new)**
Thin wrapper: getGitRoot() -> getDoctorReport(gitRoot) -> output(report, formatDoctorReport) -> exit based on report.overall.healthy.

tasks.title: Add merge blocker when review subagent times out
tasks.description:
When a ralph review subagent times out, markTaskNeedsReview is called but the PR itself has no GitHub-level blocker. The next iteration's worker or CI auto-merge can merge the PR without any review having occurred.

When a review subagent times out or fails:
- Add a 'review-pending' label to the PR, OR
- Post a comment noting the review was incomplete
- Do not proceed to merge until a review subagent successfully completes

This prevents the rubber-stamp pattern observed in session 01KHW4RP where all 10 PRs merged with zero reviews.

tasks.title: Spike: Validate claude-agent-acp 0.18.0 runtime compatibility
tasks.description:
Cannot determine from code analysis alone whether the _meta.claudeCode.* fields survive the MCP-to-native-tools migration in PR #316. Needs runtime testing.

## Context

PR zed-industries/claude-agent-acp#316 (merged 2026-02-18) removed the custom MCP server that proxied tools and switched to Claude Code's built-in tools. This changes how tool calls flow internally, which could affect the _meta structure on SessionUpdate events.

## What to validate

1. Install claude-agent-acp@0.18.0 globally
2. Run a ralph loop (single iteration, simple task) and capture events.jsonl
3. Check events for these critical fields:

_meta.claudeCode.toolName:
- Still present on tool_call and tool_call_update events?
- Value is bare name ("Bash") not MCP-prefixed ("mcp__acp__Bash")?
- Our normalizeTool() already strips prefixes, so prefix change is safe — but field absence is NOT safe.

_meta.claudeCode.toolResponse:
- Still present on tool completion events?
- Still has stdout/stderr structure?
- Or has it moved to rawOutput / _meta.terminal_output.data?

--dangerously-skip-permissions:
- Still accepted as a CLI flag?
- Still skips permission prompts?

session/request_permission:
- Still sends option.kind = "allow_always" / "allow_once"?
- Still sends option.optionId field?

4. Check the 0.14.0, 0.15.0, 0.16.0, 0.17.0 changelogs for any other breaking changes between our 0.13.2 and target 0.18.0.

## Fallback paths already in our code

extractToolName() has 4-level fallback: _meta.claudeCode.toolName -> _meta.toolName -> name -> title
extractToolOutput() has 3-level fallback: rawOutput -> _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse -> output

If fields moved but data is still present somewhere in the update, our fallbacks may already handle it. The spike should confirm.

## Outcome

Document which fields changed (if any) and whether our existing fallback chains handle them. If changes needed, create follow-up tasks with specific field mapping updates.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
[SPIKE COMPLETE] ACP 0.18.0 runtime validation against ralph session 01KJ4VNM972YKRADFPC84B55RY (16 iterations, 27k events).

## Core Fields — All Present and Working

- _meta.claudeCode.toolName: Present on all 1,733 tool_call events. Always bare names (Bash, Read, Edit, etc.) — no MCP prefix.
- _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse: Present on 1,690 completion events. Tool-specific structure intact (stdout/stderr for Bash, content/filenames for Grep, etc.).
- rawOutput: Present on all 1,733 completion events as string. extractToolOutput() hits this at priority 1.

- `available_commands_update` (17 events): Same — returns null.
- `null` updates (32 events): Handled gracefully.
- `config_option_update`, `current_mode_update`: NOT observed in this session.

## Phased Tool Call Model (ACP 0.14+)

- tool_call events: Have kind, status:"pending", rawInput (always empty {}). Our code falls through rawInput to input field correctly.
- tool_call_update streaming: Have content array with {type:"content"} blocks, no rawOutput.
- tool_call_update completion: Have rawOutput (string), status, _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse.

- No impact: extractToolOutput() hits rawOutput first, diff blocks are in content array.

## Bash Code Fence Language

- Not applicable: rawOutput is plain string, no SDK-injected fences.

## Fallback Chain Status

- extractToolName(): Level 1 (_meta.claudeCode.toolName) always hits.
- extractToolOutput(): Level 1 (rawOutput) hits on completions. Level 2 (toolResponse) present as backup.

## Untested

- Permission event field structure (option.kind, optionId): Session used yolo mode, so no permission events were generated. Would need a non-yolo run to verify. Low risk — the handleRequest code already uses these fields and the session ran successfully.

## Verdict

No code changes needed. Existing fallback chains handle ACP 0.18.0 correctly.

tasks.title: Spike: Audit mock completeness vs real adapter behavior
tasks.description:
The ACP test mock (tests/mocks/acp-mock.js) is minimal and may not reflect real adapter behavior after the upgrade. Needs assessment.

## Current mock limitations

1. Only emits agent_message_chunk — never sends tool_call, tool_call_update, agent_thought_chunk events
2. No empty-string finalization signal (real Claude Code sends content.text === "" to signal stream end)
3. Permission handling only tested indirectly via mock's mirrored logic
4. No _meta.claudeCode.* fields in emitted events (tool name/output extraction untested at integration level)
5. SessionUpdate discriminator values hardcoded as strings, not validated against SDK types

## What to investigate

1. Run a real ralph session and capture events.jsonl
2. Compare the real SessionUpdate structures against what the mock emits
3. Identify gaps: which real event patterns are NOT covered by mock or unit tests?
4. Specifically check:
   - tool_call events: do they have _meta.claudeCode.toolName in the real adapter?
   - tool_call_update events: do they have rawOutput or _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse?
   - Does the real adapter send duplicate tool_call events (the "alreadyCached" pattern from PR #316)?
   - Are there new SessionUpdate variants (e.g. usage_update) that the translator should handle?

## Outcome

Either:
- The mock is sufficient and unit tests in ralph.test.ts cover the gaps (likely)
- Or create tasks to extend the mock and/or add integration test scenarios

## Note

This can be combined with the runtime compatibility spike if convenient — both require running a real ralph session. But the focus here is on test coverage, not adapter compatibility.
tasks.closed_reason: Parent ACP spike completed; mock concerns addressed during ACP migration work

tasks.title: Skip kspec-agents.md regeneration when content unchanged
tasks.description: kspec agents generate currently always updates the timestamp in kspec-agents.md even when no actual content has changed. This creates unnecessary git diffs. Should compare the generated content (excluding the timestamp comment) against the existing file and skip writing if identical. The hash file (.kspec-agents-hash) already tracks meta hash for staleness — if the meta hash matches, the file content is the same and generation can be skipped entirely with a 'kspec-agents.md is already up to date' message.

tasks.title: Migrate skill rendering to Claude Code plugin system
tasks.description:
Claude Code does not support nested skill directories (.claude/skills/kspec/<id>/ is NOT discovered). The official namespacing mechanism is the plugin system.

## Goal

Render kspec core skills as a Claude Code plugin so they are properly namespaced and discovered. For non-Claude platforms (Codex, etc.), use flat prefix naming since they lack plugins.

### Claude Code target structure
.claude/plugins/kspec/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (name, version, description)
.claude/plugins/kspec/skills/help/SKILL.md -> invoked as /kspec:help

### Non-Claude target structure
.agents/skills/kspec-help/SKILL.md (flat prefix)

## Key Implementation Points

### Path construction (3 strategic functions in skill-render.ts)
- getSkillSubdir() - currently adds kspec/ prefix for core skills on claude-code
- getRenderedSkillPath() - constructs full output path
- getPlatformDefaultOutputDir() - returns .claude/skills for claude-code
- claudeCodeRenderer defaultOutputDir needs to change for core skills

### Plugin manifest generation
- Generate .claude/plugins/kspec/.claude-plugin/plugin.json during skill render
- Include kspec version, description

### Migration
- Remove old .claude/skills/kspec/ directory (monolithic skill + broken nested renders)
- skill render --clean needs to handle old to new path transition
- Similar pattern to PR #440 migration logic

### Non-Claude platforms
- Codex renderer uses .agents/skills/ (flat) - use kspec-<id> prefix instead of nesting
- Other future platforms: same flat prefix approach

### Files affected (from codebase exploration)
- src/parser/skill-render.ts - core path logic, PlatformRenderer, claudeCodeRenderer
- src/cli/commands/skill-diff.ts - render/status/diff/verify commands
- src/cli/commands/setup.ts - getSetupStatus() directory scanning
- src/parser/validate-skills.ts - findSkillFiles() directory discovery
- 14 test suites with path assertions

### What already exists
- templates/skills/help/SKILL.md - lean CLI map content ready for plugin rendering
- templates/skills/manifest.yaml - core skills manifest
- PlatformRenderer interface is well-abstracted

### Also resolve
- Existing monolithic .claude/skills/kspec/SKILL.md (591 lines) replaced by plugin-rendered skills
- kspec-agents.md Finding Information table should show /kspec:help after migration (fix generateSkillsTable in agent-data-sections.ts)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Spike to explore design space and produce spec-plan for interactive triage system.

## Problem
Inbox triage is currently agent-driven and ephemeral. Triage decisions (reasoning, evidence, actions, user decisions) are lost between sessions. No way for users to interactively review/override agent triage. No way for subsequent agents to act on prior triage work reliably.

## Design Space

### 1. Triage Metadata on Inbox Items
Add structured fields: triage_status, triage_reasoning, triage_evidence, triage_action, user_decision, spec_gap flag, automation_eligible flag. Key question: extend InboxItem schema or separate TriageRecord?

### 2. Interactive Triage UI (Web UI via Daemon)
Per-category triage mode with one-by-one item presentation. Shows description, agent reasoning, evidence, recommended action. User chooses from options or overrides. Free-form input for reasoning. Next/previous navigation. Writes through daemon API to shadow branch.

### 3. Agent Handoff Export
Context-rich export of triage decisions for fresh agent sessions. Include full item context, triage metadata, user decision, relevant refs. Format must give new agents enough context to act without re-researching. Possibly: kspec inbox export --triaged

### 4. Daemon API Extensions
GET/PUT /api/inbox/:ref/triage, filtering by triage_status, bulk updates.

## Key Questions
- Schema: inline on inbox items or separate triage records?
- History: version triage decisions (agent triages, user overrides)?
- Workflow: integrate with existing /triage skill?
- Export: what format maximizes agent effectiveness?

## References
- Triage skill: .claude/skills/triage/
- Inbox schema: src/schema/inbox.ts  
- Daemon API: packages/daemon/src/
- Web UI inbox: packages/web-ui/src/routes/inbox/
- Triage report artifact: .kspec/artifacts/triage-report-2026-02-22.html (example of current ephemeral output)

- packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts (line 22)

1. Configure Bun bundler with proper package resolution/externals
2. Use workspace package imports (e.g., kynetic-spec/parser) instead of relative paths

The underlying issue is the monorepo structure - daemon lives in packages/daemon/ but imports from src/ at the repo root via relative paths.

tasks.title: Audit test suite and plan migration from static analysis to behavioral tests
tasks.description:
The test suite relies heavily on static analysis patterns — reading source files and checking for string patterns (e.g. expect(content).toContain(...)). This approach cannot catch runtime bugs and breaks on refactors (e.g. end-loop.test.ts had regex pattern tests that could not detect the false-positive bug that caused a real ralph loop exit).

Deep dive:
1) Inventory ALL test files repo-wide and categorize by test approach (static analysis vs behavioral vs E2E).
2) Identify which static-only tests have the highest risk of missing real bugs.
3) Design a migration plan — options include: unit tests that import functions directly, integration tests with fixtures, CLI behavioral tests, or Playwright E2E tests.
4) Create follow-up tasks for the actual migration work.

Known areas with static analysis tests:
- Daemon tests (tests/daemon-*.test.ts)
- Ralph end-loop tests (tests/ralph/end-loop.test.ts) — session close handlers, marker removal
- Likely others across the test suite

The pattern to eliminate: reading source with fs.readFile then expect(content).toContain(...)
tasks.closed_reason: Audit complete. Identified ~3,500 lines of static analysis tests across 14 files covering ~98 ACs. Created 10 follow-up tasks: 9 E2E replacement tasks for daemon APIs and 1 deletion task for tests that don't need replacing. All tasks are automation-eligible with concrete endpoints, AC annotations, and file references.

tasks.title: Add path-based CI test filtering
tasks.description:
Configure CI to only run the test suite when files that affect test outcomes are changed. Use GitHub Actions path filters to skip tests for documentation-only, skill-only, or other non-code changes.

Approach: Define paths that trigger tests (src/**, tests/**, packages/**, package.json, etc.) rather than paths that skip tests. This is safer — new code paths get tested by default.

Examples of changes that should skip tests:
- .claude/skills/**
- docs/**
- templates/agents-sections/**
- *.md (except possibly SKILL.md files that get loaded at runtime — evaluate)
- .kspec/**

Consider: GitHub Actions path filtering with paths/paths-ignore on the test job.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Rewrite computeIterationSummaries() in src/sessions/store.ts to use
prompt.sent event positions as iteration boundaries instead of relying
on the data.iteration field (which suffers from a closure capture race
in ralph's fire-and-forget event logging).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Notes

### Problem
computeIterationSummaries() in src/sessions/store.ts:718-802 groups events by data.iteration field. Ralph's fire-and-forget appendEvent() call at src/cli/commands/ralph.ts:1573-1579 captures the loop iteration variable by closure reference. By the time the async callback executes, iteration has advanced, so streaming events get tagged with wrong iteration numbers. Result: kspec session log show reports most iterations as "4 events" when they had hundreds.

A separate task (@01KJ5WV0) fixes the capture-by-value bug in ralph.ts. This task makes the counting system resilient to producer-side data errors.

### Approach: Index-Based Boundary Splitting
Ralph emits awaited prompt.sent events with { phase: "task-work", iteration: N } at ralph.ts:1463 at the start of each iteration. Use these as authoritative iteration boundaries.

CRITICAL: Use array indices from readEvents() output, NOT seq values. appendEvent() is explicitly not concurrency-safe (store.ts:260) — concurrent fire-and-forget calls can produce duplicate seq numbers. Array indices provide deterministic splitting immune to seq races.

### Algorithm
1. Read all events via readEvents() (returns sorted array)
2. Find boundary events: type === "prompt.sent" AND data?.phase === "task-work" AND typeof data?.iteration === "number" — record their array index and iteration number
3. Validate: filter out non-monotonic iteration numbers, deduplicate
4. If no valid boundaries → legacy fallback (current data.iteration grouping, extracted into helper function)
5. Build index ranges: [0, boundary1.idx), [boundary1.idx, boundary2.idx), etc.
6. Pre-boundary events merge into first iteration
7. Extract tasks_started/tasks_completed per iteration (unchanged logic)

### Files to Modify
src/sessions/store.ts:
- Rewrite computeIterationSummaries() (lines 718-802) with boundary algorithm
- Extract current logic into legacyIterationGrouping() helper for fallback
- Update getSessionLogDetail() (~line 820) to derive iteration_count from summaries.length instead of calling countIterations() separately
- Add countIterationsBoundaryAware() — lightweight boundary counter for getSessionLogSummary() (used by session log list and session log stats) to prevent iteration_count disagreements between list and show views

tests/session-log-show.test.ts:
- Update existing fixtures (~line 171) to include phase: "task-work" field
- Add tests:
  1. Multi-iteration with prompt.sent boundaries (index-based grouping)
  2. Wrong data.iteration on streaming events (still grouped correctly)
  3. Legacy fallback — no prompt.sent events with phase field
  4. Malformed boundaries — prompt.sent with missing phase/iteration (graceful fallback)
  5. Single iteration — one boundary captures all events
  6. Pre-loop events — session.start before first prompt.sent merged into iteration 1
  7. Mixed phase prompt.sent — both task-work and reflect present, only task-work used
  8. Duplicate seq values — concurrent events with same seq, boundary math correct

### Key Implementation Details
- SessionEvent.data is typed as unknown (types.ts:105) — treat boundary data as untrusted, validate phase and iteration fields before use
- readEvents() at store.ts:320-340 sorts by seq — index order follows seq order
- Reflect prompt.sent uses phase: "reflect" (ralph.ts:1648) — safely excluded
- Subagents and wrap-up agents don't emit prompt.sent to parent session (confirmed in src/ralph/subagent.ts:229)
- No changes needed to types.ts, ralph.ts, or session.ts

### Verification
1. npx vitest run tests/session-log-show.test.ts
2. npm run dev -- session log show 01KJ4VNM — verify accurate counts across all iterations (not "4 events" for most)
3. Cross-check: session log list iteration counts match session log show
4. Full suite: npx vitest run

Legacy fallback preserved for sessions without boundaries. Added countIterationsBoundaryAware() for getSessionLogSummary() consistency. getSessionLogDetail() now derives iteration_count from summaries.length. 8 new test cases covering: boundary grouping, wrong data.iteration resilience, legacy fallback, pre-boundary merging, single iteration, mixed phases, malformed boundaries, duplicate seq values. All 35 session-log-show tests pass.

tasks.title: Design native task-limit enforcement for ralph agent iterations
tasks.description:
## Problem

Ralph loop agents are not stopping after completing one task per iteration. Evidence from session 01KJ5WZPNDYY68ZX143D06FXCB shows an agent submitted task @01KJ4SMA, then immediately started and completed task @01KJ5WV0 with zero ralph intervention between them. The maxTasks: 1 setting was never enforced.

Two root causes:

1. **No event-to-agent tracking**: Ralph has no way to attribute a `kspec task submit` or `kspec task complete` to the currently active agent iteration. The marker file approach is passive — ralph writes it, but only when it detects a complete command in the event stream. Since the agent used `submit` (not `complete`), the marker was never written.

2. **Submit not treated as completion**: `detectTaskCompleteCommand()` in ralph.ts (line 229) explicitly excludes `kspec task submit`. But submit means the agent's work is done — a review agent should take over. Submit should count the same as complete for task-limit purposes.

3. **Shell script hook is fragile**: The current `ralph-task-limit-guard.sh` is a shell script that parses JSON with jq, walks directories to find project root, and reads a marker file. This should be a native kspec command (like `kspec session checkpoint` is for the Stop hook) for reliability and testability.

## Investigation Goals

- How can ralph reliably track which events belong to the active agent? Options: session scoping, event correlation IDs, agent turn boundaries
- What's the right enforcement point? PreToolUse hook blocking `task start`, or injecting a stop signal, or both?
- Should the hook be `kspec ralph guard` or similar native command that reads ralph state directly instead of a marker file?

## Design Deliverables

- Clear design for native task-limit hook (replacing ralph-task-limit-guard.sh)
- Updated detection logic: submit counts as completion for limit purposes
- Event attribution approach so ralph knows what the active agent did
- Spec updates if the current @ralph-task-limit spec needs changes
- New task(s) derived from the design for implementation work

## Key Files

- src/cli/commands/ralph.ts (lines 227-231 detectTaskCompleteCommand, 1520-1557 limit counting, 1314-1773 main loop)
- .claude/hooks/ralph-task-limit-guard.sh (current shell script hook)
- src/cli/commands/setup.ts (hook installation, GUARD_SCRIPTS)
- src/cli/commands/session.ts (session checkpoint as model for native hook)
- .kspec/modules/cli.yaml (@ralph-task-limit spec)
- templates/agents-sections/06-ralph-loop.md (agent instructions)
- .claude/skills/task-work/SKILL.md (agent stop instructions)

tasks.title: Fix phased tool call event handling for ralph display and session stats
tasks.description:
## Problem

After upgrading to @agentclientprotocol/sdk@0.14.x, tool call info (command names, file paths, etc.) is no longer displayed in ralph loop output. Only the tool result/output is shown.

## Root Cause

The ACP SDK now sends tool calls in two phases:
1. `tool_call` event with `rawInput: {}` (empty) and `status: pending`
2. `tool_call_update` event moments later with populated `rawInput: { command: "...", description: "..." }`

The event translator in events.ts extracts the summary on the first event (gets empty string from empty rawInput), then when the second event arrives with populated input, the logic at line 648 doesn't always re-emit a tool_update with the now-available summary.

## Affected Code (comprehensive list)

### Core translator (primary fix)
- **src/ralph/events.ts lines 632-683** (`tool_call` case): Summary extraction from empty rawInput yields "". Need to handle phased arrival — when tool_call_update arrives with populated rawInput and existing summary was empty, emit a tool_update event with the summary.
- **src/ralph/events.ts line 648**: The check `if (summary && !hadSummary)` — needs to correctly detect "summary was empty before, now has content"
- **src/ralph/events.ts lines 685-738** (`tool_call_update` case): May need to also check for newly-available summary here, not just in the tool_call case

### CLI renderer (may need adjustment)
- **src/ralph/cli-renderer.ts lines 175-198** (`renderToolStart`): Currently shows empty summary on first event. Should either defer display until summary available, or update display when summary arrives via tool_update
- **src/ralph/cli-renderer.ts lines 200-211** (`renderToolUpdate`): Should display summary when it arrives in the update phase

### Session stats (double-counting bug)
- **src/sessions/store.ts lines 979-1028** (`computeToolUsageStats`): Counts BOTH phased events as separate tool calls, leading to doubled tool usage stats. Must deduplicate by toolCallId — only count unique tool calls, not phased updates
- **src/sessions/store.ts lines 455-484** (`countTaskCompletions`): Accesses `rawInput.command` — safe since first event has empty rawInput (won't false-match), but should be verified

### Session display
- **src/cli/commands/session.ts lines 1508-1556** (`summarizeEventData`): Shows tool_call events — first phased event will show only tool name without command details. Should either skip events with empty rawInput or prefer the populated version
- **src/cli/commands/session.ts lines 1646-1737** (`sessionLogShowAction`): Displays events, may show tool twice (once per phase)
- **src/cli/commands/session.ts lines 1856-1924** (`sessionLogStatsAction`): Uses computeToolUsageStats — inherits double-counting bug
- **src/cli/commands/session.ts lines 1992-2027** (`sessionLogSearchAction`): Searches events, may find duplicate matches for phased events

### Iteration summaries
- **src/sessions/store.ts lines 718-802** (`computeIterationSummaries`): Extracts task start/complete refs from rawInput.command at lines 780-789 — only works when rawInput populated (second event), which is correct but should be documented

## Test Coverage Needed

### Existing tests to update
- **tests/session-log-stats.test.ts lines 187-210**: Tests computeToolUsageStats with single events only — need phased event pair tests to verify no double-counting
- **tests/ralph.test.ts**: Tests event translation — need phased tool_call event pairs

### New tests needed

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Audit Results (from ralph loop post-mortem)

### Root Cause
Agents see trait references (e.g. "Inherited from @trait-error-guidance") in kspec item get output but don't know to run `kspec item get @trait-slug` to resolve them. They fall back to searching .kspec/modules/*.yaml files one by one — 139 messages in one observed case.

### Skills to Update (prioritized)

**HIGH impact (fix first):**
1. `/kspec:task-work` — Add CLI lookup table after "Verify Work Is Needed" section. Include: task get, item get, trait get, search, item list, trait list. Add explicit pattern: "When item get shows 'Inherited from @trait-slug', run item get @trait-slug. Do NOT search YAML files."
2. `/kspec:review` — Add "Looking Up Trait Definitions" subsection under Trait AC Coverage. Add golden path: item get → trait get → grep for annotations → validate.
3. `local-review` (Claude skill) — Expand step 1 to say "for each inherited trait, run kspec item get @trait-slug". Expand step 3 with trait lookup recipe.

**MEDIUM impact:**
4. `pr-review` (Claude skill) — Add trait lookup reminder in AC Coverage section.
5. `/kspec:writing-specs` — Add "Finding Where Things Live" section with search/list/item get recipes.

**LOW impact:**
6. `triage-inbox` — Replace `kspec item list | grep` with `kspec search`.

### Cross-Cutting
Consider adding a "CLI Lookups" convention rule via `kspec meta set` so it appears in AGENTS.md Essential Rules for all agents regardless of skill.

### Specific Content
The audit agent drafted exact text to add to each skill. The key table to add everywhere:

| Need | Command |
|------|---------|
| Task details | `kspec task get @ref` |
| Spec + all ACs | `kspec item get @ref` |
| Trait definition | `kspec item get @trait-slug` or `kspec trait get @trait-slug` |
| Search by keyword | `kspec search "keyword"` |
| List by type | `kspec item list --type feature` |
| All traits | `kspec trait list` |

### Automation Notes
Straightforward text additions to skill markdown files. No code changes. Can be automated once content is approved.

tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #509. Fixed env pollution when vitest runs inside ralph loop by stripping KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION and KSPEC_SESSION_ID from child process env in kspec() test helper and ralph.test.ts direct spawnSync call. All 3513 tests pass. Codex review clean.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Failing Tests (4 total, 3 files)

### 1-2. session-create.test.ts — JSON parse errors (lines 774, 860)
Tests: 'should return error as JSON when --json is active and validation fails' and 'should include guidance in JSON error object'
- Run: kspec session create --budget abc --json (expectFail)
- Then: JSON.parse(result.stderr)
- Fails because: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set in env (inherited from ralph), pointing to ralph's session. session create validates this env var (src/cli/commands/session.ts:2080-2088) and calls warn() which writes '⚠ Current KSPEC_SESSION_ID (...) is invalid: ...' to stderr BEFORE the JSON error object. JSON.parse fails on the warning prefix.

### 3. session-create.test.ts — env injection method (line 740)
Test: 'should inject via .env when OpenCode detected'
- Expects injection.method === 'opencode_dotenv' but gets 'fallback'
- Ralph env vars interfere with harness detection logic

### 4. ralph.test.ts — KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION inheritance (line 612)
Test: 'KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION is not inherited by non-ralph child processes'
- Spawns child with { ...process.env } expecting KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION absent
- Running inside ralph means process.env.KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION IS set
- Gets '01KJ8MK...' instead of null

### 5. session-budget-integration.test.ts (intermittent)
Test: 'should clean up budget.json after normal exit'
- Similar env pollution from ralph session vars

## Root Cause
Ralph sets KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION and KSPEC_SESSION_ID on process.env. The kspec() test helper in tests/helpers/cli.ts uses spawnSync which inherits process.env. Tests that expect clean env get ralph's vars instead.

## Fix Approach
In tests/helpers/cli.ts, the kspec() helper should strip ralph-specific env vars (KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION, KSPEC_SESSION_ID) from the spawned process env by default. Tests that explicitly need these vars already pass them via the env option.

Specifically in cli.ts around the spawnSync call: build the child env from process.env but delete KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION and KSPEC_SESSION_ID unless the test explicitly provides them via opts.env.

The ralph.test.ts line 607 also needs fixing: it uses { ...process.env } directly in its own spawnSync (not via the helper), so it needs the same treatment.

## Verification
Run tests both standalone (npx vitest run) and inside ralph loop to confirm both pass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

Codex PR review said 'No PR Task trailer was present, so spec/trait AC coverage checks were skipped per instructions' on PR #510. This defeats the purpose of spec-first development — reviewers should always validate against specs.

## Affected Skills

### 1. .claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md (line 128)
Current: 'If no Task trailer exists, proceed with pure code review (skip AC checks).'
Fix: Replace with instructions to dig deeper — check commit trailers, search tasks list, check AC annotations in changed files, then validate against found specs. Only fall back to pure code review if genuinely no spec coverage exists for the change.

### 2. .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md
Current: Requires task ref as a hard validation gate ('Task reference required. Error immediately.')
Fix: Instead of erroring, dig for context the same way — commit trailers, task list search, AC annotations. The PR body trailer is a convenience, not a prerequisite.

### 3. .claude/skills/local-review/SKILL.md
Current: AC coverage checks are unconditional (good), but only when spec context is already known.
Fix: Add step to discover spec context if not explicitly provided — same dig-deeper pattern.

## Dig-Deeper Pattern (apply to all three)

When no Task trailer in PR body:
1. Check commit messages for Task: or Spec: trailers
2. Search recent tasks: kspec tasks list — match by title/description to PR scope
3. Check if changed files have // AC: @spec-ref annotations pointing to specs
4. If a spec is found, validate AC coverage identically to trailer-present case
5. Only skip AC validation if genuinely no spec exists for the changed behavior

## Principle
Reviewers should be investigators, not form-checkers. The absence of a trailer is a signal to look harder, not permission to skip validation.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Bug: ralph signal handler (src/cli/commands/ralph.ts ~lines 1057-1071) queues Promise.all for fs.unlink(budget) + closeSession() but does not await it — process.exit(0) in .finally() fires before I/O completes. This causes budget.json to persist after SIGINT, failing ac-signal-cleanup.

Root cause: fire-and-forget async cleanup in synchronous signal handler. The normal exit path (finally block ~line 1513) correctly awaits the same cleanup.

Fix: await cleanup promises before calling process.exit(). Either use async handler pattern or set a flag and let the event loop drain. Only one instance of this pattern exists — no other signal handlers in the codebase have this issue.

Test: tests/ralph/session-budget-integration.test.ts testSignalCleanup() — currently flaky, should pass reliably after fix.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fixed unawaited async cleanup in ralph signal handler. The signalCleanup function created Promise.all() for budget deletion + session close but never awaited it — process.exit(0) in .finally() fired before I/O completed. Changed to async IIFE pattern: void (async () => { try { await Promise.all([...]); } catch {} finally { process.exit(0); } })(). Updated static analysis test in end-loop.test.ts to match new pattern. Added AC annotation for @ralph-task-limit ac-signal-cleanup to both SIGINT and SIGTERM signal tests. All tests pass.

tasks.title: Add CI lint to prevent static analysis test pattern
tasks.description:
Add a vitest test that fails if any test file reads source code files — the static analysis anti-pattern this project is migrating away from.

The pattern to detect: test files under tests/ that use readFile/readFileSync on paths containing src/ or packages/*/src/. These read implementation source code and assert on string patterns instead of testing behavior.

Approach: Write tests/lint/no-static-analysis.test.ts that:
1. Globs all tests/**/*.test.ts files
2. Parses each file looking for readFile/readFileSync calls where the path argument references src/ (using simple regex)
3. Fails with a clear error message: "Test file X reads source file Y. Tests should exercise behavior (import functions, call CLI, make HTTP requests) not scan source code for string patterns."

No allowlist needed — there are no valid exceptions.

This should run as part of npm test so it catches new static analysis tests before they merge.

Note: The project uses Biome (not ESLint), and Biome doesn't support custom rules. A vitest lint test is the right approach — it's the same pattern used for other convention enforcement (see tests/convention-validation.test.ts).

This task is blocked on all E2E migration and deletion tasks completing first.

tasks.title: Shadow repair: handle missing /bin/sh — use direct git commands instead of spawning shell, fails on
tasks.description: **What**: `kspec shadow repair` (and other shadow branch operations) fails on systems where `/bin/sh` is not available, such as NixOS or fish-only systems. All git operations in `src/parser/shadow.ts` use `execSync()` and `execAsync()` (which is `promisify(exec)`), both of which default to spawning `/bin/sh` to interpret the command string. **Where**: `src/parser/shadow.ts` — all `execSync()` calls (lines ~154, 170, 189, 584, 595, 614) and all `execAsync()` calls (lines ~841, 863, 882, 909, 933, 1007, 1027, 1030, 1179). The `repairShadow()` function at line 1785 is the primary trigger but the issue affects every git-invoking function in the file. **How**: Replace shell-spawning `exec`/`execSync` with `spawnSync`/`spawn` using `{ shell: false }` (or simply omitting shell). Pass git commands as arrays: `spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-dir'], { cwd, stdio })`. This avoids needing `/bin/sh` entirely. The `spawn` import already exists at line 12 but is unused for most operations. For `execAsync` calls, use `child_process.execFile` (which does not use a shell by default) wrapped with `promisify`. **Done when**: (1) All `execSync`/`execAsync` calls in `shadow.ts` use `spawnSync`/`execFileAsync` instead of shell-based execution. (2) `kspec shadow repair` succeeds on a system without `/bin/sh`. (3) All existing shadow tests pass. (4) No string interpolation of git commands (eliminates shell injection risk as a bonus).

tasks.description: **What**: `kspec task patch @ref` hangs indefinitely when invoked without piped stdin and without `--data`. The command reads from `process.stdin` using a `for await` loop (line 999-1003 in `src/cli/commands/task.ts`) which blocks forever waiting for input when stdin is a TTY. **Where**: `src/cli/commands/task.ts`, lines 993-1004 — the `else` branch of the `if (options.data)` check. When `--data` is not provided, the code does `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` which never resolves if stdin is a terminal. **How**: Add TTY detection before attempting to read stdin. If `process.stdin.isTTY` is true and `--data` was not provided, print an error message explaining that either `--data <json>` must be provided or JSON must be piped to stdin, then exit with a validation error. Example: `if (!options.data && process.stdin.isTTY) { error('Provide --data or pipe JSON to stdin'); process.exit(EXIT_CODES.VALIDATION_FAILED); }`. Alternatively, add a short timeout on stdin reads. **Done when**: (1) Running `kspec task patch @ref` without `--data` and without piped stdin immediately prints a helpful error and exits. (2) `kspec task patch @ref --data '{...}'` still works. (3) `echo '{...}' | kspec task patch @ref` still works. (4) Batch exec engine (`src/cli/batch-exec.ts`) still works with task patch.

The `generateFreshnessComment()` function (line 160) uses `version` from the package but this is only in the output, not the hash. Add `data.version = version` (importing `version` from the package, which is already imported at the top of the file for `generateFreshnessComment`). This way, any version bump automatically invalidates the hash and triggers regeneration. tasks.description:
**What**: `kspec search` can find observations (e.g., @01KJ73ME) via `loadMetaContext()` which reads the meta.observations array from kynetic.yaml, but `kspec item get` fails for the same reference because the `ReferenceIndex` only indexes spec items and tasks — not meta entities like observations, workflows, conventions, or agents.

This is not a write conflict or index corruption. It is an architectural gap: search and item-get use different resolution paths. Search loads observations from meta context, while item-get only resolves through the ReferenceIndex which does not include meta entities.

**Where**:
- `src/cli/commands/search.ts` — loads observations via `loadMetaContext()` (lines 241-257)
- `src/cli/commands/item.ts` — uses `refIndex.resolve()` which only covers spec items
- `src/parser/refs.ts` — `ReferenceIndex` class that builds the resolution index
- `src/cli/commands/meta.ts` — has dedicated `meta observe get` subcommand for observations

**How**:
Two options (pick one):
1. **Extend ReferenceIndex** to include meta entities (observations, workflows, agents, conventions) so `item get` can resolve them. This is the deeper fix but has namespace collision risk.
2. **Improve error message** in `item get` to suggest `kspec meta observe get @ref` when a ref fails to resolve, since observations have their own dedicated get command. This is lighter and avoids mixing namespaces.

Option 2 is recommended: observations already have `kspec meta observe get`, so the real bug is a confusing UX, not missing functionality.

**Done when**:
- `kspec item get @observation-ref` either resolves the observation or provides a clear error message suggesting `kspec meta observe get @ref`
- Alternatively, if extending ReferenceIndex: meta entities are resolvable via `item get` with correct type display

tasks.title: Ralph loop needs iteration-level timeout. When a spawned agent gets stuck (e.g., tool call hanging o
tasks.description:
**What**: Ralph loop has no per-iteration timeout. When a spawned agent gets stuck (e.g., a tool call hanging on stdin, like the `kspec batch --commands ""` hang), ralph waits indefinitely. Claude Code's per-bash-command timeout (120s default) does not cover all hang scenarios — an agent can be alive but unresponsive at the ACP protocol level.

**Where**:
- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` — main loop at line ~1127, the `agent.client.prompt()` call at line ~1373 and the reflection prompt call. These are the two main await points that can hang.
- `src/acp/client.ts` — the ACP client that manages the session/prompt lifecycle

**How**:
- Add a configurable `--iteration-timeout <minutes>` CLI option (default: 20 minutes) to the ralph command registration (line ~868).
- Wrap the `agent.client.prompt()` calls in a `Promise.race` with a timeout. On timeout: (1) kill the stuck agent process via `agent.kill()`, (2) log the timeout as a failed iteration, (3) apply the existing retry/failure escalation logic.
- The timeout should cover the entire iteration (task-work prompt + optional reflection prompt), not individual prompts, since an iteration is the atomic unit of work.
- Consider using `AbortController` / `AbortSignal` if the ACP client supports it, otherwise use `Promise.race` with a timer.

**Done when**:
- `kspec ralph --iteration-timeout 15` kills a stuck agent after 15 minutes and continues to the next iteration (or exits if max failures reached)
- Default timeout is 20 minutes
- Timeout events are logged to the session event store with type `iteration.timeout`
- Existing retry and failure escalation logic handles timeouts the same as other iteration failures

tasks.title: CLI args should accept both kebab-case and underscore variants (e.g. depends-on and depends_on). Cur
tasks.description:
**What**: Batch command validation rejects underscore variants of argument names (e.g., `depends_on`) even though kebab-case (`depends-on`) and camelCase (`dependsOn`) are accepted. Agents generating JSON batch payloads naturally use underscores, which is the standard JSON/Python naming convention. The error message suggests the kebab form, creating a frustrating feedback loop.

**Where**:
- `src/cli/batch-exec.ts` lines 180-216 — `kebabToCamel()` and `getKnownArgNames()` functions
- `src/cli/batch-exec.ts` lines 308-327 — unknown arg validation loop
- `src/cli/batch-exec.ts` lines 434-496 — `buildCommandArgv()` which also needs to handle underscore keys when building CLI argv

**How**:
1. Add a `underscoreToKebab()` or `underscoreToCamel()` normalizer alongside `kebabToCamel()`.
2. In `getKnownArgNames()`, add underscore variants to the known names set (e.g., for `depends-on`, also add `depends_on`).
3. In `buildCommandArgv()`, normalize incoming arg keys before classification — convert underscores to kebab-case before looking up in positionalNameSet and optionMap.
4. In the required-args check (lines 330-348), also check underscore variants.

A cleaner approach: add a single `normalizeArgKey(key)` function that converts any variant (kebab, camel, underscore) to a canonical form, then use it everywhere.

**Done when**:
- `{"command": "task set", "args": {"ref": "@task", "depends_on": ["@dep1"]}}` works in batch mode
- All three forms accepted: `depends-on`, `dependsOn`, `depends_on`
- Same normalization applies to all options, not just depends_on
- Add test cases for underscore variant args in batch validation tests

tasks.title: Ralph event handler iteration attribution should use session-scoped mapping instead of shared mutabl
tasks.description:
**What**: Ralph event handler uses a `sessionIterationMap` (Map<string, number>) to attribute late ACP session updates to the correct iteration. However, the current implementation has a race condition: when a new ACP session starts for iteration N+1, late updates from iteration N's session can arrive after `sessionIterationMap.set(newSessionId, N+1)` but the old session's listener may still fire. The `_sid` closure variable in the `on('update')` handler captures the session ID correctly, but there is no cleanup of old listeners when starting a new session.

The Codex review on PR #484 identified that the shared mutable `sessionIterationMap` approach is fragile — a session-scoped listener pattern would be more robust.

**Where**:
- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` line 1061 — `sessionIterationMap` declaration
- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` lines 1305-1337 — the `on('update')` handler that uses `sessionIterationMap.get(_sid)` for iteration lookup
- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` line 1369 — where new sessions are registered in the map

**How**:
Two approaches (pick one):

1. **Session-scoped listeners** (recommended): Instead of one persistent `on('update')` handler, register a new listener per ACP session that captures the iteration number in its closure. Remove the old listener when the session ends or a new one starts. This eliminates the shared mutable map entirely.

2. **Cleanup old sessions**: When starting a new ACP session, remove the previous session's entry from `sessionIterationMap` and call `agent.client.off('update', oldHandler)` to prevent stale callbacks. Less clean but simpler delta.

Both approaches should also ensure the translator is reset between iterations (it already creates a fresh translator per retry, but verify per-iteration reset).

**Done when**:
- Late updates from a previous ACP session are attributed to the correct iteration (the one that created that session)
- No shared mutable state for iteration tracking — either session-scoped closures or explicit cleanup
- Existing event logging tests still pass
- Event log entries show correct iteration numbers even when sessions overlap

tasks.title: Plan import warnings treated as errors in batch mode. The no YAML code block in specs section warnin
tasks.description:
**What**: When `kspec plan import` runs inside batch mode, non-fatal warnings (e.g., 'no YAML code block in specs section') cause the batch to fail and roll back. The plan-import command uses `warn()` for non-fatal issues and `process.exit(EXIT_CODES.SUCCESS)` on completion. In batch mode, `process.exit()` is intercepted and throws `BatchExitError`. The exit code 0 is correctly detected as success (line 859 in batch-exec.ts). However, the warnings written to stderr via `warn()` are captured by `OutputCapture` and when the captured output is returned, it may be treated as an error indicator by the batch result processing.

The core issue is that `plan import` calls `process.exit(0)` even on success (line 687 of plan-import.ts). In batch mode, this throws `BatchExitError(0)`, which IS handled as success (batch-exec.ts line 859). But the warnings in captured stderr make the output look like a failure. Additionally, the batch atomic mode may see stderr output as part of the error string when `BatchExitError` code is non-zero for other plan import failures.

**Where**:
- `src/cli/commands/plan-import.ts` line 687 — `process.exit(EXIT_CODES.SUCCESS)` which triggers BatchExitError in batch mode
- `src/cli/commands/plan-import.ts` lines 124-135 — warning emission for non-fatal parse errors
- `src/cli/batch-exec.ts` lines 849-875 — BatchExitError handling in `dispatchCommand()`
- `src/cli/batch-context.ts` — OutputCapture that captures both stdout and stderr

**How**:
1. In `plan-import.ts`, replace the final `process.exit(EXIT_CODES.SUCCESS)` with a simple `return`. The batch executor expects normal returns for success — only use `process.exit()` for failures. This is the main fix.
2. Alternatively, ensure that `dispatchCommand()` in batch-exec.ts distinguishes between stderr warnings and actual errors when a `BatchExitError(0)` is caught — treat exit code 0 as success regardless of captured output content.
3. Consider adding a `warnings` field to `BatchCommandResult` so warnings can be reported without marking the command as failed.

**Done when**:
- `kspec plan import` with warnings runs successfully in batch mode (no rollback)
- Warnings are still visible in batch output (not silenced)
- Plan import still fails correctly in batch mode for actual errors (YAML parse errors, missing module, etc.)
- Add a test case: batch with a plan import that produces warnings should succeed
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #609. Fixed batch-mode plan import by replacing process.exit(EXIT_CODES.SUCCESS) with return in plan-import.ts success path, preventing BatchExitError interception. Added regression test in batch-exec-engine.test.ts covering warning-only plan import succeeds in batch (ac-34, ac-23). All CI checks passed.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:

**What**: When `kspec plan import --update` encounters an existing spec, it replaces the entire `acceptance_criteria` array instead of merging. If a spec already has ac-1 through ac-9 and a plan adds ac-10, --update overwrites all ACs with only what the plan document contains, losing ac-1 through ac-9.

**Where**: `src/cli/commands/plan-import.ts` lines 271-303 (the --update branch). The update logic builds a `Partial<SpecItemInput>` and sets `updates.acceptance_criteria = spec.acceptance_criteria` (line 296), passed to `updateSpecItem()` in `src/parser/yaml.ts` line 1522. `updateSpecItem` does direct property assignment (`targetObj[key] = value` at line 1560) with no merge logic.

**How**: Implement an AC merge strategy in the update path. When `updates.acceptance_criteria` is set and the existing item already has ACs:
1. Index existing ACs by their `id` field (e.g., "ac-1", "ac-2")
2. For each AC in the plan update: if an AC with the same `id` exists, replace it; otherwise append it
3. Preserve existing ACs whose IDs are not in the update set
Best done in `plan-import.ts` before calling `updateSpecItem`, since general updateSpecItem callers may want full replacement semantics.

**Done when**:
- `kspec plan import --update` with a plan that adds one new AC to an existing spec preserves all pre-existing ACs and appends the new one
- A plan that modifies an existing AC (same id) updates that AC in place while preserving others

tasks.title: ULID short ref ambiguity in batch operations: when two ULIDs share a prefix (e.g. 01KJ4SNE9 and 01KJ
tasks.description: ULID short ref ambiguity in batch operations: when two ULIDs share a prefix (e.g. 01KJ4SNE9 and 01KJ4SNEC), short refs like @01KJ4SNE fail. kspec already has a shortest-unique-ID utility — this should be used anywhere refs are displayed (triage list, task list, inbox list, promote result_ref, etc.) so that presented refs are always unambiguous and copy-pasteable into subsequent commands.

Review verified spec alignment for unambiguous copy-pasteable refs and confirmed @batch-exec own + inherited trait AC annotation coverage. CI checks passed on head 691228e72.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:

**What**: When two ULIDs share a prefix (e.g., 01KJ4SNE9... and 01KJ4SNEC...), the default 8-character short ref `@01KJ4SNE` is ambiguous and fails to resolve. The `ReferenceIndex.shortUlid()` method (in `src/parser/refs.ts` line 310) already computes the minimum unique prefix, but many places in the codebase use a hardcoded `_ulid.slice(0, 8)` instead. There are 69 occurrences of `_ulid.slice(0, 8)` across 19 files.

**Where**: All places that format ULID refs for display need to use `shortUlid()` instead of `_ulid.slice(0, 8)`. Key files with hardcoded slicing:
- `src/cli/commands/triage.ts` (14 occurrences) — triage list, record, act, get, start
- `src/cli/commands/inbox.ts` (9 occurrences) — inbox list, add, promote
- `src/cli/commands/item.ts` (6 occurrences) — item list, get, add
- `src/cli/commands/plan.ts` (9 occurrences) — plan list, get
- `src/cli/commands/search.ts` (4 occurrences) — search results
- `src/cli/commands/session/context.ts` (4 occurrences) — session context display
- `src/triage/actions.ts` (1 occurrence) — promote result ref
- `src/parser/validate.ts` (8 occurrences) — validation output
- Several other files with 1-3 occurrences each

The `ReferenceIndex` is already available in most of these contexts (it's built during `initContext()` or `buildIndexes()`).

**How**:
1. For each file, replace `_ulid.slice(0, 8)` with `index.shortUlid(_ulid)` where a ReferenceIndex is in scope
2. For files where no index is available, either thread the index through or create a lightweight shortening utility
3. For triage records (which aren't indexed in the main ReferenceIndex), consider building a local index or a dedicated triage ULID shortener
4. Ensure that refs displayed by any list/get/result command are always copy-pasteable into subsequent commands without ambiguity

**Done when**:
- No occurrences of `_ulid.slice(0, 8)` remain in display-facing code paths
- All displayed refs (triage list, task list, inbox list, search results, promote result_ref, etc.) use `shortUlid()` or equivalent
- A test with two items sharing an 8-character ULID prefix shows that displayed refs are still unique and resolvable

tasks.title: Triage promote action should optionally delete the inbox item after creating the task. Currently pro
tasks.description: Triage promote action should optionally delete the inbox item after creating the task. Currently promoted items stay in inbox requiring manual cleanup. Consider --consume flag or making deletion the default for promote (with snapshot preserved in triage record).
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #617. Implemented promote consume-by-default behavior in triage act, added --keep escape hatch, and updated dry-run messaging to indicate delete vs keep. Verified AC coverage for @triage-cli-commands (ac-1..ac-17) including new consume/keep scenarios and trait coverage checks; CI checks passed on head 791ea48.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:

**What**: When `kspec triage act` executes a "promote" action, it creates a new task from the inbox item but leaves the original inbox item in the inbox. This requires a separate manual `kspec inbox delete` step to clean up, which is tedious and easy to forget. The inbox item's text is already preserved in the triage record's `item_snapshot` field, so the original is not needed for audit trail purposes.

**Where**: 
- `src/triage/actions.ts` lines 54-74 — the `promote` case in `executeTriageAction()`. Currently creates the task and returns, but never calls `deleteInboxItem()` for the promoted item.
- `src/cli/commands/triage.ts` lines 235-289 — the `triage act` command handler. This is where the `--consume` flag would be parsed and passed to `executeTriageAction()`.
- The `delete` and `duplicate` cases (lines 77-90, 117-130) already call `deleteInboxItem()` — the promote case can follow the same pattern.

**How**: Two reasonable approaches:
1. **Flag approach**: Add `--consume` flag to `kspec triage act` that deletes the inbox item after promote. Pass it through `ExecuteTriageActionOptions` to `executeTriageAction()`.
2. **Default behavior**: Make deletion the default for promote (since the snapshot is preserved in the triage record), with a `--keep` flag to opt out.

Recommendation: Option 2 (delete by default) is cleaner since every promoted item has its text preserved in `item_snapshot`. The `--keep` flag is the escape hatch. The `delete` and `duplicate` cases already delete inbox items as their default behavior, so promote doing the same is consistent.

Implementation:
1. Add `consume` option to `ExecuteTriageActionOptions` (default true for promote)
2. In the `promote` case of `executeTriageAction()`, after creating the task, call `deleteInboxItem()` for `record.inbox_ref` unless consume is false
3. Add `--keep` flag to `kspec triage act` command that sets `consume: false`
4. Update dry-run output to mention deletion

**Done when**:
- `kspec triage act <ref>` on a promote record creates the task AND deletes the inbox item
- `kspec triage act <ref> --keep` creates the task but preserves the inbox item
- Dry-run output mentions that the inbox item would be deleted
- The `item_snapshot` in the triage record still contains the original text for audit trail
- Tests cover: promote with deletion (default), promote with --keep, dry-run output

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:

**What**: Web UI pages lose their filter state when the browser refreshes. For example, filtering tasks by status=in_progress or triage by tag=cli is lost on reload. Filter state should be persisted in URL query parameters so that refreshing preserves the view, and URLs are shareable/bookmarkable.

**Where**: The tasks page (`packages/web-ui/src/routes/tasks/+page.svelte`) already partially implements URL-based filters — it reads from `$page.url.searchParams` (line 39-47) via the `filterParams` derived value. However, the triage page (`packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte`) uses local `$state` variables (`filterTag`, `filterStatus` at lines 43-44) that are NOT synced to URL params. Other list pages (items, inbox) likely have the same issue.

Key files to update:
- `packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte` — filterTag and filterStatus need URL param sync
- `packages/web-ui/src/routes/items/+page.svelte` — check if filters use URL params
- Any other list/filter pages under `packages/web-ui/src/routes/`

**How**: Follow the pattern already established in the tasks page:
1. Read initial filter values from `$page.url.searchParams` (from `$app/stores`)
2. When a filter changes, use `goto()` (from `$app/navigation`) to update URL params without a full page reload: `goto(\`?status=\${filterStatus}&tag=\${filterTag}\`, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true })`
3. Use `$derived` to compute filter values from URL params (like tasks page does)
4. This approach gives: URL persistence, back/forward navigation, shareable links

For the triage page specifically:
- Replace `let filterTag = $state('')` with reading from `$page.url.searchParams.get('tag')`
- Replace `let filterStatus = $state('all')` with reading from `$page.url.searchParams.get('status')`
- Add `goto()` calls when filters change

**Done when**:
- All list/filter pages read initial state from URL query params
- Changing a filter updates the URL without full page reload
- Refreshing the page preserves filter state
- Browser back/forward navigates between filter states
- The triage page URL shows filters like `?status=untriaged&tag=cli`

tasks.title: Web UI WebSocket connection unreliable - continually disconnects and reconnects. Needs investigation
tasks.description: Web UI WebSocket connection unreliable - continually disconnects and reconnects. Needs investigation into reconnection logic, heartbeat handling, or fallback to polling.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #622 (commit a5ccb212). Stabilized WebSocket reconnect lifecycle by ignoring stale socket events, suppressing reconnect after intentional disconnect, and preserving reconnect on unexpected disconnect; added regression tests in tests/websocket-manager.test.ts. Also hardened serve status uptime parsing/retry to clear regression flake. AC coverage reviewed for @daemon-server and inherited traits; regression gates passed (npm test + PR checks).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:

**What**: The Web UI WebSocket connection continually disconnects and reconnects. The `WebSocketManager` in `packages/web-ui/src/lib/websocket/manager.ts` has exponential backoff reconnection (1s, 2s, 4s... max 30s, max 10 attempts), but users report seeing frequent disconnect/reconnect cycles in the console logs. This suggests either the server is closing connections, the keepalive/heartbeat mechanism is missing, or reconnection resets are happening incorrectly.

**Where**:
- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/websocket/manager.ts` — The WebSocketManager class. Key areas:
  - `connect()` (line 150): creates WebSocket, sets up onopen/onmessage/onerror/onclose handlers
  - `scheduleReconnect()` (line 371): exponential backoff logic, max 10 attempts
  - `onclose` handler (line 183): triggers reconnect on any close event, even clean ones
  - No heartbeat/ping mechanism — if the server expects periodic pings, the connection may time out
- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/stores/connection.svelte.ts` — Connection store wrapping the manager
- Server-side WebSocket handler (in the daemon code) — check if it sends pings or has idle timeouts

**How**: Investigation and fix areas:
1. **Add heartbeat/ping**: Implement a periodic ping from client to server (e.g., every 30s). Many WebSocket servers close idle connections after a timeout (often 60s). The client should send a ping command and expect a pong response.
2. **Don't reconnect on clean close**: The `onclose` handler (line 183) calls `scheduleReconnect()` unconditionally. If `event.code === 1000` (normal closure) and the client initiated it via `disconnect()`, skip reconnection. Currently `disconnect()` clears the timer, but there's a race if onclose fires after disconnect resets state.
3. **Check server-side idle timeout**: The daemon's WebSocket server may have an idle timeout that closes connections. Either increase it or implement heartbeat to keep alive.
4. **Consider connection health check**: After reconnecting, verify the connection is actually healthy (e.g., send a ping and wait for response) before transitioning to 'connected' state.
5. **Investigate MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS**: After 10 failed reconnects, the connection is abandoned permanently. Consider resetting the attempt counter after a successful connection that lasts longer than some threshold (e.g., 60s).

**Done when**:
- WebSocket connection remains stable for extended periods without spurious disconnects
- Client sends periodic heartbeat/ping to prevent idle timeout
- Clean disconnects (code 1000 from client-initiated disconnect) don't trigger reconnection
- Console shows clean connection lifecycle without repeated disconnect/reconnect spam
- Connection lost indicator (10s threshold) only triggers for genuine server unavailability
- Tests cover: heartbeat keeps connection alive, clean close doesn't reconnect, reconnection works after genuine server restart

tasks.title: Verify and fix codex-acp adapter integration for ralph
tasks.description:
Several issues identified with the codex-acp adapter that prevent it from working correctly with ralph:

## Issues

### 1. CRITICAL: Env injection writes to wrong config file
injectCodexEnv() in src/sessions/store.ts writes KSPEC_SESSION_ID to ~/.codex/config.json using JSON format. But Codex CLI reads ~/.codex/config.toml (TOML format). The injection has no effect — Codex never sees the session ID.

Fix: Rewrite injectCodexEnv to read/write ~/.codex/config.toml using TOML format. The key path is shell_environment_policy.set.KSPEC_SESSION_ID. Same for removeCodexEnv.

### 2. Auto-approve args may use wrong config keys
The adapter registers these auto-approve args: -c approval_policy="never" and -c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access". But codex-acp help shows sandbox_permissions (array), and the config file uses trust_level. Need to verify which keys codex-acp actually accepts and what values produce full auto-approve behavior.

### 3. No integration test with real codex-acp
All tests use mock ACP. No test verifies that ralph can actually spawn and communicate with @zed-industries/codex-acp. At minimum, a smoke test that spawns codex-acp and checks ACP handshake would catch protocol mismatches.

### 4. Package name fix pending (PR #565)
The adapter registry had codex-acp instead of @zed-industries/codex-acp. Fix is in PR #565, pending merge.

## How to verify
- kspec ralph run --dry-run --adapter codex-acp shows correct package name
- kspec ralph run --max-loops 1 --adapter codex-acp completes one iteration successfully
- Session ID reaches kspec subprocesses inside the codex agent
- Auto-approve args produce no permission prompts during ralph loop

tasks.title: Make git root/shadow detection resilient to restricted runtimes
tasks.description: Issue: In the Codex execution runtime, Node shell-based git calls (execSync with string commands like "git rev-parse --show-toplevel") can fail with spawnSync /bin/sh EPERM even when git itself is available. Impact: getGitRoot() and related checks return false negatives, kspec treats repo as non-git/non-shadow, and writes can fall back to root-level files (for example project.tasks.yaml) instead of .kspec worktree paths. Findings: (1) kspec shadow status returned Not a git repository in this runtime while user environment returned healthy shadow JSON. (2) Running getGitRoot() through parser returned null before fix. (3) Task add created an untracked root project.tasks.yaml due to shadow detection failure. Why: the implementation depended on shell invocation semantics instead of direct process execution, which is fragile in sandboxed/restricted runtimes. Proposal: standardize git invocations in detection-critical paths to direct argv-based spawn/execFile style calls, add regression tests that simulate shell-unavailable execution behavior, and audit other shell-form git calls that can influence path resolution.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #567. Replaced shell-string git detection calls in shadow parser with argv-based sync git invocation () via shared runGitSync helper; updated isGitRepo/getGitRoot/branchExists to avoid /bin/sh dependency in restricted runtimes. Verified CI green and runtime behavior via kspec shadow status/getGitRoot; infra task had no spec_ref so AC coverage gate was N/A.

notes.author: @codex
notes.content: Investigation summary: reproduced mismatch where kspec shadow status failed in Codex runtime but succeeded in user shell. Root cause is shell-form Node git execution failing under restricted runtime (/bin/sh EPERM), which made getGitRoot/isGitRepo/branchExists return false negatives and caused non-shadow fallback writes. Confirmed by direct module probe (getGitRoot returned null before patch) and by root project.tasks.yaml creation from task add before fix.

tasks.title: Ralph: Stream terminal/run output to session files and return bounded previews
tasks.description:

Done when: reproducing command-heavy codex run no longer grows heap unbounded from terminal/run output, and full output is still retrievable from session artifacts.

tasks.title: Session events: Add oversized payload guardrails with externalized blob pointers
tasks.description:
Problem: large ACP updates can inflate JSONL event lines and memory pressure. We need safety limits without losing auditability.

Scope (steps 3-4):
1) Add framing/event safety caps (line/payload size) to prevent single-message heap blowups.
2) For oversized payload fields (toolResponse stdout/stderr, rawOutput, large chunk text), write full content to session blob files under .kspec/sessions/<id>/blobs/.
3) Store compact pointer objects in events.jsonl (path, bytes, sha256, truncated=true, preview).
4) Update session log show/search behavior to surface previews by default and optionally resolve blob content on demand.

Non-goal: silently dropping payloads. If payload is externalized, events must keep enough metadata to reconstruct/audit.

tasks.title: Investigate and stabilize kspec validate failures/noise baseline
tasks.description:
What:
`kspec validate` currently fails/noises in ways that block reliable use as a quality gate. Create a single validated baseline and implement the minimum fixes/policy decisions to make output actionable.

Current observed state (2026-02-27):
- Reference errors: 6 (all from `@observations` resolving to multiple items).
- Alignment warnings: 156 (including 137 status mismatches).
- Completeness warnings: 390.
- Automation-without-spec warnings: 128.

Root-cause findings already confirmed:
1) Slug namespace collision:
   - `@observations` is ambiguous between a spec slug and a skill id.
   - `ReferenceIndex` currently merges spec/task/plan slugs and meta ids into one slug namespace.
2) Validate mode-flag behavior bug:
   - Mode flags are intended to isolate checks (`--refs`, `--schema`, etc.) but non-selected checks still run because undefined options are treated as enabled in parser validation.
   - `--staleness` also does not participate in runAll detection, causing unexpected extra checks.
3) High warning volume is mostly data + policy driven (not one parser crash):
   - Many specs have statuses that do not match task-derived expected status.
   - Many automation-eligible tasks have no spec_ref.

tasks.title: Clarify core skill update behavior for local template edits
tasks.description:
**What**: Remove ambiguity in `kspec skill update` when core templates change locally but package version is unchanged.

**Problem**: `skill update` short-circuits on version match, so same-version template edits are skipped with no clear next action. During local core-skill/template iteration this appears broken, and users only discover later that `skill install-core` was required.

**Scope**:
1. Update `skill update` behavior in `src/cli/commands/skill-install.ts` so same-version cases are not silently misleading. Acceptable outcomes:
   - detect template/file drift and still update files, OR
   - keep version gate but emit explicit guidance (`use kspec skill install-core`) in both normal and `--dry-run` output.
2. Ensure output clearly distinguishes: version up-to-date vs template content out-of-sync.
3. Add/adjust tests in `tests/core-skill-update.test.ts` (and `tests/core-skill-install.test.ts` if needed) covering the same-version local-template-change path and expected messaging/behavior.

**Verification**:
- `npx vitest run tests/core-skill-update.test.ts tests/core-skill-install.test.ts`
- Manual CLI check on changed-template scenario shows deterministic behavior (update or explicit guidance), including `--dry-run`.

**Done when**:
1. Same-version template changes are no longer silently skipped without actionable guidance.
2. Users can reliably tell whether to run `skill update` vs `skill install-core`.
3. Tests cover the scenario and pass.

tasks.title: Fix ralph orchestrator memory leaks causing OOM after ~30 iterations
tasks.description:
The ralph orchestrator process (kspec ralph run) accumulates memory across loop iterations until it hits the ~4GB V8 heap limit and crashes with OOM. This happens even with --restart-every 1 because that only restarts the spawned agent subprocess, not the orchestrator itself.

Stack trace ends at StringDecoder::DecodeData — the orchestrator reading stdio from the spawned agent.

Memory leaks identified:

1. Event listeners stacking (primary) — src/cli/commands/ralph.ts ~L1700-1748. update and request listeners registered on agent.client but never removed. On agent restart, new listeners added to new client; old closures capture translator/renderer/state preventing GC. Fix: call agent.client.removeAllListeners() before agent.kill() in restart-every block and in finally cleanup.

2. Framing buffer accumulation — src/acp/framing.ts ~L87. JSON-RPC framing uses this.buffer += chunk string concatenation. Buffer not reset across newSession() calls. Fix: ensure fresh ACPClient/framing on agent respawn or add buffer reset method.

3. Unbounded Maps/Arrays — src/cli/commands/ralph.ts. sessionIterationMap: new entry per iteration, never cleared (~L1424, 1757). recentTaskRefs[]: grows without bound (~L1423, 1845-1849). ACPClient.sessions Map: accumulates per-session entries, never pruned (~client.ts L77). Fix: prune old entries, cap arrays, delete closed sessions.

4. Async event logging fire-and-forget — src/cli/commands/ralph.ts ~L1714-1720. appendEvent() with full ACP update objects queued via .catch(() => {}). Pending writes hold update objects in memory until I/O completes. Fix: consider backpressure or limiting concurrent pending writes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Event listeners are removed before agent.kill() in restart-every block and finally cleanup
- ac-2: sessionIterationMap entries are pruned after each iteration (keep only current)
- ac-3: recentTaskRefs is bounded (e.g. keep last N or clear per iteration, only needed at wrap-up)
- ac-4: ACPClient.sessions entries are removed when sessions end
- ac-5: Ralph loop can run 30+ iterations with codex-acp adapter without OOM
- ac-6: Existing ralph tests pass
