tasks.title: Fix: Truncate oversized ACP prompt payloads
tasks.description: Ralph subagent and worker prompts embed raw JSON.stringify() of task/spec/session data inline. For large payloads (tasks with many notes, large specs), the resulting JSON-RPC line exceeds the Codex Rust binary read buffer, causing 'agent_client_protocol::rpc: failed to parse incoming message'. The parser receives a partial fragment and fails. Observed on the review subagent path, but the worker prompt has the same vulnerability.
tasks.closed_reason: PR #590 reviewed and merged at head 690d0648

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Root Cause: Ralph prompts embed raw JSON.stringify() of task/spec/session data inline. For large payloads, the JSON-RPC line exceeds the Codex Rust binary read buffer causing parse failures. Approach: 32KB total prompt budget with largest-first truncation. Truncated sections show a blockquote notice with CLI fetch command and compact identity summary. Changes: (1) subagent.ts — SUBAGENT_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES, formatJsonSection(), truncatePromptIfNeeded(), compactSummary(). Updated buildSubagentPrompt(). (2) ralph.ts — Updated buildTaskWorkPrompt() with same helpers. (3) ralph/index.ts — Exported new helpers. (4) tests/ralph.test.ts — 14 new tests covering formatJsonSection, truncatePromptIfNeeded, and end-to-end buildSubagentPrompt truncation. (5) Spec ac-10 updated to reflect truncation behavior.

tasks.title: Fix merge driver non-interactive flag and improve conflict resolution
tasks.description:
**Background**: Shadow branch diverged (170 local vs 260 remote commits). During merge, the merge driver was registered without --non-interactive, causing it to hang on stdin when conflicts were detected. This left files unmerged (ours version only), silently losing 12 task completions, notes, and remote-side spec changes.

**Already done (this session):**
1. Diagnosed root cause: git config had `kspec merge-driver %O %A %B %P` but needed `--non-interactive` flag
2. Fixed local git config to include --non-interactive
3. Performed isolated rebase in /tmp worktree to produce correctly merged state
4. Applied corrected data as patch commit on kspec-meta (no force push needed)
5. Restored all 12 lost task completions with notes, verified 705 tasks intact
6. Marked 37 stale active sessions as abandoned, compacted all sessions (383MB reclaimed)
7. Created backup branches: kspec-meta-backup-2026-02-28 (pre-merge local), kspec-remote-pre-merge (pre-merge remote)

**Still to do:**
1. Fix shadow.ts registration — ensure kspec init/setup always registers driver with --non-interactive
2. Add TTY detection fallback — merge driver should auto-detect when stdin is not a TTY and default to non-interactive mode (defense in depth)
3. Fix exit code behavior — in non-interactive mode, exit 0 even with conflicts (they're auto-resolved with ours-defaults + comments). Exit 1 breaks git rebase.
4. Improve notes array merging — when both sides modify notes, union by timestamp instead of picking one side. Notes are append-only logs.
5. Resolve inbox item about .kspec-agents-hash auto-resolution (01KJDFFJ)
6. Restore 8 lost notes on @01KJDQ11 (observations slug fix task) — local had detailed work log that was replaced by remote's 3 automated notes
7. Consider timestamp-aware conflict resolution for status fields (task state has natural ordering)
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #601. Fixed merge driver: (1) shadow.ts validates/fixes stale config missing --non-interactive, (2) TTY detection auto-enables non-interactive when stdin is not TTY, (3) non-interactive mode exits 0 even with conflicts per spec ac-10. All tests pass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Session work completed (2026-02-28):

Root cause: merge driver registered without --non-interactive flag. When git invoked it on conflicting YAML files, it attempted interactive resolution via readline on unavailable stdin, hanging indefinitely. The ours file was never written with merged content, so git used unmodified ours version — silently losing remote-side changes.

Key finding: merge driver has NO timestamp awareness — purely structural 3-way merge. For notes (append-only), it picks one side instead of unioning both.

Rebase approach worked: 170 local commits rebased onto 260 remote in isolated /tmp worktree. Auto-continue script handled non-YAML conflicts. All 169 commits applied. Result: 705 tasks with both sides preserved.

One data loss: Task @01KJDQ11 notes — 8 local notes replaced by 3 remote (ours-bias in rebase context). Backup branches available: kspec-meta-backup-2026-02-28 (local), kspec-remote-pre-merge (remote).

notes.author: @claude

tasks.title: Fix ralph loop OOM — O(1) seq assignment + event logging backpressure
tasks.description: Ralph loop hits 8GB heap OOM after ~133 minutes. Root cause: getEventCount reads entire events.jsonl on every appendEvent call (O(n) per append, O(n²) total), and session update logger fires appendEvent via Promise.resolve().then() with no backpressure — thousands of concurrent file reads/writes accumulate in flight.

Added/updated tests in tests/ralph.test.ts and tests/sessions.test.ts including explicit AC coverage for @cli-ralph ac-27 and @session-events ac-2; AC coverage audit confirms @cli-ralph ac-1..ac-27 covered.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes:

## Fix 1: O(1) seq assignment in appendEvent (src/sessions/store.ts)

Replace getEventCount (reads entire file, counts lines) with getLastSeq:
- Read last ~4KB of events.jsonl (fs.read with position = fileSize - 4096)
- Find last complete JSON line (last newline boundary)
- Parse it, extract seq field, return seq + 1
- Empty/missing file returns 0
- This is O(1) regardless of file size

## Fix 2: Backpressure in session update logger (src/cli/commands/ralph.ts)

Replace fire-and-forget Promise.resolve().then() pattern in createSessionUpdateLogger with a sequential queue:
- Maintain a queue of pending updates and a processing flag
- When an update arrives: push to queue, start processing if not already
- Process loop: shift from queue, await appendEvent, repeat until queue empty
- This ensures at most ONE appendEvent is in flight at a time
- Updates are still non-blocking from the caller's perspective (event handler returns immediately)
- Queue should be bounded (e.g., 1000 entries) — drop oldest if exceeded with a warning

## Files
- src/sessions/store.ts — getEventCount → getLastSeq
- src/cli/commands/ralph.ts — createSessionUpdateLogger backpressure queue
- tests/sessions-store.test.ts — update seq assignment tests
- tests/ralph.test.ts — update/add logger backpressure tests

tasks.title: Fix WebSocket upgrade blocked by Elysia beforeHandle return value
tasks.description:
## Problem

WebSocket connections to the daemon never upgraded — server returned HTTP 200 with JSON body instead of 101 Switching Protocols. Every connection failed with close code 1006 (abnormal closure), cycling through reconnect attempts until max reached.

The Web UI showed continuous "Connecting... failed... Reconnecting..." loops. All 21 WebSocket E2E tests (api-websocket.spec.ts, connection.spec.ts, triage.spec.ts) failed. CI never caught this because E2E tests are not included in the shard-based test pipeline.

## Root Cause

In Elysia 1.4, when a derive() middleware is present in the route chain, returning a value from a WebSocket beforeHandle hook short-circuits the upgrade and sends the return value as an HTTP 200 response.

The daemon's ws beforeHandle (server.ts:227) returned { wsRequestId: requestId } on two code paths (lines 242 and 269). This was intended to pass a correlation ID to the open() handler, but Elysia treated it as the HTTP response body.

Progressive reproduction confirmed:
- cors only → 101 (works)
- cors + derive → 101 (works)  
- cors + derive + ws beforeHandle returning value → 200 (broken)

Without derive middleware, Elysia correctly discards the beforeHandle return value. The interaction between derive and ws beforeHandle causes the composed handler to treat the return as an early response.

## Investigation

1. Observed browser console showing repeated WS connection failures with code 1006
2. Used curl with WebSocket upgrade headers — confirmed server returns HTTP 200 with {"wsRequestId":"..."} body
3. Traced through Elysia source (adapter/bun/index.mjs) — ws handler at line 250-371 never reached
4. The composed lifecycle handler (compose.mjs) runs derive as a transform hook, then lifecycle beforeHandle hooks
5. Created progressive reproduction isolating the exact combination: derive + ws beforeHandle return value
6. Verified fix: removing return statements from beforeHandle produces 101 Switching Protocols

## Fix

Commit 7848744c8 — packages/daemon/src/server.ts:
1. Changed wsProjectPaths from Map<string, string> (keyed by ULID requestId) to WeakMap<Request, string> (keyed by Request object)
2. Removed both return { wsRequestId: requestId } statements from beforeHandle
3. Changed open() to retrieve project path via ws.data.request from the WeakMap
4. WeakMap auto-cleans when Request is garbage collected — no manual delete needed

## Related

Predecessor task @01KJDQ1GZ addressed client-side reconnect race conditions (PR #622) but missed the server-side root cause. The client-side fixes remain valuable for handling legitimate disconnects, but the server was never actually upgrading connections.

Local npm test passed (163 files, 3620 tests, 0 failures) and CI checks passed on reviewed head 7848744c8458750090a28a84346743f6a2e17fdf. tasks.title: Design agent runtime architecture — from ralph loop to reactive agent service
tasks.description:
Replace the ralph batch loop with a reactive agent runtime that dispatches named agents based on task state changes. The outcome is a spec plan (importable via kspec plan import).

## Vision

Move from explicit "ralph loop with N iterations" to an always-on service that watches for task state and dispatches the right agent. Same agent definitions also usable for one-shot CLI invocations.

## Key Design Areas

1. **Agent definitions in kspec meta** — Named agents with roles, adapters, skills, permissions (e.g. worker, reviewer, pr-merge). Defined in .kspec/ like other meta, not hardcoded in ralph.ts.

2. **Reactive dispatch** — Runtime watches task state changes and dispatches:
   - pending/ready → worker agent
   - pending_review → review agent  
   - needs_work → fix-cycle agent
   Different agents for different task states, not one monolithic loop.

3. **CLI one-shot invocations** — `kspec agent <name> "prompt"` spawns a defined agent for a single task. Same agent definitions, same runtime, just not long-lived.

4. **Session model evolution** — Sessions become long-lived (service lifecycle), with individual agent invocations as first-class units within a session. Not bounded by iteration counts.

5. **Unified event logging** — Every agent invocation (including what are currently subagents) logs events to the session. Eliminates the current gap where review subagent tool calls are fire-and-forget to terminal only.

6. **Task counting fix** — Current countTaskCompletions() scrapes events for rawInput.command strings, which fails for claude-agent-acp (empty rawInput) and codex-acp (array format). New architecture tracks agent invocations and outcomes structurally.

## Outcome

A spec plan document suitable for `kspec plan import` covering the module, features, requirements, and acceptance criteria for the agent runtime system. Should address migration path from current ralph loop.

tasks.title: Fix batch exec copying sessions/blobs to temp dir
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #638. Added ac-7 flush failure test using mkdir-fails-on-non-dir approach (ESM can't spy fs.writeFile directly). Documented Phase 2 partial commit limitation in flush() JSDoc. All 7 ACs have test coverage. 21/21 batch-write-buffer tests pass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: src/cli/batch-exec.ts:644 does fs.cp(realSpecDir, tempDir, { recursive: true }) with no exclusions. This copies .kspec/sessions/ (including all blobs/) into /tmp. Sessions blobs are LLM response text stored per-event — a long ralph loop session can have thousands of 15MB blob files. The 25G temp dir had one session with 6360 blobs at ~3.9MB avg.

Two places need to exclude sessions/:
1. Initial copy (line 644): add filter option to fs.cp to skip sessions/
2. Copy-back clear (lines 690-703): skip sessions/ when clearing realSpecDir and when copying back from temp — sessions written during batch should not be overwritten.

Batch operations never read or write session data, so sessions/ is completely irrelevant to the atomic copy. Same logic likely applies to skills/rendered output.

The recursive grep explosion compound issue: when kspec search commands run inside the batch temp dir, they scan blob files, producing large output stored as new blobs, which grow exponentially in subsequent searches.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Approach decided: replace full fs.cp temp dir with in-memory write buffer overlay. Spec created at @batch-write-buffer. Implementation target: src/cli/batch-exec.ts executeAtomic() — replace lines 643-644 (fs.cp) and lines 690-703 (clear+copy-back) with overlay read/write/commit/rollback.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Spec updated after dual review (codex + subagent): ac-5 now concretely states sessions/ must never be copied, ac-6 clarified to process-local buffer visibility (testable without concurrency infra), new ac-7 added for flush failure atomicity — must not leave partial writes on disk.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
WIP checkpoint: WriteBuffer class and tests complete, batch-exec.ts wiring not yet done.

Done:
- src/cli/batch-write-buffer.ts: WriteBuffer class with write/read/delete/has/flush/discard, staging-file atomicity for ac-7, module singleton (activate/deactivate/get)
- tests/batch-write-buffer.test.ts: unit tests for all ACs including integration tests verifying no sessions/ copy and atomic rollback

Remaining (next session):
- Wire WriteBuffer into src/cli/batch-exec.ts executeAtomic():
  1. Remove fs.cp(realSpecDir, tempDir) at ~line 643
  2. Call activateBatchBuffer(realSpecDir) instead
  3. Replace the fs.writeFile path inside the command runner to call buffer.write() (or intercept via an env var / patched writeFile in the subprocess)
  4. Replace clear+copy-back block (~lines 690-703) with buffer.flush() on success, buffer.discard() on failure
  5. Call deactivateBatchBuffer() in finally

Note: The subprocess model means each command runs in a separate spawnSync call. The buffer singleton won't span across spawned processes. Need to re-evaluate approach — either (a) make batch commands run in-process instead of spawned subprocesses, or (b) use a temp file protocol for buffered writes between parent and child. See batch-exec.ts for the exact spawn model before deciding.

tasks.title: Implement: Web UI assets bundled in npm package
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #642. Added build:web-ui pipeline step, resolveWebUiPath bundled fallback via import.meta.url, 5 unit tests covering all ACs, and upgraded CI to Node 22.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

The kspec npm package bundles the pre-built web UI static assets so the daemon can serve the web UI when installed in any project, without requiring a local web UI build. The build pipeline copies packages/web-ui/build to dist/web-ui/, and resolveWebUiPath falls back to that location relative to the daemon module.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given npm run build is executed, when build completes, then packages/web-ui/build output is copied to dist/web-ui/ in the package
- ac-2: Given kspec is installed in a project with no local web UI build, when daemon starts and resolves web UI path, then resolveWebUiPath returns the bundled dist/web-ui/ path relative to the daemon module location
- ac-3: Given kspec is installed as an npm package in a non-monorepo project, when browser opens http://localhost:3456/, then daemon serves the bundled web UI and returns HTTP 200 with HTML content
- ac-4: Given an explicit webUiDir option or WEB_UI_DIR env var or local packages/web-ui/build is present, when daemon starts, then the explicit or local path takes precedence over the bundled dist/web-ui/ fallback

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation hints:

Build pipeline (package.json): Add a build:web-ui step that runs 'cd packages/web-ui && npm run build && shx cp -r build ../dist/web-ui' (or equivalent). Wire it into the main build script so dist/web-ui/ is always populated after npm run build.

resolveWebUiPath fallback (packages/daemon/src/server.ts): Add a 5th lookup after the existing 4. Use import.meta.url to find the daemon module's own location, then resolve relative to it:
  const selfDir = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
  const bundledPath = join(selfDir, '..', '..', 'web-ui');  // dist/daemon/ -> dist/ -> web-ui/
  if (existsSync(bundledPath)) return bundledPath;

This works whether kspec is run from dist/ (installed package) or during development.

Also update package.json 'files' array if dist/web-ui/ isn't already covered by the 'dist' glob — it should be, but worth confirming.

tasks.title: Shadow branch auto-push silently swallows failures — fire-and-forget push (shadow.ts:1159-1164) uses
tasks.description: Shadow branch auto-push silently swallows failures — fire-and-forget push (shadow.ts:1159-1164) uses spawn with stdio:ignore and detached:true, making divergence errors completely invisible. In a 4-hour ralph container session, 50+ commits accumulated locally with no indication pushes were failing. The push fails because host and container both commit to kspec-meta concurrently, causing divergence on the first push attempt, and every subsequent auto-push also fails silently. Fix should: (1) capture push exit code even in fire-and-forget mode (spawn with stdio:pipe, read stderr, unref after), (2) on push failure, log warning to stderr so it appears in agent output and JSON mode, (3) consider returning a result from autoCommit/shadowPush indicating push status so callers can surface it (e.g. kspec batch could include push_failed:true in response), (4) on repeated failures, escalate visibility — e.g. after 3 consecutive push failures, emit a prominent warning. The local commit always succeeds regardless — this is about VISIBILITY of sync failures, not blocking commits. Related: the merge driver handles YAML conflicts well (56/57 commits rebased cleanly), so the recovery path works — the problem is purely that nobody knows recovery is needed.

tasks.title: Stream agent text output to stdout in kspec agent run
tasks.description:
kspec agent run currently calls runInvocation() without an onUpdate callback, so the agent's text response is never printed to the terminal. The user sees nothing until completion, when only the session ID and outcome are shown.

Fix: In src/cli/commands/agent.ts (around line 363), pass an onUpdate handler to runInvocation that prints text content blocks to stdout as they arrive. In --json mode, suppress streaming. At the end, still output the session summary.

Implementation details:
- runInvocation accepts onUpdate?: (update: SessionUpdate) => void
- SessionUpdate events with content arrays contain text blocks (type: 'text')
- In interactive mode: process.stdout.write(block.text) for each text block
- In --json mode: skip the onUpdate handler entirely
- SessionUpdate type is imported from src/acp/index.ts

Relevant files:
- src/cli/commands/agent.ts — add onUpdate to runInvocation call (line ~363)
- src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts — runInvocation signature with onUpdate
- src/acp/index.ts — SessionUpdate type definition

tasks.title: Add --text flag to kspec session log show to replay agent output
tasks.description:
kspec session log show has no way to read the actual text response from a completed agent invocation. The session.update events contain content blocks with the agent's text, but --events only shows event metadata, not content.

Fix: Add a --text flag to session log show that extracts and prints the assistant text from session.update events in chronological order.

Implementation details:
- Events are stored in .kspec/sessions/<session-id>/events.jsonl
- Filter for type === 'session.update'
- From each event's data.content array, collect blocks with type === 'text'
- Print the text in order to stdout (no extra formatting — just the content)
- --text and --events are independent flags (both can be used together or separately)
- Externalized blobs: if content is a blob pointer, resolve it (same logic as --resolve-blobs)

Relevant files:
- src/cli/commands/session/log.ts — session log show command
- src/session/ — session event reading utilities

Workaround (until fixed):
  cat .kspec/sessions/<id>/events.jsonl | python3 -c "
  import sys, json
  for line in sys.stdin:
    e = json.loads(line)
    if e.get('type') == 'session.update':
      for block in (e.get('data',{}).get('content') or []):
        if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get('type') == 'text':
          print(block.get('text',''), end='')
  "

Test: Integration test that creates a session with known text output and verifies --text prints it.

Spec ACs to cover: @session-log-show ac-11 (--text flag replays assistant text)

tasks.title: Rewrite {skill:foo} references to adapter-specific format when injecting skills into agent prompt
tasks.description:
When buildPromptWithSkills injects skill content into the agent prompt, cross-skill references like {skill:writing-specs} or {skill:plan} are passed through as-is. These are meaningless to the agent unless it knows the format.

Adapters have different invocation formats:
- claude-agent-acp  -> /skill-name  (Claude Code slash commands, e.g. /kspec:task-work)
- codex-acp         -> $skill-name  (Codex CLI format)
- unknown/fallback  -> leave {skill:foo} as-is

Fix: In src/agent-runtime/prompts.ts, after resolving skill content, apply a substitution pass over the concatenated prompt replacing {skill:foo} with the adapter-appropriate format. The adapter ID is available via agent.adapter (resolved via resolveAdapter in src/agents/adapters.ts).

Note: Claude Code uses kspec: namespace prefix for kspec skills (e.g. /kspec:task-work not /task-work). Check .agents/skills/ directory naming convention and the skill manifest to understand the correct prefix.

Relevant files:
- src/agent-runtime/prompts.ts  — resolveSkills, buildPromptWithSkills
- src/agents/adapters.ts        — adapter resolution, adapter IDs
- src/schema/meta.ts            — AgentSchema.adapter field, platform_config
- .agents/skills/               — rendered skill names (kspec-task-work -> /kspec:task-work)

tasks.title: Handle ACP permission requests in invocation — auto-approve tool calls in dispatch mode
tasks.description:
Root cause of agent hanging on Edit/Write/Bash calls: invocation.ts only registers a client.on('update') handler but never registers a client.on('request') handler. When claude-agent-acp sends a request_permission (or similar JSON-RPC request) asking the client to approve a tool call, the kspec ACP client has no handler — the request sits unanswered, the agent waits forever, and after 5 minutes the session/prompt times out.

The --dangerously-skip-permissions flag is irrelevant here — that is a Claude Code CLI flag. This adapter (claude-agent-acp) uses the Claude Agent SDK which has its own ACP-level permission protocol.

Fix: In src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts, register a 'request' handler on the ACP client alongside the existing 'update' handler. Auto-approve all permission requests in dispatch mode (auto_approve=true). In non-auto-approve mode, either deny or surface the request to the caller via onUpdate.

The ACPClient already has respondPermission(), respondReadTextFile(), respondWriteFile() methods — they just need to be wired up.

Relevant files:
- src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts — add client.on('request', handler) around line 309
- src/acp/client.ts — respondPermission(), respond(), request event emission (line 99-100)
- src/acp/types.ts — RequestPermissionRequest, RequestPermissionResponse types

Verify fix: kspec agent run worker --task @some-eligible-task should now complete Edit operations without hanging.

Spec AC: @agent-invocation-lifecycle ac-11

tasks.title: Fix out-of-order agent_message_chunk streaming and duplicate session event seqs
tasks.description:
`kspec agent run` output is occasionally garbled (e.g. `**Also/ 38 ... for`) even though the canonical assistant message in `~/.claude/projects/<session>.jsonl` is well-formed. 1) streamed stdout preserves chunk order for a prompt under injected append delays
2) `events.jsonl` seq values are strictly monotonic and unique

4) no behavior regression for `--json` mode

tasks.title: Fix batch write buffer bypass — loadSpecFile and other read paths skip buffer
tasks.description:
The batch write buffer (ac-2) requires read-after-write consistency: if command A writes a file and command B reads it in the same atomic batch, B must see A's write. This contract is violated because multiple read paths use raw fs.readFile/fs.readdir instead of buffer-aware helpers.

## Observed symptom

Batch with multiple item ac add commands targeting the same spec item: only the last AC survives. Each command loads the item via loadSpecFile (raw fs.readFile), sees the pre-batch state with no ACs, builds its single AC, then writes to the buffer — overwriting the previous command's buffered write.

## Root cause

readYamlFile() checks getActiveBatchBuffer() before fs.readFile (yaml.ts:138-150). But loadSpecFile() at yaml.ts:1279 uses fs.readFile directly, bypassing the buffer entirely. Several other read paths have the same issue.

## Fix approach

Extract a shared buffer-aware file read helper and wire it into all .kspec/ read paths. Two categories:

### HIGH priority (cause data loss in common batch operations):

1. yaml.ts:1279 — loadSpecFile() uses raw fs.readFile
   - Called by loadAllItems() which is used by nearly every command
   - This is the confirmed cause of the AC overwrite bug

2. yaml.ts:200 — findTaskFiles() uses raw fs.readdir
   - Called by loadAllTasks(); batch task mutations could miss new task files

3. yaml.ts:461 — findManifest() uses raw fs.readdir
   - Manifest discovery; unlikely to change during batch but still a bypass

4. yaml.ts:1117 — expandGlobRecursive() uses raw fs.readdir
   - Glob expansion for manifest includes; could miss buffered files

5. meta.ts:128 — findMetaManifest() uses raw fs.readdir
   - Meta manifest discovery during batch

### MEDIUM priority (affect less common batch paths):

6. meta.ts:601,668,716,722 — skill loading (loadSkillContent, loadSkillDocs, loadSkillSupportingFiles)
7. shadow.ts:318 — detectRunningFromShadowWorktree uses fs.readdir
8. skill-render.ts:341,354,390 — copyDirectory and readRenderHash
9. validate.ts:1417 — checkOrphanedSkillDirs
10. setup-seeding.ts:320 — getModuleNames
11. prompts.ts:63,118 — loadKspecSkillIds, resolveSkills

### LOW priority (read git metadata, not spec data):
12. shadow.ts:246,287 — isWorktree, detectRunningFromShadowWorktree (.git file reads)

## Implementation guidance

- Create a readFileBufferAware(filePath) helper next to readYamlFile that checks the buffer for raw string reads (not parsed YAML)
- For fs.readdir bypasses, the buffer doesn't currently support directory listing. Options: (a) add a listDir method to WriteBuffer that overlays buffered paths onto real readdir results, or (b) accept the limitation and document that batch commands cannot create new files that need to be discovered by readdir in subsequent commands (this is less common than read-after-write on existing files)
- Focus on HIGH priority items first — loadSpecFile is the confirmed bug
- Search exhaustively: grep for all fs.readFile and fs.readdir in src/parser/ and src/cli/ to ensure nothing is missed beyond this list
- Add tests: batch with two item ac add commands to same item should preserve both ACs

Added regression coverage including repeated item ac add preservation and rollback safety for skill supporting files. AC coverage for @batch-write-buffer verified in targeted and full test runs.

tasks.title: Fix dispatch engine re-triggering workers on completed tasks
tasks.description: The dispatch engine repeatedly spawns stale worker invocations for tasks that have already been completed. Root cause: (1) no staleness check at dequeue time - queue entries created from intermediate state transitions are never validated against the task's current state before spawning, (2) CLI postDispatchEvent self-triggers back into the same dispatch engine that spawned the current invocation, creating redundant queue entries for every state transition an agent makes during its work. Over 3 fix cycles this produced 4+ wasteful invocations that each spawn a full agent process only to discover the task is already completed.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #681. Two-pronged fix: staleness check at dequeue time discards stale queue entries, and KSPEC_SESSION_ID guard suppresses self-triggering from dispatched agents. All review issues resolved.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Implemented two-pronged fix: (1) staleness check in _drainQueues loads current task states before spawning and discards entries where the task has moved to a different state than what triggered the enqueue, (2) postDispatchEvent now returns early when KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set to prevent self-triggering from dispatched agent invocations. Added AC-17 and AC-18 to @agent-dispatch-engine spec. Tests pass.

tasks.title: Prevent dispatch agents from killing host daemon
tasks.description:
Dispatch worker agents can accidentally kill the daemon hosting the dispatch engine by running kspec serve stop/restart. This happened in practice during fix cycle 4 of @implement-task-board-kanban — the agent tried to debug E2E failures by manually starting a daemon, which killed the dispatch daemon and severed the WebSocket connection.

tasks.title: Implement dispatch reconciliation loop
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #685. Implemented periodic reconciliation loop (AC-19, AC-20) with shared _evaluateAllTasks helper, .unref() on timer, and 8 new tests.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Context: Dispatch engine is event-driven (CLI posts + file watcher). Events can be silently lost (1s timeout on fire-and-forget HTTP post, daemon busy with shadow mutex, file watcher miss). When events are lost, tasks stall indefinitely — no periodic re-scan exists. Fix: Add a configurable reconciliation interval (default 60s) that re-runs bootstrap logic, enqueuing tasks that match dispatch rules but have no active/queued invocation. Add reconcileIntervalMs to DispatchEngineOptions (0 = disabled). Wire up via setInterval in start(), clearInterval in stop(). Covers AC ac-19 and ac-20 on @agent-dispatch-engine.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Implemented AC-19 and AC-20: periodic reconciliation loop in DispatchEngine. Added reconcileIntervalMs option (default 60s, 0/null disables). Reconciliation re-evaluates all task states against dispatch rules, skipping tasks with active or queued invocations. Timer starts in start(), cleared in stop(). 8 new tests covering: re-enqueue after missed events, dedup against queued, skip non-dispatchable states, interval config, disable with 0/null, timer cleanup on stop. All 55 dispatch tests pass. Also set timeout_minutes: 120 on ui-worker, 60 on ux-reviewer.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: daemon route handler at packages/daemon/src/routes/validation.ts:221 accessed result.traitCycles, but the validate() function (src/parser/validate.ts) returns traitCycleErrors. The undefined property was serialized as a missing field in JSON, causing the client to crash when accessing .length on undefined.

Fix: Changed result.traitCycles to result.traitCycleErrors in the daemon route. Also added defensive normalization in fetchValidation() (packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts) to default all array fields to empty arrays via nullish coalescing, preventing similar crashes from missing API fields.

notes.content:

tasks.description: The filter dropdown selectors on the /triage page are non-functional — selecting a value has no effect. Likely causes: (1) Svelte 5 event binding issue (onchange vs on:change), (2) reactive state not updating when select value changes, (3) select elements may be missing bind:value or change handlers. notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fixed dropdown filters on triage and inbox pages. Root cause: filter state used $state + $effect sync from URL params, combined with bind:value (two-way binding) on select elements. This created a race condition where bind:value would set state immediately, but the $effect reading stale URL params could reset it back before goto() completed. Fix: changed filter state to $derived from URL search params (single source of truth) and replaced bind:value with one-way value attribute on selects. This matches the working TaskFilters.svelte pattern. Also fixed the same issue on the inbox page which used identical broken pattern.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause identified: inbox page imported `page` from `$app/stores` (Svelte 4 store API) instead of `$app/state` (Svelte 5 runes API). When using $app/stores with $derived, the store subscription doesn't properly track fine-grained changes to nested properties like url.searchParams, causing filter state derivations to not react to URL changes from goto().

Fix: Changed import from '$app/stores' to '$app/state' and removed $ prefix from page references (page is now a reactive object, not a store).

Note: The triage page (routes/triage/+page.svelte) has the same issue — still uses $app/stores. Captured separately.

tasks.title: Dispatch engine should poll for eligible pending tasks on start and periodically
tasks.description: The dispatch engine is event-driven: it only picks up tasks when a trigger event fires (task.ready, task.in_progress, etc.). Tasks created before dispatch starts, or created without an explicit state transition event, are never picked up. Fix: (1) On dispatch start, sweep all pending+eligible tasks and emit synthetic task.ready events for them, (2) Add a periodic poll (e.g. every 60s) to catch any tasks that fell through without events, (3) Ensure task add with automation=eligible also emits a dispatchable event when dispatch is running.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:

Fix: Changed to $state(false) so all tool calls start collapsed regardless of status. User-toggled expand state is naturally preserved across periodic refreshes because Svelte's keyed {#each} (keyed by block.seq) reuses component instances and their internal state when the same key appears in a re-rendered array.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fixed shadow branch health status bug. Root cause: the daemon's /api/meta/shadow endpoint was passing ctx.shadow.worktreeDir (full absolute path like /home/user/project/.kspec) as the 'directory' option to getShadowStatus(), which expects just a directory name (like '.kspec'). getShadowStatus joins projectRoot + directory, so the full path produced an invalid path like /home/user/project//home/user/project/.kspec, causing all three health checks (branchExists, worktreeExists, worktreeLinked) to fail. Fix: use ctx.config.shadow.directory (the directory name from project config) instead. Added regression test verifying that passing a full path as directory produces unhealthy status.

tasks.title: Support git < 2.42 in kspec init (--orphan worktree fallback)
tasks.description: kspec init fails on git < 2.42 because 'git worktree add --orphan' was introduced in git 2.42. Debian 12 (bookworm) ships git 2.39, Ubuntu 22.04 ships 2.34. Need a fallback that creates the orphan branch and worktree using older git commands (create orphan branch manually, then add worktree).
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #703. Added git < 2.42 orphan-worktree fallback in shadow initialization using a temp-repo flow that never touches the project working tree, with AC coverage for @config-shadow ac-10 in tests/shadow.test.ts and CI green on the merged head.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: IMPORTANT: The fallback must NEVER modify the project working tree. The approach is: (1) create a temp dir in /tmp, (2) init a bare/empty repo there to create the orphan branch, (3) push that branch back to the project repo, (4) use standard 'git worktree add' (no --orphan) to attach. Do NOT use 'git checkout --orphan' in the project dir — that would blow away the user's working tree.

notes.author: Jacob Chapel

tasks.title: Add dispatch filter UI and default automation eligibility
tasks.description:
The dispatch engine feeds non-eligible tasks (manual_only, needs_review) to agents because:

1. The AgentEditForm UI has no filter editing — dispatch triggers show only the event type, with no way to view or configure filter criteria (automation, tags, priority).

2. addTrigger() creates rules as { on: event } with no filter, and the engine's _matchesFilter() returns true when filter is undefined.

3. Default agent definitions (from kspec setup) lack filter: { automation: eligible } on their rules.

Fix requires three changes:

A) UI: Add filter editing per dispatch trigger row — automation dropdown (eligible/any), tag chips, priority threshold. Default automation to 'eligible' for task.ready and task.needs_work triggers. Show existing filters as badges.

B) Engine: Default to automation: eligible for task.ready and task.needs_work events when no filter is specified. This is a safety net so even unconfigured agents don't pick up ineligible tasks.

C) Setup: Update default agent definitions to include filter: { automation: eligible } on task-worker dispatch rules.

See new ACs on @ui-agent-dispatch (ac-5 through ac-9) and @agent-dispatch-engine (ac-21, ac-22).

tasks.title: Fix active fleet showing completed agents as still active
tasks.description: The dispatch engine shows completed invocations as still active. Root cause: in _spawnInvocation (dispatch.ts), the cleanup chain is shadowMutex.runExclusive(runInvocation).then(drainQueues).finally(cleanupActiveDetails). The .then() calls _drainQueues which spawns the NEXT invocation via shadowMutex.runExclusive — but .finally() only runs after .then() completes. This means the old invocation's activeInvocationDetails entry persists until the next invocation finishes. Evidence: agents page shows reviewer as '1 active' with 15m elapsed, but sessions page shows that reviewer session completed 12m ago — the cleanup is blocked behind the currently running worker invocation (which holds the shadowMutex). Fix: move activeInvocationDetails.delete and activeCount decrement into the .runExclusive callback (after emitting the event), BEFORE the drain step. The .then should only handle draining, and .finally should only handle abort controller cleanup.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #710. Fixed dispatch active fleet cleanup ordering by moving activeCount decrement and activeInvocationDetails deletion into the shadowMutex runExclusive callback before queue drain, so completed or terminally failed invocations no longer appear active while the next invocation runs. Added regression coverage for success and retry-exhausted failure paths in tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts. Task has no spec_ref, so AC coverage was not applicable; targeted local regression tests passed and PR CI was green on the merged HEAD.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fix applied and PR created (#710). Root cause: in _spawnInvocation, the cleanup chain was .runExclusive(runInvocation).then(decrementActiveCount + drainQueues).finally(deleteActiveDetails). The .then() called _drainQueues which acquired shadowMutex for the next invocation, blocking .finally() until that next invocation completed. Fix: moved activeCount decrement and activeInvocationDetails.delete into the runExclusive callback so they run while the mutex is still held, before drain can spawn the next invocation.

tasks.title: Implement bidirectional shadow branch sync
tasks.description: Shadow branch sync is push-only: after each commit, shadowPushAsync fires a detached git push. But there is no pull — other clones sharing the same remote kspec-meta branch never receive updates until manual kspec shadow sync. This causes: (1) divergence between clones (tasks created in clone A are invisible to clone B), (2) frequent merge conflicts when both clones push, (3) manual intervention required to reconcile. Fix: (a) Change shadowPushAsync to pull-rebase before pushing (using the kspec merge driver for YAML conflict resolution), (b) Add periodic background pull in daemon mode (configurable interval, default 60s), (c) Ensure CLI commands also pull before read operations that depend on fresh state (e.g. task list, session start). The merge driver (kspec merge-driver) already handles YAML merges non-interactively.

AC coverage verified for @config-shadow ac-11 and ac-12 with targeted shadow tests; required CI checks passed on the merged head.

tasks.title: Replace legacy session fallback reads with detect-and-warn
tasks.description:
Remove transparent fallback reads from legacy .kspec/sessions/ and replace with a
detect-and-warn pattern. Currently legacy.ts has *WithFallback and *Merged wrappers
that silently read from the old location, but only session/log.ts uses them — daemon
routes, stale-close, compact, and checkpoint already read only from .kspec-sessions/.

## Intent

One consumer (dispatch engine) — transparent fallback adds complexity for marginal
benefit. Better to warn everywhere and let the user run `kspec session migrate`.

## Scope

### Remove fallback read functions from legacy.ts
- Delete: getSessionWithFallback, readEventsWithFallback, listSessionsMerged,
  getAllSessionLogSummariesMerged, resolveSessionIdWithFallback,
  searchSessionEventsWithFallback, computeToolUsageStatsWithFallback
- Keep: hasLegacySessions, getLegacySessionsDir, migrateLegacySessions,
  emitLegacyDeprecationWarning (repurpose for detect-and-warn)

### Update session/log.ts
- Replace imports from legacy.ts with direct store.ts calls
- Add legacy detection warning when hasLegacySessions() is true
- Lines: 27-32 (imports), 215, 533, 551, 775, 808, 921 (call sites)

### Add detect-and-warn to daemon session routes
- packages/daemon/src/routes/sessions.ts — check hasLegacySessions on list endpoint,

The order matters — if you only change the URL, the $effect watching the URL won't fire because the component state still holds the ref. Look at how the open effect works: it watches searchParams, sets state, fetches task. The close effect must be the inverse: watch for modalOpen becoming false, clear selectedTaskRef, clear URL. The specs page pattern works there because its state model is simpler (detailOpen + selectedRef). The task views have more state to clear.

tasks.description: replaceState and pushState (both from $app/navigation and window.history) do not update $page.url. Verified spec alignment and fresh regression coverage with npm test passing (4294 passed, 3 skipped).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: replaceState/pushState do NOT update $page.url (SvelteKit issue #10661, intentional). Only goto() goes through the router and updates the page store. The codebase already uses goto() correctly in triage, inbox, and TaskFilters — but 3 files use the broken pattern.

Files to fix:
1. packages/web-ui/src/routes/specs/+page.svelte
   - Line 43: window.history.pushState (set ?ref= on select) → goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true })
   - Line 53: window.history.pushState (remove ?ref= on close) → goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true })
   - Remove import of nothing from $app/navigation if replaceState was imported

2. packages/web-ui/src/routes/tasks/+page.svelte
   - Line 124: replaceState(url, {}) → goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true })
   - Change import from { replaceState } to { goto } from $app/navigation

3. packages/web-ui/src/routes/tasks/board/+page.svelte
   - Line 103: replaceState(url, {}) → goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true })
   - Change import from { replaceState } to { goto } from $app/navigation

Also in the close effects: since goto() properly updates $page.url, the open effect will see urlRef=null after close and won't reopen. The lastProcessedRef guard can be simplified or removed since the root cause is fixed.

Key goto options:
- replaceState: true — don't pollute browser history
- keepFocus: true — don't steal focus from current element
- noScroll: true — don't scroll to top

Reference: triage page line 206 already uses this exact pattern correctly.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Additional scope: Add a development convention or documentation reinforcing that all URL mutations in the web UI must use goto() from $app/navigation — never replaceState, pushState, or window.history methods. This prevents future regressions. Options: (1) Add a rule to the development or web-ui conventions via kspec meta, (2) Add a comment block at the top of a shared helper, (3) Both. The convention should explain WHY (replaceState/pushState don't update $page.url, causing stale reactive state) and reference the SvelteKit issue #10661.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes:

This is primarily a component swap task. For each surface:
1. Import renderMarkdown or the StreamingMarkdown component
2. Replace plain text / whitespace-pre-wrap rendering with
   {@html renderMarkdown(content)} wrapped in prose classes
3. Ensure prose styling works in each component's layout context

Priority order (most impactful first):
- Task notes (heavily used, often contain code blocks)
- Task descriptions
- Spec descriptions
- Observations
- Workflow descriptions
- Inbox items

ThinkingBlock and ToolCallView are intentionally excluded — they
render agent internals where monospace/pre is the correct format.

tasks.title: kspec shadow repair removes the .kspec worktree before verifying it can recreate it. If git is not o
tasks.description:
Shadow repair safety: repairShadow() in src/parser/shadow.ts calls fs.rm(worktreeDir) at line 2729 BEFORE attempting git worktree add at line 2739. If worktree recreation fails (git unavailable, disk error, permissions), the .kspec directory is gone with no recovery path for the user.

The kspec-meta branch data survives in .git/ and can be recovered with git worktree add .kspec kspec-meta, but users would not know this.

Design decision needed: (1) Verify git availability and worktree add feasibility BEFORE any fs.rm, (2) consider in-place repair (re-link broken worktree without deletion), (3) add a backup/restore mechanism, (4) at minimum print recovery instructions if recreation fails. tasks.description:
Fix task budget false-positive when stale KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set outside a ralph loop.

Location: checkBudget() in src/sessions/store.ts (lines ~3495-3524).

Current behavior: checkBudget() validates (1) sessionId is set, (2) budget file exists, (3) started_this_cycle >= max_per_cycle. It does NOT check whether the session is actually active. A stale KSPEC_SESSION_ID from a completed/abandoned session causes false budget exhaustion errors.

tasks.title: Implement: ANSI Terminal Output Rendering
tasks.description:
Implement ANSI terminal color rendering in the web UI session stream.

Spec: @ansi-terminal-rendering (8 ACs)

Integration point: packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/session/ToolCallView.svelte (line ~112, the <pre> tag rendering outputText).

Approach:
1. Add ansi-to-html (or similar) package to packages/web-ui/
2. Create a shared utility (e.g. lib/utils/ansi.ts) that converts ANSI SGR sequences to styled HTML spans
3. In ToolCallView.svelte, pipe outputText through the ANSI parser before rendering with {@html}
4. Support standard 16 colors, 256-color (38;5;N), and 24-bit true color (38;2;R;G;B)
5. Define ANSI color palette as CSS custom properties using oklch, integrated with existing token system in tokens.css
6. Handle graceful degradation: if ESC chars (0x1B) were stripped, detect orphaned CSI parameters like [32m and strip them for clean plain text
7. HTML-escape all non-ANSI content before insertion (XSS safety) — DOMPurify already in codebase
8. Strip non-SGR codes (cursor movement, clear screen) rather than rendering them
9. Pipeline: ANSI parsing applies only to tool/bash output in <pre> blocks — never touches markdown-rendered agent text

Data flow: events.jsonl → daemon API → session-utils.ts parseEventsToBlocks() → ToolCallView.svelte
ANSI codes survive JSON serialization as UTF-8.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #760 (merge commit 0e4a16a7b755b31949e09fab8e55efcb1a0ff2cb). Implemented ANSI terminal output rendering in the web UI session stream with SGR parsing, theme-aware ANSI color tokens, orphaned/private-mode CSI stripping, XSS-safe HTML conversion, and preview truncation safety in ToolCallView. Reviewed AC coverage for ac-1 through ac-8 in packages/web-ui/tests/ansi.test.ts with no inherited trait ACs applicable; GitHub test shards and smoke E2E were green on the merged head.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

Parse and render ANSI SGR (Select Graphic Rendition) escape sequences in terminal/bash tool output displayed in the session stream. Convert ANSI color codes to styled HTML spans so terminal output appears with the same colors and formatting as a real terminal. Currently ToolCallView.svelte renders output in a plain <pre> tag — ANSI codes show as garbled raw text.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given tool output contains ANSI SGR escape sequences (e.g. \x1b[32mPASS\x1b[0m), when the output is displayed in ToolCallView, then the text renders with corresponding CSS colors instead of showing raw escape codes
- ac-2: Given tool output uses standard ANSI colors (30-37 foreground, 40-47 background, 90-97 bright, 100-107 bright background), when rendered in the web UI, then colors map to a terminal-like palette that works in both light and dark themes
- ac-3: Given tool output contains formatting codes (bold=1, dim=2, italic=3, underline=4, strikethrough=9), when rendered in the web UI, then corresponding CSS styles are applied (font-weight, opacity, font-style, text-decoration)
- ac-4: Given tool output contains reset codes (\x1b[0m for full reset, or specific resets like \x1b[22m), when rendered, then styling resets correctly without leaking to subsequent text
- ac-5: Given tool output contains ANSI parameter sequences but the ESC character was stripped or lost during storage, when rendered, then the raw bracket sequences are stripped rather than displayed as garbled text — fallback to clean plain text
- ac-6: Given tool output may contain user-controlled content alongside ANSI codes, when ANSI codes are converted to HTML, then all non-ANSI content is HTML-escaped before insertion to prevent XSS
- ac-7: Given tool output is 10000+ characters with many ANSI sequences, when rendered, then parsing and rendering completes without visible delay

- ansi.ts: Parses SGR codes → styled HTML spans with HTML escaping for XSS safety

- ToolCallView.svelte: Uses containsAnsi() to conditionally render via {@html ansiToHtml()} for tool output

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Guide

### Covers ACs: ac-resolve-roots, ac-no-worktree-unchanged, ac-submodule-safe, ac-performance

### 1. Add resolveProjectRoots() to src/parser/shadow.ts

New function alongside existing getGitRoot(). Returns ProjectRoots interface:
{ mainRoot: string, worktreeRoot: string, isWorktree: boolean } | null

Algorithm:
- Single git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir call (two-line output)
- Parse toplevel (line 1) and commonDir (line 2)
- Resolve commonDir against toplevel if relative
- Submodule guard: use path segment analysis (split on path.sep, check for .git followed by modules segments), NOT raw string .includes(). Return isWorktree=false for submodules.
- If resolvedCommonDir === path.join(toplevel, '.git'), return isWorktree=false (main repo)
- Otherwise return { mainRoot: path.dirname(resolvedCommonDir), worktreeRoot: toplevel, isWorktree: true }
- Return null if git commands fail

Keep getGitRoot() as-is for interactive commands (init, setup, doctor).

### 2. Add projectRoot to KspecContext in src/parser/yaml.ts

interface KspecContext {
  rootDir: string;         // code checkout root (worktree root when in worktree)
  projectRoot: string;     // main repo root (where .kspec lives, daemon identity)
  specDir: string;         // unchanged
  sessionsDir: string;     // unchanged - at projectRoot
  // ... rest unchanged
}

### 3. Update initContext() in src/parser/yaml.ts

Current flow makes 2+ git spawns. New flow makes 1:
- Call resolveProjectRoots(cwd) once at the top
- Pass roots.mainRoot to loadProjectConfig(cwd, roots.mainRoot)
- detectRunningFromShadowWorktree unchanged (reads .git file, no spawn)
- Pass roots.mainRoot to detectShadow(cwd, options, roots.mainRoot)
- Return: rootDir = roots.worktreeRoot, projectRoot = roots.mainRoot
- sessionsDir = path.join(roots.mainRoot, ".kspec-sessions")
- Handle null roots (not a git repo) same as current getGitRoot null handling

### 4. Add mainRoot? param to src/parser/config.ts

findProjectRoot(startDir, mainRoot?) and loadProjectConfig(startDir, mainRoot?)
When mainRoot provided, skip getGitRoot call. KSPEC_BATCH_PROJECT_ROOT still takes priority.

### 5. Add mainRoot? param to detectShadow() in src/parser/shadow.ts

detectShadow(startDir, options?, mainRoot?) — use mainRoot instead of getGitRoot when provided.

### Tests

File: tests/parser/resolve-project-roots.test.ts

Setup pattern:
```
const mainDir = await createTempDir();
await initGitRepo(mainDir);
execSync('git commit --allow-empty -m "init"', { cwd: mainDir });
const wtDir = path.join(await createTempDir(), 'wt');
execSync(`git worktree add ${wtDir} -b test-branch`, { cwd: mainDir });
```

Cases:
1. Main repo: mainRoot === worktreeRoot, isWorktree === false
2. Linked worktree: mainRoot = original, worktreeRoot = wt, isWorktree === true
3. Worktree outside parent dir: still resolves
4. Not a git repo: returns null
5. Submodule: isWorktree === false
6. Detached worktree (--detach): same as linked

File: tests/worktree-context.test.ts
Integration tests for initContext from worktree. Need to set up a full kspec shadow branch in the main repo, then verify initContext from the worktree finds .kspec, returns correct rootDir/projectRoot/specDir/sessionsDir.

notes.content:
## Implementation Guide

### Covers ACs: ac-shadow-commands, ac-serve-default, ac-false-positive-guard

### 1. Shadow CLI commands in src/cli/commands/shadow.ts

5 call sites use getGitRoot(process.cwd()). Replace each with resolveProjectRoots:
- Line ~143 (shadow status)
- Line ~207 (shadow repair)
- Line ~297 (shadow log)
- Line ~346 (shadow resolve)
- Line ~459 (shadow sync)

Change pattern:
```
// Before:
const gitRoot = getGitRoot(process.cwd());
// After:
const roots = resolveProjectRoots(process.cwd());
const gitRoot = roots?.mainRoot ?? null;
```

Import resolveProjectRoots from ../../parser/shadow.js alongside existing getGitRoot import.

### 2. Serve commands in src/cli/commands/serve.ts

ALL subcommands default --kspec-dir to process.cwd()/.kspec via Commander option defaults.
Affected lines: ~134 (start), ~153 (stop), ~172 (status), ~191 (restart).
The restart subcommand at ~590 passes opts.kspecDir back into startServer.

Fix: resolve --kspec-dir default via worktree-aware path for all subcommands.
Simplest approach: resolve once in a shared helper or preAction:
```
async function resolveKspecDir(explicitDir?: string): Promise<string> {
  if (explicitDir) return explicitDir;
  const ctx = await initContext();
  return ctx.specDir;
}
```
Or use resolveProjectRoots() directly to find mainRoot and append .kspec.

### 3. detectRunningFromShadowWorktree false positive fix in src/parser/shadow.ts

Current code at ~line 467-471 has worktreeName.includes("kspec") which short-circuits
before the structural check (manifest+modules) at ~lines 477-491.

Fix: reorder checks so name heuristic is a signal, not definitive. Require the
structural check to confirm before returning positive. Only return mainProjectRoot
if BOTH the name/config match AND the structural check pass.

Decision order:
1. Check if worktree name matches configured shadow directory name exactly → strong signal
2. Check if worktree name is the default (.kspec) → strong signal
3. If neither matches but name contains "kspec" → weak signal, MUST confirm with structure check
4. Structure check: directory contains kspec manifest files + modules/ or .tasks.*
5. Return positive only if signal + structure both pass

### Tests

- kspec shadow status from a linked worktree: succeeds and shows main repo shadow health
- kspec serve start from worktree without --kspec-dir: defaults to main repo .kspec/
- kspec serve restart from worktree: uses resolved path through restart flow
- Code worktree named kspec-feature: NOT detected as shadow worktree
- .kspec/ worktree: still correctly detected as shadow worktree

notes.content: CLARIFICATION: For serve fix, use resolveProjectRoots() directly (not initContext) to avoid full context init overhead. Pattern: const roots = resolveProjectRoots(process.cwd()); const kspecDir = roots ? path.join(roots.mainRoot, '.kspec') : path.join(process.cwd(), '.kspec');

tasks.title: Prioritize pending_review over pending in dispatch scheduling
tasks.description: Without git worktree isolation, dispatch serializes agents into a single slot. Current STATUS_PRECEDENCE ranks pending (2) above pending_review (3), so the worker picks up new tasks before the reviewer handles submitted work. This creates a bottleneck: completed work sits in review while more work piles up. Fix: swap pending_review above pending in STATUS_PRECEDENCE (pending_review: 2, pending: 3). Once worktree-based agent isolation lands and agents run concurrently in separate working copies, this ordering becomes moot — but until then it ensures the review-then-work cycle completes faster.

tasks.title: Implement: Remote Branch Fallback in Workspace Health Reconciliation
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #833. Added tryRestoreBranchFromRemote() to reconcileWorkspaceHealth() — checks configured remotes (origin first) for missing canonical branches and restores them locally. Graceful degradation on failure with debug-level logging. All 4 ACs covered with dedicated tests. Full test suite passes (4772/4772). CI all green.

notes.author: Jacob Chapel
notes.content:
Implementation notes (auto-generated from spec):

reconcileWorkspaceHealth() in workspace.ts checks for the canonical branch using refExists() which only checks local refs (git show-ref --verify refs/heads/<branch>). When a canonical branch exists on a remote (e.g. origin) but not locally, the workspace is incorrectly marked unhealthy with missing_canonical_branch. The health check should attempt to fetch or verify the remote ref before declaring the branch missing. This enables dispatch to self-heal workspaces whose local branches were pruned or never fetched, without requiring manual intervention.


Acceptance Criteria:
- ac-1: Given A workspace record references a canonical branch that does not exist as a local ref, when reconcileWorkspaceHealth() runs and the branch exists on a configured remote (e.g. refs/remotes/origin/<branch>), then The health check fetches or creates the local branch from the remote ref and does not emit a missing_canonical_branch issue
- ac-2: Given A workspace record references a canonical branch that does not exist locally or on any remote, when reconcileWorkspaceHealth() runs, then The missing_canonical_branch issue is still emitted (existing behavior preserved)
- ac-3: Given The remote branch fetch fails (network error, permissions, etc.), when reconcileWorkspaceHealth() attempts the remote fallback, then The failure is logged at debug level and the missing_canonical_branch issue is emitted as if no remote existed (graceful degradation)
- ac-4: Given reconcileWorkspaceHealth() restores a branch from remote, when The workspace health state is computed, then The canonical_branch_head is updated to the resolved commit from the restored branch

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Implementation complete. Added tryRestoreBranchFromRemote() helper that checks configured remotes (origin first) for the canonical branch when it's missing locally. If found, creates the local branch from the remote ref. Graceful degradation on failure with debug-level logging. The existing canonical_branch_head resolution in reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry naturally picks up the restored branch's commit. All 4 ACs covered with dedicated tests in dispatch-workspace-remote-branch-fallback.test.ts. Full test suite passes (4772/4772).

tasks.title: Implement inline registry purge for closed dispatch workspace records
tasks.description:
The dispatch workspace registry (project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml) accumulates records indefinitely. Records transition through lifecycle states ending in 'closed' but are never removed from the file. Over time this causes unbounded growth.

Implement inline purge logic in saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord (src/parser/dispatch-workspaces.ts) that removes closed records whose closed_at timestamp exceeds a retention threshold (default 7 days). The purge runs inside the existing withFileLock scope so no new locking is needed. The shadow commit that follows registry writes already handles durability — purged records are simply fewer records in the same write.

Key implementation details:
- Add purge logic to saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord only (NOT mutateDispatchWorkspaceRecordAtomically — different semantics)
- Filter out records where lifecycle_state === 'closed' AND timestamps.closed_at is older than 7 days
- The first write after shipping will purge the backlog of old records automatically
- provisionDispatchWorkspace reads closed records (includeClosed: true) to reuse workspace identity (canonical branch, worktree paths) during re-provisioning. After purge, re-opened tasks beyond the retention window get fresh identities. This is acceptable since the worktree and branch are already reaped by cleanup
- reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry already filters to non-closed records (nonClosedRecords at ~line 1272) — no interaction
- validateSingleOpenWorkspacePerTask only checks non-closed records — no interaction

Files: src/parser/dispatch-workspaces.ts (purge logic in saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord), tests/ (new test file for purge behavior)

tasks.title: Investigate and fix npx ENOENT crash in dispatch agent spawn
tasks.description:
When the daemon is started via kspec serve start (which spawns bun as a child process), subsequent agent spawns using npx fail with ENOENT. This causes the daemon to crash because the spawn error is unhandled (no child.on('error') handler in spawner.ts). Investigation findings:
- npx resolves fine from the shell, from bun directly, and from kspec agent run
- The daemon started via direct bun invocation can spawn agents without issue
- Only the kspec serve start path fails (spawn('bun', ...) -> spawn('npx', ...))
- Concurrent spawns are not the issue (tested and ruled out)
- PATH is not being mutated by any code in the spawn chain
- Appears to be a Bun-specific issue with PATH resolution in nested spawn chains

Current mitigation committed: use bunx (Bun built-in) instead of npx when running under Bun runtime. This avoids the PATH resolution issue but the root cause in Bun's spawn behavior is not fully understood.

Additional issues identified:
- spawner.ts has no child.on('error') handler, so spawn failures crash the entire daemon process instead of being caught by the invocation try/catch
- Stale reviewer worktree records after crashes create a blocking cycle (addressed by the branch adoption plan tasks)

tasks.title: Implement per-task dispatch drain coalescing
tasks.description:
Add a per-task coalescing window to the dispatch engine that defers queue draining when multiple state change events arrive for the same task in rapid succession.

## Problem

When rapid sequential CLI commands transition a task through multiple states (e.g., unblock → start → submit within seconds), each transition fires an independent dispatch event. Because handleStateChange() immediately calls _drainQueues(), the engine can spawn agents for intermediate states before subsequent transitions arrive. This caused a task-worker to be spawned for the transient in_progress state AND a pr-reviewer for the final pending_review state, when only the reviewer was needed.

## Approach

Replace the immediate _drainQueues() call in handleStateChange() with a per-task coalescing timer:

1. Add a `coalesceTimers: Map<string, NodeJS.Timeout>` to DispatchEngine tracking pending per-task drain timers
2. Add `coalesceWindowMs` option to DispatchEngineOptions (default 5000ms, 0 to disable)
3. In handleStateChange(), after enqueuing, instead of calling _drainQueues() directly:
   - If a timer exists for this taskId, clear it
   - Schedule a new timer for coalesceWindowMs
   - When timer fires, call _drainQueues() (which already handles stale pruning via ac-17)
4. In stop(), clear all pending coalescing timers
5. In post-invocation re-evaluation, coalescing also applies

## Key files

- `src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts` — DispatchEngine class (handleStateChange, _drainQueues, stop, constructor)
- `tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts` — existing dispatch tests

## Testing considerations

- Tests that rely on immediate drain behavior will need coalesceWindowMs: 0 or explicit timer advancement
- New tests needed for: rapid transition coalescing, per-task independence, timer cleanup on stop, single-event delay behavior, post-invocation coalescing
- Use fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers) to avoid actual 5s waits in tests

All 8 ACs covered with tests using fake timers. Existing tests updated with coalesceWindowMs: 0 for backward compatibility.

notes.content: Spec gap analysis: No conflicts with existing dispatch engine ACs. ac-7 (dedup) operates on event identity, coalescing operates on drain timing — complementary layers. ac-17 (stale pruning) is the mechanism we rely on — the delayed drain ensures pruning sees the final state. ac-23/ac-24 (fresh state at drain) are compatible since delayed drains still load from disk. The coalescing window is purely additive between enqueue and drain.

(2) Added ac-7 (scoping) — explicitly states bootstrap, reconciliation, and post-invocation drains are NOT subject to coalescing. (3) Added ac-8 (drain re-entrance protection) — timer callbacks can fire concurrently, need mutex/flag to serialize drains. Also: existing tests should use coalesceWindowMs: 0 for minimal churn; new coalescing-specific tests use fake timers.

Key design decisions:
- Checks are grouped by logical name for gate evaluation; latest fresh run per name determines gate state
- Required flag uses 'any run required' semantics — if any run for a check name was marked required, the gate is required
- Stale checks (applies_to_version mismatch) cause failing state for required gates, not pending
- Skipped required checks are treated as satisfied (explicit skip is an acceptable outcome)
- Running checks leave gates in pending state
- Informational checks are always satisfied regardless of status
- Reuses isVersionStale from subject-bindings.ts for staleness detection

tasks.title: Fix agent spawn ENOENT by using absolute paths instead of PATH resolution
tasks.description:
The daemon crashes with ENOENT when spawning agents via bunx/npx because PATH resolution fails in detached/nested Bun spawn chains. This was first seen with npx, and a prior fix switched to bunx under Bun — but bunx (a symlink managed by mise) suffers the same PATH loss.

Root cause: When the daemon runs as a detached Bun process (kspec serve start -d), subsequent child_process.spawn calls with a custom env object can lose PATH resolution for commands like bunx/npx. This is likely a Bun quirk with mise-managed symlinks in detached spawn chains.

Fix (two parts):
1. Eliminate PATH dependency entirely — use process.execPath (absolute path to bun binary) with 'x' subcommand instead of bunx. Under Node, resolve npx to absolute path at module load time. This makes spawn immune to any PATH changes or resolution failures.
2. Add child.on('error') handler in spawner.ts — previously missing, so ENOENT crashed the daemon. Now spawn errors propagate cleanly through Promise.race against initialization.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #848. Used process.execPath + 'x' subcommand under Bun and absolute npx path under Node to eliminate PATH dependency for agent spawning. Added child.on('error') handler so spawn failures propagate cleanly instead of crashing the daemon.

tasks.title: Suppress no-op workspace registry writes during periodic reconciliation
tasks.description:
## Problem

The dispatch engine's periodic reconciliation (every 60s) unconditionally rewrites
project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml and commits to the shadow branch — even when nothing
has actually changed. This creates ~1 commit/minute of pure timestamp churn on the
kspec-meta branch.

## Root Cause

reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry() in src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts (around line 1462)
always calls saveWorkspaceRecordToRegistry() with updated_at: now and last_reconciled_at: now,
then calls commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() — regardless of whether any meaningful field changed.

The call chain is:
1. dispatch.ts _reconcile() (called every 60s by setInterval)
2. -> reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry() in workspace.ts
3. -> Computes new health, lifecycle_state, active_role, cleanup, integration, canonical_branch_head
4. -> Unconditionally writes record with fresh timestamps
5. -> Commits to shadow branch

## Fix

Add dirty-checking before the save in reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry(). Compare the
computed state fields against the existing record. Only call saveWorkspaceRecordToRegistry()
and commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() if at least one meaningful field differs.

Fields to compare (the meaningful fields):
- canonical_branch_head
- lifecycle_state
- active_role
- health (deep compare — status, issues)
- cleanup (deep compare — status, eligible, reason, detail)
- integration (deep compare — status, target_branch, target_commit, publication_mode, outcome, detail)

Fields NOT to compare (timestamps are consequences, not triggers):
- timestamps.updated_at — only set when meaningful change occurs
- timestamps.last_reconciled_at — can track in memory but must not trigger write
- timestamps.closed_at — derived from lifecycle_state transition, compared via lifecycle_state

## Implementation Notes

- The comparison should use a helper function (e.g. isRecordDirty(existing, computed)) for testability
- For deep comparison of health/cleanup/integration sub-objects, compare the serializable fields excluding their own updated_at timestamps
- last_reconciled_at can still be useful for staleness detection — consider keeping it as an in-memory concern on the dispatch engine rather than persisted, or only persisting it when piggy-backing on a dirty write
- The commit message dispatch-workspace-registry @@... should only appear when there is a real change

## Spec Coverage

Implements @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-10.

## Testing

- Unit test: call reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry() twice with identical task state; assert no commit on second call
- Unit test: call with a changed field (e.g. health goes stale); assert commit happens
- Unit test: verify isRecordDirty() helper returns false for timestamp-only differences
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #860. Added dirty-checking to reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry() via isWorkspaceRecordDirty() helper that compares meaningful fields (canonical_branch_head, lifecycle_state, active_role, health, cleanup, integration) excluding updated_at timestamps. Registry file and shadow branch commit are now suppressed when periodic reconciliation produces no meaningful state change, eliminating ~1 commit/minute of timestamp churn. 12 tests covering all branches of the dirty-check logic plus integration verification.

- Modified reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry() to skip saveWorkspaceRecordToRegistry() and commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() when no meaningful field changed.

tasks.title: Fix double @@ in dispatch-workspace-registry shadow commit messages
tasks.description:
## Problem

Shadow branch commit messages for dispatch-workspace-registry operations show double @@:
dispatch-workspace-registry @@01KKNRC5KR8DTW5JVETBX9CMS8

Should be:
dispatch-workspace-registry @01KKNRC5KR8DTW5JVETBX9CMS8

## Root Cause

generateCommitMessage() in src/parser/shadow.ts (line 1012-1014) has a default case
that unconditionally prepends @ to the ref:

  default:
    parts.push(operation);
    if (ref) parts.push(' @' + ref);

All named cases (task-start, task-complete, etc.) also use '@' + ref and expect bare
refs without the @ prefix. This contract works for those callers.

But commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() in src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts (line 1000-1003)
passes taskRef which is already @-prefixed (comes from record.task_ref / nonClosedRecords[0].task_ref
which stores refs in canonical @ULID format):

  commitIfShadow(ctx.shadow, "dispatch-workspace-registry", taskRef)

## Fix

Strip the @ prefix from taskRef before passing it to commitIfShadow in
commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow(). Use taskRef.replace(/^@/, '') to normalize.

Check all other callers of commitIfShadow to verify they pass bare refs — this may
be the only call site with the issue since the others go through CLI command handlers
that work with bare refs.

## Files

- src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts — commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() around line 1000
- src/parser/shadow.ts — generateCommitMessage() around line 1012 (for reference only)
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #861. Fixed double @@ in dispatch-workspace-registry shadow commit messages by stripping @ prefix from taskRef before passing to commitIfShadow(). Two contract tests added. All CI green, all 4955 tests pass.

notes.content: Fix applied: stripped @ prefix from taskRef in commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow() before passing to commitIfShadow(). Used taskRef.replace(/^@/, '') to normalize. Added 2 tests to shadow.test.ts documenting the contract.

tasks.title: Fix dispatch engine stop() not awaiting second-generation invocations
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #880. Fix prevents second-generation invocations during engine shutdown by clearing queues before awaiting runningInvocations and adding a !this.running guard at the top of _spawnInvocation. Defense-in-depth: 3 layers prevent post-shutdown spawning. 7 tests fixed to set running=true for direct _spawnInvocation calls, polling timeout increased for git worktree latency. All 106 dispatch tests pass, full suite (5471 tests) clean, CI all green.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts fails in ~15% of post-fix dispatch sessions. Most common failing test: "should remove completed invocation from getStatus before draining next invocation" (line 1810).

Two failure modes:
1. ENOTEMPTY on temp dir cleanup — async operations still writing after stop() returns
2. invocationCount never reaches 2 — second invocation never fires within 500ms polling window

## Root Cause

engine.stop() at src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts:927-928 snapshots this.runningInvocations and awaits them via Promise.allSettled. But when a running invocation completes, its .then() handler (line 2139-2168) calls _drainQueues which may call _spawnInvocation, adding NEW promises to this.runningInvocations AFTER stop() already captured its snapshot. So stop() returns while second-generation invocations are still running — their git worktree operations race with cleanupTempDir in afterEach, causing ENOTEMPTY.

## Implementation

1. Fix stop() to loop until runningInvocations is empty:
```ts
// Replace single snapshot+await with loop
while (this.runningInvocations.size > 0) {
  await Promise.allSettled(Array.from(this.runningInvocations));
}
```

2. Guard the completion handler's _drainQueues call with this.running check (line 2140 already checks but the drain may spawn before the check). Ensure _spawnInvocation returns false early when !this.running.

3. Increase the test polling timeout from 500ms (50*10ms) to at least 2000ms to accommodate real git worktree operations under load.

## Key Files
- src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts — stop() at line 899, _spawnInvocation at 1772, completion handler at 2029-2176
- tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts — fleet cleanup tests at line 1798+, polling loop at line 1858

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Revised approach from the original plan: instead of a while loop in stop() (which risks hanging indefinitely if an invocation never resolves), we clear queues BEFORE awaiting runningInvocations. This way completion handlers that call _drainQueues find nothing to spawn — no second-generation invocations can be added. Combined with a !this.running guard at the top of _spawnInvocation, a single-pass if/allSettled is sufficient. Fixed 7 tests that called _spawnInvocation directly without starting the engine (set running=true via type assertion). Also increased fleet cleanup polling timeout from 500ms to 2000ms for git worktree operation latency.

   - message_start, message_progress, message_complete
   - thinking_start, thinking_progress, thinking_complete

  session event queries for the affected session)

tasks.title: Implement session summary stats persistence and live counters
tasks.closed_reason: Merged in PR #888. Implemented session summary stats persistence on close (ac-persist-on-close) and live event counters for active sessions (ac-live-counter). Schema extended with optional event_count/iteration_count/tasks_completed fields. closeSession() computes stats from events.jsonl before writing. getSessionMetadataOnly() reads persisted values instead of hardcoding 0.
