notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

All sessions show "0 events" in the web UI session list and dispatch invocation list. 
The session list API uses getSessionMetadataOnly() which hardcodes event_count, iteration_count, 
and tasks_completed to 0. It intentionally skips reading events.jsonl for performance (ac-metadata-only), 
but the stats were never populated through any other mechanism.

## What needs to happen

Three new ACs were added to cover this:

### 1. ac-persist-on-close (@session-summary-cache)
When a session reaches a terminal status, compute stats from events.jsonl and persist them 
in session.yaml. This is the core fix — once stats are in the metadata file, the list endpoint 
picks them up for free.

**Where to look:**
- closeSession() in src/sessions/store.ts (lines ~432-462) — already reads metadata, writes 
  session.yaml, and does a shadow commit. Add countEventLines() call before the write.
- SessionMetadataSchema in src/sessions/types.ts (line 55) — add event_count: z.number().optional() 
  (and iteration_count, tasks_completed) so values survive the Zod parse round-trip. Optional so 
  existing sessions without these fields still load.
- getSessionMetadataOnly() in src/sessions/store.ts (line 1878) — change hardcoded 0 to read 
  from metadata: event_count: metadata.event_count ?? 0

### 2. ac-live-counter (@session-summary-cache)
Active sessions need live stats without re-scanning events.jsonl on every list request.

**Approach investigated:**
- Add an in-memory Map<sessionId, number> to SessionSummaryCache (src/sessions/cache.ts)
- Increment on each event append, serve from memory for active sessions
- The invocation runtime (src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts) has a single funnel for all event 
  writes: the appendSessionEvent wrapper at line ~343. After appendEvent succeeds, notify the cache.
- IMPORTANT: appendSessionEvent is in library code, but SessionSummaryCache is daemon-side. 
  Use a callback on InvocationOptions (like the existing onUpdate callback) to keep layers decoupled. 
  Something like onEventAppended?: (sessionId: string) => void
- The dispatch engine (src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts) constructs InvocationOptions at ~line 2001 
  and already passes onUpdate — wire the new callback there.
- On session close, discard the live counter entry (the persisted YAML value takes over).

### 3. ac-recompute-stats (@session-log-list)
CLI command: kspec session log recompute-stats [--session <id>]
- Without --session: iterate all non-active sessions missing event_count in their session.yaml
- With --session: do just one
- Run countEventLines(), write back to session.yaml
- Report how many sessions were updated
- Fits alongside existing kspec session compact as a maintenance command

## Key files
- src/sessions/store.ts — closeSession(), getSessionMetadataOnly(), countEventLines()
- src/sessions/types.ts — SessionMetadataSchema
- src/sessions/cache.ts — SessionSummaryCache class
- src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts — appendSessionEvent wrapper, InvocationOptions
- src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts — constructs InvocationOptions for dispatch

## What does NOT need to change
- The daemon list API endpoint (packages/daemon/src/routes/sessions.ts) — already reads from cache
- The web UI — already displays event_count from SessionLogSummary
- The detail endpoint — already computes real count via getSessionLogSummary()

## Spec coverage
- ac-summary-stats and ac-active-refresh already existed but were not implemented properly
- ac-persist-on-close, ac-live-counter, ac-recompute-stats are new ACs added in this investigation
- ac-metadata-only is satisfied — list still doesn't scan events.jsonl (reads persisted value instead)

tasks.title: Implement cross-agent task dispatch exclusivity
tasks.description:
The dispatch engine currently allows multiple agents to have active invocations for the same task simultaneously. For example, when a task-worker submits a task (transitioning to pending_review), the file watcher detects the state change and dispatches a pr-reviewer — even though the task-worker invocation is still running (e.g., waiting for CI). This results in two agents working on the same task concurrently, causing conflicts.

Root cause: handleStateChange() in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts (around line 828-837) loops through agents, matches dispatch rules, and calls _enqueue() without checking if any agent already has an active invocation for that task. The existing _hasActiveOrQueuedInvocation() check (line 1112) is per-agent (agentId + taskId) and only called during batch re-evaluation (_evaluateAllTasks with skipIfActive), never during live event processing.

The helper _activeTaskRefs() (line 1137) already returns all task refs with active invocations regardless of agent type — this can be used as the basis for a cross-agent guard.

Implementation approach: Before enqueueing in handleStateChange() and before spawning in _selectNextCandidate(), check if any agent (not just the current one) has an active invocation for the task. If so, the entry should remain queued (deferred), not discarded. The post-invocation re-evaluation (ac-24 path at line 2166) already re-evaluates all tasks after an invocation completes and drains queues, so deferred entries will be picked up naturally.

Key constraint: Deferred entries must still be subject to staleness checks (_pruneIneligibleQueueEntries) before spawn — if the task state changed while deferred, stale entries should be discarded as usual.

Files: src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts (handleStateChange, _selectNextCandidate, possibly _hasActiveOrQueuedInvocation or a new cross-agent variant), tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts.

AC coverage: @agent-dispatch-engine ac-26.

tasks.title: Fix max_concurrent violation from concurrent drain paths
tasks.description:
The dispatch engine can violate the per-agent max_concurrent limit when multiple drain paths execute concurrently. For example, after a worker invocation fails, the post-invocation re-evaluation (line 2178) calls _drainQueues() directly. Simultaneously, a coalesced timer or reconciliation scan also calls _drainQueues(). Both see activeCount=0, both call _selectNextCandidate(), both spawn — resulting in two workers running despite max_concurrent=1.

Root cause: _serializedDrain() (line 1612) uses drainInProgress/drainPending flags to serialize drain execution, but only the coalesced timer path (line 1591) goes through _serializedDrain(). Five other call sites call _drainQueues() directly, bypassing serialization:
- Line 844: handleStateChange with coalesceWindowMs <= 0
- Line 1017: bootstrap
- Line 1053: reconciliation
- Line 2085: retry wake-up setTimeout callback
- Line 2178: post-invocation re-evaluation

Fix: All _drainQueues() call sites must go through _serializedDrain() (or equivalent serialization). This ensures only one drain executes at a time — concurrent requests are coalesced into a single follow-up drain.

Important nuance: @per-task-dispatch-drain-coalescing ac-7 says bootstrap/reconciliation/post-invocation drains execute immediately (no coalescing DELAY). This is compatible with drain SERIALIZATION — 'immediately' means the drain is requested without waiting for a timer window, but execution still waits for any in-progress drain to complete. These are orthogonal concerns.

Files: src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts (all _drainQueues call sites), tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts.

AC coverage: @agent-dispatch-engine ac-27, @per-task-dispatch-drain-coalescing ac-9.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

The session checkpoint stop hook currently checks three things:
1. Uncommitted git changes
2. Tasks in in_progress status
3. Incomplete todos on active tasks

With the dispatch system running agents that handle tasks autonomously, the task/todo warnings are almost always noise. Interactive sessions get repeatedly blocked by warnings about tasks being worked on by other agents. The checkpoint's real value is preventing data loss from uncommitted git changes.

## What to do

Remove task status and todo completeness checking from the checkpoint. Keep only the uncommitted git changes check.

### ACs to implement
- ac-git-only: Only uncommitted git changes are reported. Task status and todos are not checked.
- ac-3 (existing): Exit silently when no issues found.

### ACs that were removed (clean up their implementations)
- ac-session-scope, ac-no-session-scope, ac-session-failsafe — these were task-scoping ACs that filtered in-progress tasks by session ownership. All three were removed from the spec since task checking itself is being removed.
- ac-1, ac-2 — dynamic numbering and conditional instructions. These were relevant when there were three check categories but are redundant now that there's only git changes + ac-3.

### Key files
- src/cli/commands/session/checkpoint.ts — performCheckpoint() is the core function. Remove the task querying logic (lines ~48-77 for session-scoped filtering) and todo checking. Keep only the git status check.
- src/cli/commands/session/types.ts — CheckpointIssue type has discriminators "uncommitted_changes", "in_progress_task", "incomplete_todo". Remove the latter two.
- tests/cli/session-checkpoint-scoping.test.ts — Entire test file tests task-scoping behavior. Should be removed or gutted.
- tests/ralph-replacement.test.ts — Has checkpoint tests. Update to reflect git-only behavior.

### What NOT to change
- The hook format ({"decision": "block", "reason": "..."}) stays the same
- The retry detection via stop_hook_active stays the same
- The silent exit on clean pass (ac-3) stays the same
- The hook installation in kspec setup — that's a separate task

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Problem

The checkpoint and prompt-check hooks are currently always installed by kspec setup into .claude/settings.json with no way to control this via project configuration. The checkpoint hook is being scoped down to git-only checks (separate task), and should be off by default since most projects using dispatch don't need it. The prompt-check (spec-first reminder on UserPromptSubmit) is lightweight and useful, so it should default to enabled.

## What to do

Add a hooks configuration section to kspec.config.yaml and make kspec setup respect it when installing/removing hooks.

### ACs to implement on @project-config
- ac-hooks-section: hooks section in kspec.config.yaml allows independent enable/disable of each hook (checkpoint, prompt-check)
- ac-hooks-missing-keys: When hooks section exists but a key is absent, resolve to that hook's default
- ac-hooks-no-config: When no hooks section or no config file, all hooks resolve to defaults
- ac-hooks-validation: Invalid values in hooks section produce a validation error

### ACs to implement on @cmd-session-checkpoint
- ac-default-disabled: New projects without checkpoint preference don't get the hook installed
- ac-install-when-enabled: When config enables checkpoint, setup installs it
- ac-remove-when-disabled: When config disables or doesn't mention checkpoint, setup removes it if previously installed

### Config shape

kspec.config.yaml gains:
```yaml
hooks:
  checkpoint: true    # or false, default: false
  prompt_check: true  # or false, default: true
```

### Key files
- src/schema/spec.ts — ManifestSchema has a `hooks` field (currently z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()). Replace with a proper typed schema for the hooks config.
- src/cli/commands/setup.ts — Lines ~303-328 install the stop hook unconditionally. Needs to read config, conditionally install/remove checkpoint, and conditionally install/remove prompt-check.
- .claude/settings.json — The target file where hooks are installed/removed. Setup already reads and writes this file.

### Defaults
- prompt-check (UserPromptSubmit hook): ENABLED by default — lightweight spec-first reminder
- checkpoint (Stop hook): DISABLED by default — with dispatch handling tasks, most sessions don't need pre-stop blocking

### Important behaviors
- kspec setup must be idempotent — running it multiple times with the same config produces the same result
- Removal: if a hook was previously installed and config now says disabled (or absent with default=disabled), setup removes that hook entry from .claude/settings.json
- The hooks section in ManifestSchema already exists but is untyped. Give it a proper Zod schema.
- kspec init should NOT add a hooks section to kspec.config.yaml — let the defaults apply. Users opt in by adding the section.

### Dependencies
- This task does NOT depend on the checkpoint scope reduction task (removing task/todo checks). They're independent — this controls installation, that controls what the hook checks.

tasks.title: Add WebSocket events for review mutations
tasks.description:
Broadcast WebSocket events when review records are created or mutated,
so the UI can refresh without polling.

Without real-time events, users would need to manually refresh to see
new threads, verdicts, or disposition changes from agent reviewers.

What: Add a "reviews:updates" WebSocket topic. Emit events on review
creation, thread creation/update, verdict submission, check recording,
and lifecycle transitions. Event types: review_created, review_updated,
thread_created, thread_updated, verdict_submitted, check_recorded,
lifecycle_changed.

How: Follow existing WebSocket patterns (tasks:updates, plans:updates).
Add broadcast calls at the end of each mutation endpoint handler.
Events carry the review ULID and the mutation type so the client
knows which query keys to invalidate.

tasks.title: Implement diff content API endpoints
tasks.description:
Add daemon endpoints for serving parsed git diffs and entity content
for the review content viewers.

Why: The diff viewer needs structured diff data (not raw text) to render
syntax-highlighted diffs with line numbers. The structured content viewer
needs plan/spec content to display with section markers. The daemon runs
in the repo and has access to git and .kspec/.

What: GET /api/diff?base=X&head=Y returns parsed diff with file list,
stats, and structured hunks. GET /api/diff/file?base=X&head=Y&path=P
returns single-file diff for lazy loading.
GET /api/diff/context?base=X&head=Y&path=P&start=N&end=M returns
expanded context lines for a file region.
GET /api/reviews/:id/content returns parsed plan/spec content for
structured reviews.

How: Run `git diff --unified=3 base..head` on the server, parse with
parse-git-diff into typed structures (files, chunks, changes with line
numbers and change types). For context expansion, run `git show
commit:path` and extract the requested line range. For entity content,
use existing kspec plan/spec loading functions. Return structured JSON
matching the input format expected by @git-diff-view/svelte.

tasks.title: Build code diff viewer with inline commenting
tasks.description:
Build the GitHub-style unified diff viewer for code reviews with
inline comment threading.

Why: Code reviews need a visual diff to be useful. Showing threads
as a flat list without diff context is how the review looks today
via CLI — the web UI should show threads anchored to the code they
reference, with the full diff visible.

What: File list sidebar with changed files and diff stats (+/- lines).
Per-file unified diff with syntax highlighting, old/new line numbers,
added/deleted/unchanged lines with color coding. Collapsed unchanged
regions with "show N more lines" buttons. Click-to-comment on any
diff line (opens inline form that creates code-anchored threads).
Existing threads rendered inline at their anchor positions. Lazy
loading for diffs with many files (20+).

How: Use @git-diff-view/svelte for rendering — it provides native
Svelte diff components with a widget system (renderWidgetLine) for
injecting comment thread components between diff lines.
onAddWidgetClick handles the click-to-comment interaction. extendData
attaches existing comment threads to their anchor lines. Use
parse-git-diff on the server (in the diff API) to parse raw git diff
output into the structured format git-diff-view expects. TanStack
Query for fetching diff data and comment threads. Lazy file loading
via intersection observer or expand-on-click.

tasks.title: Enforce canonical field ordering in YAML serialization
tasks.description:
toYaml() in src/parser/yaml.ts uses sortMapEntries: false, relying on JS object insertion order to keep _ulid first. This is fragile — any code path that reconstructs objects with different key order would silently break the convention.

This matters because git log -L regex relies on _ulid being the first field of each entry to find block boundaries (e.g. /^- _ulid:/ for tasks, /^_ulid:/ for modules).

Fix: Add a custom sortMapEntries comparator to toYaml() that enforces a canonical key order with _ulid always first, followed by slugs, title, type, then remaining keys alphabetically (or in a defined priority order).

Applies to all .kspec/ YAML files: project.tasks.yaml, project.inbox.yaml, modules/*.yaml.
tasks.closed_reason: Reviewed, approved, and merged to dev. Canonical key ordering implemented in toYaml() with custom sortMapEntries comparator. All 4 ACs covered by 15 tests. No regressions in related serialization tests.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Implemented canonical key ordering in toYaml() via custom sortMapEntries comparator. Priority tiers: _ulid(0) > slugs(1) > title(2) > type(3) > description(10) > spec relationships(15-19) > status/state(20-23) > relationships(25-32) > work metadata(35-38) > vcs/review(40-44) > timestamps(60-70) > notes/todos(80-81) > automation(90). Unknown keys sort alphabetically at tier 50. Added 15 tests covering all 4 ACs.

tasks.description:

Covers ac-3 of @yaml-serialization-invariants. Separate from the field ordering work (ac-1, ac-2, ac-4) because round-trip stability touches all YAML write paths and may require auditing multiple serialization call sites.

Fix: extractRawTaskArray + mergeTaskPreservingRawShape — non-target tasks are preserved as raw data, and target tasks only include fields that were in the original file or carry non-default values. Added 13 tests covering toYaml round-trip, file-level round-trip, and saveTask/mutateTaskAtomically no-op stability.

tasks.title: Audit shadow commit messages for ref consistency gaps
tasks.description:
Audit all shadow branch auto-commit message patterns in generateCommitMessage() (src/parser/shadow.ts) and their call sites. Identify every operation that drops or omits the entity ref from the commit message.

Known gap: task-add uses "Add task: <title>" instead of including the ref (shadow.ts:990).

Output: A list of all inconsistencies, and one task per fix (or a single task if the fixes are small enough to batch). Each fix should reference @trait-shadow-commit ac-2/ac-3.
tasks.closed_reason: Audit complete. Analyzed generateCommitMessage() and ~80 commitIfShadow() call sites. Found: ~65 operations using default case (ac-2 format violation), 4 call sites missing entity refs (ac-3 violation), 2 link commands bypassing structured format entirely. Created 3 fix tasks: expand switch cases, fix missing refs, fix link bypass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Audit complete. Analyzed generateCommitMessage() and all ~80 commitIfShadow() call sites across 18 source files. Findings documented in next note.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Audit Findings

### generateCommitMessage() switch coverage
Only 10 of ~75 operation strings have explicit cases. The remaining ~65 fall through to the default case which produces 'operation @ref' — violating ac-2 (no colon separator) and producing inconsistent formatting.

### Explicit cases (10):
task-start, task-complete, task-note, task-add, inbox-add, inbox-promote, item-add, item-set, item-delete, derive

### Issues found:

**1. inbox-add: missing ref (ac-3 violation)**
- inbox.ts:108 passes ref=undefined, detail=text
- Produces: 'Inbox: <text truncated>' — no entity ref at all
- Should include the inbox item ULID after creation

**2. task-add: conditional ref (ac-3 gap)**
- shadow.ts:990 — when ref is present, produces 'Add task @ref: title' (good)
- But fallback path (line 993) produces 'Add task: <title or ref>' — ambiguous, may drop ref
- Call site in task.ts:1155 always provides both ref and detail, so the fallback is dead code from meta.ts:1126 which also provides both

**3. link add/remove: bypass generateCommitMessage entirely (ac-2 violation)**
- link.ts:125 passes raw string 'Add implements link: @from -> @to' as the operation
- link.ts:394 passes raw string 'Remove implements link: @from -> @to'
- These go to default case, producing the raw string directly — no @ prefix on refs, inconsistent format

**4. setup skill-install-core: no entity ref (ac-3 violation)**
- setup.ts:1182 passes operation='skill-install-core', ref='N core skills'
- ref is a count string, not an entity ref

**5. batch: no entity ref (ac-3 N/A)**
- batch-exec.ts:818 uses shadowAutoCommit directly with 'batch: N commands'
- No specific entity — acceptable for batch operations

**6. workflow-*: no ref passed (ac-3 violation)**
- workflow.ts:134,319,379,420,458,730,788,975 — all pass operation only, no ref
- Produces: 'workflow-start', 'workflow-abort', etc. — no workflow run ref

**7. session-compact: uses session_id, not entity ref (ac-3 borderline)**
- session/compact.ts:200 — passes session_id slice or 'all'
- Technically includes a ref but it's a session ID not a spec/task ref

**8. tasks-assess: uses 'automation' as ref (ac-3 violation)**
- tasks.ts:511 — passes ref='automation', detail='N task(s)'
- Produces: 'tasks-assess @automation' — ref is a label, not an entity

**9. dispatch-workspace-registry: uses bareRef (ac-3 OK)**
- workspace.ts:1012 — passes bareRef (task slug)
- Falls through to default — produces 'dispatch-workspace-registry @ref'

**10. Default case format inconsistency (ac-2 violation)**
The default case produces 'operation @ref' (space-separated, no colon).
ac-2 requires 'operation: @ref-short' (colon separator).
~65 operations use default and produce non-conforming messages.

### Summary of violations:
- **ac-2 (format):** ~65 operations use default case with wrong separator. link commands bypass entirely.
- **ac-3 (ref present):** inbox-add, workflow-*, setup skill-install, tasks-assess all miss entity refs.
- **Known gap confirmed:** task-add fallback path (line 993) can drop ref, but currently all call sites provide both args.

tasks.title: Rewrite review-verdicts-and-resolution-lifecycle ac-3 for per-cycle model
tasks.description:
Rewrite @review-verdicts-and-resolution-lifecycle ac-3 to describe the
per-cycle review model instead of the single-record iteration model.

Why: The current ac-3 states "the same review record tracks iteration
through its event log and compare context updates without losing the
audit trail." This conflicts with the per-cycle model where each review
cycle gets its own record. The original assumption predated the dispatch
review flow — review records were conceived as long-lived mutable
artifacts, but in practice each review cycle is a discrete assessment.

What: Rewrite ac-3 to describe that review cycles create new review
records, with the collection of records comprising the full review
history. Verify that existing code and tests referencing ac-3 are
compatible with the rewrite — the current implementation already
supports creating multiple reviews per task, so this is primarily a
spec alignment, not a code change.

How: Use kspec item ac set @review-verdicts-and-resolution-lifecycle
ac-3 to rewrite the AC text. Check tests tagged with this AC for
compatibility. Update any test annotations if needed.

don't represent a final assessment.

The task's review_ref is updated to point to the new record.

makes it impossible to see what happened in each cycle. Separate
records per cycle give clean timeline artifacts and match the mental
model of individual reviews on a pull request.

always create a new review when picking up a pending_review task
that already has a closed review_ref. Update review_ref on the task
to point to the new record. The old record remains closed and
accessible via the activity timeline.

review_ref and create fresh. The dispatch orientation prompt surfaces
the prior review ref. Code changes: update review-task-integration
to handle review_ref replacement, ensure old review records are
findable by task ref for timeline rendering.

tasks.title: Implement task activity git query
tasks.description:
Build the function that queries shadow branch git history to extract
the raw commit data for a task's YAML block.

Why: This is the data extraction layer for the activity timeline.
git log -L tracks all commits that touched a specific line range,
capturing the complete history regardless of commit message content.

What: Create a getRawTaskCommits(specDir, taskRef) function that:
1. Finds the task's _ulid line in project.tasks.yaml
2. Finds the next _ulid line (or EOF) to determine block boundaries
3. Runs git log -L <start>,<end>:project.tasks.yaml in the shadow
   branch worktree with diff output
4. Returns structured commit objects with hash, timestamp, author,
   message, and raw diff hunks

How: Shell out to git in the .kspec worktree directory. The _ulid-first
invariant (@yaml-serialization-invariants ac-1) guarantees reliable
block boundary detection. Return raw data — normalization into typed
activity entries is handled by a separate task.

Covers: @task-activity-git-query ac-1, ac-2.

tasks.title: Normalize git diff data into typed activity entries
tasks.description:
Parse raw git diff hunks from task commit history into typed, structured
activity entries for the timeline.

Why: git log -L returns raw diffs showing which YAML fields changed in
each commit. These need to be translated into meaningful activity records
that humans and the timeline UI can consume. The commit message alone is
insufficient — it may be a generic "task-set @ref" while the diff reveals
the actual change was a status transition, a new note, or a review linkage.

What: Create a normalizeTaskActivity(rawCommits) function that:
1. Parses diff hunks to identify which fields changed (added/removed lines)
2. Maps field changes to activity types:
   - status field change → "state_change" with from/to values
   - new entry in notes array → "note_added" with content preview
   - review_ref set/changed → "review_linked" with review ref
   - submission_linkage set → "submitted" with branch/commit
   - priority/tags/description changes → "field_updated" with field name
   - multiple field changes in one commit → multiple activity entries
     with shared timestamp and commit ref
3. Falls back to commit message parsing when diff is unavailable or
   unparseable (e.g. "Start @ref" → "started")
4. Returns chronologically ordered typed entries with: type, timestamp,
   author, summary, and optional detail fields

How: Parse YAML diff lines to detect field-level changes. For array
fields like notes, detect insertions by looking for new _ulid entries.
For scalar fields like status, extract old/new values from -/+ lines.
Group changes per commit but emit separate activity entries per
meaningful change. Commit message serves as fallback context.

Covers: @task-activity-git-query ac-3, ac-4.

Review 01KKWEBZ approved with 3 nits: dead submission_linkage case, nested map field leakage, and missing review-* patterns — all low impact due to diff-first strategy.

Three-layer approach: (1) parseCommitMessage maps 14 shadow branch commit patterns to activity types (ac-3), (2) parseDiffChanges extracts field-level YAML changes from unified diff hunks (ac-4), (3) normalizeTaskActivity combines them — tries diff first, falls back to commit message. 30 tests pass.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fixed the dead submission_linkage case in diffChangesToEntries. Root cause: parseDiffChanges used a regex that only matched scalar YAML fields (key: value on one line). tasks.title: Fix YAML.stringify anchor/alias crash when sortMapEntries reorders shared references
tasks.description:
## Problem

`toYaml()` crashes with 'Unresolved alias (the anchor must be set before the alias): a1' when serializing objects that contain shared JS object references.

## Root Cause

Commit c6138a963 added `sortMapEntries: canonicalKeyComparator` to `YAML.stringify()` in `toYaml()`. The `yaml` library detects shared JS object references (same object used in multiple places) and serializes them as YAML anchors (`&a1`) and aliases (`*a1`). When `sortMapEntries` reorders keys, it can place an alias before its anchor definition, producing invalid YAML.

## Reproduction

```typescript
const shared = { status: 'not_run' };
const data = { roleStates: { worker: shared, reviewer: shared } };
YAML.stringify(data, { sortMapEntries: comparator }); // throws
YAML.stringify(data, {});                              // works
```

## Where It Triggers

Dispatch workspace registry records: Zod schema defaults create shared object instances (e.g. the same default `RoleBootstrapStateSchema` object is reused for both worker and reviewer). When `saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord()` calls `writeYamlFilePreserveFormat()` → `toYaml()`, the shared references trigger the anchor/alias crash.

## Bisect Evidence

- Passes on main and on aa53ca909 (commit before canonical ordering)
- Fails on c6138a963 (canonical ordering commit) and all subsequent commits
- 7 of 8 tests fail in dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts
- 1 of 1 fails in dispatch-workspace-and-scheduler-flow.test.ts (cascading: bootstrap crash prevents invocations)

## Investigation Paths

1. **Deep-clone before serialization**: `toYaml(structuredClone(obj))` breaks shared references so the yaml library won't generate anchors. Simple but adds overhead for every YAML write.
2. **Set `yaml` library option to avoid anchors**: Check if `YAML.stringify` accepts an option like `anchorPrefix: false` or a custom `createNode` that avoids Alias nodes.
3. **Deep-clone only in dispatch-workspaces.ts**: Narrower fix — clone the workspace data before saving. Targets only the known trigger.
4. **Strip shared refs in Zod output**: Ensure Zod schema `.default()` calls return fresh objects (they should, but verify the dispatch workspace schema).

Option 1 is the safest systemic fix since any Zod schema with shared defaults could trigger this.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev. Fixed toYaml() anchor/alias crash by JSON round-tripping input to break shared object references before YAML.stringify. Regression test added.

tasks.title: Unify tool call event parsing and fix phased input streaming
tasks.description:
## What

Unify the dual tool call event parsing paths (HTTP batch via parseEventsToBlocks and WebSocket live via incrementalBlockUpdate) into a single shared module, and fix the accumulator to correctly propagate tool call input from ACP phased events so the web UI and CLI watch display actual tool inputs instead of {}.

## Why

The ACP SDK sends tool calls in three phases:
1. **Registration** — tool_call with rawInput: {} (empty, just announces a call will happen)
2. **Input** — tool_call_update with rawInput: {command: "...", ...} (actual parameters, the real "start")
3. **Completion** — tool_call_update with status + rawOutput (the end, though intermediate updates can precede it)

Currently:
- The SessionEventAccumulator reads rawInput from phase 1 (empty {}) and emits tool_call_start. When phase 2 arrives with populated rawInput, the accumulator only checks for status transitions and silently drops the input.
- The HTTP path (parseEventsToBlocks) correctly handles this at line 265-268 by updating existing.input from tool_call_update events. But the WebSocket path (incrementalBlockUpdate) has no equivalent — tool_call_complete only updates status/duration, never input.
- deduplicatePhasedToolCalls accesses data.update.sessionUpdate (legacy format) but ACP events store data.sessionUpdate directly — it silently skips all ACP events.
- ToolCallView.svelte on-demand fetch only extracts output, never input. If block.input is {} from streaming, expansion shows INPUT: {}.

The result: tool calls show no input preview during live streaming, and expanding completed tool calls shows {}. The HTTP path works correctly for historical sessions but uses different parsing logic than the streaming path, creating a maintenance burden and behavioral inconsistency.

## How

### 1. Create shared event field extraction module

Extract the field resolution logic from parseEventsToBlocks into a shared module (e.g., session-event-fields.ts or extend session-utils.ts):

- unwrapSessionUpdate(data) — normalize ACP (data.sessionUpdate) vs legacy (data.update.sessionUpdate) format
- extractToolCallFields(update) — resolve toolCallId (toolCallId | tool_call_id | id), toolName (title | tool | toolName | name), rawInput (rawInput | input) consistently
- extractToolCallResult(update) — resolve rawOutput (rawOutput | output | content), status, error flags

Both parseEventsToBlocks and incrementalBlockUpdate should use these shared extractors. The field resolution order should be defined once.

### 2. Fix the SessionEventAccumulator to emit tool_call_input events

When the accumulator's tool_call_update handler receives an event with populated rawInput (and no status transition), emit a new tool_call_input event containing tool_call_id, tool_name, and tool_input. Add the ToolCallInputEventData type to session-event-types.ts.

### 3. Update incrementalBlockUpdate to handle tool_call_input

Add a tool_call_input case that finds the existing block by toolCallId and updates its input in-place. Add 'tool_call_input' to the sessionEventTypes set in the page component's handleAgentEvent.

### 4. Fix deduplicatePhasedToolCalls for ACP format

Use the shared unwrapSessionUpdate helper so it handles both data.sessionUpdate (ACP) and data.update.sessionUpdate (legacy) correctly. Currently silently skips all ACP events.

### 5. Update CLI watch handler

The CLI watch command (src/cli/commands/agent.ts) also consumes WebSocket events. Add tool_call_input handling to update the displayed input for in-progress tool calls.

### 6. Refactor parseEventsToBlocks to use shared extractors

Replace inline field resolution in parseEventsToBlocks with calls to the shared extraction functions. This ensures any future field name changes or new ACP formats only need updating in one place.

### Key files

- src/agent-runtime/session-event-accumulator.ts — emit tool_call_input event
- src/agent-runtime/session-event-types.ts — add ToolCallInputEventData type
- packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/session/session-utils.ts — shared extractors, update incrementalBlockUpdate
- packages/web-ui/src/routes/sessions/[id]/+page.svelte — add tool_call_input to WS event set
- src/sessions/store.ts — fix deduplicatePhasedToolCalls format handling
- src/cli/commands/agent.ts — handle tool_call_input in CLI watch
- packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts — no changes needed (already broadcasts all accumulator events)

### Testing approach

- Unit test the shared extraction functions with both ACP and legacy format events
- Unit test the accumulator emits tool_call_input for phased events
- Unit test deduplicatePhasedToolCalls with ACP format events (currently silently broken)
- Unit test incrementalBlockUpdate handles tool_call_input correctly
- Verify parseEventsToBlocks produces identical blocks to sequential incrementalBlockUpdate calls for the same event sequence
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev. Unified tool call event parsing across HTTP and WebSocket paths via shared extraction module (session-event-fields.ts). Fixed ACP format handling in 6 store.ts functions. Added tool_call_input event emission in accumulator for phased streaming. Updated CLI watch and web UI incrementalBlockUpdate. 56 new tests, all passing.

tasks.title: Detect stale integration target when dispatch base branch config changes
tasks.description:
## What

When `dispatch.base_branch` changes in `kspec.config.yaml` after workspaces have already been provisioned, the existing workspace records preserve the original `integration.target_branch` value. This causes agents to merge into the wrong branch (e.g., `main` instead of `dev`).

## Why

A real dispatch run had the reviewer agent merge a task branch into `main` even though `dispatch.base_branch` was set to `dev`. The workspace record was originally created before the config was changed, and the stale `target_branch` was never updated. The dispatch prompt faithfully reported the stale value, so the agent acted correctly on wrong data.

## How

1. During workspace re-provisioning (when an existing record is found), compare `existingRecord.integration.target_branch` against the currently resolved `baseBranch` from config.

2. When a mismatch is detected and the workspace's integration state is still `pending` (no merge has happened yet):
   - Update the workspace record's `integration.target_branch` to match the current config.
   - Log/note the change so it's visible in workspace status.

3. When a mismatch is detected but the workspace has active integration state (e.g., in-progress merge, or the canonical branch was forked from the old base):
   - Surface the conflict as an actionable warning or error during provisioning.
   - Do NOT silently use either value — let the operator decide.

4. Add tests covering:
   - Workspace provisioned with base_branch=main, config later changed to dev, re-provision updates target.
   - Workspace with completed integration is NOT silently retargeted.
   - Dispatch prompt reflects the updated target after re-provisioning.

## Spec Coverage

Implements @dispatch-workspace-configuration ac-6 and ac-7.

tasks.title: Replace hardcoded branch names in merge skill template with dynamic references
tasks.description:
## What

The merge skill template (`templates/skills/merge/SKILL.md`) hardcodes `dev` as the merge target branch in example commands on lines 50, 57, and 97. When an agent reads this skill, it may follow the hardcoded examples instead of the dispatch-provided integration target.

## Why

The merge skill is used by both human-directed and dispatch-driven workflows. In dispatch mode, the correct merge target comes from the workspace metadata (injected into the dispatch prompt). But the skill's example commands showing `git checkout dev` and `git log origin/dev..HEAD` create a competing source of truth that can mislead agents — especially if the dispatch target is a different branch.

## How

1. Replace hardcoded `dev` references in `templates/skills/merge/SKILL.md` with generic placeholders like `<integration-branch>` or instructional text that tells the agent to use the dispatch-provided target branch (from the `Integration target` line in the dispatch prompt context, or from `KSPEC_DISPATCH_MERGE_TARGET` env var).

2. Add a note in the skill that in dispatch mode, the merge target is always provided in the dispatch prompt context and should be used verbatim — never assumed.

3. Run `kspec skill render` to regenerate the rendered output in `.agents/skills/`.

4. Verify the rendered skill no longer contains hardcoded branch names.

tasks.title: fix session cache invalidate leaves ghost in knownSessionIds
tasks.description:
SessionSummaryCache.invalidate() deletes the entry from this.entries but does NOT remove the session ID from this.knownSessionIds. On the next refresh(), the session is not in entries (so not treated as active or existing-non-active) but IS in knownSessionIds (so not treated as new). It falls into a dead zone — invisible until a full cache rebuild (daemon restart).

**Root cause:** cache.ts:97-99 — invalidate() only calls this.entries.delete(sessionId), missing this.knownSessionIds.delete(sessionId).

**Impact:** After dispatch completes an invocation and calls cache.invalidate(preSessionId) (dispatch.ts:2258), the completed session disappears from the /api/sessions list. It reappears only on daemon restart or cache clear.

**Fix:** Add this.knownSessionIds.delete(sessionId) to the invalidate() method. This causes the next refresh() to classify the session as 'new' (line 202: currentIds has it, knownSessionIds does not), re-read session.yaml from disk, and return it with correct completed status and persisted stats.

**File:** src/sessions/cache.ts, invalidate() method (line 97-99).

**Verification:** Unit test that calls invalidate() then getAll() and confirms the session reappears with updated status. Integration: watch a dispatch session complete and confirm it appears in /api/sessions immediately.

Root cause confirmed: entries.delete() alone left a ghost in knownSessionIds, causing refresh() to skip re-reading the session. Pre-existing failures in agent-dispatch-engine and review-cli tests are unrelated.

tasks.title: Implement event envelope and bus
tasks.description:
The event bus with standard envelope is the foundation for everything.
Today, handleStateChange() does dedup, rule matching, enqueue, and
drain inline. This task refactors that into a publish/subscribe model.

Why: Every subsequent feature (hooks, schedules, composition) needs a
central place to emit and subscribe to events with identity, causation
tracking, and loop prevention. Without the bus, each feature wires into
handleStateChange() directly.

What: Create an EventBus class with typed event envelope (event_id,
event_type, emitted_at, source_type, source_id, correlation_id,
causation_id). Add emit(event) and subscribe(pattern, handler).
Refactor existing dispatch rule matching into a subscriber. Add
invocation lifecycle events by routing existing onInvocationEvent
through the bus. Implement chain depth limit using correlation_id
tracking (default max 5). Add configurable ring buffer for recent
event retention.

How: The bus lives inside DispatchEngine and shares its lifecycle.
Task event dedup remains for task.* events only. Non-task events have
unique event_id and skip dedup. Events are delivered in emission order
per source. The ring buffer is a simple circular array.

Covers: @dispatch-event-envelope ac-1 through ac-6.

tasks.title: Implement shared action model and action run tracking
tasks.description:
Implement the action model and action run abstraction. Every action
execution (hook, schedule, or join trigger) produces an action run
with unique ID, status, duration, and optional linked invocation_id.

Why: Action runs are the uniform abstraction that overlap policies,
UI status, event logging, and action history key off of. Without
this, overlap tracking only works for agent actions and the UI
can't show command/kspec action status.

What: ActionExecutor class with execute(action, eventContext) that
returns an ActionRun. Each action type has its execution path.
Action runs emit action.started and action.completed/failed events
on the bus. Template interpolation resolves {{var}} from envelope
and payload.

How: The executor is used by both HookExecutor and ScheduleEngine.
All four action types produce action runs. Agent action runs link
to invocation_id. Command and kspec runs track PID and exit code.

Covers: @dispatch-action-model ac-1 through ac-9.

tasks.title: Implement command action with structured form
tasks.description:
Implement the command action using structured program + args form
instead of shell strings. Eliminates injection risks.

Why: Shell string interpolation with user-controlled values is an
injection vector. Structured commands are safe by construction.

What: Command actions specify program (string) and args (string[]).
Template variables are interpolated as literal strings within each
arg element, never passed through shell parsing. Event context is
available via namespaced KSPEC_* environment variables with an
allowlist and 1KB size limit per value. Shell mode is off by default.

How: Use child_process.spawn (not exec/execSync) with shell: false.
Each arg is a separate argv element. Template values go into args
via string replacement, not shell expansion. The allowlist for env
vars is derived from the event payload schema.

Covers: @dispatch-command-action ac-1 through ac-4.

tasks.title: Emit session lifecycle events
tasks.description:
Emit session.ended, session.idle_timeout, and session.cancelled
events when dispatch sessions reach terminal states. Also define
the contract for how agent action runs close when their linked
invocation reaches a terminal state.

Why: End-of-session hooks are a headline goal. Without this task,
session.* events exist in the taxonomy but are never emitted. Also,
if action runs don't close on invocation terminal states, overlap
accounting and composition join counts hang indefinitely.

What: Hook into the invocation completion handlers (which already
emit invocation.completed/failed/stalled) to also emit the
corresponding session.* event with terminal_reason and work_summary.
Define the mapping: invocation.completed -> session.ended,
invocation.failed -> session.ended (with failure reason),
invocation.stalled -> session.idle_timeout. Agent-initiated
cancellation -> session.cancelled. Also: when an agent action run's
linked invocation reaches a terminal state, the action run is
closed (action.completed or action.failed emitted) so overlap
tracking and join accumulators can progress.

How: The session_id == invocation_id identity means we can emit
session events from the same completion handler. Work summary is
derived from session event log (task notes added, PRs created,
tasks completed — read from session metadata on close).

Covers: @dispatch-event-taxonomy ac-2,
@dispatch-event-payload ac-3.
Also covers action run closure: when an agent action's linked
invocation ends, the action run is completed/failed accordingly.
This is emergent behavior from wiring invocation terminal events
to action run state, not a direct AC on @dispatch-action-model.

tasks.title: Implement schedule tick engine
tasks.description:
The schedule engine evaluates cron expressions and fires schedule.tick
events, enforcing overlap policies against action runs (not just
invocations).

Why: Makes schedules run. Overlap must work for all action types.

What: ScheduleEngine with 60-second evaluation loop. Tracks per-
schedule state: last_tick, next_tick, run_count (accepted runs),
active_run_ids (array — multiple active runs possible with allow
policy), buffered_tick. Overlap checks against action runs, not
invocations — this works for command/kspec/notify too. Config
reload via versioned snapshot.

How: Integrates with DispatchEngine lifecycle (start/stop). Subscribe
to action.completed/failed events to clear active run state. All
runtime state is volatile (resets on daemon restart). Backfill on
start: if backfill: true, check current time against cron and fire
one catch-up. tick_time in payload is the scheduled wall-clock time,
not evaluation time. Manual triggers emit normal schedule.tick events
with overlap policy enforced.

Covers: @dispatch-schedule-entities ac-1 through ac-6,
@dispatch-schedule-runtime ac-1 through ac-5.

Fix cycle 1 findings resolved: AC-4 and AC-6 tests now exercise the evaluation loop directly.

tasks.title: Implement composition join accumulator
tasks.description:
The join accumulator enables fan-in synthesis by tracking action run
completions per composition group.

Why: Pipeline chaining works with hooks alone. Fan-in needs a
primitive that counts completions before firing.

What: JoinAccumulator subscribes to action.completed events,
tracks completions by group_id, fires on_complete when threshold
is met or timeout expires. Group_id is auto-generated per activation
or inherited from correlation_id. Only successful completions count
toward threshold; failures are tracked for partial results. Timeout
starts when first run begins. State is volatile (daemon lifetime).

How: Define composition schema in meta YAML. Subscribe to
action.completed/failed on bus. Match runs to groups via group_id.
State is Map<group_id, GroupState>.

Covers: @dispatch-composition-patterns ac-2, ac-3,
@dispatch-composition-correlation ac-1 through ac-4,
@dispatch-composition-schema ac-1, ac-2.

- CompositionSchema with _ulid, id, name, join_count, on_complete (shared ActionSchema), timeout_ms, enabled

tasks.title: Update dispatch agent instructions for merge conflict handling and branch freshness
tasks.description:
Current problem: Reviewer agents block tasks on ANY merge conflict,
even simple textual ones (e.g., two additive features editing the same
file). This wastes a human round-trip for trivial resolution.

Three changes needed:

1. **Worker: rebase on target before starting work.** Task workers
   should rebase their branch on the integration target (e.g., dev) as
   the first step when starting or resuming work. This keeps branches
   fresh and lets workers optimistically resolve conflicts as they
   arise.

2. **Reviewer: resolve simple conflicts, MUST-FIX complex ones.**
   Update merge skill and review-gates so reviewers attempt to resolve
   straightforward textual conflicts (parallel additive edits). If the
   conflict is unclear or semantically complex, the reviewer should NOT
   block — instead, submit a MUST-FIX finding noting the merge
   conflict, what files are affected, and what the reviewer knows about
   the conflict. This sends it back to the worker via needs_work.

3. **Worker: best-effort non-destructive conflict resolution.** When a
   worker receives a needs_work with merge conflict findings, they
   should attempt best-effort resolution. Only block if there is
   genuine uncertainty about correct resolution that requires human
   judgment.

Files to update:
- templates/skills/merge/SKILL.md — conflict handling guidance
- .agents/skills/review-gates/SKILL.md — role boundary for reviewers
- kspec-agents.md blocking rules — clarify merge conflicts are not
  automatic blocks
- templates/agents-sections/ — if branching/rebase guidance lives there

After updating, run kspec agents generate and kspec skill render.

tasks.title: Implement integration target branch sync
tasks.description:
Why: The integration target branch (dispatch.base_branch) is captured
at workspace provisioning and never updated. Over time it drifts from
remote, making merges increasingly stale and conflict-prone. The engine
needs to keep it fresh.

What: Fetch + fast-forward sync of the integration target from remote
at three trigger points: engine start (before bootstrap), periodically
when no reviewer is active (deferred when reviewer is active), and
before workspace provisioning when stale. Fast-forward only — no merge
commits created. Transient fetch failures warn but don't degrade.

How: Add a syncTargetBranch() method to DispatchEngine that runs
git fetch <remote> <base_branch> followed by git merge --ff-only
<remote>/<base_branch> in the project dir (not a worktree). Track
lastSyncTimestamp to gate before-provision syncs. Hook sync into
three places: (1) start() — sync before bootstrap evaluation;
(2) reconcile timer — sync as first step of reconciliation pass,
skip if reviewer invocation active; (3) workspace provisioning path —
sync if lastSyncTimestamp > sync_interval ago. Use a running guard
(like ShadowSyncScheduler) so slow fetches don't stack. When no
remote is configured, all sync operations are skipped silently.

Covers: @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-pull-target-on-start,
ac-pull-target-periodic, ac-pull-target-periodic-deferred,
ac-pull-target-before-provision, ac-pull-ff-only,
ac-transient-no-degrade, ac-no-remote.

tasks.title: Implement dispatch engine degraded state
tasks.description:
Why: When the integration target branch diverges from remote (local
has unpushed merges, or remote was force-pushed), the engine cannot
provision workspaces from a reliable base. It needs a degraded state
that blocks new work while letting in-flight work finish, with clear
operator guidance and automatic recovery.

What: A degraded state machine for the dispatch engine. Enters
degraded when fast-forward sync fails due to divergence. Blocks new
workspace provisioning. Exposes degraded status via CLI and API.
Broadcasts state transitions on WebSocket. Auto-recovers when the
next periodic sync succeeds. Tracks consecutive transient failure
count for escalated warnings (threshold 5) without entering degraded.

How: Add a degraded state object to DispatchEngine: { active: boolean,
reason: string, enteredAt: Date | null }. In syncTargetBranch(),
classify failures: ff-only rejection with local-ahead = "unpushed
merges" guidance, ff-only rejection with remote-rewritten = "force
push" guidance. When degraded is active, the drain loop skips
provisioning but continues processing in-flight invocations. On
successful sync while degraded, clear the state and trigger a queue
drain. Track consecutiveTransientFailures counter (reset on any
success); log escalated warning when threshold exceeded. Extend
status() response with { degraded: { active, reason, enteredAt } }.
Extend the dispatch status CLI to show a prominent warning line.
Broadcast sync_state events on the agents WebSocket topic on
enter/exit.

Covers: @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-divergence-enters-degraded,
ac-divergence-log-guidance, ac-degraded-no-provision,
ac-degraded-status-api, ac-degraded-status-broadcast,
ac-degraded-auto-recover, ac-degraded-recovery-logged,
ac-repeated-transient-escalation, ac-repeated-transient-no-degrade.

All 9 ACs covered by 13 new tests. 2 nits recorded (unused _mergeOutput param, misleading test comments on divergence case classification).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Implemented degraded state machine for the dispatch engine. Key design decisions: (1) Divergence classification uses git rev-list to count local-ahead and remote-ahead commits, distinguishing three cases: unpushed merges (local only), remote rewrite (remote only), and mutual divergence. Each case includes operator-actionable resolution steps. (2) Transient failures track both count and first-failure timestamp for duration reporting in escalation warnings at threshold 5 — these never enter degraded state per spec. (3) Recovery triggers a queue drain so pending tasks get processed immediately. (4) WebSocket broadcast uses a new SyncStateEvent type on the 'agents' topic. (5) CLI shows prominent DEGRADED banner with reason, resolution, and duration. All 13 new tests pass; all 14 existing target-sync tests pass; full suite has 1 pre-existing failure in review-cli.test.ts (examined_commit field, unrelated).

tasks.title: Implement dispatch branch push lifecycle
tasks.description:
Why: Dispatch branches exist only locally. If the host dies or the
worktree is cleaned up, all in-flight work is lost. Pushing to remote
provides durability, visibility for other developers/CI, and enables
the resume-from-remote path that workspace.ts already partially
supports (tryRestoreBranchFromRemote).

What: Push dispatch branches to remote at key lifecycle points:
first invocation completion (set upstream tracking, safely replace
stale remote refs from previous runs), subsequent invocation
completions (normal push), and the integration target after reviewer
merges. Also push the integration target during periodic sync when
it has unpushed commits (retry for failed post-merge pushes). Delete
remote dispatch branches on workspace cleanup. Serialize integration
target pushes so at most one runs at a time. All push failures are
non-fatal.

How: Add pushDispatchBranch() and pushIntegrationTarget() helpers.
pushDispatchBranch detects whether upstream tracking exists (via
git rev-parse @{u}) to decide first-push vs normal-push behavior.
First push uses --force-with-lease to safely handle stale remote
refs (ac-first-push-replaces-stale-ref). Hook into dispatch.ts
post-invocation path (fire-and-forget with error logging).
pushIntegrationTarget uses a dedicated mutex (separate from
shadowMutex) so concurrent pushes skip rather than queue. Hook into:
(1) reviewer merge completion, (2) periodic sync (check
isAheadOfUpstream before pushing). For cleanup
(ac-cleanup-remote-branch), extend the existing workspace cleanup in
workspace.ts to delete the remote ref when the workspace has upstream
tracking. Respect remote_sync config toggle. Skip when no remote.

Covers: @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-first-push-sets-tracking,
ac-first-push-replaces-stale-ref, ac-subsequent-push,
ac-push-non-fatal, ac-push-target-after-merge,
ac-push-target-periodic, ac-target-push-serialization,
ac-cleanup-remote-branch, ac-no-remote.

Integrated into DispatchEngine post-invocation, periodic reconciliation, and workspace cleanup paths. All push failures are non-fatal. 9 ACs covered with 19 tests. tasks.title: Replace CLI local computeDisposition with shared implementation
tasks.description:
Replace the naive local computeDisposition (line 117 of src/cli/commands/review.ts) and computeGateState (line 132) with the shared implementations: computeDisposition from src/parser/review-operations.ts and evaluateGates from src/review/checks.ts.

The local computeDisposition ignores version staleness, gate state, and unresolved blockers — it just checks if any verdict is request_changes or approve. The local computeGateState ignores version staleness on checks.

The shared computeDisposition considers effective verdicts (filtered by version staleness), gate evaluation, and unresolved blocker threads. The shared evaluateGates handles check staleness and returns a GateEvaluationResult object (not a string).

Why: The CLI, daemon (packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts), and web UI must agree on disposition and gate state. The local reimplementations produce different results — the CLI shows 76 approved reviews while the daemon shows 4. This makes the CLI output unreliable and masks data inconsistencies.

1. Remove the local computeDisposition function (lines 117-126 of src/cli/commands/review.ts)
2. Remove the local computeGateState function (lines 132-137)
3. Import computeDisposition from ../parser/review-operations.js
4. Import evaluateGates from ../review/checks.js and extractSubjectVersion from ../review/subject-bindings.js
5. Replace computeGateState calls with evaluateGates + version extraction. evaluateGates returns a GateEvaluationResult object (with .state, .checks, .summary) — extract .state for the current gate_state string usage

tasks.title: Remediate existing review data with version mismatches
tasks.description:
Write a one-time migration script to fix applies_to_version on existing verdicts and checks that have type mismatches with their review's subject. Of 110 existing reviews, the daemon computes only 4 as approved (correct: 76) because verdicts/checks were stamped with code_compare versions on task-subject reviews.

The daemon computes disposition dynamically via computeDisposition() in src/parser/review-operations.ts, so correcting the stored applies_to_version will immediately fix the web UI display without any daemon code changes.

Why: After the CLI fix (@task-cli-verdict-auto-version and @task-cli-check-auto-version), new reviews will have correct versions, but the 110 existing reviews will remain broken in the web UI. The data must be corrected for the reviews index to show accurate dispositions.

How:
1. Write a script that loads all review records from the shadow branch via loadReviewRecords()
2. For each review, extract the subject version via extractSubjectVersion(review.subject) from src/review/subject-bindings.ts
3. For each verdict and check, compare applies_to_version.type with the subject version type
4. If mismatched in either direction (code_compare on entity subject, or entity_version on code subject), replace applies_to_version with the version derived from the review subject. Note: if the review subject itself has changed since the verdict was created (e.g. via refreshSubject), the corrected version will still be 'stale' relative to the current subject — this is correct behavior, not a bug
5. Save the corrected reviews and commit to shadow branch
6. Verify daemon API now returns correct dispositions by querying GET /api/reviews?status=all and checking disposition counts
7. Delete the script after use — it's a one-time fix

tasks.title: Dispatch engine CLI calls must not crash the engine on failure
tasks.description:
**What:** Any kspec CLI call from the dispatch engine (`_runKspecCommand`, `_addTaskNote`, `_blockTask`) that fails must not crash the engine. Currently, `_blockTask` throws a `DispatchMutationError` when the CLI exits non-zero. When this happens inside the workspace provisioning catch block in `_spawnInvocation`, the throw escapes and propagates through `_drainQueues` → `_serializedDrain` → `_bootstrap`, crashing the entire engine startup. The same pattern exists in `_addTaskNote` and anywhere `_runKspecCommand` is called from error recovery paths.

**Why:** This crashed a live dispatch engine: workspace provisioning failed (pre-existing worktree), the engine tried to block the task via CLI, the CLI failed (broken `bin/kspec.cjs` path), `_blockTask` threw, and the bootstrap crashed. The engine appeared "running" but could never drain queues again. Tasks sat queued for 12+ minutes with no invocations spawning.

**How:** Make `_blockTask` and `_addTaskNote` non-throwing when called from error recovery paths. Options:
1. Wrap all `_blockTask`/`_addTaskNote` calls in try/catch at their call sites in `_spawnInvocation` error handlers — log warnings on failure but always return gracefully
2. Or make `_blockTask`/`_addTaskNote` themselves catch and log rather than throw (simpler, but changes their contract for callers that want strict behavior)

Option 1 is safer — keep the strict throw behavior for non-recovery paths but ensure error handlers never propagate. Also audit all `_runKspecCommand` call sites in dispatch.ts to verify none can crash the engine.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev as b90454547ad1951c1f8cdd0677196add75195667 after review approval. Verified npm test passes (286 files, 6514 tests). tasks.title: Handle git worktree collisions between multiple project checkouts
tasks.description:
**What:** When two checkouts of the same repo (e.g., `kynetic-spec` and `kynetic-spec-dispatch`) each run dispatch, git worktrees are repo-global — a worktree created from one checkout is visible to the other via the shared `.git/worktrees` pool. If one checkout provisions a worktree at a path, the other checkout's `git worktree add` fails with "path already exists and is not a registered git worktree."

**Why:** This caused a live dispatch failure: an accidental dispatch run in `kynetic-spec` created a worktree at `kynetic-spec/.kspec-worktrees/<task-slug>`. When `kynetic-spec-dispatch`'s engine later tried to provision for the same task, it resolved a different `worktree_root` (correctly, to `kynetic-spec-dispatch/.kspec-worktrees/`) but found no collision there. However, the git repo already had a worktree registered at the first path, and provisioning failed when it tried to create a second worktree on the same branch. The engine should scope workspace identity to its own `projectDir` and treat worktrees owned by other checkouts as foreign.

**How:** During workspace provisioning, when `git worktree add` fails due to a path conflict:
1. Check if the existing worktree path is under a different project's `worktree_root` (compare against `this.projectDir`)
2. If so, treat it as a foreign worktree — don't reuse it, don't error fatally
3. Either provision at the engine's own `worktree_root` with a disambiguated path, or surface a clear error explaining the cross-checkout collision with actionable guidance

Also consider: the workspace registry in `.kspec/` is shared (same shadow branch). Records with `worktree_root` pointing to a different checkout should be ignored by the current engine during reconciliation and health checks. New spec AC ac-8 on `@dispatch-workspace-configuration` covers this behavior.

tasks.title: Auto-unregister projects when watcher detects permanent directory removal
tasks.description:
**What:** When the file watcher determines a project's `.kspec/` directory is permanently unavailable (ac-34), the daemon should proactively unregister the project instead of leaving a stale entry. Currently the watcher stops itself but the project remains registered as a ghost in ProjectContextManager.

**Why:** Ephemeral test directories and accidentally registered projects leave stale entries that pollute the project picker, trigger recovery loops, and waste watcher resources. Existing ac-20 handles reactive cleanup (on next request), but the daemon should also clean up proactively when it already knows the directory is gone.

**How:**
- Add an optional `onPermanentFailure` callback to `KspecWatcher` (packages/daemon/src/watcher.ts)
- In `handleWatcherError()`, after exhausting retries and confirming the directory is gone, invoke the callback with the project path
- In `ProjectContextManager.startWatcher()` (packages/daemon/src/project-context.ts), pass a callback that calls `unregisterProject()` for that path
- `unregisterProject()` already handles stopping the watcher, removing from registry, and cleaning up — just needs to be triggered from the watcher death path

tasks.title: Implement cancelled-task dependency cleanup during task cancellation
tasks.description:
What: Extend task cancellation so cancelling a task also removes that task from downstream depends_on arrays, records the cleanup on affected tasks, and leaves the task graph in a consistent post-cancellation state.

Why: A cancelled prerequisite represents abandoned work, not completed work. Leaving downstream dependency links in place creates stale blocking state and forces operators to manually repair task graphs after routine cancellation decisions.

How: Update the cancellation flow to discover downstream tasks that reference the cancelled task, remove those dependency refs, append clear audit notes on affected tasks, and persist the task cancellation plus downstream cleanup as one atomic shadow mutation. Preserve current ready semantics so only completed dependencies satisfy readiness; downstream tasks should become ready only because the cancelled dependency link was explicitly removed. Add direct test coverage for zero, one, and many downstream dependents, unchanged unrelated tasks, downstream readiness after cleanup, and no observable partial state after the command completes.

tasks.title: Fix shared-checkout integration branch targeting when current branch differs

What: Fix dispatch shared-checkout integration targeting so sync/push and related integration-branch mutations do not require the configured integration branch to be the currently checked-out branch in the shared checkout. Dispatch should verify the configured integration branch exists locally and/or remotely; if it does not exist locally but does exist remotely, create or restore the local branch and use it as the mutation surface. Why: The current refusal path and DEGRADED error that says dispatch will not mutate the integration target when the shared checkout is on another branch was not the intent. It contradicts the approved shared-checkout plan, which treats shared-checkout correctness as the product contract rather than requiring one branch topology. In practice, it is often ideal for the human-facing shared checkout to have some other branch checked out while dispatch still targets the configured integration branch safely and deterministically.

How: Replace the current-branch equality guard in the isolated integration-target path with branch existence and resolution logic for the configured integration branch. Reuse existing branch resolution and branch-restore helpers where possible, ensure the isolated targeting path can create/use the integration branch when it exists remotely, and preserve checkout coherence and non-clobbering safety checks so dispatch only refuses truly ambiguous or destructive cases. Update regression coverage so tests assert: (1) non-checked-out integration branch still syncs/pushes through the shared checkout correctly, (2) missing local branch is restored/created from remote when available, (3) already-checked-out integration branch still works, and (4) task worktrees remain untouched.

tasks.title: Add CLI mutation input validation
tasks.description:
**What:** Add validateEnumOption() checks to all CLI mutation commands
that accept typed options without runtime validation. Audit identified
9 unvalidated enum options across mutation commands: task add --type,
item add --type, item set --type/--status/--maturity, inbox promote
--type, plan add/set --status, review check add --status.

**Why:** These commands persist invalid values to shadow branch YAML
files. On next read, safeParse drops those records silently — the
primary data corruption vector reported in GitHub #899. Fixing
mutations is highest priority because it prevents new corruption.

**How:** Each fix follows the existing validated pattern at
src/cli/commands/task.ts line 1067 (task add --automation):
1. Import the Zod schema (e.g. TaskTypeSchema from ../../schema/common.js)
2. Call validateEnumOption(value, Schema.options, "field name") before
   the value is used
3. On failure: call error() with the result message and process.exit()
4. On success: use the validated value

Specific locations:
- src/cli/commands/task.ts ~line 1147: task add --type (TaskTypeSchema)
- src/cli/commands/item.ts line 708: item add --type (ItemTypeSchema)
- src/cli/commands/item.ts line 1089: item set --type (ItemTypeSchema)
- src/cli/commands/item.ts: item set --status (ImplementationStatusSchema),
  --maturity (MaturitySchema)
- src/cli/commands/inbox.ts: inbox promote --type (TaskTypeSchema)
- src/cli/commands/plan.ts: plan add/set --status (PlanStatusSchema)
- src/cli/commands/review.ts: review check add --status (ReviewCheckStatusSchema)

Covers: @cli-input-type-safety ac-1, ac-3.

tasks.title: Tighten daemon API input schemas
tasks.description:
**What:** Replace loose t.String() with strict t.Union([t.Literal(...)])
in Elysia schemas for all daemon API endpoints that accept typed fields.
This covers both mutation endpoints (8 with loose enum body fields) and
query endpoints (7+ routes with loose enum filter params).

**Why:** The web UI uses these endpoints. Loose t.String() schemas mean
arbitrary values are accepted. For mutations, this risks data corruption.
For queries, this causes silent empty results on typos — the same problem
as CLI filters. Framework-level Elysia validation rejects requests before
the handler runs.

**How:** For each endpoint, replace loose Elysia types with strict unions
derived from Zod schemas. Reference pattern exists at
packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts (PATCH /api/meta/agents/:id) which
uses Schema.options.map(v => t.Literal(v)).

Mutation endpoints:
- packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts:
  POST /comments: kind, anchor.type, anchor.side
  POST /verdicts: decision
  POST /checks: status
  PATCH /lifecycle: target
- packages/daemon/src/routes/triage.ts:
  POST /: action
  POST /:ref/override: action
- packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts:
  POST /events: from_status, to_status

Query/filter endpoints:
- packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts: GET /api/tasks — status, type,
  automation filter params
- packages/daemon/src/routes/items.ts: GET /api/items — type, maturity,
  implementation filter params
- packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts: GET /api/reviews — status,
  disposition filter params
- packages/daemon/src/routes/triage.ts: GET /api/triage — status, action
- packages/daemon/src/routes/plans.ts: GET /api/plans — status
- packages/daemon/src/routes/sessions routes — status, agent_type
- packages/daemon/src/routes/validation.ts: search — type, status

Keep existing manual handler validation as defense-in-depth.

Covers: @api-input-type-safety ac-1 through ac-4.

in src/parser/yaml.ts, and tighten PlanSpecSchema.type from

tasks.title: Consolidate type definitions to schema source of truth
tasks.description:
**What:** Replace all hardcoded enum arrays, Elysia literal unions,
CLI help text values, and type assertions with derivations from the
canonical Zod schemas. Also resolve the automation status divergence
where three independent Zod schemas define incompatible value sets
for the same semantic concept.

**Why:** The audit found 5 hardcoded enum arrays in daemon routes,
10+ CLI help strings with hardcoded values, and type assertions in
aggregation routes — all duplicating what Zod schemas already define.
Worse, there are 3 incompatible "automation" enums:
- AutomationStatusSchema (task.ts): eligible, needs_review, manual_only
- TaskEventPayload automation (event-payloads.ts): eligible, not_eligible, assisted
- AgentDispatchFilterSchema (meta.ts): eligible, ineligible
Only "eligible" overlaps across all three. These must be reconciled.

**How:**
1. Reconcile automation enums — determine the canonical set and
   derive the others from it, or document why they are intentionally
   different domains

2. Replace hardcoded arrays in daemon routes with schema derivations:
   - packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts: VALID_TASK_STATUSES
     → derive from TaskStatusSchema.options
   - packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts: VALID_DECISIONS,
     VALID_CHECK_STATUSES, VALID_LIFECYCLE_TARGETS, validKinds,
     validSides → derive from corresponding Review*Schema.options
   - packages/daemon/src/routes/aggregation.ts: remove type assertions
     with hardcoded enum values

3. Replace Elysia hardcoded literals:
   - packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts line 108: automation literal
     union → derive from schema like line 105 does for dispatch events

4. Make CLI help text derive from schemas. Either:
   (a) Generate help strings: `"Task type (${TaskTypeSchema.options.join(', ')})"` or
   (b) Accept that help text is documentation and may list a subset,
       but validation must use the schema

5. Follow existing correct patterns:
   - src/triage/constants.ts: `VALID_ACTIONS = TriageActionSchema.options`
   - meta.ts:105: `t.Union(Schema.options.map(v => t.Literal(v)))`

Covers: @schema-derived-type-definitions ac-1 through ac-4.

tasks.title: Fix reviews API status filter validation mismatch
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev after approved review @01KM6D0SQGK35V7A845JPDABRN. Preserved GET /api/reviews open-by-default behavior while updating UI callers to request all valid lifecycle states explicitly, eliminating invalid status=all requests. Verified with kspec validate (warnings only, pre-existing) and npm test (6690 passed, 3 skipped).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## What

The reviews API status filter sends 'all' as a query param value, but the Elysia validation schema only accepts valid ReviewLifecycleState values: draft, open, closed, archived. This causes validation_error on two code paths:

1. **Reviews list page** (`packages/web-ui/src/routes/reviews/+page.svelte:31`): `getStatusFilter()` returns literal 'all' when user selects "All statuses", sent as `?status=all`.
2. **Task detail modal** (`packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts:1700`): `fetchReviewsForTask()` hardcodes `url.searchParams.set('status', 'all')` to fetch all reviews for a task regardless of lifecycle state.

The daemon route handler (`packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts:154`) has logic to treat 'all' as "skip filtering", but Elysia's schema validation (`enumArrayUnion(ReviewLifecycleStateSchema.options)` at line 246) rejects the request before the handler runs.

## Why

This was introduced by the input validation hardening work (@plan-input-validation-hardening). The validation correctly restricts to valid enum values, but the UI was relying on a non-enum sentinel value 'all' that predated the validation.

## How

Three coordinated changes:

### 1. Backend: Change no-param default from 'open' to 'no filter'
**File:** `packages/daemon/src/routes/reviews.ts` lines 150-156
- Currently: no status param → defaults to `['open']`
- Change to: no status param → no filtering (show all)
- Remove the `statusFilters[0] !== 'all'` special case (dead code after validation was added)

### 2. UI reviews page: Flip the default/all semantics
**File:** `packages/web-ui/src/routes/reviews/+page.svelte`
- Default page load: navigate with explicit `?status=open` (so "Open" is still the landing view)
- "All statuses" option: remove the status param entirely (no param = no filter = all)
- Update `getStatusFilter()` (line 30-34): remove the `'all'` return path; when URL has no status param, treat as "all" (undefined → no param sent to API)
- The page should load with `?status=open` on initial navigation (or redirect if no status param) so the user still sees open reviews by default

### 3. Task modal: Remove hardcoded status=all
**File:** `packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts` line 1700
- Remove `url.searchParams.set('status', 'all')` — with the backend change, no status param means all reviews

### Verification
- Navigate to /reviews → should show open reviews, URL has `?status=open`
- Select "All statuses" → URL loses status param, shows all reviews, no validation error
- Select specific status → URL has that status, filters correctly
