tasks.title: Implement CLI daemon proxy detection and routing
tasks.description:
Add daemon detection to CLI startup and command routing logic so
commands are transparently proxied through the daemon when available.

Why: With the entity cache and command API in place, the CLI can
route through the daemon to make it the single writer. CLI mutations
go through the daemon, the daemon updates its cache immediately,
and all clients (web UI, other CLI instances, agents) see consistent
state.

What:
- Daemon detection on CLI startup: read port file from
  ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port, send health check ping to that port
- Fast failure: if port file doesn't exist or connection is refused,
  skip to direct mode within 50ms. If health check doesn't respond,
  timeout within 200ms and skip to direct mode.
- Command routing: when daemon is detected, serialize the CLI
  command into a command API payload and POST to the daemon's
  command endpoint. Deserialize the response, write stdout/stderr
  to process streams, exit with the returned exit code.
- Timeout handling: if a read-only command times out, fall back to
  direct mode and emit a warning on stderr. If a mutating command
  times out, return an error (no fallback) because the daemon may
  still be processing the mutation
- KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1: skip daemon detection entirely, go straight
  to direct mode
- --daemon flag: require daemon routing, fail with clear error if
  daemon is unavailable (no fallback)
- Project registration: if daemon is running but current project
  is not registered, register it before routing the command
- Detection result cached for the CLI process lifetime — don't
  re-detect per subcommand

How: Detection runs early in the CLI preAction hook
(src/cli/index.ts). Use the existing port file reading logic from
src/cli/commands/serve.ts. For command serialization, reuse the
batch command JSON format (command path + args object). Use
fetch() for HTTP calls — Bun and Node both support it natively.
Cache the detection result in module-level state (same pattern as
syncMode).

Covers: @cli-daemon-proxy ac-auto-detect, ac-direct-fallback,
ac-force-direct, ac-force-proxy, ac-transparent-output,
ac-mutation-coherence, ac-read-from-cache, ac-timeout-fallback,
ac-timeout-mutation-error.
@daemon-proxy-detection ac-port-file-check, ac-fast-detection,
ac-health-timeout, ac-project-registered.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Creating src/cli/daemon-proxy.ts module for daemon detection, health check, project registration, and command routing. 

Detection runs early in preAction hook. Uses PidFileManager.readPort() for port file check, fetch() for health check with 200ms timeout, and caches result at module level (same pattern as syncMode).

Command routing serializes to batch JSON format (command + args) and POSTs to daemon /api/command endpoint with X-Kspec-Dir header. Reads response stdout/stderr/exitCode and writes to process streams.

Timeout handling: read-only commands fall back to direct mode with stderr warning; mutating commands return error (no fallback).

KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 skips detection entirely. --daemon flag requires daemon routing, fails with error if unavailable.

Edge cases: project registration before routing, connection refused fast-fail, port file missing fast-fail.

tasks.title: Enhance test runner with smart caching and condensed output
tasks.description:
## What

Enhance `scripts/test.cjs` to:

1. **Condensed output by default** — Instead of streaming all vitest output to stdout, capture it and show only:
   - On success: final summary stats (test files, tests, duration) — no individual test results
   - On failure: only failed tests with condensed error messages, plus the summary
   - Always: the path to the full log file

2. **JSON-based log capture** — Use vitest's native dual-reporter support:
   - `--reporter=json --outputFile.json=<path>` for structured machine-readable results
   - `--reporter=verbose --outputFile.verbose=<path>` for full human-readable log
   - Parse the JSON after vitest exits to produce the condensed terminal output

3. **Content-based caching to skip redundant runs** — Compute a deterministic cache key from:
   - `git ls-files -s` blob SHAs for test-affecting paths (src/, tests/, packages/*/src/, package-lock.json, vitest.config.ts, tsconfig.json) — blob hashes are pure content hashes, unaffected by commits/rebases
   - `git diff` of unstaged changes against those same paths
   - Untracked file contents in those paths
   - `process.version` (Node version)
   - The vitest args passed to the script (so `npm test` and `npm test tests/foo.test.ts` are separate cache entries)
   If cache key matches a previous run, report results from cached JSON without re-running vitest.

4. **Session-scoped cache isolation** — Cache directory structure:
   - `/tmp/kspec-test-cache/<session-id>/<key>.json` when `KSPEC_SESSION_ID` is set (dispatch agents)
   - `/tmp/kspec-test-cache/_default/<key>.json` for interactive use
   This prevents parallel dispatch agents from interfering with each other's caches.

5. **`--fresh` flag** — Force a full re-run, clearing the session's cache directory.

6. **Agent documentation** — Add rules to the `testing` convention (via `kspec meta set`) covering:
   - Default caching behavior (won't re-run if repo state unchanged)
   - How to force fresh runs (`--fresh`)
   - Condensed output behavior and where full logs live
   - Session-awareness under dispatch

## Why

Currently the test script streams all vitest output unfiltered. This creates excessive noise — especially for agents that only need to know pass/fail and which tests broke. Agents in dispatch also frequently re-run the full suite redundantly when repo state hasn't changed (e.g., after committing already-tested code). Content-based caching avoids this waste while session isolation keeps parallel agents independent.

## How

All changes are in `scripts/test.cjs` plus convention updates:

- Replace `stdio: "inherit"` with piped stdout/stderr, streamed to log files in real-time
- Add `--reporter=json --outputFile.json=<tempfile>` and `--reporter=verbose --outputFile.verbose=<logfile>` to the vitest args
- After vitest exits, read the JSON file and format condensed output to terminal
- Implement cache key computation using `git ls-files -s`, `git diff`, and `child_process.execSync`
- Store/lookup cache entries in the session-scoped directory
- Add `--fresh` arg parsing alongside existing `--dry-run`
- Update testing conventions via `kspec meta set`

The key insight for caching: `git ls-files -s` outputs blob SHAs which are content-addressed — identical file contents always produce the same blob hash regardless of commit history. This means committing unchanged files does not invalidate the cache.

Key discovery: vitest's --outputFile only works for JSON/junit reporters, not verbose — solved by piping stdout/stderr in condensed mode and writing log file ourselves.

tasks.title: Fix pre-existing test failures: STACK_TRACE_ERROR, daemon timeouts, and CLI timeouts
tasks.description:
## What

Fix 30 failing tests across 10 test files that are failing on main. These are pre-existing failures unrelated to any recent work.

### Failure categories

**1. STACK_TRACE_ERROR (17 tests across 6 files)**

Vitest internal errors — likely import/module resolution or ESM issues causing tests to fail before assertions run.

Files affected:
- `tests/canonical-task-workspace-contract.test.ts` (1 test)
- `tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts` (5 tests)
- `tests/dispatch-target-sync.test.ts` (5 tests)
- `tests/dispatch-workspace-registry.test.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/setup-pipeline-unification.test.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/cli/session-note-limit.test.ts` (1 test)

All share the same stack trace pattern:
```
Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR
  at task (node_modules/@vitest/runner/dist/index.js:796:27)
  at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/@vitest/runner/dist/index.js:823:16)
```

**2. Daemon startup timeouts (5 tests in 1 file)**

`tests/cli-serve.test.ts` — All 5 tests fail with "Daemon failed to start within 5 seconds". The tests spawn `kspec serve start --daemon --port <random>` and poll for readiness.

**3. CLI command timeouts (3 tests in 2 files)**

- `tests/enhanced-setup.test.ts` (1 test) — `kspec setup --dry-run --skip-skills` times out at 30s
- `tests/native-guard-setup.test.ts` (2 tests) — `kspec setup` times out at 30s

**4. Mock assertion failure (1 test in 1 file)**

`tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts` — expects `runInvocation` spy to be called but it never fires. Likely a timing issue or changed internal API.

## Why

These failures cause the full test suite to exit non-zero, which blocks review gates on unrelated work. The test runner now caches failure results, so these will persist as cached failures until fixed.

## How

Investigation approach for each category:

**STACK_TRACE_ERROR:** Run one affected file in isolation with `--reporter=verbose` to see the actual import/resolution error. The generic STACK_TRACE_ERROR is vitest masking the real error. Check if these tests import modules that were recently refactored or renamed. May need import path fixes or missing re-exports.

**Daemon timeouts:** Check if the daemon binary path is correct (`dist/daemon/index.ts` run via Bun). Verify the health check endpoint. Consider increasing the 5-second timeout or checking if the daemon port binding is failing silently. Run `kspec serve start --daemon --port <port>` manually to see if it starts.

**CLI timeouts:** `kspec setup` timing out at 30s suggests it's blocking on something — possibly trying to fetch remote data, waiting for user input, or hitting a deadlock. Run `kspec setup --dry-run --skip-skills` manually with KSPEC_DEBUG=1 to see where it hangs.

**Mock assertion:** Read the test to understand what triggers `runInvocation`. Check if the function signature or call site changed. May need the mock setup updated to match current internals.

tasks.title: Fix: git subprocess interactive prompt hang in daemon/dispatch
tasks.description:
## What

When dispatch or the daemon's shadow sync scheduler runs on a cloned repo where the user lacks push/fetch credentials (e.g., a repo they don't own), git operations (fetch, push) trigger an interactive credential prompt (Username for https://github.com) instead of failing. This hangs the process indefinitely — the daemon and dispatch engine become unresponsive.

## Why

The existing specs (@dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-push-non-fatal, ac-transient-no-degrade) require that auth failures are caught and handled gracefully — logged as warnings, engine continues. However, the implementation spawns git subprocesses that inherit the default terminal prompt behavior. When no credential helper is configured (or it cannot authenticate), git blocks on stdin waiting for manual input. The error-handling code never executes because git never returns.

Affected code paths:
- Dispatch target sync: _syncTargetBranch() runs git fetch <remote> <branch> periodically and at startup
- Dispatch branch push: pushDispatchBranch() runs git push after invocation completion
- Integration target push: pushIntegrationTarget() runs git push after reviewer merges
- Shadow sync scheduler: ShadowSyncScheduler.syncOnce() runs fetchRemote() periodically from the daemon

## How

Set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 in the environment for all git subprocesses spawned by the dispatch engine and shadow sync scheduler. This environment variable tells git to fail immediately with an auth error instead of prompting for credentials interactively. The existing error-handling logic (non-fatal warnings, transient failure tracking, degraded state escalation) then works as the specs intend.

Specific locations to patch:
- All spawnSync/execSync git calls in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts that touch remote (fetch, push, ls-remote)
- The fetchRemote() call in src/parser/shadow-sync-scheduler.ts
- Any shared git utility used by these paths (check if there is a central spawn wrapper)

Prefer setting the env var at the lowest common layer (e.g., a shared git spawn helper if one exists) rather than at each individual call site.

tasks.title: Wire agent spawner into automation subsystem action executors
tasks.description:
The automation subsystems (schedule engine, hook executor, join accumulator) can execute command, kspec, and notify actions, but agent actions fail immediately with zero duration. The action executors for these subsystems are created without the ability to spawn agent invocations. The task-dispatch path works because it uses a separate invocation mechanism that doesn't share this limitation.

tasks.title: Extract setupShadowDetection() to shared test helpers
tasks.description:
What: The daemon-entity-cache.test.ts file contains a local setupShadowDetection() helper that initializes a git repo and creates a fake .kspec/.git worktree pointer in a project directory. This enables initContext() to detect the .kspec/ shadow worktree and resolve specDir correctly. Extract this helper to tests/helpers/cli.ts alongside the existing setupMultiDirFixtures(), initGitRepo(), and createTempDir() helpers so any future test can reuse it.

Why: setupMultiDirFixtures() creates project directories with .kspec/ subdirectories containing manifests and task data, but no git repos. Update daemon-entity-cache.test.ts to import from the shared location. Consider whether setupMultiDirFixtures() itself should call setupShadowDetection() on each project directory by default (evaluate whether any existing consumers would break — check that none rely on the no-git behavior). Add a JSDoc comment explaining why shadow detection setup is needed and when to use it.

tasks.title: Fix file watcher not starting for WebSocket-registered projects
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev in 39e80b193a2247ab9a52253c6cc9fc060da528fd after approving review @01KMSK834SEZEHF94MCSJFJV77. WebSocket project auto-registration now awaits watcher startup before binding the connection and rejects registration when watcher creation fails; focused daemon-session-sync coverage passes, and the unrelated daemon-command-api failures reproduce on base dev.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Root Cause

Four project registration paths exist in the daemon. Three start file watchers, one doesn't:

1. HTTP middleware (project-context.ts:113) — starts watcher ✓
2. POST /api/projects (projects.ts:87) — starts watcher ✓
3. Server startup (server.ts:559) — starts watcher ✓
4. WebSocket handler (project-resolution.ts:56) — does NOT start watcher ✗

The web UI connects via WebSocket first, registering the project with wasRegistered=true. This "uses up" the registration event without starting a watcher. All subsequent HTTP requests find wasRegistered=false and skip setup. The entity cache loads once during WebSocket registration and never invalidates.

## Impact

List endpoints (/api/tasks, /api/items, /api/sessions) serve stale cached data. Detail endpoints work because they fall back to disk reads.

## Recommended Fix

Centralize startWatcher() into the onProjectRegistered callback in server.ts so every registration path gets a watcher automatically. startWatcher is already idempotent (this.watchers.has() guard), so the startup project's explicit startWatcher call becomes a harmless no-op.

Optionally remove the now-redundant explicit startWatcher calls from HTTP middleware and POST /api/projects, or leave them as defense-in-depth no-ops.

## Tests Needed

- Unit test: WebSocket registration triggers startWatcher
- Integration test: after WebSocket registration, file changes invalidate the entity cache

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## What

Add a read-only GET /api/debug/cache-status endpoint that exposes the internal state of the entity cache registry and file watchers for all registered projects.

## Why

When investigating daemon issues (stale data, missing watchers, stuck cache domains), there is no way to inspect cache state without reading source code and guessing. During investigation of a bug where WebSocket-registered projects had stale list data, the inability to see per-domain cache state (ready vs loading vs degraded) and watcher status added significant debugging time. This endpoint provides introspection needed to diagnose daemon data issues quickly.

## How

### New public API surface on ProjectEntityCache (src/daemon/entity-cache.ts)

The cache module's internals are private. The endpoint needs new public methods:

1. A registry iterator — export a function like getAllRegisteredCaches() or listCacheProjects() to enumerate all projects in the cacheRegistry Map
2. getDomainEntryCount(domain) — returns index size and detail cache size for a domain (currently only getTaskIndex() etc. are available, no generic count method)
3. getDomainError(domain) — returns lastError for degraded domains (currently private on DomainStore)
4. Add a lastInvalidatedAt timestamp field to DomainStore — NOT currently tracked. Update it in invalidateDomain() and writeThrough() code paths.

### Route implementation (packages/daemon/src/routes/)

- New route factory createDebugRoutes({ getEntityCache, projectManager }) — this is the first route needing both data sources
- Combine entity cache data (domain states, counts, errors, timestamps) with ProjectContextManager data (watcher status)
- Response shape per project: { path, watcherStatus, domains: { tasks: { state, indexCount, detailCount, lastError, lastInvalidatedAt }, ... } }

### Documentation

- Add the endpoint to daemon API conventions or a meta convention so agents and developers know to use it for debugging
- Document the response shape and what each field means

### Notes

- No /api/debug/ namespace exists yet — this is the first endpoint. Sets a precedent for future debug tooling.
- No authentication beyond existing localhost-only binding.
- Read-only — no mutation risk.

tasks.title: Fix cache domain state regression during reload
tasks.description: What: loadDomain() sets store.state to loading before starting an async reload, causing API routes that gate on domain state to skip enrichment and return null data. Where: src/daemon/entity-cache.ts loadDomain() state transition (line ~800), doLoadDomain() index/detail population (lines 830-852). Downstream: packages/daemon/src/routes/sessions.ts task_title resolution guard (lines 597-632). Why: During active dispatch, frequent .kspec/ mutations trigger repeated domain reloads. Each reload flips state to loading, causing session detail endpoints to return null task_title. The UI renders the raw ULID, then re-fetches and gets the title back, visible as flickering. Fix by keeping state ready during reloads of already-populated domains and swapping in new data atomically on completion. Transition to degraded only on reload failure.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Fix loadDomain() to preserve ready state and serve stale data during reload.

Root cause: loadDomain() unconditionally sets store.state = 'loading' on line 800, even when the domain was previously 'ready'. This causes downstream guards (e.g., sessions.ts task_title resolution) that gate on state === 'ready' to skip enrichment during reloads, returning null data.

Fix plan:
1. In loadDomain(), when store.state is 'ready', skip setting state to 'loading' — keep it ready so reads continue to succeed
2. In doLoadDomain(), build new data into local variables first, then assign all properties at once at the end of the case block (semi-atomic swap). This prevents partial state where index is new but details are cleared.
3. On reload failure of a previously-ready domain, transition to 'degraded' (matches AC: graceful-degradation)
4. The 'loading' state only applies to first-time loads (from 'unloaded')

Test plan: Write tests for ac-stale-during-reload that verify:
- Domain state remains 'ready' during reload
- Old cached data remains accessible during reload
- New data replaces old after reload completes
- On reload error, domain transitions to 'degraded' (not back to 'loading')

tasks.title: Replace synchronous process spawning in dispatch engine
tasks.description: What: The dispatch engine uses spawnSync() for kspec CLI commands and git operations, blocking the Node.js event loop for 200ms-2s per call. Also bootstrap.ts and workspace.ts functions called from the dispatch path for workspace provisioning. Why: While spawnSync blocks, the daemon cannot serve HTTP or WebSocket requests. The UI sees timeouts and stale data. Error recovery paths chain 2 sequential spawnSync calls (400ms-2s total block). Convert all sync spawning in the dispatch execution path to async equivalents. - Error recovery paths (lines 2342-2420 in dispatch.ts) are best-effort and should use fire-and-forget async (no await needed per task description)
- _addTaskNote and _blockTask are called from both sync and async contexts — need to make callers async too

- pathExists can be replaced with fs.access (no child process needed)
- commandAvailable can use promisify(execFile)

- Fire-and-forget calls must not cause unhandled promise rejections

tasks.title: Fix workspace reconciliation cycle for completed task records
tasks.description: What: Workspace reconciliation enters an infinite restore-delete cycle for completed tasks whose branches were cleaned up. Registry reconciliation (reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry) calls reconcileWorkspaceHealth which unconditionally attempts tryRestoreBranchFromRemote when a canonical branch is missing locally. For terminal tasks (completed/cancelled with merged integration), this restores branches from remote tracking refs that serve no purpose. Artifact reconciliation (reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts) then deletes those same branches because they have no matching worktree, producing errors when timing misaligns. This repeats every reconciliation cycle, generating DispatchWorkspaceError noise for resolveCommit and deleteDispatchBranch failures. Where: src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts — reconcileWorkspaceHealth (tryRestoreBranchFromRemote call around line 1185), reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts (branch cleanup loop around line 2821), and deleteDispatchBranch. The two functions are called sequentially from dispatch.ts during periodic reconciliation. Why: reconcileWorkspaceHealth has no awareness of task terminal state or integration status — it treats every missing branch as needing recovery. reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts builds its tracked-branches set only from worktree entries with metadata, so registry-only records (no worktree on disk) are invisible to it. The two phases have no shared view of which branches should exist. Fix requires two changes: (1) health reconciliation must check task and integration status before attempting branch restoration (ac-12), (2) artifact reconciliation must consult the workspace registry when deciding whether an untracked-worktree branch is orphaned (ac-13).

Approach: Two targeted changes to break the restore-delete cycle.

AC-12 fix (reconcileWorkspaceHealth):
- Add taskStatus + integration status parameters to reconcileWorkspaceHealth
- Before calling tryRestoreBranchFromRemote, check if task is in terminal state (completed/cancelled) AND integration is merged/abandoned
- If so, skip the branch restoration and instead return the last persisted health state or a degraded healthy status (branch is expected to be missing for terminal+merged records)
- This prevents the futile restore that artifact reconciliation will undo

AC-13 fix (reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts):
- Load registry records at the start of artifact reconciliation
- Build a Map of canonical_branch -> record for quick lookup
- In the orphan branch cleanup loop (line 2821-2826), before deleting a dispatch branch, check if it belongs to a registry record
- If the record exists and is in closing/closed/cleanup_blocked state with merged/abandoned integration, allow deletion (cleanup is expected)
- If the record exists and is NOT in a terminal/cleanup state, skip deletion (branch is still needed)
- If no record exists, proceed with deletion as before (true orphan)

Edge cases:
- Records in 'stale' state with missing branch should still be preserved (may be recoverable)
- Records transitioning through cleanup should still allow branch deletion when the reaper handles it
- The trackedBranches set from worktree metadata remains authoritative for worktree-backed branches

tasks.title: Fix dispatch shadow mutation lock contention and leak between daemon and agents
tasks.description:
## What

The dispatch shadow mutation file lock (.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation) suffers from two related failures:

1. **Lock leak**: The daemon process (workspace.ts withDispatchShadowMutationLock) acquires the lock for workspace lifecycle operations but can fail to release it. When this happens, the daemon PID remains alive, so the existing stale-lock detection (which only checks for dead PIDs) cannot reclaim the lock. All agent CLI mutations are blocked indefinitely.

2. **Lock monopolization during reconciliation**: reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry (workspace.ts:2153) acquires the file lock once for the entire batch of non-closed workspace records, then performs N git operations per record (refExists, resolveCommit, findExistingWorktreeForBranchUnderRoot, pathExists) plus conditional saves and a shadow branch commit. With multiple active workspaces this holds the lock for seconds, starving concurrent agent CLI mutations.

Both failures produce the same symptom: reviewer (or worker) agents cannot run any mutating kspec command (review verdict, task complete, task note, etc.) and burn their entire session retrying.

## Why

The dispatch engine, worker agents, and reviewer agents all compete for the same file lock:

- The daemon acquires it during workspace reconciliation (every 60s), state change handling, and invocation lifecycle management (mark active/idle).
- Worker agents acquire it for every mutating kspec CLI command (task note, task submit, etc.) via the preAction hook in cli/index.ts.
- Reviewer agents acquire it for every mutating kspec CLI command (review verdict, task complete, etc.) via the same hook.

The lock exists to serialize shadow branch writes and prevent concurrent commits from corrupting the worktree. This is correct. But the current implementation has no mechanism to:
- Guarantee release if the holder gets stuck (ac-7)
- Enforce a maximum hold duration (ac-8)
- Yield between record evaluations during batch reconciliation (ac-9)
- Reclaim from an alive-but-stuck holder (ac-10)
- Protect against shadow branch corruption when force-reclaiming (ac-11)

Observed in dispatch session 01KMV580P5VCWH2WFYCJCD9B3H: 269 lock timeout errors over 16 minutes. The reviewer agent could not complete a single mutation. Lock holder was PID of the daemon process. A subsequent reviewer session (01KMV6PRTZEJYVPHKKW5S3DGQC) hit the same issue with a leaked lock held for 48+ minutes.

## How

### 1. Lock release guarantee (ac-7)
Audit ALL acquireFileLock call sites. Ensure every acquisition is wrapped in try/finally that calls release(). The withDispatchShadowMutationLock wrapper already does this, but verify no code path acquires outside the wrapper. Add a safety timeout to the release() call itself so a failed release doesn't silently swallow the error.

Call sites to audit:
- withDispatchShadowMutationLock (workspace.ts:1389) — the main wrapper
- persistWorkspaceRecord (workspace.ts:1454) — via the wrapper
- reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry (workspace.ts:2153) — via the wrapper
- cleanupReviewerDispatchWorkspace (workspace.ts:2606) — direct acquisition
- provisionDispatchWorkspace (workspace.ts:3156) — direct acquisition
- reapDispatchWorkspace and related lifecycle functions (workspace.ts:3533, 3653, 3750)
- maybeAcquireDispatchMutationLock (cli/index.ts:93) — CLI preAction hook

### 2. Maximum hold duration ceiling (ac-8)
Add a configurable max-hold-duration to the lock metadata (written alongside PID and timestamp in the lock directory). Configuration via KSPEC_SHADOW_MUTATION_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_MS environment variable, defaulting to 30000ms. When a waiting process checks staleness, compare elapsed time against the ceiling. If exceeded, treat as reclaimable regardless of PID liveness. The existing stale detection in file-lock.ts (which checks process.kill(pid, 0)) becomes one of two reclamation paths: dead PID OR exceeded ceiling.

Design note: this deliberately reverses the existing design principle in file-lock.ts (line ~119) that "age alone never breaks mutual exclusion." The rationale is that an alive-but-stuck holder blocking all agents for minutes is worse than the theoretical risk of reclaiming during a legitimately slow operation. The 30s default provides ample headroom for any normal operation.

### 3. Reconciliation lock granularity (ac-9)
Refactor reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry to acquire/release the file lock per-dirty-record rather than for the entire iteration. Each record that needs saving gets its own lock-acquire → save → commit → release cycle. Clean records (no state change) are evaluated without the file lock since they only read.

Performance consideration: this means N git commits instead of 1 per reconciliation cycle. Mitigate by only committing for records that are actually dirty (isWorkspaceRecordDirty returns true). In practice most records are clean during routine reconciliation, so the commit count stays low.

The in-memory shadowMutex in dispatch.ts should continue to serialize daemon-internal operations. The file lock yield only helps external CLI processes interleave — daemon-internal operations (handleStateChange, markActive, markIdle) still queue behind shadowMutex within the daemon process, which is correct for preventing daemon self-contention.

### 4. Alive-but-stuck reclamation (ac-10)
Extend the staleness check in acquireFileLock retry loop (file-lock.ts) to read the lock timestamp and compare against the max-hold-duration ceiling. If the lock has been held beyond the ceiling, reclaim it even if process.kill(pid, 0) succeeds. Log a diagnostic identifying the previous holder PID and hold duration.

### 5. Shadow worktree protection on force-reclaim (ac-11)
When a lock is reclaimed via the duration ceiling path (not the dead-PID path), the new holder must check the shadow worktree for uncommitted dirty state before starting its own mutation. If dirty state exists (uncommitted files from the previous holder's interrupted write), roll back with git checkout/reset before proceeding. This prevents the new holder from accidentally committing partial state from the old holder alongside its own changes.

tasks.title: Purge unrecoverable workspace records so non-terminal tasks can be re-provisioned
tasks.description:
## What

The dispatch scheduler permanently blocks non-terminal tasks from being provisioned when a workspace registry record exists but is unrecoverable. The task is enqueued on every reconciliation cycle, evaluated for queue eligibility, found unhealthy, and discarded — indefinitely.

## Why

Workspace provisioning is a two-phase operation: (1) write a registry record to the shadow branch, (2) create the canonical git branch and worktree. If the agent session fails between phases — for example, the spawned process crashes, times out, or hits a resource error before running `kspec task branch` — the registry record persists but the canonical branch never exists.

The queue eligibility check in `_workspaceCandidateHealth` uses a binary branch: if a workspace record exists, eligibility requires `health.healthy === true`. If the record doesn't exist, the task is eligible for fresh provisioning. There is no third path for "record exists but is unrecoverable." The existing discovery fallback only runs for resumable task states (in_progress, pending_review, needs_work) — not for pending tasks entering the queue via task.ready events.

This means any non-terminal task whose workspace was partially provisioned (record written, branch never created) is permanently stuck. Each reconciliation cycle re-enqueues and re-discards it, producing repeated log noise with no path to resolution.

## How

When the scheduler evaluates queue eligibility for a task with an existing but unhealthy workspace record:

1. After all recovery paths have been exhausted (local branch check, remote branch fallback, submission linkage adoption), and the workspace remains unrecoverable (health status invalid with missing canonical branch or equivalent).
2. If the task is in a non-terminal state (not completed, not cancelled).
3. Purge or reset the stale registry record so the task becomes eligible for fresh provisioning on the next dispatch cycle.

The fix should be in the `_workspaceCandidateHealth` method or the reconciliation path that feeds it. The key invariant: a stale workspace record must not permanently prevent a live task from being dispatched. The existing ac-5 correctly detects the unhealthy state; this work closes the gap between detection and resolution.

Spec coverage: @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-14.

Approach: AC-14 implementation for purging unrecoverable workspace records.

Problem: _workspaceCandidateHealth in dispatch.ts has no path for non-terminal tasks with existing but unrecoverable (health.status=invalid) workspace records. The record blocks fresh provisioning indefinitely.

Plan:
1. Add deleteDispatchWorkspaceRecord() in src/parser/dispatch-workspaces.ts — removes a workspace record by workspace_id atomically within the file lock, following the same raw YAML preservation pattern as save/mutate.

2. Modify _workspaceCandidateHealth in dispatch.ts:
   - After determining a workspace exists but is unhealthy (eligible=false, exists=true)
   - Check if the health reason indicates an unrecoverable state (health.status=invalid => missing_canonical_branch or missing_adopted_branch)
   - Check that the task is non-terminal (not completed/cancelled)
   - If both conditions met: purge the stale record via deleteDispatchWorkspaceRecord
   - Return {eligible: false, exists: false, reason: null} so the task becomes eligible on the NEXT cycle
   - This applies for ALL non-terminal tasks, not just resumable ones (the discovery fallback already handles resumable states)

3. The fix targets the gap between detection and resolution: ac-5 already detects the unhealthy state, this work closes the gap by purging the stale record.

Edge cases:
- Resumable tasks (in_progress/pending_review/needs_work) already go through discovery first. If discovery fails AND record is unrecoverable, same purge should apply.
- Non-resumable tasks (pending via task.ready) with unrecoverable workspaces get purged directly.
- Terminal tasks are excluded (they should proceed to cleanup, not re-provisioning).

tasks.title: Rewrite pagination ACs to behavioral language and add envelope ACs
tasks.description:
Two existing ACs prescribe the response wire format ({items, total,
offset, limit}) rather than describing pagination behavior. This
conflicts with the envelope normalization in this plan. Additionally,
@api-contract has no ACs for a normalized response envelope or typed
cache status signaling.

Why: @trait-api-endpoint ac-4 says "returns {items, total, offset,
limit} wrapper" and @api-contract ac-4 says "returns paginated
results with {items, total, offset, limit} wrapper." Both prescribe
a specific shape instead of describing the behavioral contract
(accepts pagination params, response includes total count and
pagination metadata). If left unchanged, the new envelope shape
{data, meta} would violate these ACs. The new envelope and cache
status ACs define what "correct" looks like for the server-side
migration.

What:
1. Rewrite @trait-api-endpoint ac-4 to: "accepts limit and offset
   query params, response includes the total count of matching
   items and the pagination parameters applied" — behavioral, no
   shape prescription.
2. Rewrite @api-contract ac-4 to: "returns paginated results
   including total count and the pagination parameters applied" —
   behavioral, endpoint-specific detail without shape.
3. Add two new ACs to @api-contract:

ac-envelope:
  Given: the daemon is running and receives an API request
  When: an endpoint that serves entity data from the cache returns
  a response
  Then: the response uses a normalized envelope with a typed data
  payload and a metadata object containing cache readiness state,
  and pagination fields (total, offset, limit) when applicable.
  Non-cache endpoints (health, projects, command, mutation

use "item ac add" on @api-contract. Use given/when/then block
scalars.

tasks.title: Add cache warming UX ACs to data freshness spec
tasks.description:
The @ui-data-freshness spec covers caching, invalidation, and
WebSocket-driven updates but has no ACs for cache warming behavior —
what the UI should do when the server reports its cache is still
loading. The warming UX tasks depend on these ACs.

Why: Four new behaviors need AC coverage: showing skeletons instead
of empty content, auto-transitioning when cache is ready, retry
fallback for missed events, and timeout error state. Without these
ACs, the warming UX has no testable contract.

What: Add four ACs to @ui-data-freshness using kspec batch:

ac-warming-skeleton:
  Given: the server signals that its cache is still warming
  When: the UI receives the response
  Then: a loading skeleton is displayed instead of empty content,
  and the warming response is not persisted in the client cache
  as real data

ac-warming-auto-transition:
  Given: the UI is displaying a loading skeleton due to cache warming
  When: a real-time event indicates the cache domain is ready
  Then: the affected queries are invalidated and the view transitions
  to real data without user interaction

ac-warming-retry-fallback:
  Given: the UI is displaying a loading skeleton due to cache warming
  When: no real-time domain-ready event has been received
  Then: the UI retries the request at short intervals as a fallback
  for missed or delayed real-time events

ac-warming-timeout:
  Given: the UI has been retrying a cache-warming response
  When: the retry ceiling (30 seconds) is reached without the cache
  becoming ready
  Then: the UI displays an error state with a manual retry option
  instead of continuing to show the loading skeleton

How: Use kspec batch with four "item ac add" commands targeting
@ui-data-freshness. Use given/when/then block scalars.

tasks.title: Define unified API response envelope type and wrapper
tasks.description:
Today, daemon API responses have inconsistent shapes: list endpoints
return {items, total, offset, limit}, aggregation endpoints return
{counts: {...}}, and cache warming state is an ad-hoc _cache_status
field mixed in at the top level. This makes it impossible for the
web UI to have a single response handling path.

Why: A normalized envelope is the prerequisite for centralized cache
warming detection in the UI. Without it, every fetch function needs
its own logic to find and interpret the cache status field, and the
UI cannot distinguish "cache is warming, data is empty" from "data
really is empty."

What: Define a generic ApiResponse<T> type with two fields: `data`
(typed payload — array for lists, object for aggregation/detail) and
`meta` (object with total, offset, limit as optional numbers, and
cache_status as a required "ready" | "loading" literal). Create a
server-side wrapper function (e.g. wrapResponse) that route handlers
call to construct envelope responses. Export the type from the shared
types package so the web UI can import it.

How: Add the Zod schema and TypeScript type to the shared types
package. The wrapper function takes the domain data, pagination
params, and cache domain state, and returns the envelope. For cache
warming responses, it returns {data: default-empty, meta: {
cache_status: "loading"}}. For normal responses, cache_status is
"ready". This is an internal contract change — no API versioning
needed since the only consumer is the web UI.

Covers: @api-contract ac-envelope.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Define ApiResponse<T> envelope type + CacheStatus type + wrapResponse helper.

Key files:
- packages/shared/src/api.ts — Add CacheStatus type, ApiResponseMeta, ApiResponse<T> interfaces
- packages/daemon/src/routes/response-envelope.ts — New file for wrapResponse() helper
- packages/shared/tests/types.test.ts — Add type tests for new types
- tests/api-response-envelope.test.ts — Behavioral tests for wrapResponse()

Design decisions:
1. CacheStatus = "ready" | "loading" (per ac-cache-status-field). Current codebase also uses "degraded" | "unloaded" but the task spec specifically calls for "ready" | "loading" literal. Will keep CacheStatus narrowed to what the spec requires.
2. ApiResponseMeta has: cache_status (required CacheStatus), total/offset/limit (optional numbers for pagination).
3. ApiResponse<T> = { data: T; meta: ApiResponseMeta }
4. wrapResponse() takes domain data, optional pagination, and cache domain state. Returns envelope.
5. This task only defines types and the wrapper. Route handler migration is a separate task (@task-migrate-route-handlers-envelope).
6. Existing PaginatedResponse<T> kept for backward compat — the migration task will update routes.

- Cache warming: wrapResponse returns {data: defaultEmpty, meta: {cache_status: "loading"}}
- Normal response: cache_status is "ready"
- Non-paginated endpoints: meta has cache_status but no pagination fields

tasks.title: Broadcast cache domain ready event via WebSocket
tasks.description:
The daemon's EntityCache tracks per-domain loading state (unloaded →
loading → ready/degraded) but does not notify WebSocket clients when
a domain finishes loading. The web UI currently has no way to know
when to refetch after receiving a cache-warming response except by
polling.

Why: WebSocket push is the primary mechanism for the UI to transition
from loading skeleton to real data. Without it, the UI must poll at
fixed intervals (2s), adding latency and unnecessary requests. The
daemon already has a PubSubManager that broadcasts entity mutation
events — domain-ready events follow the same pattern.

What: When EntityCache transitions a domain to "ready" from any
non-ready state (loading, degraded, or unloaded), broadcast a
domain_ready event on a "cache:status" topic via PubSubManager. The event payload includes
the domain name (e.g. "tasks", "items", "sessions") and the project
path. This event is scoped to the project, matching how entity
mutation broadcasts work.

How: In the EntityCache class (src/daemon/entity-cache.ts), after
the domain state transitions to "ready", call pubsub.broadcast()
with topic "cache:status", type "domain_ready", and payload
{domain, project}. The PubSub instance needs to be accessible from
EntityCache — either pass it in at construction or emit an event
that the route layer relays. Follow the existing broadcast pattern
used in route handlers (e.g. tasks.ts broadcasts on "tasks:updates"
after mutations).

Covers: @daemon-entity-cache ac-domain-ready-event.

tasks.title: Update web UI fetch functions for unified envelope
tasks.description:
The web UI's api.ts contains ~20 fetch functions (fetchTasks,
fetchItems, fetchInbox, fetchPlans, fetchSessions, fetchReviews,
etc.) that each return response.json() directly, typed to the old
per-endpoint shapes (e.g. PaginatedResponse<TaskSummary> with
{items, total, offset, limit}). After the server migrates to the
unified envelope, these functions will receive {data, meta} but
still expect the old shape.

Why: Without updating the fetch functions, TypeScript types will be
wrong, destructuring will break, and components will receive
undefined where they expect arrays. This is the client-side
counterpart of the server migration.

What: Update all fetch functions in the web UI API layer to unwrap
the envelope. Each function should extract response.data and
response.meta, returning the domain data to callers. Update the
TypeScript return types to match. The meta object (including
cache_status) must be inspectable before the data is returned —
the downstream cache warming interceptor
(@task-ui-cache-warming-interceptor) checks cache_status and throws
a CacheWarmingError for "loading" responses before data reaches
TanStack Query's cache.

How: Import the ApiResponse<T> type from shared types. Each fetch
function calls response.json() to get the envelope, then returns
the unwrapped result. For static mode (isStaticMode()), update the
static data helpers to return the same envelope shape — wrap their
pre-baked data with {data, meta: {cache_status: "ready"}}. This
means the unwrap path is identical for both live and static modes,
no branching needed. Update all TypeScript interfaces
(PaginatedResponse, etc.) to match the new contract. Update
component-level destructuring as needed.

Covers: @api-contract ac-envelope (client-side).

tasks.title: Implement cache warming detection and retry in query layer
tasks.description:
After the fetch functions unwrap the envelope, the web UI has access
to meta.cache_status on every response. But TanStack Query doesn't
know that a cache_status: "loading" response is transient — it caches
it with the normal 30s staleTime, meaning users see empty pages for
up to 30 seconds even after the server cache is ready.

Why: Cache warming responses must not be treated as successful data.
They need to trigger automatic retry so the UI refetches when the
server is ready. Without this, the existing staleTime (30s) and
retry config (1 retry, 1s delay) are insufficient — the UI caches
the empty response and stops trying.

What: Add a centralized mechanism in the query layer that detects
cache_status: "loading" responses and treats them as retryable
transient conditions rather than successful empty results. Configure
retry behavior: 2-second intervals, maximum 15 attempts (30-second
ceiling). The retry should be specific to cache warming — normal
successful-but-empty responses (cache_status: "ready" with zero
items) must NOT retry.

How: Two approaches to evaluate: (1) Throw a typed CacheWarmingError
from the fetch function when cache_status is "loading" — TanStack
Query's retry mechanism handles it naturally. The retry callback
checks error type to only retry CacheWarmingError. (2) Use TanStack
Query's queryFn meta or select to flag warming responses and
configure per-query retry. Option 1 is simpler and recommended.
Either way, the warming response must not enter the query cache as
successful data.

Covers: @ui-data-freshness ac-warming-retry-fallback,
ac-warming-timeout. Also covers ac-warming-skeleton's requirement
that warming responses are not persisted in the client cache — the
CacheWarmingError prevents TanStack Query from caching them as
successful data. The skeleton rendering itself is in
@task-ui-warming-skeletons.

tasks.title: Subscribe to cache domain ready events for query invalidation
tasks.description:
The web UI already subscribes to WebSocket events for entity mutation
invalidation (e.g. when a task is updated, the tasks query is
invalidated). Cache domain ready events need the same treatment —
when the server broadcasts that a domain finished loading, the UI
should invalidate queries for that domain so they refetch immediately
instead of waiting for the next retry interval.

Why: WebSocket push is faster and more efficient than retry polling.
When the daemon's tasks cache finishes loading, the UI should refetch
within milliseconds, not wait up to 2 seconds for the next retry.
This is the primary transition mechanism; retry is the fallback for
missed events or reconnection gaps.

What: Add a WebSocket subscription handler for the "cache:status"
topic alongside existing mutation topic handlers. When a
"domain_ready" event is received, map the domain name to TanStack
Query keys (e.g. domain "tasks" → query key ["tasks"], domain
"items" → query key ["items"]) and call
queryClient.invalidateQueries() for those keys. This triggers an
immediate refetch of any active queries for that domain.

How: The web UI's WebSocket handler (in the query/websocket
integration layer) already maps topics to query invalidation. Add
"cache:status" as a subscribed topic. The domain_ready event
payload includes {domain, project} — use the domain field to
determine which query keys to invalidate. If the domain maps to
multiple query keys (e.g. "meta" covers several endpoints), all
related keys should be invalidated.

Covers: @ui-data-freshness ac-warming-auto-transition.

tasks.title: Show loading skeletons and timeout error across all views
tasks.description:
The web UI has existing skeleton components (Skeleton, BoardSkeleton,
SessionStreamSkeleton, SidebarMenuSkeleton) but no view currently
uses them for cache warming. Views either show empty content or their
own initial loading state only on first mount. Once TanStack Query
has cached data (even an empty warming response), views show that
cached data with no indication that it's incomplete.

Why: This is the user-facing piece — without it, the interceptor and
WebSocket plumbing work correctly but users still see empty pages
during cache warming. The existing skeleton components were built
for exactly this purpose but have never been connected to the cache
warming signal.

What: Update all list views in the web UI to detect when the query
is in a cache-warming retry state and render the appropriate skeleton
component instead of empty content. Views to update: tasks board
(BoardSkeleton), items list, sessions list (SessionStreamSkeleton
for detail), inbox, plans, reviews, and triage. Also add a timeout
error state component: after 30 seconds of retrying, show an error
message ("Unable to load [entity]. The server cache did not become
ready.") with a manual Retry button that resets the retry counter
and tries again.

How: The cache warming interceptor (previous task) either throws
CacheWarmingError or sets a flag. TanStack Query's isError +
error type, or a custom isPending-like flag, can be checked in
each view's template. When warming is detected, render the skeleton.
When the retry ceiling is exceeded (error is CacheWarmingError and
failureCount >= 15), render the error state instead. The Retry
button calls queryClient.resetQueries() for the relevant key.

Covers: @ui-data-freshness ac-warming-skeleton (skeleton rendering
and view integration — the "not persisted in cache" requirement is
handled by @task-ui-cache-warming-interceptor), ac-warming-timeout
(error state UI and retry button).

tasks.title: E2E test for cache warming to ready transition
tasks.description:
There are no tests verifying the cache warming UX end-to-end. The
daemon's cache warming behavior, WebSocket domain_ready event, and
the UI's skeleton/error/transition flow need integration coverage
to prevent regression.

Why: The cache warming flow spans three systems (EntityCache →
WebSocket PubSub → TanStack Query + Svelte views). Unit tests for
individual pieces don't catch integration failures — e.g. the
WebSocket event fires but the query key mapping is wrong, or the
skeleton renders but doesn't transition when data arrives.

What: A Playwright E2E test with three scenarios: (1) Navigate to
a view while the daemon cache is still warming — verify that a
loading skeleton is visible instead of empty content. (2) After
the cache finishes warming, verify the skeleton is replaced by
real data without user interaction (driven by WebSocket
domain_ready event). (3) Simulate a cache that never becomes ready
(or takes >30s) — verify the error state appears with a working
Retry button.

How: Register a new project mid-test to trigger fresh cache warming
— this is the most realistic way to control timing without test-only
endpoints. Navigate to the new project's view immediately after
registration to catch the warming window. For the timeout scenario,
add a test-only daemon endpoint that injects an artificial delay
into cache domain loading (behind a KSPEC_TEST flag) so the 30s
ceiling can be hit reliably without needing a massive dataset. Use
existing Playwright fixture patterns from the e2e test suite.

Covers: @ui-data-freshness ac-warming-skeleton, ac-warming-auto-
transition, ac-warming-retry-fallback, ac-warming-timeout.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
## Implementation Plan: Consolidate web-ui tests into root tests/

### Problem
1. `npm link` in root `test:e2e` scripts overwrites the system `kspec` binary — unsafe for dispatch agents
2. Tests split across `packages/web-ui/tests/` and `tests/` — agents miss common patterns
3. E2e fixture (`test-base.ts`) calls `spawnSync("kspec", ...)` requiring global binary instead of using existing `CLI_PATH` from `tests/helpers/cli.ts`

### Target Structure
```
tests/
├── e2e/
│   ├── *.spec.ts            ← 45 playwright spec files (moved from packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/)
│   └── fixtures/
│       ├── test-base.ts     ← daemon fixture (moved, updated paths + CLI_PATH import)
│       ├── project-tests/   ← AC coverage test fixture
│       ├── kynetic.yaml     ← e2e YAML fixtures
│       ├── kynetic.meta.yaml
│       ├── project.*.yaml
│       ├── modules/
│       └── tasks/
├── web-ui/
│   ├── ansi.test.ts         ← 12 vitest unit tests (moved from packages/web-ui/tests/)
│   ├── board-utils.test.ts
│   ├── api-envelope.test.ts
│   ├── api-static.test.ts
│   ├── cache-warming-view-states.test.ts
│   ├── fleet-buffer.test.ts
│   ├── plan-embedded-content.test.ts
│   ├── query-client-retry.test.ts
│   ├── reference.test.ts
│   ├── session-utils.test.ts
│   └── ws-cache-invalidation.test.ts
├── helpers/cli.ts           ← existing, already exports CLI_PATH
└── [existing 200+ tests]
playwright.config.ts          ← moved from packages/web-ui/ to root
```

### Step-by-step

#### Step 1: Move playwright config to root
- Move `packages/web-ui/playwright.config.ts` → `playwright.config.ts`
- Update `testDir: "./tests/e2e"`
- Update `outputDir` to `"test-results"` (root-relative)

#### Step 2: Move e2e fixtures

This causes two problems: (1) the root test:e2e script uses npm link to make the built kspec binary globally available, which overwrites the system kspec — unsafe for dispatch agents; (2) agents working on tests miss common patterns because helpers and tests live in different package trees. Moving everything under tests/ eliminates npm link by using the existing CLI_PATH helper, and puts all tests in one discoverable location.

## Target structure

```
tests/
├── e2e/                       ← from packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/
│   ├── *.spec.ts              ← 44 playwright specs
│   └── fixtures/              ← from packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/
│       ├── test-base.ts       ← daemon fixture (key changes here)
│       ├── project-tests/     ← AC coverage fixture
│       └── *.yaml, modules/, tasks/
├── web-ui/                    ← from packages/web-ui/tests/
│   └── *.test.ts              ← 11 vitest unit tests
├── helpers/cli.ts             ← existing, exports CLI_PATH
└── [existing 200+ tests]
playwright.config.ts           ← from packages/web-ui/playwright.config.ts
```

## What changes

**test-base.ts** (core safety fix):
- Import CLI_PATH from ../../helpers/cli.ts
- Replace spawnSync("kspec", [...]) → spawnSync("node", [CLI_PATH, ...]) (2 callsites: start + stop)
- Update E2E_FIXTURES to join(__dirname, ".") (fixtures now colocated)
- Update WEB_UI_BUILD to join(__dirname, "../../../packages/web-ui/build")

**11 web-ui unit tests** — update all path references:
- Regular imports: ../src/lib/... → ../../packages/web-ui/src/lib/...
- vi.mock() paths: same transformation (~30 mock calls across 6 files)
- vi.importActual() paths: same transformation (2 files: query-client-retry, cache-warming-view-states)
- ../../shared/src/... → ../../packages/shared/src/...

**playwright.config.ts** — move to root, update testDir to "./tests/e2e"

**vitest.config.ts** — update exclude: **/packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/** → **/tests/e2e/**

**Root package.json** scripts:
- test:e2e: remove npm link, run npx playwright test tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts tests/e2e/api-server.spec.ts
- test:e2e:full: remove npm link, run npx playwright test

**packages/web-ui/package.json** — remove e2e scripts (now root-level)

**Root .gitignore** — add playwright-report/

## What stays the same
- E2e isolation design (ephemeral ports, temp dirs, isolated HOME)
- 44 e2e spec files keep import { test } from "../fixtures/test-base" (relative structure preserved)
- Vitest sharding auto-discovers tests/web-ui/*.test.ts
- CI workflow calls npm run test:e2e — script change handles it

## Risks to verify during execution
- $lib alias mocks in unit tests: vi.mock intercepts by module name so should work, but verify
- node dist/cli/index.js serve start --detach: confirm daemon still detaches properly via node vs shebang binary
- @playwright/test available at root via workspace hoisting but not declared in root package.json — consider adding explicitly

tasks.title: Fix TanStack Query reactivity bug: loading state never resolves
tasks.description:
What: The web UI pages at /, /agents, and /automation show a loading
skeleton forever on fresh page load. The page never transitions to
showing content. Navigating away to another page and back causes the
content to appear correctly.

Why: This is a live application bug affecting every user on every
fresh page load of these three pages. It also blocks ~46 e2e test
failures across dashboard.spec.ts, agents.spec.ts, automation.spec.ts,
and other specs whose tests time out waiting for content that never
appears past the loading skeleton.

Evidence (HAR capture, 2026-03-30): A fresh load of /automation fires
5 API queries (agent/status, meta/agents, hooks, schedules,
events/recent). All return 200 OK with valid data within 2 seconds.
No CacheWarmingError, no retry loops. The UI stays in loading skeleton
state indefinitely. When the user navigates to another page and returns,
the page renders correctly because the TanStack Query cache already has
data and the component reads it on mount.

Root cause hypothesis: TanStack Query Svelte v6 (installed at 6.1.0,
package @tanstack/svelte-query) uses a createRawRef proxy in
node_modules/@tanstack/svelte-query/src/containers.svelte.ts to bridge
query observer state into Svelte's reactivity system. The proxy uses
$state.raw inside a Proxy set trap with Object.defineProperty
getter/setter closures. The hypothesis is that when the query observer
transitions from {isLoading: true} to {isLoading: false, data: ...},
the proxy's update() function writes the new values, but Svelte's
$derived in the page component (e.g. let loading = $derived(
agentStatusQuery.isLoading || ...)) does not re-evaluate because the
reactive tracking doesn't follow through the proxy indirection.

CRITICAL: This bug has survived multiple previous fix attempts. Each
time a plausible root cause was identified, a fix was applied, and the
issue remained unchanged. Do NOT write fix code until the actual break
point is proven with runtime console output.

How:
1. Add console.log instrumentation in the installed
   node_modules/@tanstack/svelte-query/src/createBaseQuery.svelte.ts:
   - In the $effect at line 74, log when observer.subscribe callback
     fires and the isLoading value from createResult()
   - In the update() function of createRawRef (containers.svelte.ts),
     log when properties are being set and their values
2. Add console.log in packages/web-ui/src/routes/automation/+page.svelte
   in the $derived(loading) expression to log when it re-evaluates and
   what values agentStatusQuery.isLoading etc. return
3. Build the web UI (npm run build:web-ui), start the daemon, do a
   fresh page load of /automation, capture console output
4. The logs will show exactly where the chain breaks: does the observer
   callback fire? Does update() get called? Does $derived re-evaluate?
5. Write a fix targeting only the confirmed break point
6. Verify the fix works on fresh page load (Ctrl+R, not navigate-back)
   for all three pages: /, /agents, /automation
7. Remove all instrumentation before committing

If the fix requires changing TanStack internals, use a pnpm patch
(pnpm patch @tanstack/svelte-query) or create a local wrapper function
that components use instead of createQuery directly.

Key files:
- node_modules/@tanstack/svelte-query/src/createBaseQuery.svelte.ts
- node_modules/@tanstack/svelte-query/src/containers.svelte.ts
- packages/web-ui/src/routes/+page.svelte (dashboard loading logic)
- packages/web-ui/src/routes/agents/+page.svelte (agents loading logic)
- packages/web-ui/src/routes/automation/+page.svelte (automation loading)
- packages/web-ui/src/lib/query/client.ts (QueryClient configuration)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Investigation complete. Root cause identified:

In @tanstack/svelte-query 6.1.0, `createBaseQuery.svelte.ts` subscribes to the query observer inside a `$effect()` callback (line 74). In Svelte 5, `$effect` callbacks are deferred — they don't run until the component's rendering phase completes. This creates a timing issue:

1. Component renders with initial `isLoading: true` state
2. Query observer starts fetching data (via observer construction, not subscription)
3. Data returns from API (confirmed by HAR evidence: all return 200 OK within 2s)
4. Observer tries to notify subscribers, but `$effect` hasn't run yet
5. `$effect` eventually runs and subscribes, but the observer doesn't re-notify for already-delivered results
6. The `update(createResult())` call never fires, so `isLoading` stays `true` in the proxy

This is confirmed by TanStack/query PR #9810 (open, not yet merged) which fixes exactly this bug with the description: "If you do await someQuery.promise, the $effect for the subscription will never run, and therefore the await will never resolve."

Navigation-then-return works because on re-mount, the cache already has data, so `createResult()` returns `isLoading: false` from the initial `createRawRef(createResult())` call.

Fix approach: Create a local `createQuery` wrapper in `packages/web-ui/src/lib/query/createQuery.svelte.ts` that re-exports a fixed version subscribing eagerly (synchronously during init) instead of inside `$effect`. This avoids patching node_modules and can be removed when upstream merges PR #9810. All page imports will be updated from `@tanstack/svelte-query` to the local wrapper.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation complete. Created packages/web-ui/src/lib/query/createQuery.svelte.ts — a local wrapper around @tanstack/svelte-query's createQuery and createInfiniteQuery.

Key change: observer.subscribe() is called eagerly (synchronously during component init) instead of inside a deferred $effect. This ensures the subscription is active before any async fetch completes, preventing the race where updateResult() sees no diff because the observer already transitioned while no subscribers were attached.

The wrapper inlines createRawRef and watchChanges from TanStack internals (not publicly exported) and can be removed once upstream merges PR #9810 or equivalent.

Verification:
- Build succeeds (109 modules transformed, adapter-static output written)
- All web UI tests pass (119/119)
- All unit test shards pass for web-ui-related tests
- Pre-existing failures in dispatch-workspace-config/cleanup tests are unrelated (timeout flakes)

22 component files updated to import from the local wrapper.

tasks.title: Migrate API-only e2e specs to vitest using app.handle()
tasks.description:
What: 15 Playwright e2e specs containing 279 tests are currently skipped
(via test.describe.skip) in tests/e2e/ because they test HTTP API
contracts without any browser interaction — they use Playwright's
request fixture for HTTP calls but never use the page fixture. These
tests should be migrated to vitest using the Elysia app.handle()
pattern so they run without Chromium overhead.

Why: Running API contract tests in Playwright wastes resources: each
test spawns a Chromium process and a daemon subprocess despite never
opening a browser page. Migrating to vitest makes them run in the
fast shard pipeline (npm run test:shard1/2/3) with sub-second
execution per test instead of multi-second Playwright overhead.
The tests themselves are valuable — they cover 56 spec acceptance
criteria across @api-contract, @batch-item-fetch-api,
@daemon-agent-dispatch, @daemon-server, @multi-directory-daemon,
@review-records-daemon-api, @session-list-pagination-api,
@session-text-search, @triage-daemon-api, and @ui-api-aggregation.

How: Use the existing app.handle(Request) pattern established in
tests/daemon-api-input-validation.test.ts. This pattern imports
createServer from packages/daemon/src/server.ts, creates an Elysia
app instance, and calls app.handle(new Request(url, options)) directly
without starting an HTTP server. Required headers for each request:
Host: localhost, X-Kspec-Dir: <tempDir>, Content-Type: application/json.

For each of the 15 specs:
1. Create a corresponding vitest file under tests/daemon-api/
   (e.g. tests/e2e/api-tasks.spec.ts → tests/daemon-api/tasks.test.ts)
2. Convert Playwright request.get/post/delete calls to
   app.handle(new Request(...)) calls
3. Convert Playwright expect() assertions to vitest expect()
4. Set up shared beforeAll that creates a temp dir with fixtures,
   initializes git repo with shadow worktree simulation (same setup
   as tests/daemon-api-input-validation.test.ts)
5. Run the new vitest file and confirm all tests pass
6. Delete the skipped Playwright spec

Each spec can be migrated independently. The 15 specs (listed by
file name and test count):
api-tasks.spec.ts (35), api-items.spec.ts (26),
api-sessions-pagination.spec.ts (23), api-meta.spec.ts (23),
api-inbox.spec.ts (18), api-reviews-list.spec.ts (18),
api-reviews-threads.spec.ts (17), api-errors.spec.ts (14),
api-aggregation.spec.ts (11), api-projects.spec.ts (10),
api-agent-dispatch.spec.ts (9), api-server.spec.ts (8),
api-sessions-legacy.spec.ts (7), api-sessions-search.spec.ts (3),
api-triage.spec.ts (37).

tasks.title: Fix stale-selector e2e failures across UI specs
tasks.description:
What: Approximately 35 e2e test failures across multiple UI specs are
caused by stale data-testid attributes or Playwright locator selectors
that no longer match the current Svelte component markup. The UI was
refactored after these tests were written, and the test selectors were
not updated.

Why: These tests were passing when written but broke as components
were refactored. They represent valid behavioral assertions — the
features they test still exist, only the DOM structure changed. Fixing
the selectors restores coverage for features like item detail views,
command palette search, task navigation, review badges, and validation
display. This task depends on @task-fix-loading-page-e2e because some
of these specs share pages with loading-affected specs and the loading
fix may change which failures remain.

How:
1. Run the full e2e suite: npx playwright test
2. For each failure with a "locator not found" or "element not visible"
   error in test-results/<test>/error-context.md, compare the selector
   used in the test (getByTestId, getByRole, locator) against the
   current component markup in packages/web-ui/src/
3. Update the test selector to match the current markup. Prefer
   updating the test over adding new testids — only add data-testid
   attributes to components when no stable selector exists (role,
   label, text content)
4. Run the individual spec to confirm the fix

Affected specs (from failure categorization of test-results/ directory):
- items.spec.ts: ~12 failures (AC expansion, collapse button, coverage
  indicator, markdown renderer, linked task section, trait chips,
  slide-over panel selectors)
- search.spec.ts: subset of ~15 failures (placeholder text, no-results
  message, result grouping, ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation)
- tasks.spec.ts: ~4 failures (modal close, spec link, review badge,
  navigation link selectors)
- task-board.spec.ts: subset (modal URL param trigger, close action)

tasks.title: Fix timing and race condition e2e failures
tasks.description:
What: Approximately 38 e2e test failures are caused by timing and race
condition issues where tests assert on UI state before asynchronous
operations have completed. Common patterns include: WebSocket
subscription not established before testing real-time features, dialog
open/close animations not finished, keyboard event handlers not yet
registered, search debounce timers still pending, and scroll or
navigation state not settled.

Why: These tests verify real asynchronous behavior (WebSocket updates,
dialog interactions, search-as-you-type) but use insufficient wait
strategies. The features work correctly for users but the tests race
against async operations. This task depends on @task-fix-loading-page-e2e
because some timing failures may be masked by or compound with the
loading state bug.

How: For each timing failure, identify the async operation being raced
and add the appropriate Playwright wait pattern:

- WebSocket readiness: Before testing WS-dependent features, wait for
  the connection indicator element (data-testid or text "Connected")
  to be visible. The connection.svelte store manages WS state and the
  Sidebar.svelte component renders the indicator.
- Dialog animations: After triggering dialog open/close, use
  await expect(dialog).toBeVisible() or .toBeHidden() instead of
  fixed setTimeout delays. Svelte transitions take variable time.
- Keyboard handlers: After page.goto(), wait for a known interactive
  element to be ready before sending keyboard events (e.g. wait for
  the command palette trigger to be attached)
- Search debounce: The CommandPalette.svelte uses a 300ms debounce.
  After typing, use page.waitForResponse() or waitFor on result
  elements rather than fixed delays.
- Navigation: After goto() or click(), use page.waitForURL() or
  waitFor on destination content rather than assuming immediate state.

Affected specs (from failure categorization):
- search.spec.ts: ~10 failures (Cmd+K handler, debounce, result
  clearing, navigation, palette reset, Escape key)
- automation-session-idle.spec.ts: ~9 failures (WebSocket subscription
  timing, event arrival within test window)
- agents.spec.ts: subset (dispatch start/stop state propagation,
  edit dialog data loading, dialog close animation)
- task-board.spec.ts: subset (WebSocket message timing, modal open)
- cache-warming-views.spec.ts: subset (cache warming cycle timing,
  retry exhaustion)
- connection.spec.ts: 2 failures (WebSocket reconnection backoff)
- sessions.spec.ts: subset (scroll events, WebSocket event arrival)

Can be parallelized — each spec file is independent.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Analysis complete. 99 E2E test failures found across multiple files. Key timing patterns identified:

1. search.spec.ts (15 failures): All tests fail because beforeEach only waits for domcontentloaded. The CommandPalette keyboard handler is registered in onMount() and SvelteKit hydration hasn't completed. Need to wait for app readiness (sidebar visible or similar) before sending keyboard events.

2. connection.spec.ts (2 failures): Tests use fixed waitForTimeout(500) which is unreliable for WebSocket state changes. Need to wait for UI state changes instead. The offline test doesn't properly handle the reconnection race.

3. cache-warming-views.spec.ts (4 failures): Tests using page.clock.install() for fake timers. The clock-based retry exhaustion tests fail because the CacheWarmingBanner never appears — likely because the fake timer approach doesn't properly advance through TanStack Query's retry mechanism.

4. sessions.spec.ts (8 failures), items.spec.ts (12 failures), plans.spec.ts (7 failures), validate.spec.ts (7 failures), task-board.spec.ts (5 failures), tasks.spec.ts (4 failures), and others: Mix of timing issues from waitForTimeout, page readiness, and WebSocket subscription timing.

Non-task scope failures: api-triage.spec.ts (13 failures) appears to be API-level failures, not timing issues — different task scope.

Approach: Fix timing issues file by file starting with highest impact. Core fix patterns:
- Replace waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded') with waiting for a visible interactive element
- Replace fixed waitForTimeout with proper Playwright wait assertions
- Fix clock-based tests for cache warming
- Add proper wait-for-element patterns for WebSocket-dependent tests

tasks.title: Fix stale fixture and envelope drift e2e failures
tasks.description:
What: Approximately 15 e2e failures are caused by two related issues:
(1) Test fixture YAML files in tests/e2e/fixtures/ contain data that
doesn't match the current Zod schemas in src/schema/, causing the
daemon to reject or misinterpret fixture data. (2) A small number of
tests expect API responses in the old unwrapped format ({items, total})
when the daemon now wraps responses in the {data, meta} envelope via
wrapResponse() from packages/daemon/src/routes/response-envelope.ts,
or vice versa.

Why: The fixture data was written against earlier schema versions and
hasn't been updated as schemas evolved. The envelope migration wrapped
most endpoints in {data, meta: {cache_status, total, ...}} format but
some test assertions still expect the old shape. These are mechanical
mismatches — the features work correctly, only the test data and
assertions are stale.

How:
Stale fixtures (10 failures):
1. For each failing test, check the daemon's console output or response
   body to identify what the daemon rejects or returns differently
2. Compare the fixture YAML (e.g. tests/e2e/fixtures/project.tasks.yaml,
   project.reviews.yaml, modules/core.yaml) against the corresponding
   Zod schema in src/schema/ (TaskSchema, ReviewSchema, ItemSchema etc.)
3. Update fixture data to conform to current schemas — add missing
   required fields, fix enum values, update nested structure
4. Run the individual spec to confirm

Envelope drift (5 failures):
1. For each failure, check whether the daemon endpoint uses wrapResponse
   (grep for wrapResponse in packages/daemon/src/routes/<domain>.ts)
2. Check whether the client API function (packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts)
   uses unwrapEnvelope/unwrapPaginatedEnvelope/unwrapListEnvelope
3. If the daemon wraps but the test expects unwrapped: update the test
   assertion to account for the {data, meta} envelope
4. If the client unwraps but the daemon doesn't wrap (e.g. automation
   routes /api/hooks, /api/schedules, /api/events/recent return raw
   {items, total} without envelope): the pair is intentionally
   consistent, check if the test itself is wrong

Affected specs: plans.spec.ts (stale fixtures for plan ref resolution),
reviews-detail.spec.ts (interaction fixture data), items.spec.ts
(AC fixture schema), session-context.spec.ts (spec filter fixture),
triage.spec.ts (triage action fixture), static-mode.spec.ts (envelope
format in static responses), dashboard.spec.ts (2 aggregation count
assertions expecting unwrapped data).

tasks.description:
What: tests/e2e/api-websocket.spec.ts contains 14 tests that verify
the WebSocket protocol by using page.evaluate() to open raw WebSocket
connections from the browser context. These test protocol-level
concerns (message format, ack/nack, subscribe commands, close codes,
heartbeat ping/pong) rather than user-visible behavior. They should
be split into two groups: behavioral UI tests (stays in Playwright)
and protocol tests (moves to vitest).

Why: API-level WebSocket protocol tests don't need a browser — opening
a raw WS connection via page.evaluate() is an unnecessary indirection
when a vitest test can use the ws npm package or Bun's native WebSocket
client directly. Meanwhile, there are zero e2e tests that verify
WebSocket-driven UI features from the user's perspective: real-time
data updates, connection status display, and live streaming. These
behavioral tests are the actual coverage gap.

How:
Behavioral UI tests (new Playwright spec, e.g. websocket-ui.spec.ts):
- Connection indicator: Navigate to any page, verify the sidebar shows
  "Connected" text (rendered by Sidebar.svelte from the connection
  store at packages/web-ui/src/lib/stores/connection.svelte)
- Real-time task updates: Navigate to /tasks, use the daemon fixture's
  API to change a task status (POST /api/tasks/:ref/start), verify the
  task list updates without page refresh
- Real-time inbox count: Navigate to /inbox, POST /api/inbox to add an
  item, verify the sidebar inbox badge count increments
- Agent streaming: Navigate to / (dashboard), start dispatch via API,
  verify the active fleet section appears with streaming output
- Disconnection: Stop the daemon, verify "Disconnected" indicator
  appears; restart, verify reconnection

These tests depend on @task-fix-query-loading-state because pages must
render content before WebSocket-driven updates can be observed.

Protocol tests (new vitest spec under tests/daemon-api/):
- Move raw protocol assertions (message format {action, request_id,
  payload}, ack format {ack, request_id, success}, subscribe command,
  close codes 1000/1001, heartbeat timing) to a vitest test that
  connects to the daemon using a WebSocket client library
- These need a real running daemon (unlike HTTP tests that use
  app.handle()), so use the daemon subprocess pattern with
  ephemeral port allocation

Original spec covers these ACs (preserve coverage in new locations):
@api-contract ac-25 through ac-31, @trait-websocket-protocol ac-1
through ac-5, @daemon-server ac-4.
