tasks.title: Replace count-based e2e assertions with behavioral assertions and fixture-derived counts
tasks.description:
## What

Reduce the brittleness of e2e tests that assert task counts. Several Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/` assert exact task counts as proxies for behavioral checks (e.g., "active filter hides completed tasks" → `toHaveCount(7)`). Adding or removing a row from the e2e fixture (`tests/e2e/fixtures/project.tasks.yaml` and the per-task split format under `tests/e2e/fixtures/tasks/<ULID>/task.yaml`, both of which coexist in the fixture) cascades into multiple test assertion edits across multiple files.

## Why

Hardcoded count assertions couple test behavior to incidental fixture content. They:

- Cascade fixture changes into multiple unrelated test files (one fixture row addition recently broke 6 assertions across 3 files in 2 separate fix cycles)
- Don't actually verify the behavior under test (e.g., "active filter hides completed" is provable without knowing the total count)
- Get out of sync silently — comments saying "fixture has 7 tasks" are not enforced
- Make the cost of adding fixture coverage for new features artificially high

The single legitimate exception is the daemon API contract test that verifies the daemon returns all fixture tasks — that test genuinely needs absolute totals, but should derive them from the fixture rather than inline literals.

## How

For each existing count-based assertion, choose the right replacement:

### 1. Behavioral assertions for filter tests

In `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts`:

- "Default Active filter hides completed" — verify no completed badge is visible AND at least one task is visible. Existing code already iterates and checks `not.toContainText(/completed/i)` and `not.toContainText(/cancelled/i)`; the count assertion is redundant. Keep the cancelled check as a defensive guard even though no cancelled task exists in the fixture.
- "All Statuses filter shows completed" — verify at least one completed badge is visible after switching to "All Statuses".
- "Switching back to Active hides completed" — verify the previously-visible completed badges are no longer visible after switching.
- "Automation=eligible filter" — verify every visible item carries the eligible automation badge (or none carry ineligible/manual badges).

### 2. Relative counts for watcher / mutation tests

In `tests/e2e/file-watcher.spec.ts`:

- "Adding a task via file watcher updates the list" — capture the count before the append, append the row, and assert `before + 1` after waiting for the new row's title to appear via `filter({ hasText })`. The title-based wait is the real behavioral check; the count assertion just guards against duplicates.
- "Second-project mutation does not affect first project" — capture the first-project list snapshot before the second-project mutation and assert it is unchanged after, without baking in absolute totals.

### 3. Fixture-derived counts for the API contract test

In `tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts` (the test currently named "daemon returns task counts matching fixture data"):

- This test verifies the daemon `/api/tasks` returns all fixture tasks and groups them correctly by status. It legitimately needs absolute counts.
- Derive expected per-status counts from the fixture itself at test-fixture-load time. Implementation path: extend `tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts` so the daemon fixture exposes `expectedTaskCounts: Record<string, number>` (or similar), computed by parsing the task data from whichever is the canonical source for the e2e daemon (verify whether that is `project.tasks.yaml` or the split per-task directories — both exist in the fixture and the manifest uses `task_storage.format: split`).
- The contract test then asserts against `daemon.expectedTaskCounts.pending` etc. instead of hardcoded numbers.

## Files in scope

- `tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts` — the API contract test that fetches `/api/tasks` and asserts per-status counts (currently hardcoded around lines 537–554).
- `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` — filter tests that hardcode active/all/automation counts.
- `tests/e2e/file-watcher.spec.ts` — watcher tests that hardcode pre/post counts.
- `tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts` — daemon fixture setup; add the helper that exposes derived expected counts.

## Out of scope

- The Status Summary tests in `dashboard.spec.ts` (lines around 246–303) that use `interceptDashboardAPIs` and a parallel hardcoded `fixtureTasks()` mock. Those do not break when the real fixture changes because they consume mocked data. They have a separate drift problem (the mock has already drifted from the real fixture) and should be addressed in their own task.
- Other e2e tests where the count IS the contract being tested (e.g., "exactly 3 workflow steps", "exactly 1 fleet card", "exactly 2 review revisions"). These assert known, intentional cardinality, not incidental fixture content.
- Inbox, observation, plan, and review fixtures. These are stable enough that count-based assertions on them are not currently a problem.
- Unit and integration tests outside `tests/e2e/`.

## Done when

- Adding a new task row to the e2e fixture (either `project.tasks.yaml` or the per-task split format) does not require editing any count assertions in `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` or `tests/e2e/file-watcher.spec.ts`.
- The Active filter test in `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` asserts filter behavior directly (no hardcoded total count, no completed/cancelled badge visible, at least one task visible).
- The All Statuses filter test in `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` asserts at least one completed badge is visible after switching to All, with no hardcoded total count.
- The "switching back to Active" test in `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` asserts previously-visible completed badges are no longer visible after switching back, with no hardcoded total count.
- The automation-eligible filter test in `tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts` asserts every visible task carries the eligible badge, with no hardcoded matching count.
- The "task added via watcher" test in `tests/e2e/file-watcher.spec.ts` uses a relative count (`before + 1`) rather than an absolute literal.

tasks.title: Custom lint rule for unsafe daemon-spawn patterns in test files
tasks.description:
## What

Add a custom lint rule that fails the lint pass when a test file spawns a kspec daemon without registering cleanup that runs on every exit path. Two anti-patterns to detect:

1. A call to `runKspec("serve start --detach ...")` (or `execSync`/`spawn` of the same string) without an `onTestFinished` registration in the same scope before the next assertion.
2. A direct `spawn(...)` call where the binary path matches `dist/daemon/index.js`, again without an `onTestFinished` registration before any subsequent assertion or await.

The rule must allow the cleanup to be registered via any of: `onTestFinished(...)`, a wrapping `try { ... } finally { ... }` whose finally calls a stop helper, or a covering `afterEach` whose body calls `serve stop` or `process.kill` against the same scope. False positives are worse than false negatives here — if the rule can't statically prove cleanup is missing, it should pass.

The rule lives next to the existing custom-rule precedent: `tools/eslint-rules/no-daemon-ts-imports.js` (rule definition) and `tests/lint-no-daemon-ts-imports.test.ts` (vitest test that asserts the rule catches violations and doesn't false-positive on safe code).

## Why

Without lint-time enforcement, the cleanup pattern is a gentleman's agreement that future test authors will violate. Inbox item @01KKSGTN documented exactly this regression at exactly the file in scope, and the bug persisted for 3+ weeks because nothing flagged it. A lint rule converts a recurring footgun into a build-time error.

The rule doesn't need to be perfect — it needs to catch the pattern that just leaked 142 daemons over 3 days. Detecting `serve start --detach` as a string in a test file is enough; AST sophistication is a nice-to-have.

## How

1. Read `tools/eslint-rules/no-daemon-ts-imports.js` to understand the rule structure (what context the rule receives, how it reports violations, how it's wired into the lint runner).
2. Read `tests/lint-no-daemon-ts-imports.test.ts` to understand how rules are tested in this project (fixture file pattern, RuleTester invocation, etc).
3. Read `tests/cli-serve.test.ts` after the prerequisite task @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup has landed, so the rule can be developed against a clean tree where every daemon-spawning test is already correct. The clean tree becomes the no-false-positive baseline.
4. Implement `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js`:
   - Match string literals containing `serve start --detach` in test files (path matches `tests/**/*.ts` or `tests/**/*.test.ts`).
   - Match `spawn(...)` calls where the first arg is a path-resolution that includes `dist/daemon/index.js` or a constant like `DAEMON_ENTRY`.
   - For each match, walk forward in the same statement scope looking for an `onTestFinished` call, a `finally` block, or an enclosing function with an `afterEach` reference. If none found before the next `expect`, `await`, or function-scope exit, report.
   - Provide a fix-it suggestion in the report message (text, not auto-fix): "Register cleanup via `onTestFinished(() => process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM'))` immediately after the spawn returns."
5. Implement `tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`:
   - **Positive cases** (rule should flag): test files that call `runKspec("serve start --detach ...")` with no `onTestFinished` after; tests that `spawn` the daemon binary and run an `expect` before any cleanup registration.
   - **Negative cases** (rule should NOT flag): tests using the standard `beforeEach`/`afterEach` daemon cleanup pair where the spawn is in the same `describe` block; tests that register `onTestFinished` immediately after spawn; tests that call `spawn` for non-daemon binaries.
   - Test fixtures live as inline source strings, not real test files, to keep them isolated.
6. Wire the rule into whatever runs custom rules in this project. Check `package.json` and lint configuration files for how `no-daemon-ts-imports.js` is invoked. If oxlint doesn't support custom rules in this version, follow the same vitest-test-as-lint-runner pattern that `lint-no-daemon-ts-imports.test.ts` uses.
7. Run `npm test -- tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts` and `npm test -- tests/cli-serve.test.ts` to confirm the rule passes against the post-prerequisite-task clean tree.
8. Update the project's `testing` convention via `kspec meta set testing --add-rule` with the cleanup-pattern requirement (see "Convention update" below). The convention documents the rule for human readers and links the lint rule as enforcement.

## Convention update (run as part of this task)

Run:

```bash
kspec meta set testing --add-rule "Test daemons must register cleanup via vitest's onTestFinished at spawn time, not in the test body. Prefer direct spawn() (see tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts) so the OS reaps the daemon via process group on parent death. If a test must invoke 'kspec serve start --detach' because the CLI command itself is under test, read the PID immediately after the spawn returns and register process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM') in onTestFinished — never rely on inline cleanup that won't run on assertion failure."
```

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A custom lint rule exists at `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js` with documented purpose, options (none), and structure matching `no-daemon-ts-imports.js`.
- AC2: A vitest test exists at `tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts` covering at least four positive cases (rule should flag) and at least four negative cases (rule should pass), including the standard `beforeEach`/`afterEach` pattern as a negative case.
- AC3: The rule is wired into the project's lint pipeline by the same mechanism `no-daemon-ts-imports.js` uses. Running `npm test` (or whichever script invokes the rule) executes it.
- AC4: After the prerequisite task @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup has landed and this task is complete, the rule passes against the entire `tests/` directory with zero violations.
- AC5: The project's `testing` convention has a new rule entry covering the cleanup pattern, added via `kspec meta set testing --add-rule`.
- AC6: A test that intentionally violates the rule (added to `tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts` as a positive case) is correctly flagged with a message that includes the suggested fix.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring `tests/cli-serve.test.ts` — covered by prerequisite @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup (must land first).
- Auto-fix capability — the rule reports and suggests, but doesn't rewrite code.
- Detection of leaked daemons at runtime — that's the inboxed reaper idea, deferred.
- Production daemon code changes.
- Linting test files outside the `tests/` directory.

## Background

This task is the second half of a two-task fix for a daemon-leak bug observed on 2026-04-09 (142 orphan daemons accumulated over 3 days). The first task (@task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup) fixes the actual leaky tests. This task adds lint-time enforcement so the pattern can't regress. Inbox item @01KKSGTN documented the underlying bug 3+ weeks before it was rediscovered — a lint rule would have caught the regression immediately and saved that delay.

## Related

- @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup (prerequisite — must land first)
- @01KKSGTN (inbox, original bug report)
- @01KNT3GG (inbox, daemon parent-watchdog complement)
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-daemon-ts-imports.js` (precedent for custom rule)
- `tests/lint-no-daemon-ts-imports.test.ts` (precedent for rule testing)

tasks.title: Add per-file progress to test runner non-verbose mode
tasks.description:
## What

Add minimal per-test-file progress output to `scripts/test.cjs` in non-verbose mode. Currently the runner prints `Cache cleared (--fresh)` and then nothing until the final summary, leaving the user unable to distinguish "running" from "stuck." Print one short line per completed test file (e.g., `✓ tests/parser.test.ts (66 tests, 350ms)`) so liveness is visible without dumping the full vitest verbose stream.

## Why

On 2026-04-09 a user lost 11+ minutes thinking `npm test` was hung because the runner's non-verbose mode produces no terminal output between cache-cleared and final summary. The user's mental model (formed when the suite ran in ~150s) was that prolonged silence = stuck. Real cause: vitest output is piped to a log file the user doesn't know exists, and heavy-serial integration tests now legitimately take 8-15+ minutes.

This affects every first-time user, every dispatch-spawned agent, every dev returning to the project after a break. The friction is recurring and high-volume even though the bug is small.

User feedback context: "I don't want tests to spam a bunch of stuff, but showing some low token usage progress would be nice." The progress signal must be MINIMAL — one line per test file at most, not full vitest verbose output.

## How

1. Read `scripts/test.cjs` end to end. The runner currently spawns vitest with `--reporter=json --outputFile.json=... --reporter=verbose` and pipes both stdout and stderr to a log file. In verbose mode it tees to terminal as well; in non-verbose mode it writes only to the log.
2. Choose a low-token progress strategy. Options:
   - **Tail the log file in-process**: as bytes are written, parse for completed test file lines (`✓ <file> (N tests, Xms)`) and forward only those to stderr. Drop everything else.
   - **Add a custom vitest reporter**: write a small reporter that emits one stderr line per file completion. Wire it as a third `--reporter=...` arg. This is cleaner but adds a new file to maintain.
   - **Process the JSON reporter output as it streams**: vitest writes the JSON file at the end, not incrementally, so this option doesn't work.
   The tail-and-filter approach is simplest and self-contained in `scripts/test.cjs`.
3. Implement the chosen approach. Output format target (one line per file):
   ```
   ✓ tests/parser.test.ts (66 tests, 350ms)
   ✓ tests/cli-serve.test.ts (32 tests, 12.4s)
   ✗ tests/foo.test.ts (5 tests, 2 failed, 800ms)
   ```
   No emojis if the project convention forbids them — use ASCII markers `PASS`/`FAIL` instead. Check the existing condensed output formatter in `scripts/test.cjs` for the project's color/marker conventions.
4. Make the new output show ONLY in non-verbose mode. Verbose mode already streams the full vitest output and doesn't need the per-file summary on top.
5. Do not change the final summary, the cache behavior, or any other runner logic. This is a progress-output-only patch.
6. Manually verify by running `npm test --fresh` and confirming:
   - You can see test files completing in real time
   - The terminal does NOT get spammed with individual test names, error stacks, or stdout from tests
   - Total token volume is roughly one short line per test file (~150 lines total for the full suite, vs ~9000 lines in verbose mode)
   - Final summary still appears as before

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `scripts/test.cjs` in non-verbose mode prints one short line per test file as it completes, including pass/fail status, test count, and duration.
- AC2: The new output is suppressed in verbose mode (where the full vitest stream is already shown).
- AC3: The new output respects the existing color/marker conventions used by the runner's condensed final summary.
- AC4: Total non-verbose terminal output for a full suite run is roughly proportional to the number of test files (~150 lines), not to the number of tests (~7500+).
- AC5: The final summary, exit code, cache behavior, and log file contents are unchanged.
- AC6: A user running `npm test --fresh` cold can tell within 30 seconds whether tests are progressing or genuinely stuck, without consulting the log file or using `--verbose`.

## Out of scope

- Verbose mode changes (already streams full output).
- Performance optimization of the test suite itself (separate inbox item).
- Updates to the kspec-agents.md `~150s` baseline figure (separate inbox item — full suite is now 8-15+ minutes).
- Custom vitest reporters as standalone modules — keep it self-contained in `scripts/test.cjs` unless that approach proves clumsy.
- Per-test progress (only per-file).

## Background

A live observation on 2026-04-09 found that a user ran `npm test --fresh` and waited 11+ minutes thinking it was hung. Real cause: the runner pipes all vitest output to a log file in non-verbose mode and shows nothing on the terminal. Combined with a misleading `~150s` baseline in kspec-agents.md and the actual 8-15+ minute duration of the full suite (heavy-serial integration tests run 6-20s each), the user's "tests are stuck" perception was rational. This task addresses the symptom (no progress signal). The trajectory of test duration itself is captured in a separate inbox item.

## Related

- @daemon-sensitive-cli-test-determinism (existing spec — not modified)
- `scripts/test.cjs` (the file being modified)
- `vitest.config.ts` (two projects share globalSetup)

tasks.title: Scaffold project config file during init setup
tasks.description:
Write a project config file at the project root as part of
the setup step that runs during init, using resolved defaults
and commented placeholders for knobs that real projects are
expected to customize.

Why: New projects consistently need the same config file with
the same shape, but currently every project author writes it
by hand. Scaffolding it once during setup removes an entire
class of first-day friction and eliminates silent dispatch
breakage from a missing file.

What:
- Add a setup step that runs after the existing skill
  rendering step and before the existing agents file
  generation step.
- The step writes a project config file at the project root
  with the following content:
  * A dispatch section containing publication_mode set to
    manual_merge, with an adjacent comment listing the other
    accepted values from the dispatch publication mode schema.
  * A dispatch section containing base_branch resolved from
    the current repository's default branch (detect via the
    same helper the dispatcher uses to resolve a default
    base; if detection fails, use the literal string "main"
    and comment that the value was a fallback).

  and the force flag is not set, the step is reported as
  skipped with a reason.

  the existing content to a sibling file with a timestamped
  extension and report the backup path before writing the
  fresh template.

  existing config loader in the same invocation; if loading
  fails the setup step must fail loudly rather than leaving
  a broken file.

  same format as existing steps.

under src/cli/commands/setup.ts. Add a new step function
next to the existing skill rendering and agents file
generation steps, register it in the pipeline ordering, and
reuse the existing step result reporting helper so output
formatting matches. The config schema and loader live under
src/parser/config.ts; reuse its loader for the validation
check. Default branch resolution is already used by the
dispatch workspace resolver under src/agent-runtime; reuse
its helper rather than reimplementing it.

fresh-project path, the existing-file skip path, and the
force-overwrite-with-backup path. Integration test that
runs init with setup on a fresh temp directory and asserts
the scaffolded file exists, is valid on load, and contains
the documented keys. Fixture test that an empty project
with only the scaffolded file behaves identically to a
project with no config file at all.

ac-placeholder-base-branch, ac-placeholder-coverage,

tasks.title: Expand and repair auto-generated gitignore entries
tasks.description:
Make the init gitignore writer enumerate every transient
directory kspec can create under the project root, and
ensure a repair path runs during setup to add any missing
entries on existing projects.

Why: The current gitignore writer misses at least one
transient directory that is created lazily by later commands,
which causes untracked content to appear after normal task
work. Also, existing projects need a non-destructive way to
get the missing entries added on upgrade.

What:
- Build a single canonical list of transient directories
  that kspec may create at the project root, sourced from
  the constants used by the commands that create them (for
  example: shadow worktree path, worktree pool root, session
  storage path, plan drafts path). The list must be a
  shared constant, not duplicated inline in init.
- Update the init gitignore writer to append every entry in
  the canonical list idempotently, preserving any existing
  user-authored content above or below the managed block.
- Use a managed-block marker pair (start and end sentinel
  lines) so the setup step can detect and update the
  managed block without touching user content outside it.
- Add a setup step that runs on every invocation (not just
  init) and appends any missing entries from the canonical
  list, reporting which entries were added.
- Never remove entries a user added manually, even if they
  fall inside the managed block.
- When the managed block is absent on an existing project,
  create it at the end of the file with all canonical
  entries and report that the block was created.

How: The existing gitignore writing logic lives in
src/cli/commands/init.ts. Extract the entry list to a shared
constant alongside the existing path constants used by the
commands that create transient directories. Add the managed
block marker handling (a small helper that parses, updates,
and serializes the block). Register the setup step in the
pipeline so it runs during init with setup and during
standalone setup invocations.

Testing: Unit tests for the managed block parser covering:
no existing block, existing block with same entries,
existing block with fewer entries, user content interleaved
above and below the block. Integration test that runs init
on a fresh project, then runs commands that create each
transient directory, and asserts git status reports no
untracked content. Test that user entries outside the
managed block are never touched.

Covers: @complete-auto-gitignore ac-all-transient-paths-present,
ac-no-untracked-after-common-commands,
ac-existing-entries-preserved, ac-kspec-entries-idempotent.

Added managed-block gitignore handling, setup/init integration, configurable shadow/worktree support, and task coverage tests.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: 

1. Create shared constant KSPEC_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES in src/parser/shadow.ts alongside existing path constants. Entries derived from: SHADOW_WORKTREE_DIR (.kspec/), SESSIONS_WORKTREE_DIR (.kspec-sessions/), TRANSIENT_PLANS_DIR (plans/), dispatch worktree_root (.kspec-worktrees/), dispatch workspace metadata (.kspec-dispatch-workspace.json), dispatch shadow mutation lock (.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation).

2. Add managed-block sentinel markers (# >>> kspec managed / # <<< kspec managed) and a helper that parses/updates/serializes the block. The helper: reads .gitignore, finds the managed block (or creates it at end), ensures all canonical entries exist inside the block, never removes user entries inside or outside the block.

3. Replace the per-entry ensureGitignore/ensureSessionsGitignore/ensurePlansGitignore with a single ensureKspecGitignore() that uses the managed block approach.

4. Add a setup step that calls ensureKspecGitignore() on every setup invocation, reporting which entries were added.

5. Update initializeShadow() to call the new unified function.

Edge cases: existing projects without managed block markers (create block with all entries), user content above/below block preserved, idempotent on re-run, force flag preserves byte-for-byte (trait AC).

Test plan: 8 own ACs + 4 trait ACs. Tests for managed block parser: no block, block with same entries, block with fewer entries, user content interleaved. Integration test for init + git status.

tasks.title: Scaffold default project agents and conventions
tasks.description:
During init setup, scaffold the full default agent roster
(task worker, code reviewer, primary development agent, plan
reviewer) and baseline conventions for commits, architecture,
and testing into the meta spec. Every scaffolded agent has
write authorization enabled unconditionally. The scaffold
runs once per project and persists a first-run marker so
subsequent setup runs do not resurrect items the user has
removed or renamed.

Why: Every real project manually adds these same defaults
immediately after init, and restricted-mode authorization is
not a supported execution path today — agents that cannot
write cannot do useful work. Scaffolding the full roster
with write authorization enabled removes repetitive
boilerplate, ensures task dispatch, code review, and plan
review work out of the box, and gives the auto-generated
agent instructions file something to render from the first
time it runs. The first-run marker is what prevents the
scaffold from becoming a recurring reset that fights the
user. This task supersedes the older ralph-replacement
acceptance criteria for worker and reviewer scaffolding;
tests that covered those criteria must be re-annotated to
the acceptance criteria on this spec rather than deleted.

What:
- Add a setup step that runs after the hook installation
  step and before the agents file generation step.
- Read a first-run marker from the setup seeding state
  file (the same state file used by permission and memory
  seeding). The marker is a named flag indicating whether
  the default agents and conventions scaffold has ever
  completed for this project.
- When the marker is absent (first run) the step creates
  the following meta items:
  * A task worker agent with a stable identifier, a
    descriptive name, write authorization enabled
    unconditionally, and dispatch rules that respond to
    task ready and task needs-work events with the
    automation eligibility filter set by default.
  * A code reviewer agent with a stable identifier, a
    descriptive name, write authorization enabled
    unconditionally, and a dispatch rule that responds to
    task pending-review events.
  * A primary development agent with a stable identifier,
    a descriptive name, capabilities for code, test,
    refactor, and review, and write authorization enabled
    unconditionally.
  * A plan reviewer agent with a stable identifier, a
    descriptive name, review capability, write
    authorization enabled unconditionally, and the plan
    review, writing specs, and plan skills attached.
  * A commits convention with two rules: one for commit
    message format and one for task reference style.
  * An architecture convention containing a single
    placeholder rule that explicitly instructs the user
    to replace it with project-specific rules.
  * A testing convention containing a single placeholder
    rule that explicitly instructs the user to replace it.
  After creation, the step writes the first-run marker
  and reports each created item in the setup summary.
- Write authorization on every default agent must be set
  to the unconditional "always allow" setting. Restricted
  or per-action approval modes are not valid defaults for
  any scaffolded agent.
- The plan reviewer agent's description must include
  inline guidance explaining how to switch adapters if
  the default adapter's authentication fails, using only
  commands and flags that exist in the CLI.
- Any existing built-in agent scaffolding (for example,
  the ralph-replacement task worker and pr reviewer
  creation paths already present in the setup command)
  must be folded into this step rather than continuing
  to exist as a parallel code path. There must be exactly
  one scaffold site for default agents.
- When the marker is present (subsequent run) the step
  does nothing and reports "defaults already seeded" with
  an itemized status that distinguishes between items
  that still exist, items that appear to have been
  removed by the user, and items that appear to have been
  renamed. Removed and renamed items are NEVER recreated
  in this mode; the step is a report-only no-op.
- When setup is invoked with the force flag, the step
  treats force as "reseed missing items only": for each
  scaffold item whose original identifier no longer
  resolves and whose scaffold marker has not been
  explicitly cleared, recreate the item and report it as
  force-recreated. Items that resolve (including renamed
  ones) are never overwritten.
- Items carry a scaffold-origin tag on creation so the
  subsequent-run detection can distinguish "user removed
  the scaffold default" from "user renamed the scaffold
  default to something else". The tag is a stable field
  on the meta item; use the existing meta item tag/trait
  field rather than inventing a new one.
- After the step runs, invoke the existing agents file
  regeneration so the auto-generated instructions reflect
  the scaffolded defaults without requiring a separate
  command.

How: The meta item creation pathway is exposed as library
functions under src/parser/meta.ts; call those directly
from the setup step rather than shelling out to the CLI.
The setup seeding state file pattern is already used by
permission seeding and memory seeding — add a new field
to the same state file rather than creating a new file.
The existing "ensure built-in agents" step in
src/cli/commands/setup.ts currently creates the
ralph-replacement task worker and pr reviewer; consolidate
that logic into this step so there is one scaffold path,
and re-annotate any tests previously asserting the
ralph-replacement AC behavior to the new acceptance
criteria on this spec. Scaffold-origin tagging uses the
existing tag field on meta items; pick a reserved tag
string (for example "scaffold-default") and document it.
Rename detection walks the meta item list looking for
items carrying the scaffold-origin tag whose identifier
differs from any known scaffold default identifier.

Testing: Unit tests for:
- First-run path creates every default agent and
  convention, writes marker, verifies every agent has
  write authorization set to the unconditional value.
- Second-run path with all items present: no-op.
- Second-run path with one item removed: not recreated,
  reported as intentionally removed.
- Second-run path with one item renamed: original id not
  recreated, renamed item preserved unchanged.
- Force-reseed path with missing items: recreated and
  reported; existing items untouched.
Integration test running init with setup on a fresh temp
directory asserting the four expected agents and three
expected conventions exist with the right shape, every
agent has write authorization enabled, and the first-run
marker is present. Follow-up integration test removing
one default, running setup again, asserting the removed
item stays removed. Re-annotate the existing
ralph-replacement worker/reviewer scaffold tests onto the
new ac-task-worker-agent and ac-pr-reviewer-agent
acceptance criteria.

Covers: @default-project-agents-and-conventions
ac-task-worker-agent, ac-pr-reviewer-agent,
ac-primary-dev-agent, ac-plan-reviewer-agent,
ac-plan-reviewer-agent-skills,
ac-plan-reviewer-adapter-guidance,
ac-all-defaults-write-authorized, ac-commits-convention,
ac-architecture-convention, ac-testing-convention,
ac-agents-md-reflects-defaults, ac-first-run-marker-written,
ac-removed-defaults-not-recreated,
ac-renamed-defaults-preserved, ac-force-reseed.

tasks.title: Scaffold default session reflection hook
tasks.description:
During init setup, scaffold a single reflection hook that
fires on any idle agent session (no per-agent filter) and
prompts the session to run the reflect skill, so reflection
runs out of the box for every agent.

Why: Session reflection is valuable from the first session,
but requires a hook that every project currently adds by
hand. Treating reflection as a universal concern rather
than a per-agent one removes the need to look up individual
agent identifiers at scaffold time and simplifies the setup
graph — the reflection hook no longer depends on the
default agent scaffold running first.

What:
- Add a setup step that runs after the scaffold default
  agents and conventions step and before the agents file
  generation step.
- Create one hook by identifier if it does not already
  exist: a reflection hook that fires on the session idle
  event, applies to every agent session (no agent filter),
  and prompts the session to run the reflect skill.
- Do not create the hook if its identifier already exists
  in the hook list. Skip silently in that case and report
  it as an idempotency skip.
- If the hook was previously created by this step and has
  since been removed by the user, the step must not
  recreate it. Detect this by checking for a marker field
  on the hook (a known tag or a deterministic identifier
  component) that only the scaffold writes, and by
  remembering that the scaffold previously completed. Use
  the existing setup seeding state file to persist the
  "scaffolded reflection hook" marker across invocations.

How: Hook CRUD is exposed via library functions under
src/parser/hooks.ts (or the equivalent module). Reuse the
setup seeding state file pattern already used for permission
seeding and memory seeding to record that the hook scaffold
has run. The filter and action payloads are documented in
the hook schema in src/schema/hook.ts; follow that schema
exactly rather than shelling out to the CLI. The hook's
agent filter must be empty or a wildcard so every session
matches, not a list of named agents.

Testing: Unit tests for create, idempotent skip, and
removed-by-user non-recreation. Integration test running
init with setup and asserting exactly one reflection hook
exists with no agent filter. Test that removing the hook
and re-running setup without force does not recreate it.

Covers: @default-session-reflection-hook
ac-reflection-hook-present, ac-hook-idempotent,
ac-hook-removable.

tasks.title: Make default module a referenceable item
tasks.description:
Turn the default module that init creates into a real
referenceable module item so plan derivation can target it
without requiring the user to create a module first.

Why: On a fresh project, plan derive currently fails with
"requires --module" because the file init creates is a
placeholder list container, not a module item. This forces
users to run an extra command before their first plan
derive will work, which is exactly the kind of guesswork
the release is trying to remove.

What:
- When init creates the default module placeholder, also
  create a real module meta item with a deterministic slug
  (for example, derived from the project name or a fixed
  "default" slug — pick one and document it), a title, and
  a description that explains it is the default module.
- Preserve the existing placeholder file shape so that
  library code which expected it continues to work, but
  ensure the new module item is discoverable by the normal
  item lookup and is accepted by plan derive.
- When the user edits the title, slug, or description of
  the default module, persist the edits through normal
  item set flows. Subsequent plan derive invocations that
  target the default module must follow the current slug.
- When a project already has one or more user-created
  modules, init still creates the default module; a later
  setup invocation must not remove it unless the user
  explicitly removes it.
- Document the default module's existence in the setup
  summary and in the init output.

How: The default module file is created in
src/cli/commands/init.ts; find the code that writes
modules/main.yaml and augment it to also create a module
item via the same library function that kspec module add
uses (under src/parser/modules.ts or the equivalent). The
plan derive module check lives in src/cli/commands/plan.ts
under the derive handler — verify that the newly created
item resolves through the same lookup path that kspec
module add items do.

Testing: Integration test that runs init on a fresh temp
directory and asserts the default module item is
resolvable by reference. End-to-end test that imports a
plan, approves it, and runs derive targeting the default
module without any intermediate module creation. Test
that editing the default module's slug via item set
persists and is visible to plan derive.

Covers: @derivable-default-module ac-default-module-resolvable,
ac-plan-derive-accepts-default, ac-default-module-editable.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:

The fix is to change both generators to produce proper module items with _ulid, slugs: [main], type: module, title, description, and status. The module item will be written as a top-level YAML document (like tests/fixtures/modules/core.yaml), which extractItemsFromRaw() already handles by checking for _ulid at the top level.

Key changes:
1. shadow.ts: generateShadowModule() - generate a real module item with ulid, slug 'main', title derived from project name

- Existing projects already initialized won't be affected (no migration needed, this is for new init)
- The slug 'main' is deterministic and human-friendly
- User can still edit title/slug/description via kspec item set

2. ac-plan-derive-accepts-default: init, import plan, approve, derive targeting @main - succeeds

tasks.title: Actionable plan import format errors and empty-plan derive guard
tasks.description:
Make plan import strict about structural invariants
(title, acceptance criterion shape), tolerant of plans
that have no specs or tasks yet (warn instead of fail),
and move the "no derivable work" failure to plan derive
so empty-but-intentional plan content can land before
the structured work is written.

Why: Plan import currently silently accepts documents
whose title cannot be extracted (importing them as
"Untitled Plan") and fails later at derive time with
cryptic schema errors. At the same time, users
legitimately want to land a planning document that
contains prose and links before any specs or tasks have
been authored. The right split is: import stores content
(and warns if the plan is empty); derive refuses to
materialize anything when there is nothing to materialize.
Users discover both conditions with self-contained
messages.

What:
- Change plan import so that when the parser cannot
  extract a title from the document, the command fails
  with a non-zero exit code rather than importing as
  "Untitled Plan". The error message must name the
  expected structural form of the title (a top-level
  heading as the first significant element) and show a
  one-line example.
- Change plan import so that a document with a valid
  title but neither a specs section nor a tasks section
  containing derivable work imports successfully with a
  warning. The warning must name both expected sections,
  explain that derive will fail until at least one is
  populated, and appear in normal and JSON output modes.
- When an acceptance criterion fails schema validation,
  fail the import with an error that names the spec slug
  (or index if unslugged), names the failing criterion's
  identifier (or index), and lists every required field
  of an acceptance criterion with a brief description.
  Do not leak raw schema validator output.
- Change plan derive so that a plan with no specs and no
  tasks fails with a non-zero exit code and a message
  that names both expected sections, explains the plan
  has no derivable work, and points the user at plan
  import to update the plan's content.
- Extend the import command's help output to include a
  minimal runnable example of a plan document that uses
  all required structural elements (title, specs section
  with one spec, tasks section with derive directive).
  The example must be copy-pasteable.
- Error and warning messages must never reference files
  outside the project (skills, README, docs) — everything
  needed to correct the input must be in the message
  itself.
- The dry-run flow for import must produce the same
  errors and warnings as a real import so users can
  preflight their document.

How: The parser entry point is parsePlanDocument in
src/parser/plan-document.ts. Today the title extraction
is best-effort; change it to required and propagate a
typed error. Introduce a typed "empty plan" signal
(not an error) that the import command translates into
a warning. The import command handler lives in
src/cli/commands/plan-import.ts and already consumes
parser errors — route the new error types and warning
signal to human messages there. The derive command
handler lives in src/cli/commands/plan.ts under the
derive subcommand; add the empty-plan guard check at
the top of the handler so it fails before any shadow
branch work begins. Help output is registered when the
command is built; add the runnable example as a help
text block.

Testing: Unit tests for parser behavior covering: missing
title, empty plan body, malformed acceptance criterion.
CLI tests for import covering the title error (non-zero
exit), empty plan warning (zero exit, warning captured),
AC shape error (non-zero exit). CLI tests for derive
covering the empty-plan failure (non-zero exit, actionable
message). Snapshot test for import help output containing
the runnable example. Test that dry-run import produces
the same errors and warnings as a real import.

Covers: @plan-import-format-guidance ac-missing-title-fails-import,
ac-empty-plan-import-warns, ac-empty-plan-derive-fails,
ac-ac-shape-mismatch-fails-import,
ac-ac-shape-mismatch-describes-shape,
ac-help-describes-format, ac-error-no-external-references.

tasks.title: Implement single-command version upgrade
tasks.description:
Add an upgrade command that detects version skew between a
project and the installed kspec version, runs all required
migrations, re-renders skills, regenerates the auto-generated
agent instructions file, repairs gitignore entries, and
reports the net result.

Why: Projects today go through silent breakage on upgrade
because required migrations are run manually, rendered
skills go stale without warning, and new defaults are not
backfilled. A single upgrade command eliminates version
skew as a failure mode.

What:
- Add a new top-level command named upgrade. It accepts no
  required arguments. It accepts a dry-run flag and a
  force flag.
- Version detection pipeline:
  * Target version: read from the package manifest the CLI
    ships with. This is always authoritative.
  * Source version — preferred path: read the last-known
    version from a dedicated field in the existing setup
    seeding state file (the same file that already stores
    permission and memory seeding state). A new field name
    is added there; no new file.
  * Source version — fallback path: if no recorded version
    exists, infer it from the observable shape of project
    state. Build a small set of probes for distinguishing
    known major-version states: for example, the presence
    of a legacy monolithic task storage file versus the
    per-task split directories, the presence or absence of
    the scaffolded project config file, the presence or
    absence of the review-plan rendered skill, the content
    of the task storage format marker field in the
    manifest. Each probe maps to a bounded version range.
    The inferred version is the newest version consistent
    with every probe result.
  * Source version — unknown: when no set of probes is
    conclusive (for example, a project with hand-edited
    state that does not match any known shape), report
    the source as unknown and treat the project as if it
    were on the oldest supported version. Every step in
    the upgrade pipeline must be safe to run in this mode
    because the fallback is "run everything".
  * The source version result carries a confidence
    marker: exact (read from state file), approximate
    (inferred from probes), or unknown. The upgrade
    reports the marker alongside the version.
  * When source and target match with exact confidence,
    report the project as current and exit successfully
    without making changes. When source and target match
    with approximate confidence, still run the pipeline
    (as a safety net) but label it as a refresh rather
    than an upgrade.
- Upgrade pipeline (each step reports its result):
  1. Run the existing task storage migration. Report the
     number of tasks migrated (or zero).
  2. Re-render skills using the existing setup force-render
     behavior. Report how many skills were added, updated,
     and removed since the previous state.
  3. Regenerate the auto-generated agent instructions file
     using the existing generation command. Report whether
     the file changed.
  4. Run the gitignore repair step from the gitignore
     completion work. Report which entries were appended.
  5. Scaffold any missing files that the init setup scaffold
     steps would create on a fresh project (config file,
     default module, default agents and conventions, default
     reflection hook) — but only create what is missing;
     never overwrite. Each skipped item is reported as a skip.
  6. Write the new current version to the last-known version
     state file.
- When the dry-run flag is set, every step reports what it
  would do without making changes, and no state file is
  written.
- When any step fails, the command exits with a non-zero
  status and reports which step failed and what state the
  upgrade left the project in.
- The command output ends with a manual follow-up section
  that lists any scaffolded or updated files the user
  should review.

How: The existing setup force pathway under
src/cli/commands/setup.ts already covers most of the
mechanics (skill re-render, agents regeneration). Build the
upgrade command as a composition of existing step functions
plus the new task storage migration invocation (library
function under src/cli/commands/task-migrate.ts or the
equivalent). Store the last-known version in the same
state file pattern used by setup seeding; add a new field
rather than a new file. The command handler registration
goes in src/cli/index.ts alongside the other top-level
commands.

Testing: Integration tests covering each upgrade scenario:
pre-versioning project (no state file), current project
(no-op), project with legacy task storage, project with
stale skill renders, project with missing gitignore
entries, project with missing scaffolded files. Test
dry-run for each scenario. Test failure propagation when a
step fails.

Covers: @single-command-version-upgrade ac-detects-skew,
ac-source-version-fallback, ac-source-version-unknown,
ac-reports-skew, ac-runs-task-storage-migration,
ac-rerenders-skills, ac-regenerates-agents-file,
ac-restores-gitignore-entries, ac-idempotent-when-current,
ac-reports-manual-follow-ups, ac-dry-run-reports,
ac-dry-run-no-writes.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Build upgrade command as composition of existing setup step functions.

Version detection: Read lastKnownVersion from .setup-state.json (exact confidence), fall back to probe-based inference (approximate), then unknown as last resort. Probes: task_storage.format field, kynetic manifest version, presence of kspec.config.yaml, presence of rendered skills.

Upgrade pipeline steps (reusing existing functions):
1. Task storage migration - extract inline closure from task.ts into a reusable function
2. Re-render skills - reuse renderSkillsForSetup()
3. Regenerate agents file - reuse generateAgentInstructions()
4. Gitignore repair - reuse ensureKspecGitignore()
5. Scaffold missing files - reuse scaffoldProjectConfig(), scaffoldDefaults(), ensureDefaultReflectionHook()
6. Write lastKnownVersion to .setup-state.json

Dry-run and force flags threaded through to each step. JSON output via output() dual-mode pattern.

Test plan: 12 spec ACs + trait ACs (error-guidance, exit-codes, dry-run, json-output). E2E tests using kspec() helper in temp dirs with initGitRepo + kspec init.

tasks.title: Author release notes and expose via CLI
tasks.description:
Create a standardized release notes file in the repository,
add a CLI command to display its entries, wire them into
the upgrade command's output, and update the release skill
to be the single source of truth for how release notes are
authored and maintained.

Why: Without release notes, users upgrade blind and have
no way to discover new configuration knobs or behavioral
changes. A single canonical source that the CLI reads
directly prevents drift between documentation and reality.
The notes are intended for humans first — keeping the file
format simple and human-authored (rather than a strict
machine-readable schema) keeps friction low and lets the
release skill document the conventions the CLI relies on.

What:
- Create a single canonical release notes file in the
  repository root in standardized markdown with one
  per-version section per release. The file is human-
  authored, reviewed by humans, and shipped in the
  published package. No new machine-readable schema.
- Define the section conventions (version heading,
  summary paragraph, "New or changed configuration"
  subsection, "Breaking changes" subsection) in the
  release skill rather than in this plan so authoring
  and CLI consumption share one source of truth.
- Populate the file with an entry for every released
  version since versioning began, plus an "unreleased"
  entry for changes staged for the next release.
- Add a top-level CLI command that reads and displays
  release notes. The command accepts no arguments to
  show the current version's notes, and accepts from and
  to version flags to show a range. Invalid version
  ranges produce actionable errors. Output is the
  markdown section as authored; no reformatting, no
  alternate structured output mode.
- Extend the upgrade command from the prior task so that
  it reads the release notes file, filters to every
  intervening version between the previous and current
  versions, and appends those sections to its output.
- Update the existing release skill with a "Maintaining
  release notes" section that covers: where the file
  lives, how to add an entry, the section conventions
  above, when to promote the unreleased entry to a
  versioned one, and the exact pre-release check that
  ensures the notes for the version being released are
  non-empty. Enforcement of the update step lives in the
  release skill, not in a separate specification.

How: The file lives at the repository root and is added
to the published files list in the package manifest. A
new parser module under src/parser/release-notes.ts
exposes load, get-version, and get-range functions using
a small heading-based markdown walker. The CLI command
handler lives in src/cli/commands/release-notes.ts. The
upgrade command imports the range helper and prints the
relevant slice. The release skill lives under the shared
release skill file (see skills list); patch it with the
new section.

Testing: Unit tests for the parser covering well-formed
input, missing version, and range queries. CLI tests for
the display command covering current and range modes.
Integration test that the upgrade command's output
includes the relevant notes for a simulated version skew.
Skill change is verified by a test that loads the skill
and asserts the new section headings exist.

Covers: @release-notes-accessible ac-current-version-notes,
ac-version-range-notes, ac-upgrade-surfaces-notes,
ac-notes-mention-new-config.

- New src/parser/release-notes.ts: loadReleaseNotes (reads file), getVersionNotes (returns markdown slice for version), getRangeNotes (returns intervening slices sorted chronologically by file order). Heading-based walker; no reformatting. Errors: file not found, unknown version, invalid range.

tasks.title: Remove doctor false positive and add scaffold checks
tasks.description:
Fix doctor's skill rendering check to look at the real
rendered skill locations, add a check for the scaffolded
config file, add a version skew check that points at the
upgrade command, and ensure every warning and error
includes a concrete resolution command.

Why: Doctor currently emits a persistent false-positive
warning about missing rendered skills even when skills are
clearly rendered, and misses several conditions that the
other tasks in this plan make detectable. Users ignore
doctor output because they have learned it is unreliable.
Doctor should be the single reliable signal that a project
is ready for work.

What:
- Replace the existing rendered skills check with one that
  inspects the real rendered skill locations (the same
  locations the setup command writes to). The check must:
  * Report healthy when any supported rendered skill
    location contains the expected skill files.
  * Report a warning when no supported rendered skill
    location contains any rendered skills, and name the
    command that re-renders.
  * Never report a warning when the setup command would
    consider the project up to date.
- Add a scaffold check that reports a warning if the
  project is missing the scaffolded config file, and
  names the scaffold command (upgrade or setup with
  force, depending on which is user-facing).
- Add a version skew check: read the last-known version
  from the state file (added by the upgrade command
  task); if it differs from the currently installed
  version, emit a warning and name the upgrade command.
- Audit every other check's warning and error messages.
  Every message must include a concrete command or action
  the user can run. Messages that say "run setup" must
  now name the specific setup subcommand or flag.
- The task storage legacy error must name the upgrade
  command as the preferred resolution, with the
  task-migrate command as the lower-level fallback.
- Doctor output format stays the same: sections with
  check results, a summary line, and a non-zero exit code
  when errors are present.

How: The doctor command handler lives in
src/cli/commands/doctor.ts. Find the rendered skills
check and inspect the real rendered-skill directory
constants from the setup command (they are the same
constants the skill rendering step writes to). Add new
check functions for the scaffold presence and version
skew. The existing check output formatting helper already
takes a resolution message — ensure every call site
provides one.

Testing: Unit tests for each new check covering healthy
and unhealthy paths. Integration test that runs init with
setup on a fresh temp directory and then runs doctor,
asserting no warnings are emitted. Snapshot test for the
doctor output format showing resolution commands on every
warning and error. Test that after a simulated version
downgrade, doctor surfaces the version skew warning.

Covers: @doctor-reports-actionable-state ac-skills-check-accurate,
ac-skills-check-missing, ac-config-scaffold-detected,
ac-version-skew-detected, ac-all-actionable.

notes.author: @claude

Approach:

1. Skills check (ac-skills-check-accurate, ac-skills-check-missing): The existing check in src/parser/setup-status.ts scans .claude/skills/ and .factory/skills/ for kspec-managed markers. Core skills on claude-code render to .claude/plugins/kspec/skills/ and are plugin-provided — setup-status does NOT scan that location. If missing, emit warning naming `kspec upgrade` (user-facing single-command upgrade that scaffolds missing files; fallback is `kspec setup --force` per upgrade.ts code).

3. Version skew check (ac-version-skew-detected): Read lastKnownVersion from .kspec/.setup-state.json and compare to getKspecPackageVersion(). If they differ, emit warning naming `kspec upgrade`. If lastKnownVersion missing (pre-upgrade project), skip the check silently.

tasks.title: Fix meta set multi-value option parity
tasks.description:
Make repeated multi-value options on meta set accept and
preserve every value the user supplies, matching the
behavior of the meta add flow.

Why: Repeated add-rule, add-skill, and add-capability flags
on meta set currently drop all values except the last,
silently. This diverges from meta add (which preserves all
repeated values) and forces users to run multiple commands
to do what should be one atomic update. It is a real logic
bug, not a documentation gap.

What:
- Audit the meta set command handler for every flag that
  accepts repeated values (at minimum: add-rule, add-skill,
  add-capability, remove-rule, remove-skill,
  remove-capability). Confirm which are currently
  last-write-wins.
- Change each affected flag to be a variadic option (or the
  equivalent in the CLI library the project uses) so the
  handler receives an array of every supplied value.
- Update the handler logic to append every supplied value
  for add flags and remove every supplied value for remove
  flags, in a single atomic write to the meta item.
- When a single invocation contains both add and remove
  flags for the same field, apply removes before adds so
  the user's intent is unambiguous (an explicit "replace
  these with those" reads correctly).
- The fix must not change the behavior of meta add; that
  flow already works correctly and the regression tests
  must protect it.

How: The handler lives in src/cli/commands/meta.ts under
the set subcommand. The CLI library is commander; the
correct pattern is to declare the option as variadic
(option with three dots in the declaration) and consume
it as an array. Compare the implementation of meta add
for the exact pattern.

Testing: Unit tests for the handler covering: repeated
add-rule preserves all rules, repeated add-skill preserves
all skills, repeated add-capability preserves all
capabilities, repeated remove flags remove all named
values, mixed add and remove flags apply in the expected
order. Regression test for meta add behavior to ensure the
fix does not break it.

Covers: @meta-set-multi-value-parity ac-repeated-add-rule-all-kept,
ac-repeated-add-skill-all-kept, ac-repeated-add-capability-all-kept,
ac-remove-flags-unchanged, ac-mixed-add-and-remove.

Verified repeated meta set add/remove flags preserve all supplied values, remove-before-add ordering, and no meta add regression. npm test passed (2120 suites, 7763 tests).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Fix multi-value option parity in meta set command.

The bug: Commander option declarations in meta set use single-value syntax (<val>) instead of variadic (<val...>). When repeated flags are passed, Commander keeps only the last value.

Affected options: --add-capability, --add-tool, --add-convention, --add-skill, --add-rule, --add-tag, --remove-capability, --remove-tool, --remove-convention, --remove-skill, --remove-tag (11 options total).

Already correct: --add-dispatch-rule (uses collectRepeatedOptionValues accumulator).

Fix plan:
1. Change all 11 affected option declarations to use collectRepeatedOptionValues accumulator (consistent with existing --add-dispatch-rule pattern).
   - Using accumulator rather than variadic <val...> because add-rule values may contain spaces/quotes, and the accumulator pattern is already established in this codebase.
2. Update all handler code to iterate arrays instead of treating values as single strings.
3. For mixed add+remove: apply removes first, then adds (per spec).
4. Write E2E tests covering all 5 ACs.
5. Regression test for meta add behavior.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation complete. Changes:

1. Option declarations: Changed 11 options on meta set to use collectRepeatedOptionValues accumulator (--add-capability, --add-tool, --add-convention, --add-skill, --add-rule, --add-tag, --remove-capability, --remove-tool, --remove-convention, --remove-skill, --remove-tag). Each now receives an array instead of last-write-wins string.

2. Handler logic: Restructured the agent handler to apply removes before adds (per ac-mixed-add-and-remove). All array field mutations iterate the full arrays.

3. Convention handler: Updated --add-rule to iterate the array for conventions.

4. Tests: 12 new test cases covering all 5 ACs plus regression tests for meta add behavior, deduplication, multi-tool operations, and remove-then-re-add ordering.

5. Full test suite: 7763 tests pass, 0 regressions.

tasks.title: Shadow worktree cross-contamination guard
tasks.description:
Ensure kspec commands that create or repair the shadow worktree cannot mutate shadow state belonging to any other working tree of the same git repository, regardless of which working tree they are invoked from. When a user invokes a shadow-lifecycle command from a linked git worktree, the command must not touch the main working tree's shadow worktree and must tell the user where to run it instead.

Closes 10 new ACs on @worktree-support: ac-init-linked-wt-unchanged, ac-init-main-wt-unchanged, ac-init-guidance-direction, ac-init-guidance-path, ac-setup-linked-wt-unchanged, ac-setup-main-wt-unchanged, ac-setup-guidance-direction, ac-setup-guidance-path, ac-shadow-ops-scoped-to-main, ac-shadow-ops-concurrent-safety.
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev after approved review @01KP4RAJ. Verified targeted shadow/worktree regressions and full npm test pass (347 files, 7763 tests, 5 skipped, 0 failed).

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
WHY — incident context.

On 2026-04-11 around 03:38 local time, two concurrent npm test runs inside dispatch-managed linked worktrees reached a shadow-lifecycle code path with the cwd set to the linked worktree. The operation succeeded — but succeeded against the main working tree's shadow worktree, not the linked one. The spec data on the kspec-meta branch was preserved (tip 4c9c302e6 intact), but the main repo's .kspec/ working tree and its worktree admin entry were destroyed. The failure was silent: the destructive command returned exit code zero with no output, and only surfaced later as every subsequent kspec CLI invocation breaking until manual recovery.

The incident is reproducible from a clean repo using only native git commands — it does not require kspec to trigger. The underlying git behavior (a bare relative worktree name resolving across the shared worktree admin of all linked worktrees of the same repo via find_worktree_by_suffix in git's worktree.c) is documented and stable; kspec's guarantee must be built on top of it. The guarantee is product-level: kspec is the primary interface to spec data for every user of the project, and a silent path where concurrent automation destroys a user's spec state is a data-integrity regression.

Recovery is straightforward once the user knows what happened — the shadow branch preserves all data and kspec shadow repair from the main repo rebuilds the worktree — but 'knows what happened' is a high bar for a silent failure. The fix needs to make the failure either impossible or loud.

The secondary lesson is that the project's test helpers have a latent amplifier: a subprocess-spawning helper that silently inherits the vitest worker's cwd when a caller forgets to pass one, which is how an unrelated test reached the buggy code path without anyone writing a line of code targeting the shadow worktree. Enforcing explicit cwd at the test helper layer removes the amplifier and makes any future variant of the same class of bug fail loudly at its origin rather than silently in a shared directory.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
HOW part 1 of 3 — code changes.

Implementation details are owned by the task worker. The following are the known constraints and starting points; the worker is free to propose a different implementation if it closes the ACs more cleanly.

1. Shadow-lifecycle operations must identify their target by absolute path. In src/parser/shadow.ts, each call to git worktree add or git worktree remove for the shadow directory currently passes the bare relative directory name (lines 2777, 2787, 2811, 2818, 2958, 2978). Replace with the absolute path already computed at or near the top of each function (worktreeDir exists in repairShadow at line 2952; an equivalent should be computed once in initializeShadow). Audit createOrphanBranchFallback specifically to confirm it passes an absolute worktreeDir, not directoryName, to every git worktree invocation it makes. This single-mechanism change closes the cross-worktree vector for any correctly-routed caller.

2. Add an entry guard to initializeShadow and repairShadow as defense-in-depth, not as the primary fix. At the top of each function, call a new helper assertMainWorkingTree(projectRoot) that uses a single git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir invocation to detect whether projectRoot is a linked worktree. On detection, throw a ShadowError with an instructional message naming the main working tree's path (derived from the parent of the git common directory). No bypass flag. Framing: after step 3 lands, the common-path callers always pass mainRoot and the guard never fires — the guard exists to catch any future caller (or regression) that forgets to resolve, so that the destructive path cannot reopen.

3. Correct kspec init's project root resolution. src/cli/commands/init.ts:155 currently calls getGitRoot(targetDir) directly, which returns the linked worktree root when invoked from a linked worktree. Replace with the same pattern src/cli/commands/shadow.ts:28 uses: resolveProjectRoots(targetDir)?.mainRoot ?? getGitRoot(targetDir). Then add explicit detection of the linked-worktree case before calling initializeShadow, and hard-error with instructional message naming the main working tree path. Hard error (non-zero exit) is the chosen implementation per the task's lean-toward-option-(b) direction.

4. Audit kspec setup and other lifecycle entry points. Verify src/cli/commands/setup.ts:600 and :617 pass projectRoot resolved via the worktree-aware path. Also audit src/cli/commands/shadow.ts end-to-end even though it already uses resolveCliProjectRoot(). Apply the same hard-error pattern to any setup path that would invoke a lifecycle op from a linked worktree.

5. Grep for every caller of initializeShadow( and repairShadow( in src/ — explicitly including src/cli/commands/init.ts, src/cli/commands/setup.ts, src/cli/commands/shadow.ts, src/parser/index.ts, and any daemon-side caller. Document the audit in a task note with per-caller verdict: resolves to main / resolves to linked and needs fix / N/A.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
HOW part 2 of 3 — test helper and convention rule.

6. Test helper cwd enforcement. Change tests/helpers/cli.ts:111 so kspec() requires cwd: string. Delete the cwd ?? process.cwd() fallback at line 167. Run tsc --noEmit to find every caller that compile-fails; fix each by passing the correct per-test temp dir. Known offender: tests/clone-for-testing.test.ts:99 via import { kspecOutput as kspec } from ...

7. Add the convention rule to the testing domain via:

   kspec meta set testing --add-rule "Test helpers that drive kspec CLI subprocesses must require an explicit cwd parameter. Never fall back to process.cwd() — a missing cwd is a test bug, not a default. A silent fallback caused a shadow worktree destruction incident on 2026-04-11."

After adding the rule, run kspec agents generate to refresh kspec-agents.md and commit the regenerated file alongside the source changes.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
HOW part 3 of 3 — regression tests.

All tests must use isolated temp dirs created via createTempDir() from tests/helpers/cli.ts and register cleanup via onTestFinished. None may touch the real project's .kspec/ or any path outside their own temp tree. Every test must include an // AC: @worktree-support ac-<id> annotation immediately above the test block for each AC it covers.

Shared baseline fixture — 'main unchanged' assertion method. Before the operation under test, capture: (1) git worktree list --porcelain full output, (2) the SHA of the shadow branch tip via git rev-parse kspec-meta, (3) the target of readlink .kspec/.git (or fs.readFile on the .git file), (4) the mtime and inode of the .kspec/ directory. After the operation, re-capture all four and assert byte-equal on the first two and identity on the last two. This catches silent gitdir pointer mutations, worktree admin entry changes, and directory re-creation that a naive 'does .kspec/ exist' check would miss.

Test files to add:

a. tests/shadow-cross-worktree-isolation.test.ts — Low-level test calling initializeShadow() / repairShadow() directly with a linked worktree path as projectRoot. Asserts the guard throws with a message naming the main path. Closes ac-shadow-ops-scoped-to-main.

b. tests/init-from-linked-worktree-existing-shadow.test.ts — Main has a healthy shadow. Linked worktree invokes kspec init. Assert baseline comparison on main (unchanged), linked worktree has no .kspec/ created, stdout/stderr contains the main working tree path, exit code is non-zero. Closes ac-init-linked-wt-unchanged, ac-init-main-wt-unchanged, ac-init-guidance-direction, ac-init-guidance-path.

c. tests/init-from-linked-worktree-empty-main.test.ts — Main has NO shadow. Linked worktree invokes kspec init. Assert main still has no .kspec/, linked worktree has no .kspec/, stdout/stderr contains the main working tree path, exit code is non-zero. Closes the same four init ACs for the empty-main edge case.

d. tests/setup-from-linked-worktree.test.ts — Analogous to (b) for kspec setup. Closes all four setup ACs.

e. tests/repair-from-linked-worktree-broken-main.test.ts — Main's shadow is broken (worktree dir exists but .git pointer is invalid). Linked worktree invokes kspec shadow repair. Assert main's shadow is recovered (the command proceeds via resolveCliProjectRoot → mainRoot), linked worktree has no .kspec/ created, command exits successfully. Verifies ac-shadow-commands still holds and that the new guard does not over-fire on legitimate shadow ops. Closes ac-shadow-ops-scoped-to-main for the repair flow.

f. tests/shadow-lifecycle-concurrent.test.ts — Spawn two kspec subprocesses concurrently: one from main running kspec shadow repair, one from a linked worktree running the same. Await both. Assert main's shadow is in a consistent state (kspec shadow status succeeds) and the linked-worktree invocation was refused cleanly (per the option (b) lean) while the main invocation ran to completion without damage. Closes ac-shadow-ops-concurrent-safety.

8. Dispatch worker smoke test. After the guard lands, run a minimal dispatch invocation (a dry-run or a short task) to verify kspec shadow status, kspec shadow log, kspec shadow resolve, and kspec shadow sync all still function from within a dispatch-managed linked worktree — these commands should NOT go through initializeShadow/repairShadow and the guard should not fire. Document the verification in the task note. Per ac-dispatch-cwd, dispatch agents legitimately run from linked worktrees and must remain able to read shadow state.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
NOT IN SCOPE.

- Changing the shadow branch name, layout, or storage format.
- Changing how the dispatch engine creates or manages its own worktrees — dispatch worktree lifecycle is owned by @dispatch-invocation-worktree-isolation and is unchanged by this task.
- Adding mutation-lock coverage for shadow lifecycle operations. @scoped-dispatch-shadow-serialization already defines serialization for metadata mutations; this task is orthogonal and does not need new locks.
- Broader refactoring of tests/helpers/cli.ts beyond the single required-cwd enforcement.
- Retroactive forensics on the 2026-04-11 dispatch sessions — root cause is already proven and reproduced.
- A dependency on @complete-auto-gitignore or its task — unrelated.
- Feature-flagging the guard or adding a bypass environment variable. Any legitimate use case is better served by running from the main working tree.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
SUCCESS CRITERIA.

1. All six new regression tests pass after the fix and fail against the unfixed baseline (confirming they catch the bug — run in both directions as part of the fix verification).
2. Full test suite passes including the pre-existing shadow/worktree/dispatch tests.
3. Manual verification from a linked worktree: kspec init, kspec setup, and kspec shadow repair. First two hard-error and emit instructional output including the main working tree path. Third succeeds against main.
4. Reproducing the /tmp/gw-test suffix-match scenario against a kspec-fixed build leaves the main shadow worktree intact.
5. tsc --noEmit passes with the required-cwd signature on tests/helpers/cli.ts.
6. The new convention rule appears in kspec-agents.md after kspec agents generate.
7. Dispatch smoke test confirms read-side shadow commands (status, log, resolve, sync) still work from linked worktrees.
8. Task note at completion includes: (a) the file/line changes made, (b) the list of ACs closed per test, (c) the before/after output of the /tmp/gw-test suffix-match repro, (d) the convention rule ID that was added, (e) the dispatch smoke-test verification result, (f) the grep audit from HOW step 5 with per-caller verdicts.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
REPRODUCER (for worker reference).

Minimal standalone repro in /tmp — does not involve kspec code at all, confirms the underlying git behavior the fix must guard against:

  cd /tmp && rm -rf gw-test && mkdir gw-test && cd gw-test
  git init -q
  git config user.email t@t.com && git config user.name t
  echo hi > x && git add x && git commit -qm init
  git checkout -q --orphan meta
  git rm -qrf . 2>/dev/null
  git commit -q --allow-empty -m meta
  git checkout -q main
  git worktree add .kspec meta -q
  git worktree add ./sub HEAD~0 -q
  cd sub
  git worktree remove .kspec --force    # exit 0, removes /tmp/gw-test/.kspec
  cd ..
  git worktree list                      # .kspec is gone

The pre-fix kspec code hits the same pattern when initializeShadow/repairShadow is called from a cwd inside a linked worktree: it runs git worktree remove directoryName --force where directoryName is the bare string '.kspec'. Git's find_worktree_by_suffix matches the suffix across the shared worktree admin and finds the main working tree's shadow worktree.

Post-fix, the same repro must leave the main .kspec/ intact — the test in tests/shadow-cross-worktree-isolation.test.ts should reproduce this scenario programmatically.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach (user-approved):

3-layer defense:
1. Absolute paths to git worktree add/remove in shadow.ts (lines 2777, 2787, 2818, 2958, 2978, 205) - closes root cause
2. Function-level guard assertMainWorkingTree() in shadow.ts - defense in depth
3. Command-level hard-error in init.ts and setup.ts - user-friendly early exit

Plus:
- Required cwd in kspec() helper (tests/helpers/cli.ts)
- Testing convention rule via meta set
- 6 regression tests with baseline fixture assertion method
- Shared error message in strings/validation.ts as linkedWorktreeError()

Test-first: write tests, run against unfixed baseline to confirm they catch the bug, implement fix, re-run.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation complete. Ready for review.

(a) File/line changes:
- src/parser/shadow.ts:
  * ShadowError union: added LINKED_WORKTREE_NOT_SUPPORTED code.
  * New exported helpers: buildLinkedWorktreeMessage(), assertMainWorkingTree() — shared message builder + defense-in-depth guard.
  * initializeShadow: added assertMainWorkingTree() call at entry; replaced bare directoryName with absolute worktreeDir in worktree remove (L2850), worktree add remote (L2860), worktree add --orphan (L2883), worktree add local (L2892).
