tasks.title: Suppress CLI auto-start daemon in tests to stop orphan daemon leak
tasks.description:
## What

Add `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1` as the default env for tests that spawn the `kspec` CLI subprocess so `maybeAutoStartDaemon()` (src/cli/index.ts:143) does not fire implicitly and leave orphan detached daemons pointing at soon-to-be-deleted test fixtures.

## Why

On 2026-04-14 a root-cause investigation of four blocked tasks (all hitting `build-workspace-artifacts` bootstrap failures during dispatch reviewer provisioning) surfaced 45 orphan `dist/daemon/index.js` processes accumulating since morning (~4.3 GB RSS total; one runaway at 61% CPU after 3+ hours). They were all spawned implicitly by the CLI's auto-start hook when test subprocesses ran any `kspec` command outside the `skipCommands` list (`init`, `serve`, `help`, `kspec`) without `KSPEC_SESSION_ID` or `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON` set. The resulting resource pressure is the most plausible trigger for the review-worktree build failures (the diagnostic output is truncated at 4000 chars from the start, so the actual error tail is lost — see separate follow-up).

The prior daemon-leak fixes (@task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup and @task-lint-rule-test-daemon-cleanup, both merged 2026-04-09) targeted EXPLICIT daemon-spawning patterns (`serve start --detach` strings and direct `spawn(DAEMON_ENTRY, ...)` calls). They do not cover the IMPLICIT auto-start path, and the lint rule cannot see it because there is no spawn in the test source — the CLI binary spawns the daemon transparently on the test's behalf.

## What to change

1. `tests/helpers/cli.ts` — in the `defaultEnv` block around line 187 (inside `export function kspec(...)`), add `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON: "1"`. Because line 208 merges env as `{ ...cleanEnv, ...defaultEnv, KSPEC_AUTHOR: "@test", ...env }`, caller-provided `env` still wins, so tests that need to exercise the auto-start code path can opt in by passing `env: { KSPEC_NO_DAEMON: "" }` (empty string is the existing documented reset — see `src/cli/pid-utils.ts:27` `isFalsyNoDaemonValue`).

2. `tests/setup.test.ts` — in the local `cleanEnv()` at line 190 (inside `describe("kspec setup without agent environment", ...)`), add `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON: "1"` to the returned env object. That test uses direct `spawnSync` rather than the `kspec()` helper, so the helper default does not reach it and it needs its own fix.

## What NOT to change

- Do NOT touch `src/cli/index.ts` or any production code. tasks.title: Capture bootstrap failure output tail so actionable error detail is preserved
tasks.description:
## What

Change `summarizeOutput()` in `src/agent-runtime/bootstrap.ts:129` to slice the TAIL of the combined stdout+stderr output (`combined.slice(-4000)`) instead of the HEAD (`combined.slice(0, 4000)`).

## Why

This is a bug fix, not a behavior change. The function is the sole source of the `failureMessage` / `steps[].output` text stored on dispatch workspace metadata and surfaced in `[DISPATCH-BOOTSTRAP]` task notes when a bootstrap step fails.

Build-tool error messages (`npm error`, `vite build failed`, `tsc error TS####`, stack traces) always emit at the END of stdout/stderr — after the progress output that dominates the first N thousand characters. The current head-slice throws the error away and captures only the startup banner plus the first chunk of progress noise. On 2026-04-14 this blind spot wedged root-cause analysis of four simultaneously-blocked tasks (`@task-scaffold-project-config`, `@task-complete-gitignore`, `@task-derivable-default-module`, `@task-plan-import-format-guidance`). Every one of them had an identical block reason that cut off mid-Svelte-warning with no visible error, and the actual failure cause had to be inferred from system-level evidence (orphan test daemons, resource pressure) rather than read directly from the recorded output.

## Spec alignment

This fix is in service of existing acceptance criteria, not a new behavior:

- `@dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract` ac-6: 'Bootstrap fails because dependencies or runtime requirements cannot be satisfied automatically ... the dispatcher records the failure with ACTIONABLE DETAIL and either blocks the task or marks the workspace unhealthy.' Recording 4000 chars of banner text with the error trimmed off does not satisfy 'actionable detail'.
- `@trait-error-guidance` ac-1 (inherited by `@dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract`): 'includes description of what went wrong'. The head-slice consistently omits the description of what went wrong.

No new AC is required. No spec update is required. The fix brings the implementation into compliance with specs that already exist.

## What to change

1. `src/agent-runtime/bootstrap.ts:129` — change `return combined.slice(0, 4000);` to `return combined.slice(-4000);`.

2. Keep the 4000-char budget (do not widen it; this task is scoped to slice DIRECTION, not to slice SIZE — budget changes are a separate design question).

3. If the tail starts mid-line, that is acceptable — the tail-most bytes are the highest-value bytes. Do NOT add line-boundary alignment logic; it has edge cases and the simple fix is enough.

## What NOT to change

- Do not touch the 4000-char constant. Do not introduce a separate constant or config knob.
- Do not change which streams are captured or how they are concatenated (the `trim().filter(Boolean).join('\n')` prep stays as-is).
- Do not alter the metadata shape (`steps[].output`, `failureMessage`) or how it is written.
- Do not extend this task to also fix the orphan reviewer worktree cleanup — that is tracked separately in inbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `summarizeOutput` returns the LAST 4000 characters of combined stdout+stderr when the combined length exceeds 4000 characters.
- AC2: `tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts` — add a new behavioral test that stubs a bootstrap step with a step command that writes a long predictable stream ending in a distinctive error sentinel (something like `DISPATCH_BOOTSTRAP_TEST_ERROR_SENTINEL_${nonce}`) and exits non-zero. Assert that the recorded `failureMessage` and `steps[].output` on the persisted metadata BOTH contain the sentinel. This is the regression guard — without it the head-slice could silently return.
- AC3: Existing `@dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract` ac-6 test coverage (the test 'records actionable bootstrap failure detail and blocks the task before invocation' near `tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts:1433`) still passes.
- AC4: Full `npm test` suite passes.

## Covers

- `@dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract` ac-6 (bug fix honoring existing AC)
- `@trait-error-guidance` ac-1 (inherited — bug fix honoring existing trait AC)

## Background

Root-caused during the 2026-04-14 investigation of four blocked tasks. See session notes for the full trace. Also see the sibling fix `@task-tests-suppress-cli-auto-start-daemon` (the test-daemon leak that was the actual TRIGGER of those failures); this task fixes the DIAGNOSTIC that made the trigger invisible. The two tasks are independent — either can land first.

tasks.title: Restrict default reflection hook to first idle event
tasks.description:
What:
Restrict the default session reflection hook scaffolded by kspec setup to fire only on the first session idle event of each invocation. Update the spec @default-session-reflection-hook to add a new acceptance criterion describing this behavior, clarify the existing ac-reflection-hook-present wording so it does not conflict with the new constraint, and update the setup pipeline scaffold plus its tests so the created hook carries the required filter.

Why:
Session idle events fire after every turn of a multi-turn session (@session-idle-event, @multi-turn-session-lifecycle). Without a turn-count filter, the default reflection hook triggers reflection on every turn rather than once per invocation. The per-agent reflection hooks that preceded the universal default hook carried a turn-count filter for this reason; when they were consolidated into a single default hook the constraint was not preserved.

How:
1. Update spec @default-session-reflection-hook: amend ac-reflection-hook-present so its wording does not imply the absence of all filters, append a description line describing the first-idle-event constraint, add ac-fires-once-per-invocation, and add relates_to @dispatch-hook-filter.
2. Update the setup pipeline function that scaffolds the default reflection hook so the saved hook object includes a filter matching session idle events with turn count equal to the first turn. The filter value must be persisted as a numeric type — string values never match the exact-equality semantics of hook filter matching and would silently disable the filter.
3. Update the setup reflection hook test suite:
   a. Remove or replace the existing assertion that the scaffolded hook has no filter; assert instead that the hook carries the documented filter shape with a numeric value.
   b. Add a semantic test that exercises the hook filter matching path with two synthetic session idle payloads (one representing the first turn, one representing a later turn) and asserts the hook matches the first and not the second. A shape-only assertion does not validate the acceptance criterion.
   c. Add a round-trip test that writes the scaffolded meta, reads it back through the YAML parser, and asserts the filter value's runtime type is numeric.
4. Run kspec agents generate after the spec change so the generated agent instructions stay in sync with the updated acceptance criteria, and run kspec validate to confirm the spec still parses.
5. A backfill path for existing projects whose scaffolded hook was created without a filter is out of scope — captured as a separate inbox item.

Testing:
Existing creation, idempotency, and user-removal tests remain in place and must continue to pass. New coverage: (a) creation asserts the documented filter with a numeric value, (b) a semantic test verifying the hook filter matches the first-turn event and not subsequent-turn events, (c) a YAML round-trip test verifying filter value type persistence.

Covers: @default-session-reflection-hook ac-fires-once-per-invocation

tasks.title: Persist cleanup completion status on successful workspace reap
tasks.description:
What:

The dispatch workspace registry persists a cleanup.status field per workspace record with allowed values not_scheduled, scheduled, blocked, completed. Each record also has closed_at and updated_at timestamp fields already defined on the schema — this task populates them on successful cleanup rather than adding new fields.

When a workspace's physical cleanup (worktree removal + dispatch branch deletion, performed by the reap code path in src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts reapDispatchWorkspace) completes successfully, the registry record must have cleanup.status transitioned to completed and closed_at populated. Today, the reap path does not write this transition back to the registry: it removes physical artifacts and returns action=reaped while leaving cleanup.status=scheduled. Because the lifecycle-state resolver requires cleanup.status===completed to produce lifecycle_state=closed, no record ever reaches closed, and the retention-purge path (closed records older than the retention threshold, currently 7 days) never fires.

Why:

Because records never reach closed, several invariants break:

1. The workspace registry file grows unbounded — every provisioned workspace accumulates a record instead of being retention-purged.

2. The dispatch engine's active target set (per @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-active-target-rebuilt-on-start: every non-closed record's target branch contributes to the set) continues to include target branches of workspaces whose work is long since merged. When operators clean up deleted integration branches out-of-band, the periodic target-sync (60s interval) fetches those deleted branches and produces warning log spam every cycle, indefinitely.

3. Because the lifecycle-state resolver checks health.status!==healthy BEFORE the merge/cleanup-eligibility transitions, records whose worktrees have been physically removed (by reap itself) get flipped to lifecycle_state=stale on the next reconciliation and remain stuck there. The reap-success path actively creates stale records.

4. Operators cannot trust registry record counts as a signal of active workspaces — the count monotonically grows.

Observed in the current deployment snapshot: 138 records stuck in closing, 252 records stuck in stale, 0 records in closed.

How:

1. Ordering decision (important): Write the registry transition AFTER successful physical removal, not before. Rationale: a pre-removal write would briefly advertise a record as closed while its worktree still exists, and cleanup.status=completed takes resolver precedence over every other state. A post-removal write window leaves a brief scheduled+missing-artifacts state which is safe (resolver treats the record as stale until healed by reconciliation — see step 3 below).

2. On the success branch of reapDispatchWorkspace in src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts (after worktree removal and branch deletion return without error), write a registry update that sets:
   - cleanup.status = completed
   - closed_at = <current ISO-8601 timestamp> (if not already set)
   - updated_at = <current ISO-8601 timestamp>

   Persist via the protected shadow-mutation write path matching @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-8 (commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow or the equivalent guarded path). One shadow-branch commit per cleanup invocation.

3. Self-heal for lost writes: If the process crashes between physical removal and the shadow commit, the record is left with cleanup.status=scheduled and no physical artifacts. Reconciliation must detect this state and heal it forward: when reconciliation observes cleanup.eligible=true AND no tracked physical artifacts remain AND cleanup.status!==completed, transition cleanup.status to completed. This makes the invariant in @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-successful-cleanup-persists-completion durable across interruptions.

4. Idempotency: If cleanup.status is already completed at entry to the reap path, do not re-write the record and do not produce a new shadow commit. Per @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-10, no-op reconciliation must not mutate updated_at.

5. Investigate blocked-path shadow persistence and capture findings as a task note: The two existing blocked branches in reap call writeWorkspaceMetadata(existing.workerWorktreeDir, ...) which writes to the worker worktree's on-disk metadata rather than the shadow registry. Investigate whether this path satisfies @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-8 (protected shadow-mutation path). Document findings as a task note immediately after investigation, including: (a) whether the current path produces a shadow commit, (b) whether losing the worker worktree would lose the blocked-status write, (c) the operational plan if a gap exists — either migrate the write to the shadow path within this task, or record the decision to capture as a follow-up task with rationale. Do not proceed with production changes to the blocked path without recording that decision in a task note first.

6. Partial failure handling: Reap removes the reviewer worktree before the worker worktree. If reviewer removal succeeds and worker removal fails, reap currently throws and never writes completion. The record should remain cleanup.status=scheduled (consistent with partial physical removal) and the caller should see the error. Do not attempt to write completed on partial success.

Testing:

- Success path: A workspace record in closing lifecycle with cleanup.status=scheduled, when reap runs to success, the record has cleanup.status=completed and closed_at populated on return.
- Lifecycle resolver: Given a record with cleanup.status===completed, the resolver returns closed.
- Shadow persistence (ac-8): The completion transition appears in a shadow-branch commit, not only in working-tree state.
- Idempotent re-entry (ac-10): Calling reap a second time on an already-completed record does not produce a new shadow commit and does not change updated_at.
- Lost-write self-heal: A record with cleanup.status=scheduled and no physical artifacts, when reconciliation runs, transitions to cleanup.status=completed without requiring a second reap call.
- Blocked paths unchanged: A reap attempt blocked by active-invocation or unresolved-integration checks still produces cleanup.status=blocked with cleanupBlockedReason preserved, not completed.
- Partial physical removal: If reviewer worktree removal succeeds but worker worktree removal throws, the record remains cleanup.status=scheduled and the error propagates.
- Cross-feature regression: After a successful reap, the dispatch engine's active target set (via /api/agents/dispatch/status) does not include the cleaned-up branch. Follows naturally from @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-active-target-removed-on-cleanup once the transition lands.
- Existing reap-path tests continue to pass.

Rollout note:

First post-fix reconciliation may cascade roughly 138 closing records and 252 stale records through closed in quick succession, with those older than the retention threshold being purged in the same write. This could produce a large shadow commit. Observe the first-run size empirically; if batching is needed, add it then. Do not pre-emptively add batching in this task — defer until empirical need is confirmed.

Out of scope:

- Backfill or migration of the pre-fix stuck records. Tracked separately via an inbox item that decides the backfill approach.
- Narrowing the dispatch target-sync filter to exclude stale/closing/cleanup_blocked lifecycle states. Tracked separately via an inbox item about defense-in-depth filter narrowing.
- Migrating the blocked-path writes to the shadow path if step 5 discovers they are not ac-8 compliant AND the in-task fix would expand scope too far. Capture the decision and any follow-up task in the task note from step 5.

Covers: @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-successful-cleanup-persists-completion, ac-successful-cleanup-populates-closed-at, ac-completed-cleanup-resolves-to-closed, ac-8, ac-10.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Blocked-path shadow persistence investigation (step 5):

Found: Both blocked branches in reapDispatchWorkspace (workspace.ts:3049-3074) call writeWorkspaceMetadata(existing.workerWorktreeDir, metadata), which writes only to the worker worktree's on-disk .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json file. These paths do NOT: (a) acquire withDispatchShadowMutationLock, (b) write to project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml registry, or (c) call commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow. No shadow commit is produced, so the blocked status is lost if the worker worktree is removed or the process crashes.

Reconciliation does NOT compensate: createCleanupRecord (workspace.ts:1212-1223) only emits 'scheduled' or 'not_scheduled' — it never re-computes cleanup.status=blocked. Blocked status originates exclusively from the reap path's writeWorkspaceMetadata call.

Gap: This violates @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-8 for blocked-state transitions. However, in practice the next reconciliation cycle with cleanupEligible=true will compute cleanup.status=scheduled (not blocked) and re-run reap, which will re-block. So the invariant is eventually consistent via re-computation, not durably persisted.

Decision: Migrate the blocked path writes to the shadow persistence path (withDispatchShadowMutationLock + saveWorkspaceRecordToRegistry + commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow) within this task. Rationale: (1) the primary fix already introduces the shadow-persist pattern in reap, so using it consistently for both blocked and completed paths is a minimal scope addition, not scope creep; (2) it closes the ac-8 gap atomically rather than leaving a follow-up task for the same file; (3) it makes the reap path's registry semantics uniformly durable, simplifying reasoning about invariants.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implementation plan:

Approach:
1. Idempotency gate at entry to reap success path: If existing.metadata.cleanupState.status === 'completed' OR the registry record's cleanup.status is already 'completed', short-circuit and return action='reaped' without any writes. Per ac-10, no timestamp bump.

2. Post-removal shadow write on success path: After worktree removal + branch deletion succeed (line 3119), load the current registry record for this workspace and invoke persistWorkspaceRecord with cleanup.status='completed', cleanup.updated_at=now, timestamps.updated_at=now, and timestamps.closed_at=existing||now. This goes through withDispatchShadowMutationLock + saveWorkspaceRecordToRegistry + commitWorkspaceRegistryToShadow (same pattern as line 1767).

3. Partial-failure safety: The physical-removal steps happen BEFORE the registry write. If removal throws, the write never runs; record stays cleanup.status='scheduled' per the task spec. No try/catch around removal — propagate errors.

4. Blocked paths migration: Replace writeWorkspaceMetadata calls in the two blocked branches with a full persistWorkspaceRecord that writes cleanup.status='blocked' through the shadow path. This closes ac-8 gap for blocked state.

5. Reconciliation self-heal in reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry: Before computing cleanup via resolveRegistryStateForTaskStatus, detect the lost-write state: (worker worktree missing-from-disk OR branch missing-locally-and-not-restorable) AND cleanup.eligible AND cleanup.status \!== 'completed'. When detected, set cleanup = {status: 'completed', eligible: true, reason, detail, updated_at: now}. This lets resolveLifecycleState return 'closed' (via cleanup.status check taking precedence). The health.status\!=='healthy' check order is preserved — only cleanup.status takes precedence (existing line 1371).

tasks.title: Implement kspec plan delete command with referential safeguards
tasks.description:
## What

Add a `plan delete` subcommand to the `kspec plan` command group. The subcommand removes a plan record from the durable plan store, enforcing a status gate and referential-integrity checks before mutation. Provides an explicit confirmation bypass, and emits structured payloads that enumerate all applicable refusal reasons for automation consumers.

## Why

kspec has commands to create, read, update, list, and annotate plans but no way to remove one. The `@plan-crud` spec is titled "Plan CRUD Operations" yet only covers CRU. Setting status to `rejected` preserves the record and still counts in `kspec plan list`, so cleanup of test leftovers and abandoned drafts is impossible — manual YAML edits to `.kspec/` are forbidden by the shadow-branch rule. The plan list grows monotonically and signal degrades.

## How

1. **Command registration.** Register `plan delete <ref>` in the plan command group alongside `add`/`get`/`set`/`list`/`note`/`derive`/`branch`/`export`. Follow the `kspec inbox delete` pattern: single positional ref, `--force` flag to skip confirmation.

2. **Ref resolution.** Resolve the ref against the plan store. On not-found, emit the structured not-found payload defined by ac-51; do not fall through into the refusal path.

3. **Status gate.** If status is not `draft` or `rejected`, record a `status-blocked` refusal reason naming the current status (ac-41).

4. **Referential-integrity checks.** Gather all applicable refusal reasons, do not short-circuit on the first:
   - **Derived work (resolvable-at-request-time).** Iterate the plan's `derived_specs` and `derived_tasks`. For each entry, attempt to resolve the reference through the `ReferenceIndex`. Collect each that still resolves as a `derived-work-blocked` reason with the resolved item's ref. Orphan entries (refs that no longer resolve) are skipped. If any resolved, record the reason (ac-42, ac-43).
   - **Referencing tasks.** Iterate tasks with a non-null `plan_ref`. For each, call `ReferenceIndex.resolve()` on the raw `plan_ref` value — do not string-compare `plan_ref` to the target ULID. If the resolver returns the target plan's ULID, record the task as a `referencing-tasks-blocked` blocker. This correctly handles `plan_ref` values stored as either slug or ULID (99.5% of production values today are slug-form). (ac-44)

5. **Emit collected refusals.** If any reasons were collected, emit the complete set — human output summarizes all applicable reasons; JSON output lists each with its blocking items under a stable shape (ac-50). Do not proceed to confirmation or mutation. The human-readable refusal message concatenates all applicable reasons per ac-50 — not just the first detected — so the ac-42/ac-44 "the user is told" phrasing does not imply single-reason output.

6. **Confirmation.** If no refusal reasons were collected, prompt before mutating (ac-45). `--force` bypasses the prompt (ac-46). Follow the same non-interactive conventions already used by `item delete` / `inbox delete`; do not invent new policy for JSON / non-TTY modes — inherit from the established pattern.

7. **Mutation via refactored `deletePlan()`.** The existing `deletePlan()` helper in `src/parser/plans.ts` currently returns `Promise<boolean>` and silently collapses "not-found" and caught I/O exceptions into `false`. Refactor it to `Promise<void>` that **throws** on not-found and on I/O failure, matching the sibling helpers `savePlan` and `mutatePlanAtomically`. The refactor is low-blast-radius: three test call sites in `tests/parser-plans.test.ts` and `tests/yaml-round-trip-stability.test.ts` need updating; zero production callers exist today. In the CLI handler, the not-found case is handled by the ref-resolution step (item 2), so `deletePlan()` is only called with a known-present ULID; a try/catch around the call surfaces real I/O errors as distinct from refusals. If `deletePlan` throws ENOENT (a concurrent writer removed the plan between pre-resolution and unlink), convert the error to the ac-51 not-found outcome so ac-53 idempotency holds under concurrency. Other I/O errors propagate.

8. **Audit trail.** The mutation flows through the standard shadow-branch auto-commit pipeline via `commitIfShadow`, producing a commit with a conventional-commit message (e.g. `chore(plan): delete @plan-slug`) that satisfies ac-48.

9. **Cache invalidation is automatic — do not add an explicit call.** The daemon watches `.kspec/project.plans.yaml` via `KspecWatcher`. On write, the watcher invokes the registered cache-invalidation callback, which maps the file to the `plans` cache domain and schedules a debounced reload. The CLI-layer ref index is per-command (rebuilt on each invocation) — there is no persistent ref-index state to invalidate. The task must **not** introduce an explicit invalidation call; doing so would diverge from how `plan add` / `plan set` / `plan note` behave today.

10. **Branch preservation.** The plan's `branch` field is a reference to a git branch created via `kspec plan branch`. Do not delete the branch itself (ac-49).

11. **Idempotency.** Because not-found is returned for a second removal (ac-53), automated callers can retry or double-invoke without a special refusal path. No explicit code is needed beyond item 2 — the ref-resolution step naturally produces the right outcome.

12. **Help content.** Update `kspec help plan` and any command-help manifests so `delete` appears in the subcommand list.

13. **Tests.**
    - Happy-path removal on `draft` plan; on `rejected` plan.
    - Refuse on each of `active`, `approved`, `completed`; refusal reason `status-blocked` with current status.
    - Refuse when a resolvable derived spec exists; reason `derived-work-blocked` with the blocking spec ref.
    - Refuse when a resolvable derived task exists; reason `derived-work-blocked`.
    - Succeed when all `derived_specs` and `derived_tasks` entries point at unresolvable refs (ac-43).
    - Refuse when a task has `plan_ref` stored as the plan's slug (coverage for resolver-based matching, not raw string comparison).
    - Refuse when a task has `plan_ref` stored as the plan's ULID.
    - When refusal applies for multiple reasons simultaneously (e.g., status-blocked AND derived-work-blocked), the JSON payload lists both.
    - Refusal where `plan_ref` resolves to the target plan AND all `derived_specs`/`derived_tasks` entries are orphaned — only `referencing-tasks-blocked` reason is emitted, with no empty `derived-work-blocked` entry in the payload.
    - Confirmation declined leaves the plan intact; `--force` bypasses the prompt.
    - Not-found ref returns the structured not-found payload; shape distinguishable from refusal payloads.
    - Second removal after successful removal returns not-found, not a refusal (ac-53).
    - Plan's notes are destroyed with the plan; git log of shadow branch still shows the pre-deletion state.
    - Plan's git branch still exists as a git ref after plan removal (ac-49).
    - Unrelated plans retain content, status, notes, derived-work links, branches, and timestamps (ac-52).
    - Shadow-branch commit is produced with a conventional-commit message naming the deleted plan.
    - `deletePlan()` throws on I/O failure (simulate with a locked-file or permission-denied fixture); the CLI surfaces a real error rather than a misleading not-found.
    - Update the three existing `deletePlan()` test call sites to the new `Promise<void>` + throws contract.

## Out of Scope

- Cascading delete (removing derived specs/tasks alongside the plan).
- Deleting the plan's git branch.
- Bulk deletion of multiple plans in one command.
- Soft-delete / undo / archive beyond the existing `rejected` status — the shadow-branch git history is the recovery path.

tasks.title: Extend daemon background shadow sync to all registered projects
tasks.description:
What: The daemon must run background shadow-branch sync for every registered project with shadow remote tracking, not only the project the daemon was launched with. Coverage includes all four registration paths — daemon startup, POST /api/projects, middleware auto-registration via X-Kspec-Dir, and WebSocket project resolution — plus unregistration cleanup (both explicit API DELETE and watcher-permanent-failure) and daemon shutdown. Starting background pulls for a project that already has them must be idempotent.

Why: Today the daemon instantiates a single ShadowSyncScheduler at startup bound to the startup project path. Projects registered afterward receive file watchers and session-sync schedulers but no shadow-sync scheduler. Their shadow branches never pick up remote changes until the user runs `kspec shadow sync` manually. Users serving multiple projects from one daemon (common on developer machines and during dispatch) expect each project to stay in sync. An analogous gap for session sync was closed previously; shadow sync was missed.

How:
1. In packages/daemon/src/server.ts, replace the single `shadowSyncScheduler` variable with `shadowSyncSchedulers: Map<projectPath, ShadowSyncScheduler>`, mirroring the shape of `sessionSyncSchedulers`.
2. Extract `startShadowSyncForProject(projectPath)` and `stopShadowSyncForProject(projectPath)` helpers. Start must be idempotent: if an entry already exists in the map for that project, return without starting a second scheduler. Otherwise read per-project shadow config, return early if remote tracking is not configured, and otherwise instantiate and start a scheduler. Stop removes and stops the scheduler entry if present.
3. Change the startup block to call `startShadowSyncForProject(startupProjectPath)` instead of constructing the scheduler inline.
4. Invoke `startShadowSyncForProject` from the shared `onProjectRegistered` callback in server.ts — the same callback already passed to the projects API routes, the `project-context` middleware, and WebSocket project resolution. This single wiring covers all four registration paths.
5. Invoke `stopShadowSyncForProject` via `projectContextManager.setUnregisterCallback` in server.ts so that both API DELETE and watcher-permanent-failure paths stop pulls.
6. On daemon shutdown, iterate `shadowSyncSchedulers` and stop every scheduler before the process exits.
7. Replace the startup-bound `onPull` handler with a per-project one: when the scheduler for a given project pulls, refresh the shadow metadata cache for that specific project's entity cache — not the startup project's.
8. Add behavioral tests modeled on tests/daemon-session-sync-multi-project.test.ts:
   (a) Project registered via POST /api/projects after startup receives a background shadow pull on the next interval.
   (b) Project registered via X-Kspec-Dir middleware receives a background shadow pull on the next interval.
   (c) Explicitly unregistering a project (API DELETE) stops its background pulls.
   (d) When only the startup project is registered, it still receives background pulls (single-project regression guard).
   (e) A project registered without shadow remote tracking configured does not cause a scheduler to be created.
   (f) Registering the same project twice (e.g., middleware auto-register followed by explicit POST /api/projects) results in only one scheduler being created — verified by counting scheduler constructions or interval firings.
   (g) The per-project `onPull` handler, when invoked for a non-startup project, refreshes that project's shadow metadata cache and not the startup project's.

Acceptance criteria satisfied: @config-shadow ac-13, ac-14, ac-15, ac-16, ac-17.

Out of scope: Changes to the sync fetch/rebase/push logic itself. Dispatch-mode interaction with shadow sync. Multi-daemon coordination. WebSocket broadcast of shadow_sync events (re-use existing scheduler broadcast callback).

tasks.title: Set up docs rendering in the web UI
tasks.description:
Wire the web UI to render Markdown docs content at a
/docs/* route tree.

Why: Docs are reached through the web UI per
@docs-reachability; the rendering pipeline is the bridge
from authored Markdown to rendered pages.

What: Extend packages/web-ui with a [...slug] dynamic
route under /docs that maps URL paths to Markdown files
under the repository's top-level docs/ directory, rendered
through the existing marked + Tailwind typography +
highlight.js pipeline. Docs content is bundled into the
static build so pages work in VITE_STATIC_MODE and in
daemon mode without any API call. Adjust vite.config.ts
(server.fs.allow) to permit reading from ../../docs.
Rendering produces anchored headings and client-side
routing for inter-page navigation.

Covers: @docs-reachability ac-2, ac-3,
@docs-navigation-shape ac-2.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Build-time bundling of docs content via Vite virtual module plugin.

Implementation plan:
1. Vite plugin (vite-plugin-docs.ts): Scans ../../docs/ at build time, reads all .md files, exports a manifest (slug -> {title, content, path}) as a virtual module 'virtual:docs'. This ensures zero runtime network requests - content is embedded in the JS bundle.
2. /docs/[...slug] catch-all route: Dynamic route that looks up slug in the manifest, renders markdown through existing marked + highlight.js pipeline, produces anchored headings (id attributes on h1-h6).
3. Navigation: Add 'Docs' entry to Sidebar (in a new group or alongside existing) and MobileNav. Links to {base}/docs.
4. vite.config.ts: Add server.fs.allow for ../../docs so dev server can read the docs directory.
5. Anchored headings: Custom marked renderer extension for h1-h6 that adds id attributes and anchor links.

Key decisions:
- Using virtual module pattern (not raw file imports) for clean build-time bundling
- Content bundled into JS means it works in both VITE_STATIC_MODE and daemon mode without API calls (AC ac-2, ac-3)
- Client-side routing via SvelteKit goto() for inter-page navigation
- Reusing existing renderMarkdown() pipeline with heading anchor extension

ACs covered:
- @docs-reachability ac-2: Content bundled at build time, no network requests needed
- @docs-reachability ac-3: Static pages, no daemon or SSR required
- @docs-navigation-shape ac-2: Anchored headings with stable direct links

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 1: Addressed all 3 review blockers.

1. Source-scanning tests (blocker): Removed all existsSync/readFileSync-based tests that asserted on source file content. Replaced with behavioral tests: docs module interface tests (plugin pipeline e2e), filterSectionEntries tests (direct function calls with mock data), resolveDocsLink tests (direct function calls). notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fix cycle 3: Addressed the blocker — broken out-of-tree .md links (e.g. ../INSTALL.md from getting-started.md). Root cause: event.preventDefault() was called unconditionally before checking resolveDocsLink() result. Two fixes: (1) click handler now only prevents default when resolution succeeds, (2) added render-time link rewriting in the markdown renderer that rewrites in-tree .md links to SPA routes using the docs manifest. notes.content: [FIX_CYCLE: 4] Review verdict: changes_requested by codex

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fix cycle 4: Addressed both blocker threads about out-of-tree .md links leading to 404s. Root cause: links like ../INSTALL.md from getting-started.md were left as-is in the rendered HTML, but those relative paths are meaningless in the built SPA. Fix: added resolveOutOfTreeHref() that computes the repo-root-relative path for links that escape the docs/ tree, and the markdown renderer now rewrites them to GitHub blob URLs (e.g. https://github.com/lepahc/kynetic-spec/blob/main/INSTALL.md). The repoUrl is configured in vite-plugin-docs and embedded in the virtual module manifest at build time. Rewritten links are marked as external (target=_blank). tasks.title: Make task reads immediately consistent after review verdict transitions
tasks.description: After `kspec review verdict --decision request_changes` auto-transitions a linked task from pending_review to needs_work, an immediate `kspec task get` can still return stale pending_review state before a later read shows needs_work. This creates ambiguity for automated reviewer flows that verify transition completion immediately after submitting a verdict. tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev after approved cycle 3 review. Task mutations now update task cache immediately, invalidate stale task history, and the daemon regression test covers immediate request_changes -> task read consistency.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: After thorough investigation of the review verdict -> task state propagation flow, identified that post-verdict task reads can be stale because:

1. The CLI review verdict handler (review.ts) mutates task state via mutateTask() which writes to disk, but the daemon entity cache is only updated post-command via the generic writeThrough in command.ts. If the writeThrough silently fails (non-fatal catch), the cache remains stale.

2. The daemon REST API route (reviews.ts) does per-ULID writeThrough for transitioned tasks, which is more targeted but relies on the incremental update path.

3. The core issue: mutateTask() does NOT notify the entity cache about the state change. The notification depends entirely on the post-command writeThrough or file watcher (debounced 100ms).

Fix approach: Add inline entity cache write-through within the review verdict handler itself for transitioned task ULIDs, ensuring the cache is updated atomically with the mutation - not deferred to post-command hooks. This makes the verdict handler self-contained for cache consistency.

Edge cases: concurrent commands, write-through failures, entity cache context availability.
Test plan: 8 ACs to verify, integration tests using daemon command API with mock cache, plus CLI-level tests for the direct path.

tasks.title: Remove project-specific inference from dispatch bootstrap; prevent dispatcher runtime environment from leaking into bootstrap step subprocesses
tasks.description:
What:
The dispatch bootstrap phase currently does two kinds of work that were never intended to be part of the general dispatch contract and that originate in one particular project's self-hosted use of dispatch.

(1) When the dispatcher prepares a workspace for bootstrap, it inspects the workspace for a specific set of files (a node package manifest and lockfile, a node build script, a fixed list of directory paths and artifact output paths) and auto-prepends synthetic bootstrap steps to run a package-manager install command and a build command when those files are present. The specific tooling, commands, and paths match one particular project's TypeScript monorepo layout. Any project that uses the dispatcher either gets these synthetic steps implicitly (even if they never configured them) or gets nothing useful from the inspection (if the project is in a different ecosystem).

(2) The kspec serve command deliberately sets a runtime-mode environment value on the daemon it launches so the daemon itself runs under a production runtime configuration. The dispatch bootstrap phase spawns step subprocesses whose environment is a wholesale spread of the dispatcher's own process environment. As a result, that runtime-mode value flows into every bootstrap step subprocess, even though it was set for the daemon and was never intended to influence step behavior. Package managers that honor the variable for dependency pruning (for example, npm treating production mode as omit-dev) produce partial installs; build tools that branch on it produce mismatched builds. The resulting failures surface as module-not-found errors in steps that run after the install, which makes the root cause (a dispatcher-introduced env value) hard to discover.

The combined effect of (1) and (2) was observed as a concrete failure: a reviewer workspace's bootstrap reported a successful install and then a following step failed because a declared devDependency had been silently pruned. The install step was synthetic (dispatcher-authored, item 1) and the pruning env value was dispatcher-introduced (item 2) — two leaks compounding.

Why:
The dispatch runtime bootstrap contract is meant to be a general mechanism that any kspec project can rely on. Baking one project's build layout, tooling, and artifact paths into the dispatcher means: other projects cannot trust the contract without reading the implementation; the self-host project itself cannot evolve its layout without also changing dispatcher code; operators who launch the dispatcher under different runtime conditions observe different bootstrap behavior than they configured, with no diagnostic connecting the cause to the effect.

Analogous precedent for the env scope already exists in the codebase: the agent invocation lifecycle contract requires the agent spawner to strip specific host-introduced variables that would interfere with agent startup, on the principle that variables set for one layer should not silently flow to another. The bootstrap step boundary is structurally the same case.

Reproducer A (configured-only behavior):
1. Start the kspec daemon on a codebase that contains a node package manifest and lockfile in its workspace root.
2. Leave the codebase's dispatch configuration empty — declare no bootstrap steps.
3. Prepare a task workspace and have the dispatcher run the bootstrap phase.
4. Observe that the dispatcher spawns no subprocess commands against the workspace and reports bootstrap success.

Reproducer B (runtime-mode env isolation):
1. In the same setup, configure a bootstrap step whose command records its subprocess environment to a file in the workspace.
2. Before starting the daemon, arrange for a runtime-mode env value to be set in the daemon's own process environment (the serve command does this automatically).
3. Run the bootstrap phase.
4. Observe that the runtime-mode value is absent from the recorded subprocess environment.

How (implementation sketch — adjust after reading the contract ACs):

Primary files expected to change:
- src/agent-runtime/bootstrap.ts — bootstrap module. The step execution site that spreads process.env into child env is in the runShell function around line 88.
- src/cli/commands/serve.ts — the buildDaemonChildEnv function sets the runtime-mode variables on the daemon child env. This function is the source of the leaking values and is correct for its own purpose. Do not change it. The fix belongs at the bootstrap step execution boundary, not at the daemon launch.

Steps:
1. Three new atomic ACs have been added to @dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract covering: (a) bootstrap subprocess command fidelity (no dispatcher modification or addition to declared commands); (b) dispatcher runtime mode configuration values are absent from bootstrap step subprocess environment; (c) declared step order is preserved. All three are origin- and implementation-agnostic in their wording. Implement to satisfy them.

2. Remove all project-specific inference from the dispatcher's bootstrap module:
- Remove the hardcoded build artifact path list.
- Remove the hardcoded build input path list.
- Remove the function that auto-generates a package-manager install step when a workspace manifest and lockfile are detected.
- Remove the function that auto-generates a build step when a build script is declared.
- Remove the reachable helpers that exist only to support the above (the workspace-dependency health check, the manifest-walking dependency resolver, the search-root helper, the build-input mtime walker, the build-output artifact check). These become unreachable once the two implicit step functions are removed. Expect the removal to be on the order of 150 lines.
- Remove the corresponding invalidation-reason strings from state and metadata. The enumerated invalidation signals named in the existing contract (canonical-branch-head change, bootstrap-config change, prior bootstrap failure) are unchanged.

3. Update the bootstrap step execution path so the subprocess environment it spawns each step under has the runtime-mode configuration values removed from the inherited environment, before merging the step-intended variables (role marker, source marker, step name). Do not otherwise modify the inherited environment. Do not touch env that the step's own command sets within itself. The concrete variables to exclude are those the dispatcher sets on its own process at daemon launch for runtime configuration — in the current codebase, those applied by buildDaemonChildEnv in src/cli/commands/serve.ts. The isolation logic should source its list from the same place the dispatcher sets them, so additions stay in sync automatically — do not maintain a second hardcoded list at the bootstrap boundary.

4. Migrate this self-host project's previously-implicit provisioning into its own kspec config: define the install and build commands as explicit bootstrap steps in this project's dispatch configuration, with whatever invocation form is needed to produce a correct development-environment install. This migration is a configuration change for this project only and has no impact on the dispatcher's contract beyond what the code removal in (2) already produced. The kspec configuration surface is implementation detail, not spec surface.

5. Add regression tests annotated against each new AC:
(a) AC a (command fidelity): configured bootstrap step with command string S; assert the spawned subprocess's argv matches S without dispatcher modification; also assert a workspace with no configured steps produces zero spawns.
(b) AC b (runtime mode env isolation): for each environment value the dispatcher sets on its own process to configure its own runtime (enumerated from the daemon-launch env assembly), set that value on the dispatcher process, run a configured bootstrap step that records its subprocess environment, and assert the value is absent.
(c) AC c (order preserved): configured steps in order [S1, S2, S3]; assert spawn order is S1, S2, S3.

6. Update or remove any existing tests and fixtures that asserted on the implicit step generation, the hardcoded path lists, or the health-check functions being removed.

7. Regenerate agent instruction artifacts if any referenced the implicit behavior.

Transition behavior (expected, not a required action):
- Existing workspaces with cached bootstrap state from before the change will auto-invalidate via the existing bootstrap-config-changed signal once this project's kspec configuration gains the new explicit steps, because the configuration hash is computed over configured steps only. No manual metadata reset is required.
- After this change, manual deletion of a workspace's node_modules or build output between invocations is no longer detected by the dispatcher. Reuse proceeds on the existing no-invalidation-signal rule. Operators are responsible for workspace cleanliness between invocations; this is a narrowing of dispatcher scope and is within the existing bootstrap contract.

Acceptance:
- The three new ACs on @dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract are annotated by passing behavioral tests.
- Dispatcher bootstrap module contains no project-specific layout, artifact paths, source paths, tooling names, or package-manager command strings.
- This self-host project's provisioning continues to work via its own configured bootstrap steps, producing an install that matches the declared dependency set regardless of the daemon's runtime environment.
- Bootstrap state metadata contains no invalidation-reason strings tied to the removed implicit behavior.

Interactions and non-issues (stated explicitly so a reviewer does not need to re-research):
- The existing tracked-source-mutation opt-in rule on the bootstrap contract is not relaxed by this change.
- The dispatch workspace registry does not record env-derived or tooling-derived fields and does not require a schema change.
- No change is made to the agent invocation lifecycle contract or its env-stripping behavior. The bootstrap env isolation is a separate boundary with the same pattern.

Out of scope:
- Any language-specific or package-manager-specific logic inside the dispatcher. If a concrete project needs one, it defines the step in its own config.
- Broader env sandboxing beyond the runtime-mode class named in the new ACs. PATH, TMPDIR, locale, authentication env, and other operational environment are not in scope.
- Changes to the kspec configuration surface itself. The self-host project's configured-step migration is an implementation detail of this project's configuration, not a change to the dispatcher contract.

tasks.title: Narrow dispatcher runtime-mode env isolation set to runtime-mode keys only (align implementation with bootstrap contract ac-12 scope)
tasks.description:
What:
The dispatcher exports an environment-variable-name constant DAEMON_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS from the serve command source. It lists three keys. The same constant is used at two different code boundaries:

- At the CLI-to-daemon boundary, the daemon-child-env builder function destructures all three keys from the inherited environment to strip them from the daemon child env, then conditionally re-injects one of the runtime-mode selector keys with a production value based on the configured runtime.

- At the daemon-to-bootstrap-step boundary, the bootstrap step subprocess-env builder function imports the constant and removes every listed key from process.env when assembling each bootstrap step subprocess environment.

One of the three keys is a CLI-only control flag: the daemon-child-env builder strips it on spawn but never re-injects it, so the daemon process never has it. Stripping it again at the bootstrap step boundary is currently a no-op.

The dispatch runtime bootstrap contract acceptance criterion that governs the bootstrap step isolation scopes the behavior to runtime mode configuration values. A CLI-only control flag is not a runtime-mode value. The implementation therefore overshoots the acceptance criterion's scope by continuing to include the CLI-only flag in the constant that both boundaries share.

Why:
Reason one — align implementation to the spec acceptance criterion. ac-12 on @dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract is explicit that the isolation covers only runtime-mode configuration. The implementation reading more broadly invites confusion for future readers and tests.

Reason two — prevent silent regression of the original bug class. The current constant's name and placement suggest "everything the daemon spawn wrangles." A future developer adding a new CLI-only control flag to that constant (because that is the naming signal) would unintentionally also have that flag stripped from every bootstrap step subprocess. If a step shells out to a nested CLI invocation that needs to observe the flag, the nested invocation would silently not see it. Narrowing the shared export to runtime-mode keys, and leaving CLI-only stripping as a local concern of the daemon-child-env builder, eliminates that drift vector.

How (implementation sketch — adjust after reading current code):

Primary files expected to change:
- src/cli/commands/serve.ts — houses the current exported constant and the daemon-child-env builder function.
- src/agent-runtime/bootstrap.ts — imports the current constant in the bootstrap step subprocess-env builder.
- tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts — contains the ac-12 regression test that iterates over the current constant.

Steps:

1. Rename the exported constant in the serve command source from DAEMON_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS to DAEMON_RUNTIME_MODE_ENV_KEYS. Narrow its contents from three keys to the two runtime-mode selector keys (the Node.js and Bun runtime-mode selectors). This constant is the source of truth for runtime-mode keys shared across the daemon-spawn and bootstrap-step boundaries.

2. Leave the daemon-child-env builder function's inline destructure of all three keys unchanged. It continues to strip the CLI-only control flag locally and the two runtime-mode selectors. After the change, this inline destructure is the sole stripper of the CLI-only control flag. Do not factor the CLI-only control flag out into a second shared constant — it is a single-caller concern and a shared export would re-introduce the problem this task is solving.

3. Update the bootstrap step subprocess-env builder in the dispatcher bootstrap module to import the renamed constant. No other logic change to that function.

4. Add doc comments that carry the maintainability intent of the split so a future reader understands why the two concerns are kept separate. Three comment sites:

tasks.title: Gitignore entries miss the .lock/ directory suffix created by acquireFileLock, so dispatch mutation locks appear as untracked content while held
tasks.description:
What:
The kspec file-lock library (`src/parser/file-lock.ts`, function `acquireFileLock` at line 92) implements an advisory lock by creating a directory at `${filePath}.lock/` via `fs.mkdir` and releasing it via `fs.rm`. The `.lock` suffix is an internal convention of the library; every caller passes a base path.

The gitignore writer at `src/parser/gitignore.ts` (function `buildKspecGitignoreEntries` at line 28) emits gitignore entries that include the dispatch shadow mutation lock base path (`.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation`) but does not emit any pattern that covers the `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation.lock/` directory that `acquireFileLock` actually creates at runtime. While the lock is held, the lock directory appears as untracked content at the project root and surfaces in tooling that inspects git status (for example, a session-end checkpoint warning).

The same structural gap applies to any other caller of `acquireFileLock` whose lock base path is at the project root or in a location not covered by a broader gitignore rule. Audit (see step 3) shows that in the current codebase only the dispatch shadow mutation lock is at project root; every other caller locks files inside `.kspec/`, which is already covered by a broader rule.

Why:
This violates an existing acceptance criterion. `@complete-auto-gitignore` ac-no-untracked-after-common-commands states: "Given a fresh project is initialized, when a representative set of commands that create transient state has been run and git status is inspected, then no kspec-created directory appears as untracked content." Running dispatch acquires the shadow mutation lock, which produces a transient untracked `.lock/` directory — a direct AC violation. The directory is short-lived, so the bug is easy to miss but noisy when it surfaces.

How (implementation sketch — adjust after reading current code at `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch`):

Primary files expected to change:
- `src/parser/file-lock.ts` — owns the `.lock/` suffix convention.
- `src/parser/gitignore.ts` — builds the gitignore entry list.
- `tests/` — add regression tests annotated against the governing AC.

Steps:

1. In `src/parser/file-lock.ts`, export a small helper that maps a lock base path to its lock directory path (currently `${filePath}.lock`). Suggested name: `getLockDirPath(filePath: string): string` returning the raw filesystem path (no trailing slash). Refactor `acquireFileLock` to construct its lock directory via this helper so the `.lock` suffix convention has a single documented source of truth.

   The helper returns a plain filesystem path string. Gitignore pattern formatting (appending a trailing slash to scope the entry to a directory) is the responsibility of the gitignore builder, not this helper. This keeps the file-lock module single-purpose.

2. In `src/parser/gitignore.ts`, import the helper from step 1. For each existing gitignore entry that corresponds to a lock base path passed to `acquireFileLock` at runtime, emit both the base path entry AND the lock directory entry. Compose the lock directory entry via the helper and append a trailing slash at the builder site (consistent with how the builder already formats shadow-dir, sessions-worktree-dir, and worktree-root entries).

   In the current codebase, the one lock base path that requires this treatment is `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation`. After this change, the managed block will contain both `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation` and `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation.lock/`.

3. Confirm the audit of `acquireFileLock` call sites rather than re-doing it. The pre-seeded enumeration from a reviewer grep is:

   - Lock base paths at project root (need both base + lock-dir gitignore entries):
     * `src/cli/index.ts:101` — resolved via `KSPEC_SHADOW_MUTATION_LOCK_FILE` env; base path `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation`.
     * `src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts:1681` (inside `withDispatchShadowMutationLock`) — via `getDispatchShadowMutationLockPath()` at `src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts:152`; base path `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation`.
     Both resolve to the same base path. One gitignore addition covers both.

   - Lock base paths inside `.kspec/` (already covered by existing `.kspec/` entry in gitignore, no new entry needed):
     * `src/parser/plans.ts`
     * `src/parser/yaml.ts`
     * `src/parser/reviews.ts`
     * `src/parser/meta.ts`
     * `src/parser/dispatch-workspaces.ts`
     (Plus any other caller discovered during implementation — if any caller has a base path not covered by either case above, add the same base + lock-dir pattern.)

   Record the confirmed enumeration in task notes so future callers of `acquireFileLock` can follow the same rule.

4. Verify that `needsKspecGitignoreUpdate` in `src/parser/gitignore.ts` correctly reports that the managed block needs an update when the new lock-directory entry is absent. The function delegates to `updateManagedBlock`, which compares existing block contents against the current `buildKspecGitignoreEntries` output — so the new entry will be detected automatically once the builder returns it. Confirm via the upgrade self-heal test in step 5b.

   Known pre-existing limitation (do not attempt to fix in this task): when a `.gitignore` exists without a managed block and `--force` is not set, `needsKspecGitignoreUpdate` returns false per `@trait-idempotent-file-scaffold ac-existing-file-preserved-without-force`. Users who never adopted the managed block will not auto-heal via `kspec upgrade`. This is unchanged by this fix.

5. Add regression tests annotated against `@complete-auto-gitignore ac-no-untracked-after-common-commands`:

   (a) Lock-held git-status test: initialize a fresh project (use `setupTempFixtures()` and `initGitRepo()` per the test helpers table in AGENTS.md), acquire the dispatch shadow mutation lock via `acquireFileLock` from `src/parser/file-lock.ts` against the appropriate base path, run `git status --porcelain` via the existing test-runner shell helper, assert that `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation.lock/` does not appear in the status output, release the lock in a `finally` block.

   (b) Upgrade self-heal test: initialize a fresh project so it has a managed block containing the current entries, manually strip the lock-directory entry from the managed block on disk, call `ensureKspecGitignore` against the project root, assert that the lock-directory entry is re-added inside the managed block.

6. Optional snapshot test: `buildKspecGitignoreEntries()` returns an exact ordered list of entries. A snapshot assertion guards against accidental removal or reordering in future edits. Include if it fits the project's testing style; otherwise skip.

7. Update any other tests that iterate over or hardcode the exact gitignore entry list.

Acceptance:
- `buildKspecGitignoreEntries` returns entries that cover both the base path and the lock-directory path for every `acquireFileLock` caller whose base path is at the project root or otherwise not covered by a broader ignored directory. In the current codebase, this means the managed block gains `.kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation.lock/`.
- The lock directory path is composed via a single helper exported from `src/parser/file-lock.ts`. The `.lock` suffix is not hand-written in the gitignore module.
- `acquireFileLock` constructs its lock directory via the same helper, so the suffix convention has one source of truth.
- Task notes record the confirmed enumeration of `acquireFileLock` call sites and whether each site's base path needs new gitignore coverage.
- Regression test (5a) passes: holding the dispatch shadow mutation lock does not produce untracked content.
- Regression test (5b) passes: `ensureKspecGitignore` self-heals a managed block that is missing the lock-directory entry.
- Existing tests continue to pass; any iterating over the exact entry list are updated accordingly.

Interactions and non-issues (stated explicitly so a reviewer does not need to re-research):
- No spec amendment. `@complete-auto-gitignore ac-no-untracked-after-common-commands` already covers this behavior; this task brings the implementation into compliance.
- The companion AC `ac-all-transient-paths-present` lists example transient paths (shadow worktrees, worktree pools, session storage, inbox scratch, plan drafts) but does not mention lock directories. The enumeration is illustrative, not exhaustive; no AC amendment is proposed. Flag during review if a stricter reading is preferred.
- No change to file-lock semantics. The helper exposes an existing convention; it does not alter how locking works.
- No change to managed-block format or the `@trait-idempotent-file-scaffold` behavior of the gitignore writer.
- The `kspec upgrade` flow picks up the new entry automatically via `needsKspecGitignoreUpdate` → `updateManagedBlock`, which consume the same builder output. Fixing the builder fixes all three writers (init, setup, upgrade) that route through `ensureKspecGitignore`.

Out of scope:
- Changing the `.lock` suffix to anything else.
- Migrating from directory-based advisory locks to a different locking mechanism.
- Retroactively editing existing users' `.gitignore` outside the managed block.
- Fixing the pre-existing no-managed-block no-force limitation in `needsKspecGitignoreUpdate`.
- Session-end hooks, checkpoint logic, or any behavior outside the gitignore writer and file-lock helper.

tasks.title: Implement portable skill supporting-file reference resolution
tasks.description:
Implement the portable reference rewrite path for skill supporting files
across skill rendering and adapter prompt injection.

Why: A script-backed merge helper is only usable if skill-authored content
can point at the right rendered script path for whichever platform or
adapter is consuming the skill. Today only {skill:...} alias references
are rewritten; supporting-file paths are not.

What:

  markdown output and prompt-injected skill content both rewrite that
  form to the active platform or adapter path.

  any reference that escapes the skill's own directory tree.
- Preserve existing {skill:...} alias rewriting behavior.

How: Reuse the current skill render and prompt rewrite infrastructure
instead of creating a parallel substitution system. Keep the reference
rewrite deterministic from the source skill id, supporting directory,
and active render root so helper links remain stable across rerenders.

Reference form: {supporting:<relative-path>} where relative-path is relative to the skill's own directory (e.g., {supporting:scripts/merge-helper.sh}).

Key design decisions:
1. New regex alongside SKILL_REFERENCE_TOKEN_RE: SUPPORTING_FILE_REFERENCE_RE matching {supporting:<path>}
2. Resolution: At render time, rewrite to the platform-specific project-root-relative path of the rendered supporting file copy. E.g., for claude-code: .claude/skills/<skill-id>/scripts/merge-helper.sh; for codex: .agents/skills/<skill-subdir>/scripts/merge-helper.sh

Edge cases:
- Path with ../ segments → rejected
- Absolute paths → rejected
- Missing supporting file → explicit error naming the file
- Nested supporting file paths (scripts/subdir/file.sh) → resolved correctly
- Non-markdown supporting files referenced from markdown → resolved

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Implement merge helper as a bash script at templates/skills/merge/files/detached-reviewer-merge.sh.

Architecture:
- Script reads dispatch env vars: KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_BRANCH, KSPEC_DISPATCH_MERGE_TARGET, KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_HEAD, KSPEC_DISPATCH_WORKTREE_ROOT
- Uses git worktree list to find the occupied worktree for the integration target
- Performs merge via git -C <occupied-worktree> merge --no-ff <canonical-branch>
- This works because all worktrees share the same git repo

Flow:
1. Validate required env vars
2. Find occupied worktree for integration target via git worktree list --porcelain
3. Check if canonical head is already ancestor of integration target → no-op
4. Check if occupied worktree has dirty state (tracked modifications or staged drift) → refuse with guidance
5. Run git -C <occupied-worktree> merge --no-ff <canonical-branch> -m <message>
6. On conflict: abort merge, report conflict guidance, exit non-zero
7. On success: verify the occupied worktree matches the new tip

Tests: E2E style using temp git repos with multiple worktrees.
4 ACs to cover: occupied-target-clean-refresh, helper-no-op-merge, helper-refuses-dirty-target, helper-safe-conflict-exit.

tasks.title: Make default session reflection reliable after setup and upgrade
tasks.description:
Fix the default session reflection race where a session.idle hook
fires but its session_prompt action can lose to auto-close and fail
because the session is already inactive. Keep this task
self-contained: do not rely on chat history or a particular affected
project.

Why:
- kspec currently has a runtime fallback idle grace that is too short
  for post-idle session_prompt hooks under realistic dispatch timing.
- Default dispatch agents created by setup can appear correctly
  scaffolded while still depending on that too-short fallback for
  default reflection promptability.
- setup-created default-session-reflect hooks include the first-idle
  turn_count filter, but upgrade-created hooks do not, even though
  @default-session-reflection-hook ac-fires-once-per-invocation
  already promises once-per-invocation reflection.
- This task depends on @task-default-session-reflection-spec-updates so
  implementation and review happen against finalized spec ACs rather
  than mixing spec authoring and implementation in one task.

What:
- Raise the centralized default idle grace used for session.idle hook
  promptability from the current 100 ms to 5000 ms. The default must
  apply when an agent does not override idle_grace_period_ms and a
  same-session idle hook may queue a prompt.
- Ensure kspec-created default dispatch agents get the same effective
  5000 ms idle grace behavior after fresh setup. Prefer a single
  source of truth so runtime fallback, setup defaults, and future
  scaffold code do not drift.
- If explicit session blocks are used to make the scaffolded default
  behavior visible in metadata, update src/cli/commands/setup-defaults.ts
  so DefaultAgentDef and the saved agentData preserve session mode
  auto_close and idle_grace_period_ms 5000 for dispatch-capable
  default agents.
- Update src/cli/commands/upgrade.ts where it creates a missing
  default-session-reflect hook so newly scaffolded hooks include the
  first-idle filter matching the setup-created hook and
  @default-session-reflection-hook ac-fires-once-per-invocation.
- Preserve existing user intent: do not recreate default agents/hooks
  that kspec records as deliberately removed, and do not overwrite an
  existing default-session-reflect hook during this task. Any repair
  of already-existing customized or legacy hooks belongs in a
  separate migration proposal.
- Keep validation/doctor warning behavior out of this task; that
  follow-up remains tracked separately by inbox item @01KQ8PRY.

How:
- Update src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts so DEFAULT_IDLE_GRACE_MS is
  the healthy default used when session.idle hooks exist and an agent
  does not override idle_grace_period_ms.
- Update the default-agent scaffold path only as much as needed for
  fresh setup to satisfy @default-project-agents-and-conventions
  ac-default-agents-reflection-promptable. If explicit session blocks
  are emitted, ensure setup-defaults preserves them from definition
  through saved metadata.
- Update the upgrade scaffold for default-session-reflect so a newly
  created hook has filter.turn_count equal to 1. Reuse the setup-side
  hook shape if practical so setup and upgrade cannot drift again.
- Keep existing first-run/user-removal behavior intact: setup and
  upgrade must not recreate or overwrite default agents/hooks that a
  user deliberately removed or customized.

Testing:
- Add or update a dispatch/invocation regression test that drives an
  idle session with a session.idle -> session_prompt hook and proves
  a prompt queued within the default grace window is accepted for the
  same session rather than failing with an inactive-session error.
- Add or update setup default-agent tests so a fresh setup followed by
  reading the generated meta data demonstrates that default dispatch
  agents satisfy the reflection promptability behavior. If the chosen
  implementation emits explicit session metadata, assert the generated
  metadata shows mode auto_close and idle_grace_period_ms 5000.
- Add or update upgrade command tests so a project missing
  default-session-reflect receives a hook whose behavior is first-idle
  only. The observable metadata check should confirm the generated
  hook has filter.turn_count equal to 1.
- Add or preserve upgrade tests proving user intent is respected: a
  previously removed default-session-reflect hook is not recreated,
  and an existing hook is not overwritten by this task.
- Keep tests behavioral: exercise setup/upgrade/runtime outputs and
  hook execution behavior. Do not add tests that merely search source
  files for literal strings.

Covers:

- @default-project-agents-and-conventions ac-default-agents-reflection-promptable
- @default-session-reflection-hook ac-fires-once-per-invocation

tasks.title: Normalize AC ids and annotations to ac-* format
tasks.description:
Follow-up from @plan-spec-catalog-health-and-validation-trust implementation validation.

Intent:
Normalize the remaining catalog acceptance criterion ids that do not use the ac-* prefix, and update all matching AC annotations so validation can classify explicit AC coverage without relying on mixed id conventions.

Why:
The validation-trust plan made invalid AC annotations explicit and reduced most annotation debt, but parser behavior currently treats annotation tokens as AC ids only when they match ac-*. The live catalog still contains valid AC ids such as creates-isolated-copy, exit-code-constants, parent-pending-children-done, and related annotations. Those appear as blanket refs/no-credit even when the annotation is meant to name a concrete AC. The agreed cleanup direction is to normalize the ids and annotations to ac-* rather than broaden the parser around mixed legacy ids.

What:
- Identify every spec/trait acceptance criterion id that does not start with ac-.
- Rename each such id to a stable ac-* id that preserves the existing meaning.
- Update every code/test/docs annotation that references the old id to the new id.
- Preserve behavioral meaning; do not rewrite spec scope or create placeholder ACs.
- Pay special attention to currently known examples under @cmd-clone-for-testing, @cli-exit-codes, @cmd-log, @stale-status-detection, @cmd-setup, @ralph-adapter-validation, and @multi-ref-batch.
- Add a task note summarizing all renamed ids as old -> new mappings.

Testing:
- Run kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok and verify the remaining blanket_ref findings caused by non-ac-prefixed ids are gone or explicitly explained.
- Run kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok.
- Run focused tests covering the touched annotation surfaces, at minimum clone-for-testing, validate/completeness annotation scanning, and any CLI behavior whose annotations were renamed.
- Run npm test -- --run for the focused files touched by the annotation updates.

Out of scope:
- Broad missing-own-AC coverage cleanup beyond updating annotations that match renamed ids.
- Changing parser semantics to support arbitrary AC id tokens.
- Renaming AC ids that already use ac-* unless needed to resolve a direct collision.

tasks.description:

format wherever kspec validates, creates, or renames acceptance
criteria.

Why:
Coverage annotations and completeness validation can only be
trustworthy when the catalog and annotation parser agree on the token
shape used for acceptance criterion ids. The catalog schema currently
accepts any string, while the annotation scanner only treats ac-*
tokens as explicit AC ids.

What:
- Add a reusable acceptance criterion id validator/pattern for the
  required ac-prefixed kebab-case token format.
- Apply that validator to the acceptance criterion schema so persisted
  spec and trait items with invalid AC ids fail schema validation.
- Apply the same validation to `kspec item ac add --id ...` before
  the item is mutated.
- Apply the same validation to `kspec item ac set <ref> <ac-id>

- Keep automatic id generation on `kspec item ac add` producing ids
  in the required format.
- Make the user-facing error identify that the id must use the
  ac-prefixed kebab-case format.

command validation, item schema validation, tests, and future import
paths do not drift. Do not introduce a broader parser that accepts
legacy non-prefixed ids as valid explicit AC ids.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: The bug was in validateSpecItemRecursive() in src/parser/validate.ts. Two issues:
1. The nestedFields list was missing 'traits', so nested trait items weren't recursively validated.
2. Unlike extractItemsFromRaw() in yaml.ts, the validation function didn't strip nested item arrays (objects with _ulid) from items before calling SpecItemSchema.safeParse().
