When the daemon entry is preceded by a token, that prev token is the runtime; if prev is `bun` (or a path ending in `/bun`) the hardcodedBunRuntime message fires instead. Other prev tokens (e.g. `node`) route through the directDaemonSpawn message.

Detached-serve preserved: the new exec/execSync direct-entry detector only matches when a daemon entry token is present, so `exec("kspec serve start --detach")` still has no daemon entry tokens and still routes through the existing detached-serve detector for the missingCleanup message. notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 3: addressed precision blocker on exec/execSync direct-entry detection.

Blocker (line 588): the prior cycle's exec/execSync detector treated any shell token ending in dist/daemon/index.js as a daemon launch — so exec("echo dist/daemon/index.js"), exec("cat /…/dist/daemon/index.js"), and exec("grep -r dist/daemon/index.js src/") were all reported as direct daemon launches even though those commands only consume the path as an argument. That violated @daemon-test-guardrail-precision ac-unrelated-subprocesses-not-reported.

Fix: tightened the detector in readDaemonEntryInvocation to require the daemon entry token in an executable position. Two accepted shapes:
- Direct-executable: tokens[0] is the daemon entry (e.g. exec("dist/daemon/index.js --port 0")).
- Runtime form: tokens[0] is a recognised JS runtime (node / bun, bare or path-suffixed) AND tokens[1] is the daemon entry (e.g. exec("node dist/daemon/index.js …"), execSync("bun dist/daemon/index.js …"), exec("/usr/bin/node dist/daemon/index.js …")).

A new isRecognisedShellRuntimeToken helper encapsulates the runtime-token check (exact match on node/bun, or path with that final segment). Substring-of-runtime tokens like nodemon and bunyan are not recognised, so nodemon dist/daemon/index.js is not flagged. The runtime-form report retains its bun-vs-node split: leading bun/path-ending-in-/bun routes through the hardcoded-bun message; everything else uses the direct-spawn message.

Detached-serve preserved: exec("kspec serve start --detach") still has no daemon-entry token in any position, so it goes through the existing detached-serve detector and the missingCleanup message — verified by the existing regression test.

Behavioral tests added (5 new in tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts under the unrelated-subprocesses-not-reported describe):
- exec("echo dist/daemon/index.js") — daemon path as argument to echo
- execSync("cat /workspace/dist/daemon/index.js") — absolute daemon path as argument to cat
- exec("grep -r dist/daemon/index.js src/") — daemon path as argument to grep
- exec(`echo ${someFlag} dist/daemon/index.js`) — template literal where daemon path is not in the executable position
- execSync("nodemon dist/daemon/index.js") — substring-of-runtime token must not be confused with node

Manual verification of the reviewer's probe: synthetic exec("echo dist/daemon/index.js") test file now exits 0 with 0 diagnostics. Synthetic positive probes (node runtime / direct executable / bun runtime) still emit the correct directDaemonSpawn or hardcodedBunRuntime messages.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 5: closed precision blocker on direct daemon launches via process.execPath.

Blocker (line 640): readDaemonEntryInvocation's spawn-like runtime form only recognised string/template literals as runtimes — process.execPath (a MemberExpression that resolves to the absolute path of the currently-running Node interpreter) fell through, so spawn(process.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY, '--port', '0']) and execFile(process.execPath, ['dist/daemon/index.js', '--port', '0']) were silently accepted even though they directly launch the compiled daemon entry. That violated @daemon-test-guardrail-precision ac-direct-daemon-entry-invocations-flagged.

Fix: added isProcessExecPathExpression predicate and routed it through isRecognisedRuntimeArg.

- isProcessExecPathExpression matches the exact MemberExpression process.execPath: non-computed, object is an Identifier named 'process', property is an Identifier named 'execPath'. Other shapes (computed access process['execPath'], aliased bindings like 'const node = process.execPath; spawn(node, ...)', or unrelated MemberExpressions whose property name happens to be execPath) are NOT recognised — keeping the predicate strict avoids false positives on objects that share the property name.
- isRecognisedRuntimeArg now returns true for the MemberExpression first, then falls back to the existing literal/template runtime-token check.
- The runtime descriptor in the report message reads 'process.execPath' (instead of '<runtime>') for the new form so authors see exactly which call shape was matched.

Precision preserved: spawn('cat', [DAEMON_ENTRY]), execFile('grep', [DAEMON_ENTRY, 'src/']), spawnSync('nodemon', [DAEMON_ENTRY, ...]), execFileSync('docker', ['run', 'image', 'dist/daemon/index.js']), spawn(other.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY]), and spawn(process.argv0, [DAEMON_ENTRY]) all continue to pass clean — none are recognised JS runtimes.

Behavioral tests added (6 new in tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts under ac-direct-daemon-entry-invocations-flagged / ac-unrelated-subprocesses-not-reported):
- spawn(process.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY, '--port', '0']) — positive (reviewer probe)

- spawnSync(process.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY, '--port', '0']) — positive sync variant
- execFileSync(process.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY, '--port', '0']) — positive sync variant
- spawn(customRuntime.execPath, [DAEMON_ENTRY]) — precision (other-object .execPath must not flag)
- spawn(process.argv0, [DAEMON_ENTRY]) — precision (other process property must not flag)

Strictness preserved: dynamic property expressions, other property names, and computed access on unrelated objects remain unrecognised.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 7: closed both halves of the exec/execSync precision blocker.

Blocker (line 797): the runtime-flag walk treated every first non-dash token as the script path. Two real Node/Bun runtime-option classes broke that assumption:

- Value-consuming options like `--require ./preload.js`, `-r ./preload.js`, `--conditions production`, `--input-type module` consume their next whitespace-separated token as the option's VALUE, not as the script. The previous walk reported `./preload.js` as the script and silently accepted real launches like `exec("node --require ./preload.js dist/daemon/index.js --port 0")` (false negative).
- Eval-mode flags `-e`, `--eval`, `-p`, `--print` (and the bundled `--eval=...` / `--print=...` forms) put the runtime in eval mode — there is no script; subsequent tokens are the eval source string or argv to the eval'd code. The previous walk reported `dist/daemon/index.js` as the script and emitted a false-positive directDaemonSpawn for `exec("node --eval dist/daemon/index.js")`.

Fix: two new narrow predicates in tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js (lines 663 and 730), and three classes in the exec/execSync walker (eval / value-consuming / standalone-flag) at lines 944-957. Eval-mode aborts. Value-consuming flag skips both flag AND value. Standalone flag skips one token. The bundled `--require=value` form is one token starting with `-` and falls through to standalone-flag.

The value-consuming set is curated to documented Node/Bun options. New runtime options added in future versions are NOT modelled by default — false negatives are recoverable; over-broadening would weaken precision.

Behavioral tests added (13 new in tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts): 6 positives (--require, -r, --conditions, mixed flag classes, --require=value, template literal) and 7 negatives (--eval, -e, --print, -p, --eval=CODE, daemon as --require value with following script, daemon as -r value alone). All address the reviewer's specific probes.

- execSync("node -r ./register.js dist/daemon/index.js --port 0") → directDaemonSpawn (was: 0 diagnostics)
- exec("node --eval dist/daemon/index.js") → 0 diagnostics (was: directDaemonSpawn)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fix cycle 13: closed cycle-12 blocker by replacing the substring-based detached-serve classifier with a positional-aware one. The cycle-12 reviewer's repros (exec("kspec search \"serve start --detach\"") and spawn("kspec", ["search", "serve start --detach"])) now exit 0 with 0 lint errors against a synthetic oxlint probe. Approach: instead of patching the substring check, refactored the classifier so it walks the actual kspec argv tokens (quote-aware shell tokeniser for shell strings, per-element walk for argv arrays, helper-args tokeniser for runKspec/kspec) and requires the first two non-flag positionals after the kspec executable to be exactly `serve` then `start` with `--detach` (or `--detach=...`) appearing as a flag token. Same root-cause fix applied symmetrically across all four call shapes (runKspec/kspec, exec/execSync, spawn/spawnSync/execFile/execFileSync). tasks.title: Add guardrail regression tests for detached cleanup timing
tasks.description:
What:
- Add guardrail tests for detached daemon starts where cleanup exists
  somewhere in the file but is not registered for the just-started daemon
  before later awaits, assertions, or daemon observations.
- Include a regression case where an `afterEach` hook exists but the test
  assigns the PID only after an assertion or awaited observation.
- Include an allowed case where the test captures the PID or child handle
  and registers scoped cleanup immediately after the detached start returns.
- Include suppression tests proving a guardrail disable must be local to the
  violating statement and must state the behavior being exercised.
- Keep the allowed case narrow; do not make a broad `afterEach` hook alone
  sufficient evidence of safe cleanup.

Why:
The rule currently treats some file-level cleanup patterns as enough even
when an assertion between startup and PID capture can still leak the daemon.
The plan goal is deterministic daemon cleanup, not merely cleanup-shaped
code somewhere nearby.

How:
- Use synthetic snippets in `tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts`.
- Model the unsafe sequence as `serve start --detach`, then `await` or
  `expect`, then PID capture or assignment.
- Model the safe sequence as startup, immediate PID capture, immediate
  `onTestFinished`/`afterEach`-backed cleanup registration, then later
  awaits/assertions.

Testing:
- First run the new cases and observe the unsafe case fails to be reported
  against the current rule.
- After the implementation task, run:
  `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`.

notes.content:
Added regression tests for detached cleanup timing in tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts under a new 'daemon test guardrail precision: detached cleanup timing' describe block.

Test plan (3 unsafe + 2 allowed-narrow + 4 suppression = 9 cases):
- UNSAFE (failing-before-fix per task spec):
  1. afterEach closes over let pid; runKspec serve --detach; expect; pid = readPidFromFile.
  2. afterEach closes over let pid; runKspec serve --detach; await waitForReady; pid = readPidFromFile.
  3. afterEach closes over let child; spawn(kspec,[serve,start,--detach]); await waitForReady; child = readChildFromPidFile.
- ALLOWED narrow (continue to pass):
  4. runKspec serve --detach; const pid = readPidFromFile; onTestFinished(process.kill); expect.
  5. const child = spawn(kspec,[serve,start,--detach]); onTestFinished(child.kill); expect.
- SUPPRESSION:
  6. per-line oxlint-disable-next-line WITH '-- reason' on the offending detached start (accepted).
  7. per-line oxlint-disable-next-line WITHOUT '-- reason' (rejected via localized-disable rule).
  8. file-wide oxlint-disable (rejected via localized-disable rule).
  9. oxlint-disable-next-line attached to an unrelated preceding statement (still flags the offending detached start — failing-before-fix).

Verified current rule behavior with scratch lint runs before writing the assertions: cases 1-3 and 9 fail today because the rule treats an ancestor afterEach with a process.kill/child.kill SIGTERM pattern as proof of cleanup; cases 4-8 pass today.

tasks.title: Fix guardrail detached cleanup timing analysis
tasks.description:
What:
- Update `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js` so detached daemon
  starts are considered safe only when scoped cleanup is registered before
  later awaits, assertions, or daemon observations can run.
- Stop treating the mere presence of an ancestor `afterEach` hook as proof
  that the newly-started detached daemon is protected.
- Preserve and, where needed, tighten support for local disable comments so
  each accepted suppression applies only to the violating statement and
  states the behavior under test.

Why:
A detached daemon can leak if a test fails between startup and cleanup
registration. The guardrail should prevent that exact ordering bug instead
of allowing it because cleanup appears elsewhere in the file.

How:
- Reuse or extend the rule's existing statement-order scan instead of
  introducing a second independent traversal.
- Treat cleanup registration as valid only when it appears in the same test
  control flow before the next awaited operation, expectation, or daemon
  request, unless the statement itself is a local documented exception.
- Keep helper internals and dedicated guardrail fixture strings allowlisted.

Testing:
- Run:
  `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`.
- Run a targeted source audit of `tests/cli-serve.test.ts` for detached
  startup cases and confirm every remaining exception is local and
  behavior-specific.

Covers: @daemon-test-guardrail-precision ac-detached-cleanup-before-observation, ac-local-exception-is-local,
ac-exception-reason-states-subject; @daemon-test-harness-guardrails
ac-detached-serve-without-cleanup-flagged, ac-exceptions-are-localized

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 4: addressed both reviewer MUST-FIX blockers on tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js.

Blocker 1 (line 252, hasCleanupAfter accepted conditional cleanup): tightened the cleanup walker to require unconditional registration on the straight-line path. subtreeContainsDaemonCleanupCall now prunes descent into IfStatement, ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression (short-circuit), all loop bodies (While/DoWhile/For/ForIn/ForOf), SwitchStatement cases, and TryStatement.handler when walking OUTSIDE a registered cleanup callback. The predicate now requires the first call argument to be a string literal naming one of those events. Arbitrary names like 'message', 'disconnect', 'warning' no longer credit cleanup because their callbacks fire during normal IPC and are not guaranteed to run before the test ends.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Fix cycle 1: addressed the return-boundary blocker in @01KR4F56. Root cause: cleanupChildOnStartupFailure sent SIGTERM and resolved null synchronously, so the helper's promise to the caller resolved BEFORE the OS reaped the child — exactly what the reviewer's process.kill(pid, 0) probe surfaced. Fix: cleanupChildOnStartupFailure now returns a Promise that resolves only after child.once('exit', …) fires; failure-path callers (timeout, malformed-stdout, child error) await it via a small failStartup helper before calling finish(null). Edge cases: early-exit detection via child.exitCode/signalCode, kill-returns-false handling for spawn-rejected handles, idempotent across cascading branches via cleanup.done flag. Tests tightened to drop the 200ms grace window in the malformed-stdout and timeout cases — reap must be observable on return, not 200ms later. Also independently re-verified with the reviewer's exact probe shape: result=null, process.kill(pid,0) → ESRCH immediately (both branches). notes.content: Additional flaky evidence from review of @01KR3W7PPVDFR8F03VQ6J54M3K on 2026-05-08: full npm test -- --fresh failed tests/daemon-build.test.ts after 180000ms timeout in 'compiled daemon entrypoint starts and serves health checks and SPA routes under node and bun' (full log /tmp/kspec-test-cache/01KR4K02B1FTKXJTQH2SJCBC2D/f38f29fddaf6fcaa.log). notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: probeCacheReady polled /api/tasks for cache_status="ready", but the disk-fallback path returns "ready" when the entity cache is not yet registered (cacheDomainState=undefined → toCacheStatus → "ready"). Under full-suite load the daemon's startup-project registration is delayed (startSessionSyncForProject + startShadowSyncForProject yield before registerEntityCache runs), so the readiness probe matched during that window. After the probe matched, loadAll() flipped the tasks domain to "loading" before the test's assertion fetch could run — producing the observed flake.

Fix: switched probeCacheReady to /api/debug/cache-status, which reports domains=null until registerEntityCache runs and reports actual per-domain state thereafter. The probe now rejects the premature-ready window and only accepts when the tasks domain has actually transitioned to "ready". Added an explicit assertion to the happy-path fixture test that verifies domains and tasks state via the same endpoint, so a regression to the buggy probe would fail deterministically.

Verification: `npm test -- --fresh` (full suite) passed cleanly — 2410 of 2410 suites, 8827 of 8832 tests, 5 skipped. Targeted runs of tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts, tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts, and tests/daemon-build.test.ts also passed when run together (16 suites, 26 tests, 10.4s).

Out of scope: the daemon-build.test.ts 180s timeout reported in the supplemental note uses readiness mode "health" (not "health-and-cache"), so it does not exercise probeCacheReady. That single observation has no obvious failing assertion in the focused log; if it recurs after this fix lands, it will need separate investigation (likely a transient build/spawn issue under shared CI load).

tasks.description: During review of @01KR3W7PPVDFR8F03VQ6J54M3K, full npm test -- --fresh failed once in tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts at beforeEach line 482 for 'daemon websocket protocol — runtime parity bun runtime connect, subscribe, and broadcast behave consistently' with STACK_TRACE_ERROR. notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts was running in the default vitest pool, where it spawned ~15 real daemon child processes (including bun) per file while competing with the rest of the default pool's CLI-subprocess fan-out. Under that contention, the bun runtime parity beforeEach (line 482) intermittently exceeded the 15s/stage cache-readiness budget — surfacing as STACK_TRACE_ERROR even though the file passed deterministically when re-run in isolation. The previous fix (ac91faa58) addressed the cache-status race for the Node path, but the bun parity slot still flaked under the same load profile reported in the parent review for @01KR3W7PPVDFR8F03VQ6J54M3K.

Fix: moved tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts into the heavySerialSuites list in vitest.config.ts, alongside the other CLI-/daemon-spawn-heavy suites (integration.test.ts, agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts, daemon-build.test.ts). The heavy-serial project runs after the default pool drains with maxWorkers=1 / fileParallelism=false, eliminating cross-file subprocess contention. Coverage is unchanged — all 15 tests still execute against real daemon children, including both runtime parity slots, with the same AC annotations.

Verification: Two consecutive `npm test -- --fresh` (full-suite) runs passed cleanly:
- Run 1: 2412/2412 suites, 8830 of 8835 tests, 5 skipped, 1947.8s. websocket-protocol ran in heavy-serial with all 4 runtime parity tests (node + bun × 2) green.
- Run 2: 2412/2412 suites, 8830 of 8835 tests, 5 skipped, 1949.1s. Same results, bun parity 975ms/570ms.

Targeted: `npm test -- --fresh tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts` also passed (15 tests, 7.1s) with the heavy-serial project tag visible in the per-test output.

Why this isn't weakening coverage: the change is purely test pool assignment in vitest.config.ts — no production code, no test-body change, no AC removal. The test still spawns real daemon children, exercises both runtimes, and asserts the documented heartbeat-degradation behavior. The only effect is that it runs serially after the default pool instead of contending with it.

tasks.title: Tighten daemon hardening specs for cleanup binding and approved helpers
tasks.description:
## Task 1 — Tighten daemon hardening specs for cleanup binding and approved helpers

Proposed slug: `task-tighten-daemon-hardening-specs`
Type: `task`
Priority: `P2`
Plan ref: `@plan-daemon-test-fixture-hardening`
Spec ref: `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`
Additional related spec: `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision`
Tags: `daemon-tests`, `specs`, `guardrails`, `follow-up`
Depends on: none
Automation: leave unassessed until Jacob approves.

### Description

#### What
Update the daemon-test hardening behavioral specs so the current contracts explicitly cover two validation gaps:

1. `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene` must cover the case where a fixture has already spawned or obtained a child process handle, then the caller-provided cleanup-registration hook throws before readiness succeeds. The expected behavior is that the helper stops the owned child before returning or surfacing the cleanup-registration failure.
2. `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision` must define cleanup binding and approved-helper boundaries precisely enough that static guardrails cannot be satisfied by a cleanup callback that exists before an observation but does not yet bind the just-started daemon's pid/child/stop handle, and cannot be bypassed by wrapping an unsafe daemon start in an arbitrary local helper function.

Concretely, update the existing spec items rather than creating a new broad feature:

- Add or revise acceptance criteria under `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene` for cleanup-registration failure after child ownership exists.
- Add or revise acceptance criteria under `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision` so:
  - cleanup for a detached daemon is considered registered only when it captures or otherwise owns the concrete pid, child handle, or stop handle for that just-started daemon before later awaits/assertions/daemon observations; and
  - approved helpers are explicit shared daemon-test fixture utilities or documented guardrail internals, not arbitrary local functions in a test file.
- Because this task tightens currently overclaimed contracts before the regression/fix tasks land, set each touched spec whose tightened AC lacks current source/test evidence from `implemented` to `in_progress --no-cascade`. Leave a spec `implemented` only if the worker records exact existing evidence proving every newly tightened AC is already covered.
- Add a task note or spec note summarizing the validation evidence that motivated the tightening.

#### Why
The daemon hardening work added useful specs, tests, and guardrails, but validation found that two requirements were underspecified:

- A real daemon fixture can currently spawn a child, call `opts.registerCleanup(stop)`, and leak the child if the registration callback throws before the readiness `try/catch` begins. The spec says owned children are stopped on startup failure, but does not explicitly name this cleanup-registration failure phase.
- The static guardrail can accept patterns where a cleanup callback is registered before an assertion/await, but the pid/child binding happens after that assertion/await; if the observation fails, the cleanup callback runs without owning the daemon. It can also miss unsafe starts hidden behind arbitrary local helper functions. The spec says cleanup must be associated with the just-started daemon and direct daemon startup outside approved helpers must be reported, but workers need sharper wording to avoid implementing a weaker syntactic check.

Tightening the specs first prevents follow-up implementation tasks from playing whackamole against ambiguous contracts.

#### Evidence
Current spec evidence:

- `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene` currently reports `Implementation: implemented`. Existing AC `ac-owned-child-stopped-after-startup-failure` requires a fixture that has obtained a child process handle to stop that child before returning startup failure, but it does not explicitly name cleanup-registration hook failure after child ownership exists. Existing AC `ac-cleanup-registered-before-readiness-wait` requires cleanup to be registered before readiness can fail, but it does not state what the helper must do if the registration hook itself throws.
- `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision` currently reports `Implementation: implemented`. Existing AC `ac-detached-cleanup-before-observation` requires cleanup before later awaits/assertions/daemon observations, but it does not define “registered cleanup” as cleanup bound to the concrete pid, child handle, or stop handle for the just-started daemon. Existing AC `ac-direct-daemon-entry-invocations-flagged` says direct daemon startup outside an approved helper is reported, but it does not define the approved-helper boundary precisely enough to exclude arbitrary local wrapper functions.

Current source evidence:

- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:653-658` spawns the daemon child.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:677-687` defines the scoped `stop()` function.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:689-693` invokes `opts.registerCleanup(stop)` before the readiness `try/catch`.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:729-782` calls `await stop()` only from the later readiness/launch failure catch path, so a synchronous `registerCleanup` throw before that block bypasses cleanup.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:226-266` implements `isInHelperFunction`, which classifies helper-shaped function scopes.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:268-284` scans preceding statements for cleanup before observations.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:369-447` recognizes cleanup call shapes without proving that the cleanup callback already owns the concrete pid/child/stop handle for the just-started daemon.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:656-789` walks cleanup registration/body shapes.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:2193-2224` decides whether detached daemon cleanup is present before reporting.
- `tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js:2598-2604` skips detached cleanup reports when `isInHelperFunction(node)` is true, which is the local-wrapper escape hatch the tightened spec must exclude or bound explicitly.

Concrete AC wording to consider:

- `ac-cleanup-registration-failure-stops-owned-child`: Given a daemon test fixture has spawned or obtained a child process handle and constructed a cleanup/stop handle for that child; When the caller-provided cleanup-registration hook fails before the fixture reports readiness; Then the fixture stops the owned child before returning or surfacing the cleanup-registration failure.
- `ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation`: Given a test starts a detached daemon and registers cleanup before later awaits, assertions, or daemon observations; When the cleanup callback does not yet own the concrete pid, child handle, or stop handle for that just-started daemon before an intervening observation can fail; Then the guardrail reports the detached daemon startup as missing scoped cleanup.
- `ac-approved-daemon-helper-boundary-explicit`: Given a test wraps daemon startup in a local helper function or another helper-like abstraction; When that helper is not an explicit shared daemon-test fixture utility or documented guardrail internal; Then the guardrail treats the wrapped daemon startup the same as an inline unsafe daemon start and reports violations of the fixture/cleanup contract.

#### How
1. Inspect current specs:
   - `mise exec -- kspec item get @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`
   - `mise exec -- kspec item get @daemon-test-guardrail-precision`
2. Update the existing specs through the supported kspec CLI workflow. Use `kspec item ac add` or `kspec item ac set`/`kspec item ac update` if supported for acceptance-criterion changes; use `kspec item note` if supported for validation-evidence notes; use `kspec item set @ref --status in_progress --no-cascade` for implementation-status corrections. Check `--help` for exact command names before editing. Do not manually edit `.kspec` files unless the CLI has no supported way to express the change.
3. Keep the new language behavioral and implementation-neutral:
   - describe spawned/owned child processes and cleanup registration, not specific TypeScript function names, except in notes/evidence;
   - describe approved helper boundary in terms of shared daemon-test fixture utilities and documented guardrail internals, not a broad pattern like “any helper function.”
4. If the new ACs are not implemented at the time this task lands, set the touched spec implementation status to `in_progress --no-cascade`.
5. Run:
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --alignment --warnings-ok`
6. Leave the root source tree unchanged unless the supported spec workflow requires a generated file update. Verify:
   - `git status --short --branch`
   - `git -C .kspec status --short --branch`

#### In scope
- Tightening existing spec AC wording/status for the two identified gaps.
- Adding concise notes that preserve the validation evidence.

#### Out of scope
- Implementing fixture cleanup changes.
- Implementing lint rule changes.
- Adding regression tests.
- Marking any follow-up implementation task automation-eligible.

#### Validation
- `mise exec -- kspec item get @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`
- `mise exec -- kspec item get @daemon-test-guardrail-precision`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --alignment --warnings-ok`

---

Spec tightening accepted: added cleanup-registration failure AC, cleanup binding AC, and approved-helper boundary AC; both touched specs remain in_progress for follow-up implementation.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Tightened both specs and recorded validation evidence. Changes (atomic batch): (1) Added @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene/ac-cleanup-registration-failure-stops-owned-child requiring the fixture to stop the owned child when the caller-provided cleanup-registration hook throws before readiness. (2) Added @daemon-test-guardrail-precision/ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation requiring cleanup to capture or otherwise own the concrete pid/child/stop handle for the just-started daemon before any intervening await/assertion/observation. (3) Added @daemon-test-guardrail-precision/ac-approved-daemon-helper-boundary-explicit defining the approved helper boundary as explicit shared daemon-test fixture utilities or documented guardrail internals; arbitrary local wrappers count as inline unsafe starts. (4) Set both specs to status=in_progress --no-cascade because the tightened ACs lack source/test evidence: tests/helpers/daemon.ts:691-693 calls opts.registerCleanup(stop) outside the readiness try/catch (synchronous throw bypasses stop()); tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js cleanup classifier recognizes cleanup-shaped CallExpressions but does not verify the captured pid/handle was bound at registration time, and the Program:exit detached-cleanup check skips reports when isInHelperFunction(node) is true (which classifies any named local function in a test file as a helper). (5) Recorded the validation evidence as item notes on each spec. Validation: kspec validate --refs and --alignment both pass with warnings-ok; touched specs do not appear in any new warnings. No source tree changes.

tasks.title: Add real daemon cleanup-registration failure regression
tasks.description:
## Task 2 — Add real daemon cleanup-registration failure regression

Proposed slug: `task-add-register-cleanup-failure-regression`
Type: `task`
Priority: `P2`
Plan ref: `@plan-daemon-test-fixture-hardening`
Spec ref: `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`
Tags: `daemon-tests`, `fixtures`, `regression`, `follow-up`
Depends on: `@task-tighten-daemon-hardening-specs`
Automation: leave unassessed until Jacob approves.

### Description

#### What
Add focused regression coverage proving that the real daemon test fixture stops an owned daemon child if cleanup registration fails after spawn but before readiness completes.

The target fixture is `startTestDaemon` in `tests/helpers/daemon.ts`. Add or extend tests in `tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts` so they cover this sequence:

1. Create a valid temporary test daemon project using the existing helper setup.
2. Call `startTestDaemon(project, { registerCleanup })` with a `registerCleanup` callback that throws a deliberate error when invoked.
3. Ensure the helper rejects with the cleanup-registration failure or a wrapped diagnostic that includes the cleanup-registration failure.
4. Verify that any child process spawned by the helper is stopped before the helper returns the rejection to the caller.
5. Verify the daemon endpoint is not still reachable after rejection.

#### Why
Validation found a real leak edge case in the current helper shape. The helper spawns the daemon child and then calls `opts.registerCleanup(stop)` before entering the readiness `try/catch`. If `registerCleanup` throws, the helper rejects immediately and does not call `stop()`, leaving the child alive. This contradicts the intended startup-failure hygiene for any failure after the fixture owns a child.

A regression test must land before the implementation fix so the bug is reproduced and the fix cannot accidentally become a no-op.

#### Evidence
Current source behavior:

- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:653-658` spawns the daemon child.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:677-687` defines the scoped `stop()` function.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:689-693` invokes `opts.registerCleanup(stop)` before the readiness `try/catch`.
- `tests/helpers/daemon.ts:729-782` calls `await stop()` only from the later readiness/launch failure catch path, so a synchronous `registerCleanup` throw bypasses cleanup.

Current spec evidence:

- `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene ac-owned-child-stopped-after-startup-failure` requires a fixture that has obtained a child process handle to stop that child before returning startup failure.
- `@task-tighten-daemon-hardening-specs` is expected to tighten this spec or add a cleanup-registration-specific AC. Annotate the regression with the actual resulting AC id from `kspec item get @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`.

#### How
1. Inspect the current helper and tests:
   - `tests/helpers/daemon.ts`
   - `tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts`
2. Prefer an existing test seam that starts a real daemon child with a bounded timeout and dynamic port. Do not hardcode ports.
3. The test must deterministically observe the spawned child or pid before causing `registerCleanup` to throw. Do not rely on endpoint-unreachable checks alone, because a child can be alive but not ready yet. If needed, add a narrow non-behavioral test-only observer seam that exposes `{ child, endpoint }` immediately after spawn and before cleanup registration; the seam must not catch the registration error, call `stop()`, alter startup ordering, or implement cleanup behavior.
4. Keep the test bounded and deterministic:
   - use dynamic port allocation or fixture-provided endpoint data;
   - use bounded fetch/wait helpers for endpoint checks;
   - assert the captured child has exited or is no longer alive after the rejection is observed;
   - always kill/wait for the captured child in a `finally` block if it is still alive, so the intentionally failing pre-fix regression cannot leak a daemon.
5. Annotate the test with the tightened AC from `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene` once Task 1 has created it. If the exact AC id differs from this proposal, use the actual AC id from `kspec item get`.
6. Run the focused test and relevant validation:
   - `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

#### In scope
- Regression tests for `registerCleanup` throwing after the fixture owns a daemon child.
- Test-only helper seams if needed to observe process cleanup deterministically.

#### Out of scope
- Fixing `startTestDaemon` production test helper behavior. That belongs to the dependent implementation task.
- Changing mock daemon fixture behavior.
- Changing static guardrail behavior.

#### Validation
- Before `@task-fix-register-cleanup-failure-leak`, the focused suite is expected to fail only on the new regression assertion proving the cleanup-registration leak, with no unrelated failures.
- After `@task-fix-register-cleanup-failure-leak`, the same focused suite must pass.
- `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

---

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Added regression test 'startTestDaemon registerCleanup failure cleanup' in tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts targeting @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene ac-cleanup-registration-failure-stops-owned-child.

Approach:
- Introduced a narrow non-behavioral test-only seam __testObserveSpawn on StartTestDaemonOptions in tests/helpers/daemon.ts. It runs synchronously between spawn() and registerCleanup, exposes only { child, endpoint }, and does not catch the registration error, call stop(), or alter startup ordering. The seam was needed because registerCleanup's signature only exposes 'stop' (not the child), so the test would otherwise have no deterministic way to assert post-rejection that the spawned daemon was terminated.
- The test captures { child, endpoint } via the seam, drives registerCleanup to throw a sentinel error, and asserts: the helper rejects with the sentinel (or a wrapped diagnostic that contains it); the captured child has exited or been signaled by the time the helper rejects; and the resolved endpoint is no longer reachable via a bounded fetch.
- A finally block SIGKILLs the captured child if it is still alive, so the intentionally failing pre-fix regression cannot strand a daemon between this task and the dependent fix task.

Validation results:
- mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts: 9/10 pass; the new test fails only on the child-still-alive assertion (line 665), which is the intended regression assertion proving the cleanup-registration leak. No unrelated failures.
- mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts: lint guardrails (53 + 160 tests) all pass; only the new regression assertion still fails as designed.

- mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok: exit 0 (only pre-existing malformed_ac_token warnings in unrelated test files).

This task is intentionally a pre-fix regression: the test must fail until @task-fix-register-cleanup-failure-leak lands the helper-side fix that calls stop() before surfacing a registerCleanup failure.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Pre-review proactive fix (commit 0233c88c3): replaced bare it.fails() with the validated selective expected-failure pattern.

Why: /kspec:reflect ran after the initial submission and surfaced two prior observations the worker missed during implementation:
- @01KR3ZR8 (resolved) — bare it.fails() was DISPROVED in cycle 2 review of @task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions because ANY thrown assertion in the body satisfies the marker (parser failure, oxlint crash, partial fix all count as 'expected failure').

tasks.description:
## Task 3 — Fix real daemon cleanup-registration failure cleanup

Proposed slug: `task-fix-register-cleanup-failure-leak`
Type: `task`
Priority: `P2`
Plan ref: `@plan-daemon-test-fixture-hardening`
Spec ref: `@daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene`
Tags: `daemon-tests`, `fixtures`, `cleanup`, `follow-up`
Depends on: `@task-add-register-cleanup-failure-regression`
Automation: leave unassessed until Jacob approves.

### Description

#### What
Fix `startTestDaemon` in `tests/helpers/daemon.ts` so a thrown cleanup-registration callback cannot leak the daemon child that the helper just spawned.

Expected behavior:

- If `opts.registerCleanup(stop)` throws after the child process is spawned, `startTestDaemon` stops the owned child before rejecting.
- The rejection preserves the cleanup-registration failure clearly enough for the caller to diagnose it.
- The fix does not weaken existing launch-failure, readiness-failure, diagnostics, or success-path cleanup behavior.

#### Why
The fixture is used by daemon-backed tests to avoid process leaks and ambient daemon coupling. A cleanup-registration callback is caller-provided code, so it can throw because of a test framework misuse, Playwright/Vitest lifecycle error, or future wrapper regression. Once `startTestDaemon` has spawned a child, it owns that child until it either returns a handle or tears it down. Returning a failure while the child remains alive recreates the daemon leakage class this hardening work is intended to prevent.

#### How
1. Start from the regression added by `@task-add-register-cleanup-failure-regression`.
2. In `tests/helpers/daemon.ts`, protect the cleanup-registration call after `stop` is defined and before readiness begins.
3. On registration failure:
   - call `await stop()` or an equivalent bounded child cleanup path;
   - preserve the original cleanup-registration error as the surfaced error, or as the explicit cause/message/diagnostic detail of a wrapper;
   - if cleanup itself reports an error, include or log that secondary cleanup failure without replacing the original cleanup-registration failure as the primary rejection reason;
   - do not wait for readiness after registration has failed.
4. Ensure this does not introduce unhandled promise rejections from the readiness/launch race.
5. Keep existing behavior intact for:
   - `spawn`/`ENOENT` launch errors;
   - health/cache readiness timeout diagnostics;
   - successful startup and caller-owned stop;
   - Playwright fixture cleanup registration.
6. Run:
   - `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts`
   - `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/e2e-fixture-daemon-cleanup.test.ts`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

#### In scope
- Real daemon fixture cleanup-registration failure behavior.
- Bounded cleanup and diagnostic preservation for that failure path.

#### Out of scope
- Mock daemon fixture changes.
- Lint guardrail changes.
- New Playwright product-flow tests.

#### Validation
- The regression from `@task-add-register-cleanup-failure-regression` passes.
- Existing startup-failure and readiness diagnostics tests still pass.
- `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts`
- `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/e2e-fixture-daemon-cleanup.test.ts`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach:

Fix in tests/helpers/daemon.ts:711-715: wrap opts.registerCleanup(stop) in try/catch. On failure: await stop() (which calls killChildScoped → SIGTERM/wait/SIGKILL with bounded timeout), then rethrow the original cleanup-registration error so the rejection clearly preserves it. If stop() itself throws, append secondary cleanup failure detail to the error message without replacing the registration error as the primary cause. Do not enter the readiness wait when registration has failed.

Why preserve the original error directly (not wrap it):
- The regression test asserts errorMessage.toContain(sentinel) — wrapping would still pass IF we include the message, but throwing the original Error keeps the stack and cause intact for caller diagnosis.
- The task spec says 'preserve the original cleanup-registration error as the surfaced error, OR as the explicit cause/message/diagnostic detail of a wrapper'. Direct rethrow is the simplest form that satisfies this.

Why not enter readiness:
- We bail BEFORE the readiness try/catch by throwing inside the registerCleanup catch. This avoids the readiness/launch race entirely.

Why bounded:
- killChildScoped uses a 5s SIGTERM grace then SIGKILL, so stop() is bounded.

Test update:
- The regression's expectCleanupRegistrationLeak wrapper exists explicitly to throw a 'remove this wrapper' error post-fix. I will inline its post-fix assertions (child terminated AND endpoint unreachable) at the call site and delete the helper, as the wrapper documents.

Test plan:
- mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts (focused suite must pass with all 11 tests including the now-active regression)
- mise exec -- npm test (full suite — must remain green; only the regression test should change behavior)
- mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok
- mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok

notes.content:
Implementation complete (commit 07488494e):

Fix in tests/helpers/daemon.ts:712-741:
- Wrapped opts.registerCleanup(stop) in try/catch.
- On caller-provided hook throw: await stop() (bounded via killChildScoped → SIGTERM, 5s grace, SIGKILL).
- Rethrow the original registration error directly so the caller diagnoses the misuse, not a wrapper.
- If stop() itself throws, append secondary failure context to the registration error's message; never replace the primary cause.
- Bail before the readiness try/catch, so we never enter the readiness/launch race once registration has failed (no unhandled-rejection risk).

Test update in tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts:
- Removed the staged-failure expectCleanupRegistrationLeak wrapper as instructed by its own 'STAGED REGRESSION CLOSED' message.
- Inlined the post-fix contract assertions: captured child terminated (exitCode/signalCode set) AND endpoint unreachable via bounded fetch.
- Kept the safety-net SIGKILL block in finally so any future regression cannot strand a daemon.

Existing behavior preserved: launch errors (ENOENT) still surface via the launch/readiness race and the readiness try/catch's stop() call still runs on timeout / probe failure / launch error. Successful startup unchanged. The new failure path is reached only when the caller-provided hook throws.

tasks.title: Add guardrail regressions for unbound cleanup callbacks and local wrappers
tasks.description:
## Task 4 — Add guardrail regressions for unbound cleanup callbacks and local wrappers

Proposed slug: `task-add-guardrail-binding-wrapper-regressions`
Type: `task`
Priority: `P2`
Plan ref: `@plan-daemon-test-fixture-hardening`
Spec ref: `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision`
Tags: `daemon-tests`, `lint`, `guardrails`, `regression`, `follow-up`
Depends on: `@task-tighten-daemon-hardening-specs`
Automation: leave unassessed until Jacob approves.

### Description

#### What
Add focused lint-rule regression tests proving the daemon-test guardrail reports two unsafe patterns that validation found it can currently miss:

1. A detached daemon start followed by an `onTestFinished` cleanup callback before an observation, where the callback closes over a pid/child variable that is assigned only after an intervening `expect`, `await`, or daemon observation.
2. A detached daemon start hidden inside an arbitrary local helper function in a test file, where that local helper is not one of the approved shared daemon-test fixture utilities or documented guardrail internals. Add direct daemon entrypoint local-wrapper coverage only if a pre-fix check proves that specific shape is still a false negative; otherwise treat existing direct-entry local-helper coverage as a control, not as a new failing regression.

Target test files:

- `tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts`
- `tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts` if that is where the existing rule self-check belongs for repository-wide guardrail behavior.

#### Why
The guardrail is supposed to prevent daemon leaks and fixture bypasses, not only catch simple inline examples. Validation found false negatives:

- Registering `onTestFinished(() => killPid(pid))` before `expect(...)` is not safe if `pid = readPidFromFile()` happens after the `expect`; a thrown assertion leaves the cleanup callback unbound to the daemon.
- Wrapping `runKspec("serve start --detach ...")` in a local `startDetachedDaemon()` helper must not make the unsafe daemon start invisible. The approved-helper boundary should be explicit, not inferred from the presence of any helper-looking function.

Regression tests must land before the lint rule fix so the false negatives are reproduced and future workers cannot satisfy the task by changing unrelated code.

#### How
1. Inspect current guardrail tests around:
   - daemon command classification;
   - detached cleanup timing;
   - local suppressions;
   - repository-wide no-leaky-test-daemon checks.
2. Add failing examples for unbound cleanup callbacks, including at least:
   - `let pid; runKspec("serve start --detach ..."); onTestFinished(() => killPid(pid)); expect(...); pid = readPidFromFile();`
   - the same shape with an `await waitForReady(...)` or daemon fetch before `pid`/`child` assignment;
   - a child-handle variant if the current rule supports child-handle cleanup recognition.
3. Add failing examples for arbitrary local wrappers that reproduce the current detached-start false negative, including at least:
   - a local function that calls `runKspec("serve start --detach ...")`, then a test calls that function without approved fixture cleanup;
   - a local function or const-arrow wrapper that calls `spawn("kspec", ["serve", "start", "--detach", ...])`;
   - assertions that the wrapper body or wrapper call produces a `no-leaky-test-daemon` diagnostic before any approved cleanup exemption can apply.
   If direct daemon entrypoint wrappers are added, first verify they fail pre-fix; otherwise keep them as existing-pass/control coverage and do not count them toward the new regression requirement.
4. Add allowed examples only for genuinely safe/approved shapes:
   - pid/child/stop handle is captured before the cleanup registration and before any later observation;
   - shared daemon fixture utilities remain allowed when they are in approved helper paths/functions;
   - unrelated subprocesses remain unreported.
5. Annotate tests with the tightened AC ids from `@daemon-test-guardrail-precision` once Task 1 has created them. If the exact AC ids differ, use the actual ids from `kspec item get`.
6. Run:
   - `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
   - `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

#### In scope
- Lint regression tests for false-negative patterns.
- Narrow allowed examples needed to prevent over-tightening.

#### Out of scope
- Implementing the lint rule fix.
- Changing real daemon fixture cleanup.
- Broad repository lint cleanup unrelated to no-leaky-test-daemon.

#### Validation
- New unsafe examples fail before the lint rule fix and pass after it by producing `no-leaky-test-daemon` diagnostics.
- Existing allowed examples still pass after the lint rule fix.
- `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
- `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok`

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: added 12 regression tests at the end of tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts in two new top-level describe blocks — 'cleanup callback bound before observation' (for ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation) and 'approved helper boundary is explicit' (for ac-approved-daemon-helper-boundary-explicit).

Pre-fix probe (npx oxlint + temp project) confirmed 4 false negatives in the current rule:
1. onTestFinished closes over a let pid that is bound only after expect()
2. onTestFinished closes over a let pid that is bound only after await waitForReady(daemon URL)
3. onTestFinished closes over a let child handle that is bound only after await
4. onTestFinished captures pid before a daemon-host fetch but pid is bound only after the fetch (covers the daemon-fetch observation gate)

And 4 false negatives for arbitrary local wrappers:
1. function declaration wrapping runKspec(serve start --detach ...)
2. const arrow wrapping spawn(kspec, [serve, start, --detach, ...])
3. function declaration wrapping execSync(kspec serve start --detach ...)
4. function expression assigned to a const wrapping spawnSync(kspec, [serve, start, --detach, ...])

Direct daemon entrypoint wrappers (spawn(node, [DAEMON_ENTRY, ...]) inside a local helper) are ALREADY flagged by the existing CallExpression visitor (which fires before isInHelperFunction is consulted), so per the task instructions I treated those as existing-pass control coverage and did NOT add a new failing regression for that shape. A note in the new describe block explains this explicitly.

Allowed/control cases added:
- pid captured as const before onTestFinished registration (canonical safe binding shape)
- child handle captured by the spawn statement and onTestFinished kills it before any observation
- shared fixture wrapper inside tests/helpers/daemon.ts (path-allowlist boundary preserved)
- inline detached start with proper inline cleanup (baseline must not regress)

Tests verified: 8 unsafe regressions FAIL pre-fix (rule produces 0 errors / no diagnostic), 4 allowed control tests PASS, the existing 160 tests in the file PASS. Companion file tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts (53 tests) PASS unchanged. The failures are intentional and reproduce the false negatives Task 1's tightened ACs codified — they will pass once the lint rule fix in the follow-up task lands.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 1: addressed the blocker thread on review @01KR6QFSSGT6SZA00W662XTRM2.

The reviewer's blocker on the prior submission flagged that the eight new unsafe-regression tests landed as active red assertions against the unfixed lint rule, so the targeted required suite (`npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts`) failed eight tests and the branch could not merge as a standalone snapshot. The reviewer offered two paths: land the lint-rule fix together (out of scope per this task — the description explicitly excludes implementing the lint rule fix) or keep the red regressions out of the required suite until the lint-rule fix lands.

Fix: took the second path by converting the eight unsafe regression tests from `it(...)` to `it.fails(...)`. Each `it.fails` test still runs the same `runOxlint(...)` invocation and the same inner `expect(...)` assertions, so the false-negative shape is still verified end-to-end. The inversion just flips the today/tomorrow polarity:

- Today: the rule produces no diagnostic, `expect(result.exitCode).not.toBe(0)` throws, `it.fails` turns the throw into a pass — the suite is green.
- After the lint-rule fix lands: the rule produces the diagnostic, the inner assertions pass, and `it.fails` will then FAIL — that failure is the structured signal to the lint-rule-fix worker to flip those specific eight tests from `it.fails(...)` back to `it(...)` as part of their landing change.

This locks the regressions in (the false negatives cannot be silently lost; any future change to the rule that doesn't address them will trip the it.fails inversion) without contributing red to a green branch.

The four allowed-narrow control tests remain as plain `it(...)` — they pass today (the rule does not flag the canonical safe shapes) and must still pass after the fix.

Both describe-block docstrings have been updated to document the it.fails inversion contract and the flip-on-fix-landing protocol explicitly, so the next reviewer or worker can see the contract without having to reconstruct it from the diff.

Verification:
- `mise exec -- npm test -- --fresh tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts` → 225 of 225 tests pass (53 in the no-leaky-test-daemon file, 172 in the guardrails file).

- `mise exec -- kspec validate --completeness --warnings-ok` → exit 0 (existing completeness warnings only).
