tasks.title: Align merge-helper and integration-target specs around branch-lock ownership
tasks.description:
What:
- Update the existing @detached-reviewer-merge-helper description so it says the helper keeps the integration branch authoritative by using helper-owned temporary merge state, not by refreshing a persistent occupied target worktree.
- Replace @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-occupied-target-clean-refresh with the following final behavior; do not keep the old refresh semantics under a different ID:

  AC id: ac-helper-uses-ephemeral-target-worktree
  Given: A reviewer runs the supported detached merge helper and the integration target branch is not checked out in any non-helper worktree.
  When: The reviewed canonical head needs to be merged into the integration target.
  Then: The helper creates an internal temporary target worktree, performs the merge there, advances the integration target ref on success, and removes the temporary worktree before exiting.

  AC id: ac-helper-leaves-no-target-branch-lock
  Given: The supported detached merge helper exits after a successful merge, no-op merge, or conflict/error path.
  When: Git worktrees are listed for the repository.
  Then: No helper-created or dispatch auxiliary worktree remains checked out on the integration target branch.

  AC id: ac-helper-occupied-target-refuses-with-free-branch-guidance
  Given: The integration target branch is already checked out in a non-helper worktree before the detached merge helper runs.
  When: The helper cannot safely take exclusive ownership of the target branch for its temporary merge worktree.
  Then: The helper refuses before moving refs, identifies the blocking worktree, and reports guidance to free or detach that existing checkout without instructing the reviewer to check out the integration target in another auxiliary worktree.

- Rewrite @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-helper-refuses-dirty-target so it applies to dirty or staged drift in a pre-existing occupied target checkout and preserves the same refusal-before-ref-move behavior.
- Rewrite @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-helper-safe-conflict-exit so conflict cleanup is defined in terms of aborting/removing the helper-owned temporary target worktree, not leaving an occupied integration worktree refreshed.
- Keep @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-helper-no-op-merge semantics, explicitly noting that no persistent target worktree is created or dirtied on the no-op path.
- Add these ACs to @dispatch-integration-mutation-scope:

  AC id: ac-occupied-target-refusal-identifies-blocker
  Given: Dispatch is running from a checkout that does not itself have the integration target branch checked out, and another worktree has that target branch checked out.
  When: Dispatch attempts an integration-target sync or push for that branch.
  Then: Dispatch refuses before moving refs and reports the blocking worktree path with guidance to free or detach that checkout.

  AC id: ac-auxiliary-worktrees-do-not-hold-target-locks
  Given: Dispatch uses worker, reviewer, helper, or plan-scoped auxiliary worktrees while the dispatch root is not checked out on a specific integration target branch.
  When: The auxiliary operation completes, fails, or is cleaned up.
  Then: Those auxiliary worktrees do not keep that integration target branch checked out in a way that prevents the dispatch root from syncing or pushing the target branch.

- Add this AC to @dispatch-remote-branch-sync:

  AC id: ac-occupied-checkout-degraded-recovery
  Given: An integration target entered degraded state because the target branch was checked out in another worktree.
  When: A later sync or push evaluation finds that no other worktree has the target branch checked out and the target operation succeeds or is a no-op.
  Then: The degraded state for that target is cleared and queued work for that target becomes eligible without requiring a dispatch-engine restart.

Why:
The existing spec already says reviewer guidance must not tell reviewers to check out the integration branch manually, but the helper script itself emits recovery text that requires exactly that. The spec also assumes an occupied target worktree can be refreshed, which conflicts with the dispatch root's safety guard for plan integration targets. These AC updates make exclusive branch-lock ownership explicit.

How:
- Use `kspec item ac add` for the new ACs and `kspec item ac set`/equivalent item edit path for replacement wording on the existing helper ACs.
- Ensure no final helper AC still promises to refresh a persistent occupied target worktree after the target ref moves.
- Set the touched specs to implementation `in_progress` with `--no-cascade` unless the implementation and regression task lands in the same change.
- Verify `kspec item get @detached-reviewer-merge-helper`, `kspec item get @dispatch-integration-mutation-scope`, and `kspec item get @dispatch-remote-branch-sync` show the intended ACs exactly once.

Testing:
- kspec item get @detached-reviewer-merge-helper
- kspec item get @dispatch-integration-mutation-scope
- kspec item get @dispatch-remote-branch-sync
- kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok

Covers: @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-helper-uses-ephemeral-target-worktree, ac-helper-leaves-no-target-branch-lock, ac-helper-occupied-target-refuses-with-free-branch-guidance, ac-helper-no-op-merge, ac-helper-refuses-dirty-target, ac-helper-safe-conflict-exit; @dispatch-integration-mutation-scope ac-occupied-target-refusal-identifies-blocker, ac-auxiliary-worktrees-do-not-hold-target-locks; @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-occupied-checkout-degraded-recovery

notes.content:
Implemented occupied-checkout degraded-state auto-recovery.

  status API (dispatch.ts, agent-dispatch.ts).

  degraded targets so periodic reconciliation retries immediately rather than
  waiting sync_interval seconds.

  early return for occupied-checkout degraded targets, then clears degraded
  state on a successful push or clean no-op. Divergence and other unsafe
  states are NOT cleared by a push — they still require a successful

  removal, including the broadcast sync_state recovery event and getTargetSyncStatus
  reporting no degraded target.
- Occupied-checkout cleared via the periodic-sync push path when no commits
  are pending push.
- Divergence-degraded state stays put across a successful push (regression
  guard for the "preserve hard failures" requirement).

Updated existing daemon-api expectations to include kind on the degraded-target
shape.

tasks.title: Promote folder-backed index consistency into the shared trait contract
tasks.description:
What:
- Update the existing shared trait `@trait-folder-backed-entity-1`, not a
  new duplicate trait, so the task, plan, review, and future folder-backed
  storage contracts inherit one common index-consistency rule.
- Add these acceptance criteria to `@trait-folder-backed-entity-1` with the
  exact ids and wording below:

  `ac-index-entry-created-with-folder`
  Given: A folder-backed entity is created
  When: The creation is persisted
  Then: The entity directory, authoritative sidecar files, and bounded index
  entry are written in the same logical atomic mutation

  `ac-indexed-mutation-updates-index`
  Given: A persisted folder-backed entity changes any field, count, derived
  summary, relationship, lifecycle value, or resource metadata that belongs
  in that entity type's bounded index projection
  When: The mutation is persisted
  Then: The authoritative sidecar update and the corresponding index entry
  update are committed as one logical atomic mutation

  `ac-index-repair-converges`
  Given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from authoritative entity
  folders
  When: an index repair successfully rewrites the index and no later entity
  mutation occurs
  Then: A subsequent dry-run rebuild reports no index changes

  `ac-semantic-defaults-do-not-drift`
  Given: An indexed optional field has equivalent persisted forms such as an
  omitted value and an empty default collection
  When: Index drift is computed or an index repair is verified
  Then: The semantically equivalent forms are treated as equal and do not
  produce repeated update drift

- Add `@trait-folder-backed-entity-1` directly to the traits list for:
  `@task-directory-storage`, `@task-index-file`,

tasks.title: Add red tests for plan and review index consistency after every folder mutation
tasks.description:
What:
- Add failing-before-fix regression coverage for plan and review folder
  mutations that currently can leave `project.plans.yaml` or
  `project.reviews.yaml` out of sync until a rebuild is run.
- Extend the existing focused suites instead of creating a hidden one-off
  harness:
  - `tests/plan-rebuild-index.test.ts`
  - `tests/review-rebuild-index.test.ts`
  - `tests/parser-plans-folder.test.ts`
  - `tests/parser-reviews-folder.test.ts`
  - CLI suites only where a behavior is exposed only through CLI commands,
    such as `tests/cli-plan-resource.test.ts` and
    `tests/review-resource-cli.test.ts`.
- Cover these plan operations in a temp project configured for folder-backed
  storage:
  - create/import a plan and immediately dry-run rebuild the plan index;
  - import a plan document with sibling `resources.yaml` metadata plus
    `resources/` files, then immediately run
    `kspec plan rebuild-index --dry-run` and assert `resource_summary` has
    no drift before any repair;
  - mutate indexed metadata such as status, derived refs, branch, or module;
  - add and clear notes so `notes_count` is reflected or removed;
  - add, replace, and delete a plan local resource so `resource_summary`
    stays current.
- Cover these review operations in a temp project configured for
  folder-backed storage:
  - create a review and immediately dry-run rebuild the review index;
  - add a thread/comment, add a check, add a verdict, close or reopen when
    the command/API supports it, and verify the index counts/disposition;
  - add, replace, and delete a review local resource so `resource_summary`
    stays current;
  - include a review whose detail file has `external_links: []` while the
    index omits `external_links`, then prove repair converges.
- Add a small task baseline assertion showing the existing task data manager
  already satisfies the same trait after `task add`, `task set`, task note,
  and task delete flows. Put it in `tests/task-data-manager.test.ts` unless
  an existing task CLI regression suite is a narrower fit.
- Each new assertion must run `rebuild-index --dry-run` after the mutating
  operation and assert zero drift without first running repair.

Why:
These tests pin the user-facing invariant before implementation work: every
normal mutator must keep the bounded index current in the same action that

tasks.title: Make plan and review folder mutators update indexes atomically
tasks.description:
What:
- Update plan and review storage so every operation that writes an
  authoritative folder sidecar also updates the bounded index entry within
  the same logical buffered mutation when indexed data changes.
- Audit and fix every public mutating path that can write plan/review folder
  data, including:
  - plan import/create, plan set/status changes, plan note changes, plan
    derive output, plan branch metadata, plan delete;
  - plan resource add/replace/delete, import-time sibling resource
    persistence through `persistPlanResourcesFromSibling(...)`, and any
    API/static helper that mutates `resources.yaml`;
  - review add/create, review comment/thread changes, review check changes,
    review verdict changes, review lifecycle changes, review delete;
  - review resource add/replace/delete and any API/static helper that
    mutates `resources.yaml`.
- Normalize index equality for semantically equivalent optional/default
  values. At minimum, `external_links` omitted from an index entry and
  `external_links: []` in a review detail file must compare equal so
  `review rebuild-index --repair` converges.
- Ensure resource-summary updates are not missed. If a resource manager
  writes `resources.yaml` directly, route that write through the owning
  plan/review storage manager or add an owner-specific index refresh inside
  the same write buffer.
- Keep rebuild-index as a recovery/repair path. Do not make normal CLI/API
  mutators call rebuild-index after the fact as their consistency strategy.
- Preserve existing wrapper keys and unknown sibling data in
  `project.plans.yaml`, `project.reviews.yaml`, and entity detail sidecars.

Why:
The folder sidecar and bounded index are one logical storage record. If a
mutator updates only the folder, list/dashboard/API consumers can see stale
state until a manual rebuild runs; if repair repeatedly reports the same
drift, operators cannot distinguish real damage from false drift.

How:
- Use `src/parser/task-data-manager.ts` and the split backend as the model:
  callers submit mutations; the storage layer coordinates all affected
  files and the shadow commit.
- Update `src/parser/folder-backed-entity.ts` only for reusable equality,
  projection, or write-buffer helpers that are genuinely shared by plan and
  review storage. Keep plan/review-specific projection field lists in their
  existing managers.
- Update `src/parser/plan-storage-manager.ts` and
  `src/parser/review-storage-manager.ts` so `save*`, `mutate*`, delete, and
  resource-summary refresh paths cannot bypass index updates.
- If plan/review resource managers currently bypass these storage managers,
  change those managers to accept an owner index-refresh callback or call a
  small exported `refreshPlanIndexEntry` / `refreshReviewIndexEntry` helper
  that runs inside the same active write buffer.
- Keep locks scoped so concurrent mutations for the same index cannot
  interleave partial writes.

Testing:
- Run the tests added by `@task-add-folder-index-consistency-regressions`
  and confirm the red cases now pass.
- Run existing related suites:
  `npm test -- --fresh tests/plan-rebuild-index.test.ts tests/review-rebuild-index.test.ts tests/parser-plans-folder.test.ts tests/parser-reviews-folder.test.ts tests/plan-folder-migration.test.ts tests/review-folder-migration.test.ts tests/upgrade-folder-storage.test.ts`
- Run `npm run typecheck`.

tasks.title: Implement branch-coherent merges and sync/push for clean occupied integration targets
tasks.description:
What:
- Implement the already-approved spec behavior that treats an eligible clean existing checkout of the integration target branch as a valid branch-coherent merge/sync/push surface.
- Update `templates/skills/merge/scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh` so it:
  - detects whether `KSPEC_DISPATCH_MERGE_TARGET` is checked out in an existing worktree;
  - if the target is checked out in exactly one eligible clean non-auxiliary project/user worktree, runs the merge of `KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_HEAD` in that checkout;
  - if the target is not checked out anywhere, keeps the current helper-owned temporary worktree path;
  - if the target checkout is auxiliary, dirty, staged, in an in-progress Git operation, or would have untracked/ignored files overwritten by the merge, refuses before moving refs and prints recovery guidance naming the blocking path;
  - on merge conflict, aborts the merge in the selected merge surface, removes any helper-owned temporary worktree, and leaves the target ref unchanged;
  - never uses `git update-ref` or equivalent ref-only movement to advance a branch that is checked out in any worktree;
  - never requires or instructs the reviewer to check out the integration target inside the detached reviewer snapshot.
- Run `kspec skill render` after editing the template script so rendered merge-skill copies receive the same behavior.
- Update dispatch mutation-scope implementation in `src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts` and dispatch sync/push callers in `src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts` so startup sync, periodic sync, before-provision sync, and post-merge push can operate through an eligible clean occupied target checkout instead of degrading solely due to occupancy.
- Keep existing refusal/degraded behavior for unsafe states: auxiliary target checkouts, dirty or staged occupied target checkout, in-progress Git operations, untracked/ignored overwrite hazards, ambiguous/multiple target checkout surfaces, divergence, missing refs, merge conflicts, and remote failures.

Why:
The previous target-lock hardening fixed a real class of leaked helper-created target worktrees, but it overcorrected by treating every occupied target checkout as unsafe. Normal projects often keep `main` or a plan target branch checked out in the root worktree. The intended safety invariant is not exclusive branch occupancy; it is branch-coherent mutation plus no newly leaked helper-created target locks.

How:
- In the helper script, split target occupancy into exactly these paths:
  1. target free: current temporary target worktree merge, with cleanup on all exits;
  2. exactly one eligible clean non-auxiliary target checkout: checkout-aware merge in that worktree;
  3. auxiliary target checkout: refusal before ref movement with cleanup/blocker guidance;
  4. dirty/staged target checkout, in-progress Git operation, or untracked/ignored overwrite hazard: refusal before ref movement;
  5. ambiguous/multiple occupied target checkouts if observable: refusal before ref movement with blocker guidance.
- Preserve pinned-head semantics by merging `KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_HEAD`, not an advanced canonical branch tip.
- Preserve no-op behavior before creating or mutating any worktree state.
- Ensure selected existing target checkout is clean using tracked/staged checks, in-progress-operation checks, and merge/sync overwrite-safety checks. Do not reject harmless untracked/ignored files that Git would not overwrite.
- For dispatch sync/push, have mutation-scope resolution return enough information for callers to operate from the selected coherent surface when the branch is checked out in an eligible non-auxiliary checkout, and keep existing ref-only/free-branch behavior only when the target branch is not checked out.
- Do not run destructive tests against live `~/Projects/kynetic-spec` or `~/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch`; use temp repos/fixtures.
- Do not change kspec spec descriptions or acceptance criteria in this task; those edits are applied separately before the task is created.

Testing:
- Update `tests/detached-reviewer-merge.test.ts` coverage for:
  - clean eligible occupied target checkout merges successfully and remains coherent with the target tip;
  - occupied target checkout with tracked modifications refuses before moving refs;
  - occupied target checkout with staged drift refuses before moving refs;
  - occupied target checkout with an in-progress merge/rebase/cherry-pick refuses before moving refs;
  - occupied target checkout with an untracked/ignored overwrite hazard refuses before moving refs, while harmless untracked/ignored files do not block;
  - auxiliary/detached-reviewer target checkout refuses before moving refs and is not used as the merge surface;
  - conflict through occupied checkout aborts and restores target checkout coherence;
  - free target still uses and removes a helper-owned temporary worktree;
  - no-op path does not dirty any existing worktree and does not create persistent target checkout state;
  - helper output does not instruct the reviewer to manually check out the target branch in the detached reviewer snapshot.
- Add/update dispatch tests for:
  - clean eligible occupied target checkout does not enter degraded state during startup sync;
  - clean eligible occupied target checkout does not enter degraded state during periodic sync;
  - clean eligible occupied target checkout does not enter degraded state during before-provision sync;
  - clean eligible occupied target checkout does not enter degraded state during post-merge target push;
  - dirty/staged/in-progress/overwrite-hazard occupied target checkout still refuses/degrades with blocker guidance;
  - auxiliary target checkout still refuses/degrades with cleanup/blocker guidance and is not selected as a mutation surface;
  - clearing the dirty/unsafe condition lets later sync/push recover without restart;
  - worker/reviewer/helper/plan-scoped/detached-reviewer worktrees are not selected as mutation surfaces even if they are the only occupied target checkout.
- Run:
  - `npm test -- --fresh tests/detached-reviewer-merge.test.ts`
  - `npm test -- --fresh tests/dispatch-plan-target-lock-e2e.test.ts`
  - `npm test -- --fresh tests/dispatch-target-sync.test.ts tests/dispatch-degraded-state.test.ts`
  - `npm run typecheck`
  - `kspec validate --refs --alignment --completeness --warnings-ok`

In scope:
- Merge helper behavior for clean/free/dirty/unsafe/auxiliary/ambiguous occupied target states.
- Dispatch sync/push mutation-surface selection for eligible clean occupied target checkouts.
- Tests and rendered merge-skill artifacts needed to prove the approved specs.

Out of scope:
- Editing specs, acceptance criteria, or task metadata beyond source annotations needed for implementation coverage.
- Changing plan target selection semantics.
- Auto-merging remote divergence or changing ff-only sync policy.
- Treating dirty/staged target checkouts as safe.
- Treating auxiliary target checkouts as valid mutation surfaces.
- Running tests or cleanup against live main/dispatch worktrees.

Covers:
- @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ac-helper-path-in-reviewer-guidance

notes.content:
Approach: 

1. Add classification helper for target worktree checkouts (auxiliary vs eligible vs unsafe). Auxiliary = inside dispatch worktree_root OR contains .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json metadata file. Unsafe = tracked mods, staged drift, in-progress git op (MERGE_HEAD/REBASE_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD/REVERT_HEAD/BISECT_LOG). Eligible = otherwise.

2. resolveDispatchIntegrationMutationScope returns a new mutationCwd field. When projectDir is on the target, mutationCwd = projectDir. When exactly one eligible non-auxiliary worktree owns the target, mutationCwd = that path. When unsafe/auxiliary/ambiguous: throw DispatchWorkspaceError with appropriate code. When free, mutationCwd = null (ref-only path).

3. dispatch.ts merge call uses mutationScope.mutationCwd directly for the working-tree merge step. fetch/push remain in projectDir.

4. Shell helper: detects worktrees on target branch, classifies each (auxiliary by metadata file or path under worktree_root from KSPEC_DISPATCH_WORKTREE_ROOT env hint, dirty/in-progress checks). Selects eligible cleanly: refuse for auxiliary/unsafe/multiple-eligible, merge through eligible worktree for exactly-one-eligible, ephemeral helper-owned worktree for free branch.

5. Tests: rework existing 'occupied-blocks-sync' tests to use auxiliary marker (write .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json or place under .kspec-worktrees) to keep refusal semantics. Add new tests for clean eligible occupied checkout = valid mutation surface. Add tests for dirty/staged/in-progress/overwrite-hazard refusal. Add tests for auxiliary refusal.

Edge cases: ensure projectDir checkout coherence still fires when projectDir is on target. Ensure no leaked target locks by helper across all paths. Validate that helper does NOT instruct reviewer to manually check out target. Use temp repos only — no live workspace damage.

tasks.title: Define layered runner config storage, schema, and shared TypeScript types
tasks.description:
What:
- Add storage and loader support for two runner config layers:
  - Project runner config stored as a repo-managed artifact at `project.runners.yaml` in the shadow worktree root, alongside `kynetic.yaml`; when viewed from the main checkout this appears as `.kspec/project.runners.yaml`. It is loaded only after shadow branch context is available and is never read from root-branch `kspec.config.yaml`.
  - System runner config stored at `<daemon-config-dir>/projects/<project-key>/runners.yaml`, where `<daemon-config-dir>` is the same directory returned by `getDefaultDaemonConfigDir()` unless tests override it.
- Define `<project-key>` as the lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the canonical absolute project root path after realpath normalization. Do not truncate it, do not include the raw path in the directory name, and use the same helper in CLI, daemon, and tests.
- Define separate raw schemas for project runner config and system runner config, plus a merged effective runner type under a shared module such as `src/agents/runner-config.ts`.
- Project runner config must accept only portable project-specific values, initially limited to non-secret runner values such as `env.set`, `privacy.disable_nonessential_traffic`, and diagnostics preferences that are safe to commit.
- Project runner config must reject known adapter/harness secret keys and secret-looking names in `env.set`, including names containing `API_KEY`, `AUTH_TOKEN`, `ACCESS_TOKEN`, `OAUTH_TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, and known Claude/Codex/OpenAI credential variable names.
- System runner config must accept the full initial effective runner shape with these explicit fields and defaults:
  - `kind`: required string enum whose only accepted value in this plan is `acp_process`.
  - `adapter`: required string reference to an existing registered adapter.
  - `process.executable`: optional existing executable or command path. If omitted, the adapter's normal spawn command is used.
  - `process.args`: optional string array of additional non-secret arguments appended to the ACP process invocation, default empty.
  - `process.cwd`: optional system-config-relative or absolute cwd override for the child process only.
  - `env.inherit`: enum `ambient`, `minimal`, or `none`, default `minimal` for configured runners.
  - `env.pass`: string array of allowed inherited variable names, default empty.
  - `env.set`: string record for non-secret literals, default empty.
  - `env.secrets`: record keyed by child environment variable name, where each binding has `source` and `required`, default empty.
  - `privacy.disable_nonessential_traffic`: boolean default true.
  - `diagnostics.retain_raw_logs`: enum `never`, `on_failure`, or `always`, default `on_failure`.
- System runner config must reject known adapter/harness secret keys and secret-looking names in `env.set`; use `env.secrets` bindings for those child environment variables instead.
- Merge project and system config into effective runners by runner name, with system scalar values replacing project scalar values and system map keys overriding project map keys.
- Preserve source metadata for validation and diagnostics so each effective runner can report which layer supplied or overrode each field.
- Export named TypeScript interfaces or inferred aliases for project, system, and effective runner config so runtime, CLI, API, and Web UI serialization code can share the vocabulary.
- Add parser/loader tests for omitted runner files, project-only portable values, system-only runners, system-over-project overrides, invalid project secret-looking env values, invalid missing effective `kind`, invalid missing effective `adapter`, invalid enum values, and preservation of existing config behavior.

Why:
kspec needs a durable layered storage format for execution harnesses before agents, dispatch, CLI, daemon, or UI code can reference them consistently. The repo layer carries portable project values; local system config owns machine-specific process settings, argument/env/cwd configuration, and credentials.

How:
- Keep existing `kspec.config.yaml` behavior unchanged. Use shared helper plumbing only when needed to locate the project root.
- Prefer a dedicated loader module over embedding runner config in the root manifest. The chosen sidecar keeps operational runner values separate from behavioral kspec items while remaining repo-managed in the shadow branch.
- Use Zod schemas for both layers and include a custom project-layer validator that blocks known secret/API-key names.
- Keep secret values out of every schema shape. `env.secrets` entries name sources only; they must not include fields named `value`, `token`, `api_key`, or `secret`.
- Add or update tests in the existing parser/config test area. If no narrow suite exists, create `tests/runner-config.test.ts` using temp project and temp user-config fixtures.
- Validate `process.cwd` values with system-config-relative and absolute path cases.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/runner-config.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`

Covers: @agent-runner-configuration ac-named-runners-loaded, ac-project-runner-storage-is-repo-managed, ac-system-runner-storage-is-local, ac-system-overrides-project-values, ac-project-layer-accepts-portable-runner-values, ac-project-layer-blocks-known-secret-keys, ac-effective-runner-kind-and-adapter-required; @runner-environment-secret-boundaries ac-project-env-literals-are-non-secret, ac-secret-env-names-use-bindings, ac-secret-bindings-system-only, ac-secret-values-not-stored-inline

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Approach: create src/agents/runner-config.ts with three Zod schemas (project, system, effective) plus loaders. Project loader reads .kspec/project.runners.yaml (gated on shadow context). System loader reads <daemonConfigDir>/projects/<sha256(realpath(projectRoot))>/runners.yaml (defaults to getDefaultDaemonConfigDir but accepts test override). Helpers: deriveProjectKey(rootDir), getSystemRunnersPath(projectRoot, overrides?), getProjectRunnersPath(shadowDir). System schema is the full effective runner shape with kind enum (acp_process only), required adapter ref, optional process.executable/args/cwd, env.{inherit,pass,set,secrets}, privacy and diagnostics. Both layers reject secret-looking env.set names; env.secrets bindings only allowed from system. Merge: per-runner-name field-level overlay with system winning on scalars and map entries; env.set/env.pass merged so system keys/values replace project entries; output keeps source metadata per field (which layer supplied it + override info). Tests in tests/runner-config.test.ts using createTempDir+initGitRepo for project layer (.kspec/ subdir) and a temp dir as injected daemon config root. - The resolver input must include the agent definition, effective runner registry, invocation cwd, session id, auto-approve setting, and base invocation env.

  - `adapterId`: resolved existing registered adapter id.
  - `adapter`: the `AgentAdapter` spawn contract.
  - `cwd`: invocation cwd.
  - `env`: complete runner-scoped env overlay for the adapter process.

  - `diagnostics`: redacted selected-runner, source-layer, override, and selected-adapter details.
  - `cleanup`: optional async cleanup hook.
- Update `src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts` so one-shot and dispatch invocations call the resolver before spawning instead of directly calling `resolveAdapter(agent.adapter)`.
- Preserve legacy behavior by treating an agent without `runner` as an implicit `acp_process` runner around the existing adapter/default adapter resolution.
- When both `runner` and `adapter` are present, use the runner's adapter for spawn, skill-formatting, auto-approve args, and session metadata.

tasks.title: Build runner environment and secret resolution boundaries
tasks.description:
What:
- Implement a `buildRunnerEnv(...)` helper consumed by the runner resolver.
- Support `env.inherit` policies exactly as follows:
  - `ambient`: start from sanitized `process.env` for legacy compatibility.
  - `minimal`: start from an empty env and copy only runner `env.pass` names plus process variables required to spawn the configured command on the host platform.
  - `none`: start from an empty env except kspec-required invocation variables and literal runner settings.
- Preserve existing stripping of nested-agent variables such as `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION` before any inheritance policy is applied.
- Apply `env.set` after inheritance.
- Resolve `env.secrets` from approved system-layer sources. The initial implementation must support `source: user_env` by reading the host environment variable with the same name as the target secret name.
- If a required secret cannot be resolved, return a typed preflight failure before adapter spawn.
- Add kspec-required invocation variables, including `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1`, `KSPEC_SESSION_ID`, and `KSPEC_SHADOW_MUTATION_LOCK_FILE` when provided, after runner environment policy is applied.
- Apply privacy defaults when `privacy.disable_nonessential_traffic` is true: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` unless the runner explicitly sets a different value in `env.set`.
- Add a shared redaction helper for diagnostics that replaces secret values with a redaction marker in CLI output, session events, task notes, daemon responses, and Web UI payloads.
- Replace or route existing `injectEnvForAdapter(...)` usage so session id injection is part of the resolved runner contract while preserving existing Claude/Codex harness-specific injection behavior.
- Add tests for every inheritance mode, pass list behavior, literal overrides, required secret failure, optional secret omission, privacy default injection, explicit privacy override, nested-agent env stripping, and diagnostic redaction.

Why:
Headed and non-headed agent runtimes cannot rely on daemon ambient auth or user shell state. kspec needs an explicit boundary for credentials and configuration that is portable across daemon and dispatch contexts while keeping repo/project config free of harness secrets.

How:
- Keep secret values in local variables only long enough to populate the child process env.
- Do not write secret values into project runner config, system runner config, session JSONL, task notes, review records, WebSocket events, or Web UI stores.
- Tests must assert negative cases by checking absence of secret literals in serialized diagnostics and by verifying secret-looking keys are rejected from literal env values.
- Do not change global `process.env` as part of a runner invocation.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/agent-runner-env.test.ts tests/agent-invocation.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`

Covers: @runner-environment-secret-boundaries ac-env-inheritance-policy-applied, ac-env-set-overrides-allowed-values, ac-project-env-literals-are-non-secret, ac-secret-env-names-use-bindings, ac-secret-bindings-system-only, ac-secret-values-not-stored-inline, ac-required-secret-missing-blocks, ac-diagnostics-redact-secrets, ac-privacy-defaults-applied; @runner-invocation-semantics ac-session-env-injected-through-runner, ac-runner-cleanup-restores-state; existing @codex-acp-adapter-registration ac-2, ac-3

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Root cause: the shared filesystem lock /tmp/kspec-test-daemon-port-start.lock (introduced in commit 6076c6f) had no stale-holder detection. A SIGKILL/OOM that killed a prior test runner mid-startup left the directory behind, and every subsequent acquirer blocked for the full PORT_START_LOCK_MIN_TIMEOUT_MS=120s default. With a vitest test timeout of 5s, the failures surfaced as deterministic timeouts in the two acquirePlaywrightFixtureResources setup-failure cases and the nine startTestDaemon cases — exactly the cluster reported in the review snapshot. Reproduced locally by 'mkdir /tmp/kspec-test-daemon-port-start.lock' + npm test (90s timeout, same two failures).

Fix: switched from mkdir-based to file-based atomic acquisition (writeFileSync wx) with owner metadata (pid, hostname, startedAt). The contention loop falls into a bounded stale-recovery branch past a 100ms grace window: read the recorded owner, check process.kill(pid, 0), reclaim if dead. The recovery also handles legacy mkdir-only directory leftovers via rmSync(force, recursive). Best-effort exit/signal handlers release this process's held locks on normal teardown; SIGKILL still falls through to the recovery branch, but no longer blocks downstream runs.

Added spec AC ac-shared-startup-lock-recovers-from-crashed-holder to @daemon-test-teardown-boundedness covering this contract. Three behavioral regressions in tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts pin the new behavior via an isolated __testLockPath seam (dead PID file → reclaim, legacy directory leftover → reclaim, live holder PID → timeout, never evict).

Quality gates: format:check green, lint 0 errors, typecheck green, full npm test green (2665 suites / 10156 tests). Repro'd that the originally failing tests pass under both 'no stale lock' and 'stale legacy directory leftover' starting states.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Fix cycle 1 — addressed the blocker thread from review @01KT0C2G7MD6191D1NQBKY92V7.

Root cause: registerPortStartLockExitHandlers installed an anonymous SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP listener that called process.kill(process.pid, signal) without removing itself first. Node suppresses default termination while a signal listener is installed, so the re-raise re-entered the same handler in a tight loop. Test runners that had acquired the port-start lock would not terminate under SIGTERM — a direct violation of the daemon teardown boundedness contract this task is meant to enforce.

Fix (tests/helpers/daemon.ts:463-489): named the handler so it can call process.removeListener(signal, handler) before re-raising. With our listener gone, re-raise hits default disposition (process exit) unless another listener (e.g. the host test runner) owns termination semantics — in which case that listener takes over. Extracted the handler factory as exported __createPortStartLockSignalHandler so contract regressions can exercise it in-process with stub release / reRaise callables rather than actually sending signals to the test runner.

Regression coverage (tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts):
- Factory unit test: installs the actual factory output on benign SIGUSR2, invokes it, asserts (a) handler removed itself from process.listeners, (b) release ran exactly once, (c) reRaise was called with the same signal. Pre-fix the handler had no removal step, so process.listeners would still contain it after invocation.
- Subprocess e2e test: spawns a Node subprocess that mirrors the remove-then-re-raise shape, sends SIGTERM, asserts it exits within 5s with signalCode === SIGTERM. Pre-fix the subprocess would loop and only die from the test's SIGKILL safety net.

Both tests annotated against @daemon-test-teardown-boundedness ac-uncooperative-process-stop-is-bounded.

notes.content:

Root cause: registerPortStartLockExitHandlers installed anonymous signal listeners that called process.kill(process.pid, signal) without removing themselves first. Node suppresses default termination while a listener is installed, so the re-raise re-entered the same handler in an infinite loop. Test runners holding the port-start lock would not terminate under SIGTERM — violating the daemon teardown boundedness contract.

Fix (tests/helpers/daemon.ts:463-489): named the handler so it calls process.removeListener(signal, handler) before re-raising. With our listener gone, re-raise hits default disposition (process exit) unless another listener (e.g. host test runner) owns termination semantics. Extracted handler factory as exported __createPortStartLockSignalHandler so regressions can exercise the shape in-process via stub release/reRaise callables.

Regression coverage (tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts): (1) factory unit test installs handler on benign SIGUSR2, invokes it, asserts it removed itself from process.listeners + release ran exactly once + reRaise called with same signal. (2) subprocess e2e test spawns a Node subprocess mirroring the remove-then-re-raise shape, sends SIGTERM, asserts exit within 5s with signalCode SIGTERM. Both annotated against @daemon-test-teardown-boundedness ac-uncooperative-process-stop-is-bounded. Pre-fix both fail; post-fix both pass.

tasks.title: Tighten existing runner contracts for closure gaps
tasks.description:
What:
- Update only existing runner-related specs. Do not create duplicate runner specs from this follow-up plan.
- Reopen exactly these specs before adding ACs because the follow-up broadens implemented contracts that later tasks will implement:
  - `kspec item set @runner-process-invocation-inputs --status in_progress --no-cascade`

- Add these ACs to `@runner-process-invocation-inputs`:

  AC id: ac-relative-system-cwd-resolves-from-config-dir
  Given: A system runner config declares `process.cwd` as a relative path.
  When: kspec resolves the runner invocation contract, runs preflight, or spawns the adapter process.
  Then: The child-process cwd is the normalized path resolved relative to the directory that contains that system runner config file.

  AC id: ac-effective-adapter-command-preflighted
  Given: A runner-backed agent resolves to a registered adapter command and the runner does not override `process.executable`.
  When: runner validation or dispatch preflight checks whether the invocation can spawn.
  Then: The effective adapter command is checked under the runner-resolved cwd and process environment search path before prompt forwarding or dispatch acceptance.

- Add these ACs to `@runner-resolution-and-preflight`:

  AC id: ac-registry-load-failure-reports-config-error
  Given: Project or system runner config exists but cannot be parsed or validated into an effective runner registry.
  When: kspec validates, lists, edits, or prepares an agent that references a runner.
  Then: The diagnostic identifies the runner registry as unavailable, identifies the failing config layer and config path, includes the validation or parse reason, and redacts secret-looking values.

  AC id: ac-registry-load-failure-blocks-runner-spawn
  Given: Project or system runner config exists but cannot be parsed or validated into an effective runner registry.
  When: kspec prepares a runner-backed one-shot or dispatched invocation.
  Then: No adapter process is spawned and no prompt content is forwarded until the registry-load error is fixed.

- Add this AC to `@runner-invocation-semantics`:

  AC id: ac-dispatch-preflight-uses-canonical-session-id
  Given: Dispatch prepares a runner-backed task invocation and preflight needs session-scoped environment, diagnostics, or interpolation.
  When: the same invocation is later recorded as active and passed to `runInvocation`.
  Then: dispatch preflight and the actual invocation use the same canonical session id.

- Add these ACs to `@runner-operator-surfaces`:

  AC id: ac-daemon-agent-patch-returns-runner-state
  Given: A daemon client updates an agent definition through the agent PATCH endpoint.
  When: the saved agent has a runner field or resolves through legacy adapter compatibility.
  Then: the response includes the same `adapter`, `resolved_adapter`, and redacted `runner_validation` shape that the agent list endpoint would return for that saved agent.

  AC id: ac-web-ui-invocation-rows-show-resolved-adapter
  Given: The Web UI displays active or queued invocation rows whose daemon payload includes a runner name and resolved adapter identity.
  When: the rows are rendered.
  Then: visible row text and the row's accessible label include both the runner identity and the resolved adapter identity.

- Add notes to the touched specs naming this follow-up plan and the closure evidence that motivated the stricter ACs.

Why:
The runner layer landed functionally, but closure validation found several places where the specs let implementations satisfy the letter while preserving ambiguous runtime behavior: relative system cwd values were accepted without a deterministic base, registry-load failures could be collapsed into unknown-runner fallbacks, dispatch preflight could diverge from the actual invocation session, daemon mutation responses could be less enriched than list responses, and active/queued Web UI rows could hide resolved adapter identity behind weak presentation.

- Use `kspec item get` to capture each touched spec before editing.
- Use `kspec item ac add` for each new AC id exactly as written above.
- Use `kspec item note` to record the follow-up context; do not edit unrelated ACs.
- Do not mark any touched spec back to `implemented` in this task; implementation tasks provide that evidence later.

tasks.title: Resolve system runner cwd deterministically
tasks.description:
What:
- Update runner config loading/resolution so a relative `process.cwd` from system runner config is normalized against the directory containing the system `runners.yaml` file, not against the daemon or CLI parent process cwd.
- Keep absolute `process.cwd` values unchanged except for normal path normalization.
- Preserve the existing rule that project runner config cannot supply `process.cwd`; only system runner config owns machine-local cwd policy.
- Ensure the resolved invocation contract, preflight executable checks, session metadata/diagnostics summaries, and actual adapter spawn all consume the same normalized cwd string.
- Update docs that currently describe `process.cwd` as system-config-relative so they match the implemented behavior.
- Add regression tests covering:
  - relative system cwd resolves from the system config directory;
  - absolute system cwd remains absolute;
  - changing the parent process cwd does not change the resolved child cwd;
  - preflight and spawn use the normalized cwd.

Why:
The original plan said `process.cwd` could be system-config-relative, but the implementation stored and spawned the raw string. A relative cwd would therefore be interpreted relative to whichever shell, daemon, or test process launched kspec, which is not a stable machine-local runner policy.

How:
- Prefer resolving cwd during effective runner construction or immediately after loading the system layer, while the system config file path is still known.
- If `mergeRunnerConfigs(...)` needs the system config path, extend its inputs or add a wrapper so tests cannot call the old raw merge path accidentally for cwd-sensitive behavior.
- Keep diagnostics redacted as today; do not expose secret env values while adding cwd source/path details.
- Do not change legacy adapter-backed invocation cwd behavior.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/runner-config.test.ts tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts tests/agent-runner-process.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`

Covers: @runner-process-invocation-inputs ac-relative-system-cwd-resolves-from-config-dir, ac-runner-cwd-is-invocation-only, ac-invocation-diagnostics-identify-inputs
tasks.closed_reason: Merged to dev at 29f68905ee946e9b79bf5fa4a711854494e3736d after clean review. Summary: system runner process.cwd is normalized from the system runners.yaml directory; preflight, diagnostics, contract, and spawn paths consume the normalized cwd; docs and regression tests updated.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Approach: Normalize system process.cwd inside mergeRunnerConfigs by adding a third options parameter { systemConfigPath?: string }. When systemConfigPath is provided, resolve relative cwd against dirname(systemConfigPath); absolute paths pass through path.resolve (which normalizes . and ..). resolveEffectiveRunners always passes system.path so production callers get the normalized cwd. Tests calling mergeRunnerConfigs(null, system) directly with absolute cwd remain valid. Downstream buildRunnerContract, summarizeRunnerInvocation, and runner-validation probe see the already-normalized string from EffectiveRunner.process.cwd — so preflight, diagnostics, and spawn all consume the same normalized string by construction.

Edge cases:
- Relative cwd + no systemConfigPath (test-only path): leave as-is (no regression for existing tests)
- Absolute cwd + systemConfigPath: pass through path.resolve (normalizes . and ..)
- Relative cwd + systemConfigPath: path.resolve(dirname(systemConfigPath), cwd)
- Project layer never supplies cwd (schema rejects), so we don't need a project-config-path

Test plan (regression tests):
- runner-config.test.ts: relative cwd resolves from system config dir; absolute cwd remains absolute; parent process cwd change has no effect; resolveEffectiveRunners produces normalized cwd
- agent-runner-process.test.ts: contract.cwd equals normalized path; preflight uses normalized cwd; spawn (via contract.cwd) uses normalized cwd; mergeRunnerConfigs without systemConfigPath leaves relative cwd unchanged (so we keep tests honest)

tasks.title: Preserve registry-load failures as first-class runner diagnostics
tasks.description:
What:
- Add a shared redacted diagnostic shape for runner registry load failures. The shape must include a stable reason such as `runner_registry_unavailable`, the failing layer (`project` or `system` when known), the config path, and parse/validation issue messages with secret-looking values redacted.
- Update runner validation/listing surfaces so malformed project or system runner config is reported as a registry-load/config error, not as an absent runner name.
- Update one-shot invocation and dispatch preflight so a runner-backed agent blocks before spawn/prompt when the registry cannot be loaded.
- Update daemon agent list, daemon agent PATCH, and dispatch-status API enrichment so they attach the registry-load diagnostic to runner-backed agents when the registry is unavailable instead of returning only legacy adapter fallback state.
- Preserve legacy adapter-backed behavior for agents without `runner`: they may continue to list and invoke through the adapter path when runner config is absent or invalid.
- Add tests proving malformed project config, malformed system config, and validation issues distinguish registry-unavailable from true unknown-runner diagnostics.

Why:
Collapsing loader failures into an empty registry makes a malformed YAML/schema problem look like `unknown_runner`, and daemon responses may fabricate a resolved adapter from legacy fields. Operators need the real config-layer error so they know which file to fix before dispatch retries or UI debugging begins.

How:
- Reuse the existing `LayerLoadResult.issues` and config paths from `resolveEffectiveRunners(...)` instead of reparsing files in each surface.
- Keep redaction at one helper boundary and reuse it for CLI output, task notes, daemon responses, session events, and Web UI payloads.
- Do not include raw config contents in diagnostics.
- In dispatch, task notes should include the stable reason and config path but no secret values.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/agent-runner-cli.test.ts tests/cli-agent.test.ts tests/daemon-api/agent-runner-surfaces.test.ts tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts tests/daemon-api/agent-dispatch.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`

Covers: @runner-resolution-and-preflight ac-registry-load-failure-reports-config-error, ac-registry-load-failure-blocks-runner-spawn, ac-invalid-runner-blocks-before-prompt; @runner-environment-secret-boundaries ac-diagnostics-redact-secrets; @runner-operator-surfaces ac-daemon-agent-api-includes-runner

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Implemented runner registry-load failure diagnostics.

Approach:
- New src/agents/registry-load-failure.ts defines the shared RegistryLoadFailure shape (reason runner_registry_unavailable, layer, config_path, redacted issues) with diagnoseRegistryLoad/summarizeRegistryLoadFailure/describeRegistryLoadFailures helpers and a defense-in-depth secret redactor for issue messages.

CLI agent list (JSON + human) and dry-run validation_state prefer registry_load_failures over unknown_runner. The validate command emits registry_load_failures in JSON output.
- Dispatch preflight reads diagnoseRegistryLoad from resolveEffectiveRunners and passes registryLoadFailures into the resolver. Task notes include the stable reason and failing config paths. Legacy adapter-only agents stay on their existing path.
- Daemon meta.ts extracts a shared loadRunnerEnrichmentContext + buildAgentRunnerFields helper used by GET /api/meta/agents and PATCH /api/meta/agents/:id so both responses return the same adapter/resolved_adapter/runner_validation block. Dispatch status agent_definitions attach the same diagnostic for runner-backed agents.
- runner-config readYamlFile catches YAML parse errors and records them as LayerLoadResult.issues so the diagnostic chain works for both parse failures and Zod schema violations.

Tests: 17 new behavioral tests added across CLI (10), daemon API (5), and dispatch preflight (2). Each scenario distinguishes registry-load failure from unknown_runner and asserts redaction defense-in-depth.

tasks.title: Make dispatch preflight match the eventual runner invocation
tasks.description:
What:
- Generate the dispatch invocation's canonical session id before runner preflight, and pass that same id to preflight, active invocation tracking, event emission, session context, and `runInvocation`.
- Update dispatch preflight tests so any runner env/session injection or diagnostic interpolation sees the same `KSPEC_SESSION_ID` that appears in active invocation records and invocation lifecycle events.
- Update runner preflight so runner-backed invocations check the effective adapter command under the resolved runner cwd and env search path even when `process.executable` is omitted and the command comes from the registered adapter.
- Keep implicit/legacy adapter-only agents on their current compatibility path unless they are explicitly runner-backed.
- Ensure deterministic unspawnable-command failures still take the AGENT-SKIP path: no active invocation, no prompt forwarding, no retry counter increment, and a redacted task note.

Why:
Dispatch currently runs a runner preflight before allocating the final tracked session id, so future session-scoped runner behavior can diverge between preflight and the actual invocation. Preflight also skips adapter command spawnability when no runner executable override exists, even though a runner's env/PATH policy still controls whether the adapter command can spawn.

How:
- Move `preSessionId = ulid()` before the preflight resolver call in `src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts` and reuse it for every later session-id field.
- Adjust `probeRunnerInvocationExecutable(...)` / `preflightRunnerInvocation(...)` to distinguish implicit legacy invocations from named runner-backed invocations; named runner-backed contracts should preflight the effective adapter command under runner env/cwd whether the command source is runner config or adapter registry.
- Keep diagnostic details bounded to runner id, adapter id, command reference, and unspawnable reason.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts tests/agent-runner-process.test.ts tests/agent-runner-e2e.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`

tasks.title: Align daemon mutation responses and Web UI invocation rows with runner state
tasks.description:
What:
- Refactor daemon agent enrichment so GET agent-list responses and PATCH `/api/meta/agents/:id` responses share the same code path for `adapter`, `resolved_adapter`, and redacted `runner_validation` fields.
- Add daemon API tests where PATCH sets a valid runner, clears a runner, sets an unknown runner, and runs while the runner registry is unavailable. Assert the returned body matches the list endpoint's runner-state shape for the updated agent.
- Update active and queued invocation row components so runner identity and resolved adapter identity are both visible in row text and available to assistive technology.
- Preserve current compact display for legacy adapter-only rows, but ensure resolved adapter is still visible for those rows when daemon payloads provide it.
- Add or update Web UI tests/E2E fixtures for runner-backed active rows, runner-backed queued rows, legacy rows, and invalid-runner diagnostics. The tests must assert rendered text or accessible labels, not only `title` attributes.

Why:
The list endpoint was enriched, but PATCH returned the raw saved agent, so API clients could observe a less complete contract immediately after editing runner fields. Active and queued rows also displayed runner identity while leaving resolved adapter identity weakly exposed. Operator surfaces should make the resolved harness visible wherever dispatch state is shown.

How:
- Prefer extracting a local helper in `packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts` or a shared daemon utility rather than duplicating enrichment logic.
- Use daemon-provided fields in the Web UI; do not parse runner config in browser code.
- Do not expose raw env maps or secret source values in UI or API payloads.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --fresh tests/daemon-api/agent-runner-surfaces.test.ts`
- `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/agents.spec.ts`
- `npm --workspace packages/web-ui run check`

tasks.title: Preserve Git checkout failure details in `kspec plan branch` text errors
tasks.description:
What:
- Fix the text-mode error path for `kspec plan branch <ref>` when Git checkout/branch creation fails because local worktree contents would be overwritten.
- The human-readable stderr must include the underlying Git failure text, such as `The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by checkout`, the affected path(s), and Git's `Please move or remove them before you switch branches` guidance.
- The human-readable stderr must not print `[object Object]` for structured details objects.
- Preserve structured output behavior: `--json` and YAML/error-object output must continue to include the top-level error, `details.message`, and `details.suggestion` without ANSI color codes in JSON mode.

Why:
- `kspec plan branch` already captures Git's stderr through `branch-helper.runGit()`, but text-mode `error()` currently stringifies the wrapped details object as `[object Object]`.
- This hides the actionable reason for the branch failure and makes dirty/untracked worktree conflicts look like a mangled kspec error instead of a normal Git safety refusal.
- Plan branch creation is the command users are told to run for shared plan branches, so its runtime Git failures need to satisfy the existing error-guidance and semantic-exit-code traits.

How:
- Start from `src/cli/commands/plan.ts`, `src/cli/branch-helper.ts`, `src/cli/output.ts`, and `tests/plan-branch-helper.test.ts`.
- Add a focused regression test in `tests/plan-branch-helper.test.ts` that uses a disposable fixture repo and `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1`/direct CLI execution to avoid daemon/proxy interference.
- The regression should create a branch-creation checkout conflict by configuring dispatch base branch to a branch that contains a tracked path, then leaving an untracked file with the same path in the current worktree before running `plan branch`.
- Assert the text-mode command exits with runtime-error exit code `3`, stderr includes the real Git checkout refusal and the conflicted filename, and stderr does not include `[object Object]`.
- Assert `plan get` still shows no `branch` value for the plan after the failed checkout, because plan metadata must only update after a successful branch checkout/create.
- Add or update a JSON-mode assertion for the same failure class: the command exits with runtime-error exit code `3`, stderr parses as JSON, has `success: false`, has `error: "Failed to create or resume plan branch"`, includes the Git failure in `details.message`, includes guidance in `details.suggestion`, and contains no ANSI escape codes.
- Implement the smallest production change that makes structured error details render usefully in text mode. Prefer a shared formatter in `src/cli/output.ts` if other commands pass `{ message, suggestion }` details objects; avoid special-casing only one test string if a general formatter cleanly preserves existing behavior.
- If the generic formatter changes text output for other commands, update/add focused tests for `error()` or affected command tests so JSON/YAML output remains unchanged and text output stays readable.
- Do not change branch naming, branch source selection, remote rehydration, shadow commit behavior, or daemon dispatch target-sync logic in this task.

Testing:
- `npm test -- --run tests/plan-branch-helper.test.ts`
- If `src/cli/output.ts` is changed generically, also run the smallest existing output-format/error tests that cover `error()` behavior; if no focused test exists, add one and include it in the verification command.
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint -- --quiet`
- `npx oxlint src/cli/output.ts src/cli/commands/plan.ts tests/plan-branch-helper.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 node dist/cli/index.js validate --warnings-ok` only if the implementation changes kspec metadata; otherwise no metadata validation is required for source-only code changes.

Covers:
- `@trait-error-guidance ac-1`
- `@trait-error-guidance ac-2`
- `@trait-error-guidance ac-6`
- `@trait-json-output ac-1`
- `@trait-json-output ac-3`
- `@trait-semantic-exit-codes ac-4`

Coverage note:
- Existing inherited trait coverage on `@plan-branch-creation` is sufficient for this bug; no new spec or AC is required.

tasks.title: Add shared-guidance neutrality convention and review guidance
tasks.description:
What:
- Add or update project-local convention/reviewer guidance for this
  self-hosting repository so changes to package-shipped external guidance are
  reviewed for project neutrality before approval.
- The guidance must apply when a task or plan changes any of these shared or
  package-derived surfaces:
  - `templates/skills/`
  - `templates/agents-sections/`
  - `templates/skills/manifest.yaml`
  - `plugin/plugins/kspec/skills/`
  - rendered package/core skill outputs under `.agents/skills/` when their
    source is a package core skill rather than a project-local `.kspec/skills/`
    skill
  - rendered package/core skill outputs under `.factory/skills/` when they
    are generated from package core skill sources
  - generated `kspec-agents.md` sections that come from package templates
- The convention/reviewer guidance must state the semantic review rule:
  package-shipped guidance describes universal kspec mechanics only;
  Kynetic self-hosting branch policy, repo paths, quality gates, generated
  artifact maintenance rules, dispatch workflow choices, agent ids, and
  external review policy belong in project-local context.
- The guidance must require reviewers to check both directions:
  - shared/package text does not hard-code Kynetic-only policy as universal;
  - any still-needed Kynetic self-hosting instruction removed from shared
    text has a project-local home such as `AGENTS.md`, project-local
    `.kspec/skills/`, or project meta conventions.
- Prefer a project-local kspec convention domain plus reviewer skill/checklist
  wording over new specs or AC-tagged tests. Attach the convention/checklist
  to the reviewer agents that review task work and plans in this repository,
  using `kspec agent list` and `kspec meta get` to identify the current agent
  ids before editing.
- Do not add a broad markdown scanner or string-denylist test in this task.
  If implementation discovers an already-existing obvious-token lint, keep
  any changes narrow and non-semantic; do not present it as proof of prose
  neutrality.

Why:
Project-neutrality of prose is semantic and brittle to validate by scanning
strings in markdown. Reviewers and agents can judge whether guidance is
universal, while mechanical tests should stay focused on rendering,
installation, and generated-artifact consistency.

How:
- Use kspec CLI/meta commands for project-local convention and agent metadata
  edits; do not manually edit `.kspec` YAML files.
- Keep the guidance self-contained so a future reviewer has no chat history:
  define shared/package surfaces, allowed local homes, and examples of
  Kynetic-specific material that must not be framed as universal.
- If a project-local reviewer skill is added or edited, render skills and
  regenerate agent instructions as needed so the guidance reaches reviewer
  agents.

Testing:
- `kspec agent list`
- `kspec meta get <reviewer-agent-ref>` for the affected reviewer agents
- `kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`
- If conventions, skills, or generated agent instructions change, run
  `kspec agents generate` and/or `kspec skill render` as appropriate and
  inspect the generated reviewer guidance.

Covers: convention/reviewer-gate prerequisite only; no spec AC is claimed.

tasks.title: Sanitize Active Fleet preview terminal output
tasks.description:
What:
- Improve the compact Active Fleet/task-board preview of running agent output so raw terminal control bytes do not render as mangled-looking text in fleet cards.
- In `packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/board/fleet-buffer.ts`, sanitize completed display lines before they enter the compact `lines` array used by Active Fleet cards.
- Strip ANSI/CSI terminal escape sequences from preview lines, normalize CRLF newlines to LF, treat bare carriage returns as terminal progress-line rewrites, apply backspace controls, and strip remaining non-printing terminal control characters.
- Preserve the existing bounded preview behavior (`MAX_DISPLAY_LINES`) and line-buffering semantics.
- Preserve split escape sequence handling by keeping incomplete buffered text raw until a newline completes the display line.

Why:
- Agent/CLI streams can contain color codes, cursor/progress rewrites, backspaces, and other terminal bytes that are meaningful in a terminal but confusing in the browser card preview.
- The Active Fleet row promises the last few lines of output; those lines should be readable enough for status scanning without requiring users to open full logs.
- This is separate from the CLI `[object Object]` error-formatting fix: this task only addresses web UI compact preview rendering of terminal-like streams.

How:
- Keep the sanitizer preview-only and pure; do not mutate backend event payloads, session event storage, canonical logs, or the session-event accumulator.
- Implement small helper functions in `fleet-buffer.ts` rather than adding a full terminal emulator/xterm dependency.
- Apply sanitization only when a line is complete; do not sanitize `state.buffer` while the line is still partial.
- Treat remaining bare `` characters as terminal-style line rewrites after CRLF has been normalized.
- Avoid broad product/UI changes outside `packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/board/fleet-buffer.ts` unless tests reveal the preview path requires them.
- Fix any formatter issues in the existing exploratory edits before submitting the task for review.

Testing:
- Add/update `tests/web-ui/fleet-buffer.test.ts` coverage for:
  - stripping ANSI color/control sequences from completed display lines;
  - split ANSI sequences across chunks staying buffered until the line completes;
  - bare carriage returns keeping only the latest progress-line content;
  - CRLF normalization preserving distinct lines;
  - backspace controls applying before display.
- Run:
  - `npm test -- --fresh --run tests/web-ui/fleet-buffer.test.ts`
  - `npx oxlint packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/board/fleet-buffer.ts tests/web-ui/fleet-buffer.test.ts`
  - `npm run format:check`
  - `npm run typecheck`
- If implementation touches other web UI files, also run the smallest relevant additional web-ui test slice and include those commands in the task note.

Covers:
- `@ui-task-board ac-4`

Out of scope:
- Do not change `src/cli/output.ts`, plan-branch error formatting, CLI JSON/YAML/text output contracts, or exit-code semantics.
- Do not change backend stream/event payloads, WebSocket event schema, session-event accumulation, stored session logs, or full-log rendering.
- Do not attempt full terminal emulation, cursor positioning, alternate screen handling, or xterm-style rendering in fleet cards.
- Do not change Active Fleet card layout, task ordering, dispatch status semantics, or `MAX_DISPLAY_LINES`.

Proposal review:
- Native `plan-reviewer` read-only review returned CLEAR before task creation.
- Reviewer agreed existing `@ui-task-board ac-4` is sufficient coverage and noted optional extra coverage for non-SGR CSI sequences is not blocking.

tasks.title: Add generic ACP process adapter profile
tasks.description:
Add a production-safe generic ACP process adapter profile so custom ACP-compatible executables can be configured without pretending to be the mock ACP test adapter and without inheriting package-specific argv from `claude-agent-acp`, `codex-acp`, or any other model-specific built-in adapter.

Why:
- Runner-backed invocations currently let `process.executable` replace only the adapter command while keeping the selected adapter's base args and auto-approve args.
- That is correct for package-backed adapters, but it forces custom ACP executables to use `adapter: mock-acp` solely to get empty argv.
- The runner registry needs a generic adapter profile for "spawn this ACP executable exactly as configured by the runner" without adding headed-Claude-specific support.

What:
- In `src/agents/adapters.ts`, extend `AgentAdapter` with optional metadata `requiresProcessExecutable?: boolean`. Non-generic adapters keep required `command: string`; adapters with `requiresProcessExecutable: true` have no adapter-level command and may be resolved only through a runner that supplies `process.executable`.
- Register a new built-in adapter id `generic-acp` with `requiresProcessExecutable: true`, `args: []`, no `command`, no model-specific launch args, no `autoApproveArgs`, and a description that identifies it as a generic ACP process profile for runner-supplied executables.
- Extend `RunnerResolutionReason` in `src/agents/runners.ts` with `missing_process_executable` and use that stable reason for all generic ACP missing-executable failures.
- Extend runner resolution so `generic-acp` runner-backed invocations require `runner.process.executable` during runner contract resolution. Runner-backed failures must use `RunnerResolutionError("missing_process_executable", ...)` with details `{ runner, adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`.
- When a `generic-acp` runner supplies `process.executable`, the returned effective adapter/contract must contain that executable as the command before preflight/spawn. The generic adapter must not expose, preflight, or spawn any placeholder command.
- Reject direct/legacy `generic-acp` usage before spawn through the `resolveRunnerInvocation` implicit/adapter-override path in `src/agents/runners.ts`. If an agent sets `adapter: generic-acp` without a runner contract, or a one-shot command selects `--adapter generic-acp` without a runner, resolution must fail with `RunnerResolutionError("missing_process_executable", ...)` and details `{ adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`; do not spawn a placeholder command.
- In CLI and validation surfaces, make the missing-executable failures operator-actionable. Diagnostics must identify the adapter id `generic-acp`; runner-backed diagnostics must also identify the runner name and missing `process.executable` field. Expected files include `src/agents/runner-validation.ts` and `src/cli/commands/agent.ts`.
- Preserve existing semantics for all package-backed adapters: `process.executable` continues to replace only the command while keeping that adapter's base args and auto-approve args.
- Preserve runner `process.args` semantics: for `generic-acp`, runner args are appended to the invocation exactly as configured after the empty generic adapter contribution.
- Preserve prompt behavior for `generic-acp`: do not map it to `claude-code`, `codex`, or `droid` skill-reference formatting unless a separate future spec adds an explicit formatting-profile field.
- Add or update CLI/operator diagnostics so `kspec agent runners validate` surfaces `generic-acp` as a registered adapter and reports missing `process.executable` as invalid rather than as a later spawn failure.

Testing:
- Add adapter registry tests in `tests/agent-runtime/adapter-auto-approve.test.ts` proving `getAdapter("generic-acp")` is registered with `requiresProcessExecutable: true`, has `args: []`, has no `command`, and has no `autoApproveArgs`.
- Add runner resolver tests in `tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts` proving a `generic-acp` runner with `process.executable` resolves to that executable and has `extraArgs` equal only to runner `process.args`, even with `autoApprove: true`.
- Add a package-backed regression test in `tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts` using a non-generic registered adapter with `args`, `autoApproveArgs`, runner `process.executable`, runner `process.args`, and `autoApprove: true`; assert the command is overridden, adapter base args remain on the adapter, and `extraArgs` contains adapter auto-approve args followed by runner args.
- Add a negative runner resolver test in `tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts` proving a `generic-acp` runner without `process.executable` fails during contract resolution with reason `missing_process_executable` and details `{ runner, adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`.
- Add preflight/process coverage in `tests/agent-runner-process.test.ts` proving a valid `generic-acp` runner preflights only the runner-declared executable and never preflights or spawns a placeholder generic command.
- Add CLI diagnostics coverage in `tests/agent-runner-cli.test.ts` so `kspec agent runners validate --json` reports missing `process.executable` for `generic-acp` as an invalid runner with reason `missing_process_executable` and details `{ runner, adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`, and human output includes redacted guidance.
- Add direct/legacy invocation coverage in `tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts` for `resolveRunnerInvocation` implicit `agent.adapter: generic-acp` and `adapterOverride: "generic-acp"`; both must fail before spawn with reason `missing_process_executable` and details `{ adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`.
- Add CLI dry-run coverage in `tests/cli-agent.test.ts` for `agent.adapter: generic-acp` and `--adapter generic-acp` without a runner; both must fail before spawn with guidance to use a runner-backed config.
- Add prompt-formatting coverage in `tests/agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts` showing `adapterId: "generic-acp"` leaves skill references in portable form and does not rewrite them as Claude, Codex, or Droid platform references.
- Run `npm run format:check`.
- Run `npm run lint -- --quiet`.
- Run focused lint for touched files, for example `npx oxlint src/agents/adapters.ts src/agents/runners.ts src/agent-runtime/prompts.ts tests/agent-runtime/adapter-auto-approve.test.ts tests/agent-runner-resolver.test.ts tests/agent-runner-process.test.ts tests/agent-runner-cli.test.ts tests/cli-agent.test.ts tests/agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts`.
- Run `npm run typecheck`.
- Run `npm test -- adapter-auto-approve agent-runner-resolver agent-runner-process agent-runner-cli agent-invocation-lifecycle`
- Run `kspec validate --schema --warnings-ok`.
- Run `kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok`.
- Run `kspec validate --alignment --completeness --warnings-ok`.

Covers:
- @runner-process-invocation-inputs ac-generic-acp-process-requires-executable
- @runner-process-invocation-inputs ac-generic-acp-process-uses-runner-executable
- @runner-process-invocation-inputs ac-generic-acp-process-omits-built-in-launch-args
- @runner-operator-surfaces ac-generic-acp-validation-reports-missing-executable
- @runner-invocation-semantics ac-generic-acp-auto-approve-contributes-no-args
- @runner-invocation-semantics ac-generic-acp-skill-formatting-is-neutral
- @runner-resolution-and-preflight ac-generic-acp-direct-invocation-requires-runner

Out of scope:
- Do not add `headed-claude`, Claude-specific auth, browser automation, or terminal/PTY-specific branches to kspec.
- Do not change global `process.executable` override semantics for `claude-agent-acp`, `codex-acp`, `droid-acp`, or other package/model-specific adapters.
- Do not change legacy/ad-hoc adapter compatibility except for the explicit `generic-acp` missing-executable rejection.
- Do not allow arbitrary unknown adapter refs in system runner config.
- Do not add runner-level auto-approval args or a separate prompt-formatting profile in this task; those are larger schema decisions.
- Do not migrate local machine runner configs as part of the implementation task; after the code lands, operators can switch local configs from `mock-acp` to `generic-acp` separately.

tasks.description:

Add daemon routes rooted at `/api/tasks/:ref/resources` so browsers and static/live UI code resolve task resources through the task's versioned refs:
- `GET /api/tasks/:ref/resources` returns the task detail `resolved_resources` projection.
- `GET /api/tasks/:ref/resources/:resourceId` returns one resolved resource projection or a structured 404 when the task has no matching resource id.
- `GET /api/tasks/:ref/resources/:resourceId/bytes` serves bytes only when the resolved resource status is `present`; it sets `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `X-Kspec-Resource-Sha256` from the current matching resource.

- Resolve plan-owned refs through the source plan manifest and task-owned refs through the current task's resource manifest. Use the existing resource resolver and manifest helpers; do not raw-join user-authored paths.
- Binary browser URLs in live multi-project mode must include selected-project context just like review resource URLs.
