tasks.title: Register, sanitize, and emit dispatch lifecycle events
tasks.description:
### Covers

- ac-applied-control-is-auditable
- ac-noop-control-is-auditable
- ac-failed-control-is-auditable
- ac-failure-events-use-closed-error-codes

### Required context

Identifiers are exactly dispatch_control.pause_applied, dispatch_control.start_applied, dispatch_control.resume_applied, dispatch_control.stop_applied, dispatch_control.noop, and dispatch_control.failed. Every payload always has scope global/task, action start/pause/resume/stop, authority stopped/running/paused, projection stopped/running/paused/draining, outcome applied/noop/failed, reason, actor, source cli/api/ui/daemon_startup/daemon_shutdown/recovery, and timestamp. Task scope has canonical task_id and optional task_ref; global scope has neither. reason defaults to `operator request`, removes control characters, collapses/trims whitespace, and is at most 240 Unicode code points; actor is at most 120 and task_ref 200 after the same removal/normalization. Prompts, secrets, terminal buffers, workspace paths, raw input errors, and raw failure errors are absent.

The failure predicate is exhaustive and closed: request validation -> validation_failed; missing task -> task_not_found; multiple resolved tasks -> task_identity_ambiguous; submitted ref/id disagreement -> task_identity_mismatch; matrix rejection -> invalid_transition; lock/store I/O/timeout -> control_store_unavailable; malformed committed control object -> control_store_corrupt; commit false/throw or committed-object verification failure -> control_commit_failed; bounded cancellation wait -> cancellation_timeout; verified signal failure -> cancellation_failed; durable session close failure -> session_closure_failed; copied versus current ownership tuple mismatch -> cleanup_ownership_mismatch; leader birth-token mismatch or PID reuse -> cleanup_process_birth_mismatch; leader absent with a safely verified owned live group -> cleanup_leader_missing_group_alive; unreadable/malformed ownership or birth proof -> cleanup_identity_unverifiable; unsupported platform or live group without an immutable matching member proof -> cleanup_group_unverifiable; every uncategorized fault -> internal_error. No predicate overlaps another.

### Deliverable

One typed sanitized outcome emitter: applied start/pause/resume/stop uses its matching `*_applied` identifier and no error_code; an idempotent result uses `dispatch_control.noop` and no error_code; every failed predicate above uses `dispatch_control.failed` with exactly its mapped code after the durable outcome is known.

### Implementation

Register domain/types in both schema owners. Implement the predicate-to-code table above in a closed `DispatchControlErrorCode` mapper shared by every emission site; reject unknown code strings at schema validation. Emit exactly once after a committed applied/noop/failed outcome, never before commit or during retry observation. Emit on `agents`; the UI owner invalidates queryKeys.agents.all and refreshes the automation event log.

### Files

- Create: tests/dispatch-control-events.test.ts
- Modify: src/schema/event-registry.ts
- Modify: src/schema/event-payloads.ts
- Modify: packages/shared/src/schemas.ts
- Modify: packages/shared/src/websocket.ts
- Modify: src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts
- Modify: tests/event-registry.test.ts
- Modify: tests/event-payloads.test.ts
- Modify: tests/event-bus.test.ts

### Behavioral tests

In tests/dispatch-control-events.test.ts create `captureDispatchControlEvents` and `emitOutcomeFixture`. Drive one applied start/pause/resume/stop, one noop, and each of the seventeen failure predicates. For each, capture identifier, full payload, and event count: assert the exact identifier/outcome/code mapping, one event only after the fixture's commit barrier, global/task identity presence rules, all five sanitization/bound cases, all forbidden classes, and rejection of every non-enum code. Existing event-registry/payload/bus tests assert cross-schema registration and agents-topic publication.

### Verification

- npm test -- tests/dispatch-control-events.test.ts tests/event-registry.test.ts tests/event-payloads.test.ts tests/event-bus.test.ts
- npm run typecheck
- npm run lint
- git diff --check

### Reviewer handoff

Provide identifier, enum, sanitizer, and durable-result tables.

tasks.title: Add canonical lifecycle API and compatibility adapters
tasks.description:
### Covers

- ac-status-reports-authority
- ac-status-reports-projection
- ac-status-reports-active-count
- ac-status-reports-queued-count
- ac-status-reports-held-count
- ac-status-reports-held-task-identity
- ac-status-reports-held-task-scope
- ac-status-reports-held-task-mode
- ac-status-reports-held-task-reason
- ac-failure-api-uses-closed-error-codes
- ac-api-failures-do-not-expose-raw-errors

### Required context

Canonical routes are GET /api/agent/status and POST /api/agent/dispatch/control with `{scope,action,task_ref?,task_id?,reason?}`. Canonical success/noop is HTTP 200 `{ok:true,data:{global_authority,projection,cleanup_state,active_count,queue_depth,held_count,held_tasks,task_controls,degraded_targets,outcome,task_id?,task_ref?},error:null}`. Canonical failure is `{ok:false,data:<complete current lifecycle status>,error:{code,message,suggestion,details?}}`, where details contains typed field names/canonical IDs only. Codes/statuses are validation_failed 400; task_not_found 404; task_identity_ambiguous, task_identity_mismatch, invalid_transition, cleanup_ownership_mismatch, cleanup_process_birth_mismatch, cleanup_leader_missing_group_alive 409; control_store_unavailable, control_store_corrupt, control_commit_failed, cleanup_identity_unverifiable, cleanup_group_unverifiable 503; cancellation_timeout, cancellation_failed, session_closure_failed, internal_error 500.

Inline public wire schema (do not infer it from parent prose): `CleanupState = {status:"idle",entries:[]} | {status:"pending"|"failed",entries:CleanupEntryStatus[]}`; `CleanupEntryStatus = {cleanup_id:string,scope:"global"|"task",task_id?:string,status:"pending"|"failed",phase:"owned"|"signals_sent"|"sessions_closed",error_code?:CleanupErrorCode}`. Canonical ULIDs are required and task_id is required iff task scope. Idle requires empty entries. Pending requires non-empty/all entry status pending, each forbidding error_code. Failed requires non-empty/at least one entry status failed; every failed entry requires error_code and every pending entry forbids it. CleanupErrorCode is exactly cancellation_timeout/cancellation_failed/session_closure_failed/cleanup_ownership_mismatch/cleanup_process_birth_mismatch/cleanup_leader_missing_group_alive/cleanup_identity_unverifiable/cleanup_group_unverifiable/internal_error. Entries are global-first then task_id/cleanup_id sorted, with no duplicate cleanup_id or scope/task owner. `HeldTask = {task_id:string,task_ref:string|null,title:string|null,scope:"global"|"task",mode:"paused"|"stopped",reason:string,actor:string,source:"cli"|"api"|"ui"|"daemon_startup"|"daemon_shutdown"|"recovery",controlled_at:string,updated_at:string}`. `TaskControl` has the same task_id/ref/title/mode/reason/actor/source/timestamps plus `cleanup_state:CleanupState`; its nested entries are empty or the one matching task entry. held_tasks and task_controls are arrays sorted by canonical task_id with no duplicates; held_count equals held_tasks.length.

Matching-scope gating is exact: global transitions and legacy global aliases filter only `scope:"global"`; task T transitions filter only `scope:"task",task_id:T`; aggregate arrays/counts are observability only. Task metadata mutations are allowed despite global cleanup, but work creation still requires independent running global authority and empty global-scope cleanup. Thus stopped global with only unrelated task cleanup permits global start and reconciliation while matching task admission remains denied.

Request identity is global with no task fields or task with at least one task_ref/task_id; aliases resolve before mutation, both fields must agree, and canonical mutation data adds required `task_id` and nullable `task_ref` only for task scope. Global mutation data forbids them; error data is current status and carries no request alias; legacy aliases add no identity. While matching global cleanup is pending/failed, global start/pause/resume return canonical 409 invalid_transition; unrelated task cleanup does not. While matching task cleanup is pending/failed, task pause/resume do the same; global/other-task cleanup does not alter the task record. Stop retries only matching scope. Successful cleanup removes only that entry and only a later start/task resume can reopen work, subject to global authority.

Public GET /api/agent/status HTTP 200 is unwrapped and always keeps dispatch_enabled, active_invocations[] `{session_id,agent_id,task_ref,task_title,elapsed_ms,resolved_adapter}`, queued_invocations[] `{agent_id,task_ref,task_title,wait_ms,resolved_adapter}`, queue_depth, agent_definitions[] `{id,name,adapter,resolved_adapter,completed_sessions}`, degraded `{active,reason,enteredAt}`, and degraded_targets[] `{branch,reason,enteredAt,kind}`. Active/queued rows add runner only when configured; definitions add runner only when configured and runner_validation `{status,diagnostics[]}` only when current resolution emits it; diagnostics retain current reason/message/details? presence. It appends global_authority, projection, cleanup_state, held_count, held_tasks, task_controls. Store unavailable/corrupt is canonical 503; status-mapping failure is canonical 500.

Internal GET /api/agent/dispatch/status has these exact bases before appending globalAuthority, projection, cleanupState, heldCount, heldTasks, taskControls: engine-present 200 `{running,activeInvocations,queuedInvocations,invocations,queued,degraded,degradedTargets}` with invocation `{invocationId,sessionId,agentId,agentName,taskRef,elapsedMs,resolvedAdapter,runner}` and queued `{agentId,agentName,taskRef,waitMs,runner,adapter}` (taskRef/runner/adapter are omitted when undefined by JSON); no-engine 200 `{running:false,activeInvocations:0,queuedInvocations:0,invocations:[],degraded:{active:false,reason:"",enteredAt:null},degradedTargets:[]}` and omits queued. Its 500/503 bodies use the same respective engine-present/no-engine base plus lifecycle additions and error_code; degraded/degradedTargets remain present and no-engine/error never invents queued.

Mutation aliases retain these complete HTTP response rows. Native Elysia invalid-body 400 remains its current validation-details body, unwrapped and otherwise unchanged. Both cwd errors are path-free: validation 400 error is exactly `Invalid dispatch working directory`; conflict 409 error is exactly `Dispatch is already running for another project`.

| Route | 200 success/no-op rows | 400/409 legacy rows | 500/503 translation rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST /api/agent/dispatch | start `{dispatch_enabled:true}`; same-cwd no-op `{dispatch_enabled:true,reason:"Already running"}`; stop `{dispatch_enabled:false}`; no-engine stop `{dispatch_enabled:false,reason:"No engine running"}` | cwd 400 `{dispatch_enabled:false,error:"Invalid dispatch working directory"}`; conflict 409 `{dispatch_enabled:true,error:"Dispatch is already running for another project"}`; invalid transition 409 `{dispatch_enabled:<current-running-boolean>,error:"Invalid dispatch lifecycle transition",error_code:"invalid_transition"}` | pre-commit 503 `{dispatch_enabled:<prior-running>,error_code:<control_store_unavailable|control_store_corrupt|control_commit_failed>}`; post-commit cleanup 409/500/503 `{dispatch_enabled:false,reason:"cleanup_pending",error_code:<mapped cleanup code>}`; other 500 `{dispatch_enabled:<prior-running>,error_code:"internal_error"}` |
| POST /api/agent/dispatch/start | `{started:true,status:<complete current internal status>}`; same-cwd no-op `{started:false,reason:"Already running",status:<complete current internal status>}` | cwd 400 `{started:false,error:"Invalid dispatch working directory"}` with no status; conflict 409 `{started:false,error:"Dispatch is already running for another project",status:<complete current internal status>}`; invalid transition 409 `{started:false,error:"Invalid dispatch lifecycle transition",status:<complete current internal status>,error_code:"invalid_transition"}` | pre-commit 503 `{started:false,error_code:<control_store_unavailable|control_store_corrupt|control_commit_failed>}`; post-commit cleanup 409/500/503 `{started:false,error_code:<mapped cleanup code>}`; other 500 `{started:false,error_code:"internal_error"}` |
| POST /api/agent/dispatch/stop | `{stopped:true}`; no-engine `{stopped:false,reason:"No engine running"}` | invalid transition 409 `{stopped:false,reason:"invalid_transition",error_code:"invalid_transition"}` | pre-commit 503 `{stopped:false,error_code:<control_store_unavailable|control_store_corrupt|control_commit_failed>}`; post-commit cleanup 409/500/503 `{stopped:false,reason:"cleanup_pending",error_code:<mapped cleanup code>}`; other 500 `{stopped:false,error_code:"internal_error"}` |

Raw exceptions, stacks, project paths, cwd paths, and dynamic error strings are forbidden in every canonical and alias response. The only mutation 409 error strings are the two fixed cwd messages or the exact invalid-transition bodies above.

### Deliverable

Canonical control/status plus additive POST /api/agent/dispatch, POST /api/agent/dispatch/start, POST /api/agent/dispatch/stop, and GET /api/agent/dispatch/status adapters, all deep-equal to the rows above.

### Implementation

Implement the tables verbatim in packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts and packages/shared/src/api.ts. Route identity resolves ref/id before a successful task-scoped control and returns the canonical ULID in canonical data/status. Preserve no-engine omission of queued, every conditional runner field, native Elysia invalid-body details, every no-op reason, and complete start status. Do not route API errors through raw Error text.

### Files

- Create: tests/daemon-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts
- Modify: packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts
- Modify: packages/daemon/src/server.ts
- Modify: packages/shared/src/api.ts
- Modify: tests/daemon-api/agent-dispatch.test.ts
- Modify: tests/daemon-agent-dispatch-routes.test.ts

### Behavioral tests

In tests/daemon-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts create `createLifecycleRouteFixture`, `requestLifecycleRoute`, and `captureLifecycleEvents`; use existing in-process route helpers. Add shared serializer/Zod/type fixtures for idle, all-pending, all-failed, and mixed failed-plus-pending CleanupState plus full HeldTask/TaskControl rows; accept exact valid rows and reject pending-with-error, failed-entry-without-error, failed aggregate with no failed entry, idle-with-entry, unknown/mixed-case fields, bad IDs/order/duplicates/count. Deep-equal matching-scope global/task transition responses, including global start with unrelated task cleanup, task mutation under global cleanup with zero start, and alias global-scope-only gating. Retain all canonical codes, complete alias rows, forbidden fields, and native Elysia validation.

### Verification

- npm test -- tests/daemon-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts tests/daemon-api/agent-dispatch.test.ts tests/daemon-agent-dispatch-routes.test.ts
- npm run typecheck
- npm run lint
- git diff --check

### Reviewer handoff

Provide canonical/alias field/status fixtures and forbidden-field matrix.

tasks.title: Add safe lifecycle CLI commands
tasks.description:
### Covers

- ac-failure-cli-uses-closed-error-codes
- ac-cli-failures-do-not-expose-raw-errors

### Required context

Grammar is exact: `kspec agent dispatch start [--reason TEXT] [--json]`; `kspec agent dispatch pause [--reason TEXT] [--json]`; `kspec agent dispatch resume [--reason TEXT] [--json]`; `kspec agent dispatch stop [--reason TEXT] [--force] [--json]`; `kspec agent dispatch task pause|resume @task [--reason TEXT] [--json]`; `kspec agent dispatch task stop @task [--reason TEXT] [--force] [--json]`; `kspec agent status [--json]`; and `kspec agent dispatch status [--json]`. Every mutation POSTs only `/api/agent/dispatch/control`; neither start nor stop may call `/api/agent/dispatch`, `/start`, or `/stop`. Both status commands GET only `/api/agent/dispatch/status`, never public `/api/agent/status`.

CLI consumes only internal GET `/api/agent/dispatch/status`; it does not import/share the UI public-response converter. Its exact schema has camelCase top-level `cleanupState/heldTasks/taskControls` and intentionally snake_case nested rows. `cleanupState` is `{status:"idle",entries:[]}` or `{status:"pending"|"failed",entries:[{cleanup_id,scope:"global"|"task",task_id?,status:"pending"|"failed",phase:"owned"|"signals_sent"|"sessions_closed",error_code?}]}`. Idle requires empty entries; pending requires non-empty/all pending entries and forbids every error_code; failed requires non-empty/at least one failed entry, requires error_code on each failed entry, and forbids it on pending entries. IDs are canonical; task_id is required iff task scope; the cleanup-code subset is exact; entries are global-first then task_id/cleanup_id sorted with unique cleanup/scope-owner identity. `heldTasks` is canonical-task-id-sorted unique rows `{task_id,task_ref:null|string,title:null|string,scope:"global"|"task",mode:"paused"|"stopped",reason,actor,source:"cli"|"api"|"ui"|"daemon_startup"|"daemon_shutdown"|"recovery",controlled_at,updated_at}`. `taskControls` is canonical-task-id-sorted unique rows with the same identity/ref/title/mode/reason/actor/source/timestamps plus nested `cleanup_state` containing no entry or exactly its matching task entry. `heldCount === heldTasks.length`. Canonical task mutation JSON requires canonical `data.task_id` and nullable `data.task_ref`; global mutation JSON forbids both; legacy aliases expose neither.

Success/noop exits 0. Human mutation success is exactly `Dispatch <action>: <authority> (<projection>)`; a task success appends ` for <canonical-task-id>`. JSON success/noop is exactly `{ok:true,data:<canonical control data>,error:null}`. `kspec agent status` and `kspec agent dispatch status` preserve their current detailed invocation/queue human and JSON projection and append authority/globalAuthority, projection, cleanupState, activeCount, queuedInvocations, heldCount, heldTasks, and taskControls using the internal-status casing; human output appends `Authority: <authority>`, `Projection: <projection>`, `Active: <active-count>`, `Queued: <queued-count>`, `Held: <held-count>`, and `Cleanup: <cleanupState.status>`. No status output removes an existing field. Gating filters matching scope: global commands/aliases inspect only global entries; task T commands only task/T entries; counts/arrays never gate. Stopped with only task entries permits global start, while those matching tasks remain denied. Direct global start/pause/resume with global pending/failed or matching task pause/resume with task pending/failed returns fixed invalid_transition; stop retries only matching scope. Task metadata mutation may succeed during global cleanup but starts no work until global authority permits it.

Human failures use exactly `Error: <message>` then `Suggestion: <suggestion>`; JSON failures use exactly `{ok:false,data:null,error:{code:<code>,message:<message>,suggestion:<suggestion>}}`. The closed mapping is:

| Code | Human/JSON message | Suggestion | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| validation_failed | Invalid dispatch lifecycle request. | Check the command options and try again. | 1 |
| task_not_found | Task not found. | Verify the task reference with `kspec task get`. | 3 |
| task_identity_ambiguous | Task reference is ambiguous. | Use a canonical task ULID. | 3 |
| task_identity_mismatch | Task identity does not match the resolved task. | Provide one matching task reference or task ID. | 3 |
| invalid_transition | Dispatch lifecycle transition is not valid from the current authority. | Check dispatch status and choose a valid action. | 3 |
| control_store_unavailable | Dispatch control storage is unavailable. | Retry after the daemon can access the control store. | 3 |
| control_store_corrupt | Dispatch control storage is corrupt. | Repair the dispatch control record before retrying. | 3 |
| control_commit_failed | Dispatch control change could not be committed. | Retry; if it persists, inspect shadow-branch health. | 3 |
| cancellation_timeout | Dispatch cancellation timed out. | Retry hard stop after active work settles. | 3 |
| cancellation_failed | Dispatch cancellation failed. | Retry hard stop and inspect daemon logs. | 3 |
| session_closure_failed | Dispatch session closure failed. | Retry hard stop after the session store is available. | 3 |
| cleanup_ownership_mismatch | Dispatch cleanup ownership could not be verified. | Do not retry blindly; inspect the matching session evidence. | 3 |
| cleanup_process_birth_mismatch | Dispatch process identity changed before cleanup. | Do not signal the process; inspect the matching session evidence. | 3 |
| cleanup_leader_missing_group_alive | Dispatch cleanup found a live verified process group. | Retry hard stop after the process group exits. | 3 |
| cleanup_identity_unverifiable | Dispatch cleanup identity cannot be verified. | Restore readable ownership evidence before retrying. | 3 |
| cleanup_group_unverifiable | Dispatch cleanup group cannot be verified. | Do not signal the group; restore verification evidence before retrying. | 3 |
| internal_error | Dispatch lifecycle command failed. | Retry; if it persists, inspect daemon logs. | 3 |

TTY hard stop without --force asks exactly `Hard-stop dispatch? Active matching invocations will be cancelled and session, branch, workspace, worktree, snapshot, and audit evidence will be preserved. [y/N]`. Decline prints `Hard stop cancelled.`, sends no request, and exits 2. --force sends no prompt. A non-interactive human invocation without --force prints `Error: Hard stop requires --force when stdin is not a TTY.` then `Suggestion: Re-run with --force.` and exits 1; JSON never prompts and has the same --force requirement. When KSPEC_SESSION_ID is nonempty, global or task stop fails before prompt/HTTP with `Error: A dispatch-owned session cannot hard-stop its host.` then `Suggestion: Run this command outside the dispatch-owned session.`, exit 3, even with --force. Start/pause/resume never prompt. Help calls stop `Hard-stop dispatch: cancel matching active invocations, close sessions, preserve evidence.` and pause `Pause dispatch: active invocations finish naturally.`

### Deliverable

Parser/routing, human/JSON output, confirmation, and exits for all global/task controls.

### Implementation

Implement the grammar, endpoint routing, exact output table, confirmation order, force/TTY/JSON behavior, and KSPEC_SESSION_ID preflight. Validation/usage exits 1; every runtime/daemon/store/cancellation/recovery/task lookup code uses the table and exits 3. Never interpolate a response path, cwd, raw exception, or daemon error string.

### Files

- Create: tests/cli-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts
- Modify: src/cli/commands/agent.ts
- Modify: src/cli/exit-codes.ts
- Modify: src/cli/output.ts
- Modify: tests/cli-agent-commands.test.ts
- Modify: tests/cli-agent.test.ts
- Modify: tests/cli-daemon-endpoint-regression.test.ts

### Behavioral tests

In tests/cli-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts create `runLifecycleCli`, `recordLifecycleRequest`, and `withTtyInput`; use tests/helpers/cli.ts `kspec` with an explicit cwd and sanitized environment. For every command grammar row assert canonical POST body or internal-status GET, then deep-equal every cleanupState/HeldTask/TaskControl field, ordering, count, conditional task identity, exit/stdout/stderr/JSON against the tables; malformed/duplicate/unsorted rows fail closed rather than render. Inject each closed code through the daemon fixture and assert exact message/suggestion/code/exit and no raw response text. Exercise pending/failed global and task prohibited actions with no second request, retry-stop failure, retry success to idle, then a separate successful reopen. Exercise accepted/declined TTY stop, non-TTY no-force, JSON no-force, --force, and KSPEC_SESSION_ID before-request rejection. In tests/cli-daemon-endpoint-regression.test.ts extend its existing helpers: every mutation must record POST `/api/agent/dispatch/control`; both status commands must record GET `/api/agent/dispatch/status`; assert no legacy mutation or public-status request was recorded.

### Verification

- npm test -- tests/cli-agent-dispatch-lifecycle.test.ts tests/cli-agent-commands.test.ts tests/cli-agent.test.ts tests/cli-daemon-endpoint-regression.test.ts
- npm run typecheck
- npm run lint
- git diff --check

### Reviewer handoff

Supply command/body/route, closed-code message/suggestion/exit, prompt transcript, KSPEC_SESSION_ID preflight, and endpoint-regression request tables.

### Covers

### Required context

Inventory: packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts; packages/web-ui/src/routes/agents/+page.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/agents/DispatchStatus.svelte, ActiveInvocationRow.svelte, QueuedInvocationRow.svelte, HeldTaskRow.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/lib/query/ws-invalidation.ts; packages/web-ui/src/routes/+page.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/routes/tasks/board/+page.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/board/ActiveFleetRow.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/routes/automation/+page.svelte; packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/automation/DispatchTriggersSection.svelte and EventLogSection.svelte. Authority is always separately labelled from projection and from degraded/blocked state. Absent authority maps dispatch_enabled true to running and false to stopped; false with active work keeps active evidence visible and labels the projection `Legacy unknown/stopping`. Static mode is stopped with zero counts, empty controls, and read-only buttons.

`packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts` exclusively parses/validates public snake_case and returns camelCase UI types; components consume camelCase only. Exact mapping: CleanupState status/entries stay status/entries; CleanupEntry `cleanup_id,scope,task_id,status,phase,error_code` -> `cleanupId,scope,taskId,status,phase,errorCode`; HeldTask `task_id,task_ref,title,scope,mode,reason,actor,source,controlled_at,updated_at` -> `taskId,taskRef,title,scope,mode,reason,actor,source,controlledAt,updatedAt`; TaskControl maps `task_id,task_ref,title,mode,reason,actor,source,controlled_at,updated_at,cleanup_state` -> `taskId,taskRef,title,mode,reason,actor,source,controlledAt,updatedAt,cleanupState`, recursively. Root `global_authority,cleanup_state,active_count,queue_depth,held_count,held_tasks,task_controls,degraded_targets` -> `globalAuthority,cleanupState,activeCount,queueDepth,heldCount,heldTasks,taskControls,degradedTargets`. Idle requires empty entries; pending requires non-empty/all pending and no errorCode; failed requires non-empty/at least one failed, errorCode on every failed entry and none on pending entries. CleanupErrorCode is exactly `cancellation_timeout|cancellation_failed|session_closure_failed|cleanup_ownership_mismatch|cleanup_process_birth_mismatch|cleanup_leader_missing_group_alive|cleanup_identity_unverifiable|cleanup_group_unverifiable|internal_error`; IDs/order/uniqueness/count invariants remain exact. Mixed snake/camel or malformed conditional combinations fail closed. Route fixtures use wire snake_case; API-helper assertions deep-equal camelCase converted models and round-trip-equivalent semantics. Task requests send wire `task_ref`; accepted wire task data returns `task_id/task_ref`, converted to UI `taskId/taskRef`; global responses contain neither.

Global actions are exactly:

| Authority / projection | Badge and evidence | Visible enabled actions | Hidden or disabled actions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stopped / stopped, cleanup idle | `Stopped`; zero/returned active, queued, and held evidence remains visible | Start | Pause, Resume, Hard stop hidden |
| running / running | `Running`; active, queued, and held evidence visible | Pause; Hard stop | Start and Resume hidden |
| paused / paused | `Paused`; held evidence visible | Resume; Hard stop | Start and Pause hidden |
| paused / draining | `Paused — draining`; active and held evidence visible until active reaches zero | Resume; Hard stop | Start and Pause hidden |
| stopped / global-scope cleanup pending or failed | `Stopped — cleanup pending` or `Stopped — cleanup failed`; aggregate active/held/cleanup evidence remains visible | Retry hard stop | Start, Pause, Resume hidden; Retry hard stop uses hard-stop confirmation |
| stopped / no global-scope entry but unrelated task cleanup exists | `Stopped`; aggregate task cleanup evidence remains visible | Start | Global Retry, Pause, Resume hidden; matching task remains denied |

Matching-scope controls are exact. Global actions inspect only global-scope entries: stopped with only unrelated task entries shows Start, not global Retry, and matching tasks remain held. Task T actions inspect only task/T entries and remain configurable while global authority is paused/stopped/has cleanup; mutation may change T metadata but never starts work until the independent global gate permits. Absent record shows Pause task and Hard-stop task; paused shows Resume task and Hard-stop task; stopped/no matching entry shows Resume task; stopped/matching pending-or-failed shows Retry hard stop and hides Resume task. Counts/aggregate arrays never determine action visibility. A stale-button 409 refreshes unchanged evidence. Successful retry renders the matching control idle without auto-resume. Hard-stop task uses confirmation; pause/resume never confirm. Static mode renders applicable controls disabled and makes no request.

Hard stop confirmation has role dialog, accessible name `Confirm hard stop`, text `Active matching invocations will be cancelled. Session, branch, workspace, worktree, snapshot, and audit evidence will be preserved.`, Confirm and Cancel buttons; Cancel makes no request. Status changes use a polite atomic live region; mutations keep focus on the invoking control after success/error refresh and errors show only the fixed mapped message/suggestion. Add stable test IDs `dispatch-authority`, `dispatch-projection`, `dispatch-active-count`, `dispatch-queued-count`, `dispatch-held-count`, `dispatch-action-start`, `dispatch-action-pause`, `dispatch-action-resume`, `dispatch-action-stop`, `dispatch-confirm-dialog`, `dispatch-confirm-cancel`, `dispatch-live-status`, and `held-task-<canonical-ulid>`.

### Deliverable

Every consumer consistently projects lifecycle evidence and valid controls; agents events invalidate queryKeys.agents.all and refresh the automation event log.

### Implementation

Update every listed consumer and implement the global/task tables verbatim. Separate authority/projection from degraded/blocked; show active/queued/held evidence in every specified view. Implement the named test IDs, dialog role/name, labels, polite live status, focus restoration, keyboard operation, narrow layout, reduced-motion-safe indicators, agents topic invalidation through queryKeys.agents.all, and automation event-log refresh. Only sanitized mapped failures may render.

Exact surface schemas differ only at named boundaries. Public API wire is snake_case. Internal/CLI has camelCase top-level lifecycle names but intentionally snake_case nested rows and does not share the UI converter. UI API helpers convert public wire to camelCase recursively: CleanupEntry `cleanup_id,task_id,error_code` -> `cleanupId,taskId,errorCode`; HeldTask `task_id,task_ref,controlled_at,updated_at` -> `taskId,taskRef,controlledAt,updatedAt`; TaskControl applies those mappings plus `cleanup_state` -> `cleanupState`; root `global_authority,cleanup_state,active_count,queue_depth,held_count,held_tasks,task_controls,degraded_targets` -> `globalAuthority,cleanupState,activeCount,queueDepth,heldCount,heldTasks,taskControls,degradedTargets`. CleanupState idle is empty; pending is non-empty/all entries status pending with no error code; failed is non-empty/at least one entry status failed, every failed entry has an error code, and pending entries have none. Entries are exact `{cleanup_id,scope,task_id?,status,phase,error_code?}` on wire/CLI and corresponding camelCase in UI; canonical identity, closed codes, order, uniqueness, nested matching-task, and held-count invariants apply. Matching-scope actions filter global only or task/T only; unrelated scopes never alter a mutation, but global authority independently gates starts. Task requests may carry slug/ref, canonical task identity appears only for task scope.

### Deliverable

Exact cross-surface fixtures, not field-only smoke tests.

### Implementation

Repeat only these cross-surface subsets: canonical global start/pause/resume/stop and task pause/resume/stop; slug input returning canonical task ID; full idle, all-pending, all-failed, and mixed failed-plus-pending cleanup rows; exact public snake/internal-CLI hybrid/UI camel conversion and semantic round trip; malformed aggregate/entry/error conditional, mixed-case, order, duplicate, count rejection; stopped global plus unrelated task cleanup permits start but denies that task; global cleanup does not prevent task metadata mutation but prevents work start; all seventeen failures; matching-scope invalid transitions and retries; alias rows proving global aliases inspect global scope only; endpoint/prompt/session branches; matching events. tasks.title: Serve packaged Pagefind assets from the Node daemon for real local docs search
tasks.description:
## Covers

- `@docs-search ac-1`: real locally served searches return navigable matching docs pages.
- `@docs-search ac-2`: local search loads its packaged index from the same-origin Node daemon, without a non-local request.
- `@docs-search ac-3`: local and public indexes built from the same docs content return the same canonical result set.

## Defect

The Node static routes in `packages/daemon/src/web-ui-static.ts` serve `/_app/*` and root-level assets, but not nested `/pagefind/*` assets. Pagefind entry and lazy index/chunk requests therefore fall through. `tests/e2e/docs.spec.ts` masks this production defect: `serveStaticPagefind()` intercepts `**/pagefind/**` and fulfills requests from `dist/web-ui/pagefind`, so the test does not prove that the real local daemon serves offline search assets. The separate synthetic public/local parity fixture does not replace that daemon-backed proof.

## Implementation

1. Add a narrow Node-daemon route for generated files under `/pagefind/*`. Reuse the existing static response behavior and preserve the existing bundle-root path-containment boundary. The route must remain limited to the Pagefind subtree; do not introduce broad arbitrary nested-file serving.
2. Preserve the existing missing-file behavior and cache policy. Serve a normal Pagefind entry asset with its correct content type, and preserve exact bytes plus an appropriate binary content type for a representative nested Pagefind index/chunk asset. Reject a direct traversal/path-containment attempt without exposing a file outside the permitted subtree. This is a focused regression boundary, not a general static-server security audit.
3. In `tests/e2e/docs.spec.ts`, remove `PAGEFIND_BUILD`, `serveStaticPagefind()`, imports/constants used only by it, and local `page.route('**/pagefind/**')` fulfillment. The local proof must use the existing default Node-daemon fixture and packaged `dist/web-ui/pagefind` output.
4. Run real searches for all six `DISPATCH_DOCS` at the existing wide and narrow viewports, verify each result is navigable and renders the expected heading, and make the network proof non-vacuous: collect observed Pagefind requests, Pagefind transport failures, non-2xx Pagefind responses, and requests to non-local origins; require at least one observed Pagefind request, require every observed Pagefind request to use the daemon origin, and require all failure/non-local collections to be empty. Keep console-error and uncaught page-error collections empty as well.
5. Retain an honest `ac-3` canonical result-set parity check using local/public indexes generated from identical docs content. A synthetic parity fixture may remain for that comparison, but it must not be presented as the `ac-1`/`ac-2` real-daemon proof. Preserve deterministic generation/copying of the Pagefind bundle; change build scripts only if a real packaging defect is found and cover that change directly.

## Focused regression proof

Use TDD: first capture a RED focused route test and interception-free E2E failure, then make them GREEN.

The Node route coverage should use only representative cases:

- a normal entry asset such as `/pagefind/pagefind.js`, including relevant content type and cache behavior;
- one nested binary index/chunk asset, including byte-for-byte fidelity, appropriate content type, and cache behavior;
- one missing Pagefind asset returning the existing not-found response;
- at least one direct traversal/path-containment rejection proving the route cannot read outside its permitted subtree.

Do not require a fixture for every emitted Pagefind extension or every conceivable encoded separator, malformed URL, directory, or traversal spelling. Keep machine-readable `// AC: @docs-search ac-N` annotations on tests that prove the corresponding behavior.

## Likely files

- Modify `packages/daemon/src/web-ui-static.ts`.
- Modify `tests/daemon-web-ui-startup-asset-coherence.test.ts`, or create a narrowly named adjacent Node static-route test if that is clearer.
- Modify `tests/e2e/docs.spec.ts`.
- Inspect as needed, but normally leave unchanged: `packages/daemon/src/server.ts`, `tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts`, `scripts/build-docs-search.cjs`, `packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/DocsSearch.svelte`, `tests/web-ui-docs-search.test.ts`, and root `package.json`.
- Treat `packages/web-ui/build/pagefind/**` and `dist/web-ui/pagefind/**` as generated verification output; do not hand-edit them.

## Verification

Run the task-specific proof from the repository root:

```bash
npm test -- tests/daemon-web-ui-startup-asset-coherence.test.ts
npm run build:docs-search
npm run build:web-ui
npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/docs.spec.ts
git diff --check
```

If route tests move to a new focused file, run that exact file instead. Also run the project-defined work gates from the attached instructions.

## Out of scope

- Broad nested static serving, catch-all filesystem serving, or unrelated Bun/static-route redesign.
- Public search ranking, matching, content, canonical URL, or index-scope changes.
- Using request interception, `route.fulfill`, an API mock, a synthetic-only index, or an alternate static server as evidence for the local Node-daemon path.
- Unrelated docs, lifecycle, dispatch, daemon, or web UI cleanup; hand edits to generated outputs.

Validation must be schema-derived — the source of truth for what
constitutes valid input is the canonical schema definition, not a
separate hardcoded check. Error messages must be actionable,

items.title: Idempotent File Scaffolding Trait
items.description:
A scaffolding step that creates a file or writes to a managed block inside a file on disk follows a uniform set of rules so users can predict its behavior without reading its implementation: the target file is never modified unless the force flag is set; when force is set, the existing file is backed up to a sibling path before being replaced and the backup path is reported in the step's output; the step is safe to re-run and produces the same visible result on the second run as the first when no inputs changed; the step always reports its action (created, skipped, force-recreated) in a stable format consumable by the setup summary; and the step never destroys user content outside the file it owns.

Scope: this trait applies only to scaffolding that writes files on disk. Scaffolds that create meta-spec items (agents, conventions, hooks, modules) have different force semantics — they use first-run-only creation with "reseed missing items only" on force — and must not inherit this trait.

acceptance_criteria.given: A file scaffold step's target file already exists
acceptance_criteria.when: The step runs without the force flag
acceptance_criteria.then: The existing file is preserved byte-for-byte and the step reports "skipped"

acceptance_criteria.given: A file scaffold step's target file already exists and the step is invoked with the force flag
acceptance_criteria.then: The previous content is preserved as a sibling backup with a timestamped name, the backup path is reported before the overwrite, and only then is the file replaced with a freshly scaffolded template

acceptance_criteria.given: A file scaffold step's target file does not exist
acceptance_criteria.when: The step runs with or without the force flag
acceptance_criteria.then: The file is created and the step reports "created"

acceptance_criteria.given: Any file scaffold step completes
acceptance_criteria.then: The step's action (created, skipped, force-recreated) and any backup path are included in the summary in a stable format

without any server-side help.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader is on any app route in the web UI
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader looks at the primary navigation
acceptance_criteria.then:
A "Docs" entry is present and navigates to the docs
landing page

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reader is running the web UI against a local kspec
daemon, disconnected from the internet
acceptance_criteria.when:
The reader navigates to the docs surface and reads a
page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page renders fully without any network request to
a non-local host

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader visits the publicly deployed docs
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader navigates between docs pages
acceptance_criteria.then:
Pages render without requiring a running kspec daemon
and without server-side rendering

items.title: Docs Navigation and Page Shape
items.description:
Within the docs surface, a sidebar shows the current
section's pages with the current page indicated, a table
of contents for the current page shows its headings, and
every heading carries an anchor that can be copied as a
stable direct link.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader is on a docs page
acceptance_criteria.then:
A sidebar lists the pages of the current section, the
current page is visually indicated, and a table of
contents for the current page's headings is present

acceptance_criteria.given: A docs page has headings
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader hovers or clicks a heading
acceptance_criteria.then:
The heading has a stable anchor that can be copied as a
direct link to that section of the page

items.title: Getting Started Section
items.description:
The Getting Started section walks a new reader from a
machine with nothing installed to a working kspec project
they have directed their agent through. It contains, at
minimum, pages covering these stages, in this order:

- Overview — what kspec is and who it is for
- Installation — install via npm, supported Node versions,
  verifying the install
- Initializing a Project — running init and setup, what
  gets created, what the reader should not edit by hand
- Connecting Your Agent — agent setup for at least one
  supported agent family, and how to confirm the
  connection works
- Your First Action — directing the agent through a first
  meaningful authoring step
- Where to Go Next — pointers into Guides and Concepts

The section may grow additional pages as kspec evolves
without breaking this contract, provided the stages above
are covered. Pages are linear: each ends with a "next"
link to the following page.

acceptance_criteria.given: The Getting Started section is published
acceptance_criteria.when:
A maintainer follows the section's pages in order in a
clean environment
acceptance_criteria.then:
The pages cover install, project initialization, agent
integration, and at least one authoring action, with
the commands or procedure for each step shown on its
page in a form that can be executed without consulting
material outside Getting Started

acceptance_criteria.given: A Getting Started page other than the last is published
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page ends with a "next" link pointing to the
subsequent page in the section's reading order

acceptance_criteria.given: The Initializing a Project page is published
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page names the shadow branch, identifies the
project's shadow directory, names the health-check and
repair commands, and instructs the reader not to edit
shadow state by hand

items.title: Concepts Section
items.description:
The Concepts section gives the reader durable mental
models for kspec. It contains, at minimum, pages covering
these concepts:

- What kspec Is — the system's purpose and shape
- Working With kspec Through an Agent — the mental model
  for directing an AI agent: how to frame requests, what
  the agent decides on its own, what it asks about, and
  how to read the shape of what it has done
- Specs, Tasks, Plans, and Inbox — the decision matrix for
  what goes where
- The Shadow Branch — what it is, why spec state is kept
  there, how it shows up in day-to-day use
- Traits — what they are and how they compose acceptance
  criteria across specs
- Reviews — the per-cycle review record model and how it
  gates work
- Agents and Dispatch — how agents execute work and how
  dispatch assigns it
- The Web UI and the Daemon — what each surface is for and
  when to use them

Each page follows the same shape: what it is, why it
exists, how it surfaces in use, and — where helpful —
what alternatives were considered. The section may grow
additional concept pages as kspec evolves without breaking
this contract, provided the concepts above remain covered.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader opens the Concepts section
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader consults the section landing page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The concept pages listed in the description are
present and linked from the landing page

acceptance_criteria.given: A Concepts page is published
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page answers what the concept is, why it exists,
and how the reader will encounter it in use, without
enumerating command flags or schema fields that change
per release

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reader wants to decide whether a unit of work is a
spec, task, plan, or inbox item
acceptance_criteria.when:
The reader consults the Specs, Tasks, Plans, and Inbox
page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page provides a decision rule for each of the four
kinds that the reader can apply without reading
further material

items.title: Guides Section
items.description:
The Guides section covers common end-user workflows as
sequential procedures framed around the reader's goal. It
contains, at minimum, guides covering these workflows:

- Starting a New Project
- Directing Your Agent Effectively
- Importing and Approving a Plan
- Authoring and Completing a Task
- Reviewing an Agent's Work
- Upgrading kspec to a New Version
- Recovering From Shadow Branch Issues

Each guide begins with the reader's goal, lists the
prerequisites (including "completed Getting Started" where
applicable), provides the sequence of steps, and ends
with a verification the reader can perform to know the
goal is accomplished. The section may grow additional
guides as kspec evolves without breaking this contract,
provided the workflows above remain covered.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader opens the Guides section
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader consults the section landing page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The guides listed in the description are present and
linked from the landing page

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader opens any guide
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader reads the guide in order
acceptance_criteria.then:
The guide states the reader's goal, names its
prerequisites, presents the steps in sequence, and
ends with a verification the reader can perform to
confirm the goal was met

acceptance_criteria.given: A guide names a kspec command
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader wants the full flag list for that command
acceptance_criteria.then:
The guide points the reader to the command's help
output rather than transcribing the flags inline

items.title: Troubleshooting Section
items.description:
The Troubleshooting section is an index of recovery
procedures keyed by the symptom the reader observes — in
their own output or in their agent's output. Entries grow
as new failure modes emerge in the system; the section's
initial coverage includes at minimum these symptoms:

- Shadow branch is out of sync with remote
- Shadow branch worktree is broken or missing
- Daemon cannot bind to its port because the port is in use
- "Cannot run kspec from inside the shadow directory" error
- Upgrade reports a pre-plan state or partial scaffold
- Agent dispatch refuses to assign a task
- A review is blocking merge with an unresolved thread

Each entry follows the shape: symptom → what this means →
recovery procedure → commands to run by name → what a
healthy outcome looks like. Entries link to the
corresponding concept page where the underlying system is
explained rather than re-explaining the primitive inline.

acceptance_criteria.given: A Troubleshooting entry is published
acceptance_criteria.when: A reviewer reads the entry's title and opening
acceptance_criteria.then:
The entry is titled and opened in terms of the symptom
the reader observes in their own output or their
agent's output, not in terms of the internal cause
name, so the entry is findable by readers who cannot
yet name what is wrong

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader reads a troubleshooting entry
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader follows the recovery procedure
acceptance_criteria.then:
The entry describes the symptom, explains what the
symptom means, states the recovery procedure in prose,
names the commands to run, and describes what a
healthy outcome looks like so the reader knows when
recovery has succeeded

acceptance_criteria.given:
A troubleshooting entry mentions a kspec primitive the
reader may not know
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader wants to understand the primitive
acceptance_criteria.then:
The entry links to the corresponding page in the
Concepts section rather than re-explaining the
primitive inline

items.title: Release Notes Available in Docs Without Duplication
items.description:
The docs surface presents release notes as a single page so
a reader can see what changed in the currently installed
version and any prior released version without leaving the
docs. The notes shown are always the same as the single
source of truth already consumed by the CLI's release-notes
command, so authoring release notes remains one action and
the docs cannot drift from what the CLI shows.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader is on the docs surface
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader navigates to the release notes page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page presents release notes for the current version
and an index of prior versions, with each version
anchored so direct links to a version work

acceptance_criteria.given: The docs surface is built
acceptance_criteria.when:
A reviewer compares the rendered release-notes page
against the canonical release notes source file used
by the same build
acceptance_criteria.then:
The rendered content is equivalent to the source file
and no second copy of release notes content exists
elsewhere in the repository

items.title: README Is a Concise Landing Page
items.description:
The README is a concise landing page targeting a reader
deciding whether to adopt kspec. It contains an overview
paragraph, an install section, a first-steps pointer
consisting of one or two commands plus a link to the docs
surface, and a small set of cross-links into the docs
sections. It does not embed guides, concept explanations,
or reference content — those live in the docs surface and
the README links to them.

acceptance_criteria.given: The README is published
acceptance_criteria.when: A reviewer reads the file end to end
acceptance_criteria.then:
The file contains at minimum sections covering
overview, installation, first steps, and cross-links
into the docs, and does not embed guides, concept
explanations, or reference content

acceptance_criteria.given: The README is published
acceptance_criteria.when: A reviewer looks for next-step links
acceptance_criteria.then:
Links are present into the docs sections sufficient to
reach Getting Started, Concepts, and Guides in one
click from the README

items.title: Folder-Backed Resource Documentation
items.description:
User-facing documentation and CLI help describe the folder-backed plan and
review layouts, exact resource commands, exact resource API routes,
resource reference syntax, derivation copy/reference behavior, upgrade
behavior, and troubleshooting guidance. Documentation follows the
implementation contracts from the storage/resource specs; it does not
create separate storage behavior.

acceptance_criteria.given: The folder-backed resource feature is documented
acceptance_criteria.when: A user reads the documentation or command help
acceptance_criteria.then: The docs name the exact plan/review resource commands, resource API routes, `resources.yaml` fields, and `kspec plan derive --materialize-resources` behavior

acceptance_criteria.given: The folder-backed storage format is released
acceptance_criteria.when: A user reads upgrade or troubleshooting documentation
acceptance_criteria.then: The docs explain the `kynetic: "1.2"` manifest fields, `kspec upgrade` migration path, previous-shadow-commit rollback guidance, and `entity_storage_incompatible` recovery options

items.title: Resource Documentation Covers UI and Task Markdown Behavior
items.description: User-facing documentation describes live UI routing, task markdown resolution, drift, and static export behavior for local resources.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user reads the local resources concept page, guide, or release notes
acceptance_criteria.when: the documentation describes task resource references
acceptance_criteria.then: it states how task descriptions may reference resources with `./resources/<relative-path>` and how plan-owned and task-owned copies are resolved

acceptance_criteria.given: a user reads the local resources concept page, guide, or troubleshooting material
acceptance_criteria.when: the documentation describes task resource references
acceptance_criteria.then: it states that drifted, missing, or unresolved task resources are surfaced as status messages instead of silently serving replacement bytes

acceptance_criteria.given: a user reads the local resources guide or troubleshooting material
acceptance_criteria.when: the documentation describes live web UI resource rendering in multi-project mode
acceptance_criteria.then: it states that browser image and link resource URLs need URL-level selected-project context because element fetches cannot send `X-Kspec-Dir`

acceptance_criteria.given: a developer needs to verify resource behavior end to end
acceptance_criteria.when: they read the resource guide or troubleshooting material
acceptance_criteria.then: they can follow exact temp-project steps that validate CLI storage, daemon bytes routes, live UI image/link rendering, selected-project browser URL routing, and static export asset existence without restarting or stopping the daemon

items.title: Docs Top-Level Sections
items.description:
The docs surface presents five top-level sections, no more
and no fewer: Getting Started, Guides, Concepts,
Troubleshooting, and Release Notes. Each section has a
landing page and a set of child pages. Exhaustive
enumerations of every command flag or schema field are
explicitly absent and are left for a follow-up plan to
produce from canonical sources.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reader opens the docs surface
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader consults the primary docs navigation
acceptance_criteria.then:
The five top-level sections shown are Getting Started,
Guides, Concepts, Troubleshooting, and Release Notes,
in that order

acceptance_criteria.given: A section has at least one page
acceptance_criteria.when: The reader opens the section's landing page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The landing page summarises the section's purpose in
one paragraph and links to each child page in reading
order

items.title: Spec Item
items.description:
A spec item is the fundamental unit in Kynetic Spec.
Everything - features, requirements, constraints, decisions,
tasks - is represented as an item with consistent structure.

acceptance_criteria.given: any piece of spec content
acceptance_criteria.when: it is stored in the spec
acceptance_criteria.then: it exists as an item with id, title, type, and content

acceptance_criteria.given: an item
acceptance_criteria.then: it has a ULID assigned automatically

items.title: Required Item Fields
items.description:
Every item MUST have:
- _ulid: Canonical unique identifier (auto-generated)
- title: Human-readable name (required, user-provided)

All other fields are optional with sensible defaults.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user creates a new spec item with only a title
acceptance_criteria.then: the item has a generated ULID and preserves the provided title as required fields

items.title: Optional Item Fields
items.description:
Items MAY include:
- slugs: Human-friendly aliases (array)
- type: Item type (feature, requirement, etc.)
- status: Maturity and implementation status
- priority: high | medium | low
- tags: Freeform labels (array)
- description: Detailed content (multiline)
- acceptance_criteria: Testable conditions (array)
- depends_on, implements, relates_to: References (arrays)
- traceability: Links to code, tests, commits
- created, created_by: Lifecycle metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec item is created without optional metadata such as slugs, tags, description, or relationships
acceptance_criteria.when: the item is retrieved or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: the item remains valid and the omitted fields do not prevent storage

items.title: Derive Hint After Item Creation
items.description: After creating or modifying a spec item, CLI shows a hint suggesting task derivation: 'Derive implementation task? kspec derive @new-item'

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs 'kspec item add' and creates a new spec item
acceptance_criteria.then: CLI shows hint: 'Derive implementation task? kspec derive @new-slug'

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs 'kspec item set @existing-item --description new'
acceptance_criteria.then: CLI shows hint: 'Derive implementation task? kspec derive @slug'

items.title: Acceptance Criterion Identifier Format
items.description:
Acceptance criterion identifiers use a uniform ac-prefixed kebab-case
token format everywhere they are stored, edited, validated, and
referenced by coverage annotations.

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item or trait has acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria.when: the item is stored in the project catalog
acceptance_criteria.then:
Each acceptance criterion identifier conforms to the ac-prefixed
kebab-case token format

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project catalog contains an acceptance criterion identifier that
does not conform to the required token format
acceptance_criteria.then:
Validation reports the offending acceptance criterion identifier
as invalid

acceptance_criteria.given:
A user supplies a new acceptance criterion identifier that does not
conform to the required token format
acceptance_criteria.when: the user asks kspec to add the acceptance criterion to an item
acceptance_criteria.then: The command rejects the identifier before mutating the item

acceptance_criteria.given:
A user supplies a replacement acceptance criterion identifier that
does not conform to the required token format
acceptance_criteria.when: the user asks kspec to rename an existing acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then: The command rejects the identifier before mutating the item

acceptance_criteria.given:
A user asks kspec to add an acceptance criterion without supplying
an identifier
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec generates the acceptance criterion identifier
acceptance_criteria.then: The generated identifier conforms to the required token format

acceptance_criteria.given: A user supplies patch data that would store an acceptance criterion identifier that does not conform to the required token format
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec validates the patch for a single item patch or bulk item patch
acceptance_criteria.then: The update is rejected before the catalog item is mutated

items.title: ULID Identifier System
items.description:
ULIDs (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifiers)
serve as the canonical, immutable identifier for every item.
They are time-sortable, globally unique, and can be shortened
for display like git commit hashes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: a ULID is auto-generated

acceptance_criteria.given: a ULID "01KEZCJPHZ86X9PA509GREWDM0"
acceptance_criteria.when: it needs to be displayed briefly
acceptance_criteria.then: it can be shortened to "01JHNK" (first 6+ chars)

acceptance_criteria.given: an item's ULID
acceptance_criteria.then: the ULID never changes

items.title: ULID Format
items.description:
ULIDs are 26-character strings in Crockford base32 encoding.
Format: TTTTTTTTTTNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
- First 10 chars: Timestamp (millisecond precision)
- Last 16 chars: Random component

Example: 01KEZCJPHZ86X9PA509GREWDM0

acceptance_criteria.given: the system generates a ULID for a new item
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a 26-character Crockford base32 string with a 10-character time component followed by a 16-character random component

items.title: ULID Immutability
items.description:
Once assigned, a ULID is NEVER changed and NEVER reused.
If an item is deprecated, its ULID remains; a superseding
item gets a new ULID and links via supersedes relationship.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing item is updated, deprecated, or superseded
acceptance_criteria.then: the original ULID remains unchanged and any replacement item receives a different ULID

items.title: ULID Shortening
items.description:
ULIDs can be shortened for display and references, similar
to git commit short hashes. The system resolves short ULIDs
to full ULIDs, erroring if ambiguous.

Minimum recommended: 6 characters
Full length: 26 characters

acceptance_criteria.given: an item has a full ULID
acceptance_criteria.when: a unique shortened ULID prefix is used for display or as an @reference
acceptance_criteria.then: the system resolves that prefix back to the same full ULID

items.title: Slug Alias System
items.description:
Slugs are human-friendly aliases that point to ULIDs.
They make specs readable and references memorable.
Multiple slugs can point to the same item, and slugs
can evolve without breaking references (the ULID is canonical).

acceptance_criteria.given: an item with ULID "01JHNK8QW0..."
acceptance_criteria.then: "@core-primitives" resolves to that item

acceptance_criteria.given: an item with slugs ["auth-login", "user-login"]
acceptance_criteria.when: either slug is used as a reference
acceptance_criteria.then: both resolve to the same item

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug "old-name" assigned to an item
acceptance_criteria.then: references to "@old-name" produce a warning but still resolve

items.title: Slug Format
items.description:
Slugs MUST be lowercase, alphanumeric, with hyphens allowed.
Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$

Examples: auth-login, user-model, impl-session-v2

acceptance_criteria.given: a user provides a slug containing uppercase letters, spaces, or underscores
acceptance_criteria.when: the slug is validated during item creation or update
acceptance_criteria.then: the command rejects the slug because it does not match the lowercase hyphenated slug pattern

items.title: Slug Uniqueness
items.description:
Each slug MUST be unique within the spec. Two items cannot have the same slug.

Enforcement:
- Validation: kspec validate reports duplicate slug errors
- Prevention: CLI commands reject duplicate slugs at creation/update time

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug 'auth-login' exists in the spec
acceptance_criteria.then: duplicate slug error is reported if another item also has 'auth-login'

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug 'auth-login' exists in the spec
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec item add --slug auth-login is run
acceptance_criteria.then: command fails with 'slug already exists' error

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug 'auth-login' exists in the spec
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec item set @other --slug auth-login is run
acceptance_criteria.then: command fails with 'slug already exists' error

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug 'auth-login' exists in the spec
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec task add --slug auth-login is run
acceptance_criteria.then: command fails with 'slug already exists' error

acceptance_criteria.given: a slug 'auth-login' exists in the spec
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec task set @other --slug auth-login is run
acceptance_criteria.then: command fails with 'slug already exists' error

items.title: Slug Resolution
items.description:
When a reference like "@auth-login" is encountered:
1. Check if it matches a slug exactly
2. If not found, check if it's a ULID prefix
3. If still not found, report broken reference error
4. If ambiguous (multiple matches), report ambiguity error

acceptance_criteria.given: a new item is created with slug 'my-feature'
acceptance_criteria.then: reference resolves to the newly created item without requiring reload

acceptance_criteria.given: an item exists with slug 'auth-login'
acceptance_criteria.then: reference resolves to that item

acceptance_criteria.given: no item exists with slug 'nonexistent'
acceptance_criteria.then: broken reference error is reported

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple items share ULID prefix '01KEZ'
acceptance_criteria.then: ambiguity error is reported listing matching items

items.title: Reference System
items.description:
The @reference syntax links items together. References can
point to slugs or ULIDs (full or shortened). The system
validates that all references resolve to existing items.

acceptance_criteria.given: an item with depends_on ["@auth-session"]
acceptance_criteria.then: the reference is checked against the slug index

acceptance_criteria.given: a reference "@01JHNK"
acceptance_criteria.then: it resolves to the full ULID

acceptance_criteria.given: a reference to a non-existent item
acceptance_criteria.then: an error is reported with the broken reference

items.title: Reference Syntax
items.description:
References use the @ prefix to distinguish from plain strings:

- "@slug-name" - Reference by slug
- "@01JHNK" - Reference by short ULID
- "@01KEZCJPHZ86X9PA509GREWDM0" - Reference by full ULID

References appear in relationship fields:
depends_on, implements, relates_to, tests, supersedes, blocked_by

acceptance_criteria.given: a relationship field contains @slug, @short-ulid, or @full-ulid values
acceptance_criteria.when: the item is parsed or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: those values are recognized as references rather than plain text and are available for resolution

items.title: Reference Validation
items.description:
All references MUST be validated:
1. Parse @ prefix to extract identifier
2. Attempt slug lookup, then ULID prefix lookup
3. Report errors for unresolved references
4. Report warnings for deprecated targets

Validation is triggered by `kspec validate --refs`

acceptance_criteria.given: an item contains one valid reference and one unresolved @reference
acceptance_criteria.then: the valid reference resolves successfully and the unresolved reference is reported as an error

items.title: Relationship Types

acceptance_criteria.given: an item links to other items using depends_on, implements, relates_to, tests, or supersedes
acceptance_criteria.then: each link retains its relationship type so tools can distinguish prerequisite, realization, association, verification, and replacement semantics

items.title: depends_on Relationship
items.description:
"A depends_on B" means A requires B to be completed/available.
Used for: ordering work, tracking prerequisites.

For tasks: Auto-blocks A until B is completed.

acceptance_criteria.given: User provides a depends_on reference without @ prefix (e.g., --depends-on 01KH7XA9)
acceptance_criteria.then: the CLI auto-prefixes @ to normalize the reference (stores @01KH7XA9); applies to task set, task add, and derive commands

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has depends_on referencing incomplete tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: the task is excluded from tasks list and tasks ready by default, but is still accessible via task get @ref

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has depends_on with a valid @-prefixed reference
acceptance_criteria.then: the dependent task is automatically unblocked and appears in tasks list and tasks ready

items.title: implements Relationship
items.description:
"A implements B" means A is a realization of B.
Used for: requirement-to-task, feature-to-module.

Enables traceability from high-level to concrete.

acceptance_criteria.given: item A implements item B
acceptance_criteria.then: A is linked to B showing concrete realization (e.g., requirement implements feature, task implements requirement)

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple items implement the same item
acceptance_criteria.then: all implementers are shown enabling traceability from high-level to concrete

items.title: relates_to Relationship
items.description:
"A relates_to B" is a general association without specific semantics.
Used for: cross-references, "see also" links.

acceptance_criteria.given: item A relates_to item B
acceptance_criteria.then: B is shown as a related reference (general association without specific semantics like 'see also')

acceptance_criteria.given: item A relates_to item B
acceptance_criteria.then: relates_to is accepted as valid cross-reference without enforcing specific constraints (unlike depends_on or blocks)

items.title: blocks Relationship
items.description:
"A blocks B" means B cannot proceed while A is unresolved.
The inverse of depends_on, used for explicit blocking issues.

acceptance_criteria.given: item A blocks item B
acceptance_criteria.then: task B cannot transition to in_progress while A is unresolved (blocking relationship enforced)

acceptance_criteria.given: item A blocks item B
acceptance_criteria.when: item A is resolved or completed
acceptance_criteria.then: item B becomes unblocked (blocks relationship is inverse of depends_on)

items.title: tests Relationship
items.description:
"A tests B" means A validates or verifies B.
Used for: linking test items to features/requirements.

acceptance_criteria.given: item A declares a tests relationship to item B
acceptance_criteria.then: item A is shown as evidence that validates item B

items.title: supersedes Relationship
items.description:
"A supersedes B" means A replaces B, which is now deprecated.
The old item's ULID remains stable; the relationship links them.

acceptance_criteria.given: item A supersedes item B
acceptance_criteria.then: item B remains identifiable by its original ULID and the relationship points to item A as its replacement

items.title: Project Config File
items.description:
A kspec.config.yaml file in the project root (main branch) that provides
project-level configuration for shadow branch setup, identity, validation,
and daemon settings. Loaded before shadow branch detection. All fields
optional with backward-compatible defaults.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with no kspec.config.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: all settings resolve to current defaults with no behavior change

acceptance_criteria.given: a kspec.config.yaml exists in the project root
acceptance_criteria.then: config is parsed, validated, and available on KspecContext.config before shadow detection

acceptance_criteria.given: a kspec.config.yaml with invalid YAML syntax

items.title: Configurable Author Identity
items.description: Project-level default author via kspec.config.yaml identity.author. Establishes the author precedence chain - env var (KSPEC_AUTHOR, highest), then config identity.author, then git user.name, then OS user (lowest) - used to resolve an actor when a write supplies no explicit value. The chain only produces a CANDIDATE actor. Per @actor-identity-model, every new actor-bearing write passes that candidate (and any explicit caller value) through write-time classification before persistence: values recognized as the configured human identity or a canonical agent are stored in canonical form, while a resolved value that classifies to no configured human or agent identity is rejected on new writes rather than persisted as a free-form author. The configured human identity is itself derived from this chain, so a chain-resolved write is normally attributed to that canonical human; classification reconciles recognizable variants. This reconciles the earlier wording, which appeared to let arbitrary git/OS-derived names persist verbatim, with @actor-identity-model's write-time validation boundary.

acceptance_criteria.when: a note or inbox item is created without KSPEC_AUTHOR env var set
acceptance_criteria.then: the author is recorded as the configured value

acceptance_criteria.then: the env var value wins

acceptance_criteria.given: no config author and no KSPEC_AUTHOR env var
acceptance_criteria.then: the author candidate falls back to git user.name then OS user, and that candidate is passed through write-time classification before persistence; it is stored as the canonical configured human identity (the chain value defines that human), and only a value classifying to no configured human or agent identity is rejected on a new write

acceptance_criteria.when: Any session write operation occurs (create, append, close, compact)
acceptance_criteria.then: Writes always go to .kspec-sessions/, never to .kspec/sessions/.

acceptance_criteria.given: Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/ but have not been migrated
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns only sessions from .kspec-sessions/. A warning is shown indicating N legacy sessions exist and advising to run kspec session migrate.

acceptance_criteria.given: A session is read from the legacy .kspec/sessions/ location
acceptance_criteria.then:
A deprecation warning is emitted (stderr, not stdout) noting
the legacy location. Warning includes guidance to run kspec session migrate.

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec setup or kspec init runs
acceptance_criteria.then:
sessions/ is added to .kspec/.gitignore so no new session files
are tracked on kspec-meta. Existing history is preserved in git.

acceptance_criteria.given: Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/
acceptance_criteria.then:
Copies session directories from .kspec/sessions/ to .kspec-sessions/.
Does not delete originals.

acceptance_criteria.given: Some sessions already exist in .kspec-sessions/
acceptance_criteria.then:
Skips sessions that already exist in target.
Reports count of migrated and skipped sessions.

items.title: Session CLI Unified Filtering
items.description:
Align CLI session log commands with the daemon API filtering
capabilities. Currently the CLI has --status, --agent, --since
but lacks --agent-id, --trigger, --task, and combined filters.
Unify the filter vocabulary so CLI and UI use the same fields.

acceptance_criteria.given: Sessions exist with different agent_id values
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec session log list --agent-id worker is run
acceptance_criteria.then: Only sessions with agent_id "worker" are listed

acceptance_criteria.given: Sessions exist with various triggers
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec session log list --trigger manual is run
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only sessions with matching trigger are listed.
--trigger dispatched matches all task.* triggers.

acceptance_criteria.given: Sessions exist with task_id references
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec session log list --task @task-slug is run
acceptance_criteria.then: Only sessions linked to that task are listed

acceptance_criteria.given: The existing --agent flag is used
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec session log list --agent claude-agent-acp is run
acceptance_criteria.then:
--agent continues to filter by agent_type as before.
Both --agent and --agent-type are accepted as synonyms.

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple filters are specified
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec session log list --status completed --agent-id worker --since 7d is run
acceptance_criteria.then: All filters are AND'd together

acceptance_criteria.given: Any filter combination is applied
acceptance_criteria.then:
Output includes the filter criteria and filtered results in
structured JSON matching the daemon API response shape

inherited_acs.then: only items with matching status shown
only items with matching tag shown
output shows at most N items
output skips first N items
output shows items matching all filters (AND logic)
empty list shown with informative message
summary shows total matching items and filter state
outputs only the total number of matching items as a plain integer (no item details); ignores --limit and --offset; in JSON mode outputs {"count": N}
output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
output includes all data available in human-readable mode
error is returned as JSON object with error field
references use @ prefix consistently
timestamps use ISO 8601 format
--json takes precedence over other format options

items.title: Review Record Core Model
items.description:
kspec stores review records as first-party artifacts with a typed subject,
separate lifecycle and disposition states, authorship, timestamps, an
append-only event log, and links to the object under review.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A review is created for a plan, task, committed code change, or other
supported artifact
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record captures subject binding, lifecycle state, author,
timestamps, and an empty event log in first-party kspec metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: A review progresses through work
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review record has separate lifecycle_state (draft, open, closed,
archived) and computed disposition (pending, approved,
changes_requested) fields rather than collapsing lifecycle and outcome
into one status enum

acceptance_criteria.given: A review references external systems such as GitHub
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review record stores those links without making them the source of
truth for local review state

acceptance_criteria.given:
Any mutation occurs on a review record including status changes,
verdict submissions, thread resolution, check additions, close, and
archive actions
acceptance_criteria.then:
An append-only event is recorded with event type, actor, timestamp,
and relevant payload so the full review history can be reconstructed
from the event log

items.title: Review Record Storage and Identity
items.description:
Review records are stored as a first-party top-level entity with stable
references so they can be addressed through normal kspec lookup and audit
flows without being modeled as spec items.

acceptance_criteria.given: A review record is created
acceptance_criteria.when: It is persisted in kspec metadata
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record is stored in dedicated first-party review storage rather
