than being embedded ad hoc under plans, tasks, or module files

acceptance_criteria.given: A review record exists
acceptance_criteria.when: It is referenced through kspec commands
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review has a stable ULID-backed identity and can be addressed by
an @review ref using the shared reference system

acceptance_criteria.given: Review records are stored in the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then: The review data is persisted in dedicated first-party review storage rather than embedded inside plans, tasks, module files, or other unrelated entity files

items.title: Folder-Backed Review Storage
items.description:
Reviews are stored as folder-backed entities so review records can own
local evidence such as screenshots, logs, and supporting files without
rewriting or bloating one project-wide YAML file. The first slice stores
the full structured ReviewRecord in `review.yaml` and does not split
threads, checks, verdicts, notes, or events into separate sidecars.

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed review is loaded or mutated
acceptance_criteria.then: `.kspec/reviews/<review-ulid>/review.yaml` contains the full review detail record, including subject, related refs, threads, checks, verdicts, events, notes, and external links

acceptance_criteria.given: Folder-backed reviews exist in a project
acceptance_criteria.when: `.kspec/project.reviews.yaml` is read for list, filter, cache warm-up, or dashboard summary surfaces
acceptance_criteria.then: The index contains review ULID, lifecycle, subject summary, related refs, disposition, timestamps, and resource summaries, but not full review detail or resource bytes

acceptance_criteria.given: A review has an attached screenshot resource declared in `resources.yaml`
acceptance_criteria.when: The review is opened in the web UI or exported to the static UI snapshot
acceptance_criteria.then: The screenshot can be discovered and loaded from a stable review-scoped resource URL or exported asset path

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed review is deleted through review storage behavior
acceptance_criteria.then: The review index entry and `.kspec/reviews/<review-ulid>/` directory are removed in one logical shadow mutation

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Validated. Review folder mutators keep the bounded index projection in sync without repair; tests/review-rebuild-index.test.ts, tests/parser-reviews-folder.test.ts, tests/review-folder-migration.test.ts, tests/review-resource-cli.test.ts pass and built-CLI smoke confirms kspec review add / verdict / comment followed by kspec review rebuild-index --dry-run reports no drift.

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity contains a declared local resource
inherited_acs.when: A user, UI route, API route, static export, or agent resolves a `./resources/<relative-path>` reference for that entity
inherited_acs.then: The reference resolves only to a declared file inside the owning entity's `resources/` tree

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity has one or more declared local resources
inherited_acs.when: The entity is read through list, detail, API, static export, or agent-context surfaces
inherited_acs.then: Consumers can discover resource id, label, relative path, content type, byte size, content hash, and git version metadata without embedding large file contents in index records

inherited_acs.given: A resource reference contains an absolute path, parent traversal, an undeclared resource path, or a symlink escape
inherited_acs.when: The resource is imported, attached, served, exported, or resolved
inherited_acs.then: The operation is rejected with actionable guidance and no file outside the owning entity resource tree is read or written

inherited_acs.given: A local resource is binary or large text
inherited_acs.then: The resource remains as a sidecar file and structured records store only bounded metadata or pointers

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity with local resources is deleted
inherited_acs.then: The entity's owned resource files are removed in the same logical mutation as the entity record

inherited_acs.given: A resource version is recorded for later resolution or drift detection
inherited_acs.when: The project is stored in git
inherited_acs.then: The version metadata uses content hash plus git commit and repository-relative path when a commit is available, without maintaining a separate resource history log inside kspec

inherited_acs.given: A static export includes entities with declared local resources
inherited_acs.then: Resource files are copied under `assets/resources/<entity-type>/<entity-ulid>/<relative-path>` and exported metadata reports that exported path

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity exists in the system
inherited_acs.then: The entity has its own directory named by its full ULID under that entity type's storage root

inherited_acs.given: Folder-backed entities exist in a project
inherited_acs.when: The entity index is read for listing, filtering, cache warm-up, or dashboard summary surfaces
inherited_acs.then: The index contains bounded identity, lifecycle, summary, and relationship fields without embedding full documents, unbounded detail logs, or resource file bytes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity directory contains unknown files or directories
inherited_acs.when: The entity is read or updated
inherited_acs.then: Unknown entries are ignored by entity semantics and preserved across writes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from entity directories
inherited_acs.then: The index can be regenerated from entity folders and sidecar metadata
The entity directory, authoritative sidecar files, and bounded index entry are written in the same logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A persisted folder-backed entity changes any field, count, derived summary, relationship, lifecycle value, or resource metadata that belongs in that entity type's bounded index projection
inherited_acs.then: The authoritative sidecar update and the corresponding index entry update are committed as one logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from authoritative entity folders
inherited_acs.when: an index repair successfully rewrites the index and no later entity mutation occurs
inherited_acs.then: A subsequent dry-run rebuild reports no index changes

inherited_acs.given: An indexed optional field has equivalent persisted forms such as an omitted value and an empty default collection
inherited_acs.when: Index drift is computed or an index repair is verified
inherited_acs.then: The semantically equivalent forms are treated as equal and do not produce repeated update drift

items.title: Review Subject Bindings
items.description:
Review records identify what is under review using git-backed compare
semantics for code subjects and per-entity content hashing for shadow
branch subjects. v1 covers committed code only.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A review is created for a plan, task, spec, committed code, or other
supported artifact
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record captures subject type plus a stable local ref or external
identity that can be used to reopen the review later

acceptance_criteria.given: A review subject has both a local kspec ref and an external identity
acceptance_criteria.then:
The local ref remains authoritative while external identifiers are
kept as linkage metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: A review targets committed code
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record stores base_commit, head_commit, and optionally
merge_base_commit as the frozen compare context, with branch names
stored only as optional metadata and never as the authoritative
identity

acceptance_criteria.given: A review targets a shadow-branch entity such as a plan, spec, or task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record stores the shadow branch commit plus a per-entity content
hash so review mutations on the same shadow branch do not
self-invalidate the subject freshness check

acceptance_criteria.given: The reviewed subject has changed since the review was created
acceptance_criteria.when:
Staleness is evaluated after a review refresh updates the subject
version
acceptance_criteria.then:
Verdicts and checks whose applies_to_version does not match the
refreshed subject version are identified as stale, and for
shadow-branch subjects the entity content hash is compared rather
than shadow branch HEAD which would self-invalidate on every review
mutation

items.title: Review Comment Threads and Anchors
items.description:
Review comments support both general feedback and threaded targeted
anchors. Code anchors use diff-side semantics (base or head side, file
path, line range, commit). Structured anchors target sections or fields
in plans, specs, and other artifacts. Each thread has a ULID-based
identifier and a kind that distinguishes blocking from non-blocking
feedback.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer wants to leave general feedback
acceptance_criteria.when: A comment is created without a target anchor
acceptance_criteria.then:
The comment is stored as a general review thread entry with a ULID
thread identifier, author, kind, and timestamps

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer wants to comment on code
acceptance_criteria.when: The comment targets a file and line or range
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review record stores a code anchor with path, side (base or
head), line_start, line_end, and commit so the comment can be
rendered against the correct diff context

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reviewer wants to comment on a plan, spec, or other structured
artifact
acceptance_criteria.when: The comment targets a section, field, or logical anchor
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review record stores the structured anchor and renders it as
targeted feedback on that artifact

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer or author replies to an existing review comment
acceptance_criteria.then:
The conversation is preserved as a durable thread rather than
isolated standalone comments

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer creates a thread
acceptance_criteria.when: The thread kind is specified or defaulted
acceptance_criteria.then:
The thread stores a kind field that distinguishes at least blocker,
question, and nit so the system can determine which unresolved
threads should block approval and which should not

acceptance_criteria.given: Unresolved threads exist on a review
acceptance_criteria.then: Only threads with kind blocker prevent the review from being approved while unresolved nit, question, and idea threads do not block

items.title: Review Checks and Gate Evaluation
items.description:
Reviews can include recorded checks and derived gate state such as test
runs, local verification, CI runs, or manual attestations. Each check
records the compare context it applies to so gate evaluation uses only
checks that match the current reviewed state.

acceptance_criteria.given: A review requires tests, static checks, or other gates
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review stores check records with name, status, timestamps,
runner, required flag, evidence payload or link, and the
applies_to_version context (base_commit and head_commit) identifying
which reviewed state the check ran against

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has no external CI for a reviewable artifact
acceptance_criteria.when: An agent or human performs verification locally
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review record can store that verification as a first-party check
run rather than requiring GitHub Actions

acceptance_criteria.given: External CI exists
acceptance_criteria.when: A check run is mirrored into the review record
acceptance_criteria.then:
The local review gate references the external run while preserving
the normalized local status model

acceptance_criteria.given: Review policy requires all required gates to pass before approval
acceptance_criteria.then:
The system distinguishes required vs informational checks and
enforces the required ones

acceptance_criteria.given:
Multiple runs exist for the same logical check over the life of a
review
acceptance_criteria.then:
Check history is preserved while the current gate decision is
computed from the latest run whose applies_to_version matches the
current head_commit

acceptance_criteria.given:
The reviewed subject has been updated with new commits since the last
check run
acceptance_criteria.then:
Checks whose applies_to_version head_commit does not match the subject's current version are treated as stale and do not satisfy required
gate checks

items.title: Review Verdicts and Resolution Lifecycle
items.description:
Reviews support individual reviewer verdicts, blocking requests for
change, thread resolution, and iterative re-review cycles without losing
audit history. Each verdict records the compare context it applies to so
approvals can be invalidated when the reviewed state changes. Reviewer
identity is a plain string matching the author convention used by task
notes and git config (e.g. "user@example.com" or "agent-name").

acceptance_criteria.given: One or more reviewers act on a review
acceptance_criteria.when: They approve, request changes, or leave non-blocking comments
acceptance_criteria.then: Their verdicts are recorded with an applies_to_version that is auto-derived from the review's subject type — code_compare (base_commit and head_commit) for code subjects, entity_version (content_hash) for task/plan/spec subjects — identifying the reviewed state. The caller does not provide version information; the system derives it. Verdicts are stored distinctly from the overall review disposition

acceptance_criteria.given: A targeted review thread results in follow-up work
acceptance_criteria.then: The thread can be marked resolved with timestamp and actor

acceptance_criteria.given: a review subject goes through multiple cycles
acceptance_criteria.when: it moves from review to changes requested to re-review
acceptance_criteria.then: each review cycle produces its own review record; the collection of records across cycles comprises the full review history without losing the audit trail, with each record preserving the verdict, disposition, and compare context from its cycle

acceptance_criteria.given:
Required gates are failing, blocking threads are unresolved, or
blocking change requests remain open
acceptance_criteria.then:
The computed disposition cannot be approved while those blockers
remain open

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple reviewers have recorded verdicts on the same review
acceptance_criteria.when: The aggregate review disposition is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: The default aggregation rule is that any changes_requested verdict whose applies_to_version matches the subject's current version (base_commit and head_commit for code subjects, or content_hash for entity subjects — both derived from the review subject, not provided by the verdict submitter) blocks approval, and at least one explicit approve verdict matching the current version is required for the review to be considered approved

acceptance_criteria.given:
Review policy requires more than one approval, distinguishes reviewer
roles, or allows explicit override authority
acceptance_criteria.then:
Each verdict record includes a reviewer identity string, a role
field with a default value, and a timestamp so aggregation queries
can filter by role and count approvals without a schema redesign

acceptance_criteria.given: The reviewed subject has been updated since the last approval
acceptance_criteria.then:
Verdicts whose applies_to_version does not match the subject's
current version are treated as stale and excluded from the
aggregation computation

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reviewer submits a new verdict on the same review after a
previous verdict
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only the latest verdict per reviewer whose applies_to_version
matches the current subject version is considered, so a reviewer
who requests changes and later approves the same version does not
remain permanently blocking

acceptance_criteria.given:
A review is no longer active because its subject completed, was
cancelled, or was superseded
acceptance_criteria.then:
The system supports explicit closed or archived terminal handling
rather than relying on deletion as the only cleanup path

items.title: Review Record Validation
items.description:
Review entities use explicit schema validation so nested review data is
checked consistently during parsing, persistence, and command mutation.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Review records, threads, checks, verdicts, events, and subject
bindings are persisted or mutated
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review model is covered by first-party schema validation rather
than relying on loosely typed metadata blobs

acceptance_criteria.given:
Invalid review data is supplied through import, CLI mutation, or
future automation paths
acceptance_criteria.then: The system rejects the mutation with actionable validation feedback

items.title: Review Task Lifecycle Integration
items.description:
Review records integrate with task workflow signals and compatibility
fields without replacing the lightweight task lifecycle model already
used by kspec. The integration defines exact synchronization rules for
when review state drives task transitions and when it does not.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task is in pending_review or needs_work
acceptance_criteria.when: A review record exists for that task or its code work
acceptance_criteria.then:
The task can link to the active review record via a review_ref field
while task status remains the lightweight workflow signal

acceptance_criteria.given: A review is created with a task as its subject
acceptance_criteria.when: The review add command runs with a task subject
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review_ref field on the task is automatically set to the new
review record ref

acceptance_criteria.given: A code review is created with a related task ref
acceptance_criteria.when: The review add command runs with --related @task-ref
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review stores the task in related_refs and the task's
review_ref is set to the new review, so code reviews can be
discovered from task context even when the subject is code not
a task

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer sets a changes_requested verdict on a task review
acceptance_criteria.then:
The task is automatically transitioned to needs_work if it was in
pending_review

acceptance_criteria.given:
A task is in pending_review with no active review record or a
review_ref pointing at a closed review
acceptance_criteria.when: The task state is rendered or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: The system surfaces a warning about the inconsistent review linkage

acceptance_criteria.given:
A task-associated review records changes requested and later returns
for re-review
acceptance_criteria.when: The task moves between needs_work and pending_review
acceptance_criteria.then:
The review history remains intact instead of being replaced by ad hoc
task notes

acceptance_criteria.given: A task or review has an external PR URL or provider identifier
acceptance_criteria.when: Review state is rendered or audited locally
acceptance_criteria.then:
The external link is treated as compatibility linkage, not the sole
durable review record

items.title: Typed Spec-Criterion Anchors
items.description:
Review threads can target a single acceptance criterion of a spec item
through a typed anchor that carries the spec reference and the
criterion identifier as distinct validated fields. The typed form is
the canonical way to write criterion-targeted feedback, replacing the
loose structured-anchor convention for new writes. Records written
under the loose convention remain fully readable: readers accept both
shapes, and legacy records load and validate without modification.

acceptance_criteria.given: a reviewer targets a specific acceptance criterion of a spec item
acceptance_criteria.when:
the thread is created through a supported write interface with a
spec-criterion anchor
acceptance_criteria.then:
the anchor stores the spec reference and the acceptance-criterion
identifier as distinct typed fields, and the stored record
round-trips through load and save unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given:
a spec-criterion anchor whose spec reference is not a valid
reference or whose criterion identifier does not match the
established acceptance-criterion identifier format
acceptance_criteria.when: the anchor is validated during thread creation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected, no thread is stored, and the feedback
names the offending field

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review record written before the typed variant existed,
containing loose structured anchors — including the convention
that gestures at an acceptance criterion through section and
field values
acceptance_criteria.when: the record is loaded and validated
acceptance_criteria.then:
the record loads and validates without error and the anchor
content is preserved exactly as written, with no migration or
rewrite required

acceptance_criteria.given:
review data containing an anchor whose type is not an accepted
variant
acceptance_criteria.then:
the feedback enumerates the complete set of accepted anchor
variants, including the spec-criterion and plan-text variants

items.title: Plan-Text Anchors
items.description:
Review threads can target a span of a plan document through a typed
plan-text anchor. The plan document divides into sections derived
from its headings on the server side, and the anchor addresses a span
with four fields: the identifier of the containing section, the
offset of the span within that section, the quoted text of the span,
and the ordinal of the plan revision the anchor was created against.
Offsets are counted in Unicode code points from the start of the
section's content — never bytes and never UTF-16 code units — so
every write surface measures the same span identically regardless of
text encoding. Together these fields fully describe the anchored span:
given the anchor and the content of its creation revision, the exact
span is recoverable without consulting any other state. Plan-text
anchors are valid only on reviews whose subject is a plan; the
anchored plan is the review's subject.

acceptance_criteria.given: a reviewer targets a span of text in a plan document under review
acceptance_criteria.when:
the thread is created through a supported write interface with a
plan-text anchor
acceptance_criteria.then:
the anchor stores the section identifier, the offset of the span
within that section counted in Unicode code points, the quoted
span text, and the ordinal of the plan revision it was created
against, and the stored record round-trips through load and save
unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the content of a plan revision
acceptance_criteria.when: the document is divided into sections
acceptance_criteria.then:
each heading begins a section whose identifier derives
deterministically from the heading text, duplicate heading texts
disambiguate deterministically by document order, content before
the first heading forms a single leading section with a fixed
identifier, and identical content always yields identical section
identifiers

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan-text anchor with a negative offset, an empty quoted text,
or a creation revision that is not a positive integer
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected, no thread is stored, and the feedback
names the offending field

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan-text anchor whose creation revision ordinal is a positive
integer that does not exist in the subject plan's revision
history
acceptance_criteria.when: the anchor is validated at creation time
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected with feedback naming the revision field
and the ordinal that failed to resolve

acceptance_criteria.given:
a thread creation that supplies a plan-text anchor on a review
whose subject is not a plan
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected with feedback stating that plan-text
anchors apply only to plan-subject reviews

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan-text anchor whose quoted text does not occur at the stored
offset within the stored section of the creation revision's
content
acceptance_criteria.when: the anchor is validated at creation time
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected with actionable feedback and no thread
is stored

items.title: Advisory Idea Threads
items.description:
Review threads support the kind idea alongside blocker, question, and
nit. An idea thread carries a forward-looking suggestion that is
advisory only: whatever its resolution state, it never participates
in approval gating. In all other respects idea threads behave like
every other kind — they hold entries and replies, resolve and reopen,
and appear in the review's event history.

acceptance_criteria.given: a reviewer opens a thread with kind idea
acceptance_criteria.when: the thread is created through a supported write interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
the thread stores kind idea, and reply, resolve, and reopen
operate on it exactly as they do for the existing kinds

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review whose only unresolved threads have kind idea, with all
required checks passing against the current subject version and a
current approval verdict
acceptance_criteria.then: the disposition is approved

acceptance_criteria.given: a thread whose kind is not one of blocker, question, nit, or idea
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is rejected with feedback enumerating the accepted
kinds

items.title: Configurable AC Coverage Scanner
items.description: AC coverage scanning requires explicit per-project configuration. Projects declare which paths contain test files, and the scanner adapts its annotation parsing to the source language of each file. When unconfigured, the scanner is inactive and validation communicates what is missing and why.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with no coverage scanning configured
acceptance_criteria.then: no files are scanned for AC annotations

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with no coverage scanning configured
acceptance_criteria.when: validation runs with completeness checks enabled
acceptance_criteria.then: a warning explains that coverage scanning is inactive and how to enable it

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with coverage scan paths configured
acceptance_criteria.then: files under those paths are scanned for AC annotations

acceptance_criteria.given: a source file in a configured scan path
acceptance_criteria.when: the scanner parses it for AC annotations
acceptance_criteria.then: the comment syntax used matches the file's language

acceptance_criteria.given: a file whose language cannot be determined
acceptance_criteria.then: the file is skipped

acceptance_criteria.given: a project upgrading from implicit scanning behavior
acceptance_criteria.then: the guidance warning surfaces (coverage does not silently disappear)

items.title: Coverage Annotation Scope Boundaries
items.description:
AC coverage scanning is limited to the configured coverage surface.
Annotations outside configured scan paths or inside excluded paths do
not create coverage credit and do not create invalid-annotation debt.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has one or more coverage scan paths configured
acceptance_criteria.when: completeness validation scans for AC annotations
acceptance_criteria.then: Only files under the configured scan paths are considered

acceptance_criteria.given:
A configured coverage scan path contains files that match a
configured exclude pattern
acceptance_criteria.when: completeness validation scans for AC annotations
acceptance_criteria.then: Matching files are skipped

acceptance_criteria.given: A skipped file contains text that looks like an AC annotation
acceptance_criteria.then: The skipped text produces no coverage credit

acceptance_criteria.given: A skipped file contains text that looks like an AC annotation
acceptance_criteria.then: The skipped text produces no invalid annotation findings

items.title: AC Verification Record Store
items.description:
Durable storage for per-acceptance-criterion verification stamps. A
stamp records that a criterion's test mapping was confirmed,
capturing when the verification happened, which actor performed it,
and which provenance class produced it — a validation pass, an
ingested test run, or an explicit re-verification. Stamps live in an
operational sidecar within the project's shadow-branch metadata,
keyed by the owning item's canonical identifier and the criterion
id; spec source files never carry verification state. The store
holds one current stamp per criterion, and superseded stamps remain
recoverable through the metadata's version history. Stamp writes
commit to the shadow-branch history like other metadata mutations,
so a fresh checkout of the metadata reproduces the store.

acceptance_criteria.given: a verification stamp stored for an acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.when:
the owning spec item is later renamed or moved to a different
spec source file
acceptance_criteria.then: the stamp still resolves to the same acceptance criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
a verification stamp written with a verification time, an
actor, and a provenance class drawn from the recorded classes
— validation pass, ingested run, or explicit re-verification
acceptance_criteria.when: the stamp is accepted and read back
acceptance_criteria.then:
it carries the same verification time, actor, and provenance
class

acceptance_criteria.given:
a verification stamp write missing its verification time, its
actor, or its provenance class
acceptance_criteria.then:
the write is rejected and the stored verification state is
unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a project's spec source files
acceptance_criteria.when: any verification stamp is written or replaced
acceptance_criteria.then:
the content of every spec source file is byte-identical to its
content before the write

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion that already has a stored verification
stamp
acceptance_criteria.when: a new stamp is written for that criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
reads return only the new stamp as the current verification,
and the prior stamp is recoverable from the metadata's version
history rather than from the live store

acceptance_criteria.given: a verification stamp write that completes
acceptance_criteria.when:
the project's shadow-branch metadata is checked out fresh
elsewhere
acceptance_criteria.then: the same current stamps are reproduced in the fresh checkout

acceptance_criteria.given:
a stored stamp whose item identifier or criterion id no longer
resolves to an existing acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
loading succeeds, the unresolvable stamp is excluded from
resolved verification reads, and validation reports it as an
orphaned verification record rather than silently dropping it
or failing

items.title: AC Freshness Resolution
items.description:
The read contract resolving an acceptance criterion's annotation
freshness from two provenance sources — bootstrap-derived and
recorded. When no recorded verification stamp exists, freshness
derives from version-control history of the annotation's location
— a bootstrap value that requires no prior bookkeeping, so every
annotation whose location has version-control history has
freshness from day one. When a criterion has annotations at
several locations and no recorded stamp, the bootstrap value is
the most recent of the history values of the locations that have
version-control history; locations without history contribute no
value. A location with
no version-control history — an uncommitted file, or a line that
exists only in the working tree — yields no bootstrap value;
until such a location gains history or a recorded stamp is
written, the criterion's freshness is absent, and absent
freshness is a distinct, observable outcome — not a present-time
value, not an error. Once a recorded stamp exists for a
criterion, resolution returns the stamp verbatim as the resolved
freshness; resolution never compares a recorded stamp against
annotation history, and the bootstrap-derived value remains
separately retrievable alongside it, so a consumer assessing
whether a stamp predates later annotation edits performs that
comparison itself. Resolved freshness always names its provenance
source, recorded values also carry the stamp's provenance class,
and a freshness value is expressed as a timestamp, a commit
reference, or both.

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion with at least one annotation in a
configured scan path whose location has version-control
history, and no recorded verification stamp
acceptance_criteria.then:
the result is a bootstrap value derived from the
version-control history of the annotation's location, labeled
with the bootstrap provenance source

acceptance_criteria.given: an acceptance criterion with a recorded verification stamp
acceptance_criteria.then:
the recorded stamp is returned verbatim — carrying its
provenance class — as the resolved freshness, and the
bootstrap value is not used as the resolved freshness,
including when the version-control history at the
annotation's location is more recent than the stamp

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion with a recorded verification stamp and
at least one annotation in a configured scan path whose
location has version-control history
acceptance_criteria.when:
a consumer requests the bootstrap-derived value alongside the
resolved freshness
acceptance_criteria.then:
both the recorded stamp and the bootstrap-derived value are
returned, each labeled with its provenance source, and the
resolution neither alters nor compares them

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion with annotations at several locations
in configured scan paths, at least one location having
version-control history, and no recorded verification stamp
acceptance_criteria.then:
the bootstrap value is the most recent of the history values
of the locations that have version-control history, locations
without history contribute no value, and the result is
labeled with the bootstrap provenance source

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion with no recorded verification stamp
whose annotations are all at locations with no version-control
history
acceptance_criteria.then:
no freshness value is produced for that criterion, the absence
is reported as a distinct observable outcome, and no
present-time or fabricated value is substituted and no error
is raised

acceptance_criteria.given: a resolved freshness value
acceptance_criteria.when: it is delivered to a consumer
acceptance_criteria.then:
it carries a timestamp, a commit reference, or both, and it
names its provenance source

acceptance_criteria.given:
an acceptance criterion with no annotation in any configured
scan path and no recorded verification stamp
acceptance_criteria.then:
no freshness value is produced for that criterion — absence is
reported as absence, not as a default or fabricated value

items.title: Session Verification Evidence
items.description:
Verification stamps can attribute a verification to the work
session that produced it. The session linkage is part of the stored
record: reading a stamp yields the producing session's identity
from the record alone, so a consumer can answer "when was this
criterion last verified, and by which session" without correlating
other data sources. Session linkage is optional — verifications
produced outside any session omit it. When a session reference is
supplied, it must be a well-formed session identifier; a malformed
reference rejects the write rather than storing an unusable
linkage.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a verification stamp written with the identity of the session
that produced the verification
acceptance_criteria.then:
the record carries the session reference alongside the
verification time, actor, and provenance class

acceptance_criteria.given: a verification stamp produced outside any recorded session
acceptance_criteria.when: it is written without a session reference
acceptance_criteria.then:
the stamp is accepted, and reads return it with no session
linkage

acceptance_criteria.given:
a verification stamp write carrying a session reference that
is not a well-formed session identifier
acceptance_criteria.then:
the write is rejected and the stored verification state is
unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a stored stamp carrying a session reference
acceptance_criteria.then:
the producing session's identity is returned with the stamp,
from the stored record alone, without consulting session logs
or any other records

acceptance_criteria.given:
a stored stamp whose session reference names a session that no
longer exists
acceptance_criteria.then:
the read succeeds, the stamp remains a valid verification, and
the session linkage is reported as unresolvable rather than
being dropped or failing the read

items.title: Coverage Record Compatibility
items.description:
The verification record store is additive and optional. A project
containing no verification records is fully valid, behaves exactly
as it did before the store existed, and is never rewritten by tool
upgrade. The store materializes only when the first stamp is
written. Because the store is purely additive, a project that
contains one remains fully operable by tool versions predating the
store — such tools neither read nor modify it. That older-tool
guarantee is the purpose served by two verifiable properties:
metadata readers leave sidecar directories they do not recognize
unread and unmodified, and creating the store modifies no
pre-existing metadata file an older reader depends on. Stored records
declare a record-format version: data declaring a newer record
format than the running tool supports is refused rather than
misread, and records carrying unrecognized fields survive
read-modify-write cycles intact.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project containing no verification record store
acceptance_criteria.when: any command or daemon request reads coverage or freshness data
acceptance_criteria.then:
the operation succeeds, freshness resolves through the
bootstrap provenance source alone, and no store is created as
a side effect of the read

acceptance_criteria.given:
an existing project created before the verification record
store existed
acceptance_criteria.when: the tool is upgraded and ordinary commands run
acceptance_criteria.then:
no project data is rewritten, no migration step is required,
and the project manifest's declared format version is
unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with no verification record store
acceptance_criteria.when: the first verification stamp is written
acceptance_criteria.then:
the store is created as part of that write and the write
succeeds without any prior setup or migration step

acceptance_criteria.given:
a verification record store declaring a record-format version
greater than the running tool's maximum supported record
format
acceptance_criteria.when: the store is read or written
acceptance_criteria.then:
the operation on the store refuses with an error naming both
the declared version and the maximum supported version, the
store is not modified, and operations not involving the store
remain unaffected

acceptance_criteria.given:
stored verification records containing fields the running tool
does not recognize, within a supported record-format version
acceptance_criteria.when:
the tool reads the store and writes a stamp for a different
criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
the unrecognized fields persist unchanged in the stored
records

acceptance_criteria.given:
a project's shadow-branch metadata containing a sidecar
directory the running tool does not recognize
acceptance_criteria.when: the metadata is loaded, validated, and written elsewhere
acceptance_criteria.then:
the operations succeed and the unrecognized directory's files
are neither read nor modified

acceptance_criteria.given:
a project's shadow-branch metadata without a verification
record store
acceptance_criteria.when: the store is created by the first stamp write
acceptance_criteria.then:
no metadata file that existed before the write is modified by
the store's creation

items.title: Test Result Run Store
items.description:
Durable storage for normalized completed test runs submitted to a
kspec project. A run record captures one completed execution from
any producer — local tool, CI job, agent, or other runner — without
assuming the producer's framework, repository layout, package
manager, or result-file format. The store persists the normalized
run envelope, the normalized test cases, mappable acceptance-criterion
references, unmapped cases, producer metadata, execution timestamps,
and optional code revision. It lives in project metadata as an
additive folder-backed sidecar at `coverage/test-runs/index.yaml` plus one
folder-backed run entity per accepted run under
`coverage/test-runs/runs/<run-ulid>/run.yaml`; project source files and
spec source files are never rewritten by ingestion.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a completed test run submitted in the supported normalized run
envelope
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run is persisted with its run identity, producer metadata,
timestamps, test cases, mapped acceptance-criterion references,
unmapped cases, and optional code revision

acceptance_criteria.given:
two submitted runs produced by different test frameworks or CI
systems
acceptance_criteria.then:
the stored records use the same kspec-owned schema and contain no
framework-specific top-level fields required for correctness

acceptance_criteria.given: a project's spec files and source files before ingestion
acceptance_criteria.then:
no spec source file and no code source file is modified by the
ingestion; only the project metadata sidecar changes

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid normalized run with canonical run id 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run is stored as
coverage/test-runs/runs/01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV/run.yaml and the
coverage/test-runs/index.yaml summary is updated in the same
mutation; ingestion uses the folder-backed entity trait for the run
folder and does not store framework-native artifact files in this plan

acceptance_criteria.given: more than one accepted run in the store
acceptance_criteria.when: consumers request the latest ingested run
acceptance_criteria.then:
the store returns the run with the latest completed-at timestamp,
breaking exact timestamp ties deterministically by run identity

acceptance_criteria.given:
a submitted run missing required envelope fields or containing
an invalid case status
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run is rejected with field-specific diagnostics and the store
remains unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given:
a stored run record carrying unrecognized fields within a
supported record-format version
acceptance_criteria.when: a later run is ingested or the store is read
acceptance_criteria.then:
the unrecognized fields survive unchanged and do not prevent
supported fields from being read

acceptance_criteria.given:
a test-run store or run record declaring a record-format version
newer than the running kspec version supports
acceptance_criteria.when: the store is read or written
acceptance_criteria.then:
the operation refuses with an error naming both versions, the
store is not modified, and unrelated project operations remain
available

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity exists in the system
inherited_acs.then: The entity has its own directory named by its full ULID under that entity type's storage root

inherited_acs.given: Folder-backed entities exist in a project
inherited_acs.when: The entity index is read for listing, filtering, cache warm-up, or dashboard summary surfaces
inherited_acs.then: The index contains bounded identity, lifecycle, summary, and relationship fields without embedding full documents, unbounded detail logs, or resource file bytes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity directory contains unknown files or directories
inherited_acs.when: The entity is read or updated
inherited_acs.then: Unknown entries are ignored by entity semantics and preserved across writes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from entity directories
inherited_acs.then: The index can be regenerated from entity folders and sidecar metadata
The entity directory, authoritative sidecar files, and bounded index entry are written in the same logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A persisted folder-backed entity changes any field, count, derived summary, relationship, lifecycle value, or resource metadata that belongs in that entity type's bounded index projection
inherited_acs.then: The authoritative sidecar update and the corresponding index entry update are committed as one logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from authoritative entity folders
inherited_acs.when: an index repair successfully rewrites the index and no later entity mutation occurs
inherited_acs.then: A subsequent dry-run rebuild reports no index changes

inherited_acs.given: An indexed optional field has equivalent persisted forms such as an omitted value and an empty default collection
inherited_acs.when: Index drift is computed or an index repair is verified
inherited_acs.then: The semantically equivalent forms are treated as equal and do not produce repeated update drift

items.title: Normalized Test Result Ingestion Contract
items.description:
The ingestion boundary accepts one kspec-owned normalized result
format. Producers, reporters, and adapters translate framework-native
output into this format before the core store, coverage engine, or
daemon routes see it. The contract models runs, suites, and cases in
general terms; it records stable case identity, display names,
optional file/line locations, status, duration, diagnostic text,
producer/source metadata, and zero or more acceptance-criterion
references. It intentionally does not import a Vitest, JUnit, GitHub
Actions, or kynetic-spec-specific result shape as the internal model.

acceptance_criteria.given: a producer submits test results
acceptance_criteria.when: the ingestion boundary accepts the payload
acceptance_criteria.then:
the payload conforms to the kspec normalized run envelope rather
than to a framework-native result schema

acceptance_criteria.given: a normalized test case in a submitted run
acceptance_criteria.then:
the status is one of passed, failed, errored, skipped, or unknown,
and unknown or skipped cases never count as positive coverage
evidence

acceptance_criteria.given: a normalized test case with a producer-supplied stable id
acceptance_criteria.when:
the same logical case appears in a later run from the same
producer and project revision
acceptance_criteria.then:
consumers can match the case by that stable id without relying on
display-name text alone

acceptance_criteria.given:
a normalized test case whose producer cannot provide a file or
line location
acceptance_criteria.then:
ingestion still accepts the case and records location absence as
absence rather than inventing a project-specific path

acceptance_criteria.given:
a failing or errored normalized case with diagnostic text or a
failure message
acceptance_criteria.then:
the diagnostic material needed for a human to identify the
failure is preserved without requiring the original native result
file

acceptance_criteria.given: a run produced by a local command, CI job, or agent session
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run identifies the producer kind and producer label, and may
carry optional source details such as command, CI URL, agent
session id, or code revision without making any of those details
mandatory for all producers

inherited_acs.given: Any input surface accepts a field with a defined type constraint
inherited_acs.when: The provided value does not satisfy the constraint
inherited_acs.then:
The operation is rejected before any data is persisted or
state is mutated

inherited_acs.given: An input validation error occurs for a constrained field
inherited_acs.when: The error is reported to the caller
inherited_acs.then:
The message includes the set of valid alternatives for the
field, not just the field name and invalid value (extends
@trait-error-guidance ac-5 which requires identifying the
field/value but not listing valid alternatives)

inherited_acs.given: A field's type constraint is defined in a canonical schema
inherited_acs.then:
The validation is derived from that schema definition rather
than a separately maintained check

items.title: Test Result AC Mapping
items.description:
Ingested results map test cases onto acceptance criteria through the
normalized result contract, not through project-specific file names or
the shape of one repository's test suite. A case may carry explicit
criterion references emitted by a reporter or adapter, and adapters
may also extract references from agreed text tokens in test names or
suite names before producing the normalized payload. Core ingestion
validates mapped references against the project's current spec corpus,
records all valid mappings, and keeps invalid or absent mappings as
unmapped result data that later surfaces can show. No result is
silently discarded only because it cannot be mapped.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a normalized test case carrying explicit acceptance-criterion
references
acceptance_criteria.then:
each reference that resolves to an existing criterion in the
project is attributed to that criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
a framework-native result whose test name contains an agreed
acceptance-criterion token
acceptance_criteria.then:
the adapter emits explicit normalized references, and the core
ingestion path handles them exactly like any other explicit
mapping

acceptance_criteria.given:
a normalized case whose mapped reference names a missing item or
criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
ingestion records a structured unmapped-or-invalid mapping entry
naming the case and offending reference, and does not attribute
the case to any wrong criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
a normalized run containing test cases with no acceptance-criterion
mapping
acceptance_criteria.then:
those cases remain attached to the run as unmapped cases so UI,
CLI, or validation surfaces can report them later

acceptance_criteria.given: one test case intentionally covers multiple acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria.when: the case carries several valid criterion references
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run attributes the same case outcome to every referenced
criterion without duplicating the stored case payload

acceptance_criteria.given:
a kspec project whose package name, manifest file, test directory,
and spec item slugs differ from kynetic-spec
acceptance_criteria.when: its normalized test results are ingested
acceptance_criteria.then:
mapping behavior depends only on the project's loaded spec corpus
and normalized references, not on kynetic-spec-specific names,
paths, or test framework conventions

items.title: Test Result Ingestion Interface
items.description:
Test-result ingestion is exposed through matching CLI and daemon
interfaces that accept the same normalized payload and produce the
same stored run, validation diagnostics, cache updates, and events.
The daemon does not run arbitrary test commands for this plan; it
accepts completed run records submitted by trusted local tools, CI, or
agents. Successful ingestion is a project metadata mutation and uses
the shared mutation pipeline so the shadow commit, cache update, and
typed event order match the rest of the redesign program.

acceptance_criteria.given: the same valid normalized run payload
acceptance_criteria.when:
it is submitted once through the CLI and once through the daemon
ingestion route in equivalent projects
acceptance_criteria.then:
both paths produce the same stored run shape, mapping report, and
affected-domain event payloads before stamp-writing behavior is
layered on by the ingestion-provenance stamp task

acceptance_criteria.given: a caller wants test results represented in kspec
acceptance_criteria.then:
the daemon accepts a completed result payload and never executes
a configured test command as part of this plan

acceptance_criteria.given:
a run submitted through CLI, daemon route, CI helper, or agent
session
acceptance_criteria.then:
the run records the submitting actor resolved by the shared actor
identity rules and records source metadata sufficient to identify
whether the run came from local, CI, agent, or other producer

acceptance_criteria.given:
a run submitted from inside a kspec session or outside any
session
acceptance_criteria.then:
the session id is recorded when supplied and valid, and absence
of session id remains valid for non-session producers

acceptance_criteria.given: a daemon-served ingestion succeeds
acceptance_criteria.when: subscribers observe the emitted event and re-fetch the latest run
acceptance_criteria.then:
the shadow commit exists and the daemon read model reflects the
ingested run before the event is observable

acceptance_criteria.given: a static-export or read-only project snapshot
acceptance_criteria.when: a caller attempts to ingest a run
acceptance_criteria.then:
the interface refuses with a read-only/static-mode error and does
not pretend the result was stored

acceptance_criteria.given:
a valid or invalid normalized payload is submitted with dry-run
preview enabled through the CLI or daemon ingestion route
acceptance_criteria.when: ingestion validates and maps the payload
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response reports the run id, validation diagnostics, mapping
summary, affected items, and event scopes that would result, but
no run folder, index entry, verification stamp, shadow commit,
cache update, or event broadcast is produced

inherited_acs.then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
output includes all data available in human-readable mode
error is returned as JSON object with error field
references use @ prefix consistently
timestamps use ISO 8601 format
--json takes precedence over other format options
exit code 0
exit code 1
exit code 2
exit code 3
exit code 0 with empty result set
exit code 1 with usage information
exit code 1
exit code meanings documented in code
includes description of what went wrong
includes suggested action to resolve
suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
indicates current state and valid next states
indicates which field/value failed validation
guidance included in structured error object
returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing
show what would be changed without applying
no files are modified
clear indication that this is a preview
error shown but no state changed
dry run takes precedence (no changes made)
JSON output includes dry_run boolean field

items.title: Ingested Run Verification Stamps
items.description:
Passing ingested results can confirm the test mapping for their
mapped acceptance criteria by writing verification stamps with
ingestion provenance. Failed, errored, skipped, unknown, unmapped, or
invalidly mapped cases do not write positive verification stamps.
Detailed run data remains in the test-run store; the verification
stamp records only the current verification fact supported by the
existing stamp schema — verified time, actor, provenance, optional
commit, and optional session linkage.

acceptance_criteria.given:
an accepted run containing a passed case mapped to an existing
acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion's verification stamp is written or replaced with
provenance ingestion, the run's completion time, the submitting
actor, and any supplied commit or session linkage

acceptance_criteria.given:
an accepted run containing failed, errored, skipped, or unknown
cases mapped to an acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
those cases do not write positive verification stamps for that
criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
an accepted run containing cases that cannot be mapped to any
acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
no verification stamp is written for those cases, and their
unmapped status remains available from the run record

acceptance_criteria.given: a run ingestion writes verification stamps
acceptance_criteria.when: the verification record store is read by existing consumers
acceptance_criteria.then:
the stamps conform to the existing verification stamp schema and
do not require consumers to understand test-run store internals

acceptance_criteria.given:
the same valid normalized run payload with passing mapped cases is
submitted through the CLI and daemon ingestion paths in equivalent
projects
acceptance_criteria.then:
both paths produce the same verification stamp writes, stamp-write
count, non-positive mapped case count, and stored verification
effects in the run record

acceptance_criteria.given:
more than one accepted run has written ingestion-provenance
verification stamps
acceptance_criteria.when: a consumer presents freshness based on ingested-run evidence
acceptance_criteria.then:
it labels the stamp as positive ingestion-provenance evidence from
an ingested run while the detailed latest-run, failed-run, or
unmapped evidence remains in the test-run store for the coverage
state engine to evaluate

items.title: Coverage Evidence Index
items.description: A per-project read model that joins the spec corpus, acceptance criteria, static coverage annotations, annotation freshness, verification stamps, and ingested test-run outcomes into one evidence index. The index is the only backend input used by coverage-state computation. It records what evidence exists for each criterion, whether any mapped latest result is failing or errored, which mappings are unmapped or invalid, and what freshness values are available. Criterion evidence lists annotations, freshness values, verification stamps, and ingested results when those evidence types apply. Unmapped or invalid ingested cases are exposed separately as project/index-level diagnostics rather than being attributed to any criterion. It never derives final UI state in the client and never assumes kynetic-spec-specific test files, slugs, packages, or framework output.

acceptance_criteria.given: a loaded kspec project with spec items and acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria.when: the coverage evidence index is built
acceptance_criteria.then:
every acceptance criterion in the corpus has exactly one evidence
entry, including criteria with no annotations, no stamps, and no
ingested results

acceptance_criteria.given: an indexed criterion with any combination of annotations, freshness values, verification stamps, and ingested test results, and a project-level index with unmapped or invalid ingested cases
acceptance_criteria.then: criterion evidence includes applicable annotations, freshness values, verification stamps, and ingested results, and unmapped or invalid ingested cases are exposed separately rather than being attributed to a criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
several ingested runs contain mapped results for the same
criterion
acceptance_criteria.when: the evidence index selects result evidence for state computation
acceptance_criteria.then:
it uses the latest accepted run relevant to that criterion,
breaking exact completed-at ties deterministically by run id and
preserving older runs for later history consumers

acceptance_criteria.given: an ingested run contains cases with no valid criterion mapping or cases whose attempted mapping is invalid
acceptance_criteria.then: those cases are exposed separately from criterion evidence and are not attributed to any criterion

acceptance_criteria.given:
normalized results from different producers in projects whose
layouts differ from kynetic-spec
acceptance_criteria.then:
index behavior is identical for equivalent normalized records and
does not inspect framework-native fields or kynetic-spec paths

acceptance_criteria.given: a web or CLI consumer requests coverage evidence

items.title: Coverage State Engine
items.description:
The backend service that computes one deterministic corpus coverage
state for every acceptance criterion from the coverage evidence index.
Internal causes may distinguish failing test evidence, missing
evidence, stale spec text, stale covering code, and stale mapping
confirmation, but user-facing presentation collapses to the four
buckets defined by @coverage-state-presentation: covered, failing,
not yet, and re-verify. Corpus coverage has no not-applicable state;
in-code not-applicable annotations neither cover nor exempt criteria.

acceptance_criteria.given: any acceptance criterion in the loaded spec corpus
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion has exactly one computed state and a machine-readable
explanation naming the evidence and rule that produced it

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion whose only annotations are not-applicable markers or
whose tests mark it not-applicable
acceptance_criteria.then:
the result is not a not-applicable state; the criterion is treated
according to the ordinary evidence rules, with N/A markers
contributing no positive coverage evidence

acceptance_criteria.given:
the latest relevant ingested evidence for a criterion contains a
failed or errored mapped case
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion's presentation bucket is failing even if older
passing evidence or static annotations also exist

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion with current positive evidence from a coverage
annotation, a passing mapped ingested result, or a verification
stamp that is not stale under the engine's freshness rules
acceptance_criteria.when:
no latest mapped case is failing or errored and no re-verify cause
applies
acceptance_criteria.then: the criterion's presentation bucket is covered

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion with no positive coverage evidence from annotations,
verification stamps, or mapped ingested results
acceptance_criteria.then: the criterion's presentation bucket is not yet

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion with positive evidence whose confirmed freshness is
older than the criterion text, covering annotation, or mapped test
evidence it depends on
acceptance_criteria.when: no latest mapped case is failing or errored
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion's presentation bucket is re-verify and the internal
cause identifies which dependency is stale

acceptance_criteria.given: computed internal coverage-state causes
acceptance_criteria.when: any API, CLI, or UI-facing response presents the state
acceptance_criteria.then:
each state maps to exactly one of covered, failing, not yet, or
re-verify, and detailed causes are secondary metadata

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion with multiple evidence facts that could imply
different buckets
acceptance_criteria.when: state computation runs repeatedly over the same inputs
acceptance_criteria.then:
the same state, presentation bucket, and explanation are produced
each time according to the documented precedence rules

items.title: Coverage Freshness and Revision Comparison
items.description:
Coverage state can determine whether existing evidence must be
re-verified because the acceptance criterion text, covering
annotation, or mapped test evidence changed after verification. The
comparison reads version-control history and project metadata; it does
not require storing operational state in spec source. Criterion text
comparisons are per acceptance criterion, not only per whole spec
item, so changing one criterion does not force unrelated criteria on
the same item into re-verify.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion has positive verification evidence and its given,
when, or then text changes afterward
acceptance_criteria.then:
that criterion enters the re-verify bucket with a spec-text
change cause unless newer positive evidence supersedes the change

acceptance_criteria.given:
one criterion on a spec item changes while a sibling criterion on
the same item does not
acceptance_criteria.then:
the unchanged sibling is not marked re-verify solely because the
item file changed

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion's positive evidence relies on a coverage annotation
location and that annotation line changes after verification
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion enters the re-verify bucket with a covering-code or
mapping-change cause unless newer positive evidence supersedes it

acceptance_criteria.given:
an ingested run carried a code revision and later source changes
affect the mapped test case or annotation location
acceptance_criteria.when: the engine can compare those revisions
acceptance_criteria.then:
the state explanation reports whether the run evidence is current
or requires re-verification because code changed after the run

acceptance_criteria.given:
positive evidence exists but the engine cannot compare a required
freshness source because revision metadata is absent or
unresolvable
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion does not get silently marked covered; it either
remains not yet when there is no positive evidence or enters
re-verify with an unknown-freshness cause

acceptance_criteria.given: a consumer requests why a criterion is stale
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend can resolve the relevant prior and current versions
acceptance_criteria.then:
it can provide a per-criterion text or metadata comparison for
that criterion without requiring the consumer to diff the entire
spec item locally

items.title: Coverage State API and Cache
items.description: The daemon exposes coverage-state reads as server-computed data with explicit cache ownership, pagination/filter support where needed, and static-mode fallback. Consumers can request corpus rollups, per-item rollups, per-criterion state detail, and unmapped-result summaries without rebuilding the evidence join client-side. Cache invalidation follows the same project metadata, source annotation, verification stamp, and test-run changes that affect state computation. This spec uses the read-endpoint portions of @trait-api-endpoint; mutation and shadow-commit endpoint behavior is non-applicable for coverage-state read endpoints and remains owned by ingestion and shared mutation paths.

acceptance_criteria.given: a daemon client requests coverage-state summary for a project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response includes counts for covered, failing, not yet, and
re-verify plus the denominator used for corpus coverage

acceptance_criteria.given:
a daemon client requests a spec item or acceptance criterion
coverage detail
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response includes the computed state, presentation bucket,
explanation, relevant latest run evidence, freshness values, and
any unmapped result references affecting that view

acceptance_criteria.given:
a web client renders a coverage badge, spec workspace row, or
Validate matrix row
acceptance_criteria.then:
it consumes server-computed state/rollup fields and does not
reproduce the state derivation rules locally

acceptance_criteria.given:
spec source, configured annotation scan paths, verification
stamps, or test-run records change
acceptance_criteria.when: a subsequent coverage-state request is served
acceptance_criteria.then:
stale cached state is not returned for affected criteria or
rollups

acceptance_criteria.given: a static export contains coverage-state data
acceptance_criteria.when: a client reads the exported snapshot
acceptance_criteria.then:
it can render the last computed state and rollups as read-only
data, and mutation or ingestion actions are unavailable

acceptance_criteria.given:
a project with thousands of acceptance criteria and many
annotations
acceptance_criteria.then:
the daemon reuses the cache/read model instead of rescanning and
recomputing the full corpus for every request

inherited_acs.then: returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing

items.title: Coverage State Events
items.description: Coverage-state changes broadcast through the reserved coverage-state event family on the spec-item domain topic. Events identify affected items and criteria by canonical identifiers and carry enough information for clients to refresh precise rows or rollups. They are emitted only after the daemon cache/read model reflects the changed state, matching the shared mutation/event ordering contract. This spec owns coverage-state event payloads, cache/event ordering, coalescing, and targeted invalidation semantics; base websocket connection lifecycle, heartbeat, close-code, and generic reconnect behavior remain existing websocket foundation behavior.

acceptance_criteria.given: a coverage-state-affecting mutation succeeds
acceptance_criteria.when: the daemon broadcasts the resulting event
acceptance_criteria.then:
the event is published on the spec-item domain topic using the
reserved coverage-state event family rather than on a parallel
coverage-only topic

acceptance_criteria.given: an event identifies affected coverage state
acceptance_criteria.then:
the payload identifies affected spec items and criteria by
canonical identifiers sufficient to refresh exactly those rows or
rollups

acceptance_criteria.given: a subscriber receives a coverage-state event
acceptance_criteria.when: it immediately re-fetches the affected coverage state
acceptance_criteria.then: the response reflects the state that caused the event

acceptance_criteria.given:
a source or metadata file changes outside a daemon-served
mutation path
acceptance_criteria.when: watcher fallback invalidation is all the daemon observes
acceptance_criteria.then:
open clients still refresh affected coverage views even if no
precise typed mutation event was available

acceptance_criteria.given: one ingestion or metadata mutation affects many criteria
acceptance_criteria.then:
the daemon can coalesce payloads by affected item/rollup so a
single run does not require one websocket message per criterion

inherited_acs.then: server assigns unique connection ID and sends connected event with session_id

inherited_acs.when: subscribe command sent with topics array
inherited_acs.then: server tracks subscription and sends ack with request_id
server broadcasts event with format {msg_id, seq, timestamp, topic, event, data}
server sends ping frame
connection is closed with code 1001
server pauses non-critical broadcasts until drain event
use code 1000 for clean close, 1001 for timeout, 1011 for error
client resets sequence tracking (lastSeqProcessed = -1) since server generates new sequence

items.title: Coverage Resolution Mutation Interface
items.description:
Coverage resolution actions are one shared mutation surface for
operator responses to backend-computed coverage state. The surface
exposes exactly three actions against an acceptance criterion:
explicit re-verification, spec-text revert, and dispatch-fix request.
Every action is available through equivalent CLI and daemon interfaces,
consumes the current server-computed coverage-state read model, supports
dry-run previews, refuses static/read-only snapshots, and reports its
stored effects and affected coverage-state scopes without requiring a UI
client to reconstruct state or mutation semantics locally.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a caller wants to resolve a coverage-state issue for a specific
acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.when: the coverage resolution mutation interface is enumerated
acceptance_criteria.then:
it exposes exactly the supported action kinds explicit-reverify,
spec-text-revert, and dispatch-fix, each with a stable request and
response shape naming the target item and criterion

acceptance_criteria.given: any coverage resolution action is requested
acceptance_criteria.when: the action validates its target before applying changes
acceptance_criteria.then:
validation reads the current backend coverage-state detail for that
criterion, including freshness comparison findings, and rejects the
action if the current state no longer satisfies that action's
preconditions

acceptance_criteria.given:
the same valid coverage resolution request is submitted through the
CLI and through the daemon route in equivalent projects
acceptance_criteria.then:
both paths produce the same stored effect class, response summary,
affected coverage-state scopes, and diagnostics, differing only in
occurrence-specific ids and timestamps; typed event equivalence is
specified separately by @coverage-resolution-events-compatibility

acceptance_criteria.given: any coverage resolution request is submitted in dry-run mode
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response reports the action that would run, affected items and
criteria, precondition diagnostics, and exact stored effects that
would be attempted, but no verification stamp, spec source edit,
task, shadow commit, cache update, or event broadcast is produced

acceptance_criteria.given: a static-export snapshot or read-only project context
acceptance_criteria.when:
a caller attempts to apply any non-dry-run coverage resolution
mutation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the interface refuses with a read-only/static-mode error and does
not pretend the resolution was stored or dispatched; dry-run preview
requests may still return computed previews when all required data is
available without writing

acceptance_criteria.given: production code handles a coverage resolution action
acceptance_criteria.when: it obtains coverage state for validation, previews, or responses
acceptance_criteria.then:
it uses the current production read path that includes freshness
comparison and cache ownership, and it does not directly derive a
raw read model from partial evidence in a way that bypasses
freshness comparison

inherited_acs.then: returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing
show what would be changed without applying
no files are modified
clear indication that this is a preview
error shown but no state changed
dry run takes precedence (no changes made)
JSON output includes dry_run boolean field
exit code 0
exit code 1
exit code 2
exit code 3
exit code 0 with empty result set
exit code 1 with usage information
exit code 1
exit code meanings documented in code
includes description of what went wrong
includes suggested action to resolve
suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
indicates current state and valid next states
indicates which field/value failed validation
guidance included in structured error object

items.title: Explicit Coverage Reverification
items.description:
A caller can explicitly re-verify a criterion whose current presentation
bucket is re-verify and whose current state has positive non-failing
evidence. The action
writes a verification stamp with re_verification provenance using the
existing verification record store. It records the acting actor,
verification time, optional code commit, and optional producing session;
it never runs tests and never invents evidence for a criterion that has
no current positive basis.

acceptance_criteria.given: a caller requests explicit re-verification for a criterion
acceptance_criteria.when: the current coverage state is checked
acceptance_criteria.then:
the action is accepted only when the criterion is currently in the
re-verify bucket, has positive evidence, and has no latest mapped
failed or errored result; covered, not-yet, and failing criteria are
rejected with guidance to refresh the view, add evidence, or fix
failing tests instead

acceptance_criteria.given: an explicit re-verification request satisfies its preconditions
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion's verification stamp is written or replaced with
provenance re_verification, the resolved actor, the mutation time,
optional comparable commit metadata, and optional session linkage

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion was in the re-verify bucket only because existing
positive evidence was older than comparable freshness sources
acceptance_criteria.when:
explicit re-verification writes a newer stamp and coverage state is
recomputed
acceptance_criteria.then:
the criterion no longer remains in re-verify for that stale cause
unless another current failing, missing, or stale cause still applies

acceptance_criteria.given: a caller explicitly re-verifies a criterion
acceptance_criteria.when: the action executes through either CLI or daemon
acceptance_criteria.then:
the action writes only verification metadata and never runs a test
command, imports framework-native result data, or fabricates an
ingested run

items.title: Coverage Spec Text Revert
items.description:
A caller can resolve a stale-spec-text coverage cause by applying a
content-level inverse edit to the current acceptance criterion text. The
revert uses the focused per-criterion comparison supplied by the coverage
freshness layer, changes only the selected criterion's given/when/then
text through normal kspec mutation machinery, and creates an ordinary
forward shadow commit. It is not a raw git revert and never rewrites
unrelated criteria or operational sidecars.

acceptance_criteria.given: a caller requests a spec-text revert for a criterion
acceptance_criteria.when:
the current coverage state and focused criterion comparison are
checked
acceptance_criteria.then:
the action is accepted only when the current state includes a
stale_spec_text cause and the prior criterion text can be resolved
from project metadata history

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec-text revert request is submitted in dry-run mode
acceptance_criteria.then:
the preview reports the current and prior given/when/then values,
the fields that would change, the prior commit or timestamp used,
and the affected coverage-state scopes without modifying files

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec-text revert request is applied
acceptance_criteria.then:
it applies the inverse content edit through the normal kspec item
mutation path, creates a forward shadow commit describing the
criterion revert, and does not run git revert or mutate the code
repository directly

acceptance_criteria.given:
an item has several acceptance criteria and only one criterion is
targeted for spec-text revert

the criterion text changes after a revert preview or before an
apply request reaches the mutation path
acceptance_criteria.when: the mutation validates the expected current criterion fingerprint
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation refuses rather than overwriting newer text, and the
response tells the caller to refresh the coverage detail

items.title: Coverage Dispatch Fix Request
items.description:
A caller can convert a coverage-state issue into ordinary kspec task
work for an agent or human to fix. The action creates or reuses a task
