that targets the affected item and criterion, includes the current
coverage-state explanation and relevant evidence, and optionally marks
the task dispatch-eligible through existing task automation fields. The
action does not introduce a special coverage-only work queue, does not
bypass plan/task approval policy, and does not spawn a bespoke agent
outside the existing dispatch engine.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a caller requests dispatch-fix for a criterion with a failing,
not-yet, or re-verify coverage issue
acceptance_criteria.then:
an ordinary kspec task exists whose title, spec reference, body,
and metadata identify the targeted item and criterion, the current
presentation bucket, the machine-readable explanation, and the
latest relevant run or freshness evidence when available

acceptance_criteria.given: a dispatch-fix request is accepted
acceptance_criteria.then:
the work is represented by normal task records and existing
automation/dispatch fields, not by a parallel coverage-specific
queue or an ad-hoc daemon agent invocation

acceptance_criteria.given:
an unresolved dispatch-fix task already exists for the same item,
criterion, action kind, and current issue fingerprint
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation finds the existing task by a durable idempotency key
stored in the task body, returns that task, and records no duplicate
task unless the caller explicitly asks to create another one

acceptance_criteria.given:
dispatch-fix is requested in projects with different package names,
test frameworks, file layouts, or result producers
acceptance_criteria.then:
the body uses normalized coverage-state evidence and kspec refs,
and does not assume kynetic-spec paths, Vitest output, package
scripts, or repository-specific branch names

acceptance_criteria.given:
a caller asks the dispatch-fix action to make the task automation
eligible
acceptance_criteria.then:
the task uses the existing automation fields and remains subject
to normal dispatch engine reconciliation, dependencies, and
operator policy; the coverage action itself does not start an
agent outside those mechanisms

items.title: Coverage Resolution Events and Compatibility
items.description:
Successful coverage resolution mutations invalidate the coverage-state
read model and broadcast targeted coverage-state events on the spec-item
domain after the post-mutation state is visible. The implementation is
additive and backward-compatible: projects with no verification or
test-run stores still load, dry-run and static snapshots are read-only,
and consumers that do not understand the new actions can continue to
read coverage state and metadata.

acceptance_criteria.given: any coverage resolution mutation succeeds through the daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: clients receive the resulting coverage-state event
acceptance_criteria.then:
a same-tick refetch of the affected coverage detail or rollup
observes the post-mutation read model

acceptance_criteria.given: a resolution mutation affects one criterion or one item
acceptance_criteria.then:
it identifies affected item and criterion scopes precisely when
known, and uses a project-wide scope only when precision is not
available

acceptance_criteria.given:
equivalent successful resolution mutations arrive through the daemon
REST route and through the daemon command-proxy CLI path
acceptance_criteria.then:
clients observe the same typed coverage-state event family, topic,
affected scopes, and payload schema from both origins

acceptance_criteria.given: a project has no verification record store or no test-run store
acceptance_criteria.when:
resolution actions are previewed, rejected, or applied where their
preconditions are otherwise satisfied
acceptance_criteria.then:
absence is handled as ordinary coverage-state absence; reads do not
materialize stores, and the first action that writes a store follows
the existing first-write materialization contract

acceptance_criteria.given: the coverage resolution mutation plan implementation is complete
acceptance_criteria.when: project validation and focused tests run
acceptance_criteria.then:
they prove CLI/daemon equivalence, dry-run no-effects behavior,
static/read-only refusal, neutral-project behavior, event-after-cache
ordering, and no production bypass of the current-state read path

inherited_acs.then: server assigns unique connection ID and sends connected event with session_id

inherited_acs.when: subscribe command sent with topics array
inherited_acs.then: server tracks subscription and sends ack with request_id
server broadcasts event with format {msg_id, seq, timestamp, topic, event, data}
server sends ping frame
connection is closed with code 1001
server pauses non-critical broadcasts until drain event
use code 1000 for clean close, 1001 for timeout, 1011 for error
client resets sequence tracking (lastSeqProcessed = -1) since server generates new sequence

items.title: Core Primitives AC Backfill
items.description:
Add acceptance criteria to foundational spec items under @core that
currently lack them: ULID system, slug system, reference system,
item types, relationship types, and status lifecycle. These are the
building blocks — their ACs define what correctness means for everything
built on top.

acceptance_criteria.given: All feature and requirement items under @core module
acceptance_criteria.then: Zero "missing acceptance criteria" warnings for @core descendants

acceptance_criteria.given: Each newly added AC
acceptance_criteria.then: It follows given/when/then format with concrete, observable outcomes

items.title: Entity Folder Migration and Compatibility
items.description:
Projects using monolithic plan or review files migrate to folder-backed
storage through `kspec upgrade`. The new project format is `kynetic: "1.2"`
with `task_storage.format: split`, `plan_storage.format: folder`,
`review_storage.format: folder`, and `resource_storage.format:
entity_scoped`. Newer kspec versions that require folder-backed plans or
reviews block incompatible projects with structured guidance instead of
silently reading or rewriting ambiguous data.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new project is created with the kspec version that includes folder-backed plans and reviews
acceptance_criteria.then: The manifest declares `kynetic: "1.2"`, `task_storage.format: split`, `plan_storage.format: folder`, `review_storage.format: folder`, and `resource_storage.format: entity_scoped`

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has monolithic plan or review records
acceptance_criteria.then: The command reports the target manifest fields, directories, sidecar files, index changes, resource manifest changes, warnings, and previous shadow commit without writing them

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has monolithic plan or review records and the user runs `kspec upgrade`
acceptance_criteria.then: Plans and reviews are decomposed into the folder-backed layout, lean indexes are written, the manifest is updated to the 1.2 storage fields, and all changes are committed as one logical shadow mutation

acceptance_criteria.given: A monolithic plan or review record contains existing fields or unknown fields
acceptance_criteria.when: It is migrated to folder-backed storage
acceptance_criteria.then: The migrated entity preserves its ULID, slugs, refs, timestamps, lifecycle state, known fields, and unknown record fields

acceptance_criteria.given: A newer kspec command or daemon route needs folder-backed plan, review, or resource behavior and finds `kynetic` below `1.2` or missing `plan_storage.format: folder` or `review_storage.format: folder`
acceptance_criteria.then: It fails with `entity_storage_incompatible` guidance to run `kspec upgrade` or use a kspec version compatible with the existing manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: A project declares folder-backed plan or review storage but has monolithic records without corresponding entity directories or index entries that do not match folders
acceptance_criteria.when: The relevant entity storage manager initializes
acceptance_criteria.then: It fails with a structured `partial_entity_storage_layout` incompatibility instead of partially reading or rewriting ambiguous data

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon API route needs plan, review, or resource data from an incompatible project
acceptance_criteria.when: The route handles the storage incompatibility
acceptance_criteria.then: The response is HTTP 409 with top-level error `entity_storage_incompatible`, a domain-specific code, migration suggestion, and cache-domain context when available

items.title: Subprocess Argument Literalness
items.description:
Dynamic values that flow into version-control subprocess invocations
— branch names, remote names, revision identifiers, timestamps — are
treated as literal data and are never interpreted by a shell.
Repository metadata is externally influenceable (a cloned repository
controls its own branch and remote names), so queries over that
metadata must treat every dynamic value as literal data.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A repository's checked-out branch has a name containing shell
metacharacters (command substitution, semicolons, quotes,
backticks)
acceptance_criteria.when:
The tool reads current-branch or upstream-tracking metadata for
that repository
acceptance_criteria.then:
The metadata is returned containing the exact literal branch
name, and no command embedded in the name is interpreted or
executed

acceptance_criteria.given:
A version-control query incorporates a dynamic value (branch
name, remote name, revision identifier, or timestamp) containing
characters a shell would interpret (substitution, quoting,
separators, expansion)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The query operates on the exact literal value — it succeeds or
fails based solely on whether the real value exists or is valid,
no embedded command is executed, and no shell interpretation
alters the query's meaning

acceptance_criteria.given:
A version-control query runs against a directory that is not a
repository, or the underlying subprocess fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
The helper reports failure through its documented null, empty,
or default result rather than raising an error

items.title: Subject Revision Vocabulary
items.description:
A review subject's revision number means exactly one thing per
subject type. For plan subjects, it is the ordinal of the first-class
plan revision the review examined. For task, spec, and code subjects,
it derives from the review's recorded subject-refresh sequence: the
version captured at review creation is revision 1, and each recorded
subject refresh increments the ordinal — no dedicated field stores
it. A grouping of sibling reviews against the same subject is a
sequence of review passes ordered by creation; review passes are
never labeled with the revision vocabulary, and revision numbers are
never derived from sibling-review order.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review on a task, spec, or code subject whose subject has been
refreshed N times since the review was created
acceptance_criteria.when: the subject revision ordinal is reported
acceptance_criteria.then:
the ordinal is N+1, derived from the review's recorded
subject-refresh events with no dedicated stored field

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review on a plan subject bound to plan revision N, whatever the
count of recorded subject refreshes on the review
acceptance_criteria.then: the reported value is the bound plan revision ordinal N

acceptance_criteria.given:
a surface or interface presents the set of sibling reviews
against one subject
acceptance_criteria.when: the grouping is labeled and ordered
acceptance_criteria.then:
the grouping is identified as review passes ordered by creation
date and is not labeled with the revision vocabulary

items.title: Folder-Backed Entity Trait
items.description:
An entity that adopts folder-backed storage owns a stable per-entity
directory, keeps list/index projections bounded, preserves unknown files,
and can rebuild its index from authoritative folder contents. This trait is
storage-shape behavior shared by tasks, plans, reviews, and future
folder-backed entities.

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity exists in the system
acceptance_criteria.then: The entity has its own directory named by its full ULID under that entity type's storage root

acceptance_criteria.given: Folder-backed entities exist in a project
acceptance_criteria.when: The entity index is read for listing, filtering, cache warm-up, or dashboard summary surfaces
acceptance_criteria.then: The index contains bounded identity, lifecycle, summary, and relationship fields without embedding full documents, unbounded detail logs, or resource file bytes

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity directory contains unknown files or directories
acceptance_criteria.when: The entity is read or updated
acceptance_criteria.then: Unknown entries are ignored by entity semantics and preserved across writes

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from entity directories
acceptance_criteria.then: The index can be regenerated from entity folders and sidecar metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity is created
acceptance_criteria.then: The entity directory, authoritative sidecar files, and bounded index entry are written in the same logical atomic mutation

acceptance_criteria.given: A persisted folder-backed entity changes any field, count, derived summary, relationship, lifecycle value, or resource metadata that belongs in that entity type's bounded index projection
acceptance_criteria.then: The authoritative sidecar update and the corresponding index entry update are committed as one logical atomic mutation

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from authoritative entity folders
acceptance_criteria.when: an index repair successfully rewrites the index and no later entity mutation occurs
acceptance_criteria.then: A subsequent dry-run rebuild reports no index changes

acceptance_criteria.given: An indexed optional field has equivalent persisted forms such as an omitted value and an empty default collection
acceptance_criteria.when: Index drift is computed or an index repair is verified
acceptance_criteria.then: The semantically equivalent forms are treated as equal and do not produce repeated update drift

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Folder-backed index consistency hardening validated. Evidence: npm run format / format:check / lint / typecheck / build green; focused storage suites pass (tests/task-data-manager.test.ts, tests/plan-rebuild-index.test.ts, tests/review-rebuild-index.test.ts, tests/parser-plans-folder.test.ts, tests/parser-reviews-folder.test.ts, tests/plan-folder-migration.test.ts, tests/review-folder-migration.test.ts, tests/upgrade-folder-storage.test.ts — 199 tests); CLI resource suites pass (tests/cli-plan-resource.test.ts, tests/review-resource-cli.test.ts — 52 tests); built-CLI smoke in a temp project confirms task add / task start / plan add+set / review add+verdict+comment leave the index converged (kspec task|plan|review rebuild-index --dry-run reports no changes after each normal mutator). Normal mutators keep indexes clean without repair across tasks, plans, and reviews.

items.title: Entity-Scoped Local Resources Trait
items.description:
A folder-backed entity that owns rich context can include local resource
files beside its structured data. Resource files live under the owning
entity's `resources/` directory and are declared in `resources.yaml`.
User-authored references use `./resources/<relative-path>`; consumers
receive normalized owner/type/resource metadata instead of arbitrary file
paths.

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity contains a declared local resource
acceptance_criteria.when: A user, UI route, API route, static export, or agent resolves a `./resources/<relative-path>` reference for that entity
acceptance_criteria.then: The reference resolves only to a declared file inside the owning entity's `resources/` tree

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity has one or more declared local resources
acceptance_criteria.when: The entity is read through list, detail, API, static export, or agent-context surfaces
acceptance_criteria.then: Consumers can discover resource id, label, relative path, content type, byte size, content hash, and git version metadata without embedding large file contents in index records

acceptance_criteria.given: A resource reference contains an absolute path, parent traversal, an undeclared resource path, or a symlink escape
acceptance_criteria.when: The resource is imported, attached, served, exported, or resolved
acceptance_criteria.then: The operation is rejected with actionable guidance and no file outside the owning entity resource tree is read or written

acceptance_criteria.given: A local resource is binary or large text
acceptance_criteria.then: The resource remains as a sidecar file and structured records store only bounded metadata or pointers

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed entity with local resources is deleted
acceptance_criteria.then: The entity's owned resource files are removed in the same logical mutation as the entity record

acceptance_criteria.given: A resource version is recorded for later resolution or drift detection
acceptance_criteria.when: The project is stored in git
acceptance_criteria.then: The version metadata uses content hash plus git commit and repository-relative path when a commit is available, without maintaining a separate resource history log inside kspec

acceptance_criteria.given: A static export includes entities with declared local resources
acceptance_criteria.then: Resource files are copied under `assets/resources/<entity-type>/<entity-ulid>/<relative-path>` and exported metadata reports that exported path

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity exists in the system
inherited_acs.then: The entity has its own directory named by its full ULID under that entity type's storage root

inherited_acs.given: Folder-backed entities exist in a project
inherited_acs.when: The entity index is read for listing, filtering, cache warm-up, or dashboard summary surfaces
inherited_acs.then: The index contains bounded identity, lifecycle, summary, and relationship fields without embedding full documents, unbounded detail logs, or resource file bytes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity directory contains unknown files or directories
inherited_acs.when: The entity is read or updated
inherited_acs.then: Unknown entries are ignored by entity semantics and preserved across writes

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from entity directories
inherited_acs.then: The index can be regenerated from entity folders and sidecar metadata
The entity directory, authoritative sidecar files, and bounded index entry are written in the same logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A persisted folder-backed entity changes any field, count, derived summary, relationship, lifecycle value, or resource metadata that belongs in that entity type's bounded index projection
inherited_acs.then: The authoritative sidecar update and the corresponding index entry update are committed as one logical atomic mutation

inherited_acs.given: A folder-backed entity index has drifted from authoritative entity folders
inherited_acs.when: an index repair successfully rewrites the index and no later entity mutation occurs
inherited_acs.then: A subsequent dry-run rebuild reports no index changes

inherited_acs.given: An indexed optional field has equivalent persisted forms such as an omitted value and an empty default collection
inherited_acs.when: Index drift is computed or an index repair is verified
inherited_acs.then: The semantically equivalent forms are treated as equal and do not produce repeated update drift

items.title: Schema and Structure
items.description:
Defines the schema layer: what item types exist, how validation
works, the file structure options, and the status lifecycle
for both specs and individual items.

items.title: Item Type System
items.description:
The type field classifies items. Core types are defined,
but the system is extensible for project-specific types.

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item is created with type set to a supported core item type
acceptance_criteria.when: The item is loaded and validated
acceptance_criteria.then: The type is accepted and the item is classified according to that schema type for downstream commands

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item omits the type field or uses an unsupported type value
acceptance_criteria.then: Validation fails with an error indicating that a recognized item type is required

items.title: Module Type
items.description:
type: module

High-level organizational unit. Groups related features.
Examples: "Authentication", "API", "Data Export"

acceptance_criteria.given: a module-type item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: module structure is validated (must have title, can have features array)

acceptance_criteria.given: a module contains nested features and requirements
acceptance_criteria.then: modules can contain features, features can contain requirements (proper hierarchy enforced)

items.title: Feature Type
items.description:
type: feature

User-facing capability. Something the system does.
Examples: "User Login", "Data Export", "Search"

acceptance_criteria.given: a feature-type item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: feature structure is validated (must have title, can have requirements array, can be nested in modules)

acceptance_criteria.given: a feature has acceptance_criteria defined
acceptance_criteria.when: the feature is displayed or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: AC are shown/validated as testable outcomes for the feature

items.title: Requirement Type
items.description:
type: requirement

Specific, testable requirement. Details how a feature works.
Examples: "Passwords must be hashed with bcrypt"

acceptance_criteria.given: a requirement-type item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: requirement structure is validated (must have title and description, should have implements relationship to parent feature)

acceptance_criteria.given: a requirement specifies testable details
acceptance_criteria.when: the requirement describes how a feature works
acceptance_criteria.then: acceptance criteria can be added to define specific testable conditions

items.title: Constraint Type
items.description:
type: constraint

Limitation or boundary the system must operate within.
Examples: "Must support 10k concurrent users", "Must use PostgreSQL"

acceptance_criteria.given: a constraint-type item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: constraint structure is validated (must have title and description defining system boundary or limitation)

acceptance_criteria.given: a constraint defines a system limitation
acceptance_criteria.when: the constraint is enforced in implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: the system operates within the defined boundary (e.g., 10k concurrent users, must use PostgreSQL)

items.title: Decision Type
items.description:
type: decision

Architectural decision record (ADR-style).
Captures why a choice was made, alternatives considered.
Examples: "Use PostgreSQL for persistence", "Choose YAML over JSON"

acceptance_criteria.given: a decision-type item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: decision structure is validated (must have title, description, should include why the choice was made and alternatives considered)

acceptance_criteria.given: an architectural decision is documented
acceptance_criteria.then: the decision record serves as ADR-style documentation explaining the rationale and context

items.title: Task Type
items.description:
type: task (and subtypes: epic, bug, spike, infra)

Actionable work item. May be derived from spec items
or created standalone. See @tasks module for details.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task-type spec item is created
acceptance_criteria.then: task structure is validated (must have title, can have spec_ref to link to spec item, can have task-specific fields like priority and status)

items.title: Status Lifecycle
items.description:
Items track two dimensions of status:
- maturity: How stable/reviewed is the spec content?
- implementation: Is it built? Tested?

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item defines both status.maturity and status.implementation
acceptance_criteria.when: The item is loaded, displayed, or updated
acceptance_criteria.then: Both status dimensions are preserved and handled independently on the same item

acceptance_criteria.given: A command changes only one status dimension on an item
acceptance_criteria.then: The targeted status dimension changes without overwriting the other status dimension

items.title: Maturity States
items.description:
status.maturity tracks spec content stability:

- draft: Initial capture, may change significantly
- proposed: Ready for review, seeking approval
- stable: Approved, changes require process
- deferred: Intentionally postponed, not abandoned
- deprecated: Superseded or no longer relevant

Lifecycle: draft -> proposed -> stable -> deprecated
            draft -> deferred (for stub specs)
            deferred -> draft (when resuming work)

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec item with maturity: deferred
acceptance_criteria.then: the deferred status is recognized and displayed correctly

acceptance_criteria.given: creating or updating a spec item
acceptance_criteria.then: the value is accepted and persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: a user sets maturity status via CLI to an invalid value
acceptance_criteria.then: the command fails with a clear error listing valid values and no changes are written

items.title: Implementation States
items.description:
status.implementation tracks build progress:

- not_started: No work begun
- in_progress: Currently being implemented
- implemented: Code complete
- verified: Tests pass, reviewed

This is informational; tasks track actual work.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user sets implementation status via CLI to an invalid value (e.g. 'specified')
acceptance_criteria.then: the command fails with a clear error listing valid values and no changes are written

items.title: Cascade Status Updates
items.description: When updating a parent item's implementation status, CLI offers to cascade the update to nested children. Prevents status drift between parent features and child requirements.

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has children and user runs 'kspec item set @parent --implementation implemented'
acceptance_criteria.then: CLI prompts: 'Update N child items to implemented? [y/n]'

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has children, user runs 'kspec item set @parent --implementation implemented', and user responds 'y' to the cascade prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: All child items are updated to 'implemented' and each child update is logged

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has children, user runs 'kspec item set @parent --implementation implemented', and user responds 'n' to the cascade prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: Child items are NOT updated and retain their original status

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has children and user runs 'kspec item set @parent --implementation implemented --json'
acceptance_criteria.then: No cascade prompt is shown and children are NOT automatically updated

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has NO children and user runs 'kspec item set @parent --implementation implemented'
acceptance_criteria.then: No cascade prompt is shown (since there are no children to cascade to)

items.title: File Structure
items.description:
Specs can be organized as single files or directory trees.
The structure is auto-adaptive: start simple, split when needed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project stores its spec as a single manifest file or as a root manifest plus included files
acceptance_criteria.then: Both layouts are supported and produce the same logical spec graph

acceptance_criteria.given: A project begins with a small manifest and later needs to split spec content across files
acceptance_criteria.when: The structure is reviewed for growth
acceptance_criteria.then: The file organization model supports starting simple and moving to a directory-based layout without changing the spec model

items.title: Single File Structure
items.description:
For small projects, everything in one file:

project/
  kynetic.yaml    # Or kynetic.spec.yaml

All items inline in the manifest.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project keeps all spec content inline in a single kynetic.yaml or kynetic.spec.yaml manifest
acceptance_criteria.then: Items are read from that single manifest without requiring includes

items.title: Directory Structure
items.description:
For larger projects, split into directories:

project/
  spec/
    kynetic.yaml       # Root manifest with includes
    modules/
      auth.yaml        # Module-specific items
      api.yaml
    decisions/
      ADR-001.yaml     # Decision records

Uses `includes` field in manifest to reference files.

acceptance_criteria.given: A root manifest declares includes for module or decision files
acceptance_criteria.then: The included files are resolved and merged into one loaded project spec

items.title: Auto-Adaptive Structure
items.description:
The CLI can suggest splitting when specs grow:
- Threshold: ~500 lines or 20+ items
- `kspec split --suggest` shows recommendations
- `kspec split --apply` restructures (with git-friendly renames)

Not MVP - this is a convenience feature.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project grows to roughly 500 lines or 20 or more items
acceptance_criteria.then: The CLI reports recommendations for which spec content should be split into separate files

acceptance_criteria.given: A user accepts the recommended split plan
acceptance_criteria.then: Spec files are reorganized with git-friendly renames and manifest includes are updated to match the new layout

items.title: Manifest File Discovery
items.description:
Defines how kspec discovers manifest files in a project directory.

Discovery algorithm:
1. Check for explicit names: kynetic.yaml, kynetic.spec.yaml (in order)
2. If not found, scan directory for *.yaml files (excluding *.tasks.yaml, *.inbox.yaml, *.meta.yaml, *.runs.yaml)
3. For each candidate, validate it contains a 'kynetic:' version field
4. Return first valid match (alphabetical order for non-explicit names)

This provides backward compatibility while supporting project-specific naming like {slug}.yaml.

acceptance_criteria.given: A directory with kynetic.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns kynetic.yaml path

acceptance_criteria.given: A directory with kynetic.spec.yaml but no kynetic.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns kynetic.spec.yaml path

acceptance_criteria.given: A directory with {slug}.yaml containing kynetic version field
acceptance_criteria.when: Finding the manifest and no kynetic.yaml or kynetic.spec.yaml exists
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns {slug}.yaml path

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple *.yaml files matching pattern
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns first alphabetically after checking explicit names

acceptance_criteria.given: A *.yaml file without kynetic version field
acceptance_criteria.then: File is skipped as invalid manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: Any production code path needs to read the project manifest
acceptance_criteria.then: Must use the manifest discovery API (findManifestInDir/findManifest), never hardcode a filename like kynetic.yaml

items.title: YAML Conventions
items.description:
YAML has pitfalls (Norway problem, type coercion).
These conventions ensure safe, predictable parsing.

acceptance_criteria.given: A manifest contains YAML values that are prone to implicit coercion or formatting ambiguity
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec parses or rewrites the file
acceptance_criteria.then: The YAML conventions preserve predictable values instead of silently changing their meaning

acceptance_criteria.given: A project follows the quoting and literal-block conventions defined under @yaml-conventions
acceptance_criteria.when: Its YAML is round-tripped through kspec
acceptance_criteria.then: The resulting file remains readable and semantically equivalent to the original content

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: The 'yaml' library (v2.8.2+) has a known behavior where block scalars containing whitespace-only lines accumulate extra blank lines on each parse-stringify cycle. This is expected library behavior, not a bug. The writeYamlFilePreserveFormat() function includes a workaround that filters whitespace-only lines from output. See src/parser/yaml.ts for implementation details.

items.title: YAML 1.2 Required
items.description:
Parsers MUST use YAML 1.2 (not 1.1).
YAML 1.1 has dangerous implicit typing:
- "NO" -> false
- "on" -> true
- "3.14" might become float

YAML 1.2 is stricter and safer.

acceptance_criteria.given: a YAML file is parsed by kspec
acceptance_criteria.then: YAML 1.2 parser is used (not YAML 1.1) to avoid dangerous implicit typing

acceptance_criteria.given: YAML content contains strings like 'NO', 'on', 'true'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are treated as strings, not booleans (YAML 1.2 is stricter and safer)

items.title: Quote Ambiguous Strings
items.description:
Strings that might be misinterpreted MUST be quoted:
- "NO", "YES", "true", "false", "on", "off"
- Numbers that should be strings: "3.14", "1.0"
- Special values: "null", "~"

The linter should catch unquoted ambiguous values.

acceptance_criteria.given: YAML content contains ambiguous values like 'NO', 'YES', '3.14', 'null'
acceptance_criteria.then: warnings are emitted for unquoted ambiguous strings (they must be quoted to prevent misinterpretation)

acceptance_criteria.given: YAML content has properly quoted ambiguous values
acceptance_criteria.then: quoted values are accepted without warnings (e.g., '"NO"', '"3.14"', '"null"')

items.title: Multiline with Literal Blocks
items.description:
Multiline strings SHOULD use literal block style (|):

description: |
  This is a multiline description.
  It preserves newlines.

This is cleaner than quoted strings with \n.

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec item has multiline description
acceptance_criteria.then: literal block style (|) is used for cleaner formatting (preserves newlines without \n escape sequences)

acceptance_criteria.given: multiline content uses literal block style
acceptance_criteria.then: newlines are preserved and the content is readable (recommended practice for descriptions and notes)

items.title: Schema Validation
items.description:
Validation ensures specs conform to schema and conventions.
Schema is defined in Zod (source of truth), exported to JSON Schema.

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec with all required fields
acceptance_criteria.then: validation passes with exit code 0

acceptance_criteria.given: a spec with a broken @reference
acceptance_criteria.then: validation fails with error listing broken ref

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has automation=manual_only
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec validate runs and child tasks depend on this parent and are automation=eligible
acceptance_criteria.then: warning issued: manual_only parent @X blocks eligible children @Y, @Z

items.title: Zod Schema Definition
items.description:
Schema is defined using Zod (TypeScript validation library):
- Source of truth for item structure
- z.infer<> generates TypeScript types
- z.toJSONSchema() exports JSON Schema for docs/external tools

Zod chosen for ecosystem size, type inference, JSON Schema export.

acceptance_criteria.given: Manifest or item data is loaded into kspec
acceptance_criteria.then: Zod definitions act as the source of truth for accepted structure and for any validation errors that are reported

items.title: Validation Modes
items.description:
`kspec validate` supports scoped and combinable mode flags.

Mode flags:
- --schema
- --refs
- --orphans
- --alignment
- --completeness
- --conventions
- --staleness
- --skills
- --drift

Behavior:
- No mode flags: run full validation surface
- One mode flag: run only that mode's checks
- Multiple mode flags: run the union of selected checks

CI should run `kspec validate` (full baseline) and may run scoped modes for focused debugging.

acceptance_criteria.given: No mode flags are passed to kspec validate
acceptance_criteria.then: All validation modes execute.

acceptance_criteria.given: A single mode flag (for example --staleness or --completeness) is passed
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the selected mode's checks execute.

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple mode flags are passed
acceptance_criteria.then: Validation executes the union of selected modes and does not run unselected modes.

items.title: Validation Output
items.description:
Validation output includes:
- List of errors (must fix)
- List of warnings (should fix)
- Summary counts

JSON output (--json) for programmatic consumption:
{ "valid": false, "errors": [...], "warnings": [...] }

acceptance_criteria.given: Validation finds schema, reference, or completeness issues
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec validate finishes in text mode
acceptance_criteria.then: Output lists the errors, warnings, and summary counts needed to understand the result

acceptance_criteria.given: A user runs kspec validate --json
acceptance_criteria.then: Stdout contains valid JSON with validity, errors, and warnings fields for programmatic consumers

items.title: Spec Completeness Validation
items.description: Validation checks for spec quality beyond schema conformance. Warns about incomplete specs to help maintain spec-as-source-of-truth principle.

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item exists without acceptance_criteria
acceptance_criteria.then: A warning is shown: 'Item @slug has no acceptance criteria'

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec item exists without a description
acceptance_criteria.then: A warning is shown: 'Item @slug has no description'

acceptance_criteria.given: A parent item has implementation:implemented but children have not_started
acceptance_criteria.then: A warning is shown about status inconsistency between parent and children

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple completeness issues exist
acceptance_criteria.then: A summary is shown with counts by issue type (e.g., '3 items missing AC, 2 status mismatches')

items.title: AC Annotation Integrity Reporting
items.description:
AC coverage annotations are only valid when they point at a spec item
or trait acceptance criterion that exists. Invalid annotations are
reported as repairable completeness findings and do not provide
coverage credit.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A configured coverage scan path contains an AC annotation whose
target reference cannot be resolved
acceptance_criteria.then:
An invalid-annotation finding identifies the target reference and
the source location

acceptance_criteria.given:
A configured coverage scan path contains an AC annotation whose
target resolves to something other than a spec item or trait
acceptance_criteria.then:
An invalid-annotation finding identifies the target as an invalid
coverage target and reports the source location

acceptance_criteria.given:
A configured coverage scan path contains an AC annotation whose
target spec or trait exists but whose AC id does not exist on that
target
acceptance_criteria.then:
An invalid-annotation finding identifies the target reference, the
missing AC id, and the source location

acceptance_criteria.given:
A configured coverage scan path contains an AC annotation that
names a spec item or trait with acceptance criteria but does not
name specific AC ids
acceptance_criteria.then: The annotation does not count as coverage for that target

acceptance_criteria.given: A configured coverage scan path contains a coverage-claiming AC annotation (one without a not-applicable marker) that names an existing spec or trait AC
acceptance_criteria.then: The named AC is treated as covered by that annotation

acceptance_criteria.given: A configured coverage scan path contains an AC annotation with a malformed ac-prefixed acceptance criterion token
acceptance_criteria.then: An invalid-annotation finding identifies the malformed token and the source location

notes.author: Jacob Chapel
notes.content: Post-implementation validation found that the remaining non-ac-prefixed acceptance criterion ids and matching annotations prevent this behavior from being fully trusted in practice. Marked implementation in_progress while @task-normalize-ac-ids-and-annotations is pending; restore implemented/verified after that task normalizes ids and validation confirms explicit annotations are no longer misclassified as blanket refs.

items.title: Alignment Guidance Enhancement
items.description: Alignment guidance shown during task workflows includes reminder about test coverage for specs with acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has spec_ref linking to a spec with acceptance_criteria
acceptance_criteria.when: Alignment guidance is shown (e.g., during task complete)
acceptance_criteria.then: Guidance includes: 'Linked spec has N acceptance criteria - consider test coverage'

items.title: Validation Task Data Source
items.description:
Validation uses the same task data model that normal kspec consumers
use, so reference, schema, and completeness findings cover every
persisted task record regardless of the task storage layout.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project contains persisted task records in the supported task
storage layout
acceptance_criteria.then: Every persisted task record is included in the validation task set

acceptance_criteria.given:
A persisted task contains a field that validation treats as a
reference
acceptance_criteria.then:
The reference contributes to validation findings with the task as
the source

acceptance_criteria.given: A persisted task record cannot be parsed as a valid task
acceptance_criteria.then:
A validation finding identifies the affected task record instead
of silently omitting it

items.title: Versioning
items.description:
Two version numbers: format version and spec version.
Git provides history; tags provide baselines.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project defines format version, spec version, and git tag baselines
acceptance_criteria.then: Those three version signals are treated as distinct concerns for schema compatibility, spec release tracking, and historical comparison

items.title: Format Version
items.description:
The `kynetic` field in manifest declares format version:

kynetic: "1.0"

Tools use this to know which schema to apply.
Breaking format changes bump major version.

acceptance_criteria.given: A manifest declares a kynetic format version
acceptance_criteria.then: The declared format version determines which schema compatibility rules are applied to that file

items.title: Spec Version
items.description:
The `project.version` field tracks the spec's own version:

project:
  version: "1.2.3"

Follows semver:
- MAJOR: Breaking requirement changes
- MINOR: New requirements, non-breaking clarifications
- PATCH: Typos, editorial

acceptance_criteria.given: A manifest declares project.version as a semver string
acceptance_criteria.when: The project spec is loaded or displayed
acceptance_criteria.then: That version is preserved as the spec own-version separate from the manifest format version

items.title: Git Tag Baselines
items.description:
Use annotated git tags for spec baselines:

git tag -a spec-v1.0.0 -m "Initial stable release"

Enables: kspec diff --since spec-v1.0.0

acceptance_criteria.given: A repository has annotated tags marking spec baselines
acceptance_criteria.when: A user compares spec history against a baseline tag
acceptance_criteria.then: The tagged revision can be used as the comparison point for spec diffs

items.title: Data Format Forward Compatibility
items.description:
Defines the forward-compatibility contract layered on the project
manifest's declared format version: each released version of the
tool declares a maximum supported format version it can read and
write, and project data declaring a newer format version is refused
rather than operated on.

Decision semantics:

- Stamping: the format version is written to the project manifest at
  initialization and advanced only by the upgrade flow — never
  implicitly by ordinary commands.
- Checking: the declared format version is compared against the
  maximum supported version at two points during context
  initialization. First, the locally declared version is checked
  before any project data is read, mutated, or synchronized —
  including any background synchronization performed as a side
  effect of context initialization. Second, when that
  synchronization imports project data, the declared version of the
  imported data is checked again before any project data is read or
  mutated, so data upgraded elsewhere to a newer format is refused
  by the same invocation that imported it. The imported
  synchronization itself is permitted — it transfers data already
  authored elsewhere; the guarantee defended at both points is that
  data declaring a newer format is never read or mutated. The check
  applies uniformly to CLI commands and daemon-served requests.
- Newer than supported: the operation refuses with a deterministic
  error code reserved for this condition. The refusal names both the
  project's declared format version and the running tool's maximum
  supported format version, directs the user to upgrade their kspec
  installation (or use the newer version that wrote the data), and
  guarantees no project data was modified.
- Unrecognized version values: a declared format version that cannot
  be interpreted as a known version is refused as incompatible with
  the literal value named in the error. It is never silently treated
  as the oldest format.
- Diagnostic exemption: the project health diagnostic is the sole
  surface that does not refuse — it completes read-only and reports
  the version mismatch with upgrade guidance.
- Older than supported: not refused by this contract. Existing
  per-domain storage-compatibility gates continue to govern older
  formats (lenient reads where safe, refusal with upgrade guidance
  where the operation requires a newer layout).
- A manifest with no declared format version retains its existing
  legacy interpretation and is not affected by this contract.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project manifest locally declares a format version greater
than the running tool's maximum supported format version
acceptance_criteria.when:
Any command that reads or mutates project data, other than the
project health diagnostic, initializes project context
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command refuses with a deterministic error code reserved for
newer-than-supported format versions; the error names both the
project's declared version and the tool's maximum supported
version, includes guidance to upgrade the tool installation, and
no project data is modified — including by any synchronization
performed as part of context initialization

items.title: Schema-Derived Type Definitions
items.description:
Every surface that references a constrained type — CLI option help
text, API route schemas, runtime validation arrays, type assertions
— must derive its definition from the canonical schema rather than
maintaining a separate copy. When multiple representations of the
same type exist, they drift independently and create silent
inconsistencies.

This includes hardcoded arrays used for validation, API framework
type definitions, CLI help strings that list valid values, and
type assertions that enumerate possible values. All of these must
trace back to a single canonical schema definition.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A runtime validation check references a set of valid values
for a type that has a canonical schema definition
acceptance_criteria.then:
They are derived from the canonical schema rather than
maintained as a separate hardcoded array or set

acceptance_criteria.given: An API endpoint defines the allowed values for a field
acceptance_criteria.then:
They are derived from the canonical schema definition,
not hardcoded independently

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI command's help text lists valid values for an option
acceptance_criteria.then:
The listed values are derived from the canonical schema so
they stay in sync when the schema changes

acceptance_criteria.given:
Two or more schema definitions exist for the same semantic
concept
acceptance_criteria.then:
They share a single source definition or one is explicitly
derived from the other, with no independent incompatible
copies

inherited_acs.given: Any input surface accepts a field with a defined type constraint
inherited_acs.when: The provided value does not satisfy the constraint
inherited_acs.then:
The operation is rejected before any data is persisted or
state is mutated

inherited_acs.given: An input validation error occurs for a constrained field
inherited_acs.when: The error is reported to the caller
inherited_acs.then:
The message includes the set of valid alternatives for the
field, not just the field name and invalid value (extends
@trait-error-guidance ac-5 which requires identifying the
field/value but not listing valid alternatives)

inherited_acs.given: A field's type constraint is defined in a canonical schema
inherited_acs.then:
The validation is derived from that schema definition rather
than a separately maintained check

items.title: Task System
items.description:
Tasks are first-class items that track work. They can be derived
from spec items or created standalone. The task system enables
kspec to function as a work tracker, not just a spec format.

items.title: Task Types
items.description:
Tasks have types that indicate their nature and relationship
to spec items. Some types expect spec linkage; others don't.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is created or derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the type is stored as one of the supported task classifications: task, epic, bug, spike, or infra

items.title: Task Type - task
items.description:
type: task

Atomic unit of work. May be spec-derived or standalone.
Default task type if not specified.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with type 'task' is created
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted as atomic unit of work with standard task lifecycle (pending -> in_progress -> completed)

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has no type specified
acceptance_criteria.when: the task is created or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: it defaults to type 'task'

items.title: Task Type - epic
items.description:
type: epic

Groups related tasks. Often derived from features.
Can have subtasks that depends_on it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with type 'epic' is created
acceptance_criteria.when: other tasks reference it via depends_on
acceptance_criteria.then: the epic serves as a container grouping related subtasks

acceptance_criteria.given: an epic is often derived from a feature
acceptance_criteria.then: subtasks can be created with depends_on relationships to the epic

items.title: Task Type - bug
items.description:
type: bug

Defect fix. May or may not link to spec item.
Used for issues found after implementation.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with type 'bug' is created
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted as defect fix work (may or may not have spec_ref depending on whether it reveals spec gap)

acceptance_criteria.given: a bug is found after implementation
acceptance_criteria.when: it doesn't correspond to existing spec item
acceptance_criteria.then: bug task can be created standalone without spec_ref

items.title: Task Type - spike
items.description:
type: spike

Research or investigation task. Time-boxed exploration.
Output is knowledge, not code.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with type 'spike' is created
acceptance_criteria.when: the task is time-boxed research or investigation
acceptance_criteria.then: it is validated as spike with expected output being knowledge/findings, not code

acceptance_criteria.given: a spike task is completed
acceptance_criteria.then: the note documents findings and recommendations (what was learned)

items.title: Task Type - infra
items.description:
type: infra

Infrastructure or tooling work. Not spec-derived.
Examples: CI setup, dependency updates, tooling.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with type 'infra' is created
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted as infrastructure/tooling work without requiring spec_ref (examples: CI setup, dependency updates)

items.title: Task States
items.description:
Tasks have explicit states (set via commands) and derived
states (computed from dependencies). The state machine
controls valid transitions.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task in pending state
acceptance_criteria.then: task transitions to in_progress

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with depends_on another pending task
acceptance_criteria.then: the dependent task is NOT in the ready list

acceptance_criteria.given: a task blocked by dependencies
acceptance_criteria.then: task becomes ready (unblocked)

items.title: State - pending
items.description:
status: pending

Initial state. Work not yet started.
Transitions: start -> in_progress, cancel -> cancelled

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has status pending
acceptance_criteria.when: a user runs kspec task start or kspec task cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the task transitions to in_progress or cancelled respectively

items.title: State - in_progress
items.description:
status: in_progress

Work actively being done.
Transitions:
- complete -> completed
- block -> blocked
- cancel -> cancelled

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has status in_progress
acceptance_criteria.when: a user runs kspec task submit, kspec task block, or kspec task cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the task transitions to pending_review, blocked, or cancelled respectively

items.title: State - blocked
items.description:
status: blocked

Work paused due to blocker.
Can be set manually (external blocker) or auto-computed
when depends_on items aren't completed.

Transitions: unblock -> in_progress (or pending)

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is blocked
acceptance_criteria.when: the blocker is cleared and the task is unblocked
acceptance_criteria.then: the task returns to the status it had before being blocked

items.title: State - completed
items.description:
status: completed

Work finished successfully. Terminal state.
Should include closed_reason describing outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is marked completed
acceptance_criteria.then: the task remains in the terminal completed state and stores a closed_reason describing the outcome

items.title: State - cancelled
items.description:
status: cancelled

Work abandoned. Terminal state.
Should include closed_reason explaining why.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is cancelled
acceptance_criteria.then: the task remains in the terminal cancelled state and stores a closed_reason explaining why work stopped

items.title: Derived State - ready
items.description:
"ready" is a computed view, not stored state:
ready = (pending OR needs_work) + all depends_on completed + no blockers

`kspec tasks ready` returns tasks in this state.
This is the primary query for "what can I work on?"

needs_work tasks are sorted before pending — fix cycles take priority.

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks exist in pending, needs_work, blocked, and unmet-dependency states
acceptance_criteria.then: only pending or needs_work tasks with completed dependencies and no blockers are returned, with needs_work tasks listed before pending tasks

items.description: The needs_work status represents 'reviewer found issues, worker must fix' - enabling a fix cycle between reviewer and worker in the ralph automation loop. items.description: Cancelling a task removes stale downstream dependency links and records that cleanup as part of the same cancellation operation. This keeps ready semantics unchanged while repairing the task graph when abandoned work is removed.

items.title: Task Schema
items.description:
Tasks are items with additional fields for work tracking.
Key principle: don't duplicate spec content, reference it.

acceptance_criteria.then: the task keeps execution metadata plus a spec_ref link instead of duplicating the linked spec's description and acceptance criteria

items.title: Spec Reference Field
items.description:
spec_ref: "@feature-slug"

Links task to the spec item it implements.
The spec item has the full description, acceptance
criteria, etc. Task adds only execution metadata.

Optional for free-form tasks (bug, infra).

acceptance_criteria.given: a task implements a spec item or represents free-form work
acceptance_criteria.then: spec_ref points to the linked spec item when present and may be omitted for free-form bug or infra tasks

items.title: Work Metadata Fields
items.description:
Task-specific fields for work tracking:

- priority: 1-5 (1 highest) or high/medium/low
- complexity: Relative size estimate (fibonacci or 1-5)
- assignee: Who's working on it (optional)
- blocked_by: Manual blockers (strings, not refs)
- closed_reason: Why completed/cancelled

These fields don't exist on regular spec items.

acceptance_criteria.given: task-specific metadata is present
acceptance_criteria.then: priority, complexity, assignee, blocked_by, and closed_reason are accepted on tasks without becoming required fields on regular spec items

items.title: Task Timestamps
items.description:
Auto-populated timestamps:

- created_at: When task was created
- started_at: When status became in_progress
- completed_at: When status became completed/cancelled

Format: ISO 8601 (2025-01-14T10:00:00Z)

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is created, started, or completed or cancelled
acceptance_criteria.when: task lifecycle commands persist the change
acceptance_criteria.then: created_at, started_at, and completed_at are auto-populated as ISO 8601 timestamps at the matching lifecycle transition

items.title: VCS References
items.description:
vcs_refs links tasks to git branches/commits/tags:

vcs_refs:
  - ref: "feat/user-login"
    type: branch
  - ref: "abc123"
    type: commit

Minimal schema, extensible as needed.

acceptance_criteria.given: vcs_refs are attached to a task
acceptance_criteria.then: each vcs_refs entry stores a git reference string and a type such as branch, commit, or tag

items.title: Task Derivation
items.description:
Tasks can be derived from spec items via explicit command.
Not automatic - you run `kspec derive @feature` when ready.

acceptance_criteria.given: a feature without derived tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: a task is created with spec_ref pointing to feature

acceptance_criteria.given: a derived task exists for a feature
acceptance_criteria.then: no duplicate is created (idempotent)

items.title: Derive Command
items.description:
kspec derive <ref>     # Derive task for single item
kspec derive --all    # Derive for all items without tasks

Creates task with:
- title: "Implement <item title>" (adjustable)
- type: task (or epic for features with children)
- spec_ref: @<item>
- derivation: auto

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec derive @item or kspec derive --all
acceptance_criteria.when: derivation creates work for an uncovered item
acceptance_criteria.then: the created task includes a derived title, task type, spec_ref, and derivation metadata

items.title: Derivation Idempotency
items.description:
Derivation is idempotent:
- If task with spec_ref to item exists, skip creation
- Use --force to create additional task anyway
- Useful for re-running derive without duplicates

acceptance_criteria.given: a task already exists for an item's spec_ref
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec derive is run again without --force
acceptance_criteria.then: no duplicate task is created for that spec item

items.title: Task Notes
items.description:
Notes are append-only log entries on tasks. Track progress,
findings, blockers. Critical for agent handoff.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task in progress
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec task note @task "Found issue with X"
acceptance_criteria.then: note is appended to task's notes array

acceptance_criteria.given: an earlier note that's wrong
acceptance_criteria.then: new note links to old one (old preserved)

items.title: Note Structure
items.description:
Note entries have:
- _ulid: Entry identifier
- created_at: Timestamp
- author: Who added it
- content: The note text (multiline)
- supersedes: ULID of entry this corrects (optional)

Notes are never deleted, only superseded.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is added to a task
acceptance_criteria.then: the entry records its ULID, created_at timestamp, author, content, and optional supersedes reference while preserving earlier notes

items.title: Note CLI Commands
items.description:
kspec task note <ref> "message"      # Add note
kspec task note <ref> --supersedes <id> "correction"
kspec task notes <ref>               # Show notes log

JSON output available for all commands.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec task note @task "message" or kspec task notes @task
acceptance_criteria.then: the note is appended to the task log and the notes command returns the append-only note history

items.title: Task Todos
items.description:
Todos are lightweight checklist items that emerge during work.
Start simple; promote to full tasks when complex.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task in progress
acceptance_criteria.then: todo is added to task's todos array

acceptance_criteria.given: a todo that's complex
acceptance_criteria.then: a new task is created, todo marked promoted_to

items.title: Todo Structure
items.description:
Todo entries have:
- id: Local numeric ID (within task)
- text: The todo description
- done: Boolean
- done_at: When marked done (if done)
- added_at: When created
- added_by: Who added it
- promoted_to: @ref if promoted to task (optional)

acceptance_criteria.given: a todo is added to a task and later marked done or not done
acceptance_criteria.then: it records a local id, text, done state, timestamps, author, and keeps the same identity across later status changes

items.title: Todo CLI Commands
items.description:
kspec todo add <ref> "text"     # Add todo
kspec todo done <ref> <id>      # Mark complete
kspec todo promote <ref> <id>   # Promote to task
kspec task todos <ref>          # List todos

Todos are for quick capture; promote when complex.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec task todo add, kspec task todo done, kspec task todo undone, or kspec task todos
acceptance_criteria.then: the task todo list is updated and the current todo entries can be listed from the task

items.title: Task Storage
items.description:
Tasks are stored alongside or separate from specs.
Auto-adaptive: start alongside, separate when volume grows.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project uses the task system
acceptance_criteria.then: the system supports storing them either alongside module specs or in a dedicated tasks directory without changing task semantics

items.title: Storage - Separate Directory
items.description:
For larger projects, separate tasks directory:

spec/
  modules/
    auth.yaml
tasks/
  backlog.yaml
  active.yaml
  archive/
    2025-01.yaml

Separates concerns, enables archiving.

acceptance_criteria.given: a larger project uses separate task storage
acceptance_criteria.when: tasks are persisted under tasks backlog, active, or archive files
acceptance_criteria.then: task data is stored separately from module spec files and can be archived independently

items.title: Task Queries
items.description:
The key task query: "what can I work on?"
`kspec tasks ready` is the primary interface for agents and humans.

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks with various states and dependencies
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks that are pending with met dependencies shown

acceptance_criteria.given: ready tasks exist
acceptance_criteria.then: highest priority ready task returned

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple ready tasks exist with the same priority
acceptance_criteria.then: tasks are ordered by creation time ascending (oldest first within priority tier)

items.title: Ready Tasks Query
items.description:
kspec tasks ready

Returns tasks where:
- status = pending OR needs_work
- all depends_on tasks are completed
- no manual blocked_by entries
- sorted: needs_work first, then pending (fix cycles take priority)

This is THE command for "what can I work on next?"

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks have mixed statuses, blockers, and dependencies
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns only ready tasks and orders needs_work ahead of pending

inherited_acs.given: A system evaluates whether a task can be picked up for work
inherited_acs.then: Only tasks with status pending or needs_work are considered ready. All other statuses (in_progress, pending_review, completed, blocked, cancelled) are excluded.

inherited_acs.given: A task has depends_on references to other tasks
inherited_acs.then: All depends_on tasks must have status completed. If any dependency has a non-completed status (pending, in_progress, needs_work, pending_review, blocked, cancelled), the task is not ready.

inherited_acs.given: A task has a blocked_by array
inherited_acs.then: The blocked_by array must be empty. Any entry in blocked_by prevents readiness regardless of other conditions.

inherited_acs.given: A consumer applies additional filters (automation status, tags, priority thresholds)
inherited_acs.then: Consumer-specific filters are applied on top of base readiness, never instead of it. A task must pass base readiness before any consumer filter is evaluated.

items.title: Next Task Query
items.description:
kspec tasks next

Returns single highest-priority ready task.
Sorting: priority (asc) -> created_at (asc)

Useful for agents: "give me one thing to do"

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple ready tasks exist
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns the single ready task with the highest priority, breaking ties by oldest created_at first

inherited_acs.given: A system evaluates whether a task can be picked up for work
inherited_acs.then: Only tasks with status pending or needs_work are considered ready. All other statuses (in_progress, pending_review, completed, blocked, cancelled) are excluded.

inherited_acs.given: A task has depends_on references to other tasks
inherited_acs.then: All depends_on tasks must have status completed. If any dependency has a non-completed status (pending, in_progress, needs_work, pending_review, blocked, cancelled), the task is not ready.

inherited_acs.given: A task has a blocked_by array
inherited_acs.then: The blocked_by array must be empty. Any entry in blocked_by prevents readiness regardless of other conditions.

inherited_acs.given: A consumer applies additional filters (automation status, tags, priority thresholds)
inherited_acs.then: Consumer-specific filters are applied on top of base readiness, never instead of it. A task must pass base readiness before any consumer filter is evaluated.

items.title: Task Query Filters
items.description:
kspec tasks list [filters]

Filters:
- --status <state>    # By status
- --type <type>       # By task type
- --tag <tag>         # By tag
- --assignee <who>    # By assignee
- --spec-ref <ref>    # By linked spec item

All queries support --json output.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user runs kspec tasks list with --status, --type, --tag, or --meta-ref and optionally --json
acceptance_criteria.then: only matching tasks are returned and JSON output remains available for the filtered result set

items.title: Multi-Value Status Filter
items.description:
The --status filter on list commands should accept multiple values via
comma-separated syntax or repeated flags. The backend ItemIndex.query()
already supports TaskStatus[] -- this closes the gap in the CLI layer.
Agents currently pipe through grep to filter by multiple statuses.
tasks list uses TaskStatus values (pending, in_progress, pending_review,
blocked, completed, cancelled) while item list uses ImplementationStatus
values (not_started, in_progress, implemented, verified). Validation must
use the correct enum per command.

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending_review
acceptance_criteria.when: A comma-separated status value is provided
acceptance_criteria.then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress --status pending_review
acceptance_criteria.when: The --status flag is provided multiple times
acceptance_criteria.then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned (same as comma-separated)

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status pending
acceptance_criteria.when: A single status value is provided
acceptance_criteria.then: Behavior is unchanged from current -- only tasks with that status are returned

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status invalid_value
acceptance_criteria.when: An invalid TaskStatus name is provided
acceptance_criteria.then: Error message lists valid TaskStatus values and exits non-zero

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec item list --status invalid_value
acceptance_criteria.when: An invalid ImplementationStatus name is provided
acceptance_criteria.then: Error message lists valid ImplementationStatus values and exits non-zero

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec item list --status implemented,verified
acceptance_criteria.when: Multi-value status is used on item list with ImplementationStatus values
acceptance_criteria.then: Same comma-separated and repeated-flag behavior works for spec item listing

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending --json
acceptance_criteria.then: JSON output contains only tasks matching the specified statuses

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress, (trailing comma)
acceptance_criteria.when: A trailing or leading comma produces an empty string after split
acceptance_criteria.then: Empty strings are silently ignored, only valid status values are used

inherited_acs.then: only items with matching status shown
only items with matching tag shown
output shows at most N items
output skips first N items
output shows items matching all filters (AND logic)
empty list shown with informative message
summary shows total matching items and filter state
outputs only the total number of matching items as a plain integer (no item details); ignores --limit and --offset; in JSON mode outputs {"count": N}
output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
output includes all data available in human-readable mode
error is returned as JSON object with error field
references use @ prefix consistently
timestamps use ISO 8601 format
--json takes precedence over other format options

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run
acceptance_criteria.then: shows recommendation (review_for_eligible, needs_review, or manual_only)

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run
acceptance_criteria.then: shows summary counts of recommendations at end

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation @task-ref is run
acceptance_criteria.when: a specific task reference is provided
acceptance_criteria.then: assesses only that task

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation @task-ref is run
acceptance_criteria.then: returns non-zero exit code

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task
acceptance_criteria.when: task has spec_ref pointing to resolvable spec
acceptance_criteria.then: has_spec_ref criterion passes

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task
acceptance_criteria.then: has_spec_ref criterion fails

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task with spec_ref
acceptance_criteria.when: linked spec has at least one acceptance criterion
acceptance_criteria.then: spec_has_acs criterion passes

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task
acceptance_criteria.then: spec_has_acs criterion is skipped (neutral)

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task
acceptance_criteria.then: not_spike criterion passes

acceptance_criteria.given: assessing a task
acceptance_criteria.then: not_spike criterion fails

acceptance_criteria.given: computing recommendation
acceptance_criteria.then: recommends manual_only regardless of other criteria

acceptance_criteria.given: computing recommendation
acceptance_criteria.when: spec_ref is missing or spec has no ACs
acceptance_criteria.then: recommends needs_review

acceptance_criteria.given: computing recommendation
acceptance_criteria.when: all criteria pass (has spec, has ACs, not spike)
acceptance_criteria.then: recommends review_for_eligible (agent/human must verify spec/AC adequacy)

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: applies only obvious cases: spikes -> manual_only, missing criteria -> needs_review

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: does NOT mark task as eligible (requires agent/human review)

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: adds note to task explaining the assessment

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: note includes reason explaining what is missing

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: task appears with review_for_eligible recommendation but automation field is NOT modified

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --dry-run is run

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --dry-run --auto is run
acceptance_criteria.then: shows auto mode changes without applying them

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --json is run
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs structured JSON with criteria details for each task

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation --json is run
acceptance_criteria.then: JSON includes summary counts of recommendations

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs 'No unassessed tasks' message

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run without --all
acceptance_criteria.then: tasks already marked eligible/needs_review/manual_only are skipped

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec tasks assess automation is run
acceptance_criteria.then: non-pending tasks (completed, cancelled, in_progress, blocked) are excluded

items.title: Task Activity Timeline
items.description: Unified chronological view of all activity on a task derived from stored history entries and linked review records. State transitions, notes, review events, and submission changes are merged into a single timeline. Recent activity shown by default in task get; full history available via --activity flag.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has had state transitions recorded via stored history entries
acceptance_criteria.then: the most recent activity entries are shown after the notes section, including state changes, notes, and review events in reverse chronological order, capped at a reasonable default count

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has state transitions, notes, and linked review records

review events (creation, verdict submission, thread resolution,

acceptance_criteria.then:
each activity entry is a structured object with type, timestamp,

inherited_acs.then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
output includes all data available in human-readable mode
error is returned as JSON object with error field

items.title: Task Activity Git Query
items.description:
The mechanism for deriving task activity from shadow branch git history.
Queries all commits that modified a task's data block to extract the
complete history of state transitions and mutations, including manual
edits and batch operations.

acceptance_criteria.when: the activity query runs against the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then: all commits that modified the task's data are returned, including the creation commit, state transitions, notes, and field changes, regardless of commit message content

acceptance_criteria.then: only commits that affected that task's data are included; changes to other tasks in the same file are excluded

acceptance_criteria.given: a commit message follows the shadow branch auto-commit format

the operation type (start, submit, complete, note, block, etc.)

acceptance_criteria.when: the raw commit data is normalized into activity entries
acceptance_criteria.then: each meaningful field change is translated into a typed activity entry that identifies what changed, such as state transitions, notes added, review linkage, or submission updates

items.title: Review Fix-Cycle Diff Context
items.description:
When a reviewer examines work after a fix cycle, they receive context
about what changed since the prior review. The review record stores
the commit it examined so diffs can be computed across cycles.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review record is created for a task with dispatch workspace
metadata available
acceptance_criteria.then:
the review record stores the examined commit (the HEAD of the
detached review snapshot) as metadata on the record; reviews
created without workspace context leave this field null

acceptance_criteria.given:
a prior closed review record with an examined_commit exists
for the same task
acceptance_criteria.when: a new review cycle begins and the reviewer receives orientation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the reviewer prompt includes a summary of what changed between
the prior review's examined commit and the current submission HEAD

acceptance_criteria.given: diffs are requested between review cycles
acceptance_criteria.when: the merge target or prior examined commit is unreachable
acceptance_criteria.then: the diff is gracefully omitted with a note rather than erroring

items.title: Per-Task Directory Storage
items.description:
Each task is stored as its own directory, with separate files for
core data and notes. A lean index file contains only the fields
needed for listing and filtering. Task semantics, CLI surface, and
schema types visible to consumers are unchanged.

items.title: Per-Task Core Data File
items.description:
tasks/<ulid>/task.yaml contains the complete task record excluding
notes. This includes all current field values plus an append-only
history section that records field-level changes with metadata.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task's mutable field is modified
acceptance_criteria.then:
The current field value is updated in-place and a history entry
is appended recording the timestamp, author, command that made
the change, the field name, the previous value, and the new value

The history section provides a complete audit trail of all field
