and new values

acceptance_criteria.given: A task file contains fields not defined in the task schema
acceptance_criteria.when: The task is mutated and written back to disk
acceptance_criteria.then: The unknown fields are preserved in the written file

items.title: Per-Task Notes File
items.description:
tasks/<ulid>/notes.yaml contains the task's append-only notes array,
stored separately from core task data so that note growth does not
affect task field reads or history.

acceptance_criteria.given: A note is added to a task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The note is appended to tasks/<ulid>/notes.yaml; the task.yaml
file is not modified

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has no notes
acceptance_criteria.then:
The file contains an empty notes array or does not exist; both
are treated as zero notes

acceptance_criteria.given: A note supersedes a previous note
acceptance_criteria.then:
The new note is appended with a supersedes reference to the
original, consistent with existing note supersession semantics

items.title: In-File Task Activity
items.description:
Task activity is recorded directly in the per-task files rather than
reconstructed from version control history. Field changes are
recorded in task.yaml's history section. Note additions are evident
from notes.yaml entries. The activity timeline is assembled from
file contents alone.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task's activity timeline is requested
acceptance_criteria.then:
Field changes come from the task's stored history entries and
note events come from stored note entries; the timeline is
assembled from persisted data without version control queries

acceptance_criteria.given:
A task has been through multiple status transitions, note additions,
priority changes, and review linkages
acceptance_criteria.when: The full activity timeline is requested
acceptance_criteria.then:
All changes are present in chronological order with timestamps,
authors, commands, and field-level details

acceptance_criteria.given: A task created before the storage migration has no history entries
acceptance_criteria.then: the activity timeline is empty until in-file history or notes exist; no best-effort recovery from version control history is attempted

items.title: Task Data Manager
items.description:
A single module that owns all task storage operations. All consumers
(CLI, API, batch, automation) read and write tasks exclusively
through this module. It encapsulates the storage format behind a
consistent interface so callers provide mutations, not I/O strategy.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any consumer needs to read or write task data
acceptance_criteria.when: It interacts with the task data manager
acceptance_criteria.then: Callers do not know or care about the underlying storage format

acceptance_criteria.given: A consumer requests a list of tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: Only index data is read; per-task detail files are not accessed

acceptance_criteria.given: A consumer requests full details for a specific task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The manager assembles the complete task from index and per-task
files transparently

acceptance_criteria.given: A consumer provides a task mutation
acceptance_criteria.then:
All affected files, locking, and shadow branch commits are
handled by the manager as a single coordinated operation

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple mutations target different tasks concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: Non-overlapping mutations proceed without contention

acceptance_criteria.given: A mutation affects both indexed and non-indexed data
acceptance_criteria.then:
All writes happen within a single atomic operation that either
all succeed or all roll back

acceptance_criteria.given: The task data manager is initialized
acceptance_criteria.then: The split per-task directory format is always used

acceptance_criteria.given: Two mutations target the same task concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then:
One acquires the lock and proceeds while the other waits; no
data corruption occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: A delete and a mutation target the same task concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: One completes fully before the other begins; no partial state or corruption occurs

items.title: Atomic Multi-File Task Writes
items.description:
Task mutations that span multiple files (index + task.yaml + notes.yaml)
must be atomic. All task writes — single or batch — either fully
succeed or fully roll back.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task mutation requires writing to the index and a per-task file
acceptance_criteria.then:
Both files are written within a single buffered transaction that
commits atomically to the shadow branch

acceptance_criteria.given: A write to the per-task file succeeds but the index write fails
acceptance_criteria.then: Neither write is persisted; the shadow branch state is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: A batch operation modifies multiple tasks
acceptance_criteria.then:
All index updates and all per-task file writes are collected in
the write buffer and flushed as a single shadow branch commit

acceptance_criteria.given:
A single logical operation affects multiple tasks (e.g.
cancellation with dependency cleanup)
acceptance_criteria.then:
All affected task directories and index entries are written in
a single atomic operation

items.title: Task Listing Performance
items.description:
Listing and filtering tasks reads only the index file, not individual
task directories. This keeps list operations fast regardless of how
many tasks exist or how much data each task contains.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A caller requests a filtered list of tasks (by status, tag,
priority, automation eligibility, or any combination)
acceptance_criteria.then: Only project.tasks.yaml is read; no per-task directory is accessed

acceptance_criteria.given: Tasks have extensive notes and history
acceptance_criteria.when: A filtered task list is requested
acceptance_criteria.then:
The response time is proportional to the number of tasks, not
the total volume of notes and history across all tasks

items.title: Task Detail Loading
items.description:
Loading a single task's full details reads the index entry plus the
per-task directory contents. This is the only operation that accesses
per-task files.

acceptance_criteria.given: A caller requests full details for a specific task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The manager reads the index entry for filterable fields and the
per-task directory (task.yaml + notes.yaml) for complete data;
the result is a unified task object indistinguishable from the
current monolithic format

acceptance_criteria.given: A per-task directory is missing but an index entry exists
acceptance_criteria.then:
The manager returns the index data with a warning indicating
the per-task directory is missing; it does not fail silently
or throw an unrecoverable error

items.title: Task Storage Format Activation
items.description: Split per-task directory format is the only supported storage format. New projects default to it. Legacy projects (kynetic 1.0 without task_storage.format: split) are detected at runtime and blocked with migration guidance. The schema continues to accept both enum values for parsing compatibility, but monolithic is rejected at the task data manager level.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new project is created with kspec init
acceptance_criteria.then: The project defaults to split storage format with kynetic version 1.1

acceptance_criteria.then: An error is raised with guidance to run kspec task migrate

acceptance_criteria.then: An error indicates that migration must be run before the data can be used

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has split format configured and no tasks exist at all
acceptance_criteria.then: The system operates normally with an empty task set

items.title: Task Storage Migration
items.description:
A built-in command to migrate task data from the monolithic format
to the split per-task directory format. Also handles backfilling

Each task gets its own directory with separate core data and
notes files

items.title: Task Automation Eligibility
items.description: Tasks have an automation eligibility status that indicates whether they can be processed by unattended automation loops (like ralph). Eligibility is determined by human judgment during triage - assessing whether the task is unambiguous, appropriately scoped, and has sufficient context (spec + notes + description) to be standalone. This prevents automation from attempting tasks that require human decisions, clarification, or oversight.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task exists
acceptance_criteria.then: it has an optional automation field with enum values: eligible, needs_review, manual_only

acceptance_criteria.given: a new task is created
acceptance_criteria.then: the task has no automation field (treated as unassessed)

acceptance_criteria.given: ralph is selecting tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks with automation: eligible are presented to the agent

acceptance_criteria.when: the agent determines the task is not suitable for automation
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent marks it as needs_review and adds a note explaining why (note is required)

acceptance_criteria.then: they can set automation to any value (eligible, needs_review, manual_only) or clear it

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is marked needs_review
acceptance_criteria.when: it needs to become eligible again
acceptance_criteria.then: a human must review and explicitly set automation: eligible

acceptance_criteria.given: ralph is selecting tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: a task has no automation field (unassessed)
acceptance_criteria.then: that task is not presented to the agent

acceptance_criteria.then: that task is not presented to the agent

inherited_acs.given: A system evaluates whether a task can be picked up for work
inherited_acs.then: Only tasks with status pending or needs_work are considered ready. All other statuses (in_progress, pending_review, completed, blocked, cancelled) are excluded.

inherited_acs.given: A task has depends_on references to other tasks
inherited_acs.then: All depends_on tasks must have status completed. If any dependency has a non-completed status (pending, in_progress, needs_work, pending_review, blocked, cancelled), the task is not ready.

inherited_acs.given: A task has a blocked_by array
inherited_acs.then: The blocked_by array must be empty. Any entry in blocked_by prevents readiness regardless of other conditions.

inherited_acs.given: A consumer applies additional filters (automation status, tags, priority thresholds)
inherited_acs.then: Consumer-specific filters are applied on top of base readiness, never instead of it. A task must pass base readiness before any consumer filter is evaluated.

items.title: Review Record Per-Cycle Lifecycle
items.description:
Each review cycle produces a self-contained review record that is
opened, investigated, verdicted, and closed. This is analogous to
individual PR reviews on GitHub — each reviewer's review is a
discrete artifact, and the collection of reviews across cycles
comprises the full review history for the task.

acceptance_criteria.given: a reviewer submits an approve or request_changes verdict
acceptance_criteria.when: the verdict is recorded on the review
acceptance_criteria.then:
the review record automatically transitions from open to closed,
preserving the verdict as a point-in-time artifact

acceptance_criteria.given: a task re-enters pending_review after a fix cycle
acceptance_criteria.when: a reviewer begins reviewing the updated work
acceptance_criteria.then:
a new review record is created and linked to the task via
review_ref; the previous review record remains closed as a
historical artifact accessible through the activity timeline

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has multiple closed review records from successive cycles
acceptance_criteria.then:
each review appears as a distinct entry with its own verdict,
disposition, and cycle context

items.title: CLI Interface
items.description:
The kspec CLI is the primary interface to Kynetic Spec.
Follows git's plumbing/porcelain model: low-level primitives
for scripts/agents, high-level commands for humans.

items.title: CLI Design Principles
items.description:
The CLI is designed for both human and agent use.
Consistent structure, predictable output, clear errors.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user compares multiple kspec commands across resources such as item, task, and link.
acceptance_criteria.when: They inspect the command names, output shape, and error messaging.
acceptance_criteria.then: The CLI presents a consistent command vocabulary and predictable human-readable responses instead of resource-specific one-offs.

items.title: Batch Command Execution
items.description: Execute multiple mutating kspec commands from inline JSON, files, or stdin with shared validation, atomic or immediate execution modes, and structured result reporting.

acceptance_criteria.given: JSON array piped via stdin
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec batch runs with no --file or --commands flag
acceptance_criteria.then: Commands are read from stdin and executed in order

acceptance_criteria.given: --file flag with path to JSON file
acceptance_criteria.then: Commands are read from the file and executed in order

acceptance_criteria.given: --commands flag with JSON string
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec batch --commands with inline JSON runs
acceptance_criteria.then: Inline JSON is parsed and commands execute

acceptance_criteria.given: Default mode (no --continue flag) with 5 commands where command 3 fails at runtime
acceptance_criteria.then: In atomic mode: all changes rolled back. In immediate mode: commands 1-2 committed, commands 4-5 not executed. Exit code is 1

acceptance_criteria.given: Immediate mode (--continue implies --no-atomic) with 5 commands where command 3 fails at runtime
acceptance_criteria.then: All 5 commands are attempted, command 3 failure is recorded, other commands succeed, exit code is 1

acceptance_criteria.given: Batch with 3 commands where command 2 has invalid syntax
acceptance_criteria.then: Validation fails before any execution, no commands run, error identifies the invalid command by index, exit code is 1

acceptance_criteria.given: --dry-run flag with valid batch
acceptance_criteria.then: All commands are validated but not executed, output shows what would run, no state changes occur

acceptance_criteria.given: Batch where command 2 references slug created by command 1
acceptance_criteria.then: Pre-validation recognizes the forward reference as valid, execution succeeds for both commands

acceptance_criteria.given: Atomic mode (default) with 3 successful mutating commands
acceptance_criteria.then: A single shadow branch commit is created containing all changes (not 3 separate commits)

acceptance_criteria.given: Immediate mode with --continue, commands 1-2 succeed, command 3 fails
acceptance_criteria.then: 2 individual commits (commands 1-2), no commit for command 3

acceptance_criteria.given: Batch containing a read-only command like item get
acceptance_criteria.then: Validation rejects with error identifying the non-mutating command

acceptance_criteria.given: Batch containing a command that normally requires confirmation (e.g., item delete without --force)
acceptance_criteria.then: Command executes without prompting for confirmation (batch mode is implicitly non-interactive)

acceptance_criteria.given: Malformed JSON input (from any source)
acceptance_criteria.then: Parse error with line/position info if available, exit code 1, no commands executed

acceptance_criteria.given: Empty JSON array []
acceptance_criteria.then: Error message says batch contains no commands, exit code 1

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec batch runs without --no-atomic
acceptance_criteria.then: Atomic mode: commands execute against isolated copy of state

acceptance_criteria.given: Atomic mode, 5 cmds where cmd 3 fails
acceptance_criteria.then: ALL changes discarded, no shadow commit, state identical to before batch, exit 1

acceptance_criteria.given: Atomic mode, commands modifying state

items.title: Atomic isolation via write buffer
items.description:
Atomic batch isolation is implemented via an in-memory write buffer (overlay), not a full directory copy to /tmp.

The overlay intercepts file writes during batch execution, buffering them in memory. Reads check the buffer first (returning the pending write if present), then fall through to the real .kspec/ directory. On success, all buffered writes are flushed to disk atomically. On failure, the buffer is discarded — real .kspec/ is never touched.

This replaces the current fs.cp(realSpecDir, tempDir) approach in batch-exec.ts, which copies the entire .kspec/ directory including sessions/blobs/ (potentially GBs of data) for every batch run.

acceptance_criteria.when: a command writes a file to .kspec/
acceptance_criteria.then: the write is stored in the in-memory buffer, not written to disk

acceptance_criteria.given: command A writes a file and command B reads the same file in the same batch
acceptance_criteria.then: command B sees command A's buffered write (read-after-write consistency); this applies to ALL read paths — readYamlFile, loadSpecFile, loadAllItems, loadAllTasks, and any other function that reads .kspec/ files — not just the primary readYamlFile helper

acceptance_criteria.given: all batch commands succeed
acceptance_criteria.then: only the buffered files (those actually written) are flushed to disk — files not touched by the batch are unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: any batch command fails in atomic mode
acceptance_criteria.then: the buffer is discarded with no disk writes — .kspec/ state is identical to before the batch

acceptance_criteria.given: a batch runs against a .kspec/ directory containing large sessions/blobs/ data
acceptance_criteria.then: .kspec/sessions/ is never copied to the temp location — only files actually written by batch commands exist in the buffer

acceptance_criteria.given: a batch is executing and has buffered writes not yet flushed
acceptance_criteria.when: another kspec process reads .kspec/ from disk
acceptance_criteria.then: the reading process sees the original pre-batch state (buffer is process-local and not visible outside the batch process)

acceptance_criteria.given: all batch commands succeed but writing the buffer to disk fails partway through the flush
acceptance_criteria.then: the error is reported and .kspec/ is left in a consistent pre-batch state — no partial writes are silently committed

acceptance_criteria.given: a new function or code path is added that reads files from .kspec/
acceptance_criteria.when: the function uses fs.readFile or fs.readdir directly instead of a buffer-aware helper
acceptance_criteria.then: the read bypasses the write buffer, violating ac-2; all .kspec/ file reads MUST go through a buffer-aware helper (e.g. readYamlFile or a shared readFileBufferAware) that checks getActiveBatchBuffer() before falling back to disk

acceptance_criteria.given: two concurrent async operations each activate a write buffer within the same process
acceptance_criteria.when: both operations are in progress simultaneously
acceptance_criteria.then: each operation sees only its own buffer; writes from one operation are invisible to the other, and discarding one buffer does not affect the other

items.title: Semantic Exit Codes
items.description:
Exit codes are semantic, not just 0/1:

- 0: Success
- 1: General error
- 2: Usage error (bad arguments)

- 5: Conflict (already exists, etc.)

Scripts can handle specific cases.

acceptance_criteria.then: All commands use consistent exit codes for the same error types (e.g., all 'not found' errors exit 3, all validation errors exit 4)

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Enhancement: Formalize exit code implementation

**Current state:** Exit codes are defined in spec but implementation uses magic numbers inconsistently.

**Goals:**
1. Centralized constants - single source of truth
2. Documentation - help users script with kspec
3. Consistency audit - ensure all commands follow the spec

**Exit code definitions (from spec):**
- 0: SUCCESS - Operation completed successfully
- 1: ERROR - General/unexpected error
- 2: USAGE - Bad arguments, invalid command usage
- 3: NOT_FOUND - Referenced item doesn't exist
- 4: VALIDATION - Spec validation failed
- 5: CONFLICT - Item already exists, duplicate slug, etc.

**New additions to consider:**
- 6: PARTIAL - Some operations succeeded, some failed (for batch operations)

**Documentation format:** Add to 'kspec help' or new 'kspec help --exit-codes' subcommand showing all codes with descriptions.

items.title: kspec task add
items.description:
kspec task add [options]

Creates a new task in pending status.

Required:
- --title <title>: Task title

Options:
- --description <description>: Task description (omitted if empty string)
- --type <type>: Task type — task, epic, bug, spike, infra (default: task)
- --spec-ref <ref>: Link to spec item (validated: must be a spec item, not a task or meta item)
- --meta-ref <ref>: Link to meta item — workflow, agent, or convention (validated: must be a meta item)
- --plan-ref <ref>: Link to plan this task is derived from (validated: must be a plan, not a task or spec)
- --priority <n>: Priority 1-5 or P1-P5 (default: 3)
- --slug <slug>: Human-friendly slug alias (validated for uniqueness)
- --tag <tag...>: Tags (repeatable, supports comma-separated)
- --depends-on <refs...>: Task dependencies (validated: each ref must resolve to a task)
- --automation <status>: Automation eligibility — eligible, needs_review, manual_only

Examples:
  kspec task add --title "Implement feature" --spec-ref @feature-spec
  kspec task add --title "Fix bug" --type bug --priority P1
  kspec task add --title "Multi-tag task" --tag cli urgent

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Enhancement: List all tracked commits and git log passthrough

**New features (ACs list-all-tracked, passthrough-args, passthrough-invalid):**

1. **List all tracked commits without ref:**
   Running `kspec log` without any ref should show all commits that have Task: or Spec: trailers. This gives visibility into all tracked work across the repo.
   Implementation: Use git log --grep pattern that matches either trailer:
   git log --grep='Task: @' --grep='Spec: @' --all-match=false
   Respects existing --limit flag (default 10).

2. **Passthrough git log args:**
   Allow passing additional git log flags after -- separator:
   `kspec log @ref -- -p --stat --graph`
   This enables power users to get diffs (-p), stats (--stat), or other git log formatting without kspec needing to wrap every possible option.
   Implementation: Detect -- in argv, split args, pass remainder to git log.
   Commander.js supports -- passthrough via .passThroughOptions() or manual argv handling.

**Backward compatibility:** Existing usage unchanged. New features are additive.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Design: Stale status detection

**Problem:** Spec-task alignment can drift over time. A parent task may stay pending while all children are done. A spec may be marked implemented without any task tracking the work. These inconsistencies reduce trust in the system.

**Solution:** Add --staleness flag to validate command that checks for status mismatches.

**Detection rules:**

1. **Parent pending, children done:**
   - Find tasks that are pending/in_progress
   - Check if they have spec_ref to a parent item
   - Check if all child specs under that parent are implemented
   - If so, warn about the parent task

2. **Spec implemented, no task:**
   - Find specs with implementation_status = implemented
   - Check if any completed tasks have spec_ref pointing to it
   - If none, warn about orphaned implementation

3. **Task done, spec not started:**
   - Find completed tasks with spec_ref
   - Check the linked spec's implementation_status
   - If not_started, warn about the mismatch

**Output format:**
```
Staleness warnings (3):
  ⚠ Task @parent-task is pending but all linked specs are implemented
  ⚠ Spec @orphan-spec is implemented but has no completed tasks
  ⚠ Task @done-task completed but spec @stale-spec is not_started
```

**Flags:**
- --staleness: Enable staleness checks
- --strict: Treat warnings as errors (exit 4)

Enhancement: Auto-detect and setup existing kspec repos

**Problem:** When cloning a repo that already uses kspec (has kspec-meta branch), users must manually run 'git worktree add .kspec kspec-meta'. This is easy to forget, causing confusing 'no kspec found' errors.

**Solution:** Detect this situation and offer to fix it automatically.

**New option:** --auto-worktree

**Integration points:**
- kspec setup: Primary place for this check

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Design: Test repo setup command

**Problem:** Setting up isolated repos for testing requires multiple manual steps:
1. Clone or copy the repo
2. Remove remote origin (avoid accidental pushes)
3. Ensure kspec-meta branch is available
4. Create .kspec worktree
5. Checkout correct branch

Missing any step causes confusing errors (e.g., stale .kspec data if worktree wasn't created).

**Solution:** Single command that handles all setup steps.

**Command signature:**
```
kspec clone-for-testing [source] [dest] [options]

Arguments:
  source    Source repo path (default: current directory)
  dest      Destination path (default: temp directory)

Options:
  --branch <name>   Branch to checkout after cloning
  --json            Output result as JSON
```

**Implementation approach:**
1. Use git clone --no-hardlinks for full independent copy
2. cd into dest, remove origin: git remote remove origin
3. Check if kspec-meta branch exists: git branch --list kspec-meta
4. If exists, create worktree: git worktree add .kspec kspec-meta
5. If --branch specified: git checkout <branch>
6. Print result path (or JSON)

**Use cases:**
- Integration tests that need clean repo state
- Manual testing of risky operations
- Reproducing issues in isolation

items.title: Grep-like Content Search
items.description:
kspec search <pattern>
kspec item list --grep <pattern>
kspec tasks list --grep <pattern>

Enables content search across all spec items and tasks. Searches ALL text content including titles, descriptions, notes, and acceptance criteria text.

Behavior:
- Pattern is treated as regex (like grep)
- Case-insensitive by default
- Searches recursively through all text fields
- Returns the ITEMS/TASKS themselves (not line snippets)
- Shows which field(s) matched for context
- Works with existing filters (--type, --tag, etc.)

Examples:
- kspec search "TODO" → returns all items/tasks mentioning TODO
- kspec search "shadow.*branch" → regex pattern across all content
- kspec tasks list --grep "authentication" → tasks mentioning authentication

Output shows items with match location:
01KF1234 [pending] P2 Implement auth flow
  matched: notes[1].content, description

The search finds items; the pattern is just the filter criteria.

acceptance_criteria.then: Returns items/tasks where any text field matches, showing the item itself (not just the matched line)

items.title: CLI Command Suggestions on Error
items.description:
When user enters an invalid command, suggest close matches.

Behavior:
- On unknown command, compute distance to all valid commands
- If close match found (e.g., 'task list' vs 'tasks list'), suggest it
- Threshold-based: only suggest if match is close enough
- Also handles subcommand typos (e.g., 'inbox ad' → 'inbox add')

Output format:
  error: Unknown command 'task list'
  Did you mean: kspec tasks list?

Consider also accepting common aliases:
- 'task' as alias for 'tasks' (singular/plural flexibility)
- 'ls' as alias for 'list'
- Other common patterns from git/npm conventions

acceptance_criteria.given: A user enters an unknown command such as `kspec task list` or a mistyped subcommand.
acceptance_criteria.then: It suggests a sufficiently close valid command instead of only reporting the failure.

items.title: Ralph Output Formatting
items.description:
Structured formatting for ralph streaming output. Translates ACP events into readable CLI output with visual separation between agent messages, tool calls, and results. Follows patterns from kynetic chat/session UI with chalk-based colors, section headers, timestamps, and noise suppression.

Key learnings from kynetic beads history:
- Finalization is critical for streaming state
- Library limitations guide input format requirements
- Tests must verify end-to-end rendered output
- Treat LLM output as untrusted content

Implementation references:
- ui-event-translator.ts pattern for ACP event translation
- event-display.ts for display summaries
- aggregated-message.ts for message structure

acceptance_criteria.given: ACP agent streams agent_message events
acceptance_criteria.then: messages show with visual separation (section header or newline), chalk.blue for content, and streaming indicator while incomplete

acceptance_criteria.given: ACP agent streams tool_call and tool_call_update events
acceptance_criteria.when: tool calls are displayed in CLI
acceptance_criteria.then: shows tool name, input summary (command for Bash, path for Read/Write, pattern for Grep/Glob), status indicator (pending/running/completed/failed), and truncated output (first 20 lines or 1000 chars with expansion hint)

acceptance_criteria.then: shows relative timestamp from session start (e.g., +5s, +2m) prefixed to the event line

acceptance_criteria.then: messages are suppressed from CLI output (logged to session events only)

items.title: Ralph wrap-up agent on loop exit

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Design decisions and implementation context:

**Syntax choice:** Hybrid approach selected over variadic positional or flag-only. Rationale: maintains backward compatibility with existing single-ref positional usage while adding batch capability via --refs flag. Matches existing pattern used by --depends-on.

**Error handling:** Continue-and-report strategy (not fail-fast). Process all refs, succeed where possible, report failures at end. Consistent with existing item patch --bulk behavior.

**Exit codes for batch operations:**
- 0: All operations succeeded
- 1: All operations failed  
- 2: Partial failure (some succeeded, some failed)
- 3: Invalid input (empty refs, mutual exclusion violation)

**Commands in scope (7 total):**
- task complete --refs
- task cancel --refs
- task set --refs
- task delete --refs
- item set --refs
- item delete --refs
- inbox delete --refs

**Edge cases to handle:**
1. Duplicate refs in --refs: Dedupe silently, process each unique ref once
2. Ref resolves to wrong type (e.g., spec ref passed to task command): Fail for that specific ref with 'not a task' error
3. Options unsafe for batch (e.g., --slug): Document which options shouldn't be used with multi-refs

items.title: Plan Revisions
items.description:
Plans carry a first-class revision history. A revision marks an
intentional publish of the plan document: an explicit publish action
mints one, and completing a document re-import into an existing plan
mints one. Draft edits that replace content without publishing do
not. A revision record stores its ordinal, author, summary note,
timestamp, and a pointer to the shadow-branch commit containing the
published content; the document body is never duplicated into the
revision record. Revision authors use the same actor attribution
vocabulary as other authored records; no revision-specific author
format exists. The revision data upgrade gives every plan that
existed when it ran at least revision 1. Plan creation mints
nothing: a plan created after the upgrade — directly or through an
initial document import — starts with an empty revision history
until its first publish or document re-import mints revision 1. A
plan persisted before revision support and not yet upgraded
likewise loads with an empty revision history. A review of a plan
resolves to the revision it examined through the review's pinned
subject version, with no new field on the review record.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing plan with N recorded revisions
acceptance_criteria.when: an explicit publish action is performed with a summary note
acceptance_criteria.then:
a revision record is created with ordinal N+1, the acting author,
the supplied summary note, a creation timestamp, and a pointer to
the shadow-branch commit containing the published content

acceptance_criteria.given: a plan document is re-imported into an existing plan
acceptance_criteria.then:
a new revision record is minted for the updated content carrying
the same fields as an explicit publish, with the summary note
supplied by the caller or recorded as a stated default

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan whose content is replaced through a non-publish update
path, or whose metadata or notes are mutated
acceptance_criteria.then: the plan's revision list is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a revision record is stored
acceptance_criteria.then:
it contains only bounded metadata and the commit pointer — no
copy of the document body — and resolving the pointer returns
content byte-identical to the document as published

acceptance_criteria.given: a plan with one or more revisions
acceptance_criteria.then:
ordinals form a strictly increasing sequence starting at 1 in
publish order, and each revision exposes its ordinal, author,
summary note, and timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: a project whose plans were created before revision support
acceptance_criteria.then:
every existing plan has exactly one revision with ordinal 1 whose
pointer designates the plan's content as of the upgrade

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan record persisted before revision support and not yet
upgraded
acceptance_criteria.when: the plan is loaded and validated
acceptance_criteria.then: it loads without error and reports an empty revision history

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan created after the revision data upgrade has run, with no
publish or document re-import yet completed on it
acceptance_criteria.when: the plan is loaded and its revisions are read
acceptance_criteria.then: it loads without error and reports an empty revision history

a plan review whose pinned subject version matches the content

acceptance_criteria.when: the revision the review examined is resolved

items.title: Folder-Backed Plan Storage
items.description:
Plans are stored as folder-backed entities so the markdown plan document and
local supporting resources can live together without bloating the plan index.
Each plan directory contains `plan.md`, `plan.yaml`, optional `notes.yaml`,
`resources.yaml`, and `resources/`. List and detail consumers continue to
see the same plan identity, status, lifecycle, content, notes, and
derived-ref semantics.

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed plan is loaded for detail or derivation
acceptance_criteria.then: `.kspec/plans/<plan-ulid>/plan.md` is the authoritative source of plan markdown content

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed plan is loaded or mutated
acceptance_criteria.when: Plan identity, status, source path, module, branch, timestamps, notes, or derived refs are needed
acceptance_criteria.then: `.kspec/plans/<plan-ulid>/plan.yaml` stores the authoritative bounded plan metadata while `notes.yaml` stores plan notes when notes are present

acceptance_criteria.given: Folder-backed plans exist in a project
acceptance_criteria.when: `.kspec/project.plans.yaml` is read for listing, filtering, or cache warm-up
acceptance_criteria.then: The index contains plan ULID, slugs, title, status, source path, module, branch, derived refs, timestamps, and resource summaries, but not full markdown content, notes, or resource file bytes

acceptance_criteria.given: A folder-backed plan is eligible for removal under the existing plan removal rules
acceptance_criteria.then: The plan index entry and `.kspec/plans/<plan-ulid>/` directory are removed in one logical shadow mutation

items.title: Plan Import Into Existing Plan
items.description:
Re-import a plan document into an existing plan record, updating
the plan content. This closes the round-trip editing loop:
export → edit → re-import.

Only the plan record's content and title are updated. No specs or
tasks are created or modified — that happens at derive time.

Only allowed for draft or approved plans. Active and terminal
plans cannot be updated.

A plan exists in draft status and an edited plan document

acceptance_criteria.then:
The existing plan record's title is updated from the H1
heading (if present) and content is replaced with the file
content. A note is auto-appended: "Content updated from file"

acceptance_criteria.then:
Plan content is replaced with the file content.
Plan title is preserved unchanged (not cleared).

acceptance_criteria.then:

items.title: Plan Import Content-Only Storage
items.description:
Change plan import to store content only and default to draft status.

Import creates the plan record with the full document as content
but does NOT create specs or tasks. All materialization (spec
creation, task derivation) happens via kspec plan derive.

This respects the draft→approved→derive lifecycle and prevents
import-time churn during iterative plan editing.

Supersedes most of @plan-import ac-11 through ac-37.
See AC Migration tables in Implementation Notes for the
precise mapping of each existing AC.

items.title: Enhanced Plan Derivation
items.description:
Enhanced plan derive command that parses plan content and creates specs and tasks. This is the materialization step — it takes a plan document stored as content and creates the corresponding spec items and tasks.

Absorbs all spec/task creation logic previously in plan import (topological ordering, slug dedup, parent resolution, trait mapping, dependency mapping, implementation notes, etc.).

Derive is a one-shot operation — once a plan is derived, it transitions to active and its specs/tasks are managed directly.

Replaces the current simple single-task derive behavior. Supersedes @plan-derive (ac-5, ac-6). Bidirectional link display is preserved via ac-bidirectional-links.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A plan exists in approved status with ## Specs YAML in its
content field
acceptance_criteria.then:
The plan content is parsed using parsePlanDocument().
Specs from the ## Specs YAML block are created as spec items
under the specified module.

acceptance_criteria.given: A plan exists in approved status
acceptance_criteria.then:
If the plan has no stored module ref, command fails with
EXIT_CODES.USAGE_ERROR and message requiring --module

acceptance_criteria.then: Uses the module ref stored on the plan record from import

acceptance_criteria.then:
Specs are created under @mod-b, not @mod-a.
The explicit --module flag overrides the stored value.

Plan specs have parent references to other specs in the
same plan
acceptance_criteria.then:
Specs are created in topological order so parent specs
exist before their children

acceptance_criteria.then:
Command fails with EXIT_CODES.USAGE_ERROR and message

acceptance_criteria.then: A unique slug is generated by appending a numeric suffix

Trait refs are normalized (@ prefix added if missing)
and stored on the created spec

acceptance_criteria.then:
Dependency refs are normalized and stored on created specs.
When deriving tasks, spec depends_on maps to task depends_on.

acceptance_criteria.then: Tasks are derived and the flag is accepted without error or warning

acceptance_criteria.given: Tasks are derived from plan specs
acceptance_criteria.then: Each derived task has spec_ref pointing to the source spec and plan_ref pointing to the plan

acceptance_criteria.then: Additional tasks are created with plan_ref, spec_ref (if specified), and depends_on mappings

items.title: Plan Resource Derivation Semantics
items.description:
Plan task definitions can explicitly reference plan-owned resources via a
`resource_refs` list containing `./resources/<relative-path>` entries.
Derived tasks keep versioned references to those plan resources by default;
task-owned copies are only created by an explicit materialize/copy option.

acceptance_criteria.given: A plan document contains a manual task definition in the `## Tasks` YAML block
acceptance_criteria.when: The task needs one or more plan-local resources
acceptance_criteria.then: The task definition can declare `resource_refs: ["./resources/<relative-path>"]` entries that must resolve against the source plan's `resources.yaml` manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: A plan task definition declares one or more valid `resource_refs`
acceptance_criteria.when: The plan is derived into tasks without explicit materialization
acceptance_criteria.then: The derived task records plan-owned resource references instead of copying resource bytes into the task directory

acceptance_criteria.given: A derived task records a reference to a plan-owned local resource
acceptance_criteria.then: The task resource reference records owner type, owner ref, resource id, relative path, content hash, and available git commit/path identity from derivation time

acceptance_criteria.given: A task references a plan resource whose current content no longer matches the version recorded at derivation time
acceptance_criteria.when: The task detail, agent context, or API resource resolver presents the resource
acceptance_criteria.then: The consumer is told the resource has changed rather than silently receiving an unversioned replacement

acceptance_criteria.given: A derivation command explicitly requests materialized task-owned copies of plan resources
acceptance_criteria.then: Each copied resource is stored under the derived task's resource tree and the task resource reference points at the task-owned copy

items.title: Plan Summary Metrics
items.description: Defines shared semantics for plan-linked task counts and progress metrics across interfaces.

acceptance_criteria.given: a plan has linked tasks in multiple statuses, including cancelled tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: plan-linked task counts or progress metrics are presented in any interface
acceptance_criteria.then: cancelled tasks are excluded from any plan metric that is not explicitly reporting cancelled-task status

items.title: Plan Branch Association

acceptance_criteria.then: The branch field is null

acceptance_criteria.given:

acceptance_criteria.then: They parse successfully with branch defaulting to null

The plan derive command surfaces branch awareness so users know

items.title: Plan Document Format Error Guidance
items.description:
Plan import is tolerant of documents that have no specs or
tasks yet (planning content is allowed to land before the
structured work has been written), but is strict about
structural invariants that downstream commands rely on:
the title must be extractable, and any specs or acceptance
criteria that are present must match the expected shape.
An imported plan with no specs or tasks surfaces a visible
warning so the user knows content is still missing, and
plan derive refuses to run against a plan that has no
derivable work. Errors and warnings are self-contained —
users can correct the input without reading source or
external documentation.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A plan document whose first significant element is not a
top-level heading
acceptance_criteria.then:
The import fails with an error that identifies the
expected title location and the structural form the
parser recognizes

acceptance_criteria.given:
A plan document with a valid title but neither a specs
section nor a tasks section containing any derivable
work
acceptance_criteria.then:
The import succeeds, the plan is stored as content,
and a warning is reported that names both expected
sections and explains that derive will not run until
at least one is populated

acceptance_criteria.given: A plan was imported with no specs and no tasks
acceptance_criteria.when: Plan derive is invoked for that plan
acceptance_criteria.then:
Derive fails with a non-zero exit code and an error
that names the expected sections, explains that the
plan has no derivable work, and points the user at
the import command to update the plan's content

acceptance_criteria.given:
A plan document where an acceptance criterion is not
expressed in the expected shape
acceptance_criteria.then:
The import fails with an error that locates the
malformed criterion by its containing spec and its
position within that spec

acceptance_criteria.given:
A plan document's acceptance criterion fails shape
validation
acceptance_criteria.then:
The error message enumerates every required field of
an acceptance criterion with a one-line description
of each field's purpose

acceptance_criteria.given: A user queries help for the plan import command
acceptance_criteria.then:
The output includes a minimal runnable example of a plan
document and names every required structural element

Any import error, derive error, or empty-plan warning
from this spec is surfaced
acceptance_criteria.then:
The message is self-contained and does not require the

correct the input

items.title: Unified Health Check Command
items.description:
The `kspec doctor` command aggregates all health checks — shadow branch,
agent setup, and daemon status — into a single unified report. Each check
reports a severity (ok, warning, error). The overall verdict is healthy
only when no errors exist. Warnings (e.g. daemon not running) do not
cause a non-zero exit.

Architecture: library function in src/parser/doctor.ts returns DoctorReport,
CLI command in src/cli/commands/doctor.ts formats and outputs it. Daemon
status logic extracted from serve.ts into a shared getDaemonStatus()
to avoid duplication.

exits with code 1

items.description:
Persistent triage metadata system with interactive UI. Triage decisions
(reasoning, evidence, actions) are stored as TriageRecords in
project.triage.yaml, surviving inbox item deletion. Supports agent
triage, user override, action execution, and context export for agent handoff.

gated.

items.title: Task budget enforcement
items.description:
Replaces the marker file + PreToolUse bash hook with enforcement built into kspec
task start. When a session has a budget configured, kspec task start checks the
budget before proceeding and increments the counter on success. Ralph resets the
budget at each iteration boundary. Single-writer guarantee: ralph resets only
between iterations (agent not running), agent is only writer during its turn.
Budget only gates task start — review subagents that call task complete do not
trigger budget logic since they don't start new work.

acceptance_criteria.then:

and let the iteration end naturally without starting new tasks

Each dispatch creates an isolated session with its own event log and

engine and CLI one-shot mode.

items.title: Dispatch Role Workflow Entry Contract
items.description:

The dispatcher selects the configured workflow or skill entrypoint for
that role independently from the orientation block

acceptance_criteria.given: Worker and reviewer adapters or harnesses differ
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatcher renders adapter-appropriate invocation syntax and
includes the publish path instructions against the recorded base branch,
using the recorded publication mode for that workspace

acceptance_criteria.given: Manual merge-back is the selected publication path
acceptance_criteria.then:
It includes explicit conflict-handling guidance and when to stop or
escalate rather than auto-resolving blindly

acceptance_criteria.given:
A role-specific workflow entrypoint or publication mode is missing or
invalid
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatcher fails fast with actionable guidance instead of
delivering a half-oriented prompt with no valid workflow entry

items.title: Agent Dispatch Engine
items.description:
Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule
acceptance_criteria.when: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event
acceptance_criteria.then:
The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change
acceptance_criteria.then:
Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached
acceptance_criteria.when: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine is running
acceptance_criteria.when: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then:
The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

acceptance_criteria.given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)
acceptance_criteria.when: A state change matches the event type
acceptance_criteria.then:
The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

acceptance_criteria.given:
The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event
acceptance_criteria.when: Both events arrive within a short window
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)
acceptance_criteria.when: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules
acceptance_criteria.then:
The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn
acceptance_criteria.when: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash
acceptance_criteria.then:
The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent
acceptance_criteria.then:
An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

acceptance_criteria.given: global stop authority is committed
acceptance_criteria.then: dispatch does not report stop success

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)
acceptance_criteria.when: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine builds a prompt for an agent invocation
acceptance_criteria.when: Task data is available on the state change
acceptance_criteria.then: The prompt includes the task title and human-readable trigger context (new assignment, fix cycle, continuing work, or review)

acceptance_criteria.given: A task.needs_work trigger fires
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: The last 3 task notes are included in the prompt, each truncated to 200 characters, so the agent can see reviewer feedback

acceptance_criteria.given: A task.pending_review trigger fires and the task has a review_url
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: The prompt includes the review URL for the reviewer agent

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent definition has a prompt_template with {{variable}} placeholders
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch engine builds the prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: Placeholders are interpolated with task_ref, task_title, trigger, and review_url values; unresolved placeholders pass through unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: A queued dispatch entry is about to be spawned as an invocation
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch engine dequeues the entry and prepares to run it
acceptance_criteria.then: The engine loads the task current state and verifies it still matches the dispatch rule trigger event; if the task has moved to a different state, the entry is discarded without spawning

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI command transitions a task state while running inside a dispatched agent invocation (KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set)
acceptance_criteria.when: The CLI would normally post a state change event to the daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: The event is suppressed to prevent self-triggering, since the file watcher will independently detect the change

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine is running and has been started
acceptance_criteria.when: A configurable interval (default 60 seconds) elapses since the last reconciliation scan
acceptance_criteria.then: The engine re-evaluates all current task states against dispatch rules (identical to bootstrap logic), enqueuing any tasks that match an agent's dispatch trigger but have no active or queued invocation, ensuring that missed or lost events are recovered automatically

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine reconciliation interval is configured via DispatchEngineOptions
acceptance_criteria.when: The engine is created with a custom reconcileIntervalMs value (or the default of 60000ms)
acceptance_criteria.then: The periodic reconciliation scan runs at the configured interval, and setting the interval to 0 or null disables periodic reconciliation entirely

acceptance_criteria.given: a dispatch rule has no filter configured (filter is undefined or empty)
acceptance_criteria.when: a task state change matches the rule's event type
acceptance_criteria.then: the engine defaults to requiring automation: eligible for task.ready and task.needs_work events — only automation-eligible tasks are dispatched unless the rule explicitly specifies a different automation filter value

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec setup creates default agent definitions (task-worker, pr-reviewer)
acceptance_criteria.when: the default dispatch rules are generated
acceptance_criteria.then: task-worker's task.ready and task.needs_work rules include filter: { automation: eligible } by default

acceptance_criteria.given: the dispatch engine has just completed an agent invocation and is about to choose the next invocation to spawn
acceptance_criteria.when: the engine prepares to drain queues
acceptance_criteria.then: the engine operates on a full and current view of all task states loaded from disk, not a stale or partial snapshot from prior queue entries alone

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent invocation completes (success or failure after retry exhaustion)
acceptance_criteria.when: the dispatch engine prepares to drain queues for the next invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: the engine re-evaluates all current task states against dispatch rules (with skipIfActive deduplication) before draining, ensuring tasks that reached a dispatchable state during the prior invocation are visible to the drain loop

acceptance_criteria.given: the post-invocation re-evaluation (ac-24) fails due to a transient error (disk read failure, parse error, etc.)
acceptance_criteria.when: the dispatch engine proceeds to drain queues
acceptance_criteria.then: the failure is logged as a warning, and the drain still runs on pre-existing queue entries — re-evaluation failure does not block dispatch of already-queued work

acceptance_criteria.given: A task state change matches an agent's dispatch rule
acceptance_criteria.when: Any agent — including a different agent — already has an active invocation for the same task
acceptance_criteria.then: At most one invocation may be active for a given task across all agents at any time; additional eligible invocations remain queued and are picked up automatically when the active invocation completes (whether successfully or after retry exhaustion) without requiring a new external event. Deferred entries are subject to the same staleness checks as any queued entry before spawn.

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine enforces a per-agent max_concurrent limit
acceptance_criteria.when: Multiple queue drain paths execute concurrently from any source (event-driven, post-invocation, retry wake-up, reconciliation, or bootstrap)
acceptance_criteria.then: max_concurrent is never exceeded — concurrent drain requests are serialized so that candidate selection and concurrency accounting for a given agent cannot race

acceptance_criteria.given: the dispatch engine performs internal bookkeeping (task notes, task blocking, git operations, workspace provisioning) within the daemon's Node.js event loop
acceptance_criteria.when: those operations involve child process spawning or file I/O
acceptance_criteria.then: they use asynchronous APIs so the event loop remains available to serve HTTP and WebSocket requests concurrently

acceptance_criteria.given: A dispatch entry has been dequeued for spawn and the dispatch engine has marked the task in-flight, but no active invocation has been registered for that task yet.
acceptance_criteria.when: Startup, periodic, or post-event reconciliation invokes workspace artifact cleanup.
acceptance_criteria.then: The task reference is included in the cleanup protection input so the pre-active spawn window receives the same artifact protection as a registered active invocation.

acceptance_criteria.given: Periodic reconciliation is enabled and a reconciliation pass is still running
acceptance_criteria.then: The dispatch engine does not start a second reconciliation pass before the running pass completes

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine is stopping while one or more reconciliation passes are in flight
acceptance_criteria.then: No in-flight reconciliation pass continues mutating dispatch state after stop has returned

acceptance_criteria.given: a candidate remains eligible after dequeue
acceptance_criteria.when: it reaches the final creation boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: current global control determines whether creation is permitted

acceptance_criteria.given: a candidate remains eligible after dequeue
acceptance_criteria.when: it reaches the final creation boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: its canonical-task control determines whether creation is permitted

acceptance_criteria.given: an invocation is active in a scope
acceptance_criteria.then: the invocation may finish naturally

acceptance_criteria.given: a session belongs to an active invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: pause does not close the session

acceptance_criteria.given: a scope is paused
acceptance_criteria.then: current task state is re-evaluated before work starts

acceptance_criteria.given: a scope is paused
acceptance_criteria.then: current dispatch rules are re-evaluated before work starts

includes suggested action to resolve
suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
indicates current state and valid next states
indicates which field/value failed validation
guidance included in structured error object

inherited_acs.given: A system evaluates whether a task can be picked up for work
inherited_acs.then: Only tasks with status pending or needs_work are considered ready. All other statuses (in_progress, pending_review, completed, blocked, cancelled) are excluded.

inherited_acs.given: A task has depends_on references to other tasks
inherited_acs.then: All depends_on tasks must have status completed. If any dependency has a non-completed status (pending, in_progress, needs_work, pending_review, blocked, cancelled), the task is not ready.

inherited_acs.given: A task has a blocked_by array
inherited_acs.then: The blocked_by array must be empty. Any entry in blocked_by prevents readiness regardless of other conditions.

inherited_acs.given: A consumer applies additional filters (automation status, tags, priority thresholds)
inherited_acs.then: Consumer-specific filters are applied on top of base readiness, never instead of it. A task must pass base readiness before any consumer filter is evaluated.

items.title: Canonical Task Workspace Contract
items.description:
Each dispatchable task owns one canonical mutable branch lineage and one
canonical workspace identity. Workers and fix-cycle workers attach to the
mutable task branch, while reviewers attach to an isolated snapshot context
anchored to that branch lineage.

acceptance_criteria.given:
The dispatcher provisions workspace state for a task and the base
branch has been resolved
acceptance_criteria.when: It establishes the task's code identity
acceptance_criteria.then:
One canonical task branch is created from the resolved base branch and
the originating base commit is recorded

acceptance_criteria.given:
A worker invocation and a later needs_work fix-cycle invocation run for
the same task
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatcher prepares their code context
acceptance_criteria.then:
Both use the same canonical mutable task branch rather than creating a
new branch per cycle

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reviewer invocation is prepared for a task with an existing canonical
branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
The reviewer gets a separate isolated worktree materialized from the
recorded canonical branch head in detached HEAD or equivalent read-only
mode, and the dispatcher never attempts to check out the same local
branch in two worktrees

acceptance_criteria.given: A task transitions to needs_work after review
acceptance_criteria.when: A follow-up worker invocation is prepared
acceptance_criteria.then:
The worker resumes on the same canonical branch lineage instead of
forking a new task branch

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatcher generates a canonical branch name for a task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The branch name follows the deterministic format
`dispatch/task/<normalized-task-slug-or-task>/<short-task-ulid>` where
the slug portion is normalized to kebab-case and the ULID suffix makes
collisions impossible without relying on role-specific prefixes

acceptance_criteria.given:
A task branch has been integrated into its recorded base branch or the
task has been explicitly abandoned or reset
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatcher reconciles the workspace lifecycle
acceptance_criteria.then:
The canonical task branch becomes cleanup-eligible rather than
remaining indefinitely active

items.title: Dispatch Workspace Registry
items.description:
The dispatcher persists canonical workspace metadata in a first-party
registry so branch, worktree, integration, and cleanup identity survive
restarts and can be reused across worker, reviewer, and fix-cycle
invocations.

acceptance_criteria.given: A canonical task workspace is provisioned
acceptance_criteria.then:
A first-party workspace record is stored in kspec-managed metadata on
the shadow branch rather than existing only in daemon memory

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has an active canonical workspace
acceptance_criteria.then: At most one active canonical workspace record exists for that task

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace record exists
acceptance_criteria.when: It is stored in the registry
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record includes at minimum workspace id, task ref, resolved base
branch, base head at branch point, canonical branch, canonical branch
head, per-role worktrees, bootstrap state, integration status, health
status, timestamps, and cleanup state

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon restarts or reloads dispatch state
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatcher reloads workspace records from the registry and
reconciles them against the filesystem instead of losing
branch/worktree continuity

acceptance_criteria.given:
A workspace record's referenced branch or worktree is missing,
unhealthy, or out of sync with its recorded state
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record transitions to an explicit non-healthy state such as invalid
or stale, with actionable recovery data rather than silent fallback

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace record is tracked over time
acceptance_criteria.then:
The transition states are explicit and behavioral: `provisioning`
during initial branch/worktree/bootstrap setup, `ready` after
provisioning/bootstrap with no running invocation, `active` while a
role invocation is attached, `stale` when reconciliation finds missing
or invalid recorded state, `integrating` when PR or manual merge-back
is pending or in progress, `closing` when merged or abandoned state
schedules cleanup, `cleanup_blocked` when cleanup safety checks fail,
and `closed` after tracked worktrees are removed and the record is
finalized

acceptance_criteria.given: Integration or cleanup state changes over the life of the task
acceptance_criteria.then:
Those transitions are durably persisted on the shadow branch for
restart recovery and later review workflows

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch runtime writes workspace registry state such as provisioning, reconciliation, bootstrap, integration, or cleanup updates into project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml on the shadow worktree
acceptance_criteria.then: The registry mutation is durably committed on the shadow branch through the protected shadow-mutation path before the dispatcher treats the new registry state as authoritative, so daemon restart or later reconciliation cannot lose the update in an uncommitted dirty worktree

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch runtime writes a workspace record to the registry file and closed records exist whose closed_at timestamp exceeds the retention threshold
acceptance_criteria.when: The registry file is saved through saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord
acceptance_criteria.then: Closed records older than the retention threshold are removed from the file atomically within the same write and lock scope, requiring no separate cleanup step. Purged records are no longer available for workspace identity reuse during re-provisioning; re-opened tasks receive fresh workspace identities.

acceptance_criteria.given: The periodic reconciliation runs and computes a new candidate state for a non-closed workspace record
acceptance_criteria.when: The computed state (health, lifecycle_state, active_role, cleanup, integration, canonical_branch_head) is identical to the currently persisted record
acceptance_criteria.then: The registry file is not rewritten and no shadow branch commit is created for that record. Timestamps such as updated_at must not change unless a meaningful field has changed. last_reconciled_at may be updated in memory for staleness evaluation but must not trigger a write or commit on its own.

acceptance_criteria.given: An automation-eligible task is already in_progress and its recorded branch or workspace is missing when the dispatcher tries to resume it
acceptance_criteria.when: the dispatcher reconstructs active workspace state for that task
acceptance_criteria.then: the dispatcher attempts to recover or re-provision the canonical workspace and branch lineage instead of discarding the in_progress queue entry as workspace missing

acceptance_criteria.given: reconciliation evaluates workspace health for a record whose task is in a terminal state (completed or cancelled)
acceptance_criteria.when: the canonical branch is missing locally
acceptance_criteria.then: health reconciliation skips branch restoration attempts and evaluates the record using its last persisted state rather than trying to recover git refs that are no longer needed

acceptance_criteria.given: artifact reconciliation identifies a dispatch branch with no matching worktree
acceptance_criteria.when: the branch belongs to a workspace record still tracked in the registry with a non-closed lifecycle state
acceptance_criteria.then: artifact reconciliation preserves the branch rather than treating it as orphaned — only branches with no registry record or whose registry record has lifecycle_state closed are eligible for deletion

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace record exists for a non-terminal task (any status except completed or cancelled) and reconciliation determines the workspace is unrecoverable — all recovery paths (local branch check, remote branch fallback, submission linkage adoption) have been attempted and failed
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch scheduler evaluates the task for queue eligibility
acceptance_criteria.then: The stale record is purged or reset so the task becomes eligible for fresh provisioning on the next dispatch cycle, rather than being permanently discarded from the queue as unhealthy

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace cleanup completes without a blocking condition
acceptance_criteria.then: The record's cleanup status is completed

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace cleanup completes without a blocking condition
acceptance_criteria.then: The record has a closed_at timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace record's cleanup status is completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The lifecycle state is next evaluated
acceptance_criteria.then: The lifecycle state resolves to closed

acceptance_criteria.given: Daemon startup or periodic reconciliation finds a provisioning lifecycle state, unclassified non-closed workspace record, or metadata-backed dispatch artifact that may belong to a task whose invocation is not currently active.
acceptance_criteria.when: Artifact cleanup is about to evaluate that workspace's worktrees, reviewer snapshot, root directory, or dispatch branch for destructive cleanup.
acceptance_criteria.then: Reconciliation first classifies the workspace as preserved for retry, active/in-flight, stale/unhealthy with actionable recovery detail, or cleanup-eligible state. A `closing` workspace with satisfied cleanup prerequisites and no active/in-flight/provisioning ownership may be classified cleanup-eligible so scheduled cleanup can reach `closed`.

acceptance_criteria.given: Cleanup removes a dispatch artifact because its artifact-local metadata is untrusted and no trusted protection state classifies it as protected.
acceptance_criteria.when: A later dispatch reconciliation or scheduling cycle evaluates a non-terminal task that still needs work.
acceptance_criteria.then: Recovery is driven from trusted task and registry state; the task can be requeued, reprovisioned, or marked stale with actionable recovery detail without relying on the removed corrupt artifact metadata.

includes suggested action to resolve

guidance included in structured error object

items.title: Dispatch Workspace Cleanup Policy
items.description:
The dispatcher cleans up dispatch worktrees and task branches
deterministically so it does not leave stale directories or refs behind.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A reviewer snapshot worktree finishes and no retention or debug hold
exists
acceptance_criteria.then:
The reviewer worktree becomes immediately cleanup-eligible while the
canonical worker worktree persists across in_progress and needs_work
continuity

acceptance_criteria.given:
A task reaches completed or cancelled status, or the workspace
integration outcome becomes merged or explicitly abandoned
acceptance_criteria.then: The workspace enters `closing` and scheduled cleanup is created

acceptance_criteria.given: Cleanup executes for a workspace with tracked dispatch worktrees
acceptance_criteria.then:
Worktree directories and their corresponding git worktree metadata are
removed from the configured dispatch root without touching the main or
shadow worktrees

acceptance_criteria.given:
A canonical task branch still has active invocation ownership or
unresolved integration status
acceptance_criteria.then:
The branch is not deleted and the record moves to `cleanup_blocked`
with actionable guidance

acceptance_criteria.given:
Daemon startup or periodic reconciliation finds orphaned dispatch
worktrees or task branches under the dispatch root
acceptance_criteria.when: Registry and filesystem state are compared
acceptance_criteria.then:
The dispatcher either reattaches them to a workspace record or cleans
them up deterministically instead of leaving orphaned state

acceptance_criteria.given: project has a dispatcher-managed worker or reviewer worktree under the configured dispatch root with .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json metadata, but no matching registry record on the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.when: daemon startup or periodic reconciliation compares registry and filesystem state
acceptance_criteria.then: the dispatcher reconstructs or reattaches a canonical workspace record from the on-disk metadata before reviewer or worker eligibility is pruned, or deterministically blocks or cleans the workspace with actionable recovery detail if the metadata cannot be trusted

acceptance_criteria.given: reconciliation finds a metadata-backed dispatch worktree whose checked-out branch layout predates the canonical dispatch/task/* naming contract, such as a rollout-era feat/* branch
acceptance_criteria.when: the dispatcher reconciles legacy upgrade-path state
acceptance_criteria.then: it normalizes that workspace onto the canonical workspace record or retires it deterministically with explicit task-linked diagnostics instead of silently leaving reviewer handoff ineligible

acceptance_criteria.given: Artifact cleanup evaluates a dispatcher-managed worktree, reviewer snapshot, root directory, or dispatch branch for work that is active, in-flight, or in provisioning.
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup determines whether that artifact is eligible for destructive removal.
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup preserves the artifact instead of removing, pruning, or deleting it.

acceptance_criteria.given: Artifact cleanup discovers the same protected task or workspace through any destructive cleanup surface.
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup evaluates worker worktrees, reviewer snapshots, root directories, workspace records, or dispatch branches.
acceptance_criteria.then: The protected artifact receives the same preserve outcome regardless of which cleanup surface discovered it.

acceptance_criteria.given: Artifact cleanup cannot load or trust the registry, metadata, or protection state needed to classify whether a dispatcher-managed artifact is protected or safely cleanup-eligible.
acceptance_criteria.when: The artifact would otherwise be considered eligible for destructive cleanup.
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup does not blindly delete the artifact; it reconstructs or reattaches trusted state, blocks cleanup with actionable guidance, or proceeds only after existing cleanup policy classification determines the metadata is untrusted and cleanup is safe.

acceptance_criteria.given: Registry state and centralized cleanup protection state are loaded and trusted, and cleanup finds a dispatcher-managed artifact under the configured dispatch worktree root whose per-workspace metadata is missing, unreadable, or unparseable.
acceptance_criteria.when: No non-closed registry record, active task ref, in-flight task ref, or provisioning ownership classifies that artifact as protected.
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup may classify the artifact-local metadata as untrusted and remove the artifact as cleanup-eligible instead of preserving it for metadata recovery.

acceptance_criteria.given: Registry state and centralized cleanup protection state are loaded and trusted, and cleanup finds an unknown file or directory directly under the configured dispatch worktree root.
acceptance_criteria.when: The entry is not equal to, contained by, or otherwise associated with a protected active, in-flight, provisioning, or non-closed workspace artifact.
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup treats the entry as dispatch-owned garbage and may remove it instead of preserving it as user/operator data.

acceptance_criteria.given: Cleanup repeatedly preserves protected dispatch artifacts during normal daemon reconciliation
acceptance_criteria.when: detailed cleanup diagnostics have not been explicitly enabled
acceptance_criteria.then: Preservation diagnostics are not emitted for each preserved artifact

acceptance_criteria.given: Detailed cleanup diagnostics have been explicitly enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup preserves a protected dispatch artifact
acceptance_criteria.then: A preservation diagnostic identifies the cleanup surface, artifact, and preservation reason

acceptance_criteria.given: dispatch evidence belongs to active, in-flight, paused-held, or stopped-pending-cleanup work
acceptance_criteria.when: a destructive cleanup surface evaluates it
acceptance_criteria.then: lifecycle control alone does not make the evidence cleanup-eligible

items.title: Adopted Branch Cleanup and Recoverability
items.description:
Cleanup and health reconciliation treat adopted/manual branches differently
from dispatcher-owned branches so dispatch can preserve externally-owned
refs while still cleaning local worktrees and surfacing actionable recovery
states.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Cleanup runs for a workspace whose canonical branch was adopted from a
manual or externally-created branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
Dispatch removes local worker and reviewer worktrees plus runtime
metadata as appropriate, but preserves the adopted branch ref unless an
explicit policy says the branch is dispatcher-owned

acceptance_criteria.given:
Cleanup runs for a workspace whose canonical branch is
dispatcher-managed
acceptance_criteria.then:
Dispatch may still delete the dispatcher-owned branch using the current
cleanup lifecycle

acceptance_criteria.given: Reconciliation evaluates a non-healthy workspace
acceptance_criteria.when:
The canonical branch is missing locally, the remote locator is known,
or only the reviewer snapshot is missing
acceptance_criteria.then:
Health state distinguishes recoverable adopted-branch rehydration,
missing dispatcher-managed canonical branch, and missing reviewer
snapshot as separate recovery paths with specific guidance

acceptance_criteria.given:
Dispatch created or fetched a local branch ref only to rehydrate an
adopted externally-owned branch into the local checkout
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup runs after the workspace closes
acceptance_criteria.then:
Cleanup policy distinguishes the external source branch from the local
dispatch-side mirror ref so local rehydration state can be removed
without deleting or mutating the externally-owned branch lineage
