items.title: Branch Provenance in Dispatch Workspace Registry
items.description:
Dispatch workspace records capture whether the canonical branch is
dispatcher-managed or adopted, plus the locator and ownership semantics
needed to rehydrate and preserve that lineage correctly across restarts and
reconciliation.

acceptance_criteria.given: A workspace record is persisted for a task
acceptance_criteria.when:
The canonical branch is dispatcher-managed or adopted from existing
task state
acceptance_criteria.then:
The record stores branch provenance and locator data sufficient to
distinguish ownership, remote recovery source, and cleanup semantics

acceptance_criteria.given: A metadata-backed workspace is reconstructed or reconciled
acceptance_criteria.when: The canonical branch was previously adopted from a non-dispatch branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
Recovery preserves that adopted canonical branch identity instead of
normalizing it back to the deterministic `dispatch/task/*` namespace

acceptance_criteria.given:
Existing dispatcher-managed workspace records created before provenance
tracking existed
acceptance_criteria.when: They are read after the migration
acceptance_criteria.then:
They default to dispatcher-managed ownership semantics without breaking
current dispatch continuity

items.title: Dispatch Branch Integration Contract
items.description:
Each canonical task branch carries explicit integration metadata so workers
and reviewers know which base branch to target for PRs or local merge-back
instead of assuming `main`.

acceptance_criteria.given: A canonical task branch is provisioned
acceptance_criteria.then:
The resolved base branch and branch-point commit are recorded as the
integration target metadata for that task

acceptance_criteria.given: A worker or reviewer invocation is prepared
acceptance_criteria.when: Orientation or workflow entry content is rendered
acceptance_criteria.then:
The canonical branch, integration target branch, and canonical head or
snapshot under review are included explicitly

items.title: Detached Reviewer Merge Helper
items.description:
In manual_merge publication mode, reviewers working from detached review snapshots have one supported merge helper path for completing review after approval. The helper is distributed with the merge skill, is invokable from the detached review workspace, and performs the standard clean merge mechanics without requiring the reviewer to rediscover ad hoc git workarounds.

The helper keeps the integration branch authoritative by selecting a branch-coherent merge surface for the resolved integration target. When the target branch is not checked out in any worktree, the helper may create and remove a helper-owned temporary target worktree. When the target branch is already checked out in exactly one eligible clean existing worktree, the helper performs the merge through that checkout so Git advances the branch, index, and working tree together. An eligible existing worktree is a pre-existing non-auxiliary project/user checkout, not a detached reviewer snapshot and not a worker, reviewer, helper, plan-scoped, or other dispatch-created auxiliary worktree. The helper must not move a checked-out target ref behind that checkout, must not require the detached reviewer snapshot to check out the target branch manually, must not use leaked auxiliary target checkouts as merge surfaces, and must not leave helper-created target checkout state behind.

items.title: Remote Branch Fallback in Workspace Health Reconciliation
items.description: reconcileWorkspaceHealth() in workspace.ts checks for the canonical branch using refExists() which only checks local refs (git show-ref --verify refs/heads/<branch>). When a canonical branch exists on a remote (e.g. origin) but not locally, the workspace is incorrectly marked unhealthy with missing_canonical_branch. The health check should attempt to fetch or verify the remote ref before declaring the branch missing. This enables dispatch to self-heal workspaces whose local branches were pruned or never fetched, without requiring manual intervention.

items.title: Dispatch Remote Branch Sync
items.description:
Automatic remote synchronization for dispatch-managed branches and the active integration target set. Ensures dispatch work is durable (pushed to remote), each active integration target stays fresh (pulled from remote), and sync failures degrade only the affected target branch.

An active integration target is any distinct integration target branch referenced by a non-closed workspace, plus the project's configured base branch, which is always active even when no current workspace targets it. Each workspace resolves its integration target at provisioning time: plan-scoped tasks use the target selected by @plan-branch-dispatch-target, and all other workspaces use dispatch.base_branch.

The sync remote is determined by convention: the first remote returned by git remote (typically origin). A future dispatch.remote config field can override this if multi-remote setups arise.

Design decisions:
- Dispatch branches are pushed after first invocation completion (not on creation), since an empty branch is noise.
- Integration targets use fast-forward only during remote sync; divergence is a structural problem requiring operator intervention, not auto-merge.
- Existing workspaces provisioned from an older target commit are not rebased; staleness resolves naturally at merge time.
- The active integration target set is rebuilt from the workspace registry on engine start rather than maintained incrementally, avoiding stale-set races between workspace lifecycle changes and sync bookkeeping.
- Degraded state, staleness tracking, and push serialization are scoped per integration target branch so a diverged or busy target does not block tasks targeting healthy branches.
- The push and pull paths share a single source of truth for active integration targets. Separate push-side and pull-side target tracking is not allowed because the two views could diverge.
- When two reviewers merge concurrently into the same integration target, git ref serialization decides the winner: one merge succeeds and the other fails non-fast-forward. The failing task follows the normal needs_work review path. This is expected behavior, not a dispatch bug.

items.title: Dispatch Integration Mutation Scope Contract
items.description: Integration-branch operations mutate only an eligible branch-coherent mutation surface for the configured integration branch. An eligible occupied mutation surface is a pre-existing non-auxiliary project/user checkout of the integration target branch, not a worker, reviewer, helper, plan-scoped, detached review, or other dispatch-created auxiliary worktree. Dispatch does not spill into unrelated repository state, does not mutate worker or reviewer task worktrees as side effects, does not move checked-out integration target refs behind their worktrees, and fails safely when the intended mutation surface is ambiguous, auxiliary, or unsafe.

acceptance_criteria.then: in_progress tasks are considered dispatch candidates and can be queued without waiting for a new external state transition

acceptance_criteria.given: agent definitions include dispatch rules and filters
acceptance_criteria.when: dispatch event types are validated and built-in worker defaults are seeded

items.title: Dispatch Scheduling Priority Model
items.description:
Dispatch ordering is governed by one explicit cross-agent scheduler
contract spanning candidate kind, numeric task priority, continuity or
affinity, and fairness. Agent definition order must not be the deciding
rule for cross-agent work ordering.

acceptance_criteria.given: The scheduler evaluates queued or candidate invocations
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only candidates that satisfy the applicable eligibility contract are
ranked: pending and needs_work candidates must pass base task
readiness, in_progress and pending_review candidates must come from
explicit continuation or handoff dispatch support, and any candidate
with stale workspace state or unresolved dependency blocking is
excluded

acceptance_criteria.given: Eligible candidates exist across candidate bands
acceptance_criteria.then:
The fixed band order is in_progress first, then needs_work, then
pending_review, then pending

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple eligible candidates share the same candidate band
acceptance_criteria.then:
Lower numeric task priority values (P1 before P5) rank ahead of higher
numeric values before continuity or FIFO is considered

acceptance_criteria.given:
Multiple eligible candidates share the same candidate band and the same
numeric priority
acceptance_criteria.then:
Continuity or affinity signals may prefer continuing an active review
or fix-cycle chain before unrelated work

acceptance_criteria.given:
Continuity or affinity would otherwise keep skipping other equal-band,
equal-priority work indefinitely
acceptance_criteria.when: A candidate exceeds the scheduler's starvation threshold
acceptance_criteria.then:
Continuity or affinity is ignored for that comparison and the oldest
equal-band, equal-priority eligible candidate wins

acceptance_criteria.given:
pending_review and pending candidates both exist and no in_progress or
needs_work work is waiting
acceptance_criteria.when: The scheduler selects the next invocation
acceptance_criteria.then:
pending_review work remains ahead of pending work as a hard scheduler
rule, not merely an affinity preference

acceptance_criteria.given: The scheduler chooses between worker and reviewer candidates
acceptance_criteria.then:
The chosen order follows the scheduler contract above rather than agent
definition order alone

acceptance_criteria.given: queued dispatch candidates are excluded during eligibility pruning
acceptance_criteria.when: the scheduler discards a worker or reviewer candidate
acceptance_criteria.then: dispatch diagnostics identify the task ref, agent, and exclusion reason for each discarded candidate instead of logging only aggregate discard counts

items.title: Dispatch Workspace Orientation Prompt
items.description:
The dispatch prompt explicitly orients the agent to its workspace, branch,
integration target, role, focus, and current bootstrap state so the agent
starts from the correct operational context without guesswork.

acceptance_criteria.given: A worker or reviewer invocation prompt is built
acceptance_criteria.then:
The prompt includes the workspace path, canonical branch, integration
target branch, task ref, role, focus, and the reason this invocation
was selected

acceptance_criteria.given:
The dispatcher has branch mode, canonical head, bootstrap, health, or
dependency status for the workspace
acceptance_criteria.then:
The prompt states whether the workspace is a mutable worker branch or a
detached review snapshot, identifies the canonical head being resumed or
reviewed, and summarizes relevant prepared state and caveats

acceptance_criteria.given: The invocation is part of a fix cycle or review cycle
acceptance_criteria.then:
The prompt makes the cycle context explicit, including whether a
follow-up worker will resume the same canonical branch after review and
which base branch remains the publication target

acceptance_criteria.given: A worker or reviewer invocation prompt is built with workspace metadata
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent receives the dispatch prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: The prompt includes an explicit instruction that the agent must run all commands from the assigned workspace directory, not the project root, because the workspace is an isolated git worktree with the correct branch checked out

items.title: Scoped Dispatch Shadow Serialization
items.description:
Shadow-branch protection serializes only kspec metadata mutations, not the
full lifetime of every invocation, so isolated code work can overlap safely
across worker and reviewer roles.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Two isolated invocations are running concurrently in separate code
worktrees
acceptance_criteria.when: Neither invocation is performing a kspec mutation
acceptance_criteria.then:
They are allowed to continue in parallel without waiting on a global
invocation-level mutex

acceptance_criteria.given:
Multiple invocations attempt shadow-branch mutations such as task note,
task submit, task needs-work, or plan/task metadata writes
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only the mutation sections are serialized so shadow branch integrity is
preserved

acceptance_criteria.given: A mutation-level lock cannot be acquired or a protected mutation fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
The error is surfaced as a mutation failure, not disguised as a generic
workspace execution failure

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple dispatch-scoped kspec CLI mutations are queued behind a held lock
acceptance_criteria.when: The lock holder process is alive, executing, and has not exceeded the maximum hold duration ceiling
acceptance_criteria.then: Waiting mutations block until the lock is released

acceptance_criteria.given: A dispatch mutation is waiting for the shadow mutation lock
acceptance_criteria.when: The lock holder process is no longer alive
acceptance_criteria.then: Stale lock detection identifies the orphaned lock, cleans it up, and the waiting mutation acquires the lock without manual intervention

acceptance_criteria.given: The KSPEC_SHADOW_MUTATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable is set to a finite value
acceptance_criteria.when: A dispatch mutation waits for the lock
acceptance_criteria.then: The explicit timeout is honored, overriding the default wait-indefinitely behavior

acceptance_criteria.given: The shadow mutation lock is acquired for a protected operation
acceptance_criteria.when: The operation completes, whether successfully or with an error
acceptance_criteria.then: The lock is released before any subsequent work continues in that code path

acceptance_criteria.given: The shadow mutation lock has been held by a process
acceptance_criteria.when: The hold duration exceeds a configurable maximum (KSPEC_SHADOW_MUTATION_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_MS environment variable, defaulting to 30000ms)
acceptance_criteria.then: The lock is eligible for reclamation by other processes regardless of whether the holder process is alive

acceptance_criteria.given: Periodic reconciliation evaluates multiple workspace records requiring shadow mutations
acceptance_criteria.when: Other processes are waiting to acquire the shadow mutation lock
acceptance_criteria.then: Reconciliation yields the lock between individual record evaluations so waiting mutations can interleave

acceptance_criteria.given: A process attempts to acquire the shadow mutation lock and the current holder process is alive but has held the lock beyond the maximum duration ceiling
acceptance_criteria.when: The acquiring process evaluates lock staleness
acceptance_criteria.then: The lock is treated as orphaned and reclaimed, with a diagnostic message identifying the previous holder

acceptance_criteria.given: A process reclaims the shadow mutation lock from a holder that exceeded the maximum hold duration
acceptance_criteria.when: The new holder begins its protected operation
acceptance_criteria.then: The new holder checks the shadow worktree for uncommitted dirty state from the previous holder and rolls back uncommitted changes before proceeding with its own mutation

items.title: Review and Fix-Cycle Workspace Discovery Before Discard
items.description:
Queue pruning for `pending_review` and `needs_work` performs workspace
discovery and recovery before treating a task as missing or ineligible, so
dispatch can recover work that already exists outside the local checkout.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A queued `pending_review` or `needs_work` dispatch entry has no healthy
local workspace candidate
acceptance_criteria.then:
Dispatch first attempts recovery from registry state, metadata-backed
worktrees, recorded task submission linkage, and remote or review
locators before discarding the queue entry as missing

acceptance_criteria.given: One of those recovery paths succeeds
acceptance_criteria.then:
The queue entry remains eligible and normal provisioning proceeds on the
recovered or adopted canonical branch lineage

acceptance_criteria.given: No trustworthy recovery path exists for the review or fix-cycle task
acceptance_criteria.then:
The engine emits explicit task-linked diagnostics and recovery guidance
rather than silently pruning the work as stale or synthesizing a fresh
unrelated branch

acceptance_criteria.given:
Multiple branch signals exist, such as existing registry state,
explicitly repaired task linkage, captured submission linkage, and
remote or review-derived discovery
acceptance_criteria.when: Dispatch resolves the branch-of-record for review or fix-cycle work
acceptance_criteria.then:
It applies explicit precedence in that order and blocks with
diagnostics rather than guessing when the competing signals cannot be
reconciled safely

items.title: Per-Task Dispatch Drain Coalescing
items.description: When multiple task state change events arrive for the same task in rapid succession, the dispatch engine defers queue draining behind a per-task coalescing window instead of draining immediately after each enqueue. This ensures that only the final landing state is evaluated for dispatch, preventing spurious agent spawns for transient intermediate states (e.g., unblock → start → submit within seconds spawning both a worker and a reviewer instead of just the reviewer).

acceptance_criteria.given: A task state change event is received by the dispatch engine
acceptance_criteria.when: The engine enqueues matching agent dispatch entries
acceptance_criteria.then: Instead of draining queues immediately, the engine schedules a per-task coalescing timer (configurable, default 5 seconds). If the timer is already pending for that task, it is reset to the full window duration.

acceptance_criteria.given: A per-task coalescing timer expires with no further events for that task
acceptance_criteria.then: The existing stale-entry pruning (ac-17 of @agent-dispatch-engine) evaluates queue entries against the task's current on-disk state, discarding entries whose expected status no longer matches, and only the entries matching the final landing state survive to be spawned.

acceptance_criteria.given: State change events arrive for different tasks concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: Each task's coalescing timer is independent — a rapid transition on task A does not delay dispatching for task B whose timer has already expired or was never set.

acceptance_criteria.given: The coalescing window duration is configurable via DispatchEngineOptions
acceptance_criteria.then: The coalesceWindowMs option controls the per-task drain delay (default 5000ms). Setting it to 0 disables coalescing and preserves the current immediate-drain behavior for backward compatibility.

acceptance_criteria.given: per-task coalescing timers are pending
acceptance_criteria.then: matching timers are cancelled

acceptance_criteria.given: A single task state change event arrives with no subsequent events for the same task
acceptance_criteria.then: The drain proceeds normally after the coalescing delay. The only observable difference from pre-coalescing behavior is the added latency of the coalescing window.

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine drains queues from bootstrap (ac-8), periodic reconciliation (ac-19/20), or post-invocation re-evaluation (ac-24) paths
acceptance_criteria.then: The drain executes immediately without coalescing delay. Coalescing only applies to drains triggered by individual state change events via handleStateChange(). These full-scan paths are deliberate evaluations, not reactions to rapid external events.

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple per-task coalescing timers expire at approximately the same time, or a timer fires while a drain is already in progress
acceptance_criteria.when: The timer callbacks attempt concurrent _drainQueues() calls
acceptance_criteria.then: A drain-pending flag or mutex serializes drain execution. If a drain is already running, the pending drain request is coalesced into a single follow-up drain after the current one completes, rather than running concurrently.

acceptance_criteria.given: A drain is triggered from any source (coalescing timers, post-invocation re-evaluation, retry wake-ups, reconciliation, or bootstrap)
acceptance_criteria.when: A drain is already in progress
acceptance_criteria.then: The new drain request is coalesced into a single follow-up drain after the current one completes, rather than running concurrently. This serialization governs execution ordering, not dispatch timing — drains that bypass coalescing delay are still triggered immediately but wait for any in-progress drain to complete before executing.

acceptance_criteria.given: a matching pending drain exists
acceptance_criteria.then: that drain does not start work

acceptance_criteria.given: a matching invocation is active
acceptance_criteria.then: that invocation is cancelled

items.title: Dispatch Canonical Task Identity
items.description:
Dispatch treats the resolved full task ULID as the authoritative identity for every task-scoped runtime decision. Human-readable task refs, slug refs, and unique ULID-prefix refs may be accepted as command/display aliases, but they do not define scheduler, active invocation, in-flight, workspace, cleanup, registry, or session identity.

This requirement intentionally owns the new alias/canonicalization behavior instead of adding ACs directly to already-implemented broad specs. It relates to the existing dispatch, workspace, event-payload, and reference-resolution contracts that it tightens.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task-scoped dispatch event, watcher change, bootstrap candidate, reconciliation candidate, retry candidate, or post-invocation candidate identifies a task by full task ULID, unique task ULID prefix, slug ref, loaded task object, or a task_id plus a task_ref that resolves to the same task
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch runtime accepts that input for scheduling or lifecycle processing
acceptance_criteria.then: The accepted candidate is associated with the resolved full task ULID as its canonical task identity, and any raw/display task ref is kept separate from that identity for prompts, logs, status text, or CLI command text only.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task-scoped dispatch input identifies a task only by an unresolved or ambiguous task ref, or includes a task_id plus a task_ref that resolves to a different task than the task_id
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch runtime normalizes the input before scheduling, workspace provisioning, cleanup protection, session creation, or event emission
acceptance_criteria.then: The input is rejected or skipped with an operator-actionable diagnostic identifying the provided task_id when present, the provided task_ref when present, the source path, and the resolution outcome; no queue entry, active invocation, in-flight marker, workspace record, cleanup protection entry, session metadata, or invocation/session payload is created using the invalid or mismatched raw ref as task identity.

acceptance_criteria.given: A dispatch event includes a valid full task_id and omits task_ref
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatch runtime accepts the event
acceptance_criteria.then: The runtime uses the provided task_id as the canonical task identity, derives `@<task_id>` as the default display ref when no better display ref is available, and does not reject the event solely because task_ref is absent.

acceptance_criteria.given: Refs such as `@task-slug`, `@<full-task-ulid>`, and a unique `@<task-ulid-prefix>` all resolve to the same task
acceptance_criteria.when: Bootstrap, file-watcher, API-event, periodic reconciliation, post-invocation reconciliation, retry wake-up, or queue-drain paths evaluate active, queued, deferred, or in-flight dispatch work for that task
acceptance_criteria.then: Scheduler dedupe treats those refs as one task and does not enqueue or spawn duplicate work for the same agent and canonical task identity.

acceptance_criteria.given:
One agent has an active or in-flight invocation for a task under one valid task ref alias
And another agent has a queued or newly eligible candidate for the same task under another valid task ref alias
acceptance_criteria.when: The scheduler selects the next invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The second candidate remains queued or is deferred until the active or in-flight invocation for the canonical task identity completes, and before any later spawn it is subject to the same stale-candidate checks as any other queued entry.

acceptance_criteria.given: A non-closed dispatch workspace record exists for a task using any historical or display task ref that resolves to that task
acceptance_criteria.when: Provisioning, reconciliation, validation, cleanup, or lookup evaluates workspace state for the same task using a different valid alias
acceptance_criteria.then: The registry compares records by canonical task ULID, reuses the existing non-closed workspace record when appropriate, and rejects or reports more than one non-closed workspace record for the same canonical task identity.

acceptance_criteria.given: Existing dispatch workspace registry records were persisted before canonical task identity was recorded separately from task_ref
acceptance_criteria.when: Workspace registry loading, validation, provisioning, or reconciliation encounters those records
acceptance_criteria.then: Records whose historical task_ref still resolves to a task are backfilled or interpreted with that task's canonical ULID identity; records whose historical task_ref cannot resolve are marked stale or invalid with recovery guidance and must not cause duplicate workspace provisioning for any resolvable task alias.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has a canonical dispatch branch or workspace lineage
acceptance_criteria.when: A worker, reviewer, fix-cycle worker, cleanup pass, or artifact reconciliation refers to that task by slug, full ULID, unique ULID prefix, or after the task's primary slug changes
acceptance_criteria.then: The existing branch/workspace lineage is selected by canonical task ULID; the dispatcher does not create a new workspace id, branch lineage, worktree path, or workspace record solely because the display ref changed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task has active, in-flight, provisioning, stale, or non-closed workspace state under one valid task ref alias
acceptance_criteria.when: Workspace artifact cleanup evaluates branches, worktrees, reviewer snapshots, root directories, or metadata-backed artifacts that refer to the same task by another valid alias
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup protection resolves both aliases to the same canonical task identity and preserves artifacts that are protected by active, in-flight, provisioning, stale/recoverable, or non-closed registry state.

acceptance_criteria.given: A task-scoped invocation or session lifecycle event is emitted or persisted
acceptance_criteria.when: The payload or session metadata includes task identity fields
acceptance_criteria.then: It includes the canonical full task ULID identity separately from any display task ref, and downstream dispatch consumers use the canonical task id for identity decisions rather than the display ref.

acceptance_criteria.given: The scheduler, workspace registry, event ingress, or cleanup protection discards, defers, reuses, rejects, or preserves state because another alias already represents the same canonical task
acceptance_criteria.when: Diagnostics or status output identify the decision
acceptance_criteria.then: They include the canonical task ULID when known, the original raw task ref when available, the agent id or workspace id when applicable, and the exclusion, reuse, rejection, or preservation reason.

acceptance_criteria.given: An automation agent action from a schedule, hook, or composition join is task-bound by explicit action task_ref or by a triggering event task_ref/task_id, and that task identifier is a slug ref, full task ULID ref, unique task ULID prefix ref, or task_id plus display task_ref pair
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon automation spawner creates the downstream agent invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The spawner resolves the task binding before session creation, passes the canonical full task ULID as the invocation task_id, retains the chosen human-readable task ref only as task_ref/display metadata, and rejects unresolved, ambiguous, or mismatched task bindings with an action-run failure before creating a session or invocation payload for the raw ref. An explicit action task_ref is the authoritative task binding when present; event task_id/task_ref fields are used for task identity only when task_binding derives the task from the event.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project-context caller starts a task-scoped invocation through the invocation runtime, including dispatch scheduler spawns, one-shot CLI agent runs, daemon automation agent actions, retry/fix-cycle spawns, or tests that model those production paths
acceptance_criteria.when: The invocation runtime persists session metadata or emits invocation/session lifecycle events for that task-scoped invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The persisted and emitted task_id is the resolved full task ULID, the task_ref field is the display ref when one is available, and callers that cannot resolve a provided task ref do not create a task-scoped session whose task_id is the unresolved slug or raw ref. Legacy sessions that already stored a raw ref may still be read through compatibility filters, but new project-context task-bound sessions must not be written with raw refs as task_id.

acceptance_criteria.given: Lifecycle reconciliation or cleanup needs the integration target branch for a task, and a non-closed workspace registry record for that task exists with either task_id set to the full ULID or only a historical task_ref that resolves to the same task through a slug, full ULID ref, or unique ULID-prefix ref
acceptance_criteria.when: The dispatcher loads the workspace target branch for that task during cleanup, integration, reconciliation, or terminal-state processing
acceptance_criteria.then: The dispatcher selects the record by canonical task identity and returns the existing target branch independently of which valid alias is supplied; it must not miss the record, fall back to a different target, or create conflicting lifecycle state solely because the persisted display ref differs from the current canonical ref.

acceptance_criteria.given: Dispatch runtime, cleanup, reconciliation, review/fix-cycle recovery, or CLI/operator workspace status code looks up workspace records for a task identifier
acceptance_criteria.when: The query identifier or stored record contains task_id, task_ref, slug ref, full ULID ref, or unique ULID-prefix ref data that can be resolved to a task
acceptance_criteria.then: The lookup compares the resolved full task ULID rather than exact raw task_ref strings, treats exact raw-ref equality only as a degraded fallback when neither side can be resolved, and exposes any raw task-ref-only helper as test-only/deprecated or replaces it with a canonical-safe API so production callers cannot reintroduce alias-sensitive workspace lookup.

items.title: CLI Input Type Safety
items.description:
All CLI commands must validate their inputs against the defined type
constraints before executing. This applies to both mutation commands
(which persist data) and query commands (which filter data). When a
command accepts an option or argument with a constrained type — an
enum, a number within a range, a reference format, or any value with
a schema-defined shape — it must reject invalid values with a clear
error rather than passing them through unchecked.

Mutation commands that accept invalid input cause data corruption:
values are written to YAML and silently dropped on next read. Query
commands that accept invalid filters silently return empty results,
wasting the user's time debugging "missing" data.

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI mutation command accepts a typed option
acceptance_criteria.when: The provided value does not match the option's type constraint
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command exits with non-zero status and stderr describes the
invalid value and lists what is valid, before any write occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI query command accepts a typed filter option
acceptance_criteria.when: The provided value does not match the filter's type constraint
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command exits with non-zero status and stderr describes the
invalid value, rather than silently returning empty results

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI command accepts a typed option
acceptance_criteria.when: The provided value satisfies the type constraint
acceptance_criteria.then: The command executes normally

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI command option has a default value
acceptance_criteria.then: The default value itself satisfies the type constraint

inherited_acs.given: Any input surface accepts a field with a defined type constraint
inherited_acs.when: The provided value does not satisfy the constraint
inherited_acs.then:
The operation is rejected before any data is persisted or
state is mutated

inherited_acs.given: An input validation error occurs for a constrained field
inherited_acs.when: The error is reported to the caller
inherited_acs.then:
The message includes the set of valid alternatives for the
field, not just the field name and invalid value (extends
@trait-error-guidance ac-5 which requires identifying the
field/value but not listing valid alternatives)

inherited_acs.then:

than a separately maintained check

items.title: CLI Daemon Proxy Mode
items.description:
When a daemon is running, the CLI routes commands through it instead
of operating directly on the shadow branch. This makes the daemon
the single writer, eliminating coherence issues between CLI mutations
and daemon state. The CLI auto-detects daemon availability and routes
accordingly. Users can force either mode explicitly.

items.title: kspec session checkpoint
items.description:
Pre-stop hook for Claude Code integration.

Checks for uncommitted git changes (staged, unstaged, untracked) before allowing session to end. Focuses on preventing data loss from uncommitted work.

One-time trigger: Reads stop_hook_active from Claude Code stdin JSON to detect retry. First trigger blocks with instructions, subsequent triggers allow stop.

Output: JSON formatted for Claude Code hook consumption with clear kspec-branded message instructing agent to commit changes. Uses {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} format.

Installation: Controlled by project configuration (kspec.config.yaml). Disabled by default. When enabled, kspec setup installs this hook to project-level .claude/settings.json. Hook format requires matcher field (even if empty string).

acceptance_criteria.given: The checkpoint hook is triggered
acceptance_criteria.then: Only uncommitted git changes are reported as issues. Task status and todo completeness are not checked.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new project runs kspec init or kspec setup
acceptance_criteria.then: The checkpoint hook is not installed.

acceptance_criteria.given: Project configuration has checkpoint enabled
acceptance_criteria.then: The checkpoint hook is installed.

acceptance_criteria.given: The checkpoint hook was previously installed
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec setup runs and checkpoint is disabled or unconfigured
acceptance_criteria.then: The hook is removed.

items.title: kspec session prompt-check
items.description:
UserPromptSubmit hook for spec-first workflow reinforcement.

Outputs a lean reminder on every user prompt: '[kspec] Before implementing behavior changes, check spec coverage. Update spec first if needed.'

Design rationale:
- Always injects (no filtering) - Claude is smart enough to apply when relevant
- Minimal token overhead - short, instructive message
- Non-blocking - context injection, not gating

items.title: Meta-Spec System
items.description:
Meta-spec is the layer that defines HOW work happens, separate from
WHAT is being built (spec) and tracking WORK (tasks).

The key distinction:
- Spec: What to build (features, requirements)
- Tasks: Work to do (implement feature X)
- Meta-spec: How to work (check spec before implementing)

Meta-spec enables a self-improvement loop:
1. Define workflows → 2. Track adherence → 3. Identify friction →
4. Propose improvements → 5. Update workflows → (repeat)

Meta-spec complements prose docs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) rather than
replacing them. Structured definitions + prose guidance work together.

items.title: Dispatch Event Taxonomy
items.description:
Defines the event domains and maintains a registry of valid event type identifiers. Events use dotted-namespace domains. The registry is an explicit enumeration of known events, not a free-form string pattern — event identifiers must be registered to be valid.

Event domains:
- task.ready, task.in_progress, task.needs_work, task.pending_review (existing, unchanged)
- invocation.started, invocation.completed, invocation.failed, invocation.stalled
- session.idle, session.ended, session.idle_timeout, session.cancelled
- schedule.tick
- action.started, action.completed, action.failed (universal action run tracking — every hook, schedule, and composition action produces action run events regardless of action type)

Identity model: session_id and invocation_id are the same value. A "session" in the dispatch context IS an invocation — they are not separate entities. invocation.* events use session_id as the canonical identifier. action.* events use action_run_id as their canonical identifier and link to session_id when the action type is agent.

All events carry the standard envelope defined by @dispatch-event-envelope.

acceptance_criteria.then:
A corresponding invocation.completed, invocation.failed, or

acceptance_criteria.when: The session reaches a terminal state

items.title: Session Idle Event
items.description:
Event emitted each time an agent completes a turn and the session
enters idle state. This event enables post-turn automation and
signals that the session is ready for follow-up prompts.

The session idle event fires while the session is still alive and
receptive to prompts. Hooks on this event can inject follow-up
prompts via the session prompt action type, enabling
trigger-driven multi-turn conversations.

acceptance_criteria.then: The hook does not execute

acceptance_criteria.then: Existing configurations are unaffected

items.title: Dispatch Action Model
items.description:
The shared action model used by hooks, schedules, and composition join triggers. An action describes what to do when an event matches.

Five action types:
- command: Run an executable with explicit arguments
- kspec: Run a kspec CLI command
- agent: Spawn an agent invocation
- notify: Emit a WebSocket notification
- session_prompt: Deliver a prompt to an active session

Every action execution produces an action run — a lightweight tracking record with unique ID, status, duration, and optional linked invocation_id (for agent actions). Action runs are the uniform abstraction that overlap policies, UI status, event logging, and action history key off of, regardless of action type.

Template variables use {{var}} syntax resolved from the triggering event's envelope and payload.

acceptance_criteria.given: A command action is configured
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command runs asynchronously as a child process; the action
does not block event processing; an action.started event is
emitted; on completion an action.completed or action.failed
event is emitted

acceptance_criteria.given: A command action is configured with a timeout
acceptance_criteria.when: The command exceeds the timeout duration
acceptance_criteria.then:
The process is terminated and an action.failed event is emitted
with timeout as the reason

acceptance_criteria.given: A kspec action is configured
acceptance_criteria.then:
The kspec command runs in the project root directory; shadow
branch mutations use the existing per-mutation scoped lock
(consistent with @scoped-dispatch-shadow-serialization), not
a per-command lock; the parent event's correlation_id is injected
via KSPEC_CORRELATION_ID env var so CLI-emitted events inherit
the causal chain for loop prevention

acceptance_criteria.then:
A new invocation spawns using the standard invocation lifecycle;
the action run tracks the linked invocation_id

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent action spawns a non-task-scoped invocation
acceptance_criteria.then:
The invocation is not subject to per-task exclusivity; it is
subject only to the target agent's max_concurrent

items.title: Session Prompt Action Type
items.description:
Action type that delivers a prompt to an active session that is
currently in idle state. Unlike the agent action (which spawns a
new invocation), a session prompt action targets an existing
session.

This is the mechanism that allows hooks on session idle events to
inject follow-up prompts into the same conversation. The agent
retains full conversation context across turns.

Session prompt actions can only target sessions that are alive
and idle. If the target session is already closed or in prompting
state, the prompt is queued or fails gracefully.

acceptance_criteria.when: The action executes and the target session is in idle state
acceptance_criteria.then: The prompt is delivered to the session as a follow-up turn

acceptance_criteria.then:

items.title: Dispatch Hook System
items.description:
A hook is an event-triggered action. Hooks are configured in
kynetic.meta.yaml under a top-level hooks section. Each hook has:
on (event type from registry), filter (structured payload filter),
action (from the shared action model), name (label), and enabled
(boolean).

Hooks run asynchronously and independently. Multiple hooks can
match the same event. Hook failures are isolated. Configuration
changes take effect on the next event without daemon restart.

acceptance_criteria.then:

items.title: Dispatch Schedule Entities
items.description:
Schedules are first-class entities in kynetic.meta.yaml that fire
events on a cron-style cadence. Each schedule references an action
(from the shared action model) with overlap policy, enable/disable,
and optional backfill on restart.

Overlap policies control behavior when a previous action run (not
just invocation) is still active: skip (drop the tick), buffer_one
(queue at most one), allow (start subject to concurrency limits).

Schedule evaluation has minute-level resolution.

acceptance_criteria.when: The cron expression matches the current time
acceptance_criteria.then:
The configured action executes with schedule context in the
event payload

acceptance_criteria.then:
The tick is skipped and the schedule advances to the next
occurrence

acceptance_criteria.when: Multiple ticks arrive while the action is running
acceptance_criteria.then:
At most one tick is buffered; additional ticks are dropped;
the buffered tick runs when the active action completes

acceptance_criteria.then: No action is taken until the schedule is re-enabled

acceptance_criteria.given:
A schedule with overlap_policy: allow fires while the previous

acceptance_criteria.when: The new action is attempted and the target agent has max_concurrent: 1

acceptance_criteria.given: Schedule configuration changes while the schedule engine is running
acceptance_criteria.then:
Updated schedules use new settings; added schedules are evaluated
from the next cycle; removed schedules stop ticking but in-flight
actions complete normally

acceptance_criteria.given: A schedule tick is accepted and its action begins executing
acceptance_criteria.when: A concurrent evaluation cycle checks whether the schedule has an active run (for overlap policy enforcement)
acceptance_criteria.then: The run is recognized as active from the moment the tick is accepted, not from when the action completes

items.title: Dispatch Composition Patterns
items.description:
Multi-agent coordination patterns built on the event bus and hook
system. Composition is achieved through event-driven chaining:

1. Fan-out: Multiple agents match the same event (existing).
2. Pipeline: A hook on one agent's completion triggers another,
   passing outcome context via the agent action input contract.
3. Synthesis (fan-in): A join configuration waits for N related
   action runs to complete before triggering a synthesis action.
4. Conditional routing: Separate hooks for success vs failure
   outcomes enable different follow-up paths.

acceptance_criteria.then:
Agent B receives context about A's session and outcome per
the agent action input contract

acceptance_criteria.then:

acceptance_criteria.then:

which runs completed, which failed, and which timed out

for the same agent
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the failure hook fires; the completion hook does not

items.title: Dispatch Composition Correlation and Join Semantics
items.description:
Defines how composition groups are created, how group_id propagates
through chained actions, what counts toward the join threshold,
and behavior on daemon restart.

Key distinction: a composition config (stored in meta YAML) defines
the join rules. A composition activation is a runtime instance of
that config with a unique activation_id. One config can have multiple
concurrent activations (e.g. a scheduled fan-out that runs nightly).
API/UI status refers to activations, not configs.

A composition config exists and a triggering event matches

tagged with the composition's config_id)
acceptance_criteria.when: The join accumulator processes the event

acceptance_criteria.then:
The run counts toward the join threshold; failed and stalled

acceptance_criteria.then:

begins, not when the group is configured

acceptance_criteria.then:
In-progress composition groups are lost (volatile state);
the group does not resume and the on_complete action does not

items.title: Multi-Turn Session Lifecycle
items.description:
Event-driven session lifecycle where sessions remain alive between
turns. After each agent turn completes, the session enters an idle
state and emits a session idle event. The
session stays open until something explicitly closes it — a
timeout, a close action, or the absence of any queued prompts
after a grace period.

The lifecycle is: spawn → idle ⇄ prompting → close. The session
loops between prompting and idle until a close decision is made.
This enables post-turn automation (reflection prompts, chained
analysis) and allows external sources to deliver follow-up
prompts to a running session.

A multi-turn session is a single invocation. The session
identifier represents the full lifecycle from spawn to close,
regardless of how many turns occur. The invocation completed
event fires once at session close. The session idle event
provides the per-turn observation point.

items.title: Active Session Registry
items.description:
A runtime registry of active sessions that allows actions to
deliver prompts to live sessions. Maps session identifiers to
handles providing prompt delivery and state query capabilities.

The registry is volatile (daemon lifetime). It exposes a minimal
interface for prompt delivery, state query, and close requests.
This keeps action execution decoupled from session internals
while enabling the session prompt action type.

acceptance_criteria.then:
It receives a handle if the session is active, or no result
if the session has been closed

acceptance_criteria.when: Active sessions exist in the registry
acceptance_criteria.then:
All registered sessions are closed and the registry is
cleared

items.title: Automation Action Type Completeness
items.description:
When the daemon starts automation subsystems (schedule engine, hook executor, join accumulator), each subsystem must be capable of executing every supported action type. The supported action types are: command, kspec, agent, notify, and session_prompt. Each action type has prerequisites that must be satisfied before execution — agent actions need the ability to spawn invocations, notify actions need the ability to broadcast to clients, session_prompt actions need access to active sessions.

If an automation subsystem cannot execute a configured action type, the failure must be diagnosable from the action run record and event log.

acceptance_criteria.given: a schedule is configured with any supported action type
acceptance_criteria.then: the action executes successfully regardless of action type

acceptance_criteria.given: a hook is configured with any supported action type
acceptance_criteria.then: the action executes successfully regardless of action type

acceptance_criteria.given: a composition join trigger has any supported action type
acceptance_criteria.then: the action executes successfully regardless of action type

acceptance_criteria.given: an automation subsystem cannot fulfill a configured action type
acceptance_criteria.then: the action run fails with an error message identifying what capability is missing and which action type requires it

acceptance_criteria.given: an automation action fails for any reason
acceptance_criteria.when: the failure event is emitted to the event bus
acceptance_criteria.then: the event payload includes the error description and failure reason from the action run so the cause is diagnosable from the event log

items.title: Scaffolded Project Config File

The scaffolded file uses only documented config keys, is valid

items.title: Default Project Agents and Conventions
items.description:
When a project is initialized with full setup for the first
time, the meta spec is seeded with a complete set of default
agents covering task work, code review, general development,
and plan review, plus baseline conventions for commits,
architecture, and testing. Every default agent has write
authorization enabled unconditionally so agents can operate
without per-action approval. These defaults establish the
minimum context every project needs for normal task work,
code review, and plan review to function out of the box.
After the initial seed, the scaffold never recreates items
the user has deliberately removed or renamed — the scaffold
is first-time-only state, not a recurring reset.

This spec is the single source of truth for the default
agent roster. Older specs that describe individual scaffold
agents by name are superseded by this one, and their tests
are re-annotated against the acceptance criteria below.

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh project completes full setup
acceptance_criteria.when: The meta spec agents are listed
acceptance_criteria.then:
A task worker agent is present with dispatch rules that
respond to task ready and task needs-work events, uses
the automation eligibility filter by default, and has
write authorization enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh project completes full setup
acceptance_criteria.when: The meta spec agents are listed
acceptance_criteria.then:
A code review agent is present with a dispatch rule that
responds to task pending-review events and has write
authorization enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh project completes full setup
acceptance_criteria.when: The meta spec agents are listed
acceptance_criteria.then:
A primary development agent is present with capabilities
covering code, test, refactor, and review, and has
write authorization enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh project completes full setup
acceptance_criteria.when: The meta spec agents are listed
acceptance_criteria.then:
A plan reviewer agent is present with the review
capability and has write authorization enabled

acceptance_criteria.then:

both attached to the agent

documentation

acceptance_criteria.then:

A commits convention exists with rules covering commit

items.title: Default Session Reflection Hook
items.description: When a project is initialized with full setup, a single reflection hook is scaffolded that fires on any idle agent session regardless of which agent owns it, and prompts the session to run the reflect skill. Reflection applies to every session uniformly so setup does not need to enumerate individual agents. Users may disable or remove the hook without breaking any other setup invariant. The hook fires only on the first session idle event of an invocation, not on every turn of a multi-turn session.

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh project completes full setup
acceptance_criteria.then: A single reflection hook is present that triggers on session.idle events from any agent session (not scoped to a specific agent) and prompts the session to run the reflect skill. The hook may carry filters limiting which idle events trigger reflection

is created

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent runs a multi-turn session that produces multiple session idle events
acceptance_criteria.when: Each session idle event is emitted
acceptance_criteria.then: The hook's action executes only for the first idle event of the invocation

items.title: Single-Command Version Upgrade
items.description:
A dedicated upgrade command brings a project from any
previously-supported kspec version to the currently
installed version in a single invocation. The command
detects version skew, runs all required migrations,
re-renders skills, regenerates agent instructions, and
reports the net result. The upgrade is idempotent and safe
to run when the project is already current.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project was initialized with an older kspec version
and its last-known version is recorded in project state
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command reads the recorded last-known version and
identifies it as the source version for the upgrade

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has no recorded last-known version
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command infers a source version from the shape of
project state and records it with approximate confidence

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project's source version cannot be identified or
inferred
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command reports the source version as unknown,
names the target version, and proceeds with the full
upgrade pipeline as if the project were on the oldest
supported version

acceptance_criteria.given:
The upgrade command has determined source and target
versions
acceptance_criteria.when: The command begins its upgrade pipeline
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command reports the source version and the target
version before any changes are applied, and marks the
source as approximate or unknown when it was inferred
rather than read directly

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project uses a task storage format that is no longer

acceptance_criteria.then:
The task storage migration is run as part of the upgrade
and reports whether any tasks were migrated

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project has skill files rendered from a previous

Core skills are re-rendered so the rendered files match

items.title: Release Notes Accessible via CLI
items.description:
Users can view the release notes for the currently installed
version and any intervening versions without leaving the
command line. Release notes live in a single project file
that is the source of truth for human readers and the CLI
alike, and the upgrade command surfaces the relevant slice
of that file as part of its output. The file format is
chosen and documented in the release skill so authoring
and CLI consumption stay in sync.

The release notes for every intervening version are
included in the output

items.title: Portable Skill Supporting File References
items.description:
Skill-authored content can reference supporting files that live beside a
skill, such as scripts, reference documents, assets, and legacy docs,
using one portable authoring form. Rendered skill output and adapter
prompt delivery both resolve that portable form to the platform-specific,
project-root-relative path of the rendered supporting file copy for the
active skill runtime.

The contract covers both direct skill markdown and markdown files copied
from the skill's supporting directories. It rejects missing or out-of-
boundary references so agents do not receive broken helper links.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A skill markdown file or copied markdown supporting file contains a
portable reference to a supporting file within the same skill
acceptance_criteria.when: The skill is rendered for a specific platform
acceptance_criteria.then:
The rendered content points to the platform-specific, project-root-
relative path of that rendered supporting file copy

acceptance_criteria.given:
An agent definition injects a skill whose markdown contains a portable
supporting-file reference
acceptance_criteria.when: The invocation prompt is built for a specific adapter
acceptance_criteria.then:
The prompt contains the adapter-appropriate, project-root-relative
path for that supporting file instead of the unresolved portable form

acceptance_criteria.given:
A portable supporting-file reference points to a file that does not
exist in the source skill
acceptance_criteria.when: The skill is validated, rendered, or injected into a prompt
acceptance_criteria.then:
The operation fails with explicit guidance naming the unresolved file
reference instead of silently producing a broken path

acceptance_criteria.given:
A portable supporting-file reference attempts to escape the skill's
own directory tree
acceptance_criteria.when: The skill is validated, rendered, or injected into a prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: The operation is rejected and no escaped path is emitted

items.title: Layered Agent Runner Configuration
items.description:
kspec resolves named agent runners from two simple configuration layers. The
repo/project layer stores portable project-specific values only. The local
system layer stores machine/user-specific process settings, executable
references, arguments, working-directory policy, credential bindings, and
local overrides. The effective runner is the merged result, with system
values overriding project values for the same runner.

acceptance_criteria.given: The project runner config or system runner config contains one or more named runner entries
acceptance_criteria.when: Runner configuration is loaded for a project
acceptance_criteria.then: Each named runner is available to agent resolution by its configured name

acceptance_criteria.given: Portable project-specific runner values are defined for a project
acceptance_criteria.then: They are stored in a repo-managed runner config artifact rather than in agent meta records or process environment variables

acceptance_criteria.given: Local runner values are defined for a project
acceptance_criteria.then: They are stored under the user-level kspec daemon config directory and are not committed to the project repository or shadow branch

acceptance_criteria.given: The same runner field is present in both project and system runner config
acceptance_criteria.when: The effective runner config is resolved
acceptance_criteria.then: The system value is used for that field

acceptance_criteria.given: Project runner config contains supported portable runner values such as non-secret env.set entries, privacy defaults, or diagnostics preferences
acceptance_criteria.then: Those values are accepted as project-layer runner inputs and retain project-layer source metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: Project runner config contains a known adapter or harness API key, auth token, OAuth token, credential variable, or secret-looking literal field
acceptance_criteria.then: The project config is rejected before it can become the effective runner configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: A merged effective runner definition is loaded
acceptance_criteria.when: The runner is validated for invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The effective runner has a kind and an adapter reference before it can be used to spawn an agent

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent definition contains a runner field
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent definition is loaded from meta storage
acceptance_criteria.then: The runner field is accepted as an optional string reference to a named runner

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing agent definition has an adapter field and no runner field
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent is invoked or listed
acceptance_criteria.then: The adapter field continues to work with the same behavior as before the runner layer exists

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent definition has both runner and adapter fields
acceptance_criteria.then: The named runner determines the resolved adapter and execution harness for that invocation

items.title: Runner Resolution and Preflight
items.description:
Agent invocation resolves a runner before spawning an adapter process. Resolution
produces a single invocation contract containing runner identity, adapter identity,
command, arguments, environment, cwd, process diagnostics, and cleanup hooks. Invalid
runner configuration fails before prompt forwarding.

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec agent run starts a one-shot invocation for an agent with a runner field
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation uses the resolved runner contract instead of directly resolving the agent adapter field

acceptance_criteria.given: The dispatch engine prepares an eligible queued invocation for an agent with a runner field
acceptance_criteria.then: The dispatch engine uses the same resolved runner contract as one-shot agent run

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent references a runner name that is not present in the effective runner registry
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares a one-shot or dispatched invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: No adapter process is spawned

acceptance_criteria.given: An invocation is blocked because the configured runner name is unknown
acceptance_criteria.when: The failure is reported to the user, session, or task
acceptance_criteria.then: The report names the missing runner and suggests checking both project runner config, system runner config, and the agent definition

acceptance_criteria.given: Runner validation fails because a required field, adapter reference, process setting, or security setting is invalid
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation fails before any prompt content is sent to an adapter process

acceptance_criteria.given: An invocation uses a runner-backed agent
acceptance_criteria.then: The metadata includes the runner name and the resolved adapter id

acceptance_criteria.given: An invocation uses a runner-backed agent
acceptance_criteria.then: The event includes the runner name and the resolved adapter id

acceptance_criteria.given: Project or system runner config exists but cannot be parsed or validated into an effective runner registry.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec validates, lists, edits, or prepares an agent that references a runner.
acceptance_criteria.then: The diagnostic identifies the runner registry as unavailable, identifies the failing config layer and config path, includes the validation or parse reason, and redacts secret-looking values.

acceptance_criteria.given: Project or system runner config exists but cannot be parsed or validated into an effective runner registry.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares a runner-backed one-shot or dispatched invocation.
acceptance_criteria.then: No adapter process is spawned and no prompt content is forwarded until the registry-load error is fixed.

acceptance_criteria.given: An invocation selects the generic ACP process adapter without a runner contract.
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation is rejected before spawning an adapter process with reason `missing_process_executable` and details `{ adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Follow-up plan @plan-agent-runner-contract-hardening-follow-up: closure validation found that runner registry load/parse failures could be silently collapsed into the unknown-runner fallback, hiding the actual config layer, path, and validation reason. Added ac-registry-load-failure-reports-config-error and ac-registry-load-failure-blocks-runner-spawn so registry-load failures must report the failing layer and must block adapter spawn and prompt forwarding. No prior ACs were edited.

items.title: Runner Process Invocation Inputs
items.description:
Runners describe the process inputs kspec applies while preparing an ACP
adapter invocation. The resolved contract identifies the existing adapter,
optional command reference, child-process arguments, child-process cwd,
environment policy, and redacted diagnostics used for that invocation.

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner configures an executable or command path
acceptance_criteria.when: Runner preflight validates the invocation contract
acceptance_criteria.then: The resolved invocation contract identifies the command reference that will be spawned or returns a typed unspawnable-command diagnostic

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner declares additional non-secret arguments or argument templates
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares an ACP process invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: Those arguments are appended only to the spawned process invocation and are not persisted into adapter definitions

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner declares a working-directory policy or cwd override
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares an ACP process invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The cwd is applied only to that child process invocation and does not change the daemon or parent process cwd

acceptance_criteria.given: Runner validation, dry-run, preflight, or spawn preparation succeeds or fails
acceptance_criteria.then: Diagnostics identify the runner name, resolved adapter, command source, cwd policy, argument source, and env policy without exposing secrets

acceptance_criteria.given: A system runner config declares `process.cwd` as a relative path.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec resolves the runner invocation contract, runs preflight, or spawns the adapter process.
acceptance_criteria.then: The child-process cwd is the normalized path resolved relative to the directory that contains that system runner config file.

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner-backed agent resolves to a registered adapter command and the runner does not override `process.executable`.
acceptance_criteria.when: runner validation or dispatch preflight checks whether the invocation can spawn.
acceptance_criteria.then: The effective adapter command is checked under the runner-resolved cwd and process environment search path before prompt forwarding or dispatch acceptance.

acceptance_criteria.given: A system runner selects the generic ACP process adapter and omits `process.executable`.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec resolves the runner invocation contract.
acceptance_criteria.then: Resolution fails with reason `missing_process_executable` and details `{ runner, adapter: "generic-acp", missing_field: "process.executable" }`.

acceptance_criteria.given: A system runner selects the generic ACP process adapter and declares `process.executable`.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares the ACP process invocation.
acceptance_criteria.then: The spawned command is the runner-declared executable.

acceptance_criteria.given: A system runner selects the generic ACP process adapter.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares the ACP process invocation.
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation does not include package-runner or model-specific launch arguments from other built-in adapters.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Follow-up plan @plan-agent-runner-contract-hardening-follow-up: closure validation found that relative `process.cwd` values from a system runner config were accepted without a deterministic resolution base, and that the effective adapter command was not preflighted under the runner-resolved cwd and PATH before prompt forwarding. Added ac-relative-system-cwd-resolves-from-config-dir and ac-effective-adapter-command-preflighted to remove that ambiguity. No prior ACs were edited; implementation evidence belongs to later tasks.

items.title: Runner Invocation Semantics
items.description:
Runner-backed invocations preserve existing agent semantics while making the
resolved harness explicit. Skill reference formatting, auto-approval flags,
session environment injection, lifecycle cleanup, and dispatch preflight all
operate from the resolved runner contract.

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner resolves to an adapter with adapter-specific skill invocation formatting
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec builds the agent prompt with skills
acceptance_criteria.then: Skill references are formatted according to the resolved adapter

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent invocation runs with auto_approve enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: The resolved runner contract supplies adapter or runner auto-approval arguments
acceptance_criteria.then: Those arguments are appended to the spawned process for that invocation

acceptance_criteria.given: An invocation has a kspec session id
acceptance_criteria.when: The runner contract requires environment or harness-specific session injection
acceptance_criteria.then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID reaches child kspec commands through the resolved runner injection path

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner modifies temporary config, environment files, hook settings, or invocation-local process state
acceptance_criteria.when: The invocation closes or fails during startup
acceptance_criteria.then: Runner cleanup restores prior mutable state or removes temporary state best-effort

acceptance_criteria.given: Dispatch evaluates an agent that references a valid configured runner whose adapter is not a built-in adapter id
acceptance_criteria.then: The agent is accepted if the runner resolves to a spawnable ACP adapter contract

acceptance_criteria.given: Dispatch evaluates an agent whose runner cannot resolve to a spawnable adapter contract
acceptance_criteria.then: Dispatch reports the runner validation failure instead of relying on a later spawn error

acceptance_criteria.given: Dispatch prepares a runner-backed task invocation and preflight needs session-scoped environment, diagnostics, or interpolation.
acceptance_criteria.when: the same invocation is later recorded as active and passed to `runInvocation`.
acceptance_criteria.then: dispatch preflight and the actual invocation use the same canonical session id.

acceptance_criteria.given: An agent invocation runs with `auto_approve` enabled and resolves to the generic ACP process adapter.
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec prepares the invocation argument list.
acceptance_criteria.then: The generic adapter contributes no adapter-specific auto-approval arguments.

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec builds a skill-bearing prompt for a runner that resolves to the generic ACP process adapter.
acceptance_criteria.when: skill references are rewritten for adapter delivery.
acceptance_criteria.then: The prompt keeps the generic portable skill-reference text instead of applying an adapter-specific platform rewrite.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Follow-up plan @plan-agent-runner-contract-hardening-follow-up: closure validation found that dispatch preflight could compute session-scoped env, diagnostics, or interpolation against a different session id than the one later recorded as active and passed to runInvocation, allowing preflight/invocation drift. Added ac-dispatch-preflight-uses-canonical-session-id to require a single canonical session id across preflight and execution. No prior ACs were edited.

items.title: Runner Operator Surfaces
items.description:
Operators can inspect and configure agent runner usage through the same
surfaces that already expose agents and dispatch state. CLI, daemon API,
WebSocket status data, and the Web UI show runner identity, resolved adapter,
validation state, and redacted diagnostics.

acceptance_criteria.given: Agent definitions include runner-backed and legacy adapter-backed agents
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec agent list is run in human-readable or JSON mode
acceptance_criteria.then: Each agent entry shows its runner name when present and its resolved adapter identity

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has runner configuration
acceptance_criteria.when: An operator runs `kspec agent runners validate` or `kspec agent runners validate --json`
acceptance_criteria.then: The command exits with status 0 only when every selected runner is valid

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon serves agent definition data
acceptance_criteria.then: The response includes runner name, resolved adapter identity, and redacted runner diagnostics where available for each agent

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon serves dispatch status data
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests active invocation state
acceptance_criteria.then: The response includes runner name with resolved adapter identity for active invocations

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon serves dispatch status data
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests queued invocation state
acceptance_criteria.then: The response includes runner name with resolved adapter identity for queued invocations

acceptance_criteria.given: The Web UI displays the agents page
acceptance_criteria.when: Agents are loaded from the daemon API
acceptance_criteria.then: Agent cards display runner identity when present and resolved adapter identity for all agents

acceptance_criteria.given: The Web UI displays active agent invocations
acceptance_criteria.when: Invocation data is loaded from the daemon API
acceptance_criteria.then: Active invocation rows display runner identity when present

acceptance_criteria.given: The Web UI displays queued agent invocations

acceptance_criteria.then: Queued invocation rows display runner identity when present

acceptance_criteria.given: The Web UI agent edit form is available
acceptance_criteria.when: A user edits an agent's execution settings
acceptance_criteria.then: The form can set or clear the runner field without forcing a raw adapter edit

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon client updates an agent definition through the agent PATCH endpoint.
acceptance_criteria.when: the saved agent has a runner field or resolves through legacy adapter compatibility.
acceptance_criteria.then: the response includes the same `adapter`, `resolved_adapter`, and redacted `runner_validation` shape that the agent list endpoint would return for that saved agent.

acceptance_criteria.given: The Web UI displays active or queued invocation rows whose daemon payload includes a runner name and resolved adapter identity.
acceptance_criteria.then: visible row text and the row's accessible label include both the runner identity and the resolved adapter identity.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project has a runner that selects the generic ACP process adapter and omits `process.executable`.
acceptance_criteria.when: An operator runs `kspec agent runners validate`.
acceptance_criteria.then: The validation output reports that runner as invalid and includes a redacted diagnostic with reason `missing_process_executable`, adapter `generic-acp`, and missing field `process.executable`.

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Follow-up plan @plan-agent-runner-contract-hardening-follow-up: closure validation found that the daemon agent PATCH response could return a less-enriched payload than the list endpoint (missing resolved adapter and redacted runner validation), and that active/queued Web UI invocation rows could omit the resolved adapter identity even when the daemon supplied it. Added ac-daemon-agent-patch-returns-runner-state and ac-web-ui-invocation-rows-show-resolved-adapter for response parity and visible/accessible adapter identity in invocation rows. No prior ACs were edited.
