items.title: Runner Environment and Secret Boundaries
items.description:
Runner-launched adapter processes receive an explicit environment assembled
from the effective runner config. Project config may provide only portable
non-secret values. Secret bindings and machine-local credential sources live
in system config, and diagnostics never expose secret values. Host, daemon,
and nested-agent environment variables do not leak into runners unless the
effective runner policy allows them.

acceptance_criteria.given: The effective runner config declares an environment inheritance policy
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec builds the adapter process environment
acceptance_criteria.then: The resulting process environment contains only variables allowed by that policy plus kspec-required invocation variables

acceptance_criteria.given: The effective runner config declares literal non-secret environment values
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec builds the adapter process environment
acceptance_criteria.then: The declared values override inherited values for the same keys

acceptance_criteria.given: Project runner config declares literal environment values
acceptance_criteria.then: Known API key, auth token, OAuth token, credential variable, and secret-looking environment names are rejected from the project layer

acceptance_criteria.given: Any runner config layer declares literal environment values
acceptance_criteria.then: Known secret-looking environment names are rejected from literal values with guidance to use system secret source bindings

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner declares a secret source binding
acceptance_criteria.then: The binding is accepted only from system runner config and not from project runner config

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner declares a secret reference or source binding
acceptance_criteria.when: The runner configuration is parsed or shown in diagnostics
acceptance_criteria.then: The secret source reference is retained without persisting or displaying the secret value from either config layer

acceptance_criteria.given: The effective runner config declares a required secret source
acceptance_criteria.when: That secret source cannot be resolved for an invocation
acceptance_criteria.then: The invocation is blocked before adapter spawn

acceptance_criteria.given: Runner resolution, preflight, spawn, or adapter startup fails
acceptance_criteria.when: Diagnostics are recorded in CLI output, session events, task notes, daemon API responses, or Web UI state
acceptance_criteria.then: Secret values are redacted from every diagnostic surface

acceptance_criteria.given: A runner launches an external agent runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: The adapter process environment is built
acceptance_criteria.then: The process receives kspec's default nonessential-traffic and telemetry suppression variables unless the effective runner config explicitly disables that default

items.title: Dispatch Event Envelope and Delivery Semantics
items.description:
Defines the universal event identity and lineage contract for the
dispatch event bus. Every event emitted by any source carries a
standard envelope with identity, causation chain, and ordering
metadata. This is the contract that makes dedup, fan-in grouping,
loop prevention, replay decisions, and event logging reliable.

Non-goals: persistent event store, guaranteed delivery, replay.
Events are transient (daemon lifetime). Session event logs provide
the durable audit trail.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any event is emitted on the event bus
acceptance_criteria.then:
The event carries an envelope with event_id (unique per occurrence),
event_type (dotted namespace), emitted_at (timestamp), source_type
(task_watcher, api, invocation_lifecycle, schedule_engine, manual),
and source_id (originating entity identifier)

acceptance_criteria.given:
An event is caused by processing a previous event (e.g. a hook
on invocation.completed fires, causing a new invocation whose
completion emits another event)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The event carries causation_id (the event_id that directly caused
it) and correlation_id (the root event_id of the causal chain,
propagated transitively); when a kspec hook action triggers a
CLI command that emits events (e.g. task state changes), the
CLI propagates correlation_id via KSPEC_CORRELATION_ID env var
so re-entry events maintain the causal chain for loop prevention

acceptance_criteria.given:
Task events arrive from both file watcher and API within a
short window
acceptance_criteria.then:
Task events are deduplicated using the existing (task_id,
from_status, to_status) mechanism; non-task events have unique
event_id and are not deduplicated

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple events are emitted from the same source in sequence
acceptance_criteria.then:
Events are delivered in emission order per source; subscribers
process events sequentially per source to preserve causal order

acceptance_criteria.given:
A hook on invocation.completed triggers an agent whose completion
matches the same hook (or a cycle of hooks)
acceptance_criteria.when: The causal chain depth exceeds a configured maximum (default 5)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The event is rejected with a logged warning identifying the
cycle via correlation_id and causation_id chain; the automation
chain stops without crashing

acceptance_criteria.given: The event bus has been running and processing events
acceptance_criteria.when: A consumer queries recent events (API or UI)
acceptance_criteria.then:
A configurable ring buffer (default 500 events) retains recent
events in memory for inspection; older events are dropped

acceptance_criteria.given: The event bus has accepted more related events than its retained recent-event history can hold
acceptance_criteria.when: Earlier related events age out of the retained recent-event history
acceptance_criteria.then: Event-lineage state for aged-out events no longer accumulates beyond the retained recent-event lifetime

acceptance_criteria.given: Events from a source have completed delivery to matching subscribers
acceptance_criteria.when: No later event delivery for that source depends on the completed delivery
acceptance_criteria.then: Source-ordering state for the completed delivery no longer accumulates over daemon lifetime

items.title: Meta Manifest
items.description:
The meta manifest (kynetic.meta.yaml) is the root file for process
definitions. It lives alongside kynetic.yaml and defines agents,
workflows, conventions, and observations.

Unlike spec items which define product features, meta items define
how work is done on the project.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with kynetic.yaml
acceptance_criteria.when: kynetic.meta.yaml is created with valid structure
acceptance_criteria.then: kspec meta show outputs summary with counts for agents, workflows, conventions, and observations (exit code 0)

acceptance_criteria.given: a meta manifest exists
acceptance_criteria.then: output includes "Meta: X agents, Y workflows, Z conventions" line; validation errors for meta items use "meta:" prefix to distinguish from spec errors

acceptance_criteria.given: kynetic.meta.yaml has invalid schema
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message identifies the invalid field path and expected type (e.g., "meta:agents[0].capabilities: expected array")

items.title: Meta Manifest Format
items.description:
Meta manifest structure:

```yaml
kynetic_meta: "1.0"

agents:
  - _ulid: ...
    id: claude
    name: Claude Code Agent
    ...

workflows:
  - _ulid: ...
    id: spec-first
    trigger: behavior change
    ...

conventions:
  - _ulid: ...
    domain: commits
    ...

observations:
  - _ulid: ...
    type: friction
    ...

includes:
  - meta/agents.yaml
  - meta/workflows.yaml
```

Version field enables schema evolution.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project defines a meta manifest with kynetic_meta, agents, workflows, conventions, or observations sections
acceptance_criteria.when: the manifest is loaded by kspec
acceptance_criteria.then: the file is parsed as a meta manifest using the declared kynetic_meta version field

acceptance_criteria.given: a meta manifest uses an unsupported or malformed version declaration
acceptance_criteria.then: validation reports a meta-manifest schema error instead of silently accepting the file

items.title: Meta Includes
items.description:
Meta manifest supports includes for organization:

```yaml
includes:
  - meta/agents.yaml
  - meta/workflows.yaml
  - meta/conventions.yaml
```

Allows splitting large meta-specs into focused files.
Same pattern as spec manifest includes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a meta manifest declares include files for agents, workflows, or conventions
acceptance_criteria.when: the project meta context is loaded
acceptance_criteria.then: items from the included files are merged into the effective meta manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: a meta manifest references an include path that cannot be loaded
acceptance_criteria.then: validation reports the missing or unreadable include instead of ignoring it

items.title: Meta Validation Integration
items.description:
`kspec validate` includes meta-spec validation:

- Schema validation for all meta item types
- Reference resolution (@refs in workflows, observations)
- Cross-validation with product spec (meta-refs exist)

Unified validation ensures consistency across both layers.

acceptance_criteria.given: a meta item violates its schema or contains an invalid field value
acceptance_criteria.then: the output includes a meta-scoped validation error describing the failure

acceptance_criteria.given: a workflow, observation, or task meta_ref references a missing or wrong target
acceptance_criteria.then: reference validation reports the unresolved or invalid meta reference

items.title: Meta Manifest File Discovery
items.description:
Defines how kspec discovers meta manifest files in the spec directory.

Discovery algorithm:
1. Check for explicit name: kynetic.meta.yaml
2. If not found, scan directory for *.meta.yaml files
3. For each candidate, validate it contains a 'kynetic_meta:' version field
4. Return first valid match (alphabetical order for non-explicit names)

This provides backward compatibility while supporting project-specific naming like {slug}.meta.yaml.

acceptance_criteria.given: A directory with kynetic.meta.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns kynetic.meta.yaml path

acceptance_criteria.given: A directory with {slug}.meta.yaml containing kynetic_meta version field
acceptance_criteria.when: Finding the meta manifest and no kynetic.meta.yaml exists
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns {slug}.meta.yaml path

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple *.meta.yaml files
acceptance_criteria.then: Returns kynetic.meta.yaml if present, else first alphabetically

items.title: Agent Definitions
items.description:
Agent definitions describe the roles, capabilities, and conventions
for agents (AI or human) working on the project. They're trackable
items that can be referenced by tasks.

This enables structured understanding of who can do what, and
provides context for workflow decisions.

acceptance_criteria.given: agents are defined in meta manifest
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs table with columns: ID, Name, Capabilities (comma-separated); one row per agent; exit code 0

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec meta agents --json runs
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs JSON array with objects containing: id, name, description, capabilities (array), tools (array), session_protocol (object), conventions (array)

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent reference @agent-id is used
acceptance_criteria.then: validates reference resolves to an agent definition; error if reference points to non-agent meta item

items.title: Agent Schema
items.description:
Agent definition structure:

```yaml
- _ulid: 01KF...
  id: claude              # Short identifier
  name: Claude Code Agent # Display name
  description: |
    Primary development agent for this project.
  capabilities:
    - code
    - test
    - refactor
```

items.title: Workflow Step Navigation
items.description:
Step-by-step progression through workflow runs via the next command.

## Command

`kspec workflow next [run-ref] [--skip] [--notes text] [--json]`

## Behavior

1. If no run-ref provided:
   - Find active runs
   - If exactly one: use it (AC inference)
   - If multiple: error with list of run IDs to choose from
   - If none: error 'No active workflow runs'

2. Complete current step:
   - Record StepResult with status='completed' (or 'skipped' if --skip)
   - Set started_at to previous step's completed_at (or run's started_at for step 0)
   - Set completed_at to now
   - Capture --notes if provided

3. Advance to next step:
   - Increment current_step
   - Display next step with [type] prefix and content

4. If was last step:
   - Set run status='completed'
   - Set completed_at
   - Output summary: total duration, steps completed, steps skipped

## Output Format

```
Completed step 1/5: [check] Does the spec cover this change?

Step 2/5: [action] Update spec if needed
```

- src/cli/commands/workflow.ts (add next subcommand)
- src/parser/meta.ts (findActiveRuns helper)

Requires @workflow-run-foundation to be implemented first.

items.title: Workflow Enforcement Modes
items.description:
Entry/exit criteria display and enforcement modes (advisory vs strict).

## Extended WorkflowStepSchema

Add fields to WorkflowStepSchema in src/schema/meta.ts:
```typescript
entry_criteria?: string[],  // Conditions before step
exit_criteria?: string[],   // Conditions after step
```

## Behavior

### Advisory Mode (default)

When workflow.enforcement is 'advisory' or omitted:
- Entry criteria displayed when showing next step
- Exit criteria displayed after completing step
- --skip allowed without --force
- Criteria are guidance only, not blocking

### Strict Mode

When workflow.enforcement is 'strict':
- Entry criteria must be confirmed with --confirm flag to proceed
- Exit criteria must be confirmed with --confirm flag to advance
- --skip requires --force flag
- Record entry_confirmed/exit_confirmed in StepResult

## Output Format

```
Step 2/5: [action] Update spec if needed
  Entry criteria:
    - Spec coverage has been checked
    - Change scope is understood
  Exit criteria:
    - Spec reflects intended behavior change
```

In strict mode without --confirm:
```
error: Entry criteria not confirmed. Use --confirm to acknowledge.
```

## CLI Flags

Add to `kspec workflow next`:
- `--confirm`: Acknowledge entry/exit criteria (required in strict mode)
- `--force`: Allow --skip in strict mode

## Key Files

- src/schema/meta.ts (extend WorkflowStepSchema)
- src/cli/commands/workflow.ts (criteria display, enforcement)

## Dependencies

Requires @workflow-step-navigation to be implemented first.

items.title: Workflow Advanced Features
items.description:
Pause/resume functionality and structured step inputs.

## Pause/Resume Commands

```
kspec workflow pause @run-id [--json]
kspec workflow resume @run-id [--json]
```

### Pause Behavior
- Set status='paused'
- Set paused_at timestamp
- Shadow commit with 'workflow-pause' message
- Output: 'Paused run @id at step N/M'

### Resume Behavior
- Verify status='paused' (error if not)
- Set status='active'
- Clear paused_at
- Shadow commit with 'workflow-resume' message
- Output current step ready to continue

## Structured Step Inputs

### StepInputSchema
```typescript
{
  name: string,           // e.g., 'spec_ref'
```

- `--input key=value` (repeatable)

1. When step has inputs defined, display them:


2. If required input missing: error 'Missing required input: spec_ref'

Step types:

- check: Verification step (pass/fail)

- action: Something to do

- decision: Branch point
  Has options for different paths

Steps are executed in order. Agents interpret them,
they're not automatically enforced.

items.title: Workflow Execution Model
items.description:
Workflows are ADVISORY, not AUTOMATED. This is a deliberate design choice.

Execution model options:

1. **Documentation** (default): Workflows exist as reference documentation.
   Agents read them when relevant, but no runtime enforcement.
   `kspec meta workflows` displays them for human/agent reference.

2. **Checklist**: Workflows can be displayed as interactive checklists.
   `kspec meta run @workflow` presents steps one at a time,
   agent confirms each step completion. Progress tracked but not enforced.

3. **Hook integration**: Workflows can inform Claude Code hooks.
   A hook could query `kspec meta workflows --trigger "commit"`
   and inject relevant workflow steps into the prompt.
   Still advisory - hook provides context, agent decides.

Why not automation?
- Workflows describe nuanced processes that require judgment
- "Check if spec covers this" can't be reliably automated
- Automation creates brittleness; advisory enables adaptation
- Trust agents to follow documented processes

Future: Workflow adherence tracking via observations.
Friction observations on workflows indicate where guidance fails.
This creates a feedback loop: observe friction → improve workflow.

```yaml
# Optional execution hints
steps:
  - type: check
    content: Does the spec cover this change?
    on_fail: Update spec first
    execution:
      mode: prompt  # prompt, silent, or skip
      timeout: null # Optional timeout for automated checks
```

execution.mode values:
- prompt (default): Show step, wait for confirmation
- silent: Log step, don't wait
- skip: Skip in checklist mode (documentation only)

acceptance_criteria.then: the workflow is available as advisory documentation without automatic enforcement

acceptance_criteria.given: a workflow is run in checklist mode with execution hints on steps
acceptance_criteria.when: the guided runner advances through the workflow
acceptance_criteria.then: prompt, silent, and skip execution modes change how each step is surfaced without changing the underlying workflow definition

items.title: Convention Domains
items.description:
Standard convention domains:

- commits: Git commit message format
- notes: Task note writing style
- naming: Slug/identifier conventions
- tags: Tag taxonomy and usage
- branching: Git branch naming
- documentation: Doc writing standards

Projects can define custom domains as needed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project uses one of the documented standard domains such as commits or naming
acceptance_criteria.then: it is grouped and described under its domain without extra configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: a project defines a convention with a custom domain not in the standard list
acceptance_criteria.then: the convention is accepted and remains queryable by that custom domain

items.title: Convention Validation Strategy
items.description:
Conventions support optional validation with domain-specific strategies:

```yaml
- _ulid: 01KF...
  domain: commits
  rules:
    - Use conventional commit format
  validation:
    type: regex
    pattern: "^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|test|chore)(\\(.+\\))?:\\s.+"
    message: "Commit must follow conventional format"
```

Validation types by domain:

- commits: regex pattern matching on message
- notes: word count range, required sections
- naming: regex pattern for slugs/identifiers
- tags: enum list of allowed tags
- branching: regex pattern for branch names
- documentation: prose (advisory only, no automation)

Validation configuration:

```yaml
validation:
  type: regex | enum | range | prose
  # For regex:
  pattern: "^pattern$"
  message: "Error message when validation fails"
  # For enum:
  allowed: [value1, value2, value3]
  # For range:
  min: 10
  max: 500
  unit: words | chars | lines
```

Validation is optional - conventions without validation field
are advisory-only and appear in documentation.

`kspec validate --conventions` runs all validatable conventions.
Prose-type conventions are skipped with info message.

acceptance_criteria.given: a convention includes regex, enum, or range validation metadata
acceptance_criteria.then: the corresponding validation strategy is applied to matching content

acceptance_criteria.given: a convention uses prose validation guidance only
acceptance_criteria.then: the convention is reported as advisory and skipped from automated enforcement

items.title: Observations
items.description:
Observations capture feedback about workflows and conventions.
This is the mechanism for the self-improvement loop - agents
record friction, success, questions, and ideas, then patterns
emerge that inform workflow improvements.

Observations can be promoted to tasks with --meta-ref, creating
trackable work to improve processes.

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent encounters workflow friction
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs "OK Created observation: <ULID-prefix>"; observation stored with fields: _ulid, type, content, created_at (ISO8601), author, resolved (false), workflow_ref (if --workflow provided)

acceptance_criteria.given: observations exist
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs table with columns: ID, Type, Workflow, Created, Content (truncated); shows only unresolved by default; --all includes resolved

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation exists
acceptance_criteria.then: creates task with: title from --title, description from observation content, meta_ref from observation's workflow_ref; outputs "OK Created task: <ULID-prefix>"; observation updated with promoted_to field pointing to new task

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation exists
acceptance_criteria.then: observation updated with: resolved=true, resolution=text, resolved_at (ISO8601), resolved_by (author); outputs "OK Resolved: <ULID-prefix>"

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec meta observations --json runs
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs JSON array with full observation objects including all fields

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation has already been promoted (has promoted_to field)
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message: "Observation already promoted to task <task-ref>; resolve or delete the task first"

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation is already resolved (resolved=true)
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message: "Observation already resolved on <date>: '<resolution-text-truncated>'"

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation is already resolved
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message: "Cannot promote resolved observation; use --force to override"

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation has promoted_to pointing to a completed task
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec meta resolve @obs runs with no explicit resolution
acceptance_criteria.then: auto-populates resolution from task completion reason if available; prompts for resolution text if task has no completion reason

items.title: Observation Schema
items.description:
Observation structure:

```yaml
- _ulid: 01KF...
  type: friction        # friction, success, question, idea
  workflow_ref: "@spec-first"  # Related workflow (optional)
  content: |
    Spec-first check feels heavyweight for typo fixes.
    Interrupts flow for trivial changes.
  created_at: "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z"
  author: "@claude"
  resolved: false
  resolution: null      # Filled when resolved
```

Types capture the nature of the feedback.
workflow_ref links to relevant workflow for tracking.

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation defines type, content, author, created_at, and optional workflow_ref
acceptance_criteria.then: the observation validates and can be listed by meta observation commands

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation references a workflow that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.then: validation reports the invalid workflow_ref instead of accepting the observation silently

items.title: Observation Types
items.description:
Observation types:

- friction: Something that's hard, slow, or frustrating
- success: Something that works well (positive feedback)
- question: Uncertainty about how to proceed
- idea: Potential improvement or new approach

All types feed the improvement loop. Friction and ideas
most often lead to workflow changes. Success confirms
what's working. Questions may reveal documentation gaps.

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation is recorded with type friction, success, question, or idea
acceptance_criteria.then: the observation remains categorized under that type

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation uses a type outside the documented set
acceptance_criteria.then: validation rejects the unsupported observation type

items.title: Observation Promotion
items.description:
Observations can be promoted to tasks:

```bash
kspec meta promote @obs-123 \
  --title "Simplify spec-first for trivial changes" \
  --priority 2
```

Creates task with:
- title from --title
- meta_ref pointing to related workflow
- description from observation content
- origin: observation_promotion

Original observation marked with promoted_to reference.

acceptance_criteria.given: an unresolved observation is promoted with kspec meta promote and a task title
acceptance_criteria.then: a new task is created with origin observation_promotion and description seeded from the observation content

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation has a related workflow_ref when it is promoted
acceptance_criteria.then: its meta_ref points to the same related workflow and the observation records the promoted task reference

items.title: Observation Resolution
items.description:
Resolving observations:

```bash
kspec meta resolve @obs-123 "Addressed by --quick flag in v0.2"
```

Sets:
- resolved: true
- resolution: "Addressed by --quick flag in v0.2"
- resolved_at: timestamp
- resolved_by: author

Resolved observations remain for history.
Unresolved observations show in session context.

acceptance_criteria.given: an unresolved observation is resolved with a resolution message
acceptance_criteria.then: the observation is marked resolved and stores the resolution text with resolver metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: session context is generated while unresolved observations still exist
acceptance_criteria.then: those unresolved observations are surfaced until they are explicitly resolved

items.title: Observation-Task Resolution Loop
items.description:
The observation→task→resolution loop defines how observations connect
to tasks and when they get resolved.

**Promotion creates linkage**:
When an observation is promoted to a task:
- observation.promoted_to = @task-ref
- task.origin = "observation_promotion"
- task.description includes observation content

**Task completion does NOT auto-resolve**:
Completing a task does not automatically resolve linked observations.
This is intentional:
- Task might address the observation partially
- Multiple tasks might be needed
- Agent should explicitly confirm resolution

**Explicit resolution required**:
After completing the task, agent runs:
```bash
kspec meta resolve @obs "Addressed by task @task-ref"
```

**Convenience: resolve-from-task**:
If observation has promoted_to pointing to a completed task:
```bash
kspec meta resolve @obs
# Auto-populates: "Resolved via task @task-ref: <task.reason>"
```
Prompts for resolution text if task has no completion reason.

**Session context reminder**:
When task with origin="observation_promotion" is completed,
session context shows reminder:
"Consider resolving linked observation: @obs-ref"

**Querying the loop**:
```bash
# Find observations that spawned tasks
kspec meta observations --promoted

# Find tasks from observations
kspec tasks list --origin observation_promotion

# Find unresolved observations with completed tasks
kspec meta observations --pending-resolution
```

This explicit loop ensures observations aren't lost when tasks
complete, and creates traceable process improvement history.

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation was promoted to a task and that task is later completed
acceptance_criteria.then: the linked observation remains unresolved until an explicit meta resolve step is taken

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation points to a completed promoted task and kspec meta resolve is run without custom text
acceptance_criteria.when: resolution is inferred from the task linkage
acceptance_criteria.then: the observation is resolved using task-based context instead of requiring a manual duplicate explanation

items.title: Observation Content Search
items.description:
Add content search to observation listing and global search. Currently
kspec search includes observations but cannot filter to observations only,
and kspec meta observations has type/workflow/status filters but no content
search. Agents grep observation YAML when they need to find observations
by content.

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec meta observations --search shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then: Only observations whose text matches the pattern are returned

acceptance_criteria.then: Pattern is treated as regex (consistent with kspec search behavior)

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec meta observations --search cli --type friction
acceptance_criteria.then: Both filters apply (AND logic) -- only friction observations matching cli

acceptance_criteria.given: An observation has matching text in its description but not title
acceptance_criteria.then: The observation is found (search covers all text fields)

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec meta observations --search pattern --json
acceptance_criteria.then: JSON output contains only matching observations

acceptance_criteria.given: User wants to search only observations via the global search command
acceptance_criteria.then: Results are limited to observation matches only (excludes items, tasks, inbox)

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec search pattern --observations-only --items-only
acceptance_criteria.then: Error message explains the flags are mutually exclusive and exits non-zero

inherited_acs.then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
output includes all data available in human-readable mode

--json takes precedence over other format options
only items with matching status shown
only items with matching tag shown

items.title: Session Context
items.description:
Session context is ephemeral state tracking current focus,
active threads, and open questions. Unlike other meta items,
context is dynamic and stored in a separate file (.kspec-session)
that can be gitignored.

Context helps with session continuity and handoff between agents.

acceptance_criteria.given: a session has focus, active threads, or open questions stored in .kspec-session
acceptance_criteria.then: the current session context is shown alongside other startup information

acceptance_criteria.given: no .kspec-session file exists for the project
acceptance_criteria.then: kspec treats context as empty instead of failing to start the session

items.title: Context Schema
items.description:
Session context structure:

```yaml
# .kspec-session (gitignored)
focus: "@task-meta-spec"    # Current work focus
threads:                     # Active conversation threads
  - "Designing observation promotion flow"
  - "Deciding on context persistence"
open_questions:              # Unresolved questions
  - "Should conventions be auto-validated?"
  - "How to handle cross-project inheritance?"
updated_at: "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
```

Ephemeral by design - not part of project history.

acceptance_criteria.given: session context contains focus, threads, open_questions, and updated_at
acceptance_criteria.when: kspec meta context or session start reads the file
acceptance_criteria.then: the values are parsed and presented as structured session state

acceptance_criteria.given: the .kspec-session file is malformed
acceptance_criteria.when: context commands attempt to read it
acceptance_criteria.then: the user receives a parse or validation error instead of corrupted context state

items.title: Context Storage
items.description:
Context is stored in .kspec-session:

- Separate from meta manifest (ephemeral vs stable)
- Gitignored by default (session-specific)
- Auto-created when context commands used
- Can be deleted without losing project configuration

This keeps project-level meta (agents, workflows) separate
from session-level state (focus, threads).

acceptance_criteria.given: a context command writes focus, thread, or question data for the first time
acceptance_criteria.then: a .kspec-session file is created separately from the meta manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: the .kspec-session file is deleted
acceptance_criteria.when: the project meta manifest is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: agents, workflows, conventions, and observations remain unchanged because session context is stored independently

items.title: Context Integration
items.description:
Context appears in session start output:

```
=== Session Context ===
Focus: @task-meta-spec (Design meta-spec concept)

Active Threads:
  - Designing observation promotion flow

Open Questions:
  - Should conventions be auto-validated?
```

Helps agents quickly understand current state.

acceptance_criteria.then: the startup output includes a session-context block summarizing those values

acceptance_criteria.given: session context is empty

items.title: Meta CLI Commands

CLI commands for interacting with meta-spec. Follow the same

kspec meta observations [options]

items.title: kspec meta resolve

items.title: Meta Reference Integration
items.description:
Tasks can reference meta items via meta_ref, just like spec_ref.
This enables tracking work on process improvements - the key to
the self-improvement loop.

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec task add --meta-ref @workflow-id runs
acceptance_criteria.when: the @workflow-id is a valid workflow reference
acceptance_criteria.then: task created with meta_ref field set to @workflow-id; outputs "OK Created task: <ULID-prefix>"

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks exist with meta_ref fields
acceptance_criteria.then: outputs only tasks where meta_ref matches @workflow; same output format as regular task list

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec task add --meta-ref @invalid-ref runs
acceptance_criteria.when: the reference does not resolve to a meta item
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message: "meta_ref '@invalid-ref' does not resolve to a valid meta item (agent, workflow, or convention)"

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec task add --meta-ref @spec-item runs
acceptance_criteria.when: the reference is a product spec item (not meta)
acceptance_criteria.then: exits with code 1; error message: "meta_ref '@spec-item' points to a spec item; use --spec-ref for product spec references"

items.title: Task meta_ref Field
items.description:
Tasks gain meta_ref field parallel to spec_ref:

```yaml
- _ulid: 01KF...
  title: Simplify spec-first for trivial changes
  type: task
  meta_ref: "@workflow-spec-first"
  status: pending
  ...
```

meta_ref points to workflow, agent, or convention.
Enables queries like "what tasks improve this workflow?"

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is created or updated with meta_ref pointing to a workflow, agent, or convention
acceptance_criteria.then: the linked meta_ref is stored alongside task metadata parallel to spec_ref

items.title: task add --meta-ref
items.description:
kspec task add gains --meta-ref option:

```bash
kspec task add \
  --title "Add --quick flag to spec-first" \
  --meta-ref @workflow-spec-first \
  --priority 2
```

Creates task with meta_ref linking to meta item.
Validation ensures meta_ref resolves to valid meta item.

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec task add is run with --meta-ref @some-meta-item
acceptance_criteria.then: the created task stores that meta reference for later queries and validation

items.title: Meta Reference Queries
items.description:
Query tasks by meta_ref:

```bash
kspec tasks list --meta-ref @workflow-spec-first
```

Returns all tasks linked to that workflow.
Useful for tracking improvement progress.

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple tasks reference the same workflow or other meta item
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks linked to that meta item are returned

items.title: Meta Reference Validation
items.description:
meta_ref field validation rules:

1. **Reference must resolve**: The @ref must point to an existing item
   Error: "meta_ref '@xyz' does not resolve to any item"

2. **Reference must be meta item**: The resolved item must be a meta
   item (agent, workflow, convention), not a product spec item.
   Error: "meta_ref '@xyz' points to spec item; use --spec-ref instead"

3. **Type hints** (optional): For stricter validation, meta_ref can
   specify expected type:
   ```yaml
   meta_ref:
     ref: "@spec-first"
     type: workflow  # Validates ref is a workflow
   ```
   Error: "meta_ref '@xyz' expected workflow, got agent"

4. **Validation timing**: Checked on:
   - `kspec task add --meta-ref`
   - `kspec validate` (full validation)
   - `kspec task set --meta-ref` (updates)

5. **Circular reference prevention**: meta_ref cannot point to
   the task itself or create reference cycles.

Implementation: Validation uses the same reference resolution
as spec_ref, but filters for meta item types. Meta items are
identified by their source file (kynetic.meta.yaml or meta/ includes)
or by explicit type markers.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task meta_ref does not resolve to any item
acceptance_criteria.when: the task is created, updated, or validated
acceptance_criteria.then: validation reports that the meta_ref cannot be resolved

acceptance_criteria.given: a task meta_ref points to a product spec item or mismatched hinted type
acceptance_criteria.then: the command rejects the reference with an error explaining the expected meta-item type

items.title: AC Annotation Coverage Semantics
items.description: Coverage annotations map behavior tests to specific acceptance criteria so completeness validation reflects real behavior coverage. For specs and traits that define acceptance criteria, completeness accounting uses explicit AC-level mappings rather than bare spec-level references. Coverage credit accrues only to annotations that claim coverage; an annotation carrying a not-applicable marker claims no coverage — it neither covers a criterion nor exempts it.

acceptance_criteria.then: The annotation is reported as an invalid AC annotation warning and grants no acceptance-criteria coverage credit

acceptance_criteria.then: The annotation grants no coverage credit for any of the AC ids it names

acceptance_criteria.given: A well-formed coverage annotation carrying a not-applicable marker names a resolvable target and acceptance-criterion ids that exist on that target
acceptance_criteria.when: completeness validation runs its annotation integrity checks
acceptance_criteria.then: The annotation produces no invalid-annotation finding, remaining a valid task-scoped marker while the in-code convention exists, though integrity checks on its target reference and AC ids still apply

items.title: Shadow Branch
items.description:
Shadow branch for transparent spec/task state auto-tracking.
Uses gitignored worktree (.kspec/) pointing to orphan branch (kspec-meta).
Separates metadata commits from main branch history.

Key properties:
- Shadow branch has files at root (not nested under spec/)
- .kspec/ is a git worktree pointing to the shadow branch
- Main branch gitignores .kspec/
- All kspec read/write operations target .kspec/
- Changes auto-commit to shadow branch

items.title: Shadow Branch Concept
items.description:
Orphan git branch storing kspec state in gitignored worktree.

Problem solved:
- Commit bloat from task state changes
- History pollution on main branch
- Review noise in PRs

Solution:
- Orphan branch (kspec-meta) with files at root
- .kspec/ worktree always available
- Auto-commit on state changes
- Main branch never touched by kspec operations

acceptance_criteria.given: a project is initialized with shadow branch support
acceptance_criteria.when: a mutating kspec command updates spec or task state and git history is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: the metadata change is committed on the orphan shadow branch through the .kspec worktree and the current code branch history remains unchanged

items.title: Shadow Directory Structure
items.description:
Directory layout for shadow branch:

project/
  .kspec/                    # Git worktree (gitignored by main)
    .git -> ../.git/worktrees/.kspec
    kynetic.yaml             # Root manifest
    kynetic.tasks.yaml       # Tasks
    kynetic.meta.yaml        # Meta-spec
    project.tasks.yaml       # Project tasks
    project.inbox.yaml       # Inbox
    modules/
      core.yaml
      cli.yaml
      shadow.yaml
  src/                       # Normal source (on main branch)
  tests/
  .gitignore                 # Contains: .kspec/

Shadow branch contents (at root):
- kynetic.yaml - manifest
- *.tasks.yaml - task files
- *.inbox.yaml - inbox files
- modules/*.yaml - spec modules

acceptance_criteria.given: a project has been initialized with the shadow branch worktree
acceptance_criteria.when: the user inspects the project root and the .kspec directory layout
acceptance_criteria.then: the main worktree contains a gitignored .kspec worktree and the shadow worktree root contains the manifest, task/inbox files, and modules directory at top-level paths

Files are not tracked by the shadow branch. Subdirectories are permitted but flat structure is recommended. No automated cleanup or lifecycle management — files persist until manually removed.

items.title: Auto-Commit on State Changes
items.description:
All state-changing kspec commands automatically commit to shadow branch.

Commit messages by command:

Task lifecycle:
- task start @ref      -> "Start @{slug}"
- task complete @ref   -> "Complete @{slug}: {reason}"
- task block @ref      -> "Block @{slug}"
- task unblock @ref    -> "Unblock @{slug}"
- task cancel @ref     -> "Cancel @{slug}"
- task set @ref        -> "Update @{slug}"

Task notes/todos:
- task note @ref       -> "Note on @{slug}"
- task add             -> "Add task: {title}"
- task todo add        -> "Todo on @{slug}"
- task todo done       -> "Todo done on @{slug}"
- task todo undone     -> "Todo undone on @{slug}"

Inbox:
- inbox add            -> "Inbox: {text}"
- inbox promote        -> "Promote to @{slug}"
- inbox delete         -> "Inbox delete"

Items:
- item add/set/delete  -> "{action} @{slug}"
- item ac add          -> "AC on @{slug}"
- item ac set          -> "AC update on @{slug}"
- item ac remove       -> "AC remove on @{slug}"

Derive:
- derive               -> "Derive from @{spec}"

Implementation:
- After write, run: git -C .kspec add -A && git -C .kspec commit -m "..."
- Low overhead (local commits only)
- Commit includes all changes from the operation

acceptance_criteria.then: shadow branch has new commit with appropriate message

items.title: Shadow Recovery
items.description:
Recovery mechanisms for shadow branch issues. Provides CLI commands for
diagnosing and repairing shadow branch problems.

Commands:
- `shadow status`: Check health of shadow branch
- `shadow repair`: Recreate worktree when branch exists but worktree broken
- `shadow log`: View recent commits on shadow branch

Handles common issues:
- Worktree directory deleted (recreate from existing branch)
- Worktree disconnected from git (remove and recreate)
- Stale worktree references in git

acceptance_criteria.then: the pre-repair shadow directory is preserved or restored and the failure reports recovery guidance instead of leaving the checkout without its shadow directory

acceptance_criteria.when: the flow chooses a shadow recovery action
acceptance_criteria.then: it reuses or reattaches the existing shadow state via repair semantics instead of treating the checkout as a brand-new init

items.title: Lazy Shadow Sync on Reads
items.description: Replace the blocking shadowPull() on every CLI direct-mode read with a lightweight drift check. Only pull when the local shadow branch is behind or diverged from remote. Uses FETCH_HEAD mtime to avoid redundant git fetch calls, and compares ahead/behind counts when fetch data is fresh. FETCH_HEAD path is resolved via git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD from the same cwd used for fetch, ensuring correctness in worktree setups. When reads are served by the daemon, the daemon's entity cache and background sync scheduler handle freshness instead of per-request drift-check (see @daemon-entity-cache and @daemon-read-path).

acceptance_criteria.given:
A CLI read command runs (e.g. task list, item get) and
shadow branch has remote tracking configured
acceptance_criteria.then:
Instead of unconditionally calling shadowPull(), a lightweight
drift check runs first. If no drift detected, pull is skipped
and the command proceeds with local state.

acceptance_criteria.given: The shadow branch is a git worktree of the main repository
acceptance_criteria.when: Drift check needs to determine fetch freshness
acceptance_criteria.then:
FETCH_HEAD path is resolved via git rev-parse --git-path
FETCH_HEAD from the worktree dir (the same cwd used for
fetch operations). In worktrees, git fetch writes FETCH_HEAD
to the worktree's git dir (e.g. .git/worktrees/-kspec/),
not the common git dir. The drift check must stat the same
file that fetch updates.

acceptance_criteria.given:
FETCH_HEAD mtime (resolved per ac-fetch-head-location) is
within the freshness threshold (derived from
shadow.sync_interval config, default 60s)
acceptance_criteria.then:
Git fetch is skipped. Drift is determined solely by comparing
local HEAD against the cached upstream ref from the last fetch.

acceptance_criteria.given:
FETCH_HEAD mtime is older than the freshness threshold
or FETCH_HEAD does not exist
acceptance_criteria.then:
A git fetch is performed to refresh remote refs, then
local HEAD is compared against upstream.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Network is unavailable or git fetch exceeds 5 seconds
during drift check
acceptance_criteria.when: Drift check attempts a fetch due to stale FETCH_HEAD
acceptance_criteria.then:
The spawned git fetch process is killed (SIGTERM with
SIGKILL fallback) and drift check proceeds with local
state only.

acceptance_criteria.given: A fetch timeout or network failure occurs during drift check
acceptance_criteria.then:
No error is surfaced to the user. The command proceeds as if
no drift was detected.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A fetch timeout or network failure occurs during drift check
and --debug-shadow flag or KSPEC_DEBUG=1 is set
acceptance_criteria.then:
A debug-level log is emitted describing the fetch failure,
visible via --debug-shadow for troubleshooting.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Drift check detects local shadow branch is behind remote
(remote has commits not present locally)
acceptance_criteria.when: A read operation is about to proceed
acceptance_criteria.then:
shadowPull() is called to integrate remote changes before
the read proceeds. Behavior after pull (conflict handling,
warnings) remains unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Drift check detects local shadow branch is ahead of remote
(local has unpushed commits, but remote has no new commits)
acceptance_criteria.when: A read operation is about to proceed
acceptance_criteria.then:
No pull is performed. Local state is already up to date with
all remote changes. The unpushed commits will be pushed on
the next write or daemon sync cycle.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Drift check detects local and remote have diverged
(both have commits the other does not)
acceptance_criteria.when: A read operation is about to proceed
acceptance_criteria.then:
shadowPull() is called to integrate remote changes, using
the existing rebase + merge driver strategy.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Remote tracking is configured but the upstream ref does not
exist after a successful fetch (e.g. first run, never pushed)
acceptance_criteria.when: Drift check compares HEAD vs upstream
acceptance_criteria.then:
Drift check returns true (sync needed) as the safer default,
allowing shadowPull() to handle the situation.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Drift check determines local HEAD matches upstream
(zero behind, zero diverged)
acceptance_criteria.then:
No pull is performed. Command proceeds immediately with
local state. No network calls are made when FETCH_HEAD is
fresh and refs match.

acceptance_criteria.given: User runs kspec session start and remote tracking is configured
acceptance_criteria.then:
Session start bypasses the drift check and always performs a
full shadowPull(), ensuring the user sees the latest remote
state when beginning a work session.

acceptance_criteria.given: KSPEC_NO_SYNC=1 environment variable is set
acceptance_criteria.when:
initContext() runs (regardless of syncMode — drift-check,
always, or skip)
acceptance_criteria.then:
All pre-read sync is disabled, including drift check and
unconditional pull for markAlwaysSync commands like session
start. KSPEC_NO_SYNC takes highest precedence over all
syncMode values.

acceptance_criteria.given: shadow.sync_interval is configured in kspec.config.yaml
acceptance_criteria.when: Drift check determines FETCH_HEAD freshness threshold
acceptance_criteria.then:
Uses the configured sync_interval value (in seconds) as the
freshness threshold. If not configured, defaults to 60 seconds.

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI command is dispatched via Commander
acceptance_criteria.when: The preAction hook runs before the command handler
acceptance_criteria.then:
syncMode is determined centrally in the preAction hook based
on command annotations (markMutating, markAlwaysSync) and
stored as module-level state. Both the preAction initContext
call (via maybeAutoStartDaemon) and the action handler
initContext call read syncMode from this shared state.
No per-command manual syncMode passing is required.

acceptance_criteria.given:
initContext() is called multiple times within the same CLI
command (e.g. preAction via maybeAutoStartDaemon, then
action handler)
acceptance_criteria.when: The second (or subsequent) initContext call runs
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only the first initContext call per command lifecycle
executes the sync action (drift check, pull, or skip).
Subsequent calls within the same command skip pre-read
sync entirely, preventing double-pull.

acceptance_criteria.given: A read request is served by the daemon API (not a CLI direct-mode invocation)
acceptance_criteria.then: The per-request drift-check defined by this spec is not performed. The daemon relies on its entity cache (populated and invalidated by the file watcher) and the background sync scheduler for data freshness. The drift-check contract applies only to CLI direct-mode reads where initContext() runs in-process.

items.title: Always Sync on Shadow Writes
items.description:
Write operations always perform a full sync (pull then push) to
ensure consistency. This preserves the current pull-rebase-before-push
pattern in commitIfShadow/shadowPushAsync. Write commands skip the
pre-read drift check in initContext since the write sync supersedes it.

Depends on @shadow-lazy-read-sync for the syncMode mechanism.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A CLI write command commits to the shadow branch
(task add, item set, etc.)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The existing pull-rebase-before-push pattern executes
regardless of drift check freshness. Writes never skip sync.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A mutating command triggers initContext() (either directly
or via preAction hook)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The pre-read drift check is skipped for both initContext
calls (preAction and action handler). The write path in
commitIfShadow provides its own sync, so the pre-read
check would be redundant overhead.

items.title: Daemon Background Sync Pushes
items.description:
Extend the daemon's periodic ShadowSyncScheduler to also push
after pulling, ensuring local commits are propagated at the
sync interval rather than only on fire-and-forget after writes.

Orthogonal to @shadow-lazy-read-sync and @shadow-write-sync —
can be implemented independently. The daemon's periodic fetch
freshens FETCH_HEAD in the worktree git dir, which the CLI
drift check benefits from for its fast path.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Daemon periodic sync interval elapses and there are local
commits ahead of upstream
acceptance_criteria.then:
After pulling, a push is attempted if local is ahead of
remote. Push failure is non-fatal (logged, not thrown).

acceptance_criteria.given: Daemon periodic sync runs its fetch from the worktree dir
acceptance_criteria.when: CLI commands run between daemon sync intervals
acceptance_criteria.then:
FETCH_HEAD in the worktree git dir is fresh from the
daemon's last fetch. CLI drift checks (which resolve
FETCH_HEAD from the same worktree dir) see it as fresh
and skip redundant fetches during the interval.

items.title: Semantic YAML Merge Driver
items.description:
A custom git merge driver that parses both versions of kspec YAML files and merges them semantically, understanding the structure of tasks, items, and other kspec entities. This prevents git from creating conflict markers that would corrupt YAML files.

Note on exit codes: This command intentionally does NOT use @trait-semantic-exit-codes because git merge drivers have special requirements - they must exit 0 to prevent git from falling back to its text merge, which would corrupt YAML.

acceptance_criteria.given: git attempts to merge two versions of a kspec YAML file
acceptance_criteria.then: kspec parses all three versions (base, ours, theirs) as structured data instead of text

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions add different items to an array (tasks, inbox, specs)
acceptance_criteria.then: both additions are included in result (union merge by ULID)

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions modify different fields of the same item
acceptance_criteria.then: fields are merged (non-conflicting field changes combined)

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions modify the same scalar field (title, description, priority) of the same item
acceptance_criteria.then: user is prompted interactively to choose which value to keep

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions modify append-only arrays (notes, todos)
acceptance_criteria.then: arrays are union merged by ULID (notes never conflict)

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions modify set-like arrays (tags, depends_on)
acceptance_criteria.then: arrays are set-unioned (duplicates removed)

acceptance_criteria.given: both versions modify nested objects (status, traceability)
acceptance_criteria.then: nested fields are merged recursively at field level

acceptance_criteria.given: one version deletes an item while other modifies it
acceptance_criteria.then: user is prompted interactively to choose delete vs keep modified

acceptance_criteria.given: merge completes with no true conflicts
acceptance_criteria.then: exit code 0, merged YAML written to output path

acceptance_criteria.given: merge has unresolvable conflicts and --non-interactive flag set
acceptance_criteria.then: conflict markers written as YAML comments, exit code 0 (prevents git fallback)

acceptance_criteria.given: YAML parsing fails on any input file
acceptance_criteria.then: falls back gracefully: copies ours verbatim, creates .kspec-merge-failed marker, exits 0

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec init runs in a new repo
acceptance_criteria.then: merge driver is configured in .git/config and .gitattributes updated in shadow branch

items.title: Web UI System
items.description:
Web-based interface for viewing, editing, and managing kspec state. Includes three deployment modes:
1. Local daemon mode runs the daemon on the configured JavaScript runtime, defaulting to Node, using Elysia with the appropriate runtime adapter. Bun remains supported as an optional configured runtime.
2. Web dashboard - SvelteKit + shadcn-svelte for full CRUD operations
3. GitHub Pages export - Static JSON snapshot with read-only SPA for public sharing

Tech stack: Elysia.js, WebSocket (not SSE), SvelteKit, shadcn-svelte. Default runtime is Node; Bun is supported as an optional configured runtime.
Distribution via npm; the runtime executable is provided by the user when an optional runtime such as Bun is selected.

acceptance_criteria.then: all daemon runtime dependencies for the configured runtime are available without additional install steps except the runtime executable itself when an optional runtime such as Bun is selected

acceptance_criteria.then: Shows a clear error message naming the missing runtime with installation guidance

items.title: Daemon Server Mode
items.description: Long-running Elysia.js server that exposes kspec state via HTTP API and WebSocket for real-time updates. File watcher drives both WebSocket broadcast and entity cache invalidation. The server binds to a resolved daemon endpoint that defaults to 127.0.0.1 loopback and can be explicitly configured for other interfaces with visible unauthenticated-exposure warnings. Supports foreground and background modes with global daemon lifecycle metadata. Includes heartbeat ping/pong for connection health monitoring on runtimes that support it.

items.title: Daemon Entity Cache
items.description:
Server-side in-memory cache for entity data served by the daemon API.
The cache uses a two-tier model: index data (summaries, counts,
references) is kept hot in memory, while detail data (full content,
notes, event logs) is loaded on demand when accessed. The file watcher
drives cache invalidation — when shadow branch files change, affected
data is selectively reloaded. Data domains load progressively so
high-priority data is available before the full cache is ready.

acceptance_criteria.given: a project is registered with the daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: the project's shadow branch directory is accessible
acceptance_criteria.then:
index-tier entity data is loaded into memory and available for
serving

acceptance_criteria.given: a project's index data has been loaded into the cache
acceptance_criteria.when: an API list or summary request arrives for that project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response is served from the in-memory cache without reading
files from disk or running git operations

acceptance_criteria.given: a request arrives for a single entity's full detail
acceptance_criteria.when: the detail data is not in the cache
acceptance_criteria.then:
the detail is loaded from disk, served, and optionally retained
in cache until the next invalidation

acceptance_criteria.given: the file watcher detects a change to a shadow branch file
acceptance_criteria.when: the changed file belongs to a registered project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the affected data domain is reloaded from disk and the cache is
updated before any subsequent request is served

acceptance_criteria.given: a file change affects only one data domain
acceptance_criteria.then: only the affected domain is reloaded, not unrelated domains

acceptance_criteria.given: a write operation mutates entity data through the daemon API
acceptance_criteria.when: the mutation succeeds and is committed to the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
the cache is updated with the new state before the response is
sent, without waiting for the file watcher to detect the change

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple API requests arrive concurrently for the same project
acceptance_criteria.then:
all requests are served from the same cached data without
blocking on each other or triggering redundant loads

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple file changes arrive within a short window
acceptance_criteria.when: the cache processes the invalidation events
acceptance_criteria.then:
only a single reload is performed for each affected data domain,
not one per file change event

acceptance_criteria.given: the cache encounters an error loading entity data
acceptance_criteria.then:
the request falls back to direct file reading and the error is
logged, rather than failing the request entirely

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple projects are registered with the daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: other projects' cached data is not affected or reloaded

acceptance_criteria.given: a project is unregistered from the daemon

acceptance_criteria.then:

but not held in the cache

acceptance_criteria.given:

acceptance_criteria.then: the session is not treated as active in the cached index

acceptance_criteria.given: a project is registered and cache loading is in progress

acceptance_criteria.then:

while remaining domains continue loading

acceptance_criteria.given: a cache domain has reached ready state and a reload is triggered by file watcher invalidation or write-through
acceptance_criteria.when: an API request arrives for data in that domain during the reload
acceptance_criteria.then: the domain state remains ready and previously cached data continues to be served until the reload completes and the new data is swapped in — the domain never regresses to loading during a reload of already-populated data

acceptance_criteria.given: a cache domain transitions to ready state (from loading, degraded, or any non-ready state)
acceptance_criteria.then: a real-time event is broadcast to all connected clients identifying the domain and project that became ready

acceptance_criteria.given: a session is active and events are being recorded

acceptance_criteria.given: the dispatch engine appends an event to an active session

items.title: Daemon Read Path Optimization
items.description:
API read routes serve responses from the entity cache. Per-request
sync operations move to the background sync scheduler so that read
requests involve no git operations or filesystem reads.

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon is running with a registered project
acceptance_criteria.then: no git operations are performed as part of handling the request

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon's sync interval elapses
acceptance_criteria.then:

is pulled, the entity cache is invalidated and reloaded

acceptance_criteria.when: the request handler builds the index
acceptance_criteria.then:
the index is built from cached entity data, not from fresh
disk reads

acceptance_criteria.then:
the daemon commits the change to the shadow branch using the
standard write path before updating the cache

items.title: Daemon Log Capture
items.description:
The daemon emits an operational log that survives the process. Daemon
output is captured to a durable log file under the global daemon state
location in every run mode, so background (detached) runs — which have
no attached terminal — leave the same diagnostic trail as foreground
runs. Log growth is bounded deterministically by size-based rotation
with a fixed default cap, and the log location is discoverable from the
lifecycle status surface.

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon was started in background (detached) mode
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon emits startup, diagnostic, warning, or error output
acceptance_criteria.then:
Each emitted line is appended to a durable log file under the
global daemon state location instead of being discarded

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running in foreground mode
acceptance_criteria.then:
The output appears on the attached terminal and the same content is
also appended to the durable log file

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon appends a line to the durable log file
acceptance_criteria.then: Each captured line carries a timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given:
Appending the next captured line would push the active daemon log
file past the configured maximum size (default 5 MiB when not
configured)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The active log is rotated before the write so the new line begins
a fresh active file, exactly one prior rotated generation is
retained, older rotated content is deleted, and the combined size
of retained log files never exceeds twice the configured maximum
size plus the size of a single captured line

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running or has previously run
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon lifecycle status command reports daemon state
acceptance_criteria.then: The output includes the daemon log file location

items.title: Shared Mutation Pipeline
items.description:
Every mutation of project state follows one shared completion
sequence: the change is applied, a shadow branch commit records it,
the server's entity cache is updated to the post-mutation state, and
a typed event identifying the affected entities is broadcast to
subscribed clients. The sequence is the same regardless of the
interface the mutation arrived through — an entity API endpoint, a
proxied CLI command, or the dispatch engine's own record keeping.
When no daemon serves the project, the same mutation logic applies
and commits the change, and the cache and broadcast stages are
skipped without error.

acceptance_criteria.given: a mutation succeeds through any daemon-served interface
acceptance_criteria.when: the originating caller observes the result
acceptance_criteria.then:
a shadow commit recording the change exists and the entity cache
reflects the post-mutation state

acceptance_criteria.given: a mutation's typed event is broadcast
acceptance_criteria.when:
a subscriber re-fetches the affected entity in response to the
event
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response reflects the post-mutation state — the broadcast is
never observable before the cache reflects the change

acceptance_criteria.given:
the same logical mutation is performed once through its entity
API endpoint and once through a proxied CLI command
acceptance_criteria.then:
both broadcast on the same topic with the same event type and
the same payload schema, differing only in the values specific
to each occurrence

acceptance_criteria.given: a mutation executes while no daemon is serving the project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the change is applied and committed to the shadow branch exactly
as it would be under a daemon, and the unavailable cache and
broadcast stages produce no error

acceptance_criteria.given:
a batch of mutations executes atomically through a
daemon-served interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
exactly one shadow commit records the batch, and a typed event
is broadcast for each affected entity after the cache reflects
the batch's full result

acceptance_criteria.given: a mutation fails at any stage of the sequence
acceptance_criteria.when: the failure is reported to the originating caller
acceptance_criteria.then:
the report includes the underlying error description rather
than only a generic failure indication

acceptance_criteria.given:
a batch of mutations executes atomically while no daemon is
serving the project
acceptance_criteria.then:
exactly one shadow commit records the batch, and the
unavailable cache and broadcast stages produce no error

items.title: Dispatch Mutation Transparency
items.description:
The dispatch engine records its own bookkeeping — failure notes,
timeout notes, and task blocking — through the shared mutation
pipeline. These mutations are applied in the engine's own process,
broadcast on the owning entity topics like any other mutation, and
report failures with their underlying detail. A bookkeeping failure
is always subordinate to the agent outcome it records: it never
replaces or hides that outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given:
the dispatch engine records a failure note, timeout note, or
block on a task
acceptance_criteria.then:
the broadcast topic, event type, and payload schema are
identical to those produced when the same mutation is performed
through the task API

acceptance_criteria.given:
the dispatch engine performs a bookkeeping mutation while
running inside the daemon process
acceptance_criteria.then:
the mutation is applied in-process: no separate process is
created on its behalf, and no request re-enters the daemon's
command interface

acceptance_criteria.given: a dispatch-initiated bookkeeping mutation fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
the underlying error description is written to the
operator-visible log, in engine-driven and one-shot execution
modes alike, and the failure is never silently discarded

acceptance_criteria.given:
an agent invocation fails and the subsequent failure-note
mutation also fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
the recorded outcome remains the invocation's original error,
and the note-write failure appears as a separate log entry
rather than replacing it

items.title: Mutation Event Coverage
items.description:
Every entity domain that clients can subscribe to receives
entity-scoped typed events for all of its daemon-served mutations.
Task changes, review creation, spec item changes, and plan-local
resource changes each broadcast on their owning domain topic,
through every interface a mutation can arrive on, with payloads that
identify the affected entity and the kind of change.

acceptance_criteria.given:
any task mutation — creation, any state transition, or any
field change, including changes with no dedicated entity
endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: the mutation succeeds through any interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
a typed task event is broadcast on the task domain topic
identifying the task and the kind of change, with prior and new
status when the change is a state transition

acceptance_criteria.given: a review record is created through any interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
a typed review-creation event is broadcast on the review domain
topic identifying the new review and its subject

acceptance_criteria.given:
a spec item is created, changed, or removed through any
interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
a typed spec-item event is broadcast on the spec-item domain
topic, and a subscriber to that topic observes the change
without relying on file-change fallback events

acceptance_criteria.given:
a plan-local resource is added, replaced, or removed through a
daemon-served plan resource route
acceptance_criteria.then:
a typed plan-resource event is broadcast on the plan domain
topic, identifying the owning plan, the resource, and the kind
of change, and a subscriber to that topic observes the resource
change without relying on file-change fallback events

acceptance_criteria.given: any entity-scoped mutation event payload
acceptance_criteria.then:
the payload identifies each affected entity by its canonical
identifier, sufficient to refresh exactly that entity and
nothing broader

items.title: Web UI assets bundled in npm package
items.description: The kspec npm package bundles the pre-built web UI static assets so the daemon can serve the web UI when installed in any project, without requiring a local web UI build. items.title: WebSocket Disconnect Lifecycle Cleanup
items.description: Ensure daemon WebSocket disconnect handling is accurate for abnormal closes. Disconnect events must reliably identify the same session created on connect, remove that session from in-memory registries, and prevent stale heartbeat/client counts after client disconnect or process termination.

acceptance_criteria.then: the connections field reflects only currently active sessions

acceptance_criteria.then: the daemon does not attempt to ping that session and emits no stale heartbeat ping log for it

acceptance_criteria.then: the session is removed from pubsub connection tracking and the disconnect log includes that session id rather than undefined

items.title: Review Content Diff API
items.description:
Daemon API endpoints for serving diff content and file data needed by
the review content viewer. For code reviews, serves parsed git diffs
between base and head commits. For plan/spec reviews, serves the
entity content for structured display.

acceptance_criteria.given: A code review has base and head commit refs
acceptance_criteria.then:
It returns a parsed diff with file list, per-file stats (+/- lines),
and structured hunks with typed change lines (added, deleted, unchanged)
including old and new line numbers

acceptance_criteria.given: A client requests expanded context for a file in a diff
acceptance_criteria.then:
It returns the additional context lines from the file at the head
commit for the specified line range, enabling "show more lines"
expansion in the diff viewer

acceptance_criteria.when: The file exists in the diff
acceptance_criteria.then:
It returns the parsed diff for a single file, enabling lazy
loading of individual file diffs

acceptance_criteria.then:
It returns the parsed entity content — for plans: sections
(title, specs array, tasks array, notes) extracted from the plan
document; for specs: structured fields (description, acceptance
criteria, traits, metadata) from kspec item get — each with
section identifiers for anchor targeting

acceptance_criteria.given: a plan review subject has markdown content that references declared plan resources with `./resources/<relative-path>`
acceptance_criteria.when: a client requests `GET /api/reviews/:id/content` for that review
acceptance_criteria.then: each affected markdown section includes byte-free plan resource context with the owning plan ref, a browser-fetchable plan-scoped resource base URL that preserves selected-project context, and bounded declared-resource metadata sufficient for clients to rewrite only declared safe resource paths without embedding resource bytes

acceptance_criteria.given: a task review subject has a description that references task resources with `./resources/<relative-path>`
acceptance_criteria.when: a client requests `GET /api/reviews/:id/content` for that review
acceptance_criteria.then: the task description markdown section includes byte-free task resource context with the owning task ref, a browser-fetchable task-scoped resource base URL that preserves selected-project context, and bounded resolved-resource status sufficient for clients to rewrite only present resources while distinguishing drifted, missing, and unresolved resolved resources without embedding resource bytes

items.title: Daemon Network Endpoint Contract
items.description:
The daemon has one canonical network endpoint contract shared by
daemon startup, daemon lifecycle metadata, CLI clients, web UI
development clients, and tests. The default endpoint is a local
loopback endpoint that does not depend on operating-system hostname
resolution. Configured host and port values are resolved once and
every daemon client uses the advertised connection endpoint instead
of constructing daemon URLs independently.

acceptance_criteria.given:
No daemon host is configured by CLI flag, environment variable,
or kspec.config.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then:
The daemon binds and advertises 127.0.0.1 without resolving
the name localhost

acceptance_criteria.given:
No daemon host is configured and binding 127.0.0.1 fails because
IPv4 loopback is unavailable
acceptance_criteria.then:
The daemon retries on ::1 and advertises URLs using bracketed
IPv6 host syntax

acceptance_criteria.given:
A daemon host is configured by CLI flag, environment variable,
or kspec.config.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: The daemon binds to the configured host value

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon bind host is 0.0.0.0 or ::
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon advertises its connection endpoint for local CLI use
acceptance_criteria.then:
The advertised connect host is a loopback address or explicitly
configured connect host, not the wildcard bind address

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon starts successfully
acceptance_criteria.then:
The global daemon metadata records pid, port, bind_host,
connect_host, api_url, ws_url, and runtime

acceptance_criteria.given:
A daemon client needs to call the daemon from CLI code, daemon
status code, scheduled-command code, agent-command code, event
code, task-event code, or web UI development code

acceptance_criteria.then:
The client calls the advertised URL instead of a separately chosen
daemon host or port

daemon.port file exists
acceptance_criteria.when: A CLI client checks daemon availability
acceptance_criteria.then:
The client attempts 127.0.0.1 with the legacy port value before
treating the daemon as unavailable

The effective daemon bind host is a non-loopback address or a
wildcard address

acceptance_criteria.then:

unauthenticated project data and mutation APIs on the configured
network interface

acceptance_criteria.when: the test creates HTTP clients, WebSocket clients, browser URLs, or daemon connection metadata
acceptance_criteria.then: the test uses the canonical resolved daemon endpoint

acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon starts or a lifecycle command reports the endpoint
