items.title: Daemon Test Endpoint Consistency
items.description:
Tests that call a daemon use the same endpoint contract as production
daemon consumers. Real daemon fixtures, mock daemon fixtures, HTTP test
clients, WebSocket clients, browser page URLs, and CLI metadata setup all
receive endpoint information from one resolved fixture endpoint instead of
constructing localhost URLs independently.

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test fixture has resolved a daemon endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: Test code makes an HTTP or WebSocket daemon request
acceptance_criteria.then: The request uses the fixture-provided client endpoint

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test fixture uses the default loopback endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: The URLs use 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost

acceptance_criteria.given: A test uses both HTTP and WebSocket daemon clients
acceptance_criteria.then: Both clients address the same resolved daemon endpoint

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI client test uses a mock daemon instead of a real daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: The test records daemon connection metadata
acceptance_criteria.then: The metadata matches the canonical daemon connection contract

acceptance_criteria.given: A test daemon listens on a dynamic port
acceptance_criteria.then: The clients receive the port from the fixture endpoint

inherited_acs.given: A running daemon has reported the endpoint clients should use
inherited_acs.when: A daemon consumer communicates with that daemon
inherited_acs.then:
The consumer addresses the reported endpoint rather than independently
choosing a different daemon destination

inherited_acs.given: The daemon is explicitly configured to listen on all interfaces
inherited_acs.when: A daemon consumer communicates with that daemon
inherited_acs.then:
The consumer addresses a non-wildcard destination reported for client
communication

items.title: CLI Lifecycle Test Endpoint Consumption
items.description:
CLI lifecycle tests may start and stop the daemon through the CLI when the
lifecycle command is the behavior under test. Once a CLI-started daemon has
reported a client endpoint, lifecycle tests that make HTTP or WebSocket
requests use that reported endpoint instead of constructing a localhost URL
from a port number.

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI lifecycle test starts a daemon and the daemon reports a client endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: The test makes an HTTP or WebSocket request to that daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: The request uses the reported client endpoint

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI lifecycle test constructs a loopback daemon URL directly
acceptance_criteria.when: The test is reviewed by guardrails or humans
acceptance_criteria.then: The direct URL construction is tied to endpoint reporting, endpoint fallback, or missing-metadata behavior under test

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI lifecycle test needs to call a daemon that was started through the CLI
acceptance_criteria.when: A reported endpoint is available in daemon lifecycle state
acceptance_criteria.then: Shared test code resolves a client endpoint for the test

items.title: Daemon-Backed Test Fixture Contract
items.description:
Daemon-backed tests use one shared fixture contract for process startup,
project setup, environment isolation, readiness, and teardown. The
contract applies to Vitest and Playwright tests that start a real daemon
process, while allowing unit tests and in-process route tests to use
narrower fixtures that do not start a daemon.

acceptance_criteria.given: A Vitest or Playwright test needs a real daemon child process
acceptance_criteria.then: Startup flows through the shared daemon test fixture

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test prepares daemon lifecycle state
acceptance_criteria.when: The fixture builds the child process environment
acceptance_criteria.then:
The daemon HOME and kspec config directory are isolated from the
ambient user environment

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test prepares kspec project data
acceptance_criteria.when: The fixture creates the project workspace
acceptance_criteria.then: The daemon reads only fixture-owned project files

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test has started a child daemon process
acceptance_criteria.when: The test completes, fails, or times out
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup targets only the daemon owned by that fixture

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test waits for daemon readiness
acceptance_criteria.when: Readiness is not reached before the timeout
acceptance_criteria.then:
The failure output reports a diagnostic bundle for the failed startup
attempt

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test needs startup synchronization
acceptance_criteria.when: The test waits for daemon readiness
acceptance_criteria.then: The wait uses bounded polling rather than fixed sleep delays

acceptance_criteria.given: A developer or CI runner has an unrelated daemon running
acceptance_criteria.then: The tests do not stop, kill, or reuse the unrelated daemon

items.title: Daemon Test Mode Boundaries
items.description:
Daemon tests choose the lightest fixture mode that still exercises the
behavior under test. Route and API handler tests use in-process app
fixtures. CLI client routing tests use mock daemons with realistic
metadata. Daemon lifecycle, runtime adapter, and WebSocket protocol tests
use real child daemons through the shared fixture.

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon API test only needs route handler behavior
acceptance_criteria.when: The test creates the daemon app
acceptance_criteria.then: The test does not spawn a daemon child process

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI test only needs to verify daemon client routing
acceptance_criteria.when: The test prepares a reachable daemon endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: The test uses a mock daemon with canonical connection metadata

acceptance_criteria.given: A CLI test verifies serve start, stop, status, or restart behavior
acceptance_criteria.when: The test manages a daemon process
acceptance_criteria.then: The test invokes the CLI lifecycle path under test

acceptance_criteria.given:
A test verifies daemon runtime, lifecycle, cache readiness, or
WebSocket protocol behavior
acceptance_criteria.when: The behavior requires the daemon process boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: The test uses a real child daemon through the shared fixture

items.title: In-Process Daemon Test Helper Boundary
items.description:
In-process daemon API test helpers advertise the route and dependency
boundary they provide. Tests that need full production-server behavior do
not rely on a helper that only assembles a narrower route subset.

acceptance_criteria.given: A shared in-process daemon API helper is available to tests
acceptance_criteria.when: A test author reads or calls the helper
acceptance_criteria.then: The helper states the server behavior boundary it represents

acceptance_criteria.given: An in-process daemon API test relies on shared route or dependency behavior
acceptance_criteria.then: The helper boundary covers the behavior asserted by the test

items.title: Daemon Test Harness Guardrails
items.description:
Focused fixture contract tests plus static and runtime guardrails keep new
daemon tests on the standardized helpers. Direct daemon child-process
startup and detached serve commands are allowed only inside the shared
helper implementation or in explicitly documented exception tests.

acceptance_criteria.given: Shared daemon fixture or helper behavior is implemented or changed
acceptance_criteria.then: Focused helper tests exercise the fixture contract directly

acceptance_criteria.given:
A test file starts a real daemon directly outside the shared daemon
fixture
acceptance_criteria.then: The check reports the direct daemon startup

acceptance_criteria.given:
A test file starts a detached daemon through the CLI without scoped
cleanup
acceptance_criteria.then: The check reports the unsafe detached daemon start

acceptance_criteria.given: The shared daemon fixture implementation starts a daemon process
acceptance_criteria.then: The check accepts the helper-owned startup code

acceptance_criteria.given:
A test needs to exercise behavior that intentionally violates the
normal fixture pattern
acceptance_criteria.then: The check accepts only a local documented exception for that test case

items.title: Daemon Test Guardrail Precision
items.description:
Static guardrails report daemon-test patterns that can leak daemon
processes or bypass the shared fixture, while avoiding reports for
unrelated subprocesses that only happen to contain similar argument words.
Cleanup-based exceptions are accepted only when cleanup is associated with
the daemon that was just started before the test makes later observations.

acceptance_criteria.given: A test invokes the real daemon entrypoint directly outside an approved helper
acceptance_criteria.when: The guardrail scans the test file
acceptance_criteria.then: The direct daemon startup is reported

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a detached daemon through the kspec CLI
acceptance_criteria.when: The test performs later awaits, assertions, or daemon observations before registering cleanup for that daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: The detached daemon startup is reported

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a subprocess that is not a kspec daemon command
acceptance_criteria.when: The subprocess arguments contain words also used by daemon lifecycle commands
acceptance_criteria.then: The daemon guardrail does not report the subprocess

acceptance_criteria.given: A test intentionally violates a daemon guardrail for behavior under test
acceptance_criteria.then: The suppression is local to the violating statement

acceptance_criteria.given: A test intentionally suppresses a daemon guardrail
acceptance_criteria.then: The suppression states the behavior being exercised

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a detached daemon and registers cleanup before later awaits, assertions, or daemon observations
acceptance_criteria.when: The cleanup callback does not yet capture or otherwise own the concrete pid, child handle, or stop handle for that just-started daemon before an intervening observation can fail
acceptance_criteria.then: The guardrail reports the detached daemon startup as missing scoped cleanup

acceptance_criteria.given: A test wraps daemon startup in a local helper function or another helper-like abstraction that is not an explicit shared daemon-test fixture utility or documented guardrail internal
acceptance_criteria.when: The guardrail scans the test file
acceptance_criteria.then: The guardrail treats the wrapped daemon startup the same as an inline unsafe daemon start and reports violations of the fixture and cleanup contract

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a detached daemon through a daemon lifecycle path
acceptance_criteria.when: The guardrail evaluates cleanup for that daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: Only cleanup operations that terminate or stop the daemon satisfy the cleanup requirement

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a detached daemon and registers cleanup-shaped code
acceptance_criteria.when: The code only probes liveness, emits documentation text, calls a non-daemon helper, or sends a non-terminating signal
acceptance_criteria.then: The detached daemon start is reported as missing scoped cleanup

acceptance_criteria.given: A test cleanup callback calls a helper by a daemon-cleanup-like name
acceptance_criteria.when: That helper is locally defined or otherwise not one of the approved cleanup primitives
acceptance_criteria.then: The helper name alone does not satisfy daemon cleanup

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts a detached daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup is registered only on process-lifecycle or global shutdown hooks
acceptance_criteria.then: That registration does not satisfy the per-test scoped cleanup requirement

acceptance_criteria.given: A test invokes a CLI command that may implicitly auto-start a daemon and then observes the started daemon's pid, metadata, process, or endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: The test performs later assertions or daemon observations before registering cleanup for that daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: The unsafe auto-started daemon ownership is reported

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Tightened ACs ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation and ac-approved-daemon-helper-boundary-explicit lack current source/test evidence. (1) The cleanup classifier in tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js recognizes daemon-shaped cleanup CALL expressions (process.kill, child.kill('SIGTERM'), killPid(pid), runKspec serve stop, etc.) and gates on registration before the next observation, but it does not verify that the captured pid/child/stop handle was already bound to the just-started daemon at the registration site; a pattern that registers onTestFinished(() => killPid(pid)) before the detached start and then assigns pid only after an intervening await/expect satisfies the current rule yet leaves cleanup unbound on the failing path. (2) The Program:exit detached-cleanup check skips reports when isInHelperFunction(node) is true. isInHelperFunction classifies any named function declaration or variable-bound function expression as a helper, so an unsafe daemon start hidden inside an arbitrary local wrapper in a test file bypasses the rule even though the wrapper is not a shared fixture or documented guardrail internal. Implementation status moved to in_progress --no-cascade pending the follow-up rule fix and regression tests.

items.title: Daemon Test Startup Failure Hygiene
items.description:
Test fixtures that start daemon-like child processes fail safely when
startup does not reach readiness. Startup failures produce bounded
diagnostics for the attempted child, and any child process already owned by
the fixture is stopped before the helper returns failure to the caller.

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test fixture attempts to start a child process
acceptance_criteria.when: The operating system or runtime rejects the process launch
acceptance_criteria.then: The caller receives a bounded startup diagnostic for that attempt

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test fixture has obtained a child process handle
acceptance_criteria.when: Startup fails before the fixture reports readiness
acceptance_criteria.then: The fixture stops the child process before returning failure

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test helper starts a child process for daemon-backed behavior
acceptance_criteria.when: The helper builds the child process environment
acceptance_criteria.then: Ambient daemon-control and session variables are not inherited

acceptance_criteria.given: A wrapper starts a fixture-owned daemon process
acceptance_criteria.when: The wrapper receives a cleanup registration hook
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup is registered before the readiness wait can fail

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon test fixture has obtained a child process handle and constructed a stop handle that owns that child
acceptance_criteria.when: The caller-provided cleanup-registration hook fails before the fixture reports readiness
acceptance_criteria.then: The fixture stops the owned child before returning or surfacing the cleanup-registration failure

notes.author: @claude
notes.content: Tightened AC ac-cleanup-registration-failure-stops-owned-child lacks current source/test evidence. tests/helpers/daemon.ts spawns the child, builds a scoped stop() that owns the spawned child, and then calls opts.registerCleanup(stop) outside the readiness try/catch. A synchronous throw inside the registration hook propagates without invoking stop(), so the owned child is leaked. No regression test exercises this cleanup-registration failure phase. Implementation status moved to in_progress --no-cascade pending the follow-up fixture fix and regression test.

items.title: Daemon Test Teardown Boundedness
items.description:
Daemon-backed test infrastructure treats cleanup as a deterministic
contract rather than a best-effort signal send. Fixtures, wrappers, and
daemon lifecycle tests that own daemon processes or daemon-like mock
children stop owned resources within bounded time, verify termination when
cleanup reports success, and preserve the primary failure when cleanup also
encounters an error.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A daemon-backed test fixture or lifecycle helper owns a daemon process
or daemon-like child process
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup reports that the process has been stopped
acceptance_criteria.then: The owned process has been observed terminated

acceptance_criteria.given:
A fixture-owned daemon process or daemon-like child ignores the initial
termination request
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup attempts to stop the owned process
acceptance_criteria.then: Cleanup reaches a bounded terminal outcome

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-like test server has an active request that does not complete
acceptance_criteria.then: Teardown reaches a bounded terminal outcome

acceptance_criteria.given:
Daemon test setup has created temporary project, home, port, or child
resources
acceptance_criteria.when: A later setup step fails before the fixture reports readiness
acceptance_criteria.then: The resources already owned by the setup are cleaned up

acceptance_criteria.given:
A daemon-backed test setup, test body, or readiness wait fails with a
primary error
acceptance_criteria.when: Cleanup also fails while handling that primary error
acceptance_criteria.then: The surfaced failure preserves the primary error

acceptance_criteria.given:
A daemon-backed test or fixture probes a daemon HTTP or WebSocket
endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: The endpoint accepts a connection but does not respond
acceptance_criteria.then: The probe reaches a bounded terminal outcome

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test fixture uses a shared filesystem-based serialization lock, and a previous lock holder has exited without releasing the lock
acceptance_criteria.when: A new daemon-backed test attempts to acquire the lock
acceptance_criteria.then: Acquisition reaches a bounded terminal outcome by reclaiming the lock from the crashed holder

items.title: Daemon Failure Observability
items.description:
When the daemon process terminates — gracefully or because of a fatal
error — the termination reason is durably recorded outside the process
and can be retrieved after the fact. Fatal conditions that would
otherwise end the process without a trace (uncaught errors, unhandled
asynchronous rejections) are captured with diagnostic detail before the
process exits. The daemon lifecycle status surface reports the most
recent termination when no daemon is running, so a user investigating a
disappeared daemon can see why it stopped without reproducing the
failure.

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon process is running
acceptance_criteria.when:
An uncaught error or an unhandled asynchronous rejection occurs in
the daemon process
acceptance_criteria.then:
The error message, available stack detail, and a timestamp are
durably recorded before the process exits, and the process exits
with a non-zero exit code

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon process has terminated for any reason
acceptance_criteria.when: A user inspects daemon state after the process is gone
acceptance_criteria.then:
A durable record of the most recent termination is retrievable
without a running daemon, containing the termination kind
(graceful shutdown, fatal error, or startup failure), the reason
detail, and a timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: No daemon is running and a prior termination record exists
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon lifecycle status command runs
acceptance_criteria.then:
The output reports that the daemon is not running and includes the
most recent termination kind, reason, and timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given:
The daemon shuts down in response to a shutdown signal or the stop
command
acceptance_criteria.then:
The termination record identifies the termination as a graceful
shutdown, so a later status check does not report it as a failure

All REST endpoints return JSON with consistent patterns. WebSocket uses topic-based pub/sub
with request_id correlation for command acknowledgment.

items.title: Mutation Event Naming
items.description:
Broadcast vocabulary is organized by entity domain: each domain has
one updates topic, and entity-scoped event types within it name the
changed subject and the change in past-tense subject_change form.
The task, spec-item, review, plan, inbox, and triage domains use
`tasks:updates`, `items:updates`, `reviews:updates`,
`plans:updates`, `inbox:updates`, and `triage:updates`,
respectively. New capabilities extend an existing domain topic with
new event types rather than adding a parallel topic for the same
entities. Two event families are reserved by name for later
capabilities: plan-revision events on the plan domain topic and
coverage-state events on the spec-item domain topic. The reserved
names are part of this vocabulary; their payloads and semantics are
defined by the capabilities that introduce them.

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of entity-scoped event types the daemon broadcasts
acceptance_criteria.then:
every entity-scoped event type follows the past-tense
subject_change form and is published on its owning domain's
updates topic

acceptance_criteria.given: a client subscribed to a single entity domain's updates topic
acceptance_criteria.when: mutations occur anywhere in that domain
acceptance_criteria.then:
every entity-scoped event for that domain arrives on that one
topic, and no other topic carries entity-scoped events for the
same domain

acceptance_criteria.given:
the two reserved event families — plan-revision and
coverage-state
acceptance_criteria.then:
the plan-revision family appears as a named reservation on the
plan domain's updates topic and the coverage-state family as a
named reservation on the spec-item domain's updates topic, each
with no payload or semantics defined

items.title: Multi-Directory Daemon Architecture
items.description:
Extends the daemon server to support multiple kspec projects simultaneously from a single
daemon process. Projects are identified via X-Kspec-Dir HTTP header. Enables E2E testing
with isolated fixtures and multi-project development workflows.

Key architectural changes:
- Global daemon with PID/port files at ~/.config/kspec/
- Project context caching with on-demand registration. The registered-project roster
  (project paths and registration metadata) is daemon-level state persisted in the daemon
  configuration directory and restored on restart; it is distinct from runtime watcher and
  cache state, which is per-process and rebuilt after a restart.
- Per-project file watchers
- WebSocket connections bound to specific projects

BREAKING CHANGE: PID/port files move from .kspec/.daemon.pid to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid

notes.author: @claude
notes.content:
Design decisions:
- X-Kspec-Dir header for project selection (clean URLs, easy for clients)
- Single bundled web UI (consistent version across projects)
- On-demand project registration (auto-register on first request)
- No memory limit on cached projects (keep until restart)
- Global PID at ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
- Per-project file watchers
- Backwards compatible (no header = startup cwd project if valid)

items.title: ANSI Terminal Output Rendering
items.description:
Parse and render ANSI SGR (Select Graphic Rendition) escape sequences in terminal/bash tool output displayed in the session stream. Convert ANSI color codes to styled HTML spans so terminal output appears with the same colors and formatting as a real terminal.

Currently ToolCallView.svelte renders output in a plain <pre> tag — ANSI codes show as garbled raw text.

Scope: SGR codes only (colors, bold, dim, italic, underline, strikethrough, reset). Cursor movement and screen control codes (CUU, CUD, clear, etc.) are outside scope and should be stripped.

Rendering pipeline: Tool/bash output stays in <pre> blocks and is never markdown-parsed. ANSI color rendering applies only inside these <pre> blocks. Agent text messages continue to use the markdown renderer. The two parsers never touch the same content.

acceptance_criteria.given: tool output contains ANSI SGR escape sequences (e.g. \x1b[32mPASS\x1b[0m)
acceptance_criteria.when: the output is displayed in ToolCallView
acceptance_criteria.then: the text renders with corresponding CSS colors instead of showing raw escape codes

items.title: API Reference Resolution
items.description:
The daemon API resolves entity references to display-ready metadata so
consumers can render human-readable titles, statuses, and types without
separate lookups. This applies both inline (fields within existing
responses) and via a dedicated lightweight index endpoint for arbitrary
resolution.

acceptance_criteria.then:

against loaded entity data. Null if the ref cannot be resolved.

acceptance_criteria.given:
An API response includes an array of references to other entities
(depends_on, blocked_by, evidence_refs, derived_specs, derived_tasks)
acceptance_criteria.then:
Each entry includes the resolved title and current status alongside
the ref string.

acceptance_criteria.given: A referenced entity has been deleted or the ref is invalid
acceptance_criteria.then:
The title field is null and the raw ref is preserved. The response
does not fail or omit the entry.

acceptance_criteria.given:
A consumer needs to resolve an arbitrary set of refs to display
metadata (e.g., rendering refs in markdown, cross-entity link previews)
acceptance_criteria.when: A lightweight index endpoint is called
acceptance_criteria.then:
Returns a map of all resolvable refs (tasks, items, traits) with
title, type, and status. Both ULID and slug keys are included
for each entity.

acceptance_criteria.given: The project has 1000+ entities
acceptance_criteria.then:
The response payload is significantly smaller than fetching full
entity lists because it only includes display metadata.

items.title: UI Data Freshness and Caching
items.description:
The web UI maintains a shared, reactive data cache that provides instant
page transitions, request deduplication, and real-time updates without
per-page independent fetching. Data fetched by one page is available to
all pages. Real-time events drive cache invalidation. The UI degrades
gracefully when the daemon is unreachable and supports read-only static
mode for exported snapshots.

acceptance_criteria.given: A page fetches data on first visit
acceptance_criteria.when: The user navigates away and returns to the same page
acceptance_criteria.then:
The page renders immediately from cached data without a loading
state, then revalidates in the background if the data is stale.

acceptance_criteria.given: Two or more pages or components need the same data concurrently
acceptance_criteria.when: Both are active at the same time
acceptance_criteria.then: Only one HTTP request is made. Both consumers share the result.

acceptance_criteria.given: A WebSocket broadcast event indicates data has changed
acceptance_criteria.when: The event is processed by the UI
acceptance_criteria.then:
Cached data for the affected entity type is invalidated and
active views revalidate in the background. If the broadcast
includes sufficient enriched data, the cache is updated
immediately without a server round-trip.

acceptance_criteria.given: The UI needs periodic status data (badge counts, agent status)
acceptance_criteria.when: The data changes on the server
acceptance_criteria.then:
The data is served from cache and kept current via event-driven
invalidation rather than timer-based polling.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user switches projects in the multi-directory daemon
acceptance_criteria.then:
All cached data is discarded. Subsequent data requests fetch
fresh data for the new project.

acceptance_criteria.given: The app is running in static mode (exported snapshot)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The request is served from the static data source. No daemon
HTTP calls are attempted.

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is unreachable or returns an error
acceptance_criteria.then:
The error is surfaced with appropriate messaging (e.g., daemon
not running vs data error). Retry behavior is appropriate for
localhost (minimal retries, short delay).

acceptance_criteria.given: A write operation is performed (start task, add note, etc.)
acceptance_criteria.then:
Related cached data is invalidated so the originating client
updates immediately without waiting for a broadcast.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user performs a hard page refresh or navigates directly to a URL
acceptance_criteria.when: The app initializes from scratch (no prior client state)
acceptance_criteria.then: The initialization lifecycle (mode detection, project loading, query enabling) completes and the page renders data. No SSR hydration mismatch prevents reactive state updates from propagating.

acceptance_criteria.given: An entity can change through more than one server-side execution path
acceptance_criteria.when: Any path changes list-visible data for an active view
acceptance_criteria.then: The active view stays fresh without a manual reload, and the freshness contract does not depend on which internal path produced the change.

acceptance_criteria.given: the server signals that its cache is still warming
acceptance_criteria.then: a loading skeleton is displayed instead of empty content, and the warming response is not persisted in the client cache as real data

acceptance_criteria.given: the UI is displaying a loading skeleton due to cache warming
acceptance_criteria.when: a real-time event indicates the cache domain is ready
acceptance_criteria.then: the affected queries are invalidated and the view transitions to real data without user interaction

acceptance_criteria.given: the UI is displaying a loading skeleton due to cache warming
acceptance_criteria.when: no real-time domain-ready event has been received
acceptance_criteria.then: the UI retries the request at short intervals as a fallback for missed or delayed real-time events

acceptance_criteria.given: the UI has been retrying a cache-warming response
acceptance_criteria.when: the retry ceiling (30 seconds) is reached without the cache becoming ready
acceptance_criteria.then: the UI displays an error state with a manual retry option instead of continuing to show the loading skeleton

items.title: UI Targeted Event Consumption
items.description:
The web client treats typed mutation events as its primary
freshness signal. An event drives one immediate, targeted refresh:
the affected entity's data and the views that include it update,
and unaffected domains are left alone. Changes that originate
outside daemon-served mutations reach the client through
file-change fallback events, which also trigger a single immediate
refresh of their affected domains. No freshness path schedules
repeated delayed refreshes to compensate for event-timing
uncertainty.

acceptance_criteria.given: a typed mutation event identifying a single entity arrives
acceptance_criteria.then:
the client refreshes that entity's cached data and the views
that include it, and does not refetch entity domains the event
does not affect

acceptance_criteria.given: any broadcast event arrives
acceptance_criteria.when: the client initiates refresh work for it
acceptance_criteria.then:
the refresh begins immediately on arrival and happens exactly
once per event, with no additional fixed-delay refreshes
scheduled for the same event

acceptance_criteria.given:
a view is open and a mutation affecting it is performed through
the CLI
acceptance_criteria.when: the mutation's typed event reaches the client
acceptance_criteria.then:
the open view updates without a manual reload and without
depending on file-change fallback events

acceptance_criteria.given:
a shadow branch file changes through a path that is not a
daemon-served mutation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the client performs a single immediate refresh of the affected
domains and open views reflect the change

items.title: WebSocket Session Event Streaming
items.description:
The session stream view receives all live session activity via WebSocket
structured lifecycle events. Messages stream progressively at newline
boundaries (not per-token). Tool calls show name and input immediately,
with output fetched on demand. HTTP serves historical sessions and
initial catch-up for live sessions already in progress.

This replaces the current model where WebSocket sends raw text chunks
and HTTP polls for structured events every 3 seconds during live sessions.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent begins composing a response
acceptance_criteria.then: A writing/thinking indicator appears for the in-progress message block.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session where the agent is composing a response
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent produces text that includes newline characters
acceptance_criteria.then:
Completed lines stream into the message block progressively at
newline boundaries. The user sees text appear line-by-line rather
than waiting for the full message or seeing per-character updates.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session where the agent is composing a response
acceptance_criteria.when:
The agent finishes the message (begins a tool call, starts thinking,
ends the session, or starts a new turn)
acceptance_criteria.then:
Any remaining buffered text is flushed to the message block.
The writing indicator is removed. The message renders as a
complete block identical to how it appears in historical playback.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session
acceptance_criteria.when: The agent initiates a tool call
acceptance_criteria.then:
A tool call block appears in "running" state showing the tool name
and input parameters. No output is shown yet.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session with a running tool call
acceptance_criteria.when: The tool call finishes (success or failure)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The tool call block updates to show completed/failed status and
execution duration. Output is not loaded until the user expands
the block.

acceptance_criteria.given: A completed tool call block is displayed (live or historical)
acceptance_criteria.when: The user expands the tool call to view output
acceptance_criteria.then:
The output is fetched via HTTP with blob content resolved
server-side. A loading state shows during the fetch. If the
fetch fails, an error state is shown with retry option.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a live session
acceptance_criteria.then:
A thinking block appears and streams text progressively
(same newline-boundary streaming as messages). Thinking
blocks render collapsed by default.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user navigates to a completed session
acceptance_criteria.then:
All events are fetched via HTTP in a single request.
Messages, tool calls, and thinking blocks render using the
same DisplayBlock components as live streaming. Tool call
blocks render collapsed — output is fetched on-demand when
the user expands the block (same behavior as live sessions).

acceptance_criteria.given: A user navigates to a session that is already in progress
acceptance_criteria.then:
Events up to the current point are fetched via HTTP (same as
historical). Then the view transitions to WebSocket streaming
for subsequent live events. No gap or duplication between
the HTTP catch-up and WebSocket stream.

acceptance_criteria.given: A live session is being viewed
acceptance_criteria.then:
No periodic HTTP polling for events occurs. All live session
activity arrives via WebSocket. HTTP is only used for initial
catch-up and on-demand tool output fetches.

acceptance_criteria.given:
The WebSocket connection drops and reconnects while viewing

acceptance_criteria.then:
Missed events are fetched via HTTP using the last known
sequence number. The view resumes WebSocket streaming
after the gap is filled.

acceptance_criteria.then:

boundaries. Tool calls show name and status transitions.

acceptance_criteria.then: The tool call block updates its input in-place. The collapsed preview shows the input summary. The expanded view shows the full input. No duplicate block is created.

The same field extraction logic (toolCallId, toolName, rawInput, rawOutput, status) is used regardless of whether events arrive via HTTP batch or individual WebSocket messages. The resulting DisplayBlocks are identical for the same event sequence.

items.title: Session Event Broadcasting
items.description:
The daemon broadcasts structured session lifecycle events over
WebSocket. Text content streams at newline boundaries — balancing
responsiveness (line-by-line updates) with efficiency (not per-token).
Event state is tracked per-session to support concurrent sessions.

acceptance_criteria.then:

type is broadcast.

items.title: API Input Type Safety
items.description:
All daemon API endpoints must enforce type constraints on input
fields at the framework schema level, not through manual checks in
handler code. This applies to both mutation endpoints (request body
fields) and query endpoints (filter parameters). When an input
contains a field with a constrained type — an enum, a bounded
number, a structured object with required shape — the framework
must reject invalid values before the handler executes. This
applies to HTTP endpoints and WebSocket message handlers.

Framework-level validation is preferred over handler-level
validation because it is declarative, cannot be bypassed by handler
code paths, and produces consistent error responses. Existing
handler-level validation may remain as defense-in-depth.

acceptance_criteria.given: An API mutation endpoint accepts a field with a type constraint
acceptance_criteria.when: The request body contains a value that violates the constraint
acceptance_criteria.then:
The framework returns a validation error before the handler
executes, and no data is persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: An API mutation endpoint accepts a field with a type constraint
acceptance_criteria.when: The request body contains a valid value
acceptance_criteria.then: The handler executes normally

acceptance_criteria.given: An API query endpoint accepts a typed filter parameter
acceptance_criteria.when: The provided value does not match the filter's type constraint
acceptance_criteria.then:
The framework returns a validation error rather than silently
returning empty results

inherited_acs.given: Any input surface accepts a field with a defined type constraint
inherited_acs.when: The provided value does not satisfy the constraint
inherited_acs.then:
The operation is rejected before any data is persisted or
state is mutated

inherited_acs.given: An input validation error occurs for a constrained field
inherited_acs.when: The error is reported to the caller
inherited_acs.then:
The message includes the set of valid alternatives for the
field, not just the field name and invalid value (extends
@trait-error-guidance ac-5 which requires identifying the
field/value but not listing valid alternatives)

inherited_acs.given: A field's type constraint is defined in a canonical schema
inherited_acs.then:
The validation is derived from that schema definition rather
than a separately maintained check
returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing

items.title: Resource-Bounded File Monitoring
items.description:
Defines the contract for how the daemon monitors project directories
for changes. File monitoring must be resource-proportional — the
daemon's resource consumption scales with the number of directories
and metadata files that need monitoring, not with the total volume
of data stored in those directories.

The daemon monitors two directory trees per project: the shadow
branch worktree for spec/task state, and the sessions directory
for session lifecycle. Each tree has distinct monitoring needs —
the shadow branch contains structured YAML that drives cache
invalidation, while the sessions directory contains metadata files
alongside large volumes of content data (blobs) that are irrelevant
to cache freshness.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project is registered with the daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: File monitoring starts for that project
acceptance_criteria.then:
Changes to structured data files in the shadow branch directory
are detected and reported within the debounce window

acceptance_criteria.given:
The sessions directory contains large volumes of content data
alongside session metadata files
acceptance_criteria.when: File monitoring starts for the sessions directory
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only session metadata and event files are monitored; content
storage directories are excluded from monitoring

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project's sessions directory has thousands of sessions with
accumulated content data
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon process resource usage is measured
acceptance_criteria.then: File descriptor count is proportional to the number of active sessions and monitored spec directories

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any supported platform
acceptance_criteria.then:
File changes are detected reliably regardless of the
operating system's native filesystem event mechanism

acceptance_criteria.given:
A monitored file is modified through an atomic write operation
(write to temporary file, then rename)
acceptance_criteria.when: The monitoring system processes the filesystem event
acceptance_criteria.then:
The change is detected and reported as a modification to the
target path

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple projects are registered with the daemon
acceptance_criteria.when: A file changes in one project's monitored directory
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only that project's change handler is invoked; no cross-project
event delivery occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: A new session directory for a session with active status is created after monitoring started
acceptance_criteria.when: Metadata files are written into the new session directory
acceptance_criteria.then: The new session's metadata changes are detected without requiring a monitoring restart

acceptance_criteria.given:
The monitoring system encounters a persistent error for a
project directory
acceptance_criteria.then:
The project is unregistered and resources are released, with
a logged error identifying the affected project

acceptance_criteria.given: The sessions directory contains both active and non-active sessions (completed, abandoned, failed, timed_out, or stalled)
acceptance_criteria.when: File monitoring is running for the sessions directory
acceptance_criteria.then: Only sessions with active status are individually watched for metadata and event changes

acceptance_criteria.given: A watched session transitions from active to any non-active status (completed, abandoned, failed, timed_out, or stalled)
acceptance_criteria.when: The status change is detected by the watcher
acceptance_criteria.then: The per-session watch is removed and its file descriptors are released

acceptance_criteria.given: A new session directory appears in the sessions directory
acceptance_criteria.when: The top-level directory watcher detects the new entry
acceptance_criteria.then: The new session's metadata is checked and a per-session watch is added only if the session has active status

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon starts with existing sessions in the sessions directory
acceptance_criteria.then: Only sessions with active status at startup time are watched

acceptance_criteria.given: A new session directory appears in the sessions directory with any status (active or non-active — completed, abandoned, failed, timed_out, stalled)
acceptance_criteria.when: The top-level directory watcher detects the new entry and its session.yaml becomes readable
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one session-change notification is emitted so consumers (entity cache, WebSocket broadcast) can refresh the session list, regardless of whether a per-session watcher is attached

inherited_acs.then: includes description of what went wrong
includes suggested action to resolve
suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
indicates current state and valid next states
indicates which field/value failed validation
guidance included in structured error object

items.title: Watcher Health Verification
items.description:
Provides runtime verification that file monitoring is actively
delivering events, not just that a watcher object exists. Silent
watcher failures — where the watcher reports as active but stops
delivering events — are detected and recovered from automatically.

acceptance_criteria.given: File monitoring is active for a project
acceptance_criteria.then:
The daemon verifies that the monitoring system can detect
a synthetic file change within the expected debounce window

acceptance_criteria.given:
The health check detects that a synthetic change was not
reported within the expected window
acceptance_criteria.then:
The monitoring system is restarted for the affected project
and the incident is logged with the project path and failure
duration

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple projects are registered
acceptance_criteria.when: One project's watcher health check fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only that project's monitoring is restarted; other projects
are unaffected

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon's cache diagnostic endpoint is queried
acceptance_criteria.then:
The response includes the last successful health check
timestamp and consecutive failure count per project

items.title: Incremental Entity Cache Updates
items.description:
Cache invalidation updates only the entities affected by a change
rather than reloading entire data domains. When the system knows
which file changed, it uses that information to patch the cached
index and detail data in place. Full domain reloads remain as a
fallback when the changed file cannot be mapped to specific
entities or when callers (such as write-through) do not provide
file-level context.

acceptance_criteria.given: The file watcher detects a change to a file in the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
The file path of the changed file is available to the cache
update logic, not just the domain name

acceptance_criteria.given: A file change maps to a single identifiable entity within a domain
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only that entity is reloaded from disk and its index and detail
entries are replaced without reloading other entities in the domain

acceptance_criteria.given: A file change maps to a file containing multiple entities
acceptance_criteria.then:
The entire file is re-parsed and all entities from that file are
replaced in the index and detail tiers

acceptance_criteria.given: A file change cannot be mapped to specific entities within a domain
acceptance_criteria.then:
The entire domain is reloaded from disk, matching the current
full-reload behavior

acceptance_criteria.given: A previously cached entity's source file is deleted
acceptance_criteria.when: The cache processes the file removal event
acceptance_criteria.then: The entity is removed from both the index and detail tiers

acceptance_criteria.given: An incremental update replaces or removes an entity
acceptance_criteria.when: Concurrent API requests read from the same domain
acceptance_criteria.then:
Readers see either the complete pre-update state or the complete
post-update state for the affected entity, never a partial mix

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple files change within the debounce window
acceptance_criteria.then:
All changed files are processed in a single update pass rather
than triggering separate reloads per file

acceptance_criteria.given: The file watcher reads and validates a changed file's content
acceptance_criteria.when: The change event reaches the cache
acceptance_criteria.then:
The already-read content is available to the cache update logic
so the file does not need to be read from disk a second time

items.title: Configurable Daemon Runtime
items.description: The daemon supports running on multiple JavaScript runtimes. The runtime is selected at startup via configuration, with node as the default. When running on an alternative runtime, the server uses a runtime adapter for HTTP and WebSocket handling. Features that depend on runtime-specific APIs degrade gracefully when unavailable rather than crashing.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has configured a daemon runtime preference
acceptance_criteria.then: The daemon spawns using the configured runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: No runtime preference is configured
acceptance_criteria.then: By default the daemon spawns using node

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any configured runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: HTTP API requests arrive, including SPA fallback routes
acceptance_criteria.then: All routes serve correctly regardless of runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any configured runtime
acceptance_criteria.then:
The client receives connection events, topic subscriptions,
and broadcast messages regardless of runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any supported runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: A WebSocket client connects and interacts with the server
acceptance_criteria.then:
Per-connection state (session ID, subscribed topics, sequence
number, heartbeat timestamps, project path) is tracked and
accessible throughout the connection lifecycle

acceptance_criteria.given:
The daemon is running on a runtime where frame-level WebSocket
ping is unavailable
acceptance_criteria.then:
The connection remains open without heartbeat enforcement and
a warning is logged at startup indicating degraded heartbeat

acceptance_criteria.given:
The daemon is running on a runtime where buffered amount
queries are unavailable
acceptance_criteria.when: The server broadcasts to WebSocket clients
acceptance_criteria.then:
Broadcasts proceed without backpressure checks rather than
failing

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any supported runtime
acceptance_criteria.then: The response includes which runtime the daemon is using

acceptance_criteria.given: The daemon is running on any supported runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: A shutdown signal is received or stop is requested
acceptance_criteria.then:
The daemon shuts down cleanly, closing connections and
removing the PID file

acceptance_criteria.given: Auto-start is enabled and a runtime preference is configured
acceptance_criteria.when: The daemon auto-starts in the background
acceptance_criteria.then: The auto-started daemon uses the configured runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: The configured runtime is not installed on the system
acceptance_criteria.then:
A clear error message names the missing runtime and provides
installation guidance

acceptance_criteria.given: kspec.config.yaml contains daemon.runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: config is loaded before daemon startup
acceptance_criteria.then: the runtime preference is available as the resolved daemon runtime used by serve start and daemon auto-start

items.title: Daemon Test Runtime Selection
items.description:
Daemon tests exercise the same runtime defaults and runtime-selection
behavior promised by the daemon runtime adapter. Generic daemon tests run
against Node by default. Runtime-specific or parity tests opt into a
runtime matrix explicitly and treat Bun as optional unless the test is
specifically validating a configured Bun environment.

acceptance_criteria.given: A daemon-backed test does not opt into a specific runtime
acceptance_criteria.when: The shared daemon fixture starts the daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: The daemon starts with Node

acceptance_criteria.given: A test starts the daemon with Bun
acceptance_criteria.when: The test is authored or modified
acceptance_criteria.then: The test declares that Bun runtime behavior is part of its subject

acceptance_criteria.given: A test claims HTTP or WebSocket parity across daemon runtimes
acceptance_criteria.when: The parity suite runs on a machine with the configured runtimes
acceptance_criteria.then: The same daemon behavior is exercised for each available runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: A parity test includes an optional runtime that is not installed
acceptance_criteria.then: The missing optional runtime is reported as a skipped runtime case

acceptance_criteria.given:
A runtime lacks a daemon capability such as frame-level WebSocket
heartbeat support
acceptance_criteria.then: The test asserts the documented degraded behavior for that runtime

items.title: Breadcrumb Navigation
items.description:
Entity views present a breadcrumb trail showing the hierarchy path
from the root to the current entity. The trail adapts to the number
of path segments and the available width by collapsing middle
segments into a single collapse indicator; collapsed segments stay
reachable through a popover that lists them in hierarchy order.
Each segment carries an indicator of its item kind, the current
segment is visually emphasized, and the full path's titles and
kinds are resolved server-side in one bounded request.

acceptance_criteria.given:
an entity whose breadcrumb path — root through current entity —
contains 4 or fewer segments
acceptance_criteria.when: the breadcrumb renders with sufficient width for all segments
acceptance_criteria.then:
every segment renders in hierarchy order and no collapse
indicator appears

acceptance_criteria.given: a breadcrumb path containing 5 or 6 segments
acceptance_criteria.then:
exactly the root segment, one collapse indicator, the two
ancestor segments nearest the current entity, and the current
segment render in hierarchy order, with the remaining segments
collapsed into the indicator

acceptance_criteria.given: a breadcrumb path containing 7 or more segments
acceptance_criteria.then:
exactly the root segment, one collapse indicator, the single
ancestor segment nearest the current entity, and the current
segment render in hierarchy order, with the remaining segments
collapsed into the indicator

acceptance_criteria.given:
a breadcrumb whose truncated form still exceeds the available
width
acceptance_criteria.then:
visible ancestor segments, including the root, collapse into
the indicator until the trail fits, and the current segment
always remains visible

acceptance_criteria.given: a breadcrumb showing a collapse indicator
acceptance_criteria.then:
a popover lists every collapsed segment in hierarchy order,
and activating a listed segment navigates to that entity

acceptance_criteria.given: the collapsed-segment popover is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user presses the up or down arrow key, Enter, or Escape
acceptance_criteria.then:
arrow keys move the selection through the listed segments,
Enter navigates to the selected segment, and Escape closes the
popover without navigating

acceptance_criteria.given:
a pointing device without hover capability or keyboard-only
input
acceptance_criteria.when: the collapse indicator is activated by tap, click, or keyboard
acceptance_criteria.then: the popover opens; opening never requires hover

acceptance_criteria.given: a breadcrumb with a collapse indicator
acceptance_criteria.then:
the breadcrumb's visible segments and the surrounding page
content do not shift position

acceptance_criteria.given:
a breadcrumb path whose segments reference spec items of
differing kinds
acceptance_criteria.then:
each segment, including segments listed inside the popover,
carries the indicator for its item kind, and the current
segment is visually emphasized relative to ancestor segments

acceptance_criteria.given: a breadcrumb is built for any entity
acceptance_criteria.then:
the titles and kinds for the entire chain come from
server-resolved data in a single bounded request, and the
client issues no unbounded entity-list request to construct
the trail

items.title: Standard View Header
items.description:
Entity views share a single header pattern: the entity reference,
a lifecycle or state indicator drawn from a shared status-token
vocabulary, counts of the entity's children where applicable, and
a zone for view-specific actions, arranged identically across
views. The header's leading chrome zone stays empty. Each entity
state is represented by exactly one visual token wherever it
appears. Detail views adopt the header as their surfaces are
redesigned: the review detail and session detail views are the
first adopters, and every other entity detail view adopts it
through the track plan that redesigns that surface.

acceptance_criteria.given: an entity detail view that presents the standard header
acceptance_criteria.then:
the header presents the entity reference, a lifecycle or state
indicator, child counts where the entity has countable
children, and a view-actions zone, in the arrangement shared
by all adopting views

acceptance_criteria.given: the same entity state presented in two different views
acceptance_criteria.when: each view renders its state indicator
acceptance_criteria.then:
one shared status token — the same color and glyph —
represents that state in both places

acceptance_criteria.given: a view header laid out at any viewport width
acceptance_criteria.then: the leading chrome zone contains no header element

acceptance_criteria.given: an entity with countable children
acceptance_criteria.then:
the counts derive from server-resolved fields or server-side
aggregation, not from client-side enumeration of full entity
lists

acceptance_criteria.given: a view that contributes actions to its header
acceptance_criteria.then:
the actions appear only within the designated actions zone and
each action is operable by keyboard

acceptance_criteria.given: the review detail and session detail views
acceptance_criteria.then:
each presents the standard view header in place of a bespoke
header

items.title: Keyboard Shortcut Registry
items.description:
All interface keyboard shortcuts are declared through one central
registry that resolves each shortcut's chord per platform,
detects binding collisions at registration, refuses
browser-reserved combinations, and falls back to a shortcut's
declared alternate chords when the preferred chord cannot be
bound. Each shortcut is declared with an activation context — a
global context or a surface-scoped context that is active only
while its owning surface is active — a binding is active only
while its context is active, and collision detection applies
among the bindings of the same context. The registry's inventory
of active bindings is enumerable with display labels matching the
active platform.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a shortcut registered through the registry and active in the
current context
acceptance_criteria.then: the bound action fires exactly once

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of registered shortcuts active in the current context
acceptance_criteria.then:
every active binding is enumerated with its display label and
the chord resolved for the active platform

acceptance_criteria.given: a shortcut declared with a platform-abstract primary modifier
acceptance_criteria.when: its binding resolves on each supported platform
acceptance_criteria.then:
the platform's conventional primary modifier is used, and the
displayed label matches the binding that is actually active

acceptance_criteria.given:
a registration that resolves to a chord already bound in the
same context
acceptance_criteria.then:
the registration is rejected with a reported collision and the
existing binding remains the only binding for that chord

acceptance_criteria.given:
a registration whose preferred chord is on the active
platform's browser-reserved combination list
acceptance_criteria.then:
the preferred chord is not bound; the shortcut's first
declared fallback chord that is neither reserved nor colliding
is bound instead, and a shortcut with no resolvable fallback
is reported as unbound rather than silently dropped

acceptance_criteria.given: keyboard focus inside a text-entry control
acceptance_criteria.when: a chord without the platform's primary modifier is pressed
acceptance_criteria.then:
no registry action fires and the keystroke reaches the
text-entry control

items.title: Persisted Preference Utility
items.description:
Interface preferences persist through one shared utility. Each
preference is declared with a namespace, a key, a value type with
validation, a schema version with an upgrade rule, and a default.
The utility's interface is storage-agnostic; the default backend
is browser-local storage, and the utility degrades to
session-scoped in-memory behavior when persistent storage is
unavailable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a preference value written through the utility
acceptance_criteria.when: the interface reloads in the same browser
acceptance_criteria.then: reading the preference returns the stored value

acceptance_criteria.given:
two preferences registered under different namespaces with the
same key name
acceptance_criteria.when: both are written and read back
acceptance_criteria.then: each returns its own value and neither overwrites the other

acceptance_criteria.given:
a stored preference value whose schema version is older than
the preference's current declared version
acceptance_criteria.then:
the result is the value produced by the preference's declared
upgrade rule, or the declared default when no rule applies —
never the unmigrated stored shape

acceptance_criteria.given:
a stored value that fails the preference's declared type
validation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the declared default is returned and the invalid value does
not propagate to the consumer

acceptance_criteria.given:
an alternative storage backend provided behind the utility's
interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
the observable read and write semantics are unchanged and
consumers never access the backing store directly

acceptance_criteria.given:
persistent browser storage is unavailable or a write to it
fails
acceptance_criteria.then:
the utility operates in session-scoped in-memory mode and the
interface remains functional

items.title: Actor Identity Resolution
items.description:
The system exposes its identity configuration — the configured
human identity and the canonical agent roster — through a single
identity surface, and classifies recorded actor strings to
canonical identities. Classification resolves recognizable
variants of agent identifiers and of the human identity to their
canonical form; strings that resolve to neither classify as
unknown without failing. Records written through any first-party
write interface resolve their actor fields through one shared
author/actor utility rather than route-local fallbacks or anonymous
placeholders, and persisted actor values are canonical:
caller-supplied or precedence-resolved values that classify as a
configured human or agent identity are stored in canonical form,
while values that classify to no configured identity are rejected
on new writes. Unknown classification remains a read-side result
for historical or externally edited records, not a way to persist
arbitrary new authors.

acceptance_criteria.given: a running daemon with a configured project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response contains the configured human identity with its
display name and the canonical agent roster — each agent's
canonical identifier and display information — in a single
bounded response

acceptance_criteria.given:
a recorded actor string that is a recognizable variant of a
canonical agent identifier
acceptance_criteria.then:
it resolves to that agent's canonical identity with actor
kind agent

acceptance_criteria.given:
a recorded actor string matching the configured human identity
or a recognizable variant of it
acceptance_criteria.then: it resolves to the human identity with actor kind human

acceptance_criteria.given:
a recorded actor string that resolves to no canonical agent
and not to the human identity
acceptance_criteria.then:
classification yields an unknown-kind result that preserves
the original string, and no operation fails because of it

acceptance_criteria.given: the same actor string and the same identity configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is identical

acceptance_criteria.given:
a review mutation arriving through the daemon without an
explicit actor value
acceptance_criteria.then:
the recorded author resolves through the configured author
precedence and is never recorded as an anonymous placeholder

acceptance_criteria.given:
an actor value about to be persisted by any first-party record
write — supplied explicitly by the caller or resolved through
the author-resolution precedence — that classifies as a
recognizable variant of a canonical agent identity or of the
configured human identity
acceptance_criteria.then:
the stored actor value is the canonical identity, never the
variant form

acceptance_criteria.given:
an actor value about to be persisted by any first-party record
write that classifies to no configured human or agent identity
acceptance_criteria.then:
the write is rejected with validation feedback, and no new
free-form actor value is persisted

inherited_acs.then: returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing

items.title: Actor Display and Next-Actor Derivation
items.description:
A single display primitive renders any recorded actor: the
canonical display name with a visual distinction between human and
agent kinds, and an honest distinct treatment for unknown actors.
A deterministic next-actor rule derives, from a review's lifecycle
state and disposition, which role the review awaits — the
reviewing party, the author of the work under review, or no one —
and every surface presenting whom a review awaits resolves the
awaited party by applying that one rule to the review's recorded
participants.

acceptance_criteria.given: any surface presenting a recorded actor
acceptance_criteria.then:
the actor's canonical display name renders with a visual
distinction between human and agent kinds, and the same actor
renders identically across surfaces

acceptance_criteria.given: an actor classified as unknown
acceptance_criteria.then:
the original recorded string is displayed with a distinct
unknown treatment and is never presented as a canonical
identity

acceptance_criteria.given: a review's lifecycle state and disposition
acceptance_criteria.when: the review's awaited role is derived
acceptance_criteria.then:
the result follows the fixed mapping — an open review with
pending disposition awaits the reviewer role; an open review
with changes-requested disposition awaits the work-author
role; an open review with approved disposition awaits the
work-author role for post-approval action; a closed or
archived review awaits no role

acceptance_criteria.given: two surfaces presenting whom the same review awaits
acceptance_criteria.when:
each derives the awaited party from that review's lifecycle
state, disposition, and recorded participants
acceptance_criteria.then: both surfaces present the same result

items.title: Historical Actor Normalization
items.description:
A one-time step of the project data upgrade path rewrites
historical actor fields to canonical identities. The step is driven
by an exhaustive actor-field inventory so every actor-bearing
storage path is either normalized or explicitly documented as
non-actor/out of scope. A declared variant map resolves recognizable
historical actor strings; operator-supplied mappings can resolve
additional historical values, and values no rule resolves are
replaced with the declared unknown or default actor for their
record kind. The step reports every rewrite and every unresolved
original, supports a preview mode that modifies nothing, and is
idempotent.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a project whose historical records contain recognizable actor
variants
acceptance_criteria.then:
those actor fields are rewritten to the corresponding
canonical identities according to the declared variant map

acceptance_criteria.given:
an actor value that no variant rule or operator-supplied mapping
resolves
acceptance_criteria.then:
the value is replaced with the declared unknown or default actor
for its record kind, and the original value appears in the
step's report

acceptance_criteria.given: the upgrade step has already run to completion on a project
acceptance_criteria.then: no record changes

acceptance_criteria.given: the upgrade is invoked in preview mode
acceptance_criteria.when: the step evaluates the project's records
acceptance_criteria.then:
it reports the rewrites it would perform and modifies no
record

acceptance_criteria.given: the upgrade step completes
acceptance_criteria.when: actor fields across the project's record kinds are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then:
every inventoried actor field value is a canonical identity or
a declared default

acceptance_criteria.given:
the upgrade implementation is checked against the project's
actor-bearing schemas, API types, and stored record shapes
acceptance_criteria.then:
the field appears in the migration inventory with its record
kind, storage path, owning schema/type, and normalization
disposition, or it is explicitly documented as not representing
a human or agent actor identity

items.title: Unified Spec Workspace Data Projection
items.description:
The spec workspace reads one backend-owned workspace projection instead
of reconstructing page hierarchy, breadcrumb paths, linked work, corpus
counts, or coverage rollups from unbounded client-side entity lists. The
projection exposes the root workspace, node detail, child-row summaries,
acceptance-criterion detail, coverage-state summaries, and lightweight
linked-work counts through bounded daemon/static API contracts. It uses
the canonical four user-facing presentation buckets from the
coverage-state engine — covered, failing, not yet, and re-verify — while
preserving transport enum values and secondary re-verify causes for API
payloads, captions, and resolution panels.

acceptance_criteria.given: a web client opens the root Specs workspace
acceptance_criteria.then:
the daemon returns corpus counts, project coverage summary, top-level
visible nodes, and per-node child/coverage/linked-work counts in one
bounded envelope; the client does not fetch every item and compute
derived workspace statistics locally

acceptance_criteria.given:
a client opens any module, feature, requirement, trait, constraint, or
other supported spec item node
acceptance_criteria.when: it requests the node's workspace detail
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response includes the node header fields, server-resolved
breadcrumb ancestors, ordered child sections, acceptance criteria when
present, coverage rollups, linked-work counts, and enough pagination
or continuation metadata to avoid unbounded child expansion

acceptance_criteria.given: a client opens an acceptance criterion as a focused workspace page
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response includes the parent item chain, criterion G/W/T text,
computed coverage state, coverage evidence summaries, sibling
criterion summaries, linked tasks/sessions/plans where available, and
any current re-verify explanation without requiring the client to join
raw coverage, task, session, and spec lists

acceptance_criteria.given:
the workspace displays state pills, bars, banners, counts, filters, or
resolution affordances
acceptance_criteria.then:
every displayed coverage value comes from the backend
coverage-state read model and maps API enum values onto the same
user-facing covered, failing, not yet, and re-verify vocabulary, with
secondary causes used only as details and never as a separate
client-computed state model

acceptance_criteria.given: a client requests any workspace projection endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when:
the request succeeds, names a missing ref, includes invalid query
input, or is processed for tracing
acceptance_criteria.then:
responses follow the existing daemon API contract: successful reads
return 2xx JSON envelopes, missing refs return 404 bodies with error,
message, and suggestion, validation errors identify fields, paginated
projections expose limit/offset/total metadata where pagination is
supported, and responses carry the request tracing header required by
the API endpoint trait

acceptance_criteria.given: workspace projection endpoints are read endpoints
acceptance_criteria.when:
they serve root, node, criterion, linked-work, or coverage projection
data
acceptance_criteria.then:
they do not mutate project state or create shadow commits; the
mutation-specific API endpoint trait criterion applies only to the
existing resolution mutation endpoints consumed by this workspace

acceptance_criteria.given:
a workspace projection request fails because a ref, criterion, query
field, snapshot section, or coverage projection cannot be resolved
acceptance_criteria.when: the error is returned to CLI, daemon, JSON, or web UI consumers
acceptance_criteria.then:
the response describes what failed, identifies the failed field or
value when applicable, and includes recovery guidance such as checking
refs, refreshing the workspace, or using an available read-only/static
path

acceptance_criteria.given:
any workspace page displays linked tasks, sessions, plans, reviews, or
observations for a spec node or criterion
acceptance_criteria.then:
each link class has a documented inclusion rule, returns server-
resolved titles/statuses/ages, and omits or degrades unavailable
classes explicitly instead of letting the client infer relationships
from raw entity scans

acceptance_criteria.given: the web UI runs from a static export or other read-only context
acceptance_criteria.then:
read projections render from the static snapshot when present,
unavailable dynamic evidence or linked-work classes are labeled as
unavailable, and mutation affordances are disabled or replaced with
read-only guidance rather than pretending writes can occur

acceptance_criteria.given:
spec items, tasks, sessions, test-run ingestion, verification stamps,
or coverage resolution mutations change workspace-visible data
acceptance_criteria.when: the daemon broadcasts existing item/task/session/coverage events
acceptance_criteria.then:
workspace query keys are invalidated at the narrowest practical scope
and the UI refreshes without polling or recomputing stale derived state
locally

acceptance_criteria.given:
the workspace cannot resolve a node, criterion, child page, coverage
projection, or linked-work class
acceptance_criteria.then:
it shows a scoped empty/error state with actionable guidance and keeps
the rest of the workspace usable

inherited_acs.then: returns 2xx status with JSON body
returns 404 with {error, message, suggestion} including similar refs if available
returns 400 with {error, details:[{field, message}]} array
accepts limit and offset query params, response includes the total count of matching items and the pagination parameters applied
shadow commit occurs with semantic message
includes X-Request-Id header for tracing
includes description of what went wrong
includes suggested action to resolve
suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
indicates current state and valid next states
indicates which field/value failed validation
guidance included in structured error object

items.title: Unified Spec Workspace Navigation
items.description:
The `/specs` surface becomes a unified page+tree workspace. Every spec
node can be expanded inline to inspect children in context, and every node
including an acceptance criterion can be opened as a focused page with a
stable URL. Row body activation expands; title/open activation navigates.
Navigation uses SvelteKit `goto()` and reactive URL state, preserves
expansion context across browser back/forward, and works without hover.

acceptance_criteria.given: any spec item or acceptance criterion shown in the workspace
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens it as a page
acceptance_criteria.then:
the browser URL identifies that node or criterion directly, can be
copied and reloaded, and restores the same focused workspace page

acceptance_criteria.given:
an existing link points to `/specs?ref=<ref>` or a ReferenceLink uses
the current spec route convention
acceptance_criteria.when: the redesigned workspace handles the URL
acceptance_criteria.then:
it opens the matching node in the new workspace instead of regressing
existing deep links

acceptance_criteria.given: a workspace row with children
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates the row body
acceptance_criteria.then:
the row expands or collapses inline without navigating; activating the
title, explicit open affordance, or keyboard open command navigates to
the node page

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has no hover-capable pointer or uses keyboard-only input
acceptance_criteria.then:
both expand/collapse and open-page actions are visible or otherwise
reachable with named controls and accessible labels

acceptance_criteria.given: the user expands several branches and then opens a node page
acceptance_criteria.when: they return via browser back or workspace navigation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the previously expanded branches remain expanded, subject only to
bounded-data eviction that is explicitly indicated to the user

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple independent branches exist in the spec tree
acceptance_criteria.when: the user expands more than one branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
each branch remains open independently; expanding one branch does not
collapse unrelated branches

acceptance_criteria.given: a node page renders its child sections
acceptance_criteria.then:
they use the same row component, coverage tokens, expand behavior, and
open-page affordances as the root tree

acceptance_criteria.given:
deeply nested paths, long titles, tags, or coverage summaries appear
in the workspace
acceptance_criteria.when: the viewport is at supported desktop and mobile widths
acceptance_criteria.then:
content wraps, truncates, collapses, or stacks without introducing
page-level horizontal scrolling

items.title: Spec Node and Criterion Workspace Pages
items.description:
The workspace presents first-class pages for the root, every spec item
node, and every acceptance criterion. Pages share breadcrumb and header
primitives, show children in typed sections, keep linked work near the
spec content, and render acceptance criteria as readable scenarios rather
than hidden sheet accordions. This plan is a read/navigation plan: spec
editing, add-AC flows, and broad spec CRUD are intentionally out of scope
unless a later approved plan designs them.

acceptance_criteria.given: the user opens `/specs` with no focused node
acceptance_criteria.then:
it shows the root Specs page with corpus counts, project coverage
summary, top-level rows, and no fake breadcrumb segment

acceptance_criteria.given:
