the user opens a module, feature, requirement, trait, or constraint
page
acceptance_criteria.then:
it shows the shared view header, breadcrumb, description, tags/traits
where applicable, child sections appropriate to the node kind, and a
linked-work strip or unavailable-state placeholder

acceptance_criteria.given: a requirement has acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria.then:
criteria appear as state-aware rows with AC ids, concise summaries,
expandable G/W/T bodies, linked evidence indicators, and open-page
affordances for each criterion

acceptance_criteria.given: the user opens a criterion page
acceptance_criteria.then:
the page shows the criterion scenario, parent requirement context,
current coverage state and explanation, evidence summaries, siblings,
and links back to related task/session/plan context

acceptance_criteria.given: linked work exists for a node or criterion
acceptance_criteria.when: the workspace page renders its linked-work area
acceptance_criteria.then:
counts and entries are grouped by entity class, use ReferenceLink or
equivalent stable navigation, and do not require opening a side sheet
to discover implementation context

acceptance_criteria.given:
a node has no children, no acceptance criteria, no linked work, or a
projection omits an unavailable class
acceptance_criteria.then:
the section is omitted or displays a concise empty/unavailable state;
blank panels and misleading zeroes are avoided

acceptance_criteria.given:
a user looks for editing actions such as add criterion, edit node
text, reorder specs, or create child item
acceptance_criteria.when: those actions are not designed by this plan
acceptance_criteria.then:
the workspace does not expose partial CRUD controls; any mention of
editing directs to later planning or existing CLI workflows

items.title: Spec Workspace Coverage State Presentation
items.description:
The spec workspace is the first major UI consumer of the completed
coverage-state engine. It presents coverage rollups, state pills, filters,
re-verify banners, and evidence captions using one shared token and label
system for the four API-facing presentation buckets. It never falls back to
the legacy boolean AC `covered` scan when state data is available.

acceptance_criteria.given: any coverage bucket is rendered in the spec workspace
acceptance_criteria.when:
the token is displayed in a row, header, rollup bar, filter chip,
banner, or criterion page
acceptance_criteria.then:
covered, failing, not yet, and re-verify each use one consistent
label/color/icon token, and backend secondary re-verify causes such as
stale_spec_text, stale_annotation_or_mapping, stale_test_result, or
unknown_freshness are translated into secondary explanation text under
re-verify instead of top-level UI states

acceptance_criteria.given:
a node or root projection includes coverage bucket counts and a
denominator
acceptance_criteria.when: the workspace renders its header or row summary
acceptance_criteria.then:
it shows a segmented rollup or compact equivalent whose counts match
the backend projection and whose denominator rules match the coverage
state engine

acceptance_criteria.given: a requirement page has criteria in more than one presentation bucket
acceptance_criteria.then:
each filter chip shows backend counts, filtering changes only the
visible criteria for that page, and a reset/all filter restores the
original ordered list without refetching raw unrelated entities

acceptance_criteria.given: a node or requirement projection has one or more re-verify criteria
acceptance_criteria.then:
a scoped re-verify banner summarizes the count and cause classes and
links to the Validate surface filtered to the same node or criterion
when that filtered destination exists

acceptance_criteria.given: a page or list contains failing and re-verify criteria
acceptance_criteria.then:
failing evidence is visually and semantically prioritized over
re-verify, and not-yet remains visually distinct from work that needs
immediate re-validation or repair

acceptance_criteria.given: the backend coverage-state projection is ready for a project
acceptance_criteria.then:
it uses the projection's presentation bucket and explanation instead
of the legacy acceptance-criterion boolean `covered` field or a fresh
client annotation scan

acceptance_criteria.given:
the coverage-state domain is warming, degraded, or unavailable in a
static snapshot
acceptance_criteria.then:
it shows warming, retry, or unavailable indicators scoped to coverage
state while preserving non-coverage spec navigation

items.title: Spec Workspace Coverage Resolution Panels
items.description:
Criterion pages and inline re-verify contexts expose coverage resolution
actions only when the current backend state says they are applicable. The
UI previews and applies the existing resolution mutations — explicit
re-verification, spec-text revert, and dispatch-fix request — without
inventing a separate mutation path, test runner, or workspace-specific
task creation flow.

acceptance_criteria.given:
a criterion is not currently in a state that supports a resolution
action
acceptance_criteria.when: the workspace renders its criterion page or inline panel
acceptance_criteria.then:
resolution controls are hidden or disabled with explanatory guidance
instead of allowing a doomed mutation attempt

acceptance_criteria.given: the user activates any resolution action from the workspace
acceptance_criteria.then:
the UI obtains and displays the existing dry-run preview before final
confirmation, including expected stored effects and affected coverage
scopes

acceptance_criteria.given: a criterion satisfies explicit re-verification preconditions
acceptance_criteria.then:
the UI calls the shared coverage resolution endpoint, records no local
fake state, and refreshes from the coverage-state event or mutation
response

acceptance_criteria.given: a criterion has a stale spec-text cause with a current revert preview
acceptance_criteria.then:
the UI submits the shared spec-text revert request with the expected
current fingerprint and handles stale-target conflicts by refreshing
and explaining that the criterion changed

acceptance_criteria.given: a criterion needs code or test repair
acceptance_criteria.then:
the UI submits the shared dispatch-fix request and presents the
resulting task reference/status without spawning agents or composing
task records in client code

acceptance_criteria.given: the workspace is running in static or read-only mode
acceptance_criteria.when: a resolution panel would otherwise render actions
acceptance_criteria.then:
it presents the current state and disables mutations with read-only
guidance; it does not offer confirmations that cannot be stored

acceptance_criteria.given:
a resolution action succeeds through the workspace, CLI, or another
daemon consumer
acceptance_criteria.then:
the affected workspace pages, filters, rollups, and criterion panels
invalidate and refresh consistently

items.title: Spec Workspace Delivery Quality
items.description:
The workspace ships as a production-quality SvelteKit surface that follows
existing web UI conventions: Svelte 5 runes, TanStack query keys,
centralized WebSocket invalidation, static-export degradation, URL changes
through `goto()`, component-level tests for stateful behavior, and browser
proof for the vertical workflow. It must replace the current tree + sheet
experience without leaving a preview-only half surface.

acceptance_criteria.given: workspace route, component, store, and API-client code is added
acceptance_criteria.then:
it uses existing Svelte 5, TanStack query wrapper, query-key factory,
api/api-static split, and design-system conventions rather than
introducing parallel data or style frameworks

acceptance_criteria.given:
workspace interactions change focused node, criterion, filter, or
expansion state represented in the URL
acceptance_criteria.then:
it uses SvelteKit `goto()` or link navigation so `$page.url` stays
reactive; direct history mutation is not used

acceptance_criteria.given: the web UI is built for static export
acceptance_criteria.when: the workspace route is included in the export
acceptance_criteria.then:
it renders read-only data from the snapshot when available, avoids
daemon-only write attempts, and keeps existing static docs/spec links
valid

acceptance_criteria.given: a user navigates the workspace with keyboard or assistive technology
acceptance_criteria.when:
they move through rows, breadcrumbs, filters, banners, and resolution
panels
acceptance_criteria.then:
focus order, names, expanded states, selected states, and action
labels are perceivable and operable without hover

acceptance_criteria.given: the implementation is ready for review
acceptance_criteria.when: it is verified in a browser against a live daemon project
acceptance_criteria.then:
the proof covers root tree navigation, opening a node page, opening an
AC page, filtering by state, following linked work, static/read-only or
disabled mutation behavior, and no horizontal-scroll regression

acceptance_criteria.given: the workspace implementation lands
acceptance_criteria.then:
focused tests cover route URL restoration, dual-gesture row behavior,
projection API client/static fallback, coverage event invalidation,
resolution preview/apply flows, and accessibility-critical keyboard
interactions

acceptance_criteria.given: the new workspace is complete enough to ship
acceptance_criteria.then:
users see the unified workspace as the primary surface, and the old
sheet-only detail experience is removed, reused only as internal code
where still appropriate, or explicitly redirected

items.title: Browser E2E Daemon Fixture Integration
items.description: Playwright tests that need daemon-backed browser behavior use the shared daemon test fixture through a Playwright wrapper. Browser URLs, API calls, isolated HOME/config state, dynamic ports, readiness, and teardown are supplied by the same daemon fixture contract used by Vitest daemon-backed tests.

acceptance_criteria.given: a Playwright test needs a daemon for API or browser testing
acceptance_criteria.when: the Playwright fixture starts a daemon
acceptance_criteria.then: startup flows through the shared daemon test fixture

acceptance_criteria.given: the Playwright daemon fixture reports an endpoint
acceptance_criteria.when: browser pages navigate or make daemon API calls
acceptance_criteria.then: the browser uses the endpoint supplied by the fixture

acceptance_criteria.given: Playwright tests start a daemon in a temp project
acceptance_criteria.when: the fixture creates the daemon environment
acceptance_criteria.then: HOME and daemon config paths are isolated from the ambient system

acceptance_criteria.given: a Playwright test daemon has started
acceptance_criteria.then: teardown stops only the fixture-owned daemon

acceptance_criteria.given: the Playwright daemon listens on a dynamic port
acceptance_criteria.when: Playwright tests make API calls or navigate browser pages
acceptance_criteria.then: the port is propagated through the daemon fixture context

items.title: URL-Driven Detail Panel State Management
items.description: All detail panels/modals that sync state with URL query parameters must use goto() from $app/navigation for URL mutations (not replaceState, pushState, or window.history). This ensures $page.url updates reactively and prevents stale-URL effect loops where panels reopen after dismissal.

acceptance_criteria.given: a detail panel or modal is opened by setting a URL query parameter (e.g. ?ref=)
acceptance_criteria.then: goto(url, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true }) is used instead of replaceState, pushState, or window.history methods, ensuring $page.url updates reactively

acceptance_criteria.given: a detail panel or modal is dismissed (click outside, ESC, close button)
acceptance_criteria.then: the URL query parameter is removed via goto() and the reactive effect that watches $page.url.searchParams does not reopen the panel because $page.url reflects the updated URL

acceptance_criteria.given: a user navigates to a page with ?ref= in the URL (e.g. from a cross-page link)
acceptance_criteria.when: the page loads and the detail panel opens
acceptance_criteria.then: dismissing the panel works correctly on the first attempt and the panel stays closed

acceptance_criteria.given: a page uses URL query parameters for filter state (status, tag, plan)
acceptance_criteria.then: goto() is used for URL mutations so $page.url stays in sync with the browser URL bar

items.title: Review Records Web UI
items.description: SvelteKit pages for viewing and interacting with review records in the browser. The primary interface for humans to see agent review activity and participate in reviews. Routes: /reviews for list, /reviews/[id] for detail. Reviews on the same subject are treated as review passes with a dropdown selector to navigate between them.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user navigates to /reviews
acceptance_criteria.then:
A list view shows reviews with lifecycle status, disposition badge,
subject type, reviewer, and linked task, with filtering by status,
disposition, and subject type, and sortable columns; defaults to
showing open reviews

acceptance_criteria.given: A user opens /reviews/[id]
acceptance_criteria.when: The review has threads, checks, and verdicts
acceptance_criteria.then: All threads are displayed with their entries, resolution state, and kind badges (blocker, question, nit, idea); checks show pass/fail with staleness; verdicts show reviewer decisions; computed disposition is prominent

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a review detail page
acceptance_criteria.then: They can create a new thread with a body and kind selection (blocker, question, nit, idea)

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a thread on a review
acceptance_criteria.then: They can add a reply to the thread

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a blocker or question thread
acceptance_criteria.then: The thread resolution state is toggled and the UI updates immediately

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is viewing a review detail page
acceptance_criteria.when: They submit a verdict (approve, request_changes, comment)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The verdict is recorded and the disposition badge updates to reflect
the new computed disposition

acceptance_criteria.given: A user views a task detail page
acceptance_criteria.when: The task has linked reviews (via review_ref or related_refs)
acceptance_criteria.then:
The reviews are shown with current disposition badge and link to the
review detail page

acceptance_criteria.given:
A thread comment has a body containing markdown (headings, code blocks,
inline code, bold, lists, links)
acceptance_criteria.when: The comment is rendered in the thread view
acceptance_criteria.then:
The body is rendered as formatted markdown with syntax highlighting
in code blocks

acceptance_criteria.given: A thread entry is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: The entry has author and timestamp fields
acceptance_criteria.then:
The author identity and relative timestamp are shown alongside
the entry body

acceptance_criteria.given: A review section (threads, checks, verdicts) has no items
acceptance_criteria.then:
An empty state message is shown (e.g., "No threads yet",
"No checks recorded")

acceptance_criteria.given: Multiple reviews exist for the same subject
acceptance_criteria.when: The user views any one of those reviews
acceptance_criteria.then: A review-pass selector is shown listing all reviews for that subject ordered by creation date, with the current review selected; selecting another review navigates to it; subject matching uses subject-ref for plan/task/spec reviews, or head-branch for code reviews

items.title: Review Code Diff Viewer
items.description:
A GitHub-style unified diff viewer for code reviews. Shows per-file
diffs with syntax highlighting, line numbers, expandable context,
and inline comment threading anchored to specific diff lines.

acceptance_criteria.given: A code review is open with base and head commits
acceptance_criteria.then:
A file list shows all changed files with their diff stats (+/- lines)
and each file is expandable to show its diff content

acceptance_criteria.given: A file diff is expanded
acceptance_criteria.then:
It shows a unified diff view with syntax highlighting, old and new
line numbers, added lines (green), deleted lines (red), and unchanged
context lines

acceptance_criteria.given: A diff hunk has collapsed unchanged regions
acceptance_criteria.when: The user clicks "Show N more lines"
acceptance_criteria.then:
Additional context lines are fetched and inserted into the diff
view without reloading the page

acceptance_criteria.given: A user hovers over a line number in the diff
acceptance_criteria.then:
A comment form opens inline between diff rows, anchored to that
file, line number, and side (old/new); submitting creates a thread
with a code anchor

acceptance_criteria.given: Existing review threads have code anchors matching lines in the diff
acceptance_criteria.then:
The comment threads are shown inline at their anchored position
in the diff, between the relevant diff rows

acceptance_criteria.given: A diff contains more than 20 changed files
acceptance_criteria.then:
Files are lazy-loaded (headers and stats shown immediately, full
diff content loaded on expand or viewport intersection)

items.title: Review Structured Content Viewer
items.description:
Content viewer for non-code reviews (plans, specs). Renders the
entity content with identifiable sections that support anchored
commenting, similar to how the diff viewer enables line-level
comments on code.

acceptance_criteria.given: A plan review is open
acceptance_criteria.then:
The plan content is rendered with identifiable sections (specs,
tasks, implementation notes) that can be targeted for comments

acceptance_criteria.given: A spec review is open
acceptance_criteria.then:
The spec content is rendered showing description, acceptance
criteria, traits, and metadata with each section targetable
for comments

acceptance_criteria.given: A user clicks a comment button next to a content section
acceptance_criteria.then:
Submitting creates a thread with a structured anchor (section,
field, anchor-ref) pointing to the selected content area

acceptance_criteria.given: Existing threads have structured anchors matching content sections
acceptance_criteria.then:
The threads are shown inline at their anchored position in the
content, adjacent to the referenced section

acceptance_criteria.given: a plan review subject's plan content contains markdown image and document links using `./resources/<relative-path>` for declared plan resources
acceptance_criteria.when: the review detail page renders the plan content section in live multi-project mode
acceptance_criteria.then: the markdown image and document targets are rewritten through the plan-scoped resource bytes URLs from the review content resource context, the browser fetches the selected project's declared bytes, and undeclared or unsafe paths are not rewritten

acceptance_criteria.given: a task review subject's task description contains markdown image and document links using `./resources/<relative-path>` for present task resolved resources, including both plan-owned refs and materialized task-owned copies
acceptance_criteria.when: the review detail page renders the task description section in live multi-project mode
acceptance_criteria.then: the markdown image and document targets are rewritten through task-scoped resource bytes URLs from the review content resource context, the browser fetches the recorded selected-project bytes, and the UI shows resource status messages instead of silently serving replacement bytes for drifted, missing, or unresolved resolved resources

acceptance_criteria.given: a task review subject's task description contains markdown image or document links using `./resources/<relative-path>` that do not match any present, drifted, missing, or unresolved task resource, including when the task has no derived resource references
acceptance_criteria.when: the review detail page renders the task description section in live multi-project mode
acceptance_criteria.then: those markdown targets remain unreplaced, the browser is not pointed at replacement bytes for them, and the UI shows an `unmatched` resource status message for each authored path with guidance to verify the reference path or re-derive the task with the resource present

items.title: Live Review Resource URLs Preserve Project Context
items.description: Review resource cards continue to provide the working browser URL comparator for local resources in live multi-project mode.

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon has multiple projects registered, the web UI has a non-default project selected, and a review has a declared image resource
acceptance_criteria.when: the browser fetches the rendered review image preview URL
acceptance_criteria.then: the request returns that selected project's review image bytes instead of the daemon default project's bytes or a project-not-found response

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon has multiple projects registered, the web UI has a non-default project selected, and a review has a declared document resource
acceptance_criteria.when: the browser opens the rendered review document link
acceptance_criteria.then: the request returns that selected project's review document bytes instead of the daemon default project's bytes or a project-not-found response

items.title: Independent Meta Sub-Domains
items.description:
The meta cache domain is composed of independently-sourced data:
project manifest metadata, shadow branch health, and session
context. Each sub-domain has its own invalidation trigger and
can be refreshed without affecting the others.

acceptance_criteria.given: A meta YAML file changes in the shadow branch
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only the manifest and project metadata are reloaded; shadow
branch health and session context are not re-evaluated

acceptance_criteria.given: The background sync scheduler runs its periodic check
acceptance_criteria.when: Shadow branch health data has changed
acceptance_criteria.then:
The cached shadow status is updated independently of the
manifest metadata and session context

acceptance_criteria.given: The session context file changes
acceptance_criteria.then:
Only the session context portion of meta is reloaded; manifest
metadata and shadow health are not re-evaluated

acceptance_criteria.given:
A project is registered and the meta domain loads for the first
time
acceptance_criteria.then:
All three sub-domains (manifest, shadow, session context) are
loaded before the meta domain transitions to ready state

items.title: Concurrent Read Command Execution
items.description:
Read-only commands executed via the command API can complete
concurrently when served from cached data. Mutating commands
and commands that require disk access continue to execute
sequentially to preserve data integrity.

acceptance_criteria.given:
Multiple read-only commands are submitted to the command
API concurrently and all required cache domains are in
ready state
acceptance_criteria.then: The commands complete without waiting for each other

acceptance_criteria.given: A mutating command is submitted to the command API
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command executes sequentially with respect to other
mutating commands and does not overlap with them

acceptance_criteria.given:
A read-only command is submitted to the command API but
one or more required cache domains are not in ready state
acceptance_criteria.when: The command falls back to disk-based data loading
acceptance_criteria.then:
The command executes sequentially to protect shared
process state during disk-based execution

items.title: Live Plan Resource URLs Preserve Project Context
items.description: Browser-rendered plan resource URLs carry selected-project context in live multi-project mode because image and link elements cannot send `X-Kspec-Dir` headers.

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon has multiple projects registered, the web UI has a non-default project selected, and a plan markdown image references a declared resource with `./resources/<relative-path>`
acceptance_criteria.when: the browser fetches the rendered image URL from the plan detail view
acceptance_criteria.then: the request returns that selected project's declared plan resource bytes instead of the daemon default project's bytes or a project-not-found response

acceptance_criteria.given: the daemon has multiple projects registered, the web UI has a non-default project selected, and a plan markdown document link references a declared resource with `./resources/<relative-path>`
acceptance_criteria.when: the browser opens the rendered document link from the plan detail view
acceptance_criteria.then: the request returns that selected project's declared plan resource bytes instead of the daemon default project's bytes or a project-not-found response

acceptance_criteria.given: a rendered live plan resource URL includes selected-project routing context
acceptance_criteria.when: the daemon resolves the resource request
acceptance_criteria.then: the request still resolves only through the owning plan's resource manifest and rejects undeclared paths, absolute paths, parent traversal paths, and symlink escapes

items.title: Shipped UI Console Hygiene
items.description:
The shipped web interface does not emit debug- or informational-level
diagnostic output to the browser console during normal operation.
Console output in the shipped interface is reserved for actionable
warnings and errors. Routine lifecycle activity — navigation, item
selection, realtime connection progress, duplicate-event suppression —
produces no console output by default.

acceptance_criteria.given:
The shipped web interface is loaded in a browser with default
settings
acceptance_criteria.when:
A user performs routine interactions (navigating views, selecting
items) and the realtime connection performs its normal lifecycle
(connect, receive events, disconnect, reconnect)
acceptance_criteria.then:
No debug- or informational-level diagnostic messages are written to
the browser console

acceptance_criteria.given:
A genuine failure occurs in the shipped interface (a request fails,
a message cannot be parsed, or an internal handler throws)
acceptance_criteria.then:
A warning- or error-level console message is emitted that describes
the failure

items.title: Web Shell Platform Target
items.description:
The kspec web interface targets the web browser as its sole runtime
platform. The application shell is a browser application served by the
daemon, with a static export fallback, and adopts no native desktop
chrome. The shell's top chrome reserves its leading zone — the
contiguous region at the inline-start edge of the top chrome, whose
extent is a single named reservation value defined by the shell
layout, sized to hold platform window controls — and no shell element
occupies it, so a native wrapper could later add window controls
without relocating existing shell elements. Keyboard chords resolve
through a central platform mapping that avoids browser-reserved
combinations on each platform.

acceptance_criteria.given:
the application shell renders in a supported browser with no
native wrapper present
acceptance_criteria.then:
the action is operable through browser-standard pointer and
keyboard input, and no shell affordance requires a native
window-manager facility — window controls, native application
menus, or OS-level global shortcuts

acceptance_criteria.given: the shell's top chrome layout
acceptance_criteria.when: its elements are laid out at any viewport width
acceptance_criteria.then:
the leading chrome zone contains no shell element — every
top-chrome element clears the named reservation value at the
inline-start edge

acceptance_criteria.given: a keyboard chord is registered for a shell action
acceptance_criteria.when: the binding is resolved on a given platform
acceptance_criteria.then:
the chord comes from the central platform mapping and does not
collide with combinations the browser reserves on that platform

items.title: Test Result Acquisition
items.description:
Future coverage behavior is ingestion-oriented: completed runs from
local tools, CI, or agents can submit structured result records to
the daemon. Submitted results use a standardized result format and
carry a deterministic mapping between tests and the acceptance
criteria they cover, expressed through test naming or result
metadata. Static annotation scanning remains the mapping and
integrity source until the coverage-track plans define the complete
ingestion schema and engine behavior. Freshness presentation names
ingested-run evidence as such and reflects the latest ingested run
when that evidence is the source being presented.

acceptance_criteria.given: a completed test run in any execution environment
acceptance_criteria.when: its results are submitted through the ingestion interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
per-acceptance-criterion outcomes are recorded and attributed to
that run

acceptance_criteria.given:
submitted results whose tests reference acceptance criteria
through the mapping convention
acceptance_criteria.then:
each mappable result is attributed to its acceptance criteria,
and results that cannot be mapped are surfaced as unmapped rather
than silently dropped

acceptance_criteria.given: a project with more than one ingested test run
acceptance_criteria.when: ingested-run freshness is presented on any surface
acceptance_criteria.then:
the presentation reflects the most recently ingested run and
labels it as the latest ingested run

items.title: Acceptance Criterion Applicability
items.description:
Corpus-level coverage recognizes no not-applicable state. Every
acceptance criterion on a spec item is expected to be coverable; a
criterion that cannot apply to its item indicates a spec-composition
defect to repair, not a state to record. Not-applicable marking is a
task-scoped concern — identifying which inherited criteria fall
outside one task's work — and lives in task coverage metadata, not in
the spec corpus. In-code not-applicable annotations are not coverage
signals: they neither cover a criterion nor exempt it. The existing
scanner and trait-validation specs that count those annotations as
coverage are incorrect under this decision and must be respecced and
fixed by the coverage storage plan before the new coverage engine
treats corpus coverage as authoritative.

acceptance_criteria.given: coverage states computed across the spec corpus
acceptance_criteria.when: any acceptance criterion's state is derived
acceptance_criteria.then:
the result is one of the recognized coverage states and never a
not-applicable state

acceptance_criteria.given: a test annotation that marks a criterion not-applicable
acceptance_criteria.then:
the annotation neither counts as coverage for that criterion nor
exempts it from the corpus coverage states

items.title: Annotation Freshness Provenance
items.description:
Every acceptance-criterion test annotation carries a freshness
timestamp with two provenance classes. A bootstrap value is derived
from version-control history of the annotation's location, so
existing annotations have freshness without prior bookkeeping. A
recorded verification stamp — written when a validation pass, an
ingested test run, or an explicit re-verification confirms the
mapping — supersedes the bootstrap value from then on. Interfaces
that consume freshness accept either a timestamp or a commit
reference, keeping the provenance source evolvable.

acceptance_criteria.given: an annotation with no recorded verification stamp
acceptance_criteria.then:
a bootstrap value derived from the annotation's version-control
history is returned

acceptance_criteria.given:
an ingested passing run or explicit re-verification that confirms
an annotation
acceptance_criteria.then:
the recorded verification stamp is returned in place of the
bootstrap value

acceptance_criteria.given: an interface that consumes annotation freshness
acceptance_criteria.when:
it receives a provenance value expressed as either a timestamp or
a commit reference
acceptance_criteria.then:
the value is accepted and resolves to a comparable freshness
ordering without requiring one canonical form

items.title: Coverage State Presentation
items.description:
Coverage state is presented as four user-facing buckets: covered,
failing, not yet, and re-verify. The re-verify bucket covers any
condition where existing evidence must be checked again, including
spec-text changes after verification and covering-code changes after
verification; those causes are exposed only as secondary detail such
as row captions, detail views, and filter facets, not as separate
presentation states. Each presentation state is represented by
exactly one visual token wherever it appears.

acceptance_criteria.given: any surface presenting coverage state
acceptance_criteria.then:
every rendered coverage state is one of the four presentation
buckets — covered, failing, not yet, re-verify — and any
re-verification cause is available only as secondary detail

acceptance_criteria.given: the same coverage state appearing on two different surfaces
acceptance_criteria.then: the same visual token represents the state on both

items.title: Client Preference Persistence
items.description:
Interface preferences — focus selection, collapse states, recents,
view toggles, and similar per-user interface state — persist in
browser-local storage through one shared, namespaced, versioned
utility whose interface is storage-agnostic. Daemon-level state —
configuration describing the daemon's own world, such as the roster
of registered projects — persists server-side in the daemon's
configuration directory and never depends on browser storage.

acceptance_criteria.given: a surface that persists an interface preference
acceptance_criteria.when:
the preference is changed and the browser session is later
reloaded
acceptance_criteria.then:
the preference is restored, and its stored value is recorded
under the shared namespaced, versioned key format

acceptance_criteria.given: daemon-level state such as the registered-project roster
acceptance_criteria.then:
the state is recovered from the daemon configuration directory
without any client involvement

items.title: Actor Identity Model
items.description:
Actor identity is a configured attribution vocabulary, not an
authentication boundary. Direct human changes are attributed to a
configured human author identity, and automated work is attributed to
canonical agent identifiers drawn from the configured runner/agent
roster. New actor-bearing writes validate against that author pool
and persist canonical identifiers; invalid or out-of-pool write
values are rejected by validation rather than being accepted as new
free-form authors. Historical records are normalized once through the
data upgrade path: recognizable variants map to their canonical
identity, ambiguous values may be resolved through assisted review or
operator-provided mapping, and values still unresolved when the
upgrade completes map to a declared unknown/default actor while the
original value remains reportable for audit. Identity powers
filtering and display such as ownership and awaiting-action views,
and carries no authentication or access-control semantics.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new record carrying an actor field
acceptance_criteria.when: it is written through any interface
acceptance_criteria.then:
the actor value is a canonical configured human author or a
canonical configured agent/runner identifier, and an invalid or
out-of-pool value is rejected by validation

acceptance_criteria.given: a project's historical records containing actor variants
acceptance_criteria.then:
every actor field resolves to a canonical configured human or
agent identity, an operator-provided mapping, or the declared
unknown/default actor, and unresolved originals appear in the
upgrade report

acceptance_criteria.given:
an identity-derived view such as awaiting-action or ownership
filtering
acceptance_criteria.then:
it derives from the canonical actor vocabulary and treats the
declared unknown/default actor distinctly from configured humans
and agents

items.title: Agent Question Mediation
items.description:
Dispatched automated task agents do not wait on user-facing
interactive question prompts. When a dispatched automation agent
requires human input, it records durable work state — task blocking
with a stated reason and task notes — and the human resumes the work
through the ordinary task lifecycle. This decision is scoped to
automated dispatch sessions only: it does not forbid future
deliberately interactive planning/chat sessions, including structured
ask/answer protocols, when those are planned as a separate user-facing
session mode.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dispatched automation agent requires human input to proceed
acceptance_criteria.then:
the signal is recorded as durable task state — blocked with a
reason — and task notes, reviewable after the fact

acceptance_criteria.given:
a surface presenting dispatched automation work that awaits human
input
acceptance_criteria.when: the user acts on the item
acceptance_criteria.then:
the action navigates to the owning task or session record, and no
surface offers inline structured-choice resolution into that
dispatched automation session

acceptance_criteria.given: a future interactive planning or chat session mode is designed
acceptance_criteria.when: it defines prompt/response or structured ask/answer behavior
acceptance_criteria.then:
that behavior is specified as user-facing interactive-session
behavior, not as dispatched automation waiting for inline user
resolution

items.title: Integration Merge Authority
items.description:
Integration merges are performed by the acting agent or human through
the merge procedure in their own execution environment. The daemon's
request handlers expose no merge-execution capability. Merges that
dispatched agents perform in their own execution environments are the
merge procedure working as intended, not a daemon capability. UI
surfaces may guide users to the appropriate workflow, but merge
execution itself remains outside the daemon API.

acceptance_criteria.given: any endpoint the daemon API exposes
acceptance_criteria.when: its request handler processes a request
acceptance_criteria.then:
the handler performs no version-control merge on a consumer code
repository

items.title: Kynetic Spec - Main Module
items.description: Default module for Kynetic Spec. Add your spec items here.

items.title: Release and Distribution
items.description:
Packaging, publication, and release verification for the
kspec distribution: what the installable artifact contains,
which runtimes it supports, and how publication is gated on
verification evidence.

items.title: Single Supported Runtime Version Range
items.description:
kspec declares exactly one supported Node.js runtime version
range, and every user-facing installation or onboarding
document that states a runtime requirement states that same
range. The package manifest's engine declaration is the
single source of truth; documentation follows it, never the
other way around.

acceptance_criteria.given: The published package's manifest is examined
acceptance_criteria.when: The runtime engine constraint is read
acceptance_criteria.then:
Exactly one supported Node.js version range is declared,
with an explicit minimum major version

acceptance_criteria.given:
A user-facing installation or onboarding document states
a Node.js version requirement
acceptance_criteria.when:
The stated requirement is compared with the declared
engine constraint

items.title: Published Artifact Completeness
items.description:
The artifact a user installs contains everything needed to
run kspec and the legal terms it is distributed under: a
license text matching the declared license identifier, the
complete built command-line interface, and the complete
built web interface. Packaging from a clean source state
produces a complete artifact; it never silently depends on
previously built output being present.

acceptance_criteria.given: The package is packed for publication
acceptance_criteria.then:
A license document is present at the package root and
its terms match the license identifier declared in the
package manifest

acceptance_criteria.given: The package is packed for publication
acceptance_criteria.then:
The declared command-line entry point resolves to a file
that is present in the package

acceptance_criteria.given: The package is packed for publication
acceptance_criteria.then:
The built web interface assets are present, including
the entry document required to serve the interface

acceptance_criteria.given: A source checkout with no pre-existing build output
acceptance_criteria.when: The package is packed for publication
acceptance_criteria.then:
The packing step itself produces the built artifacts,
and the resulting package satisfies the completeness
criteria above

items.title: Pre-Publish Verification Across Supported Runtimes
items.description:
Automated verification exercises kspec across the supported
Node.js runtime range rather than on a single version, so
the declared engine constraint is backed by evidence. At
minimum, the oldest supported major version and at least one
newer major version are both exercised, and publication is
gated on verification at the oldest supported major version.

acceptance_criteria.given: The automated test pipeline runs for a proposed change
acceptance_criteria.when: The pipeline's runtime coverage is examined
acceptance_criteria.then:
The test suite executes on the oldest supported Node.js
major version and on at least one newer major version,
as distinct runs that must each pass

acceptance_criteria.given: A release publish is initiated
acceptance_criteria.then:
Publication proceeds only after build and test
verification has passed on the oldest supported Node.js
major version

inbox.text: Cross-feature requirement pattern: How to express that core features (search, validate, export) must support all entity types. When new entity type added, should automatically imply tasks for core features. Options: (1) applies_to field on feature specs, (2) trait on entity types like @trait-searchable, (3) validation warning for missing coverage, (4) parent spec that entity types must satisfy. Surfaced when realizing search doesn't cover inbox.

Reverse spec lookup - kspec which <file> or kspec which <file:line> to find specs/ACs that reference or are implemented by a given code path. Useful for bug fixes to quickly discover what specs need updating. Could scan for // AC: annotations and spec_ref links. Instructive, helps find already-instrumented code.

Add cross-platform CI matrix testing - run core functionality tests on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Would catch issues like Unix-specific commands (which, cp -r) before they reach PR review. Consider: matrix strategy in GitHub Actions, platform-specific test skips where needed, focus on CLI commands and daemon lifecycle.
E2E tests: Use isolated port range (not 3456) + cross-platform cleanup. Current approach conflicts with existing daemons. Should use high ephemeral port range and improve cleanup mechanism.
E2E test dev mode - configure Playwright to work with vite dev server instead of requiring full build for faster test iteration (12+ seconds to 1-2 seconds)

Improve derive granularity: Research suggests specs with 4+ ACs are candidates for splitting. Potential enhancements: (1) --by-ac flag to create tasks per AC group, (2) --max-acs N to auto-group, (3) implementation_phases field in specs, (4) derive templates for common patterns (cli-command, api-endpoint), (5) complexity warnings when specs are too large. See session research on task decomposition patterns from Linear, Atlassian, BDD/Example Mapping, and AI coding assistants.

Daemon debugging improvements: (1) Add --log-file or --verbose to 'kspec serve start', (2) Log resolved web UI path on startup, (3) Capture and show stderr when daemon fails to start within timeout. Consolidated from @01KFQ586, @01KFQ595, @01KFPH3D.

Project config file (kspec.config.yaml or .kspecrc): Configure shadow remote URL (enable separate repo for specs), feature toggles, default values (author, priority), validation strictness. Enables multi-repo projects sharing specs and tailoring kspec to project needs. Consolidated from @01KFGVVJ, @01KFGVVN.

AC test coverage analysis: 'kspec coverage @spec-ref' command to scan codebase for '// AC: @spec ac-N' annotations and report which ACs have test coverage vs gaps. Soft check for review, not blocking. Consolidated from @01KFHJNR, @01KFP9A6.

Shadow sync improvements: (1) Auto-resolve using rebase/merge-driver for cleaner sync, (2) Make sync warnings visible in CLI output (currently silent unless KSPEC_DEBUG=1), (3) Auto-detect common issues with suggested fixes. Consolidated from @01KFTDA7, @01KFHZR4.

CLI array field flag patterns: (1) Generic --clear <field> or --<field> [] for clearing arrays, (2) --add-<field> vs multiple flags for append semantics. Design unified approach for depends-on, tags, blocked-by, etc. Consolidated from @01KFGRV6, @01KFR0KN.

Inbox CLI improvements: (1) Add filtering to list: --before/--after <date>, --author <name> (--tag exists), (2) Add merge command: 'kspec inbox merge @source @target' for consolidating duplicates, (3) Add --priority and --automation flags to promote command. Consolidated from @01KG95JP, @01KG95JQ, @01KG95JS.

Workflow CLI improvements: (1) 'workflow show' should infer active run like 'workflow next', (2) Warn when --input flags passed but step has no inputs defined, (3) Improve 'workflow show' output format with vertical display, status indicators, indented notes. Consolidated from @01KFKSF6, @01KFKSGC, @01KFKTNR.

Spec item slug/addressing improvements: (1) Warn/error on slug collision when creating items, (2) Make nested requirements addressable by slug (currently kspec item ac add @slug fails for items under requirements:). Consolidated from @01KGDCRG, @01KGDCRJ.

Expand @trait-multi-ref-batch to remaining commands: trait add/remove, task set --automation, inbox delete, task note. Enables batch operations like 'kspec task note @ref1 @ref2 @ref3 "shared content"'. Consolidated from @01KG71J2, @01KG95JM, @01KFVXBM.
Add --spec-ref filter to kspec task list command to filter tasks by linked spec item

Workflow lifecycle CLI design (from mining run 01KFS6MJ): kspec workflow complete @run-ref (mark run completed, archive), kspec workflow cancel @run-ref (cancel abandoned run), kspec workflow cleanup --older-than Nd (auto-cancel stale runs). Extends existing @01KFPH39 auto-cleanup with concrete subcommand design.

Item list --module flag and tree view: kspec item list --module cli to scope output to a specific module. kspec item tree @module for hierarchical view (features -> requirements). Currently 50+ items display flat, making it hard to find the right parent for new specs. Friction: during automation triage had to grep YAML files to find parent specs.

Define typed event data schemas per EventType — session.start, session.update (with tool_call/sessionUpdate variants), session.end, prompt.sent, tool.call, tool.result, note. Current z.unknown() data field makes it impossible to reliably query events without reverse-engineering from real JSONL files.

Session log compaction: at end of each ralph loop, replace raw events.jsonl with a compiled stats file (event counts by type, tool usage frequency, duration, task transitions, error summary). Keep session folders and context snapshots intact but prune the raw log. This gives trend analysis capability without unbounded log growth. Could be a kspec session compact command or automatic post-loop step.

Active context from meta: use the meta database (observations, conventions, patterns) as a dynamic context source that automatically surfaces relevant entries based on current activity. E.g. when reviewing plan-import code, auto-surface friction observations tagged with plan-import. When doing code review, pull in resolved friction patterns as review priors. Replaces manual markdown maintenance (AGENTS.md, skill docs) with structured data that stays current as observations accumulate. Could use conventions or a new meta item type for durable patterns distinct from one-off observations.

Centralize daemon port default (3456) — currently hardcoded in 6 places: src/schema/spec.ts, src/cli/index.ts, src/cli/commands/serve.ts, packages/daemon/src/index.ts, packages/web-ui/src/lib/constants.ts, packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/test-base.ts. Extract to a shared constant to prevent drift.

Formalize CLI usage analysis as a repeatable workflow. Tools exist in .claude-research/tools/ (parse-ralph-logs.mjs, parse-claude-logs.mjs, compile-data.mjs) plus interactive HTML report. Consider: kspec skill, CLI command, or standalone workflow. Re-run after implementing the 6 CLI agent-UX improvements to measure impact.

Add repeated-flag support to --status filter (ac-repeated-flag gap from PR #354). Commander.js .option() needs a collect function to accumulate repeated --status flags into an array. Currently only comma-separated works. Small fix: change .option('-s, --status <status>') to use Commander's variadic/collect pattern, then feed array into parseMultiStatus().

Shadow branch diff/changelog — since .kspec/ is git-tracked, we could show changes to stored artifacts (workflows, tasks, specs, inbox) over time. Something like kspec history @ref or kspec diff --since '1 week ago' that leverages the git history on kspec-meta branch. Could show task state transitions, spec evolution, workflow modifications, etc.
Version pinning: all projects use whatever global kspec version is installed. No lock file or constraint resolution. Consider adding version constraints to kynetic.yaml manifest.
Memory seeding: seed MEMORY.md with project-relevant starting notes during kspec setup. Could bootstrap agent effectiveness in new projects.

Tech debt: Pre-existing test anti-patterns - daemon-api-projects.test.ts has 10 no-op tests behind existsSync guards. ralph.test.ts and ralph-context-refresh.test.ts have conditional assertions without preceding guard assertions. Not from ralph loop but should fix.

Fix daemon-executable.test.ts - bun build --compile fails when routes import from parent packages. Pre-existing failure, root cause: ESM imports from parent packages can't be bundled. AC-16 on @daemon-server claimed complete but test doesn't pass.

kspec tasks assess automation --all should display stored automation status (eligible/needs_review/manual_only) alongside criteria recommendation. Currently only shows criteria-based recommendation even for already-assessed tasks, making it impossible to verify batch operations.
Silent error swallowing in setup pipeline: multiple bare catch {} blocks in setup.ts lose diagnostic info. At minimum should log at debug/verbose level for troubleshooting.

Legacy renderClaudeCodeSkill diverges from claudeCodeRenderer: uses old writeRenderHash (not platform-specific), lacks outputDir support, returns old type. setup.ts still uses it. Should route through registry and deprecate standalone function.

Codex and Claude Code renderers share ~70% duplicated render logic (content loading, frontmatter stripping, idempotency check, file writing, hash storage, dir copying). Extract shared base render function with hooks for platform-specific steps.

---

Triage 2026-02-22: 8/13 sub-items RESOLVED by PRs #408 #412 #403. Remaining: getSetupStatus staleness, skill update mutation, naming inconsistency, redundant defaults, deprecated_target reuse.
getSetupStatus always reports "current" if hash file exists, cannot detect staleness. Should load meta context and compare hash to detect when agents.md needs regeneration.
skill update mutates loaded skill objects in-place before saveMetaItem. If save fails partway, in-memory state diverges from disk. Should copy before mutation.
Naming inconsistency: isKspecManagedSkill (skill-render.ts) vs isKspecManaged (skill.ts) for same logic. Standardize to one name.
Redundant platform/tags/depends_on defaults in skill CLI — manually set before SkillSchema.safeParse which already applies them. Remove manual defaults.
deprecated_target warning type reused for skill-specific warnings (depends_on validation, orphaned dirs). Add proper skill warning types for better filtering.

Ralph loop consolidation pass: add a cleanup/consolidation iteration every N PRs or at loop end. The PR-by-PR review process misses cross-PR duplication accumulation — 32 PRs in last loop produced 24 inbox items of tech debt. A periodic consolidation step would catch dead code, duplicated utilities, and superseded implementations before they compound.

Codex skill: handle own-PR reviews — GitHub rejects REQUEST_CHANGES on your own PRs, Codex should use COMMENT event instead. Bundle this fix with skill importing refinement so it propagates to all projects.

Task-specific ephemeral AC: Support acceptance criteria directly on tasks (not just via spec_ref). Useful for implementation requirements, refactoring criteria, and one-off work that doesn't warrant a spec item. Task ACs would be checked during review but wouldn't live in the spec hierarchy. Addresses the gap where plan-imported ACs are behavioral specs vs task-level implementation requirements.

skill-render.ts lines 492, 730, 924 have LF-only frontmatter regexes. Low risk in render path (kspec generates these files with LF) but should be hardened for consistency with the CRLF fixes in skill.ts/validate-skills.ts.

Feature request: ralph loop boundary tracking in session logs. Currently no easy way to see what happened in a ralph loop iteration without cross-referencing PR timestamps, git log, and task states. A session log showing PR-to-task mapping per loop iteration would help audit and review. Originated from imgen project observation.

Design section configuration for agents generate — allow projects to control which sections appear (skills table, conventions, workflows, static templates). Key questions: where does config live, include vs exclude list, defaults, custom sections, ordering, data vs template distinction, migration path. See plan doc for full requirements.
Inbox tag management: no way to add/remove tags on existing inbox items. Only settable at creation via inbox add --tag. Need: kspec inbox tag add @ref <tag> and kspec inbox tag remove @ref <tag>.

Batch command arg naming inconsistency: inbox add accepts tag (singular) not tags. No documentation of which args each batch command accepts. Consider: consistent plural naming or better error messages with valid arg list.

Stale workflow runs accumulate: no way to prune or auto-expire old runs. After many sessions, every workflow next command requires specifying a run ID because 7+ active runs exist. Need: kspec workflow prune (expire runs older than N days) or kspec workflow cancel @run-id.

When spawning parallel review agents (e.g. Codex + /pr-review), instruct the /pr-review agent not to merge — only review. The parent agent should control the merge decision after all reviews complete. Update /pr-review skill or add a --no-merge flag.

Template/example repo for new kspec consumers: either a GitHub template repo or 'kspec create-project' command showing a fully configured consumer project (manifest, CLAUDE.md with @kspec-agents.md, skills, hooks). Real consumer projects (kynetic-bot, imgen, comfy-ecaj-nodes) serve as informal examples but a clean minimal template would lower onboarding friction.

Per-module task files and task archiving: Original design intent was project.tasks.yaml for non-spec tasks, <module>.tasks.yaml for module-scoped tasks. Never fully implemented — everything goes to project.tasks.yaml. Tradeoffs: splitting reduces file size (comfy-ecaj-nodes has 97 tasks in one file) but requires reading more files. Related: need task archiving to move completed tasks out of the active file. Both address the same scaling problem (task files growing unbounded) from different angles.

kspec validate @spec or @task — targeted validation that checks a single spec/task's AC coverage against codebase. Not full approval, just verifies each AC has at least one // AC: annotation in test files. Would make trait AC gaps immediately visible during task-work. Could be used by local-review skill as a concrete check instead of relying on agent diligence.

Terminal exit code display in ralph CLI renderer — claude-agent-acp PR #316 adds _meta.terminal_exit.exit_code on Bash tool completions (opt-in via clientCapabilities._meta.terminal_output). Low priority, ~40 lines across events.ts + cli-renderer.ts. Only concrete gain from the terminal streaming protocol — the output data itself is identical to existing _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse path. Worth adopting if Bash failure debugging becomes a pain point.

Bash code fence language change in claude-agent-acp v0.18.0 — formatted Bash output changed from ```sh to ```console. Check if ralph's noise suppression patterns, session log rendering, or any regex patterns in cli-renderer.ts or events.ts match on the code fence language. Low risk since ralph primarily reads from _meta.claudeCode.toolResponse not content blocks, but worth a grep.

Surface ACP usage/cost data in ralph session stats — after SDK bump to 0.14.x, new Usage/UsageUpdate/Cost types are available. Could add token usage per iteration and cumulative cost to session log stats and web UI. The usage_update SessionUpdate variant fires during sessions with context window utilization data.

---

IMPORTANT FINDING: Neither claude-agent-acp nor codex-acp actually emit usage_update events or populate PromptResponse.usage. Both have raw token data available but discard it. kynetic-bot works around this by scraping /context stderr (fragile regex). Upstream PR to claude-agent-acp is highest-value path — Anthropic API stream events contain usage data, just needs wiring to ACP protocol.

Explore CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE mode for ralph loops — sets minimal system prompt with only Bash, file read, and file edit tools. Disables MCP tools, attachments, hooks, and CLAUDE.md. Could reduce token overhead and speed up startup, but ralph would need to inject all project context (AGENTS.md rules, spec-first workflow, kspec conventions) into the prompt itself instead of relying on Claude Code's built-in mechanisms. Tradeoff: simpler/faster agent vs ralph becomes responsible for all context bootstrapping. Ref: anthropics/claude-code#27019

Ralph worktree isolation for task work — spawn each agent in a git worktree under a gitignored .worktrees/ dir for branch isolation. Pattern proven in kynetic-internal with jj workspaces. Key insight: kspec resolves .kspec/ via git root, but worktrees return their own root from rev-parse --show-toplevel. Solution: ralph sets KSPEC_SPEC_DIR to point to main tree's .kspec/ when spawning agents (env var already exists for batch mode). Benefits: isolated branches per task, parallel agent work, trivial cleanup of failed work, clean main branch. Unknowns: shadow branch commands from worktree context, git config inheritance, worktree lifecycle management in ralph.

Single-source task state diagram: currently duplicated in AGENTS.md, templates/agents-sections/03-task-lifecycle.md, and src/cli/help/content.ts. Adding needs_work required updating all three independently. Generate from schema or single template to avoid triple-update when adding states.

Distinguish behavioral vs testable ACs in kspec validate: workflow ACs (agent behavioral specs enforced by skills/prompts) get flagged as uncovered in test coverage, creating false MUST-FIX findings in reviews. Allow tagging ACs or specs as agent-enforced to report separately from code-testable ACs.
inbox promote missing --slug option: cannot set task slug during promotion, must use default auto-generated slug. Add --slug <slug> option to inbox promote command.
CLI gap: kspec skill set should support --id to rename a skill without delete+recreate

Spec and test kspec behavior without git: ensure kspec works in projects without git initialized, and handles git being introduced into an existing project where kspec is already in use. Cover shadow branch initialization, worktree setup on first git init, migration of .kspec/ state when git appears, and graceful degradation of git-dependent features (auto-commit, sync, shadow status).

Session checkpoint hook noise: fires repeatedly for intentionally uncommitted files (e.g. generated reports). No way to suppress for specific paths. Could support .kspec/checkpoint-ignore listing paths to exclude from dirty-tree check, or respect gitignore-like patterns. Fired 6+ times in one session for a triage report artifact.

CLI parity: kspec task add requires --title flag but kspec inbox add accepts positional text argument. task add should accept positional title for consistency. Small change in Commander.js argument definition.

Plugin registry tests: validate structurally instead of exact output matching. Current tests assert exact JSON shapes (e.g. source field structure) which breaks when Claude Code schema evolves. Better: (1) Validate marketplace.json against a Zod schema capturing required fields (plugins array, name, source, version) rather than exact values. (2) Test build output structurally — 'has plugins array with our entry' not exact field matching. (3) For known_marketplaces.json registry, test entry exists with valid path, not exact source object shape. Motivation: the source field assertion broke twice already (local → directory object) because tests coupled to implementation details.

Include triage records in static snapshot (kspec-snapshot.json). Currently the snapshot format (KspecSnapshot type) doesn't include triage records, so the triage page in static/GitHub Pages mode shows an empty state with a notice instead of displaying existing triage decisions read-only. AC-8 of @interactive-triage-ui expects read-only display. Needs: add triage records to export snapshot, update KspecSnapshot type, add fetchTriageRecordsStatic to read from snapshot.

Web UI list pages hardcode limit: 1000 with no pagination — triage page confirmed, likely affects inbox/tasks pages too. Silent truncation for large datasets. Need pagination or virtual scrolling pattern across all list views.

Trait AC annotation gaps on @triage-cli-commands: @trait-error-guidance ac-3, @trait-semantic-exit-codes ac-3/4/6/7, @trait-filterable-list ac-2, @trait-shadow-commit ac-2/3/4/6/7/8, @trait-dry-run ac-4/6. Pre-existing, not introduced by PR #458.
Web UI WebSocket connection unreliable - continually disconnects and reconnects. Needs investigation into reconnection logic, heartbeat handling, or fallback to polling.
Web UI triage page: add filter controls for triage action types (promote, delete, defer, spec-gap, duplicate). Currently no way to filter triage records by action.
Web UI: persist all filter state and current view in URL query params so refreshing the page preserves state. Applies to all list/filter pages (triage, inbox, tasks, etc).

Triage promote action should optionally delete the inbox item after creating the task. Currently promoted items stay in inbox requiring manual cleanup. Consider --consume flag or making deletion the default for promote (with snapshot preserved in triage record).

ULID short ref ambiguity in batch operations: when two ULIDs share a prefix (e.g. 01KJ4SNE9 and 01KJ4SNEC), short refs like @01KJ4SNE fail. kspec already has a shortest-unique-ID utility — this should be used anywhere refs are displayed (triage list, task list, inbox list, promote result_ref, etc.) so that presented refs are always unambiguous and copy-pasteable into subsequent commands.

Agents should check plan_ref when starting tasks. If a task has plan_ref, run kspec plan get @plan-ref to read implementation notes, algorithm details, and context. Update task-work skill and task-work-loop workflow to include this step. Plans are the right place for rich implementation context instead of cramming it into task notes.

Plan import --update replaces all ACs instead of merging. When extending an existing spec with a new AC via plan import, --update overwrites acceptance_criteria entirely. Need AC-merge strategy: append new AC IDs, preserve existing ones. Encountered during spec-plan for session-log-show ac-10.

Plan import warnings treated as errors in batch mode. The no YAML code block in specs section warning causes batch atomic rollback even though the task creation succeeded. Warnings should not cause batch failure — only actual errors should.

Ralph event handler iteration attribution should use session-scoped mapping instead of shared mutable currentIteration. Codex review on PR #484 identified that late updates from a previous ACP session can still be tagged with wrong iteration. Use session_id→iteration map or session-scoped listener. See PR #484 review comment.

CLI args should accept both kebab-case and underscore variants (e.g. depends-on and depends_on). Currently batch commands reject underscore variants even though the error message suggests the kebab form. Normalizing both forms would reduce friction, especially for agents generating JSON batch payloads where underscore is the natural convention.

Session-scoped workflow runs: workflow runs could carry a session_id, filtering workflow show/list to current session by default. Session end could auto-close orphaned runs. Reduces noise when multiple sessions active (ralph + interactive). Natural fit since workflows are already ephemeral.

Ralph loop needs iteration-level timeout. When a spawned agent gets stuck (e.g., tool call hanging on stdin), ralph has no mechanism to detect or recover. A configurable per-iteration timeout (e.g., 15-20 min) that kills the stuck agent and logs the failure would prevent indefinite hangs. Separate from Claude Code's per-bash-command timeout which didn't prevent the kspec batch stdin hang.

Shadow branch index inconsistency: observation @01KJ73ME appeared in search results but failed on kspec item get. Possible write conflict or index corruption during ralph loop session. Investigate shadow branch integrity.

Ralph CLI renderer: parallel tool calls produce confusing output. tool_result events render sequentially with no association to their tool_start, so when multiple tools run in parallel, results appear under the wrong header. Fix: include tool summary (e.g. filename) in the completed/failed status line so each result is self-identifying regardless of interleaving.

Tests fail when run inside ralph loop due to environment contamination: (1) ralph.test.ts KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION assertion expects null but env var is inherited from ralph process, (2) session-create.test.ts active session warning in stderr breaks JSON parsing, (3) session-budget-integration.test.ts references nonexistent task set-automation command. Tests should isolate from parent process env vars (KSPEC_RALPH_SESSION, KSPEC_SESSION_ID) to be reliable in all contexts.
Session event log tool-level filtering: kspec session log show <id> --tool Read would avoid grep/python one-liners when debugging ralph event issues

kspec task set --priority accepts numbers (1-5) but all documentation, conventions, and plan documents use P1/P2/P3 notation. Error message says 'Priority must be a number between 1 and 5' which is confusing when you've been writing P1 everywhere. Should either accept both formats or align documentation with the numeric API.

kspec meta set convention: add --update-rule and --remove-rule flags. Currently the only way to fix a rule is to delete the entire convention and recreate it. Surfaced during skill CLI lookups task when codex review caught a wording issue in one rule.

kspec setup should work without CLAUDECODE=1 env var in non-interactive contexts. Either add a --agent flag (e.g. kspec setup --agent claude-code) to explicitly specify the agent type, or detect based on installed tooling (~/.claude exists) rather than requiring runtime env vars. Discovered while building containerized ralph runner — entrypoint bash script can't set CLAUDECODE=1 globally because claude blocks nested sessions.

kspec agents generate should include package version in content hash (or add --force flag) so version bumps during releases automatically trigger regeneration. Currently skips because content is identical, but the version comment in the header is stale. Workaround: manually edit the version line.

Ralph PR merge should auto-delete remote branches after merge. Currently accumulates stale branches (found 13 after one session). The gh pr merge command supports --delete-branch. Add to pr-review-loop workflow merge step.

Session summary/stats command — kspec session stats @id or kspec session show @id --summary. Parse events.jsonl to show: iteration count, tasks started/completed/blocked, PRs created/merged, total duration, exit reason. Currently requires custom python scripts to extract from 14k+ line event logs.

@cmd-validate spec is stale — missing flags: --completeness, --staleness, --drift, --alignment, --skills, --conventions (all already implemented in code). Pre-existing drift, not introduced by trait AC task.
Fix @observations slug ambiguity — kspec validate reports 6 errors for duplicate slug. Pre-existing issue across main.
Triage API spec says ac-4 and ac-5 use PUT method but implementation uses POST /:ref/override and POST /:ref/act. Spec needs updating to match reality.
Triage ac-5 says sets result_ref but delete action may not produce one. Verify behavior and update spec or add test assertion.
kspec task patch appears to hang indefinitely — had to kill and use task set + task note as workaround
Plan import: generate richer task descriptions from Implementation Notes section — include file paths, what to change, verification steps instead of generic 'See plan...' text
Merge driver: auto-resolve .kspec-agents-hash file conflicts (deterministic hash, should always take latest)
Shadow repair: handle missing /bin/sh — use direct git commands instead of spawning shell, fails on fish-only systems

Add second mock adapter registration for ralph tests. Currently --adapter-cmd registers a single 'custom' adapter, making it impossible to test different adapter IDs in real (non-dry-run) runs. Options: (1) --worker-adapter-cmd / --reviewer-adapter-cmd flags, (2) env-based adapter registration (e.g. KSPEC_TEST_ADAPTERS JSON), (3) allow --adapter-cmd to accept an optional name prefix like --adapter-cmd 'worker:node mock.js'. This would enable proper integration tests for ac-2 (reviewer subagent uses reviewer adapter), ac-7 (env injection for both adapters with different harness targets), and ac-12 (different adapter IDs in session metadata). Currently these are covered by code-level AC annotations and dry-run output tests, but lack end-to-end verification with the mock ACP.

kspec validate should warn about items with identical titles in the same module — two items both named 'Generation Progress UX' with different ULIDs caused confusion during a fix session in imgen project

Meta workflow editing gap: kspec meta set cannot update workflow steps. Agents must delete+recreate workflow to edit a step, which can churn workflow ULIDs and temporarily break references. Add safe step-level update support (e.g., --set-step <index> --content/--on-fail) or preserve ULID on replace to avoid reference drift.

derive_from_specs produces sparse tasks: derived tasks get null description, no tags, automation unassessed. Agents picking up these tasks lack context to work independently. Consider: auto-populate description from spec description, copy plan tags, or allow plan document to specify per-task fields.
Reflection follow-up: add explicit parent/ancestor context to kspec item get output (human and --json) so hierarchy is unambiguous without separate tree queries.
Reflection follow-up: add optional ancestor-chain display for kspec item list --tree --search so matched descendants show parent context and avoid false orphan interpretation.
Reflection follow-up: add validation check for trait/command-contract contradictions (e.g., command AC prohibits --refs while applied traits require batch refs semantics).

Unified kspec get @ref dispatch: currently plans require 'kspec plan get' while specs/tasks use 'kspec item get' / 'kspec task get'. A single 'kspec get @ref' that auto-dispatches to the right entity type would reduce friction for agents and humans who don't know the entity type upfront.
Add stale-dist guard for CLI-based tests: detect outdated dist/cli build in tests/helpers/cli.ts and fail fast with actionable guidance (or optional auto-build) to avoid misleading failures.

Worktree guard escape hatch: add env var KSPEC_GUARD_OVERRIDE_DONT_USE that bypasses the guard hook for intentional recovery operations (git reset, rebase in .kspec). Name deliberately long to discourage agent use — humans-only for recovery scenarios.

Add commit-scope guard for automated task work: before committing, detect pre-existing staged files unrelated to the current task and prevent accidental inclusion (or require explicit acknowledgment). In this iteration, unrelated staged files were included because they were already in the index before git add on task files.

tests/ralph.test.ts helper runRalph splits args on whitespace, so quoted values (e.g., --focus "keep scope narrow") break and cause misleading unknown-command/option failures. Improve helper to accept argv arrays or robust shell-like parsing for test args.

Reflection: fix-cycle ergonomics mismatch — task-work guidance says 're-submit' needs_work tasks, but CLI rejects kspec task submit when status is needs_work and requires explicit kspec task start first. Consider allowing direct submit from needs_work (auto-transition to in_progress) or improving error/help text to show required two-step command sequence.

tests/cli/session-note-limit.test.ts has reproducible timeout instability in current baseline. During this iteration: full npm test timed out at lines 34/70/104, and isolated run timed out at lines 34/104 despite rebuilding. This appears separate from ralph prompt changes and indicates session-start note-limit path/perf regression or test flake that should be stabilized.

Reflection: add file-based payload input to task notes (e.g., kspec task note @ref --file <path> and/or --stdin). Current command only accepts positional message, which makes multiline/special-character notes brittle and conflicts with the convention to use file-based payloads for safe shell handling.

Fix pre-existing test failure: tests/enhanced-setup.test.ts 'should render core skills to codex output when codex is detected' fails with ENOENT on .codex/config.toml — test expects setup to create codex config but it is not being created. Confirmed pre-existing (not introduced by recent changes). Investigate whether codex config generation is missing or test fixture setup is incomplete.

CLI has no way to reparent a spec item (move it under a different parent). kspec item set has no --parent flag, kspec item patch doesn't accept parent_ref. If plan import places specs at the wrong level, the only fix is manual YAML editing — violating the 'use CLI, not manual edits' rule. Discovered during agent-runtime plan import review.

kspec shadow restore command: dedicated recovery for restoring sessions/, specific files, or snapshots from remote/commit without raw git. Prevents agents from cd-ing into .kspec/ for recovery (which poisons shell CWD). Needs design work — what restore scenarios to support, how to handle conflicts, UX for choosing recovery point.

kspec cleanup command: umbrella command that runs all stale-data cleanup in one shot — workflow prune (stale runs), session pruning (old blobs), maybe inbox triage of old items. Similar to 'docker system prune'. Could run on session start or as a standalone command. Would have prevented 40+ stale workflow runs accumulating.

Create a 'cli-utilities' skill (or similar) that documents shared CLI helpers — parseIntOption, exit codes, output helpers — with when/how to use each. Add a meta convention reinforcing 'check this skill before implementing new CLI commands'. Prevents agents from reaching for parseInt+isNaN when parseIntOption exists.

CLI filter options must be backed by schema fields — Zod strips unknown fields on parse, so --tag filtering silently returned nothing because tags wasn't in AgentSchema. Consider a lint rule or convention: before adding a --filter-by-X option, verify X exists in the relevant schema.

kspec commands should support manifest discovery from nested task worktrees (or accept explicit --project-root). Running kspec validate/note/submit from isolated worktrees (e.g., /tmp task worktrees) fails with No kspec manifest found. KSPEC_SPEC_DIR env var exists for batch mode but general CLI commands dont use it. Reported from imgen project task-work automation.

kspec validate trait AC coverage: inherited trait AC annotations in provider tests (e.g., // AC: @trait-slug ac-N in test files) are present but still reported as uncovered. Parser/indexer may not recognize trait annotations in Vitest files or may require specific file patterns. Distinct from behavioral-vs-testable AC distinction (01KHYTNNFY) — this is about annotations that ARE in test code but not detected. Reported from imgen project.

kspec batch atomic mode cannot resolve refs created within the same batch — e.g., item add creates @new-slug but item trait add @new-slug in the same batch fails with item not found. Workaround: split into separate commands. Consider deferred ref resolution within batch execution or explicit batch-local ID aliases.

kspec triage act has no bulk mode — no --all or --status triaged flag to execute all pending triage decisions at once. Processing 42 items required manually listing all 42 refs across 4 batch calls. Add kspec triage act --all or kspec triage act --status triaged for bulk execution.

Document acp-mock.js bidirectional RPC pattern in testing conventions — the MOCK_ACP_SEND_PERMISSION_REQUEST env var and the pending-requests map pattern for agent→client requests. Prevents future developers rediscovering this from scratch.

CLI usage telemetry: track kspec commands at a per-user level — command name, arguments shape (metadata, not full call data), success/error outcomes, and error messages. Goal: surface which commands have high error rates (bad args, wrong state, etc.) to identify friction and prioritize UX improvements. Distinguish metadata (command + flag names) from actual call data (values) for privacy. Could be opt-in or local-only (written to shadow branch alongside tasks).
Codex-only: capture harness guidance to close completed subagents proactively (or auto-close after waits) to avoid thread-limit stalls.

Restore clean kspec validate baseline: resolve duplicate @observations references, fix missing observations skill content, and clear orphan-skill warnings so validation output can reliably signal task-specific issues.

Make setup smarter when creating built-in agents: detect environment and choose appropriate default adapters (e.g., codex-acp vs claude-agent-acp), and/or allow explicit adapter overrides during setup.

auto-creates redundant tasks on promote — when promoting inbox items where the spec already exists (common in triage-from-artifact workflows), the auto-created task is always immediately deleted.
