Need a --no-task or --skip-task flag on triage act to suppress task creation when the spec is already handled.

No batch triage flow — recording and acting on N items requires 2N sequential commands (record + act for each). A batch-triage command or --act flag on triage record would let record+act happen in one pass. In a 29-item triage session, this adds significant overhead.

kspec batch format for triage commands: args expects object but triage record uses positional ref — tried to batch-triage 11 items and hit validation error 'Expected object, received array at args'. Need either documentation of correct batch format for triage or fixing the args shape.

Improve PR creation resilience: when gh pr create returns false-negative GraphQL errors (blank sha/no commits) but branch compare is ahead, automatically fall back to REST create-pull and report deterministic recovery.
pr-review: when reviewer account authored the PR, avoid GitHub APPROVE event and post COMMENT review with full quality-gate summary instead
workflow UX: allow `kspec workflow show` to default to the single active run when run-ref is omitted
Reflection: in pr-review loop, detect self-review context and post COMMENT summary instead of attempting APPROVE on own PR; keep quality-gate semantics explicit in review body.
pr-review loop: detect self-authored PR and avoid APPROVE event (GitHub forbids approving own PR); use COMMENT and continue merge path when quality gates are clean.
Add a fast local test mode for focused vitest runs that skips full pretest build during fix cycles.

Disambiguate automation status vs lifecycle status in @triage-automation docs. Add explicit note that automation:needs_review is an eligibility flag (not lifecycle pending_review/needs_work), and replace legacy 'Ralph loop' wording with dispatch-worker terminology.

Update @plan-review dispatch section to avoid role overload with pr-reviewer. Use explicit plan-worker/plan-reviewer naming and note distinction from pr-reviewer (which owns pending_review merge workflow), to prevent queue ownership confusion.
Reflection: Improve task note readability by supporting filtered views for superseded history (for example latest-only and/or hide-superseded) to reduce stale guidance noise during implementation.
Dispatch: add refresh command to re-bootstrap engine state without stopping/starting (reload agents + re-evaluate in_progress tasks).

kspec agent run produces no visible output: (1) runInvocation is called without onUpdate, so no streaming to stdout during execution. (2) kspec session log show does not display session.update text content after the fact. Fix: add --stream flag to agent run (or stream by default for interactive use), print text blocks as they arrive. Also: session log show should support a --output or --text mode that replays the assistant text from session.update events. Workaround: jq/python one-liner on events.jsonl.

Race condition: process.env.KSPEC_SESSION_ID mutation in invocation.ts is not safe for concurrent multi-project agent dispatch. invocation.ts saves/restores KSPEC_SESSION_ID in finally, and the per-engine mutex serializes within a project — but two projects running agents concurrently both mutate the same process-level env var. The injectEnvForAdapter() path (writing to .claude/settings.local.json etc.) largely mitigates this in practice, but the process.env mutation remains as a race vector. Fix: either remove the process.env mutation entirely (rely solely on adapter config injection + spawn env), or add a process-level lock around the env mutation window.

CLI DX: audit and normalize argument naming across all subcommands. Inconsistencies found: task note uses positional <message> but plan note uses --text flag; item ac set vs expected item ac update; task set --depends-on requires array but gives poor error on comma-separated string. Evaluate entire CLI surface area for consistency or add aliases based on actual/expected usage patterns.

kspec batch with task add throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'). Requires falling back to sequential CLI calls. Known issue documented in MEMORY.md but not tracked as a bug task.
kspec item add --under @parent does not set the parent relationship on the created item. Workaround: use item set --relates-to after creation. Needs investigation.

Smart test filtering: run only tests affected by branch changes. Vitest --changed works for direct imports but misses CLI subprocess integration tests (majority of suite). Would need custom dependency graph that maps source files → test files including subprocess boundaries. Goal: faster agent feedback loops. See conversation analysis for full tradeoffs.

Session lifecycle management — add kspec session archive/purge commands. Sessions accumulate fast with dispatch (842 in ~2 months). Need age-based filtering (--before date), format/agent filtering (--agent id), dry-run preview, and configurable retention policy. Currently requires manual mv/rm. Mining script at ~/Projects/kspec-session-archive/mine-sessions.py can inform what's worth keeping vs purging.

plan set should support --derived-tasks and --derived-specs flags to link work items without manual YAML edits. Currently requires bypassing the shadow branch pre-commit hook to populate these fields.

Dispatch queue does not sort by task priority (p1-p5). _compareQueueEntries sorts by status precedence then FIFO (enqueue sequence). A P3 task enqueued before a P1 task gets dispatched first. Likely a spec gap — no AC requires priority-based ordering within the dispatch queue.

---

Investigation: This is a spec gap, not an implementation bug. @dispatch-in-progress-priority only defines status bucket ordering (in_progress > needs_work > pending_review > pending). No spec requires task priority (p1-p5) as a tiebreaker within the same status bucket. Implementation matches spec — _compareQueueEntries sorts by STATUS_PRECEDENCE then FIFO (enqueue sequence). Fix: add AC to @dispatch-in-progress-priority requiring priority as secondary sort within each status bucket.

Improve discoverability/docs for editing and updating skills across the full pipeline. Current flow is hard to infer: core skills authored in templates/skills/ behave differently from project skills in .kspec/skills/, some rendered outputs are plugin-provided, and commands like skill render vs skill install-core/update are not obvious from the moment you hit stale generated skill output. Document the source-of-truth matrix, when to use skill render vs skill install-core/update vs setup, how plugin-provided skills affect diff/verify behavior, and the expected regeneration steps after editing templates/skills/, .kspec/skills/, or rendered outputs.
plan import --into leaves source_path pointing at the temporary import file instead of reflecting the updated plan provenance or clearing stale file paths

plan derive uses an explicit --module value to materialize specs, but the resulting plan record does not persist module_ref. The derive mutation updates status/derived refs/notes but leaves module_ref null, which weakens provenance and forces future derives or audits to rediscover the module context.

GitHub Actions maintenance: fix Node.js 20 deprecation warnings in workflows. PR checks now show that actions/github-script@v7 is running on Node.js 20, which GitHub says will be forced to Node.js 24 by default starting June 3, 2026. Audit workflow actions and either update affected actions to Node 24-compatible versions or set FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true / ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true as an interim compatibility step where appropriate.

Add a public `kspec plan delete` command. Internal deletePlan support exists in the parser layer, but there is no CLI surface for deleting invalid/test/duplicate plans, which forced cleanup work to use internal APIs instead of the normal kspec workflow.

Tests/fixtures should stop relying on broken-shadow fallback behavior. Several suites use setupTempFixtures()+initGitRepo(), which leaves copied .kspec directories without a real shadow branch/worktree and only worked because initContext() used to fail open into repo-root mode. Follow-up: make test fixtures explicit about shadow mode vs non-shadow mode, add helper support for initializing real shadow repos when needed, and update affected tests to stop depending on disconnected .kspec directories.

Rewrite tests that assert on static prompt outputs (like dispatch orientation context) to focus on unique/dynamic parts being inserted correctly rather than matching full static strings. Fragile prompt assertion tests break on any formatting change.

Skill/workflow name collision: local-review exists as both a workflow (in meta) and a skill (in skills list). skill get local-review fails with 'Item local-review is not a skill' because the resolver finds the workflow first. skill render local-review also fails. This means the hardened local-review SKILL.md content may not be reaching agents that reference /local-review. Discovered during be-kynetic PR review audit.

Add plan output CLI option to suppress specs/tasks YAML blocks — when agents use plan commands, the full specs and tasks blocks spam the output. Add a flag (e.g. --summary or --no-blocks) that shows plan details relevant to the task at hand without the raw YAML spec/task definitions. Useful for agent prompts and task-work sessions where the agent needs the plan context but not the import-format blocks.

kspec validate does not scan monorepo package test directories (e.g. packages/backend/__tests__/) for AC annotations — only scans tests/ at repo root. This causes false 'uncovered trait AC' warnings in projects with monorepo structures. Need test_paths config or recursive scanning.

Plan derive does not carry implementation_notes from plan task definitions into the created task descriptions. Had to manually set descriptions on all 11 tasks after derive. The implementation_notes field in plan YAML is parsed but not mapped to task.description during derive.

SUGGESTION from PR #873: ws-invalidation module subscribes to topic 'tasks' but daemon broadcasts on 'tasks:updates'. Exact-match semantics in pubsub.ts means centralized WS invalidation for task/item/inbox queries never fires. Affects all TanStack Query migrated pages. Fix: align topic names between daemon broadcast and ws-invalidation subscribe.

Session detail page triggers HTTP polling (/events?since_seq=N) on every WebSocket text chunk (debounced 3s) even though text chunks are for live streaming only. HTTP refresh should only trigger on agent_invocation lifecycle events, not text chunks. Also session events use manual fetch, not TanStack Query — bypasses cache/dedup infrastructure.

Orphaned bun daemon processes from test runs — two root causes: (1) cli-serve.test.ts:583 installed-package test starts daemon in isolated temp root but stop is mid-test-body, not in afterEach; if test throws, daemon leaks since cleanupTempDir only deletes files, does not kill processes. (2) Auto-start pid path bug at src/cli/index.ts:121 — maybeAutoStartDaemon uses PidFileManager(kspecDir) but PidFileManager expects config dir, while serve start/stop use ~/.config/kspec, so auto-start checks wrong pid file and can spawn duplicates. E2E fixture (test-base.ts:217) is safe — it stops in teardown.

Plan lint command (kspec plan lint) — semantic diagnostics for plan documents: spec-task coverage gaps, dependency validity, orphan specs, priority inversions. Standalone for draft review, also callable from plan import --dry-run. Dry-run stays focused on import mechanics (what gets created), lint focuses on plan quality (is this well-structured).

Shadow branch commit messages could carry richer detail for auditability — e.g. field names changed in task-set, old/new status in transitions, review verdict details in review-verdict-task-transition. Currently most operations use minimal messages like 'task-set @ref' or 'Start @ref' without capturing what actually changed. This would make the git log -based activity timeline more informative and reduce the need to diff YAML to understand what happened. Separate effort from the ref consistency fix — this is about enriching content, not fixing missing refs. Consider a spec under @trait-shadow-commit or a new requirement for structured commit messages with field-level change details.

Plan text drifts from reality after post-derive edits to specs/tasks via CLI. Options: (1) stop storing raw YAML after derive and reconstruct via plan export from bound specs/tasks, (2) allow text-only updates to active plans, (3) plan export --regenerate that rebuilds the YAML sections from current spec/task state. The derive-is-final design is intentional — the question is how to keep the plan artifact useful as a reference after specs/tasks evolve independently.

Plan working files should use .kspec/artifacts/ (ephemeral storage) instead of root plans/ directory. This avoids checkpoint hook flagging transient files as uncommitted changes. Update /kspec:plan skill to reference .kspec/artifacts/ as the working directory for plan import/export workflows.

Test runner (scripts/test.cjs) should default to writing full log to a temp file and showing lighter output (errors only + summary). Full log available for analysis without rerunning. Currently agents rerun the full suite multiple times with different reporter flags to find failures, which wastes minutes each time.

Refactor parseDiffChanges to YAML-parse diff sides instead of regex matching. Current regex approach treats nested map fields (e.g. submission_linkage.branch) as top-level fields, producing noisy activity entries. Fix: strip diff markers, collect before/after lines, YAML parse both sides, deep-diff the parsed objects. Gives proper nesting awareness, correct array handling, type-aware values. Could also link to task schema field definitions for deterministic typed handlers. yaml library already available.

Add integration test for @task-activity-timeline ac-3 (review events merged inline chronologically). Requires a test that creates a task, creates a review record linked to it, and verifies review events appear in the activity timeline output. Flagged during review of @task-implement-activity-display — the most complex part of the implementation lacks dedicated test coverage.

Dispatch engine pause mode — a pause button that lets in-flight agent invocations finish but prevents the engine from spawning new ones. Unlike stop (which drains everything), pause would hold the queue while active work completes gracefully. Useful for operator intervention without losing in-progress work.

Skill render pipeline requires non-obvious build step — editing templates/skills/ does not propagate to .agents/skills/ until npm run build + kspec skill install-core + kspec skill render --force. Consider having render detect stale templates or documenting the pipeline more visibly.

Plan reviewer skill: Create a /plan-review skill for two use cases: (1) Structured plan review before approval — evaluate problem diagnosis, spec change coverage, task completeness, dependency ordering, risk assessment. Currently done ad-hoc by spawning a general agent with manual instructions. A skill would standardize the review criteria and finding format. (2) Post-derive validation — verify derived tasks match the plan document: full descriptions transferred (not truncated), priorities set, spec_refs attached, depends_on graph correct, plan_ref bidirectionally linked, automation eligibility set. The validation agent in this session checked structural properties (exists, priority, deps) but missed that task descriptions were truncated summaries instead of the full what/why/how from the plan. The skill should diff plan task content against derived task descriptions to catch this class of issue.

Additional failure mode from @plan-dispatch-integration-checkout-boundaries: post-derive review approved a task that merely restated plan/spec design work ('Design shared-checkout integration branch contract') instead of producing executable implementation work. Add kspec plan patch command — plans are not patchable via any CLI command. item patch rejects plan-specific fields (derived_tasks, module_ref, etc.) as unknown keys. Root cause confirmed (2026-04-17): resetCommandTree in src/cli/batch-exec.ts:640 wipes Commander _optionValues between batch dispatches, which removes the defaults Commander applied during option parsing (--priority "3", --type "task"). Repro: echo ´[{"command":"task add","args":{"title":"x"}}]´ | kspec batch. Workaround: explicitly pass priority and type in batch args. Also noted: batch --dry-run does NOT exercise action paths — it passes even when real execution will crash.

Daemon freeze is a bun runtime deadlock (oven-sh/bun#26762), not FD exhaustion. All threads end up in futex_wait with zero CPU — event loop stops polling epoll entirely. Root cause: lock ordering violation between GeneralPurposeAllocator and thread pool drain mechanism. Reported on bun 1.3.5, still open with unmerged fix PRs (#28026, #28104, #28245). We're on 1.3.6, latest is 1.3.11. Upgrading won't fix the deadlock but picks up related stability fixes (inotify hot loop fix in 1.3.9, event loop improvements in 1.3.10). Options: upgrade bun, add health check watchdog that restarts daemon on unresponsive, switch daemon to node, or wait for bun fix to merge.

Investigate: loadWorkspaceRecordForWorktreeRoot returns undefined when workspace record exists. During dispatch re-provisioning after task unblock (blocked -> pending_review), the record lookup in provisionDispatchWorkspace fails to find an existing workspace record despite the record being present in project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml on the shadow branch. Direct Node.js testing of the same lookup (initContext + loadDispatchWorkspaceRegistry + filter) succeeds. Likely candidates: (1) race between periodic _reconcile (which acquires shadowMutex and writes to registry via reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry) and _spawnInvocation (which reads registry via provisionDispatchWorkspace without shadowMutex), (2) shadow sync timing causing stale reads during context initialization, (3) concurrent file writes from withFileLock in saveDispatchWorkspaceRecord leaving a transient partial state. Observed in hawse project with task-proposal-lifecycle — workaround was repairing submission_linkage so the adoption fallback path used the correct branch instead of depending on the record lookup.

Test daemons should self-terminate when their spawning test process dies. Currently any 'kspec serve start --detach' from a test is detached + unref'd, so when the vitest worker is SIGKILLed, OOM-killed, times out, or otherwise exits abnormally, the daemon survives and gets reparented to PID 1. Proposal: when a daemon is started for tests (e.g., env flag KSPEC_DAEMON_PARENT_PID=$$ or KSPEC_DAEMON_TEST_MODE=1), it polls kill(parentPid, 0) every N seconds and self-exits cleanly when the parent disappears. Real user 'kspec serve start --detach' invocations don't set the flag and behave unchanged. Bulletproof against SIGKILL because the daemon kills itself rather than relying on signal propagation. Complements but doesn't replace afterEach cleanup — this is the safety net for the abnormal-termination paths.

kspec plan get --json shape is unclear for plan→task lookup. Tried jq paths .tasks[] (errored) and .derived_tasks[] (errored) before falling back to filtering kspec task list --json by plan_ref. Two paths to consider: (1) document the plan get --json response shape clearly, or (2) add a kspec plan tasks @plan subcommand that returns all tasks bidirectionally linked to the plan (via plan_ref OR derived_from). Reduces friction for any what-is-in-this-plan lookup.

Reviewer agent scope guardrail: when asking a review agent to check N specific changes, also ask whether there are unrelated lint/format issues in the same files. Vitest globalSetup orphan-daemon reaper. Belt-and-suspenders defense against test daemon leaks if @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup's per-test cleanup misses something OR a vitest worker is killed by SIGKILL/OOM/Ctrl+C before its onTestFinished registrations run. Reaper would scan ps at session start and teardown, identifying daemons whose --kspec-dir is a deleted tempdir under os.tmpdir() matching helper prefixes (kspec-test-, kspec-multi-, kspec-e2e-). Only build if Task A's per-test cleanup AND inbox @01KNT3GG (parent-watchdog mode) prove insufficient. Cross-platform considerations: macOS BSD ps argv truncation (use ps -ww or /proc/pid/cmdline on Linux); concurrent runs across vitest projects (default + heavy-serial both invoke globalSetup, must be safe to run twice); never killing user daemons (match only deleted tempdirs with known test prefixes); SIGKILL+TIME_WAIT port reuse race. Don't build until evidence of recurring leaks after Task A and watchdog land. Related: @01KKSGTN (original report), @01KNT3GG (parent-watchdog idea), @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup, @task-lint-rule-test-daemon-cleanup.

Test suite duration is too long and trending worse — needs investigation and either optimization or accurate documentation. The reality: heavy-serial integration tests in tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts take 6-20 SECONDS each, with 38 tests in that file alone. tests/integration.test.ts has 193 tests, tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts has 141, all run serially. As more tests are added, the situation degrades further.

Two parallel concerns to triage:
(a) IMMEDIATE: Update kspec-agents.md with measured baseline timings (default project, heavy-serial project, full suite) and remove the misleading ~150s claim. Small doc fix.
(b) STRUCTURAL: Investigate whether the slowest tests can be optimized — most heavy-serial tests run real git operations and CLI subprocesses. Are they using the most efficient path? Can the worst offenders be parallelized within the heavy-serial group? Should some tests be re-categorized as 'really slow' and run only in CI / on-demand? Is there a faster fixture setup pattern that could shave time off CLI-subprocess-heavy tests? Bigger investigation, may require tradeoffs between coverage and speed.

User framing: 'The fact it takes that long is an issue and needs to be addressed, obviously there's only so much you can do with so many tests, but it taking that long and only to go longer with more tests is a problem.' Tags: testing, performance, infra, dx

Unify the three daemon-spawn paths under a single helper. Currently three call sites spawn the same dist/daemon/index.js binary with three different lifecycle contracts: src/cli/commands/serve.ts:366 (--detach mode: detached+unref+stdio:ignore), src/cli/index.ts:194 (auto-start: detached+unref+stdio:ignore), tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts:324 (e2e fixture: non-detached, parented in process group, child handle retained for explicit teardown). The asymmetry is the structural enabler of the daemon leak class fixed by @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup — three implementations of the same operation with three different cleanup contracts.

Proposal: extract a single spawnKspecDaemon(opts) helper that encodes the lifecycle contract explicitly:
- opts.lifecycle: 'detached' | 'parented'
- opts.cleanupHook: required when lifecycle === 'parented' (returns the child process handle)
- opts.runtime, opts.port, opts.kspecDir, opts.env: existing args
- Helper enforces: detached implies unref+stdio:ignore; parented implies child handle returned + caller must register cleanup

All three call sites migrate to use it. Production --detach behavior unchanged. Test fixtures get a single safe pattern. The architectural class of bug becomes structurally impossible because the unsafe-detached path doesn't exist outside one well-tested helper.

Should land AFTER @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup and @task-lint-rule-test-daemon-cleanup so the test refactor has a clean target. Highest-leverage long-term fix for daemon lifecycle. Related: @01KKSGTN, @01KNT3GG. Tags: daemon, refactor, infra

Add orphan daemon discovery to kspec doctor. On 2026-04-09 cleaning up 142 leaked daemons required ad-hoc pkill regex incantations because there's no CLI surface for finding orphan kspec daemon processes. @doctor-command (implemented) reports the registered daemon's health (PID alive, port responding) but does NOT scan the process table for daemon binaries that aren't tracked in any PID file or whose --kspec-dir points at a deleted path.

Proposal: add an 'orphan daemons' section to kspec doctor:
- Scan ps for processes whose binary path matches dist/daemon/index.js
- For each, parse --kspec-dir from argv
- Cross-check: is this daemon registered in any known PID file (HOME-scoped or project-scoped)? Does its --kspec-dir still exist on disk?
- Report orphans with PID, age, runtime (node/bun), and command-line
- Optional: --reap flag to SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL them with confirmation prompt
- Cross-platform: prefer /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux to avoid argv truncation; fall back to ps -ww on macOS

Plan derive topologicalSort should treat trait references as implicit ordering constraints. Currently it only sorts by parent, so if a spec declares traits: [@local-trait] and the trait is declared later in the same plan file, normalizeSpecTraits() falls back to the existing ref index and stores a raw unresolved ref. Fix: extend topological sort (src/cli/commands/plan.ts) to also consider trait refs pointing at same-plan specs as edges.

Test files are excluded from tsc --noEmit by tsconfig.json (exclude: **/*.test.ts), so test-helper API changes do not surface compile errors for missing required args. Options to explore: add tsconfig.test.json with include: [tests/**/*] wired into CI, or add a vitest typecheck step.

Consolidate setup scaffold state handling so setup scaffolds share one state file/helper instead of splitting defaults into .setup-state.json and the reflection hook into .setup-scaffold-state.json. Add an automated review/merge guard that detects task-branch conflation before approval or merge. This review snapshot for @task-scaffold-project-config contained unrelated commits and files from other tasks (test runner progress output, daemon cleanup linting, shadow worktree guard), and the blocker was only caught by manual git log/diff inspection. Consider adding `setup` (and possibly `agents generate`) to the `skipCommands` list in src/cli/index.ts:383 so `kspec setup` does not trigger `maybeAutoStartDaemon()`. Rationale: `setup` runs during project initialization, exits synchronously, and the spawned daemon then outlives the command that spawned it — three strikes against the side-effect. This is a production design question distinct from @task-tests-suppress-cli-auto-start-daemon (which only addresses the test leak by setting KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 by default in test helpers). Scope to think about before triaging: (1) does any other short-lived command in skipCommands already establish the precedent, (2) does skipping auto-start in `setup` break the first-run UX where users expect the daemon to be running by the end of setup, (3) should setup instead EXPLICITLY start the daemon at a known, idempotent point rather than relying on implicit auto-start at CLI entry. Surfaced during investigation of 4 blocked tasks on 2026-04-14.

Reviewer bootstrap failure should clean up the provisioned -review worktree before blocking the task (src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts:2504-2526 catch block for DispatchBootstrapError). Currently the catch notes + blocks + returns without calling safelyRemoveDispatchWorktree on the reviewer worktree that ensureReviewerWorktree just created. The next dispatch retry then hits assertPathSafeForWorktree (src/agent-runtime/workspace.ts:2088) and fails with 'already exists and is not a registered git worktree' as a cascading secondary error. Observed on all four 2026-04-14 blocked tasks — each had both [DISPATCH-BOOTSTRAP] AND [DISPATCH-WORKSPACE] errors concatenated in their block reason, where the second was caused by the first not cleaning up. Fix is small (one safelyRemoveDispatchWorktree call before the block) but it IS a behavior change and needs a spec-first check: @agent-dispatch-engine and @dispatch-workspace-registry are the likely homes for a new or amended AC ('on reviewer bootstrap failure, the reviewer workspace is cleaned up so a retry can provision fresh'). Triaging as inbox rather than task because the spec work to place the AC correctly is non-trivial and the current workaround — investigator kills the orphan dir manually — is survivable. Related: @task-bootstrap-failure-output-tail, @task-tests-suppress-cli-auto-start-daemon.

Extract skill orphan cleanup into shared library function. Currently duplicated between skill-diff.ts (--clean handler) and upgrade.ts (runRerenderSkillsStep). Existing projects that already have a scaffolded default-session-reflect hook without a turn-count filter will not be migrated automatically when the filter is added to setup: the scaffold skips hooks that already exist by name. Reviewer merge flow in detached snapshots should explicitly cover the case where the integration branch is already attached to another worktree and the task branch is already identical to the target branch. Fix cli-agent-commands test failures caused by /tmp/.kspec-sessions/ EACCES errors. 5 tests in cli-agent-commands.test.ts fail with 'EACCES: permission denied, mkdir /tmp/.kspec-sessions/<ULID>' from createSession() in src/sessions/store.ts. The /tmp/.kspec-sessions/ directory gets created with permissions that later test runs cannot write to (likely left by a root-owned or different-uid session). Impact: every npm test run in reviews surfaces 5 failing tests that are pre-existing/unrelated to the change under review, creating noise for reviewers and making it harder to tell whether new changes introduce regressions. Possible fixes: (1) isolate session storage to a test-scoped temp dir (createTempDir pattern) instead of sharing /tmp/.kspec-sessions/, (2) make the session store path configurable via env var and override in test setup, (3) use mode 0777 + os.tmpdir()/per-user subdir to avoid cross-user conflicts.
Add task- or ref-scoped AC coverage validation for review workflows so reviewers can surface invalid annotations in touched files without wading through repo-wide kspec validate debt.

`architecture` meta convention contains a literal PLACEHOLDER rule that gets rendered into kspec-agents.md on every `kspec agents generate`. Either populate it with real rules or remove it so unrelated tasks that regenerate agent docs do not carry cosmetic drift.

Narrow dispatch sync-target filter to exclude stale/closing/cleanup_blocked lifecycle states. The dispatch engine's active target set currently includes every workspace record whose lifecycle is not closed (per @dispatch-remote-branch-sync ac-active-target-rebuilt-on-start). Workspaces in stale, closing, or cleanup_blocked states — none of which can drive integration progress — still contribute their target branch to periodic target-sync fetches. Defense-in-depth: even after the cleanup-status transition bug (@task-persist-cleanup-completion-status) is fixed so records reach closed naturally, narrowing the filter to only provisioning/ready/active/integrating would prevent a recurrence of sync-noise if the cleanup path ever regresses. Triage surfaced this design question 2026-04-16 while investigating log spam from deleted plan branches still tracked in the registry.

Decide backfill approach for pre-fix stuck workspace records. Observed at triage time on 2026-04-16: 138 records stuck in closing, 252 records stuck in stale, 0 records in closed — all a consequence of the cleanup-completion transition bug tracked by @task-persist-cleanup-completion-status. After that fix lands, options for the pre-fix backlog: (a) let reconciliation self-heal them naturally over time (retention purge follows 7 days after closed state), (b) write a one-shot migration that transitions eligible records to completed in a single shadow commit, or (c) manual reconciliation of specific records as operators surface them. Needs a decision about operational risk (large shadow commit, data loss if heuristic is wrong) vs. convenience (immediate registry cleanup).

Dispatch workspace registry management — UI + CLI surface for operators to view, inspect, and repair workspace records without hand-editing project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml. Motivating scenarios: (a) daemon crash leaves a stale reviewer worktree record blocking dispatch with no self-service recovery path; (b) operators want to remove or purge stuck records (observed 2026-04-16: 138 records stuck in closing and 252 stuck in stale lifecycle states from the cleanup-completion transition bug tracked by @task-persist-cleanup-completion-status); (c) operators clean up dispatch or plan branches out-of-band via git branch -D or git push --delete, then need to close the referencing workspace record so the dispatch engine stops attempting to sync the deleted branch. Minimum CLI surface: list, inspect (get), remove/purge, close (force lifecycle to closed). Broader: reset bootstrap state, force re-provisioning, unblock cleanup_blocked records. Web UI: same operations surfaced through the dashboard. Related: @dispatch-workspace-registry. Consolidates prior inbox captures 01KKMJYM45E0CPNJVVXG66X2PZ (UI+CLI broader scope) and 01KMVSNV20CQ7WDSBJA4F602T1 (purge scope) and the session-2026-04-16 operator-close-after-out-of-band-branch-deletion scenario.

Clarify the 'no compound conditions' convention for acceptance criteria. The current spec-authoring guidance discourages compound conditions in Given/When/Then, but existing ACs in the codebase contain compound Givens — for example @dispatch-workspace-registry ac-14 bundles 'record exists for non-terminal task AND reconciliation determines workspace is unrecoverable AND all recovery paths have been attempted'. The rule needs an explicit decision: does 'no compound conditions' mean (a) one fact per Given/When/Then clause, with multiple Given lines acceptable to state independent preconditions, or (b) one fact per AC total? Either codify the chosen interpretation in the testing/writing-specs convention text, or retroactively refactor existing compound-Given ACs to match. Surfaced 2026-04-16 during AC authoring for @task-persist-cleanup-completion-status where the rule's interpretation affected how the draft ACs were structured.

Search guidance — multi-vocabulary reminder plus no-result hints. Two parts: (1) document in the triage/reflect/inbox-add workflows (and relevant kspec skills) that inbox and item searches should try 2-3 keyword variants since the same concept may have been captured at different times with different vocabulary, and include vocabulary-selection guidance (synonyms, partial words, related concepts); (2) enhance 'kspec search' itself to provide guidance on effective search, especially on zero-result responses — emit a short hint suggesting synonyms, partial-word matches, or related-concept searches, and optionally link to search docs or surface a short list of common variants. Surfaced 2026-04-16 after a duplicate inbox item was created during a reflection step: the duplicate topic had been captured twice before with different keywords than the ones searched, and the search commands returned no matches for the searched terms. The reflection skill explicitly warns against duplication but the search pattern used did not surface the prior captures.

When amending an AC (kspec item ac set) the CLI does not surface tests annotated to that AC that may now be stale. Encountered when amending ac-reflection-hook-present: the existing test assertion at tests/setup-reflection-hook.test.ts:108 codified the old wording and only a human review caught the drift. Options: (1) kspec item ac set warns with a list of annotated tests, (2) new kspec ac usages @spec ac-id command, (3) doctor check for AC annotations against recently-modified ACs.

Reflection: add a reviewer merge helper or documented workflow for detached review snapshots so approved work can merge into the integration branch even when the target branch is already checked out in another worktree.
Reflection: reduce prompt pressure from task notes by adding guidance or tooling to summarize large task-context dumps and agent failure payloads instead of storing them verbatim.

kspec batch --dry-run validates argv schema but does not exercise command action/init paths, so real execution can fail even after a clean dry-run (hit during @task-plan-delete-command creation 2026-04-17, see inbox 01KMV62W for the specific parsePriority crash). Options to investigate: (1) teach resetCommandTree in src/cli/batch-exec.ts:640 to preserve Commander default values (use _optionValueSources to distinguish defaults from cli/env inputs) so defaults survive between dispatches — this also fixes 01KMV62W at the root. (2) Minimum viable: add a caveat line to dry-run output that it is schema-only and does not guarantee execution success. Prefer (1) since it eliminates an entire class of silent failures.

Add --description-file <path> flag to kspec task add, item add, and similar commands that take long-form --description text. Mirrors the --content-file flag already on plan add. Eliminates JSON/shell-escaping pain for markdown descriptions (backticks, newlines, quotes) in both direct CLI use and kspec batch payloads. Noticed during @task-plan-delete-command creation where the what/why/how description was ~1200 words of markdown and required manual \n escaping plus backtick survival in the batch JSON.

Run CI Tests workflow on push to dev (or on a schedule) so race-conditional e2e bugs and accumulated lint drift surface before the next dev→main merge PR. Today dev only runs Tests on pull_request to main — regressions from 2026-04-04 (session-watcher active-scoping) sat undetected for 13 days until PR #913.

publish.yml and test.yml drifted (missing Setup Bun in publish caused v0.13.0 release failure). Investigate having publish.yml call/reuse the test.yml workflow directly, or extract a shared composite action, so the two cannot diverge. Triggered by v0.13.0 release; see PR #915 for the symptom fix.
Add file or stdin body input support for text-heavy CLI mutation commands such as review comment and review reply so multiline text and shell metacharacters do not require fragile shell quoting.

Plan writing skill should codify the decision-task anti-pattern: never draft tasks that 'evaluate and choose' something. The plan IS the decision artifact; tasks implement decisions, never make them. A task description containing 'evaluate', 'choose between', or 'decide X' is a smell — that design work belongs in Implementation Notes. Add this as an explicit anti-pattern rule in the plan-writing/spec-plan-design skill, with a before/after example.

Reference-quality example plans in skill folder. Plan-writing currently leans on the user naming exemplars ad-hoc (@plan-dispatch-event-system-expansion, @plan-task-storage-split-per-task-directory-architecture). Including 1-2 curated exemplar plans (or direct links to them) in the spec-plan-design / plan skill folder would give authors a concrete quality bar to match without the user having to point them at examples each time.

Improve the approved-merge workflow for detached review snapshots that cannot check out the integration branch because the target branch is already active in another worktree. The merge tooling or docs should support performing the required merge from the primary integration worktree instead of failing at git checkout.

Stabilize tests/test-runner.test.ts so nested runner invocations do not read stale shared _default cache results from earlier failed runs. Review-time reruns can currently fail spuriously because the assertion sees cached failed output instead of a fresh passing summary.

Strengthen docs rendering coverage so guide tests verify that each documented command points to the matching --help entry, not just that --help appears somewhere on the page. The current guides test suite let docs/guides/authoring-and-completing-a-task.md pair kspec derive with kspec task add --help, so AC-3 drift escaped until manual review. Candidate scope: extend tests/web-ui-docs-rendering.test.ts to associate command examples with nearby help references, or add a docs-specific assertion helper for command/help pairing.

AC-style convention needs three more facets beyond the existing 'no compound conditions' rule (see related inbox item about compound conditions interpretation): (1) Standalone — each AC must stand alone with no cross-references to other ACs in the same or other specs; a future reader of any AC should be able to understand its contract without following links. (2) Timeless — AC text must not contain implementation-specific identifiers (file paths, env var names, function names, library names, version numbers) because those rot as code evolves; such identifiers belong in task bodies and test fixtures, not in the spec contract. (3) Abstract class terms — when an AC governs a set of values (e.g. runtime mode configuration env variables), the AC names the class behaviorally ('runtime mode configuration values') rather than enumerating concrete members ('NODE_ENV, BUN_ENV'); the concrete list lives in test fixtures so adding a new class member does not require amending the AC. Surfaced 2026-04-21 during authoring of three new ACs on @dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract, where the user had to correct compound/cross-referencing/named-variable drafts across four revision cycles. Scope when triaged: codify these rules in the spec-authoring convention text so they are discoverable to authors and reviewers. Consider whether existing specs need a retroactive audit or whether going-forward-only is acceptable.

Gitignore backup files are not themselves gitignored. `ensureKspecGitignore` in `src/parser/gitignore.ts` creates a `.gitignore.backup-<timestamp>` sibling file when invoked with `--force` over an existing `.gitignore` that has no managed block (per `@trait-idempotent-file-scaffold ac-force-backs-up-before-overwrite`). The backup file sits at the project root and is not covered by the managed block the writer itself creates, so if ever written it would appear as untracked content and could slip into a commit. Likely not triggered in common flows but violates `@complete-auto-gitignore ac-no-untracked-after-common-commands` under the force path. Fix scope: either extend `buildKspecGitignoreEntries` to emit a `.gitignore.backup-*` pattern, or have the backup writer place the backup inside an already-ignored directory (e.g. `.kspec/backups/`). Surfaced 2026-04-21 during review of the `.lock/` gitignore fix task.

Reflection: /kspec:reflect guidance says to use 'kspec workflow show' without a run ref, but in this session the CLI returned 'missing required argument run-ref'. Align the reflect workflow/skill docs with the actual CLI, or make workflow show infer the only active run like run-ref-optional workflow commands do.

Validation API types can drift from parser validation warnings: parser CompletenessWarning now includes invalid_ac_annotation and invalid annotation subtypes, but packages/shared/src/api.ts and packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts still expose older CompletenessWarningType/subtype unions. Batch review check commands should preserve optional check intent. During review @01KQ117X, using kspec batch with review check args required:false still created a required check, so known non-blocking kspec validate evidence temporarily failed the review gate until rerun with direct --no-required.

Bug: kspec upgrade/setup scaffolds default-session-reflect without the turn_count filter required for once-per-invocation reflection. Known-good projects have filter {"turn_count":1}; comfy-ecaj-nodes after upgrade had no filter. Fix fresh scaffold to include filter {"turn_count":1}, and consider migrating an existing default-session-reflect hook that is missing the filter when it appears unmodified/default. Relevant spec: @default-session-reflection-hook ac-fires-once-per-invocation.

kspec validate/doctor should flag risky session.idle hooks whose session_prompt action depends on an agent session staying alive but the target agent lacks explicit session.idle_grace_period_ms or uses a grace period too short for post-idle actions. The warning should point at the hook, the affected default/dispatch agents, and the current effective grace so projects do not silently lose reflection prompts with errors like 'Session ... is no longer active'.

Session reflection loop baseline discovery should avoid unbounded full-list commands in mature repos. The current step instructs agents to run kspec meta observations list, kspec inbox list, and kspec tasks list before identifying reflection items; in this session those produced thousands of lines of output, consuming context and making duplicate-checking harder. Consider changing the workflow/skill to use targeted searches plus bounded summaries, or add list filters/limits suitable for reflection duplicate checks.

Clarify detached reviewer snapshot shadow-state expectations: reviewer docs/instructions should note that .kspec may not be present as a normal filesystem worktree in detached snapshots, and reviewers should use kspec CLI/review commands rather than direct git -C .kspec inspection.

Update the kspec PR/task review skill so reviewers inspect the source plan when a task was derived from a plan, using it for whole-scope context, dependency/sequence understanding, design-validation sources, and deliberate-deviation checks instead of reviewing only the isolated task text. Guidance should explain how reviewers discover the plan ref from task metadata/notes, when plan context is required vs optional, and how to read root-checkout artifacts (for example gitignored plans/design handoffs) when detached review worktrees do not contain them.

Update session reflection workflow examples to match current workflow CLI syntax. In this session, `kspec workflow show` returned "missing required argument run-ref" while the reflect instructions show it without a run ref; examples should show `kspec workflow show <run-ref>` and `kspec workflow next <run-ref> --notes ...` or explain when the ref can be omitted.

Normalize JSON output field naming across CLI: trait list --json uses camelCase (acceptanceCriteria) while item list --json uses snake_case (acceptance_criteria). Programmatic consumers must handle both conventions. Pick one convention and apply consistently.

Moved from Hawse inbox 01KQCD0J: Add a review helper or kspec command to record a standard set of passing review checks in one operation after the commands have run (fmt, diff check, validate, targeted tests, workspace tests, no-std, clippy), reducing eight repeated kspec review check commands per clean review.

Moved from Hawse inbox 01KQDB0Y: `kspec review reply --resolve` flag (or a single `kspec review address` subcommand) — replying to and resolving a thread are almost always paired in fix-cycle workflow, so doing them as separate commands × N threads doubles the CLI calls. Moved from Hawse inbox 01KQE02T1M: Consider adding cargo fmt --all --check and/or git diff --check to the standard review gates, or document why formatting checks are intentionally optional; this review found rustfmt and trailing-blank-line drift after required gates passed.

Reconcile @task-daemon-startup-bind-host-metadata (01KQWZZHH1) and @task-centralize-cli-daemon-clients (01KQWZZHTB) against the fix-cycle commit on @task-shared-daemon-endpoint-resolver (d64e038c3). Daemon IPv6 fallback path patches globalThis.URL during app.listen() to work around an @elysiajs/node bug at node_modules/@elysiajs/node/dist/cjs/index.js:906 where it constructs new URL(`http://${hostname}:${port}`) without bracketing IPv6 hosts. When the upstream bug is fixed (or we replace the @elysiajs/node adapter), the polyfill in packages/daemon/src/server.ts can be deleted. Triage decision: track as known-workaround task or close as wontfix.

Add --file or stdin support to kspec task note for multi-line bodies. Currently agents and humans must shell-escape or use intermediate env vars to set multi-line note bodies — common in fix-cycle summary notes. A --file <path> flag (matching kspec batch --file) or stdin support would eliminate the workaround.

Tooling: when a fix-cycle review on task X expands to implement work nominally scoped to dependent task Y, surface this absorption to the downstream worker. Options: (a) add a `kspec task scope-absorbed-by @X` note on Y, (b) extend `kspec task get` to flag commits that touch Ys spec ACs but were authored under @X, (c) extend kspec review submit to ask reviewers if their requested fixes overlap with downstream task scope. Reduces wasted scoping effort on downstream tasks. Scope: medium.

Tooling: surface in `kspec task get` (or `kspec validate`) when a tasks spec ACs already have behavioral test coverage annotated under a different task ULID. Helps a worker quickly see what AC work is residual annotation work vs net-new coverage. Scope: small.

Document daemon test pattern: when asserting on daemon-process behavior (exits, lifecycle file writes, error output), spawn dist/daemon/index.js directly with spawn() rather than going through kspec serve start --detach. The CLI-mediated path adds parent-polling timing the test does not control and has been observed to wedge spawnSync for 30+ seconds on startup-failure paths. See tests/cli-serve.test.ts "does NOT write connection metadata when listen() fails on EADDRINUSE" for an example.

Document or expose the kspec() test-helper KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 default. Daemon-endpoint tests must override with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON="" — easy to miss. Options: (a) add a comment in tests/helpers/cli.ts where the default is set, (b) add a kspecWithDaemon() wrapper that flips the default. Small.

Reflection: Add an automated guard for test-only exports from production src modules. The review of @task-daemon-endpoint-regression-tests caught an explicit _postDispatchEvent test-only export manually via work-gates, while existing observation @01KQZ6JZ recommends that same pattern. Update the kspec-reflect skill workflow command examples so commands that require a workflow run reference include one, especially changing 'kspec workflow show' to 'kspec workflow show @run-ref'. Reflection currently leads agents to run the documented no-argument command first, which fails with 'missing required argument run-ref'.

AC validator silently ignores annotation-shaped text inside JSDoc/block comments. The kspec-agents convention says line comments only, but when an agent places '// AC: @spec ac-N'-shaped lines inside a /** ... */ JSDoc header, the validator drops them — no coverage credit, no warning. This caused a direct fix-cycle bounce on @task-implement-shared-daemon-test-fixture (cycle 2): two ACs in the task's Covers set appeared in the test file's docstring header, validation reported them uncovered, reviewer flagged the discrepancy. Proposed fix: extend @ac-annotation-integrity-reporting (or @test-annotation-sweep) to detect AC-shaped patterns inside block comments and emit an invalid-annotation finding so silent docstring placement becomes loud. Scope: small — same scanner already walks files; needs a block-comment context check.

Shared daemon test fixture probeHealth/probeCacheReady fetch calls have no per-fetch timeout. When a port is pre-bound by a non-HTTP TCP listener (e.g. blocker server in EADDRINUSE regression tests), fetch connects, sends an HTTP request, and hangs forever waiting for a response that never comes. waitForStartup's outer timeout never fires because the await is inside fetch(). Concrete repro: I hit this migrating tests/cli-serve.test.ts EADDRINUSE; the test timed out at vitest's default 45s. Workaround was to switch the test to a custom child-exit probe, but that escape hatch only works if the test author knows the default probe will hang. Fix: wrap probeHealth and probeCacheReady fetch() calls in AbortController bounded by intervalMs (or a small per-fetch budget like DIAGNOSTIC_SAMPLE_TIMEOUT_MS) so the readiness loop's timeout is honored end-to-end.

Shared daemon test fixture (tests/helpers/daemon.ts) returns started.wsUrl with the /ws path suffix already appended (ws://host:port/ws). Existing E2E test helpers (api-watcher.spec.ts:109, api-triage.spec.ts:98) treat fixture.wsUrl as a BASE url and append /ws themselves. The Playwright wrapper has to strip the suffix to keep both sides happy. Decide which contract is canonical — either (a) document that started.wsUrl is the full ws path and update test helpers to stop appending /ws, or (b) split started.wsUrl into wsBaseUrl + wsPath so each consumer picks the shape it wants. Future consumers (mock-daemon fixtures, in-process route fixtures) will hit this same friction.

tests/helpers/cli.ts is consumed by both vitest (CJS-transpiled) and Playwright (loads .ts as native ESM because package.json type=module). The original CLI_PATH/FIXTURES_DIR used the bareword __dirname which is undefined under ESM, so the Playwright fixture migration crashed at module load. Fixed in tests/helpers/cli.ts with the typeof __dirname + import.meta.url polyfill that tests/helpers/daemon.ts already used. Audit the rest of tests/helpers/ (and any other shared test module) for the same CJS-only assumption before more Playwright fixtures consume them.

Investigate whether oxlint JS plugins expose a scope manager (context.sourceCode.getScope or equivalent) and, if so, refactor tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js to drop the manual parent-walking + position-comparison machinery (recordBinding/findApplicableBinding/functionScopeShadowsName, ~120 LOC). Surfaced during fix cycle 2 of @task-enforce-daemon-test-fixture-usage when the file-global Set was replaced with hand-rolled scope tracking. Scope: small investigation, refactor size depends on API availability.

Optimize tests/lint-no-leaky-test-daemon.test.ts and tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts to avoid per-case npx oxlint subprocess overhead. Current cost ~250ms/case × ~62 cases = ~14s for the focused suite, scaling linearly as the rule and its tests grow. Options: in-process oxlint invocation if exposed, or batched fixtures with line-numbered violation assertions per oxlint run. Lower priority than the scope-manager refactor.

kspec validate has no way to scope verification to the current change. When adding new AC annotations, the validate output is dominated by pre-existing warnings in unrelated files (19 invalid annotations in this run) — verifying that NEW annotations resolve cleanly requires manual grep + spec lookup. Possible approaches: a --since/--paths filter, --new-only that diffs against base, or a per-file annotations report. Surfaced while adding 7 new AC annotations across 2 files in @task-add-real-daemon-startup-failure-tests.

Improve task submit/review flow to surface linked-spec AC coverage gaps. During this review, full tests passed but kspec validate showed the task's linked spec @daemon-test-guardrail-precision still had missing own AC annotations. A focused check for the task's spec_ref during submission or review creation would help workers catch task-relevant coverage gaps without manually filtering repository-wide validation warnings.

Validate command should understand cross-branch AC coverage delegation. Today, kspec validate on branch A reports ACs as uncovered if their annotations only exist on a sibling dispatch branch B that hasn't merged yet. This produces review blockers on otherwise-correct work whenever a spec's AC coverage is intentionally split across sibling tasks (a common dispatch pattern). Possible angles: validate flag like --include-pending-branches that reads sibling branches for coverage; per-task scoped validate that only checks the ACs the task explicitly covers; or a task field that declares which ACs the task is responsible for vs which are delegated. Out-of-scope ideas welcome — needs triage to settle the right shape.

Fix stale npm script: package.json:57 'test:e2e:smoke' invokes Playwright on tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts and tests/e2e/api-server.spec.ts, but api-server.spec.ts was deleted in commit 8f281707c (migrated to vitest) without updating the script. Anyone running 'npm run test:e2e:smoke' gets a missing-file error. Fix: drop the api-server.spec.ts reference from line 57, or replace with another Playwright spec representative of the smoke surface (e.g. tests/e2e/connection.spec.ts). Discovered while looking for a Playwright daemon-fixture slice to run for @task-fix-real-daemon-startup-failure-handling.

Consolidate AMBIENT_DAEMON_CONTROL_VARS into a single exported list in tests/helpers/cli.ts and import it from tests/helpers/daemon.ts and tests/helpers/mock-daemon.ts. Today the two helpers each maintain their own copy — daemon.ts has 6 keys, mock-daemon.ts has 8 (adds KSPEC_DAEMON_API_URL/WS_URL twins). Drift is plausible and silent: a future addition could land in only one helper, leaving one path leaky. Consolidation also forces a deliberate decision on the canonical set (do the URL twins belong everywhere?). Small refactor.

Allow `item ac set/update` and `item ac remove` in `kspec batch`. Currently only `item ac add` is batchable, so a task that tightens an existing acceptance criterion (revising given/when/then text) cannot atomically combine the AC revision with other mutations like `item set --status` or `item note`. Tasks that revise rather than add ACs would have to split into multiple shadow commits, breaking the atomic-tightening pattern this session used (and which the daemon-test hardening tightening would have needed if the existing ACs had to be reworded instead of supplemented).

Audit and bound real-daemon test fetches with AbortSignal.timeout. tests/cli-serve.test.ts (lines 1070, 1107, 1336, 1547) and likely tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts use raw fetch() against daemon apiUrls without timeouts — same pattern that caused the daemon-build smoke 180s silent-hang fixed in @01KR76BQ. When a daemon binds but stops responding mid-request, these probes hang until the outer vitest timeout, producing no actionable diagnostics. Same fix pattern (boundedFetch + daemon stdout/stderr tail dump) should be applied across daemon-backed test suites or extracted to a shared test helper.

Investigate deterministic tests/cli-no-daemon.test.ts failure: 'KSPEC_NO_DAEMON auto-starts the daemon with the configured node runtime even when the CLI runs under bun' fails because ps -p <pid> -o command= exits 1 after the auto-started daemon PID has already disappeared. Triage whether this is an environment-sensitive test race, daemon lifecycle regression, or pre-existing failure before promoting to a task.

Reflection: align workflow show docs with CLI run-ref requirement. During session reflection, the skill examples said to run kspec workflow show without a run ref, but the CLI returned missing required argument run-ref. Triage whether to update the reflection skill command examples to include the run ref, or make workflow show default to the sole active workflow run.

Add focused task/spec AC coverage reporting for reviewers. Given a task ref, resolve its spec_ref, list own and inherited ACs, and report which AC IDs have annotations plus which are missing, so review does not require manual rg scans against project-wide validation noise.

Promote unresolved friction @01KRFQ3T (vi.spyOn mockRestore clears mock.calls) into a testing convention rule. Recurrence: a second incident occurred during fix cycle 1 of @task-gate-cleanup-preservation-diagnostics (2026-05-19) — a worker added a behavioral-looking test that read debugSpy.mock.calls after mockRestore, which silently passed regardless of production behavior; reviewer caught it. Review workflow friction: full npm test is required before approval, but in this clean detached-review cycle it took 2334.8s after the targeted cleanup/registry suites had already passed. Investigate whether review workflows can better use test-runner cache, sharding, or prior verification summaries while preserving the full-suite gate.

Reviewer workflow gap: when required full-suite testing fails on an unrelated/pre-existing test, reviewers currently hand-assemble the triage evidence. A helper or workflow step could accept the failed npm test log plus reviewed base/head, rerun or record the focused failing suite, check whether related paths changed in the reviewed diff, create/reference a follow-up task, and emit suggested review checks/evidence text that separates the raw full-suite result from the branch regression classification.

Investigate daemon read-model/source-of-truth split-brain for task status. During manual validation completion for @task-validate-daemon-dispatch-oom-hardening-slice, direct metadata via KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 kspec task get showed status completed while daemon API /api/tasks/task-validate-daemon-dispatch-oom-hardening-slice?projectPath=/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec still returned status in_progress. Preserve this as an investigation item: reproduce without restarting/changing daemon state, identify whether watcher/entity-cache/shadow sync missed the completion update, and propose a safe cache invalidation or read-model refresh fix.

Investigate invalid derived task priority handling in plan derivation. During derivation of @plan-folder-backed-plans-reviews-and-local-resources, the approved plan contained generated task priorities 6/7 even though the task schema only allows 1-5. `kspec plan derive` failed on the schema violation after partially materializing derived refs, which required manual cleanup/re-import before a successful derive. Desired follow-up: make derive validate all generated task payloads before writing any derived metadata, produce a clear error that points at the offending plan task priority and allowed range, and avoid partial refs/aliases when derivation fails. Reproduce in a disposable project/copy only; do not run migration/upgrade experiments against live kynetic-spec or kynetic-spec-dispatch clones.

Review quality gates should include npm run format:check, preferably before the long full npm test run, so submitted tasks fail fast on formatter issues and reviewers do not spend a full test-suite cycle before discovering a mechanical merge blocker.

Improve the detached reviewer merge path so missing integration-target worktrees do not require manual git worktree setup. In this review, the supported helper refused to merge because plan/plan-folder-backed-plans-reviews-and-local-resources/01ks8mmw was not checked out anywhere; the reviewer had to inspect git worktree list, create a target worktree manually, then rerun the helper. Consider either teaching the helper to create/reuse a deterministic target worktree when absent, or having dispatch/bootstrap prepare the integration target worktree before reviewer merge. Include tests for the missing-target-worktree path plus existing dirty/conflict/no-op gates.

Update web UI files:updates invalidation for folder-backed plan/review sidecar paths. packages/web-ui/src/lib/query/ws-invalidation.ts currently maps project.plans.yaml and project.reviews.yaml but not plans/<ulid>/... or reviews/<ulid>/... direct file watcher refs. Audit other multi-step kspec CLI pipelines (setup, init, scaffold steps) for the per-step commitIfShadow pattern that fix(upgrade): make plan/review/manifest storage migration atomic (6cd0bb4dbb) just removed from upgrade.ts. The pattern is risky for any sequence of logically-coupled mutations: a later failure leaves the shadow branch with the earlier steps already committed. Canonical fix is to wrap related steps in a single runWithBuffer scope with one commitIfShadow after flush.

Reflection-loop baseline commands are too noisy for large projects. The session-reflect-loop workflow currently requires unbounded 'kspec meta observations list', 'kspec inbox list', and 'kspec tasks list'; in a real review session these produced thousands of lines and truncated output, making duplicate checking expensive. Improve the workflow or CLI with concise/recent/scoped list modes for reflection baseline checks, or change the workflow to use targeted kspec search plus bounded summaries.

Improve the detached reviewer merge helper so it can auto-provision or reuse a dedicated integration-target worktree when the target branch is not checked out. During review of @01KS8XAYZTG0MN48Z78D45PBV6 the supported helper refused with that condition, and recovery required manually creating /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch/.kspec-worktrees/merge-target-plan-folder-storage-01ks8mmw before rerunning the helper. Scope: kspec-merge helper worktree management and tests/docs.
Add a reviewer-oriented changed-file lint gate or script that compares against the review base and records clean evidence when full npm run lint has pre-existing failures.
Add a reusable scratch-project reproduction helper for reviewers testing CLI edge cases, so setup for temp kspec projects does not require ad hoc Node scripts.

kspec review get text output should surface thread ULIDs alongside each thread header. Currently the text mode shows '[blocker] src/foo.ts:N (M entries)' but omits the thread ULID, so replying with 'kspec review reply --thread <ulid>' forces a detour through 'kspec review get --json | jq ...'. Hit during the fix cycle on @01KS8XAZQ5478RV2AVKG8MNB0S — I tried entry ULIDs from the JSON entries[] array first and got 'Thread not found' before realising entries and threads have separate ULIDs. Either include the thread ULID in the text header, or accept entry ULIDs in 'review reply --thread'.

When implementing plan-resource static-mode URL building in @task-plan-resource-api-ui-static, route the static href/src through the shared encodeStaticAssetPath helper (packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts) and add a behavioral test covering a resource path with # / ?. Detached reviewer merge helper gap: when the integration target branch is not checked out in any worktree, the helper fails before attempting the merge and requires the reviewer to create/check out a target worktree manually. Existing @detached-reviewer-merge-helper ACs cover only the precondition where the target branch is already checked out. Consider either having dispatch prepare the target worktree, having the helper create/manage a clean temporary target worktree when absent, or updating reviewer guidance with the supported recovery path.

kspec review resource list/get/remove subcommands omit --json from their per-subcommand help, while kspec plan resource list/get/remove all expose --json. Either align review-resource subcommands with @trait-json-output by adding --json per-subcommand (matching plan-resource), or document the deliberate divergence.

Update manual_merge detached reviewer role guidance: the prompt observed during @task-rework-detached-reviewer-merge-helper-ephemeral-target still said the merge helper handles occupied-worktree refresh automatically, but the new helper contract refuses occupied integration-target checkouts and tells reviewers to free/detach the blocking checkout before rerunning. kspec validate alignment flags intentional status regressions (implemented → in_progress) as mismatches when a spec is deliberately tightened with new ACs not yet proven by implementation evidence. The @plan-folder-backed-index-consistency-hardening flow will trigger this repeatedly. Consider: a way to mark a status downgrade as intentional pending contract work (e.g., a `pending_evidence` substate, a per-AC implementation marker, or a validate ignore-pattern), or document the expected-warning pattern.

Add `kspec plan note remove <plan-ref> <note-ulid>` CLI command, symmetric to `plan note <ref> <text>`. Routes through mutatePlanAtomically so the index notes_count stays in sync. Discovered while writing folder-index-consistency red tests: parser-level tests can clear notes via savePlan({notes:[]}) but there is no CLI path, which forces tests/users to go through the storage manager API for the symmetric operation.

Bug: kspec skill render and skill install-core copy file content but drop the source file mode, so executable scripts (e.g. templates/skills/merge/scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh at 100755) become 100644 in rendered .agents/skills/<id>/scripts/ and .factory/skills/<id>/scripts/ output. Reproducible: chmod +x source script, run kspec skill install-core --force + kspec skill render --force, observe rendered copy is 0644. Locations: copyDirRecursive at src/cli/commands/skill-install.ts:180 and copyDirectory at src/parser/skill-render.ts:552 both go through fs.readFile + writeFileBufferAware with no fs.chmod or fs.copyFile-with-mode call. Discovered during fix cycle for @task-merge-helper-clean-occupied-target-checkout — had to manually chmod +x after regenerating rendered helper. Fix scope: have both copy helpers fstat the source and apply source mode to the destination (or switch to fs.copyFile which preserves mode by default). Likely needs an AC under @platform-renderer-trait/@skill-rendering for executable bit preservation on supporting scripts.

Friction: kspec skill install-core (getTemplatesDir at src/cli/commands/skill-install.ts:123) resolves templates via import.meta.dirname relative to the running binary, so when dogfooding the kspec repo with the globally-installed kspec binary it silently reads the published v0.14.0 templates from /home/.../node_modules/@kynetic-ai/spec/templates/skills/ instead of the local checkout templates/skills/. The command still reports Updated: 13 skill(s) so it looks successful, but local template changes never reach .kspec/skills/ or downstream rendered output. This caused the prior submission on @task-merge-helper-clean-occupied-target-checkout to ship a stale .agents/skills/kspec-merge/scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh and block the review. The workaround is npm run dev -- skill install-core. Possible mitigations: (a) detect when CWD is the kspec source repo and use local templates/, (b) add a --templates-dir flag, (c) warn/error when getTemplatesDir resolves outside the project root being targeted, (d) document the dogfooding workflow in AGENTS.md.

Update detached-reviewer merge helper recovery guidance for auxiliary/unsafe occupied target checkouts to include copy-paste-safe non-cd commands such as git -C <path> checkout --detach. During review of @01KSREGBX83KKDC7JPSPCKNWQ9, the helper correctly refused a clean auxiliary dev checkout but printed cd-based recovery guidance, while reviewer prompts require commands to run from the assigned workspace.

Reviewer and merge completion guidance should mention kspec task complete --no-sync for tasks that intentionally leave linked specs in_progress, and should tell reviewers to verify linked spec implementation status after completion for spec-only or reopened-contract tasks.

Reformat templates/skills/merge/SKILL.md to satisfy oxfmt --check (file last touched in 80bb7c7c22 'docs: update merge skill for branch-coherent helper' on dev; every downstream task currently skips the format:check gate for this single unrelated file). Derive KNOWN_EVENT_FIELDS (src/agent-runtime/action-executor.ts) from the payload schemas in src/schema/event-payloads.ts instead of hand-maintaining parallel sets. Add or document file-based payload support for kspec review comment bodies and review check evidence, so reviewers can avoid shell quoting issues when recording long markdown or command text.

Review the full-suite requirement for review cycles after a confirmed blocker: consider guidance for when cached or CI evidence is sufficient before request_changes, while preserving full-suite gates before approval and merge.

Detached reviewer orientation should report when the dispatch-provided integration target commit is stale relative to the current target tip, including the current target tip, merge-base used for task-specific review, and concise current-target..snapshot changed-file summary so reviewers do not accidentally review dependency-inclusive diffs.

Consider adding a reusable runner CLI fixture/reproduction helper. Web UI svelte-check has a pre-existing 61-error/5-warning baseline across unrelated files, which makes npm --prefix packages/web-ui run check unusable as a hard review gate for focused Svelte UI work. Fix or quarantine the baseline so reviewers can distinguish introduced Svelte/type errors from existing debt.

Document the runner-config loader parameter semantics: shadowWorktreeDir falls back to projectRoot in non-shadow (traditional) mode. Add a doc comment on getProjectRunnersPath/loadProjectRunnerConfig/resolveEffectiveRunners (src/agents/runner-config.ts) so future test authors and runner-feature contributors do not assume project.runners.yaml lives under .kspec/. Document or expose a schema for kspec agent run --dry-run --json output. Resolve the 'npm run check' convention vs reality mismatch. Several runner-plan task descriptions list 'npm run check' as a Testing step, but there is no root-level check script in package.json (only packages/web-ui/package.json has one — svelte-kit sync && svelte-check). Either add a root check script that wraps typecheck/format:check/lint, or update the task derivation template/convention to use 'npm run typecheck'.
