Daemon routes diverge on shadow worktree path resolution: packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts hardcodes shadowWorktreeDir = path.join(projectRoot, '.kspec') for loadRunnerEnrichmentContext, while packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts uses ctx.specDir from initContext(). In shadow layouts these agree, but in non-shadow layouts (manifest at projectRoot, no .kspec/ worktree) they diverge — meta.ts reads project.runners.yaml from <projectRoot>/.kspec/ while dispatch.ts reads from ctx.specDir which is typically <projectRoot>. Effect: GET /api/meta/agents and GET /api/agent/status can disagree about whether the project runner layer exists. Discovered while writing mixed-layer registry-load failure tests in tests/daemon-api/agent-runner-surfaces.test.ts which had to write the malformed project.runners.yaml at both locations to test both endpoints. Fix: make both routes use the same path-resolution helper (ideally initContext-based) so they always agree.

Improve npm test fresh full-suite progress visibility during long quiet tail periods, for example by adding a lightweight heartbeat or clearer end-of-suite progress indicator so reviewers can distinguish normal long-running tests from a hung process before recording final aggregate evidence.

Audit other text-mode error() callers for [object Object] bleed-through. The fix in task @task-plan-branch-git-error-details made src/cli/output.ts:error() render details.message correctly for plain object details, but ~30 callsites (upgrade.ts, agent.ts, schedule.ts, item.ts, review.ts, etc.) were previously passing { suggestion: '...' } objects that printed '[object Object]' followed by the suggestion. The new formatter cleans this up, but there is no regression coverage for those commands' text-mode error output. Worth a focused sweep + minimal test per command that verifies stderr never contains '[object Object]'.

Add scoped filtering to kspec skill status/verify so reviewers can verify only selected or touched skills. During review of @task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills, global skill verify exited nonzero for unrelated pre-existing drift while the touched skills were in sync, forcing manual table inspection. A filter such as kspec skill verify <skill...> or --skill <id> would let review gates record precise render-drift evidence without conflating unrelated drift.

Investigate semantic exit-code spec/constant mismatch observed during validation of @task-plan-branch-git-error-details. Current @trait-semantic-exit-codes says runtime errors exit 3, but @cli-exit-codes and src/cli/exit-codes.ts define 3 as NOT_FOUND and still document older meanings. Reconcile the source-of-truth exit-code contract, update constants/docs/specs consistently, and avoid future command-local magic numbers like process.exit(3) for runtime errors until the contract is unified.

Investigate and harden shadow auto-push concurrency: bursty kspec writes can launch overlapping background pushes to kspec-meta, producing intermittent 'failed to push some refs' / Shadow auto-push failed (consecutive: 1) warnings even when later pushes catch up. Desired outcome: serialize/debounce per-shadow-worktree pushes or otherwise make auto-push warnings distinguish benign superseded pushes from real stale remote state.

Review thread entries strip backtick-wrapped inline code from finding bodies. On task @01KTDPVY (review @01KTDWNZ), a MUST-FIX blocker created via 'kspec review' rendered/stored as 'MUST-FIX:  accepts  paired with an unresolved ...' with all `code` spans (e.g. `normalizeTaskIdentity`, `task_id`, `task_ref`, file:line refs) removed — both in 'kspec review get' output AND in the --json body, suggesting the loss is at storage time, not just display. The reviewer worked around it by posting a second 'Clean finding text:' entry with the same content; consumers had to read --json to recover the finding. Triage: determine whether backtick content is dropped on thread create/reply (storage) vs. on terminal render, then fix so inline code survives round-trip. Repro: create a review thread whose body contains backtick-delimited identifiers and inspect 'kspec review get --json'.

Improve the test runner review experience for long full-suite runs: when a suite fails, surface the failure snippet earlier or provide a command/flag to extract current failure summaries from the runner log before the whole run exits. During review of @01KTD8S26A1PY21C7SYXTNTJ05, npm test ran for roughly 38 minutes and one unrelated flaky suite failure was only actionable from the final summary; earlier failure details would let reviewers prepare targeted reruns and follow-up triage sooner.

Docs tests for exact walkthroughs should validate kspec command examples against real CLI surfaces, not only assert string presence. Reflection context: resource docs review caught kspec export --out in a guide even though the docs test passed; kspec export supports --format json --output <file>, and assets are copied beside that output file. Scope needs triage: decide whether to add focused command-help checks, lightweight smoke commands, or a reusable docs-command validation helper for AC-mandated copy-paste steps.

AGENTS.md project structure omits packages/daemon/ and packages/shared/ — agents searching for daemon HTTP route code first hit the misleading src/daemon/ (only entity-cache.ts + shadow-sync-manager.ts) before finding the real server and routes in packages/daemon/src/routes/. Also non-obvious: GET /api/reviews/:id/content lives in routes/diff.ts, not reviews.ts. Fix: add packages/daemon and packages/shared to the AGENTS.md structure tree (and consider a routes-location hint), or rename/merge src/daemon. Cost ~8 search round-trips in the render-review-structured-content-resource-markdown session.

P0: daemon command endpoint hangs indefinitely on current dev build — POST /api/command never responds even for trivial 'util ulid' on a freshly restarted daemon (PID 3782630, dist built Jun 9 16:23, HEAD ee78b193a4). Client timeouts surface as 'Daemon command timed out'; queued commands chain forever behind the global DispatchMutex (no timeout, command.ts:577). All 4 registered projects lose CLI mutation path; reads via cache routes unaffected. Repro: curl -X POST 127.0.0.1:3456/api/command with any command = 60s+ no response. Direct mode (KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1) works. Discovered during release audit 2026-06-10.

Dispatch engine reports healthy while reconcile permanently fails on ambiguous workspace records. Observed in hawse (2026-06-10): two legacy non-closed workspace registry records (slug-keyed dispatch-workspace-task-proposal-lifecycle and ULID-keyed dispatch-workspace-01KNNMF8...) resolved to the same canonical completed task. AmbiguousWorkspaceTaskError (workspace.ts ~1697, workspace-identity.ts ~108) is thrown by loadWorkspaceRecordForWorktreeRoot and fires inside reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry, which runs at the top of BOTH engine start() and every 60s _reconcile() tick (src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts) BEFORE _evaluateAllTasks. Effect: engine showed running:true, degraded:false, 0 queued for over an hour while every reconcile tick failed; newly derived eligible tasks were never evaluated, and the engine could not self-heal because the cleanup that would close the closing-state records sits behind the same throw. Manual recovery (delete the duplicate alias record from project.dispatch-workspaces.yaml) immediately unblocked bootstrap. Suggested fixes: (1) surface persistent reconcile failure in degraded/degraded_targets instead of silent console logging; (2) scope the ambiguity failure to the affected task so evaluation of unrelated tasks continues; (3) consider auto-coalescing duplicate alias records when the task is verifiably completed and the branch head is merged (legacy pre-canonical-identity data exists in the wild).

DispatchEngine.handleFileChange never emits events for newly created tasks. In src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts ~1282, handleFileChange diffs each task's status against prevTaskStates and only pushes a TaskStateChange when prevStatus !== undefined && prevStatus !== currentStatus; brand-new tasks (prevStatus undefined, e.g. created by kspec plan derive or task add while the engine is running) are snapshot-recorded but never produce task.ready. Combined with the fact that direct-mode CLI mutations (KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1) emit no daemon events, the only discovery paths for derive-created tasks are engine restart bootstrap or the 60s reconcile - and reconcile can be silently dead (see related ambiguous-workspace-records item). Observed in hawse 2026-06-10: five tasks derived from an approved plan with automation eligible sat undiscovered. Suggested fix: treat prevStatus === undefined with a dispatch-eligible current status as a synthetic transition (emit task.ready for pending tasks), or have handleFileChange route new tasks through the same evaluation used by bootstrap/_evaluateAllTasks.

kspec event emit / event log resolve to the daemon default project instead of the cwd project. Observed in hawse 2026-06-10: with the hawse dispatch engine running (kspec agent dispatch status from hawse cwd showed running:true with hawse agents), kspec event emit task.ready failed with 'Dispatch engine is not running. Start it first with POST /api/agent/dispatch' and kspec event log showed 'No recent events'. The daemon (launched with --kspec-dir .../kynetic-spec-dispatch/.kspec) treats kynetic-spec-dispatch as the default project; project context for API requests comes from the X-Kspec-Dir header (packages/daemon/src/middleware/project-context.ts), and the emit route checks getDispatchEngine(projectContext.path) (routes/automation.ts ~294). Other commands (dispatch status/start) correctly scope to the cwd project, so the event CLI commands appear not to send X-Kspec-Dir (or send a different path form), landing on the default project whose engine was stopped. Effect: event emit/log are unusable and misleading in multi-project daemons - they report on the wrong project with no indication of which project they hit. Suggested fix: send X-Kspec-Dir from the event CLI like other project-scoped commands, and include the resolved project path in event log/emit output so mis-scoping is visible.

manual_only tasks trigger automated reviewer dispatch with broken submission linkage. Observed in hawse (2026-06-10): a manual_only task worked directly in the main checkout was submitted via kspec task submit from that checkout; submission linkage captured branch 'main'. The pr-reviewer dispatch rule (on: task.pending_review, no automation filter) fired, workspace provisioning tried to adopt branch 'main', failed ('currently checked out in the main repository working tree'), and BLOCKED the task - turning a normal manual flow into an error state requiring manual unblock + manual review record to complete. Suggested fixes: (1) let dispatch rules filter on automation status so manual_only tasks skip automated review dispatch (or make that the default for manual_only); (2) task submit from the integration branch could warn or record linkage as 'manual/no branch' instead of capturing the integration branch itself; (3) provisioning failure for a manual_only task could leave it pending_review with a diagnostic instead of blocking.

kspec review verdict CLI ergonomics: the flag is --decision on a subcommand named verdict (kspec review verdict --decision approve), which is easy to guess wrong as --verdict; and verdict accepts no --comment, so verdict rationale silently has no home on the verdict itself - it must be added as a separate comment thread or it gets dropped (observed 2026-06-10: a detailed approval rationale was lost on the first attempt). Same CLI-asymmetry family as the existing inbox item about task note (positional) vs review reply (--body). Suggested: accept --comment (or --reason) on review verdict and attach it to the verdict event.

Dev-only npm audit advisories remain after task-audit-fix-production-deps: 6 low severity — cookie <0.7.0 (GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x) via @sveltejs/kit -> @sveltejs/adapter-static, runed, bits-ui, svelte-toolbelt chain. npm claims fix requires 'npm audit fix --force' installing @sveltejs/kit@0.0.30 (bogus downgrade / breaking). Real fix is waiting for @sveltejs/kit to bump its cookie dep or overriding cookie >=0.7.0. Assess and resolve separately.

Playwright e2e fixture (tests/e2e/fixtures/) is incompatible with the entity-storage strict gates: manifest is kynetic 1.0 with monolithic project.reviews.yaml/project.plans.yaml, so the daemon 500s on /api/reviews and /api/plans (legacy_review_storage_removed / legacy_plan_storage_removed) and all review/plan e2e specs fail (plans.spec.ts, review-detail-page.spec.ts, review-interaction.spec.ts, reviews-detail.spec.ts, tasks.spec.ts review sections). Add testing convention rule: kspec()/kspecJson() CLI helpers isolate HOME to <cwd>/.test-home, so global daemon state paths (config dir, daemon.pid, daemon.log via getDefaultDaemonConfigDir) resolve under the temp cwd, not the real home. Mechanism exists (task 01KJTP68, spec @daemon-sensitive-cli-test-determinism) but is undocumented in conventions; cost a failed first test run in @task-daemon-log-capture.

Best-effort initContext catch sites silently swallow deterministic compatibility errors (EntityStorageCompatibilityError, TaskDataManagerError, new FormatVersionCompatibilityError). Audit during @task-format-version-ceiling found: src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts _loadAgents returns [] (dispatch engine sees no agents with zero diagnostics), dispatch.ts lenient filter/dependency paths, src/agent-runtime/prompts.ts skill-origin fallback, src/cli/commands/serve.ts resolveDefaultKspecDir falls back to cwd/.kspec, src/cli/commands/merge-driver.ts buildRefIndex, src/cli/commands/agent.ts dispatch watch. Proposal: make best-effort catches rethrow or at least log deterministic compatibility errors (shared isDeterministic* guards already exist). Two sites (upgrade, init) were already fixed in that task.

Add a testing convention rule: any npm pack --dry-run invocation in tests or verification scripts must pass --ignore-scripts. Since @task-prepack-full-build-and-verification, prepack runs the full multi-minute build, and npm 11 DOES run prepack on dry runs — a dry-run without --ignore-scripts inside vitest or a CI verification step silently re-triggers the entire build. In-repo cases (tests/release-packaging.test.ts, scripts/verify-package.cjs) already comply; the convention prevents reintroduction. The real-pack path (scripts/verify-clean-pack.cjs) intentionally keeps scripts enabled — that is the ac-4 proof.

Fix-cycle resubmit ergonomics: kspec task submit rejects needs_work status (requires in_progress), but the task-work skill fix-cycle section step 7 says only Re-submit with kspec task submit @ref — no mention of running kspec task start first. Every dispatched fix cycle hits this (observed 2026-06-11: atomic batch note+submit failed and rolled back, needed start+note+submit). Fix either direction: allow submit from needs_work with an implicit needs_work->in_progress transition, or document the required task start in the fix-cycle steps of the task-work skill.

Fix duplicate step numbering in task-work core skill: templates/skills/task-work/SKILL.md has '### 9. Regenerate Derived Files', '### 10. Commit', then '### 9. Quality Check' and '### 10. Submit' again (lines ~228-274). Renumber Quality Check/Submit to 11/12, then kspec skill render and npm run build:plugin (shared package surface — keep project-neutral).

Shell-safe path quoting for all user-facing command guidance: cycle-2 review of @task-shadow-restore-loud-failure blocked on recovery commands that interpolated paths into double-quoted shell strings ($, backticks, backslashes still expand). Fixed locally with a private shellQuotePath() in src/parser/shadow.ts, but three other guidance strings still embed unquoted paths in suggested commands: src/strings/validation.ts:133 (cd ${dir}), src/parser/shadow.ts:623 (cd ${mainRoot} && ...), src/parser/yaml.ts:822 (Run from project root: cd ${...}). Promote shellQuotePath to a shared util (e.g. src/utils/) and apply it wherever guidance embeds filesystem paths in shell commands; keep kspec @refs unquoted. Small scope.

Testing convention timing is stale: conventions say full suite ~150s (shards ~50s), but two independent full fresh runs on 2026-06-11 took ~2420s (worker and reviewer environments, 10k+ tests). Misleads agents budgeting time around npm test. Update the convention numbers (or drop absolute timings in favor of relative guidance like 'shards are ~3x faster; full suite can take tens of minutes fresh, seconds on cache hit').

Make silent 'kspec init' failure in tests impossible. Two-part fix candidates: (1) kspec init should detect non-TTY stdin and either apply defaults non-interactively (--yes semantics) or fail loudly instead of aborting with the prompt text on stdout; (2) narrow or remove the kspec() test helper's backwards-compat behavior of returning success-shaped results when exitCode != 0 but stdout is non-empty — it masks setup failures and produced months of vacuous tests (see task-fix-search-meta-entity-tests). Also audit the two remaining kspec("init") callers in tests (tests/native-guard-setup.test.ts:26, tests/cli/session-note-limit.test.ts:21) for the same vacuous-setup hazard and migrate them to setupShadowDetection()/setupTempFixtures(). Consider adding a testing convention rule: never bootstrap vitest projects with kspec("init").

Extend behavioral shadow-commit coverage (@trait-api-endpoint ac-5) to the other mutating daemon-api route suites (inbox, tasks, reviews, plans): extract the real-kspec-meta-worktree setup from tests/daemon-api/triage.test.ts Shadow commits block into a shared helper in tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts (e.g. setupRealShadowFixtures) and assert semantic commit subjects per mutation route. Today triage is the only route group with behavioral ac-5 coverage; other suites mark it N/A or rely on implicit claims.

Centralize the Elysia error-helper polyfill for app.handle() route tests: extract the .resolve error polyfill from tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts into a shared test helper (e.g. tests/helpers/) and/or add a testing convention rule documenting that errorResponse is undefined under app.handle() in Node. Prevents repeat debugging of opaque 500s when new route test files build their own Elysia app (hit again in tests/daemon-command-api.test.ts during task-command-dispatch-timeout).

scripts/build-daemon.cjs hardcodes the packages/daemon/src/pid.ts shim re-export list as a string literal — adding a new shared constant (e.g. DEFAULT_DAEMON_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS) requires editing src/daemon-shared/endpoint.ts, the pid.ts shim, AND the build script string; a missed build-script edit is silent until the bundled daemon fails at import time. Improve by generating the staged shim from the pid.ts source export list (or rewriting only the import specifier) so the list lives in one place.

task-work core skill fix-cycle section (templates/skills/task-work/SKILL.md, step 7 'Re-submit') omits that a needs_work task must first be transitioned with 'kspec task start @ref' before 'kspec task submit @ref' succeeds — submit rejects needs_work with 'Task must be in_progress'. Every fix-cycle agent hits a failed submit (or rolled-back atomic batch) on first attempt. Fix: add the task start step to the fix-cycle list and re-render skill outputs.

Add a CI gate (or lint check) that catches Node APIs newer than the declared engines minimum (>=20.0.0). This session, readdirSync recursive:true (added in Node 20.1.0) passed format/lint/typecheck/full-suite locally and in CI because both run newer Node — it was only caught by the reviewer manually reproducing under npx node@20.0.0. Options: run one CI test job on the exact engines floor (node 20.0.0), or enable an eslint-plugin-n style rule checking API availability against engines. Related but distinct from @01KFPDCY (OS matrix, not Node version floor).

Test runner: support retrying only failed files instead of full --fresh rerun. The result cache stores a whole-run verdict keyed by content hash: when one flaky file fails a full suite run, rerunning npm test returns the cached failed verdict, and rerunning the failed file in isolation (which passes) does not update the full-run verdict. Only remedy today is npm test -- --fresh (~40 min). Improvement: per-file result caching or a --retry-failed mode that reruns only previously-failed files and merges results into the cached run verdict. Cost recurs every time a known flake (see task-stabilize-full-suite-cli-dist-flakes) fires in a worker/reviewer gate run.

kspec serve logs tail mode reads only the active daemon.log; immediately after a rotation the active file may hold far fewer than the requested --lines even though daemon.log.1 contains recent history. Consider spanning the rotated generation when the active file has fewer lines than requested (read tail of <log>.1 first, then active). Small scope: logsServer() in src/cli/commands/serve.ts; rotation contract is DaemonLogWriter rename-to-<log>.1.

Testing convention timing docs are stale: convention states full suite ~150s / shards ~50s, but a full uncached 'npm test' run measured 3269s (2778 suites, 10537 tests) in a dispatch worktree on 2026-06-11. The suite has grown ~20x since the numbers were written (sharding task 01KJA66Z, Feb 2026). Misleads agents budgeting test time before submit. Scope: re-measure representative full/shard durations and update the testing convention text; consider whether 3-way sharding is still the right split at this suite size.

E2E runs (npx playwright test in test:e2e scripts) spawn daemons from dist/ but only the build:e2e step holds the build/test lock — a concurrent npm run build during a playwright run can still rewrite dist mid-run. Consider holding the per-worktree build/test lock (scripts/build-test-lock.cjs) across the playwright invocation too.

kspec meta set <convention> supports only --add-rule — there is no --remove-rule/--replace-rule, so stale convention rule text cannot be corrected via CLI. Hit concretely: after adding the build/test lock, the existing testing rule listing cache-key env exclusions ('except KSPEC_SESSION_ID and KSPEC_TEST_PROGRESS') became inaccurate (lock vars are now also excluded) and could only be supplemented with a new rule, not fixed. Add rule removal/replacement (by index or by matching text) to kspec meta set.

CLI/docs mismatch: 'kspec workflow show' requires a run-ref argument, but the reflect skill and workflow guidance document bare 'kspec workflow show' / 'kspec workflow next --notes' usage (next also required the run ref). Either default these commands to the caller's single active workflow run or update the skill docs to show the run-ref form.

Improve review workflow support for unrelated gate failures: provide guidance or CLI affordance to record a required gate as non-regressing with linked follow-up tasks, preserving the original failing command, focused rerun evidence, classification, and follow-up refs.

Standalone sub-build scripts still bypass the per-worktree build/test lock: npm run build:shared, build:web-ui, and build:plugin invoked directly (not via scripts/build.cjs) rewrite artifacts that running tests load (packages/shared/dist is imported by every spawned dist/cli process; dist/web-ui is served by test daemons). build:daemon was lock-guarded in task-stabilize-upgrade-folder-storage-test fix cycle 1 (acquire when targeting real output, KSPEC_DAEMON_BUILD_DIST_ROOT override for tests); apply the same pattern to the remaining standalone build entrypoints. Related: @01KTWBE2 covers the playwright-run gap.

Mid-suite dist/daemon rebuild race: tests/daemon-build.test.ts runs npm run build:daemon during the suite; scripts/build-daemon.cjs rmSync-deletes dist/daemon (and dist/daemon-src) before esbuild repopulates it, so parallel vitest workers spawning dist/daemon/index.js (startTestDaemon and daemon helper tests) can observe a missing or partial dist/daemon tree — same race class as the npm pack prepack incident fixed in @task-stabilize-workflow-runs-cli-dist-export. Additionally build-daemon.cjs falls back to a full tsc over all of dist/ when dist/parser/index.js is missing, which would rewrite dist/cli mid-suite. Options: build into a temp outdir and rename into place, have the test build to an isolated outdir, or serialize daemon-build tests against daemon-spawning files.

kspec-managed .gitignore block uses unanchored patterns (e.g. 'plans/') that match ANY directory with that name at any depth, not just the repo-root transient dir. This silently swallowed tests/e2e/fixtures/plans/ (folder-backed fixture storage) and required a manual '!tests/e2e/fixtures/plans/' negation placed after the managed block — fragile if the block is ever re-appended. Fix: anchor managed entries to repo root ('/plans/', '/.kspec-sessions/', etc.). Touches shipped scaffolding + @complete-auto-gitignore spec, so needs spec-first check.

startTestDaemon holds the global port-start lock through each holder's FULL readiness wait (including deliberately-failing contract-test readiness budgets + 5s diagnostic sampling), serializing all dynamic-port daemon startups suite-wide. The lock only needs to cover allocate-port -> child-binds-port; releasing it once the child has observably bound (e.g. bounded TCP connect probe) would shrink hold times from tens of seconds to <1s and remove a whole class of full-suite contention timeouts (see @01KTY9DTPW4E1G33BEFFQNK47X). Needs care for never-binding children (synthetic/failing daemons) and the @daemon-backed-test-fixture-contract spec.

Dispatch workspace cleanup sharp edge: a local branch under reserved `dispatch/task/*` can be manually/external-worktree checked out outside the configured dispatch worktree root, then later look stale to `reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts`. In Hyphoria this happened with branch `dispatch/task/task-civitai-external-id-feature-flag/01ktyaw5` checked out at `/tmp/hyphoria-main-live` while Hyphoria dispatch root was `/home/chapel/Projects/hyphoria/.kspec-worktrees`. Cleanup attempted `git branch -D dispatch/task/task-civitai-external-id-feature-flag/01ktyaw5` and threw because Git refused to delete a branch used by that worktree, aborting reconciliation before normal task evaluation. A later pending_review provisioning attempt also failed with the foreign worktree guard before the worktree was detached. Candidate hardening: branch pruning should treat a dispatch branch checked out in any worktree as protected/degraded diagnostic rather than throwing; cleanup/protection should also consider task `submission_linkage` branches before deleting untracked dispatch branches; recovery note/block mutations after provisioning failure should avoid daemon-route timeout loops or use a safer queued diagnostic path. Repro context: task `@01KTYAW5N9H5QXD67Y8WGX74HY`, branch commit `33c95cc6942ae138471f93cf57bc7c93251891b0`, local backup ref created as `refs/backup/hyphoria/task-civitai-external-id-feature-flag-20260612`; manual recovery was to submit the task from the branch, then `git switch --detach 33c95cc6` in the foreign worktree so dispatch could recover without losing work.

Audit remaining E2E specs for the response-count flake pattern fixed in connection.spec.ts: observations/plans/tasks/sessions/triage specs also use page.on(response)/waitForResponse. Look for (a) negative assertions on API traffic counts, (b) settle/stability windows shorter than the 1500ms delayed file-watcher invalidation tail (ws-invalidation.ts), (c) non-hermetic WS proxying during count measurements. Consider extracting connection.spec.ts trackTasksApi into a shared tests/e2e helper (request-initiation/in-flight/response counting + settle) parameterized by URL matcher.

Dispatch task submit should capture submission_linkage from the actual worker worktree, not blindly from the kspec command cwd. In claude-headed-acp, a dispatched worker ran kspec task submit from the project root because that is where .kspec was available; kspec captured branch: main and the main commit even though the submitted work lived on dispatch/task/task-preserve-assistant-tool-interleaving/01ktf67s. The worker had to patch submission_linkage manually before review. Candidate fixes: detect KSPEC_DISPATCH_* / .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json and rev-parse the registered workspace; add a documented KSPEC_GIT_WORKTREE=<path> override; or make command/root discovery support running kspec from the worker worktree safely. Source observation: claude-headed-acp @01KTFE72GN2DQ2HPT1YR8C3EGW.

Dispatch worker prompts/guidance should explicitly cover file-tool absolute paths in isolated worktrees. In claude-headed-acp, the task prompt warned not to cd to the project root, but an agent used absolute paths under /home/<user>/Projects/<repo>/... with Read/Edit while the real worker files lived under .kspec-worktrees/<task-slug>-<ulid>/; file tools operated on main-branch bytes and repeated edits failed with 'String to replace not found' until md5sum revealed the path mismatch. Mitigations: include 'use the worker workspace path prefix for Read/Edit/Write absolute paths, not the main repo path' in dispatch prompts, and/or emit WORKSPACE_PATH as a first-class variable in agent context. Source observation: claude-headed-acp @01KTFBYANWNJWZVGVENNJQD2G6.

kspec doctor and kspec shadow repair should agree about shadow worktree health in dispatch worktrees. In claude-headed-acp, kspec doctor reported 'Shadow Branch: Worktree directory missing — Run kspec shadow repair to recreate worktree', but immediately running kspec shadow repair reported 'Shadow branch is already healthy, nothing to repair'; spec writes still worked, suggesting a cosmetic/path-resolution-dependent doctor failure. Either doctor's check or repair's health check is wrong, and doctor should not prescribe a remedy that declines to act. Source observation: claude-headed-acp @01KTWH7D2KHHTT7QHPVCVPQKVA.

Add or document a metadata/spec-catalog review gate profile for detached reviews whose branch changes only kspec metadata and no source/package behavior. In claude-headed-acp, spec-catalog-only reviews still defaulted to a full serial npm test gate, and another review spent 431.8s on the full suite after a focused probe had already found a blocker. Desired shape: rigorous kspec validate plus exact spec/AC/status checks and source-diff confirmation, with a policy for when focused gates can short-circuit before final full-suite requirements. Source observations: claude-headed-acp @01KTWHVYG7RCPWR94BBF5BHQTW and @01KTWPHEJK2MV5F2HWRQ20M0GM.

Investigate transient kspec review for-task failures immediately after creating a folder-backed review record. In claude-headed-acp, review for-task briefly failed with EntityStorageCompatibilityError about folder-backed review storage and project.reviews.yaml index mismatch; the direct review ref remained usable and later lookup recovered, but the failure interrupted normal fix-cycle orientation. Source observation: claude-headed-acp @01KTFCX18FH04WD0BZZXNQH7CQ.

Hyphoria-mined: support secondary/spec coverage for tasks that intentionally cover ACs from multiple specs. In Hyphoria observation @01KTR3026DQV7ABTQ9H8K99V6P, a plan-derived task had a single spec_ref but AC-tagged tests for a second spec named only in Covers; kspec validate --alignment/completeness treated the secondary spec as orphan/unimplemented and task start only synced the primary spec status. Consider multi-valued spec_ref, structured covers/secondary-spec metadata, or validation/status logic that recognizes task Covers AC refs as intentional coverage while preserving clear ownership.

Hyphoria-mined: add a structured way to mark tasks as intentionally spec-exempt. In Hyphoria observation @01KTRBQV3M3Z1YAD3VSJZ23TEG, kspec validate --completeness warned on an automation-eligible product-direction/documentation task with no spec_ref even though the task explicitly stated the omission was intentional. A field such as spec_exempt: <reason> or a task kind could let validation distinguish deliberate metadata/docs/support tasks from accidentally unspecced implementation work.

Hyphoria-mined: dispatch readiness and detached review/merge should account for unmerged plan-branch lineage and post-approval integration drift. Hyphoria observations @01KTX3RHCHVD1PED1F4F3WQJEA and @01KTX4VR3EX8E282X5B3V2VHQP showed tasks naming files/UX introduced only on a reviewed-but-unmerged plan branch, and an approved branch later conflicting after main/dev moved. Consider surfacing required plan-branch lineage before worker start, rebasing/refreshing branches immediately before review or merge, and when conflicts are routine porting work, kicking back with conflict context without discarding useful approval evidence.

Hyphoria-mined: reviewer findings should include anchored-commit evidence for claimed code state. In Hyphoria observation @01KTX3XCFNXBJVA9AAYJQ4RTT9, a reviewer blocker cited an implicit Convex db.patch form that did not exist in the examined commit; the fix cycle spent time proving zero code change was needed. Add review guidance or tooling so blockers that quote code include `git show <examined-commit>:<path>`/line evidence, and workers verify each flagged line at the anchored commit before editing.

Hyphoria-mined: gate commands used as pass/fail evidence must be run bare, not through trailing pipes. In Hyphoria observation @01KTX3D1SSC8MZF499KAH0HN9P, `npm run review:gates 2>&1 | tail -30` returned exit 0 from tail while convex:typecheck had failed inside the pipeline, creating a near false-pass. Document/enforce running authoritative gates without pipes (or with pipefail plus explicit status capture) and reading persisted logs afterward for summaries.

Hawse-mined from observation @01KTS7FVE3PDNV9WCYSWQGH7TM: core task-work quality-check guidance should render project-appropriate gates instead of hardcoding Node/npm commands. In Hawse, the rendered kspec:task-work skill prescribed npm format/lint/typecheck/oxlint even though the project is a pure Rust cargo workspace with justfile gates. Workers must silently translate to cargo fmt/clippy/test/no-std. Candidate direction: gate guidance sourced from per-project config/justfile/meta conventions, with package defaults only when no project gate profile exists.

Hawse-mined from observation @01KTS65KEAE2YG3TA7ZGFBXQ82: add a way to withdraw or edit mis-posted review threads. A shell-quoting/backtick issue corrupted the first blocker body in review @01KTS56N35GKEJHWE0H9E2KSYX; the reviewer had to file a duplicate thread, resolve the broken one as duplicate, and the worker then had two blocker threads for one finding. A kspec review thread withdraw/edit command would preserve auditability while avoiding permanent broken-body duplicate noise.

Hawse-mined from observation @01KT56CS3C2KWEYJFRCMA81HC1: support review-check bundles, multi-check entry, or a documented batch pattern for standard gates. Hawse reviewers routinely record fmt, validation variants, focused tests, workspace tests, diff checks, and no-std as separate review-check commands. A reusable bundle should reduce repeated shadow-branch writes while preserving individual check names, runners, commands, and evidence.

Hawse-mined from observations @01KT59E2K1ZNWE5XEFH14JC9B0 and @01KPSDD2CAEJFSB7HMS4NMA24Q: rendered reflection skills/prompts can reference @session-reflect or @session-reflect-loop even when the project has no workflows installed, causing Workflow not found and undocumented manual fallback. Fix direction: either install/render the referenced reflection workflows into consumer project meta, or make the skill detect/document the manual fallback and avoid requiring absent workflow refs.

Hawse-mined from observations @01KTTQ4DFPF8MCTQDBWE77QE9Y and @01KTYF0RA97BYQ5ZJ3VYSF7RJB: dispatch/reviewer prompts can mention supporting script placeholders such as {supporting:scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh} while the executable in the checkout lives at .agents/skills/kspec-merge/scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh. Reviewers had to search manually before merging. Prompt rendering should expand supporting-script placeholders to the exact rendered path or include a copy-paste-safe skill-relative command.

Hawse-mined from observation @01KTTR5WAZCXEAY6KNQ49GHDQ0: CLI error/help hints for observation refs point at a nonexistent command. kspec item get <obs-ulid> and search results suggested 'kspec meta observe get <ref>', but meta observe accepts only a new observation type; the working command is kspec meta get <ref>. Update hint text and tests so observation refs point to the real retrieval command.

Hawse-mined from observations @01KNNV1D8N8PGGT3VK8YK4B9KE, @01KNNXBZ98DYVB2D6P8B96301K, and @01KNRGW0NP2H5K0JZ5P7ZRMSYZ: AC coverage validation missed crate-local Rust integration tests until coverage.scan_paths was configured. The failure mode was non-obvious because cargo tests passed and AC comments grepped correctly, but review still showed 0/N coverage. Improve validation diagnostics/config discovery: when annotations are present outside scanned roots or a project has cargo/package test directories, surface scan_paths guidance instead of only uncovered AC warnings.

Add an agent command for safely attaching existing work to a task: given an existing branch/commit/worktree and task ref, record recoverable lineage/submission linkage, mark the task in_progress, and protect/register the workspace so dispatch can pick it up without orphan-cleaning or freshly provisioning over the work. This covers the recent case where prior manual/Hermes work on a dispatch-like branch was not visible to the next dispatched agent.

Define a metadata-only/no-code-diff review gate profile. Reflection source: reviewing @task-supersede-legacy-revamp-umbrella found git diff against feat/ui-redesign was empty and the task only verified kspec metadata, but the required review gates still ran the full npm suite; npm test passed but took 2583.8s. Consider project guidance for when reviewers may mark npm gates skipped/non-required while still requiring exact entity JSON verification, successor/ref lookup, kspec validations, and detached merge-helper/no-op evidence.

Fix stale `Agent` type in @kynetic-ai/shared (packages/shared/src/api.ts). It declares `{ _ulid, slugs, role, status, capabilities, constraints }`, but the actual exported snapshot/meta agent shape (from src/schema/meta.ts AgentSchema, used by `agents: metaContext.agents` in src/export/json.ts and KspecSnapshot.agents) is `{ _ulid, id, name, ... }`. The web snapshot types agents with this wrong interface, so consumers cannot read agent.id/agent.name without a cast (hit while building static-mode identity in fetchIdentityStatic). Align the shared Agent type with the real schema and drop the cast.

Add a Svelte 5 gotcha to the svelte-5 skill: a component prop named `state` collides with the `$state` rune — the compiler interprets `$state(...)` as store auto-subscription on the in-scope `state` identifier and throws `store_invalid_shape` at runtime. Fix: rename the prop (e.g. statusState) or avoid the $state rune when a `state` binding is in scope. Hit while building ViewHeader (@ui-view-header). The skill currently documents $-prefix misuse but not this name collision.

Add a dispatch resume helper (or extend kspec task get) that surfaces the last dispatched agents in-flight worktree state in one command: uncommitted diff, AC coverage state at submit time, last commit hash, and dispatch failure reason. This is the agent-failure angle of inbox 01KV2B04 (which covers the manual/Hermes attach case). Resuming after AGENT-FAIL/AGENT-TIMEOUT currently requires 2-3 git round-trips (status, diff, log) plus a search through task notes for the failure reason. A single command would shorten resume time and reduce the risk of an agent re-doing work that was already in the worktree. Scope: small CLI surface change.

Workflow runs have no TTL or auto-close. After ~3 weeks of work, `kspec workflow next` errors with a 100+ line "Multiple active runs found" list that the user has to scroll through to find the right one. The error message is high-noise / low-signal. Options: (a) auto-close workflow runs that have been active for >7 days with no progress, (b) add a `kspec workflow runs` subcommand to list/manage active runs, (c) sort active runs by most-recent-activity so the current one is at the top. Affects every session that uses workflow start. Scope: small CLI/state-machine change.

Regression: kspec review for-task resolves a task slug differently than the canonical task ULID. In Hyphoria, `kspec review for-task @task-implement-civitai-imagegen-compiler-for-smart-image-families` returned only latest review 01KV9B27, while `kspec review for-task @01KV6Q00WAEQ63HJWXRJDGSRMC` returned all three review cycles 01KV90X9, 01KV92VR, and 01KV9B27. Investigate ref normalization/canonical ULID handling for review lookup so slug aliases and canonical refs enumerate the same linked reviews.

Extract a shared helper for shadow-backed kspec test projects used by CLI and daemon tests. Many tests duplicate canRunShadowTests plus setupShadowProject/setupShadowFolderProject boilerplate; a helper could standardize git-version gating, kspec init, shadow worktree setup, and cleanup while reducing fixture drift.

Batch review-comment support does not include plan-text anchor arguments. Direct CLI supports --plan-section, --plan-offset, --quoted-text, and --created-at-rev, but kspec batch commands "review comment" omits these options and kspec batch --dry-run rejects planSection, planOffset, quotedText, and createdAtRev as unknown arguments. Add batch schema/allowed-argument parity and behavioral coverage so automation can create plan-text anchored review comments through batch.

Reflection: consider making 'kspec workflow show' default to the current active workflow run when exactly one active run exists, or printing the exact 'kspec workflow show @run' command after 'workflow start'. This would remove a retry step during workflow-guided sessions.

Submission linkage uses global dispatch base_branch instead of plan-scoped resolved_base_branch when a dispatch task branch has no upstream at submit time. Evidence from @task-test-result-ac-mapping: plan/workspace resolved to feat/ui-redesign and reviewer merged into feat/ui-redesign, but kspec task submit ran before the daemon first-pushed/tracking-established the task branch, so submission_linkage.upstream_ref fell back to dev. Desired fix: task submit/linkage capture should prefer the dispatch workspace resolved_base_branch or owning plan.branch for managed dispatch worktrees before falling back to dispatch.base_branch; add regression coverage for manual_merge/plan-scoped branches where the task branch has no upstream yet.

Bug: kspec batch dry-run can succeed for meta set while real apply fails with TypeError options.removeCapability is not iterable. Repro from comfy-ecaj-nodes agent alignment: batch JSON with skill add then meta set commands dry-ran as 6/6 OK, but apply failed atomically at first meta set with removeCapability TypeError. Direct equivalent kspec meta set commands succeeded. Expected: batch dry-run and apply share option normalization; optional repeatable flags default to [] without callers knowing internal Commander names. Impact: batch is unreliable for multi-step project setup/agent alignment and forces non-atomic one-by-one meta set fallback.

Coverage-state read-model hardening follow-up tied to @plan-coverage-state-engine and the UI revamp: the post-closure audit found no remaining production bypass, but some lower-level exports/helpers still look legacy or easy to misuse, especially direct/raw buildCoverageStateReadModel(...) projection and deriveCoverageStateWithFreshnessComparison(...) helper paths. Goal: improve the API/logic boundary so future production code cannot accidentally bypass freshness comparison without doing so explicitly and with clear documentation. Possible fixes include renaming raw helpers to make their preconditions obvious, making raw projection helpers private/internal, adding lint/tests that daemon/API/static/export paths only use loadCoverageStateReadModel/getCachedCoverageStateReadModel, or adding documentation/comments around the proper enriched read path. Track as UI redesign/coverage-state cleanup, not a blocker for the now-completed plan.

Add a supported task resource CLI/API surface so a worker can attach validation evidence (for example screenshots, logs, recordings, reports, or generated artifacts) directly to an existing task, including while it is in progress. The operation should own and compute resource metadata atomically, append without clobbering existing refs, enforce safe paths/content hashes and lifecycle rules, expose the evidence through task detail/agent context/static export, and avoid requiring raw task patch of provenance-bearing resource_refs. Define visibility for an already-running dispatched agent and distinguish direct task-owned uploads from attaching an existing plan resource.

Make review resources immutable once a review is closed or archived so evidence supporting checks and verdicts cannot be added, replaced, or removed after closure. Enforce the rule consistently across CLI and daemon resource mutation routes, define whether reopening permits mutation or requires a new review cycle, preserve read access and static export, and add lifecycle-bound tests covering add/replace/remove before and after closure. Consider binding check evidence to exact review resource ids and SHA-256 values so verdict provenance remains auditable even across allowed pre-close replacements.

Add first-class CLI mutation commands for layered agent runner configuration (for example project runner env.set). Current kspec agent runners only validates; operators must manually edit .kspec/project.runners.yaml despite the CLI-only metadata policy. Provide safe set/patch/unset operations with project-vs-system scope, secret-boundary validation, effective-source diagnostics, atomic shadow commits, and tests.

Add scoped dispatch lifecycle controls with distinct drain and hard-stop semantics. Global pause should prevent all new invocations from starting while allowing active sessions to finish naturally; resume should restart scheduling. Global stop should remain a hard stop that cancels active invocations and clears queued work. Add equivalent task-level controls so a specific task can be paused/drained or hard-stopped without disrupting other tasks: prevent/release new scheduling for that task, optionally cancel its active invocation, preserve its dispatch workspace/session evidence, expose held/draining/stopped state and reason in CLI/API/UI status, and ensure bootstrap/reconciliation cannot bypass the hold. Define clear behavior for queued invocations, daemon restarts, idempotency, and resume.

Add programmatic predicate triggers for automation actions. Allow a hook, dispatch rule, schedule, or composition edge to run a bounded project-defined checker against an immutable event/context snapshot, then fire its configured action only when the checker returns an explicit machine-readable decision. Define a strict result protocol (fire, skip, error plus optional reason/data), timeout and output limits, deterministic working directory and sanitized environment, no implicit shell interpolation, redaction, audit records containing checker identity/version and decision, and clear retry/fail-open/fail-closed semantics. Predicate evaluation must be side-effect-free by contract or explicitly sandboxed, idempotent under duplicate events, observable in CLI/API/UI, and unable to mutate authoritative state directly. This should provide extensible conditions such as review churn or repository health without adding each condition to the core schema, while retaining native declarative filters for common cheap cases.

Add an orchestration triage agent for dispatch and task lifecycle exceptions. Feed it durable issue events such as blocked tasks, repeated review/fix churn, stalled or failed invocations, exhausted budgets, and failed programmatic predicates, with the complete task, session, workspace, and review history. Give it a bounded policy-defined action set: apply documented safe remediations, pause or reroute a task, request a specialist review, split or propose follow-up work, retry within explicit limits, or escalate to a human through a preset channel. Require structured dispositions with evidence, reason, confidence, policy/rule reference, and proposed/actual actions; durable deduplication and cooldowns; per-task serialization so it cannot race workers/reviewers; strict authority boundaries and approval gates for spec changes, destructive actions, merges, or unrecognized situations; and an auditable resolution lifecycle that prevents recursive triage loops. Support advisory-only mode before autonomous remediation and make unresolved escalations visible in CLI/API/UI.

Bind CLI-created task and spec reviews to real shadow subject versions. Review @01KXH7FDK7PTN4YWYB40T5KJNW was created for completed task @01KXH2PJ7RY9B9MQNHBFWN96QB but stored empty subject.shadow_commit/content_hash, and every check/verdict consequently used entity_version.content_hash empty. This defeats staleness detection required by @review-subject-bindings ac-4/ac-5 and @review-verdicts-and-resolution-lifecycle ac-1/ac-5. @task-bind-cli-plan-review-subject-versions fixed only plan reviews and explicitly left task/spec behavior unchanged. Triage whether task and spec subjects can share the existing real-binding helper, with behavioral CLI regressions proving non-empty hashes and stale check/verdict exclusion after entity mutation.

Reflection: reconcile dispatch reviewer role-entry rendering with the review skills actually configured for the selected agent. This review prompt mandated `$pr-review`, but `kspec meta get @pr-reviewer` lists only `review`, `review-gates`, `merge`, and `shared-guidance-neutrality`, and no pr-review skill exists in the rendered catalog. Update entrypoint resolution to select an installed/configured review skill or fail preflight with actionable guidance, and add a focused dispatch prompt regression proving reviewer prompts never name unavailable skills.

Fix the kspec-reflect skill's workflow command examples: kspec workflow show requires <run-ref>, and workflow next should consistently show [run-ref] usage. The current no-argument examples fail during reflection with 'missing required argument run-ref'. Update the package skill source and rendered outputs, with command-example coverage if available.

Reflection: count durable reviewer activity as meaningful session work. A detached reviewer can create and close a review, record checks and blocker threads, submit request_changes, and transition a task from pending_review to needs_work while leaving a clean worktree, no new commit, and no completed task. The current kspec-reflect meaningful-work gate classifies that substantive session as empty. Extend session introspection/guidance to treat current-session review verdicts and task lifecycle transitions as meaningful, with a request_changes reviewer regression.

Reflection: replace the session-reflect-loop workflow's unbounded baseline dumps with bounded duplicate discovery. In this repository, mandatory `kspec meta observations list`, `kspec inbox list`, and `kspec tasks list` produced an observations result over 264k tokens plus 1,704 tasks and was truncated, so the baseline could not reliably establish coverage. Use a bounded index/summary or candidate-keyword `kspec search` strategy across all sources, and add a large-repository regression proving reflection does not materialize every entity.

Extend concurrent mutation regression coverage to session metadata writers. @task-concurrent-mutation-regression-suite currently covers task, plan, inbox, and spec-item APIs, but session.yaml also has whole-file read-modify-write paths: updateSessionStatus, requestEndLoop, closeSession with stats, applyAutoAbandonMetadata, and dispatch ownership publication. Add deterministic behavioral overlaps proving these mutations preserve each other's fields and cannot erase durable exited_at/ownership evidence; reuse the shared per-session mutation boundary added in @task-engine-stop-recovery and avoid wall-clock-only assertions.

Replace raw session JSONL line count with a meaningful logical activity count in session summaries and the Sessions UI. Count each logical tool invocation once by toolCallId, regardless of tool_call_update/progress volume, and count completed assistant messages once after merging agent_message_chunk records. Do not treat message/thought chunks, usage updates, available-command updates, session-info updates, or repeated tool-call progress updates as separate user-facing events. Define whether lifecycle/turn-boundary records belong in the metric, keep active-session and persisted close-time summaries consistent, and add adapter-aware tests covering Codex ACP phased/streamed tool calls. Consider relabeling the UI metric from 'events' to 'activities' or another term that accurately communicates the logical count.

Batch command execution should honor direct-command option defaults. A direct 'kspec review comment' defaults --kind to nit, but the same command inside 'kspec batch' passes kind as undefined and fails atomically with 'Invalid thread kind: undefined'. Apply option defaults consistently in batch execution (or coalesce in the review handler) and add a direct-versus-batch parity regression test.

Batch JSON cannot express negated boolean options: review check with required:false passes batch validation and dry-run, but buildCommandArgv omits false booleans, so --no-required is never emitted and the stored check remains required. Define consistent JSON semantics for negated Commander flags, update argv construction, and add behavioral coverage for optional review checks.

Dispatched Codex reviewer prompts can mandate an unavailable $pr-review entrypoint even when the prepared reviewer agent is configured only with review, review-gates, merge, and shared-guidance-neutrality. In the completed @task-freeze-doc-facts-and-inventory review, 'kspec workflow start @pr-review' returned Workflow not found and no pr-review skill existed under .agents/skills, so the reviewer had to reconstruct the flow from injected skills. Align dispatch role-entry rendering and validation with @dispatch-role-workflow-entry-contract ac-1/ac-4: render the adapter-appropriate installed review entrypoint, or fail before invocation with actionable configuration guidance; add a regression for a configured prompt token that resolves to neither an installed skill nor workflow.

Improve multiword kspec help handling: kspec help agent dispatch currently accepts extra unquoted words but resolves only agent and exits 0, so callers can receive unrelated ancestor help. Either resolve the full command path or reject surplus arguments, and add behavioral Usage and Options tests for nested topics.

plans.title: CLI Agent-UX Improvements
plans.content:
# CLI Agent-UX Improvements

Research-driven improvements to reduce CLI friction for AI agents. Based on analysis of 18,581 events across 4 projects (kynetic-spec, kynetic-bot, imgen, comfy-ecaj-nodes).

## Context

Analysis showed agents hit friction from: bare command errors (15+), single-value --status filters requiring grep pipes, unknown --json flag (5 uses / 14,463 commands), no module-scoped views (dominant bypass reason in newer projects), no unified cross-reference lookup, and no observation content search. After re-baselining against current code, 7 of the original 21 recommendations were already implemented. These 6 remain.

## Specs

```yaml
- title: Command Group Default Actions
  parent: "@cli"
  type: requirement
  traits:
    - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
    - "@trait-error-guidance"
  description: >
    The tasks and task command groups should execute their most common
    subcommand when invoked without a subcommand, instead of showing help text
    and exiting with code 1. This eliminates the most frequent agent dead-end
    (15+ bare kspec tasks errors in telemetry). Scope is limited to tasks
    and task -- other groups (item, meta, inbox) can follow later if telemetry
    supports it.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-bare-tasks
      given: User runs kspec tasks with no subcommand
      when: The command is executed
      then: Output is identical to kspec tasks list and exit code is 0
    - id: ac-bare-task
      given: User runs kspec task with no subcommand
      when: The command is executed
      then: Output is identical to kspec task list (which is aliased to kspec tasks list) and exit code is 0
    - id: ac-bare-with-options
      given: User runs kspec tasks --status pending --json
      when: Options are provided but no subcommand name
      then: Options are forwarded to the default list action
    - id: ac-help-still-works
      given: User runs kspec tasks --help
      when: The --help flag is present
      then: Full command group help is shown (all subcommands listed), not just list help
    - id: ac-subcommands-unaffected
      given: User runs kspec tasks ready or any explicit subcommand
      when: A subcommand is specified
      then: The explicit subcommand runs as before, default action is not triggered
    - id: ac-unknown-subcommand
      given: User runs kspec tasks foo where foo is not a valid subcommand
      when: An unknown subcommand is provided
      then: Error with suggestion is shown (existing fuzzy matching), not the default list action
  implementation_notes: |
    Use Commander.js .action() on the parent command group to define default
    behavior. Extract shared list logic from task.ts (lines 425-511) and
    tasks.ts (lines 37-124) into a common function to eliminate the existing
    code duplication. Both task list and tasks list should call the shared
    function. The default action on tasks and task calls this same function.
    Commander.js routes unknown subcommands to the error handler before the
    default action, so ac-unknown-subcommand should work naturally.

- title: Multi-Value Status Filter
  parent: "@query-filters"
  type: requirement
  traits:
    - "@trait-filterable-list"
    - "@trait-json-output"
  description: |
    The --status filter on list commands should accept multiple values via
    comma-separated syntax or repeated flags. The backend ItemIndex.query()
    already supports TaskStatus[] -- this closes the gap in the CLI layer.
    Agents currently pipe through grep to filter by multiple statuses.
    tasks list uses TaskStatus values (pending, in_progress, pending_review,
    blocked, completed, cancelled) while item list uses ImplementationStatus
    values (not_started, in_progress, implemented, verified). Validation must
    use the correct enum per command.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-comma-separated
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending_review
      when: A comma-separated status value is provided
      then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned
    - id: ac-repeated-flag
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress --status pending_review
      when: The --status flag is provided multiple times
      then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned (same as comma-separated)
    - id: ac-single-value-unchanged
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status pending
      when: A single status value is provided
      then: Behavior is unchanged from current -- only tasks with that status are returned
    - id: ac-invalid-task-status
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status invalid_value
      when: An invalid TaskStatus name is provided
      then: Error message lists valid TaskStatus values and exits non-zero
    - id: ac-invalid-item-status
      given: User runs kspec item list --status invalid_value
      when: An invalid ImplementationStatus name is provided
      then: Error message lists valid ImplementationStatus values and exits non-zero
    - id: ac-item-list-parity
      given: User runs kspec item list --status implemented,verified
      when: Multi-value status is used on item list with ImplementationStatus values
      then: Same comma-separated and repeated-flag behavior works for spec item listing
    - id: ac-json-output
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending --json
      when: Combined with --json flag
      then: JSON output contains only tasks matching the specified statuses
    - id: ac-trailing-comma
      given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress, (trailing comma)
      when: A trailing or leading comma produces an empty string after split
      then: Empty strings are silently ignored, only valid status values are used
  implementation_notes: |
    Parse --status value by splitting on comma, then flatten if Commander.js
    provides an array from repeated flags. Trim whitespace and filter empty
    strings. Route both tasks list and task list through the shared list
    function (from spec 1 refactor) so the fix applies to both. Use
    validateEnumOption to validate each status value individually against the
    correct enum (TaskStatus for tasks, ImplementationStatus for items). Apply
    same pattern to item list --status.

- title: Output Format Option
  parent: "@cli-agent-features"
  type: requirement
  traits:
    - "@trait-json-output"
    - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
  description: |
    Add a --format <json|yaml> global option with --json, --raw, and --yaml as
    shorthands. Agents frequently try --raw and --yaml flags expecting structured
    output. --raw is a shorthand for --format json (agents associate raw with
    give me the data). --yaml is a shorthand for --format yaml. --json remains
    as a shorthand for --format json. The --format option is extensible for
    future formats. This replaces the precedence model in @trait-json-output
    ac-6 with explicit format selection.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-format-json
      given: User runs any command with --format json
      when: The format option is set to json
      then: Output is identical to current --json behavior
    - id: ac-format-yaml
      given: User runs any command with --format yaml
      when: The format option is set to yaml
      then: Output contains the same data as --json but serialized as valid YAML
    - id: ac-json-shorthand
      given: User runs any command with --json
      when: The --json shorthand is used
      then: Equivalent to --format json (backward compatible, existing behavior preserved)
    - id: ac-raw-shorthand
      given: User runs any command with --raw
      when: The --raw shorthand is used
      then: Equivalent to --format json (same data, JSON serialization)
    - id: ac-yaml-shorthand
      given: User runs any command with --yaml
      when: The --yaml shorthand is used
      then: Equivalent to --format yaml
    - id: ac-conflict-error
      given: User runs a command with conflicting format options (e.g. --json --yaml)
      when: Multiple format specifications are provided
      then: Error message explains the conflict and exits non-zero
    - id: ac-yaml-no-ansi
      given: User runs any command with --format yaml
      when: YAML output is generated
      then: Output contains no ANSI escape codes (same contract as --json)
    - id: ac-yaml-references
      given: User runs kspec task get @ref --yaml
      when: Output contains reference fields
      then: References include @ prefix (same contract as --json)
    - id: ac-global-scope
      given: User runs any command that supports structured output with --format, --yaml, or --raw
      when: The option is used on any command
      then: The option works globally (same scope as --json)
    - id: ac-unsupported-format
      given: User runs --format csv or another unsupported format name
      when: An invalid format value is provided
      then: Error message lists valid formats (json, yaml) and exits non-zero
  implementation_notes: |
    Register --format <format> as a global option alongside --json in index.ts.
    Register --raw and --yaml as boolean shorthands that set format. In the
    preAction hook, resolve shorthands to --format value, detect conflicts
    (multiple shorthands or shorthand + --format), then call setJsonMode() or
    a new setYamlMode(). Add yamlOutput() in output.ts using the yaml library
    stringify(). Update output() to check yaml mode. Update @trait-json-output
    ac-6 to reference the --format system instead of the old json takes
    precedence behavior.

- title: Module-Scoped Item Listing
  parent: "@cli"
  type: requirement
  traits:
    - "@trait-json-output"
    - "@trait-filterable-list"
    - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
  description: |
    Add --under filter to item list that scopes output to descendants of a
    given module or parent item. This is the number one remaining reason agents
    bypass the CLI to read .kspec/ YAML directly. Combines with existing --tree
    flag for hierarchical display. Promotes inbox item @01KGVK8R. Ancestry is
    determined by structural nesting in YAML source files (_path metadata),
    not by relationship fields like implements.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-under-filter
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @cli
      when: The --under flag specifies a module or parent item
      then: Only items structurally nested under the specified item (same source file, descendant _path) are listed
    - id: ac-under-with-tree
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @cli --tree
      when: Combined with --tree flag
      then: Hierarchical tree display shows only the subtree rooted at the specified item
    - id: ac-under-root-included
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @cli
      when: The specified item is a module
      then: The module itself is included in the output as the root node
    - id: ac-under-with-other-filters
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @tasks --status implemented --type requirement
      when: --under is combined with other filters
      then: Filters are applied within the scoped subtree (AND logic)
    - id: ac-under-json
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @cli --json
      when: Combined with --json flag
      then: JSON array contains only items in the subtree, each with full item data
    - id: ac-under-invalid-ref
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @nonexistent
      when: The specified reference does not resolve
      then: Error message says reference not found, suggests checking with kspec item get
    - id: ac-nested-descendants
      given: A module contains nested items at multiple depth levels (module, feature, requirement)
      when: User runs kspec item list --under @parent-module
      then: All transitive descendants within the same source file are included
    - id: ac-count-with-under
      given: User runs kspec item list --under @cli --count
      when: Combined with --count flag
      then: Count reflects only items in the scoped subtree
  implementation_notes: |
    Items do NOT have a parent field in the schema. Parent-child hierarchy is
    determined by YAML nesting, encoded in the _path metadata field (e.g.
    features[0].requirements[1]). The existing formatItemTree() in item.ts
    (lines 121-177) builds parent-child maps by parsing _path. The existing
    findChildItems() in parser/items.ts (lines 422-455) finds direct children
    only -- extend it or build a new findDescendantItems() that collects all
    items sharing the same _sourceFile whose _path starts with the target
    _path prefix. Resolve --under ref via ReferenceIndex, find the target
    _sourceFile and _path, then filter the item list. Apply other filters
    after scoping.

- title: Unified Cross-Reference Lookup
  parent: "@cli"
  type: feature
  traits:
    - "@trait-json-output"
    - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
    - "@trait-error-guidance"
  description: |
    New kspec refs command that shows all inbound references to a given entity
    across all entity types. Currently link list --to only covers spec-to-spec
    relationships. Agents grep YAML to find tasks implementing a spec, specs
    depending on another spec, or meta items referencing an entity. Related to
    inbox item @01KFHJNZ (reverse spec lookup).
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-task-spec-ref
      given: Tasks T1 and T2 have spec_ref pointing to @my-spec
      when: User runs kspec refs @my-spec
      then: Output includes T1 and T2 under a Tasks (spec_ref) section
    - id: ac-task-depends-on
      given: Task T2 has depends_on including @task-1
      when: User runs kspec refs @task-1
      then: Output includes T2 under a Tasks (depends_on) section
    - id: ac-spec-depends-on
      given: Spec B has depends_on including @spec-a
      when: User runs kspec refs @spec-a
      then: Output includes B under a Specs (depends_on) section
    - id: ac-spec-implements
      given: Spec C has implements including @spec-a
      when: User runs kspec refs @spec-a
      then: Output includes C under a Specs (implements) section
    - id: ac-spec-relates-to
      given: Spec D has relates_to including @spec-a
      when: User runs kspec refs @spec-a
      then: Output includes D under a Specs (relates_to) section
    - id: ac-trait-references
      given: Specs X, Y, Z have traits including @my-trait
      when: User runs kspec refs @my-trait
      then: Output includes X, Y, Z under a Specs (traits) section
    - id: ac-meta-ref
      given: Task T has meta_ref pointing to @workflow-1
      when: User runs kspec refs @workflow-1
      then: Output includes T under a Tasks (meta_ref) section
    - id: ac-supersedes
      given: Spec E has supersedes including @old-spec
      when: User runs kspec refs @old-spec
      then: Output includes E under a Specs (supersedes) section
    - id: ac-grouped-output
      given: Multiple entity types reference the target
      when: User runs kspec refs @ref
      then: Output is grouped by relationship type with clear section headers
    - id: ac-json-structured
      given: User runs kspec refs @ref --json
      when: JSON output is requested
      then: JSON object contains keys per reference type, each an array of referencing entities with slug, title, and type
    - id: ac-no-refs
      given: Nothing references @isolated-item
      when: User runs kspec refs @isolated-item
      then: Output says No references found for @isolated-item and exit code is 0
    - id: ac-ref-resolution
      given: User provides a ULID, slug, or short ULID
      when: The ref is resolved
      then: All reference formats are supported via ReferenceIndex
  implementation_notes: |
    New command file src/cli/commands/refs.ts, registered in index.ts. Loads
    all tasks, items, and meta items. Scans each entity reference fields:
    spec_ref, depends_on, implements, relates_to, supersedes, superseded_by,
    traits, meta_ref, plan_ref, blocked_by. Collects matches grouped by
    (entity_type, field_name). Uses ReferenceIndex for target resolution.
    Output via output() with grouped human-readable formatter. Performance:
    full scan of all entities per query -- acceptable for current scale
    (hundreds of items), may need indexing later.

- title: Observation Content Search
  parent: "@observations"
  type: requirement
  traits:
    - "@trait-json-output"
    - "@trait-filterable-list"
  description: |
    Add content search to observation listing and global search. Currently
    kspec search includes observations but cannot filter to observations only,
    and kspec meta observations has type/workflow/status filters but no content
    search. Agents grep observation YAML when they need to find observations
    by content.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-search-flag
      given: User runs kspec meta observations --search shadow branch
      when: A search pattern is provided
      then: Only observations whose text matches the pattern are returned
    - id: ac-regex-support
      given: User runs kspec meta observations --search fix or bug pattern
      when: A regex pattern is provided
      then: Pattern is treated as regex (consistent with kspec search behavior)
    - id: ac-combined-filters
      given: User runs kspec meta observations --search cli --type friction
      when: --search is combined with --type filter
      then: Both filters apply (AND logic) -- only friction observations matching cli
    - id: ac-search-all-fields
      given: An observation has matching text in its description but not title
      when: User searches for that text
      then: The observation is found (search covers all text fields)
    - id: ac-search-json
      given: User runs kspec meta observations --search pattern --json
      when: Combined with --json
      then: JSON output contains only matching observations
    - id: ac-global-search-filter
      given: User wants to search only observations via the global search command
      when: User runs kspec search pattern --observations-only
      then: Results are limited to observation matches only (excludes items, tasks, inbox)
    - id: ac-only-flags-exclusive
      given: User runs kspec search pattern --observations-only --items-only
      when: Multiple scope-only flags are provided
      then: Error message explains the flags are mutually exclusive and exits non-zero
  implementation_notes: |
    Reuse the grep utility from src/utils/grep.ts that kspec search already
    uses. Add --search option to the meta observations subcommand in meta.ts.
    Apply search filter after type/workflow/status filters. For the global
    search --observations-only flag, add a new filter option to search.ts
    alongside existing --items-only and --tasks-only flags. Make the scope-only
    flags mutually exclusive with a validation check before search execution.
```

## Tasks

derive_from_specs: true

## Implementation Notes

### Execution Order
1. Command Group Default Actions + Multi-Value Status Filter (share the list
   handler refactor -- extract common function first, then add both features)
2. Output Format Option (independent, touches global output system)
3. Module-Scoped Item Listing (independent, extends item list)
4. Unified Cross-Reference Lookup (independent, new command)
5. Observation Content Search (independent, extends meta command)

### Existing Spec Updates Needed
- @trait-json-output ac-6: Update from --json takes precedence to reference
  the new --format system and conflict error behavior
- @trait-filterable-list: Note that --status supports multi-value
- @cli-agent-features description: Mention --format, --yaml, and --raw

### Inbox Items to Promote
- @01KGVK8R -- Module-scoped item list (covered by spec 4)
- @01KFHJNZ -- Reverse spec lookup (partially covered by spec 5)

### Separate Deliverables (Not In This Plan)
- Docs task: Update AGENTS.md and skill prompts for --json discoverability
- Inbox item: Observation count in session start output

plans.title: Portable Agent Integration Infrastructure
plans.content:
# Portable Agent Integration Infrastructure

## Specs

```yaml
# ── Phase 1: Skill Meta Type ──────────────────────────────────

- title: Skill Meta Type
  slug: skill-meta-type
  type: feature
  description: |
    Add Skill as the 5th meta item type in the kspec data model.
    Metadata stored in kynetic.meta.yaml, content in .kspec/skills/<id>/ files.
    Eliminates 90% skill drift across 4 projects by making skills first-class
    data managed by kspec.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: a kynetic.meta.yaml with a skills array containing valid skill entries
      when: the file is parsed via MetaManifestSchema
      then: each skill entry validates against SkillSchema
    - id: ac-2
      given: a skill with origin core and version 0.2.0
      when: validated by SkillSchema
      then: it passes validation with origin set to core
    - id: ac-3
      given: a skill meta entry exists and .kspec/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md exists
      when: loadSkillContent(ctx, skill) is called
      then: the full markdown content of SKILL.md is returned
    - id: ac-4
      given: loadMetaContext() is called on a manifest with 3 skills
      when: parsing completes
      then: MetaContext.skills contains 3 LoadedSkill objects with _sourceFile set
    - id: ac-5
      given: a skill with id task-work exists in meta
      when: findMetaItemByRef(meta, task-work) is called
      then: the skill is returned by semantic id lookup
    - id: ac-6
      given: a skill ULID prefix is provided to findMetaItemByRef
      when: the prefix matches exactly one skill
      then: the skill is returned by ULID prefix lookup
    - id: ac-7
      given: getMetaItemType is called with a skill object
      when: the discriminator evaluates the object
      then: it returns skill (discriminated by the origin field unique to skills)
  traits:
    - trait-json-output
    - trait-error-guidance

- title: Skill Schema Definition
  slug: skill-schema
  type: requirement
  parent: "@skill-meta-type"
  description: |
    Zod schema for skill metadata. Lean schema — content lives in files.
    Fields: _ulid, id (kebab-case regex), name, description, origin (core|custom),
    version (optional semver), platforms array, depends_on refs, tags.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: a skill object with id containing uppercase or special characters
      when: validated by SkillSchema
```

## Implementation Notes

This plan builds portable agent integration infrastructure for kspec. The 5 phases
are independently deliverable:

Phase 1 (skill-meta-type): Schema + parser + validation. Foundation everything else builds on.
Phase 2 (skill-cli): CLI commands including import for migration.
Phase 3 (skill-rendering): Shadow branch to main branch rendering pipeline.
Phase 4 (agent-instruction-gen): Template + data assembly for kspec-agents.md.
Phase 5 (enhanced-setup): Orchestration + npm distribution.

Task dependencies to set post-import (derive does not infer from spec hierarchy):
- All Phase 2 tasks depend on Phase 1 tasks
- Phase 3 tasks depend on Phase 1 and Phase 2
- Phase 4 tasks depend on Phase 1
- Phase 5 tasks depend on Phase 3 and Phase 4

Key architecture decisions:
- Skill metadata in meta YAML, content in .kspec/skills/<id>/ files (avoids YAML escaping)
- Dedicated kspec skill namespace (not under kspec meta)
- Template-based AGENTS.md generation (not convention-to-prose derivation)
- Cross-branch rendering: reads shadow branch, writes main branch, no auto-commit
- Drift detection via SHA-256 hash stored in .kspec/skills/<id>/.render-hash
- Discriminator uses origin field (unique to skills among meta types)
- Clean flag only removes kspec-managed dirs (tracked via render-hash presence)

New files to create:
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts (dedicated skill commands)
- src/cli/commands/agents.ts (agents generate/status)
- src/renderer/skills.ts (rendering pipeline)
- src/renderer/agents-md.ts (agent instruction generator)
- src/renderer/index.ts (re-exports)
- templates/ directory tree (skills, agents-sections, hooks)

Existing files to modify:
- src/schema/meta.ts (SkillSchema, MetaManifestSchema, discriminator)
- src/parser/meta.ts (LoadedSkill, MetaContext, CRUD, refs)
- src/parser/validate.ts (skill validation loops)
- src/cli/commands/meta.ts (ref resolution, list, show, get)
- src/cli/commands/setup.ts (orchestration)
