plans.title: Completeness Warning Debt Reduction
plans.content:
# Completeness Warning Debt Reduction Plan

## Goal

Reduce `kspec validate --completeness` warning volume in a way that improves review signal, avoids low-value content churn, and leaves the validator stricter where the warnings are genuinely actionable.

This plan covers the four core debt classes called out in the spike:

1. Missing acceptance criteria
2. Missing descriptions
3. Missing own AC coverage
4. Missing trait AC coverage

`automation_eligible_no_spec` remains related but separate debt. It stays on its existing task track because it is primarily task/spec linkage policy, not spec-content authoring.

## Current Baseline

Snapshot captured on 2026-03-07 via `kspec validate --completeness --json --warnings-ok`.

| Warning family | Count | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `missing_acceptance_criteria` | 149 | Concentrated in modules, structural schema items, state taxonomy items, and older foundational specs |
| `missing_description` | 7 | Small, direct cleanup wave |
| `missing_test_coverage` (`own_ac`) | 106 | Broad foundation/review debt; several items cluster around validation, references, schema, and status behavior |
| `missing_test_coverage` (`trait_ac`) | 6 | All six warnings come from `@trait-priority-parameter` applied to six command families |
| `automation_eligible_no_spec` | 144 | Parallel track owned by `@task-triage-automation-eligible-missing-spec-ref` |

Compared with the 2026-02-28 baseline captured in `@task-stabilize-kspec-validate-baseline`, the current state is:

| Warning family | 2026-02-28 | 2026-03-07 | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Missing acceptance criteria | 156 | 149 | -7 |
| Missing descriptions | 6 | 7 | +1 |
| Missing own AC coverage | 93 | 106 | +13 |
| Missing trait AC coverage | 7 | 6 | -1 |
| Automation without spec | 128 | 144 | +16 |

Implication: the backlog is not steadily burning down on its own. Without explicit wave gates, completeness debt will keep moving sideways.

## Plan Principles

1. Preserve validator signal over raw warning-count reduction.
2. Prefer fixing warning generators and policy mismatches before bulk-writing specs/tests.
3. Use families that can be batch-closed together as early waves.
4. Keep the output reviewable: each wave needs a hard entry/exit gate.
5. Treat structural containers differently from behavioral specs when the warning is not actually actionable.

## Rule Refinement Candidates

These are the places where the likely right answer is validator or taxonomy refinement, not mass content churn:

- Module items such as `@core`, `@schema`, and `@tasks` are organizational containers. Requiring standalone AC on every module likely adds noise more than signal.
- Taxonomy leaves such as state definitions (`@state-pending`, `@state-blocked`) and some structural schema leaves may be better represented by parent-spec AC rather than repeated leaf-level AC.
- The placeholder `@01KJN1WT` "Test Trait" should be removed, moved to isolated fixtures, or explicitly excluded from production completeness scans. It should not drive real backlog.
- `automation_eligible_no_spec` is a workflow-policy warning family, not spec-content debt. Keep it on the parallel task track instead of mixing it into these waves.
- The existing observation `@01KHYTNNFY` on behavioral-vs-testable ACs should be revisited before forcing the long tail of own-AC coverage to zero. Some workflow/agent-behavior ACs may need distinct treatment from code-testable ACs.

## Waves

### Wave 0: Classification and Baseline Freeze

Purpose: stop arguing about categories during execution.

Scope:

- Export the current completeness warning inventory and classify each warning family as:
  - content debt
  - rule-refinement candidate
  - fixture/test-data cleanup
  - parallel-track dependency
- Document which item classes are expected to carry their own AC and which are allowed to inherit meaning from parents.
- Confirm ownership boundaries with the existing automation-without-spec task.

Acceptance gate:

- Every current completeness warning family has an explicit disposition.
- No new completeness warning types are introduced during the wave.
- The project has a written decision on whether modules and state-taxonomy leaves should continue to require standalone AC.

Suggested deliverables:

- A classification note attached to this plan or a follow-up implementation task.
- A small validator-policy task if modules/state items are formally exempted.

### Wave 1: Close Low-Churn Hygiene Debt

Purpose: remove the smallest, clearest backlog first.

Scope:

- Resolve all 7 missing-description warnings.
- Remove or quarantine the `@01KJN1WT` placeholder test trait if it should not exist in production metadata.
- Opportunistically fix single-item missing-AC or missing-description warnings encountered in touched areas when the intended behavior is already obvious.

Acceptance gate:

- `missing_description` reaches 0.
- The placeholder test trait no longer appears in completeness output.
- No new missing-description warnings are introduced by the wave.

Why first:

- This is cheap, reviewable, and creates early momentum without making policy decisions irreversible.

### Wave 2: Eliminate Priority-Parameter Trait Coverage Debt

Purpose: close the one clearly batched trait-coverage family.

Current cluster:

- `@batch-exec`
- `@task-commands`
- `@derive-commands`
- `@inbox-commands`
- `@plan-support`
- `@meta-commands`

All six currently miss the same inherited AC set from `@trait-priority-parameter`.

Scope:

- Add or repair the test annotations needed for `@trait-priority-parameter` across the six command families.
- Add direct coverage for `@trait-priority-parameter` itself so the trait does not remain an own-AC warning after the inherited warnings are closed.
- If the annotation pattern or expected test location is unclear, settle that once and codify it in review guidance before backfilling all six families.

Acceptance gate:

- `missing_test_coverage` with subtype `trait_ac` reaches 0.
- `@trait-priority-parameter` no longer appears in own-AC coverage warnings.
- Local validation/review guidance reflects the annotation pattern used by the batch fix.

Why second:

- It is a bounded family with one root trait and six consumers, so the payoff-to-churn ratio is high.

### Wave 3: Burn Down Review-Critical Own-AC Coverage

Purpose: reduce the own-coverage backlog where it most directly improves review quality and validator trust.

Priority families:

- Validation and review specs such as `@validation`, `@validation-modes`, `@spec-completeness`
- Reference and identity specs such as `@reference-system`, `@ulid-system`, `@slug-system`, `@slug-uniqueness`, `@slug-resolution`
- Core schema/type behavior such as `@type-module`, `@type-feature`, `@type-requirement`, `@type-constraint`, `@type-decision`, `@type-task`
- Relationship/status behavior such as `@rel-depends-on`, `@rel-implements`, `@rel-relates-to`, `@rel-blocks`, `@status-cascade`

Scope:

- Add tests and `// AC:` annotations for the review-critical slice first.
- Use shared helpers and grouped tests where they already exist instead of creating one-off files per spec.
- Revisit the behavioral-vs-testable distinction before tackling any item whose AC is not naturally enforceable in code.

Acceptance gate:

- Review-critical specs in this slice have zero own-AC coverage gaps.
- Global own-AC warning count drops materially from 106, with the minimum target set at 50 or fewer before the wave is considered complete.
- Any remaining own-AC warnings are classified into either:
  - still-actionable backlog
  - pending rule refinement

Why third:

- This is the warning family that most directly affects `kspec-review`, local review quality, and confidence in validator-backed approval gates.

### Wave 4: Resolve Missing-AC Debt by Splitting Structural vs Behavioral Items

Purpose: handle the largest backlog without blindly generating AC on every item.

Observed pattern:

- Many of the 149 warnings are not random omissions; they cluster around modules, structural schema items, file-structure taxonomy, status/state taxonomy, and older high-level feature containers.

Scope:

- Decide which item categories must carry standalone AC.
- For approved behavioral categories, add real AC that describe observable behavior.
- For approved structural-container categories, refine the validator so it stops demanding low-value leaf/module AC.
- Remove or consolidate obsolete items when the better fix is cleanup rather than documentation.

Acceptance gate:

- Every remaining missing-AC warning belongs to an intentionally actionable category.
- Either:
  - `missing_acceptance_criteria` drops below 40, or
  - the remaining warnings are only for categories the project has explicitly decided to keep actionable.
- Any validator refinement is covered by regression tests so the count reduction is durable.

Why fourth:

- This is the highest-volume bucket, but a large part of it appears taxonomy-driven. Running it earlier would create the most content churn for the least clarity.

## Parallel Track

`automation_eligible_no_spec` should continue on `@task-triage-automation-eligible-missing-spec-ref`.

Coordination rule:

- Do not claim completeness debt reduction from that family inside these waves.
- Re-baseline counts after that task lands, because it currently contributes 144 warnings to the same report output and affects perceived validate noise.

## Recommended Execution Order

1. Wave 0 classification/policy decision
2. Wave 1 missing-description + fixture cleanup
3. Wave 2 `@trait-priority-parameter` closure
4. Wave 3 own-AC coverage for review-critical specs
5. Wave 4 missing-AC policy split and backfill

This order intentionally moves from low-churn/high-certainty work toward the policy-heavy structural backlog.

## Exit Condition for the Overall Initiative

The completeness warning backlog is considered under control when all of the following are true:

- Missing descriptions are at 0.
- Trait AC coverage warnings are at 0.
- Own AC coverage warnings are reduced to a small, classified remainder rather than a broad unknown backlog.
- Missing-AC warnings are limited to intentionally actionable categories, not modules/taxonomy containers the project has chosen not to model that way.
- Automation-without-spec warnings are tracked independently and no longer conflated with spec-content debt planning.

At that point, `kspec validate --completeness` becomes a tractable review signal again instead of a bulk debt dump.

plans.title: Session Storage Separation
plans.content:
# Session Storage Separation

Decouple session storage from the shadow branch (`kspec-meta`) to eliminate sync conflicts, reduce shadow branch bloat, and support local-only or independently git-tracked sessions.

## Specs

```yaml
- title: Session Storage Modes
  slug: session-storage-modes
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-model-evolution"
  tags: [session, storage, mvp]
  description: |
    Configurable session storage with two modes: local (default) and branch.
    Local mode writes to .kspec-sessions/ with no git tracking. Branch mode
    writes to .kspec-sessions/ backed by a named orphan branch for persistence.
    Shadow mode (sessions on kspec-meta) is legacy read-only — never written to.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-config
      given: |
        A kspec project with kynetic.yaml
      when: |
        sessions.storage is set to "local" or "branch"
      then: |
        Session operations use the configured storage mode.
    - id: ac-config-default
      given: |
        A kspec project with no sessions.storage in kynetic.yaml
      when: |
        A session operation runs
      then: |
        Defaults to "local" mode.
    - id: ac-config-invalid
      given: |
        sessions.storage is set to an unsupported value
      when: |
        kspec validates the manifest
      then: |
        Zod validation error with message indicating valid values (local, branch).
    - id: ac-local-mode
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "local" (or unconfigured)
      when: |
        A session is created, events appended, or session closed
      then: |
        Files are written to .kspec-sessions/{id}/ with no git operations.
    - id: ac-branch-mode
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" with a branch name configured
      when: |
        A session is created or closed
      then: |
        Files are written to .kspec-sessions/ which is a git worktree
        on the configured orphan branch. Auto-commits on session lifecycle
        boundaries (create, close, stale cleanup, compact) but NOT on every event append.
    - id: ac-branch-name
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        sessions.branch is set (e.g., "kspec-sessions")
      then: |
        The orphan branch uses the configured name.
    - id: ac-branch-name-default
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" with no sessions.branch set
      when: |
        Session branch is initialized
      then: |
        Default branch name is "kspec-sessions".
    - id: ac-no-event-commits
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        An event is appended to events.jsonl during active session
      then: |
        No git commit occurs. Events are committed in bulk at session close.
    - id: ac-sessions-dir
      given: |
        Any storage mode
      when: |
        Session operations resolve file paths
      then: |
        Sessions directory is .kspec-sessions/ at project root,
        separate from .kspec/ (which remains spec/task only).
    - id: ac-sessions-dir-autocreate
      given: |
        .kspec-sessions/ directory does not exist
      when: |
        A session create operation runs
      then: |
        The directory is created automatically (mkdir -p equivalent).
    - id: ac-gitignore
      given: |
        A kspec project
      when: |
        kspec init or kspec setup runs
      then: |
        .kspec-sessions/ is added to the project root .gitignore
        (not tracked on main branch regardless of storage mode).

- title: Legacy Session Migration
  slug: session-legacy-migration
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-model-evolution"
  tags: [session, storage, migration, mvp]
  description: |
    Read-only fallback for sessions stored on the kspec-meta shadow branch
    (.kspec/sessions/) from before the storage separation. Provides migration
    path with deprecation timeline.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-read-fallback
      given: |
        A session ID is requested that does not exist in .kspec-sessions/
      when: |
        Any session read operation executes (get, list, log show, log search)
      then: |
        Falls back to reading from .kspec/sessions/ on kspec-meta.
        Result is returned normally — caller does not need to know the source.
    - id: ac-no-write
      given: |
        Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/ on kspec-meta
      when: |
        Any session write operation occurs (create, append, close, compact)
      then: |
        Writes always go to .kspec-sessions/, never to .kspec/sessions/.
    - id: ac-list-merge
      given: |
        Sessions exist in both .kspec-sessions/ and .kspec/sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session log list runs
      then: |
        Results include sessions from both locations, deduplicated by ID,
        with .kspec-sessions/ taking precedence for duplicates.
    - id: ac-deprecation-warning
      given: |
        A session is read from the legacy .kspec/sessions/ location
      when: |
        The read completes
      then: |
        A deprecation warning is emitted (stderr, not stdout) noting
        the legacy location. Warning includes guidance to run kspec session migrate.
    - id: ac-shadow-gitignore
      given: |
        kspec setup or kspec init runs
      when: |
        .kspec/sessions/ exists on kspec-meta
      then: |
        sessions/ is added to .kspec/.gitignore so no new session files
        are tracked on kspec-meta. Existing history is preserved in git.
    - id: ac-migration-copy
      given: |
        Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session migrate runs
      then: |
        Copies session directories from .kspec/sessions/ to .kspec-sessions/.
        Does not delete originals.
    - id: ac-migration-idempotent
      given: |
        Some sessions already exist in .kspec-sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session migrate runs
      then: |
        Skips sessions that already exist in target.
        Reports count of migrated and skipped sessions.

- title: Session Storage Path Resolution
  slug: session-storage-path-resolution
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-events"
  tags: [session, storage, refactor, mvp]
  description: |
    Centralized path resolution for session storage that all session
    operations use. Replaces hardcoded specDir/sessions paths with
    a resolver that accounts for storage mode configuration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-resolver
      given: |
        Any session operation needs a file path
      when: |
        It calls the session path resolver
      then: |
        Returns paths rooted at .kspec-sessions/ (project root),
        not .kspec/sessions/.
    - id: ac-path-helpers
      given: |
        Existing path helpers (getSessionDir, getSessionEventsPath, etc.)
      when: |
        They resolve session paths
      then: |
        All use the new sessions root from the resolver.
    - id: ac-context
      given: |
        initContext() is called
      when: |
        Context is resolved
      then: |
        Context includes sessionsDir alongside specDir.
        sessionsDir points to .kspec-sessions/ at project root.
    - id: ac-cli-commands
      given: |
        A CLI session command accesses session data
      when: |
        It resolves session paths
      then: |
        Uses ctx.sessionsDir (not ctx.specDir) for all session file operations.
    - id: ac-daemon-routes
      given: |
        A daemon API route serves session data (/api/sessions/*)
      when: |
        It resolves session paths
      then: |
        Uses sessionsDir from project context for all session file operations.

- title: Session Branch Worktree Management
  slug: session-branch-worktree
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, git, post-mvp]
  description: |
    Git worktree management for the session branch mode. Creates and
    maintains an orphan branch with its own worktree at .kspec-sessions/.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-init
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" and no session worktree exists
      when: |
        kspec init or kspec setup runs
      then: |
        Creates orphan branch with configured name (default "kspec-sessions"),
        adds worktree at .kspec-sessions/.
    - id: ac-commit-boundaries
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        Session lifecycle events occur (create, close, stale cleanup, compact)
      then: |
        Auto-commits to session branch at lifecycle boundaries only.
        Event appends during active sessions are NOT committed individually.
    - id: ac-sync
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" and remote tracking is configured
      when: |
        Daemon shadow sync runs
      then: |
        Session branch syncs independently from kspec-meta.
        Sync failures on one branch do not affect the other.
    - id: ac-status
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        kspec shadow status runs
      then: |
        Reports health of both kspec-meta and session branch worktrees.
    - id: ac-repair
      given: |
        Session worktree is broken or disconnected
      when: |
        kspec shadow repair runs
      then: |
        Repairs session worktree independently from kspec-meta worktree.

- title: Remove Shadow Commits for Sessions
  slug: session-remove-shadow-commits
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, refactor, mvp]
  description: |
    Remove all shadowAutoCommit calls related to session operations.
    Sessions no longer dirty the kspec-meta worktree.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-invocation-end
      given: |
        An agent invocation ends (completed, timed_out, failed, aborted)
      when: |
        closeSession() is called in invocation.ts
      then: |
        No shadowAutoCommit is called for the session.
        Task state changes (if any) still commit to kspec-meta normally.
    - id: ac-stale-cleanup
      given: |
        Stale session auto-abandon runs
      when: |
        Session metadata is updated to abandoned
      then: |
        Commit goes to session branch (if branch mode) or nowhere (if local).
        No commit to kspec-meta.
    - id: ac-no-sync-conflict
      given: |
        Dispatch engine creates sessions while daemon syncs shadow branch
      when: |
        Periodic shadow sync runs shadowPull on kspec-meta
      then: |
        No conflict occurs because session files are not in the kspec-meta worktree.

- title: Update Existing Session Specs for Storage Separation
  slug: session-spec-path-updates
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-model-evolution"
  tags: [session, storage, refactor, mvp]
  description: |
    Update existing session-related specs that hardcode .kspec/sessions/ paths
    or inherit @trait-shadow-commit, to reflect the new .kspec-sessions/ storage
    location and the removal of shadow branch commits for sessions.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-session-events-paths
      given: |
        @session-events ac-1 and ac-8 reference .kspec/sessions/{id}/
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        ACs are updated to reference .kspec-sessions/{id}/ instead.
    - id: ac-session-events-commits
      given: |
        @session-events ac-7 says "events are included in next kspec commit"
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        AC is updated to reflect storage-mode-dependent behavior:
        local mode has no commits, branch mode commits at lifecycle boundaries.
    - id: ac-session-creation-paths
      given: |
        @session-creation-and-env-injection ac-create references .kspec/sessions/{id}/
        and ac-budget-local references .kspec/sessions/{id}/budget.json
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        ACs are updated to reference .kspec-sessions/{id}/ instead.
    - id: ac-compact-trait
      given: |
        @session-compact inherits @trait-shadow-commit
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        @trait-shadow-commit is removed from @session-compact since compact
        now operates on .kspec-sessions/ which is not the shadow worktree.
    - id: ac-stale-cleanup-trait
      given: |
        @session-stale-cleanup inherits @trait-shadow-commit
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        @trait-shadow-commit is removed from @session-stale-cleanup since
        stale cleanup no longer commits to kspec-meta.
    - id: ac-session-log-list-path
      given: |
        @session-log-list ac-1 references .kspec/sessions/ in its given clause
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        AC is updated to reference .kspec-sessions/ instead.
    - id: ac-session-creation-description
      given: |
        @session-creation-and-env-injection description references
        .kspec/sessions/{id}/budget.json
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        Description is updated to reference .kspec-sessions/ paths.
    - id: ac-cli-ralph-path
      given: |
        @cli-ralph ac-22 references .kspec/sessions/{session}/tool-output/
      when: |
        This plan is implemented
      then: |
        AC is updated to reference .kspec-sessions/ paths instead.
```

## Tasks

```yaml
- title: "Add sessions.storage config to manifest schema"
  spec_ref: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, schema]
  priority: 1
  description: |
    Add sessions.storage (local|branch) and sessions.branch (string) to
    kynetic.yaml schema. Default storage to "local". Validate in Zod schema.
  implementation_notes: |
    Update src/schema/ manifest types. The config is read during initContext()
    to determine session path resolution.

- title: "Extract session path resolution from specDir"
  spec_ref: "@session-storage-path-resolution"

  implementation_notes: |
    Key files: src/sessions/store.ts (path helpers lines 54-115),

- title: "Remove shadowAutoCommit from session operations"

  implementation_notes: |
    invocation.ts lines 428, 471, 503, 527 — remove session shadow commits.
    store.ts line 1612 (stale cleanup) — remove or redirect.
    Keep task-related shadow commits unchanged.

- title: "Update existing session specs for new storage paths"
  spec_ref: "@session-spec-path-updates"
  tags: [session, storage, spec]

  description: |
    Update ACs in @session-events, @session-creation-and-env-injection,

    Update @session-creation-and-env-injection description for new paths.
    Remove @trait-shadow-commit from @session-compact and @session-stale-cleanup.
    Update @session-events ac-7 for storage-mode-dependent commit behavior.
    Review @session-end-loop-signal and @agent-invocation-lifecycle — confirm
    no AC text changes needed (they don't hardcode paths), but ensure any
    in-progress implementation uses the new path resolver.

- title: "Update kspec init/setup for session directory"
  spec_ref: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, cli]
  priority: 2
```
