This flag ordering quirk isn't documented in codex --help and caused a runtime failure that required a fix commit.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: GitHub PR review API with --input JSON file works reliably for inline comments. Pattern: write structured JSON to /tmp/codex-pr-review-body.json with {event, body, comments[{path, line, body}]}, then post via gh api repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews --method POST --input file. Codex figured out the line vs position issue on its own (first attempt used line numbers which mapped to null, then corrected to diff positions).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review as documentation quality gate: /codex pr caught real arg-name bugs in batch JSON examples that would have caused user failures. The review→fix→push cycle was fast. Worth using on all docs-heavy PRs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex plan review as pre-import quality gate caught trait ref format bug and compound AC issues. Worth making standard practice for plan imports with 3+ specs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent research (two Explore agents) during spec-plan design phase efficiently gathered session infrastructure context in ~60s instead of sequential exploration.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review on self-authored PRs creates review threads that trigger check-unresolved-comments CI gate. Requires manual GraphQL thread resolution + CI re-run before merging. Codex skill should either skip inline comments on own PRs or auto-resolve threads after posting.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Tracing ACP bugs through the chain (framing.ts → client.ts → spawner.ts → ralph.ts) was efficient because the codebase has clear layering and the override mechanism (methodTimeouts) was already in place. Minimal change (18 lines, 3 files) for the fix.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task @01KGVARW had excellent root cause analysis in its notes (specific file, line numbers, all call sites, exact reproduction). This made the fix trivial — under 10 minutes from start to merged PR. Detailed bug reports with root cause are high-leverage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Batch triage workflow: categorize inbox by theme first, quick-win deletions, then one-at-a-time promotion with AskUserQuestion showing What/Why/How context. Cross-reference against git log and completed tasks to catch already-done items. This pattern processed 61 items efficiently.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Implementation notes at promotion time: adding concrete implementation notes during inbox promote (not after) makes tasks self-contained for future agents. Include: which files to modify, patterns to follow, approximate scope.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Automation triage forces context switch to spec creation: when assessing eligibility, discovering a task needs a spec means switching from assessment mode to authoring mode (find module, find parent, create item, add ACs, link task). Consider a guided flow or --create-spec flag on task set --automation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review caught silent bug in session log list — tasks_completed metric searched for non-existent event type. Real task completions use session.update tool_call events with rawInput.command containing 'task complete'. Without review, feature would ship reporting 0 tasks for all real sessions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session event data payloads are untyped — EventTypeSchema defines the type enum but data field is z.unknown(). Had to grep through real JSONL files to discover that Ralph records task completions as session.update events with sessionUpdate: 'tool_call' and rawInput.command. This caused a bug that was only caught by Codex reviewing against real data.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Commander's .option() parse function (e.g. parseInt) silently pre-coerces values before the action handler runs. When replacing inline validation with shared helpers, the helper never sees the raw string. This caused a bug in PR #347 where derive/plan-derive still accepted '3abc' as priority 3. Fix: never use Commander parse functions for options validated by shared helpers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Using Codex (/codex pr) as an automated second reviewer caught a real bug (Commander parseInt pre-parse bypass) that manual review missed. The review-fix-re-review cycle completed in one session. Worth using for every non-trivial PR.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Documentation tasks that update README/AGENTS.md should also check skill files (.claude/skills/) for staleness on the same topics. Easy to miss because skills are a separate concern. A validate --skills --docs check could catch this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Running 4 parallel Explore/Bash subagents to research README structure, AGENTS.md structure, full CLI catalog, and recent git features simultaneously saved significant time and produced comprehensive input for the docs update.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AGENTS.md task state transitions documented task complete as working from in_progress/pending, but CLI actually requires pending_review (or --skip-review). Pre-existing inaccuracy that propagated to README. Codex caught it via runtime spot-checks that I did not do.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Stale index mutation pattern: when mutating items in a loop with a pre-built refIndex, track created slugs in a parallel Set since refIndex won't see loop-created items. Pattern: importReservedSlugs Set alongside refIndex.isSlugAvailable(). Applied in plan-import to prevent cross-namespace slug collisions within a single import run.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex iterative review as convergence loop: codex review → fix → re-review converges on correctness. 4 rounds on PR #346 found progressively deeper cross-namespace slug collision gaps (duplicate_slug handling → plans missing from refIndex → stale index for import-created specs → spec creation not checking importReservedSlugs). Each round caught a real bug.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex review depth insufficient on first pass: 4 review rounds were needed to fully validate plan-import slug safety. Each fix introduced or revealed the next gap. Root cause: Codex reviews surface-level patterns first (wrong API check) before deeper ones (stale index across mutations). Need a way to prime Codex to reason about mutation-staleness and index invalidation upfront, possibly via a review checklist or system prompt addition to the codex skill.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Test-first doc editing: building eval scenarios before trimming AGENTS.md prevented info loss. 15 scenarios + 8 stress test recall questions validated the trimmed doc (14/15 PASS, 6/8 PASS). Pattern: build test suite → make changes → validate → fix gaps.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Stress testing with real codebase exploration is more effective than synthetic padding for finding doc gaps. Agent reads actual code (building 30k+ tokens of context), then answers recall questions. Found 2 real degradation points (PR workflow steps, scope expansion) that were reinforced.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex as second reviewer on doc PRs caught a real inconsistency (scenario expected answer vs AGENTS.md rule) and a non-existent file path. Worth running on documentation PRs, not just code PRs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: GitHub PR review thread resolution requires GraphQL mutation (resolveReviewThread). REST reply endpoint posts replies but does not resolve threads. Had to discover thread node IDs via GraphQL query first.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Re-baseline research findings against current code before creating specs. In CLI agent-UX session, 7 of 21 recommendations from telemetry analysis were already implemented. Verifying each against the codebase with parallel explore agents before speccing saved significant overhead (would have created 7 unnecessary specs and 7 unnecessary tasks).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Commander.js parent-action option routing: when parent and subcommands define the same options, Commander doesn't cleanly route them. Tried passThroughOptions (requires global enablePositionalOptions, breaks --json global option), ended up using allowUnknownOption + temporary Command re-parse. Pattern works but is non-idiomatic. If more command groups need default actions, consider extracting this into a shared utility.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent research pattern: launching 4+ research agents simultaneously on different aspects of the same question (cross-project audit, usage patterns, external ecosystem, install story) produced comprehensive non-overlapping findings in ~6 minutes. Much more effective than sequential investigation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual-reviewer pattern for plans: having both an internal holistic reviewer (Claude) and an external reviewer (Codex) independently review the same plan catches complementary issues. Internal finds code-level integration problems, external finds architectural concerns. Both agreed on the same critical issues (compound ACs, inline YAML). Three revision cycles (v1 reviewed v2 reviewed v3) produced significantly stronger output.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative clarifying questions with ask tool: asking one question at a time with 3-4 concrete options (each with descriptions) before synthesizing research into a plan led to well-informed decisions. User could respond quickly because each question had enough context from the research. Better than presenting a full plan and asking for feedback.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: CLI commands targeting main project files (like .claude/skills/) must use ctx.rootDir, not ctx.specDir or path.dirname(ctx.specDir). The specDir is the spec content location (.kspec/ in shadow mode), while rootDir is always the project root. Using dirname(specDir) fails in shadow mode because .kspec/ is a worktree at the project root level. Encountered in skill render command where files were written to /tmp/ instead of project root.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Structured interview (one question at a time with pro/con analysis) before planning leads to well-reasoned architecture decisions. User engagement is higher when they see trade-offs laid out clearly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Running both internal Plan agent review AND Codex review-plan on the same plan catches complementary issues. Internal review finds code-level gaps; Codex finds spec quality issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch uses kebab-case args (depends-on) but schema fields use snake_case (depends_on). Inconsistency causes trial-and-error on first batch use.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent review of ralph loop: 5 agents reviewing different PR ranges (371-376, 377-384, 385-393, 394-402, test suite) completed in ~3min wall clock. Independent agents finding the same duplication issues confirms real problems vs noise. Effective pattern for post-loop quality review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Ralph loop PR-by-PR review process misses cross-PR duplication accumulation. PR #381 added rendering utils, #383 duplicated them in a new file, #394 consolidated render functions but missed the utilities, #401 added more dead code. Each PR passes review individually but the aggregate drift is significant (24 inbox items from one loop). Consider adding a consolidation/cleanup iteration every N PRs or at loop end.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Background PR review agent can act on stale context: agent added 172-line test file for a spec that was deleted during review. When running review agents in background while making spec/task changes in foreground, the agent does not see those changes. Required a follow-up cleanup PR.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review skill always demands // AC: @spec-ref ac-N annotations, even for infrastructure/cleanup tasks where ACs describe absence of code. Should skip AC annotation checks when task has no spec_ref or when spec type is not user-facing behavior.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Running kspec setup during development creates kspec-agents.md and .claude/skills/ in project root. These are test artifacts for the kspec project itself (which uses AGENTS.md, not kspec-agents.md). They trigger repeated stop hook warnings about uncommitted changes. Need either: (a) test isolation so setup tests dont leak into project root, or (b) cleanup step in bootstrap/dev workflow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Multi-model PR review (Claude + Codex in parallel) caught issues that single-model review missed. Codex found missing debugLog in outer catch and weak test assertions. Worth continuing this pattern for non-trivial PRs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel dual-reviewer strategy (Claude agent + Codex) is effective: Claude validates correctness, Codex catches spec-alignment gaps. Use both for PRs with spec ACs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review (gpt-5.3-codex) caught a real correctness bug in drift detection (hash-gating for sidecar changes) that the implementing agent missed. Codex reproduced the issue locally with a concrete script. High value for code review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Refactoring tasks without spec_ref have AC traceability gap — task-level ACs in notes aren't discoverable by standard // AC: @spec-ref ac-N annotation pattern. Codex review flagged this on PR #411. Options: (1) allow // AC: @task-ref ac-N, (2) require spec items even for refactoring, (3) teach reviewers to check task notes. Related: @task-skill-module-split had no spec_ref but defined 3 ACs in notes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Guard script bash code embedded in JS template literal makes quote escaping painful — single quotes inside tr/sed cause parse errors. Consider extracting guard scripts to standalone .sh files loaded at setup time instead of inline template literals.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Running codex review in parallel with PR review agent caught a real security bypass (split-quote git "reset" --hard). The dual-reviewer pattern (code-level + quality-gate) provides meaningful coverage overlap.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared test fixture fragility: tests/fixtures/kynetic.meta.yaml is used by multiple test files. Tests that append YAML keys (like meta.test.ts appending conventions:) collide when the fixture gains new top-level keys. Caused real regression in PR #413. Consider per-test fixture isolation or fixture composition helpers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent reviews (Codex + /pr-review) found complementary issues: Codex caught test annotation gaps, review agent caught shared fixture regression. Multi-reviewer pattern is high-value for quality.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Invoked /spec-plan skill but wrote implementation guide instead of plan-import-format document. User had explicitly said /spec-plan. Lesson: invoking a skill is not enough — must follow its output format from the FIRST write. When /spec-plan is invoked for plan mode, write the plan file in kspec plan import format (# Title, ## Specs with YAML code block, ## Tasks, ## Implementation Notes) from the start.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern before plan import: running both an internal plan review agent and Codex in parallel caught YAML quoting failures and substantive spec gaps (batch mode, worktree detection, remote type algorithm). Reviews converged on same must-fixes, giving high confidence. Always dual-review complex plan documents before importing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel consumer project exploration: launching 3 agents to explore kynetic-bot, imgen, comfy-ecaj-nodes simultaneously produced convergent findings (same Quick Start pattern, same hooks, same skill drift) that were far more convincing than exploring one project. Use parallel exploration when researching cross-project patterns.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal Plan agent + Codex review-plan) catches complementary issues. Internal agent finds architectural concerns, Codex finds format/structure issues. Convergent findings give high confidence. Worth standardizing for all plan imports.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Post-import verification agent catches data integrity issues that dry-run misses (null spec_ref, missing implementation notes). Should be part of standard plan import workflow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: GitHub blocks REQUEST_CHANGES on own PR. Ralph review subagents operate under the same GitHub credentials as the PR author, so they cannot post REQUEST_CHANGES reviews — only COMMENT. The pr-review skill instructs posting APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, but REQUEST_CHANGES will always fail in self-authored PRs. Need either: (1) a separate GitHub bot account for review agents, or (2) the skill should use COMMENT event with structured review content instead of REQUEST_CHANGES.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual-reviewer pattern (Claude agent + Codex) for PR review. Running both in parallel on PR #424 gave convergent findings on the critical branch-lookup bug (independent discovery by both). Codex also caught input validation gap that Claude missed. Different models find different issues — convergent findings give high confidence, divergent findings expand coverage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel review audit pattern: spawning 4 specialized subagents (worker process adherence, review process adherence, code quality, spec/AC coverage) to evaluate a ralph session. Each agent had a focused lens and found complementary issues. Total wall-clock time ~2 min for what would have been 15+ min of sequential analysis.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review convergence: running both pr-review subagent and /codex review in parallel catches different issues and convergent findings give high confidence. Both flagged dead verifyTaskCompleted code independently.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Convention vs template mental model clarified: Templates carry kspec-generic content (shadow branch, task lifecycle, ralph loop — same for ALL kspec projects). Conventions carry project-specific rules (testing gotchas, dev setup, CI limitations — unique per project). When porting content from AGENTS.md, ask: does this apply to every kspec project? Template. Only this project? Convention.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-before-implement pattern: adding ac-6 to @agent-instruction-gen before coding the noop behavior made test coverage natural and caught the right contract upfront.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: task get not showing descriptions meant had to grep raw YAML to verify task content after batch creation. Critical gap for agents working on tasks — they cannot read the description via CLI.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Platform behavior assumption: PR #440 added namespace rendering (.claude/skills/kspec/<id>/) without verifying Claude Code actually discovers nested skill directories. It does not. Future platform integration work should verify discovery behavior (e.g. create a test skill, check if Claude Code lists it) before building rendering pipelines around assumed directory structures.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Meta vs manifest confusion: skill render reads from meta (shadow branch), not template manifest. Changing manifest ID without updating meta has no effect. Need to delete+re-add skill via CLI.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent research pattern: launching 3+ research agents simultaneously to investigate different aspects (code state, git history, task completions) builds comprehensive evidence in ~3 minutes vs 15+ sequentially. Critical for large triage sessions (95 items). Each agent gets a focused investigation scope and returns structured findings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Zod superRefine pattern for status-dependent field requirements (e.g., triaged requires reasoning/decided_by, acted_on requires acted_at). Should be the default approach for any schema with status lifecycle — flat .optional() misses state invariants. First used in triage.ts, should apply to plan.ts and similar.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
Spec gap test

Reasoning: needs spec
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: CI timing race: when Codex posts a review comment after CI check-unresolved-comments has already run, the check fails because the new thread is unresolved. Requires manual re-run after resolving. Consider: (1) make check-unresolved-comments a required-last check, (2) have the review workflow auto-re-run the check after resolving threads, or (3) add a gh run rerun step to the codex review skill.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Include triage records in static snapshot (kspec-snapshot.json). Currently the snapshot format (KspecSnapshot type) doesn't include triage records, so the triage page in static/GitHub Pages mode shows an empty state with a notice instead of displaying existing triage decisions read-only. AC-8 of @interactive-triage-ui expects read-only display. Needs: add triage records to export snapshot, update KspecSnapshot type, add fetchTriageRecordsStatic to read from snapshot.

Reasoning: There's a spec gap here
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Cross-feature requirement pattern: How to express that core features (search, validate, export) must support all entity types. When new entity type added, should automatically imply tasks for core features. Options: (1) applies_to field on feature specs, (2) trait on entity types like @trait-searchable, (3) validation warning for missing coverage, (4) parent spec that entity types must satisfy. Surfaced when realizing search doesn't cover inbox.

Reasoning: first item reasoning
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] kspec validate @spec or @task — targeted validation that checks a single spec/task's AC coverage against codebase. Not full approval, just verifies each AC has at least one // AC: annotation in test files. Would make trait AC gaps immediately visible during task-work. Could be used by local-review skill as a concrete check instead of relying on agent diligence.

Reasoning: Must-have but needs spec design - targeted kspec validate for single item
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Design section configuration for agents generate — allow projects to control which sections appear (skills table, conventions, workflows, static templates). Key questions: where does config live, include vs exclude list, defaults, custom sections, ordering, data vs template distinction, migration path. See plan doc for full requirements.

Reasoning: Must-have but needs spec design - section configuration for agents generate
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Pre-analyzed triage report (HTML artifact) combined with kspec batch made processing 107 inbox items efficient. Record-then-act pattern provided good audit trail. Pattern: analyze offline, port decisions via batch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: settings.json written by 3 independent subsystems during setup (installClaudeCodeHooks, seedPermissions, enablePluginInProject via modifyJsonAtomic). Makes skip-when-unchanged optimization impossible without either a shared coordinator or consolidating all mutations into one function. Each writer reads, modifies, writes independently — interleaving prevents simple content comparison.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Post-merge branch state: When inheriting a session where a PR was already merged, the working directory may be on main. Always check branch (git branch --show-current) before committing, and create a feature branch first. Recovering from an accidental main commit requires creating a branch from HEAD and resetting main.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review caught a real type drift bug (Convention.validation schema mismatch) during web-ui type deduplication PR. The shared-type approach works well: define in @kynetic-ai/shared, re-export from web-ui, enforce with static analysis test. Dual review (Codex + CI) catches complementary issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent audit pattern: launching 4+ agents in parallel for deep-dive review of ralph loop work (PR quality, functional verification, loop behavior, process adherence) produced comprehensive results in ~90 seconds. Effective for post-loop quality assessment.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + Codex) for plan review catches different issue categories. Internal agent found consistency gaps; Codex found concurrency risks. Convergent findings give high confidence before implementation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: @trait-semantic-exit-codes ACs hardcode exit code numbers (ac-2: 'exit code 1', ac-3: 'exit code 2', ac-4: 'exit code 3') that don't match kspec's actual EXIT_CODES scheme (ERROR=1, USAGE_ERROR=2, NOT_FOUND=3, VALIDATION_FAILED=4). Every command adding trait AC test coverage needs clarifying comments explaining the mapping. Fix: update trait ACs to use semantic descriptions ('non-zero exit code indicating validation failure') instead of hardcoded numbers, or update to match kspec's actual codes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex review caught fail-open bug in getBudget() — corrupt budget.json was silently treated as 'no budget', effectively disabling enforcement. Changed to fail closed (only ENOENT returns null, parse/validation errors propagate). Pattern: for security/enforcement code, always default to the restrictive path. Codex consistently catches error-handling path issues that internal review misses.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Ralph task-limit-guard hook blocks gh pr create even when finishing current task work. The guard treats all Bash commands equally — it can't distinguish 'creating a PR for completed work' from 'starting new task work'. Result: branch pushed but PR not created, requiring next iteration to finish. Consider whitelisting gh pr create or detecting PR creation context in the guard.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: task set --depends-on replaces all deps rather than appending. When setting multiple deps in separate batch commands, only the last one survives. Must provide all deps in a single call. Consider adding --add-depends-on for append semantics (similar to --relates-to on item set which appends).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual plan review (internal agent + /codex review-plan) catches complementary issues: internal finds design gaps and terminology problems, codex finds code-level feasibility issues (missing APIs, wrong method names, breaking consumers). Convergent findings indicate high confidence. Used successfully for session-start-redesign plan.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Budget enforcement in task start integrates cleanly: check before transition, increment after save, resume case handled by existing early return. The library functions (checkBudget/incrementBudget) do the heavy lifting — CLI handler just wires them together. Good separation of concerns between store.ts and task.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent spawning for session log audit: 5 agents analyzing different log files simultaneously gave comprehensive coverage. Pattern worth replicating for any multi-file analysis task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: setupTempFixtures() returns a flat dir where tempDir IS the specDir — no .kspec/ wrapper. Agents that assume nested structure (path.join(tempDir, ".kspec")) get silent test failures. AGENTS.md test helpers table should note this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Mock ACP agent pattern (tests/fixtures/mock-acp-agent.mjs) enables fast behavioral testing of ralph subprocess orchestration. Tests real env injection, budget cleanup, and signal handling in ~2s each. Key enabler: --adapter-cmd flag + spawnRalphUntil helper that watches output markers then kills the process.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Ralph CLI uses --max-loops but internal variables and log messages say iterations. Minor naming inconsistency that causes confusion when writing tests or debugging. Example: --max-loops 1 but logs Starting ralph loop (max 1 iterations).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review caught exec()+unref() not actually preventing event loop hang (stdio pipes still buffered). Validated that /codex review-pr adds real value beyond rubber-stamping.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Pure function pattern for hook/guard commands: exporting the core logic as a testable pure function (e.g. evaluateWorktreeGuard) with stdin/process handling in the CLI layer enables fast unit testing (44 tests, no I/O) while keeping the CLI integration tests minimal (7 tests for protocol compliance). Replicate this pattern for future hook commands.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan-derived tasks with depends_on sometimes become no-ops because the dependency task already implements all shared spec ACs. Seen in iteration 3: @update-setup-with-migration-cleanup (all 6 ACs done by @implement-native-worktree-guard) and @add-multi-harness-env-injection (all injection ACs done by @implement-session-create-command). Wastes budget starts and discovery time. Potential fix: plan import could warn when multiple tasks share a spec and one depends on the other, or task start could auto-detect 'AC already covered' and offer to close.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session checkpoint hook fires repeatedly on research-only sessions with pre-existing uncommitted changes from a different task. No way to signal this is a read-only investigation session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cross-cutting skill updates need checklist: When a concept spans multiple skills (e.g., spec context discovery in codex, pr-review, local-review, review template), updating one skill without checking all related ones leads to inconsistency. Codex review on PR #511 found 4 findings where the dig-deeper pattern wasn't applied uniformly. Consider: a way to tag related skills, or a pre-commit check that flags partial updates to skill groups.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel audit agents pattern: spawning 4 specialized agents (code quality, test quality, non-test code, process quality) in parallel gives comprehensive coverage in ~2 min wall clock. Each agent needs clear scope boundaries and structured output format.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex skill silently exits with no output when OPENAI_API_KEY is not set. The skill documents gh auth preflight but not API key validation. Agents waste time discovering this. Skill should check for API key and fail fast with clear message.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session test helper extraction (task @01KJ9ZDE) went smoothly. The all-fields-optional SessionContext pattern works well for tests that each need a different subset of fields — TypeScript structural typing handles it naturally. Reduced ~315 lines of duplication across 6 files into 2 shared modules. The inbox helpers needed a tempDir parameter change (closure → explicit arg) which was the main mechanical transformation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: testUlid('PREFIX') returns identical values across calls without explicit sequence argument — deterministic with default sequence=0. Caused false-positive test pass in session-checkpoint-scoping tests where mySession and otherSession were identical. Fix options: auto-incrementing counter, require sequence param, or rename to testUlidDeterministic to make behavior obvious. testUlids() works correctly but is easy to overlook.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Self-validating task pattern: created a P1 automation-eligible task whose acceptance criteria IS verifying the fix works. Ralph picks it up, the task checks its own session_id stamp, and the result documents whether the fix works end-to-end. Useful for testing harness-level integration that can't be verified from inside an active session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Elysia body schema validation returns 422 (not 400) before the handler runs. When writing E2E tests for daemon endpoints that have body schema validation (t.Object(...)), missing/invalid body fields return 422. If the handler also has manual validation that returns 400, the schema check fires first. Account for this in test assertions — do not assume 400 for missing body fields on Elysia-validated routes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: GitHub PR thread resolution requires GraphQL mutation (resolveReviewThread), not REST API. REST API only supports replies. Pattern: get thread node IDs via graphql query on pullRequest.reviewThreads, then loop resolveReviewThread mutations. Reliably resolved all 7 threads in one pass.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: scanTestCoverage() only scanned rootDir/tests/ — missed packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/ where Playwright E2E specs with AC annotations live. Fixed by extending scan to also cover the E2E directory and .spec.ts/.spec.js file extensions. Risk: any future E2E test directory additions would silently miss coverage until the scan list is updated. Consider making E2E scan paths configurable or convention-documented.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Trait N/A annotations placed inside JSDoc block comments are not machine-parseable — the '* // AC:' pattern (where * is the JSDoc line prefix) does not match the scanner's '// AC:' regex. Must use standalone // AC: line comments OUTSIDE any /** ... */ block. Occurred in api-meta.spec.ts E2E tests, caught by Codex review, required fix commit.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC annotation verification gap: Tests annotated with wrong AC refs (e.g., Elysia 422 tests annotated as ac-23 when ac-23 requires 400+{error,details}; POST body validation annotated as ac-5/6/7 when those are for X-Kspec-Dir header). Fix: always run kspec item get @spec-ref and read AC text before annotating tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex retrospective PR review workflow: /codex pr on merged PRs surfaces real issues. Found stale dist/ bug via retro review of PR #547 that live review missed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: JS date validation gotcha in E2E tests: new Date("invalid") returns Invalid Date but does NOT throw. Tests using expect(() => new Date(x)).not.toThrow() or try/catch will always pass even with malformed timestamps - false positive. Always use isNaN(new Date(x).getTime()) for timestamp format validation. Caught this in api-websocket.spec.ts timestamp assertion (AC-29/@trait-websocket-protocol ac-3).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: CI check-unresolved-comments timing race in review fix cycle: When Codex posts inline review comments on a PR, we push a fix commit which triggers CI immediately. The check-unresolved-comments job runs BEFORE we resolve the Codex threads via GraphQL, causing it to fail on the new commit. Then requires manual workflow re-run. Mitigation: always resolve all review threads BEFORE pushing any fix commits during a review cycle.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: window.__testWs pattern for Playwright WebSocket E2E: Store native browser WebSocket in window.__testWs via page.evaluate() and access it across subsequent evaluate() calls. Browser context maintains the global between calls. Enables clean helper functions (connectWebSocket, sendAndWaitForAck, subscribeAndWaitForBroadcast) without needing Playwright WebSocket interception. Used successfully in packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/api-websocket.spec.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When deleting test files that cover spec ACs, kspec validate does not warn that AC annotations are being removed. This means coverage regressions are only caught during Codex review after the PR is up — requiring an extra fix commit. A pre-delete validate or a local-review gate that checks 'these AC annotations would disappear' would catch this earlier. Observed during task-delete-static-analysis-tests (PR #558): deleted web-ui-triage.test.ts removed all @interactive-triage-ui ac-1..ac-8 coverage; Codex caught it, required creating triage.spec.ts to recover.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: PR merged by review subagent while worker agent still editing files on same branch — local branch switches to main automatically, all pending Edit tool changes silently lost. Caused significant rework this session (re-applying all triage.spec.ts changes on new branch fix/triage-ac6-session-close-error). The review subagent and worker agent operate concurrently on the same branch in a fix cycle, creating a race condition. Potential mitigations: (1) worker agent checks for branch changes before editing, (2) ralph serializes review subagent after worker fully stops, (3) worker agent uses a local patch/stash before any branch changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal plan review + /codex review-plan) catches complementary issues — format vs substance. Worth standardizing for all plan imports.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shadow branch merge driver handles complex YAML conflicts (project.tasks.yaml with 38 divergent commits) automatically during rebase — reliable for ralph parallel sessions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (plan agent + Codex) catches complementary issues. Plan agent validates design, Codex validates contracts and test coverage. Worth keeping as standard practice for non-trivial PRs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Merge driver: auto-resolve .kspec-agents-hash file conflicts (deterministic hash, should always take latest)

Reasoning: Merge driver for hash file — low frequency conflict, manual resolution works
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Plan import: generate richer task descriptions from Implementation Notes section — include file paths, what to change, verification steps instead of generic 'See plan...' text

Reasoning: Plan import richer descriptions — improvement, not blocking
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Triage ac-5 says sets result_ref but delete action may not produce one. Verify behavior and update spec or add test assertion.

Reasoning: Triage ac-5 result_ref for delete — spec may be wrong, needs verification
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] Triage API spec says ac-4 and ac-5 use PUT method but implementation uses POST /:ref/override and POST /:ref/act. Spec needs updating to match reality.

Reasoning: Triage API spec PUT vs POST mismatch — spec needs updating to match implementation
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] @cmd-validate spec is stale — missing flags: --completeness, --staleness, --drift, --alignment, --skills, --conventions (all already implemented in code). Pre-existing drift, not introduced by trait AC task.

Reasoning: @cmd-validate spec is stale — missing 6 flags already in code. Spec drift.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content:
[spec-gap] kspec meta set convention: add --update-rule and --remove-rule flags. Currently the only way to fix a rule is to delete the entire convention and recreate it. Surfaced during skill CLI lookups task when codex review caught a wording issue in one rule.

Reasoning: Convention --update-rule — DX improvement, workaround is delete+recreate
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Triage record-then-act pattern with UI review works well at scale: batch-record 41 decisions, user reviews/overrides in web UI, batch-act on confirmed. Clean separation of agent proposals from user decisions. 12 overrides out of 41 shows useful agent-human collaboration.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex two-pass review pattern effective: implement → codex review → fix bug found → re-review clean. Caught missing previousValue in injectCodexEnv that would have broken Ralph cleanup.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-decomposed task descriptions with exact files and verification criteria make implementation fast — the per-adapter-auto-approve task took one focused session from start to merged PR.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: MOCK_ACP_VERIFY_ARGS_FILE pattern extends the existing env var verification pattern cleanly — behavioral test infrastructure for ACP agent spawning is now solid.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review as iterative second reviewer catches real bugs. Two-round pattern (review → fix → re-review) provides high-confidence quality gate for ralph adapter/env code.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan-derived task descriptions with exact line numbers and numbered change steps make implementation fast and focused. The plan-to-task pipeline produces high-quality work items.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When posting content containing $ and angle-bracket placeholders via shell-wrapped commands, interpolation can silently mutate task/PR notes; prefer literal-safe quoting or file-based payloads.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Portable {skill:<id>} tokens with renderer-side platform resolution reduced template duplication and kept Claude/Codex invocation guidance consistent across SKILL.md and supporting markdown.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel plan review (Plan agent + Codex) catches complementary issues: architectural concerns vs format/structural issues. High convergence on edge cases gives confidence. Worth standardizing as a dual-review step.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan-derived tasks need manual follow-up (batch set tags + note) to be automation-ready. The derive step should produce standalone tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Core skill update UX gap: kspec skill update is version-gated, so same-version template edits are skipped and require kspec skill install-core. This is non-obvious during local template iteration. Improve guidance (update vs install-core) or adjust command behavior to detect local template changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Holistic plan review (plan + derived specs + tasks + traits together) before any code is written caught 6 spec gaps in @plan-auto-close-stale-active-sessions including missing targeting semantics, liveness guard, corrupt events handling, and task dependency ordering. Pattern: evaluate the full derivation tree, not just individual specs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review threads require manual GraphQL resolution + CI re-trigger before merge. Multi-step dance every time codex posts inline comments.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative codex review loop (review → fix → re-review) converges well. Three rounds on PR #582 caught duplicate label, spec alignment drift, and missing test branch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Targeted dry-run + focused test loop quickly exposed core-skill source-of-truth drift; package-distribution test caught stale plugin artifact path immediately.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: CLI tests that execute dist artifacts can produce misleading failures when dist is stale; this creates avoidable debugging churn before the real code behavior is evaluated.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Using a focused validate mode matrix (schema/refs/alignment/completeness/staleness + combinations) quickly verified scoped semantics and prevented regressions while keeping turnaround fast.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Isolated worktree + backup branch pattern for shadow branch recovery. Creating a backup branch before destructive ops, then using /tmp worktree for experimental rebase, then patching the result back as a normal commit avoided force-push entirely. This pattern should be documented for future shadow branch divergence scenarios.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Merge driver silent data loss when --non-interactive flag missing from git config. No error, no warning — just hangs on stdin and leaves files unmerged. 12 task completions lost silently. Root cause: shadow.ts registration code path diverged from actual git config. Fix tracked in @01KJJGJ1.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review takes 10+ minutes because npm test subagent polling is inefficient. Consider instructing Codex to skip full suite and rely on CI, or use test shards instead of full npm test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex PR review cannot distinguish pre-existing test failures from regressions. Flags false positives (e.g. session-budget-integration flakiness on PR #590). Could pre-seed known-flaky test list or compare failure counts against main baseline.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex-then-fix cycle on PR #601 was tight: review posted, ac-9 gap caught, fixed in 1 commit, thread resolved, CI passed, merged. Total turnaround ~15 min including CI.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task budget guard blocks needs_work fix cycle transitions. kspec task start @ref fails with budget exhausted even when the task is in needs_work state (an existing fix cycle, not a new task start). needs_work → in_progress should be exempt from the budget guard since it is resuming prior work, not starting new work. Had to skip task state transitions and create PR without proper submit flow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Minimal floating-promise fix pattern: storing async function result in a variable and attaching .catch(() => {}) before Promise.race is the clean way to prevent Node.js 22 unhandled rejection crashes when a race-loser promise is later rejected by resource cleanup.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agent investigation breadth vs accuracy tradeoff — Explore agents are valuable for surveying many files quickly but their conclusions need manual verification before acting. In this session, the agent reported event listener accumulation as CRITICAL (wrong — listeners registered once per spawn) while the actual bottleneck (getEventCount O(n^2)) wasn't in its top findings. Pattern: use agents for breadth, verify claims against actual code, then form your own root cause hypothesis.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2E tests not in CI allowed a fundamental WebSocket upgrade bug to persist undetected. Previous task closed as fixed based on unit tests passing, but E2E would have shown the server never upgraded connections.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Progressive reproduction technique (incrementally adding middleware layers to a minimal Elysia server) isolated an Elysia framework interaction bug in minutes. More effective than reading framework source code.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Verifying pre-existing test failures requires stashing changes and re-running — slow feedback loop. A baseline test report or CI artifact would let agents identify pre-existing failures without manual stash/unstash.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Test-first approach for regression bugs: wrote tests that failed (confirmed bug), then fixed source, then verified tests pass. Clean feedback loop — 2 failing tests before fix, 6 passing after. Recommend this pattern for all shadow commit gap tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: item list --json returns {items:[...]} (wrapped) while tasks list --json returns a flat array. Inconsistent JSON shapes cause test type errors — kspecJson<any[]> typed as flat array silently fails when the actual shape is an object wrapper. Test authors need to know to use {items: Array<...>} for item list vs any[] for tasks list.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Item status in JSON output is a nested object {maturity: string, implementation: string} not a plain string. Tests checking item.status === "implemented" fail silently — must use item.status?.implementation. This differs from task status which IS a plain string.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Trait AC annotations (@trait-json-output, @trait-shadow-commit) consistently missed in new test describe blocks. Two consecutive tasks (agent-definition-schema, session-model-evolution) both flagged in fix cycle for missing annotations. Pattern: workers add spec-specific ACs but forget inherited trait ACs. Fix: consider checklist or template reminder when adding new integration test blocks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: PR scope verification: use gh pr view N --json baseRefOid,headRefOid then git diff <baseRefOid>..<headRefOid> --name-only to verify actual PR diff. This is more reliable than git diff origin/main..branch when the branch base predates recent merges to main.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Stale PR base masquerades as scope problem: when a feature branch is based on a commit that predates another merged PR, the merged PR files appear in the diff. Review says out-of-scope changes. Fix is rebase onto main, not code changes. Two fix cycles consumed before root cause identified. Consider adding a check in PR workflow to detect stale bases.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: git -C <path> pattern prevents CWD poisoning in recovery scenarios. Agents running git inside .kspec/ via cd poison the shell CWD for the rest of the session (Claude Code persists CWD changes). Always use git -C /path/to/.kspec/ instead of cd .kspec/ && git. Consider adding this to AGENTS.md development conventions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: agent.ts (PR #634) reimplemented parseInt+isNaN validation instead of using parseIntOption from src/cli/validators.ts — reintroducing the partial-parse bug (parseInt("5abc")===5) that parseIntOption was built to fix. The helper exists and conventions doc was added after @01KGWDPV, but agents implementing new CLI commands still miss it. Suggests validators.ts needs more prominent callout in AGENTS.md or task templates for new CLI commands.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reading actual code before judging PR review threads saved significant work: 11 of 19 open threads on PR #634 were stale (issues already fixed in the latest commit). Manual thread-by-code matching took ~10 minutes but avoided implementing fixes that were already done.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: /codex pr covering both tasks in a single pass was efficient and caught a subtle bug (parseInt partial-match "5abc"->5) that manual review missed. Dual-spec single-pass review avoids duplicated context-gathering and produces tighter non-redundant findings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative Codex PR review loop (fix → push → re-review) converged in 2 passes and caught layered bugs not visible in the first pass. Good pattern for PR polish cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: parseIntOption from src/cli/validators.ts repeatedly missed when implementing new CLI commands — parseInt+isNaN pattern introduced 4 times in one PR. Needs more prominent discovery surface (skill or convention).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: batch-write-buffer wiring blocked by subprocess spawn model: WriteBuffer is a process-local singleton but batch-exec.ts runs each command via spawnSync as a separate process. Buffer writes in the parent won't be visible to spawned child processes. Need to evaluate: (a) switch to in-process command execution, or (b) use a temp file protocol where children write to a staging dir and parent collects on success.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle had two SHOULD-FIX items from regenerated files not committed: (1) kspec agents generate was run locally but not committed to the PR branch — reviewer caught stale kspec-agents.md with ralph references; (2) kspec skill render was not run at all — .agents/skills/ rendered files still had ralph references. Both are easy to miss because the commands succeed but leave uncommitted artifacts. Consider adding these steps to the pre-PR local-review checklist or the implementation checklist notes when working on migrations that touch templates/skills.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle search-before-capture pattern worked well: searched for existing tracking of both friction points before capturing observations, confirmed neither was already tracked, then captured a single consolidated observation. This prevented duplication and kept the reflection tight.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: check-unresolved-comments CI check is triggered by push. If review threads are resolved AFTER a push (not before), CI does not re-run automatically. Workaround: empty commit to trigger fresh run. Correct order: resolve threads FIRST, then push code.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: GraphQL thread resolution + empty commit pattern worked for stale CI: (1) kspec task submit → (2) resolve threads via GraphQL mutation → (3) push code or empty commit → (4) CI re-runs with threads resolved. Resolving threads before push avoids needing the empty commit.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: shx cp -r <src> <dest> is non-idempotent when dest already exists — creates nested subdirectory on repeated runs. Build scripts must always shx rm -rf <dest> before copying. Add to build/ci convention.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon packages/daemon/src/server.ts cannot be imported directly in vitest — transitive Bun/Elysia imports break module resolution. Pattern: recreate the logic as a pure function in the test file (see daemon-server.test.ts and daemon-web-ui-bundle.test.ts). Worth documenting as a testing convention for daemon code.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: check-unresolved-comments CI check goes stale when review threads are resolved after the check already ran for that push. Fix: gh run rerun <run-id>. Reminder: resolve threads BEFORE or immediately after pushing to avoid this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill slug namespace confusion: .agents/skills/ uses kspec- prefix (kspec-task-work) for rendered output, but .kspec/skills/ uses bare slug (task-work) for runtime injection. Agent definitions must use the bare slug — but nothing in the CLI or docs makes this distinction clear. Easy to wire up agents with wrong slug and get silent skill injection failure (skills silently skipped when file not found).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: meta set has --add-skill but no --remove-skill. To fix a wrong skill slug on an agent, had to edit .kspec/kynetic.meta.yaml directly and trigger commit via task note. This is the second time a missing remove/clear flag forced a YAML edit (dispatch rules also have no CLI). These gaps accumulate quickly when wiring up new agents.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session log analysis for agent failure diagnosis: Python one-liner over events.jsonl extracted the exact tool call sequence and identified the ACP permission request gap in 2 minutes. The structured event log format made root cause analysis fast — tool_call status:pending -> 5min gap -> agent.failed was immediately diagnostic.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: package-lock.json drift from npm test / npx tsc --noEmit triggers session checkpoint stop hook every session. The right action is always git checkout package-lock.json (unless an actual install was run). Consider adding package-lock.json to stop hook ignore list or auto-restoring it before checkpoint.
observations.author: @claude
observations.resolution: Retracted: stop hook behavior is correct. package-lock.json changes should be committed if intentional (install), cleared if noise (test side-effect). Not friction.

observations.content: Testing CLI-layer decisions (e.g. isJsonMode() → onUpdate suppression) requires knowing which abstraction level to test at. Direct runInvocation unit tests give false positives; CLI subprocess tests hit adapter limitations; ESM spy approach is unreliable cross-module. The reliable pattern: use setJsonMode(true) + isJsonMode() from output.ts to replicate the exact CLI decision in-process, then assert on the result. Document this as the preferred pattern for testing CLI mode-gating behavior.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Concurrency fix pattern: isolate race to a narrow atomic helper, migrate only hot mutation paths first, verify with targeted race regressions before full-suite run, then close via worker+review-agent loop.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: PR review automation attempted APPROVE on self-authored PR and GitHub rejected it; review event selection should adapt to author/reviewer identity.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task lifecycle loop (task-work + PR + spawned pr-review) provided clean end-to-end closure with merged PR and task completion in one pass.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Worker/reviewer loop with explicit MUST-FIX feedback improved quality: first review caught behavior-level AC gaps, second pass merged cleanly with clear audit trail.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Behavior-level AC intent can be missed when tests only verify internals. Add endpoint/log effect assertions earlier in task implementation to reduce fix-cycle churn.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Context-switch hygiene worked: checkpointing dirty work to a dedicated branch plus task-note handoff preserved progress and prevented losing work when switching priority tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: CLI integration tests run against dist binary, so editing command options requires a full build before vitest; failures initially look like unknown-option regressions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Creating PRs with gh --body inline markdown containing backticks triggers shell interpolation; use --body-file for reliable automation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch invoked task-work for @01KJS8B9QSQS53CT4DR2YHP1A8 after it was already completed and PR #669 merged; stale trigger caused a no-op worker run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch invocation targeted @01KJS8BAWP2WNCD003DQX75GKY as task.in_progress after it had already been merged/completed; worker had to run a no-op verification pass.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch trigger indicated task.needs_work for @01KJS8BAWP2WNCD003DQX75GKY after the task had already transitioned to completed and PR #670 was merged; worker invocation ran as a no-op.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Pairing template-source and generated-output tests made agent instruction doc migrations low-risk and quick to verify.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Agent dispatch triggered task @01KJTHAB6NRKQE12JJ7Q7V80CK via in_progress context even though task was already completed by runtime start; caused redundant verification pass.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Autonomous dispatch triggered task @01KJTHACWHYNBEQ09GCHYH00H4 as in_progress, but task status was already completed (2026-03-04T13:02:37Z), causing redundant execution.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-level local review is noisy because kspec validate currently surfaces many unrelated global meta/reference errors, making it hard to distinguish task regressions from baseline repo issues.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Autonomous dispatch referenced @01KJTP68SV9VZ37KXF6TCEEKWB as in_progress, but task status was already completed (completed_at 2026-03-04T13:21:45.371Z), resulting in a no-op dispatch iteration.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Autonomous dispatch invoked @01KJTP69W21Z3GQE8J2HAXC4WV with trigger context task.in_progress after task was already completed and merged; dispatch source should re-validate task state before assignment.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-level kspec validate gating is noisy because global pre-existing reference/alignment errors (e.g., duplicate @observations slug) obscure whether a local task introduced new validation regressions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full kspec validate output is dominated by known unrelated repo-level meta/reference/alignment failures, which obscures task-local validation signal during implementation work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Batch item ac add with multiple adds to the same item in atomic mode: each command loads the same initial state snapshot, so only the last AC survives. Workaround: use sequential individual commands instead of batch for multiple ac adds to the same item. Root cause is atomic batch isolation — writes don't see prior writes within the same batch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Batch reports success (20/20) when buffer bypass causes silent data loss. The batch engine has no mechanism to detect that command B overwrote command A via stale read. At minimum, batch should warn when multiple commands write to the same file — that is the signal for potential read-after-write violations. Related: task @01KJWQM3 (buffer bypass fix).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec task start auto-syncs spec implementation status to in_progress. For spec-documentation tasks (filling in descriptions/ACs on an already-implemented spec), this is wrong — the spec IS implemented, we are just documenting it retroactively. task start should not change spec status when the task is purely about spec documentation, not code changes. Workaround: manually reset with kspec item set @ref --status implemented after starting.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: PR merge gating can remain blocked by stale failed runs when duplicate required check names exist on the same head SHA, requiring manual reruns even after a later successful run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer agent dispatch via ACP can fail on parse/hang paths, forcing manual retries with limited diagnostics during pr-review loops.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Strict review-fix loops with targeted regression tests before full suite runs reduced turnaround time while still catching integration defects before merge.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel pr-review + Codex review pattern on same PR: convergent findings give high confidence. Codex caught a silent edge case (in_progress no-task blind spot) that improved the logic before merge. Running both in parallel added no wall-clock time.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Alignment validation expects a linked spec to remain in_progress while its task is pending_review, which is unintuitive for spec-repair tasks on already-implemented behavior and forced a status flip during submission.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix-cycle branch isolation is easy to miss: a docs PR inherited an unrelated task commit because the work branch was created from another task branch instead of origin/main. Review had to bounce the task just to split the PR.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Direct 'kspec agent run --task' bypassed agent prompt_template and framed review invocations as implementation work, while explicit codex-acp prompt runs could fail with RPC parse errors. This makes local readonly review automation hard to trust and pushes users off the intended agent workflow.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Debugging daemon issues is slow because the daemon runs Bun (not Node) on a separate TypeScript entry point (dist/daemon/index.ts). Changes to src/parser/ need a full rebuild AND daemon restart. No hot-reload path exists.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: initContext() is called on every daemon API route. Any work it does (like shadowPull) gets multiplied by concurrent requests. Consider caching the context or moving sync to a dedicated interval instead of per-request.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: In-flight promise dedup pattern in shadowPull works well for shared async functions that get called concurrently. Avoids time-based caching that breaks tests while still preventing duplicate work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch engine running during interactive sessions causes confusion: checkpoint hooks report dispatch agent changes as uncommitted work, dispatch agent leaves files on wrong branches, no way to pause dispatch for specific tasks without stopping the whole engine. Consider: per-task dispatch hold, or checkpoint hook filtering by session_id.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session checkpoint stop hook cannot distinguish between changes made by the current interactive session vs changes made by dispatch agents on other branches. Results in repeated false-positive warnings that the user must manually dismiss.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + codex in parallel) is highly effective for plan review. They catch complementary issues — codex found slug prefix mismatch and spec conflicts, internal agent found trait binding conflicts and missing spec updates. 4-pass review (2 rounds x 2 reviewers) produced a clean import with zero issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: PR skill updated to detect local main drift. After a fix cycle on PR #718 where an unpushed commit on local main leaked into the PR diff, added a rebase-onto-origin/main check in the feature branch path. Prevents unrelated work from polluting PRs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Multi-model review convergence: Claude subagent + Codex reviews catch complementary issues. Claude finds architectural/design gaps, Codex finds implementation bugs and experimentally verifies assumptions (e.g. FETCH_HEAD worktree behavior). Neither alone is sufficient for bulletproof plans.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec item set --trait replaces the entire traits array instead of appending. No --add-trait flag exists. This caused data loss when adding a new trait to specs that already had traits — the existing traits were silently removed. Workaround: list all existing traits plus the new one in a single --trait call.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch fails with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)' when processing task add commands. The batch commands schema shows task add is supported, but runtime throws. Had to fall back to 5 sequential CLI calls instead of one atomic batch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shadow branch pre-commit hook has no sanctioned bypass for maintenance operations (e.g., bulk cleanup after session migration). Had to use git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null. Consider a kspec shadow commit command or --maintenance flag that allows direct commits with an audit note.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel dual-review pattern (internal agent + Codex) for plan documents works well. They catch different classes of issues and convergent findings give high confidence. Both rated READY on second pass after fixing first-round issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + Codex in parallel) continues to prove high value. On plan review, they found 6 convergent MUST-FIX issues and each caught unique findings the other missed. Worth maintaining as standard practice for plan and spec reviews.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: triage act promote dumps raw inbox text as task description — requires manual rewrite of every promoted task to be standalone and actionable. Should generate a structured description template or allow --description override during promote.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec inbox list --json uses _ulid field for item ID but this is not documented. First instinct is .id which returns undefined. JSON output contracts should document field names or use conventional names.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Investigate-before-triage pattern: spawning parallel agents to verify bug validity before recording triage decisions caught 7/12 already-fixed bugs. Prevents waste tasks and keeps the task list clean.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Checking spec coverage during triage surfaced real spec gaps (workflow, setup, alignment have no specs). Triage is a natural spec-gap discovery mechanism — setting tasks to needs_review for missing specs creates a forcing function.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Worktree isolation pattern for non-conflicting changes: when main tree has in-progress agent work, create git worktree off origin/main, make the change, PR from there. Avoids conflicts and doesnt require coordinating with running agents.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec review via agent before finalizing: spawning an Explore agent to review a new spec for gaps (missing color modes, pipeline separation, palette definition) catches real issues before the spec enters the system. Worth doing for any non-trivial spec.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel dual-reviewer pattern (internal agent + Codex) for plan reviews catches both overlapping and unique gaps. Convergent findings give high confidence; divergent findings broaden coverage. Two review rounds is the sweet spot.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + Codex in parallel) catches complementary issues: agent finds architectural gaps, Codex finds format/consistency issues. Used on plan-iterative-planning through 4 iterations. Worth formalizing as standard plan review workflow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative plan design through review cycles: v1 had update-from-file, reviews identified round-trip gap, v2 added import --into, v3 decoupled task derivation, v4 decoupled spec creation. Each review cycle produced a cleaner design. User steering at key decisions (v2→v3: delay spec creation) was the most impactful improvement.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex plan review output file (/tmp/codex-plan-review.md) is not unique per invocation. Stale output from previous sessions can be mistaken for current results. Need to check timestamps or use unique filenames (e.g., include plan slug or timestamp).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + Codex) catches complementary issues. Internal agent finds structural gaps, Codex finds semantic/testability issues. Worth formalizing as a standard plan review workflow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC migration tables as a review tool — mapping every existing AC to its fate (moves/stays/obsolete) surfaces gaps invisible in prose descriptions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session checkpoint hooks fire for unrelated dispatch agent work. No way to scope checkpoint to current interactive session vs background dispatch tasks. Had to dismiss 5+ warnings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: @trait-semantic-exit-codes says usage/validation errors exit 1, but centralized EXIT_CODES.USAGE_ERROR is 2 and plan import follows the code constant. Trait text and implementation contract should be reconciled.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch-mode agents cannot run daemon-backed Playwright fixtures because kspec serve start is intentionally blocked inside agent invocations.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm test only rebuilds when dist artifacts are missing, not when they are stale; fix-cycle verification on task branches can fail until a manual npm run build refreshes dist/ after source changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch mode blocks Playwright fixtures that start a test daemon with kspec serve, so daemon-backed web UI E2E coverage cannot run during autonomous task work even when the code is ready.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reused workspaces can keep stale dist/ build artifacts because npm test only checked for artifact existence, which hid source/runtime mismatches until a manual rebuild. Added stale-build freshness detection so tests rebuild automatically when source inputs are newer.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Playwright E2E daemon fixtures always attempt to start kspec serve, which makes daemon/API E2E specs fail under dispatch sessions where serve start/stop/restart is forbidden by design.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm test discovers untracked .review review-workspace tests, so unrelated sandbox failures can block validation for focused task branches
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test includes an intermittent daemon startup failure in tests/cli-serve.test.ts ('should start daemon from npm-installed package with all deps available') that can fail with ECONNREFUSED during the health check while passing on isolated rerun.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Playwright web-ui fixtures still bootstrap the daemon with kspec serve start, which is incompatible with dispatch-mode agent sessions and prevents browser tests from running under automation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Backfill task descriptions can drift across module boundaries; this core backfill task referenced @status-lifecycle and item types that actually live under @schema, which required extra CLI lookups before starting the in-scope work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session checkpoint hook fires for agent-dispatched tasks during interactive sessions. Spec ac-session-scope on @cmd-session-checkpoint should filter these out. Either implementation gap or KSPEC_SESSION_ID not set in interactive Claude Code sessions. Got 5+ irrelevant warnings this session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codex skill reviewed wrong file on first attempt despite being given explicit path. Required very explicit YOU MUST READ THIS EXACT FILE phrasing on retry. May need prompt-file pattern or path verification step in the codex skill for review-plan mode.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (Claude agent + Codex in parallel) on plan documents found complementary issues with minimal overlap. Claude agent caught code-level issues (misleading variable pattern, error handling). Codex caught spec-level issues (AC overlap with ac-19, logging mismatch). Worth standardizing for plan reviews.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fresh full npm test on PR #789 head later passed after a review-time failure in packages/web-ui/tests/prose-typography.test.ts, suggesting the built-CSS typography test can fail transiently and send shadow-branch-only tasks into unnecessary fix cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In-place parser YAML writes let concurrent readers observe partially rewritten files, which surfaced as intermittent full-suite failures in dispatch workspace registry/state tests. Shared YAML persistence paths should prefer atomic temp-file rename semantics when readers may poll live state.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test in dispatch worker worktree hit shared .kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation lock contention across unrelated task/triage/session suites, so broad verification can fail for environmental reasons instead of task-local regressions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running npm test inside an active dispatch worker workspace can fail unrelated CLI/session tests with dispatch shadow mutation lock timeouts on .kspec-dispatch-shadow-mutation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: scripts/test.cjs auto-build remediation is not parallel-safe; running two test commands that both trigger build repair can fail with cp: dest is not a directory even though each command succeeds sequentially.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Spec quality iteration: took 3 rounds of agent review to move from implementation-shaped specs to behavioral specs. Consider adding a spec quality checklist to /kspec:writing-specs skill — questions like: Would this AC survive a complete reimplementation? Does it name specific technologies? Does it describe observable behavior?
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent-browser UI audit across all pages simultaneously gave concrete findings that code-only analysis missed (raw spec_ref slugs on task cards, sidebar 30s polling, missing Active Fleet on board). The agent-browser CLI + parallel agents pattern is highly effective for UI coverage audits.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plugin cache staleness after npm link: ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ serves old skill content even after rebuild + npm link + /reload-plugins. Required manual cache replacement. Need either a cache-bust mechanism in the plugin reload flow, or a kspec command to update the cache.
observations.author: @claude
