observations.content: Review re-review cycle overhead: each plan review round required close old review, create new, open new (3 commands). A kspec review reopen or kspec review new-round shortcut that creates a linked follow-up review would reduce friction for iterative review workflows.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agent-as-reviewer for plans: spawning review agents that verify implementation details (function names, file paths, route patterns) against the actual codebase caught 3 blockers in round 3 and 3 more in round 7 that would have been painful during implementation. The review skill + kspec review CLI provided enough structure for agents to produce actionable findings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agent reviewer workflow works well as a plan review tool, not just code review. Two-pass review (first found blockers on spec conflicts and duplication, second validated fixes and approved) produced actionable findings and a clean quality gate before plan approval. The review record lifecycle (create, open, investigate, verdict, close) maps naturally to plan review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer subagent pattern (implement → commit → submit → spawn reviewer → merge) enabled 7 tasks completed in one session with independent review records. Each task had proper review artifacts and audit trail.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Subagent reviewer pattern: spawning reviewer with explicit skills (review, review-gates, merge) and clear instructions produces genuine reviews that catch real issues. All 3 reviews this session found actionable nits while correctly approving solid work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Sequential task pipeline with review gates: three dependent tasks (git query -> normalize -> display) each reviewed and merged independently. Clean dependency chain kept each review focused and each merge low-risk.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Core skill template→shadow sync is manual: after editing templates/skills/<id>/SKILL.md, you must manually cp to .kspec/skills/<id>/SKILL.md for codex/droid renders to pick up changes. kspec skill render reads from .kspec/skills/, not templates/. This step is easy to forget and the render silently shows 'no changes needed' when the shadow copy is stale.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Worker and reviewer both missed incomplete task scope — task said 'all YAML write paths' but work only covered task files. Neither the worker nor reviewer caught the gap. Need better scope-verification discipline, possibly a checklist item in work-gates or review-gates.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dismissed shard 3 test failures as 'pre-existing flaky tests' without verifying against main. They were actually regressions from the same dev branch. Rule: always verify failing tests against the base branch before dismissing them.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Bisecting test failures by checking main vs dev, then narrowing to exact commit, quickly identified root cause of YAML anchor/alias crash. This should be the standard approach for any CI failure — verify against base branch first.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent research pattern: launching codebase exploration + industry research agents simultaneously during spec-plan-design gives comprehensive foundation in one round-trip. Used effectively in dispatch event expansion planning session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session checkpoint hook repeatedly warns about plans/ files being uncommitted, but plan files are not meant to be committed (shadow branch is the durable record). Hook does not know about this convention. Happened 5+ times in one session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Resolving review threads requires individual reply+resolve calls per thread. Resolving 16 threads took 16 pairs of commands. A batch resolve (kspec review resolve-all or batch support for review resolve) would save significant time in fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec plan derive --tasks creates auto-generated implement-* stub tasks for each spec even when the plan document already defines explicit tasks covering those specs. Had to cancel 2 redundant stubs. Derive should detect overlapping spec_ref coverage and skip auto-generation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan-review-fix cycle using kspec review records + spawned reviewer agents was effective. Two passes caught real issues (oversized ACs, implementation leakage, task granularity). Using a reference plan as quality bar gave concrete evaluation criteria.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Merge conflict handling instructions update — traced root cause across 3 instruction sources, updated 4 source files propagated to 11 rendered outputs, review agent approved with zero findings. The build → install-core → render pipeline works once you know the sequence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan-to-task derivation workflow has too many manual steps when plan uses prose spec changes instead of YAML spec blocks. Had to: (1) create tasks manually via task add, (2) patch descriptions to full content, (3) batch-set automation eligibility, (4) batch-set spec refs, (5) manually edit plan YAML for derived_tasks. A single plan derive --tasks-only or plan derive that skips the spec requirement would collapse steps 1-5 into one command.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Subagent plan review with injected skills (/kspec:review + /review-gates) produced high-quality findings including a genuine MUST-FIX. The two-pass pattern (review → fix → re-review) caught all issues before the plan was approved. This pattern should be standardized in a /plan-review skill.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: review-cli integration tests assume KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_HEAD is unset, but dispatch worker environments export it, so 'review add leaves examined_commit null when not provided' fails under dispatch even though the runtime fix here is unrelated.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: No daemon log access from CLI. kspec serve has no log subcommand and the daemon runs as a background Bun process. Debugging dispatch issues required the user to manually find and share daemon stdout. A cancelled task @01KFMMMN existed for this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: getDaemonUrl() is duplicated across agent.ts, event.ts, and schedule.ts with identical implementations. Any behavioral gate (like KSPEC_NO_DAEMON) must be applied in multiple places unless routed through isDaemonRunning().
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative AC refinement with user produced clean behavioral specs. Starting from implementation-focused ACs, user feedback drove removal of implementation details, splitting of concerns (separate AC for serve command exemption), and precise wording (persistent errors vs file watcher detects).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec skill render --force updated unrelated rendered review skills but did not regenerate .agents/skills/kspec-triage-automation from the edited templates/skills/triage-automation/SKILL.md in this worktree, so the skill source/render path is unclear during task work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Post-derive review missed a semantically empty task in @plan-dispatch-integration-checkout-boundaries: @task-design-dispatch-shared-checkout-contract only restated the approved plan/spec contract and created a useless dependency gate ahead of real implementation work. Structural review of derived output is insufficient; plan/task review needs an explicit rule rejecting tasks that merely re-describe already-approved design instead of producing a concrete artifact or behavior change.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test intermittently fails in tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts role-entrypoint dispatch cases, but the same file passes when rerun in isolation. This looks like suite-level flakiness or shared-state leakage in dispatch engine tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Automated review/merge flow accepted a false 'Already up to date' conclusion. The reviewer approved and completed @01KM4BK8 even though 'dev...dispatch/task/fix-dispatch-checkout-dependency-drift-after-new-npm-deps/01km4bk8' still showed the task branch ahead by two commits. Review/merge guidance or tooling should require ancestry verification (for example rev-list/merge-base) before concluding that a branch is already integrated.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The task-work skill says a needs_work task can be resubmitted directly with 'kspec task submit @ref', but the CLI currently rejects submit from needs_work and requires an explicit 'kspec task start @ref' transition back to in_progress first. The documented fix-cycle workflow and CLI behavior should match so agents and humans do not hit avoidable resubmission failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test in the dispatch worker workspace was non-deterministic across consecutive runs on the same rebased head: two runs failed on different unrelated test sets before a third run passed cleanly. This makes fix-cycle merge gates harder to interpret when task-specific coverage is already green.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec skill render writing-specs --force reported no changes even though .agents/skills/kspec-writing-specs/SKILL.md was stale relative to templates/skills/writing-specs/SKILL.md on this branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test intermittently times out in cli-schedule-commands while isolated reruns pass, which makes task verification noisy and obscures unrelated daemon/watcher work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel explore agents (3 concurrent) for audit gave comprehensive cross-validated coverage of CLI write paths, schema definitions, and daemon routes in one round
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agent-based plan review caught trait AC overlap with @trait-error-guidance and missing triage/plan record loader coverage that the author missed
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Specs started too implementation-specific (file paths, API endpoints, technology names). Took 3+ revision rounds to reach behavioral abstraction. Should study gold standard plans before writing specs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Hardcoded SPA fallback route list in daemon server.ts requires manual update for every new web UI route. Caused /automation 404 on hard refresh. Same pattern caused prior sidebar nav issues. A wildcard fallback or auto-discovery from the SvelteKit build would eliminate the class of bug.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detailed task notes with what/why/how and specific file paths enabled dispatch workers to complete @01KM6AR9 and @01KM6EDZ autonomously on first attempt without human intervention.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Worker agents on complex tasks (e.g. @task-impl-data-manager, 5 fix cycles) show a pattern of shallow initial implementation: not reading spec ACs carefully, not using existing helpers (findTaskFiles), writing tests that only cover 2-writer cases when the AC implies N-writer correctness, and implementing stubs (throw unconditionally) instead of real routing. Unclear if this is context window pressure, insufficient upfront planning, or prompt structure. Results in reviewer catching things the worker should have gotten right — each fix cycle is one issue the worker could have anticipated.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer agents may be stopping at the first blocker found and submitting changes_requested instead of completing a full sweep. This turns N independent issues into N sequential fix cycles. Example: @task-impl-data-manager had 5 cycles where each found 1-2 new issues that could have been caught in a single thorough pass. Need to investigate whether the review skill/prompt encourages early termination or if the reviewer is just hitting context/budget limits.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Automated agent ran kspec task migrate on live project data during @task-build-migration as an integration test, creating split-brain state between per-task files and index. Task notes and specs did not prevent this. Consider adding a guard or convention: migration and activation should only run as deliberate manual steps, never as part of automated task work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Clone-to-tmp-remove-remote-test-then-push pattern worked well for safely validating shadow branch migrations. Three iterations caught: Python yaml format incompatibility, stale per-task file detection, and hybrid entry edge case — all before touching live data.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-driven scope creep from missing depends_on. task-session-prompt-action lacked a dependency on task-multi-turn-invocation, so reviewers pushed it to reimplement the idle loop and prompt queue to make integration tests pass. By fix cycle 4, the task had rebuilt the core of the multi-turn invocation refactor, creating semantic merge conflicts when both branches tried to merge into dev. Root cause: the plan derived tasks with correct spec refs but incomplete inter-task dependencies. The reviewer had no visibility into parallel in-flight work and optimized locally for test coverage. Mitigation: during plan derivation, explicitly declare depends_on for tasks whose tests require infrastructure from sibling tasks. During review, check for parallel in-flight tasks touching the same files before requesting structural additions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual review pattern (internal agent + codex in parallel) catches different issue classes and gives high confidence before plan approval. Internal finds structural issues, codex finds format issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Sequential AC numbering in plan documents causes cascading renumbering when ACs are split or inserted. Named ACs (ac-idle-transition) or omitting IDs to let derive auto-number would eliminate the cascade. Discussed with user — named ACs are preferred going forward.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Codifying spec quality rules into skills (writing-specs, plan, review-plan) during the session that discovered them prevents the same friction in future sessions. Rules emerged from concrete review feedback and were generalized into principles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Three-pass plan review pattern (write → agent review → fix → agent review → fix → agent review) caught progressively subtler issues. First pass found structural problems (missing specs, field leaks). Second pass found spec interactions (existing specs conflicting). Third pass was clean. This pattern should be the standard for complex plans.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill template → shadow branch → rendered output pipeline requires 3 separate commands (npm run build, skill install-core, skill render) with no single command to do all three. Easy to get confused about which step is missing when rendered output doesn't update. The development convention mentions kspec skill render but not the full pipeline for template authors.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Profiling git log -L before designing solutions gave concrete numbers (39s baseline, 12-18s with -n limits) that guided the architecture decision. The data made it clear that optimizing the existing approach was insufficient and a structural change was needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent evaluation for plan quality assessment — three agents (code quality, test coverage, spec status) running simultaneously produced a comprehensive audit in ~70s. Effective pattern for post-plan completion review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spawning a review agent for spec proposals before creating them catches duplication and design issues early. The agent-definition-schema review caught that kspec meta set already existed, saving a full redundant spec+task cycle.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task fix-web-ui-pages-not-rendering-on-initial-load completed cleanly in a single pass. Well-scoped task description with root cause, fix strategy, and file list made implementation fast and error-free. All 7210 tests passed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: TanStack Query v6 for Svelte 5 has a known issue where $effect subscriptions fail when query enabled conditions have multiple $state dependencies. This caused pages to not render on initial load. The fix (moving guards to API layer) works but the pattern constraint is not documented anywhere — future development could reintroduce the problem by adding !isStaticMode() or similar $state reads back into query enabled conditions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill template dev workflow requires npm run build + kspec setup + delete rendered files + kspec skill render to propagate changes from templates/skills/ to .agents/skills/. The render command reads from shadow branch (.kspec/skills/), not templates/ directly, so edits to templates are invisible until setup syncs them. This multi-step dance is error-prone during development.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative proposal refinement for skill guidance. Going through JS-specific → generic-but-enumerated → principle-based rounds produced guidance that cannot be gamed by aliasing APIs or using different file-reading techniques. The key insight was targeting the technique (reading source and asserting on strings) rather than specific function names.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel agent batching for mechanical refactoring — spawned 3 agents to convert 29 test files simultaneously, all produced clean results with passing tests. Effective pattern for large-scale mechanical changes where each file is independent.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: oxfmt converts let $state() to const in Svelte files, breaking bind: directives. No config option to disable const promotion. Required excluding all *.svelte from both oxfmt and oxlint. Watch for this if oxfmt adds Svelte-aware mode in future versions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Subagents making bulk no-unused-vars fixes frequently misidentify variables as unused when they are used in nested/sibling scopes (destructuring, Commander.js patterns, Playwright fixtures). When dispatching lint-fix agents, instruct them to verify usage by searching the file before removing any variable, and run tests after fixes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel subagent dispatch by non-overlapping file domains (4 agents across e2e tests, unit tests A-M, unit tests N-Z, source code) resolved ~1100 lint violations in a single round. Key: partition files so agents never touch the same file.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec skill render does not pick up local changes to templates/skills/ — it resolves core skill content from the installed npm package. When editing core skill templates during development (e.g., updating references), rendered output in .agents/skills/kspec-* and .factory/skills/kspec-* must be manually edited to stay in sync. npm run dev -- skill render also doesn't help. This creates a gap between source-of-truth edits and rendered output for core template skills.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: readTestOutput migration tasks are well-scoped for automation: mechanical sed replacement, clear verification (test + lint), minimal judgment. Task @task-readtestoutput-yaml-round-trip-stability completed in one pass with no issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch reviewer worktrees lack installed dependencies (node_modules). Reviewer agents must run npm install before tests, which modifies package-lock.json and triggers session checkpoint hooks about uncommitted changes. The dispatch workspace bootstrap or preparation step should ensure dependencies are installed so review worktrees are test-ready on arrival.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: readTestOutput bulk conversion tasks are well-scoped and complete quickly — sed with exclusion patterns handles the mechanical replacement, task descriptions with explicit verification steps (test + lint) give high confidence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer used merge-base diff (git diff $(git merge-base HEAD dev)..HEAD) instead of dev..HEAD to avoid false findings from parallel branch divergence. This correctly identified that yaml-round-trip-stability.test.ts and package-lock.json diffs were artifacts of dev moving forward, not actual branch changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: readTestOutput batch conversion tasks (21-call meta.test.ts) completed cleanly in one pass using replace_all edits. Pattern: grep to identify calls, replace_all for bulk substitution, targeted replace_all per variable name to strip encoding args. No fix cycles needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatched reviewer in detached worktree cannot git checkout dev for merge — dev is locked by the main worktree. Workaround: git -C <main-worktree-path> merge <task-branch>. Every dispatched reviewer hits this. Could be addressed by: (1) documenting the git -C pattern in the merge skill, (2) having dispatch prepare merge capability in the main worktree, or (3) creating a temporary local branch tracking dev in the review worktree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer dispatch with manual_merge in detached worktree cannot 'git checkout dev' because dev is already checked out by the main worktree. Must cd to main worktree (/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch) to perform the merge, violating the dispatch instruction to run all commands from the assigned workspace. Systemic for every reviewer merge in worktree-isolated dispatch. Possible fix: dispatch merge instructions should explicitly note the main worktree path for the merge step, or provide a helper command.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Batch readTestOutput migration tasks had excellent task descriptions — exact file, exact call count, exact steps, verification commands. Made automated execution fast and unambiguous.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: readTestOutput batch conversion: correctly identified and excluded bootstrap.test.ts from conversion because its readFileSync references are dependency-injected mock stubs (fsApi parameters), not actual file system reads. This pattern — DI stubs that look like fs calls — is worth checking for in future batch conversions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Iterative plan refinement with review between each version. 4 versions of daemon optimistic data layer plan, each round of user feedback materially improved the output: spec purity rules, design-as-task anti-pattern, tiered caching model, session staleness. Lightweight planning iterations are cheaper than implementation rework.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Using an approved example plan as quality reference. Comparing task detail against @plan-dispatch-event-system-expansion immediately surfaced the gap between vague and executable task descriptions. Example plans are effective calibration tools.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Questioning spec relevance before writing replacement tests saved significant effort — 3 specs removed, 2 ACs dropped, plan went from 6 tasks to 0. Investigation-first approach for test coverage plans is highly effective.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Split backend has race condition bugs: (1) concurrent in-process mutateTask calls on the same task lose mutations because per-task mutex doesn't properly serialize notes.yaml writes, (2) mutateTask + mutateTasks on overlapping tasks don't serialize, (3) writeTaskFile strips unknown fields during mutateTask (unlike monolithic backend). Also kspec validate --refs doesn't load notes/detail fields from per-task files in split format, missing dangling references. These were found during test fixture migration to split format.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec validate --refs does not load per-task detail files (notes.yaml, task.yaml) in split storage format. Validation only reads the lean index (project.tasks.yaml), so dangling references in note authors and plan_ref fields are not detected. This means split-format projects have weaker reference validation than monolithic projects.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch task with large embedded task descriptions can fail twice with Prompt is too long before any meaningful work begins. The research/planning phase loads full task description + fixture data + codebase context, exceeding context limits. The wasted invocations delay task completion and waste compute. Mitigation: task descriptions could reference external docs instead of embedding large fixture examples.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Resuming dispatched work from a dirty working tree (uncommitted changes from failed invocation) worked well. The prepared workspace bootstrap pattern preserved all prior work, and the new invocation could assess, fix, and commit without re-doing research. This validates the mutable worker branch design for dispatch continuation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task description with exact file paths, line numbers, and difference analysis between duplicates made deduplication task trivially scoped — zero discovery overhead. This is an ideal pattern for cleanup tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: file-lock.test.ts concurrent writes test is flaky (expected count:5, got count:4). Required stashing changes and re-running full suite to confirm pre-existing. Not currently tracked anywhere.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer dispatch worktrees cannot 'git checkout <integration-branch>' because the integration branch (e.g. dev) is already checked out in the main worktree. Workaround: use 'git -C <main-worktree-path> merge --no-ff <task-branch>'. The merge skill instructions should account for worktree contexts — either by detecting the situation and using git -C, or by documenting the workaround. Every dispatch review that merges will hit this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-written task descriptions with exact file/line references and skipped test locations dramatically reduce investigation time for concurrency bugs. The fix-split-backend-mutex task was completed in a single pass with no fix cycles needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-scoped task descriptions with root cause analysis, prior-art references (monolithic backend pattern), and pre-located skipped tests dramatically reduce implementation time. The preserve-unknown-fields task was completed in a single pass with no false starts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: task submit rejects needs_work status, requiring an intermediate 'kspec task start' before 'kspec task submit' in every fix cycle. The needs_work->in_progress->pending_review dance is mechanical — could be a single 'kspec task submit' that auto-transitions through in_progress when current state is needs_work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Rebase conflict resolution in dispatch fix cycles: extracting dev's full file via git show, reading both sides of each conflict completely, planning resolution strategy per-region before editing, then verifying no orphaned conflict markers after each edit. This pattern successfully resolved 4 conflict regions across 2 files integrating rawCore/unknown-field-preservation with per-task-mutex structural changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When resolving git merge conflicts via Edit tool, orphaned conflict markers can be left behind if the old_string doesn't capture the complete conflict block (all 3 markers). After each Edit resolving a conflict, always run a Grep for conflict markers to catch orphans immediately. This happened during fix cycle 2 of fix-split-backend-mutex where a <<<<<<< HEAD marker survived after resolving conflict 2.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-specified task descriptions with exact file locations, AC references, and data mappings enable single-pass implementation with no back-and-forth. Task @01KMM6PH4EQBRZW72DXWMMNFP3 went from start to submit in one focused pass.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review quality improved by reproducing suspicious test failures against the recorded base commit before classifying them as regressions. In this session, comparing the timed-out canonical workspace contract test against dev prevented a pre-existing failure from being misattributed to the submitted task, while keeping the real blocker focused on the task migrate manifest-upgrade regression.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Recording review findings through kspec review comment is brittle when the body contains shell-significant characters such as backticks or embedded command examples. In this session, a first attempt to post a blocker comment failed because the shell interpreted inline backticks before kspec saw the payload, forcing a retry with manually sanitized text. Consider a file-based payload option or stdin support for long review comment bodies.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review thread bodies are truncated in text output of kspec review get. Must use --json and manually parse to read full thread content. Common friction during fix cycles when reading reviewer feedback.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle resubmission requires kspec task start then kspec task submit from needs_work. The intermediate in_progress state adds ceremony with no value — work is already done. Could allow kspec task submit directly from needs_work, or add a kspec task resubmit shorthand.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Full-suite test runs are intermittently timing out in agent-invocation-lifecycle and canonical-task-workspace-contract while the same cases pass in isolated runs. This makes review gates noisy and expensive to verify because npm test can fail without a deterministic reproducer. Consider adding tooling or diagnostics for suite-load timeout triage and stabilization.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Fix cycle review threads: using 'kspec review get @ref --json | jq .threads' gives complete thread content when text-mode output truncates long entries. Reliable pattern for reading full reviewer feedback during fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon package import paths (packages/daemon/src/) use relative paths that resolve correctly in dist/ layout but not from source. Adding new src/daemon/ files that need to be imported by daemon package code requires: (1) dynamic imports in daemon code, (2) manual build:daemon step to copy the file, and (3) careful path selection (./entity-cache.js works at build time but not test time). This made wiring entity-cache into project-context.ts significantly harder than expected — required callback-based indirection instead of direct imports.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Callback-based integration pattern for cross-package dependencies (CacheInvalidationCallback following FileChangeCallback precedent) cleanly avoids import path issues between packages/daemon/src/ and src/daemon/ while maintaining testability.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The review workflow correctly enforced the lifecycle once the evidence was recorded: required checks attached to the review, request_changes auto-closed the review, and the task transitioned to needs_work with the review ref preserved. That integration made the review outcome durable even in an autonomous dispatch session.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review comment capture is brittle when the body contains shell-sensitive characters. In this session, malformed shell interpolation produced duplicate blocker threads before the corrected comments landed. The review tooling should support file/stdin bodies or stronger escaping guidance so reviewers can record anchored findings without creating noisy duplicates.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review record mutations like `kspec review comment` can take 20-30s with no progress output, which makes autonomous review sessions look hung and complicates recovery when a shell payload is malformed.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: The full `npm test` gate still has at least one flaky path around agent invocation timeout handling: the full suite failed on tests/agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts while the file passed in isolation, which weakens reviewer confidence in the required green-suite check.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Content-based cache key design using git blob SHAs — conversation-first design before coding produced a cache that is immune to commits/rebases/touch-without-edit. Good pattern for any repo-aware tooling.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: oxfmt --check on specific files can pass locally while CI (which runs oxfmt --check .) fails. Always run oxfmt in write mode on changed files before committing, not just --check.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on @task-remove-monolithic: adding behavioral doctor tests caught a real bug — buildTaskStorageSection hardcoded kynetic.yaml instead of using findManifestInDir. The review blocker requiring behavioral tests was justified; without them, slug-based manifests would silently skip the task-storage health check.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review CLI friction: kspec review comment/check bodies currently need shell-escaped inline strings, which broke on backticks and code-like text during this session. A body-from-file/evidence-from-file option would make automated reviews more reliable for anchored findings and evidence logs.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review gate friction: npm test was red in this review snapshot because of a pre-existing duplicate symbol in tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts. Automated review still needs to record the failure, but baseline-red suites make merge decisions noisier and slower. The workflow would benefit from a clearer way to track or surface known baseline failures separately from change-introduced regressions.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Dispatch review snapshots are detached worktrees, but the merge instructions still direct reviewers to 'git checkout <integration-branch>' in the current workspace. In this session that failed because 'dev' was already checked out in the main worktree, so the merge had to be completed via git -C against the canonical dev worktree. The review/merge workflow should either document this explicitly or provide a command that performs the manual merge against the canonical target worktree without requiring branch checkout in the detached review snapshot.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: workspace.ts and shadow.ts have independent git subprocess environments with no shared contract. When adding GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, both had to be patched separately. A shared buildGitEnv() at a lower layer could prevent future drift when new env vars need to be set for all git subprocesses.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task description that includes exact file paths, function names, affected code paths, and the precise fix makes automated agent work highly efficient — this task was completed in a single pass with no blockers or ambiguity.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Full-suite npm test is currently red on dev because tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts redeclares mockMetadata around line 2532. This forces reviewers to manually compare against base to prove the failure is pre-existing before approving unrelated work, which weakens review throughput and confidence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot always run the documented 'git checkout <integration-branch>' merge flow because the integration branch may already be checked out in another worktree. In this session, checkout of dev failed with 'already used by worktree', and the merge had to be completed via git -C against the primary worktree. Reviewer merge instructions should account for this case explicitly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on entity-cache task: all 3 review blockers resolved in a single commit with clean test pass (6898/6898). Systematic approach — read all threads, deduplicate (6→3 unique), plan all fixes, implement, test, commit. Entity cache route wiring pattern (accessor injection via options) scales cleanly to new domains.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review quality improved when I treated passing tests as insufficient and built a direct runtime repro against a temp fixture. That caught a real cache invalidation bug in manifest-backed items even though npm test was green.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Recording kspec review findings through shell commands is fragile when the body contains Markdown/backticks. My first review comment was truncated by shell interpolation, forcing a second cleanly-encoded comment. This is avoidable tooling friction around review comment capture.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 4 on entity-cache task was clean and focused: single blocker (fileToDomain mapping kynetic.yaml to only meta domain), surgical fix (return array instead of single value), reference-equality behavioral test that works without full shadow branch fixtures. 1 commit, full suite green, no scope creep.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-command shell quoting is fragile:  breaks when the review text contains backticks or other shell-significant characters. In this review cycle I had to reissue the commands using a heredoc-safe body. Consider file-based/body-stdin support or a safer CLI pattern for long review text.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: initContext() is called in 30+ route handlers and performs disk/git work every time. The lazy getCtx() pattern added in the entity cache work is effective but adds boilerplate to every handler. A cache-aware middleware that provides context lazily (only resolving on first access) would eliminate this pattern entirely and ensure new routes get the optimization automatically.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: RouteEntityCache interface as decoupling point worked well for incremental domain wiring. Adding new cache-backed domains required only: extend interface, wire route factory options, add cache-first reads and write-through calls. No changes to entity-cache.ts core. Clean separation of concerns.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache fix cycle 6 completed cleanly in one commit. The established patterns (lazy getCtx, domain state check + index lookup + disk fallback, write-through skip) made adding cache support for plans/reviews/triage/meta detail routes mechanical. 6899 tests passed, 0 regressions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache task went through 8 fix cycles. Each cycle found one more unwired domain or missing detail-tier method. Root cause: the implementation had 8 domains x 3 tiers (index, detail, write-through) x N route paths, creating a combinatorial coverage surface. The plan-before-code step should include an explicit domain-x-tier matrix for cache-like features, verified against routes before first submission.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 8 (session watcher invalidation) was resolved in a single clean pass: traced the full callback chain, identified the gap in fileToDomain, fixed the root cause rather than adding another workaround, simplified the server.ts callback, added targeted tests, full suite green. The Explore subagent for multi-file investigation kept main context clean.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cache route tests need explicit cold-path vs warm-path response-parity coverage. This review found a cache-hit-only regression in item parent resolution and incomplete loading-state behavior outside tasks/items because most checks asserted cache usage, not that cached responses exactly match disk responses across domains.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache fix cycle 10 revealed cross-domain mutation gaps: routes that trigger side effects in other domains (review verdict transitioning tasks, triage act creating tasks/deleting inbox/saving observations) only wrote through their own domain. A write-through audit should check not just 'is this domain wired?' but 'does this route mutate data in other domains?' — the second question is harder because it requires tracing through called functions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Centralizing project unregister cleanup via ProjectContextManager.setUnregisterCallback replaced a fragile per-callsite pattern. When multiple code paths can trigger the same lifecycle event (API unregister, watcher permanent failure), a single callback on the source-of-truth object ensures all paths get the same cleanup. Pattern worth reusing for other lifecycle events.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-thread creation via CLI is brittle when the comment body contains shell metacharacters like backticks; this session triggered bash substitution errors before kspec still recorded the thread. A file-based or stdin-based body option for kspec review comment would make autonomous reviews safer and less error-prone.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: The review workflow reliably handled closure: once the blocker was recorded, kspec review verdict auto-closed the review and moved the task from pending_review to needs_work without extra manual state management. That made the detached reviewer flow predictable and easy to audit.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Large multi-domain implementations (like entity-cache with 8 domains × N routes) accumulate fix cycles when review finds one domain at a time not properly wired. A self-review checklist or automated structural check before submission — verifying every route for each domain uses the correct tier — would catch these earlier and reduce fix cycle count.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Route-level cache warming tests accepted 'unloaded' for not-yet-started domains during progressive load, which let a spec violation survive multiple review cycles. Add a behavioral test that exercises requests arriving after registration but before a later domain begins loading, and assert the API returns _cache_status='loading' instead of falling back to disk.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity-cache review required many fix cycles because tests covered warmed happy paths but missed startup/default-project registration, cross-domain write-through, and loading-state behavior on secondary endpoints. Add integration coverage for startup registration and cross-domain cache coherence to catch these earlier.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Diff-first review with mandatory full-suite execution and targeted code inspection found real entity-cache integration bugs even though npm test passed. Parallel code exploration was effective for broad route-wiring changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review sessions can inherit a pre-existing failing full test suite on the integration branch (example: tests/agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts duplicate mockMetadata declaration on dev). This forces reviewers to spend extra time proving the failure is unrelated before they can render a task verdict. Consider tracking branch-health regressions or adding a first-class way to mark required checks as pre-existing base failures during review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache task hit 13 fix cycles. Root cause: initial implementation wired cache to some routes but missed others (startup project, cross-domain write-through, refs loading contract). Each review cycle found ~3 more unwired integration points. For cross-cutting features that touch many route files, workers should do a systematic route-by-route audit (checklist of every route × every cache behavior: serve-from-memory, write-through, warming-availability, degradation fallback) before first submission. This would catch most integration gaps in one pass rather than N review cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 13 was clean and efficient: read all 3 blocker threads upfront, diagnosed root causes in parallel, implemented all fixes in a single pass, added behavioral tests, all 6906 tests passed. The pattern of reading ALL review threads before starting any fix work prevents partial fixes and avoids additional cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comment capture is still shell-fragile for multiline/code-heavy bodies. In this session, kspec review comment --body with backticks and inline code triggered bash interpolation errors and produced duplicate/garbled threads before succeeding via heredoc. Consider a first-class --body-file option or stronger CLI guidance/defaults for file payloads on review comment/reply commands.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Lazy getCtx() pattern for daemon route cache integration: deferring initContext() via a closure that only initializes on first call avoids disk/git work on cache-hit requests. Pattern proven across all 8 route domains (tasks, items, sessions, meta, plans, reviews, triage, inbox) over fix cycles 5-14. Key insight: the same pattern works for both list routes (where it prevents any disk access) and detail routes (where cache hits skip initContext but misses fall through to disk loading and cache-store).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared workspaces allow concurrent npm test runs from different processes, which can contaminate review evidence with timeout-heavy false negatives. In this session, an unrelated background 'npm test --fresh' in the same workspace made the first full-suite result non-authoritative until an uncontended rerun passed. Consider a session-aware test-run lock or explicit detection/warning when another test harness is already active in the same worktree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity-cache route tests covered warm list/detail paths but missed filtered /api/sessions requests (task_id/spec_ref) and related-session endpoints, so hot-path disk fallbacks survived a green suite. Add route-level cache assertions for filter-dependent and related-session reads when reviewing or extending cache wiring.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: ReferenceIndex and AlignmentIndex constructors accept LoadedTask[]/LoadedSpecItem[] but only use _ulid, slugs, spec_ref, title, status from each element. This forces unsafe 'as unknown as LoadedTask[]' casts when passing cache summary types (TaskSummary/ItemSummary) which are structurally sufficient. Encountered in entity cache route wiring (tasks.ts, items.ts, sessions.ts). A minimal structural interface (like AlignmentTask) accepted by ReferenceIndex would eliminate the casts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cache-backed daemon routes are relying on 'as unknown as LoadedTask/LoadedSpecItem' casts from summary types. This let /api/refs return a spec status object instead of the lightweight string contract when served from cache. Consider explicit cache-view types or normalization helpers at route boundaries instead of structural casts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task-level review runs of 'kspec validate' are hard to interpret because hundreds of pre-existing completeness/alignment warnings dominate the output. Consider a scoped or baseline-aware validation mode so reviewers can distinguish new warnings from repository background noise.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache integration surfaced a latent bug in ref-resolution: TypeScript 'as string' casts hid that spec item status is an object {maturity, implementation}, not a string. Test fixtures matched the cast (string) rather than reality (object). Fix cycle 18 added normalizeStatus() and corrected test fixtures. Lesson: when adding a caching layer that serves summary types, test with realistic type shapes, not simplified casts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review sessions still get noisy when npm test fails in an unrelated flaky suite during full-run verification. In this cycle, rerunning the failing dispatch bootstrap test in isolation passed quickly and clarified that the blocker was route-level cache wiring, not the bootstrap contract itself. The repeatable pattern is: full-suite failure should be easy to classify as deterministic regression vs full-run-only flake without manual log digging.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The review flow worked well when it combined three checks in sequence: read the diff before notes, run the full suite through npm test, then rerun the failing test in isolation through the same runner. That combination quickly separated a required-check failure from the actual code-level cache regressions and kept the final review decision grounded in direct evidence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache wiring requires applying the same 3-part pattern (warmup guard, cache read, disk fallback) to every route handler independently. Easy to miss endpoints — this task had 19 fix cycles partly because routes were missed. A shared middleware or helper that encapsulates the cache-gate pattern would reduce review churn.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon cache routes are brittle when summary-tier objects are cast as full records. In this review, warm-cache paths used ItemSummary/TriageIndexSummary where full LoadedSpecItem/TriageRecord fields were required, causing silent data loss or formatter crashes. Pattern: cache-hit code must treat summary-tier and detail-tier shapes as distinct contracts and add route tests that exercise both warm-cache and disk-fallback paths.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel review exploration worked well here: reading the diff first, running direct reproductions for suspected bugs, and using focused sub-agents for route/cache passes surfaced concrete blockers quickly without fixing code in the review snapshot.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache summary types (TriageIndexSummary, ItemSummary) allow unsafe as-unknown-as casts to full types at call sites, hiding field omissions. Routes that need full data (export, spec_context with ACs) silently serve incomplete responses. TypeScript does not catch these at compile time because of the explicit casts. Consider branded types or separate accessor methods that return distinct types without cast escape hatches.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Domain-level debounce in ProjectEntityCache.invalidateDomain() effectively coalesces multi-file watcher events into single reloads per domain. Deferred promise pattern lets all callers await the same reload. This two-layer debounce (file-level in watcher + domain-level in cache) is the correct architecture for reload dedup.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session code paths still make inconsistent assumptions about session IDs: schema and runtime allow arbitrary strings, but cache invalidation and some lookup logic assumed ULID-shaped directory names. This review found two regressions from that mismatch (non-ULID watcher paths skipped invalidation; bounded session detail lookup skipped disk fallback). Capture: add cross-cutting regression coverage for non-ULID session IDs in watcher invalidation and session detail resolution.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Targeted executable repros were high-leverage in review. Small tsx scripts against the real cache logic disproved assumptions quickly, converted suspected issues into concrete evidence, and made blocker threads precise without needing speculative findings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 23 on entity cache task was clean — read both blocker threads, implemented targeted fixes (disk fallback for bounded index + source parameter for fileToDomain), 3 new tests, full suite passed first run. Reading all review feedback before coding prevented partial fixes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache fileToDomain() assumed session IDs are always ULIDs (Crockford base32 26-char regex). SessionMetadataSchema uses z.string() — session IDs can be any string. This type assumption propagated through 22 review cycles before being caught. Lesson: when a function pattern-matches on ID shape, verify the schema allows that assumption. Added 'source' parameter to disambiguate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: A tiny runtime repro was the fastest way to validate the remaining cache bug. After reading the diff and tests, monkey-patching doLoadDomain() to throw and then observing writeThrough()/invalidateDomain() behavior confirmed the first watcher invalidation was skipped after a failed reload. This is a good pattern for review: use small targeted runtime probes to confirm control-flow suspicions before recording blockers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer subagents can overstep role boundaries and execute lifecycle-changing actions (approve, merge, complete) when they are only supposed to gather evidence. This session needed manual recovery: a test subagent approved review cycle 24, merged elsewhere, and completed the task while the primary review was still in progress. Tighten agent guidance or tool isolation so spawned reviewers/awaiters cannot mutate review/task state unless explicitly delegated ownership of that action.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch churned through 23 fix cycles on task-entity-cache-impl because each automated review+fix cycle was narrow — fix the latest thread, resubmit. No mechanism for the dispatch engine to escalate to manual_only after N cycles or trigger a holistic re-review. Manual takeover resolved it in 1 cycle.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The tiered entity cache architecture (index + detail tiers per domain) enables incremental route migration. Each read route follows the same pattern: check getDomainState(), serve from getXxxIndex(), fall back to initContext() on miss. The @task-migrate-read-routes work demonstrated this — aggregation, validation/search, and background sync wiring were all straightforward additions. The prior @task-entity-cache-impl investment in progressive loading, domain-level debouncing, and write-through made the route migration a focused, low-risk change.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Split backend registration is per-module-graph: daemon routes load from dist/ while tests register from src/. Any new daemon feature that executes CLI commands in-process must register the split backend from the correct module path (the daemon's import graph, not the test's). The command API route handles this via lazy registration in getProgram(), but this pattern isn't documented and would bite future implementers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon command API: reusing existing batch infrastructure (OutputCapture, exit interceptor, buildCommandArgv, resetCommandTree) from batch-exec.ts/batch-context.ts for in-process CLI execution gave response parity with direct CLI for free. The withProjectDir pattern (temporary process.chdir) cleanly bridges daemon's project-context middleware with CLI's process.cwd()-based initContext.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle resubmit requires two commands (task start + task submit) because submit only accepts in_progress status. A convenience flag like task submit --from-needs-work or having submit auto-transition from needs_work would reduce ceremony in fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reading review JSON (kspec review get --json) provides complete thread context including anchors and all entries — sufficient to understand and address all feedback in a single pass without needing separate thread-reading commands.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Exact CLI/API parity bugs were easy to miss because tests compared against the trimmed tests/helpers/cli.ts kspec() helper or manually trimmed stdout. For parity assertions, the project needs a non-trimming CLI test helper or a convention that exact-output tests must use raw spawn output, otherwise trailing-whitespace regressions slip through review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Route-migration review found claimed cache coverage without route-by-route verification:  and  still hit disk because the new behavioral tests only exercised a subset of read endpoints. Improve migration work/review guidance so route-scoped tasks enumerate every affected endpoint and tests explicitly cover the full route inventory.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Route-migration review found claimed cache coverage without route-by-route verification: /api/meta/session and /api/sessions/:id still hit disk because the new behavioral tests only exercised a subset of read endpoints. Improve migration work and review guidance so route-scoped tasks enumerate every affected endpoint and tests explicitly cover the full route inventory.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Elysia lifecycle gotcha: onBeforeHandle does NOT fire on body validation failures. Elysia runs validation between onTransform and onBeforeHandle. Any setup that must apply to ALL responses (including validation errors) — like X-Request-Id headers — must use onTransform, not onBeforeHandle. This cost multiple fix cycles on the command API task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Using the kspec() test helper as ground-truth reference for response parity tests proved effective. The helper's .trim() is well-documented and the test logic accounts for it by checking containment rather than exact equality, while separately asserting the API preserves trailing whitespace.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon command execution reuses a cached Commander singleton, so route tests need sequential in-process coverage for global output-mode state. This review found that resetting only json/verbose left YAML mode sticky across requests and broke response parity despite a green suite.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon command API: in-process CLI execution via Commander's parseAsync leaks process-global state across requests. Five fix cycles addressed different leak vectors (console capture, process.stdout.write, output trimming, X-Request-Id lifecycle hook timing, output format mode). Each vector was non-obvious until a specific two-command sequence exposed it. Consider a comprehensive audit of all process-global state touched by CLI commands — or a sandboxed execution context that snapshots and restores all globals.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-thread commands with inline --body text are still easy to corrupt via shell command substitution when the message contains backticks. Current guidance covers $, <, >, and multiline payloads, but this review showed backticks are another concrete hazard; using file-based payloads or quoted heredocs should be the documented default for review comment bodies.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-only tasks with clear scope (add AC, update description) complete efficiently in a single pass — spec update via kspec batch, implementation verification via explore agent, AC annotation, tests pass, submit. No code changes needed when implementation already aligns.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review friction: when a daemon route fixes request isolation only in its direct execution path but still delegates batch work to a shared CLI executor, regressions can survive multiple fix cycles. In this session, /api/command was corrected to reset output mode with setOutputFormat("text"), but /api/command/batch still reused batch-exec reset logic that only called setJsonMode(false), leaving YAML mode sticky across requests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review success: adversarial verification with a tiny targeted runtime check caught a real blocker after npm test was fully green. Checking state-reset semantics directly (setYamlMode(true) then setJsonMode(false) still yielding yaml) was higher-signal than relying on broad suite status alone.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review gap: daemon-read spec clarifications can look correct on warm-cache paths while cache-miss/degraded paths still call initContext() and inherit CLI drift-check behavior. Reviewers had to manually trace fallback paths across daemon routes and parser initContext to disprove the claim.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review workflow worked well: creating an anchored review record first, then verifying the diff against runtime paths and full-suite evidence, made it straightforward to return the task to needs_work with precise blockers instead of vague feedback.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Entity cache route migration: every route that uses the entity cache needs a 3-state check (loading → return _cache_status loading, ready → serve from cache, no cache → fallback to disk). Multiple fix cycles on task-migrate-read-routes were caused by routes only checking 'ready' and falling through to initContext() during warmup. A lint rule, route helper, or code review checklist entry for 'does every cache-backed route handle the loading state?' would prevent this recurring pattern.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 6 on task-migrate-read-routes completed in a single iteration: all 4 blockers were the same pattern (missing loading guard), systematic fix to all routes, one new warmup test covering all 5 affected routes with spy assertions. Full suite (6970 tests) passed without regression. The spy-based test infrastructure established in earlier cycles made verification fast and reliable.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon read-route warmup tests covered fully-loading caches, but this review exposed two still-missed cases: partial-domain warmup in /api/search (meta or inbox loading yields partial results instead of _cache_status: loading) and the session detail path still falling back to initContext/loadAll* when task/item domains are not ready. Cache warmup coverage should exercise mixed domain states and session detail endpoints, not just all-loading route snapshots.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The cache-only review pattern worked well: reading the diff first, then checking warmup branches and comparing them against the new initContext/getShadowStatus spy tests quickly exposed regressions that payload-only tests missed. Spy-based route coverage is a strong guardrail for daemon read-path migrations.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: setJsonMode(false) has asymmetric clearing behavior — only resets when current format is 'json', silently leaving 'yaml' or other formats intact. This caused 3 fix cycles on the daemon command API task (cycles 5-6 and the batch-exec path). Every call site resetting output format should use setOutputFormat('text') instead. Consider deprecating setJsonMode(false) as a reset mechanism or making it reset unconditionally.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Route-by-route cache migration (task-migrate-read-routes) produced 7 fix cycles, each revealing another code path falling through to initContext()+disk during warmup. The spy test catches warm-path regressions but can't catch warmup fallthrough because it only tests the warm state. A 'loading-state' spy test was added in cycle 6 but only covered known routes. The root issue: incremental migration lacks an architectural enforcer that prevents new disk fallback paths from being introduced. Consider a lint rule or assertion that flags initContext() calls in route handlers, or a comprehensive warmup test that auto-discovers all registered routes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot directly merge into the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this session, the review snapshot could not git checkout dev because dev was already in use by the main worktree, which conflicts with dispatch guidance that all commands run from the assigned workspace.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: A single behavioral daemon-read-path test that hits many read routes and asserts initContext, getShadowStatus, and hasRemoteTracking are never called was an effective regression gate. It caught repeated hot-path fallback issues and gave high-confidence proof that cache-served reads stayed off disk and git paths when warm.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon command executor has repeated fix cycles (5, 6, 7) for process-global state leaking between requests. Output format, cwd, console capture, and command validation all have separate reset paths that can diverge from direct CLI behavior. Consider a single reset-all-state function or a forked execution context to eliminate this class of bug.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec task submit rejects needs_work status — requires explicit kspec task start first. In fix cycles, the worker always intends to resume and resubmit; the intermediate start transition adds friction without value. Consider allowing submit from needs_work directly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Full-suite review gate produced an unrelated or interaction-based failure in tests/native-guard-setup.test.ts while the isolated rerun passed. This makes reviewer evidence noisy: npm test does not deterministically answer whether the submitted snapshot is merge-ready, and reviewers have to spend extra time separating task regressions from pre-existing/flaky failures.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can point at a commit that is already on the integration branch, while the task still instructs the reviewer to manually merge the task branch. That creates avoidable ambiguity during approval because the correct action is to verify integration state and complete the task without a redundant merge.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The review flow worked well when driven by direct evidence: read the exact shadow diff first, verify the related implementation task/spec context, run full npm test, and record an evidence log in the review. For small spec-only tasks this gave a clean approve/complete path without over-reviewing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review workspaces with workspace-dependencies-missing can cause basic read commands like 'kspec task get' and 'kspec review for-task' to stall indefinitely. In this session the reviewer had to wrap reads in shell timeouts to finish the review. Improve detached review workspace readiness or add bounded CLI behavior for read-only commands in reviewer snapshots.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer snapshots can approve successfully, but the final manual merge step cannot `git checkout dev` inside the review worktree when `dev` is already checked out in the primary worktree. This forced an extra `git -C <repo-root> merge ...` workaround from the detached reviewer workspace. A merge helper that targets the integration worktree directly, or reviewer guidance that explicitly covers this case, would remove avoidable friction.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The review record plus merge-gate flow worked well once the code was clean: a fresh per-cycle review, explicit checks, approved disposition, then manual merge and task completion produced a clear audit trail across fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-scoped extract-and-share task with clear what/why/how description made planning trivial and execution clean. Task description suggesting evaluation of setupMultiDirFixtures() integration was a good prompt — checking all 6 consumers upfront confirmed opt-in was the right call.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review worktrees cannot always switch to the integration branch for final merge because git refuses to check out a branch already active in another worktree. Review/merge guidance should account for this by directing reviewers to merge in the primary worktree or another non-conflicting worktree.
observations.author: @claude
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing detached-review merge friction observations, especially @01KMRBVV and @01KMRGMW. Resolved during reflection cleanup to avoid duplicate tracking.

observations.content: serve start --daemon renamed to --detach as side effect of cli-daemon-proxy task. The -d shorthand is preserved but any documentation, scripts, or user muscle memory using the long form needs updating. This was forced by Commander option namespace collision with the new global --daemon flag.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, delegating the full npm test gate to an awaiter while continuing targeted diff reading and manual CLI checks kept progress moving without reducing verification quality. This pattern worked well for a 53-minute suite.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow breaks in detached review snapshots when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. The current merge instructions assume reviewers can switch to dev directly, but git refuses because dev is already in use. Reviewers then need an ad hoc git -C against the existing dev worktree to complete the local merge. This should be handled explicitly by the merge workflow or dispatch tooling.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can instruct a manual merge into dev even when dev is already checked out in the canonical worktree and the reviewed branch already points at the same commit. This forces reviewers into a no-op merge path they cannot execute locally, so dispatch/review guidance should detect same-tip/no-op cases and treat them as already merged or route the merge to the canonical worktree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Small alias tasks with clear notes (what/why/how) and existing patterns to follow execute cleanly in a single pass — good template for similar DX improvements.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch agents in worktree sessions occasionally write memory files with implementation details (4 of 336 sessions). These are scoped to ephemeral worktree paths and never reused. Dispatch agent prompts should discourage memory writes for task-scoped worktree sessions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, reproducing the failing daemon-command-api suite on the exact base dev commit avoided a false regression call and let the task be approved based on change-local evidence. This pattern is useful whenever full-suite failures may be pre-existing.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Reviewer merge from a detached dispatch snapshot hit a git worktree constraint: `git checkout dev` failed because dev was already checked out in the primary worktree. The merge had to be completed via `git -C <primary-worktree> merge ...`, which suggests kspec merge could handle branch-already-attached worktrees more directly for reviewer snapshots.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Spawning a review agent for task proposals catches implementation gaps (missing public APIs, scope underestimates) before the task enters the system. Used for both the watcher fix task and the three reflection proposals — caught that P3 was too large for a task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detailed task notes with standalone what/why/how context enable dispatch agents to complete work autonomously. The watcher fix task (@task-fix-ws-watcher-registration) was completed and reviewed (2 cycles, approved) without manual intervention.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: No way to inspect daemon entity cache state at runtime. Debugging stale data required tracing code paths and guessing domain states. Task @task-daemon-cache-diagnostic created to address this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow in detached worktrees is awkward: the review workspace could not check out integration branch dev because that branch was already attached to the primary worktree, so completing the required manual merge needed an out-of-band git -C invocation against the main worktree. A merge command or workflow helper that targets the recorded integration worktree/branch directly would remove this workaround.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review completion can drift when a newer draft review becomes the task's active review_ref after an earlier review was already approved. In this session, task completion initially stalled until the newly linked draft review was also approved and then closed. The completion flow should either pin to the approved review used for merge or surface a clear actionable error when review_ref changed mid-session.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review friction: async cache reload tests asserted state/data immediately after starting reload but never forced a mid-flight pause, so the new stale-during-reload AC looked covered while meta still exposed a partial ready-state snapshot. We should prefer controllable mid-flight test hooks or spies for reload-path ACs that promise stale-while-revalidate semantics.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: Dispatch AC-28 coverage was too narrow: the added responsiveness tests exercised async child-process paths (_addTaskNote/_blockTask/error recovery) but missed synchronous filesystem branches in bootstrap/workspace. Review caught remaining event-loop-blocking fsSync usage after the task was submitted, so dispatch bookkeeping tests should cover both child-process and file-I/O paths when the AC requires non-blocking internal operations.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Fix cycle pattern: stash-and-test to verify pre-existing failures before investigating saves significant time. Used git stash to run failing tests on prior commit, confirmed they were pre-existing on origin/dev, avoided chasing unrelated issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The review workflow held up once the merge location issue was handled: creating a fresh review record, reading the exact delta against the integration base, recording an evidence log, and running the full npm test suite before verdict produced a clean approval and merge with good auditability.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot perform the required manual merge into the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this session, git checkout dev and git worktree add <tmp> dev both failed because dev was already in use, so the merge had to be executed in the primary worktree. The reviewer/merge workflow should document or automate the correct merge target location for detached review snapshots.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: CLI fault injection via wrapper .mjs scripts: When testing flush failures or other internal error paths at the batch/CLI level, write a temporary .mjs wrapper that (1) imports and patches the target class prototype, (2) sets process.argv[1] to the CLI entry point path (to satisfy the import.meta.url entry guard), (3) dynamically imports the CLI. Run via spawnSync with the wrapper as the script arg. This avoids read-only directory timing issues and ESM inline script limitations.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-before-create pattern for specs and tasks: spawning an agent to review drafted ACs and task descriptions before creating them caught misdiagnoses and scope gaps. Two rounds of review (pre-create and post-create) caught different classes of issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Bug fix task descriptions with What/Where/Why structure and specific code locations (function names, line numbers) enable immediate targeted investigation. Task @fix-workspace-reconciliation-cycle-for-completed-task-records exemplified this — the description pointed directly to reconcileWorkspaceHealth line 1185 and reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts line 2821, eliminating exploratory search and enabling a clean two-change fix with tests passing on first run.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Retrying kspec review add after a delayed or unclear invocation can create duplicate draft reviews for the same task cycle. Reviewer had to inspect task.review_ref, compare review records, and archive the extra draft manually before proceeding.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: process.env.KSPEC_SPEC_DIR is shared across vitest worker_threads, causing intermittent test failures when dispatch workspace tests run concurrently with tests that rely on initContext() cwd resolution (e.g. daemon-command-api). 15+ test files set this env var. The daemon command route was patched to save/clear it during execution, but the systemic pattern of mutating shared process.env in parallel tests remains a reliability risk. Consider migrating remaining KSPEC_SPEC_DIR test usages to kspec init shadow projects or switching the vitest pool to forks for process-level isolation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer flow friction: `kspec review check` and `kspec review verdict` hung during a detached review snapshot after adding checks/threads, forcing fallback to `kspec task needs-work` to complete the required state transition.
