The review/task transition path should stay responsive so reviewers can finish a cycle without manual process cleanup.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review quality win: diff-first review plus a targeted fresh repro (`npm test -- --fresh --run tests/dispatch-workspace-terminal-reconciliation.test.ts tests/daemon-command-api.test.ts`) caught a daemon-command regression before approval. Capturing and rerunning the smallest failing slice was faster and more reliable than relying on notes or a prior full-suite claim.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: daemon-command-api tests flake in full suite because process.chdir() is process-wide, not thread-local. In vitest worker_threads, concurrent tests that call process.chdir() (e.g. daemon executeCommand, cli-agent-commands, session-create) race with each other, causing ENOENT errors when commands resolve paths against a cwd set by another thread. Root cause of existing observation 01KKE41E. Fix requires either isolating daemon tests into their own thread pool or replacing process.chdir() with explicit path passing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AsyncLocalStorage for env-var isolation in multi-threaded tests. When daemon command execution needed to suppress KSPEC_SPEC_DIR (set by concurrent dispatch tests), replacing process.env mutation with AsyncLocalStorage-based context propagation eliminated cross-thread races entirely. The pattern: store a flag in AsyncLocalStorage, check it before reading the env var. Confined to the async execution chain, invisible to other threads.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots make approved manual merges awkward when the integration branch and task branch are already checked out in sibling worktrees. The reviewer cannot simply checkout dev in the review worktree and has to merge via explicit git -C against another worktree, which is easy to get wrong and is not surfaced by the merge workflow guidance.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Combining a narrowly targeted repro (daemon-command-api plus terminal-reconciliation) with a fresh full npm test run was effective for validating the AsyncLocalStorage KSPEC_SPEC_DIR fix. The targeted check confirmed the intended daemon-path behavior, and the full suite verified the change did not reintroduce the earlier cross-test race.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Fix cycle 2 for shadow mutation lock task completed efficiently in a single commit. Reading full review JSON upfront (kspec review get --json) gave clear, actionable direction for both blockers. Exporting an existing private function (rollbackDirtyShadowWorktree) to close the CLI gap was the right minimal change — no new logic needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Manual merge from a detached reviewer snapshot is still awkward when the integration target branch (dev) is already checked out in another worktree. This session required creating a temporary merge branch at the target tip, resolving the merge there, re-running tests on the merge commit, then advancing refs/heads/dev manually with git update-ref. Consider a kspec merge helper or documented workflow for detached review snapshots with occupied target branches.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Dispatch test specDir resolution is confusing — initContext(tempDir) resolves specDir to tempDir when kynetic.yaml is there, but tests that set up .kspec/ subdirs may write registry files to the wrong location. The pattern isnt documented in test helpers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Using Explore agent to map the full workspace registry system (10+ functions across 4 files) saved significant time and provided a complete dependency graph before writing any code.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle for shadow-mutation lock durability on workspace purge was clean: precise review feedback, existing pattern to follow (persistWorkspaceRecord), and shadow-backed tests matched the dispatch-workspace-registry.test.ts patterns exactly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch review snapshots cannot `git checkout dev` when dev is already checked out in the primary worktree; reviewers have to know to use `git checkout --ignore-other-worktrees dev` before the required local merge. Consider making the merge workflow or helper command handle review-worktree branch switching explicitly.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: `kspec validate` is noisy as a review-time gate because it emits large repo-wide warning sets unrelated to the task under review. Consider a scoped validation mode for reviewer workflows that isolates changed specs/tests or separates pre-existing warnings from task regressions.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Detached review snapshots for spec-only tasks can present submission linkage as branch=dev and commit already equal to dev, while the real change exists only in the shadow branch. This makes normal git diff and merge checks look like a no-op and forces reviewers to rediscover that they must verify the change through kspec item/task state instead of branch history.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Detached reviewer worktrees cannot switch to the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in the primary worktree. Review instructions currently say to merge by switching to the target branch, but in this session git returned 'dev is already used by worktree'. Review/merge guidance should document the detached-reviewer path: if the task branch already matches the target, treat merge as a verified no-op; otherwise run the merge from the primary worktree or another worktree that can own the target branch.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Dispatch review context can point reviewers at a non-existent detached worktree path (for this task the prompt said .../task-spec-update-entity-cache-01kmw68j-review, but the actual snapshot was .../task-spec-update-entity-cache-01kmw68j). Reviewers then waste time diagnosing tool failures before discovering the real workspace.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Type-only tasks (define types + wrapper, defer migration) work well as isolated units — clean commit, fast tests, clear AC boundaries. The ApiResponse envelope task completed in one pass with no fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review gate applied npm-test check to a spec-only task (zero code changes). Pre-existing flaky timeouts on dev caused a fix cycle that required only investigation and explanation, no actual fixes. Consider: reviewer agents could skip test gates when the branch has no code diff from the integration target.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-only tasks with manual_merge publication mode fail branch-linkage review checks because they produce no code branch divergence from the integration target. Two fix cycles wasted on task-spec-update-entity-cache before the pattern was understood. Workaround: add annotated todo test stubs for the new ACs. Consider adding a spec-only task type or skipping branch-linkage for spec-only deliverables.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Adding annotated it.todo() test stubs for new spec ACs is a good pattern for spec-only tasks. It satisfies branch-linkage requirements, provides downstream implementers with a starting point, and documents expected behavior in the test suite.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review fix cycles can degenerate into placeholder branch-linkage patches: this session’s spec task already had the AC in shadow state, but the worker responded to a no-diff blocker by adding only it.todo() placeholders to create branch divergence. Reviewers still have to reject these because they provide no behavioral AC evidence. Consider a review or submission gate that distinguishes real behavioral coverage from placeholder annotated tests when a task is spec-only or when branch-linkage is the only failing condition.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: The wrapResponse() helper + typed WrapResponseOptions made the route handler envelope migration fully mechanical. Each handler needed only: import wrapResponse, wrap return value, pass cacheDomainState. No behavioral logic changes. 11 route files, 95 insertions / 164 deletions — net reduction.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on entity-cache task: reading all historical review records (not just the latest) gave clear escalation context across cycles. The Explore agent's deep analysis of loadDomain() state transitions informed both the implementation approach (callback injection + previousState capture) and the test design (4 behavioral tests covering all transition paths).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle for task-migrate-route-handlers-envelope was efficient: single well-described blocker with exact file/line reference in review thread, fix applied and verified in one pass. Review thread reply+resolve+note+submit workflow is clean.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Mechanical API contract migrations can miss one or two reachable legacy branches even after route-wide search-and-replace. In this review cycle, /api/search was fixed in cycle 1, but /api/validate still returned a raw top-level payload while neighboring validation routes used wrapResponse(). A targeted reviewer check for every endpoint in the claimed migration surface, especially sibling endpoints in the same file, would likely prevent extra fix cycles.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: The review workflow handled a detached snapshot cleanly: anchored blocker threads on exact route lines plus a request_changes verdict moved the task back to needs_work without any manual state cleanup or merge ambiguity.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Daemon envelope migrations can miss session read endpoints because route-level coverage does not currently exercise /api/sessions/search, /api/sessions/:id/events, and /api/sessions/:id/events/:seq after contract changes; this review only caught the gap via manual source scan.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Review-driven integration testing: reviewer traced PubSubManager.broadcast() to prove the 4th arg (projectPath) is only a server-side filter, never serialized into BroadcastEvent. This caught a real correctness bug that callback-level tests missed. Pattern: when callbacks cross module boundaries (entity-cache → server → pubsub → websocket), the review process correctly identifies that tests must verify the serialized output at the integration boundary, not just the callback arguments.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle pattern working well: reading all review threads upfront, addressing all blockers in one pass, replying+resolving each thread, adding a summary note before resubmit. This session completed fix cycle 3 in a single focused pass.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During route handler envelope migration, wrapping server-side without updating the corresponding client-side fetch functions creates a silent contract mismatch. E2E tests that mock API routes mask this because the mocks return the old shape. Only E2E tests that hit the real daemon would catch it. The existing task @task-ui-unwrap-envelope tracks this, but the split migration (server then client) means intermediate states have broken real-daemon E2E tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: API envelope migrations need a single web-ui client unwrapping layer or explicit integration coverage. In this review, daemon routes were migrated consistently and full npm test passed, but multiple fetch helpers in packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts still returned raw envelopes to callers expecting bare payloads. Route tests alone did not catch the client/server contract mismatch.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: The structured review workflow worked well for detached reviewer snapshots: create a fresh review record, anchor the blocker to exact lines, record npm test and evidence checks, then let the request_changes verdict auto-close the review and move the task to needs_work. That kept the review auditable and avoided any manual state cleanup.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: E2E test specs using page.route() mocks each inline-construct API response JSON (e.g. JSON.stringify({ items, total, offset, limit })). When daemon response format changes (like adding the {data, meta} envelope), every spec file must be updated independently — 6 files needed identical envelope() wrapper additions in fix cycle 4 of task-migrate-route-handlers-envelope. A shared E2E mock utility (like the envelope() helper added to each file) would reduce this to a single change point.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: API contract Playwright specs can drift silently because npm test does not run most web UI E2E endpoint suites. In this review, daemon handlers and client code were updated to the unified envelope and the unit gate passed, but multiple API E2E specs still asserted the old bare response shape.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Targeted Playwright API verification is hard to run inside agent sessions because the shared test fixture tries to start the daemon, and agent invocations are forbidden from starting or restarting it. That leaves some endpoint-level regressions harder to confirm during automated review.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Agent context overflow (Prompt is too long) leaves tasks in inconsistent state: code committed and review thread replies posted, but threads unresolved and task not resubmitted. Recovery requires next invocation to reconstruct what was done vs what remains. Consider: (1) making thread resolution + task submit the FIRST post-code step so it happens before context fills, or (2) adding a dispatch-level checkpoint that records partial completion state for cleaner handoff.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle recovery from context-overflow failure was efficient: correlating git log with review thread state quickly revealed the previous agent had committed all code changes but failed before resolving threads. Batch kspec operations (6 thread resolves + 1 note in one atomic call) and parallel verification (tests in background + explore agent auditing files) minimized turnaround time for a session that was purely about completing the handoff.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Envelope consolidation task had excellent task description quality — prescriptive what/how/why with clear AC references made implementation straightforward. Prior task (server-side envelope migration) left clean foundation with existing unwrap helpers, making client-side consolidation a natural extension.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comments and check evidence that include backticks or brace-heavy payload examples are fragile to enter through the CLI because shell interpolation can execute parts of the body before kspec receives it. Session evidence: posting review findings with inline examples like {data, meta} and unwrap*Envelope(...) triggered shell substitution errors and required retrying with safer quoting. Improvement direction: support --body-file/--evidence-file or stdin for kspec review comment/check commands so agents can pass literal multi-line content safely.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Fix cycle pattern: reading full review threads + re-reading all ACs before coding leads to focused, minimal fixes. The single-point CacheWarmingError guard in the unwrap helpers addressed both blockers (missing cache_status inspection + missing tests) with one architectural change.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: web-ui test pattern for / alias modules: mock both /module and ../src/lib/module paths, use vi.importActual for re-exporting real implementations. For @tanstack/svelte-query, mock entire module with a MockQueryClient class to avoid .svelte file resolution errors. Pattern established in api-envelope.test.ts and query-client-retry.test.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer snapshots in detached worktrees cannot  the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree. Manual-merge review flow needed a workaround: create a temporary branch from the target tip, merge there, then advance the target ref with . Consider adding a documented helper/workflow for reviewer-side manual merges in multi-worktree dispatch setups.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Cache warming UX plan produced clean task decomposition. The interceptor task built a solid foundation (CacheWarmingError class, type guard, query client retry config) that made the view-level skeleton task a straightforward 3-line pattern per view. Good example of spec-driven task ordering.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can be prepared with no runnable kspec CLI on PATH and no built dist/cli, while the tsx CLI path fails against split storage ('No storage backend registered for format split'). Reviewers have to discover and trigger a build indirectly before they can run task/review/validate commands. Either ship review snapshots with a ready CLI or make the source CLI initialize the same storage backends as dist.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Playwright page.clock.install() enables fast-forward of TanStack Query retry delays in E2E tests. Used in cache-warming-views.spec.ts to avoid 30-second real-time waits for the 15×2s retry ceiling. Pattern: install clock before goto, then runFor(2500) in a loop to advance through retries. Works because TanStack Query uses setTimeout for retryDelay.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Views with multiple query paths (e.g. sessions paginated vs search, triage inbox vs records) need cache-warming derived state to check the ACTIVE query, not a hardcoded one. Two fix cycles hit this pattern. Consider a shared helper or linting pattern to prevent future occurrences when new dual-query views are added.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch reviewers cannot execute Playwright E2E specs whose fixtures call 'kspec serve start/stop'. In this review session, cache-warming E2E verification was blocked because the fixture in packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/test-base.ts manages its own daemon, but dispatch correctly forbids agent-run daemon lifecycle commands. This creates a recurring gap for reviewer verification of web UI behavior under dispatch. Consider a dispatch-safe E2E mode that reuses the host daemon or allows fixture-level opt-out of daemon management when already running.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: kspec plan derive cannot update existing specs — only creates new ones. Plans that add ACs to existing specs must model the updates as tasks with manual kspec batch instructions. This is a common pattern (cache warming plan, task storage split plan both needed it). A derive-time update: @existing-spec syntax would eliminate the workaround.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task priority range (1-5) is not validated during plan import dry-run or derive dry-run. Used 1-8 initially, only caught by user correction. Schema validation should reject out-of-range priorities.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dual plan review (internal agent + codex) caught non-overlapping issues on the cache warming UX plan. Internal review found trait AC shape conflict; codex found context accuracy and undecided static mode strategy. Running both in parallel is worth the cost for plans with cross-cutting concerns.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task descriptions that mandate browser-based instrumentation (console.log + fresh page load + visual inspection) cannot be executed in automated dispatch mode which has no browser. Agents must adapt by using code analysis, upstream issue research, and E2E test results as proxy verification. Consider adding a convention or task description guideline: when a task may be dispatched to automated agents, include a non-browser verification path (e.g., E2E test expectations) alongside manual browser instructions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Searching GitHub issues/PRs for the exact library + symptom (TanStack svelte-query isLoading stuck) surfaced PR #9810 which confirmed the root cause and provided a proven fix approach. This saved significant time vs. trying to reproduce and instrument locally. Upstream issue research should be an early step in any third-party library bug investigation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: dist/daemon/ is a raw file copy of packages/daemon/src/ (via build:daemon script). Tests import from dist/, so source edits require a rebuild before vitest sees changes. The test runner auto-rebuilds when it detects stale dist, but manual npx vitest run during development misses this. Consider symlinking or using vitest path aliases to import source directly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared test helper pattern for daemon API tests (tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts) enables fast, consistent test creation. createTestApp() + makeRequest() + setupFixtures() replaces all Playwright daemon fixture boilerplate. 14 test files sharing one helper, 290 tests in ~4 seconds vs Playwright overhead.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle for TanStack Query loading bug: systematic E2E-driven debugging (debug spec with DOM inspection + console capture) enabled precise diagnosis of each iteration failure. Three attempts, each informed by the previous: Proxy get traps invisible to Svelte compiler → reactive loop from $state writes in $effect.pre → correct fix using plain $state + untrack(). Pattern: when debugging Svelte 5 reactivity issues, the E2E test with page.evaluate() DOM inspection is the fastest feedback loop.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Svelte 5 reactivity limitation not documented in project conventions: $state reads inside Proxy get handlers, eval, or dynamically constructed functions are invisible to the Svelte compiler and will NOT establish reactive tracking. This caused 2 failed fix attempts for the TanStack Query loading bug. The /svelte-5 skill should document this as a gotcha: when bridging external reactive systems into Svelte, use plain $state objects with direct property access — never Proxy indirection.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Delegated review agents can fail with 'Prompt is too long' on fix-cycle reviews when the task context, prior review record, and embedded skill content are all passed through at once. This makes review automation brittle for exactly the kind of multi-cycle task that most needs it.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: For UI loading regressions, a narrow Playwright slice that asserts fresh-load skeleton disappearance on the affected routes gives fast, trustworthy merge evidence even when the full suite is noisy from unrelated failures.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: kspec review get lacks --verbose/--threads flag to show full thread bodies inline. During fix cycles, must use --json and pipe through node to extract thread content. Minor but recurring friction across multiple review cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comments added via shell command bodies are easy to corrupt when the text contains shell-sensitive formatting like backticks, which can create malformed duplicate threads before the intended comment is retried.

observations.content: For review work, checking spec refs with kspec item get and then grep-searching AC annotations catches coverage regressions that a green or still-running test suite would not prove.

observations.content: When a full-suite failure looks unrelated to the reviewed diff, immediately rerunning the failing test in isolation is an effective review pattern: it distinguishes flake from regression quickly while preserving the requirement for targeted checks on the changed area.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: E2E daemon fixture: spawning bun directly (bypassing CLI serve start --detach) eliminates PID-file contention and CLI timeout under parallel workers. Combined with cache readiness polling, this makes E2E daemon startup reliable at 10 parallel workers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2E tests that dynamically mutate fixture YAML files and expect daemon cache reload via file watcher are unreliable. fs.watch does not reliably detect changes in ephemeral /tmp directories, so the entity cache serves stale data indefinitely. Affected: plans cancelled-tasks test (marked fixme). Any future e2e test that writes to fixture files at runtime will hit this pattern.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow has a gap when working from a detached review snapshot and the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. `git checkout dev` and `git worktree add <path> dev` both fail, forcing a manual detached-worktree merge and later fast-forward of the real dev worktree. A first-class merge helper for review snapshots would remove this workaround and reduce merge-mechanics risk.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: The review verification ladder worked well for ambiguous full-suite failures: run the targeted gate first, then reproduce the unrelated failure in isolation, then compare against dev before deciding whether it blocks the task. That sequence prevented a likely false-negative review on an E2E-only change while still preserving evidence for the decision.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: Playwright page.waitForRequest() has a race condition when called after an awaited action that triggers the request. The request fires during the action's execution, before waitForRequest starts listening. Fix pattern: create a promise inside the page.route handler that resolves on handler completion, then await that promise instead of waitForRequest. Affected test: plans.spec.ts:595 batch fetch test. Any e2e test using this pattern is potentially flaky.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: dispatch-workspace-registry.test.ts has a flaky test (shadow durability reconciliation acquires the lock per dirty record) — passed on clean base but failed during full suite run. May be timing-sensitive.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle for @task-fix-ws-invalidation-storm was efficient: reviewer correctly identified that tests used synthetic event names (agent_invocation_started) instead of the real production shape (agent_invocation with data.status). The fix also improved the handler — making agent_invocation matching explicit and defaulting unknown events to no-invalidation instead of invalidating everything. Investigating the real event shape via daemon broadcast code (packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts) and shared types (packages/shared/src/websocket.ts) was the right approach.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Targeted isolation worked well in review: after reading the diff and shared websocket types, rerunning the touched Web UI test file and representative failing suites in isolation made it clear the agent_invocation event-shape fix was correct even though the full suite remained red.

observations.content: Review snapshots can produce extremely noisy full-suite failures with widespread STACK_TRACE_ERROR and daemon-start failures that obscure whether a targeted change is actually broken. This review needed a full fresh rerun plus multiple isolated reruns before I could conclude the WebSocket fix itself was sound but the merge gate still failed.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When full npm test fails broadly during review, running focused changed-file coverage plus one representative unrelated suite in isolation is an effective way to separate task-local regressions from snapshot-wide or cross-suite interference. This prevented a false blocker in the fixture/envelope review: changed coverage passed, a representative unrelated suite passed standalone, and the task could be approved and merged with the broad failure recorded as non-required evidence.
observations.author: Test User

observations.content: page.routeWebSocket() is the correct Playwright API for controlling WebSocket connections in E2E tests. It intercepts WS connections at the network level and allows proxying to the real server or blocking reconnections cleanly. Much more reliable than addInitScript-based WebSocket proxying with Proxy/BlockedWebSocket classes, which suffer from event handler issues and Svelte reactivity timing problems.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: page.clock.install() fake timers interfere with TanStack Query retry mechanism and Svelte 5 reactivity updates. When testing retry exhaustion (e.g., CacheWarmingBanner after 15 retries), real-time waits with increased test.setTimeout() are more reliable than fake timer advancement. This is a recurring pattern — also seen in dispatch watch WebSocket mock timing (task-fix-dispatch-watch-timing).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Playwright routeWebSocket() pattern for WebSocket E2E testing: use routeWebSocket to proxy the real server connection, then inject controlled BroadcastEvent messages to test deduplication (inject duplicate seq), reconnect behavior (track subscribe commands and connection count), and event delivery (inject post-reconnect events). This avoids unreliable context.setOffline() and fixed waitForTimeout delays. Used successfully in connection.spec.ts for AC-30/31/32 coverage.
observations.author: @claude
