observations.content: Running a focused Playwright spec before the full npm test gate caught stale test assumptions quickly and kept the fix cycle tight. The targeted rerun surfaced missing page navigation and required-form-input assumptions before the expensive full suite.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Scoped review worked well here: reading the branch delta first, using merge-tree for mergeability, and running focused Playwright coverage on the touched triage export flow made it possible to approve confidently even though npm test surfaced unrelated failures in unchanged files. That combination gave enough evidence to separate task-scoped quality from pre-existing suite noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer manual_merge friction: detached review snapshots cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree, so the reviewer has to discover and use git -C against the canonical worktree. The merge workflow should expose an explicit command or dispatch-safe helper for merging from review snapshots without this manual workaround.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of older detached-review manual_merge tracking @01KMGXRB. The underlying workflow gap is still open: reviewer merge guidance still assumes checking out the integration branch inside the detached review snapshot.

observations.content: Task-review linkage semantics are unclear across the web UI, daemon review filter, and E2E fixtures: the task detail reviews section fetches /api/reviews?task=<task ULID> but the current dev fixture/backend behavior links pending-review reviews by task slug/review_ref semantics, which leaves review rows empty and makes selector-only repair tasks look incomplete.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review snapshots can accumulate unrelated commits from upstream task-branch merges, making a selector-only review fail on scope rather than behavior. We need a lightweight way to verify/crop dispatch task branches to task-attributable files or commits before resubmission.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: E2E daemon fixtures were brittle across dispatch worktrees because the harness pointed WEB_UI_DIR at packages/web-ui/build instead of the built dist/web-ui bundle. That let a stale absolute path from another worktree break board-page tests with ENOENT even though the current workspace had a valid build.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Checking git diff origin/dev...HEAD against the current tree before accepting a scope-drift review blocker prevented another wrong fix cycle. It quickly separated superseded branch history from the real submission snapshot and narrowed the remaining work to the actual failing selectors/tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review friction: selector-focused changes can validate cleanly while the required full npm test gate remains red from unrelated dispatch-suite failures. In this session, targeted E2E reruns passed but fresh full-suite reruns still failed in dispatch-workspace-registry, forcing a request_changes verdict without a task-scoped regression. This makes review disposition depend on repo-wide flakiness instead of changed-scope evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In a fix cycle, re-running the previously failing required gate on the exact reviewed head before editing code can expose stale request_changes verdicts and avoid unnecessary churn. This session's full npm test gate flipped from failing to 2082/2082 passing on the same selector-task snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review friction: required 'npm test -- --fresh' gate can fail with broad dispatch/daemon STACK_TRACE_ERROR and assertion failures unrelated to the reviewed task diff, forcing long review cycles with low signal. Session example: stale-selector review spent several minutes waiting for the required gate only to fail in unrelated suites after selector-focused checks were green. Consider a way to distinguish task-scoped verification from known repo-wide gate instability, or at minimum surface whether the same failing suites are already known/open so reviewers do not have to rediscover them each cycle.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-scoped UI/E2E fix cycles are getting blocked by the required full-suite gate even when the remaining red state is a single unrelated dispatch-workspace-registry timeout. This task's selector-focused bundle is green, but submit is still blocked on tests/dispatch-workspace-registry.test.ts 'reconciliation acquires the lock per dirty record, not once for the entire batch' (fresh log /tmp/kspec-test-cache/01KN2KXMRN1G4VQC487YAF725K/736a0c514b7215bc.log).
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing gate-friction observation @01KN2KWD; this session added fresher evidence (single remaining dispatch-workspace-registry timeout) but does not represent a new systemic pattern.

observations.content: Detached review worktrees cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree. In this session the approved merge could not run as git checkout dev inside the review worktree because dev was already checked out in the main repo worktree, so the merge had to be executed indirectly with git -C <main-worktree> merge .... This is a repeatable dispatch-review workflow gap; merge tooling should handle integration-branch worktree collisions explicitly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When the dispatch prompt's recorded integration base is older than current origin/dev, recomputing the diff against current origin/dev quickly separates the task's real delta from upstream noise. In this review it reduced the apparent scope from a 43-file recorded-base diff to the actual 13-file task delta, which made the approval decision much more reliable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Verifying the live UI consumer path with targeted code search before writing Playwright coverage avoided adding tests to stale task assumptions; this task description named tasks/items, but the active POST /api/items/batch consumer was plans embedded content.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task descriptions for UI test gaps can drift after refactors: this batch-fetch task still pointed at tasks/items flows after the real batch consumer moved to plans embedded content, which required extra investigation before implementation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When dispatch/workspace integration tests pass in isolation but fail in the full gate, moving the git/shadow/bootstrap-heavy files into a dedicated serial Vitest project can stabilize npm test without weakening coverage or globally raising timeouts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon agent-dispatch test fixtures can silently exercise removed task-storage paths unless they both declare split task storage and register the split backend, which turns one fixture drift into a broad dispatch/bootstrap failure cluster during full-suite runs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Concurrent verification runs can churn dist/web-ui and cause misleading Playwright failures from tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts ("Web UI not built") even after build:e2e succeeded. Consider isolating or locking the shared E2E web-ui artifact.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review/fix-cycle flow worked well here: blocking mocked /api/items/batch coverage forced the test to wait on the real request/response path, which produced stronger evidence before merge.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm run test:e2e:full leaves the Playwright HTML report server running after test completion, which makes local gate validation look hung until the process is interrupted manually.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm test can hang after the vitest suite has already produced passing output, which forced manual process termination during review-detail E2E verification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Covered by @task-investigate-npm-test-teardown-hang-after-green-suite-run; observed again while verifying review-detail fixes.

observations.content: Focused e2e reproduction is obscured because npm run test:e2e -- <spec> still pulls in smoke/api-server specs. Direct npx playwright test is required to isolate a single failing UI spec.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Adversarial verification worked well in this review: reading the diff first, checking the daemon route behavior, and then rerunning the same E2E command multiple times prevented a false approval based on a worker note that claimed the slice was fixed. The repeat-run check found a 1-in-3 flake and correctly sent the task back to needs_work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For CI-flake fix tasks, a single passing rerun is not strong enough evidence. In this review, one combined Playwright run failed, two later reruns passed, and only repeating the exact command three times exposed the residual flake in tests/e2e/reviews-detail.spec.ts. Review and task workflows should explicitly require multi-run stability checks when the goal is to unblock a flaky gate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For CI-oriented Playwright failures, reproducing only the named failing cases first made root-cause isolation much faster: it separated one real app bug (static-mode session detail) from adjacent test drift before widening scope.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Sessions E2E stabilization still requires expensive build-and-rerun cycles before neighboring out-of-scope failures become visible. Focused cases passed quickly, but discovering adjacent infinite-scroll/live-update failures required a much slower widened rerun.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm test can enter a non-reporting hang after scripts/test.cjs starts, which makes full-suite verification inconclusive even when targeted suites pass. This session hit the same stall twice and had to rely on narrower evidence instead of a definitive full run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For flaky Playwright slices, running a single spec with --grep plus --repeat-each and then reading Playwright error-context snapshots isolated the real failure mode much faster than rerunning the whole bundle. That pattern turned an intermittent review-detail flake into a reproducible actionability issue and gave a clean verification loop once fixed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Playwright fullyParallel can still destabilize daemon-backed E2E specs that boot an isolated daemon/web-ui fixture per test. In this session, tests/e2e/review-interaction.spec.ts passed with --workers=1 but flaked under the project command until the file was serialized; the failure mode was visible controls that never became click-stable, which looked like an app bug until worker-count isolation proved it was fixture contention.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-gate verification for review-interaction E2E was inconsistent across commands: worker notes reported 'npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/review-interaction.spec.ts' passing, while reviewer reruns and the required npm test gate still produced contradictory failures. We should make the canonical gate command and its argument-forwarding semantics harder to misread so task notes and reviews cite comparable evidence.
observations.author: agent:codex

observations.content: Focused reproduction can give a false sense of completion for fix-cycle work: this session's original sessions failures were fixed, but the task still could not clear review until a full non-cached npm test run exposed unrelated full-gate flakes in dispatch and websocket tests. The practical lesson is that required-gate reruns need to happen before resubmission, not after review records are created.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Using the shared waitForStartup polling helper to replace ad hoc 1s spin loops made the post-invocation dispatch assertions hold under full-suite load. Reusing an existing bounded readiness helper was a better stabilization pattern than inflating arbitrary sleep counts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Rebasing a needs_work dispatch branch onto the current integration target before chasing reviewer-reported gate failures made it easy to distinguish stale blockers from real regressions by re-running the focused failing subset first.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A review can stay anchored to an examined commit whose blocker failures no longer reproduce after the task branch is rebased onto a newer integration target, creating avoidable fix-cycle churn for dispatch tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review verification can report a clean rerun while the detached review snapshot still fails because the daemon serves a stale WEB_UI_DIR/index.html from a deleted worktree path. Reflection from review of @01KN3Q09YEKYDQ8JCP1RDNGAF1: focused Playwright rerun still hit ENOENT on .kspec-worktrees/.../dist/web-ui/index.html after a note claimed the path-hardening fix was complete.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused reruns plus immediate artifact inspection worked well in review. Re-running the exact Playwright subset and opening the failure screenshot exposed the stale deleted-worktree bundle path quickly, which made the blocker concrete and anchorable instead of speculative.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For isolated E2E CI blockers, reproducing only the named failing cases first and then rerunning the whole affected spec after each fix closed the issue quickly without guessing across unrelated failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Sessions live-update Playwright coverage is brittle when tests rely on real layout scrolling to enter the 'scrolled down' branch; in headless runs the scroll container may not move even with many rows, so tests need deterministic branch forcing or a dedicated helper for synthetic scroll state.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Keeping one real daemon-backed end-to-end assertion in a mostly deterministic E2E test exposed a genuine sessions live-refresh race that synthetic browser MessageEvents had masked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Repo-wide npm test failures in unrelated suites make task-level verification noisy; targeted work can be green while the required full-suite gate still reports unrelated red.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused single-spec Playwright reproduction quickly separated stale test assumptions from real watcher regressions. Reproducing only the failing api-watcher cases before editing made it obvious that one failure was a current-contract mismatch (/api/tasks envelope + tasks:updates topic) and the other was a fixture-path/listener-order race.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: E2E tests can drift from daemon fixture and API contracts because response-shape/topic assumptions and fixture path fields are duplicated inline in specs. In this session api-watcher still expected tasksBody.items, files:updates for a task-note mutation, and daemon.projectDir even though the live contracts had moved to {data,meta}, tasks:updates, and daemon.tempDir.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Meta/schema drift can silently drop observation fields: this session found tests/e2e fixtures and the web UI both using observation context, but ObservationSchema omitted the field so daemon responses lost it until an E2E failure exposed the mismatch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused Playwright debugging still has to pay the full npm run build:e2e cost because the supported e2e entrypoint always rebuilds before running a narrow spec. For retrying one loading-state case, most session time was spent rebuilding rather than reproducing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Inspecting Playwright error-context snapshots before changing code cleanly distinguished a test race from a real /workflows loading bug. The failing snapshot already showed rendered workflow cards, which prevented an unnecessary app-code fix.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots cannot perform the final manual merge in their assigned workspace when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this review cycle, git checkout dev failed with: 'dev is already used by worktree at /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch', so the approved merge had to be executed against the primary worktree path instead of the review workspace. This adds reviewer friction and weakens the 'run all commands from the assigned workspace' contract.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused Playwright reruns with --grep plus --repeat-each quickly separated a real browser-history race from non-repro full-gate flakes, which kept the fix scoped and prevented churn in unrelated E2E cases.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-level verification is noisy when npm test has an unrelated failing baseline; workers can stabilize and verify their target scope but still cannot produce a clean full-suite signal at session end.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During autonomous review/merge flows, sub-agents used for verification can overstep their requested scope and perform final lifecycle actions (approve, merge, complete task) instead of only reporting results. This creates recovery work and weakens reviewer control. Consider a stricter awaiter/worker boundary or safer prompts/tooling for verification-only sub-agents in dispatch review mode.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For scoped E2E stabilization reviews, recording one required targeted-regression check plus an optional full-suite check let the review merge confidently while still documenting unrelated baseline failures. This kept the gate focused on the changed surfaces without hiding broader repo instability.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For CI gate changes, rebasing onto the integration branch and rerunning the full suite in CI mode before editing workflow files prevented acting on stale local failures and made it clear that sharding was needed instead of a direct single-job swap.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-scoped verification on a rebased head can still be noisy when npm test is red in unrelated suites outside the change surface, making it harder to distinguish real regressions from pre-existing failures after targeted checks are already green.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer prompts can carry a stale integration-base/head snapshot, which makes the initial diff appear much larger than the real merge delta until the reviewer re-derives it from origin/<target>...HEAD.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: CI workflow path filters can silently weaken a test gate when config files are omitted. In this session, the full Playwright gate was correctly sharded and green, but playwright.config.ts was missing from pull_request.paths, so config-only PRs could bypass the E2E workflow entirely.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review threads kept the fix cycle tight: the blocker pointed to .github/workflows/test.yml with a precise path-filter gap, which made the follow-up a single-line workflow fix plus explicit thread resolution instead of a broad re-review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow in detached review snapshots is underspecified when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. This session required creating a temporary merge branch/worktree, merging there, then fast-forwarding the main dev worktree because direct 'git checkout dev' failed with: 'dev is already used by worktree'.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing observation @01KN0JCT; this session reproduced the same detached-review merge friction with the concrete failure 'dev is already used by worktree'.

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot check out the integration branch for manual merge when that branch is already active in another worktree. This session hit git's 'already used by worktree' failure and had to merge into the primary worktree with git -C. Dispatch review instructions should either direct reviewers to merge in the canonical worktree explicitly or provide a merge helper that handles worktree-aware target selection.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: The review workflow made the blocker easy to verify and record: deterministic checks plus a targeted executable reproduction against the current route code let the review distinguish a real regression from a speculative concern, while review records tied the finding, evidence log, and verdict directly to the task.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-record CLI payloads are fragile when passed as multiline shell strings. During this review, a kspec review comment command with special characters and backticks was mangled by shell interpolation and created a malformed duplicate blocker thread before cleanup. Prefer a file-based body option or another quoting-safe path for review comments/check evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test emits opaque STACK_TRACE_ERROR failures for unrelated suites and a reproducible pre-existing workflow CLI import mismatch (dist/cli/commands/plan.js -> plan-import export). This made task-local verification harder to separate from unrelated regressions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm run build currently fails in build:daemon with shx cp reporting EISDIR for dist/daemon/ while the test runner still repairs daemon build artifacts successfully.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Resolved by @01KNE1NJVFTB0TMEYXRVQDFH3M: build:daemon now compiles dist/daemon JavaScript via scripts/build-daemon.cjs instead of shx cp staging.

observations.content: During review, npm test reused cached full-suite failures and its condensed summary did not match the fresh-suite result, so I had to force npm test -- --fresh and inspect isolated reruns to determine whether the red gate was a real regression in the submitted diff. This makes review gating slower and less trustworthy when the suite outcome depends on build state or flaky unrelated failures.
observations.author: codex@openai.com

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can become stale mid-review when another actor approves, merges, or completes the task before the reviewer finishes. In this session the snapshot at f9baca482 remained under review while the linked review was approved, the task was marked completed, and dev already contained merge commit a836bb9ef. This creates wasted verification work and risks duplicate merge/task-complete actions. Consider a reviewer-facing stale-state guard or workflow step that rechecks task/review/git merge state before merge/completion actions in detached review workspaces.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a concurrency flake is hard to reproduce through the full runner, a minimal direct repro against the built artifact can isolate the lock semantics quickly before spending another hour on a fresh full-suite run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Lock tests that model an "alive other process" by writing the current process PID create the wrong semantics once same-process locking behavior matters. Those fixtures should use a real child PID to avoid masking or misclassifying concurrency bugs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot git checkout the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in the main worktree, so merge-capable review automation has to fall back to git -C against another worktree. This is systemic friction in the manual_merge review flow; detached review workspaces need a first-class merge handoff or merge command that targets the canonical worktree without ad hoc git plumbing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full-suite verification can be blocked by unrelated reproducible regressions with no obvious existing tracker. In this session npm test failed in tests/daemon-entity-cache.test.ts ('session live event counters should hand off from live counters to persisted metadata after reload'), forcing manual isolation before task submission.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer merge friction: in detached review snapshots, the documented local merge flow can fail because git cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already owned by another worktree (observed: switching to dev failed with "already used by worktree"). Review/merge guidance should document the supported path for completing an approved manual merge from a reviewer snapshot without escaping into ad hoc git -C workarounds.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review regression triage worked well: rerunning the failing test on both the review snapshot and the integration base branch prevented a false blocker, allowed the plan-branch task to merge cleanly, and produced a separate bug task for the pre-existing daemon cache failure.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test -- --fresh still has an unrelated failure in tests/cli-serve.test.ts (SIGTERM shutdown assertion) while working the daemon entity cache live-counter regression, so the repo-wide verification gate is not currently reliable for isolated daemon cache fixes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot directly check out or add the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this review, 'git checkout dev' and 'git worktree add ... dev' both failed, and the merge had to be executed against the existing /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch dev worktree with git -C. Consider first-class merge workflow support for detached review snapshots so approved manual_merge tasks do not require cross-worktree git commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For review triage, re-running the suspect failing test on a sibling worktree at the integration-target commit cleanly separated pre-existing test debt from branch regressions. That pattern let the review keep a precise blocker on the submitted change while opening a separate follow-up task for the unrelated daemon cache failure.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review CLI follow-up commands are still shell-fragile when comment bodies or check evidence contain backticks, semicolons, or multi-line content. In this session an inline  command accidentally triggered shell substitution and had to be retried with heredoc-safe payload construction. Consider adding first-class  /  options (or stdin support) for review comments/checks to reduce quoting mistakes during automated review work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Re-running a failing test on a sibling worktree pinned to the integration-target commit is an effective review pattern for separating pre-existing suite debt from regressions introduced by the submitted branch. It kept this review focused on the real blocker while still creating a follow-up task for the unrelated daemon cache failure.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Bug task @01KN664X was created from a stale reproduction snapshot after the live-counter fix had already merged to dev. Re-ran npm test -- tests/daemon-entity-cache.test.ts --fresh on dev 03bf2acf6537 and it passed; triage should confirm against current integration head before creating reinvestigation tasks for transient test failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test produced unrelated failures and STACK_TRACE_ERROR teardown noise while task-specific suites passed in isolation; representative reruns for agent-dispatch-engine and cli-serve were green. Investigate full-suite isolation or teardown interference in the test runner.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test can fail with unrelated timeout-heavy suites, forcing manual log inspection to verify whether the task’s own coverage actually passed. A summarized distinction between changed-file suites and unrelated failing suites would reduce reflection and review overhead.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewers can avoid false blockers by separating task-local verification from repo-wide test instability: targeted fresh runs for changed-area suites passed, the reviewed task merged, and the unrelated shard failures were captured as follow-up task @01KN69W9VECFXR84BR9FMTG4B1 instead of blocking the change.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer manual_merge flow is brittle in multi-worktree dispatch sessions. Attempting to checkout dev from the review worktree failed because dev was already checked out in the primary worktree, and git merge --no-ff then stalled for an editor because the merge path is not fully non-interactive. The merge workflow should provide a deterministic non-interactive path when the integration branch is already attached elsewhere.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test produced timeouts in tests/daemon-api/meta.test.ts while the same file passed immediately in isolation. This makes task verification noisy and suggests suite-order or shared-state instability in daemon API validation tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shared CLI test helpers should isolate HOME and strip ambient agent-detection env by default; doing that stabilized full-suite-only setup and dispatch flakes without product-code changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review recording is fragile when kspec review comment --body contains shell-sensitive text like backticks or multiline evidence. This session hit quoting breakage while adding blocker threads, which required retrying with simpler payloads. Consider a --body-file option or a documented stdin/file pattern for review comment/reply commands so agents can attach exact evidence without shell interpolation risk.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch workspaces can have a stale external kspec binary path and skill render may report kspec-plan as in-sync even when the rendered file text is outdated, forcing local-runner/manual verification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel npm test invocations can race in scripts/test.cjs build self-healing and fail before tests start (observed rm ENOENT on dist/daemon/index.ts when two --fresh runs started together). A build lock or serialized readiness fix would make multi-agent verification safer.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Fixed by per-worktree build/test lock (scripts/build-test-lock.cjs): scripts/test.cjs holds the lock for the whole run (readiness fixes + vitest), so parallel npm test invocations serialize instead of racing the build self-heal. Task @task-stabilize-upgrade-folder-storage-test.

observations.content: kspec validate is currently blocked by unrelated schema errors in .kspec/kynetic.meta.yaml (session.idle hooks with unsupported action types), which prevents task-level validation from cleanly distinguishing repo-wide failures from branch regressions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review threads made this fix cycle efficient: the exact file/line anchor plus explicit human-vs-JSON parity claim pointed directly to the missing structured field and the tests needed to lock it in.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fresh full-suite verification no longer fails in daemon-api/meta or dispatch-runtime-bootstrap after disabling watcher startup in daemon API app.handle() tests, but it still exposes broader unrelated serve/setup/dispatch timeout clusters. Separating targeted residual-flake fixes from broader suite-health debt is currently manual and expensive.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running multiple npm test invocations concurrently in one worktree can race on packages/web-ui build output and fail with ENOENT copyfile errors during vite build.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Moving real git/worktree/shadow I/O suites into the serial dispatch-heavy Vitest project is an effective way to stabilize dispatch timeouts without loosening global test timeouts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch review metadata can point at a detached reviewer worktree path that no longer exists even though the reviewed snapshot commit is still present in the task worktree. That forces the reviewer to rediscover the actual reviewable worktree via git worktree inspection before any review steps can begin.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For daemon API app.handle() integration tests, disabling unused project watcher startup in the shared helper and adding one focused behavioral regression test removed a full-suite timeout cluster without widening production behavior. The fix held under both targeted fresh suites and a fresh full npm test run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch review prompts can reference a nonexistent reviewer snapshot path while the actual usable worktree lives at a different .kspec-worktrees path. This forced manual path discovery before any review commands could run. Dispatch should either emit the canonical existing worktree path or validate and repair the prompt metadata before handing off the reviewer role.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review friction: inherited trait AC coverage can remain incomplete even when task-specific implementation and full test runs pass. In this session, @dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract inherited @trait-error-guidance, but tests/dispatch-runtime-bootstrap-contract.test.ts only annotated ac-1 and ac-2, leaving ac-3..ac-6 unaddressed. Consider a reviewer-facing check or focused coverage command that reports missing/N-A inherited AC annotations for the current spec under review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running the focused regression suite before the full test suite caught a schedule-engine test timing issue cheaply and kept the final full run as confirmation instead of discovery.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Long full-suite test runs have weak progress visibility; distinguishing normal progress from a hang required manual log tailing and process polling during dispatch work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already mounted in another worktree; review/merge guidance should document the supported manual-merge path for this case (for example using git -C on the primary worktree or an equivalent kspec helper).
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch workspace setup reported plan branch plan/plan-daemon-file-monitoring-reliability/01kn7nw3 as missing, but git fetch immediately resolved origin/plan/plan-daemon-file-monitoring-reliability/01kn7nw3. Branch availability checks appear to rely on stale refs and can create false blocker context during task startup.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test did not terminate cleanly after watcher changes verification; multiple vitest worker processes remained resident with no result JSON written, matching the existing teardown-hang investigation task.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review threads on specific acceptance criteria made this fix cycle fast and precise: the blocker pointed directly at @multi-directory-daemon ac-19, so the worker could narrow the spec to restore test/spec alignment without re-litigating the whole feature.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can hide shadow-branch-only task changes. In this session, git diff against the integration branch showed no code delta while the actual reviewed change lived in kspec-meta, forcing manual inspection of the .kspec worktree and shadow git history to find the real spec diff. Review tooling should surface linked shadow-branch mutations directly for spec-only tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For concurrency regressions, replacing a timing-sensitive final-state assertion with direct critical-section exclusion checks and negative warning assertions made the test stable without weakening behavior coverage.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel npm test invocations can race in the shared build output and fail with cp copyFileSync EISDIR under dist/daemon; dispatch agents should avoid concurrent build-triggering test runs in one workspace.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix-cycle reviews that include the exact failing suite and symptom make recovery fast: I reproduced the daemon command JSON regression directly, expanded the fix from KspecWatcher to SessionWatcher when the same parity test exposed the second stdout leak, then validated with the targeted parity suite before the broader watcher regression suite.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree. During merge, the reviewer had to discover the primary worktree and run git -C <repo> merge there. A dedicated kspec merge path for detached review snapshots would remove this manual worktree routing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing detached-reviewer merge friction observations (already tracked before this session).

observations.content: Parallel full-suite runs on the reviewed snapshot and the recorded base commit gave a clear regression verdict: the reviewed snapshot passed npm test, the base commit failed in tests/file-lock.test.ts and other unrelated files. This made it straightforward to distinguish task impact from pre-existing failures during review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shell-quoting kspec command bodies that contain backticks or multi-line evidence is fragile in agent-driven review flows. During review bookkeeping, a task description and review-comment attempts were mangled when passed through bash; the safer pattern is file-based payloads or quoted heredocs for any rich text passed to kspec commands.
observations.author: codex@openai.com

observations.content: AC annotations can overclaim coverage when a test is tagged to a spec AC but only proves one sub-behavior. In this review, @daemon-file-monitoring ac-8 was annotated on tests that proved permanent-failure callback and project cleanup, but not the spec's logged-error clause identifying the affected project. Reviewers had to re-read the full AC text and compare it against assertions to catch the gap. Consider adding validation or review guidance that flags annotations on multi-part ACs unless the test asserts each observable clause or explicitly scopes which clause is covered.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For flaky-test investigation, escalating from fresh targeted runs to a fresh combined run of the implicated suites and then one full fresh suite quickly distinguished a stale/non-reproducible task from a new unrelated suite failure without patching blindly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix-cycle task resumed in a valid worker worktree but remained blocked because dispatch workspace provisioning reported a foreign worktree on the canonical branch. This forced a manual unblock before normal kspec task start could proceed, even though code work and review resolution were otherwise unblocked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review submissions can reach pending_review with submission_linkage.branch set to dev and no branch delta versus the task branch. Reviewers then have to spend time proving the merge is already a no-op instead of evaluating an actual change set.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec agents generate reported kspec-agents.md as already up to date even though kspec agents status and --dry-run showed stale content after a meta convention change; I had to use status plus dry-run output to detect the mismatch and rerun generation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Bun fs.watch({recursive: true}) on Linux has three confirmed bugs: (1) opens an FD per file in the watched tree, not per directory as inotify should, (2) closing the watcher increases FD count rather than decreasing it, (3) cross-talk between watchers watching different directories with same-named files. These caused 191k+ leaked FDs and silent secondary project watcher failure. Resolved by standardizing on Chokidar in plan @plan-daemon-file-monitoring-reliability.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Empirical FD diagnosis workflow: /proc/PID/fd/ counting + categorization → standalone reproduction scripts → fix validation. This identified the root cause (blob FD leak) in under 10 minutes and validated the Chokidar+exclusion fix before any code changes. Pattern: always measure the actual system state before theorizing about runtime behavior.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec validate is noisy for small task-level verification because project-wide warning debt (orphaned specs/skills and AC annotation warnings) obscures whether a focused spec-only change introduced any new validation issues.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review/task integration handled a no-op manual merge cleanly: the review could be approved from the detached snapshot, the merge gate still ran against the recorded integration branch, and the task was completed with an explicit audit trail stating that the branch was already up to date.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots for spec-only/shadow-state tasks can show no git diff in the worktree even when the submitted kspec state changed. Reviewers have to infer that the change lives in shadow metadata and reconstruct evidence from kspec CLI output instead of getting a direct submitted-state diff.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a kspec batch payload includes apostrophes in AC text, inline shell quoting is brittle; file-based payloads are safer but still manual. A first-class --commands-file option or stdin support for kspec batch would reduce avoidable command construction failures during spec updates.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing friction @01KN818C covering shell-quoting/file-based payload issues for kspec command bodies with quotes, dollars, angle brackets, or multiline text.

observations.content: The condensed npm test runner can stay silent for minutes during long runs, which makes reviewers unable to tell whether the suite is still progressing or hung without manually inspecting processes and /tmp/kspec-test-cache artifacts. Consider emitting periodic heartbeat/progress lines or the active result/log paths while the run is in flight.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can hide the actual review delta when HEAD is already contained by the integration branch. In this session, git diff against the target was empty and manual merge was already-up-to-date even though the task still required a full review. Reviewers had to reconstruct context from kspec task/review/plan metadata and branch containment checks. Consider a reviewer-focused command or review orientation that explicitly shows the examined commit, canonical task branch, integration target, and whether the target already contains the snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session reflection workflow discoverability is inconsistent: the skill text suggests 'kspec workflow show' without a run ref and implies listing workflows, but this CLI exposes 'kspec workflow runs' and requires a run-ref for 'show'. In practice that forces trial-and-error before reflection can start. Update the reflection guidance (and any related agent instructions) to use the actual workflow commands or add a friendlier default for showing the active run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Plan reviewer agent caught compound ACs, orphaned coverage, and implementation-detail ACs across 5 review rounds. Each round improved the plan substantively. The review-plan skill guidance was correct — friction was in applying it during authoring, not in the review process itself.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Unified dispatch state can still ship as bookkeeping-only if the runtime callers are not exercised: this fix cycle added _activeTargets and status exposure, but the actual push/pull call sites remained single-branch until review traced every _syncTargetBranch/_pushIntegrationTargetAsync caller. The repeatable gap is that refactors replacing duplicate state need at least one behavior test per runtime entrypoint, not just helper/state tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Prepared dispatch workspaces can still start from a canonical head that lags the current integration target, forcing workers to replay already-merged dependency commits during the mandatory pre-work rebase. This adds avoidable conflict resolution and makes task-local changes harder to isolate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The test runner's content-hash cache made it practical to run focused dispatch regressions first and then the required full npm test sweep in the same session. That let the session keep the full-suite quality gate without paying repeated cold-run cost after a narrow sync-path refactor.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch task workflow currently instructs a rebase onto the integration target before coding, but on a stacked dispatch branch that can replay already-merged dependency commits and create misleading conflicts. In this session the branch was already at the canonical integration lineage, so the rebase attempt produced a false-positive conflict in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts and had to be aborted.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate reflection capture from the same session; superseded by @01KNA3404.

observations.content: Dispatch task workflow currently instructs a rebase onto the integration target before coding, but on a stacked dispatch branch that can replay already-merged dependency commits and create misleading conflicts. In this session the branch was already at the canonical integration lineage, so the rebase attempt produced a false-positive conflict in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts and had to be aborted.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The test runner content-hash cache made it practical to run focused dispatch regressions first and then the required full npm test sweep in the same session. That kept the full-suite quality gate intact without paying repeated cold-run cost after a narrow sync-path refactor.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The reflection docs say 'kspec workflow show' without arguments, but the CLI required an explicit workflow run ref (for example @01KNA47V). That mismatch adds avoidable trial-and-error at the end of a session.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of inbox item @01KGGPJ6, which already tracks making 'kspec workflow show' infer the active run and improving the command output.

observations.content: Fix-cycle reviews were faster once the worker rebased onto the current plan branch before editing. Resolving the conflict against the already-merged active-target-set changes exposed the real follow-up bug and avoided patching the stale single-target path.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In fix cycles on dispatch sync work, reproducing the reviewer's blocker with a focused regression test before rerunning the broader suite kept the change local and made the final verification faster.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer-approved dispatch work can still fall back to needs_work because manual merge conflicts are discovered only at publication time in the detached review snapshot. Consider earlier conflict detection against the integration target before final approval or a clearer pre-merge conflict gate in the review workflow.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon dispatch status serialization is duplicated across internal and public routes, so engine API shape changes can leave one or both route serializers stale unless both mappings and regression tests are updated together.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review blockers on exact route lines made this fix cycle fast to execute: the worker could patch the precise serializer sites, add focused regression coverage, and resolve the threads without re-auditing the whole dispatch change.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual merge into a plan branch can report conflicts from a stale local branch even when the task branch is already a descendant of origin/plan; the merge workflow should refresh or verify ancestry before escalating worker-side reconciliation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Needs-work state after an aborted manual merge can become stale when the task branch already contains the integration target tip; workers have to prove ancestry and rerun checks before they can safely resubmit.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review/test friction: launching two npm test runs in parallel can race in the test-runner build bootstrap and fail with cp EISDIR in dist/daemon while both processes try to repair the missing build output. The runner should serialize or lock its auto-build path so concurrent test invocations fail cleanly or wait instead of corrupting the bootstrap step.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Merge workflow friction: a reviewer snapshot can report manual-merge conflicts that disappear after resetting the local integration branch to the current remote tip. The merge flow should refresh the integration target before declaring a conflict so stale local state does not trigger an unnecessary fix cycle.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual-merge conflict findings can become stale after branch ancestry changes, but the task can remain in needs_work until someone manually re-checks mergeability. This session required verifying the integration target was already an ancestor and re-running a no-commit merge just to clear outdated conflict state.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual-merge review checks can go stale across fast task fix cycles. This session inherited repeated 'merge conflict' blockers that no longer reproduced on the live integration target, which cost time re-verifying branch lineage and mergeability instead of fixing code.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A detached-worktree no-commit merge simulation against the live integration target was an effective way to verify manual_merge readiness without disturbing the worker branch. It quickly separated stale merge-gate claims from real code issues.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Tests that assert prerequisite/build state against the live repo root are brittle in dispatch worktrees and full-suite runs; they should prefer isolated temp fixtures when validating environment checks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual-merge review blockers are expensive to triage because mergeability against the live integration target is not captured as a first-class, current-state check. This task went through repeated fix cycles where stale and real merge-conflict claims had to be re-proven manually with merge-base and no-commit merge checks before the branch could be reconciled.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Using merge-base ancestry plus a real no-commit merge against the current integration target gave a decisive signal for review-cycle mergeability. That combination was enough to distinguish stale reviewer findings from real semantic conflicts and guided the eventual branch reconciliation cleanly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review flow handled unrelated flaky test noise well once it was treated explicitly: rerun the full suite, confirm the failure is not introduced by the reviewed branch, create a dedicated follow-up task, and continue approving the clean change. In this session that avoided blocking a correct test-runner fix on an intermittent tests/file-lock.test.ts failure.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree, so the documented reviewer merge flow ('git checkout dev' in the assigned workspace) fails with 'already used by worktree'. In this session the merge had to be performed indirectly with git -C against the main dev worktree. The review/merge guidance should document a worktree-safe merge path for detached reviewer snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review workflow should standardize mergeability checks against the live integration target before requesting changes. This task accumulated multiple stale manual-merge conflict review cycles before the branch was actually rebased and merged cleanly, which indicates the current reviewer process can misclassify mergeability and create unnecessary fix cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow in detached review snapshots assumes 'git checkout <integration-branch>' in the current worktree. In practice this failed because dev was already checked out in the main worktree, so merge had to be executed via 'git -C <main-worktree> merge --no-ff <task-branch>'. Consider updating merge guidance or tooling to handle occupied integration branches in multi-worktree dispatch setups.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Stacked dispatch sync rebases can leave duplicate helper implementations and stale worktree git locks, which turns a straightforward rebase into manual compile-fix cleanup before task work can resume.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running the task-specific suite first (npm test -- dispatch-target-sync.test.ts) cleanly separated sync-runtime verification from an unrelated full-suite failure, which made submit/no-submit decisions much faster after a heavy rebase.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When startup-sync behavior regressed from one pass to two, a behavioral regression test that asserted per-target sync call counts on engine start caught the issue immediately; final-state-only assertions would not have. For dispatch sync integration work, asserting execution count at the behavior boundary is worth keeping when duplicate work is itself a bug.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual-merge conflict notes can become stale across quick rebases/fix cycles; this session spent a fix cycle re-verifying a branch that was already rebased. Review/dispatch flow should check merge-base ancestry against the integration target before returning a task for merge-conflict resolution.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer mergeability is still a separate manual preflight step in dispatch review. In this session the task note claimed the integration target was already an ancestor and merge-ready, but git merge-base and an actual git merge against plan/plan-workspace-scoped-integration-target-sync/01kn8bx4 showed a real content conflict in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. Consider adding an explicit worker-side mergeability/preflight check against the recorded integration target before submit so stale rebase claims fail earlier.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The current review workflow caught the issue without unnecessary churn: diff-first review, full npm test, and explicit manual-merge preflight cleanly separated code correctness from integration readiness and moved the task back to needs_work with anchored evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual merge preflight findings can go stale across fast fix cycles when the integration target advances; a fresh isolated merge check was needed to disprove a reopened conflict on an already-rebased branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Manual merge preflight against origin can pass while the dispatch-provided local integration branch still conflicts; reviewers/workers need branch-state checks against the actual local target, not only origin/<target>.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Extending tests/dispatch-target-sync.test.ts with the existing bare-remote, tracked-branch, and direct git helpers made it straightforward to add new workspace-scoped sync regressions without building a second dispatch harness.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel lint fix agents with non-overlapping file scopes — 112 errors across 3 agents in ~8 min, zero conflicts. Clear scope boundaries are essential for parallel agent work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: vi.stubEnv(HOME, tempDir) for controlling agent detection in tests — lightweight behavioral approach avoids heavy mocks while making tests deterministic across environments.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2e test fixtures with hardcoded absolute dates rot as time passes — entity cache stale detection marks old active sessions as stalled. Use relative timestamps.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec init --setup creates task-worker and pr-reviewer agents but not a plan-reviewer agent or primary dev agent. Had to manually add plan-reviewer, claude agent, and conventions after setup. Setup could offer an interactive agent selection or include plan-reviewer as a built-in agent.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec agent run failed with OAuth token expiry on claude-agent-acp adapter. No fallback or helpful error suggesting to try a different adapter. Had to manually switch to codex-acp. Could suggest available adapters on auth failure.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: codex-acp agent run for plan-reviewer completed but could not write review records — likely a shell environment or permission issue with shadow branch writes from the adapter context. Agent reported success but produced no kspec review artifacts. Should fail visibly if write operations are blocked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Not a shell/environment issue — the agent's auto_approve was set to false, which blocked all write operations (shadow branch commits for review records). Fix: set --auto-approve on agents that need to write kspec data.

observations.content: kspec plan derive requires --module but kspec init creates no modules (only an empty main.yaml with items: []). Had to discover kspec module add separately. Either init should create a default module, or derive should offer to create one, or the error message should suggest kspec module add.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec setup could prompt for project-specific conventions (commits, architecture, testing) during initial setup rather than requiring manual kspec meta add convention calls after the fact. A setup wizard step for conventions would reduce post-setup work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Plan review cycle was 7 iterations before approval. The plan-reviewer agent caught real issues (tool effect mismatches, missing state model fields, undefined mechanics) but also flagged things that were arguably style preferences (how to document cross-cutting constraints). A review strictness config or --mvp flag could help calibrate review depth for early-stage projects.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec agent run plan-reviewer with codex-acp adapter successfully recorded review findings and verdicts on later runs. The agent followed the review-plan skill accurately — created review records, added anchored comments with blocker/question/nit kinds, ran checks, and submitted verdicts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Bulk task operations: had to run 9 separate kspec task set commands to mark tasks as automation eligible. User corrected that --refs flag or kspec batch could do this in one command. The CLI help for task set should prominently mention --refs for multi-task operations.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch filter rules should support tag-based routing — e.g. filter: {tags: [ui]} to match tasks with specific tags, or filter: {tags_exclude: [ui]} for everything but. Would enable agent specialization like a UI worker vs engine worker without manually assigning tasks. Current filters only support automation status.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can hit a dead end on the prescribed manual merge flow: git checkout <integration-branch> fails when that branch is already checked out in another worktree, even when the task branch and integration branch already point to the same commit and the merge is a no-op. Review/merge guidance or tooling should recognize and handle the identical-commit case before instructing checkout/merge.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Recording review checks/verdicts triggered shadow auto-push warnings (pull-rebase conflicts) even though the local review metadata commits succeeded. Reviewer flow would be smoother if review metadata writes either avoided noisy auto-push conflict warnings in detached snapshots or provided a clearer built-in recovery path than manual kspec shadow resolve.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Spec-only updates can add acceptance criteria that narrow behavior without updating adjacent ACs, leaving the spec internally contradictory. In this session, new active-session-only watching ACs conflicted with existing @daemon-file-monitoring ac-7 because no guardrail surfaced the overlap before review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review feedback against a specific acceptance criterion made the spec inconsistency obvious and kept the fix cycle narrow: the blocker pointed directly at @daemon-file-monitoring ac-7, which let the worker update the conflicting AC and resolve the review without re-reading unrelated spec surface.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec batch mutation commands are easy to misinvoke because their argument names differ from the interactive CLI surface (for example task note expects message and item ac set expects acId). This caused avoidable failed attempts during a small fix cycle even when the intended commands were already known.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots cannot execute the documented manual merge step when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this session, `git checkout dev && git merge --no-ff <task-branch>` failed with `fatal: 'dev' is already used by worktree ...`, even though the review was approved and branch pointers were already identical. The merge workflow should define how reviewer agents handle this worktree-lock case and when branch equality makes merge a no-op.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing detached-review/manual-merge friction observations (for example @01KN63S6 and @01KN5D0X). This session reproduced the same worktree-lock failure mode rather than surfacing a new issue.

observations.content: Anchoring spec-review feedback to the exact acceptance criterion made the fix cycle fast and low-noise. The first review identified a direct contradiction between @daemon-file-monitoring ac-7 and the new active-session-only ACs; the worker narrowed ac-7, and the follow-up review could verify the specific conflict was resolved without re-litigating the whole spec.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test hit an intermittent failure in tests/file-lock.test.ts ('count: 4' vs 'count: 5') after the session-watcher refactor passed its focused suites and daemon startup suites; isolated rerun of the file-lock test passed immediately, suggesting unrelated concurrency flake in the full-suite environment.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KNBP2B from the same session context. Keep the earlier observation as the canonical tracking entry for the intermittent tests/file-lock.test.ts full-suite flake.

Consider first-class dispatch support for completing approved merges from detached review snapshots without manual worktree plumbing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review flow caught a real delayed-metadata race in SessionWatcher, and the fix-cycle model worked well: create a new review record, verify the targeted behavioral regression test, rerun the full suite, then approve and merge. That sequence produced a clean, auditable reviewer path.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review flow worked well here: the prior review isolated a real delayed-metadata race, the new behavioral regression test verified the fix directly, and the full npm test suite confirmed there were no broader regressions before approval and merge.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Already-implemented task cleanup still required a manual submit -> review -> approve -> complete sequence after verification. A direct verified-already-implemented path would reduce lifecycle overhead when work has already landed on the integration branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reusing the existing /proc/self/fd regression pattern from session-watcher tests made it fast to localize a descriptor-leak fix and choose an appropriate daemon-cache regression shape.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Vitest cannot spy on ESM namespace exports like fs/promises.opendir, so verifying handle-close behavior required a heavier vi.doMock()+fresh-import pattern instead of a direct spy.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot switch to integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. This is workable but adds avoidable merge-step friction for autonomous review flows.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For narrow daemon cache fixes, pairing a small production change with AC-annotated tests that exercise both success and failure paths made review straightforward. In this session, the opendir/finally cleanup fix plus explicit tests for successful enumeration and enumeration failure gave clear evidence for approval before merge.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Layered FD diagnosis: fix one leak, re-measure, discover the next. Each fix (watcher scoping → readdir closure) was only visible after the previous fix reduced noise. Measuring between fixes prevented conflating causes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: futex_wait + zero CPU tick delta proved bun runtime deadlock vs FD exhaustion in under 30 seconds. /proc/pid/task/*/wchan showing all threads in futex_wait is the definitive signal — no strace needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan review fix cycle requires manual correlation between review thread findings and plan text locations. No structured way to mark which review thread a plan edit addresses — reviewer has to re-read the full plan and infer.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can land on an integration-head commit where git diff at HEAD shows unrelated branch history instead of the submitted task change. Reviewers then have to reconstruct evidence from shadow commits and task metadata. Improve dispatch review context or tooling so reviewers can directly see the task-local delta for spec-only and shadow-only submissions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The cached npm test runner made the required second full-suite review run effectively free when repo state was unchanged, which is a good fit for regression triage and anti-flake review practice.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon-local relative imports without explicit .js extensions can pass under Bun but fail only after compiled dist/daemon JavaScript is executed under Node, which hides dual-runtime portability bugs until late verification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running both node and bun directly against dist/daemon/index.js gave a fast dual-runtime smoke check that exposed build/output regressions early while keeping one shared daemon artifact contract.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review sessions get low-signal output from kspec validate because warnings-only exits include large amounts of existing repo debt (orphaned specs, historical AC coverage issues). In this session the command was still useful for checking errors, but the warning volume made it harder to tell whether the reviewed task introduced anything new.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec task complete warned that linked spec @daemon-runtime-adapter has 11 acceptance criteria to verify, even though task @task-daemon-runtime-config intentionally covered only ac-runtime-selection and ac-default-bun. That warning is too coarse for incremental feature delivery and risks training reviewers to ignore it.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test still hangs during teardown after long green progress output in dispatch workspaces; targeted websocket tests and typecheck passed for @task-ws-connection-state-abstraction but the full runner did not return a final status.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Already tracked by @task-investigate-npm-test-teardown-hang-after-green-suite-run; this session reproduced the same teardown-hang pattern during full npm test after targeted daemon websocket tests passed.

observations.content: Parallel npm test invocations can race in scripts/test.cjs auto-build/bootstrap: one targeted run failed during SvelteKit postbuild while the same command passed immediately when rerun serially.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon runtime adapter tasks can hide package-line incompatibilities unless the worker verifies npm peer constraints. In this session, @elysiajs/node had no 1.1.x release and required upgrading the repo from elysia 1.1.x to 1.4.x before the adapter wiring could be valid.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Targeted daemon build/runtime checks before the full test suite gave fast signal on runtime-adapter changes, and delegating the long npm test run to an awaiter preserved momentum while still finishing with full regression coverage.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Runtime adapter review found a launcher-path coverage gap: daemon runtime tests exercised the built daemon entrypoint and config parsing separately, but not the supported  path. A project configured with daemon.runtime=node still hit Bun-only launcher logic. Add or preserve end-to-end coverage for the public launcher whenever runtime selection changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused runtime-specific tests before full npm test caught a real cross-runtime env leak quickly in serve start, which made the fix cheaper to validate before the 50-minute full suite.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Behavioral coverage for daemon auto-start/runtime selection still requires low-level test scaffolding (shadow detection, isolated HOME/PID files, runtime-specific process inspection), making these tests harder to write and easier to misconfigure than regular CLI behavior tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running focused runtime tests before the full npm test suite isolated the real regression quickly and avoided waiting on the entire suite while iterating on serve/auto-start changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC annotations can be attached to helper-level tests that never exercise the claimed behavior. In this review, @daemon-runtime-adapter ac-auto-start-runtime was tagged on a test that only asserted getDaemonRuntimeCommand() returns its input, so the auto-start path in maybeAutoStartDaemon() remained unproven. Consider stronger guidance or tooling to distinguish behavioral AC coverage from helper/unit assertions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Direct bun/node subprocess tests bypass the CLI helper env scrubbing, so leaked KSPEC_NO_DAEMON and dispatch/session vars can silently suppress incidental daemon auto-start and make runtime tests fail for the wrong reason.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Immediately after 'kspec review verdict --decision approve', the first 'kspec review get' for @01KNEESF0MS8K5BPGM1AASAJ3M still returned lifecycle=open and disposition=pending before a second read returned closed/approved. Review state reads should either reflect the verdict synchronously or clearly signal eventual consistency so merge automation does not need a blind re-read.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test can fail on an unrelated ENOTEMPTY temp-dir cleanup in tests/cli-daemon-proxy.test.ts, which forces targeted reruns to separate task regressions from suite noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel build:e2e or Playwright verification jobs can race on shared dist/web-ui and dist/daemon artifacts, producing misleading module-not-found or page-render failures. Reflection from @task-e2e-runtime-aware: verification was reliable only after serializing build:e2e and node/bun E2E runs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Node-runtime E2E verification is currently easy to over-credit: a targeted watcher test can pass while the AC-annotated UI smoke path for runtime parity still fails under KSPEC_TEST_RUNTIME=node. Reviewers/workers need a clearer canonical node verification target for @daemon-runtime-adapter parity.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Test-runner build readiness was too shallow for detached workspaces: a failed first npm run build could still leave enough artifacts for the next npm test to skip rebuild logic even though packages/web-ui/.svelte-kit/output/server/manifest-full.js or packages/shared/dist were missing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For flaky first-run build prep, pairing package-local self-healing (svelte-kit sync in packages/web-ui build) with root-level readiness checks in scripts/test.cjs stabilized npm test more reliably than fixing only one layer.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Targeted daemon runtime smoke coverage that exercises both node and bun against built web UI assets caught the remaining root-asset parity gap (/favicon.ico and related files) quickly after review and provided a fast regression check for the fix.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, full-suite failures from tests/cli-daemon-proxy.test.ts required isolated reruns on both the review snapshot and the integration base to classify them as flaky/non-regressions. This is a repeatable review burden when aggregate cleanup flakes surface without task-local signal.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Targeted node-runtime verification worked well for runtime-adapter review: focused daemon tests plus KSPEC_TEST_RUNTIME=node Playwright smoke and watcher checks were enough to validate task-scoped HTTP/WebSocket parity before treating unrelated full-suite failures separately.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Stabilizing aggregate-only test flakiness worked well by fixing the shared test helper and adding deterministic helper-level coverage first, rather than patching one flaky suite in isolation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec batch only accepting inline JSON made review-thread reply/resolve batches awkward and error-prone in shell-heavy agent sessions; a file-input mode or stdin mode would reduce quoting retries during fix cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can arrive with node_modules present but dev dependencies omitted, which makes scripts/test.cjs report missing direct dependencies and attempt npm ci from a partially populated workspace install. In this session the reviewer had to repair the workspace with npm ci --include=dev --force before required verification could run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review flow worked well for this cache fix because the task notes documented prior blockers and the diff stayed tightly scoped to src/daemon/entity-cache.ts plus behavioral coverage in tests/daemon-entity-cache.test.ts. That made it straightforward to verify the overlapping debounce-window regression and complete the merge confidently.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch worktrees can inherit NODE_ENV=production with partial node_modules, causing npm test and typecheck to fail until dev dependencies are reinstalled with NODE_ENV=development npm ci.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch workspaces with NODE_ENV=production can leave node_modules without devDependencies, and scripts/test.cjs only retries npm ci without forcing dev installs. npm test could not self-heal until npm install --include=dev was run manually.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
