observations.content: In this dispatch worker session, daemon-backed kspec task commands intermittently failed or hung (for example task get --json returned invalid JSON and a task note write stalled), while rerunning the same commands with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 succeeded. Direct-mode fallback was required to finish task lifecycle operations.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task work needed KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 because daemon-backed CLI reads returned a JSON parse error ('Unexpected token u'). Direct mode worked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon-backed kspec CLI commands in this dispatch workspace returned 'Unexpected token "u", "undefined "... is not valid JSON', which forced a direct-mode fallback with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 for task/review operations. This looks like a systemic dispatch/daemon serialization bug rather than task-specific behavior.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing daemon/direct-mode friction observations recorded earlier on 2026-04-06; session reflection search by exact phrase missed the prior items.

observations.content: In dispatch worker worktrees without a local .kspec mount, direct task commands can fail through daemon/proxy or hang until the caller forces direct mode (KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1) and points KSPEC_SPEC_DIR at the parent repo shadow state. The workflow should make the canonical shadow state explicit or route task commands there automatically.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For code-only daemon/cache work in a dispatch worktree, running tests with SKIP_BUILD=1 isolated verification from an unrelated web-ui build failure while still exercising the changed runtime and full suite.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In this dispatch worktree, mutating kspec task commands timed out through the daemon proxy even while read-only commands and the daemon itself were healthy, so I had to rerun task start/note/submit with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1. This is distinct from generic daemon timeouts because the failure mode blocked lifecycle mutations but left direct mode as the necessary workaround.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: This incremental cache task was unusually efficient to execute because the task description spelled out the single-entity patch path, fallback path, and required regression cases. That level of implementation context let me move straight from code inspection to tests and code changes without extra discovery churn.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer snapshots can hang on daemon-proxied read-only kspec commands (task get, review get/search), forcing manual KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 fallback to finish the review. This adds repeated command retries and slows deterministic review workflows in dispatch worktrees.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During dispatch fix-cycle work, read-only kspec lookups like session start/task get can stall against the daemon and require rerunning with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1. A direct-mode fallback for read-only commands would remove manual retries and make autonomous workflows more reliable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running the focused daemon cache suite before the full test suite caught two related reload-cycle regressions immediately after the batch-order fix. The pattern of targeted regression verification first, then full npm test, reduced fix-cycle turnaround without skipping full verification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In dispatch worktrees, some read-only kspec commands (search/get/note flows) timed out or hung via daemon mode and had to be re-run with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 or after a direct-mode fallback. This adds avoidable latency and makes autonomous task workflow less reliable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can arrive with a broken .kspec worktree link. This blocks normal reviewer actions like kspec search, review add, and task/review writes until someone manually runs 'kspec shadow repair'. The failure mode surfaced mid-review as ShadowError: Worktree disconnected from git, and it also showed up in detached-worktree test behavior. Consider making reviewer snapshot preparation verify or auto-repair shadow linkage before handing off the workspace.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a submitted change is intended to repair review-worktree instability, the most reliable review pattern was: run full npm test once to surface broad failures, verify the suspected fix with a narrower build-plus-targeted regression suite, then reproduce any remaining full-suite failure on dev to classify it as pre-existing or introduced. That produced a mergeable signal here without conflating a pre-existing detached-worktree parser failure with the submitted bootstrap fix.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When reviewing a fix for environment instability, the reliable path was to separate proof of the submitted fix from unrelated suite noise: run full npm test once to map failures, verify the intended repair with a narrower build-plus-targeted regression suite, then reproduce any leftover full-suite failure on dev before treating it as a blocker. That prevented a pre-existing detached-worktree parser failure from incorrectly sending this bootstrap fix back for rework.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: With NODE_ENV=production set in the shell, npm test repaired dependencies repeatedly because devDependencies were omitted, then also rewrote package manifests during verification. The test runner should either force a dev install mode for local verification or surface the environment mismatch before mutating the workspace.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A worker workspace could report Shadow branch healthy while .kspec/ was absent: kspec task note failed with .kspec directory missing, but kspec shadow repair reported nothing to repair. Shadow health/repair should detect and recover a missing worktree path instead of claiming the branch is healthy.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec review reply can hang even when the intended update is simple, which forced a follow-up read of the review record and a second shorter reply to confirm persistence during a fix cycle.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Rebasing a fix-cycle branch onto the integration target before editing exposed the overlapping incremental-cache conflict early, and pairing the review repro with a behavioral regression test made the final fallback fix straightforward to verify.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch worktrees inherit NODE_ENV=production, which causes npm test dependency readiness to omit devDependencies until the workspace is manually reinstalled with NODE_ENV= npm install --include=dev.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch worktrees can inherit NODE_ENV=production, causing npm installs and the test runner dependency check to omit devDependencies until the workspace is manually repaired with NODE_ENV= npm install --include=dev.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reproducing review-worktree failures with a minimal detached git worktree before patching the test quickly separated environment assumptions from real parser defects and led to a targeted regression.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow in detached review snapshots is misleading when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. In this session, 'git checkout dev' failed with: fatal: 'dev' is already used by worktree at '/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch'. The practical workaround was merging from the main project worktree with 'git -C /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch merge --no-ff <task-branch>'. Consider updating reviewer/merge guidance or adding a helper command for manual_merge from detached reviewer snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: After kspec session start reported a shadow sync conflict, follow-up write commands like task note, review resolve, and task submit sometimes hung in this dispatch workspace until retried as fresh CLI invocations. The writes eventually succeeded, but the lack of fast failure or clear progress signal made fix-cycle completion unnecessarily hard to verify.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Rebasing the dispatch branch onto the plan branch before finishing the fix cycle exposed the real integration conflicts early, and pairing a focused daemon regression with a full npm test -- --fresh rerun caught the overlap bug without causing another review round.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review triage was materially faster and more accurate when I reran the failing targeted tests on both the review snapshot and the integration-base commit before classifying the full-suite failure. That separated unrelated flaky dispatch-engine noise from the real regression in meta include invalidation and let the review record request changes for the right reason while capturing the flaky test as its own follow-up task.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: In a detached review snapshot, 'kspec task complete @ref --reason ...' hung when routed through the daemon and never returned, even though daemon health was OK. Workaround was to rerun with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1. This should either complete normally through the daemon or fail fast with a clear fallback path for mutating review/closeout commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Under dispatch, task state mutations like 'kspec task start' and 'kspec task submit' can hang unless KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 is set, which suggests incidental daemon startup or daemon-side task mutation coupling on lifecycle commands that should remain responsive without daemon access.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Keeping the npm-installed package startup test in the targeted verification pass immediately exposed that switching the default daemon runtime to node also required the root package to ship the @elysiajs/node adapter dependency. The packaged-install check caught a real distribution gap before review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review worktrees cannot check out the integration branch when that branch is already attached to another worktree, forcing manual detached merges and ref updates during approved manual_merge review completion. This should have a first-class merge path that works from reviewer snapshots without raw git ref surgery.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Overlapping `kspec review verdict` invocations against the same review can hang instead of failing fast or surfacing a lock/duplicate-writer message. During this session the approval write stalled until retried, which blocked read commands behind it and added avoidable recovery work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon-routed kspec task/review commands can hang in dispatch workspaces even for local shadow-branch mutations; this session had task get/submit and review reply/resolve stall until rerun with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 direct mode. Investigate daemon proxy behavior for localhost/vat connections and consider an automatic fallback or clearer direct-mode guidance for task-local mutations.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Write-through alignment was low-risk because the cache already centralized incremental task/item/session patch logic behind processDomainChanges; extending writeThrough to reuse that path avoided duplicate invalidation code and kept watcher semantics intact.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch worktrees may inherit NODE_ENV=production, so npm ci omits devDependencies and test bootstrap loops on missing packages until NODE_ENV is cleared.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon-routed task submission timed out even while kspec serve status reported the daemon healthy; I had to switch to KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 to submit the task and confirm pending_review. This makes end-of-task state transitions less reliable in dispatch worktrees.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Stabilizing the flaky post-invocation dispatch tests came from standardizing on waitForStartup-backed polling and wrapping DispatchEngine tests in try/finally so engine.stop() always runs. That combination isolated suite-order flake without changing runtime behavior.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec review resolve can report success without immediately updating review thread_state; after resolving a blocker thread during a fix cycle, a follow-up review get still showed blockers_unresolved=1 until a second bounded resolve/read check. This makes it harder to trust review closure state in automated task resubmission flows.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Long-running exec sessions for npm test can become unattachable mid-run and later report 'Unknown process id', forcing redundant reruns and making automated wait/verification unreliable for full-suite and targeted test commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon route tests that build ad hoc app.handle harnesses can drift from the shared daemon API helper setup (missing error() polyfill, stale fixture shapes), turning route regressions into harness debugging instead of behavioral verification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a route-level regression was hard to verify in a broad read-path harness, adding a dedicated daemon route test with shared fixtures and a hint-aware cache spy isolated the behavior quickly and produced durable coverage for the fix cycle.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Using file-backed JSON payloads for kspec batch kept the spec mutation workflow reliable and avoided shell quoting problems during autonomous task work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec batch argument shapes are not always obvious from the top-level command names; task note rejected body and required message, causing a failed first attempt before the actual spec update could be applied.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For detached review snapshots, checking kspec-meta history alongside the code snapshot cleanly separated the real spec-only task mutation from unrelated code-branch changes and prevented a false review scope.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can point the code worktree at an unrelated integration-tip commit while the actual submitted task change lives only on kspec-meta, which makes spec-only reviews look conflated until the reviewer inspects the shadow-branch history.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shelling kspec review comment with unescaped backticks in the body triggers command substitution and corrupts automated review comments; the CLI flow needs a safer file-or-stdin payload path for comment bodies.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running a focused daemon cache suite before the full npm test run made it clear the history-retention change was correct and separated task-specific regressions from unrelated stale dist import failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Root CLI/parser TypeScript config does not allow type-only imports from packages/daemon/src into src/, so shared parser-daemon contracts like the entity cache accessor require duplicated local types instead of a single source of truth.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test remains flaky in dispatch worktrees: tests/cli-no-daemon.test.ts intermittently times out waiting for an auto-started daemon pid file and tests/daemon-review-websocket.test.ts can fail with a transient dist module-not-found during the full run, even though the same files pass on immediate focused rerun.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The npm test wrapper can run for minutes with almost no streamed progress or completion signal in agent sessions, which led to duplicate full-suite invocations while waiting for output.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reusing the existing cache-aware loader pattern and the parser entity-cache-context test file made it straightforward to add a new cache-backed read path with focused behavioral coverage.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing the exact diff first, then validating the entity-cache contract in src/daemon/entity-cache.ts and running a focused parser suite made it easy to approve a small cache-serving change without being derailed by unrelated full-suite noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running multiple full npm test processes in the same review workspace produced misleading failures and file-collision cleanup errors. Review workflows should treat full-suite reruns as sequential-only in a shared worktree, or provide isolated temp paths per run.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Cache-serving changes can pass review with mocked ready-cache fixtures that do not match ProjectEntityCache's production contract. In this session, a triage read-path change assumed ready triage domains had populated detail entries, but the actual cache keeps triage details empty after domain load and fills them on demand. We need a shared behavioral test/helper for cache-backed read paths that exercises real warmed cache state, especially for detail-on-demand domains.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Direct npm run build from a worker worktree still fails in packages/web-ui postbuild with missing .svelte-kit/output/server/manifest-full.js, while the project test runner can self-heal and continue. This makes standalone build verification unreliable during task work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Cache-aware loaders for plans/reviews can reach ready state with only a subset of details populated because detail tiers are on-demand. Tests in this session covered empty and fully populated detail tiers but missed the partial-detail case, allowing a regression where list loaders returned incomplete subsets from cache instead of falling through to disk.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review blockers were resolved quickly once the cache contract was verified against production-ready state: compare loader logic to the entity-cache domain contract, then replace unrealistic cache-hit tests with behavior that matches how ready indexes and lazy detail tiers actually work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task state transitions can still route through the daemon path and fail with 'fetch failed' during dispatch sessions; I had to rerun kspec task submit with KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 to complete a fix-cycle resubmission. Direct-mode fallback should be automatic or the daemon path should fail closed with a seamless retry.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing daemon-routing friction observations @01KNK4JR and @01KNK66C about daemon-routed task/review commands and task submission timing out in dispatch sessions.

observations.content: Cache-loader work is converging on tests/parser/entity-cache-context.test.ts, so parallel additive test changes create mechanical merge conflicts even when both sides are correct. Consider splitting cache-context coverage by domain or loader to reduce merge hotspots for dispatch review/merge cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test can fail on a stale cached suite path that no longer exists (for example tests/_trivial-verbose-check.test.ts) and requires rerunning with --fresh to get the real result.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Read-only CLI lookups and review bookkeeping can still proxy through the daemon and hang or time out even when direct mode succeeds immediately; workers had to force KSPEC_NO_DAEMON=1 to finish reflection searches and review thread resolution.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Adding daemon-executed behavioral regression tests for helper-based error paths exposed a real shared-state/output-mode bug that unit-level helper coverage alone did not catch. For daemon concurrency and output isolation work, verify behavior through the command API as well as helper tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon route tests import compiled dist artifacts, so source edits can look unfixed until a full build refreshes dist. This made verification slower and easy to misread during daemon command API work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running focused daemon command API regressions before the full npm test suite surfaced that preserving typed exits in one command was insufficient; the targeted failure exposed the broader request-scoped exit-code bug quickly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon command response-parity coverage missed a text-mode intercepted-exit path: the reviewed change preserved exit codes and passed tests, but manual comparison against direct CLI still revealed an extra wrapper stderr line for 'review get' failures. Parity-sensitive daemon reviews should compare direct CLI vs daemon behavior in text mode, not only JSON-mode or exit-code assertions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detailed task descriptions with specific file paths, method names, and implementation steps enable near-mechanical implementation. The extend-loadalltasks task went from start to submission in one pass with zero rework.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle with clear, specific review thread (exact reproduction steps and behavioral comparison) made diagnosis and fix straightforward — completed in one pass with no ambiguity.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Batch route ALS isolation pattern: when applying ALS context wrappers (runWithEntityCache, runWithWorkingDirectory, runWithOutputState, commandExecutionStorage) to new code paths, the single command route (executeCommand) serves as the canonical reference for nesting order. Tests for batch ALS isolation must use behavioral verification (chdir interception, stdout leak monitoring, instrumented accessors) rather than injected debug commands, since executeBatch pre-validates commands against the command tree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: ALS isolation test pattern: when testing that code runs inside an AsyncLocalStorage context (e.g., runWithEntityCache, commandExecutionStorage), spy on methods that are ONLY reachable through the ALS path rather than counting accessor calls that may come from multiple sources. Examples: spy on cache domain methods (getProjectConfig/getShadowInfo) to prove entityCacheStorage is active; use getCommandExecutionStore() to verify commandExecutionStorage capture from within a command handler. This avoids false positives from post-execution paths (writeThrough, cleanup) that also call the accessor.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review flow behaved correctly after verdicting: review checks attached cleanly, request_changes auto-closed the review, and the task transitioned to needs_work without manual cleanup.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer reproduction scripts (running actual commands against built artifacts to confirm behavior) make fix cycles dramatically faster. On the batch isolation task, the cycle 3 reviewer ran a reproduction against dist/cli/batch-exec.js to confirm process.stdout.write output was dropped from batch results. This precision made the fix cycle take ~15 minutes instead of requiring re-investigation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Test timeout alignment principle: vitest testTimeout must be >= kspec CLI subprocess timeout (30s) so that subprocess-level timeout errors propagate as actionable messages rather than opaque vitest STACK_TRACE_ERROR. Applied in stabilize-unrelated-full-suite-failures task by raising default from 15s to 45s.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 1 on task-coverage-scan-config completed in single pass: reviewer's detailed reproduction steps (exact code paths with expected vs actual results) made the cache key bug immediately actionable. Composite cache key pattern (rootDir + sorted scanPaths with null-byte separator) plus prefix-matching invalidation was clean and testable.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing full-suite stabilization work was materially more reliable when the verdict depended on two consecutive uncached npm test runs in the detached review worktree instead of isolated reruns or single green passes. That exposed the difference between slow tests and subprocess fan-out/resource exhaustion, and it validated that moving the heaviest CLI suites into a serial Vitest project still exercised them under normal npm test execution.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review, kspec validate produced large repo-wide alignment/completeness warning sets unrelated to the submitted change. The warnings were real but too noisy to serve as merge evidence for a narrow task, forcing manual classification as pre-existing noise. This suggests a need for a task-scoped or touched-area-focused validation mode, or at minimum clearer separation between new issues and existing global warnings during review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Tests importing from dist/daemon/ with .ts extensions fail silently at write time because esbuild produces no .d.ts files, unlike tsc-compiled modules in dist/parser/. This creates a subtle trap: .ts imports work for dist/parser/* but break for dist/daemon/*. A lint rule or oxlint custom rule checking for .ts extensions in dist/daemon/ imports would catch this at author time.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comments that include shell-sensitive quoting are easy to mangle when sent through one-line exec commands. In this review, backticks inside a kspec review comment body triggered shell command substitution before the CLI saw the text. For agent workflows, multiline review/note payloads should use a temp file or heredoc-safe path instead of inline shell strings.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review workflow caught an isolation breach by checking git history and diff scope before relying on the worker note. Verifying the targeted daemon suites separately from the failing full suite made it possible to distinguish the real task outcome from unrelated test noise and send the task back for the correct reason.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When dispatch agents modify kspec source and run kspec validate, the installed binary is stale — it reflects pre-build code, not the changes just made. Agents must run npm run build then node dist/cli/index.js validate to verify against current code. This caused confusion during fix cycle 2 of task-coverage-scan-config where validate appeared to still show 307 warnings until the dev build was used instead.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 2 on task-coverage-scan-config completed in a single pass: read review threads, identified root cause (fixture test files with fake AC refs), designed and implemented exclude_patterns config option, threaded through all callers, wrote 9 tests, verified with full suite (7600 passed) and kspec validate (0 invalid annotations). Systematic review reading and grep-based root cause analysis kept the fix focused.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review worktrees can load kspec.config.yaml from the parent repo root instead of the review snapshot root. In this session that made branch-local coverage.scan_paths/exclude_patterns inert during review, so kspec validate still reported invalid_ac_annotation warnings even though the branch changed kspec.config.yaml. Search checked: worktree config load detached review; project config worktree mainRoot; invalid_ac_annotation detached worktree.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Combining a direct runtime repro (initContext plus scanACAnnotations in the review snapshot) with a full npm test run cleanly separated environment/config-loading defects from feature correctness. That made it possible to reject the task for a real review-gate failure without misclassifying the passing test suite as contradictory evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Preventive lint rules as bug-class fixes: when a runtime bug stems from a toolchain constraint (e.g., esbuild daemon build only produces .js files, not .d.ts), adding a custom oxlint lint rule to catch the pattern at lint time is more durable than fixing individual instances. The jsPlugins mechanism makes this lightweight to implement and test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: npm run dev -- validate fails with split storage backend not registered. Cannot locally verify kspec validate changes using branch code without the full build/install cycle. Tests cover it but ad-hoc validation during development is blocked.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Config loading fix for worktrees was identified quickly by comparing initContext() calling pattern against all other loadProjectConfig() callers — the inconsistency (mainRoot vs projectDir,projectDir) was the root cause signal.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review worktrees can execute a globally linked kspec binary instead of the workspace-local CLI, which makes validation results disagree with the code under review. Review flow should prefer node dist/cli/index.js or otherwise force the workspace build when comparing behavior in detached snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The npm test harness in review snapshots can run for many minutes without emitting progress back to the caller, which makes it hard to distinguish slow progress from a hung run during automated review. A lightweight progress heartbeat or surfaced log path earlier would reduce review uncertainty.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Comparing workspace-local validation results against a base-commit source-level validate run was an effective way to distinguish pre-existing annotation noise from regressions introduced by the reviewed task.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When implementing ref resolution logic (plan filters, entity lookups), ULID prefix matching is easy to omit even when the AC specifies it. The daemon plan filter used exact equality while api-static.ts and ReferenceIndex both had prefix support — the inconsistency caused a fix cycle. Consider: any new ref resolution should use ReferenceIndex.resolve() or replicate its full resolution order (exact ULID, ULID prefix, slug).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 2 on plan filter task completed in one pass — reviewer's blocker description was precise enough to identify root cause immediately. Mirroring the daemon's resolved-plan-identity comparison pattern in the static path was the right approach.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review snapshots can drift against a moved local integration branch: this session's detached reviewer worktree initially compared efd95569e944 against local dev e4ce9897814d, but the dispatch prompt and task submission linkage both recorded the true review base as 6a8fd6df49537d95cca2f6283be8a4aa82cc30c8. Review tooling should expose or default to the recorded submission/integration base commit so reviewers do not accidentally inspect unrelated newer dev changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm test (scripts/test.cjs) finds 0 test files when run from a dispatch worktree under .kspec-worktrees/ because vitest.config.ts excludes **/.kspec-worktrees/**. The exclude is correct for preventing test discovery of nested worktree fixtures, but it also excludes the actual project test files when the cwd is itself inside .kspec-worktrees/. Workers must fall back to npx vitest --run directly, which contradicts the testing convention. The test runner or vitest config needs worktree-awareness — possibly by resolving exclude patterns relative to the project root rather than using absolute glob matching.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Highly precise task descriptions with exact line numbers, function names, root cause vs safety net framing, and explicit test plan made a complex two-defect fix straightforward. The task for fix-worktree-linkage-capture was a model for bug task descriptions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detailed task descriptions with per-assertion replacement strategies (behavioral vs relative vs fixture-derived) enabled direct implementation without exploratory iteration. The task for e2e fixture-decoupled assertions had specific file paths, line numbers, and replacement patterns for each assertion — completed in one pass with only one minor pivot (automation badge not in list view).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: npm config omit=dev blocks test runner in dispatch worktrees: system-level npm config has omit=dev, which causes the test runner dependency-health hook to fail in an infinite loop (npm ci also omits dev deps, so the fix never resolves). The test runner fix hook should pass --include=dev to npm ci, or the dependency-health check should detect the omit config and warn.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task @task-cli-serve-test-daemon-cleanup had an exceptionally detailed description with spawn line numbers, per-test classification guidance, and specific AC for edge cases. This level of detail enabled efficient autonomous execution with correct design decisions (e.g., recognizing PID file dependency prevented incorrect direct-spawn migration).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Full npm test still left multiple review-worktree daemon processes alive under /tmp/kspec-test-* and /tmp/kspec-setup-no-agent-* after the cli-serve cleanup task merged. This indicates other tests still spawn daemons without reliable cleanup outside tests/cli-serve.test.ts. Search before capture found no existing tracking for the broader leak pattern; follow-up should inventory daemon-spawning tests across the suite and close the remaining leak sources.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: tests/test-runner.test.ts creates fixed-named scratch files directly under tests/, so concurrent executions of that suite interfere with each other and can produce false ENOENT failures during review verification. Consider isolating runner smoke tests with unique filenames or temp directories so parallel/overlapping test runs are safe.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Custom oxlint rule implementation was smooth because: (1) existing rules provided clear structural precedent, (2) task description included exact file paths and anti-patterns to detect, (3) testing the rule against the real codebase before writing test fixtures caught false positives early. The three-rule pattern (no-daemon-ts-imports, no-source-scanning, no-leaky-test-daemon) is now well-established for future custom rules.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle completed in single pass when review thread included exact file:line references and specific AC violation. The precise blocker description (progress lines written to logStream violating AC5) eliminated investigation time and made the fix obvious — remove two logStream.write() calls. Lesson: precise review threads with code anchors dramatically accelerate fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review/test sessions can be derailed by assuming npm test forwards raw vitest flags. In this session, npm test -- --fresh --runInBand failed immediately because the project runner rejects --runInBand. Consider documenting or validating unsupported forwarded flags in scripts/test.cjs so agents get a clear project-specific error before spending time on a bad invocation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review flow worked well when it combined targeted behavioral repro fixtures with recorded review checks. Reproducing the lint rule against minimal inline oxlint fixtures exposed two real rule gaps quickly and made the request_changes verdict easy to justify with executable evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle for no-leaky-test-daemon lint rule was clean: read both review blockers fully before coding, made two targeted changes (tighten afterEach pattern matching, add await/expect boundary to forward scan), added 3 repro test cases directly from reviewer descriptions, ran parallel shard verification. One commit, zero regressions. Pattern: read all threads → understand root cause → fix in one pass.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer merge ergonomics: detached review worktrees cannot directly check out the integration branch when that branch is already active in the main worktree. In this session, approving and merging an otherwise clean task required a dry-run merge in the detached review workspace, then the actual merge in the main dev worktree. This is repeatable reviewer friction and would benefit from a first-class kspec merge path for detached review snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review signal noise: repo-wide kspec validate warnings are hard to use during task review because the output mixes long-standing project completeness/alignment issues with task-specific verification. In this session, validate returned exit code 6 with many unrelated warnings, so the useful conclusion was only that there were no new task-local validation errors. A scoped or baseline-aware review validation mode would reduce noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review verification pattern worked well: creating a fresh review record, reading the diff before notes, then offloading long-running full-suite and repeated targeted test runs to awaiter agents produced clear evidence without blocking the main review flow. This pattern is worth reusing for future review cycles with expensive test suites.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a lint rule (or any code with multiple validation paths) checks the same concept in different branches, extract the shared matching logic into a single function from the start. In the no-leaky-test-daemon rule, afterEach and try/finally cleanup detection diverged across fix cycles because each was maintained independently. Extracting hasDaemonCleanupPattern() as a shared function fixed both review blockers at once and prevents future divergence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on no-leaky-test-daemon completed in a single pass. Clear, specific reviewer feedback (exact function + reproduction steps) made the fix straightforward. Callee-whitelist approach is clean and extensible.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: task submit from needs_work state requires an intermediate task start step. In fix cycles, the worker always intends to submit — the needs_work -> in_progress -> pending_review dance is mechanical.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Default branch detection logic is duplicated between workspace.ts (resolveRemoteHeadBranch/resolveCurrentBranch) and setup.ts (detectDefaultBranch). Both use the same git symbolic-ref approach. If a third consumer appears, extract to a shared git utility.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Managed-block gitignore pattern: extracting pure functions (parse/update/serialize) enabled fast unit testing and clean integration. The function-based entry builder with optional override handled custom config without coupling.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Baseline fixture assertion method — capturing git worktree list --porcelain + branch SHA + gitdir pointer + directory mtime + directory inode before and after an operation, then asserting byte-equality — caught a silent-success destructive bug in @task-shadow-worktree-cross-contamination-guard that existence checks would have missed. The linked-worktree init invocation exits 0 but silently destroys main shadow worktree via find_worktree_by_suffix. Pattern worth remembering: when a bug has an exit-0-plus-hidden-mutation shape, prove regression with byte-level snapshot assertions, not existence checks. Reusable helper lives at tests/helpers/worktree-baseline.ts. Consider promoting to a testing convention rule if the same pattern proves useful in a second destructive-bug test context (current N=1; wait for N=2 before generalizing).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle workflow: reading all review threads before any code changes gave clear scope and prevented partial fixes. Addressed all 3 blockers in a single pass without rework.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared-helper refactors in dispatch branch resolution are missing coverage for fallback-order semantics. This review found that stale remote HEAD refs now block the older current-branch fallback even though the extracted helper looked equivalent and all tests passed. Add a behavioral test around stale refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD with a valid checked-out branch so fallback-order regressions are caught automatically.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer reproduction in a temp repo caught a semantic regression that passed the full suite: after extracting dispatch default-branch logic into a shared helper, stale refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD no longer fell back to the checked-out branch. Reproducing the behavior at the CLI/library boundary was more effective than relying on green branch-wide tests alone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC annotations placed inside JSDoc block comments are invisible to kspec validate — the scanner only matches standalone line comments. Agents naturally place AC annotations in file-header JSDoc blocks, but these are silently ignored. Consider: making the validator warn when AC-like patterns appear inside block comments, or adding a lint rule.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle workflow executed efficiently in automated dispatch: review threads accessible via --json, batch reply/resolve handled all 5 threads atomically, and the task-work fix cycle steps followed naturally with clear audit trail.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comment creation is brittle when bodies contain backticks, quotes, or shell metacharacters. In this review, malformed CLI payloads created broken duplicate blocker threads that then had to be manually superseded/resolved. A file- or stdin-based body input for review comments would reduce audit-noise and cleanup work.
observations.author: @codex

observations.content: Direct temp-repo behavioral reproductions during review caught two setup/config regressions that both the targeted scaffold tests and the full suite missed. Reproducing the claimed behavior in a fresh repo remains a high-value review pattern for init/setup and config-scaffolding work.
observations.author: @codex

observations.content: Review fix cycle: discovering thread ULIDs for kspec review reply/resolve requires JSON parsing with non-obvious _ulid field. The human-readable kspec review get output shows thread content and severity but not thread ULIDs. Agents must call --json and discover the _ulid key by trial-and-error. A small UX improvement would be showing thread ULIDs in the human-readable output or accepting thread index numbers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle completed in single pass: read all 3 blocker threads, designed unified fix (consumed-set for agents, ULID-tracking for conventions), implemented, added 3 new tests covering the exact reviewer repro scenarios, full suite green, resubmitted. Reading ALL review threads before starting work prevented partial fixes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review snapshots in manual_merge mode can arrive rebased onto newer dev commits than the recorded integration target, which makes a clean task review impossible because approving the snapshot would merge unrelated work from other tasks. This session required ancestry inspection against the dispatch-provided target before code-level review. Consider a dispatch/workspace guard that rejects or re-prepares review snapshots when task branches are no longer isolated to the recorded merge target.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For review sessions, validating suspected scaffold edge cases with a minimal temp project repro worked well. A direct 'setup --force' repro exposed the mixed rename+delete bug in default-agent reseeding quickly and provided concrete evidence for an anchored blocker instead of relying on code inspection alone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review sessions still have to treat repository-wide kspec validate failures as ambient noise. In this session, validate failed for pre-existing schema/completeness issues unrelated to the task under review, so approval depended on manually classifying the result as non-blocking instead of using validate as a clean gate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review record plus manual merge flow worked well for an autonomous review cycle: create review, record checks with evidence, approve, merge the dispatch branch into the integration branch, and complete the task in one pass. The state transitions and audit trail were clear and machine-readable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Worker agent rebased task branch onto dev instead of integration target, pulling in 13 unrelated commits. The dispatch system provides the integration target in task context but doesn't enforce that workers rebase onto it rather than dev/main. Reviewer caught this as a blocker. Could be prevented by: (1) adding a pre-submit check that verifies the branch ancestry matches the integration target, or (2) documenting the rebase-onto-target rule more prominently in the task-work skill's rebase step.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can diverge from the review record's examined commit. In this session the open review still examined 303b2298f2b8 while the snapshot under review was 790807a3a503, which required manual diffing against the actual snapshot to avoid reviewing stale state. Consider surfacing snapshot-vs-examined drift directly in review/task context or auto-refreshing review subjects when a new snapshot is prepared.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A targeted temp-repo runtime repro was an efficient way to validate spec equivalence for scaffolded config. Comparing resolveDispatchWorkspaceConfig() with and without kspec.config.yaml in the same no-remote dev-branch repo exposed a real behavior regression even though the full test suite passed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review sessions benefit from a targeted regression slice before the full suite. In this session, running the changed setup tests plus a focused setup/dispatch contract slice surfaced no regressions quickly and gave high-confidence signal while the full npm test run continued.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The condensed test runner hides progress for long npm test runs. During review, the suite appeared idle for minutes and required manual inspection of /tmp/kspec-test-cache logs and process state to confirm liveness and completion progress.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Automated review comments are awkward to post safely when the body contains shell-sensitive text. In this session, a long blocker comment for kspec review had backticks in the body, the shell interpolated them, and the first attempt created a malformed duplicate blocker thread before a retried quoted command succeeded. Consider a body-file/stdin option or safer non-shell input path for long review comments.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The review workflow correctly prevented an incorrect merge even though the submitted snapshot’s task-specific code looked mostly sound: reading the diff before notes, checking git history against the integration base, and treating merge scope as part of correctness caught branch conflation before manual_merge could pull unrelated tasks into the plan branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Plan import format guidance task completed in single pass — detailed task descriptions with per-AC implementation guidance (what/how/testing) enabled focused implementation without ambiguity. Parser error accumulation pattern made adding new typed errors natural.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 6 on @task-scaffold-project-config: verifying branch state before reacting to review feedback avoided a wasted rebase. git diff and merge-base commands quickly proved the branch was clean — the issue was a stale review diff base, not branch conflation. Pattern: always verify the actual diff before accepting a review finding at face value.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When adding feature-specific failure handling to an existing success/failure gate (e.g., init --setup success footer), the pattern of replacing the general gate with feature-specific logic instead of augmenting it causes silent regressions for other failure paths. Seven fix cycles on task-scaffold-project-config; the actual code bug was a 5-line fix restoring the general setupResult.success check alongside the scaffold-specific check.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detailed task descriptions with exact file/line references, merge-order reasoning, explicit what-NOT-to-change sections, and precise AC definitions lead to fast, clean implementations with no ambiguity. @task-tests-suppress-cli-auto-start-daemon is a good template for bug-fix task descriptions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle on daemon leak task: systematic grep for all spawn/spawnSync calls across test suite found the complete set of leaking paths in one pass. The 'before/after pgrep count' verification was reliable for AC1. Key insight: cli-daemon-proxy.test.ts needed auto_start:false at config level rather than KSPEC_NO_DAEMON (which it clears for proxy detection).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer merge flow in a detached review snapshot is awkward when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. This session had to discover the failure from `git checkout dev` and then manually redirect the merge through the primary worktree with `git -C /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch merge ...`. The system should make the correct merge target/worktree explicit or provide a merge command that handles this automatically for reviewer snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: `kspec validate` is not usable as a review gate in this repo right now because it emits large volumes of unrelated pre-existing schema, completeness, and invalid-annotation failures. In this session the review had to mark validate as a non-required skipped check even after running it, which weakens confidence in validation as a reviewer workflow step.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For daemon-leak reviews, combining targeted test runs, full `npm test`, and before/after `pgrep -f dist/daemon/index.js | wc -l` snapshots was an effective verification pattern. It confirmed the fix behaviorally without relying on source inspection and clearly separated no-new-orphans from pre-existing daemon processes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC-annotated tests can still false-green behavior-preserving config work when they only assert that a command exits successfully instead of comparing resolved config behavior. In this review, the scaffolded config changed dispatch.base_branch/publication_mode relative to the empty-config case while the annotated tests still passed. For config scaffolds whose AC promises unchanged runtime behavior, review/test guidance should prefer explicit resolved-config equivalence assertions over generic command-success checks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review signal is degraded because kspec validate currently fails repo-wide with a schema error in .kspec/modules/meta.yaml plus broad completeness noise, so reviewers cannot treat validate as a task-local gate even when the change under review is narrow. This session required manual attribution to separate repo-state failures from branch-specific issues.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle 8 on @task-scaffold-project-config resolved cleanly in one pass: human reviewer provided executable reproduction evidence (temp-repo config comparison), making root cause immediately clear. Using loadProjectConfig() directly in tests for behavioral config comparison is a strong pattern for any future config-scaffolding work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comment capture is too shell-sensitive: a malformed kspec review comment invocation can create truncated duplicate threads instead of failing cleanly, which adds cleanup work and noise to the review record.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing review-comment shell-quoting friction observations such as @01KP6QNNM; broader search after capture showed this pattern was already tracked.

observations.content: Behavior-first review with isolated CLI reproductions in a temp project caught real plan-import regressions that the passing automated tests did not cover.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec review get shows truncated thread bodies in human-readable output. Agents must use --json to read full blocker descriptions, then mentally parse the JSON. A --verbose flag or automatic full-body display for blocker threads would reduce friction in fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 4 on @task-complete-gitignore was clean: single blocker, single focused commit, full test suite green. Reading the trait description carefully (it explicitly covers managed-block writes) gave the right design immediately.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: runSetupPipeline printed summary directly to console.log without checking isStructuredMode(), contaminating --json output. Fixed for the scaffold path in fix cycle 9, but other pipeline functions that call console.log directly (rather than using the output() wrapper) may have the same issue. Consider an audit of console.log calls in command handlers and pipeline functions for structured-mode compliance.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 5 on @task-complete-gitignore: cherry-pick strategy for branch decontamination worked cleanly. Reset to integration target + cherry-pick task-specific commits resolved the 'unrelated work in branch' blocker in one pass with no conflicts. Pattern: when a task branch has accumulated merge pollution, identify task-specific commits via git log filtered on affected files, reset to integration target, cherry-pick in order.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 6 for task-complete-gitignore resolved cleanly in one pass: reading the full review JSON (kspec review get --json) gave precise, actionable feedback with exact line numbers and reproduction steps. Targeted fix: one code change + 4 tests, no scope creep.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan import --into path bypassed parsePlanDocument validation entirely, allowing malformed content through. Pattern: when command handlers have multiple entry points (new vs update), validation must be shared, not duplicated or omitted. The fix was to call parsePlanDocument in both paths. Future similar commands should extract validation into a shared pre-save step.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle resubmit requires needs_work → start → submit (two transitions). In a fix cycle, the agent has already addressed review feedback and just wants to resubmit. The intermediate 'task start' step is non-obvious and caused a failed submit attempt. Consider: allow 'task submit' directly from needs_work, or have 'task submit' auto-transition through in_progress.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 4 for derivable-default-module was resolved cleanly in one pass. The reviewer's concrete repro scenario (init, add extra module before main.yaml, rename default module, run setup) made the root cause immediately clear: no persistent identity for the default module. The fix (adding default_module ULID to manifest schema) was minimal and architecturally clean — no changes to item loading or resolution pipelines, just a lookup key in setup.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Setup step functions (renderSkillsForSetup, generateAgentInstructions, scaffoldProjectConfig, ensureDefaultReflectionHook) are private to setup.ts. The upgrade command had to re-implement the same patterns rather than calling shared functions, creating duplication and divergence risk. These steps should be extracted into a shared setup-steps module that both setup and upgrade can import.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-driven development with detailed ACs made the upgrade command implementation straightforward. The task description's explicit mapping of pipeline steps to existing code locations (setup.ts function names, state file paths, CLI registration patterns) eliminated exploration overhead and enabled a single-pass implementation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review friction: upgrade-command tests mostly asserted step presence/status instead of the required side effects. The full suite passed even though obsolete rendered skills were not removed and the default module was not scaffolded. Direct temp-project repros were needed to verify behavior. This suggests a recurring review risk: broad integration coverage can still miss spec-critical side effects when tests stop at step metadata.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review success: building minimal temp-project repros was an efficient way to validate upgrade behavior claims. Creating one temp project for orphan skill cleanup and one for missing default-module scaffolding turned suspected spec gaps into confirmed blocker findings quickly, without needing to modify the review snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When implementing error paths in CLI commands, using bare console.error() after error() for guidance/suggestion text corrupts JSON output mode. The error() function's details parameter ({suggestion: '...'}) exists specifically for this — always pass guidance as details, never as a separate console.error() call. This was caught in upgrade command review cycle 2 and exists as a potential issue in any new command handler.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review thread bodies have inline code formatting stripped when displayed via kspec review get — backtick-wrapped identifiers render as blank spaces, making it difficult for agents to understand reviewer feedback without cross-referencing code locations manually.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review reruns can silently reuse cached npm test results. During this review, a second 'npm test' invocation replayed cached failures instead of re-executing, which conflicted with the review gate to run failing tests twice for flake classification. Review guidance should either require '--fresh' for reruns or the runner should make replayed results unmistakable in review contexts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle efficiency: when review threads include clear repro steps, fix cycles complete in a single pass with focused changes. The upgrade command cycle 4 fixed both blockers in one commit with 3 targeted tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC coverage can still look complete when tests annotate trait criteria that the command cannot actually exercise. In this review, upgrade-command tests tagged @trait-json-output refs/timestamp ACs even though the command emits neither, so coverage appeared present until manual review checked the assertions. This suggests a gap between annotation-presence checks and behavioral provability for optional trait ACs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: EXIT_CODES.NOT_FOUND (3) is used across the codebase as the runtime-error exit code per @trait-semantic-exit-codes ac-4, but the enum name says NOT_FOUND. This caused reviewer confusion in upgrade command review cycle 5. Consider renaming or adding a RUNTIME alias.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch for review thread replies: resolved all 4 review threads in a single atomic operation (8 commands: 4 replies + 4 resolves). Clean, efficient fix cycle closure.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Upgrade review required a manual temp-project repro because the integration tests only exercised the broken kspec-agents.md path after deleting the stored agents hash. That masked the realistic case where a corrupted artifact coexists with a matching hash and the fast-path incorrectly skips regeneration.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Direct temp-project reproductions were effective for review: building a minimal project, mutating one artifact, and rerunning the built CLI quickly separated real upgrade regressions from repo-wide validation and test noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle 6 for upgrade command: fs.access→fs.stat fix was minimal and precise. Reading reviewer's JSON repro steps before coding made the root cause immediately clear.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review triage friction: checking whether failing tests are pre-existing by adding a detached base worktree was blocked by the test runner's dependency-readiness gate. The ad-hoc base worktree could not run npm test because node_modules/direct dependencies were not considered ready there, so base-vs-head comparison required environment workarounds before any test execution. This makes the review-gate instruction to compare against base branch harder than it should be. Consider a review-friendly way to reuse/install dependencies for detached comparison worktrees or a command dedicated to running comparison checks against the integration base.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle agents must transition needs_work → in_progress → pending_review manually (two commands). kspec task submit could auto-transition from needs_work for fix cycles, since the intent is unambiguous.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agent inherited uncommitted working tree changes from a crashed predecessor (prompt-too-long failure). Reviewing and committing existing changes rather than redoing work saved significant time and avoided potential divergence. Pattern: always check git diff before starting fresh work in fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review sessions are slowed by repo-wide `kspec validate` failures that are unrelated to the branch under review. In this session the command surfaced a schema error in `.kspec/modules/meta.yaml`, orphaned skill warnings, and hundreds of unrelated completeness/annotation problems, so it could not serve as a branch-specific review gate for `upgrade` changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Targeted behavioral repros in temp repos were effective for review validation. Recreating legacy project shapes and running `kspec upgrade --json` directly made it fast to confirm blockers such as malformed version probes and missing default-module backfill without touching the branch under review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: existsSync() does not distinguish file types from directories. In upgrade probe code, existsSync('.agents/skills') returned true for a corrupted regular file, misclassifying malformed state as a valid skills layout. Convention: when checking for directories, always use statSync().isDirectory() or fs.stat() instead of existsSync(). This pattern may exist elsewhere in the codebase.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Per-cycle review records with anchored threads made re-review efficient during a long fix cycle. Prior blockers were easy to reconstruct, verify, and avoid duplicating because each cycle stayed self-contained.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Composed commands can drift from canonical command behavior when they reimplement a step instead of sharing a library path or parity contract. In this session, upgrade step 3 silently tolerated template-loading failures that the canonical agents generator treats as fatal, which surfaced only after repeated review cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When composing existing functions into new commands (e.g., upgrade reusing agents generate, skill render, gitignore repair), error handling semantics from the original call sites are frequently dropped. Silent catch blocks replace fatal errors, leading to degraded behavior that passes tests but corrupts output. The upgrade command went through 9 fix cycles, with at least 4 caused by this pattern. Convention candidate: when reusing a function, audit the original call site's error handling and replicate its severity (fatal vs recoverable vs ignorable).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 10 for upgrade command resolved in a single commit: reviewer provided exact reproduction steps (split manifest + monolithic tasks), which mapped directly to the 13-line early return that needed removal. Existing code below the early return already handled the correct behavior. Pattern: when the reviewer gives a concrete reproduction, the fix is usually removing a shortcut/optimization that bypasses the correct code path.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Existing InvocationOptions.sessionsDir field made the EACCES fix trivial — no production code changes needed. Good API design pays off.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Tests calling runInvocation() without explicit sessionsDir derive /tmp/.kspec-sessions when testDir is under /tmp/, causing shared mutable state. agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts already passes sessionsDir correctly; cli-agent-commands.test.ts did not. Convention gap: no enforcement that test callers of runInvocation always pass sessionsDir.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Workflow CLI ergonomics are opaque when resuming or inspecting a just-started workflow run. After workflow start returned a run id, workflow show still required an explicit run ref and failed with a bare missing-argument error instead of defaulting to the active run or printing the next command.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review task submission linkage can go stale relative to the current integration target. In this session the task description still pointed at older base/head commits, so the reviewer had to re-establish the real review baseline manually before trusting the preserved task context.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: agents generate embeds a timestamp in the output, making content comparison for staleness detection require a stripTimestamp workaround. The hash file should store an output content hash alongside the meta hash so corruption detection is a simple hash comparison.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Upgrade/backfill paths need preservation tests for existing manifest-owned identities, not just existence checks. In this review, modules/main.yaml backfill correctly detected the missing file but still rewrote manifest.default_module, changing project semantics. Review caught it only after an end-to-end temp-project reproduction.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec task start && kspec task submit fails because submit reads stale shadow branch state before the auto-commit from start has landed. Workaround: run start and submit as separate invocations. This affects dispatch fix cycles where needs_work must transition through in_progress to pending_review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 13 on upgrade command completed in a single pass: reviewer reproduction steps were clear enough to immediately understand, fix, test, and resubmit. Precise blocker threads with reproduction steps dramatically reduce fix cycle time.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing regressions against an integration base is harder than it should be when ad hoc base worktrees do not have reusable dependencies or a lightweight comparison path. In this session, verifying whether full-suite failures were pre-existing required creating a detached base worktree, then the test runner attempted dependency repair inside that worktree instead of reusing the current workspace installation. A lower-friction base-branch comparison workflow for reviewer snapshots would make regression classification faster and more reliable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A small behavioral reproduction in a temp project was enough to validate the review finding decisively. Deleting a core skill from project state and running 'kspec upgrade --force --json' showed that upgrade reported success while leaving the core skill missing, which made the blocker concrete without needing speculative reasoning or source-only inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: installCoreSkillsForSetup reports all core-origin skills as 'installed' even when they already exist unchanged — makes it impossible for callers (like the upgrade backfill step) to distinguish truly new installations from no-op updates. The upgrade step always reports 'done' with installed > 0 even when nothing was actually missing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Duplicate task dispatched: @01KP9ZW21H9AD2R127PS5MM6KQ duplicated already-completed @task-fix-cli-agent-session-store-eacces. The dispatch engine created and dispatched a task for an issue that had already been fixed and merged. Agent spent an invocation cycle (build + full test suite) only to discover the work was done. Consider pre-dispatch dedup checks (e.g., search for completed tasks with overlapping description keywords or matching file paths before creating new tasks).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Checking branch identity and prior merged commits before attempting review-merge work quickly proved this submission was already integrated, turning the review into a no-op closure with targeted verification instead of unnecessary merge retries.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When reviewing CLI commands that modify .kspec/, verify a successful run leaves 'git -C <project>/.kspec status --short' clean in a temp project. This catches writes that bypass shadow auto-commit, like upgrade leaving .setup-state.json modified after reporting success.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Upgrade force-path semantics are brittle across scaffold steps. In this review cycle, the reflection hook correctly respected prior user removal, but default agent/convention scaffolding still recreated user-removed defaults when upgrade ran with --force. The same user-intent rule is implemented in separate per-step code paths instead of one shared contract or regression harness, which made fix-cycle regressions likely.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Behavioral reviewer repro in a fresh temp project was effective at catching an uncovered regression. Running the built CLI against a customized project state exposed the --force scaffold-default bug even though the task's dedicated upgrade test file was green. This is a strong pattern for reviewing migration and setup commands whose correctness depends on persisted project state, not just direct unit assertions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a fix-cycle blocker is a sibling of a step already fixed in the same scaffold family (e.g., upgrade step 5b scaffoldDefaults force re-seeding vs upgrade step 5c reflection-hook force re-seeding), the fastest route to a correct fix is to look up the most recent prior fix in the same file or step family and mirror its shape. In this session, the cycle-15 reflection-hook fix (remove a force override of user-removal state) applied almost verbatim to the scaffoldDefaults case, including the one-line change and the behavioral test structure. Pattern for reviewers/workers: search git log for the preceding fix on the file under review before re-deriving a solution.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-time kspec validate output is dominated by repo-wide pre-existing schema and AC coverage debt, so a new invalid AC annotation in the upgrade test still required manual spec lookup and targeted grep instead of a change-scoped validation signal.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running npm test -- tests/upgrade-command.test.ts after the full suite failed quickly isolated the upgrade task's real signal from the known /tmp/.kspec-sessions EACCES failures, which made the review verdict defensible without blocking on unrelated infra noise.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review flow success pattern: diff-first review plus targeted tests, full-suite triage, and a manual temp-project repro gave enough evidence to distinguish branch regressions from pre-existing failures and merge confidently.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve() paths option does not accept relative specifiers like "../../../package.json" — silently fails from non-package cwds. Other places in the codebase (upgrade.ts) already use the simpler path.resolve(path.dirname(here), "..", "..", "..") pattern. Consider a shared helper or a convention doc entry to prevent rediscovery.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Editing an existing project-local skill's SKILL.md content has no dedicated CLI surface: kspec skill set only updates metadata, kspec skill import rejects existing IDs with CONFLICT. Current working path is to edit the shadow-branch file directly and rely on kspec skill render to auto-commit the change. A kspec skill update-content --file or kspec skill edit command would close this gap.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When modifying a user-visible string that is also explained in adjacent prose/comments, authors frequently update the string but miss the surrounding comment — even when the comment is literally the next few lines. Observed this cycle on src/parser/doctor.ts: the success-message suffix 'agent-specific locations' was audited, but the stale comment 10 lines above that described status.skills.rendered as 'only counting agent-specific locations' was missed, causing the reviewer to flag the same inaccuracy twice (once as a user-visible blocker, once implicitly in the codebase). Pattern: when changing a user-facing string, grep the surrounding file for other occurrences of the replaced phrase before committing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When a review finds 'this message/output is too vague', add a regex-based regression test that codifies the specificity invariant — not just assertions on the specific new strings. In task-doctor-accuracy, the original ac-all-actionable test only asserted non-empty guidance, which let vague 'kspec setup' messages persist across code paths. Adding a test that rejects any warning/error guidance matching /\\bkspec setup\\b(?\!\\s+--)/ (unless paired with a specific alternative command) converts a per-string fix into a durable invariant. This pattern generalizes to any audit-style task ('audit every X'): the fix should include a test that codifies the rule so future additions cannot regress.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Repo-level `kspec validate` output during review is dominated by unrelated pre-existing schema, alignment, and AC-coverage issues, which makes it slow to determine whether a failure was introduced by the current task. A task-local or diff-aware validation view would make review evidence much cheaper to collect.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For doctor/setup/upgrade changes, pairing full-suite results with a direct fresh temp-project repro (`init` -> `setup` -> `doctor --json`) quickly confirms the real user path stays warning-free and catches false-positive regressions more reliably than source-only inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a task description explicitly names the failure mode (e.g., "string values never match exact-equality semantics"), writing a test that exercises that specific mode via the real matching function — not a shape check — is straightforward and catches the regression the task was written to prevent. Prefer pulling the actual production function (matchesFilter) into the test over reimplementing equality checks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review cycles still inherit unrelated kspec validate noise from unchanged repo state. In this session, validation failed on .kspec/modules/meta.yaml modules[0].traits.0 expecting a string and also warned about an orphaned skill directory, so the review had to record a non-required failing check and explain it away before approving unrelated code. This should be triaged into either fixing the stale metadata or making validate/reporting distinguish pre-existing repo issues from task regressions more cleanly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Setup scaffolds that create runtime-active config (hooks, rules, dispatch entries) need tests that exercise the semantic contract, not just creation shape. Default reflection hook scaffold passed creation/idempotency/removability tests but shipped without a turn_count filter; bug would only have surfaced in a multi-turn session. Pattern: at least one test should drive the scaffolded artifact against representative event payloads.
observations.author: @claude
