observations.content: Task notes that record investigation findings and implementation plan before review materially reduce reviewer rediscovery time; in this session they let review focus on diff verification and runtime behavior instead of reconstructing intent.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot directly checkout the integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. Reviewers have to fall back to manual git -C merges against the primary worktree, adding avoidable merge-path complexity.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Large raw task dumps and verbatim agent-failure payloads in task notes create prompt pressure for later review and reflection passes. This session included a prompt-too-long failure note embedded with a large task dump, which added context volume with little durable value.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: CRUD-completeness discoverability gap across durable-record types. kspec task delete exists (@cmd-task-delete, implemented) but kspec plan delete does not (being added via @task-plan-delete-command). Neither the reflecting agent nor the 2-week-old inbox item 01KMV62W knew task delete existed until a search surfaced it. Suggests (a) CRUD completeness across record types (plans, tasks, inbox items, specs, reviews, plans, observations) should be audited for gaps, and (b) discoverability of delete/cleanup commands is lower than expected. Not urgent, but worth an audit pass once the plan delete task ships.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Initial bias toward treating an e2e failure as pre-existing flake based on PR #912's 3-failure-then-success pattern. Only user insistence surfaced the real race-conditional SessionWatcher bug. Heuristic: N consecutive same-signature failures → treat as bug-until-proven-flake, not flake-until-proven-bug. Reproduce locally before declaring flake.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Extending the existing DISPATCH_ENV_VARS/AGENT_ENV_VARS allowlist in tests/helpers/cli.ts with a third RUNNER_ENV_VARS category (CI, KSPEC_TEST_PROGRESS, FORCE_COLOR, NO_COLOR) cleanly fixed the vitest-under-CI subprocess test failures. Pattern: when asking where should env sanitation live, check whether an existing allowlist pattern fits before creating a new mechanism. PR #913 commit 1fcf3f62e.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: @daemon-file-monitoring ACs covered FD budget (active-only watching) and attach policy but missed the adjacent concern of cache-freshness notifications for newly-added non-active sessions. Task description even asserted freshness was 'sufficient' without an AC backing it. Systemic gap: spec ACs written alongside an implementation can under-cover adjacent contracts at the refactor seam (watcher↔cache, cache↔API). Consider adding an 'adjacent-contract checklist' prompt to writing-specs skill — for each AC, ask what downstream system reads the signal this AC governs, and does an AC protect that signal?
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plan delete implementation followed inbox delete + item delete patterns cleanly. The task description detailed 13 implementation steps with specific edge cases — this level of spec detail eliminated ambiguity and produced a first-pass implementation that passed 29/30 tests immediately.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fixture-backed CLI tests can claim AC coverage for git-ref and shadow-history guarantees without exercising real git refs or a real shadow worktree. Reviewing plan delete found ac-48/ac-49 tests passed while only proving the plan record disappeared. The system needs a clearer behavioral-test pattern or helper for commands whose guarantees depend on real git/shadow state.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: New shadow branch operations (like plan-delete) can silently fall through to the default commit message format in generateCommitMessage() without any lint or test catching the missing case. The plan-delete case was missing from the switch in shadow.ts, producing raw plan-delete slug instead of Delete Plan: @slug. Consider adding a test or lint that verifies all commitIfShadow call-site operations have explicit mappings.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The shadow-commit-call-site-regression.test.ts pattern (real shadow worktree via kspec init + inspecting git log in .kspec/) is a reliable way to behaviorally verify shadow commit messages. Reused this pattern successfully for plan delete ac-48 coverage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: src/daemon/ build requires manual file registration in scripts/build-daemon.cjs. Each new .ts file needs an explicit copyFileSync line or the daemon dist/ silently omits it. The build script enumerates files individually rather than copying the directory, so new modules are invisible until manually added. Hit during shadow-sync-manager.ts extraction — vitest passed but daemon E2E failed with Cannot find module. Consider changing build-daemon.cjs to copy all src/daemon/*.ts files via directory enumeration.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Extracting daemon functionality into src/daemon/ (alongside entity-cache.ts) works well for modules that need both vitest and daemon-build access. The sessionSyncSchedulers Map pattern (idempotent start/stop helpers + registration callback wiring) is a proven template for per-project daemon services.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When testing fire-and-forget async callbacks in daemon tests (e.g. onProjectRegistered in WebSocket resolution), vi.waitFor() on the spy call count is insufficient. The spy registers as called before its async body resolves, so side effects (like a scheduler appearing in the map) are not yet visible. Must wait for the side effect directly: await vi.waitFor(() => expect(map.has(key)).toBe(true)) instead of await vi.waitFor(() => expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)). This applies to all daemon callback tests where the callback does async work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Re-export shim pattern for daemon cross-package modules: when adding new modules to src/daemon/ that server.ts imports as sibling (./module.js), add a re-export shim at packages/daemon/src/module.ts that forwards exports from ../../../src/daemon/module.js. The build script copies the real implementation over the shim during staging. This matches shadow-sync.ts and session-sync.ts precedent.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Concurrency test gap: async idempotency checks can pass sequentially while still allowing duplicate work under overlapping calls. Add or document a standard pattern for Promise.all-style concurrency tests on scheduler/registration helpers so ac-16 style guarantees are verified behaviorally.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on shadow sync multi-project task was efficient: the reviewer's reproduction case (Promise.all with two concurrent starts) made the TOCTOU race immediately clear, and the in-flight promise map pattern was a clean one-variable fix. Well-specified review blockers with reproduction steps dramatically reduce fix cycle turnaround.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 4 for shadow sync task: concurrent start/stop coordination required multiple review cycles because each cycle only fixed the race scenario the reviewer demonstrated (cycle 3: start-start race via inFlightStarts, cycle 4: start-stop race via cancelledStarts). Upfront analysis of all interleaving scenarios (start-start, start-stop, stop-start, stop-stop) would have caught both in one pass. When implementing async lifecycle pairs (start/stop, register/unregister), enumerate all interleaving combinations before committing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Deferred-promise test pattern (configGate) cleanly reproduced the exact race window described in the review. Creating an explicit async gate in the mock lets the test control the interleaving precisely — start fires, gate holds, stop runs, gate releases, assertion checks. This pattern is reusable for any async lifecycle race condition test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Multi-cycle fix loop on shadow-sync-manager concurrency: 5 review cycles to cover all start/stop/re-start race orderings. When implementing async resource lifecycle with cancellation (start→stop cancellation, concurrent starts), enumerate ALL orderings in the initial test plan — including start→stop→re-start — rather than discovering them through incremental review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Vite virtual module pattern (virtual: prefix + resolveId/load hooks) works well for build-time content bundling in the web UI. Used for docs rendering — scans filesystem at build time, emits JS module with all content embedded. Clean separation: plugin handles I/O, SvelteKit routes consume the virtual import. Pattern is reusable for other build-time bundled content.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shutdown-path tests for async schedulers/registries should cover in-flight starts, not only instances already present in a map or registry at shutdown time. This session's daemon review found a real ac-17 gap after all tests were green because the shutdown test only drained current schedulers and did not model an async start resuming after shutdown began.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Shadow sync manager required 6 fix cycles due to layered concurrency races (idempotency, concurrent starts, stop-during-start, shutdown-during-start). Each cycle exposed one new edge case. Future async manager patterns should consider a global shutdown flag checked at every await point, rather than building up per-operation cancellation sets incrementally across review cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: stopAllShadowSync() fix (cycle 6) was clean and fast because the cancelledStarts mechanism from cycle 4 was composable — shutdown just needed to mark all in-flight keys as cancelled. Good example of incremental concurrency primitives paying off even when the overall cycle count is high.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review worktrees cannot complete the manual merge flow when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. This session had to fall back to 'git -C /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch checkout dev && git -C /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch merge --no-ff ...'. Merge tooling should detect the active worktree for the target branch and execute there automatically.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle for docs rendering was clean: extracting pure utility functions (filterSectionEntries, resolveDocsLink) into a separate file from virtual-module-dependent code enabled direct behavioral testing without mocking. Pattern: when a module depends on a build-time virtual module, keep pure logic in a sibling *-utils.ts file that both the main module and tests can import.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review triage can be misled by cached npm test results that report a failure until a real fresh rerun is forced. In this session, a cached skill-rendering failure disappeared on npm test -- --fresh, so regression classification required extra work. Treat cached failures as provisional in review guidance or tooling until a fresh rerun confirms them.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Checking AC coverage at the rendered behavior layer, not only helper/unit tests, prevented an incorrect approval in this docs review. The route-level acceptance criterion was only covered by a helper test, and reading the page behavior alongside the test annotations surfaced the mismatch quickly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon SPA route allowlist is fragile — every new SvelteKit route requires manually adding to the spaRoutes array in packages/daemon/src/server.ts. This has caused silent 404s at least twice (01KM6BGY and docs rendering). A wildcard fallback or auto-generated route list from SvelteKit would prevent this class of bug.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2E test screenshots provided immediate diagnosis of the SPA route bug — the raw NOT_FOUND text (vs SvelteKit 404 page) was the key signal that the daemon was rejecting the route before SvelteKit could handle it.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can surface false-negative verification failures when generated web UI build artifacts are missing. In this session, npm run build initially failed before succeeding on rerun, and npm test repaired a missing dist/web-ui/index.html automatically. Capture review-snapshot environment readiness explicitly so reviewers do not misclassify artifact-prep noise as task regressions.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Diff-first review plus independent verification with full npm test, targeted docs E2E, and built-artifact checks caught a real user-facing docs regression that passing tests alone missed. This is a strong review pattern for web UI changes that bundle static content.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Bundled docs can preserve repository-relative markdown links like ../INSTALL.md and ../AGENTS.md even though the built web UI does not ship those files. Add validation or behavioral coverage that every rendered docs link either rewrites to a bundled docs route or resolves to a shipped static asset, so offline/public docs do not expose 404 links.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Fix cycles 3-4 on docs-rendering both addressed the same underlying issue (out-of-tree .md links) but at different layers — cycle 3 fixed the click handler, cycle 4 fixed the rendered href. When a reviewer reports broken behavior, trace the full data path from source (markdown content) through transformation (renderer) to presentation (click handler) before committing a fix. Fixing only the layer closest to the symptom often leaves the root cause intact.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing touched Svelte UI files still requires reading production build warnings, not just focused unit/E2E results. In this docs review, the blocker came from a new Svelte a11y warning on the changed route component even though docs unit tests and docs E2E both passed. Treat build-output warnings on touched UI files as first-class review evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle 7 on task-docs-rendering was clean: single blocker (heading anchor hash not updating), one-line fix + E2E test, full suite pass, resubmitted in one pass. The existing E2E test patterns made adding the new test frictionless.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer workflow gap: when kspec validate fails only because of known repo-wide baseline debt, reviewers must manually classify it as non-blocking and hand-write review-check evidence. A dedicated review-oriented validate mode or baseline-aware check helper would reduce repeated reasoning and make approvals more consistent.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-thread creation via `kspec review comment --body` is brittle when the body contains backticks or markdown-style inline code. In this session the first attempt to record blockers was mangled by shell interpolation and had to be retried. A safer file-based body input or stdin mode for review comments/replies would reduce review friction and avoid corrupted review records.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Comparing `kspec validate` on the review snapshot against the integration base worked well during review. It distinguished a pre-existing validation failure from regressions introduced by the task and kept the review focused on actual branch-specific issues.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Docs section landing-page AC coverage can pass without verifying actual child-page links. In this review cycle, the section-structure test only asserted that rendered HTML contained a paragraph, so four section index pages shipped without the required stub child-page list and review had to catch it manually.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The kspec review/task integration worked cleanly in a detached reviewer snapshot: creating a fresh review, adding an anchored blocker, and submitting request_changes automatically closed the review and transitioned the task to needs_work with the new review_ref linked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix cycle 1 on task-docs-release-notes-rendering completed cleanly in a single pass. Reviewing all threads first, understanding the exact gap (isolated tests vs real config integration), then writing targeted tests with actual repo paths kept the fix focused and the full suite green.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot directly checkout the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree. The merge workflow should document or automate the safe path for merging approved task branches into the primary worktree's integration branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a feature depends on build-time wiring to canonical repository files, adding integration tests that use the real config paths and canonical source file closes review gaps quickly and gives high-confidence approval evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Placing cache mutation propagation at the TaskDataManager layer (applyTaskMutation) rather than individual CLI handlers or daemon routes ensures ALL task mutations get immediate cache consistency — single architectural chokepoint covers verdict transitions, task start/submit/complete, and batch operations.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Rebase-then-fix workflow for merge conflicts worked cleanly: rebasing onto dev surfaced conflicts in vite-plugin-docs.ts and vite.config.ts that were straightforward additive merges (both sides added new options). Tests immediately caught the slug collision from the integration, enabling a targeted fix.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cross-task synthetic slug collision: the docs-rendering task added a synthetic release-notes entry at slug "release-notes", while the docs-scaffolding task added docs/release-notes/index.md which normalizes to the same slug. Neither task could anticipate this. The collision was only discoverable at merge time. Consider adding a uniqueness check in the vite plugin for slug collisions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Docs navigation helpers now mix two section-classification schemes: normalized section pages are grouped by entry.path while synthetic entries are still modeled as repo-root files. That let release-notes/changelog fall out of the Release Notes section and into a sixth root Docs section, even though the task test suite stayed green because the tests only modeled directory-backed entries.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review, small executable repros against pure helpers (groupDocsSections and filterSectionEntries) exposed a real docs regression faster than rerunning the full UI stack. Keeping core docs logic in pure utilities made the blocker easy to prove with concrete evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer merge in detached dispatch snapshots still requires a manual detached-head plus git update-ref workaround when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. A review-aware merge path should handle advancing the integration branch ref safely without forcing the reviewer to improvise git plumbing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For docs reviews, probing the built virtual manifest directly gave fast, high-confidence verification of section order, exclusions, and synthetic entry grouping. This was a more reliable first check than starting from UI inspection alone and should be repeated for similar docs-surface reviews.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In fix cycles, kspec task submit requires in_progress state but the task is in needs_work. Worker must run kspec task start before kspec task submit every fix cycle — an extra ceremony step. Consider allowing submit directly from needs_work, or having submit auto-transition through start when the source state is needs_work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cache invalidation via delete (fall-through to disk) is a reliable pattern for keeping synchronous fast-path methods consistent without requiring async reload. Used in applyTaskMutation for historyDetails — minimal change, correct behavior, no signature changes needed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot directly switch to the integration branch when that branch is already active in another worktree. The review merge workflow should document or automate merging through the existing target worktree so approved reviews do not require ad hoc git -C discovery.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Docs content tasks: testing through the vite plugin manifest (docsPlugin + load virtual:docs) provides reliable behavioral verification of page content. Tests load the real docs/, parse the manifest, and assert on entry slugs, content strings, and rendered HTML. Pattern established in web-ui-docs-rendering.test.ts for @docs-getting-started-section ac-1/2/3.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Immediately after a review verdict moved a task from pending_review to needs_work, human-readable `kspec task get` output still showed the older status while `kspec task get --json` and the activity log reflected the transition correctly. This creates uncertainty during review closure and suggests a caching or formatting inconsistency in task-get presentation after review-driven state changes.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: Detached review worktrees cannot always follow the documented merge flow because the integration branch may already be checked out in another worktree. Review/merge guidance should document a supported detached-checkout/update-ref path or provide a helper command for this case.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing detached-review merge friction observations @01KPQHA6 and @01KPPRVW; keeping the earlier tracking rather than adding another copy.

observations.content: Docs landing-page regressions were caught cleanly by validating child markdown links against the generated docs manifest instead of asserting that link strings exist. This behavioral check is a stronger pattern for future docs navigation coverage.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC-focused docs rendering tests provided strong behavioral coverage for the Getting Started docs work: they verified reading order, next-link sequence, executable command blocks, and shadow-branch guidance, which made the fix-cycle review quick and objective.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots cannot merge directly into an integration branch when that branch is already checked out in another worktree. This session required a manual handoff to the main dev worktree path after approval, which adds avoidable merge friction to the review workflow.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: The full npm test run streamed passing suites during review but did not return promptly enough to provide a crisp final result artifact from the snapshot. Review evidence would be easier to record if the test runner guaranteed a stable machine-readable summary before shutdown.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: Parallel Explore agents are effective for multi-domain research tasks. Launching 4 agents simultaneously (one per subsystem) gathered comprehensive context for 8 concept pages in ~90 seconds. Pattern: when a task requires understanding 4+ distinct areas of the codebase, launch parallel Explore agents with focused questions rather than sequential exploration.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-thread and review-check payloads are brittle when passed through shell-quoted CLI invocations. In this session, initial  and  commands had their bodies/evidence corrupted by shell expansion when the text contained command-like strings, and the review had to be cleaned up with corrected file-backed payloads. This is a repeatable agent workflow hazard for review automation and reinforces the need for safer payload-input patterns on review commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-thread and review-check payloads are brittle when passed through shell-quoted CLI invocations. In this session, initial kspec review comment and kspec review check commands had their bodies/evidence corrupted by shell expansion when the text contained command-like strings, and the review had to be cleaned up with corrected file-backed payloads. This is a repeatable agent workflow hazard for review automation and reinforces the need for safer payload-input patterns on review commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Docs review caught 3 factual inaccuracies in Concepts pages (wrong agent count, missing plan status, false session-start claim). Validates that docs content benefits from the same review rigor as code — reviewers verified claims against actual schema, setup-defaults, and CLI output.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Docs rendering/content tests should verify that referenced kspec commands or help paths actually exist. This review caught multiple broken guide commands because the tests only validated markdown structure and link presence, not CLI correctness.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Creating review comments through shell-passed command strings is brittle when the body contains command-like text or shell metacharacters. This session produced malformed duplicate review threads before cleanup; a safer structured or file-based payload path would reduce corruption risk.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing docs against the live CLI plus running the full npm test suite quickly separated factual documentation drift from broader code regressions. That combination made the review decision high-confidence and efficient.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch review workspaces in this environment do not guarantee  on PATH even though task prompts, skills, and AGENTS instructions tell agents to run  directly. Add PATH setup for the CLI in dispatched workspaces or document  as the supported fallback so review/task commands do not fail mid-session.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: Dispatch review workspaces in this environment do not guarantee the kspec CLI is on PATH even though task prompts, skills, and AGENTS instructions tell agents to run kspec commands directly. Add PATH setup for the CLI in dispatched workspaces or document npm exec -- kspec as the supported fallback so review/task commands do not fail mid-session.
observations.author: codex@openai

observations.content: In dispatch worktrees, kspec may not be on PATH — agent had to fall back to npm exec kspec -- mid-session. This is a recurring pattern that could be addressed by the bootstrap or workspace preparation step ensuring PATH includes the project bin.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Agents authoring documentation guides fabricated CLI commands (review create, review thread, review submit, plan approve, derive) that do not exist in the shipped CLI. The fix cycle caught this, but the pattern suggests docs-authoring tasks need a convention: verify every kspec command reference via --help before committing. Could be enforced by a test that extracts bash code blocks from guide pages and validates each kspec subcommand against the CLI help tree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle for docs-guides-content was efficient: review JSON gave full thread context, CLI --help verification caught all discrepancies, and structural AC tests (goal/prereqs/steps/verification/--help) passed without modification because they test document structure rather than specific command names.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing documentation changes against live CLI help and direct command execution caught user-facing command drift that the structural docs tests missed. This review pattern is effective for command-heavy docs because it distinguishes markdown shape from command correctness.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The current docs guide coverage checks markdown structure but not whether documented commands and branch assumptions match the live CLI surface. This let invalid commands and a hardcoded integration-branch assumption survive until manual review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Docs content fix cycles benefit from a specific pattern: (1) fix content issues directly in markdown, (2) add behavioral tests through the docs rendering pipeline (docsPlugin + renderDocsMarkdown) rather than source scanning, (3) test rendered HTML structure not raw markdown. The getting-started test suite provides a reliable template for new section coverage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec review get truncates thread body text in default display, forcing agents to use --json to read full blocker descriptions during fix cycles. A --verbose or --full flag for human-readable full-text output would reduce friction.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle workflow (read review JSON, fix both files, reply+resolve threads, note, submit) completed efficiently in a single pass with no wasted investigation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 3 on docs-guides-content resolved cleanly in one pass: all 3 blocker threads shared a single root cause (--help pointer mismatch). Re-verifying all guides against AC-3 after fixing the flagged file confirmed no other issues — defensive full-scope check prevented potential cycle 4.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Docs content tests currently verify structure and cross-links but not whether recovery procedures name commands and task states that actually work. In this review, troubleshooting pages passed docs tests while recommending kspec setup where the product expects kspec upgrade, and kspec task submit from a pending_review stale-review scenario where submit cannot run. Add a docs validation pattern or helper that checks command availability and state-transition correctness for procedural docs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec review get truncates thread bodies in default output. Agents in fix cycles must use --json and parse manually to read full review feedback. A --verbose or --full flag would surface complete thread content directly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parallel explore agents for codebase research (e.g., two agents investigating different subsystems simultaneously) significantly accelerated fix cycle turnaround for docs troubleshooting task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review system (codex reviewer) validated CLI command correctness in documentation before publication. During troubleshooting docs review, reviewer tested kspec review refresh against a task-subject review and confirmed it rejects with 'Refresh is only supported for code subjects.' This caught a broken recovery procedure that would have left readers with another error instead of a fix. The review-as-verification pattern for docs content is effective at catching commands that don't match the system's actual behavior.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots in this repo may not expose the kspec CLI on PATH, forcing reviewers to translate every command to node dist/cli/index.js before they can execute the review workflow.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The reviewer merge workflow assumes the review workspace can checkout the integration branch directly, but that breaks when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree; reviewers need worktree-safe merge guidance or tooling.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: npm workspace hoisting silently drops devDependencies with optional platform-specific binaries (e.g. pagefind). 'npm install' succeeds but the package is missing from node_modules. Requires 'npm install --include=dev' to force installation. Affects any ESM-only package that uses optional deps for native binaries in a monorepo workspace.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detailed task descriptions with specific file paths, line numbers, function names, and reproducer steps enabled single-pass implementation with zero ambiguity. The bootstrap refactor task included exact removal targets, env var lists, and test specifications — work completed in one pass without any scope questions or fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle on bootstrap AC-11 tests was completed in one pass. Metadata field assertions (result.metadata.bootstrap.steps[].run) proved effective for verifying command fidelity without needing subprocess-level mocking — simpler, behavioral, and sufficient for the contract.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can hit a merge workflow gap: the documented reviewer merge flow says to check out the integration branch before merging, but in this session 'git checkout dev' failed because dev was already attached to the main worktree. Reviewers had to merge via the existing main worktree with a git -C <main-worktree> merge invocation instead. Consider updating the merge skill and dispatch reviewer guidance to handle integration branches already occupied by another worktree explicitly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Clean single-pass execution of a rename-and-narrow refactoring task (task-narrow-dispatcher-runtime-mode-env-isolation). Detailed task description with exact file paths, constant names, and doc comment content enabled direct implementation with zero ambiguity. 3 files changed, all 8297 tests passed on first run, no regressions. Confirms the pattern tracked in existing observations about detailed task descriptions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Well-seeded task descriptions with confirmed call-site audits, implementation sketches, and edge case enumeration eliminate research time and let the worker go straight to implementation. Task @task-gitignore-cover-file-lock-directory-suffix completed in a single pass with zero blockers thanks to this preparation.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can approve cleanly, but the manual merge step becomes awkward when the integration branch is already checked out in another worktree. This session had to merge into /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch via git -C after git checkout dev failed in the reviewer snapshot with 'already used by worktree'. A first-class kspec merge path for detached reviewer snapshots would remove that workaround.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Delegating long full-suite npm test runs to an awaiter agent while continuing targeted review work in parallel keeps the required verification gate intact without stalling the whole review session.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: buildTestSubprocessEnv() strips only a hardcoded subset of KSPEC_DISPATCH_* vars (KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_HEAD, KSPEC_SESSION_ID, etc). Tests that exercise dispatch environment contracts must manually strip remaining KSPEC_DISPATCH_* vars to prevent parent dispatch context from leaking. Hit directly in detached-reviewer-merge tests where KSPEC_DISPATCH_CANONICAL_BRANCH and KSPEC_DISPATCH_MERGE_TARGET leaked from the parent process. Fix: either expand the hardcoded list in DISPATCH_ENV_VARS (tests/helpers/cli.ts) to include all KSPEC_DISPATCH_* vars, or use a wildcard strip pattern.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer-side temp git repos with multiple worktrees were an effective review technique for detached merge mechanics: they made branch/ref behavior reproducible quickly and produced concrete evidence for blocker threads without touching the real integration branch.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Detached-review merge work can miss the detached snapshot contract when tests merge by live branch name instead of the recorded reviewed head, and when dirty-target checks only assert on coarse porcelain output. That leaves gaps around snapshot immutability and tracked-vs-untracked dirty state.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Fix cycle turnaround: both review blockers (over-broad dirty gate using porcelain instead of diff --quiet, and merging live branch tip instead of pinned canonical head) were addressed in a single focused commit with 3 new tests. Full suite clean. The spec-literal reading guidance in work-gates step 5 is validated — the issue was not reading the AC narrowly enough during initial implementation, and the reviewer correctly flagged the divergence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill helper payloads can be added under unsupported directories such as files/ and still pass tests when those tests execute templates/skills source paths directly. Existing skill distribution paths only ship references/, scripts/, assets/, and docs/, so source-tree tests can miss a real delivery gap. Reflection from review of @task-detached-reviewer-merge-helper: either extend the supported supporting-directory contract/renderers/build-plugin to include helper payloads explicitly, or require helper assets to live in an already-supported directory and add tests that exercise the shipped/rendered path.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Skill template supporting directories (references/, scripts/, assets/, docs/) are defined in code (SUPPORTING_DIRS constants) but not surfaced in agent-facing guidance. Worker placed a helper script in files/ which is not distributed. The CLAUDE.md skill source-of-truth section mentions templates/skills/ and .kspec/skills/ but not which subdirectories are valid. A one-line convention rule or CLAUDE.md note would prevent this class of review round-trip.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill distribution debugging: when a helper script exists in templates/skills/<id>/scripts/ but not in .agents/skills/kspec-<id>/scripts/, trace the three-stage pipeline: (1) template source in templates/skills/, (2) installed copy in .kspec/skills/ via install-core, (3) rendered output in .agents/skills/ via skill render. In dev worktrees, use 'npm run dev -- skill install-core' instead of the global kspec binary, since only the worktree source has uncommitted template changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review-time kspec validate remains dominated by repo-wide pre-existing schema and completeness failures, so reviewers have to manually downgrade it to non-blocking evidence even when the task diff is clean. A scoped validation mode for reviewed refs or changed files would make review checks much higher signal.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Inheriting well-structured uncommitted changes from a failed prior invocation worked smoothly: full diff review, AC verification, test run, commit, and submit completed in a single pass. The key enabler was that the prior agent's changes were coherent and complete — only the commit/submit step was missing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Behavioral test pattern for shipped skill content: copy templates/skills/<id>/ into a temp project via fs.cp, render through buildPromptWithSkills, and assert on rendered output. Avoids source-scanning while still testing that shipped skill source produces correct behavioral output. First used in supporting-file-references.test.ts for merge skill detached reviewer guidance.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshots can surface unrelated kspec validate schema/completeness failures from project meta/spec state, forcing reviewers to record manual optional failures instead of using validation as a clean review gate. Add a review-safe validation mode or scoped detached-review validation path.
observations.author: Codex

observations.content: kspec skill render --force regressed .agents/skills/kspec-merge/SKILL.md by overwriting the committed version with stale content. The render pipeline for the self-hosting project reads from .kspec/skills/ (which does not exist for core skills in this context) or falls back to the plugin, rather than reading from templates/. Supporting file changes in templates/ are not propagated to rendered outputs by the standard install-core + render flow.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Skill render hash computation (renderSkillBase in skill-render.ts) only includes SKILL.md content — supporting directories (scripts/, docs/, etc.) are not part of the hash. Changes to supporting files are invisible to drift detection and --force, causing stale rendered copies to persist silently.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task scope was well-defined with precise contradiction identification. Auditing existing surfaces (SKILL.md, dispatch.ts) before changing them confirmed they already enforced the correct policy, preventing unnecessary changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The session-reflect guidance documents 'kspec workflow show' without a run ref, but the CLI currently requires a run ref and errors with 'missing required argument "run-ref"'. Align the docs or make the CLI default to the single active run so the documented reflection flow works as written.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Running multiple kspec review check mutations in parallel can contend on project.reviews.yaml and cause a file-lock timeout; review record writes should be serialized or batched where supported.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Predecessor task baseline artifact pattern: when a multi-task plan has an investigation→repair dependency chain, having the investigation task produce a structured baseline document (e.g. plans/cruft-baselines/*.md) eliminates investigation overhead for downstream repair tasks. The repair task for broken spec refs completed in a single pass with zero re-investigation because the baseline task had already cataloged all broken refs, their owning tasks, and candidate repair targets.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Tests that manually patch project.tasks.yaml (lean index) to simulate terminal states (completed/cancelled) break when the validation read path switches from lean index to per-task directories. Found 5 such tests in automation-eligibility.test.ts during the validation-task-data-source task. No shared helper exists for patching both index and per-task files atomically. The patchTaskField() helper added in automation-eligibility.test.ts is a local fix — should be promoted to tests/helpers/cli.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Baseline artifact (plans/cruft-baselines/spec-catalog-health-validation-trust-baseline.md) from @task-catalog-health-baseline provided exact before/after metrics, making it easy to validate the fix addressed the root cause (Tasks checked: 0 → Tasks checked: N).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Batch-based spec creation with task retargeting: Using kspec batch for atomic item add + item ac add + task set operations in a single shadow commit is an effective pattern for spec repair tasks that need to create specs and retarget tasks together.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review fix cycle worked cleanly: precise blocker with reproduction scenario led to targeted fix (split try/catch), regression test, and full suite pass on first attempt. The structured review thread → reply → resolve → resubmit flow provides clear audit trail.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing validation from a detached snapshot exposed a source CLI dev-mode mismatch: `npm run dev -- task list --json` can fail with TaskDataManagerError `No storage backend registered for format split`, while `npm run dev -- validate --refs --json` can still exit successfully with `tasksChecked: 0`. For data-source validation work, this can hide the same class of trust failure the task is meant to prevent.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For validation data-source reviews, comparing `validate` output against a normal consumer of the same canonical model is an effective probe. In this session, source `task list` failing while source `validate --refs` returned `tasksChecked: 0` exposed a remaining fallback bug that the full test suite did not catch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review, pairing focused behavioral tests with target-spec completeness validation exposed a real AC coverage gap: the new tests passed, but excluding the file from coverage scanning meant @coverage-annotation-scope-boundaries still had all four ACs uncovered. This is a useful review pattern for coverage/config tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: SplitFileTaskBackend.loadAllTasks() silently swallows per-task parse/load failures (empty catch block at split-backend.ts:569). This makes every consumer that uses loadAllTasks() unknowingly operate on a partial dataset. Three consecutive fix cycles on the validation task were caused by this pattern — each cycle revealed a new code path that assumed loadAllTasks() returned the complete task set. Consider: (1) adding a loadAllTasksWithErrors() variant that returns Result<LoadedTask, {ulid, error}>[] so consumers can choose error handling, or (2) making loadAllTasks() itself return errors alongside successfully loaded tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch structured args for review check did not preserve optional-check intent: required:false produced a required check, so a non-blocking kspec validate evidence entry temporarily failed the review gate until corrected with direct --no-required.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The detached reviewer merge helper made manual_merge review completion reliable from a detached snapshot: after review gate approval it advanced dev and refreshed the occupied worktree without checking out the integration branch in the reviewer workspace.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC annotation scanner matches // AC: patterns inside string literals, not just real comments. Test files that contain fixture annotation strings in string literals get false matches. Current workaround: either exclude the file from scanning (loses real AC coverage) or use runtime string construction helpers (per-file boilerplate). A comment-aware scanner or a convention for fixture content would eliminate this class of issue.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, full npm run lint was not usable as a clean task gate because it reported unrelated repository baseline failures. Reviewer had to fall back to changed-file oxlint to verify the submitted diff did not introduce lint regressions. Consider tracking lint baseline debt or adding a branch-regression lint workflow so review checks can distinguish existing lint failures from task changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review, kspec validate --completeness emitted hundreds of baseline catalog warnings, so proving one spec had no coverage warnings required JSON output plus external filtering. A focused completeness validation filter by item/spec ref would make AC coverage review evidence easier and less error-prone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC annotation scanner only recognizes ac-* pattern for AC ids. Specs using named ACs (exit-code-constants, creates-isolated-copy, parent-pending-children-done, basic-multi-ref-syntax, etc.) produce false-positive blanket-ref warnings. 36 of the 38 remaining invalid annotations after wave-one repair are this category. Scanner needs to accept any non-whitespace token after the spec ref as a valid AC id.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC annotation scanner picks up secondary @-references from comment description text. E.g. // AC: @spec ac-1 — uses @short-ulid causes @short-ulid to be parsed as a separate annotation target. The scanner should only extract the first @-reference after the AC: marker, not subsequent @-mentions in the same comment line.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Classification-first approach for bulk AC annotation repair was highly effective. Running kspec validate --completeness -v to export all findings, spawning parallel research agents to classify every finding before making edits, then applying repairs mechanically by category. Reduced 227 invalid annotations to 38 (189 fixed) in one session with zero test failures.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review sessions can require splitting validation evidence when plain kspec validate fails from pre-existing catalog/schema state unrelated to a test-only branch. A documented review validation profile or gate would reduce ad hoc optional-check judgment while keeping task-scoped gates strict.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test took 1905s during review of a comments-only AC annotation diff. Review guidance may need a documented low-risk diff strategy using cached or sharded gates plus escalation to full npm test when behavior changes, so reviewers preserve rigor without unnecessary long waits.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec validate in .kspec-worktrees/ task worktrees reports Tasks checked: 0 because the shadow branch (.kspec/) is only attached to the root checkout. Dispatch workers doing validation-gate or verification tasks must run validation from the root checkout to get accurate task counts. This breaks the dispatch invariant that workers should run all commands from their assigned worktree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Baseline-then-gate plan pattern: capturing exact validation counts in an ephemeral baseline artifact before starting plan work, then running a final gate task that compares before/after counts, worked well for the spec-catalog-health-and-validation-trust plan. The pattern gives clear verification evidence and makes the final gate task straightforward. Worth replicating for future verification/cleanup plans.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached manual_merge reviewer snapshots can lack .kspec shadow state, so task-aware validation commands run from the assigned workspace report Tasks checked: 0 even when the root checkout validation has task data. This makes final-gate reviews harder when the task depends on before/after task validation counts; reviewers need either a supported root-validation helper or clearer dispatch guidance for this case.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When a test file must be excluded from coverage scanning (due to inline fixture strings confusing the line-based scanner), the fix pattern is to create a companion non-excluded test file with programmatic data that exercises the same behavioral APIs. Applied successfully for @ac-annotation-integrity-reporting in tests/ac-annotation-integrity.test.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Automated review mutations can produce mixed audit authorship unless every review check/comment explicitly passes --author. In this review, batch-created checks and the evidence-log comment were attributed to the human default while the verdict was attributed to codex, which makes the review record harder to audit. Consider inferring automated reviewer identity from session/runtime context or making reviewer workflows require explicit --author consistently.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: AC id format enforcement task (task-enforce-ac-id-format) completed cleanly in a single pass. The plan document provided clear boundary decisions. Shared pattern approach (regex + Zod schema + CLI validation + error message) kept the implementation minimal (33 insertions across 4 production files). Only 2 existing tests needed updating, confirming the codebase was mostly already conformant.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: validateSpecItemRecursive in validate.ts had its own inline nestedFields list that drifted from NESTED_ITEM_FIELDS in yaml.ts, missing traits. Duplicated constants are a recurring bug vector — consider exporting NESTED_ITEM_FIELDS and reusing it in validate.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec trait list --json omits acceptance_criteria from output, forcing per-trait kspec item get calls to inventory trait ACs. item list --json includes them for specs but not traits.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Inventory-then-repair pattern for annotation normalization: programmatic catalog scan first to confirm state, then targeted annotation fixes with before/after kspec validate --completeness metrics. Reduced blanket refs from 36 to 0 in one focused pass.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can make direct shadow-state inspection misleading: git -C .kspec failed because .kspec was not present in the snapshot, while kspec CLI commands still resolved shadow state correctly via project configuration/dispatch context.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The detached reviewer merge helper worked cleanly for manual_merge review completion: after review approval it merged the canonical task branch into dev and refreshed the occupied worktree without requiring branch checkout or manual merge commands in the detached snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task @01KQ99Z7 was created for a validation error already fixed by @task-fix-meta-traits-schema-validation (commit f0e6d14c3 on dev). The error appeared only because the globally installed kspec binary was compiled from an older snapshot without the fix. The dispatch engine assessed the validation failure using the stale binary and created a new task for an already-resolved issue. Pattern: when dev branch has code fixes that the running binary lacks, dispatch can create false-positive tasks for symptoms that are already fixed. Relates to @01KPA0Q5 (duplicate dispatch observation).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Coverage scanner treats AC annotation patterns inside JavaScript string literals as real annotations. Tests that construct fixture annotation strings must use string concatenation (e.g. "//" + " AC: ") to avoid false positives. This is non-obvious and caused the fix cycle on task-align-ac-annotation-format-tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: No warning when AC annotations are placed in files excluded by kspec.config.yaml exclude_patterns. The annotations are silently invisible to completeness validation. A diagnostic like "N annotations found in excluded file X — these will not count toward coverage" would catch this class of error at validate time.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The ac-annotation-integrity.test.ts pattern (programmatic data tests in a non-excluded file) provided a clear model for the fix cycle on task-align-ac-annotation-format-tests. Having an existing precedent for non-excluded coverage tests made the solution immediate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch atomic operations handle complex data repairs well. Used a 10-step batch to relocate an inline trait definition: remove refs, delete, recreate at new location, add ACs, restore refs. The --dry-run flag validated all 10 steps before execution, and atomicity ensured no partial state. This pattern is reliable for catalog restructuring.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review verification, npm test initially failed before running tests because the dispatch environment had NODE_ENV=production. scripts/test.cjs detected missing direct dependency pagefind and attempted npm ci, but npm inherited production-mode omit behavior and still skipped devDependencies, so the auto-fix failed with the same missing dependency. Manual workaround was NODE_ENV=development npm_config_omit= npm ci followed by NODE_ENV=development npm_config_omit= npm test. Consider making the test runner's dependency repair path explicitly include dev dependencies or emit a diagnostic that names NODE_ENV/npm omit as the cause.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Annotation-scanner tests can accidentally create scanner-visible fixture annotations when comments or string literals contain literal '// AC:' examples. Recent review cycles required moving real task AC annotations out of an excluded scanner-test file and rewording a quoted fixture pattern. Consider codifying a safe runtime-construction helper or testing convention for annotation fixture lines.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Gate verification tasks work well as lightweight validation passes over dependency chains. Running kspec validate with --completeness separated AC id format issues from unrelated missing-coverage debt clearly. The pattern of recording remaining warning categories and their owners in a task note provides good audit trail for future triage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-only tasks (adding ACs, updating implementation status) are efficiently handled with kspec batch — 9 AC additions + 3 status updates completed in 2 batch calls with atomic commits, versus 12 sequential CLI invocations.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix cycle 1 for task-centralize-ac-id-patch-validation resolved in one pass. The reviewer correctly identified a false-coverage test (CLI-proxy claiming parser-layer coverage). The existing spec-item-mutation-serialization test provided a clear pattern for the replacement. Surgical fix: 1 file changed, no production code modifications.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reflection workflow instructions showed `kspec workflow show` without a run ref, but the current CLI required `run-ref` in this detached review session. This caused an avoidable failed command during reflection and suggests command examples should include explicit run refs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For high-risk schema/passthrough validation reviews, combining parallel code exploration with a concrete temp-fixture reproduction command caught a nested catalog AC-id bypass that the full test suite did not cover.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: SpecItemPatchSchema (SpecItemInputSchema.partial().passthrough()) does not include nested catalog fields (features, requirements, etc.) as known schema properties — they pass through as unknown data. Each new validation concern for nested structures requires adding a separate recursive walk (e.g. collectNestedAcIdErrors). Consider a NestedCatalogPatchSchema or extending SpecItemInputSchema to include optional nested catalog arrays with their own validation, so schema-level safeParse catches nested issues without custom helpers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review blocker thread with concrete reproduction case (exact CLI command + observed vs expected behavior) made fix cycle efficient — one focused commit addressing the exact gap. Reviewers providing reproduction commands directly in thread bodies accelerates fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, `npm run lint -- src/cli/commands/item.ts src/parser/yaml.ts tests/ac-id-patch-validation.test.ts` still ran the hardcoded full lint target (`oxlint src/ tests/ packages/ ...`) and surfaced unrelated pre-existing errors. Reviewers need a first-class changed-file lint command or script that scopes exactly to supplied files so review evidence does not depend on remembering to bypass npm with `npx oxlint <files>`. Search before capture found no existing tracking for this lint-script friction.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Recursive nested validation (e.g. collectNestedAcErrors for acceptance_criteria in nested catalog items) required 5 fix cycles because the initial implementation only validated happy-path array shapes. Each cycle revealed one more invalid input shape: wrong container type (non-array), missing required fields, partial structures. Convention candidate: when writing validation for recursive/nested structures, enumerate ALL invalid shapes (wrong type, empty, null, partial) upfront alongside the valid case, not just the happy path.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer feedback during fix cycles for task-centralize-ac-id-patch-validation was consistently precise and actionable: each blocker thread included the exact file/line, a fixture repro command, and clear description of the gap. This made each fix cycle fast to resolve (single targeted change + tests). Effective pattern for automated review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch with item set --status triggers interactive cascade prompt when target has child items. Batch context is inherently non-interactive, but the cascade prompt blocks execution. Workaround: explicitly pass --no-cascade in batch args. Consider making batch imply non-interactive mode or auto-apply --no-cascade.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review pattern worked well: for @task-daemon-web-ui-startup-asset-coherence, durable review checks plus an explicit evidence log made the merge gate clear, while a long-running test awaiter and a focused route-order explorer provided independent verification without blocking manual diff review.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: During a detached dispatch review, creating a follow-up bug task for a pre-existing test failure caused the new task to appear in_progress under the current session, even though the reviewer only intended to record future work. The reviewer had to reset the task back to pending. Dispatch/review workflows need a way to create follow-up tasks without immediately claiming or starting them, or guidance/tooling should make this behavior explicit.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When a task renames AC ids on a spec (e.g. ac-5 → ac-host-config), downstream test/source annotations referencing the old ids silently become stale: kspec validate --warnings-ok exits 0 because the missing-AC findings are warnings, only visible with -v. This task's first cycle was kicked back as needs_work for exactly that pattern (3 stale @config-daemon ac-5/ac-6 annotations across tests/parser/config.test.ts and src/parser/config.ts). Workers performing AC-id renames should rg @<spec-ref> ac-<old-id> across the repo and update annotations in the same atomic commit, OR run kspec validate --warnings-ok -v | grep 'Missing AC' filtered for the renamed spec. Evidence: @01KQWZZFDFPSHHNAGVB8NAXJRJ fix cycle 1 review @01KQXCSWEA8NKFB23BDNCR8DVC.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Default validation output can hide task-relevant AC coverage gaps during review: kspec validate --warnings-ok exited 0 and summarized only the first warnings, while kspec validate --warnings-ok -v | rg '@config-daemon|Uncovered' exposed five uncovered @config-daemon ACs that required needs_work. Reviewers of spec/AC mutation tasks should run verbose validation filtered to the touched spec before approving, especially when worker notes claim zero missing-AC warnings. Evidence: review @01KQXEP9M670DA29T38FQVM57C for @01KQWZZFDFPSHHNAGVB8NAXJRJ.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: Plans that add ACs to a spec whose implementation is owned by other pending tasks in the same plan create unsolvable AC coverage gates. The reviewer requires behavioral coverage for new ACs, but the worker cannot add coverage without doing the implementation tasks work, which is scope creep. Observed on @task-update-config-daemon-endpoint-ac (3 fix cycles). Resolution requires either re-sequencing the plan (implementation tasks first, then spec ACs) or splitting the spec update into per-AC slices that ship with each implementation task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec validate --warnings-ok (without -v) hides per-AC uncovered counts. Previous fix-cycle agent claimed kspec validate --warnings-ok now reports zero @config-daemon missing-AC warnings, but kspec validate --warnings-ok -v showed 5 uncovered ACs. Workers and reviewers need a default that surfaces uncovered ACs by spec, or task-work skill should explicitly require running validate with -v before submit.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewers can flag missing behavioral coverage as MUST-FIX blockers on spec-update tasks even when the new ACs explicitly depend on downstream implementation tasks in the same plan for testability. Pattern: task @01KQWZZFDFPSHHNAGVB8NAXJRJ added 6 new ACs to @config-daemon, then went through a fix cycle and a block requiring a manual unblock note from Hermes clarifying that spec-update task scope is the spec mutation, not behavioral coverage owned by sibling tasks. The review-gates / work-gates checklists do not distinguish task type (spec-update vs implementation) when applying AC-coverage MUST-FIX criteria. Systemic risk: any plan that splits 'add ACs' from 'implement and cover ACs' across separate tasks will repeat this churn.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-update review scope ambiguity: in staged plans that intentionally update specs before implementation, current review guidance can treat downstream-owned behavioral AC coverage gaps as blockers. This task needed multiple review cycles and manual plan reconstruction before approving that @config-daemon ac-host-default, ac-connect-host-config, and ac-connection-metadata were owned by downstream endpoint resolver/startup tasks. Consider triaging reviewer guidance so stale/invalid annotations remain blockers, but expected uncovered ACs may pass when the approved plan explicitly assigns implementation coverage to later tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Worker preemptively applied the @01KQXEKC remediation: after renaming @daemon-proxy-detection ac-port-file-check to ac-connection-metadata-check, immediately ran kspec validate --warnings-ok and updated the two stale annotations in tests/cli-daemon-proxy.test.ts (one to ac-connection-metadata-check, one to ac-legacy-port-file-fallback) in the same submission. This avoided the needs_work cycle the prior dependent task @task-update-config-daemon-endpoint-ac hit for the same pattern. Evidence: spec mutation commit + annotation fix commit on dispatch/task/task-update-cli-daemon-proxy-endpoint-ac/01kqwzzg, validate confirmed no remaining stale ac-port-file-check references before submit. This is the @01KQXEKC friction observation closing its feedback loop on the next instance.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review friction: after renaming an acceptance criterion, stale references to the removed AC id can remain in source-level/block-comment AC coverage summaries while kspec validate --warnings-ok still exits 0 because validation has broad pre-existing warning noise and does not make this rename-specific drift obvious. In @task-update-cli-daemon-proxy-endpoint-ac, the worker note claimed no ac-port-file-check references remained, but rg found references in src/cli/daemon-proxy.ts and the test file header. This is distinct from helper-level false coverage (@01KNEDZ0): the repeatable gap is stale removed-AC references surviving in non-standalone annotation summaries after spec renames.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: During session reflection, kspec workflow show required an explicit run ref and the default human-readable output did not include the current step title/body or suggested next command. This made the reflection workflow require JSON output or remembered context to continue smoothly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task completion auto-synced @multi-directory-daemon from in_progress to implemented after completing a narrow spec-update task (@task-update-daemon-lifecycle-endpoint-ac). That spec had newly added endpoint metadata ACs and downstream implementation tasks still pending, so completion status sync can create false implemented status for broad specs when spec-update tasks are linked directly to them. Consider making task completion skip implementation-status sync for spec-update/catalog tasks or require an explicit flag before marking the linked spec implemented.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Semantic AC rename invalidates prior test coverage even when annotations remain syntactically valid. When a spec rename is a semantic shift (e.g. @daemon-proxy-detection ac-port-file-check renamed to ac-connection-metadata-check, where the new AC text requires reading metadata + connect_host routing rather than a port file), repointing existing test annotations forward to the new AC IDs creates false coverage: kspec validate passes because targets resolve, but tests still exercise the old behavior. Distinct from @01KQXZKM which addresses syntactic stale-reference leftovers; this pattern produces validation-clean but behaviorally-misaligned coverage. Triggered the review changes_requested on @01KQWZZG0BC74MJ02VRH2V9W4C with 4 of 5 blockers being semantic-mismatch annotations.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Deferring AC coverage to implementation tasks beats repointing annotations forward. When a spec evolves to describe forward-looking behavior split across multiple implementation tasks (e.g. @plan-daemon-network-endpoint-contract spans the spec-update task plus @task-shared-daemon-endpoint-resolver / @task-daemon-startup-bind-host-metadata / @task-centralize-cli-daemon-clients), removing the misleading metadata-keyed annotations and adding short comments indicating where the AC will be covered is cleaner than fabricating coverage. The implementation tasks naturally add proper behavioral tests when they land. Pattern accepted by reviewer in fix-cycle 1 of @01KQWZZG0BC74MJ02VRH2V9W4C.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cross-package shim pattern (used by packages/daemon/src/shadow-sync-manager.ts and now packages/daemon/src/{pid,endpoint}.ts) is undocumented. Pattern: a committed shim re-exports from src/daemon/<name>.ts via the relative '../../../src/daemon/<name>.js' path, then scripts/build-daemon.cjs copies the source into the staging dir AND overwrites the shim with a sibling import ('./<name>.js') so the bundled daemon does not reach back into src/. Future agents adding a 4th shared module currently have to read scripts/build-daemon.cjs to understand this. A short note in AGENTS.md or a comment block at the top of scripts/build-daemon.cjs would prevent every cross-package addition from re-deriving the pattern.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Full vitest runs intermittently fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for dist/daemon/endpoint.js (or similar dist artifacts) because tests/daemon-build.test.ts runs `npm run build:daemon`, whose scripts/build-daemon.cjs starts with fs.rmSync(dist/daemon, { recursive: true, force: true }). Other tests run kspec subprocesses concurrently that import from dist/daemon/*.js via the dist/cli/pid-utils.js shim. Hit this twice this session on full-suite runs while cli-daemon-proxy/cli-serve/daemon-endpoint suites all pass cleanly in isolation. Either scripts/build-daemon.cjs should rebuild atomically (write to a stage dir, rename) or daemon-build.test.ts should run in a serialised group / under exclusive lock so concurrent dist consumers do not see a missing-file window.
observations.author: @claude
observations.resolution: Resolved by serializing tests/daemon-build.test.ts via vitest.config.ts heavySerialSuites in commit 62bc34089. The build script's fs.rmSync(dist/daemon) window can no longer race with concurrent dist/daemon/index.js spawns from the default pool because heavy-serial runs after default drains. Atomic-rebuild (stage + rename) was the alternative, but serialization matches the existing pattern used for other side-effecting suites and required no build-script changes.

observations.content: Behavioral coverage for ac-clients-use-metadata via in-process http.createServer plus per-test process.env.HOME isolation worked cleanly in tests/cli-daemon-proxy.test.ts: drop a real daemon.connection.json into tempDir/.config/kspec/, point detectDaemon at the live server's port, and assert result.endpoint.source === 'metadata'. No source scanning, no real daemon spawn, no fixture maintenance. Same pattern for the legacy-port fallback case using only daemon.port. Worth replicating for any future CLI-resolves-X-from-config tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch fix-cycle invocations that time out can leave substantial uncommitted work in the worker worktree. The next invocation receives bootstrap=prepared and a [AGENT-TIMEOUT] note but no explicit signal that the working tree is dirty — the new agent has to run git status, evaluate the partial diff, decide whether to keep, fix, or discard, and reconstruct the prior agent intent from code alone. Concrete impact this session: the prior invocation had a 565-line, 12-file diff implementing all three blockers but never committed; recovery required reading every changed file and running targeted tests before deciding to keep the work. Possible improvement: dispatch prompt could include git status snapshot, or the dispatch engine could auto-checkpoint WIP commits at task-note boundaries during a long invocation so next-agent context is durable.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review cycle pattern that worked: using prior review records plus a full fresh suite and an isolated failed-suite rerun made it possible to distinguish a real implementation gap from a concurrent build race, and produced evidence precise enough for fix-cycle workers.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon lifecycle startup arguments drifted between explicit serve start and implicit auto-start. Endpoint-related config flags need a shared spawn argument builder or equivalent single path so configured host/connect_host behavior cannot be wired in one lifecycle path and missed in another.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The CLI shared endpoint import now depends on dist/daemon/endpoint.js, while build:daemon deletes and recreates dist/daemon. Concurrent CLI subprocesses can fail during that window, so shared runtime modules used by the CLI should not live behind transient daemon build output unless rebuilds are atomic.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon spawn args are hand-rolled in two CLI locations: src/cli/index.ts maybeAutoStartDaemon() and src/cli/commands/serve.ts startServer(). Both build a Node-style argv list of daemon flags (--port, --kspec-dir, --host, --host-explicit, --connect-host, etc.) from the same resolved daemon config, but independently. Same drift class surfaced twice on @01KQWZZH7R9W7WKATZXFB61MPC: cycle-1 review caught serve.ts not forwarding --host/--connect-host (fixed); cycle-3 review caught the auto-start path still not forwarding them. Future endpoint flags will drift the same way unless arg construction is centralized. Suggested resolution: extract buildDaemonSpawnArgs(daemonConfig, kspecDir, opts?) helper colocated with buildDaemonChildEnv (already shared). Both call sites call the helper; new flags get added in one place.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fallback/recovery tests that pre-create the failure condition can pass for the wrong reason. Example: cycle-2 e2e test pre-bound 127.0.0.1:PORT and asserted ::1 fallback — passed only because the bug treated EADDRINUSE the same as EADDRNOTAVAIL. The test read as if it verified ac-default-ipv6-fallback but actually verified the bug. Generalizable rule: any test that induces a recovery path by triggering ONE failure type must also assert the recovery was driven by that failure mode's spec-defined classification, not just that recovery occurred. Reviewers should look for this; workers should write probe/test pairs that distinguish error classes (e.g. assert reason='port_in_use' on EADDRINUSE before asserting fallback only on 'address_unavailable').
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Merge helper fails on duplicate annotation-correction commits. When two parallel task branches both fix annotations for the same renamed AC ids, both will land effectively-identical commits via different paths. The merge helper sees them as a textual conflict even though git rebase --reapply-cherry-picks (default) recognizes them as equivalent. Observed in fix cycle 5 of @01KQWZZH7R9W7WKATZXFB61MPC: dev had f26b5726/0e475fe9, task branch had c28548f35/1986fbf74 — same patches, different commits. Cost one fix cycle for purely mechanical resolution. Possible fix: have the merge helper attempt rebase with cherry-pick detection before declaring a conflict.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cycle-7 review of @task-shared-daemon-endpoint-resolver showed that explicit review evidence checks plus the detached reviewer merge helper make complex multi-cycle approvals auditable: the reviewer could verify prior blockers, record deterministic gates on @01KQYQE9, approve, merge into dev via the helper, and complete the task without manual branch switching.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Upstream task fix cycles can absorb work scoped to dependent tasks. When task A is in review and the reviewer requests changes that nominally belong to dependent task B, the fix commits implement Bs work under As task ID. The downstream worker on B then inherits a task whose stated work is mostly already done, causing scope confusion and risk of either (a) duplicating annotations, or (b) missing residual gaps. Observed during work on task-daemon-startup-bind-host-metadata after task-shared-daemon-endpoint-resolver fix cycles wired the resolver into startup, metadata, and clients.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC annotation gaps surface when test coverage is added under one task but the spec ACs are formally owned by another task. Behavioral coverage exists, but kspec validate/task get does not surface that the tests are annotated under a different ULID.
