Observed: @daemon-server ac-1/ac-9/ac-10/ac-external-bind-warning had behavioral coverage in tests/cli-serve.test.ts but no annotations until this task added them — even though the coverage was authored as part of the upstream task fix cycle.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reading task description literally caught a real ordering requirement (point 4: write daemon metadata after the server is listening) that the existing implementation violated despite passing review on the upstream task. Pattern: when a task description is directive and explicit (not just descriptive), treat each point as a requirement even if the existing code or prior reviews differ. The defensive check protected against a reviewer rejecting the work for not meeting the stated requirement.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Mirror-with-parity-test pattern for sharing code between Node and browser: when a Node-only module mixes pure helpers with platform-specific I/O (fs/net/os), creating a small browser-side mirror file containing only the pure helpers — locked in by a parity test that imports both modules and asserts they produce identical results across a fixed input matrix — keeps the two in lockstep without forcing the Node source to become platform-neutral or refactoring the build pipeline. Used in @task-centralize-web-ui-daemon-endpoints to give the web UI access to formatHostForUrl/buildDaemonUrls/normalizeDaemonHost/isIpv6Literal from src/daemon-shared/endpoint without importing node:fs/node:net at browser bundle time. Trade-off: a maintainer must update both files when adding a helper, but the parity test fails loudly on drift.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec serve start --detach + spawnSync(timeout: 30_000) interaction can hang the test runner for 30+ seconds when the daemon child dies in atypical patterns (e.g. fixed-EADDRINUSE path that exits non-zero quickly). The existing IPv6 fallback test using identical scaffolding completes in 2.5s under the cycle-1 bug because the daemon child silently succeeded (wrote metadata, stayed alive). Under the fix the daemon correctly dies on EADDRINUSE but spawnSync still wedged. Workaround: spawn the daemon binary directly via spawn(node, [dist/daemon/index.js, ...]) for tests asserting daemon-process behavior. Root cause of the wedge not fully diagnosed — likely an interaction between the parent CLI polling loop and detached-child reaping that warrants investigation if more startup-failure tests are added.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Verifying a regression test by temporarily disabling the fix and confirming the test fails — then restoring the fix — gives high confidence the test will catch a future regression of the same shape. Did this for the cycle-1 EADDRINUSE blocker: with awaitListenSuccess commented out, the daemon hung past 10s and the new test failed with the expected symptom (exitCode null). With the fix restored, the test passed in 577ms. Worth replicating for any regression test where the failure mode is async/timing-sensitive.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon Origin allow-list (buildAllowedOrigins / WS beforeHandle) and Host allow-list (localhostOnly) are derived independently with different rules and silently drift. localhostOnly always accepts Host: localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 regardless of bind host, but the Origin builder only added the resolved api_url for same-origin. A user opening the production daemon UI at http://localhost:<daemon-port> while bound to 127.0.0.1 got a same-origin browser context the daemon refused at WS upgrade (cycle-1 review blocker on @task-centralize-web-ui-daemon-endpoints). Fix mirrored the loopback aliases manually in buildAllowedOrigins, but the invariant 'Origin allow-list ⊇ (Host allow-list mapped to URLs on the daemon port)' is still hand-coded across two functions with no shared source. Future additions to the accepted-Host set will silently break production same-origin again unless someone remembers to mirror them in the Origin builder. Candidate fixes: derive both from a single 'accepted endpoints' record, or add an integration test that asserts every Host the daemon accepts has a matching Origin entry on the daemon port.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts showed a repeat flaky close-code/internal-error failure during combined targeted daemon/web-ui review runs. In this session it failed in beforeEach, then passed when rerun alone and in the full npm test suite; the prior review evidence for the same task reported the same pattern. This causes review retry/triage overhead and makes targeted test failures less immediately actionable. Investigate runtime fixture startup/cleanup or test isolation around createRuntime/start/stop for that scenario.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Discovering proxySkipCommands (init/serve/help/setup/upgrade/release-notes/shadow/doctor/clone-for-testing/batch/agent/event in src/cli/index.ts) is non-obvious for test authors writing daemon-endpoint regression tests. Commands NOT in the skip list go through /api/command proxy before the inline action handler runs — so tests for schedule/task daemon helpers must either configure the mock daemon to fail /api/command (forcing fallback for non-mutating commands) or expect the proxy hop. Discovered through debugging during task-daemon-endpoint-regression-tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: For verifying CLI commands honor metadata-advertised daemon URLs, a child-process recording mock daemon (recording-daemon.cjs) that writes one JSON object per request to a JSONL audit file works cleanly with spawnSync-based kspec() test helper. Combined with binding the mock to 127.0.0.2 (loopback alias on Linux, skipped elsewhere) the recorded Host header gives strong behavioral proof the URL came from metadata, not a hardcoded 127.0.0.1. Pattern reused across 11 CLI integration tests in cli-daemon-endpoint-regression.test.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing tasks that require exhaustive daemon endpoint consumer coverage currently depends on ad hoc source inventory. In this review, the green endpoint-focused and full suites still missed two coverage gaps until I manually searched apiUrl/wsUrl/getRunningDaemonClient/fetch/WebSocket call sites. A lightweight checklist or generated inventory for daemon endpoint consumers would make future worker and reviewer coverage decisions less error-prone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content:
Fire-and-forget CLI helpers that run AFTER a daemon proxy hop cannot be exercised behaviorally via the CLI subprocess test path. When the CLI proxies a mutating command through /api/command, the daemon executes the mutation server-side and the inline helper (e.g., postDispatchEvent in src/cli/commands/task.ts firing /api/agent/events) never runs in the CLI process. So a subprocess-based behavioral test never invokes the helper's fetch/WebSocket call, and a regression that hardcoded a different URL would still pass.

The only way to get behavioral URL-contract coverage is to add a test-only re-export (e.g., '_postDispatchEvent' alias) and invoke the helper directly from the test process with seeded daemon.connection.json metadata. Justifying coverage as transitive ('the source line uses endpoint.apiUrl + getRunningDaemonClient is unit-tested') is insufficient — reviewers reject it because both legs can pass while the integration is broken. Discovered during fix cycle 1 of @task-daemon-endpoint-regression-tests on review @01KQZ3YZVDEDPQ7K3ZJ20J2QXP — the prior cycle's explanatory comment in tests/cli-daemon-endpoint-regression.test.ts was the explicit rejection trigger.

Suggested mitigation: when adding a daemon-side fire-and-forget helper that has no production caller other than a proxied CLI command, ship the test-only re-export alongside the helper from day one.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When a fire-and-forget CLI helper (e.g., postDispatchEvent firing /api/agent/events from src/cli/commands/task.ts) needs URL-contract regression coverage but its only production callers are proxied CLI commands (so subprocess CLI tests can't reach the helper after the proxy hop), the right fix is to extract the helper into a dedicated production module (e.g., src/cli/dispatch-events.ts) imported by every production caller. The behavioral regression test then imports the function from the new module — the export is consumed by 6+ production sites, not a test seam. This satisfies work-gates (no test-only exports from src/) and resolves the conflict raised by friction @01KQZ6JZ and inbox @01KQZ7F5. Pattern demonstrated on @task-daemon-endpoint-regression-tests cycle 2 fix, which removed the prior _postDispatchEvent re-export from src/cli/commands/task.ts in favor of the production-owned extraction.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing AC-retag-only patches worked best when explicit AC annotation searches were paired with surrounding behavior reads. In this session, kspec item get plus rg for old/new AC IDs and direct fixture context review caught false AC coverage that validate and npm test could not detect.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Detached reviews of tasks that mutate specs in shadow state require manual correlation between task notes, kspec item get output, code diffs, and AC annotations. A review affordance that surfaces spec-shadow deltas next to the code diff would reduce reviewer effort and lower the chance of rubber-stamping retagged annotations.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Daemon-backed test fixtures get implicit HOME-isolation coverage from the daemon's writePidFileExclusive on $HOME/.config/kspec/daemon.pid — when ambient daemon state isn't isolated, the test child fails with EEXIST and 'Daemon already running'. Any successful test daemon spawn therefore behaviorally proves HOME isolation works; no separate assertion is needed. Confirmed in @task-implement-shared-daemon-test-fixture: a manual spawn without HOME override failed with EEXIST, while the helper-driven spawn (HOME pointed at the temp .home via createIsolatedKspecHome) succeeded in 378ms. Useful pattern for reviewers verifying isolation: presence of a successful real-daemon test is itself the gate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When a diagnostic field (e.g., 'last X response') must appear in failure output regardless of which readiness/startup code path ran, sample the endpoint once in the catch block instead of threading per-probe state through every code path. Demonstrated by tests/helpers/daemon.ts startTestDaemon: removing HealthProbeState/CacheProbeState (~77 lines of plumbing) and replacing them with a single sampleEndpointDiagnostic() call in the catch block (with a 2s AbortController timeout) both expanded diagnostic coverage (custom-mode failures previously left lastHealth/lastCacheStatus null) and shrank code. Reusable pattern for any startup-readiness helper that must produce uniform diagnostics across multiple readiness modes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC annotation placement inside JSDoc/block-comment headers caused a fix-cycle bounce on @task-implement-shared-daemon-test-fixture. The kspec convention requires standalone line comments, but the validator silently drops annotation-shaped text inside /** ... */ blocks rather than flagging it. Pattern: an agent writes 'AC coverage:' as a JSDoc summary expecting the listed refs to count; they don't, and the only signal is post-hoc reviewer or 'kspec validate --completeness' output. Inbox @01KR2EQY proposes a validator-level warning to make this loud.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Default readiness probes in tests/helpers/daemon.ts (probeHealth, probeCacheReady) await fetch() without AbortController. A pre-bound non-HTTP TCP server on the daemon port (e.g. EADDRINUSE regression scenario) causes fetch to hang indefinitely inside the readiness loop, defeating the bounded-readiness contract. The escape hatch (custom child-exit probe) requires the test author to know the default would hang. Caught this only after the cli-serve EADDRINUSE migration timed out at 45s.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared daemon test fixture (tests/helpers/daemon.ts) made the websocket-protocol, daemon-build, and cli-serve EADDRINUSE migrations straightforward. registerCleanup + extraEnv + custom readiness probes covered every per-test variation needed. Default Node runtime + isDaemonRuntimeAvailable for optional Bun made runtime parity trivial — node-required path stays green on machines without Bun.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review evidence logs currently have no first-class place in review records. During clean automated reviews, the required evidence log is best recorded through kspec review comment, but that creates an unresolved nit thread on an otherwise approved review. This makes approved review records look noisier than they are and repeats for every clean review that follows the evidence-log rule. Consider a dedicated review note/evidence-log command or guidance to attach evidence without creating an unresolved thread.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The daemon manifest validator accepts kynetic 1.0 with tasks_file: project.tasks.yaml at load time, but /api/tasks routes throw "monolithic task storage format has been removed" only at runtime. Test authors writing in-process daemon API fixtures discover this incompatibility by hitting a 500. Adding a manifest-load-time warning when 1.0 + tasks_file is detected, or rejecting it outright with an upgrade hint, would prevent re-discovery on every new test that touches task routes. Surfaced while writing tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts — captured the constraint in a LEGACY_INLINE_MANIFEST docstring but a code-level signal would be stronger.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: For helper-extraction tasks, write one representative consumer test first (the most complex one, e.g. the cache-consistency verdicts test), drive helper API design from it, then mechanically migrate siblings. Prevents the helper-grows-to-fit-one-test antipattern where the second consumer reveals an awkward API. Validated in tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts standardization: verdicts test was hardest, drove getEntityCache option + setupInlineFixtures shape, then websocket and input-validation migrations took minutes each.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Cleanup contract tests for fixtures that allocate artifacts in a shared dir (e.g. /tmp) should snapshot the dir BEFORE start, AGAIN after the fixture has run (to identify new files created by THIS instance), and assert post-stop() that only those new files were removed. Asserting that ALL pre-existing matching files disappear couples the test to other runs' leaked state and produces false failures (caught while writing the cleanup test for tests/helpers/mock-daemon.ts startMockDaemon child-process mode). Pattern: scope assertions to artifacts created during the test, not to dir history.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During session reflection, a kspec workflow notes payload containing literal command examples in backtick characters was subject to shell command substitution before reaching kspec, stripping the intended text. Existing development convention warns about dollar signs, angle brackets, and multiline payloads, but should also mention backtick command substitution or recommend file-based payloads for literal command text.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: For fixture-contract lint rules (e.g. tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js), the path-based allowlist + per-statement oxlint-disable-next-line --reason combo lets one rule serve two distinct exception classes: canonical helpers and rule-fixture files get blanket exemption by path (no annotations needed in growing helper code), while ad-hoc per-test exceptions stay narrow and self-documenting at the offending line. Avoids the cleanup-escape-hatch antipattern where a rule’s real intent (use the shared fixture) is satisfied by an unrelated structural property (cleanup is registered).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Quick verification trick for new oxlint rules: run npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json tests/ 2>&1 | grep -E "Found .*errors" once with the rule, then git stash and rerun to capture the pre-change count, then git stash pop. Identical totals prove the rule change introduced zero new violations without parsing per-file diffs of the full lint output. Used on the daemon-test-harness-guardrails rule extension.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During lint-rule reviews, tiny synthetic projects that invoke the actual oxlint rule are a strong verification pattern. They exposed false negatives for argv-style detached daemon starts, localhost URL variables, and broad or undocumented disable comments even though the submitted tests and full suite passed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session reflection: For static lint-rule reviews, small synthetic oxlint probes against temp files were highly effective. They exercised the actual rule outside the submitted fixture tests and exposed both the scoped localhost identifier false positive and the broad tests/helpers allowlist gap.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Session reflection: Review evidence/check recording is still manually assembled from multiple command outputs and prose snippets. A helper that turns common review commands, synthetic repro commands, and test/lint summaries into review check/comment payloads would reduce reviewer bookkeeping while preserving audit detail.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Identifier tracking in lint rules must be scope-aware from the start. The no-leaky-test-daemon rule used a file-global Set<string> for localhost URL bindings and produced silent false positives across distinct lexical scopes (separate it() blocks reusing const url, inner-block shadowing, let reassignment, parameter shadowing). Took two review cycles to fully surface — cycle 1 added variable-bound URL detection on top of the same flat Set, cycle 2 had to replace the whole tracking layer. Future identifier-tracking rules should default to per-scope binding records (scopeNode + position + value-property) rather than a name-only Set, even when the first use case looks single-scope.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review success pattern: custom oxlint/static guardrail rules are easiest to verify when tests create synthetic temp projects, run the real oxlint JS plugin against path-scoped fixture files, and pair focused positive/negative diagnostics with one real-codebase zero-diagnostic check. In @task-enforce-daemon-test-fixture-usage this made daemon guardrail behavior reviewable across direct daemon spawn, detached serve cleanup, localized disables, scoped localhost URL tracking, and narrow helper allowlists without relying on source-scanning assertions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Vitest's describe-level { timeout: N } sets testTimeout only — it does not inherit into hookTimeout (default 10s). Tests that build a heavy fixture in beforeEach (e.g. shared daemon: spawn child + load + cache-ready probe) reproducibly hit the 10s hook timeout under shared-worker contention even when describe declares 60_000. Symptom is a cryptic 'Hook timed out in 10000ms' that points at the beforeEach line, not the slow operation. Fix is to pass timeout as the second arg to beforeEach explicitly: beforeEach(async () => { ... }, 60_000). Hit this on tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts during validation of the daemon fixture standardization plan; the same gotcha will recur for any future test that startTestDaemon() in a per-test hook. Worth noting in tests/ conventions or a comment in tests/helpers/daemon.ts so the next author does not rediscover it.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Regression-test-only task slicing conflicted with review merge gates: @task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions intentionally added active failing tests for a later fix task, but review policy correctly requires no introduced npm test failures before merge. Future plans should either pair failing-before-fix tests with the implementation that makes them pass, mark regression-only artifacts as non-mergeable, or define an explicit gate/lifecycle for them.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review friction: this dispatch cycle had a test-only regression task whose submitted branch intentionally left one new test failing until a dependent fix task. Review policy correctly rejected the red branch, but the plan structure made that outcome predictable. Consider a tracked convention or workflow support for regression-test-only tasks: either pair the fix in the same mergeable branch, mark the task as expected-red and non-mergeable, or route it through a dedicated validation path that cannot be approved for integration while tests fail.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KR3XY2, which already captures the same regression-test-only task slicing conflict with review merge gates. Keeping @01KR3XY2 as the canonical unresolved observation.

observations.content: Review gate pattern worked well: reading the diff before notes, then running the focused failing suite twice and the full suite produced clear evidence that the submitted branch introduced a deterministic red test. Recording both failed checks plus an anchored blocker made the needs_work transition unambiguous.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Cross-task regression-first task splits (regression tests on one task, rule fix on a dependent task) can keep the integration-branch merge gate green by encoding the failing-before-fix tests as it.fails() in vitest. The assertions still execute live (so the captured classifier gaps stay covered as evidence), but the modifier flips pass/fail polarity so today's failures count as the expected outcome. When the dependent fix lands and assertions succeed, the it.fails modifier itself fails, forcing the dependent task to remove .fails before merge — preserving the plan's anti-silent-weakening intent without breaking npm test on the regression-only branch. Validated end-to-end on @task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions fix cycle 1: 6 failing tests → 6 passing as expected-failure, full suite 2402/2402 suites pass.
observations.author: @claude
observations.resolution: Cycle 2 review disproved this. Bare it.fails() is non-selective: under Vitest, ANY thrown assertion in the body counts as the expected failure, so a generic parser/helper failure (or any unrelated oxlint crash) satisfies the marker too. The validated pattern that survives review (cycle 3) is selective expected-failure: regular it() + a helper that runs the post-fix assertions, catches their throw, and re-asserts the EXACT current bug shape — so an unrelated failure re-throws and fails the test. Captured as a new success observation.

observations.content: Plan structures that pair an "add failing test" task with a separate "fix the helper" task collide with the no-failing-tests merge gate. Plan @plan-daemon-test-fixture-hardening split @task-add-real-daemon-startup-failure-tests (lands the contract test) from @task-fix-real-daemon-startup-failure-handling (implements the fix), and the first task's description told the worker to land a test that fails. Reviewer (correctly) blocked the first branch on the failing test. Resolution required combining the two tasks into one branch. Either plan templates need to mark the test-task as needing combined merge with the fix task, or the project needs a convention for landing contract tests without regression (it.todo / it.fails / skip-with-reason).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Selective expected-failure pattern for cross-task regression-first splits: instead of bare it.fails(), use a helper like expectClassifierGap(result, assertPostFixBehavior, assertKnownGapShape) that (1) runs an oxlint-ran-cleanly precondition rejecting non-{0,1} exit codes and panic/parse-error/module-not-found output, (2) calls assertPostFixBehavior which runs the AC's required post-fix assertions (exit code AND rule name AND message fragment) and is expected to throw today, (3) on throw, runs assertKnownGapShape which re-asserts the EXACT current bug shape; mismatched shapes (parser failure, partial fix) re-throw and fail the test, and (4) if assertPostFixBehavior succeeds, the helper throws an explicit error directing the dependent fix task to remove the wrapper. Validated on task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions cycle 3: passes the 6-test selective regression suite today, full suite 2402/2402 green, and the cycle-2 reviewer concern (it.fails too permissive) is resolved by construction. Forcing function preserved without sacrificing test selectivity.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec validate on a single dispatch branch reports ACs as uncovered when a sibling dispatch task on a separate branch carries the matching annotations. This blocks review even when the task description explicitly delegates that coverage to the sibling. Concrete repro: cycle 2 review of @01KR3W7Q0H2FVXHDJ51WCFAVNN was blocked because validate flagged @daemon-test-guardrail-precision missing ac-direct-daemon-entry-invocations-flagged and ac-unrelated-subprocesses-not-reported, whose coverage was scoped to sibling task @task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions (still in pending_review on its own branch). Workers must either annotate existing behavioral tests on their own branch or duplicate the sibling's failing-before-fix regressions (which then guarantees a merge conflict at the same end-of-file describe block).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Submitted task using bare it.fails() for failing-before-fix regression tests, missing that observation 01KR3ZR8 on the sister regression-first task @task-add-guardrail-classification-regressions had been disproven in cycle 2 review hours earlier. Default reading of the original commit 3f1ee8ce0 looked correct (it explicitly endorsed it.fails() with a doc-block contract); the cycle-2 disproof and cycle-3 selective replacement (commit 84c897b69 with expectClassifierGap helper) only became visible by reading meta observations. Generalisable lesson: when adopting a precedent from a sister task, re-check meta observations on that task at submission time, not just the originating commit — review-cycle disproofs land as observations, not commit message reverts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Refactor cycle saved one fix-cycle round trip. Caught the bare-it.fails() concern via /kspec:reflect search before reviewer applied the same critique that bounced the sister task to needs_work in cycle 2. The reflect skill workflow (search before propose) surfaced observation 01KR431R recommending selective expected-failure; pattern was reusable verbatim with the helper renamed to expectMockDaemonHygieneGap and gap-shape assertions matched to the mock daemon hygiene gaps (child still alive after malformed-stdout/timeout; ambient KSPEC_DAEMON_* still readable in child env). Validated selectivity locally by injecting precondition + gap-shape mismatches, both of which correctly re-throw — so the reviewer concern is resolved by construction before review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Forcing-wrapper pattern for regression-first task splits worked cleanly. The predecessor task (@task-add-mock-daemon-failure-contract-tests) wrapped each post-fix assertion in expectMockDaemonHygieneGap(assertPostFixBehavior, assertKnownGapShape): when the dependent fix lands, assertPostFixBehavior succeeds, the wrapper throws a self-describing error telling the dependent task exactly what to do ("Remove expectMockDaemonHygieneGap() and let the post-fix assertions stand"). This is stronger than bare it.fails — under it.fails ANY thrown assertion satisfies the regression, including unrelated helper errors. The forcing wrapper validates the EXACT current gap shape, so a generic spawn or fs failure cannot satisfy by accident. Reusable for any future regression-first/fix-second task pairs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Lint warnings (oxlint) can accumulate silently across tasks because the worker quality gate does not fail-on-warning. Found two pre-existing consistent-function-scoping warnings in tests/helpers/mock-daemon.test.ts that landed in the predecessor task without surfacing. Caught only because I happened to run npx oxlint on the changed files manually. A reviewer following the same workflow would not necessarily notice either. Consider either: (a) fail-on-warning in the worker quality gate, or (b) surface the warning count in the standard test runner output so workers see it without an explicit lint step.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Lifecycle cleanup tests can pass while missing the exact before-return contract if they wait after the awaited call before checking process liveness. For ACs that say a fixture stops a child before returning failure, tests should assert immediately at the return boundary and only use delayed cleanup as a fallback, not as the main proof.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of @task-fix-mock-daemon-cleanup-env-hygiene, a direct node --import tsx probe against the malformed-startup path disproved a passing test suite by checking process liveness immediately after startMockDaemon returned. Direct probes are useful review evidence for lifecycle timing contracts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing static lint-rule classifiers benefited from custom synthetic probes beyond the committed fixture tests. In the daemon guardrail review, a hand-built oxlint probe for exec/execSync direct daemon entry launches found an AC gap after the focused tests and full suite passed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Resolved during reflection cleanup: duplicate of existing observations @01KR2VYF/@01KR310Q for synthetic oxlint review probes and @01KR2YBHWS for review evidence/probe helper friction.

observations.content: Static oxlint rule reviews currently require hand-rolling temporary config and synthetic test files to probe edge-case classifier behavior. A reusable review probe helper or documented recipe would make these checks faster and more repeatable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Resolved during reflection cleanup: duplicate of existing observations @01KR2VYF/@01KR310Q for synthetic oxlint review probes and @01KR2YBHWS for review evidence/probe helper friction.

observations.content: Tests can claim AC coverage while asserting a weaker condition than the AC's wording, especially for temporal/ordering ACs ('before X', 'while Y', 'after Z'). Concrete case: @daemon-test-startup-failure-hygiene ac-owned-child-stopped-after-startup-failure says 'fixture stops the child BEFORE returning failure'. The first-cycle test waited 200ms after startMockDaemon returned null, then asserted isProcessAlive(pid)===false. That passes whether the helper kills the child before OR up-to-200ms-after returning, so the bug (resolve null synchronously after SIGTERM, child still alive on return) slipped through CI. The reviewer caught it only via an independent process.kill(pid,0) probe with no grace window. Pattern to watch for: 'await x; await sleep(N); expect(...)' — sleep before the assertion may indicate the test is asserting an eventual-consistency property when the AC requires synchronous-on-return. Mitigation: when AC contains 'before/while/on return', the assertion should fire on the same tick as the boundary, not after a setTimeout/wait.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon-entry classifier in tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js shipped through 3 sequential fix cycles for one task — each cycle the reviewer probed a child-process API family the rule didn't cover (cycle 1: missed the direct-executable spawn-like form spawn(DAEMON_ENTRY, …); cycle 2: missed the exec/execSync shell-string form). The spec phrasing 'every child-process API that can launch the daemon entrypoint' is generic, and neither the spec ACs nor tests/lint-daemon-test-guardrails.test.ts enumerates the Node child_process families the rule must handle (spawn, spawnSync, execFile, execFileSync, fork, exec, execSync), so each missing family was discovered incrementally instead of up front. Future classifier extensions that claim to cover 'every X that does Y' would benefit from an explicit family enumeration in the spec or a coverage matrix in the test file so missing entries fail at submission time, not at review.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing static classifier rules with an adversarial negative probe caught a false positive that targeted positive regressions missed: exec("echo dist/daemon/index.js") proved the daemon-entry detector was matching incidental shell tokens rather than launched behavior. Repeat this pattern for future lint/classifier reviews: include a harmless command that mentions the suspicious token and must not trigger.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Pinning a test-helper boundary with executable assertions (404 for routes outside helper scope, smoke for routes inside) converts the docstring into a regression-checked contract. Used in tests/daemon-api/helpers.test.ts createTestApp boundary block: /api/health, /api/projects, /api/debug/cache-status, /api/diff, /api/refs, /ws -> 404; non-loopback Host -> not 403; /api/tasks -> 200. Future drift (someone quietly adds a route to the helper, or removes one) fails explicitly instead of silently invalidating the docstring. Pattern reusable for other test helpers in the project.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon test fixture readiness probes that poll user-facing API endpoints can be misled by disk-fallback paths that mask cache state. /api/tasks returns cache_status=ready when the entity cache is undefined (cacheDomainState undefined → toCacheStatus → ready), so polling it during the daemon-startup window before registerEntityCache runs yields a premature match. Fix: route fixture-internal readiness probes to /api/debug/cache-status which reports domains=null until the cache is actually registered. Pattern: prefer cache-state-aware diagnostic endpoints over user-facing list endpoints for readiness signals.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review verification, running a focused test as 'npm test --fresh <file>' caused npm to treat --fresh as an npm config flag, emitting warnings and not forwarding the flag to scripts/test.cjs. Focused test evidence then needed caveats. Future testing guidance should show the correct npm script argument-forwarding form when combining --fresh with file filters.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing static classifier changes benefited from manual behavioral probes around adjacent parser/tokenization boundary cases, not just the submitted regressions. In @01KR3W7PPVDFR8F03VQ6J54M3K, targeted tests covered runtime flags and process["execPath"], but small oxlint probes for Node options with separate values found that node --require ./register.js dist/daemon/index.js and node -r ./register.js dist/daemon/index.js were still accepted, while node --eval dist/daemon/index.js false-positive reported. For future guardrail/classifier reviews, include a short manual probe matrix that checks neighboring positive and negative executable-position shapes.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When implementing static-analysis classifier rules that match runtime-invocation shapes (e.g. tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js exec/execSync runtime form), prefer enumerating the documented Node/Bun option classes (standalone flags, value-consuming flags with separate-or-bundled values, eval-mode flags, -- separator, runtime-reference forms like process.execPath / process['execPath']) before writing predicates. The daemon-test-guardrail-precision rule converged in 7 review cycles, with each cycle revealing a previously-unmodelled invocation shape (runtime-form, direct-executable, exec/execSync shell strings, shell-token in unrelated executable position, process.execPath, process[execPath], runtime flags, value-consuming flags + eval mode). Several of these were discoverable upfront from Node CLI documentation; modelling them as a closed set first would compress fix cycles for future classifier work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Static-analysis precision rule fix cycles repeat because each cycle's reviewer probes expose a SHAPE permutation the worker hadn't enumerated. Task @01KR3W7PPVDFR8F03VQ6J54M3K (no-leaky-test-daemon classifier) went 9 fix cycles, each closing one shape: cycle 1 added DAEMON_ENTRY-as-executable form; cycle 2 added exec/execSync shell strings; cycle 3 tightened to executable-position only; cycle 4 required recognised runtime in argv; cycle 5 added process.execPath; cycle 6 handled runtime flags + computed-access execPath; cycle 7 modelled value-consuming + eval flags; cycle 8 dropped misclassified standalone flags; cycle 9 added template-literal args, argv-array script-position walk, no-script flags (--version/--help), and quoted shell tokens. Pattern: each cycle the worker thinks 'all done', the reviewer probes one new permutation. A pre-submission shape-enumeration checklist for static-analysis classifiers (per AST node × per literal/template/identifier × per flag class × per shell-quote variant × per runtime-form vs direct-executable) would compress this to 1-2 cycles. Applies to ANY future precision-classifier task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Resubmit-after-fix in autonomous dispatch needs explicit 'task start' before 'task submit'. The dispatch worker enters with task in needs_work; submit requires in_progress (rejected with 'Cannot submit task with status: needs_work'). The Needs Work State spec @01KHYRCWD9CNW9FSGPFNH3NK2Y ac-3 documents that 'kspec task start' is the transition, but the task-work skill's Fix Cycle section step 7 ('Re-submit — kspec task submit @ref') doesn't mention the start step. A worker batch like [task note, task submit] rolls back atomically (had to retry as [task start, task note, task submit]). Two possible fixes: (a) auto-start when submit sees source state needs_work, or (b) call out the start step in the Fix Cycle section of the task-work skill. Hits every dispatch worker on every fix cycle.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reading review records via 'kspec review get @ref --json' surfaces exact thread anchors (file path, line_start/line_end, full body text, commit SHA) in one query. The text view truncates body text and elides anchor commits. For fix-cycle workers, the JSON path is the fastest way from review verdict to surgical fix locations: jump straight to the file:line, read the unabridged review reasoning, and write a targeted fix without re-reading the diff. Worth surfacing in the task-work skill's Fix Cycle section as the canonical first step after a cycle starts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: A JSDoc/block comment in tools/eslint-rules/*.js (or any oxlint JS plugin file) that contains the substring '*/' anywhere in its body terminates the comment block prematurely, leaving the trailing prose as invalid JS. The downstream symptom is oxlint reporting 'Failed to parse oxlint configuration file. Failed to load JS plugin: ./tools/eslint-rules/<rule>.js' with a SyntaxError pointing at a token several lines past the comment, and EVERY test that exercises the rule via runOxlint() then fails with 'Failed to parse oxlint configuration ...' as its assertion text — a single broken comment cascades into hundreds of meaningless test failures with no diagnostic that points at the comment itself. Encountered today when documenting a path-suffix matcher as '*/node' inside a JSDoc body. A pre-test 'node --check tools/eslint-rules/<rule>.js' would surface the SyntaxError immediately and pinpoint the line, but the test pipeline currently runs the rule through oxlint's plugin loader instead of node directly. Mitigation pattern: when describing path-suffix patterns in rule-file JSDocs, escape the slash (e.g. '<runtime>/node' or 'a path ending in node') or run 'node --check' on the rule file before relying on test failures to diagnose a rule load problem.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Static daemon guardrail classifier reviews are repeatedly finding misses in the hand-curated Node/Bun runtime option taxonomy. In @task-fix-guardrail-daemon-command-classification, many fix cycles handled one option class at a time, and cycle 11 still missed documented value-consuming Node options like --import and --env-file. This suggests the rule needs a more durable taxonomy strategy, such as table-driven coverage for documented option classes or generated/fixture-backed option lists, instead of relying on ad hoc additions during review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of @task-fix-detached-cleanup-timing-analysis, a small manual negative-control oxlint probe (`serve start --detach` followed by unrelated `onTestFinished`) exposed a false negative after targeted tests passed. Pattern to replicate: for static guardrail reviews, supplement regression suites with one-off synthetic probes that try to disprove the rule at the boundary of the claimed fix.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: The kspec-reflect skill says to run `kspec workflow show` without arguments, but the CLI currently requires `kspec workflow show <run-ref>`. This creates avoidable command friction during reflection; update the rendered/source skill example or CLI behavior so the instruction matches the actual command contract.
observations.author: codex
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing inbox item @01KQBGKT covering session reflection workflow examples matching current CLI command signatures.

observations.content: kspec review get text output truncates thread bodies, so during every fix cycle I need 'kspec review for-task' + 'kspec review get' + 'kspec review get --json | head' (3 commands) just to read the reviewer's actual blocker text. A --threads or --full flag (or just printing full bodies in default text output, since the thread count is usually small) would shorten the fix-cycle inheritance path.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When changing a static-analysis lint rule, run the reviewer's exact synthetic probes via direct `npx oxlint` against the unmerged rule BEFORE writing the corresponding test fixtures in tests/lint-*.test.ts. Two payoffs: (1) confirms the rule change actually flips diagnostic state on the probe (cheap signal that the AST walker logic is correct); (2) discovers real-world false positives in the existing test tree (e.g. tests/cli-serve.test.ts) before they become CI failures or motivate a permissive rollback. The probe loop is sub-second per file via `npx oxlint --config <synthetic config>` with a one-file plugins override. Done four cycles in a row on no-leaky-test-daemon — each cycle the probe-first loop caught at least one issue (false positive, missed shape, or test-code refactor needed) before tests/CI were touched.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Synthetic oxlint probe files (write minimal repro at /tmp/probe-<scenario>.ts, run 'npx oxlint --config <plugin-config>' against the rule plugin path directly) gave per-blocker feedback in <1 second during a fix cycle on tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js — vs ~9s for the targeted vitest harness and ~30min for the full suite. Effective for any AST-walker lint rule fix where the reviewer's blocker has a small concrete repro: run the reviewer's exact probe against the rule first, then add the regression test, then run vitest. Pattern applies to repeated fix cycles on the same rule.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec task note <ref> <message> only accepts the message as an inline argument. Long structured validation/audit notes (multi-paragraph test results, AC coverage tables, source-audit classifications) get composed in a tmp file and shoved through a shell variable, which is awkward and easy to mangle when content includes special chars. A --message-file path or stdin input would let validation-class tasks attach long findings without shell-escaping risk.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Validation-class tasks (e.g., @task-validate-daemon-test-fixture-standardization) recorded their full methodology in task notes — exact Playwright slice path, classification of each pre-existing kspec validate warning, source-audit grep patterns, and findings against each AC. The next plan revalidation reproduced that workflow deterministically without re-deriving the slice or rediscovering which warnings were pre-existing. Worth replicating: validation tasks should embed their slice/classification in notes, not just outcomes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task descriptions that prescribe `git -C .kspec status` as a verification step do not run under dispatch. Dispatched workers run in `.kspec-worktrees/<task>/` worktrees that contain only the source tree; the shadow `.kspec/` worktree lives at the project root. The command exits non-zero with `cannot change to '.kspec'`. Encountered while validating @01KR6M6SW9QGVJWG3VQF4WDT6C. Either omit shadow-status verification from prescribed steps or document `kspec shadow status` as the dispatch-portable equivalent.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Regression-only tasks that intentionally add a failing test before the fix lands conflict with review and manual-merge gates, because npm test must stay green before dev can advance. Define a standard staging pattern for these tasks, such as expected-failing markers, paired regression-plus-fix merge units, or explicit no-merge sequencing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch worker submitted task @01KR6M6XARDRJ17BY20Z3BG66B before any pre-submit reflection / observation-search, so it rediscovered the disproved bare it.fails staging pattern (disproven cycle 2 @01KR3ZR8, validated selective form @01KR431R) only after submit — would have caused a likely fix-cycle 2 had the next reviewer flagged it. The session-reflect-loop workflow ran AFTER kspec task submit, not before. Existing spec @01KFR7M6 ac-10 calls for a pre-submit local-review subagent, but no local-review skill is currently loaded under .claude/skills/ in this project, so the gate is not enforced for autonomous workers. Distinct from @01KGQY72 (which is about reflection running too aggressively in Ralph chains, not about timing relative to submit). Suggested fix shape: either (a) add a 'search observations + critique' step into the autonomous task-work flow before kspec task submit, or (b) ship and require a local-review skill that includes 'kspec meta observations list / kspec search' against the just-applied pattern.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec review reply --body "..." (and likely other CLI write commands that take free-form text bodies) fails with the daemon error "Unexpected token C, Cannot rea... is not valid JSON" when the body contains shell-interpolated characters such as backticks, code-fence markdown, or smart-quoted text. The daemon-side error message suggests checking daemon status, which is a misleading red herring — the actual cause is the shell mangling the body before the CLI ever sends it. Workaround: write the body to a temp file and pass it as --body "$(cat /tmp/reply.txt)". Encountered while replying to a review blocker thread on @01KR6QFSSGT6SZA00W662XTRM2; the agent had to discover the workaround by trial and error because the error message points away from the real cause. Worth either: (a) documenting the multi-line/special-char body pattern in the kspec-agents.md cli-lookups or testing convention; (b) adding a --body-file flag to kspec review reply / comment / verdict so file-based payloads work without shell interpolation gymnastics; (c) improving the daemon error message to surface the parse failure cause when the request body fails to parse.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: vitest it.fails(...) is a clean fit for the kspec convention of landing regression tests for an unfixed rule before the rule fix itself (the daemon-test-fixture-hardening plan splits work into add-regressions tasks that land first and fix tasks that land second). The pattern: each unsafe regression is written as it.fails("...", () => { /* assertions describing the behavior the rule MUST report after the fix */ }). Today the rule does not produce the diagnostic, the assertions throw, and it.fails turns the throw into a pass — the suite stays green. When the lint-rule-fix worker lands their fix and the rule produces the diagnostic, the assertions pass, it.fails fails, and that failure is the structured signal that those specific tests must be flipped from it.fails(...) back to it(...). This locks the false negatives in (any future regression to the rule re-trips them) without contributing red to a green branch. The companion control tests stay as plain it(...) so they verify the safe shapes pass today and continue to pass after the fix. Used to resolve the blocker on review @01KR6QFSSGT6SZA00W662XTRM2 for @task-add-guardrail-binding-wrapper-regressions. Worth surfacing in the kspec testing convention or the work-gates skill so future regression-tests-before-fix tasks reach for this pattern instead of either landing red into the required suite or skipping/todo-ing the regressions (which loses the lock-in).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Selective expected-failure pattern (@01KR431R) scoping: when restructuring a test from inline assertions into a selective wrapper, the post-fix contract path of the wrapper must contain ALL task-required assertions; only the subset that deterministically distinguishes bug-from-fix today belongs in the bug-shape re-assertion path. Failure mode that motivated this rule: on @task-add-register-cleanup-failure-regression cycle 2, when introducing expectCleanupRegistrationLeak around a daemon cleanup-registration leak, I dropped the task-mandated endpoint-unreachable assertion from BOTH paths under the rationale 'rejection is synchronous, daemon never binds, so endpoint reachability is not a useful pre-fix differentiator.' That rationale was correct for the bug-shape re-assertion but wrong for the post-fix contract path: a partial fix that terminates the child but leaks a listener (orphan port binding, watchdog timer, separate process group) would still pass child-terminated yet leak the endpoint, and the staged regression would mask it. Cycle 3 review @01KR6T0X correctly flagged this; fix shape (commit 354731a68): post-fix path asserts BOTH child-terminated AND bounded endpoint-unreachable; bug-shape re-assertion stays as child-still-alive only. Rule for future selective wrappers: enumerate all task-required assertions, put them all in the post-fix contract path, then choose only the deterministic-pre-fix subset for bug-shape re-assertion.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During guardrail reviews, a small AC-shaped synthetic lint probe can reveal contract gaps that focused regression suites miss. In this session the submitted focused tests passed, but a one-file oxlint probe for callback-local readPidFromFile cleanup showed the rule still accepted cleanup that did not own a concrete pid at registration time.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Static-analysis fix cycles can introduce polarity errors via additive exemptions: each cycle's reviewer probe surfaces a 'legitimate-looking' shape, the worker adds an exemption to allow it, and the exemption itself re-opens the original AC violation. Cycle 4 of @01KR6M77 (no-leaky-test-daemon callback-local cleanup) added callbackLocalKillTargetIsDynamic on the theory 'callback-local CallExpression init is a runtime read at cleanup time = valid ownership'. That re-enabled the exact AC-violating shape: onTestFinished(() => { const pid = readPidFromFile(); process.kill(pid, ...) }) — callback-local binding defers ownership entirely to teardown, violating ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation. Cycle 5 had to remove the exemption AND its 197 lines of supporting helpers. Mitigation: when adding an exemption to a precision lint, run the spec AC's negative-example shape through the production toolchain (manual oxlint probe with the AC text's literal example) BEFORE submitting. If the exemption accepts the AC's negative example, the exemption is wrong. This is distinct from the shape-permutation friction in @01KR5CYKN (worker missing positive cases) — this is the inverse: worker adding accommodations that re-introduce the failing case. Applies to any precision classifier where exemptions accumulate across cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, kspec review comment and related review commands only accepted inline shell arguments for long Markdown bodies and evidence. A blocker comment containing code-style backticks and shell-sensitive snippets was mangled by command substitution before kspec received it, requiring a follow-up reply to restore the evidence. Search found no existing inbox/spec/task coverage for review body file payloads. Consider adding file-based payload options for review comment, reply, verdict/check evidence, or documenting a safe file-payload workflow for review records.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate reflection capture. Broader search after capture found existing related observations including @01KR6THZ, @01KMR88Z, @01KPQQKX, and @01KMNH8N covering shell-passed review bodies and file-based payload friction.

observations.content: Fix-cycle work for test-flake hangs often misses the helper-internal hang class. Initial fix attempts patch what's visible at the test surface (e.g. wrapping fetch() calls in the test file with AbortSignal) while the same hang class still lives inside shared helpers used by readiness/probe paths. Concrete evidence: @01KR76BQ first cycle bounded the test-file fetches in tests/daemon-build.test.ts but left probeHealth/probeCacheReady fetches unbounded inside tests/helpers/daemon.ts; reviewer correctly identified that startTestDaemon's readiness wait could still hang past the outer vitest timeout. Mitigation pattern: when fixing test hangs, audit the helper graph reached from the failing test for the same hang class, not just the test body. waitForStartup-style polling helpers also benefit from racing each probe against the remaining budget as defense in depth.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: no-leaky-test-daemon rule went through 6 fix cycles, each cycle the reviewer found a new AST shape of the same underlying defect: cycle-3 callback-local literal kill targets, cycle-3 TS-wrapped kill targets, cycle-3 MemberExpression kill targets, cycle-4 callback-local CallExpression initializers, cycle-5 callback-local readPidFromFile, cycle-5 TS-wrapped null/undefined initializers. The AC ac-detached-cleanup-bound-before-observation describes the CONTRACT (callback must own the concrete pid at registration time) but does not enumerate the AST families that satisfy or violate it. Each cycle the rule grew an ad hoc patch for the new AST shape rather than a shared classifier, and the AST treatment between kill-target analysis and placeholder-initializer analysis drifted (placeholder check stopped at bare-Identifier-undefined while kill-target analysis already had a fixed-point unwrapTransparentExpression helper). Suggests guardrails over AST shapes benefit from either AC-level enumeration of the AST families that satisfy the contract OR a documented shared classifier so symmetric checks share the same unwrap discipline.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Multi-cycle reviewer-probe driven fix pattern (7 cycles on @01KR6M77 task-fix-guardrail-binding-wrapper-analysis). Each review cycle surfaced ONE precise manual oxlint probe demonstrating a code path that bypassed the cleanup-binding ownership check (registered-callback path, callback-local targets, member-expression roots, TS-wrapper unwrap, null/undefined initializer unwrap, try/finally finalizer direct calls). The probe-driven structure was high signal: each cycle the worker could land a targeted fix on the first attempt with focused regression tests, and the cumulative result was a far more robust static analysis than any single-pass implementation would have produced. Pattern: when the fix space is unbounded (an AST analysis covering arbitrary user code), reviewer manual probes are more effective than abstract review checklists.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Static analysis security checks added to ONE code path silently bypass via OTHER paths. The no-leaky-test-daemon ownership check was originally added to cleanupCallbackBindingStatus on the registered-callback entry, which left direct daemon-cleanup calls in try/finally finalizers, member-expression kill targets, TS-wrapped initializers, and callback-local targets as silent bypasses — each surfaced only via reviewer manual probes (cycles 1-7 on @01KR6M77). Lesson for future static-analysis work: when a predicate grants a SAFE verdict, audit every code path that can produce that verdict (every CallExpression site, every wrapper unwrap, every binding-resolution branch) and apply the same security rule uniformly. Partial enforcement is worse than visible omission because it gives false confidence.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer prompt paths can be stale or disappear before follow-on commands. In this session the review snapshot path from the prompt was missing, had to be reconstructed from git worktree metadata, and later disappeared again before reflection. Consider dispatch/reviewer workspace recovery or clearer lifecycle handling when the canonical branch and reviewed commit are still available.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Concurrent npm test invocations in the same worktree can both trigger the test runner self-build path and race on packages/web-ui/.svelte-kit/dist outputs. In this session two focused test commands run in parallel both failed before tests with a SvelteKit manifest-full.js ENOENT, while a single serial npm run build followed by serial tests passed. Consider adding a per-worktree build lock or in-progress build reuse in scripts/test.cjs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Fixed by per-worktree build/test lock (scripts/build-test-lock.cjs): npm run build / build:e2e and scripts/test.cjs serialize on the same lock, so concurrent invocations wait instead of racing on dist/ and .svelte-kit outputs. Task @task-stabilize-upgrade-folder-storage-test.

observations.content: Detached reviewer snapshot cleanup can remove the review worktree before the same reviewer process finishes post-approval actions. In this session, approval closed the review and the detached snapshot path disappeared before the merge helper/task completion verification commands ran, causing path-not-found failures and requiring recovery from the canonical task worktree. Defer snapshot deletion until the reviewer invocation exits, or provide a stable post-approval project context for merge/completion commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon-backed test files that compose 10+ daemon spawns serially in one process accumulate port-reuse and IO contention that compresses each beforeEach hook budget against the fixture readiness budget. When the hook timeout barely exceeds cumulative readiness (e.g. 60s hook vs 30s readiness), the hook can preempt startTestDaemon before it surfaces a DaemonReadinessError diagnostic — flake message becomes the bare hook timeout, not the actionable diagnostic bundle required by @daemon-backed-test-fixture-contract ac-readiness-diagnostics. Observed in tests/daemon-api/websocket-protocol.test.ts Bun parity beforeEach 2026-05-11; could recur in any file that combines a multi-test parent describe with a runtime-matrix child describe.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon process leak hygiene checks using 'pgrep -af node.*dist/daemon/index.js' produce false-positive transient PIDs because the zsh -c wrapper running pgrep matches its own command line (the regex is passed as a literal string argument). This trips up step 6 of daemon-hardening validation tasks (capture pre/post baselines). Workaround: use 'ps -eo pid,cmd | awk' with explicit $2 == node and command-line regex filter, which excludes shell wrappers. Worth either documenting the awk-based pattern in the task template, or providing a 'kspec util daemon-pids' helper that does the precise filtering once.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During detached review of a validation task, kspec validate --alignment reported the linked spec @daemon-test-guardrail-precision as implemented-but-should-be-in_progress while the validation task was still pending_review, then the warning disappeared immediately after task completion. This lifecycle artifact can look like real status drift during review; alignment reporting or reviewer guidance should distinguish transient pending_review validation-task effects from actionable mismatches.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review found a repeated AC-annotation quality gap: tests sometimes add broad inherited fixture-contract annotations (for example @daemon-backed-test-fixture-contract ac-no-ambient-daemon-control) when the test only proves the owned-resource behavior and does not set up or observe an ambient daemon. Existing annotation validation catches unresolved/malformed refs, but semantic over-claiming still relies on reviewer scrutiny. Consider guidance or a checklist for reviewers/workers to remove AC annotations that are syntactically valid but not behaviorally proven.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Forward-staged regression suites flip a rule-fix task from open-ended thinking into a mechanical checklist. When the dependent regression task encodes each adversarial probe with the selective-expected-failure helper (see @01KR431R), the rule-fix task's post-refactor verification reduces to: run npm test, collect every STAGED REGRESSION CLOSED sentinel, inline its post-fix assertions. On @task-fix-guardrail-cleanup-effect-classification (cycle 1) this surfaced exactly 10 sentinels with no surrounding suite regressions — a precise to-do list with zero ambiguity about coverage. The verification cost becomes O(staged regressions) rather than O(time spent enumerating edge cases). Pair this success with @01KR431R: that observation documents the helper's shape; this one documents the workflow leverage it gives the downstream fix task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Parameter-default Literal escape hatch when tightening static signal predicates. When tightening a rule that previously accepted any shape on a CallExpression argument, locally-defined call sites often carry an Identifier whose value comes from a function parameter with an AssignmentPattern default — e.g. tests/cli-serve.test.ts's function killPid(pid, signal: NodeJS.Signals = 'SIGTERM') { process.kill(pid, signal); }. The static check cannot prove termination from `signal` alone, but the AssignmentPattern.right Literal is statically pinnable. Threading the owning function node through the signal predicate and resolving Identifier signals against the param defaults preserves the safe shape without forcing a downstream refactor. Generalises to any stricter argument predicate on a function-arg slot — check parameter-default Literals before rejecting Identifier shapes. Validated on @task-fix-guardrail-cleanup-effect-classification: cli-serve.test.ts kept passing under the stricter classifier without changes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing staged regression-only tasks needs an explicit call-site check: a new helper-level it.fails test can appear to cover a wrapper contract even when the real wrapper does not call that helper yet. In @task-add-setup-failure-error-preservation-regressions, full tests were green and the helper regression was annotated for the right AC, but comparing the task's Playwright-wrapper bullets against tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts showed the actual wrapper setup/use paths were still unexercised. Future reviews of fixture/wrapper regressions should verify the tested seam is already on the production/test-wrapper call path, or require a wrapper-unit seam that drives the real lifecycle.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Merging origin/dev into a fix-cycle worker branch can produce duplicate test sections when sibling dispatch tasks have independently transformed the same test region. Cycle-4 of task-fix-guardrail-cleanup-effect-classification merged dev and got two copies (~250 lines each) of the cleanup-effect accepted-shape section: one from this branch's cycle-1 transformation, one from sibling tasks (task-add-guardrail-cleanup-boundary-regressions, task-add-active-request-bounded-observation-regressions) that had merged similar transformations earlier. The textual git merge could not recognize them as semantically equivalent and required ~250 lines of manual de-duplication. Pattern: when multiple sibling dispatch tasks touch the same test file with similar content transformations, merges duplicate rather than dedupe. Detection: count occurrences of a section comment after a merge. Mitigation candidate: a pre-resubmit check that flags duplicate it() titles in the same describe block, or vitest's no-identical-title rule run as part of the fix-cycle gate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewer-fixture verification via npx oxlint on synthetic probe files (cp /tmp/cycle4-fixtures/blocker[12].test.ts tests/_probe_blocker[12].test.ts ; npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json tests/_probe*.test.ts) is a fast pre-commit confirmation that the cycle's exact reviewer probes produce missingCleanup before submitting. Caught zero regressions in cycle 4 because both probes flagged after the first iteration; saved a re-review cycle. Pattern: when a review blocker cites an exact source fixture, replay it as a tests/_probe file and verify the diagnostic before committing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Closing wrapper-coverage gap (@01KRDB3E friction) via extract-seam-and-delegate has a deterministic fix-cycle recipe. When a reviewer flags that staged regressions test helpers in isolation but production wrapper does not exercise them: (1) extract a wrapper-unit seam that mirrors the wrapper's pre-try/finally setup verbatim, including the bug — same __testStageHook pattern existing helpers like createTestDaemonProject use; (2) refactor the production wrapper to delegate setup to the new seam AND the use+teardown body to the existing lifecycle helper, so the wrapper inherits both contracts the dependent fix task will harden; (3) add it.fails staged regressions per setup stage on the new seam plus a positive contract test that asserts every stage hook fires in declared order (this guards against future refactors silently dropping a stage and turning the keyed regressions into false coverage); (4) verify by stripping it.fails and confirming each new regression fails with the expected pre-fix assertion message. Demonstrated on @task-add-setup-failure-error-preservation-regressions cycle 1 (review @01KRDA6QCN3N0G8YNKR6GC7VQD): closed both blockers in one pass with 5 new tests, full suite still green, smoke E2E green, dependent fix task @task-fix-setup-failure-cleanup-error-preservation now has a single helper to harden which the wrapper inherits automatically.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: no-leaky-test-daemon: the free-identifier conservative-trust fallback in isTrustedHelperByOrigin produces a recurring discovery surface. Each review cycle on cleanup-effect classification (1, 3, 4, 5) has surfaced a new shape (unapproved import, nested no-op, signal override, parameter shadow) that falls through to default-trust and silently credits cleanup. The fix pattern has been to add another reject branch per cycle. Worth considering inverting the default: free-identifier = REJECT unless proven trusted via approved primitives. Spec-first work would be needed because that flips the rule policy.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Predicate-based architecture (one named predicate per shape: isTrustedHelperByOrigin, findLocalHelperDefinition, isTerminatingPrimitiveCall, isChildHandleReceiverTrusted) in tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js localized each cycle of fixes to existing functions plus at most one new helper, instead of forcing sprawling refactors. The sentinel-based distinction between absent and shadowed-but-opaque (LOCAL_BINDING_OPAQUE) added in cycle-5 fits the same pattern — readable, localized, and routes the use site to an explicit reject branch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Lint rule test fixtures share surface area across detection paths (helper-boundary, cleanup-classifier, observation-before-cleanup, runtime parity). A fixture intended to exercise one rule branch can trigger a different rule first, producing a confusing failure where the rule fires with the wrong message. Today I had to rewrite a wrapper-pattern probe after it triggered the helper-boundary message instead of missingCleanup. A short fixture-design checklist (or a test helper that asserts a specific message id, not just substring of output) would catch this earlier.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon.js has grown to 4271 lines as the daemon cleanup contract hardening plan adds successive classifier predicates (cleanup-effect, cleanup-boundary, helper-origin, implicit-autostart). At 4271 lines it exceeds the Read tool 25000-token limit, forcing slice reads via offset/limit and making cross-predicate consistency checks harder. After @plan-daemon-test-cleanup-contract-hardening completes, the rule should be evaluated for extraction into separate predicate modules under tools/eslint-rules/no-leaky-test-daemon/.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Structural classifier-in-test pattern for failing-before-fix on FILE properties: when an AC requires a structural property of a test file (e.g. ac-implicit-autostart-cleanup-before-observation requires every auto-start case in cli-no-daemon.test.ts to register onTestFinished before observation) but the guardrail lint rule that would enforce it does not yet exist, write a small classifier function in the regression test, read the target file via readTestOutputSync (the no-source-scanning safe-listed helper), and stage the assertion via it.fails — same flip-on-fix-landing protocol as the synthetic-fixture it.fails cases. The classifier should be paired with a sanity test that proves it finds the unsafe shape but skips the safe one, so it cannot silently collapse to always-empty findings. Used successfully in @task-add-implicit-autostart-cleanup-regressions on the real tests/cli-no-daemon.test.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: CLI commands that accept long freeform text only through inline flags are easy to damage via shell interpolation. During review/reflection, backticks and command snippets in review comment bodies and workflow notes were interpreted by the shell before kspec received them, requiring corrective follow-up text. File based text input options for review comments, replies, task notes, and workflow notes would make evidence capture safer.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer workspace preparation can fail in ways that are operational rather than task scoped. This session had a prompt-provided detached review snapshot path that was absent locally, plus task notes showing an earlier transient review-bootstrap ENOENT spawn sh failure that was later triaged as not a task blocker. A reviewer preflight or clearer recovery path for missing or failed detached review worktrees would reduce orientation time and prevent infrastructure failures from being mistaken for code blockers.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing the diff before task notes, then using an ad hoc behavioral oxlint fixture after reading the classifier, exposed a cleanup timing false negative that the existing focused and full test suites did not catch. This pattern is worth repeating for static analysis rule reviews: derive one or two executable adversarial probes from the spec edge case before approving.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel dispatch tasks that each append staged regression describe blocks to the same contract-test file (e.g. tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts) produce textually-interleaved auto-merge conflicts at the merge gate even when both sides are semantically additive. Resolution requires manual file reconstruction (split common-prefix + each side's new blocks, concatenate). Hit this on @01KRCRJR5K77Q2THCVVH3BDNFH (fix cycle 2) where dev's setup-failure cleanup + primary-error preservation regressions and this task's bounded-stop regressions both targeted the tail of daemon.test.ts. Detached merge helper escalated; worker resolved by hand.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review cycle lookup, `kspec review for-task @01KRCRJR5K77Q2THCVVH3BDNFH` and `kspec review list --task @01KRCRJR5K77Q2THCVVH3BDNFH` omitted prior approved review @01KRE691 because that review subject was stored as task:@task-add-bounded-process-stop-contract-tests. Review history lookup should normalize task refs across ULID and slug aliases so per-cycle history is complete.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing bounded process-stop changes exposed a repeatable guardrail gap: when a test cleanup helper changes from synchronous void to Promise-returning bounded cleanup, block-bodied lifecycle callbacks such as onTestFinished(() => { killPid(pid); }) can silently drop the promise. Tests can still pass while teardown reports complete before termination is observed. Consider a lint/static guard for known async cleanup helpers in lifecycle callbacks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Static-analysis lint rules that trust callees via approved-import allowlists must verify the resolved file path, not just the import specifier string. Cycle-7 review on @01KRCRJPMHMHC410TKRC5Y9HF1 caught this: APPROVED_HELPER_IMPORT_PATH_PATTERNS matched the specifier text './helpers/daemon' but never checked what it resolved to on disk relative to the importing file. A nested test at tests/e2e/synthetic-test.ts importing './helpers/daemon' resolves to tests/e2e/helpers/daemon — outside the approved-helper allowlist — and was silently credited. Fix in cycle 8 uses path.resolve(path.dirname(context.physicalFilename), specifier) + extension normalisation + match against APPROVED_HELPER_IMPLEMENTATION_PATTERNS. Mitigation when authoring/reviewing an import-trust allowlist: distinguish (a) a fast specifier-shape prefilter — useful for early reject — from (b) the authoritative resolved-path check. The prefilter ALONE is never sufficient because relative specifiers depend on the importer's location. Applies to any precision rule maintaining a trust-by-import allowlist (helper modules, dependency allowlists, module-trust policies, framework-internal imports).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Verifying reviewer's exact probes via npx oxlint BEFORE running the test suite (cycle 8 of @01KRCRJPMHMHC410TKRC5Y9HF1) caught both blocker fixes in under 30 seconds vs ~80s for the targeted suite + ~35min for the full vitest run. Built ad hoc /tmp directories with the exact reviewer fixtures and the project's plugin path, then invoked 'npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json' directly. Both reviewer probes flagged on first try. This is a confirmation of the existing pattern in @01KRDBV3QZMDSN477WYRFAT85B (reviewer-fixture verification) and reinforces: when a review blocker cites an exact probe, replay it through the production toolchain before committing to the long test cycle. Especially valuable for fix-cycle work where wrong-direction iterations cost 35+ minutes each.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The FAILING-BEFORE-FIX it.fails pattern from @task-add-active-request-bounded-observation-regressions worked exactly as designed: the regression task landed staged tests that documented the gap (it.fails wrappers + clear comments), and the fix task could flip them to it() while rewriting bodies to lock the new helper contract. Three flip sites — in-process stop() bounded teardown, AbortSignal.timeout pattern, and bare-fetch regressions — all converted cleanly. Pattern worth replicating for future paired contract-then-fix task pairs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Staged-regression test bodies that were authored as it.fails carry verbose narrative comment blocks (STAGED REGRESSION sentinel, 'Pre-fix this fails because...', 'Post-fix: the helper will...', 'with it.fails masking the assertion'). When the dependent fix task flips it.fails → it, those blocks become stale: they narrate a state that no longer exists and reference the helper's old behavior. Trimming them is mechanical but easy to leave behind because tests pass either way. Observed concretely while flipping 7 regressions across tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts and tests/e2e-fixture-daemon-cleanup.test.ts in @task-fix-setup-failure-cleanup-error-preservation — required a second pass after the it.fails → it flip to clean ~5 comment blocks. Possible mitigations: convention for staged-regression authors to use a parseable marker (e.g. // STAGED:fix-when-flipped) the fix-task worker greps for, or a /kspec:flip-staged-regression skill that pairs the it.fails→it flip with mandatory comment trimming.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Session reflection gate guidance only lists completed tasks, code changes, and recent commits as meaningful-work signals. Reviewer-only sessions can still produce substantive durable work through review records, required checks, verdicts, blocker threads, and task transitions such as pending_review to needs_work; the reflection gate should explicitly count those review artifacts so reviewer sessions are not skipped.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
