Caught in autonomous dispatch by needing to re-run kspec task start after the first invocation left the task in pending; a downstream kspec task submit then failed with Cannot submit task with status pending. Fix scope unclear (always print resulting status, hard error on no-op, or state-aware messaging) — capturing as friction rather than promoting to a task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: For docs tasks that document CLI/API surfaces, verify every flag/command/option claim against the live dev CLI (npm run dev -- <cmd> --help) and the source enum/schema values before writing — not after. The installed kspec binary may lag the worktree branch, so the installed --help cannot be trusted for unreleased surface. Catching CLI inaccuracies pre-submission was high-leverage during the runner config docs task; relying on the installed kspec --help would have produced two wrong examples (nonexistent kspec adapter list, --runner empty-string vs --clear-runner).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When a test helper installs a process-level signal handler that re-raises the signal for default disposition (e.g. process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGTERM'))), the listener MUST remove itself before re-raising or the handler re-enters in an infinite loop. Node suppresses default termination while any listener is installed for that signal, so a self-targeted process.kill re-fires this same listener instead of exiting. Fix recipe: name the handler so it can call process.removeListener(signal, handler) before re-raising. Test recipe: extract the handler creation as an exported factory taking the release/reRaise side-effects as injectable parameters; in tests install the factory's output on a benign SIGUSR2 listener, invoke directly, and assert (a) process.listeners(signal) no longer contains the handler, (b) injected release ran exactly once, (c) injected reRaise was called with the same signal. Optionally complement with a subprocess test that spawns a Node replica and asserts bounded SIGTERM exit. See tests/helpers/daemon.ts __createPortStartLockSignalHandler and tests/helpers/daemon.test.ts 'registerPortStartLockExitHandlers signal-handler boundedness' for the worked example from @stabilize-daemon-fixture-cleanup-tests-timing-out fix cycle 1.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spawning a single Explore sub-agent to map existing infrastructure (test files, helpers, fixtures, source modules) before writing any test code paid off enormously for an e2e/multi-surface task. The map surfaced reusable patterns (createTestApp, mock-acp.js, deriveProjectKeySync, sentinel-secret idiom) and let the 1140-line agent-runner-e2e.test.ts file get written straight-through with only two narrow iteration cycles on shape/path issues.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Heavy default test suite (10168 tests, ~45 min cold) is disproportionate for test-only diffs where no production code changed. The session-scoped cache amortizes repeat runs, but the first cold run is the bottleneck. A vitest smoke profile (npm run test:smoke) that excludes integration/e2e/heavy-serial when the diff touches only tests/ would speed pre-submit verification dramatically. Related but distinct from @task-stabilize-fresh-shard-test-runs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: AC annotation correctness is unenforced: an // AC: comment marker counts as coverage in kspec validate --completeness regardless of whether the annotated test actually exercises the claimed behavior. In this fix cycle, three legacy adapter-only tests carried annotations for runner-backed ACs (ac-one-shot-uses-runner-resolution, ac-dispatch-uses-runner-resolution, ac-dispatch-preflight-accepts-configured-runners) and one missing-secret test carried ac-unknown-runner-blocks-before-spawn. Coverage tooling reported them all as covered; only human code review surfaced the mismatch. Related pattern flagged in the same review: a test that fabricates engine internals (e.g., engine.activeInvocationDetails.set / engine.queues.set) and asserts on the fabricated state passes even when the engine's real queueing/resolution path regresses. Both classes of test produce false coverage and false stability. Possible mitigations: a validate rule that pairs each AC annotation with a behavioral fingerprint (function called, module loaded, route hit) and warns when the annotation's spec ref does not appear in the test's runtime call graph; a convention requiring 'behavioral' tests to avoid direct internal-state mutation on the object under test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review of @task-runner-compatibility-regressions, the task Testing section referenced packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/agents.spec.ts, but the actual Playwright test path is tests/e2e/agents.spec.ts. This stale path caused avoidable command friction during AC annotation verification. Searched 'web ui e2e agents path', 'packages/web-ui/tests/e2e', and 'agents.spec.ts'; related runner/Web UI tasks exist, but no item directly tracks stale test-path references in task/review instructions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer merge flow worked cleanly for @task-runner-compatibility-regressions: after recording required review checks and approval, .agents/skills/kspec-merge/scripts/detached-reviewer-merge.sh merged the canonical task branch to dev without checking out the target in the detached snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached-reviewer merge recovery still needs manual intervention when the integration target branch is checked out in a project-root worktree classified as auxiliary. In this review, the helper correctly refused to move refs for dev, but the reviewer had to inspect state, detach /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch, and rerun the helper before the approved task could merge.
observations.author: codex
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing detached-reviewer/manual_merge friction observations (for example @01KSBHFQ and related manual_merge entries surfaced by kspec meta observations --search manual_merge --all). Kept this session's success observation only.

observations.content: Batching review checks and the final approval verdict with kspec batch produced a complete review audit trail in one atomic shadow-branch commit after all deterministic gates passed.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: CLI JSON output drift from extended report shapes — when adding a new field to a validation/report type (e.g. RunnerValidationReport.registry_load_failures), the CLI command’s output() call does not automatically pick it up. Today this was caught by a new test that asserted the field directly; without the test, the report would carry the field server-side but clients reading the CLI JSON would silently miss it. Consider an audit lint or a wrapper that serializes the report verbatim instead of re-listing fields per command.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Shared enrichment helper kept daemon GET and PATCH responses in sync. In packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts, extracting loadRunnerEnrichmentContext() and buildAgentRunnerFields() and reusing both in GET /api/meta/agents and PATCH /api/meta/agents/:id meant the runner_validation block (including the new runner_registry_unavailable diagnostic) appears identically on read and write paths. This is the parity pattern the runner-operator-surface-parity follow-up task asks for, applied at the API layer where it belongs. Worth replicating for other mutation endpoints whose response shape must mirror the corresponding list endpoint.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review success pattern: a small behavioral probe against a mixed-layer runner registry state caught an AC gap after deterministic gates and focused tests passed; adversarial reviews should include at least one scenario that disproves the happy-path shape of new diagnostics.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Runner registry-load tests covered malformed-layer cases where the referenced runner disappeared, but not mixed-layer cases where one config layer failed while another still contributed the runner; this allowed registry-unavailable diagnostics to be gated on runner absence instead of load failure presence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Hoisting registry-load failure precedence above per-runner validation as a single mental model unified the fix across 4 surfaces (resolver, CLI list/run, daemon meta, daemon dispatch). One sentence — 'load failure always wins over surviving runner entry' — drove identical structural changes in each surface and made the regression contract obvious.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec conflict between @cli-exit-codes (requirement) and @trait-semantic-exit-codes (trait): the requirement maps exit code 3 to NOT_FOUND and exit code 4 to VALIDATION_FAILED, but the trait maps exit code 3 to runtime error and exit code 1 to validation error. Both specs are status=implemented. When task @task-plan-branch-git-error-details required satisfying trait ac-4 (runtime error → 3), the implementation had to use a literal 3 in plan.ts because there is no RUNTIME_ERROR constant and reusing EXIT_CODES.NOT_FOUND would be semantically wrong. This forces magic numbers and will recur for any future task that covers the trait. Worth reconciling the trait vs requirement (rewrite the trait to match the implementation, or add a RUNTIME_ERROR constant aliased to 3 and update other trait-covered commands).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec batch with meta set --add-skill (and likely other meta set --add/--remove array options) throws 'TypeError: options.removeCapability is not iterable' atomically — the batch dispatcher invokes the meta set handler without first initializing the option arrays it iterates. Direct CLI invocation works because commander supplies the [] default. Workaround today: run the four reviewer-agent attaches sequentially. Distinct from prior batch frictions (01KKAZ94 task add, 01KNMC9Y arg shape, 01KQBRFN cascade prompt). Fix would be to initialize default empty arrays for meta set options in the batch wrapper, or share commander defaults across both entry paths.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: There is no kspec CLI command to update a project-local skill's SKILL.md body after creation. kspec skill add --content-file writes the body once; kspec skill set covers metadata only; kspec skill import expects a fresh import path. To correct skill content (in this case, switching $review-gates to the canonical {skill:review-gates} reference syntax) the only path was to edit .kspec/skills/<id>/SKILL.md directly and then run kspec skill render --force. This contradicts the 'use the CLI, not manual edits' convention and is distinct from 01KKX2NN (templates→shadow sync) and 01KJGAKM (version-gated update). A kspec skill update <id> --content-file or kspec skill set --content-file flag would close the gap.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Reviewing generated skill artifacts can produce false drift signals when using raw file equality across platforms: Codex renders portable skill references as $skill while Claude/factory render them as /skill. Reviewers need platform-aware comparison guidance or a helper that distinguishes expected renderer rewrites from stale generated output.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a dispatch worktree edits package templates under `templates/` (e.g. `templates/agents-sections/`), the installed `kspec` binary still reads templates from its globally-linked package, not from the worktree's edited files. `kspec agents generate` and `kspec agents status` therefore report stale-state based on the upstream package, and consumer-style verification of the generated output cannot be done with the `kspec` binary alone. Workaround: `npm run dev -- agents generate --dry-run --json` (tsx-runs the worktree source against the worktree's `getPackageRoot()`) confirms what the regenerated output would look like. Task descriptions that say 'run kspec agents generate and inspect kspec-agents.md' miss this when authored generically for any template-editing task.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Generated-guidance reviews benefit from checking source templates, local dry-run rendered output, and committed generated artifacts as separate surfaces. In review @01KT5F70, the template diff and dry-run output were neutral, but committed kspec-agents.md was stale and still contained package-shipped Kynetic-specific guidance.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shared-guidance neutrality cleanup plans should satisfy Direction 2 local-preservation before each neutralization task reaches review, or explicitly sequence the local-context task first. In review of @task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills, the shared skills correctly delegated concrete Kynetic gates/artifact-maintenance commands to project-local guidance, but the plan scheduled @task-preserve-kynetic-local-template-maintenance-context after the neutralization tasks. The reviewer had to request changes because the removed instructions had no current durable local home even though a later task planned to add one.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Editing templates/skills/<id>/SKILL.md does not propagate to .kspec/skills/ (where 'kspec skill render' reads from). First render after source edits reports 'Unchanged' because the shadow copy is still the previous version, masking that the edits did not reach the renderer. Required workflow: edit templates -> 'kspec skill install-core --force' (or 'npm run dev -- skill install-core --force' when iterating locally) -> 'kspec skill render --force'. This is non-obvious for task workers neutralizing package skills; the 'Unchanged' message looks like success.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plans that stage shared-guidance neutralization alongside a sibling local-preservation task (rather than ordering preservation first) hit a Direction-2 review block. Concrete instance: plan-shared-template-project-neutrality-cleanup placed task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills and task-preserve-kynetic-local-template-maintenance-context as siblings depending on the convention task. The neutralization landed first and was correctly blocked by the shared-guidance-neutrality convention because the concrete Kynetic gates (npm run format:check, npm run lint -- --quiet, npx oxlint <changed files>, npm run typecheck) and plugin/.factory artifact maintenance rules removed from shared templates had no always-loaded local home yet. The fix was to co-ship the diff-specific portion of the local-preservation work into the neutralization fix-cycle (added to work-gates and review-gates SKILL.md on the shadow branch). Systemic pattern: when a plan introduces a Direction-2-style convention AND removes shared-text content in the same slice, the preservation step must either (a) land before any neutralization task or (b) be co-shipped within each neutralization task's diff. Sibling-task ordering with a shared dependency does not enforce this and produces predictable fix cycles.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review comments entered via shell command arguments are easy to corrupt when the body contains backticks or command-like text. During review @01KT5QTK, a blocker comment body with backticked command names triggered shell command substitution, ran an unintended skill render command, and polluted the stored review body until a clarification reply was added. Agents should have a safer file-based or stdin-based pattern for long kspec review comments.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing inbox item @01KSZFP3P, which already tracks file-based payload support for kspec review comments/check evidence to avoid shell quoting issues.

observations.content: Skill-touching reviews need a branch-aware verification path for package core templates. In task @task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills, direct file inspection showed the submitted shared templates and rendered copies contained the intended neutralized text, but kspec skill status/verify still reported the touched package-core skills task-work, review, and merge as drifted because verification compared against installed/project skill state. This makes it hard to distinguish expected package-template edits from real render drift.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shared-guidance neutrality reviews worked well when the evidence log explicitly named changed shared surfaces, checked Direction 1 for universalized Kynetic-only policy, checked Direction 2 for local-home preservation, and separately verified generated source/render consistency. This made a prose-heavy detached review auditable without relying on a brittle markdown scanner.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: kspec skill render --force does not refresh .render-hash-codex / .render-hash-droid sidecars when the action is reported as Unchanged. If a rendered file already matches what render would produce (e.g., it was hand-edited to a value that later became the canonical source), --force exits successfully and reports Unchanged, yet kspec skill status / verify continue to report drift because the stored hash still reflects the previous render. Workaround: rm the rendered file, then run --force, which triggers a Create action and updates the sidecar. Hit during fix cycle 2 of @task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills — prior cycle saw --force succeed and assumed drift was cleared, then verify still failed.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Editing core skill templates requires syncing two source-of-truth locations but kspec install-core only operates at all-13-skills granularity. kspec skill render reads from .kspec/skills/<id>/SKILL.md (shadow), not templates/skills/<id>/SKILL.md. So changing one core skill template requires also updating the shadow source. The only CLI path for templates→shadow sync is kspec skill install-core, which has no per-skill flag and processes all 13 core skills; running it can revert intentional shadow-only customizations on unrelated skills (observed pre-existing drift on observe/reflect/triage-inbox/writing-specs/plan/create-workflow in this repo). Resolving the cycle-2 blocker on @task-neutralize-work-review-merge-skills required a workaround: manually copy 3 files into the shadow worktree and commit with KSPEC_SHADOW_COMMIT=1.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: kspec agents generate (and similar template-reading commands) reads static templates from the kspec CLI binary's install location via getPackageRoot() in src/cli/commands/agents.ts (path.resolve(__dirname, ..., ..., ...)), NOT from the current working directory. In dispatch mode this means a worktree whose templates are ahead of the CLI's source (e.g., neutralization commits not yet built into the linked CLI) regenerates a kspec-agents.md that REGRESSES the static template portion while correctly picking up shadow-branch convention changes. The artifact is a mixed bag and easy to commit by accident. Observed while working @task-preserve-kynetic-local-template-maintenance-context: the linked CLI was built from /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec on an older dev commit than the dispatch worktree, so the regenerated kspec-agents.md showed pre-neutralization template text alongside the new convention rules. Likely affects every dispatched task that touches conventions/workflows/skills/templates and is asked to regenerate kspec-agents.md as a verification step.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Plans that stage 'neutralize source templates' and 'regenerate derived artifacts' as separate sibling tasks become structurally redundant when the neutralization tasks correctly regenerate their derived outputs in the same commit (per the existing 'regenerate before commit' convention). The follow-up regenerate task then has nothing to commit and degrades into a verification-only no-op task. Concrete example: @plan-shared-template-project-neutrality-cleanup staged five neutralize-* tasks plus @task-regenerate-shared-template-artifacts-and-tests, but commits aea00e34e1/a46a66f66c/6f36d05d67/250f1ab627/600cc12a44 already shipped regenerated .agents/, .factory/, and kspec-agents.md outputs. When planning template-neutralization work, either fold the regeneration check into each neutralize-* task's quality gate, or scope the follow-up task explicitly as 'verify no drift and update brittle tests' rather than 'regenerate every derived artifact'.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Template-driven (mechanical) tests survived the entire shared-guidance neutralization wave without any test updates. tests/agents-instruction-gen.test.ts reads the actual templates/agents-sections/*.md files at test time, extracts each file's first ## heading and first non-empty content line, then asserts those substrings appear in the generated kspec-agents.md. Because the assertions are derived from the current template content rather than pinned to specific phrases, neutralizing template wording does not require touching the test — it self-updates. Worth replicating in any test that verifies a 'rendered output reflects source X' invariant: read X at test time, extract a content-derived fingerprint, then assert presence in the rendered output. The pattern also kept tests/core-skill-install.test.ts and tests/core-skill-update.test.ts stable across the same neutralization wave.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review evidence log plus the detached merge helper made a no-diff/no-op review safe to complete: recording artifact, neutrality, and gate evidence in the review before approval preserved auditability even when the task branch had no code diff and the merge helper reported already integrated.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: During review, the full npm test gate can appear ambiguous near the end: after many suites pass, the process may stay alive through long 30-60s quiet waits before emitting late passing suites and the final aggregate. Reviewers should wait for the process exit, but a clearer runner heartbeat/finalization status or queryable active-suite summary would reduce uncertainty.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: Review lifecycle friction: a request_changes verdict on a task already blocked by stale dispatch bootstrap metadata can leave the task blocked instead of needs_work. In review @01KT7EHK for task @01KT7DV7P6CTBBNXGB2AJF1269, the reviewer had to manually run task unblock followed by task needs-work after verdicting. This can hide actionable review feedback from the normal needs_work worker queue until lifecycle repair is done.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Edit tool input parses Unicode escapes (e.g., \u001b) as actual bytes before the file-content matcher runs. When editing JS/TS/Python source files that contain literal 6-character escape sequences (e.g., test fixtures with "safe\u001b[31m" as readable source), the Edit tool's old_string/new_string with \u001b becomes a single ESC byte and fails to match the literal source text. Workaround: write \\u001b in the JSON input to get a literal backslash + u001b in the file value, or build the string in a sidecar Python script using chr(92)+"u001b". This cost roughly 3 failed Edit attempts and a revert/re-insert cycle on the fleet-buffer OSC fix-cycle 3. Systemic for any agent task that needs to preserve literal escape sources in code files.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During detached review of @task-generic-acp-process-adapter, review @01KTDM29 ended up with duplicate checks/verdicts and two blocker/evidence threads for the same review cycle even though the review flow intended one set of mutations. The symptom suggests review CLI mutation idempotency, author attribution, or dispatch-trigger retry behavior needs investigation before reviewers can trust review records as clean single-source audit artifacts.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Dispatched fix-cycle resubmit hits a lifecycle wall: 'kspec task submit' rejects a task in needs_work ('Cannot submit task with status: needs_work. Task must be in_progress'), but the task-work fix-cycle steps go straight from commit/note to 'kspec task submit' with no intervening 'kspec task start'. A worker following the documented fix cycle exactly stalls until it discovers it must first run 'task start' (needs_work -> in_progress) before 'task submit'. Observed this cycle on @task-generic-acp-process-adapter. Fix options: have submit auto-transition needs_work -> in_progress, or make the fix-cycle resubmit step explicitly include 'kspec task start' before 'kspec task submit'.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: tsconfig.json excludes **/*.test.ts from 'npm run typecheck' (include: src/**/* only). When a src/ function signature or options field is renamed (e.g. activeTaskRefs -> activeTaskIds on reconcileDispatchWorkspaceArtifacts/reapDispatchWorkspace), test call sites passing the old shape are NOT caught by typecheck — TS excess-property/missing-arg errors over test files never run. The mismatch surfaces only at runtime in the full ~40-min suite (here: 10 cleanup tests silently lost protection and reaped artifacts). This delayed detection by a full suite cycle and contributes to dispatch 60-min timeouts. Candidate fix: a fast type-only gate over tests (separate tsconfig with noEmit covering tests/**) run alongside typecheck, so API/option drift in test call sites fails in seconds, not after the full suite.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: reconcileDispatchWorkspaceRegistry takes two canonical-identity maps with INCONSISTENT key formats: taskStatusByRef is keyed by @<task-ulid> (DispatchEngine builds it from `@${task._ulid}`) while activeRoleByTaskRef is keyed by the BARE <task-ulid> (from _activeRoleByTaskId, which does roles.set(record.taskId, role)). The activeRoleByTaskRef parameter name also misleadingly says ref but holds a bare ULID. This asymmetry is a footgun: a canonical-identity fix that looks up both maps with the same key form silently breaks one of them, and it was the root of the fix-cycle-2 reviewer blocker (lookups were done by raw record.task_ref and missed slug-display records). Fix options: normalize both maps to one key convention (prefer bare canonical ULID for both, or a small typed CanonicalTaskId wrapper), and rename the param to activeRoleByTaskId. Observed while fixing @task-canonicalize-dispatch-task-identity.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: tests/session-lifecycle-events.test.ts asserts against a LOCAL re-implementation of DispatchEngine._emitSessionLifecycleEvent (a helper that mirrors the private method) instead of driving the real engine. Because the simulation was hand-copied from production, it encoded the SAME bug the production code had (task_ref = terminalEvent.task_id, no separate task_id) and kept passing — giving false confidence that let the canonical-identity payload bug survive two review cycles. This is distinct from the existing no-source-scanning rule: it is a parallel-implementation drift, not a source read. Pattern to flag in review: a test that copies production branching logic into the test file and asserts on the copy proves nothing about production. Antidote that worked here: an engine-driven test that subscribes to engine.eventBus and asserts the real invocation.completed/session.ended payloads. Consider a review-gates note discouraging parallel-reimplementation test helpers for dispatch event/payload logic.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review of @01KTDPVY9VEE3E3WGJFMYMGRHH, AC-tagged dispatch integration tests mocked runInvocation and proved event-bus payloads but not real persisted SessionMetadata/event history. This made a canonical-task-id regression visible only by manually tracing into src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts. Future reviews of dispatch identity changes should verify real persistence boundaries when tests mock the invocation runner.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Exported, side-effect-light CLI helper functions make review repros faster and more precise. During review of @01KTDPVY9VEE3E3WGJFMYMGRHH, importing filterSessions from src/cli/commands/session/log.ts with node --import tsx validated a canonical task filter edge case directly ({bare:1, at:0, slug:1}) without creating a temporary kspec project or mutating the review workspace. This pattern is worth preserving for CLI filtering/parsing code: keep pure logic exported separately from command wiring so reviewers can build small behavioral probes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A wide identity-canonicalization change (@task-canonicalize-dispatch-task-identity) leaked one un-canonicalized consumer site per review cycle across SIX fix cycles: scheduler dedupe/exclusivity, workspace registry/cleanup, reconcile key formats (see 01KTE2M9), terminal/session payloads, session metadata persistence, metadata-backed discovery, reviewer targeting, and finally the session log --task CLI filter (cycle 6). Each site compared task identity by raw task_ref or strict equality instead of the canonical task ULID, and each was found reactively by a reviewer rather than proactively. Root friction: there was no exhaustive, grep-able inventory of 'every place that keys on or compares task identity' to drive the change, so completeness was discovered piecemeal through review churn. Antidote for next time: before implementing a cross-cutting identity/normalization task, build and record (in the task or plan) an explicit checklist of all identity-comparison call sites (scheduler, workspace, registry/reconcile, payloads, persistence, discovery, CLI filters/targeting) and gate submission on each being converted + behaviorally tested, rather than relying on review cycles to enumerate them. Related: 01KTE2M9 (key-format asymmetry), 01KTE3Q9 (persistence-boundary test gap).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, focused oxlint over changed TypeScript files reports warnings from unchanged lines in those files, so reviewers must manually inspect the diff to decide whether warnings are new. A diff-aware focused-lint helper or review-gates command could report warnings intersecting changed hunks while preserving full changed-file lint as optional context.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full `npm test` run concurrently across multiple dispatch worktrees produces flaky failures (e.g. `git: /usr/bin/git: Text file busy` on `git init` in temp-repo tests) plus a ~74min wall-clock run. Two dispatch-workspace-config tests failed this way during a worktree-isolated full-suite run and passed cleanly on isolated re-run. The session-scoped result cache isolates results, but the git binary itself is contended across parallel agents. Friction: agents cannot distinguish env-contention flakes from real regressions without manual isolated re-runs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: In-process CLI tests (createTestProgram + parseAsync) that load split-format tasks throw TaskDataManagerError 'No storage backend registered for format split' unless the test first calls ensureSplitBackendRegistered(). The subprocess kspec CLI does this during bootstrap, but in-process command handlers do not. Cost discovery time when adding an in-process `agent run --task` canonical-identity test. Not captured in the testing convention rules or test-helper docs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached-reviewer merge recovery can leave a clean project-root checkout detached. In review @01KTFG86, the merge helper correctly refused to move refs while dev was checked out in /home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-dispatch and classified that checkout as auxiliary. Following the helper guidance required git checkout --detach in that root checkout; the retry merged safely, but the root checkout remained detached afterward. Existing merge-helper specs cover refusing auxiliary target locks, but the operator cleanup/restoration friction is not directly tracked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full 'npm test' suite (~43 min / 2569.8s cold in a fresh dispatch worktree) exceeds the dispatch headed-turn budget (600000ms / 10 min). On @add-resource-url-task-markdown-contract-tests the prior worker recorded three consecutive '[AGENT-FAIL] headed turn timed out after 600000ms' notes even though the artifacts were sound — the timeouts were the full-suite regression run, not the work. Mitigation for test-heavy/TDD tasks under dispatch: run only the touched test files (npm test -- <paths>) for fast iteration, reserve the full suite for a single final regression pass, prefer npm run test:shard1/2/3, and start the full run as a background command so the turn is not held open waiting on it. Consider whether dispatch should raise the turn timeout for test-heavy tasks or whether work-gates should explicitly steer dispatched workers to scoped/background test runs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: When resuming an in-flight task whose prior invocations failed (e.g. three '[AGENT-FAIL] turn timed out' notes on @add-resource-url-task-markdown-contract-tests), verify the already-authored artifacts before assuming they are broken. Here the three untracked files were complete and correct; the failures were full-suite-run timeouts, not bad work. Cross-checking the contract shapes (reviewResourceBytesUrl output, rewritePlanResourceLinks being project-unaware today) confirmed the it.fails FLIPPED-ON-FIX tests were red-as-designed, so the right move was commit+submit, not rewrite. Prior AGENT-FAIL notes describe invocation outcomes, not artifact quality — read the work before discarding it.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Tests-first contract tests for browser-URL ACs were authored at the URL-string layer (assert the rewritten / URL contains ?kspec_dir=), but the ACs Then clauses specify HTTP/byte outcomes (the browser fetch returns the SELECTED projects bytes, not the default projects or a 404). The shallow layer passed all gates yet a reviewer kicked it back as builder-only AC coverage. Concrete instance of work-gates AC coverage at the wrong abstraction layer rule, specific to UI URL-building features: when an ACs Then clause describes what the daemon/browser returns, a URL-shape assertion is not AC coverage — a behavioral fetch is required.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Pattern for HTTP-outcome AC coverage when the production route lands in a sibling task (tests-first / FLIPPED-ON-FIX): mount a stand-in route on the REAL projectContextMiddleware so only byte-serving is simulated while the project routing under contract (X-Kspec-Dir header > kspec_dir query > default) stays production; register two projects with the same ids but different bytes; fetch the builder/rewriter output WITHOUT X-Kspec-Dir and assert the selected projects bytes. Add a positive-control normal it that fetches a correctly-kspec_dir-scoped URL so the it.fails tests are proven to fail on the byte mismatch, not a setup/transport error. See tests/daemon-api/resource-url-browser-fetch-contract.test.ts.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer merge helper can refuse a clean integration-target checkout when the checkout retains a stale ignored .kspec-dispatch-workspace.json marker from an old integrated dispatch workspace. In this review, the root checkout was clean on dev, but the helper classified it as auxiliary until the stale marker was removed. Search found related merge-helper recovery items but no exact stale-marker cleanup coverage. Consider teaching the helper or dispatch cleanup to ignore, reconcile, or remove stale integrated markers before occupancy classification.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Folder-backed plan + entity-scoped resource seeding is reimplemented locally in 6+ daemon-api test files (plan-resources, plans, task-resolved-resources, task-resources, resource-url-browser-fetch-contract, entity-storage-incompatibility-routes): each hand-writes the project.plans.yaml 'kynetic_plans/plans' wrapper, the plans/<ulid>/ folder layout (plan.yaml + plan.md), and a resources.yaml manifest with hand-computed sha256. Cost this session: a test-failure cycle from writing project.plans.yaml as a bare array instead of the {kynetic_plans, plans:[...]} wrapper, plus a second cycle from recorded resource_refs sha256 not tracking the seeded bytes (tripping drift). A shared test helper (e.g. seedFolderPlanWithResources(dir, {ulid, slug, resources}) in tests/helpers, returning computed shas) would remove the boilerplate and make the wrapper format + sha-from-bytes invariant impossible to get wrong.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Web-UI unit tests run in the ROOT vitest project (node env), whose vitest.config.ts defines NO $app/$lib aliases. So the moment a shared web-ui util starts importing stores/project.svelte (which transitively imports $app/environment), EVERY test that imports that util chain without mocking the store breaks with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: $app/environment. This session: generalizing resource-link rewriting added a getSelectedProjectPath() import into the shared core used by both rewritePlanResourceLinks and rewriteTaskResourceLinks; three previously-passing tests imported buildPlanContentBlocks/rewritePlanResourceLinks WITHOUT a store mock. Two were fixed proactively, but the third (tests/plan-embedded-views.test.ts) only surfaced in the full regression run, costing an extra cycle. Mitigation: when a web-ui util newly reaches the project store (or any $lib/$app-dependent module), grep ALL test importers of that util chain and add the project-store vi.mock (mock BOTH the $lib/stores/project.svelte specifier AND the resolved ../packages/web-ui/src/lib/stores/project.svelte specifier, as existing web-ui tests do). Targeted runs of only the touched files miss transitive importers, so a final full/shard pass is required to catch them. A durable fix would be adding an $app/environment and $app/paths stub alias to the root vitest config so this whole failure class disappears.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Completing a FLIPPED-ON-FIX (tests-first) task requires more than converting it.fails to it. The contract suites also contain positive/negative CONTROL tests (normal it) whose assertions encode the PRE-FIX reality. Example: resource-url-browser-fetch-contract.test.ts had a guard named 'today the un-scoped rendered plan image URL falls back to the default project bytes' asserting the URL has NO kspec_dir and returns project A bytes. Once the fix lands, those controls fail because the URL now carries kspec_dir and returns project B bytes. They surfaced only in the full run as ordinary failures (not 'Expect test to fail'), so they are easy to miss if you grep only for it.fails. Mitigation when closing a FLIPPED-ON-FIX task: in each contract file, after flipping it.fails to it, also scan for control/guard tests named 'today...' or 'un-scoped' or 'falls back' or asserting the old URL shape, and update their expectations to the post-fix reality. The flip comments often literally say 'this guard project-A expectation is updated alongside flipping the it.fails tests' - treat that as a checklist item.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: A transformer's negative-path 'leaves it raw' unit test does NOT satisfy an AC whose Then clause requires the consuming UI to surface that raw value VISIBLY with actionable guidance. Concrete review kickback this session: @live-task-resource-markdown-rendering ac-unmatched-task-resource-reference-stays-raw passed every rewriteTaskResourceLinks unit test (unmatched ./resources/ stays raw in the markdown), yet the reviewer rejected it because the live task modal (TaskDetailContent.svelte) derived its 'Resources needing attention' guidance only from resolved_resources filtered to non-present statuses. An UNMATCHED reference has NO resolved_resources entry at all, so it produced zero guidance and rendered only as a broken whose path the reader never sees — 'raw in markdown' is not the same as 'visible to the user'. Related to 01KTMMHH (AC coverage at wrong abstraction layer) but a distinct failure mode: rewriter-passthrough vs UI-rendered visibility. Mitigation: when an AC's Then clause says a reference 'remains visible' or 'shows guidance', cover the UI's guidance computation directly, not just the transformer's raw-passthrough; and remember unmatched (no resolved entry) is a separate bucket from drift/missing/unresolved (which DO have entries).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: With no Svelte DOM render harness in the unit suite (root vitest is node env, no testing-library/svelte/jsdom), the way to give a UI-guidance AC genuine behavioral coverage is to extract the component's decision logic into a pure exported helper that the component consumes via $derived, then unit-test the helper directly. This session: factored findUnmatchedTaskResourceReferences (task-resource-links.ts) + extractResourceReferencePaths (resource-links.ts shared core); TaskDetailContent.svelte renders its unmatched-reference guidance solely from that helper's output, so 6 pure behavioral tests (unmatched detection, no-resolved-resources, resolved-but-non-present excluded, dedup, external-URL exclusion, no-reference cases) pin the modal's actual decision logic without a DOM render. Mirrors how the rewriter and drift detection were already covered. Keeps the component a thin wrapper over a tested function and avoids source-scanning tests (forbidden by work-gates).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch engine tests that assert on transient in-flight state (e.g. activeInvocationDetails) after only 'await waitForMockCall(runSpy)' can flake when runInvocation is mocked with mockResolvedValue. The mock resolves instantly, so dispatch's cleanup path (markDispatchWorkspaceIdle shadow op + activeInvocationDetails.delete) can run before the 10ms poll detects the call, deleting the record under the assertion. Fix pattern: gate the runInvocation mock on a test-controlled deferred so the invocation stays in-flight while asserting, then release and await it to drain cleanup. This mirrors the bootstrap-barrier pattern already used elsewhere in agent-dispatch-engine.test.ts. ~20 waitForMockCall(runSpy) sites in that file are potential latent instances; most already use barriers, but new tests reading post-spawn state should follow the gate idiom.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Static-export resource reviews are much more concrete when AC tests assert the full artifact contract: the snapshot metadata/rewritten markdown points at an exported_path, the file exists under assets/resources/<entity-type>/<ulid>/<relative-path>, and the bytes/hash match the recorded resource. In @01KTD8S2J7XS07K5DGD0FHHHDW this pattern made plan, task, review, drift, missing, and symlink-safety checks reviewable without source-scanning.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Fix-cycle resume hits a hidden state step: a task in needs_work cannot be submitted directly — 'kspec task submit' fails with 'Cannot submit task with status: needs_work. Task must be in_progress', requiring an intermediate 'kspec task start' (needs_work -> in_progress) first. The task-work skill Fix Cycle section (step 'Re-submit') documents 'kspec task submit @ref' but omits the required 'kspec task start' transition when resuming a needs_work task, so a worker following the steps literally errors before resubmitting. Hit during fix cycle on @update-resource-documentation-ui-task-markdown. Suggest the Fix Cycle steps explicitly include 'kspec task start @ref' before resubmit (or submit auto-transitions needs_work->in_progress).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Materialized task resources change the authoring path: kspec plan derive --materialize-resources rewrites a task resolved-resource path from <file> (plan-owned) to plan/<plan-ulid>/<file> (task-owned copy). Because the UI rewriter rewriteTaskResourceLinks matches ./resources/<path> by EXACT resolved path, a task description authored as ![x](./resources/diagram.png) renders for a plan-owned derive but silently stops rendering after materialization (no resolved resource has path diagram.png; it is plan/<plan-ulid>/diagram.png). Authors must reference ./resources/plan/<plan-ulid>/<file> for materialized copies. Surfaced while validating @validate-resource-lifecycle-e2e-temp-projects. Two follow-up angles worth triage: (1) docs AC ac-docs-name-task-resource-markdown on @resource-docs-ui-task-markdown-behavior should explicitly call out the plan/<plan-ulid>/ prefix for materialized references; (2) consider whether materialization should preserve the original ./resources/<file> authoring path so a description survives materialization unchanged. Note the existing rewriter unit test (resource-url-browser-fetch-contract) uses a synthetic materialized path (screens/home.png) that does not match real CLI output shape.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: De-risking a long multi-tool E2E chain by exercising it in a throwaway scratch run FIRST paid off: before writing tests/e2e/resource-lifecycle.spec.ts I ran the full CLI lifecycle (plan import -> derive default -> derive --materialize-resources -> review resource add -> export) in scratch temp dirs via bash and inspected the JSON at each step. This caught the non-obvious materialized path shape (plan/<plan-ulid>/<file>) that would otherwise have made the materialized browser-render assertions silently fail, and the 6-test spec passed on the first real run. Pattern: for cross-surface validation tasks, prove the data-producing chain in isolation before encoding it in a slow browser test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon code discoverability: src/daemon/ exists but the daemon server and all HTTP routes live in packages/daemon/src/; AGENTS.md structure tree does not mention packages/daemon or packages/shared, so agents repeatedly search src/ first. Review content endpoint additionally lives in routes/diff.ts rather than reviews.ts. Concrete cost: ~8 grep/find round-trips to locate GET /api/reviews/:id/content this session.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Generalize-first rewriter design paid off immediately: the shared rewriteEntityResourceLinks core built in @generalize-live-ui-resource-markdown-rewriting let the review structured-content viewer gain plan AND task resource markdown rendering via a ~100-line dispatch util (review-content-resources.ts) with zero new regex and full reuse of drift/unmatched semantics. Investing in the entity-generic helper one task earlier made the follow-up task mostly API plumbing plus tests.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-delta tasks that embed exact AC payloads execute deterministically under automation. Task @01KTTD04 (add daemon reliability delta ACs) included the literal AC ids and given/when/then text for all 7 ACs plus explicit how/testing guidance (verify no equivalent AC exists, use kspec batch with file-based payloads). Execution required zero interpretation: one dry-run-validated atomic batch, first-try success, no fix-cycle risk from paraphrasing. Pattern worth replicating when plans author spec-update tasks: put the exact AC text in the task description rather than describing ACs indirectly.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dependency/security reviews should include a minimum-supported-Node production install check when lockfile updates affect production dependencies. In review of @task-audit-fix-production-deps, npm audit, lint, typecheck, and full tests passed on Node 24, but Node 20 npm ci --omit=dev --engine-strict failed because file-type@22 requires Node >=22 while package.json still advertises >=20. Existing tracking covers Node docs and CI matrix, but not this review-gate/process check.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task description encoding the precise runtime interaction model paid off directly: @task-daemon-log-capture documented that routes/command.ts captures console functions as originals at module load and routes via AsyncLocalStorage, prescribed the import-order fix (logger tee as first entry-point import), and named a fallback. Implementation landed in one pass with no double-logging bug and all gates green. Pattern: for cross-cutting changes touching process-global state (console, cwd, process.exit), spell out the interception/ownership model and required ordering in the task description rather than leaving it to discovery.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle verification pattern: replicate the reviewer's exact failing check command (from the review record's check runner/evidence) locally before resubmitting. In @task-audit-fix-production-deps fix cycle 1, the review's failing check was 'Node 20 npm ci --omit=dev --engine-strict --ignore-scripts'; reproducing it verbatim (via npx node@20 against a temp package copy) before and after the fix gave direct evidence the blocker was resolved, and the thread reply could cite the reviewer's own check now passing. Generalizes to any fix cycle where the review records a concrete failing check — stronger signal than re-running generic gates.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Spec-delta tasks (spec mutation only, e.g. adding an AC to an existing implemented spec via 'kspec item ac add') trigger the task-start auto-sync that flips the linked spec's implementation status from implemented to in_progress, even though no implementation work regressed. Observed on @task-broken-shadow-safety-spec-delta: starting the task moved @broken-shadow-safety from implemented to in_progress purely because the task's spec_ref points at it. For the established existing-spec-delta task pattern this is misleading status churn and can surface as alignment-validation noise until the task completes. Possible direction: a task flavor/flag that opts out of implementation-status sync for spec-mutation-only work.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon parity features that hang off server-level wiring (global onError mappers, middleware) cannot be exercised by tests/daemon-api createTestApp — the production handler had to be mirrored into the test helper for the format-version 409 contract, creating a production/test drift point. The boundary is documented as deliberate (@task-clarify-in-process-daemon-api-helper-boundary) but there is no shared composition mechanism; each new global mapper must be wired twice and kept in sync by hand.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Empirically verifying framework semantics with a throwaway scratch script before designing around an assumption: a 10-line node -e Elysia experiment proved parent-level onError catches plugin-route errors and that route-group onError handlers fall through on undefined, which de-risked the daemon global error mapper design for @task-format-version-ceiling in under a minute. Cheaper and more reliable than doc-reading for behavior-critical framework questions.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Task description quality enabled a zero-fix-cycle dispatch run: @task-prepack-full-build-and-verification pre-stated a known tooling pitfall in its How section (npm pack --dry-run lifecycle behavior varies across npm versions), which let the worker detect that npm 11 does run prepack on dry runs and make a justified design deviation (--ignore-scripts on verification dry-run paths) with rationale recorded in task notes instead of a review fix cycle. Pattern: when plan-derived tasks document known tool quirks up front, workers can adapt safely. Worth replicating in plan authoring.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Forcing filesystem failure paths in tests: vi.mock('node:fs/promises', importOriginal) that spreads the actual module and overrides one function (e.g. rename), gated by a vi.hoisted() control flag and a path predicate (only sources matching '.repair-backup-'), cleanly forced the shadow restore-failure path in tests/shadow-restore-failure.test.ts while delegating all other fs calls to the real implementation. Behavioral alternative to vi.spyOn (unreliable for cross-module ESM per testing conventions) and avoids exporting test-only hooks from src/. Used for @task-shadow-restore-loud-failure double-failure coverage.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, full npm test can enter long quiet tails after visible test output, leaving reviewers unsure whether the run is healthy or hung. In this session the suite eventually passed, but I had to inspect the process tree manually to see an active Vitest worker and child CLI command. Consider adding a test-runner heartbeat or active-file/active-worker status line after a quiet interval so reviewers can distinguish normal long-tail execution from a stalled run without manual ps inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Executable-guidance tests: when an error message prescribes concrete shell recovery commands, write tests that parse the commands out of the message and execute them verbatim, asserting the system actually recovers — instead of only string-matching the message. On task-shadow-restore-loud-failure, review caught that the prescribed mv was wrong for occupied-destination states precisely because the reviewer executed it; the fix added tests running each prescribed rmdir/mv plus the re-run repair end-to-end, making guidance correctness regression-proof.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Security-fix regression tests need a verified-toothed payload. When hardening a shell-injection call site (e.g. migrating execSync shell-strings to spawnSync args arrays in src/utils/git.ts), a metacharacter test payload only proves anything if it (a) is valid input for the real producer AND (b) actually executes under the PRE-fix code path. Two non-obvious traps hit this session migrating git utils: git refnames forbid spaces, so $(touch f) is an invalid branch name — use a redirect like $(date>f) instead; and a payload with unbalanced trailing quotes makes the old shell invocation throw before the injection runs, so the test passes against BOTH old and new code (false coverage). Fix: before trusting the test, replay the old shell-string pattern against candidate values and confirm which actually create canary side-effect files. Settled payload: feat;$(date>canary-dollar);`date>canary-bt`;'q';dq"" — a valid refname whose substitution and backtick both fire under execSync but not under spawnSync.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Behavioral verification of emitted guidance: tests for shadow restore failures parse the prescribed recovery commands out of the error message and execute them verbatim through /bin/sh (plus re-running the prescribed kspec command), asserting recovery actually works end-to-end. This pattern caught both review blockers in @task-shadow-restore-loud-failure (state-unaware mv guidance, then shell-unsafe quoting) and generalizes: whenever code emits copy-pasteable commands, test by executing them, not by string-matching alone. See tests/shadow-restore-failure.test.ts executeRecoverySteps().
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatch task authoring pattern: @task-reenable-split-storage-ref-validation-test embedded pre-verified code-reading findings (exact file:line claims explicitly marked 'trust but re-verify the line numbers'), the precise reason the naive approach would fail (strict_refs default makes dangling refs errors, not warnings), and verbatim spec-edit text for known spec drift. Worker re-verified all claims with 3 greps, all held; tests passed first run and the task went start-to-submit with zero rework. Embedding verified claims plus uncertainty markers in dispatched task descriptions is a high-leverage authoring pattern — extends @01KFA0DV (clear problem statements) with the verify-and-mark-uncertainty nuance.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fully-skipped test suites rot silently. The skipped E2E triage suite (deleted in @task-daemon-triage-api-tests) carried two assertions that no longer matched current behavior: a strict item_snapshot equality against inbox fixture text that had since drifted, and a 422 expectation for missing fields where the project-context middleware now normalizes Elysia validation errors to 400. When porting or re-enabling skipped tests, re-verify every assertion against current behavior (run them, check fixtures, check error normalization in daemon-api/errors.test.ts) rather than copying verbatim. One lingering skip remains: tests/e2e/tasks.spec.ts:641 test.skip.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Vacuous test setup via silent 'kspec init' failure: 'kspec init' prompts interactively and aborts with exit 2 when stdin is closed (every vitest subprocess), printing the prompt text to stdout. The kspec() test helper's backwards-compat rule 'return result instead of throwing when exitCode != 0 but stdout is non-empty' then swallows the failure, so beforeEach continues against a bare unrecognized .kspec/ dir that initContext() never resolves. Search/load commands then scan nothing and tests pass vacuously on the 'No matches found' echo. This was the true root cause behind the skipped AC-7 combined search test (task-fix-search-meta-entity-tests) — deeper than the invalid fixture ULIDs the task described. Remaining callers with the same hazard: tests/native-guard-setup.test.ts:26 and tests/cli/session-note-limit.test.ts:21. Correct pattern: setupShadowDetection() + hand-written fixtures (plus seedSplitTask() for tasks, since split storage is the default and monolithic project.tasks.yaml entries fail the migration check).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Silent YAML number-parse trap with testUlid(): testUlid() returns an all-digit ULID (01000000000000000000000000), so embedding it UNQUOTED in a YAML template-string fixture makes the YAML parser read it as a number. Schema validation then skips the record with only a stderr warning, surfacing as confusing downstream 404s/empty lists. Hit in tests/daemon-api/triage.test.ts shadow-commit test (fix cycle for @task-daemon-triage-api-tests). Rule of thumb: always quote _ulid values in YAML template strings. Candidate for a testing convention rule.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fake shadow worktrees in test fixtures (setupFixtures/setupShadowDetection) enable shadow DETECTION but git commands inside .kspec/ fail, so commitIfShadow silently returns false — tests cannot assert shadow commits and the gap invites false AC coverage claims (exactly what review 01KTVCYP caught on @task-daemon-triage-api-tests). Working pattern now exists: the Shadow commits block in tests/daemon-api/triage.test.ts builds a real orphan kspec-meta worktree via mktree/commit-tree plumbing (no git>=2.42 dependency) and asserts semantic commit subjects from git log.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review success pattern: for trait AC coverage that depends on shadow persistence, a daemon route integration test can create a real linked kspec-meta worktree, drive the actual mutation routes, and assert semantic shadow commit subjects. This converted a prior false coverage annotation into behavior that is concrete, reviewable, and regression-resistant.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Negative-check verification can clobber uncommitted work: pattern of mutating a file (sed) to prove a new test fails, then restoring with git checkout <file>, reverts to HEAD and silently wipes any uncommitted fix to that same file (happened in @task-standardize-node-version-docs: doc fix had to be re-applied). Safe orderings: commit the fix before the negative check, or restore by re-applying the inverse edit instead of git checkout.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Doc/content-scanning tests: before encoding a detection regex in a consistency test, dry-run it over the full real corpus with a one-off node script (in @task-standardize-node-version-docs: confirmed exactly the 6 real Node-version statements across 47 markdown docs, zero false positives), then run a negative check proving the test fails on a regressed input. Catches both vacuous-pass and false-positive failure modes before commit.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Elysia 1.4 does not provide the error context helper under app.handle() (WebStandard adapter, Node) — route handlers destructuring { error: errorResponse } fail with an opaque 500 (error is not a function) in route-handler tests, while working in the production adapter. The polyfill (a .resolve hook mapping error to set.status + body) lives only in tests/daemon-api/helpers.ts; test files that build their own Elysia app (e.g. tests/daemon-command-api.test.ts) must rediscover and copy it. Cost this session: a full debug cycle during the command-timeout task before finding the existing polyfill. Any new route returning errorResponse and tested outside tests/daemon-api/ will hit this.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review @01KTVM27, a kspec review comment body with markdown backticks was passed through a shell command and command-substituted before kspec received it. The malformed blocker had to be superseded and resolved. Long review bodies need shell-safe submission habits or CLI support for file/stdin payloads.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing unresolved observations @01KNPC03 and @01KSDFC3; this session reinforced the same review-comment shell-safety gap.

observations.content: No quality gate runs at the declared engines minimum Node version, so code using APIs newer than the floor (e.g. readdirSync recursive:true, Node 20.1+) passes every gate on dev/CI Node and ships a silent incompatibility. Caught this session only by a reviewer's manual node@20.0.0 repro during @task-standardize-node-version-docs review. Engines-floor compatibility is currently enforced by reviewer diligence, not tooling.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review of @task-standardize-node-version-docs, running the focused release-packaging test under the declared minimum runtime () directly verified the previous compatibility blocker. For future changes tied to package engine floors, include a focused gate under the exact declared minimum runtime instead of relying only on the developer's current Node version.
observations.author: codex-reviewer
observations.resolution: Superseded immediately during reflection: shell command substitution removed the focused command text from the observation content; replacement observation records the intended success pattern.

observations.content: During review of @task-standardize-node-version-docs, running the focused release-packaging test under the declared minimum runtime (npx -y node@20.0.0 scripts/test.cjs tests/release-packaging.test.ts --fresh) directly verified the previous compatibility blocker. For future changes tied to package engine floors, include a focused gate under the exact declared minimum runtime instead of relying only on the developer current Node version.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: Dispatched tasks whose AC evidence requires watching a long GitHub Actions run (~40 min matrix on test.yml) collide with the 60-minute invocation timeout: the prior invocation on @task-ci-node-version-matrix timed out purely waiting on gh run watch, wasting the invocation and requiring a resume. Mitigation that worked on resume: trigger the CI run early, run all local gates while it executes, poll only the AC-relevant jobs (not the whole run), and submit once those jobs pass instead of blocking on unrelated jobs like e2e. Consider documenting this pattern in worker guidance or raising the timeout for CI-verification tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: PR-less verification of CI workflow changes worked exactly as designed on @task-ci-node-version-matrix: add workflow_dispatch to the workflow, push the task branch, gh workflow run test.yml --ref <task-branch> (the dispatched run uses the branch's workflow file), record the run URL in a task note as AC evidence. Produced concrete passing-run evidence for the Node 20/24 matrix without opening a GitHub PR, consistent with the repo policy reserving PRs for release-track merges. Replicable for any future .github/workflows change.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review gate friction: this mechanical three-file web UI cleanup required waiting for a full npm test run that took 3152.4s before approval/merge. Existing coverage: @task-test-cache-env-key addresses cache correctness, and @01KS9FFH covers format fail-fast ordering, but no searched item directly covers risk-scoped or faster review-gate evidence for narrow diffs. Consider triaging whether review gates can preserve confidence while using cached, sharded, or risk-scoped evidence for low-risk changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of @task-workspace-packages-private, npm test reported one unrelated failure, continued through visible suite output, then left the Vitest parent process alive with no worker children or progress. The reviewer had to inspect process state, run a focused retry, create @01KTW8SG for the flaky suite, and manually terminate the stale process tree before completing review. This suggests the test runner could benefit from stale-parent detection, clearer timeout diagnostics, or cleanup handling for hung Vitest parents after failures.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: During review test triage, running a fresh targeted npm test rerun cleared the same session-scoped test cache directory and removed the original full-suite failure log before it could be inspected. Preserve failed-run logs across --fresh reruns or copy them to a stable archive path so rerunning flaky tests does not erase evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Flaky-test forensics via session-scoped runner logs: the intermittent upgrade-folder-storage failure was root-caused without any reproduction attempt by grepping /tmp/kspec-test-cache/*/  logs from OTHER agent sessions — one preserved the exact subprocess crash (ESM export mismatch from a mid-run dist/ rewrite). Pattern: when investigating an intermittent test failure, search existing cached runner logs across sessions for the failing test name BEFORE attempting repeated reproduction runs; the evidence often already exists.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Failed/hung test-run evidence survives only incidentally: scripts/test.cjs deletes its temp runId .log/.json after caching, and a run whose Vitest parent hangs and is killed never reaches storeCachedResults — the failure evidence exists only if the process died before cleanup. The upgrade-folder-storage flake task started with no failing-assertion details for exactly this reason; diagnosis depended on a different session's leftover temp log. Improvement direction: persist failed-run summaries (failing test names + log path) durably, e.g. always store the log under the cache dir on non-zero exit even when the JSON reporter output is missing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached reviewer merge helper cleanly merged approved task work from a detached review snapshot into the dispatch target without requiring manual checkout or persistent target worktree management.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate success observation; existing detached reviewer merge helper success observations already cover this pattern. Keeping the workflow notes, but no separate new success observation needed.

observations.content: The task-work skill's Fix Cycle section (templates/skills/task-work) lists read review -> fix -> reply/resolve -> note -> 're-submit with kspec task submit', but submit rejects needs_work tasks ('Task must be in_progress') — every fix-cycle worker must run kspec task start first, which the skill never mentions. Add the start step to the fix-cycle checklist so workers don't discover it via the error message.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle pattern that worked (task-stabilize-upgrade-folder-storage-test cycle 1): instead of only patching the call sites that raced (npm pack prepack, build:daemon), the lock's reentrancy was made label-aware so any future cross-kind nested build/test fails fast with a diagnostic. Converting a silent race into a deterministic, explained failure makes regressions of the whole class self-reporting rather than intermittent. Tracing started from the reviewer's exact crash signature (missing export name) to the only in-suite trigger that rewrites that file (tsc via prepack), which kept the fix targeted.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Incident-to-lint-guard pattern: the npm pack prepack hazard was already documented in a release-packaging.test.ts comment, but the comment did not protect a second call site (cli-serve.test.ts), which caused the flaky workflow-runs dist export failure. Encoding the invariant as a custom oxlint rule (tools/eslint-rules/no-unguarded-npm-pack.js) with behavioral lint tests made it enforceable for all current and future call sites. When a test-hygiene invariant is discovered via incident, prefer a narrow custom lint rule over a code comment — comments inform one file, rules protect the whole tree.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Storage-format migrations that remove a legacy reader must migrate checked-in fixture snapshots (and the test helpers papering over them) in the same change. The kynetic 1.2 folder-backed migration left tests/e2e/fixtures/ on monolithic plan/review storage, with setupFixtures masking the gap via manifest overwrite + shell materialization and a comment deferring the Playwright fixture 'to keep watcher specs happy'. That deferral surfaced later as 45 deterministic E2E failures (route 500s) that looked like flakiness. Pattern: when a compatibility gate goes strict, grep for fixtures still on the old format before merging.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Regenerating fixtures by running the real migration code (applyPlanMigration/applyReviewMigration) against a temp copy, then copying results back, guaranteed the E2E fixture matched the storage managers' exact on-disk contract (sidecar split, lean index projection, resources.yaml stubs). Hand-authoring folder layouts would have risked subtle drift; the migration-code approach also exercised the production path as a side benefit. Replicable for any future storage-layout fixture refresh.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle dispatch raced manual maintainer intervention on @task-stabilize-workflow-runs-cli-dist-export (2026-06-12). The fix cycle was created for a merge conflict, but the maintainer resolved the conflict and merged the branch into dev (adefc545ee) before the worker invocation ran. The dispatched context was stale: it instructed conflict resolution and listed an outdated dev head, so the worker had to discover via git inspection that the merge already existed; the maintainer then completed the task concurrently mid-invocation, making the worker's task complete fail with already-completed (and roll back a batched note). Consider a pre-dispatch staleness check for fix-cycle invocations: if the canonical branch head is already an ancestor of the integration target, skip dispatch or annotate the context as already-merged. Related: @01KPA0Q5 (pre-dispatch dedup checks).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Merged-tree gate verification after manual conflict resolution proved valuable on @task-stabilize-workflow-runs-cli-dist-export: the conflict-resolution merge commit on dev differed from every tree either review had tested (two independently-reviewed branches composing), so the worker fast-forwarded the canonical branch to the merge commit and ran full gates there — format, lint, typecheck, full 10562-test suite, kspec validations. This both verified the semantic composition (new no-unguarded-npm-pack lint rule + sibling task's build/test lock) and validated the dist-rewrite fix under real contention, since the suite passed while another agent's full suite ran concurrently in a sibling worktree. Pattern: whenever a merge result differs from all reviewed trees, run gates on the integrated head before completing.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During automated review of @task-dashboard-summary-adoption, the required full npm test gate passed but took 2573.2s (~43 minutes) for a narrow dashboard/API change. This creates high review latency even when focused lint, typecheck, unit tests, and targeted dashboard E2E are clean. Consider triaging whether reviewer gates can use stronger cache reuse, sharded full-suite evidence, or a policy for task-scoped verification plus separately scheduled full-suite confirmation without weakening regression protection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task authoring pattern for dispatch (from @task-catch-justification-comments): a hygiene task with an exact file list, explicit hard bounds (comments only, no semantic/test changes), and a machine-checkable violation signal (any test-file modification = bounds violated) enabled clean autonomous completion with zero scope drift. Worker verified bounds mechanically by grepping the diff for non-comment added lines. Worth replicating for future comments-only or refactor-bounded dispatch tasks.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2E assertion budgets derived from focused single-worker timing are guaranteed flake under parallel runs: the daemon-restart reconnect test asserted Connected within 10s (30s test timeout), but spec-mandated exponential backoff (@web-dashboard ac-28, 30s cap) plus the global daemon port-start lock shared by all parallel workers means the first reconnect attempt after restart can be a full 30s gap away. Lesson: derive timing budgets for E2E assertions from worst-case spec schedules plus fixture lock contention, not observed focused-run timing. Fixed in @01KTY55GSE54FCQ5FVRW0JNXJF.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Flake-stabilization task description included the exact failing test path/line, observed failure mode (30s timeout in full run), and the focused-rerun command that passed (--workers=1). This made root-cause investigation immediate — the parallel-vs-focused asymmetry pointed straight at lock contention vs backoff timing with zero re-discovery. Worth replicating when filing flake tasks from review runs.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Test waits whose budgets exceed the 45s vitest testTimeout (or are unbounded) convert environmental contention into diagnostics-free timeout failures. In @01KTY9DTPW4E1G33BEFFQNK47X the global port-start lock wait has a 120s budget and the post-SIGTERM exit wait was unbounded, so when full-suite contention pushed either past 45s the test died as opaque STACK_TRACE_ERROR with zero diagnostics — distinct from 01KTY9Z3 (budgets too SMALL under load): here budgets are too LARGE relative to the test timeout to ever report. Rule of thumb: every wait inside a test should be bounded BELOW the test timeout and fail with a diagnostic payload (waitForStartup is the model; waitForChildExitBounded in tests/daemon-last-exit.test.ts applies it to exit waits).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Documenting flake signatures in vitest.config.ts heavySerialSuites comments (symptom + mechanism, e.g. the websocket-protocol.test.ts entry: STACK_TRACE_ERROR in full suite, deterministic in isolation, cross-file contention cause) made root-causing a new flake near-instant: the daemon-last-exit SIGTERM flake matched the documented signature exactly, pointing straight at the established remedy. Pattern worth replicating: when quarantining a suite or adding a contention workaround, record the observed failure signature and the causal mechanism in a comment at the config site, not just in task notes.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: E2E flake stabilization technique (proven on @stabilize-websocket-duplicate-event-e2e-response-count-flake): for tests that assert API traffic counts while proxying the WebSocket to a real daemon, (1) enumerate every noise source feeding the measured signal first — delayed file-watcher invalidation timers (+650ms/+1500ms in ws-invalidation.ts), slow in-flight responses under parallel load, late cache-warming domain_ready broadcasts; (2) make the measurement hermetic by cutting server->client WS forwarding after page load (safe: client manager has no heartbeat, daemon pong timeout is 90s); (3) assert on request INITIATION (synchronous on the client when invalidation fires) instead of response arrival; (4) any settle/stability window must exceed the longest delayed invalidation timer (1500ms). Root-cause analysis also proved product dedup correct before touching the test, avoiding a symptom patch.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review friction: AC coverage validation can be syntactically correct while semantically stale after a spec-only AC rewrite. In @task-respec-daemon-project-roster-persistence, @multi-directory-daemon ac-15 was changed from restart-empty/no-persistence to restore-from-daemon-config, but the existing AC-tagged tests still asserted the old empty-after-restart behavior and the full suite passed. Reviewers need to compare changed AC text against the asserted behavior, not just rely on kspec validate completeness. Related but not duplicate: @test-annotation-sweep and @ac-annotation-integrity-reporting cover annotation syntax/target validity; inbox @01KTYQ1RG covers metadata/spec-catalog gate profiles.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Metadata-only/no-code-diff reviews currently pay the full required code gate cost. In @01KV3TKK5WE5TZHTNKEDTH03JR, the reviewed surface was four plan notes plus one relates_to edge, with git diff feat/ui-redesign...HEAD empty and branch tips already equal, yet npm test still ran 2787 suites and took 2889.4s. Consider a reviewed, explicit gate policy for shadow-state-only tasks that preserves auditability with kspec validation and targeted record verification while avoiding unnecessary full-suite runs when no code changed.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Respec tasks that reword a single AC within a multi-AC feature have no granular way to mark just that one AC as not-yet-implemented. When @multi-directory-daemon ac-15 was reworded from a no-persistence contract to a restart-restore contract (now future work), the honest signal would be to flag ac-15 as not_started while the other ~40 ACs stay implemented.
