But implementation status is feature-level only, and `kspec item set <feature> --status in_progress` cascades to all 21 child items (interactive prompt), which would mislabel the bulk of genuinely-implemented behavior. Workaround used: leave the feature at implemented and track the outstanding AC via an explicit follow-up task with spec_ref to the feature. This works but is implicit — nothing on the spec itself signals ac-15 is unimplemented. Candidate improvements: per-AC implementation status, or a documented convention that outstanding ACs in an otherwise-implemented feature are tracked by an open task with spec_ref so reviewers/auditors can find them. Related: a respec that changes an AC's meaning silently invalidates existing AC test annotations pointing at it, with no automated detection — the worker must manually re-check coverage of the reworded AC.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Respec tasks that add an unimplemented AC requirement to an already-'implemented' spec must downgrade the parent spec's implementation status to in_progress, or kspec validate --alignment fails. Use 'kspec item set @spec --status in_progress --no-cascade' to update only the parent without mislabeling already-implemented child items. Observed: this respec/spec-alignment step was missed in the initial work AND in fix cycle 1 (which explicitly declined to change status, unaware of --no-cascade), causing two extra review cycles on task @01KV3TKKGFPS4FT2Z0SCG6Q1JM before it was resolved.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review completion, kspec task complete auto-synced the linked decision spec implementation status from in_progress to implemented. For spec-only or cross-spec tasks where implementation is split across follow-up work, this status mutation can be easy to miss even when the command warns to verify AC coverage. Consider making completion-time spec status sync more explicit or reviewable in the audit output.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review snapshots worked well when paired with fresh kspec review records and the detached-reviewer merge helper: prior review threads clarified fix-cycle verification, required checks made the approval gate auditable, and the helper merged the canonical branch into the target without checking out the target in the detached snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: [from task @task-identity-endpoint-classifier dispatch run] Dispatch task workspace did not materialize plan-owned resource_refs. The task prompt listed handoff resources as [OK] at relative paths (./resources/handoff/docs/00-product-context.md, etc.) and warned to read them, but ./resources/ was empty in the worker worktree. The files only existed under the plan shadow storage (.kspec/plans/<ulid>/resources/handoff/) and the separate source repo; I had to locate them via `find /`. Either materialize declared resource_refs into the worktree (or a known path) at bootstrap, or have the prompt cite the resolvable path so workers don't have to hunt.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: [from task @task-identity-endpoint-classifier dispatch run] Daemon package TypeScript types are not covered by any quality gate. `npm run typecheck` is `tsc --noEmit` over src/ only; the daemon (packages/daemon) is bundled by esbuild (build:daemon) which is transpile-only, and standalone `tsc` in packages/daemon fails structurally (rootDir/module-resolution errors from cross-package src imports). Net effect: a type error in a daemon route is caught only if a test happens to exercise it, never by typecheck/lint/build. Consider a daemon-specific tsc --noEmit config (composite/project references) wired into the typecheck gate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: No shared vitest helper for SSR-rendering Svelte 5 components — web-ui component behavior was previously only covered by Playwright E2E (the old static-analysis component tests were deleted). For @ui-view-header I built an ad hoc harness: create a web-ui vite server, ssrLoadModule(svelte/server).render + ssrLoadModule(svelte).createRawSnippet for snippet props, parse the body with jsdom, assert on rendered DOM. This is fully behavioral and fast (in the default vitest pool). A reusable tests/helpers component-render helper would let future web-ui component tests assert rendered output without standing up E2E.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review of @task-view-header-status-tokens found that shared status-token tests verified resolver determinism but did not exercise actual list/detail surfaces, allowing bespoke status rendering to remain in sibling views. For future shared UI substrate work, include at least one cross-surface behavioral assertion against real consumers, not only the shared utility table.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Additive config-schema changes are silently breaking for not-yet-rebuilt kspec binaries. When a strict sub-schema (e.g. IdentityConfigSchema in src/parser/config.ts) rejects an unknown key, loadProjectConfig treats the WHOLE config as invalid and falls back to ALL defaults (dropping unrelated dispatch/coverage/daemon settings) with only a warning. Hit this when adding identity.agent_aliases: a kspec binary built from an older checkout dropped coverage.scan_paths, which silently made a `kspec validate --completeness` run scan nothing and report a misleadingly clean result. Impact: any additive config key is effectively a breaking change during the ship/deploy gap, and the failure is silent + total rather than scoped. Worth considering per-section fallback (or preserving recognized keys) so an unknown/newer key degrades only its own section, plus a louder signal than a single warning line.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Adopting the shared StatusBadge/status-token source on a surface changes its rendered status text from the raw lowercase value (e.g. 'active', 'completed') to the token's capitalized label (e.g. 'Active', 'Completed'). Existing tests that assert the old raw text (toContainText('active'), getByText('completed'), etc.) break silently and are easy to miss in the diff — during @task-view-header-status-tokens this bit twice (a mock-data list test plus two infinite-scroll assertions far from the edited lines). Mitigation for the @ui-view-header redesign track: when a future adoption task replaces a bespoke status helper with StatusBadge, grep the surface's e2e/unit specs for the raw lowercase state strings and re-point them at the shared token (assert data-status-domain/data-status-state attributes or the capitalized label) in the same change, and always run the modified surface's e2e specs before resubmitting.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During code review, targeted runtime reproductions against the changed public contract are useful after reading AC tests: a small node --import tsx repro caught the LocalStorageBackend degraded remove() edge case even though the focused unit tests and full npm test suite passed.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: web-ui UNIT tests live in the ROOT tests/ tree, not beside their source: tests/web-ui/<name>.test.ts and flat tests/web-ui-*.test.ts (e2e in tests/e2e/). When removing or renaming an exported symbol in packages/web-ui/src, a reference grep scoped to packages/web-ui/ misses these and the breakage only surfaces as a full-suite failure (~40min). When refactoring web-ui exports, grep the whole repo (root tests/ included) for references first. Encountered while removing board-utils getStatusClasses for @task-view-header-status-tokens.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Adding a runtime (value, not type-only) import of a private workspace package (e.g. classifyActor from @kynetic-ai/shared) into core/CLI code passes typecheck, lint, and all dev-runtime tests because the workspace symlink resolves it — but the PUBLISHED package breaks at install with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, since the main package ships only dist/ and does not bundle the private dep. The only gate that catches this is the single cli-serve "npm-installed package with all deps available" test buried in the full suite; a worker running shards or just new tests would miss it and ship a broken package. All pre-existing core/daemon @kynetic-ai/shared imports were type-only (erased), so there was no precedent to copy. Fix this session was bundleDependencies + files:[dist] on shared. Worth a cheap guard: a typecheck/lint or build-time check that flags a new runtime import of an unbundled private workspace package from a tsc-compiled (non-bundled) entrypoint, so this is caught without relying on one slow E2E pack test.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatched task @task-shortcut-registry declared two handoff resources marked [OK] (handoff-app-shell-navigation -> ./resources/handoff/docs/01-app-shell-and-navigation.md; shot-command-palette -> ./resources/handoff/shots/r2-app-shell-palette.png), but the resources/ directory did not exist in the mutable worker worktree. The worker had to implement without the intended design/handoff context. Investigate whether worker-worktree bootstrap should materialize declared resources (or surface a resolvable path/command), or whether [OK] should be clarified to mean 'declared' rather than 'present-in-workspace'. Scope: medium (dispatch worktree bootstrap + resource resolution).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Replicable web-ui pattern: keep behavioral logic as a plain-TS core (no Svelte runes) with a thin .svelte/runes layer on top, mirroring src/lib/preferences/. Because the vitest config runs in node with no Svelte plugin, this gives full acceptance-criteria coverage via fast node unit tests while components/listeners stay e2e-covered. Used for the keyboard shortcut registry (registry/chord/reserved/platform as plain TS; root layout owns the single window listener).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Dispatched task workers cannot resolve plan-owned resource CONTENT from the task/CLI surface. A task body referenced resources via ./resources/handoff/... (relative paths that do not exist in the dispatch worktree); kspec task get lists the resources as [OK] but exposes no resolvable path; kspec plan resource get returns metadata plus a manifest-relative path but no content and no absolute/worktree path. The worker had to fall back to find / to locate the files under .kspec/plans/<ulid>/resources/. Consider: a CLI affordance that prints resource content or an absolute worktree-resolvable path (e.g. kspec task resource get/cat, or --content / --path on kspec plan resource get), so dispatched workers consuming resource_refs do not have to spelunk the shadow-branch plan directory.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: The web-ui type gate is not a usable binary pass/fail check for workers. npm run check (svelte-kit sync + svelte-check) carries a large pre-existing error baseline (~62 errors, dominated by the $page.params.id string|undefined pattern), so a worker cannot tell whether their change introduced new type errors without git stash + re-run to diff the counts. Root npm run typecheck (tsc) skips .svelte files entirely, so component/route type regressions are invisible to the documented quality gate. Consider a baseline-aware svelte-check wrapper (fail only on NEW errors) or recording an accepted-error baseline, so web-ui tasks have a real type gate.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review task resources can be reported as OK in task context while the advertised handoff files are not materialized at their paths in the review snapshot. During @task-actor-display-next-actor review, resources/handoff/docs and resources/handoff/reference-src paths were absent, so the reviewer could not inspect the provided screenshots/source handoff directly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For shared display primitive reviews, searching for the raw recorded field across nested components after reading the changed diff can catch missed adoption points. In @task-actor-display-next-actor, rg for entry.author/review.author/verdict.reviewer exposed inline structured-content and diff thread renderers that still bypassed ActorDisplay.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Hidden packaging invariant: src/ (the unbundled tsc-built CLI) may import @kynetic-ai/shared ONLY as erased types (import type), never as a runtime value. @kynetic-ai/shared is a private workspace package, not a runtime dependency of the published @kynetic-ai/spec; the daemon/web-UI consume it via type-only imports or by bundling (esbuild/vite). A VALUE import from anything reachable through src/parser/index.ts (which the daemon eagerly loads) compiles cleanly, passes typecheck, and passes dev/test via the node_modules workspace symlink — then fails ONLY in the installed standalone package as a late ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, surfaced solely by tests/cli-serve.test.ts ('start daemon from npm-installed package'). Hit during @task-actor-normalization-upgrade: the actor migration value-imported buildActorClassifier from shared; fix was to ship the pure classifier in core (src/parser/actor-classifier.ts) pinned to shared by a parity test. There is no lint rule, type error, or documented convention enforcing this at authoring time — only a single late installed-package test. Distinct from observation @01KNMF4A (which is the inverse: daemon->src type imports being blocked). Potential guardrail: an oxlint rule (or convention) forbidding non-type imports of @kynetic-ai/shared from src/, catching it at lint time instead of a late E2E-style failure.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Daemon API tests that run without the production entity cache can unintentionally codify degraded detail-enrichment behavior as acceptable. In review @01KV5VBT, a session breadcrumb test accepted a single-session-segment response for a task-scoped session because createTestApp had no entity cache, even though the task required the owning task/spec chain plus the session. Consider a test helper or review/testing guidance that makes cache-dependent detail routes provide a ready cache fixture or explicitly assert warming/fallback semantics.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Reviewer-created temp-project probes are effective for upgrade-path review: synthesizing the pre-upgrade layout caught a dry-run actor-normalization gap that storage-ready fixtures and the full test suite missed. Future upgrade reviewers should probe both the pre-upgrade and post-migration states when a dry-run step depends on earlier migration output.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: The shared BreadcrumbAncestryResolver (src/lib/breadcrumb-ancestry.ts) degrades to a shorter/single-segment chain in two indistinguishable cases: (a) an ancestor genuinely does not exist, and (b) a route under-provisions inputs — e.g. constructing the resolver with items:[] on a cold cache. Because both produce a valid-looking shorter chain, a route that fails to supply the parent collection silently truncates the breadcrumb instead of erroring. The sessions detail route hit exactly this: its cold-cache branch dropped task_ref and built a resolver with items:[], returning a session-only chain for a task-scoped session (caught in review as a @ui-breadcrumb ac-10 violation). Sibling routes (item/task/plan/review) avoided it only because they already disk-fallback to load items for other fields. Direction: either give all breadcrumb-serving routes a shared 'build ancestry inputs from cache-or-disk' helper so input provisioning can't diverge per route, or have the resolver distinguish 'no parent' from 'parent inputs absent' so under-provisioning surfaces in tests/review rather than as a quiet degraded chain.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review thread/reply bodies containing shell metacharacters (the literal codex@openai.com at-sign, dollar signs, backticks) get mangled by shell expansion when posted via kspec review reply/thread --body. Evidence: all 6 threads on review 01KV5VA7 (task task-review-author-resolution) had a mangled first entry where identifiers/code vanished, each requiring a manually re-typed Correction for the mangled shell-expanded body above follow-up. The development convention already says to use file-based or quoted-heredoc payloads for special-character/multiline content, but the reviewer agent (codex-acp) keeps tripping it on review prose. Candidate: add a --body-file/stdin payload to review reply/thread and remind reviewer agents to use it for any body containing code or at/dollar tokens.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: For a centralize-resolution-at-the-boundary refactor, making the centralized value a REQUIRED parameter on the leaf constructors (not an optional with a fallback) converts the architectural rule into a compile-time invariant. After removing the in-constructor getAuthor fallback and typing author as required, tsc enumerated every remaining caller that still bypassed the shared actor-write utility (addNote, the verdict-transition system note, several tests) - turning the reviewer-flagged no-independent-fallback rule into a mechanically-checkable contract and surfacing bypasses the prior cycle missed. Reusable for the sibling actor-identity tasks (e.g. normalization-upgrade).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle review pattern: anchoring re-review on the prior review's blocker threads, then checking the fix-cycle delta and targeted call-site searches, produced an efficient and auditable review. In @task-review-author-resolution, this verified six resolved blockers without re-litigating unrelated branch history, supported a concise evidence log, and cleanly separated approval from the later detached-merge conflict.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Upgrade-pipeline steps that READ records run during 'kspec upgrade --dry-run' BEFORE the storage-migration block promotes the layout. A step that uses folder-only loaders (loadReviewRecordsFromFolders/loadPlansFromFolders/split-only task manager) and gates itself on a 'fully promoted' manifest check (task=split AND plan=folder AND review=folder) will silently return 'skipped' on any not-yet-promoted project, disabling dry-run preview — caught as a review blocker on @task-actor-normalization-upgrade (violated @actor-history-normalization ac-4). Design rule for future upgrade steps: use the format-aware loaders (loadReviewRecords/loadPlans, which read both legacy monolithic and folder layouts), gate only WRITES (real runs) on promotion, let dry-run preview run on any layout, and defer (surface, don't drop/crash) record kinds whose storage genuinely cannot be read yet.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle worker path has no step forcing re-sync against the integration target before resubmit when a task was kicked back for a reviewer-side merge conflict. A reviewer-approved task (01KV4CD9, cycle 2) returned to needs_work solely because the detached merge helper aborted on a content conflict in packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts against an advanced feat/ui-redesign. The worker could resubmit the SAME approved commit that still conflicts — Jacob had to add a manual note 'specifically to prevent resubmitting the same approved commit that still conflicts.' kspec task-work fix-cycle guidance covers addressing review threads but does not say: when the kickback reason is a merge conflict, merge/rebase the current integration target into the branch and resolve before resubmit. Consider making this explicit in fix-cycle guidance, or having submit warn when the branch does not contain the integration target head. Reviewer-side counterpart already tracked in inbox @01KRD2RV (richer helper conflict output).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review, a small temp-project behavioral reproduction of the suspected operator-map edge case found a real spec violation that green unit tests and gates missed: non-canonical actor-map targets were persisted verbatim. This is a useful reviewer pattern for data migrations: when a finding depends on user-provided inputs, run the smallest end-to-end mutation that proves the persisted state, not just the resolver unit path.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing success observations @01KV4QAT and @01KV5XPH covering targeted runtime/temp-project reproduction as an effective review pattern; no new action needed.

observations.content: Interactive web-ui components have no client-mount unit-test harness. The repo's component tests only SSR-render via svelte/server (static markup), so popover open/close, keyboard navigation, and ResizeObserver-driven overflow can't be asserted in vitest. Real interaction coverage must go to Playwright e2e, which is excluded from npm test and can't run under dispatch. For the breadcrumb task this forced splitting interaction logic (truncation tiers, overflow collapse, keyboard selection) into pure functions to get behavioral unit coverage, with live DOM behavior deferred to unverifiable e2e. A client-mount harness (e.g. @testing-library/svelte or vitest browser mode) would let interactive ACs be covered and verified in the gated suite.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: No CLI path to resolve a task's declared resource_refs to files in the worker worktree. The breadcrumb task listed handoff resources as ./resources/handoff/... but those live on the shadow branch under .kspec/plans/<plan-ulid>/resources/handoff/ and are absent from the worker worktree. 'kspec task resource list' is not a command, so I had to find / -name across the filesystem to locate the reference sources and screenshots. A 'kspec task resources <ref>' (or resolved absolute paths in 'kspec task get') would remove the filesystem hunt for dispatched workers.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Splitting an interactive component's decision logic into pure, dependency-free functions (computeTrail for truncation tiers + overflow, nextPopoverIndex for keyboard selection) made the spec's count/overflow/keyboard ACs behaviorally testable in vitest without a DOM, while the Svelte component stayed a thin renderer driving those functions from a ResizeObserver and event handlers. Worth replicating for future interactive web-ui components given the lack of a client-mount test harness.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: During review of @task-breadcrumb-component, the required gates (format, oxlint --quiet, focused oxlint, typecheck, npm test, kspec validate) were green, but the targeted Playwright build surfaced a new Svelte compiler accessibility warning in the touched component (a11y_no_noninteractive_element_interactions in BreadcrumbNav.svelte). This is narrower than the existing svelte-check baseline issue: Svelte build warnings from touched files can carry review-blocking accessibility signal yet are only visible if reviewers run a web-ui/build:e2e path. Consider a focused Svelte build-warning gate or review-gates guidance for touched .svelte files so introduced compiler/a11y warnings are not discovered opportunistically.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Parallel dispatch of tasks that each build into the SAME emerging subsystem produces duplicate implementations that the later-merging task must reconcile during its rebase — well beyond its own review-feedback scope. Concrete: @task-actor-normalization-upgrade (01KV4CDA) branched when @kynetic-ai/shared could not be value-imported from the installed CLI, so it shipped CLI-safe copies (src/parser/identity-config.ts, src/parser/actor-classifier.ts + a parity test). While it was in review cycles, sibling actor-identity tasks (task-review-author-resolution, task-actor-display-next-actor) landed on feat/ui-redesign a consolidated src/identity/ module (its own buildActorIdentityConfig) AND moved @kynetic-ai/shared into bundleDependencies, removing the value-import constraint. The fix-cycle rebase then hit not a textual clash but two competing buildActorIdentityConfig definitions + a now-redundant classifier copy; resolving it meant deleting this task's parallel files and rewiring onto the merged module — a large consolidation triggered by a small operator-map blocker fix. Nothing warned either task it was duplicating the other's infrastructure, and no dedup checkpoint exists. Distinct from @01KV67E0 (re-sync timing before resubmit) and the existing task-work rebase step (which worked — it surfaced the conflict). Consider: a lightweight "is another in-flight task touching these files/this subsystem?" signal at task start, or a reviewer prompt to flag overlapping emerging modules across sibling dispatch branches before they diverge. Verified safe to consolidate by the installed-package guard test (cli-serve "start daemon from npm-installed package with all deps available"), which empirically de-risks shared value-imports — a good existing safety net.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Review of @task-actor-normalization-upgrade found that schema-reflection inventory guards can miss persisted sidecar metadata fields that loaders strip before migration logic inspects records. Concrete case: split-task task.yaml history[].author is documented author identity data, but it is not part of TaskSchema/loadAllTasks output, so the actor-normalization inventory/test suite passed while existing history authors remained unnormalized. Future exhaustive-inventory work should include raw stored shapes/sidecars, not only loader-visible schemas.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer prompts can present a stale comparison base when dependency status is canonical-branch-head-changed: in @task-breadcrumb-component, the prompt base SHA (7752194) made the first diff include unrelated actor-resolution work, while the task branch had already incorporated current feat/ui-redesign (c803347) and the actual task delta was the focused breadcrumb diff. Reviewers can recover by manually comparing against the current target tip, but the prompt should surface a branch-coherent diff base or explicitly tell reviewers how to compute the current review delta.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: When a dispatch worker edits a package core skill source under templates/skills/ from inside its dispatch worktree (.kspec-worktrees/...), 'kspec skill render' / 'kspec skill verify' cannot regenerate that worktree's tracked .agents/skills/ and .factory/skills/ outputs: kspec resolves the project root upward to the main repo, so render reads the main shadow .kspec/skills/ source and writes to the main checkout, never the worktree. The worker must regenerate the worktree's tracked rendered supporting files manually (non-markdown files like scripts/*.sh are copied verbatim — confirmed byte-identical at HEAD), and 'kspec skill verify' drift it reports reflects the main project, not the worktree. A render mode or doc note for dispatch-worktree core-skill edits would remove this guesswork.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Fix-cycle resubmit requires an explicit `kspec task start` first. A `needs_work` task cannot be submitted directly — `kspec task submit` rejects with 'Cannot submit task with status: needs_work. Task must be in_progress.' The shared task-work fix-cycle steps end with step 7 'Re-submit — kspec task submit @ref' and never mention transitioning needs_work -> in_progress, so a worker (especially an automated dispatch worker) following the steps literally hits the error on every fix cycle and has to discover the `task start` step by trial. Consider adding an explicit `kspec task start @ref` step before the re-submit in the fix-cycle sequence of the shared task-work skill (project-neutral kspec mechanics).
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Testing shadow-committed sidecar stores: drive the store's programmatic write API against a real shadow project (kspec init --setup + initContext), then assert versioned persistence with 'git show kspec-meta:<relpath>' and supersession history with 'git log --oneline -- <relpath>'. This is deterministic (no fresh-checkout clone, no Date.now/random) and proves the commitIfShadow path. Established in tests/verification-record-store.test.ts for @ac-verification-record-store; directly reusable by the sibling store tasks @task-coverage-record-compatibility (unknown-field round-trip, format gating), @task-session-verification-evidence, and @task-freshness-resolution-read-path.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Sidecar storage write APIs need explicit key-validation regression coverage before path construction. In review @01KV6W47 for @task-ac-verification-record-store, the stamp payload was schema-validated but itemUlid/acId were not; a temp-project probe showed '../../modules/specs' escaped coverage/verifications and overwrote a spec module file. Future sidecar stores should validate filename/key inputs with the canonical schemas before computing paths, and tests should include malformed-key rejection with source files unchanged.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Spec-only detached reviews with an empty code diff still require the full npm test gate under current review guidance. In @01KV6TB34ES9WYJRADMS2NA8Q8, the code diff against feat/ui-redesign was empty and verification was spec/kspec-validation focused, but npm test still ran for 2681.7s. Consider a documented reviewer gate path or helper for no-code/spec-only reviews that preserves safety while avoiding unnecessary full-suite cost.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing reflection @01KV3WHP, which already tracks defining a metadata-only/no-code-diff review gate profile after a nearly identical full-suite cost.

observations.content: Resuming in-flight work: a prior attempt on this task left the schema, store implementation, and test imports uncommitted but well-structured. Reading the diff against origin showed the prior agent's plan, and the only gap was missing test coverage. Resuming in 1-2 commands (instead of starting from scratch) is a real win. Success pattern: agents that fail partway through should still commit their work-in-progress or at minimum leave the working tree in a resumable state — not just abort and lose context.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Format pass and lint pass are separate. After `npm run format` reports success, oxlint can still flag issues like prefer-template that oxfmt did not fix. Agents in this session repeatedly run format, see green, then hit oxlint warnings on the next step. Workaround: always run `npx oxlint <files>` after `npm run format` to catch the remainder. Consider a single tidy command or an oxfmt config that covers oxlint prefer-template, or a work-gates skill note that format != lint clean.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Resuming in-flight work: a prior attempt on this task left the schema, store implementation, and test imports uncommitted but well-structured. Reading the diff against origin showed the prior agent plan, and the only gap was missing test coverage. Resuming in 1-2 commands (instead of starting from scratch) is a real win. Success pattern: agents that fail partway through should still commit their work-in-progress or at minimum leave the working tree in a resumable state - not just abort and lose context.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: Detached review base-test comparison pattern: in manual_merge review snapshots, running focused base-branch tests from the assigned review workspace via npm --prefix against a clean existing integration-target checkout preserves the no-checkout rule while proving whether a failing gate is a task-branch regression.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Package-safety hazard via TRANSITIVE imports through sessions/store.ts: importing sessionExists (a 6-line existence probe) from src/sessions/store.js transitively pulls the agent-runtime/identity module graph (parser/session-branch, agent-runtime/session-event-fields → identity/actor-write → @kynetic-ai/shared) into the importer's module graph. The function name suggests an isolated cheap probe; the reality is it's part of a heavy module root. Verified in fix cycle on @task-session-verification-evidence: importing sessionExists into src/parser/verification-record-store.ts broke the installed-package daemon-start smoke test (tests/cli-serve.test.ts) because @kynetic-ai/shared is not bundled in the published dist/. Fix pattern: when a package-safe read path (verification records, coverage, anything reachable from the unbundled CLI) only needs an existence check, inline the probe (fs.access on the metadata path) rather than delegating to sessions/store.ts. Prior observations (@01KV4ZR6, @01KV5ESQ) cover the DIRECT value-import case; this is the transitive variant. Consider exporting a package-safe probe helper from a sessions/ submodule that has no agent-runtime/identity imports, or adding a lint rule that flags imports from sessions/store.js in package-safe paths.
observations.author: @claude

observations.content: For broad daemon route migrations, running a focused route-family suite across every affected handler before the full suite is an effective regression screen. In @task-shared-mutation-pipeline, the focused 268-test migrated-route run caught runtime-only stale-reference mistakes in review verdict/lifecycle payloads, allowing a quick fix before the 40-minute full npm test gate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session reflection after @task-shared-mutation-pipeline review: shared-service extraction tasks can pass unit ordering tests and happy-path route tests while individual routes still perform durable side effects before the extracted pipeline owns apply. Future extraction work should include route-level failure-injection tests that fail at commit/cache/write-through and assert no side effects escape outside the shared service sequence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For metadata-only relationship tasks, an atomic kspec batch of link create commands followed by bidirectional kspec link list checks and kspec refs gives strong review evidence without manual .kspec inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For command-path mutation work, adding the matching REST route to the command API test harness enabled direct event-equivalence assertions in one temp project: perform the same logical mutation through REST and /api/command, capture broadcasts, and compare topic/event/payload schema. This gave behavioral AC coverage for typed event parity without command-name mapping or source-scanning tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Direct taskBookkeeping injection seams made it straightforward to prove dispatch bookkeeping behavior without depending on kspec CLI subprocess capture; this pattern kept invocation outcome, logging, and broadcast assertions behavioral while moving mutations onto the pipeline.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Several dispatch/runtime tests asserted bookkeeping by inspecting kspec-capture-mock subprocess calls. When bookkeeping moved in-process, unrelated preflight, bootstrap, stall, and redaction tests needed migration, showing transport-coupled tests make internal mutation path changes more expensive than behavior-coupled tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session pattern: adding missing daemon entity events was straightforward when each mutator produced MutationEventDescriptor data through the existing mutation pipeline and tests exercised daemon command/API behavior. Future event-coverage work should reuse the collector plus behavioral subscribed-client tests instead of adding one-off broadcast plumbing.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reflection workflow guidance says `kspec workflow show` checks the current step, but the CLI requires a run ref when an active workflow exists; after `kspec workflow start @session-reflect-loop`, the usable command was `kspec workflow show @<run>`. Aligning guidance or CLI default behavior would reduce loop-mode friction.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing workflow CLI ergonomics tracking, including @01KGGPJ6 and observation @01KTWCCAS covering workflow show/next run-ref guidance mismatch.

observations.content: Automated reviewer review comments/checks defaulted to the configured project author when --author was omitted, so the review UI showed blocker/evidence threads authored by Jacob Chapel even though the verdict reviewer was codex. Review automation should consistently set reviewer identity on review check/comment writes or provide a reviewer-scoped default.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: Daemon command-route tests can drift when RouteEntityCache mocks expose ref-only task indexes instead of production-like TaskSummary records. The mismatch hid until a task transition command used listTasks() and failed on missing depends_on; shared helpers for production-shaped cache fixtures would reduce this class of false failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For broad entity-event coverage reviews, supplement AC-tagged tests with a small focused behavioral probe around recursive or cascade side effects. In review @01KVD1BM, a direct probe of nested spec-item deletion showed a descendant was removed without its own spec_item_changed removal event, catching an entity-refresh gap that the standard test suite missed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During mutation-event reviews, enumerate every writer/mutation interface for the affected entity rather than stopping at the command path covered by AC tests; this review found the missing task-created event on derive/inbox/plan/triage creation paths only after checking alternate task creation callers.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running completeness and alignment validation before submission caught a missing task spec_ref and then an overly broad spec link; using the validation warnings plus kspec search led to the correct in-progress test-determinism spec and AC annotation before review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For targeted WebSocket freshness work, pair exact query-key unit tests with a Playwright routeWebSocket E2E path that suppresses files:updates. That combination proves typed event consumption updates the open view without relying on file fallback, and catches both over-invalidation and fallback dependency before the full npm suite.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During long review gates, npm test can go quiet for extended periods while CLI-heavy Vitest workers are still active. Reviewers may need to inspect the process tree to distinguish progress from a hang. Consider adding low-frequency heartbeat/progress output to scripts/test.cjs or the custom progress reporter, ideally including active worker or child-command context when available.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For review-record schema/read-compatibility changes, pairing monolithic project.reviews.yaml fixtures with folder-backed reviews/<ulid>/review.yaml fixtures proves both supported storage readers preserve legacy anchors. This caught the need to seed the folder-backed index before overwriting the detail fixture and made the compatibility guarantee concrete.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The exhaustive actor-field inventory is an effective schema-evolution guard: adding plan revisions[].author immediately failed the actor-normalization completeness check until the new actor-bearing field was classified and covered by a migration fixture.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon route body schemas that use framework-level enum validation can preempt route-local accepted-value feedback. During @task-idea-thread-kind, POST /api/reviews/:id/comments initially rejected invalid kind before the handler could return the required 'blocker, question, nit, idea' guidance; accepting a string at the route schema boundary and validating with ReviewThreadKindSchema inside the handler preserved the user-facing feedback. Candidate follow-up: provide or document a daemon validation helper for enum fields that need custom accepted-value messages.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For upgrade-path data migrations that write revision or pointer metadata, a focused upgrade fixture should assert the recorded commit pointer by resolving it with git show <commit>:<entity-document-path>. In @task-plan-revision-backfill this proved @plan-revisions ac-backfill-revision-one directly: dry-run wrote nothing, upgrade created revision 1, and git show <shadow_commit>:plans/<plan-ulid>/plan.md returned the exact plan body after folder-storage migration. This pattern is reusable for future upgrade steps that must designate migrated content rather than merely store a non-empty commit hash.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Shadow-backed behavioral tests worked well for review/plan revision binding: creating real plan revisions and reading through kspec review get covered storage, subject pinning, and CLI output without source scanning or UI coupling.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Computed review detail fields require manual fan-out across CLI review get, daemon review detail, static export, shared API types, and static-mode adapters. A shared review detail projection/serializer would reduce drift risk for future computed fields.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-gates requires a review evidence log, but review records do not provide a first-class evidence-log or verdict-body field. Reviewers currently have to embed the log in a blocker thread, a check evidence string, or another workaround, which is especially awkward for clean approvals with no findings.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing @session-reflect success observation about batching review checks with the final verdict; resolved to avoid reflection noise.

observations.content: Batching review checks, findings, and verdict into one kspec batch kept the review record and task transition atomic during automated review. This avoided a partial review state while still preserving per-check evidence and an anchored blocker thread.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing @01KT264AKBE2RK73W5W9HYGABM success observation about batching review checks with the final verdict; resolved to avoid reflection noise.

observations.content: Review evidence logs need a first-class home in kspec review records. During task @01KVED78FQ4APC9E42P8EB23ZP, the required evidence log had to be embedded in a blocker thread body; clean approvals would need an even less natural workaround because verdicts do not carry review-body text.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During dispatch task submission, kspec task submit captured submission_linkage.upstream_ref as the branch's git upstream ('dev') even though the dispatch prompt and KSPEC_DISPATCH_MERGE_TARGET identified feat/ui-redesign as the manual_merge target. The worker had to inspect the JSON, dry-run a full submission_linkage patch, and repair the metadata after submit. Existing @portable-task-submission-linkage lets git upstream tracking take precedence, but dispatch/manual_merge review continuity needs the dispatch-provided merge target to win or be explicitly represented so reviewers do not merge to stale project defaults.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review recording pattern worked well: after completing gates and validating the finding, batching review check records, the anchored blocker, the evidence log, and the request_changes verdict into one kspec batch produced a coherent atomic review update and task transition.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored review findings that name the exact stale AC annotation and target behavioral replacement make fix cycles fast to verify: the worker can change one traceability point, rerun coverage validation, reply with the commit, and resolve the thread without rediscovering context.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Plan-text anchor work had backend schema, CLI, daemon, and behavioral coverage, but public shared/web API type parity was missed until review. Variant-extension tasks for discriminated unions need an explicit shared package and web helper contract check so accepted backend variants are representable by typed clients.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During a long full npm test run, checking the process tree with ps --forest distinguished active Vitest CLI subprocess work from a teardown hang after quiet output. This prevented premature failure classification while still keeping evidence for the existing full-suite hang investigation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review findings that include the exact schema boundary, repro payload shape, and mutation proof make fix cycles efficient: the test-result run store blocker mapped directly to a strict input-schema change plus a behavioral regression proving top-level native metadata is rejected before sidecar mutation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Automated detached reviews that must run the full npm test gate can spend most of the review wall time waiting for the aggregate suite even when focused tests and code review already found blockers; in review @01KVSD21, npm test passed but took 2854.8s before the request_changes verdict could be recorded with complete gate evidence.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For forward-compatible sidecar stores, keeping stored-record schemas tolerant while using separate strict submitted-input schemas gives a clean boundary: external producer/native fields are rejected before mutation, while supported-format on-disk unknown fields still round-trip. This pattern resolved the normalized test-result run store fix cycle without weakening forward compatibility.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC-driven neutral fixture tests exposed an accidental boundary leak in test-result ingestion: using metadata-only fixture projects made it obvious that AC mapping should build a spec-item-only ReferenceIndex instead of loading task storage through the full project index. Repeat this pattern for general-system sidecar code where project-specific state must not shape core behavior.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For prompt-suppression and auth-failure tests, a local child-process HTTP 401 challenge preserved real git fetch/push/ls-remote behavior while eliminating external GitHub/network timing from full npm test.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Focused changed-file lint can be hard to interpret when a touched large file already has pre-existing warnings; this session's npx oxlint run on src/cli/commands/task.ts reported 22 existing no-shadow warnings, so verifying no new warnings required manual comparison rather than a clear diff-aware gate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing the real dispatch call path in addition to the directly tested helper path caught a remaining plan_ref propagation gap: direct provisionDispatchWorkspace regressions passed, but DispatchEngine still omitted plan_ref when invoking provisioning for pending_review/needs_work entries.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Fix-cycle review feedback was highly actionable when it anchored the exact dropped plan_ref call site and required an engine-level regression, not only utility-level coverage. That combination made the worker fix narrow and verifiable: pass plan_ref through the production dispatch path and prove _spawnInvocation targets the plan branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During @task-test-result-ingestion-interface, the project test runner detected stale daemon build artifacts for a new daemon route and rebuilt automatically before the focused ingestion test. That prevented source/dist drift from producing misleading daemon API test results.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review records plus the detached-reviewer merge helper gave this dispatch review a clean auditable path: required gates and evidence were recorded on @01KVV688, approval closed the review, the helper merged the canonical task branch into feat/ui-redesign without target checkout in the detached snapshot, and task completion synced the linked spec to implemented.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Reviewer gate sequencing friction: starting a focused npm test while the full npm test suite is already running in the same worktree adds no parallelism because the project build/test lock serializes both runs. In this review, the focused producer-contract run waited behind the full suite for about 859s, then duplicated coverage already included in the full run. Existing tracking covers concurrent npm test races and the lock itself (for example observations found by searching 'test lock'), but reviewer guidance could avoid launching redundant focused tests until after the full suite result is known, or record the full-suite inclusion as focused evidence when applicable.
observations.author: codex

observations.content: During coverage evidence index work, the guarded npm test auto-build path reported only `npm run build failed: Command failed` when TypeScript compilation failed. I had to run `npm run build` separately to see the actual diagnostics. A test-runner failure summary that includes the captured build stderr would reduce this repeated debug step.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC-first behavioral tests with neutral project fixtures worked well for the coverage evidence index: they validated source labeling, latest-run selection, unmapped separation, and framework neutrality before daemon/API work existed, keeping the backend read-model task scoped and reviewable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
