observations.author: codex-reviewer
observations.resolution: Superseded by corrected observation; original was polluted by shell command substitution while creating the reflection note.

observations.content: Detached review snapshots can be missing workspace-local npm package links even when bootstrap state says ready. In this review, typecheck and npm test initially resolved @kynetic-ai/shared from the parent checkout and failed on stale shared exports; node scripts/bootstrap.cjs refused because KSPEC_SESSION_ID was set, and npm install in the assigned worktree created the correct local symlinks and cleared the gates without source changes. Dispatch workspace preparation should ensure workspace package links exist, or review guidance should name npm install as the sanctioned repair when bootstrap is blocked in dispatch mode.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: Review session @01KVX0RT: an isolated temp-repo behavioral probe quickly confirmed a freshness edge case that was not covered by the submitted tests. Pattern worth repeating: when a review suspicion depends on state/history interactions, write a small disposable probe against the public helper instead of relying only on static reasoning.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review gate triage was slowed by a pre-existing build/typecheck baseline: npm run typecheck and npm test failed before task tests because @kynetic-ai/shared no longer exports symbols imported by unchanged root modules. Follow-up task @01KVX11E tracks the baseline fix; until resolved, reviewers must classify these gates carefully to avoid misattributing unrelated failures to task branches.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For stale build-baseline bug tasks, rebasing first and rerunning the reported failing gates before editing prevented unnecessary code churn; the branch was already clean, so the task could be submitted with verification evidence instead of a no-op patch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review no-op path worked cleanly for an already-integrated task branch: the reviewer created a fresh review record, recorded required gate evidence, approved, ran the detached merge helper, received an explicit no-op result because canonical head already matched dev, and completed the task without manual branch checkout or merge commands.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Full npm test during automated review took 2727.8s in this session while another dispatch worktree also had a full Vitest run active. The gate eventually passed, but parallel full-suite review runs can consume most of an automated review session and make progress hard to distinguish from a hang without process inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Resolved as duplicate/covered by existing reflection and inbox coverage: @01KVE6XH and @01KVSE5H already track long/quiet automated review gates, and @01KV3WHP tracks the metadata/no-code-diff gate-profile improvement. This session confirmed the pattern but does not need a separate pending observation.

observations.content: Freshness/revision comparison tests can miss production bugs when temp fixtures use one git repository for both spec metadata and code history. Real kspec projects have separate revision domains: shadow metadata contains spec source, while test-run producer code revisions point at the project repository. Future freshness tests should model both domains when validating spec-text versus test-code freshness comparisons.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Anchored fix-cycle review threads with concrete evidence made the worker pass efficient: the blocker named the exact source lines, explained the shadow/project revision-domain mismatch, and cited producer stamp behavior, so the fix could stay narrowly scoped and be verified with one targeted regression before rerunning full gates.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached reviewer gate friction: a clean review still required a fresh full npm test run that took 2949.0s (2907 suites, 11044 passed, 3 skipped) before approval. Existing tracking covers test progress output and historical flakes, but not a reviewer-specific trust-preserving strategy for combining cached, focused, or sharded evidence with full-suite requirements in detached review snapshots.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For daemon data derived from files outside .kspec, the existing invalidation pipeline can stay cohesive by forwarding configured source watcher events with the project root as the watched root and teaching the entity cache to treat that boundary as source-only read-model invalidation. This avoided a parallel cache path while fixing coverage-state freshness for coverage.scan_paths changes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Required full npm test as a detached source-code review gate can dominate review turnaround: this review's full suite passed but took 3199.0s after the blocker was already found. Existing tracking covers metadata-only review profiles, but source-code reviews may also benefit from clearer policy/tooling for when focused failing evidence can short-circuit full-suite work, or from faster review-safe gate bundles that preserve rigor.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Fix-cycle review worked best when the reviewer read the prior closed review first, verified the worker's narrow fix, then deliberately broadened scrutiny to the full acceptance-criteria wording. That sequence caught the remaining runtime scan-path-change invalidation gap instead of approving a fix that only handled startup-configured source paths.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: During @task-coverage-state-events, explicit task wording for owned websocket trait ACs and non-applicable inherited lifecycle ACs kept implementation scoped to typed payloads/invalidation instead of reworking base websocket behavior; pairing that with centralized ws-invalidation made the UI refresh path small and behaviorally testable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For daemon event-after-cache tests, probe the same built module graph that the daemon route uses (for example dist/parser with dist/daemon routes) and assert the immediate re-fetch from inside the pubsub.broadcast interception. This catches stale cache or duplicate module-instance problems at the subscriber behavior boundary.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Daemon command completion can still execute post-mutation broadcast work inside an entity-cache async context. Freshness-sensitive emitters that invalidate and refetch read models need a first-class fresh-read boundary/helper so event-after-cache guarantees do not depend on each route remembering to bypass the inherited cache context manually.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Contract-layer coverage resolution work went smoothly when shared parser/schema behavior was tested with an injected production read-model loader: the tests proved alias resolution, freshness-enriched current-state validation, dry-run response shape, read-only refusal, and stale-fingerprint checks before CLI/daemon adapters existed, without source-scanning production files.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For ACs that assert production-boundary behavior, dependency-injection tests should be paired with a production-default-path test. In the coverage resolution fix cycle, an injected read-model loader test missed the boundary guarantee; dynamic-importing the resolver with read-model module exports mocked let the test call the default path and fail if raw/direct builders were used.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review-spawned follow-up tasks can reference tests or source that exist only on a sibling task branch. When the dispatched worker starts from the integration target, it must first rediscover the originating branch or commit before it can patch the intended behavior; task creation should carry that source branch/commit context explicitly.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During non-interactive review close-out, /kspec:reflect guidance can be ambiguous about whether to start @session-reflect or @session-reflect-loop. The skill says to start @session-reflect when present, while loop-mode guidance says to use @session-reflect-loop for autonomous runs; an agent can accidentally start both and leave a paused interactive run. Clarify the reflection skill/workflow guidance so autonomous or dispatch contexts choose the loop variant directly and avoid creating duplicate active workflow runs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review feedback that required a stale cached coverage value to refresh through the watcher path caught a real integration gap that callback-only watcher assertions missed. For daemon cache/watch changes, behavioral tests that warm real cache state and then trigger the watcher path are stronger evidence than asserting callback delivery alone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review setup, running kspec review add in parallel with kspec item get/review reads exposed a transient folder-backed review storage compatibility error: a review detail directory existed before the index entry was visible. Existing concurrency tracking covers lost task mutation updates, but not agent behavior around mixed kspec metadata writes and reads. Agents should treat kspec mutating commands as serialization boundaries and avoid parallel kspec reads during those writes.
observations.author: pr-reviewer
observations.resolution: Duplicate recurrence of @01KTYQ1RK: transient review lookup/storage compatibility failure immediately after folder-backed review creation. This session adds an agent-behavior note about avoiding parallel kspec reads during kspec metadata writes, but the underlying issue class is already tracked.

observations.content: For detached reviewer snapshots, the supported merge helper provided a clean completion path: after review approval and required gates passed, it merged the canonical task branch into the dispatch-provided target through the existing clean target checkout without manual checkout or merge commands in the detached snapshot.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: For parser-service mutations that have no CLI/daemon adapter yet, a temp YAML source file with realistic _path metadata plus a sidecar file and temporary git repo can behaviorally prove updateSpecItem, sibling preservation, sidecar non-mutation, and forward shadow commit semantics without source scanning or premature adapter work.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For concurrency-sensitive spec YAML mutations, compute the update from a current item snapshot while holding the file lock: re-read the raw item inside the mutation helper, validate the caller's expected fingerprint against that locked snapshot, then build and apply the patch. A regression that mutates the file after planning but before mutation proves the guard without source scanning.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In CLI-heavy behavioral tests, replacing multiple per-test mutating kspec subprocesses with one kspec batch setup can reduce full-suite process/shadow-mutation fan-out while preserving user-visible coverage and producing clearer setup diagnostics. The ac-delete-confirmation stabilization used this with the existing kspec() helper and kept the confirmation tests behavioral.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When review feedback includes a concrete reproduction at a public service boundary, add the regression at that same boundary before relying on lower-level helper coverage. In this fix cycle, testing applySpecTextRevert directly for dry-run/read-only behavior proved the reviewer-reproduced contract and prevented a narrower helper-only fix from missing action semantics.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of @task-coverage-spec-text-revert, the spec required comments to remain byte-equivalent but the available normal spec mutation helper rewrites YAML through plain-object serialization and drops comments. This forced an ad hoc executable repro outside existing tests. Future tasks that require byte-equivalent preservation should either use a comment-preserving mutation primitive or include commented YAML fixtures in behavioral tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Addressed by task @task-coverage-spec-text-revert commit 4031861112: added a lock-held YAML document-node mutation helper for targeted acceptance criterion text edits and a commented fixture regression that asserts byte-level preservation.

observations.content: When a task fix appears to need new helper-level coverage, search for existing helper tests before adding another file. In the shadow cleanup stabilization, tests/helpers-cli-cleanup.test.ts already proved cleanupTempDir retry and failure propagation, so the final diff stayed focused on replacing direct fs.rm calls in tests/shadow.test.ts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review of a one-file test cleanup still required a full npm test run that took 2562.0s before approval. Existing sharding and test-cache work partially address local test cost, but review-gate latency for narrow low-risk changes remains worth triage: future work could consider better cache evidence reuse, clearer shard sequencing, or explicit policy for when targeted plus cached full-suite evidence is sufficient without weakening required gates.
observations.author: codex-reviewer

observations.content: When a spec requires byte-equivalent preservation, test at the byte boundary: add a commented YAML fixture and assert the final file bytes differ only in the intended scalar values. This caught and proved the spec-text revert comment-preservation fix without relying on source scanning.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: CLI/daemon mutation parity tests need a shared semantic response-normalization helper for occurrence-specific values such as generated evidence IDs, timestamps, temp paths, and created task refs. This would let tests compare adapter behavior without ad hoc per-suite normalizers while keeping assertions behavioral.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When a review finding concerns metadata write durability, a real shadow-backed CLI regression is the right proof: it verifies stored:true effects, shadow branch advancement, and a clean shadow worktree together, while response-shape parity tests alone can miss uncommitted sidecar writes.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During coverage resolution event wiring, recording a private mutation-pipeline descriptor from the parser gave the daemon command route a stdout-independent typed handoff. That kept human-output CLI proxy calls behaviorally equivalent to REST while filtering the internal descriptor out of public websocket broadcasts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of event-driven UI data work, cross-checking the shared WebSocket event vocabulary/reservations against query invalidation mapping and tests exposed cache-coherence gaps that route-level tests alone missed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During spec workspace projection fix-cycle review, comparing lightweight summary counts against the detailed linked-work groups exposed a false-zero session count that route tests missed. Projection API tests should assert summary/detail consistency for derived counts whenever both surfaces are returned.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Using kspec batch to reply to and resolve all addressed review threads in one atomic operation produced a clean fix-cycle audit trail and avoided partial thread state while updating multiple review findings.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The daemon-context-manager coverage source watcher flake recurred after @task-stabilize-daemon-context-manager-coverage-watch-test was completed: this session's full npm test failed once at tests/daemon-context-manager.test.ts:329 with the same watcher event array assertion, while the focused rerun and a fresh full-suite rerun passed. Search found the prior completed stabilization task and no open reinvestigation item.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: AC-aligned route E2E tests were effective for the spec workspace shell: exercising stable URLs, reload/back behavior, and criterion pages against the running daemon exposed that the projection route was reading cached summary items instead of full item details. For projection-backed UI work, route E2E coverage should hit the real daemon projection rather than only component/source checks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Automated reviewer review-record writes can default to the configured human author for checks and comment threads unless every kspec review check/comment command explicitly passes --author. In review @01KW748D9P8E6T3KJXWDZ9432T, checks and threads appeared as Jacob Chapel while the verdict was pr-reviewer, making agent-authored evidence look human-authored. This is separate from historical actor normalization and suggests review-command defaults or reviewer workflow guidance should derive the active reviewer identity consistently.
observations.author: pr-reviewer

observations.content: Route/surface replacement reviews need an explicit neighboring-workflow regression pass. In review @01KW77F1, the changed /specs tests and required npm test gate were clean, but manually checking unchanged session-context E2E exposed that /items -> /specs replacement dropped the spec related-sessions section and /sessions?spec_ref navigation. Future route replacement reviews should search for old-surface E2E/spec workflows and run focused neighboring E2E when URLs redirect or old components are removed.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Review records that include the exact failing command, selector, expected behavior, and impact make fix cycles narrow and verifiable; in this session the blocker was reproduced with the listed E2E command, fixed in one route, and validated with focused plus full gates.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For spec workspace projection regressions, pairing live daemon projection tests, static snapshot projection tests, and one route-level E2E assertion made the fix easy to verify across all shipped read paths without relying on implementation inspection.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Spec workspace UI tasks moved cleanly when page implementation stayed projection-driven: the existing spec workspace projection plus E2E fixture data let root/node/criterion pages add linked work, evidence, and empty states without client-side scans or backend coupling.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For UI route reviews, combining projection/API contract review with a focused Playwright E2E spec after the repo-wide suite provided strong evidence: the code-level data contract, AC annotations, and browser behavior were all verified without relying on screenshots or worker claims alone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For UI route scoped-link blockers, fix and test both ends of the route contract: the source link should preserve scope params, and the destination route/API/query layer should consume those params. In @task-spec-workspace-coverage-presentation, pairing focused client/API tests with a route-level E2E that asserted visible scoped Validate results caught the real behavior better than checking the link href alone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Detached review prompt listed handoff resources as OK, but the referenced handoff/docs, handoff/shots, and handoff/reference-src paths were not available as files in the detached review snapshot. Reviewers had to fall back to task/spec text and committed tests instead of inspecting the stated resources. Search before capture: no matches for detached review handoff resources or missing handoff resources.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A duplicate open review record can remain when a reviewer creates a fresh review while an earlier cycle review record is still open. After approving and completing the task, review for-task still showed the stale open/pending review until it was manually annotated and closed as superseded. Search before capture: no matches for duplicate/superseded open review records.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Session reflection after @task-spec-workspace-resolution-panels: extracting a small pure spec-workspace coverage resolution panel model made action visibility, dry-run summaries, read-only behavior, stale conflict guidance, and dispatch-fix task refs easy to cover with behavioral AC tests while keeping the Svelte route focused on rendering and mutation orchestration.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reflection workflows can be duplicated accidentally: during this session both @session-reflect and @session-reflect-loop could be started, leaving two active runs and requiring manual discovery plus pausing of the redundant run. Consider a small workflow-start guard or clearer reflect guidance so agents choose exactly one reflection mode before starting.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For UI delivery-quality tasks, first map the delivery spec to existing behavioral coverage, then add one daemon-backed vertical browser workflow as proof. This closes AC coverage with low production-code risk and gives reviewers a clear screenshot-to-surface verification path.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During detached review full-suite verification, wait through long quiet npm test intervals when the runner process is still alive and prior output is green; checking the process tree before interrupting avoided a false teardown-hang classification and produced clean aggregate evidence (2926 suites passed, 11132 tests passed).
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For session event normalization changes, pairing focused accumulator tests with display parsing tests and reusing shared field extraction kept live and historical behavior aligned while preserving phased tool-call behavior.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Immediate CLI read-after-write consistency can fail after atomic metadata batches: a successful ten-command item AC batch committed all mutations, but the immediately following item get returned the pre-batch AC set; a retrying batch then detected the new AC ID and later reads showed the committed state. Exact metadata workflows need authoritative post-write reads or explicit cache synchronization so verification does not mistake stale cache data for a rolled-back batch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Immediately after a successful atomic kspec spec batch, `kspec item get` briefly returned the pre-commit cached spec while a subsequent mutation already saw the committed new AC ID. Read-after-write cache coherence should prevent contradictory CLI results or expose a committed-read option.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of earlier observation @01KXH54FK2HAA0V0QNR2GFA1CP, which already captures immediate stale CLI readback after successful atomic metadata batches and the need for authoritative post-write synchronization.

observations.content: For exact spec-only patch tasks, one atomic kspec batch followed by a programmatic comparison of every requested Given/When/Then payload and the complete AC ID sequence produced a drift-resistant reviewer handoff while proving unlisted compatibility ACs remained intact. The same pattern is evidenced across the dispatch engine, CLI, and daemon API patch tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch task quality gates are blocked by unrelated global reference ambiguities: @observations and @spec-plan-import resolve to duplicate items, so kspec validate --refs fails even when the task's own refs and alignment are valid. Validation needs either scoped baselining or prompt resolution of duplicate canonical slugs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Removed stale legacy skill @01KJ51SSZ2NVZGXE32NR5TWPS9 and stale superseded workflow @01KGPF7BP1KF0FAQAEFXNNTPTT. kspec validate --refs --warnings-ok now exits 0 with References: OK; remaining six deprecated-reference warnings are non-failing.

observations.content: Deterministic commit barriers combined with a real temporary Git shadow worktree make committed-publication races reproducible in behavioral tests: pausing at watcher-before-commit, abort, rollback, and lock-release boundaries verifies that consumers observe only durable committed objects and exposes ordering bugs that ordinary timing-based concurrency tests miss.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review of @task-dispatch-control-persistence, an isolated temporary-repository behavioral probe exercised the equal-revision/divergent-control-content boundary and reproduced stale-authority overwrite even though all 10,606 tests passed. Executable adversarial probes are an effective review technique for persistence and concurrency invariants that ordinary happy-path suites may miss.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KVX17N, which already records that isolated temp-repository behavioral probes expose state/history edge cases missed by submitted tests. Identified during post-capture verification of the reflection result.

observations.content: Centralizing fail-closed dispatch authority at the serialized scheduling boundary covers every queue-ingress path consistently, while separately serializing current-state reconstruction prevents stale or duplicate work during lifecycle transitions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The autonomous session-reflect-loop mandates unfiltered listings of all observations, inbox items, and tasks before evaluation. In a mature repository this produced over one million characters of output and was truncated, making the required duplicate-prevention baseline both expensive and incomplete. Prefer a bounded/count-first or targeted-query baseline that still searches every source without dumping every record.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Delayed or retried atomic review recording can duplicate the same check, blocker-thread, and verdict set within one review cycle. The duplicate records then require administrative replies and resolutions so workers can distinguish canonical findings from retry artifacts.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Concurrency fix-cycle coverage was strongest when a lightweight candidate-start recorder covered the lifecycle matrix while real invocation execution covered retry and post-invocation ingress. Deterministic holdIngress barriers at each async boundary made authority races reproducible without production test hooks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Pairing deterministic pre-create race barriers with the full scheduler-flow integration test exposed a hidden per-agent concurrency reservation regression when active publication moved to the final gate.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch tests mock runInvocation across many suites without a shared contract-preserving helper. Lifecycle hooks such as beforeCreate can be bypassed silently, producing false active-state assumptions and broad local mock repairs when the real boundary changes. Consider a test helper that invokes lifecycle hooks at the simulated artifact boundary.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Deterministic barriers placed inside the real common pre-artifact path made concurrency AC coverage sensitive to hook removal or relocation while proving both persisted session and adapter-process absence. Reuse this real-boundary barrier pattern for ordering races.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For safety-critical process recovery, inject a narrow runtime for process-identity reads, group enumeration/signalling, exit verification, and durable session closure, then drive it with immutable ownership fixtures. This makes refusal paths such as PID reuse, unreadable evidence, unproved or leaderless live groups, timeouts, closure failures, and phase-crash resumption behaviorally testable without signalling real processes, while keeping the production Linux /proc implementation behind the same contract.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Durable lifecycle fix cycles benefit from two complementary verification layers: fault-injection tests at each persistence/publication/cleanup boundary prove local recovery invariants, while a fresh full-suite run catches cross-suite fixture activation leaks that focused tests cannot see. In @task-engine-stop-recovery, focused stop-recovery tests passed, but the full suite exposed parser-only fake-worktree fixtures accidentally activating the durable dispatch store; requiring authentic linked-worktree evidence fixed the regression.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Production child-process termination semantics are duplicated and can drift from the verified cleanup contract. In @task-engine-stop-recovery, agent invocation cleanup used synchronous best-effort SIGTERM and released ownership without observing exit, while bounded SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL observed-exit primitives existed only in test-side daemon helpers from @task-implement-bounded-process-stop-primitives. A shared production-owned termination primitive (including process-group signalling, signalCode exit detection, bounded escalation, and verified exit before success) should be evaluated for agent spawner/invocation and other production child owners so safety does not depend on each call site reimplementing the contract.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For process-ownership and termination changes, adversarial executable probes against real child-process behavior are an effective review gate beyond the test suite. In review cycle 4 of @01KXH2PRCMKX5GBDNJ60PPBCHS, targeted probes demonstrated a live process after durable exited_at and a stop path that emitted no signal even though the fresh full suite passed 10,694 tests; the probes directly exposed correctness gaps in lifecycle synchronization.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The autonomous session-reflect-loop mandates unfiltered kspec meta observations list, kspec inbox list, and kspec tasks list as its duplicate baseline. In a mature project these produced hundreds of thousands of tokens and truncated output, so the baseline cannot be inspected reliably; the workflow needed additional targeted kspec search queries. The reflection baseline should use a bounded or indexed summary, or a search-oriented duplicate check that remains complete at project scale.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing friction observation @01KXJ4K3, which already tracks unfiltered session-reflect-loop inventory truncation and recommends a bounded or targeted baseline.

observations.content: The autonomous session-reflect-loop mandatory baseline lists every observation, inbox item, and task before candidate keywords exist. In a mature repository this produced roughly 265k tokens of observation output plus 427 inbox and 1,705 task rows, which was truncated and therefore weakened the duplicate-detection guarantee. Identify high-confidence candidates first and run targeted kspec search queries, or provide a bounded machine-readable index for the baseline.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For process-ownership and recovery changes, behavioral tests with real OS process trees caught correctness gaps that injected runtimes missed: leader exit did not prove group exit, resistant descendants required SIGKILL escalation, and rejected or hanging initialization had to retain the spawned handle. Encoding those exact process-tree cases first produced direct evidence that exited_at is published only after full group extinction.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Schema-backed in-memory test stores can admit impossible snapshots when their commit helpers bypass the production Zod schema. In dispatch lifecycle tests, cleanup entries without targets caused startup recovery to throw while start swallowed the error, leaving annotated tests falsely green. Test doubles for schema-backed persistence should validate every committed snapshot through the production schema.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A pure canonical-identity protection classifier paired with a protected-state × destructive-surface behavioral matrix made cleanup policy consistent across task, registry, branch, worktree, reviewer snapshot, and root-pruning paths; adding physical session and registry assertions then verified the matrix represented preserved evidence rather than only classifier internals.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch supplied an unavailable reviewer workflow entrypoint. The dispatched role prompt required pr-review, but the rendered skill set exposed kspec-review instead, so the reviewer had to infer a fallback. This is repeatable for similarly configured review invocations and contradicts @dispatch-role-workflow-entry-contract ac-4, which requires missing or invalid entrypoints to fail fast with actionable guidance. The dispatcher should validate that the adapter-facing entrypoint resolves to an available workflow or skill before dispatch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For safety-critical cleanup, pair a physical destructive-surface regression test with a separate production-wiring test: the first proves protected evidence survives real filesystem and registry cleanup, while the second proves the engine supplies globally controlled identities instead of relying on manually injected classifier state.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For exactly-once lifecycle event reviews, fault-inject the event-publication or observer callback so it throws after the durable state mutation. This behavioral probe exposed that a successfully applied dispatch pause could reject and emit both an applied and failed event when publication failed, a defect not exercised by happy-path tests.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Concurrent full npm test runs across dispatch worktrees inflated one run to 48 minutes and exposed a transient resistant-descendant /proc lstat ENOENT; the unchanged file passed immediately in isolation and the fresh full suite passed once contention cleared. Full-suite scheduling or this /proc assertion needs stronger cross-worktree isolation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Concurrent fresh full-suite npm test runs in separate dispatch worktrees bypass the per-worktree build/test lock and can heavily contend for host resources. During review of @task-verify-engine-restart-races, process inspection confirmed another worktree running its own full Vitest tree while this required gate stretched to roughly fourteen minutes despite all tests passing. Existing fixes cover same-worktree serialization, not cross-worktree dispatch-wide concurrency; triage should consider host-level test admission or reviewer scheduling guidance.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For verification-only concurrency work, an exact task handoff naming test-only helpers and spelling each scenario as trigger → barrier → mutation → observation → outcome made the review independently falsifiable without moving production ownership. In @task-verify-engine-restart-races, this structure enabled direct checks of all three recovery phases, task-scope isolation, conditional cleanup errors, and evidence preservation while keeping the diff test-only.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A defect task created from review of an unmerged plan branch was dispatched against dev with plan_ref=null, leaving the affected code absent from the task workspace. Defect follow-ups need to inherit the reviewed task's plan branch or depend on its integration before becoming automation-eligible.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Real committed shadow-state fixtures paired with exact wire-response assertions exposed lifecycle store classification and preflight defects end to end that mocked or structural tests would miss; reuse this pattern for daemon APIs backed by committed authority.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A real-shadow route fixture with an actual failing Git pre-commit hook exposed a runtime/durable-state divergence that mocked lifecycle failures missed, then provided end-to-end proof that canonical and compatibility routes remove cold engines after commit failure. Reuse real persistence-boundary failure injection for APIs that coordinate durable shadow mutations with in-memory runtime state.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Layered verification proved valuable for CLI package boundaries: focused lifecycle tests validated behavior quickly, while the full installed-package regression suite caught a workspace-package runtime import that would have broken the shipped CLI. Keeping the full suite as a release gate led to a package-safe CLI-local Zod schema before submission.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: During review evidence recording, an atomic kspec batch finished successfully, but the immediate kspec review get returned zero checks and threads; rerunning the writes later revealed both copies. This delayed read-after-write visibility can make autonomous reviewers create duplicate checks and comments, then manually resolve duplicate threads. Review mutations need a reliable commit receipt plus an immediately coherent read path or idempotency keys.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For safety-critical CLI reviews, trace failure handling across local setup helpers, command-action catches, generic output formatters, and daemon response schemas rather than checking only HTTP parse paths. This session found initContext outside the closed lifecycle mapping; strict daemon-response tests could not catch it. Pair local-exception injection with exact human and JSON no-secret assertions.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The autonomous session-reflect-loop mandates unfiltered 'kspec meta observations list', 'kspec inbox list', and 'kspec tasks list' commands before identifying candidates. As project history grows, that baseline becomes unusable: this run returned about 60,000 tokens and the observations listing alone reported roughly 267,000 tokens before truncation, so the required evidence cannot actually be inspected. The workflow should use counts plus candidate-driven targeted searches (or bounded/paginated listings) while preserving search-before-capture semantics.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dispatch dependency preflight reported satisfied for a stabilization task whose affected test and supporting implementation existed only on an unmerged plan branch, while the task had plan_ref=null and targeted dev. Branch ancestry or plan linkage should be validated before declaring such follow-up tasks dispatch-ready.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KXMJKDSW3F670TPX4JBE0JTP, which already tracks defect follow-ups losing unmerged plan-branch linkage. This session provides a second confirming occurrence on @01KXNJTVMJHY7FWVZ3SFVDGACM.

observations.content: For acceptance criteria tied to rendered UI behavior, place the AC annotation on a browser test that renders the real view and asserts the visible evidence; keep parser/conversion tests annotated only for wire-boundary behavior. In the dispatch lifecycle fix cycle, exact deep conversion stayed green while active, queued, held, degraded, and blocked evidence could have disappeared from the agents view, whereas focused Playwright coverage made those ACs independently falsifiable.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Verification tasks can be dispatched as dependency-satisfied while a surface they explicitly require is owned by an unfinished task that is not in depends_on or the integration target. In @task-verify-api-cli-projection, required UI conversion verification was unavailable because @task-ui-dispatch-lifecycle-controls was needs_work and undeclared as a dependency. This forces workers to choose between duplicating unreviewed owner work and submitting incomplete surface coverage; plan derivation or readiness checks should detect required-but-unavailable owner tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Task-local cross-spec AC ownership is recorded only in prose '### Covers' sections, so automated completeness validation cannot require the corresponding exact test annotation. A task can pass refs/alignment/completeness while an explicitly assigned criterion remains unlinked, deferring detection to manual review and causing avoidable fix cycles.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Cross-surface verification was dispatched before every behavior-owner task was merged: @task-verify-api-cli-projection required the UI wire-to-camel converter but did not depend on @task-ui-dispatch-lifecycle-controls, forcing a review cycle and later block. Plan derivation or automation readiness should verify that each named surface owner is an explicit dependency of end-to-end verification tasks.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KXNQQY, which already tracks missing behavior-owner dependencies for cross-surface verification.

observations.content: Endpoint-specific strict response parsing can bypass cross-cutting invalid-project recovery when it consumes non-2xx bodies before the shared error path. In the lifecycle UI, both status and control helpers rejected the middleware string-error body as a malformed canonical envelope without clearing the stale project selection. Run invalid-project detection and selection recovery before specialized envelope validation, and cover each custom parser behaviorally.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For asynchronous controls that can remove their own keyed row, keep status announcements in a persistent parent polite/atomic live region. A browser test should perform the row-removing action, assert the child disappears, and then assert the surviving live region announces the outcome; this directly catches announcements lost during component unmount.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Pure UI wire-conversion logic is coupled to the broad SvelteKit API module. Both the UI lifecycle owner suite and the real-daemon lifecycle surface suite must mock mode, project, static-API, and constants modules just to import and exercise parseAgentDispatchStatusWire, making non-Svelte boundary verification noisier and more fragile than the parser behavior itself.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Browser route fixtures at the exact public wire boundary provide high-value cross-layer verification: returning complete snake_case responses through Playwright exercised schema validation, recursive camelCase conversion, lifecycle action derivation, accessibility state, and rendered DOM behavior together without mocking product helpers.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Playwright records intentional HTTP 4xx/503 route-fixture responses as console resource errors. Browser regressions that exercise mapped failures or static fallback must classify and assert those expected transport logs separately from unexpected console/page errors; an unconditional empty-error assertion produces false failures.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: State-machine UI regression matrices are strongest when every scenario asserts the exact scoped control set and related counts, not only that allowed controls are visible. Exact-set assertions made extra prohibited actions fail and exposed incomplete lifecycle coverage during review.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Dimension-specific Playwright coverage should set the viewport explicitly and assert page.viewportSize() at runtime. Relying on a named desktop device silently ran the lifecycle desktop matrix at 1280x720 instead of the required 1440x900.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Exact fixture drift gates are strongest when the expected fixture is compared against an independently derived complete observed universe, every fact group is bound to exported or black-box production behavior, and negative mutations prove both omission and stale-extra rejection. In @01KXPPE2FA72S6HPFV9V95488F this pattern converted partial subset checks into bidirectional contracts and exposed a genuinely stale stopped-with-cleanup lifecycle action before resubmission.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewing an incremental gate against explicitly planned future states is a high-value complement to current-state tests. In @task-freeze-doc-facts-and-inventory, mutating the inventory fixture to add one of the six construction-allowed future pages exposed that ordered landing-page equality rejected the permitted transition even though the focused and full suites were green. Pattern: when a task promises compatibility with a named follow-on state, reproduce that transition during review rather than testing only the submitted snapshot.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Reviewer reproduction of the release workflow's actual repository topology caught a publication-only regression: the normal full-clone gates passed, but rerunning the changed Git-history tests in a depth-1 clone matching the release checkout exposed unconditional historical merge-base assertions that fail before npm test can publish. When behavior depends on Git ancestry, matching CI checkout depth is a high-value review gate beyond rerunning the same command in a full developer clone.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Autonomous session reflection baseline does not scale: session-reflect-loop mandates unfiltered observation, inbox, and task lists before candidate identification. In this session observations alone returned 2,113 entries and roughly 267k tokens, truncating the combined output and preventing reliable inspection. The workflow needs a bounded summary, pagination, or candidate-first search strategy that still proves all three stores were checked.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Public fact-freeze gates are reliable when each fixture claim is bound to an independently executed or schema-derived authority and paired with a negative mutation. A real depth-1 clone test additionally exposed and then verified the correct handling of unavailable historical commit objects while preserving exact immutable OIDs. This pattern prevents fixtures and documentation inventories from self-validating.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Structured documentation fact gates are reliable when every frozen value is verified through public behavior with exact field-level assertions and paired with a stale-data mutation proving the gate fails; this prevented presence-only and self-referential fixture checks from masking mapping drift.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: For one-to-one wire-to-UI mapping contracts, use one semantically valid input where each competing field has a distinct value, then retain stale mutations that swap both mapping directions. This made a previously colliding projection/global-authority probe reject false mappings deterministically.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: In a prepared dispatch worker worktree without a local .kspec directory, foreground kspec task-state and some validation commands were interrupted before returning even when KSPEC_SPEC_DIR and the active session/invocation identity were supplied; detached daemon requests or isolated retries were required to transition and validate the assigned task.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Hierarchical generated-help requests such as kspec help agent dispatch, kspec help agent dispatch task, and kspec help agent status return only the top-level agent help instead of the deepest requested command, so operator guides that correctly delegate full flags to generated help do not land readers on the promised lifecycle options.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Documentation command references were hardened effectively by executing every exact --help path and asserting the expected Usage prefix and Options section; this catches silent ancestor-topic resolution that exit-code and nonempty-output checks miss.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Configured dispatch reviewer prompts name the pr-review role entrypoint even when that skill is not rendered or available in the Codex snapshot. Reviewers must reconstruct the flow from kspec-review and review-gates. Validate each configured role entrypoint against adapter-visible skills before prompt delivery, or align the project override with the installed core review entrypoint.
observations.author: pr-reviewer
observations.resolution: Duplicate of existing reflection inbox item @01KXQNZ5, discovered during the mandatory full reflection baseline. No separate observation is needed.

observations.content: The test runner cache can reuse a pass across an untracked-to-tracked file transition even when tests derive their input with git ls-files. In the dispatch-workspace documentation task, a pre-commit inventory test cached 142 tracked Markdown files; after committing the new document, ordinary npm test reused that result even though the tracked universe was 143, while npm test -- --fresh exposed the stale fixture. Cache invalidation should incorporate Git index/tracked-set state for tests whose behavior depends on it.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: When the monolithic full npm test run repeatedly hit the known contention-sensitive resistant-process /proc race, running the project's three supported test shards sequentially preserved complete suite coverage (10,974 passed, 3 skipped) and produced deterministic green evidence without changing unrelated code.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: The test runner reused a cached failure after new documentation files were created as untracked files, reporting repository state unchanged until --fresh was used, despite project guidance stating untracked files participate in the cache key. This can hide implementation progress whenever a test depends on newly created untracked inputs.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Behavioral documentation validation through the real docs plugin plus an executed runtime failure fixture caught and corrected a false bootstrap-output redaction claim before submission. Pairing rendered-page assertions with observable source-authority fixtures is effective for source-bound operator documentation.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: A stale-read retry while recording one review produced duplicate blocker threads and duplicate evidence-log threads in the same review. Fix-cycle workers then had to distinguish canonical findings from retry duplicates and resolve 13 threads for 5 issues; review comment creation should be idempotent or deduplicate retries.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Binding operator documentation to a real DispatchEngine failure plus public task CLI recovery exposed incorrect claims about invocation output, blocked task state, and unblock restoration that direct helper assertions missed. Behavior-backed documentation tests at the dispatcher and public-command boundary are a repeatable drift-prevention pattern.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: Running kspec skill render with an already-drifted core skill skipped the Codex render but rewrote the Factory copy from the older source, producing asymmetric runtime behavior; it also emitted untracked project-local skill copies during a package-guidance regeneration task. Render should treat drift consistently across platforms and avoid unrelated untracked outputs or provide a scoped package-core regeneration mode.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

observations.content: skill status reports core-skill supporting docs as drifted when portable references such as {skill:help} are correctly transformed to platform syntax; skill verify passes after a source-backed render, so status and verify disagree on generated/source pairing
observations.author: Jacob Chapel
observations.resolution: Duplicate of @01KT5EJA, which already captures platform-aware generated-skill comparison and portable-reference rewrite false positives.

observations.content: Dispatch documentation gates name 'kspec agents generate', but a worktree with newer generator behavior can receive stale lifecycle guidance and unrelated skill outputs from the installed CLI. Fix-cycle verification had to switch to the snapshot-local 'npm run dev -- agents generate' path; dispatch/bootstrap guidance should make generator provenance explicit or ensure the installed CLI matches the canonical branch.
observations.author: Jacob Chapel

agents.prompt_template:
Work on task {{task_ref}} — "{{task_title}}"

LOCAL WORKFLOW (no GitHub PRs):
- You are working in an isolated clone on the feat/ui-revamp branch.
- Before starting work, create a sub-branch: git checkout -b feat/ui-revamp/{{task_ref}} feat/ui-revamp
- Make all commits on the sub-branch with conventional commit format + Task: {{task_ref}} trailer.
- When work is complete, do NOT create a GitHub PR. Instead:
  1. Ensure all tests pass (npm test in project root, and npm run test in packages/web-ui if UI tests exist)
  2. Run kspec task submit {{task_ref}} (transitions to pending_review)
  3. Stop responding — the ux-reviewer agent will handle review.
- After review approval, the reviewer will merge locally into feat/ui-revamp.

UI-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:
- Use Svelte 5 runes ($state, $derived, $effect) exclusively. Never use Svelte 4 stores or $: reactive declarations.
- Reference the imgen design system at ../imgen/packages/design-system/src/ for token values and patterns.
- Use oklch() color space for all color tokens. Map tokens as Tailwind theme extensions.
- All animations MUST be gated behind @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
- Status colors: pending=amber, in_progress=orange, pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow,
  completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray. Every status must be visually distinct and
  not rely on color alone (include text labels).
- Use bits-ui primitives for dialog/sheet/accordion — do NOT recreate these.
- Every view must have empty state, loading skeleton, and error boundary.
- Follow component structure: lib/ds/ for design system CSS/tokens, lib/components/<feature>/ for feature components.
- Read .kspec/artifacts/ui-revamp-plan.md for full architectural context and wireframes.
- Reference ../kynetic-internal/packages/hub-ui/ for patterns: ActiveFleetRow, MiniTerminal,
  ChatPanel, ToolCallView, ThinkingBlock, StreamingMarkdown.

agents.name: UX Reviewer Agent
agents.description: Autonomous UX review agent. Reviews UI implementation for design quality, accessibility, spec AC coverage, and visual consistency with imgen design system tokens.
agents.prompt_template:
Review task {{task_ref}} — "{{task_title}}"

LOCAL REVIEW WORKFLOW (no GitHub PRs):
- You are reviewing work in an isolated clone. The worker committed to a sub-branch
  (feat/ui-revamp/{{task_ref}} or similar) off feat/ui-revamp.
- Find the sub-branch: git branch --list 'feat/ui-revamp/*' | grep -i "$(echo {{task_ref}} | sed 's/@//')"
- Review the diff against feat/ui-revamp: git diff feat/ui-revamp...HEAD
- Run all tests: npm test && cd packages/web-ui && npm test 2>/dev/null; cd ../..
- If issues found:
  1. Add a task note with specific findings: kspec task note {{task_ref}} "Review findings: ..."
  2. Transition: kspec task needs-work {{task_ref}} --reason "Review issues: ..."
  3. Stop responding — the worker will fix.
- If review passes:
  1. Merge into feat/ui-revamp: git checkout feat/ui-revamp && git merge --no-ff feat/ui-revamp/{{task_ref}} -m "feat(web-ui): merge {{task_ref}}"
  2. Delete the sub-branch: git branch -d feat/ui-revamp/{{task_ref}}
  3. Complete the task: kspec task complete {{task_ref}} --reason "Review passed. Merged to feat/ui-revamp."
  4. Stop responding.

UX REVIEW CHECKLIST:
- Spec AC coverage: every AC in the spec has a test with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N annotation.
- Trait AC coverage: check inherited trait ACs via kspec item get @spec-ref.
- Run kspec validate — any warnings for this spec are MUST-FIX.
- Design token usage: components use design tokens (bg-design-surface, text-design-accent, etc.),
  not hardcoded colors or raw Tailwind color classes (bg-gray-500, text-blue-400).
- Svelte 5 patterns: $state/$derived/$effect only, no legacy $: or svelte/store imports.
- Empty states: every list/collection view has an empty state with actionable guidance.
- Loading states: every async view has skeleton loading (shimmer animation).
- Error boundaries: views handle API failures gracefully.
- Accessibility: focus management in modals, aria-live for streaming, color-independent status indicators,
  prefers-reduced-motion gated animations.
- Visual consistency: compare with wireframes in .kspec/artifacts/ui-revamp-plan.md.
- Information density: cards/views are scannable, not cluttered.
- Reference ../imgen/packages/design-system/src/token-contract.css for expected token usage.
