workflows.description:
Check spec coverage before implementing changes.
Core principle: If changing behavior and spec doesn't cover it,
update the spec first.

steps.content: Does the spec cover this change?
steps.on_fail: Update or create spec before proceeding

steps.content: What is the spec status?
options: Spec exists and matches -> Derive task, proceed
Spec exists but outdated -> Update spec first
No spec exists -> Create spec first (behavior) or task directly (infra)

steps.content: Update or create spec item if needed
Derive task from spec via kspec derive @spec-item
Implement the change

workflows.description: Get context at the beginning of a work session.

steps.content: Run kspec session start to get context
Are there active (in_progress) tasks?
steps.on_fail: Pick from ready tasks or triage inbox

steps.content: Review ready tasks and inbox items
Start work on chosen task via kspec task start

workflows.description: Complete a task properly with notes and cleanup.

steps.content: Add completion note describing what was done
Run kspec task complete @task --reason "summary"
Are there uncommitted changes?
steps.on_fail: Commit changes with descriptive message

steps.content: Review if task unblocked other work

workflows.description: Triage inbox items during session context review.

steps.content: Review oldest inbox items first
For each item, ask these questions
options: Still relevant? No -> delete
Scope clear? Yes -> promote to task
Needs spec work? -> Create/update spec first
Still unclear? -> Leave, add tag, revisit later

steps.content: Has item survived 3+ triage sessions?
steps.on_fail: Either promote with clear scope or delete

workflows.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Five-phase workflow: parallel exploration (docs, code, config, tests, specs), compilation by severity, interactive triage, execution, and summary.
Structured reflection after work sessions. Surfaces learnings, identifies friction, and captures improvements for system evolution.

steps.content:
Identify what worked well this session.
Be specific: "categorizing items first" not "good planning".
Consider: workflows, tools/commands, communication, decisions.

Identify friction points - where things were harder than needed.
Focus on systemic issues, not one-off mistakes.
Consider: repetitive steps, missing commands, context loss, workarounds.

Check if friction points are already tracked.
Search specs, tasks, AND inbox before proposing new improvements.
For each: note if already tracked, partially covered, or untracked.

For untracked friction, propose concrete improvements.
Include: what it would do, how it helps, rough scope (small/medium/large).
Present findings to user - ask about each improvement one at a time
options: Worth capturing -> proceed to capture
Needs refinement -> discuss and refine
Not worth it -> skip and continue
Done with reflection -> complete workflow

steps.content:
Capture approved items using appropriate destination:
- Actionable improvements: kspec inbox add "..." --tag reflection
- Friction patterns: kspec meta observe friction "..."
- Success patterns: kspec meta observe success "..."
- Open questions: kspec meta question add "..."

workflows.description: Meta-workflow for creating new workflows. Ensures consistent structure and matching skill integration.

steps.content:
Identify the pattern to formalize.
What process/checklist are you capturing? Where is it documented?
Look for: step-by-step instructions, checklists, repeated sequences.

inputs.name: pattern_source
inputs.description: Where the pattern comes from (file:line, skill name, or description)

steps.content:
Define the trigger - when does this workflow start?
Common triggers: manual, session-start, session-end, task-complete,
behavior-change, pre-release, pr-merge

Design the steps. For each step decide:
- Type: action (do something), check (verify condition), decision (choose path)
- Content: clear instruction, can be multiline
- For checks: on_fail message
- For decisions: options list
- Entry/exit criteria if step needs verification
- Inputs if step captures structured data
See: [Step Design Guide](docs/step-design.md)

Create the workflow:
kspec meta add workflow --id <id> --trigger <trigger> --description "..."
Then edit .kspec/kynetic.meta.yaml to add the steps (until --steps flag exists).
Does this workflow need a matching skill for additional context?
options: Yes - create/update skill in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
No - workflow is self-contained or context exists elsewhere

steps.content:
Test the workflow:
kspec workflow start @workflow-id
Run through each step with workflow next
Verify inputs/notes are captured correctly
Commit changes to both main (skill) and shadow (workflow) branches

workflows.description: Autonomous reflection for loop mode. High-confidence captures only. MUST search existing before capturing. No user interaction.

steps.content:
MANDATORY FIRST STEP: Search existing state before identifying anything.
Run these searches in parallel:
- kspec meta observations list
- kspec inbox list
- kspec tasks list

This establishes baseline to prevent duplicates (ac-1, ac-3).

Identify high-confidence friction points and successes.

HIGH CONFIDENCE criteria (ac-2, ac-4):
- Concrete and specific (not vague)
- Systemic/repeatable (not one-off)
- Clear cause and effect
- Agent has certainty about the pattern

LOW CONFIDENCE (DO NOT capture):
- Vague observations
- Uncertain patterns
- One-off issues
- Hypothetical problems

For each item identified, check against search results from step 1.

For each potential item, evaluate against existing state:

AC-3: If matches existing observation/inbox/task -> SKIP IT, note existing ref
AC-4: If unique AND high-confidence -> CAPTURE IT
AC-2: If vague/uncertain -> SKIP IT

Decision matrix:
- Duplicate of existing item -> skip, note reference
- Unique + high confidence -> capture
- Vague/uncertain -> skip silently

Capture approved items automatically (no user prompt - ac-5, ac-6):

- Systemic friction: kspec meta observe friction "..."
- Successful patterns: kspec meta observe success "..."
- Open questions: kspec meta question add "..."
- Actionable improvements with scope: kspec inbox add "..." --tag reflection

Only capture items that passed the evaluation in step 3.
Be selective - lower volume, higher quality.

workflows.description: Research and design phase for plan-to-spec translation. Explore codebase, clarify requirements, design approach, review for completeness and spec gaps. Concludes with choosing import or manual execution path.

steps.content:
Explore and research the codebase.
Understand: existing specs/items in the domain, related patterns, current code structure, traits that may apply.
Use /spec skill knowledge for spec types, AC format, and trait reference.
Focus on what already exists to avoid duplication. Use parallel searches for efficiency.

Clarify requirements with the user.
Present structured questions with clear options. One question at a time - do not batch multiple questions.
Each question should resolve a specific design choice or scope decision.
Continue until no open questions remain. Capture answers as they inform the design.

Design the approach.
Synthesize exploration findings, user answers, and requirements into a concrete design.
Propose: spec items needed, AC for each, applicable traits, parent placement, and task structure.
Write the design to a durable artifact (plan file or document) so it survives session boundaries.
Design passes holistic review
steps.on_fail:
Address review feedback - fix gaps, refine AC, add missing traits. Iterate until review passes.
Review for: (1) completeness - gaps or missing scenarios, (2) consistency - specs align with existing patterns,
(3) spec coverage - proper types, AC quality, trait applicability per /spec skill, (4) edge cases.
Exit criteria: design written to file, all review issues addressed.

steps.content: Choose execution path based on the reviewed plan
options: Import path - write structured plan document and auto-generate (3+ specs, batch creation)
Manual path - create specs incrementally with kspec commands (1-2 specs, quick additions)

workflows.description: Execute plan via structured document import - write document, preview import, import as a durable plan record, iterate with --into, approve, derive, validate, and start work. Follows @spec-plan-design.

steps.content:
Write or finalize plan document.
Format: # Title, ## Specs with YAML code block (title required, optional: slug, type, parent, AC, traits),
## Tasks with derive_from_specs flag, ## Implementation Notes (plain text).

inputs.name: plan_file_path
inputs.description: Path to the markdown plan file

steps.content:
Choose whether to store a target module on the plan now or defer it until derive.
Use: kspec item list --type module
If you already know the destination module, capture its ref for import or derive. If not, you can import first and pass --module later to kspec plan derive.

inputs.name: module_ref
inputs.description: Optional module reference to store on the plan for later derive

steps.content:
Preview import with dry-run.
Use: kspec plan import <path> [--module @module] --dry-run
Review: plan title, status, stored module_ref, and that import is content-only storage.
Dry-run output acceptable - plan record preview looks correct and the document is ready to store
steps.on_fail:
Fix the plan file, title, or module choice, then re-run dry-run.
Note: import dry-run previews the stored plan record; spec/task validation happens during derive.

steps.content:
Run actual import.
Use: kspec plan import <path> [--module @module] [--status approved]
Verify: kspec plan get @plan-slug
Import stores the full document on the plan record; it does not create specs or tasks.
For revised drafts, re-import with: kspec plan import <path> --into @plan-ref

Iterate and approve.
If the document still needs changes, use kspec plan export @plan-ref --output ./plan.md, edit it, then kspec plan import ./plan.md --into @plan-ref.
When the plan is ready to materialize, approve it: kspec plan set @plan-ref --status approved

Derive specs and tasks.
Use: kspec plan derive @plan-ref [--module @module] --tasks
Stored module_ref from import is used automatically when present; explicit --module overrides it.
If you want specs only first, omit --tasks.

Review derived specs/tasks and apply any missing traits.
Use: kspec trait list for available traits.
For each created spec, consider cross-cutting concerns (json-output, dry-run, error-guidance, semantic-exit-codes, shadow-commit, filterable-list).
Apply any missing traits: kspec item trait add @spec @trait
Validate references - kspec validate --refs
steps.on_fail: Fix reference issues (dangling refs, missing spec_ref/plan_ref links, stale plan/module assumptions)

steps.content:
Start implementation.
Pick first task from: kspec plan get @plan --json (derived_tasks).
Use: kspec task start @task
Then follow /task-work for task lifecycle.

workflows.description: Execute plan via incremental spec creation - create plan record, find parent, create specs with AC, review traits, derive tasks with plan linking, validate, start work. Follows @spec-plan-design.

steps.content:
Create plan record.
Use: kspec plan add --title "Plan Title" --content "Brief description of what's being planned" --status approved
Status approved because you're committing to the work.

Find parent and create spec items.
Search: kspec search "<keyword>", kspec item list --tag <domain>, kspec item get @parent
If no suitable parent exists, create a module: kspec item add --type module --title "Module Name"
Create specs: kspec item add --under @parent --title "Title" --type feature --slug slug
Repeat for each spec.

Add acceptance criteria.
For each spec: kspec item ac add @spec --given "precondition" --when "action" --then "expected result"
Each AC independently testable. 3-5 AC per spec is typical.
Cover happy path and key edge cases.

Review and apply traits.
Use: kspec trait list to browse available traits.
Consider cross-cutting concerns for the spec type
(CLI features often need: json-output, dry-run, error-guidance, semantic-exit-codes).
Apply: kspec item trait add @spec @trait
Traits add inherited AC automatically.

Derive tasks and link to plan.
Preview: kspec derive @spec --dry-run
Create: kspec derive @spec (recursive by default, creates task tree with dependencies)
Link each derived task to plan: kspec task set @task --plan-ref @plan
Set plan active: kspec plan set @plan --status active
Add implementation notes: kspec task note @task "Implementation approach: ..."
Note: task set --plan-ref creates a one-way link (task->plan). The plan's derived_tasks array is only auto-updated by kspec plan derive, not by manual linking.
Validate all references - kspec validate --refs. Verify spec_ref and plan_ref resolve correctly on tasks.
steps.on_fail: Fix reference issues

steps.content:
Verify structure.
kspec item status @spec shows linked tasks.
For each task: kspec task get @task confirms plan_ref and spec_ref are set.
Note: check task-side links (not plan's derived_tasks which is not auto-updated in manual path).

Start implementation.
Use: kspec task start @first-task
Then follow /task-work for task lifecycle.

workflows.description: Core pattern for working on a task. Full lifecycle from start through PR merge.

steps.content:
Check for existing needs_work, in_progress, or pending_review tasks.
Use: kspec session start (shows active work first)
Priority: needs_work > in_progress > ready
Note: pending_review tasks are handled by review subagent, not worker.
steps.on_fail:
Inherit existing work instead of starting new.
Pick up needs_work task (fix review feedback) or in_progress task and continue.
Only start new work if user explicitly says to ignore existing work.

steps.content:
Choose task to work on.
Use: kspec tasks ready to see available tasks
Or: kspec task get @task to see task details

Verify work is not already done.
Check git history: git log --oneline --grep="feature-name"
Read implementation code if it exists.
steps.on_fail: Mark task complete with "Already implemented" reason

steps.content:
Start the task.
Use: kspec task start @task
This marks the task in_progress.

Work on the task, adding notes as you go.
Use: kspec task note @task "What you're doing..."
Add notes during work, not just at end.
All changes committed
steps.on_fail:
Commit changes with Task: @task trailer.
Example: git commit -m "feat: description\n\nTask: @task-slug"

steps.content:
Run local review before submitting.
Spawn a subagent using Task tool with prompt:
"Run /local-review for @spec-ref. Report all findings with severity."

If MUST-FIX findings: fix them, re-commit, re-run local review.
If SHOULD-FIX or SUGGESTION only: note findings, proceed to submit.
If actionable items not worth fixing now: kspec inbox add "..."

If this is a fix cycle (needs_work task):
  1. Read PR review comments: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews
  2. Fix MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX issues identified in comments
  3. Commit and push fixes to PR branch
  4. Submit task: kspec task submit @task
  5. Stop responding — reviewer re-reviews in next iteration

Otherwise (new work):
  1. Submit task: kspec task submit @task
  2. Create PR: /pr skill
  3. Stop responding — pr-reviewer agent handles PR review via dispatch
PR merged to main
steps.on_fail: Wait for PR review and merge before completing task.

steps.content:
Complete task after PR merged.
Use: kspec task complete @task --reason "Summary of what was done"
This marks the task completed.

workflows.description: Quality enforcement for pre-PR review. 8-step gate: own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, test quality, test strategy, test isolation, code quality, regression check, and report. Issues flagged as MUST-FIX. The goal is to find problems, not to approve.

steps.content:
Get spec reference and read acceptance criteria (own + inherited trait ACs).
Use: kspec item get @spec to see own ACs and inherited trait ACs.
Both own ACs and inherited trait ACs need test coverage.

Every own AC has test coverage with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N annotation.
Every inherited trait AC has test coverage with // AC: @trait-slug ac-N annotation.
Search tests/ and packages/ for annotations. Run kspec validate to cross-check.
steps.on_fail:
MUST-FIX: Missing AC coverage (own or trait) is a blocking issue.
List each uncovered AC. Trait AC warnings from kspec validate are blockers.

steps.content:
All tests validate real behavior (no fluff tests).
Tests should fail if the feature breaks.
Reject tests that always pass or only test implementation details.
steps.on_fail:
MUST-FIX: Identify and flag fluff tests.
A test that doesn't validate behavior is not valid.

steps.content:
Test strategy prefers E2E over unit tests.
Test the CLI as a user would invoke it.
Unit tests are okay for complex logic, but E2E proves it works.
steps.on_fail: Consider adding E2E tests for CLI functionality.

steps.content:
Tests run in temp directories (not kspec repo).
All tests must use system temp or /tmp.
This prevents nested worktree issues and data corruption.
steps.on_fail:
MUST-FIX: Tests must run in temp directories.
Test fixtures should create isolated test repos.

steps.content:
Code follows existing patterns. No duplicated logic, no ignored shared utilities.
Implementation matches conventions in neighboring files.
steps.on_fail:
MUST-FIX: Flag duplicated code, ignored utilities, inconsistent patterns.
Each finding must include file:line and description.

steps.content:
Full test suite passes (npm test). No regressions.
New code must not break existing spec or trait AC tests.
steps.on_fail: MUST-FIX: Test failures must be fixed before PR.

steps.content:
Report findings.
List all MUST-FIX issues that block PR creation.
MUST-FIX findings first, each with file:line.
Non-blocking suggestions noted separately.
When invoked as subagent, return findings to caller.
MUST-FIX items block PR creation.

workflows.description: PR review subagent workflow for loop mode. Runs local review (own + trait AC coverage, code quality), verifies spec alignment, reviews code quality, checks for regressions, fixes issues, waits for CI, posts structured GitHub review with inline comments, and merges with quality gates. The goal is to find problems and verify quality — not to rubber-stamp merges. Sequential execution (agent dispatch waits). CRITICAL: After ANY push, must re-verify CI passes before merge.

steps.content:
Run local review workflow first (ac-1).
Use: /local-review skill or kspec workflow start @local-review

This checks:
- Own AC coverage (all spec ACs have test annotations)
- Trait AC coverage (all inherited trait ACs have test annotations)
- Test quality (no fluff tests, proper isolation)
- E2E preference (integration tests over unit tests where appropriate)
- Test isolation (temp directories, cleanup)
- Code quality (no duplicated logic, consistent patterns, shared utilities used)
- Regression check (npm test passes fully)

Verify all ACs (own + trait) linked to task have test coverage (ac-2).

Check test files for own AC annotations: // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
Check test files for trait AC annotations: // AC: @trait-slug ac-N
Run kspec item get @spec-ref to enumerate all ACs (own + inherited).
Run kspec validate to cross-check trait AC coverage.

MUST-FIX if:
- Spec has own ACs but no tests reference them
- Spec implements traits but inherited ACs lack test coverage
- Tests exist but don't cover all ACs (own or trait)
steps.on_fail:
Add missing test coverage before continuing.
Tests must validate AC behavior, not just implementation.
Trait AC warnings from kspec validate are blockers.

steps.content:
Verify implementation matches spec requirements (ac-3).

This is NOT just "do tests pass" - verify:
- Implementation aligns with spec description
- All AC conditions are actually implemented
- No deviation from spec without justification

Read spec, read implementation, compare.
steps.on_fail:
Fix misalignment between spec and implementation.
Update code to match spec, or note why deviation is necessary.

steps.content:
Evaluate local-review findings (ac-4).

If MUST-FIX issues found:
- Attempt to fix them in-place
- Run tests after fixes
- Push changes

If issues cannot be resolved:
- Mark task automation: needs_review with explanation (ac-8)
- EXIT workflow

Decision matrix:
- MUST-FIX issues, can fix -> Fix and continue
- MUST-FIX issues, cannot fix -> Mark needs_review, EXIT
- Only advisory issues -> Continue with merge
- No issues -> Continue with merge

Push changes (if any fixes were made).
Use: git push

This triggers CI to run on latest code.

NOTE: Only push if changes were actually made during issue fixing.

Wait for CI to complete and pass (ac-5).

CRITICAL: This step MUST be executed EVERY time changes are pushed.
Do not skip or assume prior CI checks are valid.

Poll CI status until all checks complete.
Use: gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup

Do NOT proceed while checks are running or failing.
VERIFY the checks ran against current HEAD (latest commit SHA).
steps.on_fail:
If CI fails:
- Investigate failure
- Fix if possible
- Push changes
- RETURN TO THIS STEP and wait for CI again (do not skip ahead)

If cannot fix:
- Mark task automation: needs_review with CI failure details (ac-8)
- EXIT workflow

steps.content:
Follow PR review merge gates (ac-6).
Use: kspec workflow start @pr-review-merge

This ensures:
- All CI checks pass
- All review feedback addressed
- All @claude requests completed
- All review threads resolved

Only merge when all gates pass.

Verify PR was successfully merged.
Use: gh pr view --json state,mergedAt

Confirm state is MERGED.
steps.on_fail:
If merge failed:
- Check for conflicts or protection rules
- Attempt resolution
- If cannot resolve: mark automation: needs_review (ac-8)
- EXIT workflow

steps.content:
Mark task completed with PR reference (ac-7).
Use: kspec task complete @task --reason "Merged in PR #N. <summary>"

Include in reason:
- PR number
- Summary of what was implemented
- Any notable changes or deviations
- AC coverage confirmation

Check for friction during PR review (ac-11).

If significant friction encountered (not one-off):
1. Search existing observations first:
   kspec meta observations list --type friction
2. Only capture if unique:
   kspec meta observe friction "[REVIEW SUBAGENT] <description>"

Be selective - systemic patterns only, not one-off issues.
This step is optional - only capture if friction was encountered.

workflows.description: Execute plan via incremental spec creation - create plan record, find parent, create specs with AC, review traits, derive tasks with plan linking, validate, start work. Follows @spec-plan-design.

steps.content:
Create plan record.
Use: kspec plan add --title "Plan Title" --content "Brief description of what's being planned" --status approved
Status approved because you're committing to the work.

Find parent and create spec items.
Search: kspec search "<keyword>", kspec item list --tag <domain>, kspec item get @parent
If no suitable parent exists, create a module: kspec item add --type module --title "Module Name"
Create specs: kspec item add --under @parent --title "Title" --type feature --slug slug
Repeat for each spec.

Add acceptance criteria.
For each spec: kspec item ac add @spec --given "precondition" --when "action" --then "expected result"
Each AC independently testable. 3-5 AC per spec is typical.
Cover happy path and key edge cases.

Review and apply traits.
Use: kspec trait list to browse available traits.
Consider cross-cutting concerns for the spec type
(CLI features often need: json-output, dry-run, error-guidance, semantic-exit-codes).
Apply: kspec item trait add @spec @trait
Traits add inherited AC automatically.

Derive tasks and link to plan.
Preview: kspec derive @spec --dry-run
Create: kspec derive @spec (recursive by default, creates task tree with dependencies)
Link each derived task to plan: kspec task set @task --plan-ref @plan
Set plan active: kspec plan set @plan --status active
Add implementation notes: kspec task note @task "Implementation approach: ..."
Note: task set --plan-ref creates a one-way link (task->plan). The plan's derived_tasks
array is only auto-updated by kspec plan derive and kspec plan import, not by manual linking.
Validate all references - kspec validate --refs. Verify spec_ref and plan_ref resolve correctly on tasks.
steps.on_fail: Fix reference issues

steps.content:
Verify structure.
kspec item status @spec shows linked tasks.
For each task: kspec task get @task confirms plan_ref and spec_ref are set.
Note: check task-side links (not plan's derived_tasks which is not auto-updated in manual path).

Start implementation.
Use: kspec task start @first-task
Then follow /task-work for task lifecycle.

workflows.description:
Quality gate for reviewing and merging PRs. Ensures all CI passes, all reviews
addressed, all requests completed, and all threads resolved before merge.

CRITICAL: After ANY push, you MUST re-verify CI from the beginning. Do not trust
prior CI checks - they are invalidated by new commits. Never merge without fresh
CI verification on the current HEAD.

steps.content: All CI checks complete (none pending or running)
steps.on_fail: Wait for CI to finish. Do not merge while checks are running.

steps.content: All CI checks pass (green)
steps.on_fail:
Fix failures, push changes.
WAIT for CI to re-run completely.
THEN re-verify this step (CI passing) before continuing - do not proceed while CI is running.

steps.content:
Read ALL review comments on the PR.
Use: gh pr view --comments or GitHub UI
Check for: automated reviews, human reviews, inline comments.
All review feedback addressed (post findings, do NOT fix code)
steps.on_fail:
Post each finding as an inline PR comment with severity prefix (MUST-FIX:, SHOULD-FIX:, SUGGESTION:).
Do NOT fix code yourself — you are a reviewer, not a fixer.
If MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX found: transition task to needs_work and exit without merging.
Use: kspec task needs-work @task-ref --reason "findings summary"

steps.content:
Check for @claude mentions or other requests in comments.
Look for actions the PR agent couldn't complete (limited permissions).
Examples: add inbox items, run kspec commands, update tasks.
All requested actions completed
steps.on_fail: Complete the actions yourself before proceeding.

steps.content: All review threads resolved in GitHub UI
steps.on_fail:
Click "Resolve conversation" on each thread after addressing.
The pr-review-resolution-check CI will block merge if threads remain.

steps.content:
FINAL CI VERIFICATION: Re-check CI status NOW.
Use: gh pr checks or gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup
ALL checks must be complete AND passing on current HEAD.
If ANY changes were pushed during this workflow, CI must have re-run.
steps.on_fail:
DO NOT MERGE. Wait for CI to complete and pass.
If CI is failing, fix issues and restart workflow from beginning.

steps.content: Ready to merge?
options: Yes - all checks green, no MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX, all threads resolved
Issues found - kick back to worker (kspec task needs-work @task --reason "...")
No - need user approval to merge with known issues
Skip - user explicitly said to merge anyway

steps.content:
Merge the PR.
Use: gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
Or: GitHub UI merge button

workflows.description: Loop variant of task-work-session for autonomous agents. Auto-filters to automation-eligible tasks, auto-resolves decisions. Task selection: needs_work > in_progress > unblocking > priority. Includes local-review subagent step and fix cycle handling for needs_work tasks. Verifies work needed including trait AC coverage. Implementation quality: search for existing utilities, match code style, run full test suite. PR review handled by pr-reviewer agent dispatch.

steps.content:
Filter to automation-eligible tasks only.
Use: kspec tasks ready --eligible
This ensures only tasks marked automation: eligible are considered.

Select task by priority order.
First, run `kspec tasks ready --eligible` — its output is authoritative. Do not select exit based on assumptions.
Check in order:
1. needs_work tasks (fix cycle — address review feedback, highest priority)
2. in_progress tasks (continue existing work)
3. Ready tasks that unblock others (high impact)
4. Highest priority ready task (lowest number = higher priority)

Note: pending_review tasks are handled by the pr-reviewer agent via dispatch.
options: needs_work task exists -> fix review feedback (fix cycle)
in_progress task exists -> continue that task
Ready task unblocks others -> select that task
Only isolated ready tasks -> select highest priority (lowest number)
`kspec tasks ready --eligible` returned empty -> stop responding (agent dispatch exits automatically)
`kspec tasks ready --eligible` shows all blocked -> stop responding (agent dispatch exits automatically)

steps.content:
Verify work is needed - but VALIDATE, don't trust notes.

Notes are context, not proof. If a task is in the queue, there's a reason.

To mark "Already implemented" you MUST:
1. RUN the tests (npm test) - they must PASS, not skip
2. VERIFY own AC coverage - each spec AC has a test annotated // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
3. VERIFY trait AC coverage - each inherited trait AC has a test annotated // AC: @trait-slug ac-N
4. RUN kspec validate - zero trait AC coverage warnings for your spec
5. CHECK implementation matches spec requirements

DO NOT mark complete just because:
- Notes say "already done" (verify yourself)
- Tests exist but skip in CI (that's a gap to fix)
- Someone said it was implemented (run the tests)

Treat this like a code review - validate the actual work.
steps.on_fail:
Only if tests PASS and ACs are COVERED:
Mark task complete with "Already implemented" reason and EXIT

steps.content:
Start selected task (if not already in_progress).
Use: kspec task start @task

If task has plan_ref, load plan context before deep implementation work:
  1. Check task link: kspec task get @task
  2. If plan_ref is non-null: kspec plan get @plan-ref

Work on the task, adding notes as you go.
Use: kspec task note @task "What you're doing..."
Add notes during work, not just at end.

SCOPE EXPANSION: If you discover missing implementation while testing,
implementing it IS in scope. The goal is verified behavior, not just test files.
"Add tests for X" means "ensure X is verified" - if X doesn't exist, implement it.

Verify Definition of Done before committing.

Read task notes for any DoD criteria. Common constraints:
- "No test.skip() calls" - verify no skipped tests in changes
- "All own ACs covered" - verify each spec AC has corresponding test
- "All trait ACs covered" - verify each inherited trait AC has test
- "No TODO/FIXME" - no placeholder comments
- "No duplicated logic" - search for existing utilities before writing new code

CRITICAL: Never use test.skip() to document missing functionality.
If functionality is missing, implement it - that's in scope.

If DoD criteria exist and are not met, fix the gaps first.
steps.on_fail:
Do not proceed with DoD violations.
Either fix the gaps or escalate to user if scope is unclear.

steps.content:
Commit changes with Task: @task trailer.
All changes must be committed before submitting.

Run local review via subagent before submitting.
Spawn a subagent using Task tool with prompt:
"Run /local-review for @spec-ref. Report all findings with severity."

If MUST-FIX findings: fix them, re-commit, re-run local review.
If SHOULD-FIX or SUGGESTION only: note findings, proceed to submit.
If actionable items not worth fixing now: kspec inbox add "..."

If this is a fix cycle (needs_work task):
  1. Read PR review comments: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews
  2. Fix MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX issues identified in comments
  3. Commit and push fixes to PR branch
  4. Submit task: kspec task submit @task
  5. Stop responding — reviewer re-reviews in next iteration

Otherwise (new work):
  1. Submit task: kspec task submit @task
  2. Create PR: /pr skill
  3. Stop responding — pr-reviewer agent handles PR review via dispatch

rules: Use conventional commit format (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore)
Reference task in commit body when applicable
Keep subject line under 72 characters
Include Co-Authored-By for AI contributions
Add notes when completing significant work
Include what was done, approach taken, and why
Note any deviations from plan or unexpected findings
Keep notes concise but informative for future context
Before resubmitting after a fix cycle, add a note summarizing what changed and why — this becomes a key activity timeline entry for reviewers

examples.good: Implemented retry logic with exponential backoff. Chose 3 retries max based on API rate limits.

rules: Use kebab-case for slugs (task-user-login, not taskUserLogin)
Prefix task slugs with 'task-' for clarity
Use descriptive names that indicate purpose
Keep slugs short but unambiguous
Use lowercase tags
Standard tags include mvp, post-mvp, bug, feature, infra, design
Add domain tags like cli, schema, parser, tasks
Limit to 3-5 tags per item for focus
Use descriptive branch names that indicate the type and scope of work
Use prefixes: feat/ for features, fix/ for bug fixes, refactor/ for refactoring, docs/ for documentation
Keep branch names short but meaningful (e.g., feat/user-auth, fix/login-crash)
Use kebab-case for branch names
Before committing, verify current branch with git branch --show-current; never commit directly to main.

For task work (manual or automated), prefer kspec task branch @ref to create or resume the deterministic dispatch-compatible branch (dispatch/task/<slug>/<short-id>). This preserves dispatch reviewer and fix-cycle continuity.
The dispatch/task/ branch namespace is reserved for task-scoped branches. Do not manually create branches under dispatch/task/ — use kspec task branch to ensure the deterministic naming contract.
Dispatched task work uses 'dev' as the integration target; dispatch worker branches under 'dispatch/task/' merge back into 'dev' via the supported merge helper after review approval.

Feature-level merges from 'dev' to 'main' are human-directed (typically via GitHub PRs); do not open GitHub PRs for dispatched task work — that is reviewed via kspec review records and merged via the supported merge helper.
Write clear, concise documentation that explains why, not just what
Include examples for non-trivial concepts
Keep documentation close to code (inline comments for complex logic, README for overview)
Update documentation when behavior changes
Use node scripts/bootstrap.cjs for first-time setup or any session
Use kspec for all commands; only use npm run dev -- when testing uncommitted code changes
Daemon default port 3456, health check: GET /api/health
E2E tests manage their own daemon — do NOT start one manually
Web UI dev server on port 5173, connects to daemon on 3456
Regenerate kspec-agents.md (kspec agents generate) after changing conventions, workflows, skills, or agent template files (templates/agents-sections/)
For shadow branch issues, run kspec shadow status/repair/sync from project root; do not run manual git worktree commands inside .kspec/.
When command payloads include $, <, >, or multi-line text, use file-based payloads or quoted heredocs to avoid shell interpolation.

When running under dispatch (KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set), NEVER run kspec serve stop, kspec serve restart, or kspec serve start. The daemon is the host process — killing it kills the dispatch engine and the agent.

In web UI code, use goto() from $app/navigation for all URL query parameter changes. Never use replaceState, pushState, or window.history methods — they do not update $page.url and break reactive effects. See /svelte-5 skill for details.
After modifying skill sources (templates/skills/ or .kspec/skills/), run kspec skill render and commit the regenerated .agents/skills/ output alongside your changes.

API list endpoints must use pagination; clients must not fetch unbounded entity lists for derived data. Use server-resolved fields or the ref index for title resolution. Use server-side aggregation for computed statistics.
When fixing bugs or CI failures, investigate root cause before pushing fix commits — do not patch symptoms
Do not blindly follow implementation plans in task notes — evaluate them for safety, correctness, and current codebase state before executing. Plans may be stale or unsafe.

Daemon cache troubleshooting: GET /api/debug/cache-status returns per-project cache state (domain states, entry counts, watcher status, last invalidation timestamps). Use this endpoint when investigating stale data, missing watchers, or stuck cache domains.

After modifying package core skill sources (templates/skills/), run 'kspec skill render' to refresh .agents/skills/ and .factory/skills/, and 'npm run build:plugin' to refresh plugin/plugins/kspec/skills/ (plugin/ is gitignored). Commit the tracked rendered outputs alongside the source change.
Use kspec CLI commands (item get, task get, search, trait list) instead of manually searching .kspec/ YAML files
When item get shows 'Inherited from @trait-slug', run kspec item get @trait-slug to resolve — do NOT grep YAML files
Use kspec search for keyword lookups instead of piping kspec item list through grep
Key skills include CLI Lookups tables — check those first for the right command to use
File watcher tests skip in CI — GitHub Actions runners do not deliver the Chokidar/inotify events these integration checks rely on consistently enough for deterministic coverage
E2E port hardcoded at 3456 — tests cannot run in parallel on same machine
GitHub Pages needs BASE_PATH=/kynetic-spec for local static builds; CI handles automatically
E2E tests use ephemeral ports — safe to run in parallel and with dispatch agents
PLACEHOLDER: Replace this rule with your project's architectural constraints and patterns

Treat the following as shared/package guidance surfaces that ship to consumer projects: templates/skills/, templates/agents-sections/, templates/skills/manifest.yaml, plugin/plugins/kspec/skills/, rendered package/core skill output under .agents/skills/ and .factory/skills/ when the source is a package core skill, and generated kspec-agents.md sections derived from package templates.

Package-shipped guidance must describe universal kspec mechanics only. Kynetic self-hosting branch policy, repo paths, quality gates, generated artifact maintenance rules, dispatch workflow choices, agent ids, and external review policy belong in project-local context (AGENTS.md, .kspec/skills/, or project meta conventions), not in shared guidance.

When a task or plan changes any shared/package guidance surface, the reviewer must confirm semantic project-neutrality before approval. Mechanical render/install/update tests are not sufficient evidence that prose is project-neutral.

Reviewers must check both directions: shared/package text does not hard-code Kynetic-only policy as universal, AND any Kynetic self-hosting instruction removed from shared text still has a project-local home (AGENTS.md, project-local .kspec/skills/ skill, or project meta convention).

Project-neutrality enforcement belongs in convention and reviewer judgment, not in broad markdown scanners or string-denylist tests. Do not add prose-neutrality AC-tagged tests or broad markdown scanners as the primary enforcement mechanism.
ULIDs use Crockford base32 (excludes I, L, O, U) — invalid ULIDs cause SILENT test failures
Use testUlid() helper or kspec util ulid for valid test ULIDs
Never use JSON.stringify() for YAML — use template strings or yaml library stringify()
Playwright E2E tests excluded from vitest — run separately with npm run test:e2e
E2E fixtures are SEPARATE from unit test fixtures — never mix them
Use npm run test:shard1/shard2/shard3 for faster local dev runs (~50s vs ~150s). Full suite still required before PR.
testUlid(prefix) is deterministic unless you pass a sequence; use testUlids() or explicit sequences when tests need distinct IDs.
In tests that run git commit in temp repos, set git config user.name and git config user.email after git init.

Always use npm test (or npm run test:shard1/2/3 for faster dev runs) to run tests. Never invoke vitest or npx vitest directly — the test runner script (scripts/test.cjs) performs environment readiness checks before executing.

Test runner caches results by content hash (git blob SHAs + unstaged diffs + untracked files + Node version + vitest args + behavior-affecting env vars: CI, TZ, NODE_ENV, NODE_OPTIONS, and KSPEC_*-prefixed vars except KSPEC_SESSION_ID and KSPEC_TEST_PROGRESS). Same content = cache hit, even after commits/rebases; changing a behavior-affecting env var produces a distinct cache entry. Use --fresh to force a full re-run.

Test output is condensed by default: success shows only summary stats, failure shows failed tests with error snippets. Full verbose log path is printed. Use --verbose (or CI=true) for full streaming output.
Cache is session-scoped under KSPEC_SESSION_ID for dispatch isolation. Parallel agents get independent caches. --fresh clears only the current session's cache.
expect.anything() does not match undefined or null in vitest — use the literal undefined when asserting undefined args
vi.spyOn(Class.prototype, 'method') may have empty spy.mock.calls for cross-module ESM calls — use a closure variable to capture args instead of asserting on the spy directly
setupTempFixtures() returns a flat dir where tempDir IS the specDir — do not path.join with .kspec/ for session or budget operations

Prefer behavioral/integration tests over static source analysis. The no-source-scanning oxlint rule enforces at lint time. Use readTestOutput/readTestOutputSync from tests/helpers/cli.ts for legitimate test output file reads.
When tests fail after a code change, evaluate whether the tests are correct before adding workarounds — the test may be exposing a real bug in the change
Multi-project test fixtures need a git repo and shadow detection for initContext() to resolve specDir — use setupMultiDirFixtures() or manually init git and create .kspec/ markers

Test daemons must register cleanup via vitest's onTestFinished at spawn time, not in the test body. Prefer direct spawn() (see tests/e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts) so the OS reaps the daemon via process group on parent death. If a test must invoke 'kspec serve start --detach' because the CLI command itself is under test, read the PID immediately after the spawn returns and register process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM') in onTestFinished — never rely on inline cleanup that won't run on assertion failure.

Test helpers that drive kspec CLI subprocesses must require an explicit cwd parameter. Never fall back to process.cwd() — a missing cwd is a test bug, not a default. A silent fallback caused a shadow worktree destruction incident on 2026-04-11.

Test helpers that spawn subprocesses inheriting process.env must route env through buildTestSubprocessEnv() (tests/helpers/cli.ts) so runner-mode vars (CI, KSPEC_TEST_PROGRESS, FORCE_COLOR, NO_COLOR) plus dispatch/agent vars are stripped. Direct { ...process.env, ... } spreads leak the parent's CI-mode behavior into the subprocess and silently break non-verbose-path tests in CI.

Builds and test runs in the same worktree serialize on a per-worktree advisory lock (scripts/build-test-lock.cjs): npm run build / build:e2e waits for a running npm test and vice versa, so a 'Waiting for build/test lock' message is normal, not a hang. Lock coordination vars (KSPEC_BUILD_TEST_LOCK_*) are excluded from the test cache key.

Tests must never trigger a rebuild of the real dist/ (npm pack without --ignore-scripts runs prepack; npm run build:daemon rewrites dist/daemon) — the build/test lock fails such nested builds fast.
